review: You want free entrance? Then go to this place and plunge into warm sea water in a cold weather.You will love the view and be amazed how the nature formed these rocks.The place is not so crowded by the time I visited this place.Going solo into this place. I met a kind Ajussi who lives in Jeju. He guided me to reach the top of the rock formation. He always come to this place to see dolphins and observe sunset.
You need to pay 2000 Korean dollars to have a sight of this waterfalls. It's not a lot of money so it's good
You have to go down to get the waterfall. Entrance fee is 3k won. Crowded with people. The waterfall is quite beautifull as it
You cannot see the water in the crater because its dry better to go there on Winter... But a must place to visit also when your in Jeju.

Yakcheonsa Temple is thought to be Asia?셲 largest Buddhist temple. The main temple has one storey below ground and five stories above with a floor area of  more than 175 sq m and a ceiling height of 29 metres. The Main Hall has 18000 Buddha statues and receives many worshippers for its medicinal waters. Monks were praying and chanting when we were there - I liked it very much.

Wow wow wow!! This beach is absolutely stunning!! We enjoyed it while staying at the Hyatt Regency. It wasn't packed at all on the side of the hotels side but there was an area roped away that had more people. It was so beautiful and although the water was cold it was still enjoyable. Must go if in Jeju!
Worth a visit to this waterfall. The waterfall on one side and the sea on the others!
Wonderful waterfall with an easy walk down toward it.  The path is well marked and is usually quite busy.  Would definitely visit again

Wonderful beach in Jeju island. Very clear water. Amazing colors and good vibes all around. You can spend here one day to have relax and chill out. And If you want you can walk around. There are close to the beach a lot of restaurants and caf챕s

With a minimal fee of KRW10k one gets to kayak along the stream for 20 mins. The water is clear and deep. Each wooden kayak can only take 2 passenger with only one person rowing. The catch is the ticket counter is a distance away from the port. And the best time to go is on a weekdays. Weekends are usually crowded.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

While its really small against Western style theme parks we enjoyed an afternoon on the rides.  Also if you arw a US military service member or have a military ID (they don't know the difference between a dependent or soldier) you can get an amazing deal.  It was 9k won for 2 day combo pass for the theme park and the water park!!! Which is usually 39k won.  There is also a discount if ypu are staying at one of the resort hotels.  The park was clearly designed by someone who has visited and studied the Disney parks specifically Tokyo Disney Sea.  Which isnt a bad thing just needed to be mentioned.  This was our 2nd visit and have never had to wait in a line for the rides.  Also the rides are enjoyable the staff is friendly & helpful and the park is very well maintained.

When going into the falls we thought it was just to see the one water fall  the trails lead to several spots and additional falls. It was so gorgeous and a beautiful hike. There was a lot of stairs  and I did see some tiny kids really struggling at the last falls area. The even had a warning sign for elderly and children that the climb was difficult. It was not bad for my family and children but I could see how others may struggle.

What a beautiful walk.  The walk up is on one side of the hill and the walk down is on another so there are fantastic views to be enjoyed.  It took me a half hour to go up the 180 meters and I am in good shape.  Take water and sunscreen.

Went with my son and husband on a very hot day! Park well laid out with several drink food and shade stops on way round! We spent a few hours to see it all! Caves were a highlight - very interesting and cool!! Reptiles and birds ok - not my thing! Enjoyed water area especially cold showers we could stand under :-)) overall a good place to visit and see a range of sights! Easy to get to on main coastal bus route Enjoy
Went there since it was near the waterfall. The bridge is quite nicely lighted up during the night. We were there for 10 mins. Nothing much just the bridge during the winter night.

Well worth the small trek down.  Do a little rock/boulder hopping to the base and you can get a nice spray.  If you catch this waterfall during the rainy season or after a good rain it will be much more powerful.  Take the time to visit this place...maybe a little crowded but plenty of space to find your own spot.

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..

We?re staying at the Lotte Hotel and this place is within walking distance.  First waterfall didn?t have any fall at this time due to a drought or off season maybe.  2nd fall was nice & it involved some walking down the stairs.  Overall the park is very pretty with its vibrant colors of the trees and the famous bridge you can walk across.

We were spoiled as it was Buddha's birthday and the Lotus Lantern Festival - the temple looked marvellous with all the lanterns hanging there and it's a beautiful site overlooking the water.  All very peaceful and idyllic.

We went to see the beautiful rock formations but also enjoyed the natural swimming pools at the left side of the fork in the trail.  So much fun to enjoy the water on a hot day.  GORGEOUS views and just an awesome stop on your way around the island!

We went on a Sunday at about 10+AM and it was crowded. Transparent kayaks have to be reserved in advance so we opted for a floating water bike. When we bought our tickets we were told to come back at 12PM (the time was handwritten on the ticket). There are shade and chairs at the waiting area close to the rides where you get called out when your turn comes. Since we had more than an hour to spare we headed to Jeongbang Waterfalls (about 10 mins drive away) and made it back on time. The bike was easy to maneuver and unlike bicycles the handles do not steer. Overall an enjoyable 20 mins experience for 15000KRW.

We went on a Sunday afternoon and it was very very crowded. Read so many great reviews about this place so we were expecting hot fragrant green tea and yummy green tea cakes. We were really disappointed. We paid 9000won for a tea and cake set the cake was ok but the tea green tasted like plain water with two tiny leaves floating around...

We went in Jun and there were hardly any flowers. Mainly statues. Nothing much in the cave. Just like a normal park with a small man-made waterfall. Entrance fees not cheap  too. Don't waste your time !
We went here to see the waterfall. The stones were very slippery but otherwise it was okey. The easiest way to get here is by taxi I think.

We walked from our hotel located at the Arang Joeul Street to the Saeyeongyo bridge for almost 30 minutes. There were many locals visited and walking leisurely there. There many restaurants and the Seogwipo Submarine was located on the way there. You can see the beautiful ocean wave along the way to the bridge. The bridge connected to the Saesom island. The island was brighted by light and old korean song music at night. We visited the bridge twice in the evening to see the colourful light and daytime to observe the surrounding scenery. The trail to Cheonjiyeon waterfall can be found? on the way to the Saesom bridge. The entrance to the waterfall was after Chilsimnigyo bridge.

We walked down to the water for a better view.  Parts of the trek were without steps or handrails and are not for the weak or unsteady.  Saw several women with heels fall when attempting to traverse the rocks.  The best part was the old women divers selling their fresh seafood!

We visited with our 4 kids and it was a hit with them.  Pretty waterfall and you are able to get pretty close to it with the mist from the waterfall hitting you.  A couple of our kids crossed the river and played on the rocks on the other side.  Was worth the visit.

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.
We visited here in December and the water was cold.  We enjoyed the beauty of the sea while drinking coffee in the nearby cafe's roof top terrace.

We visited at the beginning of May and it was cold. It also rained when we were on the beach. So could not enjoy the water.However beach is very nice and clean. We had coffee in the coffee shop on beach which gives you nice view of the beach.Its just opposite Hallim park so can be combined.Would nice to spend a warm and sunny day on this beach.
We tried putting our water bottle down to see if the bottle roll up downhill.. errmmmm... Yeahhh.. not disappointed anyway

We took one walk here. Vertical rise of about 200m through nature. A couple of hours of hiking & stopping to view the plants & birds. Great view of the crater from the top. Worth the trek. Carry lots of water if it hot!

We stumbled upon this place whilst walking about but didn't regret it.I would be careful if you are accompanying very young children or old people as the stairs are made of rock and quite difficult to negotiate. Our 5 year old made it ok but required assistance.A nice place to visit but not much in the way of a waterfall when we were there. Perhaps they take the water in during the day? (that was a joke by the way!)

We stopped by Wolijeongri Beach for about 30 min. on the way to UDO; the water was very clear.  There were kids playing sand on the beach. The view was peaceful. We enjoyed our short walk along the beach. You can get some snacks and a good coffee from a caf챕 or a convenient store nearby. There is a restroom facility too.

we stayed at Black sands area and walked by Oll trail 18-19 to this beach. beach looks nice although water is cold and of course could not enjoy it fully. lots of restaurants around obviously overpriced for coming tourists.

We read some blogs that showed amazing blue-green water kayaks and paddleboards and lots of places to jump in and swim.  When we got there we found some pretty views (including a pretty violent whirlpool that formed in the river as the tide came in) but ZERO activities. So it was a bit disappointing on that level.....but still a pretty place for a stroll and lots of cafes/shops/trinket-sellers around.
We passed by just to get to Jeongbang waterfall. Nothing special but it is free entry. So no harm taking a walk and snapping some photos overlooking the sea.

We only spent 4 nights in Jeju and happened to pass by this place on our way to the city center. We decided to spend half a day soaking up the sun. These 5 hours were a highlight! The town was pretty quiet and the beach wasn't too crowded. Beautiful views! There was a nice restaurant on the water to get snacks. Water was refreshing! Note: I noticed a camp ground on the far right side of the beach. Cool idea for the future. BE AWARE there are very large spiders over near that boardwalk. Yikes!

We need to pay for the entrance fees but it is not that pricey and worth it. You need to take a few stairs to finally reached the waterfall area. The view is very sceneric and worth to take a picture on every angle of it. A must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

We manage to visit this Mysterious Road while on our way going to Hallasan but we are unable to try the road on our own. The road is really mysterious but the length of the road is not that long. We just try the road by using a mineral bootleg water and it is really awesome. You can try Visit it if you are curious about the road.

We hiked the mountain a bit late but still was very interesting. There are many trails to hike just make sure to be back to the bus station before 5:30. We missed throats bus and a Korean guy who works there showed his hospitality. He took me and 4 others to the next station and civilization ( 30 Klm away). Be light when hiking you will get some portable water and a shelter to get God about 3 Klm from the beginning. It was a very nice experience It an be very foggy

We hiked down to Jungmun Beach from the Lotto Resort and had a  great time.  The schlep was a little strenuous for a 70 year old especially on the way up.  We went pretty early in the morning on a grey and rainy day at the end of June.  There we no crowds but the water was rough and dangerous for swimming.  This made the whole scene romantic and enjoyable.  The trip was worth the effort but how worth it for you will depend on the weather and the crowds. We walked the beach as part of Olle Trail #8.  We got lost a couple of times.

We got here by bus the bus stop is about 20 minutes walk away which was amazing walking all the way up he stream area in the countryside and plenty of opportunities for photos. Very peaceful place there was a few tourists mainly Korean tourists. The water is amazing if your ok walking on some stones etc then give it a go otherwise clogs would be great cause the water feels amazing. But be careful if going in the water as me and my partner walked in quite far when we noticed there was broken glass at the bottom so we tried to walk round it but was a little concerned in case anyone gets cut. This is a beautiful and peaceful place to visit I would recommend staying here a while and just enjoying yourself without rushing.

We got an ATV (40000KRW for 2 hours) and rode around the island. It was really fun and you get to explore the whole island. There are small little cafes where you can just park your ATV and pop in for a coffee and a cake. The water is amazingly clear and blue.

We got a local bus to this park. When we went there it was quite windy so take a sweater.The park is very large with lots of stones to see. There is no cafe so take water or food. It is really worth the visit.
We find this waterfall more worthwhile visiting than the other 3 waterfalls.  We went very close to the falls to take photos and had a great time.

We drove past it on another parallel road and didnt realise how fun it was! So we made it a point to visit it and try it out before we returned the rental car. The speed went up to almost 20km/h! We didnt encounter any local motorists though there were some tourists placing water bottles to see them roll up the hill :)
We didn't like it at all. There was pretty much no water falling out of the water falls. You climb very steep stairs and get very tired. The bridge is good for a few nice clicks though.
We did it by 7 hours with 1 hour break on the top.We started 9.00a.m. We are o lot of students groups  in the morning and you could't go very fast-be patient. Bring enough water and snacks.

We climbed up Yeongsil and down Eorimok trail. Needed 5hours from Yeongsil ticket office to Eorimok ticket office. We made couple of short stops to enjoy amazing views and one longer at Witseoreum shelter for eating. Hallasan was covered by plenty of flowers it looked like pink carpet. Very beautiful. Pity that this season is dry so we could not see waterfalls at Yeongsil trail.  Next time i want to make Gwaneumsa - Seongpanak trail because those lead to summit so crater lake can be seen only from there. Nevertheless Eorimok and mainly Yeongsil trail is worth to go.

We choose Yeongsil Trail as it's the easiest but too bad in less than 1km we had to turn back. We were there in early April 2014 and the wind was blowing like crazy and it was very cold. Reason for turning back? We spotted ice and in no way wearing the suitable clothes for the climb. We even saw the waterfall freezes. Astounding and beautiful. The trees were all bare and yellowish. Don't expect greenery at this time of year.

We came on a cloudy day so the water didn't look as turquoise. So if you're opting for a blue-green picture for your Instagram do come here on a sunny day. I like how it is connected to a black sand beach and the way how Koreans pile stones to make a wish tower makes me happy. 30 mins is enough for this place.

We came here early morning to take in the fresh air and scenic views of soesokkak estuary. There are water activities like the popular transparent kayak but it was closed when I went there. Just a note for those who wants to ride the transparent kayak do come here first thing in the morning and reserve a kayak for that day. There are nearby shops selling souvenirs and other eateries as well. I tried buying the hallabong ice cream from one of the stalls and it's really delicious.

We came here but it was very hot and the sun intensity was very high. Its a long walk from the parking lot but worth it when you reach.We didn't go in the water because it was quite crowded when we went. It can be a bit tricky to climb and walk on the rocks so be careful.

We actually stayed at a hotel right on this beach.  The water is beautiful but there are signs saying no to swimming in some parts of it.  There is a cafe bene right next to it so you can grab a cup of coffee and go sit on the beach.  The only problem is that it is pretty far from anything else like all the museums and nature trails of jeju and it is kind of small which makes me think that in the summer it can get really crowded.
Way too many rules. Can't take off masks for photos  there are 3 small waterfalls that you have to pay to see. Don't waste your money. See a waterfall somewhere else in Jeju for free.
Waterfalls have always been interesting to me and this one certainly was among the top 10 I have visited.

Waterfall is easily accessible from seogwipo town and surrounded by lovely parks. Entrance fee is 2000 krw but no one was collecting fares when I was there. There is a stairway down to water fall but you can see it from the top easily. Nothing spectacular if you have seen other water falls.
Waterfall falls direct into the sea. You can get so close and almost touch the waterfall. There's a little tent nearby that sells fresh seafood.

Was there during winter  thus not much water can be seen under the bridge. Can see far away on the bridge  and the view was nice. Other than that  nothing much at the attraction. There was one fountain of various animals heads  and supposedly you are to face any one of them to throw in a coin and make a wish according to what you wanted.

Was surprised to learn this is a UNESCO listed site and once I got there just loved it. It's one of the few waterfalls where the water falls straight into the ocean. There were alot of tourists when I visited but definetley worth a look!

Was expecting more. I think once you are in Jeju you just feel like everywhere will be magical but when you reach places that give off mediocre vibes you tend to get disappointed. So don't come here with high expectations.This place is too touristy and honestly I'd rather kayak in Bali (actually water rafting there is awesome) or in Laos. Or even in Kota Kinabalu or Thailand.
Walk to the highest mountain in Jeju. Then you can find a excellent view and enjoy the strong wind. Remember bring more water and some food. And keep clean for the natural environment.

Walk around the mountain and you can see different rock formations.  The water is very clear (look at the picture as if there is no water) that you can see sea urchins. I advise you wear rubber shoes to be more comfortable walking through sharp rock formations.

Visited this place in Feb19 and was quite appalled by the treatment of the animals. The rabbits were allowed to roam within an enclosed area accessible to visitors. However there is no one monitoring that the rabbits are treated properly. The living conditions of the animals are filthy. The absolute horror was the black pig show. What's so entertaining about forcing terrified black pigs down a water slide?? Tasteless entertainment with no educational value. Paying the entrance fee of 13000won per person  I would expect some of it to be channeled to upkeep the living conditions of the animals. The blooms in the park were alright with spots for Instagram pictures but nothing spectacular.
Visited many caves in different countries. this one was formed from flowing volcanic lava instead of the usual subterranean water hundreds of thousand of years ago.

Visited during Dec. The place is nice and cool. Do put on some thick coat or rain coat before there as there will be water dripping on your head. There is bat in the cave. Do not bring a stroller as the road inside the cave is very uneven. Do bring touch light along during your visit as the light inside the cave is not so bright.

Visited at mid-day in August.  It was very hot but beautiful.  had a picnic near the carpark and took a stroll along the trail on the east end of the beach. There is a small freshwater spring on the beach at the start of the trail
visited 3 more popular waterfalls in Jeju and this one is the best.  best visit time is summer so that you can enjoy the splash when you walk close.  Imagine it would be too chilly for winter though.

Very popular tourist attraction (you know its popular when they have those cheesy fast speedboat tours on the water) but still worth the visit to see these unique shaped cliffs in the ocean if you are already in the area. Just a short simple walk along their boardwalk to see them so quite a short visit. Only 2000 Krw per adult to visit with kids under 4 free.
Very interseting to see our car moves uphill with the engine off. My tour guide explained the reason behind this but I still don't understand XD. Try to pour the water and the same thing happened.

Very interesting maze. First 2 are fairly easy but the 3rd one gets a little tricky. Water mist kept getting in the way as you try to navigate so it gets a little more complicated. The kids and adults had a fun time. Should do it without the maps given so you just have to rely on sense of direction.
very clean and not too crowded. the water is clean but a little cold. places to eat close by. be ready that the tide is around 7 pm )
Very beautiful series of waterfall with each ranging 100 to 200 meters apart from other (3 stages waterfall). Recommended for nature lover and those who love to know the history.

Very beautiful beach although one has to pay a large amount for a spot with an umbrella on the main beach. You can however walk just a bit further and find another beach. Beautiful beach with clear water. It can become crowded in summer over the weekends
Very atypical road. Strange to understand. Please take a bottle of water with you to see the mystery in action :) but do not spend more than 15 minutes here
Using bare eyes to look at the roads it appears to go up while actually its going downhill. If you put a water bottle on the road it will slide down. Interesting.

Unfortunately the weather was too windy for us to swim on that particular day in April but I'm sure that it would otherwise be perfect. It's a typical tropical beach with white sand and turquoise water. Hanging around to watch the sunset there is worth it.
U can Find all sports of planets there. Greenery every where. Can see Flowers from rachael seasons. The water gardens is beautiful. The bonsai trees are outstanding
Turkoise waters and great views of the beaches from multiple restaurants and coffee places all along the shoreline.May be a bit difficult to find parking though.

Tulips are great. But cherry blossom are ending. The tropical garden is very impressive. If only the other parts of the garden were better maintained. I would have rated this place 5 stars. The caves was very interesting. From hot garden to cold caves. The follow by waterfall. It?s very nice transition. One must spend about 3-4 hours to fully explore this garden and use the guide to walk through the garden. I really enjoyed walking this garden with many different theme. Keep up the good work and hopefully with your increased price you can do better maintenance.

Trip with friends to see underwater animals; sharks star fishes and other tortoise and outside aquarium full happiness with mini korean mart coffee and drinks and if you all like Korean food & beverages terrace
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: tried the forest healing program last month during my visit to jeju island. Guided by forest therapist we have completed forest healing trail. I can say it really helps me relax the body by focusing on natural noises flowing water  chirping mountain birds  fresh forest air and those Phytoncide!!! oh it just smells so nice >.< we got to try the foot bath and aromatherapy too. the therapist said they also have body bathing tub and aqua line  but since we dont have many time.. maybe next time. Good place to relax your mind and escape from hustle and bustle city. i will try another program if i have chance to visit it again.
tough climb to take pictures at the waterfall because of the rocks and uneven ground. but the sight is well worth it.

Took the longest trail to Mount Hallasan peak (Seongpanak Trail) - 9.6 km - but started a bit late and did not make the cut-off time at the Jindalrae shelter (7km). However it was a great walk and I visited the Saraoream peak on a side tril on the way back.  This was well worth it as there is great view and also a beautiful crater lake.  It is key that you start early and take enough water with you.  Also need good shoes. Although it was August - most of the trail is in the forest - so not so hot.
Took cab from Seongsan Ilchulbong. Beautiful site for sea and waterfall. A bit crowded but worth it. About a 30 minute walk from hotel Little France.

Took a Taxi to the waterfall from Cheonjiyeon Waterfall. Plan to get wet if you get close to the falls.Better get there before is closes. Admission of course. Lady at information desk was very helpful. We took the Airport Limo bus for 11000 won bus # 600 to the Cheoniyeon Waterfall. Since I wanted to see as much of the south end as I could before dark I am glad we got to see these areas. Go to KAL hotel and take the Limo Bus back to the Airport for 11000 Won.
This would have to be the most overrated tourist attraction Basic waterfall with 2streams of water  onto rocks below. Cost 2000 per adultDon't bother

This waterfall was a 15 min walk away from where we were staying. The trail which led to this waterfall is amazing with great views of the ocean. Waterfall itself is pretty amazing and great opportunity for few pics.

This waterfall truly was magnificent to see. I recommend going early in the morning (ticket office opens at 8:00 am). It was 8:30 am when I visited and there were a few people. At one point they all left and it was only me and the waterfall. Truly amazing. Definitely go before before all the tourists get there!!!

This waterfall provides loads of great photo opportunities. We liked this one better than the cheonjyeon waterfalls. You can get very close to the waterfall. You can also buy fresh seafood at the site.
This waterfall is very tiny but really difficult to see the water itself because it dries up time to time. You must checkout the season before visiting this place.

This waterfall is so tall and you can stand near it to take a picture. The water is so cool and refreshing.There is a stall selling orange ice-cream near the exit- really delicious and thirst-quenching.

This waterfall is much smaller than Jeongbang Falls  and is worth spending the time walking to it if you're in the area. Beautiful clear blue water beneath  it would make a good swimming spot in hot weather!
This waterfall is easily accessible from Seogwipo city by taxi or bus. You can also take a walk in the Olle trail and park around the area

This waterfall is beautiful in that the water falls all the way to the rocks in the ocean unimpeded.  You have to scramble on rocks to get closer or you can remain on the landing at the bottom of the steps and get a pretty good view.

This waterfall is a poor second to the nearby Cheonjiyeon Falls. If you want to see everything Seogwipo has to offer then pay a visit but I much preferred the other falls for both the actual waterfall and the surrounding gardens that give you access to it.

This was the only waterfall we visited on Jeju island. It was worth the visit although somehow not terribly exciting for me. I think it would be  nicer in  the summer time when you can put your feet in the water. There is a small entrance fee.
This was so beautiful! I went during April and there was a lot of water going down the falls. Such a picture perfect spot! I highly recommend it to all visitors.
This was one of our most favorite waterfalls in Korea. Amazing to see. Lots of steps down and up but worth the climb.

This was one of our favourite places from the list of to do activities in Jeju. It was really exciting to see such wonders of nature . These rock formations are few million year old and have column like shape. View of the blue water from the board walk is breathtaking. A must visit spot when you are in Jeju.

This was of our Yeha bus tour - South Course and this was a beautiful stop.  You can take steps down to the waterfall for some great photo opportunities.  There are some really large rocks that you walk and stand on.

This was my favorite amongst all the waterfalls I have been to as you can get pretty close to it. You can even wade in the pool if you want to as it's quite shallow. Very nice place to take photos. Took a short trek to Sojeongbang waterfall from the same parking area. For those driving you can enter the phone number 7331530 into the gps. Admission fee is 2000 won for adults. Make use of your youth ID card if you are below 24 years old! It's half the price and can save you a lot if you go to many attractions. Closes at 6pm though so plan your itinerary properly!

This was a surprisingly informative and enjoyable place.  An amazing amount of beautiful bonzai trees.  It also had a large amount of sculptures and two large koi ponds with waterfalls.  A very relaxing and enjoyable visit.We also got to have tea with the founder!

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.

This spectacular waterfall is worth the visit. Parking is easy and there is a small fee to walk down to the bottom of the falls. The bottom is all rocks so it could be difficult to maneuver for some. At the top is a lovely art gallery and cafe.
This scenery of falling water is really very amazing. An appropriate place for photography. There are many other beautiful places near it.
This 's an excellent place which you can go with your family. It has natural beautiful which makes you feel comfortable. You should go to Jeongbang Waterfall from 3PM - 5 PM

This rock formation was spotted on the eastern side of Jeju island. I was lucky enough to see this attraction having not spotted one a long time ago.The water present in these area is crystal clear where you can see different fishes swimming in the ocean breeze.
This place was amazing. when is summer the colours of the waters makes it picture perfect. Sometime too crowded

This place is really amazing. The waterfall is falling directly to sea and it is a treat to eyes.. The best thing is we can enjoy both of them together here.. Was really astonished by the view.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.

review: This place is just outside the love land . There is a huge parking lot just behind this row of shops. In front of these shops selling sausages and fruits is the road . Ok a visit if you are in the area.

This place is extremely beautifully especially during sunset. The rocks are carved by water to different shapes. Nice view of the ocean with a well maintained garden. It is 5 mins walk from international convention centre.
This place is easily accessable and great place to take good photographs.  The sound of the waterfall and the breeze of the wind gives us a calm mind.
This place has a very nice view. The waterfall is beautiful and the water looks pure and clean. But you have to climb all the big rocks around to get closer to the waterfall.

this park is right next to Jeongbang Waterfalls  and only costs 500 SKW. We spent an hour there reading up the interesting story of how Xu Fu  the elixir who was said to have stopped here while his envoy with 500 (3000) boys and girls set sail in search for immortal medicine for the Qin Emperor in 219BC. He was said to have left inscriptions on the cliff next to the waterfall marking his presence there.
This one has 3 tiers of waterfalls as opposed to 1.  The pools are in blue and green colors.  It also has a beautiful bridge that is decorated with 7 nymphs.

This mountain is so tiring if you try and complete the ascent in 3 hours on a hot day but it's worth it for the view at the summit! The upward root that I took was a little bland because it was all under the cover of trees so you don't actually see anything new for most of the ascent. The crater on top still had some snow on it in April and you can see the full perimeter of the island from the top. I think this view would be even more spectacular in the summer. Make sure you bring plenty of water! There is nowhere to buy it on the way down if you take the alternative route. Also be prepared to use the horrible 'hole-in-the-floor toilets' if you need to go. Needed to take a taxi back to the hostel at the end because no buses stop there. A great day out though.

This mountain is definitely worth a visit. I recommend a nice espresso and carrot juice at the bottom at Lazy Place Cafe - cool place with great views. It takes a little effort to get up to the cave with the water falling from the ceiling but well worth it especially if you?셱e a spiritual person. The other temples are serene. It is an UNESCO site of outstanding natural beauty with an historical layer at the coast below. A Dutchman was shipwrecked here in the C17th and wrote the first description of the Kingdom of Korea published in the West. I had a wonderful time with my girlfriend. Close place to stay is Mirabil.

this is the only white sand blue water beach in Korea. So i was pretty excited to see it. Its quite shallow and you can easily play around. Its well maintained just like alll other beaches in korea. there is life guard always on duty. Careful while walking near the stones.

this is one of the logest lava tube according to the information stated there. i loved it so much because that's my first lava tube visit. i went there during winter so it's cold inside. Bring your jacket along because it is cold and water dripping from top. Very good experince if you never try it. I think this is only 1/4 (1km) of the length open for public. It will take you 50mins if you would like to take pictures.

This is one of the best waterfalls in Jeju. Easily accessible from Seaogwipo city by taxi or bus from E Mart. Entrance will charged ?? 5000 or $5. This is the only waterfall in Asia that falls to the ocean.

This is no Caribbean beach so don't expect warm turquoise waters and endless stretches of fine white sand. Considering the area however it is a decent beach and worth checking out if you are in the area. It is located within the Jungmun Resort complex in Seogwipo but there is no charge so anyone can visit.Here's what to expect: yellow/orange rough sand with lots of bits of shell; water that gets deep quite quickly; STRONG undertow on stormy days. The resort restricts people from swimming during certain months (wintertime I think) because of the risk of undertow.  I mention the last point because the beach is actually quite beautiful to watch on a windy day as the waves crash into the volcanic rock.Quite often on weekends foreigners gather to play rounds of volleyball.There are spots to get food near the beach and in the resort but be ready for sky-high prices.
This is just another bridge and I wouldn't drive especially to see it but if your visiting the nearby waterfall you should also check this out. It has a lovely view and looks great at night
This is in my opinion the best of the three major waterfall sites on jeju. It wasn't overly crowded and the surrounding coastline makes for great photos.

This is an amazing place. The museum is absolutely first rate. All the exhibits have explanations in perfect English.  There are lots of interactive displays. If you are interested in the geology of Jeju you should come here first and expect to spend several hours. Outdoors there are 3 courses (walks) with exhibits of life in old Jeju. The exhibits are well done and English signs are excellent.  This place is huge and amazingly you will have it almost to yourself. It has an entry fee of about $5. That is the bargain of the century!   Don't skip any of it. It could easily take a full day if you are intellectually and esthetically inclined. It was the best thing I did on the island. I spent only about 4 hours. I would suggest you bring food and water with you. I had a few apples and tangerines.
This is an amazing collection of natural and men made stones in Jeju. In addition it has an outstanding water instillation and an indoor unique museum. Truly worth the visit

This is a very spectacular waterfall plummeting down into the ocean. The boulders add to the fun of the attraction clambering over them to see the waterfall more directly .Very well organised walk from car park down to waterfall area. Some interesting stalls at the entrance. Again very cheap to visit.

This is a three tiered waterfall. To see all three you must walk a lot of staircases. It is much smaller than what I thought but where it is quite beautiful. If in Jeju I recommend a visit(if you love the nature).

this is a spot you must see if you go to Jeju in low season. Very few people. It is visited by families with kids that try to catch the crabs on the rocks. The black volcanic sand is nice especially if you are in the mood to look for the spots where the fountains emerges from the sea. Here sea water mixes with amazingly freezing river water that brings some white sand on the shore. The view of black sand mixing with the white sand allows you to take beautiful pictures. Romantic place

This is a place where fresh water enters the ocean. But the water is calm and the surroundings are so beautiful.You can rent a kayak or a water bike. It take about 1 hour to paddle around it. It is a open place for everyone.

This is a place suitable for kids and senior citizen. It is just a short walk from the entrance to the waterfall via a flat road. We make this place the last place on our itinerary (late evening) as this place close later than any then attractions in Seogwipo. Quite a romantic walk and we even met some couples doing their wedding photoshoot here.
This is a nice waterfall to see going in to the sea. The walk down is all steps about 130 each way. The rocks at the bottom can be difficult to walk over.

This is a manmade park-like garden with a variety of plants and trees and water features. It is well worth the time it takes to walk through the grounds  just for the experience of viewing the bucolic setting. The main feature is Michon Cave which really didn't dazzle us as much as it apparently was supposed to. It's just a cave in which one walks down a slope to see some tacky lights and statues. The park  on the other hand  is scenic and pleasant. There are some concessions where they sell the usual tourist stuff.

This is a large and well-kept temple by the water.There are 4 floors to visit and many murals and small statues to see. The large golden buddhas are impressive. You can take a mat and pray on the main floor or meditate in a second floor room.I spent a total of around 45 minutes at this site.
This is a great beach with the most beautiful water on Jeju. The waters are crystal clear and the color is picturesque. The lava rocks add to the beauty of this place.

This is a circular beach that turns into a lake on the rising tide  then dries again on the ebbing tide. m The water is not too deep (about a meter) and the half moon shaped beach is one of the largest in Jeju. The sand is particularly delicate and soft on the feet. The stone sculptures are worth a viewing too. Lots of things to do nearby  Folklore Village  Namwon Keunang and Seopjikoji. Loads of free parking close by.

This is a beautiful spot to sit and enjoy nature at its best. We saw some amazing little birds and the waterfall is stunning. There was a lot of water going down the falls when we visited in April this year. This is a must do! Be ready to go up and down a lot of stairs. :)

This is a beautiful place to learn about the gardens and native korean plants.? There are many different types of gardens here and they are all well maintained and interesting.? You could stay here for a long time just learning or you could breeze through casually enjoying the scenery.? There is a tower you can go to the top of for lovely views of the area.? This is a beautiful beach! It was peacfecul to look out over the water and watch the families enjoy themselves. It was also great to drive along the coast and forget about the worries of the day.

This could be a quick stop or you could spend time enjoying the view.  There weren't too many people when we were there but of course it could be busy.  The falls are unique in that the fresh water falls directly into the sea below.  You have to take stairs to get down to the sea level.  You can't get right up to the falls but you can get close enough to feel the spray and hear the roar of the water.

the place is fun for walking between different kind of plants and animals. there are 3 caves and the weather inside it is cold during the summer time so you can walk there if you feel hot. there is also folk village and a water park

The parking is free . Entrance fee was 2000W per Pax. You first descend about 5 minutes to a blue pond with the first waterfall . Beautiful and stunning . Then you proceed to the second waterfall about 10 walk . There was a third waterfall but it was about 40 minutes walk so we decided not to do that one . A five minute walk brought us to a bridge  which would bring you to another route . Overall expect to spend between 1-2 hours here .
The park was poorly maintained  the water in the pond was murky and had many fallen leaves. The minatures looked so fake and some had paint chips. Give this a miss.
The park around the waterfall area was simple and not too long and tedious for a walk with your family. Waterfall was nice too for a photoshoot. Overall was great!

The only waterfall in Jeju that e water flows into the ocean. U can go very close to it & feel e cool Breeze. Was so amazed to c rainbow too! Worth stopping by.
The only special thing about the waterfall is that it connects to the sea. But it worths a visit in Jeju if you have time.

The only difference with other waterfalls is the water goes directly into the sea. A Hanyeo was selling her fresh catch near the Falls. A bit pricey in my opinion. Having said that it is still a must visit if it is your 1st trip to Jeju.

The only (or so I'm told) waterfall that falls into the sea in Jeju Island.  Easy walk down stairs to the bottom of the falls.  Able to walk around on the rocks and view the falls.  Really gorgeous and totally worth the visit.

The ocean waves against the beautiful volcanic rocks are just so amazing. The island is gorgeous and so much to see and do. We enjoyed going further down the beach to go into the water as well. The pineapple & tangerines are awesome.

The most memorable thing was rather on the ferry to Udo Island.The seagulls were hovering over those who had Calbee prawn crackers ready to feed them. They followed the ferry from Jeju all the way to Udo. That was a sight!Udo generally has good scenic views and interesting coral beach with clear blue waters.

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water
