I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.
The main culprit for this optical illusion is the fence. Be sure to bring water bottle with you and let it roll.

The lava tube was not claustrophobic at all. It was very comfortable and cool. The lighting is low but is still very visible and easy to navigate. Just did the first course but was glad we did! It was wet when we went and there was water dripping from the ceiling. It didn't bother me tho and didn't take away from the experience :)

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

The Jeonbang Waterfall was breath taking and is the only waterfall in South East Asia to flow directly into the ocean. The views are great and the waterfall looks so majestic. This is definitely one waterfall you should check out in Seogwipo.

The garden starts with a huge glasshouse which is a torture in the summer but we went anyway on carpe diem basis. It's awesome inside and it has little sections. Then outside there are European Japanese and Korean gardens with walkways. Coming from Europe I was not really amazed or entertained by the eurogardens but I guess with Asian perspective they were impressive. The reason I gave 4 is that the entry is expensive and they only sell water at 1 place. Also the toilets are quite dirty

the engine of the bus I am in was switch-off and yet it continue to move upwards.. only a stretch of about 250m of road.... a bottle of mineral water seems to roll upwards too...most puzzling was a bus moves up faster than a sedan car...simply strange...
The depth of water is shallow after u swim. towards ocean for 100 meter u can still stand on the sand

The clear turquoise water against black sand beach is really pretty. There were no kayaks available when i was there in autumn but it was also too cold for water activities. Otherwise would have love to go for a swim. It is a nice place to just hang out with friends or pack a picnic lunch. The view is just spectacular.Highly recommended place to visit while in Jeju.

The cave is very chilling and quite dark. The path inside the cave is quite well lit up but it is still not very easy to walk as the path is uneven and at time quite slippery due to the water being collected. But it is still a good experience to walk inside volcano carved cave to understand how nature is formed. And the power of the nature. So best to wear some comfortable and non slip type of walking shoes.

The cave is cold and wet. It's not easy to walk on undulating floor filled with watery potholes. Certain section you have to bend your body as the ceiling is too low. The cave looks the same from the opening to the end.

The car drives  up the road by itself! Great fun. ( visual effect)It only works one way. You need to drive in neutral towards the shops. If you arrived from Jejusi do a U turn after the shops to experience the effect. The effect is quite spectacular with a water bottle placed in the middle of the road. You will see clearly the bottle rolling up.
The car can move uphill in neutral gear. Water will flow uphill. Ball will roll up hill. These are the things that happen in mysterious Road.
The bus and car will still move while the enhine turns off. Use a bottle of mineral water to try. Just stop and try.

The brochure states that is a glass castle. This is definitely not a glass castle but a fun museum  so if you have kids and they are expecting to see a Cinderella kind of environment  well  this is not .What you find though it's the explanation on how glass in made and transformed in different shapes (entrance) to different kind of finished product. If you want  you can also have a go (helped by professionals)!It's a good  small scale museum and it's quite entertaining and educational. A mention of honor goes to the ticket guy at the entrance. On our way out we asked him to help us out to get a taxi. He was the sweetest and hard-core-customer orientated guy I saw in action in Jeju (and  I must admit they are all very good). He tried to get a taxi for us  getting the price  helping us (mind you  his English was limited  so he struggled a lot but nonetheless worked hard to explain us everything he could) and even giving us for free a cold bottle of water whilst waiting outside (for the taxi). You could see he was really trying his best and I hope someone from the Museum will read this feed-back and rewarding him.One thing I would avoid is the Coffee Shop inside the museum. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.

The beach's sand is actually volcanic sand/ash which is why it's black and on a good sunny day the view is marvelous. I'm not sure if it's a lucky occurrence but we spotted jumping fish a distance away from the shore line. I didn't have time to but you can rent transparent kayaks to explore the river which apparently has a whirlpool (not that dangerous according to my guide) at the head. The water is quite clear so you may actually be able to see fishes under the kayak. Otherwise enjoy the picturesque view of the estuary.

The beach was very beautiful. It has clear blue water and there were several restaurants and cafe where you can sit and enjoy the view. It was too windy when we visited though and the sand was everywhere. Spring may not be the best time to visit.
The beach was super pretty.. not a long walk.. Very clean.. it was amazing.. And the water was super clean which was really nice!! Love it!
The beach was nice enough. Very shallow waters. Lots os rocks around the beach. Lots of people. Except at 1am in the morning when I snuck back for a walk.
The beach is superb front of my hotel. Just walking 5 minutes.. a lot of restaurant here. The water is so cool and an amazing view. Not so crowded.

The beach is nice with a combination of sand and rock. Korean people use EVERY available inch of land. They pull their trailers and cars right to the edge of the beach and set up camp. Don?t understand why swimming wasn?t allowed. People were wading in the water.

The beach area as well as the water are looking clean. The sand is white. We did not go in since it was late October. The view is nice and the neighbourhood has shops and restaurants available. There is a coffee shop directly at the beach where you can rest if you find a place to rest. Usually the shop is quite crowded. At night time some fireworks ongoing. We had the Golden Tulip hotel and we were enjoying the view to the beach every morning.

The area around the waterfall is big. There are three different waterfall in the same area. You will need to walk a bit to get to the second and third tier waterfall. You can also go to the seonimyo bridge in the same area.

The answer is of course when there is no water. Even though it was raining  it wasn't raining enough to produce a waterfall. Still a pretty spot with a pleasant walk past orange blossom scented orchards.

The 1k walk is really interesting and had good info in english. It's much cooler as soon as you walk down the steps and raincoats are useful as there are water drops and wear comfortable shoes for the rocky and wet floor. Most of it is quite dark but you can still get good photos. Definitely worth the visit

Take the step down the cliff and you will find yourself a unique waterfall that is near a sea. Usually you will find waterfall upstream of a river not close to sea. The force of the water is quite huge so you can feel the breeze when you nearer to the waterfall. There are other cultural stuff nearby the waterfall as well.

Take picture with the unique statues. Listen to the local guide to understand how their ancestor's life. Do you know the 3 things Jeju women fight to keep for life: 1) Water 2) I forget you can ask if you visit but the last thing I remember: 3) MAN. :))

Suwolbong peak is a part of the tuff ring which was formed due to hydro Volcanic explosion caused due to molten lava coming in contact with water. One can see the tuff formation layer by layer formed continuously throughout the cliff. Suwolbong also has a observatory tower to monitor the weather.
Stopped by this beach after visiting Hallim Park. The sand is soft and the water is turquoise-y. But I have seen better beaches. The unique feature to me is the volcanic rock by the beaches.

Steep climb up the hill but the view worth every step. The stair halfway up is quite steep and a bit of a challenge if u have a bad knee. The best time to go is either for sunset or sunrise. There is only 1 shop to buy water up there. Make sure you have your water with you for the climb.

Staying in Seogwipo we were lucky enough to be able to walk to these amazing waterfalls which fall into the sea.  We descended  down some wooden steps to the beach and clambered over rocks to get close to the falls.  There was a great atmosphere there with many tourists all happy to help take photos of each other with the falls behind.  Well worth a visit.
Stand nearer to the waterfall for some refreshing sprinkle. Nice view and a must visit. Stepping stones to get to the waterfall may be a challenge for some.
Spent several afternoons here. When you have nice sunny weather for the day the beach is a good place for young kids - the water is calm and clear. Highly recommended.

Spent half day on Udo Island walking around different spot by tourist bus! The bus tour is highly recommended to visitors without driving liscence since you can get on any bus of the same company with the ticket. Each stop has its uniqueness but still highly recommend the first stop! Simply stopby and enjoy Jimmy's Icecream along the seaside... guarentee this to be the most memorable part of the trip! The beach is also highly recommended since you feel like visiting Maldive with the clear water and blue sky. Try to arrive the ferry terminal to avoid overcrowding!

Spent a Sunday morning relaxing on this magnificent beach.  Its emerald coloured crystal clear water and fine white sand laced with shells that makes it glitter.  A magic location!Cannot wait for the moon to appear and make my summer complete.  Walk all the way round to Geumneung beach and enjoy the stroll on the white sand.

Spent a day swimming in fresh water. Fresh sweet river water mixing with warm salty seaNo umbrella for renting. Black rocks and sandYou can rent canoas. Next to big nice black sand beach only for serfers.
Spectacular waterfall tumbling over the cliff edge into the sea

Songaksan offers an easy 3km walk around it's perimeter most of which is along its cliff (facing the waters). There is no entrance fee. Prepare yourself with a windbreaker sunglasses and some water. Very nice view along the way! You can see Sangbasan and Yongmeori Coast from certain angles. You can also see geographical strata on its cliffs. In the month of June which is near summer Hydrangeas are in full bloom adding even more colors to the already beautiful landscape!

Soesokkak is a great place to visit if you are in Jeju-do. From Seogwipo area take bus 110 and get off at Hyodon Middle School. It takes another 20 minutes of walking passing by orange farms. No entrance fees is required but if you want to try the transparent kayak or the traditional hand-pulled raft you will need to buy tickets at the counter situated on your right side before you reach the estuary. The clear green blue water is mesmerizing and definitely a great place to visit. Stop-by for a bottle of fresh orange juice to quench your thirst or a cone of ice-cream to complete the trip.

So we did minimum research on this thinking that the trip up would be somewhat difficult but we were way off that. We made it to the top but we had to push through it. Highly recommend bringing lots of water and snacks.

So the water level in South Korea is low right now due to an unusually dry rainy season so the falls were not as grand as they usually are however it was still an impressive sight and one I wont forget. BTW take a swim trunk with you and go swimming in the water at the bottom of the first falls its cold but amazing.

So didn't really plan where I wanna go but just walked. And I walked to this beach. There are signs to say no swimming after August but people were still swimming. The waters look nice and felt nice and 2 meters out and it's at chest level so watch out there.There's also surf school to teach surfers wannabes.Now the trip up though..... 300+ steps up to reach Lotte World and Shilla

Small but great little beach.  We didn't get much time here as we were on a tight schedule for our business trip but we had enough time for a half hour swim.  There were many surfers and the water was perfect.  There were many people at the beach but it was not crowded.  The beach slopes very gently into the ocean so even 20 30 feet out you're barely to your shoulders.  Nice low waves so a great place to just chill and have a leisurely swim.  There was a changing/showering place conveniently just beside the beach so that made it easy to change and be ready to go again.  Lovely little spot.

Small area but you can see clear waters around the rocks formed from the volcano. Do visit if you have time. I imagine it would be amazing to catch the sunset here but am unable to do so because of time constraints.Easily accessible by bus no. 462 from Jeju Bus Terminal.
small & clean water but sand just so so. since cloudy so that the color not too significant but still well enough. one of jeju beach but i don't see quite much special on it.

Since it is October it is a bit too cool to swim but there were some people in the water.  The beach was empty.  The temperature was only around 24 but it t was a beautiful day.  There are a lot of places to grab a coffee or have a meal.  Good place to stop off on a round the island drive!

simply breathtaking awesomewhite sandscrystal clear wateri was fascinated by the green algae scatterred in the sea(some are floating)i think its formed because of the jeju origin...from a volcano eruption
Short walk from the carpark but need to climb down stairs and walk on rocks to go near waterfall. Not suitable for stroller or wheelchair.
Short visit but the scene is beautiful. Steep climb is not recommended for old folks though. Really like the waterfall that goes into the ocean!

Sangangsan Mountain provides a short walk up stairs to a Buddhist temple and shrine. Only 1000 krw to enter. Even my teenage boys enjoyed the walk and the visit to the shrine where we were encouraged by a local to drink from the sacred water for our good health and fortune.

Samyang Beach was the only beach in Jeju that took down contact info for all visitors and even had visitors put on temperature sensitive stickers.  The swimming area is quite small and most visitors were there for surfing/windsurfing lessons which most of the beach area was allocated for.  We liked the shaded areas near the water and were able to hang out without having to pay for a parasol or a cabana.  It's not a particularly picturesque beach but it's one of the few in the city.

Reminds me of kenyas hells gate. The place is a sight to behold. Be carefull to put on comfy shoes that have great treads and grips so that you dont slip on the sometimes slippery rocks. Also find out about tides. If its high tides then definately you will be soaked by action of water on your feet. Good place though. I recommend finnishing it with a horse ride by the ajoshi at the exit for man won and a cold jeju tangerine juice.
Remember to go with sandel or any footwear that makes going into the water easy and comfortable.   You won't regret as the water is icy cold & refreshing under the hot sun.

Really nice view coz the waterfall is right next to the open sea. I could feel the splash on my face when I approached its bottom.Tips: be ready to climb the stairs after viewing the waterfall. It's not too long but you may get tired after a long day of touring in Jeju.Be careful if you want to go near the waterfall coz it's all big rocks at the bottom.
Really nice beach with a lot of restaurants near by.The water was really clear and the beach was clean so good for snorkeling and swimming.

Really gorgeous view of the waterfall which flows right into the sea. A little bit challenging to go near it as you have to walk and hop on big rocks but you could still see it clearly just by standing near the stairs. Sat near to the waterfall and my shirt got slightly wet by the water splashes. Cold but refreshing. Do wear proper shoes if you intend to walk on the huge rocks to go near the waterfall.

Really cool and Interesting lava tube under the ground of Jeju island. It shows a lot of cool facts about how it happen and also how the island is formed like it is today. The attraction is both on English and Korean. The test is easy to under stand on the sign and pictures there are. Remember to bring some good walking/waterproof shoes or boots because there are water every were and the terrain is uneven because of the lava it self.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

Pyoseon Beach might not be the most picturesque beach in Jeju but it's vast and didn't feel that crowded even in the middle of the high season. Because of the large sand area exposed during low tides  it can be quite the hike to the water then. But the low depth of the water and the large sand area makes it a good beach for children. As with most other popular Jeju beaches  there is a good selection of restaurants nearby.
Pretty beach and calm water. It's nice to sit and chill by Cafe Delmoondo.  We spent hours here.  You can just sit or walk on a trail or the street with restaurants.
Prepare umbrella or raincoat as water drips in the cave. It's amazing to see the rock formation and lava tubes. It's dark and the path is rocky and slippery so becareful.
Possibly the asia only waterfall which falls directly into the sea.. sad part is you cannot swim here.. pretty scenic

Pleasant wander around here. 2-3 hours with a stop for lunch. We took our little dog on a lead and no problem. The water garden and Bonsai were my favourite. Reasonable admission for the amount to see. Definitely a must do!

Peaceful and clean.  The water was refreshing.  The sand was fine.  The sun was shining and it just doesn't get much better than playing on this beach!  Perfect tide pools for small children to play in.  Snorkeling for the grown ups.  Plenty of places to eat and drink nearby.  Just lovely!
Paid a 1000 (or 2000?) won entrance fee and my breath was taken away by the beautiful sight! There was even a rainbow at the end of the waterfall... simply beautiful :)

Out of the big three waterfalls this was my favorite. The stairs are bit tough but totally worth it. Where a rain jacket as you will get damp. There is ajummas selling some kind of fresh seafood when you get close to the bottom.

Our tour diverted to the tea museum because we were to visit dragon head rock but the tides were too high to take out the small boat.  Anyway would've been cold on the water with the very powerful windy day.  Building is in the midst of tea fields.  You are taken through an area with China from all over the world.  Most of the China on display was either from France or Germany.  Then you enter a room where you can buy souvenirs as teas makeup made with tea and then there is a counter to buy dessert and teas or tea lattes.  They are very pricey though about $6 for a hot cup of tea.  Then after leaving that room you enter a room where you can sample tea infused makeup.  This reminded me of when we toured Fragonard perfumery in France where everyone was trying on the lotions and perfumes.  There were even large vials filled with liquids which were identified by the plant or flower beside them.  Once again similar to the perfumery labs.  Then there was a counter to order same teas dessert and even cold tea drinks that were nonalcoholic versions of cocktails but with tea in them.  These looked like they might've been good.  We finally decided we were in need of a hot drink after the sea cliffs experience.  So we bought one of those overpriced tea lattes.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Our hotel room overlooks this sea. Don't think there is a way to get down but the waterfront makes for a nice breezy walk. I suppose the reason for the decoration on the barrier is to make the walk interesting and photo worthy.

Our first time in Shinhwa World theme park visit in December 2017. One must come with the understanding that the theme park is not yet fully developed but it has some nice rides and you can spend a few hours there . My kids had a wonderful time . Since it is new  the park is not crowded. We had lunch at the food court and it was good Korean food . We were initially disappointed when the rides were suspended due to the snow. However the rides were resumed quickly after the snow stopped. We happened to have met the theme park Manager Mr Mason Kang when we ran into communication difficulty with one of the staff attending to the ride . He was very kind to explain to us that the rides would resume soon after they dry the area . His professionalism impressed us .  Our theme park experience was a great one . My kids tried the ice skating ring within the theme park compound . Everything is new and clean . We will come again ! They are going to have a Water theme park probably year after .

Other beaches such as Geumneng or Hyupjae are shallow and no waves so it is good for family with little kids. Otherwise Jungmun Saekdal beach is deep and has quite waves. If you are not a good swimmer you should have a tube or life jacket here. My kids are all teenagers and all good swimmers. They complained about other beaches: they are for toddlers not for thembut they had really good time in Jungmun Saekdal beach. Water are super clear and cool for good swim during hot summer days.
Only waterfall in asia which falls in ocean.i was amazed.must must see.very high falling.entry fee 2000 won
Only the first without the water falling is best for picture. The other two you will be on a platform far from the water.  The bridge is very big and allow you a good view.
one of the smaller waterfalls of he two but very well kept. shades of water can be seen along with a wishing well and a few picture spots on the bridge and walk way

One of the best waterfalls in Jeju that flows all the way to sea... Spent a wonderful time in our free and easy trip around Jeju island with a rented car! Will go to Jeju again for the third time again!

One of the best place I've been in Jeju!This place is quite isolated from the main road as I was stunning such a beautiful place exist where the river and sea water met! We can do a lot of water activities such as kayaking cycling in the water or riding a raft in a bluegreen water..Need to buy ticket in advance. If you go by evening for sure ticket will sold out. Honestly I dont want to write a review about this place as I prefer this place not to be crowded with people but well..For those going to Jeju this is a must visit place as the experience is quite rare and different from any other places.

One of my best spot in Jeju. We went in July end and the climate was very very hot. We were sweating like anything and in the mid way my wife said lets go back but i was like we have to go. But when we reached at the top it was so beautiful around. I forgot the stairs and all our exertion was gone. The view is so astonishing and it definitely looks like a world heritage.Tip: Do keep lot of water if visiting in summer.This peak has lot of stairs (not advisable old person or for heart patient).

One can have a magnificient view of basalt stone pillars formed along the coast due to sudden cooling and solidification of the Lava which flowed into the sea. The sudden contraction of molten lava due to the cooling effect of water has resulted in these rocks splitting into polygonal columns and forming a coast of almost 2 km long.This attraction is worth the visit and can be reached directly by trekking from Cheonjeyeon falls or taking a bus and pass thru the garden (Jusangjeollidae Promenade) and then reach the cliff at the end.Walking around the garden would be relaxing and one should not miss it. Wooden Platforms have been built to reach the end of the cliff and for a better view of the coastal line.

On month of June 2019 I booked 4 logs on 2 days dive plan. I went to Jeju for solo travel from Jakarta-Indonesia. Really appreciated all of GD expert Dive Masters who really assisted me to adapt on Korea water harsh condition. Even during strong currents the DMs assisted us to enjoy the dive itself it's amazing for me really excellent DMs service in the world ! If you have any plan to dive at Jeju-Korea we welcome you to the best DC in Jeju is Good Diver Jeju. Bravo GD Jeju ??????????????

Nothing that fantastic unless you are the one driving. The road is also only approximately 150metres long. Difficult to feel the gravity on human body/walking. Test using a vehicle or can/bottle/water poured on the road. The better deviation is Black pork stall manned by samurai-looking chefs. Mouth-watering black pork BBQ. Nice ice ball dessert nearby as well.

Nothing spectacular in terms of size other than the water is running into the ocean. It was a nice walk to get there and the view is nice from the rocks along the sea.  Ladies selling fresh seafood on the rocks.

Nothing much to say but great view!You shoud wear lightweight hiking shoes and bring water; umbrella along.Food are not allowed.You should try boating also. (10000- 20000 won per person)It is really great!

Not very big but nevertheless great for sunset watching. We went in fall but it was still warm enough. There is a place where the Hyenyo ladies who dive in water and bring you fresh seafoods cook on the spot seafoods and you can watch the sunset from there.

Not much to see or do except to take a few moments to take it the view and wind of Jeju. Many people (mostly Koreans) are seen walking along the beach picking shells or dipping their feet in the water. Not much sunbathers on this beach.

Not a bad way to fill in a couple of hours. The cave floor is very uneven as you are walking on solidified lava be sure to wear comfy shoes. Also can be quite damp so if you don't want to have water dripping on you maybe take an umbrella. Lots of information provided throughout the walk in several languages to keep you engaged also
Nice small beach. Clear water. We had sunny day so the beach and water together  was very beautiful. Have a walk there it improves your day.
Nice place to visit. Wonderfull waterfall nice place for relax. My son enjoy this place so much. We took public bus to come here and its quite easy to find.

Nice place for a short stroll from the pier to the bridge and over to Saeseom Island. We took quite a number of photos of the sea  bridge  and looking inland to Seogwipo Port. We enjoyed the sea breeze  the view of the clear waters and the displays of acrobatic jumping fish in the port. Locals stroll the area and it is a picturesque place to relax for a while. If you're into nature walks you can follow the trail around the island  which is probably small enough for you to complete in an hour or so.You can also take the submarine tour nearby at Seogwipo Port - but do check the weather conditions  our guide told us that the currents and weather play a big part in whether you'll be able to see lots of marine life during your dive.
Nice place  for young kids  is best. Not really good for adults but it was cute......will try water park next time.

Nice park surrounding this unique canyon.  3 sets of waterfalls.  An interesting bridge that goes over the canyon and a path that takes you through the woods.  Takes a bit of effort but it's worth doing if you're in the area.  The falls are not that impressive but the formations and the foliage is nice.

Never would have guessed but there's shopping  eating  a water park and movie theater at the world stadium. Jeju triathlon was headquartered here so I did that business. You can put on Hanboks (Korean clothing) and take pictures as well  that's all free.

Nearby the waterfall is a free campground. We liked it enough to stay three nights while visiting Seongwipo and Hallasan. The campground is a good size. The waterfall is refreshing to swim in. This place is worth checking out.

Near to Hyeopjae Beach with breathtaking views. It was very cold in the winter by beach so make sure get yourself wrapped up and enjoy the views here. The water was shallow and nice enough for us to walk around on the rocks and saw many green seaweeds here too.  A must visit if you are in Jeju Island.

My wife and I went to this place all of a sudden as We had no plan to cover this area. it is located in Jungmoon Resort area. the environment is like slience is spekaing everything. alongside the three water falls are awesome. Go and see.

My husband and I are in our 60's and the hike was fairly easy.  The views were amazing.  You can buy frozen water at the top and it will provide you with water for hours.  We tried octopus or abalone samples.  Meh!

My girlfriend and I went for a walk here and sat on a bench to watch the sun go down. It was a picturesque setting which we enjoyed. There are hundreds of little rock piles people have built which I recommend seeing. We were not there to swim but the water felt good on the feet!Shane & Jill

My family took the Eorimok Trail and the path is well maintained.  Remember to bring food and water along.  Recommend to start early morning as it gets hot at noon and early afternoon. It is worth the effort and a must see if you go to Jeju.

My 10 yo daughter and I have really enjoyed seeing the waterfall. It was a quick 20 minute walk up a scenic paved path with some other small falls. It was definitely worth a visit. Cost couple won to get in. There are several shops right outside and along the way to buy souvenirs and snacks.

Must visit a place. The experience of walking inside the cave where once the lava used to flow was chilling and amazing. The cave temperature was around 13 degree Celsius. The water drops were dripping from the cave top surface. There were information boards about the cave surfaces and other features as you walk inside the cave.

Mr. Jang was very kind and extremely helpful within our two days in Jeju. He went out of his way to help us with everything. His car is very comfortable and spacious. He provided us with water bottles every time we entered his car.

most important points1 start your climb early. as you must reach a certain point before noon and must start the decent by 14:30.2 take a bout 3-4 leters of water per person as there is no place to fill or buy anywhere on the climb (locals take tangerines as they are filled with liquid and sugars)we started at  the road 1131  entrance at about 08:30 and reached the midpoint at about 11:30 and then the top at 14:00large parts of the route are wood walks and steps but others are more difficult.when you reach the top make sure to take a picture of the tree with writing as proof so you can get a certificate when you reach the bottom (1000 WON)Enjoy your climb

Manjanggul Cave was a thoroughly interesting experience. The structure itself is awe inspiring and feels like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Be prepared for water droplets plopping on your head! It was a bit chilly when we visited as well.
Lovely waterfall that fall directly into the sea. Very interesting and fun! Highly recommended. Great to bring children too!

Loved it the various marine lives attraction there. Personally I liked most is the underwater aquarium where we could walk beneath the swimming fishes. Also the collection of various jellyfish and octopus on display. Stunning.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: Long trail relatively easy.. specially the first 4 KM .. are flat basically The rest is a hit steepThey will give u a certificate if u take a picture up for 1000 wanBring ur own food.  And water.. In the winter wear ur gears as its super sleepery dont go with out gears i went in april. . And in the last 1/3 of the road i slipped and injured myself many times.. Fantastic hike.. Definitely recommend it
Long lava tube and if you are into stones and caves you will find it interesting. Inside was cold and some water drops coming from ceiling. Once you reach the end that it just take a picture then go.

Located in Seogwipo area. Beautiful waterfall that easy to access as only reached 5-10 minutes walking their path. Mostly is stairs. Entrance Fee KRW2000. Have some small shops near the entrance selling local souvenir.

Little walk down pathway along the cliff on the seaside.Something to see while in the area.May be difficult for elderly or those with weak walking abilities as walk to the waterfall from parking lot consist of lots of stairs and wet floors.
Liked: The waterfall was nice and good value at $2 entry.Disliked: It was VERY busy and you were not allowed to swim here!

Less crowded than many other attractions somehow. A beautiful temple and big! Small cave behind temple worth checking out. Don't forget to drink of the water legend has it you will live a longer life!
Kids love to climb all the stones around and the waterfalll is nice too. There are lady selling fresh seafood which we didnt try. It's nice place to spend 1 hour if you have active kids.

Halla-san is the highest mountain in South Korea and the middle of Jeju Island.  There are two trails that go to the summit of the mountain.  There are a few other trails on Halla-san but they don't go to the top.  It is about 9KM from one side of the mountain to the top and about 10 KM on the other trail to the top.  There are water sources on the mountain so you don't need to carry much drinking water.  It took me between 2 to 2.5 hours to reach the summit and about the same time to go back to where I had parked my car.  The trail is fairly rocky and vertical.  On a clear day you can see all of Jeju Island and the sea below from the summit.  There is also a small pond in the middle of the summit of the dormant volcano that is Halla-san.

Had a long bikecycle trip from Jeju-do city to which I ended at this beach.It's like a small bay with white sand beach. was pretty crowded although it wasn't the season. water sport wasn't operational
Great view clean air and blue water. The climb is pretty steep but the view is totally worth the effort.
Great hike! A bit demanding!Must get to a check point before 1pm to be allowed to go to the top.The descent route is often closed and the observatory is not fair if the lake is not full of water
Good place to explore for 1-2 hours. Be prepared to walk. Bring a waterproof jacket and good walking shoes with good grip as it's wet inside the cave
Good photo opportunity. Visit during high tide to see majestic falls flowing into the ocean.Visit during rainy season to see more water crashing down.
Fascinating 100m. Our car rolled  down when on Neutral and the road is flat... Bottle of water rolling backward. Same goes when water was poured on the ground...

Everyone loved it!Make sure to bring your selfie stick and sunblock.It was really nice  I recommend it.It's not a waterfall all year around  some people say they didn't find a waterfall  I did though.Visited in Summer of 2015
Even on a cloudy rainy day it is still beautiful.  The waters were clean. There are restaurants and cafes lining the beach.  Free fountain to clean feet.
Even during slightly overcast conditions this was a very pleasant stroll.  People enjoying the very blue water and peering into tide pools.  Progressed from lava stones to smooth sandy beach.

With baby nursing rooms  kids??pools  Asia's first double water slide  private cabanas  a variety of sauna rooms  hot snacks and fresh beer  there's something here for everyone in the family

Enjoyed extra time here because the rushing water sounds were so relaxing. You can hang out on the rocks quite close to the falls.

Emerald color water with a beautiful long beach and white sand!!  a great place for families with children to play together and enjoy a quiet. It makes a beautiful scenery photo with Biyangdo Island is located directly in front of the beach.
Easy Access from Seofwipo city. You can take nice picture at the background of waterfall. Seo Bok Memorial place is very near. You can visit both place.

Easily accessible by public bus from airport! This garden is not so crowded & have nice decoration so can relax. Locals like to visit this place & not foreigners are seen during my visit there. Next to this garden have a waterwall so got another place to relax. Recommend to go teddy bear museum & kpop museum as very near to one another so this will spend one whole day.

Drove by this bridge in jeju which has a sail shape like on a sail boat.? Actually fitting since it is over a small Marina.? We were on a day tour of jeju in November 2016 on the way to some waterfalls when we passed this bridge.

Driving from Jeju city centre to Manjanggul Cave is straight forward and easy. Parking is also free for this attraction. We had to purchase a ticket prior to entering the cave through a steep and slippery rocky stair. The cave is wet and cold even in March. The grounds are contantly wet with water dripping throughout the cave. It is also not easy to walk on as the grounds are very uneven and filled with puddles of water. Walking through the cave was thrilling and filled with excitement. Round trip to and fro the cave took us about 1hr30mins. Would highly recomend to anyone visiting Jeju Island. Proper shoes are also recommended as it can be very slippery and slip and fall may happen. Kids and Older people may find this attraction tough and difficult to walk through.

Don't go out of your way for this. It's fun for a few minutes but that's about it. Our driver did the usual - setting the gear to N and let the mysterious power posses the vehicle - and repeated it with a bottle of water. Bring a packet of marbles. There's awesomeness in numbers.

Crystal clear turquoise water and green lush forest. Really spectacular. Would definitely go again. There is also a black sand beach and many restaurants and curio shops. Great visit

Could have spent half a day here. Gardens were beautiful. The lava caves were nice to walk through to break up the heat! Interesting animals throughout.  Ran out of time and missed seeing the water gardens.  Great way to spend a day outside. Especially enjoyed the bonsai garden.

It is called the 3-tier waterfall as it falls over 3 cliffs before ultimately ending up in the ocean. The legend has it that there are 7 nymphs who visit at night to bathe in the ponds. You will also find the Seonimgyo Bridge on your walk to the waterfall which is adorned by the 7 nymphs  beautifully done in metal.A definite must-do while visiting Jeju-do.

Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on   for the most part  . Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the   tourist beach experience  , selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a   pro   if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.
You will need good shoes and ~20 min, and water, the rout is amazing, clean, safe and view is breathtaking, on the way back you can buy tangerine juice form the shops - delicious!

You will have to try it youself to experience it! Tried it with a water bottle but it doesn't work. Tried it with a car and shifted to neutral, the car will ascend the inclining road. Quite interesting but will be bored after 5 minutes.

You will be enchanted by the beauty of this place. It's quite unusual to see the shallow stream meeting big ocean waves. You can come very close to the waterfall to feel the power of falling stream. Or cross the stream and walk along the shore, it's fun to jump from one rock to another. Or just sit on a big smooth rock and watch the sea.

It is advisable to use your feet to check for the stability of the rocks before stepping on them as there were some loose and moving ones amongst the pile of rocks. The rocks nearer to the waterfall are wet so be careful if you want to get even closer to the fall. The waves crashing on the shore are also rather strong, so be more cautious if you?re moving nearer towards the shore.

You need to pay an entrance fee which doesn't include the train ride (which is an additional small fee if you opt to use it). The train can take you on a short ride to view the gardens. Inside the greenhouse, it's quite warm and you can climb up some stairs to view Jeju Island from the top. There was some renovation being carried out in the lifts.? Can spend 1-2 hours here if you're not a garden fanatic!? It's located next door to the Cheonyijeon Waterfall.

You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are plenty of cars exhibited, including antique cars and modern cars. There are descriptions beside every single car including where they produce, which car firm belongs to and when it is first produced. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. I bought a wheel like key chain, it costs 10k KWD, which is relatively cheap compare to the models of cars.So, if you are a car fan or you want to have some souvenirs about cars, you are recommended to go to the car museum to buy your favorites.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

Yongmeori is a rough and dramatic coastline shaped from lava eruptions. Walking along the spectacular rock formations is an experience that only Jeju-do can offer. Firstly, some of the water pockets with bright turquoise water are striking in their uniqueness. Secondly, the sometimes bizarre rock formation are nothing if not eye-catching. Lastly, the strange (slightly grotesque) insects that scurry along some of the rocks are strangely interesting. They never touch or climb on you, every footfall makes them scurry in all direction. Yongmeori is a bit off the   classic   tourist itinerary. Most visitors enjoy a beach or two, maybe a hike at Hallasan or the Seongsan Ilchulbong, and perhaps they fit in a waterfall and museum. Jeju has so much to offer that is often overlooked. Yongmerori Coast is one of these places.

Would recommend to all visitors of Jeju. Nice atmosphere, clean beach, blue water, and great scenery. A little rocky in the water but overall it was peaceful!
Worth seeing, and I liked that it was within walking distance of our hotel. The beach area was really pretty although it is not a place to go if you want a beach and not a waterfall.

Worth a visit if you are a beach person - lots of people. Plenty of food booths and shops close by, lots of gimmicks to buy to include in your day. Water was okay - typical sand in the pants type of thing!!
Wonderful views and landscapes.  Excellent preservation of the trails and nature.  Well worth a half day.  Make sure you pack some food, water and enjoy this marvellous part of Jeju.
Wonderful hikes, but even the easiest ones can be long with some steeper sections. Bring lots of water. The hikes are popular and can be crowded, even in the off-season.

With a 2,000?? fee, this waterfall is well worth a visit! It's a short walk down from the parking lot - not hard to get to at all. You should, however, wear comfortable and supportive shoes because you need to balance on rocks in order to get close to the falls.
White sand, clear water. View of several islands. Family beach. Easy to get to, great to walk along the water's edge.

While this is  just of the roadway, it?s fairly free of visitors.   The path goes alongside running water (or not - depending on rainfall).    There was about a 30m section where the path ended and we had to walk from rock to rock before the path restarted.    On the other side was a cave - Rock Shade Residence - which olden people used as shelter.   Entire area is a beautiful evergreen valley, well worth a visit.

While it is not the only waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea as many think (I've seen them both in Indonesia and Philippines), it is definitely a cool waterfall to see and they are relatively rare. I would definitely recommend seeing this waterfall first if you're planning to check out all of the waterfalls on Jeju. It is very accessible and a great viewing experience.

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Nevertheless, we got off anyway because we saw the cashier booth.Taxi tips: later after the walk uphill, we realized we could have insisted the taxi to go a little further to the big parking area which was the main entrance. That way we would be walking downhill to see the waterfalls, and could exit at the mid hill exit near the temple, just opposite the Twosome Square. If desired, you can also continue downhill to the third waterfall.Photo tip: don't wear aqua or turquoise colors, or green or blue etc. as the the waterfall, although not big, is aqua and turquoise in colors in a sunny day. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

When we arrived we were a little surprised at the ticket price to enter. There was quite a lot of steps to get down, as we walked down you can see the waterfall. when we got down to the rocks by the waterfall there was tons of people it was so crowded. but the waterfall was very beautiful and was very nice how it was all open without any barriers keeping you from the waterfall.

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.? This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.

What's interesting is that you really, actually get to see cars/buses with their engines obviously off, rolling up the slope. Expect to see a number of tour buses. Some tour guides will demonstrate the mysteriousness of the road even further by pouring water on the ground. The water will flow upwards. 10mins is enough time to spend here. Recommended to visit once for the experience.

What I like about this waterfall is that you can either admire it from a distance or if you prefer, you can literally walk along the rocks and take a closeup shot right next to the falls. What a thrill.

What can I say...I loved Jeongbang waterfall soooo much. I went there on one of the hottest summer days in July and it was absolutely amazing. On my way down, I was complaining and whining the whole time because it was too hot. But once I got down near the waterfall, it was really windy..almost chilly!!! Cooling winds lovely views...I'll go there again before I leave Jeju!

What a amazing waterfall. I heard that there are olny few waterfall forward the ocean in the world. I had seen several waterfall. If anyone ask me what waterfall is best in your life time, I will say Jeongbang is the best. It is not that big like Victoria or Niagara, but it make feel me cheer up.

Went up and down seongpanak. Went with my parents who are in their early 50s. The way up gets a little tough after the 12:30 point. We started at 6:30 and got to that area by 11:00. On the way down gets very boring. Bring lots of water and wear shoes. You'll see old Korean people wearing stuff you'd wear to summit some crazy mountain but just good shoes with good grip (not converse) will be good for the hike. Of course hiking boots would help. Things to bring: hand sanitizer, water, sunscreen, gatorade/pocari sweat if it's very hot. Bring some food and bags for trash as you have to take it all with you. Overall probably 4/5 experience but nice to experience with family. Probably not good for young kids - people with health problems die each year per locals.

Went there to watch sunrise with Sunrise Peak background and foreground with water and rock.? The beach is large and we could find a spot without disturbance of others.? However, there is no official car park space.

went there on a rainy day. Was't hard to get down to the waterfall but it was a little difficult trying to balance myself on the rocks while holding on to a camera. Was crowded but still manageable. On my way down, I found the lady divers selling fresh catch of the day and it was awesomely fresh!

Went there in the morning via taxi. Not many people. Admission: 2000 won each.There are flights of stairs to climb down when you first reach, so imagine the climb back up once you are done. To get nearer to the waterfall, you have walk over many many many rocks. Not recommended to go after rain as it will be super slippery. However, I love this waterfall more than Cheongjiyeon waterfall. It is nicer actually and you can get closer to the waterfall (of coz getting passed the obstacles of rocks).Love it actually but no way near magnificent.

Went there as part of tour. Find it really fascinating n entertaining. Worth it to go there one afternoon. Takes only 15 mins... Bus turn off engine, pour warmer on the road, letting water bottle roll, n closing your eyes n walk!

Went on a day hike up and down the Seongpanak trail! It was a gorgeous day, about 18C and I couldn't have asked for better weather. It took about 10 hours round trip. Started around 8:30am and made it down by 6:30pm. Luckily the sun didn't go down until 7:15ish so I had plenty of light to guide me.Now, I am not a hiker by any means and this was one of the toughest hikes I've been on. To be honest, it wasn't because the trails were all that difficult - it was actually quite pleasant through the woods and there were 2 rest stops along the way. The first stop is basically a bathroom break and the 2nd had some food available before heading up the last (somewhat steeper) trail to the lake up top. Oh, by   food   I mean some cup ramen and snacks. They also sold water and sports drinks. It would be helpful for you to bring food of your own. They also have no garbage cans so you need to carry and dispose of your own trash once you get back down.The reason why this trail was difficult for me was because I simply wasn't ready for a 20km hike! By the last 5km of the descent, I felt my feet and legs were going to fall off or give in to becoming jelly due to all the stairs and rocks. Make sure you have proper shoes! All in all, I'm glad I did this hike - it was worth it when I got to the top and was able to experience amazing views and clean air. And the flowers!! It was simply beautiful. Just expect to have sore calves for a few days following :)

Went here on a hot summer afternoon and could immediately feel the drop in temperature when entering the natural reserve. The water is clean, clear and very tempting. unfortunately swimming is not allowed. Need to walk and climb stairs to reach all the 3 waterfalls, but each one was worth it. stop by near the bridge to take photos

Went here on a cloudy morning and loved it. Lots of steps to get down to the falls so grandmom stayed at the top. Pretty impressive and the bottom and it?s neat to see a waterfall so close to the ocean.If you have time, don?t forget to walk along the path along the coast to the ?Castle of Shell?. You get to the boardwalk path from the other side of the parking lot and it?s not well marked. It leads to a house on a cliff and another small waterfall. This place would have been a 4 but this extra trail makes it a 5. The cost for a family of 5 was 7,000 KRW.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.
Well, another water fall, again! haha, its nice, give it a try if never bit there. Photo look nicer tho, actual scene you might feel that the waterfall is not as big as you imagine.

Wear your sport shoes, warm jacket, bring light snacks, a bottle of water, and of course..a determination. Dont forget camera as you will blown away by the scenery from the peak. Early morning is a good time to climb

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!

We were here in October, so we weren't swimming. We drove by here one day to check it out, a day or two after a typhoon hit, and the beach was trashed a bit (just from trees and debris and stuff), but people were cleaning it up and there were still lots of people enjoying the beach. It looks like a nice place to spend a day, and there seemed to be a bunch of restaurants and cafes dotting the beach as well. We stopped at one of the cafes for a coffee and to enjoy the view of the water for a bit.

We were heading to Halim Park and chance upon this on the way. Not many people as it was winter and really cold to be at the beach but the view is just so soothing. Blue greenish ocean waters, waves splashing against the rocks, white sandy beach, etc...just picture perfect.  The wind was blowing hard on our faces. There is a stine statue there at the parking lot.Definitely want to go back again.

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We were dropped by a taxi at the beginning of the Seongpanak trail (a little way up the volcano), but you can catch the bus there if you prefer and there is a bus stop right near the entrance. The track is 9.6km (19.2km return), and took us about 6 hours return walking at a medium pace, including breaks at Sokbat shelter (4.1kms up - toilet facilities only) and at Jindallaebat shelter (7.3kms up - toilet and small kiosk). We had initially wanted to walk up the Gwaneumsa trail and then down the Seongpanak one, but were too tired to get up before 6am to achieve it in one day. Walking the Seongpanak trail up and down was a great experience in itself, even though it is apparently not as scenic as others. But, because it's one of the easier ones, it is packed with tourists, most of whom are not seasoned walkers, so be prepared for being held up a fair bit (and witnessing some pretty avoidable but hilarious injuries!).The trail is quite an easy one in comparison to other hikes we have done - no really steep bits or actual climbing - more of a gentle incline, with boardwalks in parts, dirt paths and as you get higher, rough rocky paths. The only strenuous thing about the trail is that it is long? It will take you all day, and you have to start early so you reach the Jindallaebat shelter before a certain hour (changes depending on the season, but in September it was 12:30pm) or the ranger won't let you continue - for obvious reasons, there's no lighting at night to climb back down, so he doesn't want to come and find stupidly lost tourists! You can check the times on the official Hallasan website. You don't really need proper hiking boots/other equipment for this hike (we did it in light walking shoes), but if you have weak ankles I would probably recommend wearing hiking boots with ankle support, especially for the walk back down the rocky paths. Take plenty of water and snacks - don't rely on the shelters like the Koreans do, they may sell out/be extremely busy, and you have to get to Jindallaebat by 12:30! We just bought some muesli bars, fruit, WATER and energy drinks like gatorade/powerade at a 7/11 before we left Jeju city in the morning, and were almost the only ones who had thought ahead! On the way back down, the Jindallaebat shelter will be quieter, so it's the perfect opportunity to then buy some of their hot ramen noodles or a chocolate bar. I would also recommend bringing a light rain jacket, and a waterproof backpack/cover for your backpack - it showers sporadically within the fog. I also took a plastic bag to put my camera in to keep it dry.When we began our walk, it was quite chilly at the entrance and the local walkers laughed at us wearing shorts - but by the time you get a few kilometres in, you'll be stripping off layers of clothing, so totally wear shorts if you want to - it's quite warm in the sun on the summit, so everyone will be peeling off their layers anyway! There was a thick fog hanging low over the volcano for about 2/3 of the walk, so it's a bit muggy, but the side of the mountain is lush and green, an eerily quiet forest. As you get higher, suddenly you notice you're climbing above the fog - feels like you've popped out above the clouds, on top of the world! The last part of the track is quite windy, and you can see how the wind has beaten its wooden steps, which are strewn everywhere. Be careful in the last part and beware pushy tourists! But, once you get to the summit, at Dongneung Peak (no facilities on the summit, by the way), the view is breathtakingly beautiful - like nothing I've ever seen before! The crater when we were there was overgrown with vegetation, with a small crater lake. Such a wonderful experience, and most definitely a highlight of our trip to South Korea! You must hike Hallasan during your stay at Jeju-do!

we were definitely not prepared for this - in terms of experience and equipment!started off at about 9am on the Eorimok route. the entrance was a 10 min walk from the bus stop. then, it was off on the hike!initially the trail was straightforward. then it gradually went into a steep ascent. the path was quite rocky and unstable. but there were sufficient rest stops along the way. also people going in the same and opposite direction to you so you will not be alone (unless you hike in the middle of the night)there were also multiple signboards along the route providing interesting facts about Hallasan and also maps showing your current location and remaining distances to go to the next point.there was almost a natural portable water point where you can refill your bottles. remember to stay hydrated throughout and take breaks when needed.needless to say, the views along the route were truly breathtaking but the higher elevation you reach, the colder it becomes. also, the winds were very strong!we reached the Witseoreum shelter at about 12pm and had lunch there. The locals actually brought hot water in their thermos flasks and had cup ramen there!after lunch, we started our descent on the Yeongsil trail and reached the entrance of Yeongsil at about 2pm and there was a 2km walk out of the entrance to the bus stop.by then our legs were aching and heavy, but we pushed on. overall the hike took about 5 hrs.in summary, we should have worn more proper hiking footwear, wear thicker clothing (as higher you go, the colder it gets) and more food and snacks!we decided we will come back to attempt the summit next time.

We were coming from Hamdeok Beach to the Jeongbang water falls and happened to directly pass by this place on the highway and I remembered it was one of the top places to visit in Jeju so we decided to pull over and enter.  We're very glad we did.  We spent about an hour there but you could easily spend more time.  It was awesome to see all the man made stone statues and their significance or their meaning, one of the main ones  being the mother who had 500 sons.  The museums were pretty cool as well and you could learn a ton of geography.  The setting was very picturesque with Mt. Halla in the background and the surroundings looking like you were sort of in a savanah.  We took some awesome photographs and learned a lot of information.  I think if you're able to rent a car and drive there it's a must see in Jeju.

We were attracted by the promise from the literature that this was the only waterfall in Asia with 'debouches' into the ocean. Hmmm, you almost get the impression from above that some channel engineering has helped this along. Anyway, Wikipedia tells me that this claim is not quite correct. Anyway, we arrived as then had to purchase entry tickets. The stressed out man next to the ticket gate then seemed to think that we have not purchased the correct amount of tickets. We had. It was all the more puzzling because he was only 2 feet from where we bought the tickets. Maybe he was so bored he was asleep at the wheel. Or maybe it was because we were foreigners. Anyway, once that nonsense was resolved we headed down the steps, only to be stopped half-way down at yer another ticket check! Ridiculous, three check for a 1000-or-so won entry ticket. We thought we must be in for something very special. Alas not. Said waterfall falls a few score metres, generates a modest amount of spray and attracts thousands of people taking selfies of themselves and said insipid attraction. There are some older folk selling ghastly looking octopus slices by the rocks - poor animals (the octopus that is). We were not stopped for more ticket checks on the way out, thankfully. I suggest you just look at the photo on the web and go and do something more interesting instead.

We went with my 63 year old mom, husband, and 15 and 6 year olds. It was great! It's waaaay longer, wider, taller and more interesting of a lava tube than at Volcanos national park in Hawaii! The largest accessible in the world. Bring a waterproof camera, hiking shoes or at least tennis goes, a raincoat or jacket. Won't wear white. I still can't get the ash stain out of my sons sleeve after he fell in a puddle. It's only a few dollars to get in. Do the quick museum first, if you want to know more about it. Cold, wet, dark, tired but Loved it!

We went up the Gwaneumsa Trail and down Seongpanak and thought it was a great route. Seongpanak has much better views that are easier to see while walking down, otherwise your back is facing the beauty on the way up. Both trails are majority rock. Meaning, nearly the entire hike is trying to find rocks to climb up/down. There are some wood paths, bridges, and stairs, but mostly rock which is hard on the arches of your feet. I used regular Adidas sneakers which worked, however the bottom of my feet began to ache on the way down. On the way up Gwaneumsa, we couldn't refill our water at all, then at the top - NOTHING! It wasn't until 2 km down Seongpanak (6 hours after we began the hike) that there was free water access. Nothing was sold on this hike, even though I read about ramen and drinks being sold. I was DYING for water. Bring tons!!! At Gwaneumsa there is a store to purchase beverages and 2 servings of gimbap for 3,000 won, as well as walking sticks for 20,000. I didn't use one but many did and it seemed to help balancing on all the rocks. I began the hike at 7:00am and was down by 3:45 - this included a half an hour break at the top and 2 min stop at each base camp (there were about 4 or so on each route.) I'm not an experienced hiker at all and really doubted my ability to do this, but it IS manageable!
