The scenery is fantastic - especially on the Yeongsil trail - and if the azaleas had been out it would have been even more amazing.   The whole trip took us 5 hours and then the taxi ride took about 20 minutes and cost KRW 20,000.   At the time I said it was unlikely I would ever do this hike again but now I have recovered I think I would in the Autumn to see the colours and also maybe in May to see the azaleas.   Maybe next time we will try the other way round......  Tips - lots of water, snacks, walking poles might be useful. good walking boots and a coolish day.

We decided to go to Audi because of the 3 different beaches the were there (and for Haha Hoho Burgers). Getting there was more difficult than expected. We had a rental car which was nice to be able to retreat back to air conditioning. But the line for the ferry was so long that it took about 2 hours to get on the ferry. Once on the island our first stop was for lunch at Haha Hoho. We were lucky in that they didn't sell out of burgers by the time we got there at 1:50. Buy by the time our burgers were ready 2:40 they were sold out and not taking any more orders. So get there early for lunch. The drive around the island was nice  and picturesque. The first beach we stopped at was a disappointment. The water was green with algae and smelled. There was also quite a bit of trash. With the number of people there I would expect more maintenance. We stayed only briefly hoping for better beaches down the road. The next stop was a black sand beach nestled in a cool looking cove. But again there was trash everywhere. We didn't stay long. The first two beaches were a   bust.    The third was the   coral beach.   It was clean but the water still green with algae and seaweed. The beach was rough under our feet but the kids had fun. It was pretty crowded and the water became deep quickly so not much space to play for new swimmers. The views from the island were great, especially at sunset. Overall we were underwhelmed and felt we probably should have stayed on Jeju and just visited the northern beaches.

We decided to get off the bus on the way to Jeju city and walking towards the sea it looked like a really quiet place... When we arrived on the beach front we were pleasantly surprised by all the quaint little cafes that dotted the shoreline. There's a surf school on the beach and parasols everywhere. It is a smaller beach, but clear and shallow water. You are not short for choice for lunch or snacks. We had a lovely day!

We chose to visit only one waterfall due to time constraint. It was along the way from the cliff in jungmum. That is west central near seogiwipo.We reached just before it closes at 530pm. So do check opening hours of the tourist sites. You may spend more time at one site and then the next one is closed. There were not many people cos wintertime. We bought the tickets, went down the stairs then overlooking the waterfall, we took some photos. Going down was easy, comjng up omg! We have to walk on the rocks towards the waterfall. We had seen massive waterfall in alaska so this was not that huge.However, just sitting on the rocks looking into the ocean, people watching is great. Mostly local tourists.At the ticket entrance on way back we tried the local skewer food. They dip into broth some beancurd tofu skin. Taste good. I had a breaded hotdog. Its about about $1 to $3 for the different items. Guess you need to try to be like locals to have fun!We spend about an hour here.

We choose a day with the best weather forecast, during our visit to Jeju island, to take a walk to the peak of Hallasan. We choose west trail ? it doesn't lead to the peak, but is much shorter. It took us 3h to get to the highest point of the trail and 2h to get back to the next bus stop. Everything was very exotic, as we are used to hike in Alps or Carpathians. It is worth to remember, that the temperature drops about 1째C/200m, so it should be 10째C colder on the peak than on the sea level. And it was. More surprising was that there are no possibility to buy food or drink in the park. Fortunately we took lot of water and some fruits and sweets (old habit from   real   mountains). The trail was very   civilised   ?mostly steps, easy and very safe (however with ice or snow it's for sure not a pice of cake). More walking than climbing. Not so much people (May seems to be off season), but we were not alone. The view from the trail and the peak just beautiful. In my opinion it's worth to spent half a day on Jeju to see it.

We can't quite remember the order but my wife and I saw 3 waterfalls when we went looking for one. All the waterfalls were spell binding, gushing with water even in summer (April) However, 2 are fenced for safety reasons and the third one has a board warning you against swimming. You can, although, dip your feet in the cold water at the unfenced one. At the first one, you can make a wish and throw a coin into the shallow end of the fall. And if your schedule isn't packed, it's a great place to sit back and read a book.

we can enjoy this place with family and toddler or young kids,  not recommend for gentlemen. but very educative for children. located inside the Jungmun Tourist Complex, you can get anythink you need in this tourist complex like various restaurant, hotels , 3D art museum, Belive it or not. Kpop Museum , Conventionl Centre , Waterfall Etc

We came here as part of a tour from Hong Kong and no one else went to climb up to the top, but me and my boyfriend did. It's about a 30 minute walk - you can take it slowly and take photos along the way, but it can be a bit steep. However, the views are great (on a clear day) and you get a good workout (after sitting on a bus for so long). The ascent/descent paths are clearly marked and separated, so it's quite well organised and the path/fence is very well maintained. At the top, you can overlook the big crater, which is now overgrown with lots of lush grass and trees - quite beautiful. You can also overlook the water and the town below etc. The way down has lots of stairs, so watch out if you have bad knees.

We came here after the Manjungal caves. The maze is challenging enough and took us about 35min to solve, but it was fun and worth the entrance price. It was a hot day so take a bottle of water with you to stay hydrated. Also, whilst in the maze we noticed some pretty large spider webs with some fairly big spiders, so careful of those. All in all, its a great family activity. There's also some lovely cats in the park that are friendly and you can pet them.

We are a relatively fit family, but were not properly prepared for hiking Halla Mountain.  We made it as far as the Observatory (approx. 6 hours round trip). Since it rained days before, the summit was closed due to poor trail conditions.  Although some portions of the hiking trail are level & nicely paved (w/ wooden planks), the majority of the trail is very steep & rough (comprised of large, uneven volcanic rocks). Unfortunately, we wore Nike running shoes & Converse tennis shoes which did not provide adequate support & protection needed on the feet.  Since the incline & steps are uneven, you need to be careful where you step in order to prevent ankle or knee strains/sprains.  We saw some people fall on the jagged volcanic rocks & get scrapped pretty badly.  We found wood branches along the way to use as hiking sticks for balance.  This hike is alot tougher than the hike to the upper falls of Yosemite.  So we recommend that you come prepared:- sturdy hiking shoes and hiking poles- at least 2 bottles of water per person (there are 2 drinking wells w/ a communal drinking cup; we drank it & had no stomach probs)- bug repellent (we were there in the humid summer)- cooling scarf (to wet & wrap around neck)- energy food (power bars, fruit/nuts)- backpack (carry out your trash)- small first aid kitTip: There is a parking fee to park in front of the entrance.  All of the parking spots are usually taken very early.  Otherwise, if you park on the street or arrive by taxi/bus, there is no fee to enter the park.

Waterfalls are very accessible in Jeju. Jeongbang is the most unique as we seldom see a waterfall that goes straight to the sea. Going by public bus is easy and the path towards the falls are already paved except for the rocky part near the falls itself. I suggest you take your time in sitting on one of the rocks and just enjoy the relaxing view. If you're patient, you can wait for 10-20 mins for tourists to leave and you can have the view all by yourself.  For photography enthusiasts, have a wide angle lens ready =D

Water was very clear and sand was clean. There are some shops on the beach, and toilet facilities close by. Plenty of eating places around the area too. A nice beach to spent a day or just a little while. There are people firing fireworks at night. So if you happen to be there when that happen, you are in for some light show.
Water was crystal clear - not too cold. Many great restaurants nearby. Floats available for rent. It was a little busy, but not too crazy.

Want to do a bush walk with nice scenery ?  Eorimok Trail & Yeongsil Trail in Hallasan National Park in Mt Halla will be a good choice when you visit Jeju Island in South Korea. Be sure to take a bush hat, sun screen lotion and bottles of water. Along the trails, there are a couple of water refill spots for refilling water from the mountain. The cheapest way is to take a bus No. 740 from the Jeju City Outer Bus Terminal if you stay at Jeju city.  Get off at the stop for the entrance to Eorimok Trail. From there, it will be uphill passing nice vegetation & trees until you reach Yeongsil Trail. Follow this Yeongsil Trail, you may be lucky to see Mt Halla deer. Once you start walking downhill on the Yeongsil Trail, you will see beautiful mountain scene. At the exit of Yeongsil Trail, you will need to walk a couple of Km downhill along the road to reach the Yeongsil Entrance to get the bus 740 back to Jeju City Outer Bus Terminal. Bus 740 travels between Jeju City and Seogwipo-si and uses the same bus stop at Yeongsil Entrance. When you get onto the bus, be sure it is going back to Jeju City Outer Bus, not the bus going to Seogwipo-si.[ The walk on Eorimok Trail & Yeongsil Trail will easily takes 5 hours plus.   Air brushes are available at the entrance / exit of the trails ]

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. The area that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock is apparently the filming location of the Korean drama series, Jewel in the Palace (鸚㏝룝).For more of my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/oedolgae-rock-and-great-sea-view.html

Walked to the bridge as it was near my hotel (M stay hotel seogwipo). It's a nice bridge and you can walk across it to saeyong island, where you can have a short hike around the island. Nice views during the hike where you can see the ocean and three different islands. It's also near Cheonjiyeon waterfall.

Walked over from our hotel to the waterfalls and enjoyed the view.  Absolutely gorgeous. As a group, we enjoyed climbing up and down stones to get closer to the falls for pictures or over to see the fishermen (and women) slightly further away from the falls.

Walk down to the falls is quiet and serene. A couple of local women were offering the fresh seafood they have just caught for sale. One just need to pay small amount and the woman will cut up the seafood and serve it with some sauce. People will just eat it fresh like sashimi.To get bearer to the fall, one need to navigate through rocks. Care should be taken else one may fall or drop your camera of smartphone. We were lucky to spot a rainbow at the place where the water splashed on the rocks! This is real rare and definitely made our day.

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Visited this place which is really a lava tube rather than a cave.  It is about 1 kilometer from end-to-end.  Inside the tube you can see different rock formations created by the lava flow, among them the turtle-shaped rock at 600-meter mark.  It is cool inside the tube and water is dripping everywhere.  It is recommended that you wear appropriate footwear while taking this tour as it could really be slippery and some areas are not so well-lit.  Maybe this is intentional to give the place a more realistic feel.

Visited the cave as a part of a bus tour. We entered through the 2nd section and were given 40 mins to walk to end of the cave and back. Grounds are uneven and slippery due to water dripping from the ceiling, hence proper shoes are necessary. The lighting was quite dim and there were only a couple of descriptions along the way. I didn't come out with a full appreciation of the lava cave. The cave wasn't very spectacular but it's worth a visit if you are in the area.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

Visited Hamdeok Beach (⑤댁) with my boyfriend. We took a walk around the beach. It was really windy and cold. The wind was strong. The beach is very clean and beautiful. The waters are clear. We took some pictures there and we happened to see couple having wedding photoshoot (with the beautiful scenery).Many people from various age groups visited this beach. It is a nice place to take a walk and chill out. There are hotels, shops, convenience stores, cafes and restaurants nearby the beach. There is also public toilet nearby the beach (near the carpark). We drove there. It is very convenient and we can get some snacks while chilling out there.

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.
Very unique waterfall by the sea. walk up close and feel the water spray across your face, while the sea waves lap your feet below. great view and refreshing experience.

Very scenic place to see a pretty high waterfall flow directly into the sea!! There is an admission fee of $2000 Korean won entrance fees per Adult. Short walk from the ticket booth with steps reaching downwards to the waterfall. Interestingly if time permits, one can walk to the end of the big car park in front of the ticket office and there is an Olle trail near the sea that leads to a Castle of Shell and a smaller waterfall!

Very pretty beach on a sunny day. The colour of the water is so beautiful. Nicely prep walkway all along the whole beach area. Lots of places for coffee and a quick lunch. We had dinner at a local eatery, the owner was nice and friendly.  He helped BBQ our black skin pork belly for us. So yummy with water Kimchi and beer.
Very peaceful and beautiful place. Loved walking around and seeing all the beautiful bonsais, scenic view, beautiful waterfall and fishes. Would definitely love to visit again <3

very nice paintings on the walls inside the temple. peaceful and quiet at the compound. there are 3 levels to the temple and you can actually walk up to look around all 3 of the levels. it also has a nice garden behind. you can drink from the water at the 2   tanks   which is located one on each side of the temple.
Very interesting road that the car or bus or water bottle can walk by themself without anything, very weird
Very good for relax and some swimming (water in September was not too hot). If you had a time - visit a nice small island ahead, very recommended! :)

Very good exercise, the longest route takes about 6 hrs if you walk fast (as it says 8 hrs) but u need to go in the morning so that u should return before dark.Lot of locals doing this but don't forget to bring water n packed lunch!
Very dim, and  pools of waters on floor. Understand it is UNESCO site but it should be properly lighted up as least to what are showed in the photo which attracts us to come and visit.
Very beautiful waterfall. You have to go there The place is amazing. Not only the waterfall but also the nature, with the water and ducks and fish
Very beautiful beach with clear water & nice scenery. For me, this is one of best place to visit in Jeju.

Up & down of the mountain took us 9.5 hours including some short rest time during the hike. We started the hike around 9am (recommend to start early, we were late), and came down around 6:30pm. Our legs were like jelly legs after the hike, but is worth the hike. You can see nice view along the journey. Please do not forget to greet everyone you met with   anyeonghaseyo  , they are all very friendly people. Wear a pair of good hiking shoes, bring some snacks with you and also water. The stalls along the mountain are closed during our hike, luckily we have prepared enough snacks and water. The view at the peak is breathless. A lots of old korean aunties and uncles also managed to reach the peak, so I guess we all younger than them have no excuses of not fit to hike, right? haha...Wear sport attire, although some said it will be freezing cold at the peak (about 1950 meters height), but believe me, you wont feel cold as you have already all sweat during the hike. We spent about 30mins to 1 hour at the peak taking photos, resting and having our snacks before going down again. A pair of good hiking shoes is important so that you won't get blister on your feet. We will go back again in different season if we have the chance. We were travelling there in Oct 2018.
Unique setting near the sea-shore. The water flow was good, take tangerine from market outside the falls and enjoy water sprinkling out of the falls.

Unfortunately it was raining when we got to the beach, but it didn't take away from the beauty of this beach. The sand is white and the water is beautiful clear blue. There's a restaurant on the beach and a caffe right near. I want to go back with nice weather!

Understand there are three courses here - 30 mins, 60 and 90. Basically it?s a very light forest with pine and a few other trees that I am not familiar with. You choose the course and just take your time to walk - the air is fresh, nobody speaks loudly. The path will meander through trees, laughing statues, water fountain, and more trees. Would definitely recommend coming this place for those who want to calm their nerves and leave the city behind. We took the 30 mins course and came out refreshed.

Udo or ?Cow Island? lies off the UNESCO World Heritage island of Jeju and is so named because its profile resembles a sleeping or resting ox. The fun begins with a 15 minute ferry ride from Seongsan Harbour, costing ??5,500 return trip. As the boat glides over the choppy waters, you can watch on deck the antics of Korean school students on excursion feeding the seagulls in mid-flight, with lots of shrieks and screams. Upon arrival at Cheonjin Port, shuttle buses will be waiting to take you around the island for a round (hop-on hop-off) trip ticket which you pay after the first stop. It?s a pity we could not understand the Korean commentary provided by the bus driver, as he had his captive audience in stitches along the journey. We enjoyed the rustic scenes of thatched farm houses and fields, surrounded by the azure blue seas. We made stops at Geommeolle Beach (black sands and cliff backdrop) and Seobin Baeksa Beach (white grains of rhodolith). The half day excursion to Udo was a joyful and unruffled experience!

Udo isn't for everyone and I actually wish that a lot fewer people would visit because the island can get crowded with tourists in cars or on ATVs and scooters. I have lived in Korea 2.5 years and travelled extensively during my time here. I will be going back for my 4th visit next week, each visit for no less than 2 nights. The snorkelling is great especially in places that most Koreans deem   too dangerous   simply because the water is deep. There is one of the best raw fish restaurants in Korea on this little island. The sea surrounds you and the sights are lovely in every direction. There really isn't a lot to do on the island which is exactly why I love it. Sea. Seafood. Sights. It is all amazing.

Udo Island, a small volcanic island 10 minutes by ferry from Jeju Island. A day out on this island can be a bore to those who have no affinity to the outdoors, particularly that of the sea.But if you love the care-free life of roaming from one sandy beach to another rocky one. In between with lots of coastal features to be awed by, then this is the little paradise on earth.Udo is an island which allows you to go the entire distance around the coastal roads, in under 4 hours, including stops for pictures, strolls, ice-cream, desserts and of course a whole host of meals.  There are rugged, rocky coastlines and little stretches of sandy beaches with emerald waters.Getting from point to point on the island is very easy, either on bicycles, rental motorbikes and scooters. Mainlainders can ferry in their car for their own pleasure. We rented a motor-scooter for 25, 000 Won for just over 4 hours. The rental is for 2 hours (Won 25000)

Udo is simply beautiful. You should rent either a bike or a moped once you arrive. You can easily circle the whole island with stops in a couple hours. The enclosed beaches, volcanic rocks, crystal clear water, and very green landscape is exquisite.The road is not really crowded even during the busy summer months. I really enjoyed Udo Island, but then again what major natural location in Jeju-do disappoints? Whether you visit the lava tube caves, craters, dramatic coastline, waterfalls, nearby islands, beaches, mountains, and forests, Jeju-do is a natural paradise.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

Udo is a beautiful island but I would recommend a day trip as Jeju island has a lot more to offer. My friends and I climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong in the morning and then hopped on a boat to Udo, the port is very close and boats go regularly. If you have a car I would recommend leaving it behind as the queue for cars was extremely long. Once we got there we boarded one of the shuttle buses, while they're restricted in where they go it only costs 1,000 won for a single trip, versus renting an electric car that cost about 40,000 but only last 2 hours. The beach we went was not nice, the water was dirty and full of rubbish but the locals didn't seem to mind.Overall it's a nice island but the beaches on Jeju are a lot nicer and cleaner, a day trip is all I would recommend.

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.
Tried with car, stroller, water bottle in the rainNothing workedDrive all the way to this road in the rain for nothingStarted trying it at the   start here   sign
Traveler should wear a suitable clothes & shoes for hiking here. Bring also the drinking water. When you reach at the peak of this mountain, take a seat & enjoy the view from the top.

Transportation to the island: rent a car to drive there, or get 4 people to share a cab (costs around 50,000 won from jeju city). There's also the bus option but I wouldn't recommend as its not the easiest to navigate around the ferry pier. Then take the ferry which leaves every one hour, costs around 5500 won. The ferry is a short ride, only ten mins away! Transportation within the island: the shuttle bus costs only 5000 won, pretty convenient, and it'll take you to the main 4 spots. There's also option of ATV and car rental, which id recommend ATV since its mostly single-lane roads on the island. Food: everyone wanna try the peanut flavored ice cream but I found it's extremely mediocre. It's not 'peanut flavored' but just normal ice cream with peanut powder sprinkled. Save your stomach for the seafood pot! Although not the cheapest I've had, but still pretty worth a try! Get the option with octopus cook on the table if you can stomach the scene (I know lots of my friends can't). A lot of light walking you can do around the island, the weather was still quite cold so we couldn't get into the water. I love that you can go hill climbing at one spot and the dip your toes into the (chilly) ocean the next.

Took the Seonpanak trail, one of the 2 only trails that will lead to the summit. It is a longer route compared to the other but was supposely less challenging. Well, still a very tough hike to me. Much of the path and climbs are big rocks so good hiking shoes and walking stick will be very helpful. No water along the way though one sign mentioned there is one, which was WRONG and not updated. My son believed in that signboard and finsihed his water way before half into the hike. Big mistake!Not much to see along the way, except if you take a detour to view sara oreum. Took about 3.5hrs to reach Jindalrae office/ shelter (which is 1500m high) and after much thought, decided to turn back due to lack of drinking water.Descending is much tougher for me and took longer time. Deers and boars were spotted.Do go early so that you do not have to park too far from the park entrance as the carpark gets filled up fast and you will need to park along the roadside. Go during weekdays if possible to avoid the crowds.Take note there is time limit to reach Jindalrae so that you can continue to the summit.

Took eight to nine hours to complete the hike via the gentler route. View at the top is really amazing you'll get to see a beautiful crater lake which sadly we're not allowed to go further down to. Terrain is mad crazy so make sure you're in good footwear made for hiking. Bring plenty of foot, water and a deep heat in case your aches/injuries act up (which most likely will). Be prepared as this hike will definitely take a toll on your legs which will hurt for days after the hike. Update boards can be seen along the way, the terrain is labelled and broken down into easy, normal and difficult segment. BUT, DO NOT BE FOOLED! The normal terrain is just as tough as the difficult terrain. Big boulder of rocks which are freakinggggg steeeeep! Trekking poles will definitely come in useful! If you intend to hike here, be prepared for an arduous journey, smelly puke-inducing restrooms at the two pitstops all in return for a spectacular view at the peak. A really good once in a lifetime experience, no regrets but I will defo not do it again. hahaha

Took bus 781 from City Hall in Jeju City about 30-40min bus ride for 1300KRW. Had some breakfast at the Seongpanak bus station (base camp), got a bottle of water and a snickers then started the hike. Read that it would take 8-9 hours roundtrip, got to the top in less than 3, a very slow and steady rising hike firstly through the forest and later up the mountain. Stunning views from about 1800m and up, saw some water also in the crater, quite crowded at the summit. Ate my chocolate bar, took a selfie and started walking down. Total time return trip to the bus station was 6 hours. Best tip is to not pause at the middle camp which you must reach before 12:00 if you want to get to the peak, but instead just walk on to the top and have some lunch or break up there, you will then skip most of the crowd, try to head back down before 13:00, as you need to leave the peak before 13:30 it does get crowded on the descent and will just increase your time spent by waiting for slow groups.The views are spectacular, do recommend, no fees.

Took around 6 hours up and 4-5hours down the volcano. Really pretty with all the snow around, but on the way down snow started to melt and the ground is slightly muddy. traveled there in the winter period from December to January. You should go and reserve an entire day for this winter hike!If you choose not to climb to the peak, at around half way mark there is a crater which is around 3 hours up and another 3 hours down. The crater is filled with water but is frozen in winter. But i would recommend heading to the peak for the best views! There is a rest station at 2/3 hours mark with toliets and 2nd rest station at the 4/5hours mark near to summit. The 2nd rest station has a small shop that sells coffee, instant noodles, gloves, small tidbits. But best if you bring along some gimbap along to fill your stomach.

Took a 15min ferry to Udo and a tour bus that you could get on and off from at the sights, visited the Udo Peak, The black sand beach where we ate fresh abalone and the pristine coral sand beach...extremely clear water and so beautiful!!

Too fascinating when seeing all the traits of massive lava flow in the cave, which is actually part of the lava tube. Must bring along a powerful torch if you want to enjoy from the ceiling to the ground. Relying just on the phone torch or the lights inside will hinder your enjoyment and appreciation of this natural masterpiece as you will be only focusing on your steps. Do walk the entire 1 km so you can see the big massive lava lumps which stretches from the ground to the ceiling. Water drippings and water patches are common, wear a cap and windbreaker will help. In fact the temperature inside is a few degrees lower than the outside

Too bad we went in fall, I would have so wanted to go in those beautiful turquoise waters. But we sat in front of the beach and didnt realize how much time had passed by. The colours are impressive. My favorite beach in Jeju.

Today me and other guest are very lucky that the hostel owners very kind and friendly gave us a ride back to hostel, on the way back, he just de route to show us this place which near to love land, it's just a very short distance which the road seems like is going up slop, but, when the car put on free gear at the starting point, the car is actually keep moving on downhill. Visitors having fun by placing drinking water bottles on the road and let the bottle roll on its own. Personally, nothing very special, its just kind of illusions optic.

To reach the waterfall from the parking area (free parking), you need to go down the stairs (not a lot of steps, but in my opinion, the steps could be quite steep). During my visit, there were a lot of school / college students, so the waterfall area were quite crowded. The view itself is actually quite spectacular, but as there were too many people that time, we decided to stay for around 15 minutes only.

To make sure hikers are able to return to base before sundown, you have to enter the trail no later than noon and must reach the final section of the approach by 12:30.  Gwaneumsa trail was about 8.7 km long taking about five hours at a leisurely pace.  Most of the hike was in a shaded area which would make it comfortable even during summer.   The first 3 kilometers were just a stroll with nicely laid out boardwalks for some stretches.  There are railings parallel to the trails in case an injured person needs to be transported from higher elevation, which made it extra reassuring for me.  Although steep, it was still a relatively easy hike and I made it through the last section without much problems.  From about 1600 m above and onwards, the trails were covered in ice and snow which slowed me down a bit as I didn?t even think about carrying crampons in late March.  As I got a late start the summit area was a little crowded with hikers having lunch or taking breaks.  Luckily, the Baekrokdam peak is a crater and there was a relatively wide area for people to sit around at the summit.  Unlike the Baekdusan Cheonji Lake, Baekrokdam is devoid of any water except a small patch of water that looks like a small puddle from the top.  While not particularly scenic, it is nice to stand at the highest point in the country.  Because of the strong winds, I didn?t stay long and started to head down the less steep Seongpanak Trail which was about 9.7 km to the parking lot.  Few kilometers from the summit was easy with boardwalk paths and steps.  There was a three kilometer stretch of snow covered trails that made the descent quite stressful though.  Once the snow covered area was cleared, it was a long but relatively flat walk rest of the way which my knees were thankful for.  The entire round trip took about nine hours total without much rest.  Having crampons would have shaved at least an hour off of that time.

To get the best view you have to walk down steps to water level, then across a   flattened   stone area to a tent where a local vendor sells things.  Go just past the tent for the best view.  Best on a clear day with blue sky and water in the background.  Plan 30 minutes max.

To be honest, I didn't expect anything from this waterfall, but once we got there, it was pretty nice. It wasn't big like the one in U.S (Niagara fall), but this is only waterfall I know that flows right to the ocean! We paid about $2 to see the waterfall. We took some pictures and left there within 30 mins. Was this worth to see? It's a toss up but I'd say yes.

TLDR:Long hike, not that easy if you're not fit. 8-9 hours, 19.6km in total.Bring at least 3L of water each. They do sell water at the checkpoint, though only in 600ml bottles.Wear shoes with good sole and ankle protectionConsider taking a small towel (or two) to wipe away sweatBring a warm jumper and possibly a clean, dry shirt. Even in summer it's cold at the topStart the hike before 8.30am if you want to reach the peak because if you don't make it past the checkpoint at around 7km in, before 12.30pm, you won't be allowed to go to the peak.Bring a plastic bag for your rubbish because there are no bins at all on the hikeFor those who want moreRemember that this hike is longer than an average work day and you will need to replace water lost through sweat. Pack around 3L of water per person. Also pack some protein and carbohydrate heavy snacks such as nuts and dried fruits to keep up your energy levels. If you sweat a lot, consider bringing an electrolyte drink sachet to use halfway (or buy a can of Pocari sweat at the checkpoint). At the checkpoint, you can buy instant noodles, 600mL water bottles and Pocari sweat. If you don't want noodles for lunch, bring lunch. But keep in mind it's cold at the top so some warm noodles can be perfect. The noodles are a bit spicy though, so if you don't like spicy food, maybe bring your own lunch. There are absolutely 0 facilities for heating or preparing food. They won't even give you hot water for any noodles you don't purchase from them. Also there are no rubbish bins on the entire hike so you'll need to bring a plastic bag to carry out your own rubbish. The toilets are pretty gross and may or may not have toilet paper so consider bringing tissues. Also the toilets generally have no sinks, so bring some hand sanitiser gel.A small towel or two to wipe away your sweat wouldn't go astray, and a warm coat/jacket and clean, dry shirt will make your time at the peak much more comfortable (addressed in a later section).We took the 781 bus from Jeju city hall at around 6.55am. We arrived at the Seongpanak stop around 7.25am.Make sure you give yourself enough time to get to the Jindallae Shelter (checkpoint around 7km into the hike) before 12.30pm. If you don't make it to the shelter before 12.30pm you will not be allowed to continue up to the peak. It's very disappointing, I'm sure, to hike for 7km, hoping to see the peak and then be told you can't go because you missed the 12.30 deadline. I can't stress this enough. At the shelter, we heard some Americans complaining that they had missed the deadline by 24 minutes (they had started the hike at 10.30am) and that there was no information available on the trail or online about this rule. They were wrong on two counts- there are at least 5 signs along the trail up to the shelter stating that you need to pass by 12.30pm (in English). Also there are a number of blogs about this hike online which also talk about the rule. Now we started at around 7.30am and made it to the shelter by 10am, but we didn't stop to rest at all before the shelter. The walk up to the shelter is 90% easy level with gentle slopes and a few short harsher sections. If you are fit enough to contemplate doing a 19.4km hike then this section should be fine for you. If you start the hike around 8.30am, you will have no issues making it to the checkpoint in time and you should make it back to the bottom by 6/6.30pm. Earlier if you don't rest too long and are relatively fit.Note: there are several places that you can stop to rest just after the shelter. If you are running close to the 12.30pm deadline, just get past the shelter and then stop to rest once you've gone past. Just make sure you don't rest too long because you've probably got another 5-6 hours before you get back to the end of the trail including the rest of the walk to the peak, and you don't want it to get dark or have to rush on the way down.The next section after the shelter is graded as 'normal' by the signs along the route. This section does have a few challenging sections but also some easier stretches as well. If you have regular short rests then it's manageable for people of minimal to moderate fitness with some huffing and puffing.The last 1-1.5km of the walk to the peak is where it starts to get difficult. By this stage you've already hiked uphill around 8km and for probably 3-3.5 hours. The way to the peak is hundreds and hundreds of stairs often with many oddly shaped rocks to navigate around whilst traversing increasingly steep steps. If you're not super fit then you will struggle on this section. At one point we were setting ourselves goals to make it up 3 sets of staircases before we would rest for 1 minute then start again. But the important point is you are so close to the top now, so just keep pushing.The top can be quite crowded. We made it by around 11.30am and hung around for about 30mins to take photos and admire the view. My next piece of advice is- bring a warm jumper because the wind is cold up there and if you're anything like me, you will be sweaty which makes the wind even colder. Another point: if you're a sweaty person, consider bringing an extra dry/warm shirt (or two) with you to change into at the top (and possibly on the way back down). If you're prone to sweat a lot, this can make a huge difference to your enjoyment at the peak because you will by dry and warm. Your photos won't look so sweaty either. Make sure you take a picture of all members of your party with the peak stone marker or the crater to prove that you reached the top.Keep in mind that the way back down can take longer than the way up because you are now passing many people on their way up and going down is very hard on your already exhausted legs and feet. It can take 4-5 hours to get back down from the peak. We started going down at 12pm and made it to the bottom by 4pm, but we stopped several times.The path is quite narrow so on your way down, you will have to stop to let people pass in the other direction many times (unless it's significantly past the 12.30pm deadline, in which case everyone will be going down). The section between the peak and the checkpoint is very hard on your feet and legs. It will feel like forever but just remember that the track gets gradually easier and gentler the closer you are to the end. Stop at the checkpoint for lunch if you haven't already had it, or you feel like some hot noodles to warm you up.Keep on all the way down, being very careful not to slip. There are many rocks and if they are slightly wet, they are very slippery. Eventually you'll make it to the bottom. Then you can take your photographic evidence of reaching the peak to the little tourist office and for 1000 won each, you'll get a certificate saying that you reached the 1950m summit of Mt Hallasan. Congratulations!Sore feet and legs and weary bodies, you can catch the 782 bus back to Jeju city for a well earned rest.

Tips & things to take note:- Bring LOTS of water. On average 2litres per pax.- Bring sufficient food - basically breakfast,lunch,dinner.- Got to reach the checkpoint by 1pm to be allowed to attempt summit- Got to start descent from summit by 2.30pm- Gets cold and windy at the peak so bring a windbreaker.- You have to carry your own trash down. No bins on the mountain at all.We took 11hours and took the Seongpanak trail up and Gwaneumsa trail down. Seongpanak is easiest as its gentler but its the longest trail. Gwaneumsa is much more scenic. We were beginner hikers and hence probably took longer. The tourist  centre told us it would take ~9hrs. Spotted a deer on our way down on the Gwaneumsa trail. It was pretty scary though, we walked for 1hr+ without spotting a single human. (probably cause we were slow)My legs ached for 4 days straight but I have no regrets. My knees and ankles were insanely sore by the end of the hike. If you've even the slightest knee/leg issues, please think THRICE before you attempt Hallasan.Also, toilets are only available at the bottom (before the hike) and at the checkpoint. The toilets are GROSS. I couldn't do it no matter how hard I tried. Toilet was damp and stinky and lots of flies. No water system & its a squat system for ladies. Basically peeing into a hole filled with other people's waste. Saw another lady peeing in the woods instead...Also, all the announcements are in Korean, though signboards are in English.Aim to start hiking by 7am-8am. Any later, you may not reach checkpoint/summit in time unless you have a good enough stamina.Hiking sticks and shoes would help tremedously. Though we did it with regular sneakers. LOTS OF BUGS. Bring insect repellent though again, we didn't have one.Overall, its worth it and wouldn't do it again but have no regrets.

Though it just rain yesterday, but the waterfall seems to be so small and the water current also very little. Many says that it falls directly to the sea, but it is not true. it falls into a small pond where the water overflow(or may be connected under) into the sea. It is below my expectation.

This works better for coaches, small cars might not see the   magic   so obvious. We tried using water bottles and it worked. Quite fun and it's really amazing. But it only takes 10 mins to view this attraction, nothing much.

This waterfall was my favorite thing I saw on Jeju Island.  It is a beautiful waterfall that empties into a small pool draining directly into the ocean, and it's a lovely spot to just enjoy the sounds of the water and the tide.  Very much worth the visit.

This waterfall lies in the southern part of the island, specifically in Seogwipo. Pay an entry fee of 2000 KRW and you can experience it up close for some photo-opportunity but just remember to wear a good air of shoes and be very careful when walking around or climbing over large rocks for a closer feel of the cool breeze. It's worth the trip.
This waterfall is so beautiful. Showing your ID/ passport and if you are below 24, you can get discounted price.

This waterfall is not very big as compare to other but the view is breath-taking as the water falls into the edge of the cliff at the sea front. One can feel the mist of the water fall spraying onto the face as one walk closer to the cliff of the water fall. However, be very careful while walking on the rock towards the waterfall as the rock gets more slippery as one get nearer to the waterfall. But it is definitely worth the risk and the slow walk as the pictures that comes out from the shot is gorgeous!

This waterfall is easily accessible in south Jeju Island with spacious parking lot at entrance.  Entrance fee is 2000 won, reasonable and worth a visit.  We arrived around 4:50pm and was just in time to watch the sun set there.  If you want to get closer to the waterfall, be prepared to get a slightly wet but it?s a great experience.

This waterfall is beautiful and worth visiting. The only drawback is the slightly treacherous rocks to get to the water, but our boys thought it was a real adventure. A very reasonable fee of 2,000 Won which clearly helps maintain the area, which had nice toilets. Very clean. I wish I could have enjoyed the fresh sashimi from the free divers, but the boys got restless! Worth a visit for some gorgeous views and photo opportunities!
This waterfall is amazing, but be careful, it's almost dry in summer!! Only negative point: we need to pay to access to it.

This waterfall falls into the ocean so it?s higher than the Cheon ji Yeong falls. The steps are steep, easy going down, harder to get up. Not recommended for people with limited mobility. No wheelchair or stroller friendly.

This waterfall apparently is the only waterfall in Asia to cascade into the sea.You can get up close to the waterfall, unlike Cheongjeyeong and Cheongjiyeon. Do remove your footwear and have a dip in the cooling water. I personally preferred this waterfall out of the few that we visited.

this was the tallest waterfalls i visited ever. multiple waterfalls nearby, nice pictures to take there, a lot of shops. there's as well a small waterfall nearby that you can take a lot of nice pictures there on the bridge & down in the waterfall itself. Overall it was fantastic

This was the same village that Dae Jang Geum (鸚㏝룝) was filmed. It looked like a huge place in the show but in actual fact is that this place is really tiny! It should not take anyone more than 10 mins to complete. We were shown how water was collected from the rain by wrapping a rope on the tree that links into the water pots. The tourguide said that in those days, women in Jeju island work while the men stay at home. The lady touring us in the area carried the water trout to show us how Jeju women in the past used to carry water. There is one small house that according to the lady, is still inhabited. We were not allowed to enter but we can take pictures from outside the house. The house smells of the aroma of freshly cooked rice. We were told that someone is actually cooking. After touring the small compound comes the main part of the program - promoting honey. It seems like there are many version of how real honey should be. For this version, the honey doesn't melt in water. One can see the hives when it's placed in water and swirled around. We were given different honey to try: Pure honey, lingzhi and 5 flavors. For some reasons, they also sell handcream made of horse oil. It smells quite nice though. But I still have a whole box of lanolin cream at home so decided not to buy. They are not cheap either.

This was the only waterfall we visited in Jeju and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Unlike the others (according to what I read online), you can walk right up to the waterfall itself, although you'll need to brave the rocks to do it. Loved sitting here right by the edge of the water and just letting the spray wash all over me.

This was the last stop on our vacation. Unfortunately it was also the only grey/cloudy/cold day. The island was still a must see for us. The ferry ticketing area can be very confusing, so be prepared if you don't know any Korean. We figured it out after about 5 minutes of standing around, staring in confusion. Once we reached the island, we rented an electric car (from Gulliver's Travels) with side-by-side seating for 占35,000 for 2.5 hours and cruised around the island following the path. The beaches were incredible. White sand, crystal clear water at the shore, turning into turquoise water a little farther out. Even with the grey sky, it still looked amazing. We didn't climb out to the lighthouse (if you climb to the top of Hallasan on your visit, you'll understand why. Ow.) but we got some great photos of it. Peanut ice cream is way overrated in my opinion, but it was still a must since we were on Udo! My husband got the hallabong ice cream. We liked that one more, but the stuff they put on it tastes like mashed up hallabong peel, so it was bitter and we just scraped it off. There is a restaurant that serves (I forget the name, I am guessing) Hallasan fried rice. They make it look like a volcano! We really wanted to go, but needed to catch the ferry back. Overall, if it had been warmer and the we could actually see the sun, it would have been much more enjoyable. We talk about going back and spending a night on the island so we have the time to walk around it, instead of having to drive/rent a bike.

This was rated as one of the top 3 to visit in Jeju so we actually stayed at the nearby Airstay Hamdeok Hotel.  It  was very nice.  The beach is clean and had pristine waters and black rocks.  The sand was fine and felt good to walk on with your bare feet.  There were some really nice picturesque views so we took a ton of photos. There was a connected path to a hill and it allowed for some decent small hikes.  We went in March so the flowers on the hill were blooming with yellow and purple colors.  There were also some white flower blossoms coming out from the trees. With the ocean or the city views in the background from the hill, it allowed for some very unique photos for your memories.  After the little hike, we played around in the water on the beach and it was nice because it was low tide and you could hang out in one of the exposed sand bars. It was very pretty and relaxing. Definitely a must see if you're in Jeju!

This was part of a day tour. After climbing a mountain and being someone who doesn't exercise, this place was too much for me. Like mentioned in other reviews, this place is dark, the path is naturally uneven with puddles of water from rain and natural water. I came out earlier to enjoy some hot ramen at the convenience stall and didn't regret it.

This was one of my favorite parts of Jeju. We went during the sunrise which reading everywhere said was most ideal, and it was gorgeous. It?s a lot of steps to get to the top. I would suggest bringing a bottle of water.

This was my 3rd waterfall visit in Jeju and my favourite, probably because the waterfall goes directly to the sea. Also, we saw some haenyeo (female divers) there and they were selling fresh sashmi seafood on the rocks next to the sea. It was definitely a very unique eating experience!

This was an exciting attraction. It takes about 1 hour to get to the end of the tube and back. The closer you get to the end the colder it gets. Also pe prepared to get a little wet, as there are drops of water falling from the top. You wont need an umbrella or anything like that. Getting here is tricky. As I was waiting for the bus to get here (990) I found a taxi and got him to take me for $4,000 won. This saved me a lot of time. It might have been too much but it saved me time, since the bus comes by every 45 minutes or so. There are restaurants at the entrance, they over charge for water so make sure you are prepared if you like to drink water. Definitely an amazing experience and a must do in the area.

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.  FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

This was a nice walk up to the top. There's a lot of stairs, but it's not nearly as bad as I thought it was going to be. We went in Oct on a fairly sunny day (temp was probably in low-mid 20's) and you definitely want some water and sunscreen with you. I'd recommend going when it's more cloudy, if you can. There are a couple little shops along the way to the top (the first few levels of stairs, not all the way along) where you can also purchase water, and there is some tasty Jeju orange ice cream for sale too. The views are pretty, as is the temple, and it wasn't too busy when we were there in the middle of the afternoon.
This was a nice place to visit with the waterfall flowing right next to the ocean. It's a very short hike down but it's worth it to see the nice waterfall. It cost 2,000 won to enter.

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!

This was a great beach and was easy to get to with a bus station right on the corner. Entrance was lined with a variety of vendors and there was a supermarket, well stocked in case you forgot something. There were many stores and restaurants nearby to quench your post-swim hunger. The beach was quite nice, water felt great and overall was pretty clean. The shower/bathroom area wasn't that good, but we didn't expect it to be.

This was a beautiful climb, but let me tell you, it's a climb. Granted we seemed to go on a particularly hot day at like 1:00 pm so that didn't help.I recommend taking water with you, but if you don't feel like carrying it, there is a store about half way up that you can get water and snacks. There are also lots of souvenir stores and restaurants at the base to stock up on supplies before heading up. I also recommend sunscreen and bug spray.There was a short line to pay about $2.00 for an entry fee. You received a ticket stub with a pretty picture of the volcanic crater on it. The trail is one-way: meaning there is one trail that goes up to the peak and one that returns down. This cuts down on congestion and ensures a scenic route the entire way. There are lots of places to take pictures and rest along the way. The time it takes to complete the trail all depends on your fitness level, but it is advertised as a 50-minute round-trip experience. At the peak, there are numerous places to sit and relax. You can see a beautiful 360-degree view of Jeju and Udo. Other items of interest: Horseback riding is available here and you can see the famous female divers of Jeju.

This trail takes about 2 hours to get to the top, if you walk fast you could do it faster. It is uneventful and going to the top the first 70% you can only see trees. At the top there was too much fog/pollution so you could only see the crater, which had almost no water in it. There are stairs and wooden platforms so it is more like taking a simple stroll through the woods at a bit of an incline.

This top site in Jeju island is also known as Seongsan Sunrise Peak or 掠길ε뷴낡 It earns its reputation as Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site, and once you reached the top, you will see why. Be warned, it is a reasonable difficult climb that will easily take 20min to hike up. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water during hot weather. The uphill stairway will take you to a majestic dormant crater that offers spectacular view of the sunrise, hence the name. Be prepared for massive crowd of tourists throughout your climb, and get your vantage point to capture some of the majestic scenery throughout your climb.On your way down after enjoying the panoramic view of the UNESCO World Natural Heritage surrounding, make sure you allow enough energy to take the downhill path on the left to explore the Haenyo women diver performance at certain times. We were there after 3pm, so missed out on them unfortunately.

This three tier waterfall is one of the three waterfalls in Jeju, the other two being Cheonjiveon and Jeongbang waterfalls. The forest surrounding the waterfall has been designated as a natural monument and as per Korean legend seven nymphs bath at the pond of this waterfall in the night.Located at a walkable distance from Seogwipo Harbour, the visit to this attraction calls for climbing of stairs. So avoid this place if you hate to climb steps. For others a good pair of shoes is a must.

This site consists of a large network of staircases that you climb to see a crater as well as a beach where the woman divers do a demonstration.The walk up the stairs is very long. It is not impossible and there are many places to take breaks without holding up the line. The spot is very busy so there will be an unbroken line of people going up and down. I would suggest taking water with you. The view from the top is quite nice. Allow 1 hour to do the climb at a leisurely pace.At the beach the woman divers do demonstrations on a set schedule. Check the times when you arrive. They will suit up for the dive, sing a song and then go into the water looking for seafood. When we were there a lady came back with an octopus. It does not take long for them to find something so it is worth it to wait to see the catch.There are bathrooms and snack shops there as well.

This road is interesting! When we are about to reach the site, the driver turned off the engine, and yet the bus is moving upwards!! Amazing!We even went down the bus to try running backward on the road, and one can feel like you are being pulled from the back. Also, we try by pouring water onto the road itself, which is a good test.And yes, the food stall along the road is more interesting.

This review will be written from the point of view of a middle aged woman of average fitness, not someone for whom a 20 km trek is a walk in the park.Mount Hallasan is the highest peak in South Korea and if you are on Jeju island it's definitely worth visiting. We took the Seongpanak trail, a scenic , easy route which reaches the summit. Plan on one day for the trek up and down. Here are some tips:1. It goes like this - You take a bus or taxi to the Seongpanak trail, and start climbing. It's a mix of  some steps and an easy trail. After a while you reach the first stop - I forget the name - where you can use  the restroom. There's a small shelter where we had our packed sandwiches. After this, the trail becomes a little steeper, and you reach the next stage - the jindeballat rest stop.( Times by which you must reach the Jindeballat stop and when you must start your descent are posted on the trail). There are restrooms here - but inspie of information to the contrary , there was no food for sale. After this the climb becomes a little tricky , and you need around 2 hours to reach the summit . The views are amazing from the summit. The Koreans hiking the mountain were not only super fit, they were the sweetest people I've met. When I became tired near the summit, so many encouraged me with words like   Fighting!     Turn around and see how far you have come.  Tips :1. Wear good hiking shoes - at points , the trail is slippery, and good shoes with ankle support are helpful.2. Carry a stick. You can get your own hiking stick or buy one from the store at the bottom.3. Carry plenty of water and snacks.4. Take a selfie at the summit and you can get a certificate at the bottom stating you have completed the climb ( costs 1000 won)5. You do need a certain degree of cardiovascular fitness to make the climb comfortably. But apart from that, the uneven  rocks and boulders are a little tough to climb, so make sure you do some core and lower body exercises too. 6. If you climb down slowly, it gets a little dark by the time you reach the base. Carry a head lamp.

This post is about logistics and what to expect from the hike. My partner and I hit Hallasan around 6:45 in the morning on a Saturday to avoid the crowds. We drove to Seongpanak parking lot (free and was filling up quickly. A tour bus with dozens of hikers was already there) which was about a 30-minute drive from Seogwipo. From there we took a $15.00 taxi ride to the Gwaneumsa parking lot. As this was not a loop trail, we wanted to take the steeper/harder route in and have gentler descent (easier on our knees) back to our car. Turns out, doing it this way we avoided what felt like hundreds of people ascending when we were heading back later in the day. The Gwaneumsa parking lot has a fee. (Sorry TA fans, I didn't get the amount since we took a cab --- I am sure it is nominal, like all fees in RoK:) People are allowed to camp at the Gwaneumsa section of the park and I saw a few people starting their day as we marched to the trailhead. We were under tree cover and walked along a dry river bed for the first couple of miles. At this time of day, we only ran into seven other hikers on this trail. After you cross the river via bridge, the hike starts to get a little steeper. About two hours in, you hit a large, modern shelter and toilets. Good time to take a break and snack. Or keep carrying-on as you will get a chance to sit, eat and gaze at another resting place. After the shelter, you will cross a much larger, newer suspension bridge. Fresh water available here. The climb will get a bit harder for next half quarter mile. Continue past the foundation of the destroyed shelter. After you ascend the 18-22 inch tall stone steps, you will reach a ridge which is the other good stop.  No shelters (in fall you should opt for the shelter), but a nice wooden platform from which to gaze at how far you've come. Crows will land in search of scraps. At this point you are very near the top, only a couple more hundred feet to go.The crater was dry when we visited (first weekend in October), but still a wondrous site. The seasoned, local hikers brought burners and ramen and were happily chowing down near the crater. Darn! That would have been nice. The  t-shirt, fleece jacket and windbreaker I was wearing barely sustained me, so the hot ramen sounded freakin' great.The hike down Seongpanak was not nearly as enjoyable since we were bombarded by the late starters heading up. At one point, the hikers coming up were in a jam ? seriously, no one could move, there were so many people. There?s a large shelter a third of the way down. As another reviewer noted, be sure to wear supportive shoes with rigid shanks as you're constantly stepping on uneven rock.  I had on trail runners, which was fine going in, but heading down, my feet were pretty battered. The boardwalk was a nice breather when we could get it.*Seongpanak gentler ascent, (and descent) but be prepared to share the trail with dozens and dozens of other people.*Free parking at Seongpanak -- fills up quickly as early as 7am on weekends.*Toilets available on trail.*Take bimbimbap for a nutritious, affordable, and portable snack. Mandoo is another good one -- good balance of carbs and fat.*Listen and look Nuthatches, Wrens, Great T*ts, and other winter birds on the Gwaneumsa trail.*The park states you must hit the summit by noon. I think this is why so many people were rushing to hit the peak at the same time.

This places is one of the a must place to visit in jeju. i think its getting more popular after 1bak2il had recording here, so many tourist and their fans come here to visit. Admission 2000won, you also can try raw seafood while watching the waterfall. and you can feel the cold water sprinkle on your face.

This place was gorgeous! It is a Korean beach so it is crowded please keep that in mind. I am a Floridian and we have some of the best and most peaceful beaches on earth. But this, even for me, was truly an experience. One the amount of people was impressive but less crowded than Busan beach. Try to get here early and pay the money for the umbrella spot. They all cost the same, but you wanna be in the first row so you can see the water.The water is truly beautiful. The color is very different than floridan green blue waters. The ocean here is the deepest darkest blue I've ever seen, and the part that meets the beach is a light bright crystal blue. There are many families and watching the kids is really cute. We spent a lot of time floating around. Next time I would bring a float so we could inner tube around like the locals did.You can order food and the vendors or restaurants will bring them to your umbrella.Fried chicken is a must for Koreans on the beach. We actually were super hungry before going (next time we will do it differently) so we went to Korean food chain Mom's Touch that serves amazing crispy fried chicken in bbq glaze with pickled radishes. So on the beach we got ice cream and fresh fruits.Warning for travelers: more of a cultural heads up. There are showers- like beaches in America have...you do have to pay to use them, but there are no private changing rooms or showers it's all a show for anyone to see. Now it is gender separated, but don't be shocked to find you'll have to strip down in front of strangers. My husband is Korean and didn't warn me, but it was too late once I walked in, plus he already paid for my shower and I really needed a shower. But here's the thing you'll notice that no one cares about you, and no one looks at anyone. Just shower off, do your thing and you'll be outta there in no time. If this is too much for you to handle...then skip the shower and head back to your place to shower in your comfort level.

This place was crazy crowded but it was a Sunday. Still, there was much to see. Unfortunately, the Haenyo weren't doing any demonstrations (I think the water was too rough or something). My wife and I hiked up to the 'peak' and got a nice view  both of Jeju, Udo, and also the crater. Pretty cool! The hike was a bit strenuous and it was a little warm that day, so make sure to pack enough water. There were quite a lot of people around too so mind the crowd. Either way, it's worth the visit but probably best to go mid-week if possible. There are numerous great views to appreciate both on the way up and the way down. The path down takes a slightly different route too, which is nice.

This place toally blew me away with the beautiful rock erosions.  I never expected that this would be the highlight of my trip to Jeju.  I could see the clarity of the blue green water up close.  Assured that the seawater was so clean without any fishy smell, we even ventured to sample the live seashells.  What an unforgettable experience we had, dining on the rocks with the gentle waves lapping in front of us.

This place seems to be a lowkey secret place for the local. I went there early autumn so? maybe that's why it's so surreal and empty and looks like I had the whole   pools   for myself. Water's still not cold yet and don't forget to bring mask to see so many tiny fishes down under. Mother-nature created 3-4   pools   and amazingly, it happened to be different depth levels too so to make sure it safe, you can let your kids swim in the most shallow one, just be careful of the sharp rocks (hey it's all natural). Great view with the ocean and beautiful color on a sunny day!
