This place of interest is beside the beach and not far from the airport. It is a volcanic stone due to many years under the sun, water and wind which erode the stone and form this dragon head. It is also up to individuals to creatively imagine the head.There are also many tales about this dragon head - one about the Dragon king is sick and young son went up the high mountain to seek the eternal medicine for the father. After getting the medicine, he was discovered by the protection god who was angry of his act and use lighting to strike him resulting in this burnt head.

This place is really so pretty and peaceful! The assortment of various trees and flowers was so nice, especially in the fall as you could see all the different citrus fruits almost fully ripe. The waterfalls were so nice too and the big coi carps could be the sole reason for the visit!  A bit smaller than I expected but still worth it :)

This place is only about 8 km from Jeju downtown.  Worth a quick visit to see for yourself the   supposedly   optical illusion where things (water, cars, etc) seem to roll uphill, instead of downhill....

This place is new of 7 wonders by UNESCO. There are a lot of place for you to take a beautiful pictures with the view mountain, ocean and city. They call this place s sunrise peak, you can check the schedule of sunrise in the stones in the front gate. You can buy a ticket around KRW 2,000 to enter. Then you can climb the mountain with hundreds of stairs (I didn't count it). Prepare yourself before climbing, better take a bottle of water. There are a view rest area while you climb the stairs. At the top you can see the very beautiful landscape. It's worth dude!

This place is known for its so called gravity. A lot of tourists will visit this place when they are at Korea. My tour guide demo to us by putting a water bottle down the slope, instead of going down, it goes the opposite direction . Very interesting.

This place is just WOW. The views, the nature, the sea, everything. Even when it is a bit rainy or foggy, it is still a great experience. They do not let you in with any sort of snacks or food other than water, just so you know. You must try the raw seafood that the   mermaids   catch every morning. It is located at the bottom near the entrance. That is, if you like raw seafood. There is plenty of parking and there is even a Starbucks near by and other restaurants.

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.
This place is easily accessible. It offers a great view of the waterfall and it seems during the spring or summer season, you can even go into the waters for some refreshing moments.

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This place is a must visit when you are in Jeju. That said, expect lots of tourists. Do try to be early, before 10 am, or at odd hours like lunch time, when most tourists are somewhere else. The climb up was not too tough, my 2 boys made the climb up quite easily. The stairs up might be a little tough for older folks. Views are excellent,worth the climb. Do bring enough water and some light snacks for rest and recharge at the top. During the climb up, there are benches to sit and rest. The restaurants in surrounding area at the foot, served mainly seafood. Prices are a little high, we had an abalone porridge and grilled mackeral for 45,000 won. There is a Lotteria and a Starbucks just before the ticket office. If you are on a budget or not into seafood, do bring some sandwiches or kimbap, you will be hungry after the climb.
This park has 9 zones, botanic garden, caves , flower garden, water garden....We spent a present day out in the park.

This one is located near  Hyeopjae  Beach,  so you can see the Biyangdo island as well. i liked it. Its pretty spacious and got necessary facilities like combini nearby, toilet and place with free water. it also got nice view and some of typical jeju sculptures of  female divers and spirits that protect the Island. Sand is white and feels nice.

This museum, which focuses on the women divers of Jeju, is well designed and well laid out. It offers a fascinating look into the lives (past and present) of these divers, who spend up to 2 minutes underwater at a time without any breathing apparatus to catch abalone and other sea life. Our guide told us that the divers' current age range is 55 to 85. Younger women have no interest incontinuing this cultural tradition, which is an incredibly difficult way to earn a living and to help support a family.Nicely curated, the museum offers an excellent film about the divers and shows various aspects of their lives, including past and current swim wear. the tools that have been used, models of fishing villages and the Jeju traditional fishing boat. I thoroughly enjoyed this close look at a rare way of life that likely won't be around much longer.

This mountain (aka Sunrise Peak) is located to the eastern seaboard of the island and is not accessible easily if you are staying in one of the hotels in Jeju-ri (city area) in the north. You need to take public transport which can take you more than 1 hr (Blue intercity bus, flat rate 1200 W) or 50+ min by express bus (Red, flat rate 2000 W). It is advisable to put up overnight in one of the many hotels or guest houses in Seongsan itself so that you can wake up early and start your ascend to watch the sunrise.This will take about 25-40 min to climb up the well laid out steps if you do not stop along the way to take pictures. However it is advisable to stop along the numerous rest areas and take your own time to ascend. Certain parts can be quite steep so come with a good pair of canvas sneakers or hiking shoes, sunglasses, sun screen, bottles of water. The climb up is worth the effort as you will be rewarded with the fantastic views from the peak. Going down is much easier and you can stop at the foothill to watch the women divers putting up a demo at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. At the foothill is a public toilet and a McDonald and cafe apart from stalls selling souvenirs and cold drinks.
This landmark is very well maintained with beautiful structures. Very instagram friendly. Location is also pretty near many places like teddy bear museum, several waterfalls and casino resorts.

This is, so far, the best waterfall I have ever been. You need to go down from a lot of big rocks to go near the falls. That is what makes it exciting. Wear comfortable shoes and I recommend to wear pants.

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking.  There are different areas to see at this park including 3 long lava caves, an area with bonsai (my favouite), an area of flowers, a water area, a stone area, old JeJu houses and my least favourite...caged birds some in dubious conditions! I took lots of photos.  Plenty of places to get snacks and drinks but chicken a la flies is not my cup of tea!  A nice place to take a picnic.  There are lots of buses there but they all follow a route...if you go left you have a reasonable amount of quiet time from the hoards of yellow hat people and all the selfie photographer's.

This is unlike most Korean beaches because most Koreans go to the beach right up the road. Lots of space to play and relax in the sand and in the water. Beautiful sunset. Emerald water. And white sand. Shallow water is great for kids. No parasols (umbrellas), and no commercial building stores  - nice! Doesn't feel like a Korea beach at all. Tip: Park on the right near the camping area. That's where you will find a nice quiet sandy spot next to natural sand dunes. Wow!
This is to me the nicest waterfall in Jeju, having visited four in total as you can get close to it and see the waterfall right into the sea...Not grand but nice...

This is the type of waterfall which discharges directly into the sea so coming here you will get two views - the waterfall and the sea. However the trick is in how near you want to get to it - first you got to navigate the deep steps, then the rocky and slippery ground to get as close to the waterfall as they allow you.  So it is very important to come with proper footwear. Then it?s a matter of how many shots you want to take. There is also a corner where some hawkers are selling fresh seafood. Not sure if it?s sashimi as we aren?t hungry.

This is the thing you should visit when you are in jejuto go up and down it takes 1h, not too difficult but good enough to make you tired!the view is amazing at the top, bring your own water cose it can be really there is a beach on the righ side at the bottom when you go down, some grand ma are selling fish down the beach, nobody are there

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is the only waterwall that flows directly into the sea. To give another better reason to see this waterfall, you'll catch a rainbow where the water is falling, but only in clear sky mornings. It's beautiful sight to behold so it's a must see!

This is the only waterfall that falls into the sea and it's awesome. The steps down can be a bit slick when you get  near the waterfall, but in the rainy season the waterfall is massive and a great view.

This is the only waterfall in Asia which falls directly into the ocean. Admission fee is 2000 won. You'll need to climb over quite a number of rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. Be careful of the slippery rocks if you go after raining. In my opinion, Jeongbang Waterfall is worth to visit than any other waterfalls in Jeju.
this is the nice beach evervi seen, all water us so clean.beside have lots of resturant , hotel.. mini shop
This is the most attractive place in jeju. The view from the peak was good but not breathtaking. Anyway, it is still better than the waterfalls which are just little falls.

This is the largest waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea, and one of the only ones that is not fenced up at the bottom. Usually, when you visit waterfalls, it's always staring at it from a distance, where a viewing platform has been built. This is different, you get to walk ALL THE WAY to below that waterfall, and if you are open to wading through knee deep water, go touch that waterfall.The spray of water is refreshing, and the scenery rocks. You'll feel one with nature.

this is the easiest waterfall among all in jeju in terms of access.we walked for about 15 minutes before reaching the waterfall.however,to reach the waters,u have to go through slippery rocks-definitely not for kids or elderly.wear comfortable walking shoes.however,the view from the upper part of the waterfall(before descending down the many stairs) was already breathtaking.there were also foodstalls selling snacks-we had the ice cream and the grilled squid.super delicious.do try it.oh and don't forget the orange juice (hallabong).the freshest i have ever tasted.good snack,superb juice to wash it down,beautiful scenery-i could not ask for more.do visit if you are in jeju.preferably early morning before the crowd.
This is the best waterfalls so far amoung them all, reason is because you can reach the bottom of the falls. There is no barricades or things blocking your way. And it flows directly to the sea
This is the best waterfall to visit as it's rare to see a waterfall that goes straight into the sea. After seeing this waterfall, you won't want to look at the other 2.

This is the best waterfall I've seen among the famous ones in Jeju (Jeongbang, Cheonjiyeon, Cheonjeyeon). It also requires more physical effort since you have to climb and go down several stairs. There are also a number of viewing decks: for me, the one near the pavilion is the best (less people there too). Highly recommended unless you hate stairs. Best to bring shoes with good grip though since the stairs can be slippery when wet.

This is the 1st attraction we visited when we arrived at Jeju. Its near our hotel in Seogwipo.We saw a group of tough ladies, the Haenyeo, scuttling over the rocky beach. They were hunting for seafood hidden between the rocks.The waterfall was nearby, beautiful with strong steady stream of water gushing into the sea as it had been raining a lot recently.A lot of people around the area as it was an easy to reach attraction with a short walk down the stairs...

This is super easy to do... From Jeju city go to Jeju Bus Terminal and the lady at the desk will tell you which bus to get. In this case, 740. This takes you to a ticket office and car park. From there you can get a taxi or walk 2.5km to the start of the trail. We walked and it took about half an hour (but it is all uphill). I would say there are about 3 sections to this walk:1. Through the forest - stream nearby and wildlife (I saw a deer). This is relatively flat until the end when you have to climb some stairs. 2. The hard part- walking along the ridge of the mountain going up the stairs. This is tough on the knees but there are loads of places to stop and absorb the view. 3. Along the top- relatively flat through a forest part and then open until you get to the rest stop. It is the easiest hike and does not go to the top of Hallasan, but it is beautiful and gave you stunning views of the top of Hallasan (which you would not get if you were actually on it). Make sure you bring water, snacks and hand wipes. The rest stop at the top sells only instant noodles and has no running water.

This is quite an interesting place to visit. Do remember it's a long lava tube cave.Take note:1) Stairs to the cave can be steep.2) The floor of the cave is in its natural form. It's wet, slippery, jagged and uneven. There are large puddles everywhere so watch where you step.3) When we went, there isn't really any special colorful lighting in it. It was quite dim. We used our cellphone as our flashlight in some of the darker and very uneven floor areas.4) It's cold so wear some warm clothing. There may be water dripping from the ceiling as well. Overall we enjoyed the lava cave.

This is quite a climb in places and in winter time will need crampons, but it will reward you with amazing views on a clear day and even in cloudy weather is really worth the trek. Choose your route by the least fit member of your group and remember to take food and especially water with you.There is a cut off point which you need to reach by 13:00 if you are going right to the top, so that means an early start.

This is probably one of my favourite beaches of all time. Do not be put up by busy pictures... The water is shallow, for about 200m or more out to sea so the area for children to play and people to swim or snorkel is huge. We set up towels on the short and put up our own umbrellas and it really didn't feel crowded at all. There are loads of shops and restaurants around, as well as loads of places to rent rubber rings etc. I also saw lots of water sports happening outside of the safe swim zone. Truly a great day or so out!! And sunset is beautiful too.

This is one of the most beautiful beaches in Jeju island. The sea was so amazing, water so clear and having light ocean blue color. from here you could see the Biyangdo island, very close. However, it was rather cold and windy for us, so we could not swim just wandering around. we spent around 2hrs here. we got here by intercity bus no. 702 (about 1 hr) from jeju bus terminal.

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.
This is my second times visit, the water fall still strong and powerful. Feel the fresh of the fresh water from waterfall while enjoying the breeze from the salt water. Amazing place to revisit.

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is my favourite one of the three waterfalls i visited in Jeju! (April 2018)This place consist of three level waterfalls. The first level you will only see the waterfall if it has rained enough and the waterlevel is high enough to create the waterfall. The second one is the biggest of the three levels. It can be seen from two places. First is by the staircase and upclose. The second one is going over the bridge and after that (stone) stairs up on your rightside after crossing over the bridge. You can get a great view for the 2nd waterfall!The third and last level is the furtherst and the smallest one of all. If you are not fit enough or you can't walk very well, I advise to skip this one as there are a lot of stairs to go down and up afterwards.The first 2 levels are good enough to get a great view out of the place.

This is my favorite as the waterfalls and the blue water coupled with mandarin ducks swimming and moving around, I really feel like I'm in a fantasy land or living in the fairy tales movie that we used to see.  Highly recommended for photography and relaxation!

This is in my opinion the best waterfall in Seogwipo. I don't know if it's the biggest or the tallest, but it is truly unique, as water falls down into the ocean in the middle of a pebble beach. I visited it on a rainy and windy day, and because of it it might have left a stronger impression on me. I could really feel the forces of nature. Also, since the water falls onto the beach, you can take pictures really close to the waterfall. Overall, it is a must see waterfall if you come to Seogwipo, even though it doesn't get more than 20 minutes to get a nice view of the fall and its surroundings.

This is enormous highly worthwhile visiting. While I've visited caves around the world this is the first time I've seen lava tubes. They are huge you could drive a semi trailer through most of them. Defiantly worth seeing just for this aspect.It's quite wet on the floor of the cave, while you won't get wet, there are puddles of water. The ground is extremely uneven in places so good footwear is essential.There is heaps of signage in English on how they were formed.Highly worthwhile.

This is all about geology.... How lava tubes are formed during volcanic eruptions and the rock formations produced. It's something different from what most resort islands offer. A journey to the center of the earth.... cut short to about 1 km. Yes 1 km. So, if you aren't into walking for 1 km in and 1 km out, this is not the place for you. Especially so since the temperature drops significantly as you descend down the steps. It was the month of May, with outside temperatures ranging from 25-28 degrees Celsius, but as you walk into the cave, the chill can get to you. The ground is uneven and wet, with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Be prepared for all this.

This is a very well maintained mountain park as expected of any Unesco World Heritage site. My wife and I visited on a Monday and it was packed with people. We climbed up from Yeongsil and climbed down to Eorimok. It's impossible to lose your way. The hike is moderate and you don't have to be very fit to do it. Trainers or tennis shoes are adequate in May. You can do it at a leisurely pace or try to break a speed record. Hot noodles is available at the top (this is not the summit trail) or you can pack your own lunch and there are also a couple of water stations along the way on the Eorimok trail. The view from around the top is expansive but hardly breathtaking. Overall it's a pleasant and enjoyable hike.If you park at Yeongsil and return at Eorimok or vice versa, you can take a taxi back to your car for 20,000 wons.

This is a very interesting place to visit. Our driver put his car in neutral gear, turned off the engine and put his keys on the dashboard, and the car rolled uphill! We got off and watched other people put bottles of water on the road and they rolled uphill as well! It is actually an optical illusion, but still a strange sight to behold. You don't have to stay here for long - maybe 30 minutes will do.

This is a very interesting coastline with hexagonal rock columns shooting from the water. It is very unbelievable that nature created these columns, since they actually look man-made. It is 2,000 won per person for entrance fee, and it is totally worth it. The only regret is that it is so famous, so it is packed with tourists. The endless blue ocean, dramatic coast line, and the unique stone pillars make this one of my favourite attractions in Jeju.

This is a very accessible waterfall. Kudos to the local government for making it as easy as possible to enjoy the natural landmarks on the island. A flight of steps down and a very short walk brings you to the waterfall. There are large rocks to climb over and also a rocky flat   beach  . Young children will especially love climbing over the rocks and exploring the pools of flowing water. I have a sturdy 4 year old and a 5.5 year old and I think the waterfall impressed them less than the natural rocky playground they happily found themselves in. Do keep a very close eye on young children as the rocks are sharp edged and uneven, some even loose when you step on them.
This is a rather nice beach with clear blue water and fine sand. There were very few people there when i visited, making it a great spot to relax and suntan in the summer.

This is a nice place for sightseeing and exploring the Jeju waterfalls. There was a roughly 5-10 minutes walk before reaching the waterfall, which was fairly simple and pleasant too. The waterfall does not differ greatly from your other waterfalls, so if you?re looking for a unique and different sightseeing experience, I suggest giving this a miss. However, it was still quite magnificient and beautiful if you enjoy sightseeing and waterfalls. Overall, do spend about an hour here to leisurely stroll and sightsee this Jeju wonder.

This is a national park in the true sense.  There are long walking trails to see amazing sites, and you must be prepared to spend time and be in good shape for the walks.  Also, bring plenty of water for the walks.  The park has awesome views and long and winding roads.

this is a must-see. A temple in the cave made by ancient volcano corruption. It is on the top on the hill. Great views on the sea, pieceful atmosphere. You can drink water from thespring, it is a water from the mountain and it is clean.
This is a lovely waterfall, but try to avoid the peak season otherwise it's a bit busy.  Beautiful how the water flows right next to the sea.  Good for a paddle as well.

This is a long but fairly gentle trail up Mt Hallasan. It was extremely busy with people going both ways and most of the path is on wooden boardwalks and steps or basalt rocks. The later are uneven and I'd recommend hiking boots for comfort. There is a place to refill water bottles about half way up and the second of two shelters does some basic foods - noodles, but better to take everything you want with you. The toilets are grim. The crater at the top was rather disappointing with a muddy pool of water at the bottom on the day we went, but there were some splendid views across Jeju Is over all the parasitic volcanos. The lower slopes were very pretty with fall colours at the end of October. However, I've done better hiking with far fewer people in other countries.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).

This is a heritage site regarded as one of the New 7 wonders. Many people come to this place. The parking is huge but can be tight at times. Better to come here in fair day, so that you will enjoy the view. Bring your camera and water too. There are quite number of fastfood on the area if you need to buy snacks.
This is a fun place to visit, as apart from the waterfalls you can walk around the area and see many different attractions.
This is a cool waterfall. With 35 degree heat the splashing from the powerful waterfall was a nice way to cool down. Of the many waterfalls in Jeju, I feel that this is the best one.

This is a beautiful waterfall that empties directly into the sea. Once at the bottom the mist was very refreshing on a hot day. There are places where kids can wade but I'd recommend water shoes. I saw an adult sandal get swept into the sea. I brought my two kids (age 8 and 4). At the bottom of the stairs there were some very big rocks that were difficult for my 4 year old to navigate, had to carry him part of the way. My 8 year old did just fine. We didn't have water shoes and even though they had fun, they would have been a lot more comfortable with better foot protection. Good site, family friendly with some caution due to big rocks/slippery, not good for toddlers or smaller.
This is a beautiful area. The breeze, sun, and walk were refreshing. The water was many colors of blue! Lots of people though!

this is  rare chance to walk down lava tubes and look at the odd shapes and formations caused by the molten rock. You can see different layers of lava that once flowed here and see how the laval squeezed through smaller passages.   Consider bringing an umbrella or a very light shell. It can be damp and sometimes water drips from the ceilings. Also, it's significantly cooler than outside.   All in all, a must.

This hike will make a great day trip. Make sure to leave early as you're likely to spend a couple of hours on the mountain, either walking/climbing or admiring the view. Wear proper hiking boots/shoes and layers of clothes. Bring sufficient water. Toilets are very clean.

This high peak volcano is worth going for climbing... We went with my friend early march, the path was still snowyall the way!  Better to bring some equipement although it is possible to rent shoes at the convenient store down there.We were in march in a very low touristic season so it was quite nice to hike under the frozen pine trees with a beautiful blue sky. I think in high season on weekend, it could be crowdy! As it is a volcano, the walk is really sportive, meaning 6-10% continously during 2h. Get the first plane area, bring some candy bar or fruit, water of course, you will be enjoy this break on the roof of south Korea :=)

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!

This fall flows right into the ocean. i liked this one better than the others in the city because you can get into the water at the base of the falls and get your feet wet. also there was a tent with some of the famous diving grannies selling raw seafoods. i highly recommend trying this as it was a truly unique experience. the raw plate cost 20,000w which was cheaper than most of the nearby restarunts.

This excellent beach has a lil' bit of everything.  Located not far away from Jeju City/Airport, Hamdeok provides great atmosphere filled with Restaurants, Coffee Shops, waterfronts and one of the most beautiful sunsets in Korea! We sat down in the beachfront walk, cracked open a couple of beers and enjoy the evening breeze.  It was so cool watching people prepping their dinner and drinkin' some Soju while the sound of the waves and live music was heard across the darkness of the night.  We follow the music and found this young talented musician playing guitar and singing on front of a young crowd.  That was the Cherry on top of the Cake!  Stroll & Enjoy!

This dragon head rock is actually a volcanic rock formation happened years back. The molten magma touches the freezing cold sea water forming a unique shape. It looks like a dragon head from certain angle. I will suggest to visit it during the night as there will be lightings on it. The surrounding are filled with alot of seafood eateries. Will suggest to try out any of them. Seafood pot, abolone porridge and their sea produce are very tasty. For aviation lovers, this site is very near to the airport, you may find some strategic spot to view airplanes take of and landing.

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. But the walk along the cliffs was really nice and I enjoyed the beautiful cliff formations.

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

This cave is actually a volcanic Lava tube, not limestone cave. So don't expect to see amazing things like what you see in Guilin and Yunan.Same as reviewer ggkoh, I visited there after a day of persistent rain. The cave is wet, filled with small pool of water here and there. The floor bed is rocky and uneven. So be equipped with a jacket comes with hood (or raincoat) and a good pair of track shoes.

This bridge in Seogwipo harbour goes across to a small island which takes about 20 minutes to walk around.? It is a nice place to go at sunset, there are nice views and many birds in the trees.? Also nearby are the Cheoniyeon waterfalls, and a few shops and cafes.

This boardwalk has a nice garden , It leads you to a scenic point where the beautiful basalt formations can be seen, the color of the water is truly amazing. It is a nice stop if you are doing the Olle trails

This beautiful hike did not disappoint. It's easy to get to by city bus, and foreigner friendly upon arrival. The trek itself takes about 10 hours total. My friends and I are active hikers, and I initially thought we could do it in less time... but with 2 shelter stations along the way, there seemed to be no rush. The earlier you go the better. You cannot go to the top if you arrive at the last shelter past 1 o'clock. It'll take you about 4 1/2 hours to get to that final shelter. BRING YOUR OWN SNACKS AND WATER SUPPLY. The final shelter has noodles and bottled water for sale, but that's it. So be sure to bring your own. Once you reach the top you'll be blown away by the crater and then view. Pictures do not do it justice. Be sure to bring:- food- water- plastic bag (for your garbage... there are no garbage bins)- good hiking shoes - the trail is very rocky at points.. the more grip the better- a hat- a sweater - depending on the wind, it'll be cooler at the top- a cameraHappy hiking!

This beach was ok. The sand felt nice and there were plenty of people around to make it feel like a happening spot, without being overcrowded. You can easily grab a bite to eat nearby. In my opinion, I would go here for a beach day if I really wanted a beach day, but I wouldn't plan to go there as a must- see beach.One thing I noticed about the beaches in Korea... The Koreans dress more modestly than at almost any other beach in the world ( including Dubai) ... Most seemed to be covered up with water - type shorts and shirts vs. the typical shirtless man and bikini clad women. It's something you should consider !

This beach was actually quite dirty when I went. The sand and the sea were littered with trash some jerks must have thrown in there. There were clearly employees around who weren't picking it up. Had I a trash bag, I would have done it myself! I swam anyway, the water was cool and such. There were pretty awful showers (basically a HUGE ROOM with no privacy) for 2,000 won.

This beach was absolutely breathtaking! The sparkling fine sand, emerald clear water, and green hills all around made for a perfect beach day! Unlike what was stated in previous reviews from July 2019, we never had any problems with being able to swim freely and as far out as desired. There was also no line set out not to cross. This is the first beach I've been to with provided shading tents and umbrellas, but it was definitely nice for when we wanted a short break from the sun! We also never had to pay to use these, so I'm not sure if that is something only done during the busy season. The beach was not over crowded, especially at low tide, and it was easy to find little secluded areas if you wanted to be away from the majority of people. Locals were walking and swimming around to clean up trash, so it was honestly one of the cleanest beaches I have been to! Plenty of yummy restaurants to eat at, as well as bars for those wanting to stay out late and still have a view of the water. Be warned, there are no stores close by that sell towels, sunglasses, or other beach essentials, so make sure you are fully prepared! Definite   must see   while in JeJu!

This beach is surrounded by cafes, seafood, and one amazing restaurant in particular -   Arepa Grill!   At the end of the main strip facing the water, this place offers the most amazing Venezuelan food and ice cold beer They have a delicious vegetarian arepa that they can make vegan upon request. It's a nice change from the cafes that are all quite similar. I did, however, enjoy the bean bags at   Woodstock.
This beach is so beautiful. The view is breathtaking. Clear waters, blue ocean, white sand, and can swim here too.

This beach is beautiful and amazing! The main beach is usually filled with many tourist, but they have umbrellas and chairs you can rent to get out of the sun every once in a while! There is a great camping site just off the beach where many families camp and it is very cheap 7,000-15,000won. The sand is so soft on the beach and in the ocean! There are many sandbars so the water isn't too deep and makes it great for relaxing in the water! There are great restaurants around, and even the best pizza restaurant place I've been to in all of Jeju! They even have Inflatable tube rides on the back of jetskis and boats. They also have smaller inflatable tubes you can rent for a small price of 5,000 won.

This beach is amazing. It is by far one of my favorites on Jeju. As soon as you arrive there is just a great atmosphere and a great vibe! The view is amazing. There are rocks to take pictures on, chairs set up for the perfect beach picture. The white sand and the blue sea water are beautiful. The water is clear and inviting! It also has great places to eat, a burger place, a taco place, and many cafes where you can get coffee, teas, ice creams, etc. It can get crowded, but should be expected for any beach in Jeju during beach season.

This beach is a great place for tourists! Upon arriving there are lots of vendors with delicious food and things you might need for the beach (towels, hats, beach mats, swim suits, booze, etc). The main beach is usually very crowded (understandably). I like to go to the beach to the right, it's just a 5 minute walk on the sidewalk, clearly visible with a clear understanding it's leading to another beach. This part of the beach seems to be less crowded with all of the same benefits! Great place to relax, enjoy the sun, and swim in the water!

This beach is a good one.  The sand is soft and powdery and the clear water very gradually gets deep which allows us to comfortably walk unusually far into the ocean.  The other special characteristic is that there is a big change from low tide to high tide.  The high tide, which occurred around 10 pm when we were there, completely covers up a pretty large beach area.  It's pretty fascinating.  The food and drink shops near the beach were a bit of a letdown for us because they were overpriced.

This attraction is much smaller then the other similar sounding spot - Cheonjeyeon. There is just one waterfall here and its q quick short walk to the view point. Like all other spots, swimming is not allowed here as well. Good for a quick visit before visiting the Saeyeongyo Bridge.

This 6 KM (one-way) hike begins steeply, with nicely laid-out stairs climbing up through a beautiful, dense forest of oaks and maples.  It is very peaceful here, and our early (8 AM) start put us on the trail ahead of the crowds that showed up later in the day.  Most of the elevation gain -- total about 700M -- is accomplished in the first third of the hike.  The reward is a lovely stroll with some ups and downs through open meadows for the remainder of the hike to the Witse Oreum shelter.  Two springs are available if you need water on the way (but fill your water bottle directly:  I saw people drinking from the dippers hanging by one of the springs).  Views of the Halla crater wall and sweeping views downslope, of other parasitic cones and the sea, can be spectacular here on a clear day.  We went back down the Eorimok trail to our rental car, but other hikers we met recommended a one-way hike up the Yeongsil Trail (not so long) and then down the Eorimok (but then you have to take a bus or have two cars to do a shuttle).  Neither trail goes to the top of the crater, those areas being closed for extensive restoration.  However, the views were fantastic and I don't feel that I missed out on anything except a hard climb.

they charge admission now to see this seashore.  as if that's not bad enough, it was closed by the time we arrived at 5pm.  but what wasn't closed were the numerous vendor stands that seemingly sprung up to cash in on the tourists here.  the most interesting thing we noticed were various coconuts with small holes drilled in them with a straw sticking out.  this is supposed to be 'fresh' coconut water.  protip: there are no coconuts in korea.  superprotip: they re-use these containers without rinsing them out, over days/months/years, you get the idea.if you don't mind paying to see this 'natural wonder,' at least avoid the vendor stands like the plague, cause that's what you'll likely catch there.

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

These cliffs formed when Hallasan erupted and lava flowed to the sea. When the lava hit the sea, the contrast in temperatures caused the rock to form hexagonal columns, giving us this beautiful view! This is a really neat sight to see, but you don?t need to linger. It?s a great place to stop on your way to the waterfalls. Parking is cheap and plentiful.

There were many scenic views at this attraction. I enjoyed both the ascent and descent. Even with the chilly breeze, one is sure to perspire upon arrival at the peak. The view into the crater at the peak was another awesome feast for the eyes. The sea as the backdrop served as a picturesque addition to the already scenic composition. After the descent, there were opportunities to witness the infamous women free divers of Jeju. These minimalist free divers were equipped with their orange flotation devices, masks and dry suits, sustained their tradition daily in the frigid waters to harvest seafood from the shallow depths. Why pass on this opportunity?

There was a tour group with a guide when we visited. We saw his demonstration of water flowing upstream and a water bottle that roll upstream too. very interesting, when you switch off the car engine and witness the car rolling upwards.

There lies 3 waterfall spots in Seogwipo, south of Jeju. I have went to all 3. But this Cheonjeyeon (not to be confused with Cheonjiyeon waterfall) itself has 3 waterfalls around the area. So in fact, there are 5 waterfalls in Seogwipo. The ticket is more expensive compared to the others but it is worth it as you can visit 3 falls and an arching bridge with nymphs (angels) carvings on the side. I prefer this place to Cheonjiyeon Falls.

There is not much to see on the way to the top. Remember it's a 19k hiking and you need to use your time wisely in a day. We went on a cloudy day. It wasn't too hot but the hiking was difficult with rocks covering most of the roads. So get yourself a real pair of hiking shoes! My feet got hurt and it was slippery after rain. Some parts have stairs, which are highly appreciated... The top view was great but maybe it was dry, we did not see water in the crate. Spring and Fall might have more to see. My friend and my legs have been hurting since we accomplished it...

There is a start sign & stop sign. Upon reaching the start sign, switch to neutral gear, on hazard light, and keep your car engine on. It will start to move forward on a uphill slope. Very slowly. Of course, do be alert and keep your eye infront and foot hover on brake if necessary.It is a one lane traffic, so not all cars are stopping to be wow by this nature forces, you might be honked by other drivers for slowing down and doing this anti-gravity act. Well... just ignore them. They will move on by cutting your lane.There is a convenient shop next to it and car park. You can park your car there and come down to try it with a half-filled water bottle. It will perform the same too, rolling up on a up-slope.However, beware of cars. There is still on-coming traffic.

There is a standard entrance fee of 2000krw. After you buy the ticket you will proceed into the entrance and you can see the waterfall infront of you. Hang on to your ticket because somewhere along the route, they will check your ticket. Most people will walk to as near to the falls as possible to take pictures. It was quite crowded on the day. The rocks / boulders are not so easy to walk on. So we stayed near the staircase. Yes, there are stairs to climb down to the falls and then you have to climb up again.I would say it is quite a normal waterfall - just to tick off that you have seen it.

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty. Yes, the beach itself is a soft sand frame for spectacular sunsets punctuated by occasionally clear blue-green waters, but it's also a growing epicenter for the worst kind of overbooked tourism. Pros: The beach itself is broad, and the area in front of the main beach lends itself to a safe experience for attended children: there is a large, open region of sand at low tide and shallow water at high tide for kids to play in.  The view is nice, and the sunsets are extravagant. There is camping nearby with good tree cover, adequate facilities for showering, stores for trinkets and swimming paraphernalia, and places to buy food and drink. There is also a small but growing night life near the beach that has a distinctly island feel, far from the thumping of your standard Korean club scene. Cons: The swimming area is unbelievably small, so not only does everyone get to experience a sardine style of   swimming   in water that rarely goes past the hips of an adult, the water is also full of sand and debris due to the high person-per-square-meter ratio. Visibility underwater is often zero, so don't expect to see fish on a busy day - which is pretty much the entire high season. There is garbage everywhere, both in the water, and in large, reeking piles near the parking lot. The noise is unbelievable (just like the parking) and the local restaurants - with only one or two exceptions - cater to the lowest common denominator for quality.  Hyeopjae is being targeted by packaged family tours, and yet there is a laughably inadequate infrastructure in place to ensure a safe, organized experience for children. The beautiful volcanic rocks along the sides of the beach and in some parts of the water are playgrounds of minor and major injury. The often unattended children that race up and down the beach are in no way warned about or protected from these hazards. The forest of beach umbrellas tightly packed on the   main beach   is both uncomfortably crowded and poorly organized for parents to keep an eye on their kids, and for kids to find their parents when they get lost. The lifeguards are simultaneously overworked and overzealous. They are simply too busy whistling at people to keep them safe from the dangers of hip-deep water (a strange and annoying tradition amongst Jeju lifeguards) to effectively keep an eye out for people - especially children - who are may be in real trouble.Bottom Line: If you've never had the chance to explore Jeju, you won?t know just how bad Hyeopjae is. Moreover, as I said in the beginning, some people actually enjoy the mass market appeal of tourist traps, and I don't begrudge them their tastes. All I'm saying is Jeju has an embarrassment of better beaches with better food and better facilities. In fact, you only have to travel up or down the road for 15 minutes in either direction to find beautiful, secluded areas where you lavish on an empty beach and swim in truly pristine waters. Q.E.D.

There are three main waterfalls in the south of Jeju and this was the first one we saw, it is the only one by the sea and is about 15 minutes walk from downtown Seogwipo. There is a nice little park before the entrance to the waterfall.We went in the afternoon and it was crowded with many people taking pictures. Would suggest going early in the morning (they open at 8am), better for pictures with the sun shining on the waterfall and less people. Bring proper footwear or shoes you don't mind getting wet as it is very rocky and you can get wet from the spray. Entrance fee is 2000 won and it is a short walk down some stairs to the waterfall.

There are statues of the Future Buddha, Maitreya; Bodhisattva of Compassion,? an outdoor huge Golden statue of Buddha, hundreds of miniature green Buddhas.? If you climb up the 471 steps, you will reach a cave with a statue of the Bodhisattva of Compassion. The tears that she constantly cries for all the pain of this   ocean of suffering   world collects in pools up the stairs below the altar.? Visitors drink it and make prayers before it. If you drink 3 sips of the water, you will enjoy longevity in good health. Great temple to visit.

There are sign posts to mark the start and end of the 100 metres stretch of the Mysterious Road.  Pretty fun to play   magic   with family and friends. Put your car to neutral gear, release your foot off the accelerator and notice the car moving   uphill   on the road.  Recreate the same effect with a bottle or ball rolling uphill.  The Mysterious Road is actually a gravity hill i.e. a place where a slight downhill slope appears to be an uphill slope due to higher surroundings, creating the natural illusion that water flows uphill or that a car left out of gear rolls uphill.  Worth a fun stop if you self-drive!

There are several beautiful beaches on Udo, but we preferred the  popcorn  beach above the others. Cristal clear water and white popcorn like beach sand. you can rent snorkel gear from the cafes near the beach. We went there after watching the sunrise from sunrise peak. Ferry was W35000 for a return including our car. Do take your own snacks and drinks.

There are no words to describe the beauty of this beach. OMG a little piece of heaven. The water, the sand, the view was soooo beautiful and peaceful. Loved it!!!!I'm a girl who grow up  on a beautiful Mediterranean island and Hamdeok beach made me feel like home!!! Please take me back there!!!

There are many waterfalls in Jeju, we decided to have a look at Cheonjiyeon. There is a large parking lot, eateries and a couple of souvenir shops, 7eleven etc when you arrive. To walk to the waterfall is about 10-15 min along a small tree lined river. Many tourists and tourists groups are visiting the waterfall so it will be quite crowded. The waterfall as such is nice, but not too tall or spectacular. everybody takes a few selfies and then heads back to the parking lot pretty much. If nearby it makes to stop by and visit but it is not worth a long journey just to see this waterfall.
There are many caf챕s, restaurants and convenience stores. Not my favourite beach but in general very nice and clean water. I recommend it if you come with children.
There are lots of things to see here, we spend 2 hours here. Beautiful trees, caves, stones, small waterfall. It is all about nature and traditional korea living.
There are in fact three beaches: one for little children with soft and smooth waters, one for surfers and one for swimmers
There are a number of waterfalls in Jeju, but only one deserves your time. It's amazing to see just how close the water flows directly to the sea.

There are a lot of negative reviews basically saying this waterfall is just average. It may not have that 'wow' factor but one should not visit if they are expecting the niagra falls. The one valid complaint are the stairs, slightly steep, and the rocks that need to be traversed to get closer to the falls. One has to be careful when hopping and stepping from rock to rock. Also, it can be a bit crowded with picture taking tourists.I found Jeongbang to be a modest waterfall, but nonetheless very charming. Great pictures can be taken on approach and up close, right next to the pool where you can feel the freshwater spray. Turn your back to the waterfall and a nice ocean view greets you, with two small mountain isles off in the distance. For the more adventurous, there are rocks of all sorts to be found closer to the sea. Most visitors snap a few pics and leave, but hanging out by the sea for a spell was also quite enjoyable.  While the rocks won't be confused with the rainbow, it was fun to pick out unique looking rocks from the saltwater, but watch out for the waves!

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

There are 4 main attractions and you easily spend 1.5- 2 hours there, we only go to 2 waterfalls as we afraid there won?t be enough time to go to other places.4 main attractions :Seoningmo bridgeCheonjiyeon Waterfall2nd Waterfall3rd WaterfallSome stairs here and there, don't miss it if you are in Jeju,
There are 3 waterfalls, but only the 2nd one is above average. However, the hiking between those waterfalls is very nice.

There are 3 waterfalls near my guesthouse and I chose to visit Jeongbang Waterfall first; no special reason as I have a direct bus to there. Admission fee for adult is 2000 won, and youth will be 1000 won (the ticket ahjumma will ask for your birth year). So you will have to walk down a few stairs and cross over stones to reach the waterfall. It was cooling to just sit down here and enjoy the waterfall. But please remember to wear cover shoes in order to prevent falling. Not only you can take photos with the waterfall, there?s a connecting sea right beside and you can take beautiful picture. Solo travellers please remember to bring a selfie stick :)

The wind blows hard in this area (as the wind turbines might hint at). But the water is beautiful, the sand is white and the rock formations around are really special. It gets crowded but not as crowded as some others on the island. I have seen better beaches for sure, but here in Jeju this one is probably as good as it gets.

The whole trail takes about 45 mins to an hour to complete. It was truly interesting to be inside a lava tube and during the walk, there were informational signs to explain parts of the tubes! I would recommend bringing a hoodie and water proof shoes as it is very wet and slippery inside :) The dampness will make you feel cool even in the summer.

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the   Manjanggul Lava Tube   enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

The waters were gentle and one saw more people in water than out there, although a selfie moment happening is never far in South Korea. Also great for a walk( into the village area, but please don't take photos without asking, off the coast as they share the coast with visitors freely and it is respectful to enter their space on their terms)

The waterfalls was nice and a real up close look was possible as the access allowed visitors to go all the way to the base of the waterfall. I like the views just before sunset, as there are haneyeo serving sashimi on the rocks nearby, giving it an additional local touch.In addition, the kids liked the fun and adventure of walking on the rocks up to the waterfall.
the waterfall wasn't really interesting but the 2000 years old Chinese signature and the diving women who serve seafood that only a minute ago was alive, were very interesting.
The waterfall that falls direct to the sea. Although not as majestic as I thought. But you can see rainbow where the water is falling, in a clear day.

The Waterfall is very close to Seogwipo, within walkig distance.  It costs 2000eon adults to enter but you can get very close to the Waterfall.  There are even seafood being sold next to the cliffs so you can eat seafood, watch the sea and enjoy the waterfall.  We took a few pictures and then   left because the downside is that there are a lot of people.

The waterfall is said to be the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly into the sea - although it seems to fall into a cove, not directly into the ocean.  The spot is very touristy and busy, but is a nice waterfall in itself.  You can paddle in the water to cool off and kids love playing on the rocks.

The waterfall is rather small, but it is almost in the middle of a city. When you arrive you will be on top of the cliff in which Jeongbang flows off of. Located near Seogwipo city, Jeongbang Waterfall is 23 meters high and is very close to the sea. This is why people tell that the water falls directly into the ocean. A legend says that servant of Emperor Jin of China, called as Seo Bul, sent to the area in order to search the magical herb of eternal youth in Mount Halla. People interested in seafood can taste fresh abalone sashimi with garlic slices & hot pepper paste as dipping. It is offered by ajummas, who collect them directly at this spot. Don쨈t forget to wear good shoes to avoid becoming a casualty.

The waterfall is not too far from the entrance. Just take a short walk around 5-8 minutes and then you will find the waterfall. For young children, must assist by adults, because on the way to waterfall there are many big rock. The wind is so strong. The waterfall is special because it's located near beach.

The waterfall is not so large when we came, so we can walk up near to it to take some pictures. It is only a short walk down from the entrance, but be careful when walking on the stones as it can be very slippery and very crowded at times. The falls itself is very unique as it flows straight to the ocean and it cost only 2000 won to enter.

The waterfall is not as impressive as it was advertised and there is an admission fee.Frankly, I don't think they should charge for admission as there is really nothing to do except to see the waterfall. If you have time to spare, visit other attractions.

The waterfall is in walking distance from the center of Seogwipo, even if there are a fee steps to get to the waterfall it's worth the visit!The view is fantastic, and the vapour coming from the waterfall is refreshing (especially in summer).Beware just of the last few meters because are on rocks, and sometimes slippery.

The waterfall is beautiful, it gave me the urge to jump in it under the hot sun. There is a entrance charge for that. For those who are from places like Malaysia, Philippines where surrounded with beautiful waterfalls, you might don't feel like spending money just to see this waterfall.
The waterfall is beautiful and takes only a mere 10 minutes to go down. There were people stacking stones, which also made the environment look more aesthetic.
The waterfall is amazing, but the steps to the waterfall are steep and slippery.

The waterfall faces the ocean so you can imagine the great view there. Among the famous waterfalls in Jeju, go to this one if you only have time to visit 1. Also, wear comfortable footwear as you need to navigate pass some big unstable rocks to reach the bottom of the waterfall.
The water was cool (it was a hot day), we went on a weekday so it was not too crowded. Take off your shoes and frolick.
The water was beautiful, so we stop by for a quick dip in the ocean. It was very shallow so we went out pretty far at one point. There were many schools of fish and clams in the ocean.
The water is shallow and clear, full of sea shells, hermit crabs, and small fish. It is great place for little kids to swim safely.

The water is amazing. There are 3 waterfall spots and a beautiful bridge to see at this attraction. Highly recommended although the walk can be a pain, especially the last waterfall.The bridge is also quite a sight to behold. This is probably the best waterfall in Jeju.

The water is a beautiful emerald color but the beach is too crowded. Too many parasols, shops, and small hotels. Go to the beach down the road if you want a more relaxing day at the beach.Tip: There are some decent beach style restaurants on the main road. There is nice a pizza cafe with covered outside seating. Also there is a Mom's Touch that servers fast food (chicken sandwiches).This beach is ranked as one of the top beaches in Jeju by Koreans. I was disappointed but I realized that the standards are different. Hey if you want simple food, people, and shade then this is the place to go.

The water here is gorgeous! For some reason, the sand was all covered up (strange) but we still had a nice time sightseeing. It was too cold for anything else! Lots of restaurants and places to stay. We stayed at the Beach Story Hotel, which was nice and cheap since no one was around!

The walking trail at Yongmeori Coast is just a few hundred meters (~700 m) long, but the layered sedimentary structures made from rocks and volcanic ashes, and dramatic shapes created by erosion from hard ocean-waves and wind make it breathtaking art of nature and truly resembles Geopark. It is known that the site is indeed designated as one of the nine Jeju sites certified by the Global Geopark Network in 2010. Personally, this is one of my best scenic places in Jeju in the view of both geology and photography lover.The part of these cliffs appeared stretched out from nearby Sanbangsan Mountain. The meaning of Yongmeori in Korean is Dragon Head. Interestingly, the rough surface of rocks and dramatic shapes formed by rocks due to erosions make it look like a dragon's head going underwater.This part of Jeju is also famous for women sea-drivers. During our visit, we have got an opportunity to try out a few fresh kinds of seafood sold by Korean grandmothers along the coastline. Another attraction near this cliff is the huge shipwreck which is actually a reproduction built as the Hamel Castaway Memorial to commemorate a Dutch sailor (Hendrick Hamel). It is said that he was drifted to the shore of Jeju by a typhoon in 1653. He then wrote a book providing the West some insights into Joseon Korea for the first time. All together this place is very impressive and must not be missed.

The walk up sunrise mountain was  windy and relatively easy. Steps all the way up with many spots for you to rest and take in the beautiful view. Don't miss out on this mountain if you are going to Jeju. Entrance fee is 2000W. They charge for everything here, waterfalls and parks all have an entrance fee.

The walk to the waterfall was nice although it is kind of man made. The natural sights at the side was beautiful nonetheless.However, the waterfall itself was just ok. It didn't seem like that's the focal point of this attraction but it was good enough for a trip there.

The walk to Cheonjiyeon Falls is quite easy and beautiful. The waterfall is quire charming as well. However, compared to Cheonjeyeon Falls (which is a 3 tiered waterfall attraction in Jeju not mentioned in TripAdvisor), Cheonjiyeon is still second best.

The view was stunning and the crater is large and definitely a great place to take photos. Before you start hiking, i advice you should bring a bottle of drinking water, because there's no stores that sell one near the peak. A windbreaker or double layer clothes are useful, coz the wind was pretty strong. I sweated a lot. But reaching the top will pay all physical efforts!Last but not least, Keep your trash to yourself. Trash disposal bins are very rare. i Highly recommend this place.!

The view was amazing even if you did not make it up to the top. From halfway point onwards, you could see the awesome seaview. We went in the afternoon so that we could catch the divers' performance at 3pm. What impressed me the most about the performance was that the Ajumma actually went into the cold waters in winter! For that, it was worth my time standing out in the cold to show them our support.

the view of the waterfall is great! however, many will get closer to the waterfall by walking through the very rocky area from the stairway. kids and elderly need to be careful and also to secure your belongings, if things were to drop into the rocks, may be hard to retrieve. ensure you wear proper footwear!
The view especially sunset was just amazing to observe. Crystal clear water, cosy cafes scatetred around gives happy vibes !

The unique thing about this waterfall is it's by the sea. Do wear proper shoes as you would have to climb down stairs and rocks if you want a closer look at the falls. Like most attractions in Jeju, it was awfully crowded. Ap, one doesn't really get a chance to sit and enjoy the falls, which is a pity.

The trip up and down the 1.95km tall mountain took me the entire day but experience and view was really worth it. It would have been better if I had been properly equipped as I was in normal walking shoes and a small bottle of water while everyone else had their trekking shoes and stick with them which made going up and down more quickly and safe. There are alot of routes but not all the routes will lead you to the peak. Spoke to a few people on my way up and they shared that this is most tedious route as its the longest. There is only one way up and down which makes trekking easy for solo traveller like me.It'd be good if you can bring some food and lots of water with you where you can picnic with many korean families when you reach the peak. Do prepare to start early as you will have to reach a certain checkpoint before they allow you to continue your way up the peak. It was a heartwarming experience for me when all the korean people who walked past me would encourage me to press on and they would share they food around at the peak. Korean families usually do this as a family activity where the grandmother, grandfather, parents and kids would climb leisurely. If a grandparent can do it, so can you. Thats all :)

The stairs down into the cave system are steep and plentiful, so if you have trouble with stairs then you should skip it.  Also, if you don't like walking on uneven ground then you should skip it, because most of the cave floor is natural stone, so it's rough and uneven in many places.  There's also small standing pools of water in places, so watch where you step.  You don't have to walk the whole cave length, since it's very long indeed, so you can just do what we do and walk part of the way and then back again.  But you do need appropriate footwear, and no, high heels are NOT appropriate footwear.And remember, this is a natural cave system, not a fun park, so don't go expecting anything beyond what it is.

The small village seemed to be tended by a couple who actually live in the village.  I believe the village is government subsidized as well, but perhaps the couple who lives there gets additional money from selling some products (more on that later).A lady who lives there gave us a tour of the houses at the village.  She started off with where she lives - which is traditional on the outside, but seemed to have all the modern features on the inside.  We then got a small explanation of the milling device there as well and a water collecting jar.  We were also allowed to put one of the water jars on our backs.  A little pig pen and outhouse were shown as well.Unfortunately, the final destination for the tour was a small room where our tour guide could give us a hard sell on some products - mainly some horse cream or something like that...  That sort of ruined the tour, but I could imagine that this could be the tour guide's main source of income.  And she was kind when we said no to the hard sell.The tour was informative in many ways as the tour guide provided a lot of information and stories of the hardship and struggles of the native Jeju people.

The slopes at this area created an optical illusion.  That's is.  Drive there and simply wait for a tour bus to arrive and observe where they switch off their engines. Do the same.  After which, loiter around the snack stalls and every few minutes, a tour guide would demonstrate with a bottle of water how gravity defies nature (illusion).  That's all this place offers.

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The Seongpanak trail that goes to the summit is curentlyclose, until July 31st. I went all the way to the start of Seongpanak  trail and had to take 2 buses to go Gwaneumsa trail.The hike was nice but difficult. The first part was nice, 3,1km of normal hiking, until we reached the hard part, very steep, with stairs and rock. The climb fromSamgakbong shelter to the summit was not too hard, but a bit warm because of the sun. It as very humid, so be sure to pack a lot of waterand food as there are no vendors on the trail. It easy to reachthe trail by bus, but we took a taxi back to our hotel as we were too tired. A very good exercice and a good hike. I would doit again! ;)

The Seongpanak Trail is the easiest, though the longest trail to hike up Mount Hallasan (bit over 9km). It's a beautiful path with a gradual ascent and some steep sections. The difficulty in this trail is the surface, as the majority of the time you are walking on volcanic rocks that make your footing uneven and it does wear you out. I hiked in Chaco sandals and was ok, but I'm used to it. I highly recommend wearing comfortable shoes. I also suggest getting an early start, before 8am. Because it's the most gradual ascent, this is also a busy trail with hikers constantly going both directions. Bring snacks and plenty of water. There is a re-filling spring water station a bit more than half way to the peak. Highly recommend if you are an outdoorsy person and can handle long walks/hikes.

The Seongeup Folk Village was a walled-in village in the southeast of the island where stone homes showed the construction, culture and lifestyle of the island?s people long ago.Obviously, Jeju wants to maintain some type of historical reference to the old lifestyle.  Our tour guide made it interesting by talking about some practical aspects of the design of the huts (how it was heated, how it was built, etc), but this just wasn't my thing.  In fact, several families that help with the upkeep of the huts actually live in other huts in the community.  That said, those huts have modern adjustments like windows, electric power, etc so even they have moved beyond the   old ways  .  The village had a few shops and a restroom and outside the village was a convenience store with drinks available and another restroom. For me, the bottom line was - I would have preferred to spend the time at a natural landmark (waterfall, cave, hiking trail, etc) instead of doing this, but it was part of an all day tour.  There are simply too many other options to see in Jeju for this to make it to the top of the list, unless it is your   thing  .

The road was called mysterious road as it seem to be a up slope but your vehicle can move slowly up like going down slope. The area is less crowded at around 7-9am until the tour bus came, where many people actually went down to crowd around this road. The tour bus would stop at the start of the slope and off its Engine and slowly moved up to the end and turn into the car park where the tourists would come down and see cars moving up. Some of them would pour water to show that the water went up instead of down. It is quite mind boggling. But actual fact that this road is due to the surrounding which makes you have the perception thinking it is a up slope but actually it is down.Way to get there is by Car or Bus. It is close to Jeju LoveLand and it is down the same road, so it is not too difficult to find.

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head.
