The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.

The principal purpose of the bridge is to provide a walkway to Saeseom Island. The area close by is great for photography - clean water, interesting rock formations, local flora etc. The circuit of the island is also very pleasant, particularly in good weather.

The place was small, there weren't many things to see and entrance fee was insanely expensive at 10,000\ for an adult. Not a recommended place to go, best to go elsewhere like the waterfalls or jusangjeollidae rocks.

The place was hot and mosquito infested honestly due to the Aug weather. However if you have enough repellent with you, this is a good place to walk over, sit on the rocks, chill by the waterfall, feel the cold clear air and pose till you are tired.

The place is usually crowded.  Make sure to wear good walking shoes to walk and climb, some drinking water to quench thirst along the way. Not suitable for elderly and people who are not keen in climbing. Otherwise, is worth to visit - it is a Unesco World Heritage site after all.  If you are not there to catch sunrise, any season is fine.

The place is breathtaking, starting from the parking lot with all the old ladies selling the traditional stuff, the park is amazing with the clear water and swimming ducks & fish, the sakora tree is more than beautiful, then the waterfall i can?t even describe its beauty....and the ticket cost only 2000 Korean won . Inside the park there is a clean toilet and services alsoIf you go to jeju you must visit it

The pictures we saw of this place on the internet before visiting showed people swimming beneath the falls. However, when we got there (with great difficulty as signage is completely absent), we found an abandoned petty waterfall and pool full of stagnant water and mosquitoes. There was a sign forbidding swimming so it must have fallen into disregard recently.

The paths up and down the crater are well-maintained with hand-rails and steps to minimize slips and falls. The views from the peak are extremely scenic looking down at the blue sea water and misty 1950-m highHallasan far in the midst of the island. A left path leads to the cliff-bay where fresh seafood is available to prepare as you order and motor boat-rides at 10,000 per person are available.

The park is quite large. Access to the cave is via two flight of stairs downwards into the earth. The temperature inside is colder than the outdoors, with the pathway often wet with water dripping from above the cave. Lighting is limited, and one has to use flash to take pictures, though a little tweaking of the camera could bring pretty good results without using the flash. There are written explanations regarding the lava layers. Because of time constraints, we were not able to finish exploring the cave to its end.

The Park is quite a distance away from other major sights but it is different in that the star attraction are those   grandfather stone sculptures  .Be prepared for lots of walking on easy trails.  There are small pebbles everywhere so do watch the kids and carefully navigate those wheelchairs and baby strollers.The underground museum near next to the water reservoir/water sculpture is definitely for those interested in geology.  It is a good place to take a break and use the restrooms as there is another set of lavatories near the car park.

The park is nice and had a good size. There are a variety of different sections and when you add it all up it gives a good mini summary of Jeju - with the caves, stone park, waterfall, historical aspects, flower garden, and bird park. If you have only 2-3 days in Jeju this should be a must on the itinerary.

The park is built for the waterfall. Was there during dusk, though there are sufficient lighting around. The waterfall is a tad disappointing, especially when you came from Jeongbang Waterfall. However it is suitable for people of all ages, the walk to the waterfall is very easy.
The park has different areas including water garden, bird garden, bonsai garden, cave and folk village... Overall, the garden is very nice, huge but the entrance ticket is a bit bit bit pricey.

The only waterfall in Jeju that drains directly into the ocean is worth stopping by for around half an hour. Ample parking space, free admission, good accessibility and the ability to get quite close to the waterfall even if it isn't that tall.
The natural waterfall in the raw form and walking in the rocks is fun. The surprise was a fresh Jeju orange juice nearby, the seller was honest and nice.

The moment I set my eyes on this island, I knew I was in heaven. The water looked extraordinary blue and the view was nothing short of a perfect dreamy scenery. We took a day trip on the ferry from jeju. On the island, we took the hop on hop off bus. Take any bus, doesn't really matter.. They will then tell you which color buses u can hop onto at the next destination along with a list of places they will stop at. I think it costs around 2200 won. The island was crowded specially with all the bikes but still it is not to be missed. The first stop was the udo peak. A hike of around 30 mins to a lighthouse from where you can see the entire islans. The view of the sunrise peak on jeju all along the hike was incredible! Then the bus took us to 2 beaches..one was a black sand beach which had a little cave but tides were high that day. We missed the 2nd beach and went to the last one with white sand. This beach was quite close to the port and we walked to the port from here along the coast. It was a beautiful walk and less crowded.There are lot of shops and cafes in front of the last beach.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The lava tubes are very interesting and quite large - especially compared to those in other parts of the world. The only word of caution is to bring a raincoat and sneakers if it has been raining, as the water will trickle down through the rock and will drip considerably as you walk through. Definitely worth a stop.

The lava tubes are an interesting walk and it was cool to see the largest lava column in the world.A good thing to visit but not essential if pushed for time, an hour is ideally needed to look about the open portion of the tunnels.If you have a waterproof, take it along- it's surprisingly wet.If you are getting there by bus-we got the 701, it is a 2.5km walk or another bus to the entrance. We opted to walk because of the bus infrequency. Taxiing it there would be easiest.

The lava cave is like a small adventure if you are keen at exploring. Bring a torchlight or make sure you have one installed in your handphone as the cave floor is uneven and slippery. Wear good shoes and a warm jacket with hoodie or wear a cap as water occasionally drips from the top. There is a short trek up a flight of stairs to reach the cave entrance. Lockers available near toilets. Set aside one and a half hours to finish the cave and return as it is slippery at certain sections. Wear good shoes and walk slowly and carefully. I was apalled at how some kids manage to walk pretty fast without their parents holding on to them. In summary, I do not find this cave spectecular, not much for photography too. Just a straight tunnel like structure. We were tired out by the time we went to the cave as we climbed seongsan ilchubong in the morning. Not recommended to combine the cave with other trekking activities in a day. Imo, I find the cave interesting but not a must visit.

The lack of literature on the Seongeup Folk village was compensated by the cheerful caretaker who gave informative, colourful and refreshing description of their well preserved ancient village.The village revealed a period of time when peace and security were prevailing, and privacy was highly respected. No one would enter the village when the two horizontal portable poles placed across the main entrance were not removed.Visitors would learn about the social structure of the days gone by, when men were out-numbered by women, when men stayed home and were pampered, while the women became the   work-horses   of the family.  Apart from becoming skilled divers, many womenfolk had to travel long distance daily, carrying heavy loads of water supply or agricultural products back to their homes.One would be surprised to learn that rudimentary recycling system was already being practiced. The caretaker must be congratulated for so cleverly circumvented the description the   grand father   stone status, which was in the shape of a male organ.  She described the statue as a god that offered protection against the demons, and promoted fertility for the living.

The Jeongbang Waterfall is one of the   Big Three   on Jeju. This one is particularly stunning as the water falls down over the cliffs to the beach below. You can get very close to the water (your camera will get wet) and get some stunning photos. There are good facilities at the top and the walk down isn't too strenuous.

The island was teeming with dragonflies and it felt like something out of a Disney film. At any rate, if you are in the area visiting the nearby waterfall, or going on a boat or submarine trip, it is a lovely walk with spectacular views all round.I wouldn't suggest going here specifically, but if you are nearby..... it's worth a look.

The island is windy. Quite convenient to go around as there's shuttle bus with blue and red route that bring you around the island. The bus driver will narrate in Korean to explain the places, although we don't understand but is a fun trip to go along with mostly korean. The field grows full of canola flowers (yellow), very beautiful. Also, with nice cliff with plunging waves, good place to take pictures. The water is clear blue at the beach. Unfortunately, we only planned for half day trip so we can only complete the blue route. So, best to plan for a day as it probably takes you full day to admire the scenery.

The indoor gardens are very lovely especially the flower and cactus gardens. We were there on a sunny day in May and expected it to be hot inside. But these are not just greenhouses. They are greenhouses with air conditioning and so it was pleasantly cool and we took our time to walk around and admire the plants in comfort. The gardens are very well maintained without a leaf out of place. The arrangements are very pleasing and and these two gardens are simply beautiful. Go on a sunny day when the light and shadow creates a most charming effect.As for the outdoor gardens, the Italian one is very picturesque with a magnificent water feature. This is not so much a garden but nonetheless very attractive.Definitely worth a visit.

The hot springs have a good reputation and are very popular amongst Koreans. There is a large indoor area, separated of course for male and female, and then an outdoor area with 4 small pools the size of a hot tub and one larger lap pool which has cold spring water. Out of the 4 smaller pools 3 have hot water, 1 has cold water.The overall condition of the outdoor pools is quite shocking actually and I was surprised. In Korea almost everything is well maintained and in good condition, at these hot springs the paint coating came off at the pools, the pool furniture was old and falling apart, just very surprised to see it in this poor condition. It was busy nevertheless. There is a mix of couples and families, kids running around, people talking loudly, so it is not really serene and peaceful as a hot spring should be. The bathing experience was good, very relaxing, no doubt, but the overall experience was mediocre.

The hiking was great.  I decided to stop and buy a few bottles of water at the last rest stop/cafeteria and quickly used them to replenish my water-backpack.  I then gave the empty bottles back, and the attendant said take your own garbage down!  The way I see it is I bought the water NOT the bottles and I was in no mood for his sarcastic rude remakes.  If you are selling food and water THEY not ME should have a garbage disposal system, even if it costs customers a bit more money.  I found they were very selfish and demining to me, and I would not recommend buying anything from them.   They only are encouraging people to pollute and dispose of there trash  along the trail.  As for me, I hid my trash in front of their exit door to prove a point.

The hiking trail is well designed and fellow hikers are courteous. There are multiple trails with varying levels of difficulty. Some parts are fairly steep. Stairs are installed in most parts of the trail that we climbed on, though I am not sure if this is the case with all trails. The midway station includes food and water facilities. There are no garbage cans anywhere on the trail, nor indeed even at the entrance to the trail. Make sure you do not bring too many things that require disposal when you climb.

The hike is very picturesque, it's not very steep or in any way difficult. The view is amazingly beautiful, the caldera overlooking the water and even the stairs add to the amazing look of the place (I usually prefer natural hiking trails). It is not very big though, so it takes little time to hike up and down, so it's better to plan something to do in the neighborhood and not come just to see this place, as it might not be satisfying on its own.
The hike is not for everyone, but the -lace is defitely beautiful and deserves a visit. The waterfalls are gorgeous.

The hike is definitely not an easy hike. Some very steep slopes and sloshy like snow at the top can make it a little slippery. However definitely worth the view at the top. To note: - You need to get to the checkpoint before midday in winter. Otherwise you'll be turned around and can't reach the summit- You have to reserve a hiking spot for the day. This is all done online and you simply bring the QR code to the gates at the front and pass on through. - Bring lots of water and snacks as there is a shelter at the checkpoint which is indoors and warm, perfect for warming up and getting some energy. - Bring gloves for the summit as it is extremely cold up there due to windchill.

The experience was exactly like what I read from reviews and so I'll just focus on key things.-If for youngsters,  no issues.-For people not used to visiting caves-*wear shoes that don't slip*bring a torch if darkness is a concern *wear a light jacket- there are unexpected water drops, huge temperature difference with outside -Using mobile phones, not easy to take good photos. What you see is better than what is captured by phones. Online photos look so much better than what we saw.-Flowers outside the cave are lovely. Good photo taking spots.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee was 2000 W per head and 1000W per car . After buying the tickets , you descend about 5-6 flights of stairs onto the base of the waterfall . There you can clammer on the rocks for better photos of the waterfall or catch the sea waves crashing upon the rocks . After which you climb back up and then one can see stalls selling iced water with ice .The stalls also sold orange juice and ice-cream. Overall expect to spend about 45!minutes here .

The drive there was pleasant as you passed through many scenic places. Saw some homes with unique design.As we were at the start of Mysterious Road, our taxi driver switch off the engine and let the car just roll ?up the road?. Was wondering how could this happen!!! We witness some other vehicles doing the same. Our taxi driver took a bottle of waterAnd pour it in the middle of the road, the water didn?t flow backward. A group of Chinese tourist ,were doing the same thing, the guide say it?s a scam.  But the truth is ?Optic Illusion ?Nice backdrop of mount hallasan

The dragon head lava rock was indeed a sight to behold, jutting out of the cliffs. That is if you could catch a glimpse of it amongst hordes of tourists jostling for a vantage point to capture it on their phones, with selfie sticks flailing about.Being only the dragon head, it was quite a pint size cliff, and there was only a tiny area /platform from which to view it.To make the most of our drive there, we walked several meters down a stepped path quite close to the waters and enjoyed our moments there on the rocks.

The coastline along the bottom of Jeju-do, near Seogwipo is truly beautiful. Such clear blue waters and jagged, unusually shaped rocks and little rock pools everywhere - they look as though they were made for people to swim in! Oedolgae is found along this coastline, and while it is really only mildly interesting (it is just a strange-shaped rock sticking out of the water - apparently once scared off invading Mongolians), it is worth seeking out just to walk along the paths in the park near it. The rock pools along the coast line here would be perfect to swim in, in hot weather.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.

The cave is very nice, different from all other sights in Jeju. It?s a short walk but the ground is wet inside and can be slippery, also a bit dark in certain places. Wear a hoodie as water drops from the cave roof. Not recommended for people with mobility issues.Once inside, the sight is beautiful, it?s an amazing work of nature.
The bus was on the road with engine off. Instead of reverse it moves forward (the road is on uphill). Water was pour on the road and it flow upwards, against the gravity of the road.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The building itself was amazing and the indoor gardens were impressive. You can take an elevator up to the 5the floor lookout for a nice view through windows that need cleaning. The outside gardens were mixed. Japanese garden was the nicest overall but smaller than I would have guessed. The Italian and French gardens were impressive by scale alone but the details were far under kept. Green water, weeds??? And I between the larger gardens were under kept areas like a? garden that looked lame at best.? With all that it was still worth a quick stop but don't get your expectations too high.

The building is attached to the   jeju tourism   board (or something like that). It costs about 4 or 5 000 won to get in  then handed a coupon for a discount at the cafe or any of the products. The children enjoyed it as they got to make chocolate for 10 000 which included a take home mold. The museum isn't much to look at but just enough to make your mouth water. It is close enough to all the other activities in the area  if traveling with kids  this is a good   trade off   point to let them have some fun.

The bridge is in vicinity of my guesthouse and also the Cheonjiyeon waterfall that we visited before the quick stop. It was around sunset when we arrived there. There are free parking onsite. The bridge itself is just average, but it was a nice stroll to Saeseom Island.

The bridge is beautiful to look at, and provides a nice walk to an island that provides more opportunity to stroll near the water.? Big tourist attraction, and if you prefer staying away from the crowds, you may not enjoy this.? Great picture taking venue, and it doesn't cost anything, except a little workout for your feet and legs.

The Botanical gardens is set up in to different gardens and a large doom/ indoor area set up into zones. The plants on show were very nice but I have seen a lot better. This could be because of the South Korea climate. Look at the surface and it's well kept then you notice dirty water in the ponds. What I did enjoy was watching some of the workers weed some of the areas they are so methodical. As we were part of a day tour this was just one of our many stops and our time was limited. Perhaps I would have enjoyed it more if I didn't have such a tight schedule. I would rate this attraction as Good but there isn't a good rating and average would do it a disjustice. I thought the entrance fee to be very high considering the country it's in. You don't pay much more to go in Kew Gardens, London's Botanical garden that can actually take you days to get round.

The best we have seen in Jeju.Though the water was a bit too cold for us to swim, it's great for wading during low tide.You can even rent clear bottom kayak to paddle around.There are lots of convenient stores, burger and coffee places and other local eateries around there.Definitely worth a visit.

The best waterfall to visit! Don't waste time to other waterfall, this is the best one. I managed to see rainbow at the waterfall was simply amazing! Made the whole trip worthwhile! Just wear the right shoes there as there are some rocks to walk on before getting close to the waterfall

The beautiful white color of the sand comes from the large amounts of crushed seashells that have been mixed in with the sand. The long seashore stretches for 9 km and has cobalt colored seawater and evergreen forests scattered around the vicinity, making the scenery very beautiful. Just off the beach is Biyangdo Island. The white sandy beach is about 20 meters long, and the water is 1.2 meters deep with no sudden drops. In the evergreen groves, there are plenty of convenient facilities and campgrounds for visitors to use.
The bears are adorable! It is also a 10 min walk from the cheonjeyeon waterfalls, alive museum and 3100w away from the cliffs!

The beach was fine and no rocks, but a lot of seaweed. The water was clear and very shallow, so it's good for kids, but I was a bit bored since I like to play in the waves.I think they should clean the beach more often since I found too much trash around

The beach was almost empty when we went there. It was sunny, quiet and very nice. The beach is very shallow, so it requires like a hundred meters of walking to reach a place where a grown up guy's feet don't touch the sand anymore. It was the perfect beach for just walking around in the shallow water. I would absolutely go there again. We took a bus from Seogwipo (＿?洹?ъ), which took quite a while but they're not expensive. And the drivers are crazy so be prepared for a thrill ride!

The beach is next to the main hotel area and suitable for swimming. It has soft white sand, mixed with some lava stones (where small crabs hide). At my visit it was almost empty even though the water was warm and very clear.
The beach is family friendly with shallow, calm and beautiful color of turquoise water.  White soft sand.  My kids had so much fun snorkeling and chasing small fish for hours.

The beach has beautiful, clear emerald waters (the pictures doesn?t do the place justice as its much better experienced in person), and a really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries. We got there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. Near the beach there are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice. Easy to hail a taxi there too for those who wants to travel to their next location  by cab. Parking lots available too for those who are driving.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.

The beach has beautiful, clear  waters, and really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries and tea.We went there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. There are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice near the beach . Easy to get a taxi there too. Parking lots are available too.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.
The beach by bus is easy to get to the bus stop is located about 1 or 2 minutes away, the beach is clean and the water is lovely and blue

The area of the beach is nice but the sandy part and the open water space is soooo small... You cannot even go for a swim here. The water was dirty and full of water plants. I honestly thinking every beach in Europe is way more attractive than this. Italy, Greece, Croatia....Have they actually seen clear azure waters?! If this is jejus prettiest beach then im really sorry for koreans
The admission to this waterfall for adults is 2000KW. It was very overcrowded, which caused the time to be rushed. Worth seeing, but come early in the morning to beat the crowds.

The actual Hyeopjae beach, at the north end of town can get very crowded, but is close to the cafes on the main street. Personally we prefer the Geunmung beach end which is to the south, just past the Hallim park entrance.Both beaches are stunning with turquoise water and great views out to the island. The beaches shelve very gently which makes them great for kids. Geunmung particularly is awesome for the kids as it has little bays and rock pools too.

Tested on the car that we rented~N Gear and the car really move up slope~Tried it with water too, but did not see the effect~Not too sure if it cos the sky is dark~ Go at night if you rent a car~ Can reverse the car as many times as you want~

Taxi took us here as part of a few hours tour.  It's a pretty waterfall, but I thought Cheonjiyeon Falls was more impressive with 3 layers so if you are nearby, it's worth going, however, if you only have time to go to one, I'd choose the latter :).  Both have small entrance fees per person.

Taking a quick ferry ride will bring you to a breathtaking place called Udo Island. Rocky coasts, beautiful beaches, and crystal clear waters are what you will find on this little farming and fishing island. I decided to rent a bike on my trip and wander around the coastline. In my opinion, it was the best way to see the island. Amazing photo opportunities and tons of places to get some fresh seafood along the way. The clear and shallow water is great for children to play in. Tons of little tidal pools as well. Biking allowed you to be outside and experience the people and the culture of the island. It is probably not a place for people that do not enjoy the outdoors or those that are afraid of a little bit of exercise!

Take your time and enjoy the views. After rain, the waterfall is very pretty and worth the walk from the car parking area. Vendors sell drinks and traditional snacks at various spots and there are many photo spots.

Summary: You have to go here if you're on Jeju. But what can I add to the many reviews already here?The signs to the women's diving show are very clear. From the ticket office, just follow the signs down to the beach to the left of the peak. If the only way to make the show is to sacrifice something else on your itinerary, I wouldn't do it. But it was pretty cool if you happen to be there at the right time. You see the divers actually catch live octopus right in front of you.I recommend taking a snack up to the top and enjoying it there. There are plenty of places to sit down at the top and relax before you head back down. Also, definitely take at least one bottle of water if it's a hot day. You might even want two.If you plan to catch a taxi from this site to somewhere else, you'll have to walk just a little ways. We asked a taxi driver who was waiting on another family where we could get a taxi, and he told us where to walk. We had to wait about 10-15 minutes for one to show up that didn't already have people in it, but they always drive by eventually.

Suggest to start early, before 7am. We started at 7am, and managed to reach the summit before 1pm, but had to descend before 1.30pm. Took a total of 10 hours, up and down. If I can do the hike, anybody else can too, for a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Remember to do proper warm-up before starting and bring along enough water to hydrate yourself. Proper hiking shoes are important and hiking sticks are definitely helpful.
Such a unique place as the water falls directly to the sea. Not far from the city centre, definitely worth to visit.
Such a great waterfall in Jeju island, it's good to be able to take photo with this Mother Nature. You will not be regret to climb down and up to the waterfall. A place that must visit.

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Spent the day here after going to to the Tuff Cone. I like how they have a lot of business by the beach and how the main beach is enclosed like a cove.  You have either the option to pay to sit under an umbrella, I believe it was 20,000 KRW for all day or you can just go find a shaded area to sit by the rocks.  We chose to latter as you wouldn?t be in the sun and didn?t have to spend the 20,000 KRW.  The water is beautiful and clear, there are plenty of lifeguards at the beach, and it?s a family oriented beach.

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.
Spectacular waterfall! Definitely worth a visit. If you are staying in Tae Gong Gak Guesthouse, the waterfall is just a 10-15 minute walk away :)

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.

So we visited this beach in May, so it wasn't super warm. We arrived, wanting to sit on the beach in our swimwear, take a dip for a bit and enjoy the sun. Turns out most people there only went to this beach to take selfies...?Luckily, off the main beach, to the right side down some steps, there was a quiet area. We decided to sit there and have some time to ourselves, rather than be in other's people pictures. That was a great spot, with a marvelous view of the mountain and the beautiful blue water!

So I read a review that the hike up Hallasan was not very difficult so I thought I could do it in my Asics running shoes...well, I don't recommend that you do the hike up Hallasan without proper hiking gear.  Pack lots of water and food so that you can replenish yourself on the long hike up.  We went in early October and it was warm so dressing in layers was a godsend.  The route we took was to take Seongpanak up to the summit and then take Gwaneumsa trail down.  Taking Seongpanak to the summit took approximately 4.5 hours with 1 lunch break at the 3rd resting place before the summit. The resting place had washrooms and also a snack bar.  I saw people with cup ramen etc. Be prepared for the washrooms to be stinky.  It's the nature friendly kind.  The last stretch up to the summit on the Seongpanak trail is quite steep and some parts very rocky.  But the view makes up for it all!  Instead of hiking down the same trail, we came down the Gwaneumsa trail and wow, the views were breathtaking.  There were times when I had to stop and just take in the view just a bit longer because it was so beautiful.  T he Gwaneumsa trail doesn't have as many resting places so use the washroom when you can.  It took us a total of 9.5 hours to hike up and down Hallasan and I would do it again the next time I am in Jejudo Island!!

So happy we took the time to make the climb.  It's a lot of stairs to the top, so I would suggest you take along some water, and possibly some snacks, so you can take a rest part way up.There is one way up, and another down, which keeps things moving quickly.

So everyone says it would take you an average of 50 mins to do one round. I travelled with 2 elderly folks and it took us almost 120 mins so they wouldn't feel so physically stressed. In a way, walking with them was a great blessing - the multiple stops gave me many opportunities to go trigger happy on my camera and to enjoy the breeze. Do note that even though it gets hot during the climb, it is advisable to bring a windbreaker at least. Leave your bags in the vehicles if possible and go appropriately dressed. The climb is easy - mostly gentle gradients and low and even steps  - and there is even a rest point midway for you to purchase mineral water at 1000KRW. It was not crazily exorbitant. There is a toilet midpoint along the ascending trail and one towards the end of the descending trail. If you are planning to see the women divers, check with your guide so you hit at just the right time. They were diving at 1.30pm and 3pm that day and we managed to catch the earlier slot.

Small confession: it's the only museum we've visited in Jeju so I can't compare it to others and say it was better, BUT the museum is great. It was something new and an interesting experience even for my parents who are in their early 50s. Overall, I do recommend you to go there. FYI: there aren't places there where you can refill your bottles with fresh water.

Small area with lovely white sands - not good for swimming on a windy day, but the views are great and there were no crowds. Some small food shops close by and you are close to walking trails and terrific rock scapes by the water. Loads of plastic rubbish and litter take away much of the beauty of the place, but it is still very worth a visit.

Since Jeju is best travelled by car, the mysterious road (it's actual name) is definitely worth checking out. Putting the car on the apparent downslope in neutral gear will make the car move backwards and vice-versa...freaked us out until we discovered the optical illusion behind it. Be careful of all the other cars trying it out as well as pedestrians attempting something similar by pouring water onto the road surface.

Should go and visit this museum as it forms part of the culture of Korea especially the women divers of this island is very brave to dive into the sea for food. In the past, they wore normal hand made diving clothes and dive in to get food. They did the same thing when it is winter time and imagine the water is freezing cold. Right now, they wear normal diving suits but the tradition still lives on.
Several nice waterfalls around here. This is one of the nicest. Swimming is not allowed, but you can cool down anyway, so nice for kids as well!

Seonpanak is known to be the more difficult route, however both to the summit have their difficulties. Seonpanak definitely has nicer views than Gwaneumsa, thats why we chose to walk down this trail, as your back is facing the beauty on the way up. This route has TONS of rocks which make it hard to balance and hike without the proper shoes. There are 4 or 5 base camps, only one offering water, and one with (disgusting) squat toilets. It took about 3 1/2 hours to hike from the summit, to the bottom. My legs are KILLING ME. But, it was worth it!

Seongsan Ilchulbong Sunrise Peak  is a UNESCO World Natural Heritage formed 100,000 years ago by an under water eruption.it has the best view of sunrise.The peak is about 600 ft above sea level and takes an hour to reach the top. It has a beautiful view .

Seongsan Ilchulbong is certainly the top scenic spot in Jeju island. It?s basically a crater formed from volcanic eruptions, so it?s definitely has geological phenomena associated on top of being scenic. We drove from Jeju city to Seongsan for about an hour. There?s ample parking spots and entry fee is only 2000 KRW. Hiking involves climbing lot of stairs and takes about an hour to the top. We had a 2 year old with us and we could easily pick her and go to the top. I recommend carrying water and small snack items for energy. View from the top is very beautiful and obviously you see the crater when you reach the top. I think it?s top 3 spots to visit in Jeju Island and definitely a must if the weather is nice. Bonus if you during sunrise or sunset!! There are coffee shops (starbucks, McDonald, Paris Baguette etc.) and some local souvenir shop at the entrance. Enjoy

Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone that has been formed from not so old (5000 years old) volcanic eruptions. It is 180-meter-high and one can walk to the top. Note that it has been well accommodated: there are stairs starting from the bottom to the top so that the walk is fairly easy. It takes about an hour for going to the top and come back, depending of course on how long one stays up-hill to enjoy the view. The view is the main thing here. It is just amazingly beautiful!First of all, one should pay attention to the different rock formations, some of them, featuring interesting shapes (see one of the two pictures I shared). Second, it is really great to stop all along the way up to enjoy the view from Jeju (see the second of the pictures I shared). On the top, one gets an amazing view on the other side (i.e. the sea). I was there in the middle of the day (there was no other way out in my case), but I can fairly well imagine the extra in being there at sunrise or sunset.Finally, note that there is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, I strongly recommend this place and the walk. One moreover should definitely try to be there at sunrise/sunset. Please make sure to have enough water (it was really hot on the day I walked there) and be prepared: it could be crowded. The place is quite popular. There is a good reason for Seongsan Ilchulbong to be one of the top attractions of Jeju Island.

Seogpanak is an awesome hike, can def recommend it! It takes about 3.5-4h one way, without long stops. Bring enough water and food with you and there aren't any shops. Toilets are unfortunately not clean, so you may want to bring some disinfectant lotion and/or toilet paper.The first part of the hike is easily accessible, the latter part less so. You're walking on lava / stones most of the time so not really recommendable for people with weak ankles. Overall the hike is awesome and def worth a day's trip!

Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ? Check out of hotel for catch your flight back home.Have a safe and enjoyable holiday!Telephone Numbers of Attractions For GPS:Citrus Fruit Museum - 732 2114Geomun Oreum - 7108981Joongang Underground Mall - 723 1510Jusenggeolli Cliffs - 7381521Lotte Hotel - 731 1000Alive Museum - 805 0888Trick Art Museum - 787 8774Seongeup Folk Village - 787 1179Traditional 5 day market (Jeju-si) - 7435985Seongsan Harbour (Ferry to Udo Island) - 782 5671Seongsan Ilchubong - 783 0959Cheongyejeong Waterfall - 760 6331Cheongjiyeong Waterfall - 733 1528Jeongbang Waterfall - 733 1530Teddy Bear Museum - 738 7600Jeju Folk Village - 787 4501Jeju Sea-World - 784 2333Aqua Planet Jeju - 780 0900Manjanggul Cave - 710 7903Oedolgae - 760 3033

See other reviews on rubbish, food, clothing, water etc Travelling from seongwipo - take bus 782 (stock up on snacks/lunch at the convenience store nearby if haven't done so already as your options are limited once you get there). Bus Tickets cost 1800 won per person one way. Purchase tickets from ticket office or bus driver (take small change) and the trip takes around 30mins, dropping you off right at the entrance of the walking trail. (take bus 781 if travelling from Jeju city). Take the 781 bus to return to seongwipo.

Samchoon (Mr Kim Si-Nam), was our guide for a 2 day taxi tour in jeju! Samchoon was super friendly, considerate and warm hearted! Samchoon really felt more like family to us!Samchoon texted me 2 days before to confirm the time and location of pickup and asked about my itinerary and gave suggestions on the order of location we should visit first. Samchoon made sure we get the best experience we could have in jeju!Samchoon was very well prepared. In his taxi, he had prepared water, phone cable for charging, wet & dry tissues, umbrellas, raincoats and even torchlights for caves.First thing he told me was that we didn't have to worry about time and that we can take as much time at any location. He wouldn't rush or give us a time limit. So that we could enjoy every place to the fullest. Samchoon even said that he will not charge us extra even if we exceed 8 hours, he said that he would want us to enjoy and not feel rushed. Samchoo said he was a photographer in the past and actively helped to take beautiful pictures throughout the 2 day trip. He knew exactly where the spots to stand so that the pictures came out amazing!Samchoon was very accomdating to our changes in the itinerary he gave suggestions on alternatives. Samchoon knew that we like to take photos to so on the last day he brought us to see the sunset so that we could take nice pictures! True enough the sunset and view was breath taking! Samchoon is really familiar with all the places and routes and the rides between locations was really smooth and comfortable! Samchoon even has a 40 year accident free award!To Samchoon, A very big thank you for making our jeju trip so fun and enjoyable! Thanks for taking such good care of us! We will miss you and the beautiful Jeju island! Will definitely go back to look for him when in jeju!

Rented the ATV for 3hrs40m for 45, 000won and that was the most fun we had on our trip so far. The island is small so we ventured the coastline stopping to see the beautiful clear waters,  rode on horses and took photos by a quaint lttle lighthouse. The peanut ice cream was a little disappointing as it was more icey and the paeanut taste was barely there. The people in Udo are really warm and helpful.
Really nice waterfalls. Awesome view of the beach from the top. Entrance is just 2,000 KRW with 50% discount for military.

Really enjoyed watching how the water flowed into the sea. Interesting. Pretty much that's all you can do with a Waterfall. Beware though, the steps to climb back up from the Waterfall are quite steep, so if you're traveling with elders and kids, be prepared to walk up.
Quite windy, nearby Hallim Park and HyeopJae beach. Camping available. Showers with cold water for 2000 won. Foot washing station. Small convenience store.

Put your rented car on neutral going   uphill   and experience it. Mysterious probably because for most it?s a baffling experience having your car in neutral but going uphill, backwards or forward ? hands off the wheel and feet off that pedal. The place is on the way to Jusangjeolli by way of the Mount Halla route from Jeju town. 5-10 minutes (no crowd here) and you have covered one of the ?touristy? sites in Jeju. A woman attempted to see what would happen with a plastic water bottle placed on the road, nothing did.  Why would any vehicle with so much metals built into it got pulled but not a plastic bottle? Go figure. I have encountered a similar experience at a site in Saudi Arabia near Madinah which has a longer stretch for that ?mysterious? experience.
Pro: Great caves, delicious hallabong icies, beautiful water liliesCons: Quite expensive, a little bit dated, the peacocks look sickly

Pretty waterfall. It?s easy to get to, a short walk brings you there. Unfortunately you aren?t able to get into the water. This waterfall is more accessible as compared to Jeongbang waterfall. So for older folk and young children, this might be more suitable. I prefer Jeongbang just because I get to play in the water. Admission is 2000 won for an adult.
Pretty good stuff for an accessible waterfall. The surrounds are pleasant, it's cheap to get in, but it's  busy in the summer months.

positives: truly beautiful and amazing views of nature scenery and the waterfalls. also, one can take a leisurely stroll in the attached garden park. entry fee was only 2000 won.negatives: there was a bit of a crowd the day we visited, although it was still manageable. the entrance to the falls could be tricky to find if you planning to go there on foot from Seogipwo town. DO NOT follow google maps as it will only point you to the exact geographical location of the falls. You should walk down along taepyeong road until you see the bridge and the sea. cross the bridge and you will see a big carpark. the ticket office will be on the right side, near 7-11

Please visit this place only if you really love and in great passion to help preserve the nature. This attraction requires reservation as it only allow 400 hikers daily. There are 10 sessions and 3 different trails, a one-hr one, a 2.5-hr and a 3.5-hr one. All hikers will be lead by a center guide. Though the guide speaks only Korean and knows only limited English, there are signage and descriptions on each special location.We joined the first session and started at 9. We were required to arrive at least 10 minutes before 9, then bought the ticket (2000 won each) and showed the tickets to the Information Desk. Then we were given a badge which we needed to put on all the time and returned to the Desk after the hike. No food, including candies and gums, are allowed. Only water, without colours or tastes, is allowed to bring into the site. There is a water machine inside the Information Desk.The   Gotjawal   forests, grow in the center of the Geomunoreum crater, are very dense and luxuriant. While you can only look from the outlook points at Sangumburi 掠긷訝 and Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone 掠길ε뷴낡, this activity is an authentic encounter inside the crater, with the geological formation, vegetation and traits of lava activities

Please note that in Winter (Starting from Nov), they prohibit people from going up the mountain at 12 noon. So please plan and at least reach the entrance before 12 noon! We arrived at 11 and we didn't manage to go all the way to the summit. It was a pity. But we were greeted with great scenery as we made our way to Witseoreum rest point. It's a UNESCO site, and I think the people there took great effort to put wooden planks and build the almost endless stairway for visitors to climb the mountain. We took about 2hours to reach Witseoreum because we were taking so many photos along the way (and the stairs are really quite tiring!) There's a shop that sell coffee and cup noodles at Witseoreum but there's always a queue to get the cup noodles because the weather is cold and everyone feels like eating it! Good to pack some water and kimbap to keep you full as you climb the mountain.

Pleasant hike with young children, remember your water it was very hot on a mid august afternoon. Not too difficult a walk a few steps but enough photo shots to break it up for the kids. The view from the to is excellent out over the crater , to udo and remember to look at the pyroclastic cones behind you on the mainland. Don't forget the temple at the bottom in the car park worth a look.

part of the rock was eroded. it appeared more like a rabbit instead of dragon head. Suggest to go to Heopjae beach which is 5 minutes walk or next to Halim Park. It is overwhelming with crystal clear sea water fine sandy beach, and unique volcanic rock formation within your reach.  It is free and really worth going. The intercity bus will stop right in front of the seaside.
overly touristy entrance, path to waterfall messy. sight nothing special- at least in gloomy weather

Overall a clean, well laid-out museum at a very reasonable price at 9,000won each for adults.- Not as many exhibits as we’ve seen at the Smithsonian in DC or Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola but still worth the visit to learn about Korea’s aviation history- Placards translated into multiple languages - Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese. - We don’t have kids but it seemed there were a large number of child friendly play and exhibit areas.- On the third floor was a go-cart type racing track and pizza cafe. It was about 30,000won a person so we didn’t try it but it looked cool.- From the 4F observatory you can see Hallasan Mt, the tea fields of O’Sulloc, and Shinwha Theme And Water Parks.We spent about an hour there in total.

Out of the 3, this is the most dangerous but also the most fascinating, mostly due to the old lady divers at the bottom selling freshly caught seafood. So fresh you can taste the salt. Waterfall is beautiful on it's own, the trek down is pretty steep but easy. Only concern is once you're nearby the waterfall you have to hop onto the rocks to get closer, which can be pretty dangerous for the elderly, kids or those who are not sure footed.A must see if you're into waterfalls.

OUR TRAILS: Yeongsil trail (up) - Eorimok trail (down) Based on advice from friends, we (four of us) opted for the 'easiest' Yeongsil trail to embark on our climbing adventure.. (personally, my friends and I do not think the hike up was that easy). To save ourselves from walking woes (about 2km from bus drop-off point to start point), we got a cab (from Seogwipo; about KRW25,000) to drive us right to the start point, where a cafe is located. Upon arrival, the temperature was about 6 degrees with strong wind (downtown Jeju was about 13 degrees). We immediately purchased head scarves and gloves for the climb.The beginning of the trail started out easy but not much of colorful scenery (thou it was still autumn). The steps got steeper and steeper at about altitude 1,300~1,550m. These was the part where I guessed we stopped several times to gasp for air. And that was only halfway of the climb! After the steep climb, we reached the easiest portion of the entire climb. The boardwalk to Witsae-oreum Shelter. A place where we could no longer differentiate the sky and the sea, it was a great place for us to take a group photo (with Mt Halla peak as the background). When we reached the shelter, all of us dashed for quick toilet break and joined the queue to purchase some instant noodles and energy drinks. The very optimistic us then rest our feet till 4pm and made our way down the Eorimok trail. Going down the trail within 1.5hrs (before the sky turned dark) was crazy. There were just too many steps or uneven routes to descend. However, the consolation was the different colorful scenery from Yeongsil (many oreums could be seen). Our fastest speed at our physical condition then, we took 2 hours to descend (I guessed we were the last batch of humans) and the sky has already turned dark when we finally reached the exit at Eorimok trail. There was no more bus nor taxi but thank god for the kindness and efforts of the nearby workers; they drove us to the foot of the mountain and got us a cab. Without them, we would never return back to our guesthouse safely. God bless them!LEARNING POINTS & OBSERVATIONS 1) Yeongsil (grand) and Eorimok (colourful) trails offer different sceneries. 2) Always double the time/ distance, advised by a Korean. (LOL). They are fast walkers and climbers. Few occasions, we managed to reach our destination after 2x their estimation.3) Saw many Korean seniors and children ascending/ descending Mt Halla. They lead a healthy lifestyle!4) Do not stop for photo taking. Take few shots and proceed with the climb.5) Lessen individual's weight for the climb. Forget about DSLR and tripod! LOL.6) Apart from a solid windbreaker/ jacket, small haversack with water, museli bars, gloves, scarf and hp are a must. Hiking sticks are recommended.7) Experienced strong telecom signals up in the mountains.8) The only toilet (after the starting point) available can be found at Witsae-oreum Shelter only (No tap for hand wash).9) Rubbish (@ Witsae-oreum Shelter) can only be thrown at the exit only. 10) Not to proceed further and U-turn if very tired. Because descending can be more demanding and tired too.11) @ Witsae-oreum Shelter, all climbers have to proceed down the mountain by 4pm (October). Please refer to Mt Hallasan's website as the information are very accurate and informative.SUMMARYWe took more than 6 hours exploring these two trails. Of course, time would be lesser if we did not make many stops along the way.  We were gasping for air while climbing up Mt Halla but the overall scenery was really breathtaking. Despite suffering muscle pains for the next 5 days, all our efforts were worth it.RECOMMENDATIONHighly recommended if individual is fit, adventurous, loves beautiful scenery and has time on his/ her plate. Personally, I recommend to teenagers and above. : )
Our taxi driver brought us there and be our camera man, this is the only waterfall that meet directly to the sea water.

Our stamina is not so good so it took us 5 hours round trip for Yeongsil Trail up to Witsae Oreum Shelter and back. There was no Ramen available at the shelter so if you plan to go, better bring lunch box, you will be tired and eat a lot anyway. There are plenty of hikers from old people to children so you wont get lost, even if you want. Yeongsil trail has 4 parts of itFirst part is wooden steps, you will pass some creeks and a lot of shade / trees.Second part is the most strenous part. Lots of rocks and steep climbs , so watch your step. There are some observation deck for you to take photos and rest. And more wooden steps with crazy inclination. After you pass the big rocks crossing,(third part) it will be open area with no shade and this has the best view. And the most leisure part because its flat with almost no inclination. There is water fountain where you can fill up your drink for free. Walk 10-15 minutes from the water fountain and you will reach Witsae Oreum Shelter. Tips : Use sunscreen all over your body, even if its windy and cold at the beginning of the trail, when it reach the open area with no shade, the sun ray will hit you so hard. Wear hat. My scalp got sunburnt. Even better go with long sleeve and long pants. Go very very early like 7 am because the parking lot will be full later.

Our guide dropped us at Seonimgyo Bridge at around 8am, and said he would pick us up around 11.30am.  3.5hrs for waterfalls?  I thought he must have made a mistake...Surprise surprise... We enjoyed the morning stroll across the park near Seonimgyo Bridge (with autumn leaves still visible in end Nov).  After a million selfies, we made our way to the 1st waterfall and was awestruck!  So beautiful!  Well strictly speaking, this is not a waterfall but a lake of some sort.  But who cares about the misnomer?To reach the 2nd falls, there is a well-marked trail.  A medium-distance walk with its fair share of up and down slopes.  Not arduous and I would definitely recommend it.  The waterfall is not Niagara, but I found it pretty in its subtlety.The 3rd falls has a warning - the trail may be difficult for children and elderly.  Since I am neither, I had assumed incorrectly that I would find it manageable.  Wrong!  It was a very very long way down (which was fine), and an equally long long way up (nearly killed me).  Was it worth it?  I am afraid not... for the 3rd falls. So my recommendation would be to visit the first 2 falls, but give the 3rd a miss (unless you want a workout).

Our guide brought us to this place, let us alight and asked us to observe the strange phenomenon. He switched off the car engine and we saw the car still moving uphill without the engine switched on. He then demonstrated by pouring a bottle of water at one spot along the road and we could see the trail of water wriggled its way uphill without the application of any external interferences. The phenomenon was strange and unexplainable. Was it that a magnetic force beneath the earth on this road had triggered off that momentum? My guide did not explain and I could not find any explanation on any of the signboards around the vicinity. I remembered few years back when I was in Shanghai, I visited the mausoleum of the great Chinese revolutionary martyr, Song Qingling which was located at the western part of the city. Prior to her demise, she had requested that her body be buried at this cemetery site beside her late parents, the influential and rich Song family. I was astonished to learn from our tour guide and saw with my own eyes the strange phenomenon of the cypress and pine trees planted around the mausoleum was bending inwards and downwards from all angles towards the direction of the cemetery site where her body was buried. It was not just the left rows of trees, not just the right rows of trees but the trees planted at all the other corners surrounding the rectangular burial plot that were seen pointing inwards and downwards with the focus at the burial ground. The lush green trees appeared like bodyguards saluting, bending their heads and standing humbly for her directions. My guide informed us that the cemetery was a specially chosen grand and auspicious geomancy burial ground and that account for the strange phenomenon. The Chinese believed that if your body is buried on an auspiciously good Fengshui geomancy chosen ground, your future generations will benefit and prosper. I am not an expert in Fengshui and was hoping to get a scientific explanation for the weird phenomenon. Right here, at this strange mysterious road in Jeju, I was also trying to observe if the trees growing around the vicinity of the mysterious road bend towards and focused at the core center where the strange phenomenon occurred but I could not see what I saw at Song Qingling's mausoleum. Both strange phenomenon seemed to be unrelated in their nature and in terms of scientific theory of explanation that a strong magnetic force beneath the earth is in operation. The `Bermuda Triangle' is also another unexplainable phenomenon whereby it was unexplainable as to where so many ships vanished in strange occurring environment. I had watched a Chinese TV series on science whereby the film director sought to provide scientific explanations to the many strange `unexplainable' and `supernatural' phenomenon around China.
