I really hope that some days, the same film director could incorporate the strange phenomenon that occurred at this mysterious road, the ship vanishing Bermuda Triangle and that of the Song Qingling's burial site in his series and provide a scientific theoretical explanation for the weird occurrence. The visit to this mysterious road had triggered off my curiosity and I left the place, confused and thinking of the limits in science.

Our guide added this to our itinerary and we were glad he did. It's a beautiful location and the waterfall itself is lovely. It can get a bit busy with Chinese tourists, so you have to pick your photo taking opportunities when you can, but well worth a visit.

Our favourite activity on Jeju Island! Pretty limited view from the top due to clouds but great experience hiking up and down the mountain. We started at 7:30AM up Seongpanak trail (181 Bus until trail entrance from Jeju City 3,000 won pP) and arrived at the top of the mountain three hours later (with very short stops at the breaking points).We then went down Gwaneumsa trail which took about three and half hours (felt a bit steeper) but definitely more picturesque! At the bottom there is the 475 bus (not frequent, ca. hourly but you can kill time at the nearby temple or little supermarket). The bus gets you to Jeju National University (1,200 Won pP) and from there you can take other local busses like the 365 (also 1,200 Won pP) which get you into the city centre. Most important:- Bring lots of water (we had 2 Liters each and easily finished it before the end), some people had no water or hardly any and where really struggling! No shops on the trail!- sun screen and a hat (although ca. 2/3 of the trail was covered by trees)- take enough food because you will burn energy! (Remember to take all your trash back with you as there are no bins/cans anywhere on the mountain).- good hiking footwear because you are often skipping from stone to stone- there are cut of points on both trails ca 2km (guess) before the top which you have to pass before 13:00 in August (so don?t start your hike too late). We saw some hikers that had to run in the lunch time heat to still pass the cut off point.Hope this helps!! Enjoy!!

Our family visited the Cheonjiyeon Falls on the first day of our trip. We came out quite late, around 5 pm and we decided to come here as this was one of the attractions that were opened at that time. The admission fee was reasonably cheap. The area was not that big as I imagined, you walk from the entrance to the waterfall and then back. The waterfall is quite nice to look at and I'm pretty sure it might look more majestic if you come here at night. Even though I came on a cloudy and rainy day, it didn't ruin the mood much, it makes the waterfall more mysterious and I liked the atmosphere.

Our family visited   Cheonjiyeon Falls   on June 8th, 2019. To get to the waterfall, you have to walk a lot. There were a lot of small markets that sold simple snacks, which was sweet, but the way to the waterfall was not worth it. Although the way to the waterfall was harsh, still the waterfall was beautiful. I recommend this waterfall to whom that likes walking. If your stamina is poor, you will be tired . I don't think the waterfall was worth walking a lot.

Our family spent much effort taking a nice family picture near this waterfall - and it turned out GREAT!! Hahaha... Nice place to go, for the sight, the EXERCISE!!But it can get quite crowded though. Older folks may find it hard to climb on the uneven rocks but they can get near enough for picture with the waterfall at the background. To get REAL near to the waterfall, leave it to the young ones!

Our driver/tour guide took us here on the way back to the hotel. Actually, he said it was his first time there as well. My 17-year old son and I felt the uphill rolling and it was a weird feeling. Not sure why it was doing it, but we saw some tourists pouring water on the pavement and watching the water rolling uphill. Many years ago, I took my son to a similar   mystery road   in Manzanillo, Mexico. Back then, may be he was too young to feel it, or may be I was a terrible tour guide, but this time he finally got it. So, it was fun for us to take the quick detour and had some laughs.  Oh, and it was free and there are road signs tell you how to experience the   mystery  .

Our destinations on Jeju were varied and sparse hence the need to engage private transport. We spent 4 days in Jeju and visited locations including Seongsan Ilchulbong, Samganburi Oreum, Jeongbang waterfall, Seogwipo submarine and Jeju Folk Village. We also hiked up to Sara Oreum, two thirds of the way up to Hallasan along the Seongpanak trail (we will try to scale Hallasan next time with some better planning).

Our 70 year old tour guide could climb these rocks to get here. The Grand Canyon of Jeju. Whilst it was breathtaking, I couldn?t help but constantly call out to the kids to be careful of the slippery rocks. There are life rings hanging on the cliffs but let?s be realistic. With currents that strong, if you fell into the water, the current would crash you straight into the rocks. We went early morning when the tide was out but could feel the tide level rising. Our guide wanted to go further as he said it was more spectacular.Make sure you go with good gripped sneakers and a jacket. You are on the edge of the ocean after all.

Optical allusion or not, this is head scratching. I stood at bottom and then put car in neutral, it rolled uphill. Best yet, poured water on road and it too flowed up?close to airport and worth the few minutes drive to see.

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.

One of the real highlights for my visit to Jeju Island. It's absolutely fascinating and I've been to a few different caves before. It's different because it's a lava tube cave and there are a few different information boards in there to explain the different features which helped to understand how it was formed. It's very well and cold in there so bring a wet jacket and comfortable walking shoes (waterproof/ resistant if possible) with good traction. There is a small descent but other than that it's rather flat in there so most people should be able to do it, just watch out for the wet surface. If you go to Jeju, you must visit this cave.

One of the nicest beaches I ever been too and I been to Aruba. The sand is white and clean, waters were shallow for great part of it. I wish I had more time to spend there. I just went but it was warm enough that if I wished I could have swam. I could see it being really crowded in summer. Loved it! Must visit in Jejudo.

One of the most visited Tourist attraction in Jeju, the Seongsan IIchulbong peak or the Sun rise peak was formed due to Volcanic eruption thousands of years ago. This peak has a huge cater in the middle surrounded by huge rocks making it look like a gigantic crown. In addition to this the other most sought-after attraction here is the old ladies diving deep into the water without oxygen masks to collect sea food. Twice a day a special show is conducted for the visitors.Though it was quite windy and cold when we visited, we were sweating a lot once on the top as we have to climb a lot of steps.Once on the top we were surrounded by the moving clouds, the experience which made us forget all the fatigue.We could not see the sunrise as it was quite cloudy when we visited, but as our guide informed, one can have a good view of the one during summer.At the base there are lot of eating joints which ensures everyone gets refreshed after a long trek.We thank our Jumbo taxi driver who shared the spare waterproof jerkins he had with him to wear when it started drizzling (Kin nam joon / +821046166650 / kimnj0424@naver.com)

One of the most popular trails in Hallasan National Park.To get here, take bus 781 from Jeju City. The fare was 1 800 KRW (the driver can give change). The journey is about 40 minutes. The stops are announced in English. The stop is Seongpanak.Set out early as you have reach Jindallaebat shelter by 1 pm in summer (12 pm in winter). Otherwise you wouldn't be allowed to reach the summit.The trail is 9,6 km long (one way), about 4,5 hours without breaks. The trail is in some parts very ROCKY so good hiking shoes and walking holes are strongly recommended. Don't worry you wouldn't climb alone. A lot of Korean will be faster than you.The view on the summit is well worth and rewarding.Bring water and sun block.You can buy a certificate for 1 000 KRW.
One of the most beautiful waterfalls in Jeju! I didn't ecpect it to be so nice! Definitely worth spending 45 minutes there. Good spot for photoes, too.

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

One of the best views on Jeju island. The climb is not that hard, my 7 year old daughter and 65 year old mom managed to do it in 25 minutes. 15 minutes to go down. Its all stairs, plenty of places to rest. There is a small shop with regular prices (yes they could have charged 5 times for a bottle of water but they do not do that so hurray for the owner) half the way. There is no shade at the top but the view is really, really great.

One of the best stops we made in Jeju. This rock formation is pretty cool and the stop is more worth it since it's a good hour's worth of walking and snapping photos (as opposed to a number of the really touristy places where it's just one kodak moment).Check the tides. The rock formation that people walk on are really close to the water, so if the tides are high, it gets slippery. Actually, some parts are slippery as it is.You have two options: going counter-clockwise, which ends up being an upward movement OR going clockwise, a downward movement.  The views are nice-ish both ways (personally the counter-clockwise views were nicer). More than that though, going counter-clockwise is a lot easier as the steps are easier to deal with moving up. Many of the people coming down were cursing the steep rocks and were tired even before it began for them. Might not recommend this if walking is difficult for you as climbing and hoping around is a must. Little children were around and they seemed to be enjoying themselves, but none of them were younger than 3 years of age.No bathrooms once you enter the formations, but ladies will sell you food and drink (mostly alcohol) if you're interested in a seaside meal.

One of the best beaches in Jeju, we loved this place for its cobalt colored crystal clear water and fine white sand and the view of Mount Hallasan.Our kids enjoyed playing in water and collecting seashells, while we enjoyed walking along the shore.Food stalls, shops, umbrella rentals are available.

One of the 3 major waterfalls in Jeju, the water falls from a height of around 22 meters and thus named Cheonjiyeon ? meaning Sky connected with Land. Though not as majestic as Cheonjeyeon , this water falls is as beautiful when it comes to its natural surroundings . A very well laid out path ensures one can enjoy the long walk from main entrance to the waterfalls. As there is not much climbing to do, tourists of all ages can visit this place.
One of few beach that the water is many hues of blue (usual sea colour of jeju is dark blue). The beach is quite wide, so you can enjoy strolling around while drinking freshly pressed orange juice.

One of 3 famous waterfalls in Jeju, along with Cheonjiyeon Waterfall and Cheonjeyeon Waterfallis but apparently the only waterfall in Asia to fall directly into the ocean.  Definitely worth the short climb down to get as near the fall for nice shots and a sea splash. If lucky, you might even catch a rainbow over the fall.  Walking shoes recommended to navigate the rocky boulders.  Do come early before the tourist horde arrive.  Adventurous hiking enthusiasts can continue to the Olle trail from the carpark entrance.
One letter difference, but these are not the waterfalls you want to see. Better to go to the Cheonjiyeon falls which are 10 mins east. These ones are very average.

ON the winter time it is better to go in the morning as the sun still arise. It is beautiful. There is some ahjumma who dived looked for seafoods in the cold water.   Daebak   Cool!! as the temperature could be below 0 degrees or even minus. My eyes even already tear up because of the cold wind. Overall I loved it!!

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

On a family trip, my fiance and I had one day to ourselves and we ended up here for a couple hours. We love being near water, so this was an easy choice for us. The natural pools were so clear and beautiful, even though it was November and cold we went into the water and enjoyed freezing our butts off from the water and wind. Still such a fun and unique experience we'll never forget. Because we came in November there were only a handful of people that came and went. We definitely recommend checking this place out for a hour or so. I imagine it can get pretty busy during the summer time but youd get to enjoy the water much more. Even in the cold weather it's worth just checking out if you're around the area.
okay, it's just a rock. but the view is amazingly beautiful. the azure water really make me want to jump in. this is a perfect spot where you should spend your evening

Okay judging by the other reviewers, I must have been there on a great day. The water was crystal clear and the experience was amazing. There is a convenient store located right on the beach for all your necessities (i.e. beer etc) and convenient ice cream and restaurants. While it was a little far away from where I was staying, it was an unforgettable experience and was my favorite part of my trip to Jeju.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). Oh gosh!  This is definitely one of the must-sees of Jeju Island!A short 15min (mostly flat) loop, and you will be rewarded with babbling brooks and crystal clear waters overlooked by towering cliffs.  Best of all, this is off the beaten path, and there were virtually no tourists around.  Oh...the tranquility.Some parts of the walk involve jumping from rock to rock in the streams.  Not a problem generally (my kids found it fun), but if you have mobility issues, you may want to bear this in mind.We would like to thank Victor of Jejueco Suites for helping us discover this hidden jem.

Ofcourse is a nice waterfal but i think it was a little overrated. Like everyplace att Jeju you have to pay a small entrance fee (2000 won) and then its just what it is, a waterfall. For sure you can take some nice pictures but thats it.

Of all the waterfalls we visited, which included all the major ones, this waterfall takes the cake. How to get there:It is easy to reach, a quick walk from anywhere in Seogwipo to the shore. Of all the waterfalls we visited in Jeju, this was one of the ONLY that you could actually play in!  The others are beautiful but this one allowed visitors to swim and play!  Not many people did but we had a BLAST enjoying the cool water on the hot summer day!

Oedolgae can be translated to   lonely rock   is one of the most popular attractions on Jeju Island. We took a taxi there and walked back (45 minutes) to our hotel in Seogwipo.
nothing special, just a waterfall. spectacular? not really, but it is special as it is one of the few waterfalls that directly falls to the sea

Nothing really special to me as I don't really know how to appreciate small waterfalls :p Interesting as it's the first waterfall I've seen that falls directly into the sea. Not that spectacular. The walk to see the waterfall is about 10mins one walk. This is one of the star attraction in Jeju but I don't find it very interesting.At the entrance, there is a long queue for squid biscuit. It's worth a try.

Not sure about summertime, but at Autumn that's powerful enough waterfall. Nothing special, but good.A short trail to reach that. 2ooo Korean Wons is cost of entrance. Mandarin sellers are all around :)
Not spectacular. Small waterfall. OK for first timer to look see. Flowers were beautiful, better than Camellia Hill. The bridge after the first two waterfall was pretty.

Not many things beat the sound of a waterfall, and this one is no exception. Not just a temple, but amazing views of the coast and water. The temples are free to enter and offer an amazing experience. A must see if in this area. Plenty of drinks, food, views and restrooms. Only con is the steps are not very friendly. We have a 3, 7 and 8 year old. 3 year old needed carried.

Not a must-visit but it's good place to explore for first-timers. The stretch of road looks like it's uphill but rolling a water bottle will make it roll uphill instead of downhill. No trip to Jeju Island would be complete without a trip to climb Seongsan Ilchubong (sunrise peak). No point come to this fall, not even if you are nearby. Not worth your time. I walked all the way in just to find out that The waterfall is so small. I don?t see how they made an attraction out of this.

Nice wiev, cold water. Not that big but worth going in hot summer days. Easy to reach, wide car parking. Entrance fee than stairs to reach sea level. Fun for kids, if you dare:...... get into the water!!!

Nice walk down to the falls. Well organized. The waterfall is not spectacular, just a stream of water coming down the mountain. 20 years ago the made electricity here, but the whole installation is gone now.

Nice looking beach and lovely water, but don?t recommend if you want to swim. Never been to a beach where the sand had a huge net over it. But then I'd never been to a beach in Korea. We werent too upset because we kept our shoes clean for the museum we visited next. My wife and I hiked the Seongpanak Trail up Hallasan in late May 2015. The trail starts relatively easy but gets more difficult after the first shelter. Make sure you have the rights shoes as the rocks can be pretty hard on your feet. This is a long climb, and for most of the trip you will be in a forest. Keep your eyes open and you may spot some of the elusive small native deer, we saw three on our trip. I am not in great shape, so it was a tough climb for me and took us 9 hrs. round trip. The rocks are really hard on your feet on the way down. Leave early since if you don't make it to the last shelter before 1 PM they will not allow you to ascend to the summit. The last shelter sells ramen and water and a few other items, but be aware you are expected to pack all of your own trash off of the mountain. There are some stores and shops in the parking lot at the entrance to the park, we bought some kimbop for lunch and packed it up with us. This is the tallest mountain in South Korea and the summit provides wonderful views at over 1900 meters high. Climbing Hallasan was a   bucket list   item for my wife, who was born in South Korea, and a memorable experience.

My wife and I hiked Hallasan last weekend, which was our first trip to Jeju Do. We've lived in Seoul for 5 years and finally made that trip south. We decided to take the Seongpanak Trail since it allows you to get to the top. Overall, the hike was great - beautiful scenery (although it was a hazy day for us so visibility was limited), challenging hike and it's something that will take up a whole day. We took a different trail down once we reached the top and the views were nicer on that one. I think there are only two trails that go all the way up. We're not hikers by any means so our legs were pretty tired on the way down the mountain. They estimate 8-9 hours total but we did it in 7! Be sure to pack some snacks and water as there's not much available on the hike. There's a small place at a checkpoint a couple hours into the Seongpanak trail where you can get some water, ramen and chocolate bars (along with some basic hiking gear) but don't expect much. We had only taken water with us (rookie mistake) and I was wishing for some extra snacks on the way down. There's also a store/small restaurant at the first entrance to the hike so you can stock up there. Overall, it's definitely worth doing as its one of the main attractions on Jeju.

My wife and I ascended Mount Hallasan in April. While it was cool in the morning, we soon had to tie our sweatshirts around our waist. We weren't sweating as much but we're winded trekking 9.6 kms. While that distance may seem daunting, the Seonpanak trail was not too difficult, even for non-trekkers like us. There are steps and wooden walkways but in parts you have to tread carefully as it gets rocky. The difficulty level steadily increases as you move upwards. But if you take little breaks and keep proceeding, your effort will be rewarded with breath taking views from the peak. Well, the Crater lake didn't match our expectations or the pictures we saw online as it had dried up. However, we were well above the cloud level and there were green and brown hills as far as the eye could see. A word of caution - there are no sources of water on the way up (although it says there's portable water at the half point) and no shops once you start the trek. So carry energy drinks and bars, at least 3-4 big bottles of water (per person) and Jeju oranges. You can get all this from the shop at the base, at the start of the trail. Go on, enjoy your trek and discover pine trees, maples trees, black Chipmunks and much more

My partner & I chose park our car at seongsan harbour so we could take the ATV. To our dismay, their ATV can only carry 1 driver. Therefore we rented the sheltered scooter that can sit 2. My husband and I made the mistake of 1. Going there at 11am instead of bright and early 2. Not driving all the way up to the entrance of the trail. There are in total 4 trails and we took the one that was located south west of the island. We had to hike 2.5km from the car to the entrance before we even begin the trail. The hike is tiring and if you are doing it leisurely like I was, I will suggest good hiking shoes, hiking sticks and lots of water. We did not reach the crater and turned back after reaching the rocks. The view was still wonderful and the weather was great but I do not encourage beginners like me to go all the way. Do what you can and enjoy the view. Its better that way.

My husband and I climb Mt Hallasan today. Though my feet are sore, i thoroughly enjoyed my hike. The trail was really well marked and in good condition (Both Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa Trail). We entered via Seongpanak Trail (9.6km gradual inclination - trail was a mix of wooden steps and rocks). It was fairly easy till Jindallaebat Shelter, and then it gets tougher but doable. We started at 8am and reached the summit at 12 pm (we?re not athletic and not super fit). We then descended via Gwaneumsa Trail (8.6km) at 1 pm and arrived at the trail head at 5.30pm. Gwaneumsa is more scenic as many blogs have mentioned so am glad we descended using this trail but Seongpanak trail is easier and is nice as well.Useful info:We took the public bus from Jeju-si city and back. Journey was about an hour one way and we found our way fairly easy with the Naver Map app. The public bus from Gwaneumsa trail entrance only runs on weekends I believe. Bring snacks, lunch and water for your climb. A windbreaker is advisable if you come from the tropics like me.Good shoes are recommended as you?ll be walking on rocks a lot of the time. Bring a raincoat too as there aren?t many shelters.Start early, you have to arrive Jindallaebat Shelter by 1230hrs (you cannot proceed after that) and you must begin your descend by 1430hrs.

My family explored this location during a family trip to Jeju Island.  My toddler twins are three years old and, with help, were able to navigate the entire length of the cave and back to the entrance.  The lava caves are fascinating and it's a good workout.  It is very damp, cool, and dripping inside - make sure to bring a windbreaker with a hood.  You can do it without (we had just sweaters) but it would have been better to be wearing that.  Plus, there are extensive puddles so waterproof shoes are a good option!  My only suggestion would be to increase the lighting a bit so guests can really appreciate the lava markings - the atmosphere with the low light is nice but I wanted to see more of the characteristics of the lava versus a non-lava flow cave.  Some people brought a flashlight and that seems like a great idea.  The price was very reasonable and there is a restaurant and clean restrooms.

My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

Must do if you enjoy hiking! We climbed to the peak of Mt Hallasan, South Korea's highest mountain.  Took us 3.5 hours up and 2 hrs down at a reasonable pace hike.  Beautiful autumn/fall leaves starting to changing colour (we hiked on the 13th Oct).  Despite what is advertised, there is a water station on the way up so you don't have to overload on water.
Museums of pushies, teddy bears, etc... Diff kinds of pushies, made into a safari, underwater, kingdoms, Olympic and more

Mt Halla is known as Korea's jewel. It is its highest peak. And well worth the trip to Jeju. We left Seagwipo very early (around 7 am) and took bus 182 (181 also goes there) to Seongpanak because we wanted to climb up to the peak. We got to the mountain around 7:45 and started the hike. The weather was super nice when we left, and we planned it that way, because we wanted to at least get some nice views of the city, and while at the summit. This is a long day of hiking, so be prepared. Bring snacks (and a trash bag, because you have to carry everything back down), and water. There are 2 checkpoints along the way that have bathrooms. The last checkpoint sells ramen for about 1500w with hot water. This is the checkpoint you have to get to before 12:30. We made it there around 11, and up to the summit before noon On the Seongpanak trail, there is also a lake with an observatory that's worth the detour.The last part of the hike up to the summit is pretty steep and rocky, so watch your footing, especially because you might be tired from walking up. Wear adequate footwear, make sure they are sturdy and comfy!Unfortunately, we didn't get that lucky with the weather as it because overcast as we were getting up there. I guess it really depends on your luck (the next day, it was super clear! Damn you Mt Halla!!) hahaha.We took the same trail down (from the summit, there is another trail, but no buses stop there. And this is where your comfy shoes are a must. The hike up was not bad, but the hike down, was torture! Our feet kept hitting the front of our hiking shoes, so we were bruised and hurt by the time the hike was done. We were also sore for the next 2 days (and we're pretty sporty, but we rarely walk for 8 hours) Overall, it's a great hike. The trail up is covered by trees, so it is cooler than it seems, but there are still some great views, especially with the fall foliage. We'd be surprised at the range of people walking the trail, old and young love to hike up this trail, and we understand why!

Mr. Lee was an excellent tour guide! On time for both full day tours, patient and takes great pictures! As a solo traveler this was a wonderful experience in Jeju island mostly because of Mr. Lee. I did both East and West coast tours with him. Car is comfortable and very clean! He was very flexible with the itinerary and squeezed in his favorite waterfall in Jeju my last day! He was awesome and I highly recommend this tour to explore Jeju!

Mountain HallasanIt was a fanatic walk ever, friendly people all around. Unfortunate in Jeju island, English is not a common language, road signs, information boards are all in Korean, mainly people speak Korean, surprisingly, you might find people speak Japanese and mandarin. There are a few entrances from around the Moutain, make sure you do your research.I believe there are more than 4 entrances. Due to limited time, I have chosen the easiest and fastest trail (Eorimok). You could take public transport or driving. There is parking 17mins walk, and payable parking 1000won, save your time. Be prepared below- Go toilet, do the necessity before you start - Go to visitor centre get a map and find out more. ( e.g. if the convenient store is open?) - 2-3 hours walk one way, the washroom only available in the destination. Choose the hiking shoes. (Bad experience, my sport shoes are ruined) - Best to start your journey at 8 or 9 in the morning, as early as you could. If you are doing other trails, allow more than 8 hours. Eorimok entrance, it took me 5hours, I took a slow walk. - Be warned after certain time (14:30, not certain), you may not be allowed to go in. - Bring a lot of water, or bring enough cash (drinkable water is not enough to supply to public), bring your own food if you don't want to end up eating spicy instant noodle.- Store only sell, instant noodle(super spicy), and spring water. (Limited to 2 portions of instant noodle per person) price: 1000won for instant noodle, 1000won for a bottle of water- Bring extra clothe to change, bring a light weight jacket. (It is a bit chilling on top)- Bring insects repellent spray or lotion- Bring wet tissue and normal tissue- Bring a bag for rubbish, smoking and littering are not allowed.The place is well protected, please respect :)  Voila! Happy Journey!

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Many tours include this spot for tourists.  I personally find it over-rated.  It is an illusionary experience where the environs surrounding the particular stretch of road gives one the impression that it is not what it is supposed to be.  Some guides would even spill water on the road to experiment.  Interesting - yes, but I would not include it as part of a tour itinerary.

many themes in the park such as tulip garden, Canola, rapeseed, cherry blossom, more than 100 years old bonsai, folk village with traditional restaurant 竊fresh grilled mackerel竊, well decorated water pond, peacock and bird park and many more. The folk village still maintain the culture of living that one should not miss. One need half a day in completing visiting the park.

Many of the paths are laid with big rocks, better to have a trekking pole (or even a pair) with you to keep your balance and to aid your walking up and downhill. It is not an easy trail but the view up on the mountain is rewarding. If lucky enough, can see sea of cloud hanging near the mountain, it's beautiful. The spring water is fresh and pure, and is a good source to refill your bottle before going downhill. It is really amazing to see the locals, many of them middle-aged, walking so fast and can carry so many food up to the mountain. At the rest point, it was a feast for the eyes to see the food they brought up for hiking - kimbap, jokbal (pork knuckle),...and many more.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.
Lucky to visit on sunny day, was slightly crowded but still managed to still the cliff. The volcanic structures were very interesting and you can see the clear blue water.

Lovely place (June). Water was warm and beautiful. Walk a little bit and you will find more places and not so crowded. There aren't many restaurants for foreigners. I recommend to try the burgers at the red container (can't remember the name). If you don't enjoy fireworks, better don't do after 7pm. There are better things to see and do in Jeju but some people don't understand that!!!

Love this beach! Plenty of restaurants and convenience stores nearby. My only complaint is they wanted to charge 20,000 to use an umbrella for the day. Too expensive! In Haeundae I've never paid more than 5,000. Anyways, the water is nice..And it's less crowded than other beaches. :)

Located on the west side of Jeju, this gem has a very nice view, were you can see some mountains across the beach. We went there during late spring, the water was very nice while basking in the sun. There's not much people there, however when summer comes, most of them will swarm all over the place. It's better to go on spring, you can enjoy the view and just listening to the water splashing on the rocks. This is one of the best beaches in Korea.

Located on the far western shore of Jeju Island, Hyeopjae receives a fraction of the visitors compared to other well-known Korean beaches. My wife and I enjoyed a spectacular sunset here after a fun half-day spent swimming and exploring the volcanic tide pools. The beach is superb for three reasons. 1) Great location (not a city-beach), scenic view of islands and volcanic rocks strung along northern portion of the beach.2) Relatively few visitors compared to other Korean beaches3) Water and beach are clean, shallow water makes the beach great for families

Located on the beach, you must go down and walk on lava stones, it's a nice place, many people take photos in front of this waterfall that comes out from the massive right on the beach, this place is connected to story of a Chinese traveller speaking the elixir of eternal youth, he hoped to find it on Jeju

Located in the middle of the Jeju island, it's a very beautiful and well managed National Park. Unfortunately, we were too late for hiking to the Hallasan and back. We decided to hike to the top of a directly opposite and much lower peak. It was easier and we were almost alone on the whole trail as well as at the peak. In the end, we had a nice picknick at the tourist and information center. If you really want to hike to the Hallasan itself, arrive and start as early as possible, be prepared with enough water, some food/snacks and other important hiking utensils.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Located in Seogwipo, it is the only waterfall in Asia that falls straight to the sea. You may cool your feet in cold river water (or even the whole body if you brave enough). There are 3 women divers who offer to try raw seafood for 20 000 won.

Located at the east coast of Jeju island, it is a crater of an inactive volcano lying out to the sea. A short walking trail to the top where you can get a beautiful view of the coastline. Next to the peak, you can watch the actual women divers show. Only two performance per day ( 1:30pm and 3:00pm ). Remember to bring sun glass, hat, sunscreen and water as the areas are wide open space with little cover. If you are thirsty, you can always try the famous local produce (fresh mandarin juice and mandarin ice block).

Located an easy walk from the Seogwipo Harbor, these waterfalls and surrounding area are quite pretty, and certainly worth the easy, pleasant walk to see them. It was only 2,000 won to enter the are, and about a 5 minute walk to the actural waterfall. As someone who loves swimming in natural water, I was a little disappointed, because you can't really swim here. It was quite crowded (when I went in early August), so all my photos are full of other people. It wasn't necessarily a beautiful nature experience, so in that way a bit underwhelming, but again, worth a look.

Located 25mins from Seogwipo, at the Jungmun area, this is a dramatic stretch of coast with hexagonal rock columns. They result from the rapid cooling and contraction of lava once it has met the water of the sea.There is a viewing platform right behind the Jeju ICC (convention centre), from where to admire the coast and the formations in particular.To access the platform, park the rental car at the designated park (KRW 1000) and buy the access tickets (KRW 2000). The platform is always busy and with all the selfies going on, one struggles to look at the rock formations.

Living in Hong Kong we're pretty used to tough hikes - this one is a little difficult but manageable for anyone who is reasonably fit or has some hiking experience. Whilst the incline on this hike is never that steep and the first part of the trail is easy with paved walkways, the terrain for the second half is pretty hard going with lots of rocks and boulders. We managed in trainers but hiking boots with a sturdy sole would probably be better, and some may feel more comfortable with poles. But it's ABSOLUTELY worth the effort for the view. The crater lake is quite impressive but more stunning is if you look back on Jeju from above the clouds. Took us about 6.5 hours up and down but bring plenty of snacks as there is only one point where you can buy water and some dubious looking packet noodles. Oh and there are no bins so bring a bag for your rubbish. If you are in Jeju and like hiking, you must do this as it's a great sense of achievement when you can say you've hiked S Korea's highest peak!

Likes:Beautiful light blue waters, similar to HyeopjaeLess people during the July/August period.A few empty umbrella spaces for us to squeeze in (thanks to less people)Can rent floatablesDislikes:No wavesRecommend to others?Yes, if you want to go to a beach on the west coast of Jeju

Less than 15 min walking, the waterfall was beautiful, and there?s food photo spot where everyone line up when u get to the waterfall. In my opinion, the admission fee was little too much for the quick walk and waterfall view. But good to visit once!

Last summer, our school went to Hamdeok Beach as a field trip. The place was conserved very neat and clean. All of my friends were excited to play around. The beach was enormous and the water was green and blue, looking amazing. However, the weather made us suffer very much. The temperature on that day went up to 29 degree, and all of us were almost burned. I highly recommend that you guys go to Hamdeok Beach when the weather gets cooler.

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.

Kim Tschang-Yeul museum had a stylish exterior designed by Tadao Ando.? Featuring the namesake artist Kim’s sculptures and paintings, the museum is very chic for a government run museum. Kim’s trademark is the water drop, which is added to what would otherwise look like rather plain patterns painted on canvas.? The sculptures mostly contained large glass water drops.? Some of the outdoor sculptures complement Ando’s architecture very nicely.? This was an unexpectedly cool visit.

Just try to get past all the tourists and walk down to the waterfall, bring a rain proof jacket :) went in November and waterfall was relatively small, probably more awesome after period of heavy rain. Great selfies ;)

just take a bus within 10min. i reached this beach. that was one of beautiful beach in jeju IMO as clear water with white sand also seaweed. it also has some windmill near around. except the beach that has a camp site. quite comfortable & relaxing place.the water was cool & the view also beautiful. it has many small crab,conch & fish. many people busy with them. ha. just no luck on i don't have a pretty sunset. anyway, worth to take time for visit here after cave & maze.

Just one waterfall, not much of a sight to behold. However, it's the only touristy waterfall that doesn't have stairs, so if you have knee problems, this is waterfall to see. On the plus side, the souvenir store near the entrance has good merchandise at good prices. They had nice hats on sale when I was there.

Just makes you wonder nature creativity. Need to have camera able to take photo in low light.Note: Long walk, water dripping, uneven and dark pathway. However don't loose hope, beautiful @ end of tunnel. Worth the efforts.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).

Just did the hike on 30 March.Trail: seongpanak up and gwaneumsa down. Goes to summit. (highly recommend to do this trail Cos going up by gweumusa is really steep though the view is nicer for gweumusa) Time taken: 4.5hrs up and 4hrs down (please go early and check the time that you need the reach the shelter and summit by.  Think should be by 1230 reach shelter and by 2 to leave summit) Weather: good.  Cold in the morning but as you hike,  you will perspire and definitely need minimum sweaters. I was only wearing teeshirt and windbreaker. In the end only tee-shirt cos it's getting warmer and you climb and when the sun is out. Need crampons?  Yes!!! It helped alot especially at the icy areas both going up and down. Not too sure where you can buy it but I managed to rent it from my hostel. Though I did see people without it,  and they did just fine.  I was wearing track shoes kind. So crampons helped alot!  How to get there: I went there from Jeju city and took bus 281 from bus terminal to seongpanak bus stop. Coming back from gwaneumsa trail: took bus 475 back to jeju  national university and change bus 360 to Jeju city.  Please check with bus driver or use kakao map/bus to help as Google Map doesn't seem to help much with he routes. Bus 475 have some timings going back. You can always find out from the visitors center at the gweumusa base. It is situated at the left side as you make your way down passing through the car park.  Shelters and food: not sure if I did miss it..  But I didn't see any food vendors, drinks stall as I hiked up and down. So I was really thirsty as the end of the trail. There's a small restaurant and a convenience store at gwaneumsa trail end. So please bring ALOT of water like at least 1.5L. Bring along food to eat up there and also plastic bag to put your trash and there are no rubbish bins around.
just climbing up in darkness is an experience by itself. wear good shoes, warm clothes, water and some munchies. take your time coming down and enjoy the scenic beauty.

Just came back from the mountain hike. See absolutely nothing......the mountain is bare with nothing, no flowers, no grass, no green leaves trees and no waterfall despite we took the most scenic yeongsil trail to the top......rather disappointed but we just take it as an exercise. For those who r interested in the mountain, pls choose the right season if you want nice scenery

Just an ordinary road but countless of tourist buses and vans parked along it. Explore the mystery personally to appreciate the magical side of it. We'd done all tricks - stopped the car engine and let it roll uphill, poured water on road and see the trail running upward, closed our eyes and walked both ways where we found the gravity is totally against us !! Great fun ~!
Just a waterfall into the ocean. If you have 30 minutes to spare, it would be a nice stop. Otherwise, there another waterfall nearby.

Jusangjeolli cliff is so worth visiting, to see such unusual yet impressive volcanic rock formations! It's really busy with other pushy tourists trying to get a photo, so I would recommend going early in the morning or later in the day. The rocks are a bit like a mini version of the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland. The water there is such a beautiful clear blue, just like the rest of the coastline around Jeju island.

Jeongbang Waterfall was near our guesthouse and it was the first stop of our trip to the east of Jeju. You can climb through the rocks and take a photo in the middle the small pond, in front of the waterfall. The water spray catches the light and acts as a prism to scatter the light into rainbows..pretty

Jeongbang Waterfall itself is beautiful.  A bonus to see the Haenyo (women sea divers) set up camp at the base of the waterfall selling fresh sashimi from their morning's catch.  The entrance is a bit touristy with a small market trying to see you all the typical Jeju fare (famous hallabong which mine were deceptively switched to regular tangerines, hallabong flavored everything, grandfather statues...).  But what makes the stop worth it is the   other waterfall   just a few min walk down the Olle trail at the same entrance.  That one isn't nearly as tall but way more impressive in my book.

Jeongbang waterfall is a marvelous sight where you could see the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean. The only minus point is how I couldn't manage to walk or hop well from one rock to another so that I couldn't get to near to the waterfall. Other than that, everything was good.

Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest, walking through these wood is believed to enhance cardiovascular function and to prevent asthma and tuberculosis. This is the most famous forest on Jeju island and here you can taste mineral water that is thought to relieve muscle and gastrointestinal problem

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju Olle Trail is completely round the island broken up into 21 different routes.In total we walked about 13km, about 3.5 to 4 hours time taken. Photography time included.We started our walk from Hyatt Jeju along the Jungmun Beach (we did Route 8 going eastwards) heading towards the Daepo Pego (port) and ended our walk at the Yakcheon Temple.Ensure that you look out for arrows (blue&orange) along the ground and olle trail ribbons (blue & orange as well) tying on trees along the way. Terrain is very varied, from easy tarmac lanes to quite difficult lava rocks along the bays. Suggest you wear proper walking shoes. Bring along your own water & snacks. There are a few restrooms along the way. If you are staying around Jungmun resort area (many hotels there), take airport bus limousine no 600 to go back to your hotel. Its about 1000 Korean Won per person.Overall is an interesting walk because you will see village, seaside, port & temple along the way. This is one of the very popular walk in Jeju, so its like a   must walk   walk.. We just did a short segment of the Olle Trail & apparently other segments are even more interesting.. Check out some photos for illustration.

Jeju Island features a trail system that circumnavigates the island allowing the most highly motivated to hike the island, on foot.  If you want to see some great coast line and get the most out of a modest walk, look for trail #7.  It takes you along some great coastline with fantastic views of the cliffs, rocks and water.  In several areas, there are steps that take you from up high down to the surf.  If you stick to the trail, the elevation changes are modest and should be doable for anyone of moderate fitness.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.

I've done the hike from the trail head at Seongpanak parking lot to the summit of Halla-san 14 times.  The hike is about 9 KM to the top.  The trail is very rocky and vertical.  There are a few drinking water sources on the way to the summit.  As you get near the top, the trail becomes a series of wooden stairs.  The trail becomes seriously vertical about 7KM from the trail head.  It took me between 2 and 2.5 hours to go up and about the same amount of time to return to my car.

I've climbed Hallasan twice now, once in December and once in early March, and both times I took this route. This route is slightly longer than Gwaneumsa, but it's also a gradual incline with several easy portions. I took this route primarily because there is not a lot of public transportation available to/from the Gwaneumsa trail, plus I'm not sure I can do a steep incline the entire way up to the summit. For Seongpanak, you have about 5 km that are easy, 2.5 km that get harder, and then a pretty brutal last 2 km. Regardless, know that there are other hiking trails around the island and even around the volcano, but only the two mentioned above will lead you all the way up to the summit.Given some of the reviews I saw that are either inaccurate or not very helpful, I hope to compile a quick list to help you decide if this is something you want to do and if so, what you will need:1) It's definitely going to be an all-day kind of thing. You will be tired afterward, so you likely won't want to schedule too many other activities for the evening. Also, it's likely that you will be sore and tired the next day or two. 2) You need to start climbing no later than 8:30 AM. As several people have mentioned, you will not be allowed to access the last chunk of the way if you're not at the second shelter by 12:30 PM (this is winter time, so the schedule varies slightly from season to season... always check the Korean tourism sites).3) Even if it's sunny, there's a chance you might need crampons. In the winter months you will need them for sure, but even last weekend people were sliding down and falling repeatedly without them. I hear that it's even worse on the Gwaneumsa trail since it's a lot more shielded from the sunshine. 4) Bring food and water! The only place you can buy something is at the very beginning of the trail, and even then the options aren't fantastic. A little protein or fruit will go a long way whenever you're starting to feel tired, and it'll help you push through. Please make sure you do not leave any of your trash along the way; there are zero trashcans, so if you carry something particularly messy, you might want to pack a bag for the waste.5) Do not use the toilet in the first shelter! It's the worst smelling bathroom ever, which is rare for Korea since things are usually so clean... I suppose it's the septic system. I suggest using the toilets at the parking lot and at the last shelter (there are two). The first one is seriously a nightmare. 6) It's not an easy hike, but it's doable even for people who don't exercise strenuously. I've seen people carrying babies all the way to the top, and I've seen small children and old people make it, too. Definitely wear the right clothing, though, and especially the right shoes. If you're hiking at a time without snow, you will spend hours circumventing rocks of all sizes and ankle support will be extremely helpful for this. Anyway, thanks for reading, I hope you have a fantastic hike!

They will show us how to make   Omecha   which it the berry layer with honey and keep in the jar for conservative before consume it. It will definitely not take you more than an hour to see everything it can offer. It only has a couple of waterfalls, a huge bridge and a lot of trees.

it was just a super long cave that is really cold, perfect when you are visiting during the hot summers. Wear comfortable shoes because you will be avoiding water puddles, trekking on uneven rocky floors. Its just a super long walk in and out.

it looks just like any other waterfall. this place can be skipped if you have other interesting places to go, or you can just stop over for a short while.

It isn't very hard to locate this stretch of road, since you'll see numerous other tourists conducting their own experiments along the road, be it with the help of a rented vehicle, an empty beverage can, or simply water.Is the stretch of road as mysterious as it claims to be? it is Only waterfall in Asia falls directly to the ocean. Not that interesting, easy to walk down, a lot of kids and old people can visit.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before.
