I got 28 hour spare time before my flight to Dhaka in my last visit to Korea. When I got this break at the very last moment, I searched Jeju air ticket and hotel booking online without any delay. As I purchased it at the last moment, I had to spend USD 125 more for air ticket and hotel booking. Jeju is a rush destination in summer. It's is a fairly large island to cover within 24 hours. Thanks to TripAdvisor and reviewers for helping me to select Seongsan Ilchulbong and Hamdaeok beach from many other attractions.Tourists have time, usually visit Seongsan Ilchulbong before dawn to observe Sunrise. That why it is also known as Sunrise peak. As I did?t had that option in hand, I climbed it at afternoon. I took a taxi from my hotel at Hamdaeok beach and it costs around USD 28. Bus is always cheaper but I had only 20 hours left in my hand to catch my return flight. Sunrise peak entry ticket costs USD 2 for adults and USD1 for child. Most of the review I read earlier suggests it takes 20 minutes to climb on the peak but as an amateur I took roughly 40 to 45 minutes to climb. There are two wide and convenient stairway to climb on the peak. I selected the left side stairway and eventually it was a right decision. Because there is a small grocery in the midway selling soft drinks and water for those who didn't buy it from the base. As usual they charge double for each drinks but it was a life saver for me. When I came down from the other way I didn't find any shop like this. There are also a  midway station if you are tired want get refreshed for a while. When I reached on the peak I was almost exhausted. The view is literally breathtaking. I was sitting there more than one hour and a half as it is so charming that made for  forget everything else of life. I came down from the other stair way. The surrounding is so calm and comfortable that I stayed their until it?s dark. Tips: Try to book air ticket and hotel upfront to save cost. Rely more in internet than locals advise because there is a high chance of misleading information due to language barrier. I lost twice in the island for relying on them and lost around 3 hours of my precious time. There are halal restaurant ( Bagdad and Rajmahal) in Jeju island. 4 days are fairly enough to cover most of the attraction of Jeju. It costs total USD 400 all inclusive  for me for a quick tour , however if you are two them many cost will be shared within you. If I could catch the early morning flight from Gimpo airport at 7:30 am and save three more hours to arrive Jeju island then I could go to Udo island as well. I couldn't do that because I had to come from Suwon city. So if you stay at Seoul, you can catch 7:30 morning flight comfortably.

I found this waterfall a better experience than Cheonjiyeon Falls as you can go very close to the waterfall. Be prepared to walk down a lot of stairs and then climb over rocks to get close to the falls, so wear comfortable shoes with good grip. Don't bother paying for the museum close to the gate, it's a waste of time but only 500 Won if you want to.

I found this place by accident. One afternoon as I was shopping at Seogwipo market area, I happen to see the sea at a distant. I thought I'd just take a walk towards there. It was a lovely surprise, as I managed to get to this very much talked about waterfalls. The water actually drains directly into the sea, and not another freshwater reservoir as more commonly seen.There is an entrance fee and plenty of souvenir shops and eateries here. It's a beautiful sight and even better sound.... the sound of the water gushing down into the ocean. The mist from the pounding of the water is so refreshing. Be prepared to walk along some steep steps...not many but quite steep.

I found out about Love Land on Google during our cruise to Asia.  So when we landed my husband and I took a taxi cab there.  It was right next door to the Museum of Modern Art so we checked that out first.  And then we walked over to Love Land.  It could also be called   Happy Land   as we would every now and then hear an eruption of laughter from other visitors.  We were certainly laughing too.The sculptures in various poses of love were whimsical and clever.  It was a nice walk that took us about an hour and a half.  At the end we went into the shop where there were small dioramas and objects for sale.Volcanoes and waterfalls I have seen before.  But I had never seen a place like Love Land.  When we returned to our cruise ship fellow cruisers said   Why didn't you tell us?!  We would have gone.

I found it well boring to be honest. I prefer stuff like the lava caves and waterfalls - I guess I just like to be wowed. However it was a peaceful place and it was surrounded by lovely countryside. Maybe a place for a stroll with your loved one. Still if you want to get there from Jeju - you can get a bus 710-1 from the bus terminal. Note there are two 710's (assume the other one is 710-2).  It costs about 3,000 KRW (40 minute ride) and there is a designated stop about 3 or 4 stops after Gyorae Entrance (not junction which is 2 stops away). Note: Gyorae Entrance is a good stop to know about as it on the north - south road (Jeju-seogwipo) which is the 781/782 bus route.... just in case you want to go anywhere else after or get bored like me :)How helpful am I!

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.

I first saw this falls on the local map I received. I investigated and stopped there using the airport limousine bus route no 600. It is a short walk from the main road and when you get closer, the sound of the water guides to its location. The water falls over a short (50-100 m) cliff, but it is beautiful and ideal to take some nature pictures. It runs into the sea immediately and provides a picturesque scene.Be careful when you visit, since the railing on the sea side was broken and seems quite a safety hazard for me.This spot does provide you with the opportunity to take some awesome pictures.

I find it as an average, nothing special ... better to walk around outside the stone park,the surrounding is quite nice with traditional hall nice traditional look toilet (no hot water, water is icey cold) I came last month (early May)

I expected a longer walk for this, given that this is what Mother Nature had blessed us with, but this cave is only opened for the first 1km to the public. Still, it was an amazing sight (with the turtle-like rock formation and the various lava formations). Wear comfortably with a cap or hoodie as the cave will be chilly and the water will drip from above! Also, bring flash lights as it can get quite dark!

I enjoyed snorkeling at the place. Inside the water is not that colorful as some famous snorkeling spot around the world, but you will see very attractive black rocks and ecosystems only seen at Jeju Island. Also there is a nice trail following the coast with great view. Though you are not going to swim, it is still good to visit.

I do a fair amount of hiking in the Green Mountains of Vermont, and I found Seongpanak trail to the summit of Mount Hallasan to be enchanting and beautiful! Though the hike may be challenging for folks with knee problems, it is a very well maintained trail (though long) that is worth the effort.Start your day out early and bring plenty of water!

I did not see the point of this activity, was just in the area and decided to go have a look, was rather disappointing. The south side offers way cooler things like the waterfalls and the hexagonal rock formations. Difficult to get a decent picture as you can not get too close either.

I decided to see two waterfalls down south at Seogwipo! Jeongbang fall is one going into the sea.A bit rocky if you would like to have a photo been taken in front of it as close as possible. There are always many people down there, be careful of your steps when taking a nice photo!I like the fall as it?s open to the sea!

I completed every single course over a period of a year so the following comments are just my opinions. If you are staying for a short period of time in Jeju courses 6 and 7 are the most popular and will probably get the most from. Both are very scenic and you will get to see some of the major sights. If you start at one of the information sites, you can pick up a Jeju Olle guide which has maps and information of the trails, guides for the Buses, to get to and from the starting points. Also I'd recommend downloading Kakao Maps app on your phone and you can zoom in and see the actual trail that you are following when you are on it. It comes in handy especially for me when I made a wrong turn on my trips. If your doing the entire course I'd recommend buying a jeju Olle Passport. Carry it with you and get it stamped at the starting points and halfway way points of the trails. I was living near jeju city and caught most of Buses from the Jeju inter city bus centre. The 101/201 express buses will take you to/ or near a lot of the starting points but I'd recommend picking up the Olle Guide first and the info in that is invaluable.Most of the Starting points are close to the roads unless you are going to one of the 3 islands. I used booking.com most of the time to book places to stay overnight as I don't speak Korean. Jeju has a lot of places to stay and there would be abundant places to stay except for maybe a couple of the more remote locations on the trail. There are offical Olle trail Hostels throughout the trails to which are very nice. If planning for no Korean speakers just check before hand that you are not traveling on a Jeju holiday as a lot of paces close down and might be harder to find a place to stay. Of course take plenty of water and there's usually 7/11 of CV's around the place where you can get snacks to eat.The trails themselves are very beautiful , Different scenes ranging from Black volcanic rock on the coastlines, Forest trails, Beautiful beaches, Hill sides, a lot of Oreums (Jeju extinct volcanoes) small towns with a chance to see wildlife and a lot of friendly people. For myself my favourite trails were routes 11, 18-1 Chuja-Do island), 1-1 (Udo island), 7. For me the stronger trails were on the southern eastern point of the island starting from route 6 through to 15.Getting to the supporting islands it you might take note you will need your Passport to catch the ferry to Udo. You must show it when buying a ticket. There are a lot of ferries going most of the day to Udo. They have a very nice Peanut ice cream there. The smaller island Gapado at the time I went there were only 2 ferries in the day and its not the most reliable service and the ferries can be cancelled due to bad weather can be cancelled due to bad weather so check beforehand if you can. Chuja-Do island was one of my favourites. When I done it they had 2 ferries a day and you can not do the whole trail in time to catch the next ferry back so be prepared to stay over night. I have heard of instances when the weather turned bad and people had to stay a couple of nights on the island because the ferries were cancelled so just plan for that just in case. it is a beautiful Island though and one of my favourites.I would also recommend going and joining the Olle Walkers Facebook group. They take guided walks along certain courses and have great information about weather and so forth. all you need to do is contribute to the group from time to time.

I chose Seongpanak as the starting point from 7am, I managed to arrive the top before noon. I took Gwaneumsa to go down. This track is difficult than previous one but the view is beautiful. Make sure to bring lots of water and your own food.

I choose the most difficult route (Gwaneumsa Trail) as the website said it offers the best view of the mountain and I stupidly assumed their difficult is not too difficult if compared to Malaysia's route (because Malaysia's one is not a proper/well maintain path).And so I was wrong :p It is all the way up up up and up, stone path (which I hate most) and wooden staircase (so descending is definitely more blessing but very challenging to your knee). I hike @ 26 April, didn't get to see much fantastic scenery as I guess I'm not at the right season as I saw some other people's review they saw great scenery. So this was more like a physical training to myself. To train the mind especially. But, the sound of the wind is like ocean waves, this was indeed very beautiful, I even record it down during descending. It took me 4hrs 10mins to reach the top, in between there are... 2 toilets I think, and if you manage to reach samgakbong shelter (1500m) not later than 12.30pm (spring/fall) you are allow to continue to hike to the top, else you'll need to return. Cross this check point there is a spring water ahead before the bridge for you to refill your water! Then what's lying ahead is the super strong wind and the sturdy steep stone/wooden staircase path ==|Long story short:1) Hike at the right season I'm sure you can see more than what I see2) choose the trail wisely. I would say as long as you have a strong will, even you are not very fit also you can do this trail, just start little bit earlier than others to give yourself more time (say 5hrs to the top). 3) Make sure you are well equip to keep yourself warm. Windbreaker and glove is a must. I had 4 layers (t shirt, thermal, windbreaker & sweater & I was still shivering at top, the wind is just too strong that we couldn't even stand still) 4) Bring water, food, chocolate and candies! 5) Good shoes is a must for less struggling during descending & less stress to your knee. Personally I don't use hiking stick so suit yourself for this. 6) count the time and familiar with your own pace if you want to reach the top. Just make sure you reach the check point then you can take your own sweet time to get to the top.Last but not least, just don't under estimate this well develop stone & wooden staircase path. Although it's only 8.7km, 1950m height, it took me 4hrs plus up and 3hrs 15mins down (with very little time rest at top coz its just too cold!)Good luck!

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I came in October so i cannot swim here but seeing only the beach has satisfied me. It is a nice beach with white sand, water is very clean and clear. It would be nice if i can come back here in summer.

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

I came here by bus .. so I waited for the bus and cars to go on neutral and watch them drive up he hill hands free.Some people poured water while other rolled a water bottle.Since this attaction takes less than 15 minutes, i would suggest also going the Jeju Art Museum next door :)

I arrived to this temple because it was on my route between Seogwipo waterfalls. I was amazed. I thought I had seen enough temples, but this was something else. It is majestic with the palm trees and little ponds in front of it. This has been one of my favourite temples in South-Korea so far.

I and my boyfriend traveled here by public bus. We visited the place at the end of October not really December but I did a very late review. It was very easy to get to the place by public buses. The bus stop right in front of the entrance and crossing the street the take the return bus. I researched the bus number, it was wrong. So I asked the bus ticket woman for help and she was really helpful.It was a very challenging hike. Be prepared with a lot of water bottles with you and really exercises before the hike. The trail we took was Seongpanak trail, which is the easiest one. It was early of the fall season. Leaves started turning into different colors, chilling, not so cold, sunny and very enjoyable.We just finished 1500m of height and ate a noodle in a shelter. Then, we turned back (blaming non-stop walking in the previous days :D) and took a quick turn in a shortstop in Saraoseum (beautiful lake, nice view of the mountain).Overall, really enjoy it! Will try it again one day.P/S: it is a natural place so not clean bathroom. A very natural way of toiletry but I really don't like it but can't blame!!

I am traveling with my 79 years old dad who has weak knees. When our driver brought us to yongmeori beach, we have no idea what we are in for. Because of my dad, we chose to enter the beach on the left entrance and exit by the right entrance which we heard is the opposite direction of what most people would do. From the entrance, we had to walk down a very steep stairs which led us directly onto the beach. Honestly, the walk down the stairs was a bit dangerous as there was no railing or any safety measures. Despite collecting entrance fee, there are no staff around if you need help. That said, the scenery was stunning. The natural formation of the rocks was beautiful and the water was clear. For a popular tourist destination, this is also one of the cleanest I have been. You don?t see any garbage around. I hope anyone who plans to visit, continue to keep this place clean. As we had to walk slowly, we completed one round of the beach in over an hour.

I also went to Cheonjiyeon Falls, but this one was incredible. I found Cheonjiyeon Falls pretty, but it didn't feel special. This waterfall is loud. You can definitely feel the power. You can feel the mist and it is just awesome. The rocks are also really fun to play around on. I spent most of my time sitting by the ocean watched the waves crash on the rocks. It was really beautiful. While it is just a waterfall, there is more to do around this one than snap a photo. I definitely recommend this one.

I absolutely recommend you to take a day trip and hike up Hallasan if you are in Jeju. Even though if it takes the whole day, since it is about 20km walking, it is worth it. If you are in okay shape I'd recommend you to go up on the Seongpanak trail. It is longer but easier than Gwaneumsa trail. The hike has a lot of stairs, so don't expect climbing. Once getting up, the most thing that shocked us what the loads and loads of bugs, since we never heard about that. They don't bite but they do get on you which is annoying. That said, the view is beautiful, to the island but also to the crater. Going down I'd recommend Gwaneumsa trail since it is a lot more beautiful and more to see. It is only the first third part that is the hardest, after that it gets okay. Remember to start climbing early since you have to reach the checkpoint before a certain time depending on the year. It takes about 3 hours to get to the checkpoint so try to check what time you have to be there before. The time is there because it takes a longer time to get down than you expect. Also bring water with you. There is only one point where you can buy going up, and only one point where you can fill your water bottle on both trails!

How they get the cars, coaches etc up the hill with the engine switched off is a bit of a mystery,I thought some kind of electro-magnetic set up under the road, then if that's the case when people poured water onto the middle of the road surface, why did the water go uphill and not downhill. Do not think it is an optical illusion as it certainly was a hill that went up and down, I walked it !.

Hiked up to the summit via the Seongpanak trail. A 35 minute ride on the 5.16 bus from the Jeju main bus terminal drops you off right at the entrance to the trail. Great hike up. Took me a little under 4 hours including a 30 minute detour which breaks off from the trail to go see the Saraureom. This trail is mostly wooden steps. Both the Saraoreum and summit crater lake were dry, but still beautiful. I do not recommend relying on the   store   at the Jinderaebal shelter. They do have hot water if you want to bring your own instant noodle mix. Bring your own food and be prepared to bag your garbage and carry it. walked down via the Gwaneumsa trail which is a bit shorter. I defenitely recommend this since the trail also has a different type of scenery, including a beautiful bridge crossing. Not sure if there is a bus back to the city from the bottom of the Gwaneumsa trail, but by the time I made it down (3 hours) I was ready to take a taxi, one of many which are available which cost me 15,000 Won (about $ 15) back to the city. Certainly worth it. Overall, a beautiful and amazing experience.One last recommendation would be NOT to attempt this hike with less than proper hiking shoes.

Hiked to the top of Hallasan yesterday morning through the Gwanmeusan Trail - started at about 7:10am and were back in our car at 2:30pm - so this start and finish time includes breaks, and you'll need them even if you are in okay or good shape. It was a bit disappointing to see the majority of water bodies in the mountain are dry at the moment - just a few ponds on the early parts of the trail, and the crater lake at the summit, which we expected would be much deeper. The trail has a combination of dirt, rocks, and steps/bridges. I wish the steps and parts of the trail didn't include so many sharp rocks - your feet WILL feel them! We did the hike in running shoes because we don't have hiking boots here. I can see the climb being a lot easier with hiking shoes. Some parts of the trail are very steep so if you have serious knee problems, I don't think this is the trail for you. Do bring lots of water and snacks - we had two liters of water for each of us and I still think my husband got dehydrated rather badly. There is really nothing to eat on the trails so bring snacks. Visibility yesterday wasn't great - pollution has been pretty high in Jeju the past couple of days - but it's still a GREAT, BEAUTIFUL view from the top. I loved all the flowers you see growing in the rocky sides of the mountain in the last third of the trail. Very happy I did it and it's a great hike, but there is not a lot to see before you get to the top. We went down the same trail, so a total of 17.4kms. It'd be interesting to see what the other trails are like, but I don't think I need to summit again.

Hiked from the Yeongsil Hiking Trail Entrance (1280m) to Witseoreum Shelter (1700m). It was a total of 3.7km (one way) hike and took me 3.5 hours up.  Note that I do not exercise regularly and this was my first hiking experience.  I guess it is manageable for anyone as long you are determined to hike up regardless of your physical condition.  The trail was tricky involving a variety of tall rocks, wooden steps, pebbles and wooden planks, a tad steep at times.  My DSLR became cumbersome by midpoint that I've decided to use it at specific points for me to better soak in the sights and watch my steps at the same time.  The sights at various points are nothing but rewarding.A hiking stick and a good pair of shoes are definitely helpful.  Note that you have to bring your trash down after your hike!Bring more water and join the locals at various rest points with some snacks (eat what the Koreans do! Gimbap / tangerines / hard boiled eggs) and just immerse yourself in listening to their chatters while looking out far at the horizon!I would love to hike on the other trails of Hallasan again.

Hi all!, we visited this place on 1 July, 2017. It is indeed a good place. when you are almost fatigued with seeing big big places such as Seopjikoji, Seongsan sunrise peak, you can visit this place while returning to Jeju si. the entrance is really amazing. Lots of tall and large stones will welcome you. We took lots of pictures there.  There are different carvings of stones of different types. There is a gallray of stone-made sculptures. We also noticed a nice water reservior type of thing. Really nice place.

Heopjae beach is on the small side and the time I went there, it was pretty crowded. But nonetheless it's super clean and it's perfect for enjoying a dip in the ocean, taking pictures, some water sports and hanging out with friends. Going there at sunset during the summer months is even better!

Heaven on Earth - volcanic stone sculptures abound - every tree a bonsai - cedar, pine, maple and more.  Azaleas were in full bloom and a delight in colour.  The birds, in particular the white peacock who posed displaying all his feathers fanned out.  Then onto the water garden with its lotus blooms, fish and waterfalls.  I would do anything to have a garden like this in which to spend my days.

Have you ever seen a more mouthwatering set of pictures? ㄴ Today we are enjoying a famous traditional dish from Jeju Island, Black pork.  Thick cuts of juicy pork belly, cooked to a smokey crisp just how I love it. Alone the pork belly is enough to eat by itself and a side of rice. But we're not here to be basic, you either go big or go home, enjoy the side dishes that come with every meal.  For example bean sprouts, ssamjang is known as a Korean bbq dipping sauce. It was mildly spicy and salty flavor with nutty fragrant. And, most importantly it compliments well Korean pork belly bbq. Lastly the infamous cabbage Kimchi, enough of a kick but not too much where you cant taste the perfect blend of food. A perfect combination, Bon-Appetite!

Hamdeok is perhaps the most popular beach in Jeju but this was the first time I visited the island on summer during peak season. The beach is packed with families who took advantage of the low tide during the day (about ~30cm of water in a 50m stretch, at least on two weeks while was there) and let the kids in the water for a very enjoyable and risk-free time at the ocean.However I was surprised by the amount of   lifeguards   there. They will drag a security rope marking a no-swin zone after it starts getting   deep   (just after the water reaches your chest) which ok its a security measure specially with so many kids, but for adults who want to take a dip is horrible. They will start blowing their whistle and order you to go back even though half my body was above water.But the worst part is that they -- the lifeguards -- place beach umbrellas all across the beach and charge you ??20000 (~20USD) to open and use them! It's already very weird that the lifeguards are also operating a rental service at the beach, but thing is they will NOT allow you to sit anywhere near them without paying (even not using the damn umbrellas) unless you look foreigner (white) so they don't loose face. I don't so I got reprimended like if was a Korean and they wouldn't leave my side until I moved.Isn't the beach a public space? This didn't happen just once but every day during my time there, overall an awful experience due to these threatening and autoritharian lifeguards.

Hamdeok Beach is really splendid! Clear aquamarine water, super fine sand, mountain in the  background.... the view is to die for! You will find beautiful volcanic rocks all around the area. There's a bridge that stretches out into the sea that gives you an even more fantastic view. A must visit if you are in Jeju!

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

Hallim Park features an extremely interesting cave complex quite unique as it has been dug by lava, a traditional Korean village, beautiful waterfalls, a bonsai garden and a section with creative sculptures. The price is very affordable and you can also visit the beautiful beach opposite the park while you're there. Worth a visit if you have spare time on your hands as it is quite far from the main attractions.

Hallasan was a good challenging climb, with the hike splits into 3 parts. The first 2 hour or so, we were hiking through mostly level ground, some rocks and little steps. As we reach the middle ground, the trail gets steeper, more rocky and almost half are made up of steps, mostly made of rocks. Using a hiking stick at this time really helps in making the climb easier. When it rains, which happened the entire day when we went, the ground gets covered with puddles and pools of water, so it was extra effort trying to choose the rocks to step on to avoid getting our feet wet. Towards the top, there are flights and flights of steps, followed by a trail made of rocks where u have to use a rope to climb up the steep rocky surface. It was challenging but overall, felt good.As it was raining, we didn't manage to get any view of the crater or lake at the summit. But the sense of accomplishment making it up was great!The way down was more challenging as after a day of rain, the trail became wetter and what used to be steps, some were submerged in water. Hence, even with a good waterproof shoes, ur feet could still get wet. Also, note that the sky turns dark at around 5pm in winter and there's no lighting in the reserve. Hence, make sure u buffer enough time to reach the foot of the mountain before that time. Otherwise, u would be hiking in the dark. Nevertheless, there would be a ranger moving down the rail lines in a cabin moving on a rail line, looking for stranded hikers. So no need to panic. However, I would still recommend planning well, checking the weather and choosing a clear day to climb. Start early so as to buffer enough time to reach the 3rd rest station by 12pm, as anytime after that, they do not allow hikers to go up to the top. Think it is for safety reason to buffer enough time for the ascend and descend. Also, to wear waterproof shoes and if available, bring a hiking stick along. Do standby a raincoat in case of light drizzle. Also bring some food along. Though they sell instant ramen and some bento at the resting stations, it closes by 2pm or so and you don't want to end up hungry.  Lastly, enjoy the climb!

Hallasan National Park is a fantastic place to explore. Firstly, the vegatation between Spring and Fall is beautiful. As you hike to higher elevations the landscape and plants slowly change. Numerous rare and even some endemic species are found here. Concerning wildlife, what visitors are most likely to see are the Roe Deer. These small deer are found throughout the park, and as I hiked quitely we came upon 5-10 throughout our 6 hour trek.In 2007 Hallasan became part of the Unesco World Heritage site calle   Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes  . This honor is only bestoyed on the most unique and important natural and cultural sites on Earth. Hallasan is a geolocial wonder, and is comparable to some of the most iconic national parks in the United States. The park probably deserves 2 days as visitors will want to hike to the crater lake on Hallasan peak, but the entirity of the park holds many exceptional sites. Many trips to Jeju island are scheduled around their trek at Hallasan. Make sure to bring plenty of water, and keep an eye on weather conditions. Hikers must start early if they want to hike to the peak, late arrivals will not be permitted to make the full trek as it takes anywhere from 6-10 hours depending on your pace.

Hallasan is the tallest mountain in South Korea and even though I was not in the best shape .. i had to do it!  In preparation i got two bottles of small water, some snacks, and the clampers for the shoe.  There is a store beneath the mountain if you forget anything .. like a hiking stick or rain jacket on a rainy day.I started at 830 am because you need to get to a certain point before 12:30 pm during spring or you're prevented by the park rangers from going to the top.The last stretch was pretty painful as was the last stretch going down the mountain.On a cloudy / rainy day, there is nothing to see up top.  However, I did get a nice sense of accomplishment :)

Halla Mountain or Hallasan is one sadistic hike. For the month of May 2018, Gwaneumsa Trail is the only trail open that summits Halla. Seongpanak is having maintenance done.We did Gwaneumsa Trail... with one slow hiker... we got to parking at about 7:30am and we were walking by 8:06am. It is beautiful and green, especially in Spring. There is one restroom stop about 1/4 way and another 3/4 way at Samgakbong shelter. There was no other support. Take water, take food, take toilet paper just in case.READ: There is only one potable water stop. It is after Samgakbong about 3.5 hours into the hike at the last downhill before the bridge and start of final red part of trail. There is a hose at the corner at bottom os stairs before the bridge. Fill up here both going up and down.Also wear good walking or hiking shoes. We witnessed two people's shoes rip up and one guy had to walk back 2.5 hours with no shoe. There is no rescue for small issues. There is a supply cart that goes up once or twice a day but only for serious rescue. There is AED in Samgakbong shelter too. No food for sale when we went in April 2018.The reason for the difficulty is the climb and distance... mostly on volcanic rocks... large ones... and lots of stairs of wood and of stone.We left at 8:06 and back in the parking lot at about 5:30. All day event. 9.5 hours going slow up Gwaneumsa Trail.
Had a few hours before catching flight, chose this beach because of location, but turns out it was a good choice. the rocks, and clear water was something you do not see in the US

Great waterfall, not very high but impressive nonetheless.  Spend a while looking about and then try some of the seafood brought up by the   haenyeo   [ladies who free-dive for shellfish].  Fresh as can be, washed down with a glass or two of soju.

Great Views, Must Go, Wear to walking shoes, Not Baby friendly for Strollers as you will have to climb a lots of stairs. If you have child?s on stroller make sure you carry Baby Pouches/Bags for carrying the baby. Drink the Tap Water - Very Springy & Natural.
great view of the waterfall and the sea, you can see the locals there selling crabs coconuts, oranges and other stuff like souvenirs

Great for kids and any others that like train ride.You will be taking a small train ride through beautiful natural forests. Some walking is require in between stations, but just have fun and enjoy what nature brings. Take pictures of mini lake... the water is clear, windmills, grassy fields, pirate ship and not to miss the last stop with beautiful tulips.

Great experience being in the caves, reading the explanation on the formation of the stalactites, lava lines and reason for the uneven heights at certain lengths of the cave. There are summarised English translation on the explanation boards which makes it easier to understand what we are looking at. Trail wise, the ground is made up of flat rocks with some shallow water holes. Wearing comfortable cover shoes would help. We saw some families with young children, about 6 years and above and they could run about on their own, so I would think this would be OK for families who want to bring their kids alone. Overall a good experience and good change from seeing the land attractions. At 2000KRW for an adult ticket, it is definitely reasonable and worth your every cent.

Great day out doors. Many options of travel within the island (drive from mainland, rent bicycles, various motorized vehicles) making it really easy.Roads are narrow so personally would avoid driving. Further the ferries can only hold that many cars which means expect long wait times during peak periods.Many nice small eateries for coffee or ice cream along the way. Beaches are really pretty too and water clear though I didn't see anyone swimming in dec (winter).Only thing that I didn't quite like was the rentals were pricey at 70000 won for 3 hrs (two motorized bicycles and one two seater). And that was after some bargaining . The guy mentioned that it takes 45 min to go around the island without stops

Great beach. The water is really clear and nice blue color. The tide comes up and down during the day though. So from 11am~ until 5pm~ you can walk few hundred meters until you reach deep enough water. But besides that one minus it is a worth visiting beach!If you want some more information on what you can find on the island, you can check out this video: http://youtu.be/X2RwSnOMgYk?list=UUYEqXBrHobdnJF591_o-vcg

Good driving views.  You will be blown away. Should visit this place in the morning before 9am to avoid the crowd especially during weekend. There are so many trails.  Please ensure you know which trail you are taking as the mountain is so huge.  Must wear proper trekking clothes and shoes. If you are driving, please ensure you go down the same way as you climb up or else, you need to get a cab to bring you back to your car. Bring water, snacks and plastic bag to throw your rubbish. You must bring down your rubbish with you.

Getting close to the waterfalls looks easier than it seems. However, that adds to the thrill of getting nearer to mother nature. It is tricky manuvering around the wet, slippery & sometimes unstable rocks & boulders in cold weather. Many a times, you find yourself balancing precariously on the boulders or have your feet stuck between the rocks as you slip or slide from the smooth rocks. You will also find visitors around you lending you a hand to help you get back on your feet. Such spontaneous camaraderie !  For the young & agile, it is fun watching them jumping from rock to rock, like Tarzan in action.  It is a thrilling on the rocks experience not to be missed !  And you get rewarded by the beautiful sight & sound of a great waterfall!

From the bottom Seongsan Ilchulbong looks daunting, but once you get walking its relatively easy, with many well placed rest spots along the way. The views at each spot are pretty great - you can really appreciate the black sand beaches from there. Take some water with you!The top of the volcano is amazing - covered in a sea of green grass, it looks like it could easily be a set in a Jurassic Park movie. There is something so primal about the feeling up there. And despite the many other hikers you will find up there, its pretty easy to find a spot to sit and appreciate it for a bit!The entrance is 2000 won. Take some water, a camera and some coins for the scopes. Also, it gets really, really gusty up at the top and along the walkway to Ilchulbong beach, so try and avoid any flyway items of clothing.

From Seogwipo , we took bus 201 and it dropped us off at the entrance. The mountain is just so beautiful to look at. It?s a very easy hike, just 25 minutes to the peak. Bring some water . Drones are not allowed.
Fresh and cool air,? sea water not polluted and the hill is very greenly. Natural scenario not damage by public

Free carpark. There?s a replica fountain of the real lava column which is found at the end of the tunnel. Entrance costs 1000 won. Descent about 80 steep steps into the tunnel. Temp change can be felt immediately. Floors are damp from the rain and the water drippings from the ceilings. Best to have a hoodie and raincoat or an umbrella. The tunnels are very dark and damp. Go slowly and let the eyes adjust to the dim conditions.  There is a marking at 850metres which is great as it is difficult to gauge the distance while walking in the dark. Then you will have 150 metres more to go before reaching the end of the tunnel open to public. The world?s largest lava column, 7.6m in height is located at the end. Advise: wear sensible shoes with good grip as the floors are damp and slippery ; warm clothing; carry a torch- or use your phone?s flashlight. It makes the trek so much easier. Lastly, restrooms located at the surface level are decent though damp and a bit stinky.

For visitors arriving by bus: Take Bus 201 from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal and get off at the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. At the same stop, wait for Bus 711-2 to reach the actual Manjanggul Cave site entrance (transfer at KWR 0 cost if using T-money or CashBee card).Note: It's a 2.5km distance from the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. Being a UNESCO Heritage site, we had expected a much better set up for the cave site. Overall lighting could be improved; brighter lighting for better visibility of the rugged paths and water puddles along the 1km lava tube (reduce risks of slipping or tripping as a fall could be quite fatal).The temperature underground can get chilly so be sure to wear warm jackets/coate and proper shoes with good traction (saw some visitors in flip-flops and sneakers, and they ended up almost slipping).

For the last day of our Jejueco tour, the first attraction we visited in the morning was Jeongbang waterfall. Situated on a high cliff by the sea, Jeongbang waterfall is the only waterfall in Asia to fall into the sea. Admission fee is 2,000 won for individuals and 1,600 won per person if you are in a group of 10 or more.When we finally reached our destination, to actually get up-close to Jeongbang waterfall, we had to walk down some (more) steep steps and make our way over a field of rocks/boulders. It was a pretty slippery (and uneven) walk, so make sure you wear footwear with good grip. But the walk was worth it: the sight of the waterfall emptying itself right into the sea which makes it a pretty unique and amazing (since we don?t really have such waterfalls in Singapore).For more photos and our Jeongbang Waterfall experience, do check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jeongbang-waterfall.html :)

For hiking enthusiasts, this is a must do!  The Seongpanak (9.6km) trail has an average hiking time of 4.5 hours and Guaneumsa (8.7km) trail has an average hiking time of 5 hours.  One must reach the Jindallaebat Shelter by 1pm to be permitted an attempt at the Baekrokdam summit.  My husband and I completed the hike in 7hrs 35mins but were perplexed to understand how it took us 5 minutes longer to descend, given that we did not take breaks while descending. Guaneumsa has the reputation of being the roughest trail on the crater, but does live up to its reputation for breathtaking views.  - There was one potable water area on each trail where nature provided delicious water refills.  - Emergency posts appear through the trails, each with its own number, so keep track of the number in case you need assistance, rescue workers can narrow down your location.  - There are incredibly handy signs along the way to pinpoint your progress and identify the level of difficulty along the trail.  Paths are well maintained and varied; wooden, rocky, skree, etc. - If you take the bus to there is no fee for hiking.- Although we did not have cell phones with us, many folks seemed to be talking an walking throughout the trails.- We chose to end at the Guaneumsa trail head because it was the closest in proximity to our hotel.  Cabs are available at the trailhead.

First, we went to see the woman diver show. It appears to occur twice per day, at 1.30pm and 3pm if I remember correctly. They were singing, then entered into the water. I found their catch more interesting than their swimming. Afterwards, we climbed the   mountain   (small but cute is the motto). The view over the volcanic crater and the island is amazing, even despite the rainy weather that we experienced. The ascend is a bit physically challenging.

First thing we've noticed is how civilized this beach is - loads of restaurants, shops , cafes nearby. We were lucky enough to visit it in September, when holiday season is over for majority of Korean guys - so, it was not that crowded. Water was very clean and the only downside, that it was already a little bit cold. If you walk few hundred meters in a right hand direction from the main beach (towards the hill), you would see a camping ground with even smaller strip of sand - and we were absolutely alone there.

First stop for sight seeing in jeju and found the beach was crowded, specially family with children. Went straight to Delmondo cafe to have a better view and it was also pretty crowded at the deck with chairs facing the beach. Looked for facility to change and for shower as the water was tempting clear and the weather hot. Sadly, only found changing room but no shower facility.

First of all, this place is huge.Formed through volcanic activity which resulted in 46 'small volcanoes' in the park itself. From what i saw, they ain't 'small'!There are a few entrances and trails. I took the Eulrimok Trail. It was pretty easy as compared to other mountains i hiked. First third, about 2.4km is quite difficult. Lots of stones and steps. Then it gradually became easier. The view is definitely awesome the moment you clear the forest area.There is a reststop at about 5km. Be sure to bring your own food. There is no cafe or shop there. The locals actually even cooked their own ramyeon by bringing them and hot water too. Some used the army-styled ration. There are no trash cans. You have to bring your trash back.You can take a public bus to this trail (gotta walk in opposite the bus stop. A good almoat 2km gentle upslope).Only bus 240 brings hikers here. You might want to check.Reminder, it is super cold in winter.

First of all ensure you hike on a non rain day.  We were worried all week because it was raining.  We got a non rain day but cloudy. When got pass 1 km up it was beautiful sunny weather.Know there are 6 trails and they start in different places and not all go to the top. We took the Eorimok Trail (Northwest). It was one of the shortest. We didn't do good research and started too late to do a longer trail.I'm moderately fit. The trail was steep! I was definitely challenged for the first 2km. It was balance of even and uneven ground. Anyone can make it up but it might take you a bit longer if you were unfit. There isn't a drone restrictions and was able to take some great video. Bring water and food.  There are places near the top to grab instant noodles and water. There is no washroom on the way up.  Bring some tissue and wet wipes just in case.Although we didnt get to go to the summit, it is a must do while visiting. Jeju.

Falls is very beautiful.  You walk down 100 steps or so, then across big rocks to the bottom of the falls.  Wear tennis shoes or flip-flops for rock hopping!  Lots of water spray, and nice wading in the cool water as it runs across a few rocks to the ocean.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Everything rolls backwards on that 50m of road! We tried it with our car without its engine, and then with a bottle of water.. It works all the same! Takes about 10 mins to experience it.. Seeing is Believing!

Even in peak season Sehwa Beach didn?t have nearly as many visitors as some of the more popular northeast Jeju beaches mainly because most of it is covered in volcanic rocks.  We actually weren?t even sure it was a beach at first.  We did see a handful of people in the water who had sidestepped all the volcanic rocks but most seemed happy taking photos standing on the rocks.  Cafes, restaurants, and convenience stores line the beach and all were good spots to admire the nice scenery of the beach.  For actually going in the water, the other popular beaches are more popular for that reason.

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh   ginseng of the sea   (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

Entrance fee is 2000 won which is not that bad but again, the waterfalls are not that big. There are other falls on Jeju with greater magnitude you should consider instead unless you stay in Seogwipo as this is literally just on the outskirts of the city.
Enjoyed how easy it was to walk from parking lot down to the waterfall, ws not expecting such a short walk! A waterfall that goes into the ocean, two awesome things in one!
Easy climb down to see the waterfall. If you are adventurous, go navigate across the rocks for better photos angles and also for a challenge. A simple waterfall for photo ops and a light stroll.

Easily the most gentle slope you can find and is a great start in Jeju. Easy path with great views. Though touristy but still very manageable. Is 2000won per pax entry and only 1 waterfall to see, you can probably finish this in half hour but we stopped at the ladies selling conch and abalone for breakfast yummy and definitely a must try....still alive when we had it ?? and is 30000won for the plate.
Easily the best nightclub spot in Seogwipo, Jeju! There is a huge waterslide. A lot of foreigners and i have to go back!

Early Morning walk is rather cold and its indeed extremely tiring to walk up the stairs to the top. But the view at the top is so beautiful, the sea water surrounding very crystal clear. Its a must go attraction.

Don't talk, just feel yourself on the walk way to clim to the top. Open your eyes and record the scene to your soul. It will treat your mind, very well. Don't forget your water bottle. Be careful when taking your selfie.

Don't need to spend so much time there, many tourist will be around there. As objects and liquid appear to roll and flow up the hill instead of down, when, in fact, such image of gravity defiance is an optical illusion rendered by the seemingly high surroundings.Roll a bottle or pour some water and see i for yourself. There is also several vendors selling food and drinks. Beware as they are abit pricey.

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)

Do this! I hiked to the peak with my sister and i'd say both of us are average when it comes to our fitness level. We took the  Seongpanak route, up and down and it took us 6.5 hours. When we got to the peak it was really chilly, so be wise and pack a light windbreaker/jersey. It's a beautiful hike through the mossy trees. Be prepared for too many stairs to count and hundreds of Asians taking selfies. You can buy yourself Kimbap at the start of the hike to fuel yourself or to eat as a much needed snack at the peak. There is one or two bathroom points on the way and a place to refill your water bottle. Entrance is free

Do not miss the chance to climb up to the top (180m) to see the huge crater & Jeju view! it's definitely worth it ..the staircases might seems endless but it wasn't that high actually. it tooks us less than 30mins to reach the top and there are a few stops where you can catch a breath before continue to climb up again. Even my 4 years old nephew make it on top too. Going up and going down is 2 different route. Don't forget to get yourself mineral water at the convenient store before you climb up. you will need it.If you going over to the cliffs for the seaview, check out the Haenyeo performance. The performance hours are 1:30 p.m. and 3 p.m. twice a day during summer but we are out of luck we did not see any at the 3pm slot that day. Seongsan ilchulbong is sunrise peak - famous with sunrise from the cater! The gate is open 1 hour before sunrise for those who wish to watch sunrise from the top.

Didn't have any high expectation when visiting this spot after the waterfalls. A good thing we visited this Dragon Head Coast while doing the west coast route.The canola flowers site is a paid visitor spot (should be around KRW2K each adult). There is a Viking ride @ the base for the young ones to try. You can see many interesting lines and grains on the side of the rocks' walls. You get to see women divers selling fresh seafoods along the coast, youngest are already in their 50s and oldest are in their 70s (still diving)...they are simply amazing.

Dark cave, chilly, dripping water and uneven steps were all I felt for one hour journey in and u-turn out of the cave. Not much to see really unless you are acompanied by an expert or archelogist who can make rock and mud come alive and tell stories. I have been to few caves over the world and find this least interesting and dull.

Created by winds and waves over thousands of years, the rock is formed resembling a dragon's head. Close by is the dragon pond Yongyeon, where the sea meets fresh water. The pond is flanked by 8 rock walls that resemble folding screens and has a stunning view.
Couldn't believe eyes when the car started to go   uphill   even though the engine has been turned off. My son and nephews put a water bottle on the road and it rolled   uphill  . Very unique

Completely worth the early morning waking up to see the sunrise. It looks completely difference bathed in the early morning light than after the sun has arisen, so check when the sun rises and wake up early!Is it easy to climb up? My wife doesn't work out, and we took about 40 minutes to walk up the stairs, with occasional stops along the way. I do work out, and even I had to pause a little here and there - bring some water, you'll be glad you did. Otherwise, it's not really difficult, just takes a bit of stamina.

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. The rocks are just unique, I only saw it in the movie! And it's kind of amazing that you see it in real! I visited here in end April with strong wind and warm sun. If you have time, you can even just stroll along the walkway or sit a bit to have a casual chat with your friends.  Please do expect a lot of tourist and students visits and long queue for toilet. But this is kind of normal for all the unique sight seeing point at Jeju Island. I would recommend this place if you happens to be in this area, and I will skip the waterfalls :)

Compare to Jeongbang waterfall, this place is much more worth for a visit as it surrounded with cherry flowers. It will definitely a nice view when full blossom of cherry flowers. Be sure you go to the right place as the name just different with a alphabet. This is CheonjIyeon that near to Saeseom Island Saeyeongyo Bridge not CheonjEyeon (3 tier waterfall) that located in Jungmun.

Coming from Seogwipo by the bus 782 ( return by 781) we have decided to do this Trail because it begins  immediatly on the parking. It was Tuesday and the trail is really quiet (we cross less than 20  runners in allday). You need to have goods shoes because we need to walk on volcanic stones. For climbing it is ok, but with small shoes in the descente it is hard to finish. 95 % of the Times you walk in a wet Forest and it is Nice ... I Climb to the Observatory ( about 6 kms) because of you arrive after 1 pm they close the Trail for the Hallansan. Well I was not disapointed because the weather was cloudy ... So the Montain was invisible. Even if it is a difficult climbing I have spent a good day on the nature ( and was happy to have some rains to refresh). Don t forget to take water with you, the spot   potable water   .. I don t find Where I can take it. Arriving at 12, we finish a 5 pm.

Coming from a country where temples are famous for their stunning decoration I did not expect much from temples in East Asian countries. But Yakchunsa Temple was beyond my expectations. The temple is stunningly decorated. The Buddha statues are absolutely beautiful. I recommend you walk up to the second floor where you will see countless mini gold Buddha in different poses on the wall to your left and you can enjoy the view of the main hall and the main Buddha from high up. There is a small building to the left of the main hall with 500   heroes  . I think they are important monks or something. At least that's what it says in Chinese characters. All 500 of them have different facial expressions and poses. Some are very comical. Do take a quick look inside. And don't forget to drink the water from the water fountain before you leave the temple. The water there is refreshingly sweet.

Come with my little girl, stayed at the hotel besides the beach.It is very hot in jeju in july, 35 degree in the afternoon.  We went to the beach at noon, water is clear and cool and the sand is smooth.Rental of umbrella and shelter at 25000w and 100000w respectively.  It is recommended to bring your own shelter.

Come prepared and you'll love it, good walking boots and waterproof jacket. If you find it too cold or dump you can go in for a few metres, and go outside, but we kept going wanting to see what is at the end, and it was spectacular, with huge lava column in blue dim light.

Climbing Mt. Halla was a highlight of our trip to South Korea! We climbed up the Eorimok trail and then down the Yeongsil trail. I would recommend going this way because Yeongsil was a lot of stairs - I'd rather do that on the way down than up. Going up probably took us a little over two hours and wasn't too strenuous (though we are in good shape). The trails are very well kept and there are signs all along (in English) showing how far you've gone and how far you have left, and how easy/difficult the next stretch is. The view from the top (even though it wasn't even the top) was unbelievably beautiful! To get there, we hailed a cab from Jeju city. We just told him we wanted to start at Eorimok trail. I would recommend a cab because if you take the bus, you have a pretty large hill to walk up before you even get to the mountain because of where it drops you off. I think the cab cost about 15,000 won. The way home, we were waiting for a bus and then saw a cab so we hailed him. This guy charged us 30,000 won, I think because Jeju city was out of his way. Make sure to bring plenty of water - at least two bottles per person - and snacks.

Climbing Mt Hallasan was absolutely amazing, and I would recommend anyone going to Jeju to attempt a climb. If you?re a bit unsure, make sure to research the trails before-hand and start walking in the morning ? many trails close at 2-3pm.Bring lots of water and snacks (although in typical Korean fashion, there is a 'restaurant' at the 'top', where all the lower trails intersect. Do your research, take a car or taxi to the start of the trail (buses will drop you off much further down the mountain, and you'll have to spend time and energy walking up along a road before you can even start the trail). The views must usually be stunning, but on the day we went, it was covered in cloud/fog. Even so, I would 100% recommend it and I would definitely go again if I went back to Jeju.

Climbed the mountain with my wife 5 year old daughter and some friends. Not a strenuous climb, but a long one. 9 hours all tolled for the return journey. Very busy on the mountain (even more so at weekends and holidays) but really worth the effort. You do not need to be too fit (I really wasn't when I did it) as long a you take your time. Take plenty of snacks and water - although there is a snack bar 2/3 of the way to the top. Glorious views on a cloudless day, and a real sense of achievement having scaled the tallest peak in Korea.

Climb down stairs to reach this waterfall but the place is hard to reach cause no ground at all, have to walk on different shapes and size of stone to reach the waterfall. Only need to spend about 15 minutes here will do. Natural scene than Cheonjiyeon Falls that with man made paths.
Cliffs formed by flowing lava and water and wind form dramatic coastline of Jeju island, great place for photos, in sunny days nice walks, don't miss it

Clearly, going in early spring is not the best idea; water's still too cold for swimming but it was perfect to go walking barefoot in the fantastically clear water. It was pleasant to walk into random warm currents while chasing after fish in the shallow water. Our driver said it was the best beach on Jeju but he said that about Hallim Park too so I would not take his word for it.
Clear waters, soft sand beach and you can find many people taking strolls and chilling by the beach. You can also visit the cafes along the beach which provides a nice view

Chilshimni Poetry Park is part of Jeju Olle Route 6 that was easy to located as it was along the main road, Namseongjung-ro road where Park sunshine hotel or Poong Gyung Hotel were. It was a free general park with playground where the locals hang out and it can be finish in 30 minutes for less. However, the highlight of the park was the ability to have a clear view Cheonjiyeon waterfalls from a height for free! We spent some time chilling at the table and benches to appreciate the falls. There was also a stairway down to Saeyeongyo bridge. As the park was part of Jeju Olle Route 6, we went out to the main road, Namseongjung-ro road, and followed the orange/blue ribbons to Oedolgae. I have rated this park a 4 stars for the beautiful view of the Cheonjiyeon waterfalls.

Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls consists of 3 waterfalls. Such a nice turquoise water. There is an entrance fee to enter this place. Make sure you have some energy because you need to climb stairs to reach each point. There is a bridge called 'Seonimgyo Bridge', meaning 7 nymphs as there has an arch carved on the side. This place open from 8am to 6pm. We came here late in the evening in a rainy day but the admin staff were so nice to allowed us to enter but with time restrictions.

Cheonjeyeon Falls are very near to the Booyoung hotel and the ICC (International Convention Center), an easy 5 minutes walk takes you to the bottom of a very steep flight of wooden steps. If you chance to go up there (no English signs, and as far as I could judge, they do not mention the fall even in Korean) you will find the falls, only to climb down - and then up again. I found it very exhaustive. The falls had very little water, so were somewhat disappointing. Apparently there is an easier, but somewhat longer, way to get there from Booyoung, going to the Botanic Gardens along the main road.

Cars and buses usually demonstrate this seemingly mysterious trick. They have their engines turned off at the beginning of the road stretch (there's an indicated sign). And while the engines are off, it seemingly feels and looks like there's this   mysterious force   pulling the vehicles towards the end of the road. Civilians also use a water bottle and place it on the road surface. Mimicking the vehicles, it too would roll towards the end of the road. Just like the saying goes, looks can be deceiving. Optical illusion is what it is.

Can't resist going there every night as it's near to my hostel. Kinda good place for dinner for solo traveller as most of the restaurant serving food for more than 2 persons. You can get local food, fusion, western, sashimi, fresh fish, pork knuckles, fresh fruits and vegetables. Price range around kw2000 to kw10,000 per dish. Now you can get hallabong orange everywhere. Sweet and seedless. Yummmm love it when it's cool. After dinner can catch the water show nearby at 8pm every night except Monday.

Came here to checkout the views and totally loved it. A nice small town to chill at with lots of parking if you're driving. Many restaurants, cafes and food trucks along the beach. Beautiful white sand and blue waters. Not crowded. Definitely coming back here! Didn't get enough of it.

Came here by using waze , there's parking , entrance fee 2000 won for adults , 1000 won for youth , walk down the stairs leading to the rocky waterfalls , got to be careful when walking around the rocks .

Came here after having our dinner nearby , stroll along this underground shopping which was not that long , bought some Korean brand cosmetic here that's all, not crowded , free filter water with paper cups for drinks , clean toilet to use , heated on a cold weather . If it's raining outside would be nice to spend some time here .

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This temple's shape was unique and located in cave. The way to this tempe was about 15 minutes in uphill stairs and had good view. Though it was hard to temple, but after climbing there was good, and could drink mineral water. Sometimes there was no climbing because of bad weather. There was another temple at the entrance of way to this temple, that temple was good and beautiful sculpture. Good place to enjoy temple and view.

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!
Bring your own water, light jacket and a keep climbing to the top. You will say WOW to the view. Breathe and smile to yourself for this amazing award.

Bring your jackets, better to be water proof! Cave temperature is around 10 plus degree or lower. Also ground is uneven so wear good shoes and walk slowly. But overall fascinating to see how geography works

Bring along a lot of water before climbing. There is few cafe that open very early at the counter ticket area, for you to have anything if you feel hungry before climbing, but just for snacking. The entrance fee is 2k Won, if im not mistake. The view was great along the way from bottom to top. After half-way through, there is a checkpoint with nice scenery of the city and ocean during dawn, which is so beautiful. Better to take picture during that time of your climbing if you climb to see the sunrise, because when you get down, it is another daylight scenery. If you are not fit enough or dont have that much stamina, don't worry, it is still okay for you to climb, you just need a strong will to arrive at the peak and keep on going. As the view from top is worth the sweat!For you to see sunrise, its better for you to be down at the entrance as early as you can, during my time, I already there by 530am, the gate open at 6am as far as I can remember. If you climb slow and steady, it will take you about an hour to climb to the peak. Just keep in mind, if there is a lot of clouds, you might not be able to see the sunrise. So check your weather before you go.
Breathtaking waterfalls, good walk with family and kids. Love the view, the air and walk. Kids enjoyed the walk too.

Blue color of beach water. Very good.  We visited there late July. The color of beach was amazing. We enjoyed swimming. Also the sunray was very strong to enjoy sun tenning. We are food a little far from here, because restaurants near beach was expensive. Also there are good places to nearby beach ; Hyeopjae cave, botanical garden, tracking beach, etc.

Black rock, golden sand, turquoise waters, green fields. Such a colourful island, easy to cycle around. The contrast of the simple life of haenyo and farmers with those vacationing was also felt strongly.

Besides all the other sightseeing places, mountains, waterfall, the markets are always our way to experience locals' life and of course snacks.We came back from hiking in Hallashan and the Dungman market is on the way to the hotel and near the Black Pork Market later for dinner, so why not?Compared to the Olle Market and the Five Day Market, the DM market seems to have more interesting snacks to refresh from all day hiking, and just good enough before dinner. ( I am sure some feed themselves here for dinner as well).The souvenirs are the same as in the Olle market but more variety than the Five Day Market (mostly for locals but more to experience the genuine daily life of Koreans). It is also at the entrance of the underground market but we didn't go underground.

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.

Before you visit this attraction, be sure to be appropriately dressed and have the essential gear.  Hiking boots are highly recommended as the ground is uneven and mostly rock.  Sun hat and shades will also be very useful when nearing the peak as the area there is more barren without much trees.  Trekking pole will also be useful for those with knee problems.You will have to start your day early as they will disallow entry to the final stretch (at the 2nd rest point).
