There are 2 rest points, both with toilets.  The 2nd rest point (higher up) sells drinks and instant bowl noodles.  Rubbish will have to be brought down and thrown when you leave the park.  I climbed in early June and there were many many many bugs and wasps at the last leg and the peak.  For those climbing during spring, please prepare some bug balm.  These are the tips;1) Start early, reach the 2nd rest stop before 12pm.  2) Have the proper gear3) If possible, have your noodles etc after you finish the peak (if you're descending via the same trail), that way, you won't have to carry your trash up the peak4) If you're driving, reach there early (before 730).  Carpark fills up pretty quick5) A mineral spring can be found along the way for cool refreshing water!

Because Jeju is a volcanic island, it doesn?t have too many beaches relative to its 300 km of coastline.  Hamdeok Beach is one of the closest beaches to Jeju City.  It?s also one of the most picturesque in Jeju making it quite crowded when it?s warm enough to go into the water.  Unfortunately when we went there were a lot of seaweed washed up on the sand.  Despite the crowd, the parking lot was quite large and there is a good selection of cafes and restaurants nearby making it a decent visit even if you don?t go into the water.

Beautiful, serene and breathtaking views. A mid-level challenge to hike up and carrying extra water was mandatory in the heat. It is the highest peak in South Korea and the geographical centre of Jeju. A most worthwhile wander.
Beautiful, clean and very well maintained. It has great collection of plants, cactus etc. Beautiful cave and water garden too. Should allocate 3 hours time to enjoy this place.

Beautiful, according to our guide we hired he claims that the this is the only waterfall in South Korea that is sea side. The place is touch crowded and a bit of walk downhill from visitor location. Otherwise, totally worth the effort.

Beautiful weather with wonderful scenic view. Took a bit of time getting to the side of the waterfall due to uneven rocks surrounding it after going down the stair for about 10 mins. Once you get past that, have a great time snapping away and find your best angles  though you have to take turns with other tourists who are doing the exact same thing. Snap away!

Beautiful waterfall. I went to all 3 waterfalls in Jeju, and this is the most amazing and my favourite. It's also along the Jeju Olle Trail 6. A short walk from the waterfall, there is a mini waterfall called Sojeonbang waterfall, which also falls into the ocean.
Beautiful waterfall. I walked to the area as it was near my hotel (M stay hotel in seogwipo). It's a huge waterfall, and a tourist attraction. The water is very clean.
Beautiful Waterfall. Because it was April there was no charge to see it, liked that part. It was sort of hot so it was refreshing to be  near the fall

beautiful view, great for swimming, warm clear shallow waters, best beach i've visited in Korea. I didn't expect to find a tropical like beach in Korea. if i have an opportunity i would definitely visit again.

Beautiful scene to be seen. Very natural. 20,000 stones of different verities. Natural as traditional village houses in India. Toilet facilities are everywhere. Very clean. Dogs and cats are not allowed.Water fountain is there. very good place for peace, health and meditation.Thanks.
beautiful moutain~not so high but highgreen,clean water,sound,windeverything is perfectrecommend

Beautiful location. Relatively easy to get to (just one change from Jeju City Bus Terminal). The park is beautiful and I'd really recommend taking your time and enjoying the scenery as much as possible. The park contains different areas (bonsai, water gardens, caves, animals, cactus) and it's so hard to believe that it's man-made. Loved the diversity here.

Beautiful indoor gardens with several rooms leading off of main garden with specialized environments. The rooms leading from the main garden that I can recall right now are a tropical plant room with orchids, a fern room, water plant room with lilies and hyacinth, and even a cactus room. It is a large indoor garden with many colorful and unusual plants to see. It was raining the day we were there so we were happy that it was enclosed. There are beautiful Korean and Japanese style gardens, among other types of gardens too, outside. Jeju Island has many beautiful places to visit and this botanical garden was a great excursion for us.

Beautiful Falls. Also its rare to see falls directly in ocean apparently only one in Asia. It said that the dragon's spirit is contained in the water which can cure diseases and bring rain during drought. Easy to access. Make sue you wearing comfatable Shoes, it does get slippery. We had some lovely click out here, spl couple ;)
Beautiful clean beach!! one of the nicest I've seen, it was spring and a bit cold so not ideal for swimming but i guess in the summer it would be really nice to go a dip as the water is very clear.
Beautiful blue/green water  with white sand beach. We didn't get in the water since it was chilly, but it looks very shallow with some rocks.   Can park and walk along the beach shore.

Beautiful beach, many people during summer but still acceptable. Very good for children because the water is very shallow. The only thing i didn't like ia that i couldn't even cool down in the water because it was so hot, like in a bath tub.There is no sunlounger, so if you want to tan, you need a mat.
beautiful beach, clear waters witha great view. a cafe is nearby where you can sit by the beachside and enjoy a hot cup of coffee with some nice pastries
Beautiful beach with crystal clear water, white and smooth beach sand that you may ever feel from the others beaches.
Beautiful beach if only few tourist there. Clear water, decent sand. Can visit with Hallim Park. There is a G25 which can provide basic food and snacks.  Nice view from Coffee Bene.
Beautiful beach and surroundings!Very clean and vivid colours You can also try some water sports here, but seems like you had to stay around the renting area

Beach is clean, water is sooooo clear with a nice colour. Sit on the beach, enjoy your coffee there. In front of the beach, is a coffee street. If you want to have a relax trip, can spend half day time there, just enjoy the breath of wind, enjoy your coffee and have a pcs of cake, read your book. Perfect! I prefer Cold weather of cause.

Be sure to wear good shoes for the somewhat uneven - but not particularly slippery - walk and a raincoat for the dripping water.    There is only 1km of the lava tube which is open to tourists, so the entire walk is 2km roundtrip.   There are a number of informational plaques along the way as well as before you even enter.    There are restrooms and a restaurant by the parking lot.

Be prepared to walk and climb and climb and climb up steps.Not diffcult but quite a way up.Good walking shoes, warm clothing and water (maybe some small snacks too) needed.There r also an different area where u can check out the Jeju women divers.Also check out the local restaurants around this attractions...They serve very good seafood food / BBQ meat.I had  some very good abalone porridge and seafood soup along some BBQ meat.

Be prepared to climb back up after going down the steps. Will need proper shoes as the floor is uneven, and does have small puddles of water  here and there.It was a nice walk in the cave, and getting a better understanding of nature involving volcanic lava flow.

Be prepared for stairs! There are 3 waterfalls to see. It can get crowded, so taking a nice picture may take a few minutes since people have to wait on each other to move. The area is full of trees, making the views all the more beautiful. Definitely worth the visit!

Bangju Church is a picturesque little church that?s unmissable on the way to Bonte Museum.  It?s the unique ark-shaped exterior along with the surrounding water that makes it photogenic and there isn?t much inside (which is off limits most of the time anyway).  Despite being a short stop, there were always a half dozen cars in the parking lot with people busy taking photos around the church.

At this place you need to walk, climb a little. Be very careful when climbing on and over rocks at the bottom of the fall to take pics. Some rocks are very slippery. You can see the water go straight into the ocean which is quite different to the other two waterfalls. It is a lovely sight!

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. When we reached Chilshimni Poetry Park (is just beside Park Sunshine hotel), we were lucky to catch a view of  the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top. There was also a resting shelter with table and benches if you want to enjoy the view of the waterfall while having snacks or lunch. Afterwhich, we left the park to the main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was) and headed to Namseong-ro road which was indicated by the blue/orange ribbons for Oedolgae. Along the way, you will pass by몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online) before reaching Hwangwooji coast first (it is a very beautiful coast with a private emerald green pool. Then there was a trail to Oedolgae where was a cliff top that you can view the Saeyeongyo bridge. Oedolgae trail is  free 1 to 2 hours trail and it is not a difficult trail, it is pretty gentle with lots of benches for rest breaks as needed. It has pretty nice coast view. There were fruits and snack sold along the trail where you just need to place 1000won at the basket where you take the fruits/snacks from (there is not one attending to the store). It is based on trust. There were rest rooms outside the trails if needed with food stalls near the free public toilet with toilet paper provided. We need all the trail by foot and there is really no need for a car.

As the title says, hiking Hallasan gives a sense of accomplishment and something to look back fondly upon. I remember reading a fellow TripAdvisor review on how she did not believe she would be able to complete the hike but she eventually did it at the expense of not being able to walk the next day.Here's my advice:- Climbing Hallasan in the winter period would have a better scenery in my opinion. Trekking during the Apr period, the barren trees across the landscape didn't look too impressive. However, looking at Hallasan pictures in winter looked amazing so that's my take on what season to climb.- Climbing gear is recommended like walking sticks for example, they would definitely be useful especially in winter or the day after heavy rain as the ground would be slip-prone.- Remember to get enough water as some have complained about the lack of water refilling stations. We had brought 3 x 2L bottles for 3 people and they were sufficient without any refill. Take note the trail with the water refills will be slightly longer than the trail without. - Best to trek early as there is a cutoff timing to reach a certain place at the trail (12.30 Korea time) - It was quite warm trekking in Apr, just prepare a jacket alongside for the peak- Buy some snacks and food for the peak and the rest stops on the way up. Buying gimbap would be a good idea, don't buy too much though for they may end up being a burden. Also, you will see some of the Koreans pack hot water and cup noodles up to enjoy so that's an option as well.As you trek, you will see plenty of Korean elderly hiking alongside you. If they can do it, you can too. (PS, we took 9.5 hours)

As someone who loves walking on rocky surfaces (yes it does sound weird when I type it like that), I really enjoyed walking down to the base of the waterfall. You don't have to walk the rocky part to get you to the waterfall though - the steps from the carpark down to the base will take you close enough. Someone the rocks are slippery so be careful. Along the way I think there were haenyeon with their very freshly caught seafood. Loved this place; would come back in a heartbeat.

As our tour guide said nest stop is the beach... i was wondering how can any beach rival Philippine beaches? But as we get nearer i saw it,,, a hill with a small island... really shaped like an oriental dragon serpent just starting to submerge into the water. It was a sight to behold! so we went down the trail and enter the coastline path... it was so beautiful! the coastline is carved by ancient volcanic eruptions and was smoothened by the waves. it was a 30min walk around the coast line and as we were walking the view just gets better and better. when we turned a corner around 14 minutes in the walk. The best view suddenly came out. no amount of words can describe the rock formations we saw. we felt small beside it. Along the way were many old ladies selling seashells and sea urchins and sea cucumbers for us to taste as sashimi (raw fish) to be downed together with soju(rice wine).These ladies were the famous jeju island deepsea divers. They dive without oxygen tanks. After the walk we were all tongue tied at the beauty of the past 30 minutes. Yongmeori means dragon head coast. and it really took a dragon size breath away from me. Entrance only 6000won (6us$)

As my country does have lotsa waterfall, this short walk for the scene just a ok to us.  Well, the difference is since we are tourist, so we visited the place. You can skip to pay the entrance fee if you are not keen on waterfall as it can be viewed and spotted before climb down for a nearer view of it.

As mentioned in the title, out of the few waterfalls that Jeju have, i think Jeongbang waterfalls is the best one. It?s just a short descent and you can go close to the waterfalls depending how brave you are. You get a good view of the sea as well.

As I've mentioned on my review to Seongpanak Trail, I'd recommend it as the point of entry then exit through Gwaneumsa Trail. But, if you prefer a more challenging option, do the other way around. I went down from the summit through the Gwaneumsa Trail. It was the first week of April and the snow hasn't melted completely yet, making it slippery. It is very much recommended to have a walking stick, in my case, I used my tripod. The scenery in this trail was awesome. There are valleys in yellow and white. You can also find a spring water along the way. Hiking Hallasan in general solo is not a problem, regardless of which trail you take, because there are a lot of other hikers you meet along the way.

As I made my way to the waterfall, I noticed some divers swimming towards the rocky beach. Two older ladies were selling freash seafood for 30000 won. The divers were women in their 60's and 70's. I dined on the seafood al fresco while taking in the the vista and clean air. Well worth the 2000 won admission price.

As I didn't have access to a car and was traveling alone whilst in Jeju I caught the city bus to the national park. This was pretty simple and the bus from the main bus terminal leaves every hour between 9 and 4 (during summer) the journey coat 3100 won. The bus stops at the end of 2 trails to the west of the mountain. (Eorimok Trail, Yeongsil Trail) . Both trails meet in the same place on the mountain and both give a varied, pretty and pleasant  walk up Mt Hallasan . There are toilets and facilities at each of the trail tickets offices which are well maintained. The paths are a mix of steps and decking to help mark the trail clearly. You get great views of the different Oreum's (small volcanoes) these trails do not lead to the summit like the longer trails that start on the east. Ensure you have snacks and plenty of water

As I can clearly assure that you wont be regret if you visit this place. This is my second visit to Seongsan Ilchulbong. We went there to catch a majestic sunset.  We reached the parking area around 5 o'clock in the morning then we straight away climbed to the highest peak. For us, it took roughly 30-40 minutes to reached the top of the observatory area. It is indeed quite challenging but its worth it. Just bare in mind to wear the most comfortable shoes and jacket, plus dont forget to bring a mineral water.

As a tour stop, the bus with engine shut off rolls up the road, this includes water and bottle, how mysterious? I say its average because I have seen this. Short vision is the road seem to be going up, but its real orientation is that of downward slope.  Therefore, it is still following the law of gravity. Conclusion, enjoy the moment and do not share your secret.

As a scuba diver I was very eager to go to this museum and get to know more about the   Jeju Mermaids  . The museums has lots of interesting information about how they live, the risks of their profession, the   team system   they use (I loved this part). If you like the underwater world, I highly recommend a visit to this neat museum.

Arrived in the morning parked easily, cost for parking at the entrance was 1800 WON and picked up a map.  Make sure you wear good shoes -- preferably with good ankle support and walking sticks.  The path is well layer out but does take some effort.  We did not get all the way to the top as it was closed due to a slide but it's nice walk.  Suggest an early start and bring water too.

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Apparently, this is the only waterfall where the water falls directly into the ocean. So based purely on this account and simply to appreciate the works of nature, do drop by and take a look. It would not take you more than 20 minutes. In front of the waterfall are a couple of old diver ladies that sell fresh abalone / sea cucumber sashimi so it was nice for my dad and I to eat these delicacies so near the waterfall. Would I do it again? I think sashimi would cost a lot less at Dongmun market but yes, the view is decent. By the way, you have to pay ~KRW2,000 to enter.

Apart from the waterfall there are many beautiful shots you can take including the trees which have beautiful flowers, a bridge overlooking a stream, a river crossing with many ?square steps? (don?t know how to nest describe it), etc. Apparently this opens till night as well and I heard the night scenes are beautiful as well. Worth a stop.

Anyone who can appreciate nature, especially geology, will love this. There are only about 5 countries in the world where you can go walk in a lava tube and South Korea is one of them.It's inexpensive to enter (2000won for those over 24, discounts for younger ages) and it is worth it.There are lights installed, but bring lights if you can. The ground is not paved and it's easy to trip. The cave also drips water, so there are puddles around. It was suuuuuper cold inside the cave in March-so cold that when we came outside to the 40 degree weather it felt like summer!!

Another UNESCO World Heritage. It have a nice view from the top but you need to climb up the stairs. Perhaps is a good exercise.  :)  You may bring along the bottled water as it takes around 30 mins to the top. There have restaurants, coffee shops, food stalls, souvenir stalls at the bottom and free car park as well.
Another in the city waterfall which means that if you are staying in Seogwipo, you must go to see this fall. Entrance is 2000 won which is justified. Beautiful views.

An interesting showcase into the folk customs of people who place men on pedestals and where women does most of the chores, while being trained to dive deep into the surrounding waters to harvest seafood for a living.

An hour is okay, but if you have the time it might be better to make this 1,5 hour. We combined this with waiting for the Mongolian horse show, which you should not miss and close to this location. You \can also enjoy the beautifull Jeju-beach on the other side of the road.This park is very well maintained. Enjoy the beautifull Bonsai trees, the waterfalls, the flowers, the cave and the statues. The cave was the least exciting to us, but the bonsai trees from over 150 years old were most impressive.

Among the beaches in Korea, this is the one that most resembles Hawaii/Australia/Thailand.  White sands and turquoise waters, with striking black lava rock.  The water is warmer than on the mainland, and it's never been as crowded as Haeundae (in Busan) when I've gone. It's easy to go, even alone, and spend a relaxed afternoon swimming and sunbathing without feeling as though you're ruffling anyone's feathers.  This beach is always the first place on my checklist when I go to Jeju!

amazing, fun to visit, u can find anykind of teddy bear, diving teddy, chef teddy, bride and groom teddy. there are many kind of thematic also here, underwater, zoo, kitchen, mini and giant teddy. unfortunately, Tesuem (teddy bear museum) have minim space for us to move and take photo. most off all..one of must-visit when u're in jeju.
Amazing view of the city as well as of the nature inside the peak.- 20 to 40 min to go up- pack water- pack sport shoesPlenty of rest areas on the way, so you can take your time
Amazing place to visit, with an incredible view, but to arrive there you have approximately 250mt of stairs! Don't forget to take some water and a hat!

Amazing lava tube, much bigger than other ones I've seen. The 1km each way feels like a very long distance!I went in the middle of a storm - the cave had waterfalls and streams flowing... quite surreal underground. A raincoat and torch are a must.

amazing landscape. A nice spot to take beautiful pictures of tranquil waters with pitch black rocks and white sand. Walk right from the main entrance till the end, you will fine some nice restaurants and cheaper places to stay. From there you can climb the hill and get the whole picture of Hamdeok area.

Amazed by the view inside the cave. Overall distance travel back and forth takes 1 hour to complete, approximately 2km. Advised to wear comfortable shoes (rocky slippery floor) and jacket as it can be very cold inside the cave. Bring an umbrella if you need it as there?s water droplets from the top of cave.

Although this place was packed with tourists, it was my favorite site in jejudo. The rock formations are like Giant's causeway in Ireland with the hexagonal rock formations at different levels. Since we visited right after the hurricane, the waves would cover the lower level of rocks but it was amazing when the water subsided and the rocks were revealed in those amazing shapes!

Although there is not a lot to do here, it is a short walk from the parking to see this absolutely beautiful view!  If you take a few minutes to watch the water swirling around the cliffs it will mesmerize you, so pretty!

Although the waterfall itself was very beautiful to see we only stayed for a few minutes if that there was a lot of people there taking pictures and sitting on the rocks once there, there wasn't much stuff to do. But on the bright side it was really nice to see.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

Although I am not a Geography buff, I found Manjang Cave an interesting place to visit.  Only 1km was open to public.  Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

After the unpleasant beach at Udo, arriving at Hamdeok beach was a delight. With just a short trip from Jeju city this little beach village is amazing. With many restaurants and cafes along the water, one could spend a nice long day here. The water is nice and clean with showers and changing rooms available nearby.

After seeing the waterfall, my family of four took a nice stroll down to the bridge.? The view in the evening is wonderful.? The bridge is also lit up nicely at night!? Of note, one can get tickets for the submarine or boat rides at this same location.

After seeing Jeongbang waterfall, this Cheonjiyeon waterfall seemed average.  Admission was the same in both waterfalls, 2,000won for adults, and 1,000won for teenagers (up to 24). To see this waterfall, you had to go thru the park, which had other monuments, trees, and flowers to admire...worth checking even in winter.

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After paying for the tickets (2000 won per adult and 1000 won per child/youth), we walked about 5-10min to the waterfall. It was a therapeutic walk through the park to reach the waterfall. Recommend to stay about an hour here to take photos with the waterfall as the backdrop.

After nearly two years spent in Korea, I can quite easily say that Hallasan is the most beautiful place I've visited while here. Dramatic scenery, including sprawling vistas and interactive cloud-cover made this an exhilarating climb. Don't expect an easy journey! I took the   easiest   trail and it took us a good 5 hours to complete, and the hike up the mountain itself was via a crowded and steep staircase.The sheer variety of landscapes you experience as you climb up is really impressive. When you reach the mid-point, there's a rest stop where you can buy water, coffee and ramen noodles (oh, Korea!), but bring your own snacks because you'll probably be up there for a while.

After hiking the Sunrise Peak, I was delighted by the fact that Jeongbang Waterfalls requires no rigorous hiking. We drove with our rental call and entered the phone number (7331530) into the GPS to get there. Parking is free. You just walk a short distance down a stairway and navigate through a few rocks to get closer to the waterfall. Overall, it is not difficult at all. The waterfall itself was so beautiful with the water flowing directly out to the ocean. If you've been to Yosemite, it kind of reminds me of the Vernal Falls/Mist trail without the heavy hiking up the steep steps. There were couples, seniors, and children sitting by the rocks enjoying the view. Of the three main waterfalls in the area, I would say Jeongbang is the best one.

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

Actually originally didn't think to visit this place. But coincidence have the chance, me and my travel partners was shock to see with our own eyes for the water and bottle both run to the upfront road which its was suppose to be opposite way....Make youself drop by to see this amazing effect while you around in Jeju. This place is just very nearby the Sex Museum which we didn't go but passby~

Some one said it caused by a natural magnetic power (as above), other one assumed by the trick of the sun's lighting a man nearly lying face down to the road parallel to look forward to the starting point... others wisely poured the water to see the flows .... Of course, our guide has explained the cause but I really do not want to tell you, let's explore by yourself.Definitely, this places is quite appropriated for your family with kids. Absolutely stunning location. Great place to sit on the beach and relax while the waterfall sprays you! If you're travelling from Jeju City, make sure you ask for directions before you try and find this waterfall (there are no buses that take you directly there so you have to walk for 15 minutes). - Guess that isn't the waterfall's fault though!

Absolutely stunning beach with great views of Biyangdo Island. Avoid July and August, as it's crowded. Wait for low tide, when the water ebbs quite far and you even take selfie with Stone Man that usually is submerged in the sea. Also great to watch jeju kitesurfing scene i great activity to try out.

About half-way between U-do and Jeju City, it's not too difficult to drive to. I would allocate not more than 1 1/2 hours to visit this attraction. The volcanic tunnels are very interesting to see. It rained for several days before our visit, so water was dripping from the cave so it's a good idea to bring a hat. Also wear good shoes. There is plenty of signage that explains the rock formations  English.If you found this review beneficial, please click   helpful.   Thanks.

A waterfall which falls right into the ocean, one of its kind and unique. Suitable even in rainy weather but take caution on the slippery rocks leading down to base of waterfall. The best of the 3 famous waterfalls around Seogwipo
A waterfall at the ocean. Easily accessible. A 5-minute hike down from the parking lot. Can get crowded, have patience.

A very short and busy road clogged by tourists, tour buses and cars trying to see and feel the uphill rolling effect. I personally did not see anything rolling uphill. Tour guides poured water and empty round mineral water bottles but it did not seem to give any credence to the anomaly. However I did see one car roll backwards (uphill) rather fast but couldn't tell if it was already in-gear, nevertheless the reverse lights weren't illuminated so I guess it wasn't rolling on it's own steam.

A very long and tiring climb if you are not used to climbing. There's lots of people both locals and tourists climbing along so you will definitely be motivated to continue climbing. Tip: bring sunglasses, pack light, grab a snack and bring a bottle of water, most importantly wear comfortable sports shoes. Just climb slowly and take a break along the way as you need so that you are not overly tired out. If you are thinking of combining this attraction with other nature sites that require ample walking or climbing, do take note that this attraction may already be rather tiring... the view and wind at the top is worth it, in my opinion. You do not see the bird's eye view you see online but nonetheless you see the vast greenery and top down view of the scenery below.

A unique must-do in my books to go where lava has gone before.   It is also a cave, so it dark, a little chilly with the occasional water drop.  The cave is left largely in its raw form (which was great) but it also meant an uneven and potholed path which requires a great deal of care walking it.

A tiring long walk but well-worth the workout as you get to soak in the beautiful green slops of the peak, and the ocean blue waters below. Lots of photo opportunities, and you also get to see the jet ski in the waters below.

A stunning waterfall that one can get close to it. Can be crowded especially in the afternoon. A short 5 min walk from the car park. the rocks where people usually gather to take picture of the stunning waterfall can be slippery, not recommended for elderly visitors.
A small beach. Crystal clear water. The wind was very strong when we visited that area. As it was winter, nobody was in the water.

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

A short 10 mins walk down down several flights of steps would lead u to the base of the fall. For the adventurous and nimble folks, you can navigate carefully across the rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. I was there on a crowded day and the task of leaping from rock to rock didn?t seem possible. It was still a nice view from the base. Do include this site in your itinerary. I think the volume of water was lesser since it was still winter when I visited.

A relaxing trail with picturesque scenery. I went during autumn and the climate was just right. The leaves turning brown was a breathtaking sight and if you're lucky, you will be able to catch a glimpse of deers along the trails.Do be careful along the steep slopes during certain parts of the trail as a missed step could result in some pain. There are water points on the trail though located a substantial distance from each other. Do bring your own food or you can buy it from a store near the summit. Bear in mind that you will have to bring along your trash and don't leave it on the mountain! (Bring along extra trash bags!)

A really beautiful sight to behold! Its a short but steep walk down to the waterfall, with an entrance fee of 2000 won. You wont be able to get too up close and personal though - the waterfall   guards   get a little touchy if you get too close to the rocks that are wet.

A really beautiful and picturesque waterfall! I was in awe when I first saw the waterfall and couldn't stop taking pictures of it from all angles. After passing the entrance, you can just follow the steps down and you can already catch an amazing view of the waterfall. Many people, including my family and I, took one step further and went down the rocks so that we could really catch the waterfall right in front of us. It was truly a spectacular view and the waterfall seemed so majestic. Definitely recommend to visit at least once when visiting Jeju!

A quiet valley in an evergreen forest, the place is almost free of foreign tourists and allows one to capture the most tranquil moments of nature. Where cliffs and reflective pools of crystal clear water meet, lined by stones, guarded by trees and filled with crisp air. The sunlight peeking through the trees permeates a serene and mesmerising ambience in the valley. Look out for the stone wells and Rock Shade Residence along the way. The Rock Shade Residence formed from volcanic lava were used by ancient inhabitants of Jeju Island as shelter. It is said that Andeok Valley has water flowing all seasons long.  With such charming beauty, its no wonder Chusa Kim Jeong-hee, a renowned Joseon-era scholar, used to visit here for contemplation and perhaps, inspiration. Spring and fall would be great for light trekking while the cool forest provides the ultimate summer shade. Nearby attractions: O'Sulloc Tea Museum, Camellia Hill and Jungmun Resorts.Trivia: Andeok Valley was also the filming location of historical K-drama   Slave Hunter   (Chuno in Korean)
A natural spot form by the volcano. It is very cold inside, recommended to bring raincoat as there as water dripping from above.

A must see when on Jeju Island. The trail to the top is well maintained and well build. Gets a bit steep at some points. If you're going doing the summer, as i did brings som water. It gets very hot and humid.

A must see when in jeju. Jeonbang Waterfall is the only waterfall that falls directly into the ocean. It?s a beautiful sight to see. However, if you are handicapped it is not accessible, as there are stairs. Make sure to wear gym/grip shoes as there are lots of rocks/ slopping hazard. There are also (henyo) female scuba divers that harvest abalone and various seafood that are available to eat nearby. Definitely check it out!

A must for visitors tot he island. An area of beauty, amazing geographical formations, haenyeo (diving women), shops and foods. A very steep climb to the top but the steps are well developed and there are small seats along the climb to take a break. Great views fro the top, but if the day is windy be prepared for some discomfort. Take a water bottle, camera and coat! Worth every step!

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

A larger version of Bontanic Gardens. Provide rental of prams for babies/ toddlers. The weather was good when I was there, hands nice and relaxing tour. They have cactus, flowers, plants, water park, caves, birds etc

A large colourful night club with large bar different seating areas and private booths and a water slide. Drinks the usual, but by sheer coincidence, being just 11.45pm when we came in, it was still my birthday by 15 mins and having my passport with me got a genuine full 75cl bottle of Johnny Walker Black Label Whisky !! Water and ice was also free but we had big beer chasers. The rest of the visit was fun but rather blurry. Just disappointed it didnt fill up, though it was mid-week.......
A great variety of exotic trees & flowers, marvellous birds, unusual sculptures,charming waterfalls, traditional symbols of  Jeju Island.  Beautiful inspiring day.

A great museum that is easily accessible.  A bus stop is located a block from the museum.  The ticket price is 1,100KRW during time of visit and well worth it.  The front desk also showed a special screening for me of the information video.  The exhibit is brilliant - informative, visual and interactive.  There's a observatory that oversees the water and the Sehwa area and a play area for small children.

A great hike for people that like to spend the day hiking. I went during the week and it was not to busy but I was told weekends is very busy. I had trouble finding the bus up to Yeongsil trail head as no english on bus signs. Took a taxi which was 25,000 won but was able to take bus home from Eoimok trail head back to Seogwipo. But this hike had much scenery to offer, I was a little bummed that we were unable to hike up to lake in the crater. This would have made the experience fantastic. No waterfalls either as it seemed to be the dry season this time of year but still a great hike. A must if you are a hiker.
A fun beach, with lots of shallows for swimming and playing in the water.  The park is well kept, there are great coffee shops and restaurants. A very nice sandy beach which is hard to find in Jeju.
A fantastic view, but take it easy if you're not into exercise. It's a steep climb to the top! We climbed on a hot day and if we didn't have water we wouldn't have made it!

A fantastic view of jeju and sea.... it takes about 40 to 45mins to climb up slowly... remember wear a pair of comfortable shoes to climb all the stairssss   and bring a bottle of water as you can have rest a point to view some scenary and rest your feet and thirst  before continue to climb to the top . You can get a very nice view at the top of the peak.. it quite cold windy as we went in October early morning around 7am seoul time, so do bring a jacket /wind breaker as well.

A difficult one if you choose to do the longest one which takes 4.5 hrs up and 4 hrs down.We went up  the  Eorimok trail which took us 2 n half hours up..its not an easy trak with steps and rocky path but the track has been laid with a lot of effort.In autumn the trees start to turn their colours .We came down the yeongsil trail which took us one hour to come down with spectac views..its an easier way to climb down than to climb up the yongsil trail.Bus 240 goes and come back at both stops with the entrance name as the stop names.But while from Eiromok entrance it's just a 10 mins walk up to the start of the trail.....its 45 mins walk to walk to the yeongsil entrance bus stop to the start of the trail.There are no tkts entrance for the hikes,but if you have rented a car then there is a parking fees.Carry some food to eat and energy bars and water n juice.
A crowded place to visit during the summer but a lovely waterfall with clean amenities for visitors. Very family friendly, reasonable prices on tourist goods.

A bit difficult to find, but a gorgeous location.   The waterfall flows into a small pool and then flows into the sea.  It was pretty crowded when we went, but still worth going.  The rocks are SLIPPERY.  Be careful when moving around on them as we saw a few people fall.  There are a few shops selling snacks and Jeju treats at the top and a proper coffee shop as well.

A beautiful view on top of Seongsan IIchulbong. Plenty of parking. We did this twice in the same day. The first hike (approximately 30 minutes to get to the top, started at 1pm) was extremely foggy and we couldn't see anything. We hiked back down and spent some time on the shore. Once the sun came out we hiked back to the top. There are several stops on the way with spectacular views of Jeju. You can purchase drinks and trinkets from one small shop about half way up. Use the restroom before going up as there is not one on the way. For a family of three to include a 10 year old we took one large bottle of water and a small backpack with some snacks and additional items. Bring a camera as it is absolutely beautiful. On the way we saw several different species of birds and spiders. At the top there are several benches where you can sit and enjoy the view. At the bottom there is a Mcdonalds, an ice cream shop, a souvenir shop, and other small shops. I suggest you try the orange ice drinks...they are great! Overall cost, 5,000 won for two adults and one child. We paid cash. Enjoy!

20km return, 8 to 10 hours hiking (be there really early in the morning - around 7-8am), some steep parts, beautiful views and pics, bring water and food (they sell only water and noodles up there) highly recommended for hike lovers. Best thing to do in Jeju!

2000krw entry.    Just beyond the ticket booth are pictures and descriptions of some of the highlights of the area along with bathroom facilities.    Further on, are some small shops and food stalls.      It?s a beautiful walk with lovely plants to get to the waterfall.   There are supposed to be 2 meter long, 20 kilo eels in the pool by the waterfall.   We couldn?t see any.    Waterfall was nice but nothing particularly special.
2000 won entrance fees for adults, but really gorgeous waterfall, nice views. Worth a visit, much more so than Cheonjiyeon Falls :)

1st falls was kinda disappointing cos there was no water coming down. Perhaps dry season? On the + side, the still water surface made excellent photo opp. After more staircases, we had the option to descend a long staircase to 2nd falls. Which we skipped and proceeded on. We crossed the bridge of the 7 nymphs - indeed an odd architecture with such a curved surface to near centre of bridge. Easiest is to walk in reverse to give the hamstrings some relief. Later on, there was a lookout point for 2nd falls. Yay. All done, we rewarded ourselves with icecream :)

180m to the top but more then worth it in the end. Taking the hike up the steps was quite a workout, so I highly suggest, prepare to break a sweat. My favorite part was taking pictures on the way down, there are many great picture opportunities. One thing I recommend is to take the extra steps down to the ocean, take your shoes off and enjoy the cool refreshing water. It is well worth it after after walking down.

1) The staff spoke limited English. When we got into the room, it appeared the A/C was not working. We told the staff and their response was that it was made such so as guests no need to turn on the A/C. A/C is only available during summer. They advised us to open the window / take a shower instead to feel fresher.1st night in the hotel, we couldn't sleep as the noise from the air (the hotel is near the airport) and road traffic entered our room as well as the dust.2) The casino opening hour was stated 10:00AM - 01:30AM. I tried to enter the casino at 11:00PM, got told that I would not be able to play (just seeing) as the casino is closing.3) Room is spacious and the bed is comfortable. However, the room and the hotel corridor have weird smell. It must be the carpet smell. The room has an old-looking room and most things in the room are payable (you only get the toiletries and 2 bottles of water)..In conclusion, very terrible experience staying in this hotel. I would not spend a single dollar to this hotel in future.

You'll take a glimpse on how Koreans were living in the past ages. The main thing there is that almost all the village looks alike except for the names and the Big Houses of Noble people in the ancient ages.Overall it's nice to visit but consumes a lot of time to visit the whole village
Worth a visit at least once. Pleasant walk round the folk village. Good collection. Could do better with more displays in English. But all in all thumbs-up for this place..

While learning about the life of Jeju folk village we enjoyed the gardens farms and orchards. They are beautiful and being taken care well. It was our first time that we saw cabbage with flowers.During our visit it was almost toward the end of closing time and probably that's the reason there're not many visitors.

When in Jeju you can choose to go to Trick Art Museum or Alive Museum. Both are about the same you pose and take funny photos with the exhibits. The Alive Museum is divided into 5 sections Trick Art Object Art Digital Art Sculpture Art and Provence Art. If you follow the route after the first three you will get to the outdoor Sculpture Art. The last section Provence Art is basically a large room with a lot of large-sized stuff dogs in Provence village setting. The dogs are not as cute as the teddy bears at Teseum. I think Alive Museum is more suited for teenagers and youg adults visiting in groups it should be more fun for them.
Went there with our taxi tour guide. The village is very nice. Check out the folk village toilet.  And don't forget to say. Eay well my friends. You'll see lol
Went as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It really is like stepping back in time to see houses and the village preserved as it was before technology existed.

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..
Well organised tour of Korean traditional village easy to navigate takes about an hour. Stop at the gift shops in between for gifts

We were taken to the folk village. We originally tried the Jeju Folk Village Museum but that was full of tourists. We were shown around several buildings that we were told were still lived in. Sorry but even primitive people had some form of furniture and cooking facilities. Yes some people may life on site and in other houses. But why show empty and it mean completely empty houses. Show us how you and your past folk lived. Some of the information was interesting until the sales pitch started. The selling of the honey and blackberry cordial which suppose to make you younger and fitter!!! I bought a ship load- not. They took us into a hut with chairs all in rows for a presentation on the value of the juice at $40 a litre bottle. Right next to the village are some restaurants which our guide wanted us to eat in at our expense!!! So I guess the real reason for coming here is their extra bit of money!!!!For most of us on our bus this stop was a complete waste of valuable time.

We were here as part of a Yeha Tour. Our guide took us around the village and pointed out some key elements of traditional KKorean living. The Village was small but well kept. We did not go into any of the houses and we did not meet any of the families. Nobody tried to sell us anything. We had free time to walk around and take pictures and then we had lunch on site just outside the gate.

We visited this place as we were told this folk village is a well maintained place compared to others. The entrance fee is KRW11000 per person. We came here around noon. We went to the restaurant to have lunch which is just a few minutes walknas you enter the village however we were told that they are closed for a private function. We end up having junk food from the convenient store near the entrance. I wish they would have informed us much earlier or put up proper notice on the matter. Anyway we went ahead to discover the village. The paths are clearly marked and easy to navigate using the map. At each exhibit there are signage but lack of the story for each place. Some of the buildings are not so well maintained. You can't enter most of the buildings. They is a cultural show which we managed to catch which ran for about 40minutes. You need to check the timing for it. Overall the place is nice but we wish we had a tour guide who is able to explain to us in detail sp we can appreciate the village and the history of it.

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.
We tour around the place on how the folks lived their lives before. Our guide also explained the statues found outside the village and how many of them were divers men and women.

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

We had an old Korean man who has lived there for all his life guiding us around his own house in English. He was very humorous and a very friendly guide. It was an interesting and refreshing experience of learning about the old village way of living in Jeju!

We did only this folk village with my family and friends. This recreated the feeling of living a long time ago in korea it communicates well the differences of different backgrounds. We did not hire the audio guide and we had two korean speakers with us who were able to read everything. It was fabulous for my kids to see and touch most of the displays plenty to keep them occupied. We saw a dance and others getting photos taken in wedding costumes and a Korean Drama being filmed. Overall the experience was a good cultural morning out. We did not eat there as we were meeting friends for lunch but it looked very traditional

We did not find anything great about this place to be honest. There was the tour guide giving a minor introduction of this village and we took some photos of the village from the top and that was all.

We caught the ferry over to the island (remember your passport or other form of photo ID) and hired a two person battery operated bike which was great fun.   Hired for 2 hours which was ok but if you want to spend longer at each stop then I would recommend at least 3 hours.   We went all around the island.  We stopped the longest at a small village where you can go down some steps to the beach and go and investigate a large cave.   There was an outdoor cafe on the beach serving fish -  very busy.  Can't remember the name of the village but it was towards the end of our circuit.  Definately a good weather day activity.
Was forced to buy honey after given a short 15 minutes trip in the village. Remember to tell the taxi driver that you don't want to go to this place!

Tranditional House and village in Jeju. If you want to know about traditional life. Janggem Korean Drama has taken place the shooting here. You also could buy tea that made from bluberry and horse bone.

Today is the last day in Jeju but since the plane is evening time so we went to Jeju folk village museum.It's worth visiting there! Every one of us really enjoyed ourselves going to learn their traditional style and ways of living! Furthermore the place is very beautifully designedmaking us just want to know what that's waiting ahead of us as we go along!I'll visit this place again if ever to go to Jeju again!

To fully enjoy cultural heritage it is recommended that you spent few hours reading and inspect all the objects that represents it.Even though it was raining during the time I visited I enjoyed the Folk village because they have a very interesting culture and history dated thousands of years.In each places represents how the Koreans house hold systems livelihood and government are highly organized.I also enjoyed the art exhibit and felt honored meeting the National artist.  He even gave me one of his works on display!After roaming around you might want to experience authentic Jeju cuisine by dropping at the Traditional Market inside the Folk village at reasonable price. Oh don't forget to try the Cactus candy!It's just unfortunate that we haven't witness any Korean traditional wedding ceremony that day due to rain.This is much better Folk Village to visit as it is bigger than the other nearby.

This was part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - that gives you an opportunity to see an old fashioned village showing homes built of thatch roofs and lava rock.  There is a couple that still lives there and explains their way of life and the way things were on Jeju.  We also got to try a tea that apparently tastes differently to people depending on what they have going on in their bodies.  I really enjoyed listening to them and learning about their culture.

This village is very well preserved and all the thatched roof houses still live in people with generations down the many 100 of years. The ancient mayor office which is called Gaeksa still remains in the centre of the village and was used to be the place of festivals for the old or parties. Likewise to the castle that was built during the korea ancie dynastiy is still preserved well.
This village illustrates how people lived before Korea became the powerhouse it now is-an interesting piece of history.

Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. So could you!

A place where you could learn a lot about Korean's traditional live and their culture. The guide giving us the tour was hilarious and we had a lot fun in the village. It is a place worth spending time to visit.

A lot of tourists about. This was a small park but it seemed quite popular. But my preference would be the village where they shot the korean series 'the legend'. Just can't remember the name of the village. Anyways I was here around 2008. Enjoyed my tour trip

A little village where most of it residence is women and children. We were brief about the history of the village by a guide in English. We were brought around the village for a visit. A glimpse of village can be found by visiting this place. It represents the Korean culture and old architectures.
500 years okd village worth to see it. Do not miss oportunity to visit it. Next time I will come again.

When you are in Jeju, South Korea a visit to the Folk Village is a must.  during our trip to South Korea from 13 - 20 April, 2014, we visited the Folk Village in Jeju. In my opinion, the place is well set up. It's worth every cent that you pay.  The place gives you a glimpse of what South Korea looks like sometime in the past.  The houses built reflect that time in history.  And the houses in the village were authentically reconstructed.  Anyway, most of us in our group were impressed.  We give rating to the place.

When we arrived, someone from the village immediately took us for a short tour. There isn't much to see but the spokesperson provided some interesting snippets about Korean life. At the end of the tour, she tried to sell us stuff which kinda put us off.

What was originally a cultural and historical tour ended with a sales talk of the local health products. They were peddling hard, so be strong with your will power if that's not what you want. The whole village is van be finished in 20 minutes and it felt more like China than Korea with the many fluent Chinese speaking guides who I think are actually Chinese
Went with my kids and parents. We explore every part of the park. From Caves, cactus to folk villages. We enjoy the plantation at the park and flowers definitely. Must visit

Went to Hallim Park on the end of September 2015, its a good thing we came at Autumn because the weather was not hot and not too cold either. The leaves were turning orange - just like in the movies. There are several flower parks in the Hallim park, such as flowers park; cactus park; bonsai park; stone cave; bird park; and folk village - where we can stop by for lunch. This place is suitable for families travelling with old ones, since the scenery is beautiful for photo-shoots.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

We were there with a tour group and this itinary was compulsory.  Interesting to understand the history and a better understanding of the culture.  The guide of the village was obviously a Chinese but they spin it to say she is Korean (didn't see any)!  Sold products after the talk and items were not cheap.  360,000 Won for the Horse Bone Powder.  50,000 Won for the Horse Oil.  Saw at other shops away from the village, selling at 30,000 Won for the Horse oil.  Bought the Horse Bone powder and realized everything was in Korean!  If this is a State product and only sold in the village, pamplets of it should be in multi - languages as it is targeted at tourists.

We were received by a Chinese -speaking   Villager   upon entering the village. It is well set up, which gives a glimpse of the old life style of the local Jeju islanders. However, after a brief talk about the life of the local people, the guide was more interested to get us all seated inside a hut to sell her products, such as honey, Omija tea, and lo and behold...horse bone pellets (remedy for loss of calcium)! Her sales pitch was pushy and rather unfriendly, and we were not that interested by her goods (the price was exorbitant), we could sense her attitude turned from lukewarm to really cold. There is no doubt some local people really live here, as to keep the tradition alive, also supported by the government to do so. I think is better to keep the selling of local goods to another area (like setting up a gift shop), rather than incorporating it as some kind of compulsory lecture within the guide tour. I find that most off-putting. I give this place an average rating. The surrounding restaurants which serve the famous pork dishes from black pig were good.

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We went to this folks village on tour. For me, this village is very nice and i learn a lot of their culture. For example, as a Chinese, we celebrate Chinese New Year. The elderly will give red packets to us as a sign of good fortune. Everything comes in red during Chinese New Year. But in Korea, they will use White packets and everything comes in Black and White during Chinese New Year. This is because in old era of Korea, when they have wars, the man will be wearing white colour war costume and when they come back to their own house, their clothes is full of Red Colour Blood, that's the reason why they thinks that Red Colour is not a fortunate colour to them. More and more stories you can learn from this place, especially from the statue, you can see usually man is eating always and woman is the one who always do everything. That's their culture. This place is really worth a visit, and by the way, we are not being brought to those shop which sells local specialty. Hence, i felt that this place is nice to visit and nice place to take photos.

We went to this folks village on our own but not with tour, therefore when we reached there, there is only 5 of us, the staff approached us and starts telling us Jeju Folks Cultural stories, the entrance is free and the guide is free, but at the end of the guide, you'll be brought to a room where they'll start selling you the local specialties, we got some discount since we're not with tour (as usually places like this required to pay tour agent some fees), but if you don't want to buy anything, just say thank you & leave, that's all 븝

We took Olle Trail number 1, and there were nothing much to see along the route, except for the hills that we climbed at the first one third of the trail. After we reached ground level, the trail took us to smaller villages which just looked like average cottages.

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu ? called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.

We spent the afternoon at Hallim Park and thoroughly enjoyed the statues, the bonsai garden, the rock sculptures, the caves and the traditional village.  The grasses section appeared to be very dry and in need of some immediate cleaning up.  We were shocked and saddened by what we saw in the bird section.  The ostriches were clearly in distress as they had lost many feathers and were showing signs of balding.  They were enclosed in an area devoid of greenery and appeared to be desperately seeking out food by nipping the air.  The enclosure did not allow for these beautiful birds to run and get the necessary exercise.  Yes, there were food dishes in various locations however they didn't seem to meet the needs of the ostriches.  The peacocks were also showing signs of stress as their plumage was rather thin.  They were enclosed in an area where the floor was of interlocking brick.  This is as far from a natural setting as possible. Our visit ended on a sour note and it is our hope that the dire situation of these birds will be addressed by those in charge.  We highly advise anyone who visits this park to make his/her concerns known as it is the only way to rectify this sad situation.

We spent a morning in the park. we saw a signage stating 'can speak mandarin' with some car parking space outside so we went down, apparently is a very small 'display village' which the 'guide' explained some of the history & activities. didn't manage to see live black pigs. the 'guide' saw we cannot enter the actual village as was occupied with people (which I am not sure how true it is). and they started selling us product in the end... however we manage to see folk village which we think should be the 'real / correct' one when we left and go straight down the road and see walls surrounding with flag & a big map (which too bad we can't understand)

We hired Mr Kim Si Nam's service for a day, touring the Eastern route of Jeju island (Woljeongri beach, Seongeup Folk Village, Manjanggul Cave, Seopikoji, Seongsan Ilchulbong and Noksan-ro). We happened upon this place along the drive to Jeju Folk Village Museum (which is a must do).
