If it’s springtime?or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju. ? Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.? Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.? Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km? to about 250 residents.? The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.? There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.? But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.? You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.? Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?? Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.? The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.? Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.? Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:? Good points:? outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;? site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival? (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:? bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;? sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.? There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.? Getting there:? Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .? There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.? Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

I have to say, when we reached the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong we were a bit underwhelmed. It's impressive if you haven't yet seen the summit of Hallasan, but if you have it really doesn't compare. The crater of Seongsan Ilchulbong is porous, so it doesn't hold water like Hallasan. And it only takes you about 20-30 mins to reach the top viewing deck. It does make for a good photo, but so do the views of Seongsan village and the coastline nearby. The view on the pathway walking towards the base of it is also impressive in itself.It's definitely worth visiting, and there are plenty of little shops/stalls selling food as well as cheap souvenirs. Nearby is Ilchulbong beach, with black sand. Haenyeo female divers are famous here, and there is a restaurant at the far end of the beach serving fresh seafood caught by the divers, but we didn't have time to eat there.

I don't understand the hype of this place. Maybe it's because I went on a Sunday and no one was around, but I walked around for about an hour and there wasn't much to see. The small houses are cute and it's interesting to read how durable they are when taking into account that they are basically made from mud and straw. But the town was absolutely dead quiet, we felt like we weren't even supposed to speak. I wouldn't recommend this 'village'. (There was a small coffee shop near the car park that sold incredibly expensive coffee).

I can't make of this place. It has plants, caves, a folk village and greenhouses. Yet none of the attractions was really top rate. I would give it a miss and visit attractions with more focus on any one of the above.
Here we can known the shape of Jeju Village, Jeju House, Jeju Entrance Fence, etc.  Here we can learn how Jeju People Live.  Nice Place to go and to see.

Has a little bit of eveything that Jeju offers, lots of trees, flowers, stones, caves and a tiny folk village.

Hallim Park is really a variety of interesting elements of Jeju Island rolled into one. The cave located within Hallim park is one of the main attractions. Other attractions include a multitude of gardens, some animal exhibits, and even a small recreated folk village.If you have more than 3-4 days on Jeju island, I would highly recommend Hallim Park. It can be combined with the excellent Hyopjae Beach located close by. Great day for families. If you are staying less than 3 days, it would probably be best to focus on the main natural attractions Jeju Island is so famous for.I enjoyed exploring the park, taking some pictures with my wife, and then relaxing at the beach.

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim Park is huge and divided into various sections. You can spend almost a day slowly strolling through the different sections for plants, animals, cactus and you can even visit underground caves. You can also visit a very small old village modelled after the olden days of Korea. It?s a place suitable for all families with kids or senior citizens. The entry ticket is on the expensive side for Jeju.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

Hallim Park has everything you would want to see. It has a big and beautiful flower garden, stone and bonsai garden, caves you can explore, a folk village, and a wonderful cactus garden.  It also has a bird garden and reptiles in cages.  You can spend at least half a day exploring everything.

Hallim Park has a mixed big of attractions --- from folk village, lava cave to bonsai and tropical gardens.  It is worth spending a couple of hours exploring.......many nice spots for taking pictures around the park........beware though, each of the attraction is not very spectacular or unique, but the park just gives a sense of the essentials in Jeju in one place

Hallim Park features an extremely interesting cave complex quite unique as it has been dug by lava, a traditional Korean village, beautiful waterfalls, a bonsai garden and a section with creative sculptures. The price is very affordable and you can also visit the beautiful beach opposite the park while you're there. Worth a visit if you have spare time on your hands as it is quite far from the main attractions.
Hallim is a beautiful place where you could see a little bit of everything (cave, flowers, village etc). Each sector is small, but it does deserve a visit while in Jeju.

Half science, half art. A museum dedicated to the formation of the igneous rocks in the area, tectonic plate movements, volcanic eruptions, formation of lava tubes, and various methods of making craters. Extremely interesting!Then rock art. Lots of interesting rocks from around the island, arranged in a way that makes them just so fascinating.Budget a couple of hours here for a leisurely walk through these sections. Add a couple more hours to see the historical village section (which we didn?t go into as we had seen these elsewhere already).

Had a port of call in Jeju. The cruise offered a number of shore excursions. Instead, we took the free shuttle into town. It dropped us off right by the underground mall (half block past it)We walked around a bit then hailed a taxi. He agreed to a fixed price of $100 USD to take us to the folk village, then to sunset peak. (The cruise was $119 per person so we saved $138)We climbed to the top. It was strenuous but with frequent stops we made it. It?s like 59 stories. At the to you get a great view of the town and the sea. You also can look down into the volcano (and see a grassy crater)A million photos later we came down. We then went and saw the women diver demonstration. That was fun. They sang for a while then went fishing. While we were there, one of the ladies caught an octopus. I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

Guide is good explaining about the village and oldtime Jeju. We came here by chartered car, not really sure how to come here by public transport. For me this place not very special, it's just different with typical hanok house that you ever see in Seoul or Jeonju.

Got a tour of the village for about 5 minutes, then they herded us into a room to hard sell their crazy product made from the bones and other parts of the horse. The products were crazy expensive and we were not allowed to leave the room until they were finished. What a waste of my precious vacation time.
Good for family with small children or elderly, or couples wait relaxing visits. It has lava caves, flowers, stones, old villages, excellent for us!!!

Going to the Jeju Folk Village is like taking a trip back in time.  I can only imagine how hardy the people of Jeju were in order to survive.  You can see replicas of ancient houses, learn about the different social classes...even play dress up....my mom dressed up as a queen of the Joseon Dynasty and I dressed up as a kisaeng (not fun with my big feet) and we got our pictures taken and had a good laugh.  For those of you who have watched Dae Jang Geum, the folk village is not to be missed.

First we were ushered by a kind lady to her village and gave us a free guided tour to the small village , we used the restroom , finally she introduced us some of the products she sell to us like jeju honey , horse cream oil . But the real Seonguep village was behind this lady village which was bigger than hers and where the korea drama   Daejungum   was filmed .

Finally we met a Filipino tourist guide here in Seongeup Village. She can speak english very well but of course we used our native tounge/language so she was able to explain to us very well the history of the village and Jeju as well. It's only from her where we learned that the famous Jeju Black Pig used to eat human poop/dung (but that was circa 1940's or earlier).  We also learned from Grace (name of the Filipino guide there) that Korean women, during the early years, were the one who work for the family while the husbands only stay at home. Sad to hear that. =/ We also learned about the history of Stone Grandfather Harabong as well as the various symbolisms used in Jeju.When in Seongeup, make sure to try their Omija, an herbal drink made out of fermented berries. It can help cure acne, headache, kidney problems and good for diabetics. Kinda pricey but worth a shot. They also have other herbal medicines which you can try. As we all know, Koreans, especially their ancestors, are used to taking medicinal plants so I guess they are really credible enough when they say that this or that plant is effective for healing ailments. Google the benefits of OMIJA.By the way, this is also the place where the famous Koreanovela Dae Jangeum (Jewel in the Palace) was filmed.If you happen to visit Seongeup Village, ask for Grace as a guide. You will definitely learn a lot. And oh, we get to check out old korean houses as well. ^_^NOTE: I think there are many communities within Seongeup village but ask your guide to specifically drop you off at the community where Grace is. No entrance fee as well.
Fascinating village,  lovely homes, very interesting place. Enjoyed our visit visit.  Allow about half hour

Excellent view and atmosphere! A long steep (with stairs) and challenging climb up the inactive volcanic island mountain that earns you good exercise and satisfaction! You can already enjoy the picturesque surroundings at the foot of the mountain with different views and you can buy some souvenir there and also enjoy a short horse ride (not free of course). If you are there on a sunny day, do buy some popsicle or ice-cream to go up.   There are entrance fees for the entrance as well. However, it is well worth it once you reached the top. It is fantastic to be on top looking down to the inactive volcano crater and enjoy the view of the sea that looks like touching the sky. You can literally feel like you are touching the sky too! The best time to go there will be during sunrise! Don't forget to take a selfie with the mountain height indicator board to boast your achievements! Oh, and just right before you reach the top, please take a look at the back downhill at the interesting look of the city below and take a selfie and also take some nice selfie around you.     On the way down, there is the fishing village where the you can enjoy the seafood while watching the women divers catch clamps and oyster. There are some fiexed timing but I have already forgotten the timing.    Seongsan Ilchulbong is indeed a must visit destination everytime you arrive in Jeju!

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh   ginseng of the sea   (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.

Ermm. I like this place. The houses are maintained like they used to be long time ago but people still live inside (watching tv) make the village so lively. The place is clean, well-protected and demonstrate Jeju culture.
Enjoyed wandering through flowers, and bonsai trees. Interesting look at the folk village and some gorgeous peacocks. Takes a couple hours tops but a nice place to visit
Cute traditional  houses with Korean villages  culture. Nice scenary  for photos  taking.  If u like  to see ancient culture,  this is a place to visit
Came here by tour, would only recommend if someone is explaining the history of the village to you. The price of the products they sell maybe slightly overpriced so so take note.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. I felt good in walking road with various ecology system. All was good to me, but reptile in small transparent box was pitiful. If had time, I want to feel natural feelings in this park keeping my composure. Excellent place to enjoy reserve.

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Been to a lot of caves in my life but these are so interesting as they have been shaped by the lava flow. There are information boards throughout the caves telling you how certain things in the cave were formed from the lava - definitely a must see if you are going to Jeju!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater, Seongeup Folk Village, Oedolgae Rock, and finally Jeongbang Falls. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

Beautiful scene to be seen. Very natural. 20,000 stones of different verities. Natural as traditional village houses in India. Toilet facilities are everywhere. Very clean. Dogs and cats are not allowed.Water fountain is there. very good place for peace, health and meditation.Thanks.

At the entrance of the village, the town mayor greets us. It?s a very small town. But this guy speaks good English, easily understandable, proceeds to his narrative of the village, it?s culture and history. Very informative and entertaining as he interjects jokes from time to time that find application in our daily lives. At the end of the tour, he will try to sell you tea concentrate (which really tastes good, just did not buy because of luggage space management) and a beauty product, horse oil cream, which if we look at his face, would seem to be doing a good job. His skin is very firm despite his old age. My friend was convinced to buy one because of his skin. Short visit but worth every minute

As per previous reviewers, we are greeted by a China lady who bring us around the village explaining the history of this village. I admit her stories and sayings are interesting and we learnt more about the old jeju village. After we say no to her products, she left us free to explore the small village. Not a place I will go back but i remembered the stories.

As for the places we visited, we loved the Manjanggul Cave, Sunrise peak and the foot bath class at the Herbal park. The maze and folk village were ok. I probably would prefer to exchange one of those two for more time at the Woljeong beach.

All these places are being preserved by the government to protect the rich history of Korea and Jeju. The place still has people staying there especially the old and young.The whole   village   is bonding as a big family which anyone has their main job to do. The guide will explain some of the daily things in the past with many preserved items. They will introduce the medicines they use such as honey, horse bone power and 5 taste tea; you also can purchase it.It is good experience.

Against the warnings we ended up in this village after visiting the Kim Younggap Gallery (highly recommended) and getting bored of waiting for the right bus. This   village   is not much more than some normal village with a few thatched roofs, interiors setup purely for presenting products. We sneaked in and out after a few snaps (luckily it was only 2 of us) only to have a woman literally running after us with a small 25000 krw box of blueberry pills. Avoid it, especially with a group or day trip!

after visiting the jeju folk village, this was quite smaller, still was easier to visit, shorter distance to drive, so if you stay is short in Jeju, come this village, ou will find all about the korean past culture, just missing big stores and restaurant like the main village have.

After the unpleasant beach at Udo, arriving at Hamdeok beach was a delight. With just a short trip from Jeju city this little beach village is amazing. With many restaurants and cafes along the water, one could spend a nice long day here. The water is nice and clean with showers and changing rooms available nearby.

After reading the reviews i was a bit reluctant about visiting the park but i am glad i did. I only wish i had more time to see everything, like all the small trails leading to the folk villages at the far back. This is not just for people who are history buffs, this park can be enjoyed by anyone who appreciates nature and quiet, peaceful walks. It is a windy area so be prepared if visiting in cool seasons. For only ~$5 this is a nice park to spend a few hours if you want to slow it down and be in nature.

After parking the rental car at Seongsan Harbor, we hopped on the ferry (KRW 1,500) to cross over to Udo. Upon alighting from the ferry at Cheonjinhang Harbor on Udo, we headed to the Udo Tour Bus counter and got ourselves a ticket each (KRW 5,000). The whole tour is conducted in Korean. Not a single hint of English but it was enjoyable. The bus driver was also the tour guide, telling us about the significance of each stop. He'd stop for 20 minutes at each place of interest and if you do not hop back on, fret not, you may hop on the other tour buses. Keep your ticket stub.The whole tour took about 2 hours. The village roads were really interesting. If I visit Jeju again, I would want to stay overnight at Udo. The atmosphere is good, the air is fresh, people are nice.

A visit to Sanbanggulsa Temple was part of one of my favourite day trips in Jeju. It is about an hour west of Seogwipo-si by bus and across the street (albeit a bit of a hike) from Yongmeori Coast which I very highly recommend. Getting to the temple requires a short and easy climb up some stairs where there is a huge golden Buddha, an army of miniature mint-green budhhas, and a gorgeous panoramic view of the ocean and village below. A little further up is another fascinating statue of Buddha in a cave. Overall, this is a nice place to visit and a great opportunity for photography.

A village that has been created to show what life in Korea used to be in the past. For an Indian like me, such places like this exist in my country which are unchanged for centuries. So it was not a marvel for me and my jaw was not exactly dropping looking at the kind of chores they used to do in the past. It could be exotic for people who have never seen something like this, but ho-hum for moi.

A very small traditional village attraction with free guide who can speak Mandarin. Very limited traditional houses to look at. No big deal. The attraction is apparently made famous by a TV series that filmed there. Nothing much to see but the guide took great efforts in explaining about each mini-attraction in the village. We ended up in a hut being given explanations on the local products they were selling (e.g. local honeys, herbal health drinks, horse bone powder, horse creams). We were not forced to buy but given that the tour was free, we were obliged to buy stuff that we could easily find for lower prices as the markets, especially Dongmun Traditional Markets in Jeju City.

A rather large village, of what we were allowed to see maybe two   houses  . A very brief history was told about the place, before we were yet again, ushered into another hut, only to persuaded into buying some super magical powder tea drink. I politely refused.

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

You may find a lot of Korean bbq pork restaurants on this street. Some shops open till 2-3pm and some closes early for lunch. They serve almost the same menu in every shop on this street!

You get an amazing view when you go up the stairs. the view also changes a lot from pine trees to sand beach volcanic rock beach and the view of Halla mountain (the highest mountain in South Korea). Everywhere was very clean and the path was clear and guide signs were easy to find. I also really enjoyed the ocean view. It's perfect if you go there on a clear day.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

When it is raining this is one of the place you should come you can just relax and have  some tea besides they sell variety of Tea which is very nice and good. They have a tester too where you can taste certain tea. There is a cafe too but mind you it's a long queing so I just skip it maybe because it is raining time so everyone go there. My favorite is the pack O'sullac Milk Tea it is so very nice. I should buy more of it. Next time will surely buy a lot of it.Besides the tea thing there is innisfree house beside it. you can make your own soap the organic cafe at the innisfree house is also nice too.So I recommmend you to come here whenever it is raining for indoor activity. even if it is not raining it is good for relaxing and enjoy the view of the tea trees.

well. this fashion street was near with my hotel & i've walked here quite many times in a week. not so special for me as i don't do shopping but i ate 2times in this street that was impressivefirst time i reached here at 1st day no any breakfast shop near around*(they are opened at 9-10am at least) quite hungry & finally i stepped in one of traditional shop that only served 3 types of food all was hangover soup ha. seem that for drunken. price not so expensive(but not cheap) and quite many stuffs. tasty but full. lady boss also quite nice although she can't well communicate with meanother times with fds that was in a quiet corridor seem quite expensive restaurant with old & korean deco. however price was acceptable & serve sausage stew. well we ate traditional sausage stew in korean style house(boss always walk out from his room & overall style was house instead of restaurant). he was quite concern do we know how to eat & taking care of our table. maybe it has no many tourist but only korean or japanese while we having dinner moment.
Well u can literally find everything here. From live seafood to dried stuff and fresh fruits. We particularly like the night market street food stalls with lots of yummy food

We?re staying at the Lotte Hotel and this place is within walking distance.  First waterfall didn?t have any fall at this time due to a drought or off season maybe.  2nd fall was nice & it involved some walking down the stairs.  Overall the park is very pretty with its vibrant colors of the trees and the famous bridge you can walk across.

We went to visit this Dragon Rock and it put a bleak end to our Jeju trip. The rock is a beautiful artwork of nature but people seem to be taking too much advantages of it. The town nearby is full of hotel and other shops for travelers just down the street from the rock. We just couldn?t walk very near to it because the way down there is dangerous and blocked with the fence.
We went to the 1st shop at black pork street. Expensive black pork but it is worth the price. Even my kids love it. We end up ordering 1 more set although expensive

We walked from our hotel located at the Arang Joeul Street to the Saeyeongyo bridge for almost 30 minutes. There were many locals visited and walking leisurely there. There many restaurants and the Seogwipo Submarine was located on the way there. You can see the beautiful ocean wave along the way to the bridge. The bridge connected to the Saesom island. The island was brighted by light and old korean song music at night. We visited the bridge twice in the evening to see the colourful light and daytime to observe the surrounding scenery. The trail to Cheonjiyeon waterfall can be found? on the way to the Saesom bridge. The entrance to the waterfall was after Chilsimnigyo bridge.

we visited two parks in Jeju. Hallim and Spirited Garden. ticket price was almost the same for both but Hallim was by far much better and bigger with good design and a lot of different and amazing trees and some birds too. It is really a must visit for Jeju visitors to spend around two hours enjoying the park.

We took city tour bus and stopped at this famous black pork street for dinner at the shop with long queue.   Minimum order is KWR 54000 for 600g pork for 2 pax ie roughly 300g per pax.  It seemed so meaty but the helper grilled the pork just nice and we finished all.

We just visited the chocolate museum as a family and it was a bit of a let down. The tickets were 6000 for adults (tickets for children in elementary I think were 4500?) and they gave us free Americano. There really wasn't that much to see  and the place smelled funny. I think if you?셱e really interested in learning about the past of cacao and chocolate in Korea then this might be a fun place to visit  but if you don't have much interest in that  it might be a waste of money.However they do offer chocolate making classes every hour for little kids under 13. So there were a lot of children there when we went. Might be a fun place to visit with children :)They also sell chocolate  and we tried a sample and it was pretty good and rich in quality. We also bought 3 bars of 70% cacao for 30 000. The original price was 36 000  but with the entree ticket you get a 6 000 discount.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내
입력주소: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내

review: We have tried black pork in Seogwipo but intended to go to Black Pork Street for the Michelin starred restaurant Dombedon. However by the time we arrived they were already closing (it was close to 11PM at that time) so we went to the restaurant next door called Hwaro Hyang.We ordered 2 portions of black pork ala carte for the both of us although they have a set menu for black pork + abalone. It was not as good as the one we had in Seogwipo but still worth a visit.Will be back for Dombedon next time!

We had an amazing time here at the spirited garden! There are so many beautiful trees to see and the people are lovely! It really felt like a spiritual experience. I felt so at peace while I was here. The citron tea was amazing and helped so much after I got a cold teaching my kids! Loved it and want to come back again!

We didn't expect much for this attraction. But it turned out so amazing. We enjoyed the path leading to the main fall with pretty things from the trees to statues. It must be good to be here in early April as of many cherry blossom trees.

We choose Yeongsil Trail as it's the easiest but too bad in less than 1km we had to turn back. We were there in early April 2014 and the wind was blowing like crazy and it was very cold. Reason for turning back? We spotted ice and in no way wearing the suitable clothes for the climb. We even saw the waterfall freezes. Astounding and beautiful. The trees were all bare and yellowish. Don't expect greenery at this time of year.

Was recommended by the people at my resort to visit this place. Reason being it is very clean. I did not do too many hikes in Jeju and this was just one of the few I did. It was a small forest garden owned by a family and now looked after by the 2nd generation daughter.She gave us a brief intro in English of the forest. One that actually does not have soil and one that offers a different season from what it actually should be.Unfortunately we did not experience this difference in season while in the forest. But we just enjoyed walking around this small forest garden admiring the trees that have sprout out.A good walk if the true forest hike may be too much to bear

Walking through this garden park is very peaceful and relaxing. There is a cool cave feature so you get to also go into caves. The captive birds are in small enclosures and the peacocks look like there tail feathers have been pulled. Also there is a white sand beach walk across the street after you are done the park. Taxi from Ramada Plaza was 26000 wan. Bus ride home was 3000 wan and took about an hour on the 702.

Visiting this place remind me such a same road in East Java with the same phenomenon. But I think that this is just an optical illusion created by Korean artist. This is my opinion : the trees and things on both sides was uniquely designed to give an image that the road seem to slope upward though it really slope downward.

Visited in the evening.  It is a local market selling Jeju specialities as well as a wet market section selling the fresh & live seafood.  Good to visit if you are into shopping for foods and want jeju local foods and street food.
Very impressive bonsai tree collection. Interesting underground caves with both lava and lime. Not crowded.
U can Find all sports of planets there. Greenery every where. Can see Flowers from rachael seasons. The water gardens is beautiful. The bonsai trees are outstanding

Transportation- You can take bus 755 to the museum takes half an hour from jeju downtown. Food- nothing nearby but you can get pretty decent coffee and jeju-special tea/drinks at the 'innisfree organic green cafe' at the same compound. The museum itself is not that exciting took us 15 mins finishing off everything including the teatree garden. The innisfree cafe/store nearby is so much more fun especially for the female fellow travellers.;)

Totally unexpected.A unique place where Bonsai trees are beautifully and elegantly presented.A big thank for Mr Sung for warm welcome and gift about this outstanding garden. Inspirational lessons from Mr Sung on how he has been developing the garden in last few decades against all obstacles. The garden seems his beautiful masterpieces?

This was a surprisingly informative and enjoyable place.  An amazing amount of beautiful bonzai trees.  It also had a large amount of sculptures and two large koi ponds with waterfalls.  A very relaxing and enjoyable visit.We also got to have tea with the founder!

This was a quite pleasant area to avoid people.  Some parts look like the backdrop of a Tim Burton movie in the winter with the leaf-less trees but it was one of the most peaceful spots in Jeju in cold weather
This street is near the night market in Jeju-si. A small street fill with restaurants selling black pork Korean BBQ. A great place for dinner.
This short walking street has many shops selling cosmetics sport apparel youngster fashion etc. It is bit quiet for the walking street may be due to the drop in the Chinese tourists.

This place is ok if you have some spare time and want a peaceful walk.As long as you don't meet any tours because they can me noisy.Its nothing special just trees and very little else.Not worth it if you have to come out of your way.

This place is nice. The museum tells you all you want to know about tea. Scent samples of tea are all over. There is a snack nook where you can try their signature desserts and beverages. I ordered the hallabong Ofredo and green tea latte cold and it was sooo good! There is a green tree plantation where you can take pictures but a warning says ?쒫eware of snakes.??So be on the safe side and that is to stay put on the edge of the plantation.:)

This place is considered clean for a local market. Mixture of raw fresh food and cooked food stores. We came here at around 10am and a number of cooked food stores are already open. Nice experience walking around and eating street food along the way. There are benches around for you to sit and have your food. Market closes at 8.30pm.
This place has several themed hiking trails. You can choose one of them according to your allotted time. You can walk comfortably under the shady trees. I recommend this place is a must-see in Jeju.

This museum is absolutely fun. From the moment I stepped in it was simply hilarious. I have always loved historical museums but I love these interactive ones even more. I was supposed to go to the Trick museum but the concierge at my hotel recommended ALIVE museum. It was a walking distance from my hotel in Jungmun so I walked over. At the beginning of the street where this museum is I saw a big sign but no museum. I had to walk a little bit before I saw the museum. I think they have to do better with the signs on the major street so visitors will be more informed on how to get there. It also looks like some wings are in still in construction. The road leading to the building looks like it needs finishing too.That being said once you get into the museum there are lots of interesting exhibitions and pictures. Most of them were famous painting s that we could interact with while taking pictures. It was fun watching other people interact with the pictures and sculptures as they took pictures. My favorites were the ALIVE Aquarium the coiled python that was squeezing the life out of me being a mermaid being dinner and fighting the leopard for my red suitcase. They are some sculptures in the museums grounds that are very interesting and interactive too. For just about $9 USD I had a very memorable day in Jeju. This is one of my favorite attractions in Jeju Island. I highly recommend visiting the ALIVE museum while on Jeju Island.

This mountain is so tiring if you try and complete the ascent in 3 hours on a hot day but it's worth it for the view at the summit! The upward root that I took was a little bland because it was all under the cover of trees so you don't actually see anything new for most of the ascent. The crater on top still had some snow on it in April and you can see the full perimeter of the island from the top. I think this view would be even more spectacular in the summer. Make sure you bring plenty of water! There is nowhere to buy it on the way down if you take the alternative route. Also be prepared to use the horrible 'hole-in-the-floor toilets' if you need to go. Needed to take a taxi back to the hostel at the end because no buses stop there. A great day out though.

This market sell all sort of things from fresh seafood to chocolate. We bought those chocolate souvenier from here. There are many shops selling similar item.One can also buy various ready to eat food (street food kind) and there are restaurants too. One thing to take note is that dustbin is rare  so you may want to bring a plastic bag to throw your litter.
This just seemed like a mountain valley filled with trees that couldn't even be seen very well because of high brush and trees around the path. Not worth the time going there!

This isn't the most amazing place in the summer time. I think if you go in the fall or spring it would be amazing. They had loofas in the trees to mimic the flowers that should be there but aren't due to the seasons. It was weird.

This is where physics takes over. Let the fun takes over. What you see don't really make sense until the guide explains it to you. All in natural surroundings and in good time. Don't forget to try out the street food there while you are at it. Made my day. Cheers again!

This is more of a shop and cafe than a museum. The museum part is just a few display cabinets that leads to a cafe with goods displayed for sale. The tea plantation across the street is a flat moderately sized area that pales in comparison to the vast rolling and picturesque tea plantation of cameron highlands.This attraction is not worth the time unless one is a tea-lover.

This is more like a nice park rather than a garden. They have beautiful walks among the trees and you can have tea and cakes in a small restaurant with the terrace seats looking out the wide green field. But the staff can?셳 speak English so there must be a tour guide to take you here.

입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: This is a refreshing place with a variety of trees. Very nice and fresh. It is packed with tourist also. There is a coffee house and a buffet dinner restaurant.

This is a manmade park-like garden with a variety of plants and trees and water features. It is well worth the time it takes to walk through the grounds  just for the experience of viewing the bucolic setting. The main feature is Michon Cave which really didn't dazzle us as much as it apparently was supposed to. It's just a cave in which one walks down a slope to see some tacky lights and statues. The park  on the other hand  is scenic and pleasant. There are some concessions where they sell the usual tourist stuff.
This is a great one stop shop to get souvenirs from jejuLots of korean street food available if you arekeen to try

This is a big market where you can find everything you need for vegetables to fish and meat to chocolates and other household products. There are also street food sold here so you can grab a bite if you're hungry.I found my favourite kkaenip kimchi here and it made me so happy. This is because there are no kkaenip kimchi sold in Malaysia.
This garden is beautiful. I loved the furniture made out of trees. And the bonsais are well preserved.
There?s a few black pork restaurant in the street. The price for a person is W18000 and the portion is just right.

There were a diverse variety and choices of street food. The younger generation of entrepreneurs were experimenting with fusion and various creative combinations. The quality offered was reasonable and reflective of local tastebuds but more effort and further refinements would make them a successful household name. Generally street food was relatively cheaper choice compared to restaurants. There were also abundant fresh food to choose from.
There is nothing much to see at all. Bare trees and plants. And super cold in March. The only fun to do is the train ride that?s about all.

There is nothing exciting with the Jeju Chilsung Fashion Street. It is a series of open-air pedestrian-only road lined with boutiques. The stores were familiar such as Starbucks New Balance Spyder MLB Tommy Hilfiger Crocs and Adidas although there are some designs that are available here that are not yet available in the Philippine market.The place was supposed to be part of the Jeju Winter Festival. Indeed there were a number of Christmas-themed displays although they were nothing compared to how lavish the Christmas displays in the Philippines are.I only strolled around the area then went to the Dongmun Market nearby. The Jungang Underground Shopping District is also close?봞s it was winter it was more comfortable shopping at the heated underground location of Jungang that it was in Chilsungro. Also the items sold at Chilsungro are from brands that are more known internationally (and thus are more expensive) than what is available at Jungang.
There are many restaurants along this street which serve Black Pork BBQ. We only eat here once so it is difficult to tell which one is good but all look good.

There are lots of walks but very badly marked.They are colour coded but the trails arn't.Very confusing especially if you can't read Korean.They range between 1-11 kms long.In march all the trees were still bare so not very attractive walks.
There are a lot of streets food here selling all types of local korean delicacies.  I love fried black pork with toppoki. Food are rather expensive here. Anyway worth a try!
The walk towards and back from the fall is very well kept. Quite romantic with the trees around . The fall is not too big but there is a calm serene feeling looking at it .
the walk through these gardens is amazing.  From 300 year on Bonsai trees to the very cool acres of caves below.  very relaxing and plenty to see and learn about.
The view is amazing. And the green is calming and lush. A lot of good photo spots. There are restaurants and some street food in the area.

The street food stalls at night were awesome in the market. However all the good one has long lines and slow moving as most of them are cooking in front of you. Not knowing which one is the best  we choose to join the crowd and stand in line with others and skipped the other with short lines. Parking is terrible even Google Maps shows many nearby parking lots. We tried two separate lots and both were full. Instead of waiting someone to pull out  I ended up parking on the side of nearby street and walked to the market.

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

The park was quiet when I visited. It was an easy walk with nice trees and scenery. It had a great calming effect on me. Love it. Just 5 minutes drive from the park is the Hanwha Resort Jeju which I went for a fantastic spa treatment. My afternoon was made perfect !

The museum becomes busier as the day goes on really busy late in the day so going early is the best plan to be stress free and see everything with little to no people there for best photo experiences.The museum is really cool and covers Korean tea history. It leads to the tea shop where you can sample some good tea cakes and teas. You can also purchase teas here as well as other tea confections.Next to the museum short 5 minute walk is the Innisfree Jeju House which I cover in another review. You can get lunch and some fresh teas to enjoy here. There is also great tea and Jeju House related products as well as fun tea soap making kits. Ones you can do there and others that you can take home.Before lunch at Innishouse but after tea and snack at the Tea Museum you should walk the plantation. Great photos in the fields next to the tea museum but across the street are two areas one with a big tree that is old an beautiful but also a tree with deep red blossom that makes for a great photo with Hallasan in the background.The Stone House was closed for renovations when we visited in April 2018.

The maze is not small and quite complicated even with the use of the map provided. Can be quite fun for the children. There are many nice spots to take pictures as the whole place is full of trees and shrubs and flower.
The market is big with several lanes. There is one particular street with amazing street-food in the evenings. Parking is a bit of problem though
The market consist of many raw seafood sellers  vegetables  till street food. The food inside were very tasty. Its a must try

The Lee Jung-Seob Street near the museum is where more time can be spent (than the Lee Jung-Seob Museum) with some good restaurants and cafes lining the street that is decorated with art influenced by him or replicas of his work. Visitors can also take a look at his old home located on this street.

The green tea plantation of O'sulloc was my last stop prior to my flight for Seoul. My recommendation is to try the O'Sulloc green tea ice cream. There were also other green tea based products displayed like soap and beauty products. As for me I enjoyed my green tea ice cream under the flowering Cherry Blossom tree.

The folk village was quite large with some interesting buildings but everything looked samey after a while. I was hoping to see a variety of performances on the stage but it was only a few songs sung by a group of women - charming enough but not what we were expecting. The foodie street also didn't have alot of stalls open though we did buy some cactus taffy which tasted like treacle and raisins and lasted us most of our trip in SK. One good thing was the interactive bits such as the old games children used to play. Having been in folk villages in other countries where there were people in traditional costumes showcasing different crafts and activity the Jeju one was a little disappointing.

The famous Black Pork Street in Jeju Island is within walking distance from the Dongmun Market and the street is lined with lots of restaurant serving BBQ black pork. We tried one of the famous restaurant recommended by a Taiwanese blog and found it to be cheap and good. It's the last restaurant along the street if you're walking from Dongmun Market. Well worth a visit.
The crater is now full of trees and plants therefore looks like another mountain but I give it a rating of 5 for the fantastic views and park. Nice place to take a relaxing walk.

Temple is nice design and along our walk we found many tangerines tree which I believe during the spring season the temple view will be good. Since It's FOC do drop by if you have time. It's along the way to Teddy Bear Museum and Cheonjeyon Fall Yeomiji Botanical Garden

Tea plantation near the city center with a tea museum containing a few old tes pots (you will probably have wider assortment in a flea market). I will probably enjoy visiting an actual farm with fruit trees and greenhouses planted to vegetables than spending time at the tea plantation. There is no entrance fee but there is also no tour guide or someone or something to explain what there is to see.

Stopped here for a little while we were driving around the island one day. We came by the day after a typhoon and weren't really expecting them to have the kayaks going (a lot of stuff was closed due to the storm). The area is still very pretty but a large tree had fallen over the path and we weren't able to go much further. You don't need a lot of time here - if you're like us and just driving around it's nice to just stop for a little while. On a side note - others have mentioned the kayaks seemed to have stopped. We thought they maybe weren't going because of the storm but I didn't see anywhere around where you could have possibly rented them either (like no buildings that looked like they housed the kayaks or offices where you could sign up or anything).

Soooo pretty! Absolutely stunning glass sculptures and the trail through the forest was an absolute highlight of my stay in Jeju. The glass tangelo trees must have taken FOREVER to complete and they were so well done. Loved the little farmhouse in the forest and the huge glass spider webs. So peaceful looking out at all the colours across the lake. Definitely recommend this place for something a little bit different.

Some sports brand but nothing exciting. We came twice but still we did not find any shops we like. Compared to shops in Seoul this is pale. Most shops selling winter coats. At end of this street turn left and just outside the wet market we find a shop bang bang. They have 2 floors lower for women and second for men. Managed to get some simple t shirts. Design was just very simple. Other than these nothing exciting here. The wet market is more exciting with tourists the korean snacks there were great! Here in this shopping street you get cafe. Very quiet cos winter. There is a shop selling desugner embroudery hackets and jeans gor guys but very expensive. The staff was speaking cantonese to the chinese customers so we assume Hong Kong shop. Nicer Jackets were $500 onwards.

So this is more a shop than a museum to me. But the cafe there is highly recommended!! You need to try the green tea cakes and the cookies as well! Wish i could've tried the ice cream but i was afraid i get sick. It's literally the best roll cake. The garden was nice and you can make your own shop at innisfree didnt have enough time though.. Remember to take pictures at the cup made of plants across the street..

Since Chinese-Korean relationship became worse there is huge decrease in tourists from china which resulted in many shops shutting down. Half a street is empty now so there's not much choice of shopping. However big shops are still good (new balance and such). You'll see almost no people there.

Seriously stunning display of flowers at Camellia Hill; the biggest arboretum in Asia famous for its forest path and beautiful gardens of camellias. The arboretum is home to 6000 camellia trees of 500 different species including species that are known to produce the world?셲 largest and earliest blossoms. The place is drop-dead gorgeous and I would of spent a whole day adoring the different flowers if I wasn't rushing to maximise my day in Jeju.We were lucky to catch the early blooms of the Cherry Blossoms which was a major highlight of the trip for us. Towards the end of the trail is a small shop that should desserts coffee and souvenirs like postcards and cosmetics. I loved their postcard selection and went a little crazy on those souvenirs but no regrets. My brother enjoyed his homemade strawberry ice cream as it was packed full of flavour!
RecommendedA lot of food truckAnd local foodFresh fruits etcNear the beach and blackpork street

Recommended by our guide. We spent around 1hr here in a Spring afternoon. Big crater with many green trees growing in it. Also able to see farms far away. Many spots to take nice photos. I would say good to visit but ok to skip it.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

Read that it was man- made garden !! After the visit I felt that this was one of the best Garden ever visited. The various plants and trees were really great and we spend a good 3 hrs walking round. The cave was wonderful ... even thou only 350m is open to public. Highly recommended even for adults .

Reaching the top will provide you a panaromic view of the town below but that?s about it. It has a small piece of land where stadium like seats had been built. You cannot roam around coz it?s restricted as it?s shaped like a bowl and it?s just covered with trees and all..

Put your vehicle on neutral and it will seemingly be rolling uphill. Very intriguing.Unable to figure out how it happened but definitely have something to do with the way the trees were planted along the road.
Pretty beach and calm water. It's nice to sit and chill by Cafe Delmoondo.  We spent hours here.  You can just sit or walk on a trail or the street with restaurants.

Our trip to Hallim Park was wonderful.  If you love nature you will love to explore the well maintained gardens.  I love the garden with Bonsai trees as well as the Cactus garden.  There are caves inside the park too which you can visit.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Our guide brought us there and we really enjoyed walking in the park. My son was walking quietly by himself taking in the fresh air. Lovely place to find peace and tranquility and to just be in tune with yourself and nature.Lovely old nutmeg trees which give out a lovely fragrance! I could come here to walk every day!

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is very small (there are not many displays to see) but there is a very large shop that sells tea products and a cafe that sells drinks and desserts.  There is a very brief tea tasting demonstration w/ narrative in Korean only.  In the cafe we had the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake we've ever tasted.  Prices for drinks & dessert was expensive ($4.50USD each for a small cup of ice cream and a slice of cake; $8.00USD for a large glass of orchid flavored iced green tea).  The tea products in the shop are also expensive.  If you are a tea connoisseur then this is the place for you.  Across the street from the museum there is an open field where the leaves are grown that you can walk around.  There is a viewing tower above the museum where you can also see the tea fields.  If you are exploring the west side of Jeju island O'Sulloc makes a great rest stop. I would not deliberately drive all the way out there just to visit this museum.

Opposite the museum is the tea field which you can walk across the road to take a photo and see how they grow the tea tree. There's parking space beside the museum. Besides there's the tea cafe and souvenir shop at the arrival floor. I would recommend the green tea smoothie top with soft cream green tea latte and green tea roll cake. It's very crowd with tourists and local people. So normally the seat are full. So if you go with friend I'd recommend one to fine the seat and one to queue up to get drink and desserts. Even its long queue to buy but it doesn't keep you wait too long. The green tea spread is the signature. There're also many selection of tea with nice packages and different aromas for your selection.

One of the must visit place in Jeju if you love watching sun rise. It takes about 30 minutes to climb up the steps to the viewing platform. We stayed at Sun Villa Pensions which was just above Nature Republic a stone throw away from the entrance of the park. You could see the crater from the balcony and Starbucks on the left. It was really convenient to have a place nearby as we had to wake up early  to hike up and catch the sunrise (6.45am). As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

A short street lined with black pork bbq restaurants. We settled on Hwaro Hyang. Not cheap but for the quality of the food it was worth it.  We have problems locating this place as there is no signage and the locals that we encountered couldn't speak english.

A road less than 15 mins about 50 meter of start sign and stop sign when our driver off his engine bus automatically roll up and roll down by itself nothing more.Some street and souvenir store in this area.

A pleasant walk among trees and nature. Many small flies hovering around at certain areas. A small cafe and convenience store near the entrance. An easy outing for elderly folks and a pleasant walk for families.

a nice place to visit. walk around the green tea farm to see the green tea trees visit the gallery to understand the background and history of tea buy the tea products at the retail shop enjoy the tea at the cafeteria. there is an Innisfree Cafe next door also which is a must visit place to enjoy the soap making process and enjoy the food and drink where I had the best yam drink I had ever tasted!

A must stop during our busy vacation here in Jeju! They have free parasols that we used during the sunny day and it made the garden a lot nicer to enjoy. We bumped into the Director that created the garden and he was very kind. I highly recommend buying his book from the store and he even gave us an autographed copy:)) You can tell that each bonsai tree in the garden has a lot of love invested. There are koi fish in the water flowing through the garden and they are well fed and taken care of. There is also a cafe in the garden that has fancy drip coffee. We went in early October and the weather was perfect.
A lover of plants and trees would love to spend hours here in this park. The lava tube may be a new experience for some . . . .
A lovely nature-based walk in a beautiful forest. Appreciating the history and beauty of these ancient nutmeg trees!

A lot to see. So many kinds of fishes  live or cooked you name it they have it. Reasonable prices are helping you enjoy shopping more! Try street food too. You?셪l love shopping and eating in there but parking is challenging! Very crowded!
A beautiful architecture Buddhist Temple. Surrounded by tangerines trees. Come and see for yourself. =)
2 giant mazes for you to try find your way out of it. One of the maze is of short trees and the other is of stone.

You should be geared for a long walk inside the park. The ticket is a bit pricey (11,000 won per adult) with nothing much to see. There are plenty of palm trees and different types of pine trees as well but not really very rare or special species.They have collection of tropical plants (bananas, guava,mango , etc) which I am sure tourists from Southeast Asia will find boring. They have lots of cacti although not very extensive collection. May be we came at the wrong time because there were only few flowering plants. Overall, quite a waste of time and money ( and energy too).
You can walk around under the shade of thick netmeg trees. Also, you can enjoy basking in the woods. The oldest tree is about eight hundred and fifty years old.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

Yes, 80% of the stuffs are made of glass, minus the buildings, the trees, etc. Basically its a small garden of glass. Visit only if you have no other itinerary.I went because it was on the itinerary of my package tour.

Wondered how we would with a Korean map, but no need to worry. The path is crystal clear, bounded by rope all the way, and very clearly signed. Much of the path is either wooden planked or hessian carpeted (I jest not !). Starting at 750m it?s a tough 1200m to the top, but a mainlybgentle ascent over 9.6km. The last 150m is a little tougher, but the views of the volcanic basin when you get there make it all worthwhile. Much of the climb amongst trees, and very popular with the locals so busy even on an early Monday start. We took 7 hours including half an hour at the top, very stiff calves this morning...

With limited time to spare, our taxi manage to meander through the winding roads, but ww were a little disappointed that autumn leaves were scant; so all we saw were a hand full of trees in red and orange hues. I guess we were too eager for autumn. Perhaps another time.

Will never forget our longest hike in our entire life! Our earlier plan was just to enjoy the view of fall foliage during the autumn and it happened that Mount Halla was the only place... Did our homework earlier before our trip there so that we can get a perfect picture of the foliage in Hallasan. Ended up, we only managed to see a lot of deciduous trees, perhaps, due to the heavy rain and wind the night before our trip. Wrong timing... There were some trees along the Yeongsil trail (the route we used) but the leaves had turned brown, not the orangey red... My husband and I couldn't feel our legs after the hike and I lost my cap due to the very strong wind! Anyhow, the view was spectacular as Hallasan is the highest mountain in Jeju!

Wide variety of shops: clothes shoes restaurant etc.  Nice place to get some shopping done.  I went here last week to go for last shopping i noticed that the street is less crowd maybe due to the   virus   spreading arpund the world and also the weather is very cold. FILA BRAND IS WAY CHEAPER here.

Wide market to find seafood, products, snack food, fruits, juices. Located over few streets, hard to speak English with sellers. You can get local food, strawberry orange chocolate, seafood. Like many market in Korea, customers can sit and eat. It is also located near to underground market. Overall, nothing much to buy but you can target local Jeju food and junk food.

When you reach the place you bet your life that the road goes uphill. The driver stopped the engine and switched to neutral. To our big surprise the car picked up speed and rolled downhill. your eyes were cheated by the bushes, trees and surroundings.

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.? This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.

What a waste of money! Very disappointing especially given the very high entrance fee (6K). The crater is just a hole in the ground covered with trees and a 1.2 km walk is a loop around grass patch and small forest on one side (next to a busy road, so you can hear the traffic). If you have never left a city before you might like it (like, you get to walk on a grass for a moment, not on a concrete sidewalk, UNBELIEVABLE NATURE EXPERIENCE, right?). Just save your money, for 6K you can have a nice lunch, not 30 minutes grass walk.

What a breathtaking, incredible walk through a well-manicured garden with hundreds of bunjae (bonsai) trees lining the path. Everything is so green and there are so many excellent places for photos. Great to spend at least an hour enjoying the nature.

Went to the 1100m point where the wetland reserve is. Didn?t occur to me that wetland exists on mountain top. A round trip takes about 20mins and was quite scenic. It was foggy when we were there, which adds to the ambience. Our guide pointed out some of the edible leaves and tree sap. Very interesting stopover on the way to the south.

Went there to see how the locals interact, to feel and absorb the local vibes. Nice to see how the locals live and behave. Pleasant to stroll through the stalls. Went there in the morning and saw many fresh local produce like seafood, meats, fruits, vegetables, household items, clothes, bags, shoes .......just about everything. We also saw many stalls selling street food - bungeoppang ( fish shaped bun-filled with sweet red beans) , eomuk ( fish cake ), hoppang ( steamed buns) , tteokbokki. ( stir fried rice cake) , gyeranppang ( egg bread ), dak-kkochi (korean chicken skewers ). Had a great breakfast on these streetfoods. We also saw lots and lots of hallabong too. Very juicy and sweet these Jeju?s iconic mandarin oranges. Not to be missed one must try the hallabong fruit juice and hallabong icecream. We also bought some local korean snacks , kimchi and souvenirs to bring home.
