My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

Mt Halla is known as Korea's jewel. It is its highest peak. And well worth the trip to Jeju. We left Seagwipo very early (around 7 am) and took bus 182 (181 also goes there) to Seongpanak because we wanted to climb up to the peak. We got to the mountain around 7:45 and started the hike. The weather was super nice when we left, and we planned it that way, because we wanted to at least get some nice views of the city, and while at the summit. This is a long day of hiking, so be prepared. Bring snacks (and a trash bag, because you have to carry everything back down), and water. There are 2 checkpoints along the way that have bathrooms. The last checkpoint sells ramen for about 1500w with hot water. This is the checkpoint you have to get to before 12:30. We made it there around 11, and up to the summit before noon On the Seongpanak trail, there is also a lake with an observatory that's worth the detour.The last part of the hike up to the summit is pretty steep and rocky, so watch your footing, especially because you might be tired from walking up. Wear adequate footwear, make sure they are sturdy and comfy!Unfortunately, we didn't get that lucky with the weather as it because overcast as we were getting up there. I guess it really depends on your luck (the next day, it was super clear! Damn you Mt Halla!!) hahaha.We took the same trail down (from the summit, there is another trail, but no buses stop there. And this is where your comfy shoes are a must. The hike up was not bad, but the hike down, was torture! Our feet kept hitting the front of our hiking shoes, so we were bruised and hurt by the time the hike was done. We were also sore for the next 2 days (and we're pretty sporty, but we rarely walk for 8 hours) Overall, it's a great hike. The trail up is covered by trees, so it is cooler than it seems, but there are still some great views, especially with the fall foliage. We'd be surprised at the range of people walking the trail, old and young love to hike up this trail, and we understand why!

Most of the park is outdoors, and we went when it was raining, so that wasn't that good. But the place is beautiful, with trees and stones lined up. There's also a museum about volcanoes as well as statues of historical figures. Very nice place although it is only accessible by car and very difficult to get a cab.

Most of famous travellers places are not free of charge but this place has no entrance fee :) I visited here in winter and fortunately there weren't many people so I was able to enjoy this forest path pretty much. Calm, beautiful and very peaceful place even thou trees were not that green. You don't need to wear athletic stuffs but sneakers are essential.One thing you need to be reminded is there aren't any trash boxes and they must be taken back with you.

Many things to eat and buy here! There are many shops selling tangerines (Jeju?s specialty) and local products. At the back of the market, there are also many street stalls that sell super yummy street food like fried chicken and mozzarella hot dogs. Something unique to try would be the Jeju Tangerine Garlic fried chicken from one of the stalls.
Many bears, took lots pictures and have cafe inside. Nearby area many tourist attractions and Cheonjeyeon Fall, Yeomiji Botanic Garden just at another street behind.

Lovely botanical garden. I went there a couple of days ago with my friends during our Jeju trip.We didn’t want to get around the whole island for the short holiday, but relax. There were a number of flowers, trees, flowers, and beautiful gardens.If you are a fan of gardens or nature, you must visit there.

Love Hallim Park! My expectation was a quick walk around an outdoor park, but it was so much more! Easily taking an entire day if you want it to, you can meander through under ground lava tubes, fruit orchards, small animal zoos, bonsai tree forests, etc.! Highly recommended.

Lots of variety here from plants, pulses, clothing, fruit and veges and fish and local street food.  The prices aren't cheap as you would expect in a market but that's the same all over Korea.  A good variety is why you would go there.
lots of nice trees, bonsais, stones & cave. This Park was made by one man alone

Lots of greenery and flowers to appreciate. Stones and sculptures were seen everywhere. A place to take it slow and just enjoy the surrounding. There were very pretty gingko trees, a sea of yellow leaves on the ground at the end of autumn..
Looks like a small valley with trees. Unimpressed and to pay KRW6,000 for entrance per person, better to use the money to buy ourselves coffee.
Looks just like a normal road, except that due to the slant of the trees it appears like things are going uphill. A trick of the eye, and a cute experience.

LEE Joong Seop Street is lovely and there are some art shops where you can do window shopping. Then this small street lead you to the house where Lee's family lived for certain period, in a 4.6m2 room for 4 family member. You will be stunned to see how small it is!! But they loved this place where they could hug all the time, kids, and the couple. Behind those free zone, the art museum is located. Admission is 1,500 KRW(1.10 USD, 0.80 Euro). You can request docent on the spot. Korean is always ready, for English, better to call in advance when you will visit. At the end of the street, there is small traditional market where you can get some street food and fresh fruits. Strongly recommend to visit to feel the artist' spirits who lived miserable period. He made lots of work for 6 years before he died, age of 40's. It looks like Van Gogh did lots of works during short period. Good to visit 3rd floor to enjoy the view toward south part of Ocean.

Keep in mind, the founder, Paek Uncheol, is quoted   ?Visiting the park is intended to be a journey through the mythology of the island, entering through the ear of Seolmundae*, progressing through the body and exiting at the feet. It represents the journey of life and death.? Taking a journey that ends in death, even if it is a metaphoric (mythical, mystical, mind-boggling) death, may not appeal to everyone, but it could be transformative if you're open to it. Allow for hours of contemplating stones, thousands, tens of thousands, of stones, natural, carved, authentic, replicas - millstones, mortars, volcanic bombs, boundary markers, 2000 ceramic jars, fossilized tree roots - locals thought its creator, who collected these stones for forty years, had gone mad. Three courses to follow, each taking one to two hours. *Seolmundae Halmang, the grandmother of Jeju Island.

Just came back from the mountain hike. See absolutely nothing......the mountain is bare with nothing, no flowers, no grass, no green leaves trees and no waterfall despite we took the most scenic yeongsil trail to the top......rather disappointed but we just take it as an exercise. For those who r interested in the mountain, pls choose the right season if you want nice scenery

Jeju Olle Trail is completely round the island broken up into 21 different routes.In total we walked about 13km, about 3.5 to 4 hours time taken. Photography time included.We started our walk from Hyatt Jeju along the Jungmun Beach (we did Route 8 going eastwards) heading towards the Daepo Pego (port) and ended our walk at the Yakcheon Temple.Ensure that you look out for arrows (blue&orange) along the ground and olle trail ribbons (blue & orange as well) tying on trees along the way. Terrain is very varied, from easy tarmac lanes to quite difficult lava rocks along the bays. Suggest you wear proper walking shoes. Bring along your own water & snacks. There are a few restrooms along the way. If you are staying around Jungmun resort area (many hotels there), take airport bus limousine no 600 to go back to your hotel. Its about 1000 Korean Won per person.Overall is an interesting walk because you will see village, seaside, port & temple along the way. This is one of the very popular walk in Jeju, so its like a   must walk   walk.. We just did a short segment of the Olle Trail & apparently other segments are even more interesting.. Check out some photos for illustration.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

Jeju Glass Castle is the famous place at Jeju. When I first went inside, I just like walk in an unreal place. Since the entire thing is made by glass. You can see glass everywhere, such as the flowers, the trees and the artworks.One of the special things in this castle is an artwork that calls ?a moment of musical concert?, this artwork show that the moment of a band that is performing. The entire performers have different emotion and music instruments. It is very hard to do this, because each performer?s face is smaller than a coin.Here also have some funny place, such as Glass labyrinth and distorting mirror. Be careful, maybe you will lose in the labyrinth, or become a fat boy/girl in the distorting mirror.Finally, I suggest that you need to be very careful in this castle, if not you will break the glass.

It's probably the best place to shop for street wear in Jeju but it's nothing compared to Seoul. After visiting this place, one realised how expensive jeju is compared to the mainland Korea.Free samples are given out when purchasing cosmetic in Seoul. Nothing of that sort in Jeju. Fashion spotted in this mall is old and pathetic. Don't get your hopes high.Only saving grace is this mall protects you from the weather elements during shopping. But so is any mall in Seoul too.

It's one of the biggest traditional markets and has many shops so you can buy almost anything you need.I usually go for seafood and vegetables which are fresh and low cost.  I particularly like raw fish (Sashimi) which can be purchased by fish (shop will catch a live one and cut sashimi while you watch) or pre-packaged (around $10 ~ 20)The market also has many street food, like spicy rice cake and pancake like dessert.It's not as clean/convenient as a shopping mall but has a lower price and more cultural feeling.

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

Its fish market but have a lot of store sale a souvenir and gift item like small soju and jeju orange, jeju cohocolate and sama candies and friend...and at the end of dongmun market they have delicious street food....and yummy

It's close to the main centre of Seogwipo, easy to find with street signs posted in English around the place, it only costs 2000 won to enter, and it's not only unique but a spectacular chance for photos. Do as the Koreans do, they sure do love a waterfall selfie.This and the nearby Cheonjiyeon Falls are two must-visit attractions in the area.I'm not sure if you can walk too close to the actual waterfall, or what the rules are for swimming in the waterfall pool, but on a hot and sunny day I seriously considered it.You do get a bit of spray from the waterfall, so keep that in mind when taking a photo so as not to get your camera too wet.

Its big, full of trees, nice view for taking pictures. Dont go there during holidays, lots of people, long queue for the service train that will bring you around. We didnt enjoyed the place coz its raining during our visit. The windmill area is beautiful, not so much flowers around coz its start of autumn. I think its better to visit during spring season.

It's an okay, nothing to be exaggerated. However, enjoying the walk towards the fall with serene and scenic view is very relaxing. During spring, strolling under the cherry blossoms trees and get to enjoy some local live band music show with people get to move their body to the grooves! Once you got out of the fall, several merchandise shops selling local snacks and merchandise. There are also arrays of local food store nearby serving varies pick of seafood. I went to the nearest restaurant near the merchandise store with red signboard. Food potion is huge and price is reasonable. It was really fresh and tasty! I stayed in the Choi Hostel around the area, so it's quite a walk and hike on the way back, what's with full bloated tummy. BTW, I only ate 2 dishes alone :P

It's actually just one short stretch of the road but interesting. The road gives you an impression that its going up hill instead it's actually going down the hill. The surrounding including the plants, trees, field and fencing are giving you that up hill impression. So when you switch off the vehicle engine that you are in, the vehicle will continue to move forward. Same goes to the test where they will show you by rolling a water bottle. Try walking backward and you can feel it. You might feel a bit disappointed as there is nothing else over there

Its a short street UG mall sells things you will find in normal shops in Jeju.  The catch here is that this place is not just underground BUT its air conditioned.  Its maintained very well with clean toilets.  We spent about 40 mins leisurely but didn't buy anything in the end.  I won't say its a must-go place but if you happened to be at Dongmun market, its a short walk to this place.

Its a really short strip of street where most BBQ restaurant are located. Most of them serve black pork . As mentioned in most reviews , the price is on the steeper side. If you like some BBQ black pork then this is the place to go. Its a tourist friendly place after all.

It's a great honour to be able to admire Mr Sung's Spirited Garden! It's absolutely a must visit whenever you are in Jeju! The garden is a real Paradise on Earth! It's a unique place that teaches you many important things! The garden features many outstanding examples of bonsai trees, beautifully shaped stones, a waterfall, a restaurant and a souvenir shop. It's easily accessible by car or by bus, and will be a worthy place for everyone, especially the nature and art admirers. I highly advise everyone to visit this incredible place!!!

It?s a very big place.. there are a cave, garden, mang kind of birds, trees ans flowers.. i think it is a good place to visit in jeju.. you can see many things here.. but it is difficult to find a bus to here and the bus is not ontime..

It?s a place must visit in Jeju island. Air is so fresh and the walk is tranquil. When you walk through the forest and appreciate wat the Korean say that it is a place for meditation. There is a tap near the entrance, water is so refreshing. Trees in the forest have been there for hundred of years . It?s a treat to see some trees with autumn leaves. There are some Low walls with black stone formations which apparently is the volcanic rock from Jeju itself.. Would definitely come back here again to spend more time in the forest At the end of the walk they even have the vacuum facility to blow off the red soil from your shoes
It will definitely not take you more than an hour to see everything it can offer. It only has a couple of waterfalls, a huge bridge and a lot of trees.

It was once the most beautiful street in Korea. As a German that comes from the countryside it was just a regular forest with a small hiking trail. Nothing real special about. I was a little disappointed.If you're in a hurry, don't visit the Bijarim Forest but rather the Lava tunnel which is close by!

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was interesting how they recreated real-life historical events and famous works of art with teddy bears.  There are two main exhibit halls.   Of course there is a gift shop where you can purchase teddy bears.  My wife and I enjoyed it and took lots of pictures.  I think you will enjoy this place, even if you don't have a thing for teddy bears. Bonus:  there is a really nice Starbucks right across the street.

It was foggy and cold when we visited Mt Hallasan after noon.We only took a short hike from the bus stop to the Eorimok Trail entrance as I'm traveling with my families with small kids. It would be nice to hike from Eorimok to Yeongsil trail. As it is still early spring time, the trees and flowers have'nt bloom yet. Overall still a nice visit.
It was an easy walk, lots of street vendors, waterfall was beautiful. Perfect weather in October! We spent 2 days in jeju and just about did it all.

It was a nice walk around Hallim Park especially if you like Bonsai trees, folk Village and more...We had a great walk aroundthe area and the weather was so freshly cold?. Went to the caves was also interesting. Beautiful garden. A place to come back. I like to put more pictures but I could only put 10 of them.

It was a foggy day but we managed to drive to the Hallasan National Park. Once we arrived, the weather was clear and with a little sunshine. Perfect to walk the Eoseungsaengak Trail. They said it will take about one hour but that is really with no stops. We took 1.5hours. There are a lot of wooden steps up the trail and some turns. We saw mainly trees and bushes. Generally it was manageable. Do wear good walking shoes. When up the top, the weather was foggy and we could not see the surrounds which was a pity. Nonetheless, we enjoyed the clear fresh air and the workout. This trail is the shortest and the best for travelers who have no time or not as fit and mobile.

It took me 2 hours to reach the peak from the bottom. There are a lot of people saying 3-4 hours but that is because they take breaks every 10 minutes.The first 70% of the trail you are in trees and can't see anything. They have steps and wooden walkways so you don't need any equipment at all. When I arrived at the top you couldn't see much around you because of the fog/pollution or whatever. The crater itself was ok, I took some photos, but the water is very very small. If you have limited time I would not suggest coming here, there are much better mountains in the mainland of Korea. When I came the rocks were all wet, but they were not smooth so it wasn't slippery. There is a bus that will take you directly here if you search online from where you are. The bottom sells a few things like water, noodles, and Korean sushi.
It is volcano. It is not active. So there are many beautiful trees and aceneries. I think it is must go place in Jeju island, South Korea. Fee: 6,000KRW.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. It is basically a Bonsai tree-themed Garden decorated with many waterfalls and beautiful ponds full of colorful koi carps. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

It is my first hiking ever, I do feel some kind of relaxation after the experience. At first, I wonder how can those people climb up to reach the top, it takes more than a thousand stairs to be on the top, I was pretty scared. But when I was first stepping on the environment, I can feel the natural beauty of the nature. It enhances me to have a greater heart to finish the journey. There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before. It is a great experience to me and is memorable.The overall journey took us about 1 hour, if you are a fan of hiking, you must enjoy it as the view is priceless. **Remember to buy a bottle of water before you go, there are shops for you to buy some snacks and drinks in the beginning of the path.

It is just a vision trick. The road appears going up when it is really going down, so cars and buses can glide down when put in neutral. The way the trees at the side of the road is planted tricks your vision. Coming from Canada, we have seen it similar to the one in Moncton, New Brunswick.
It is just a street; however, I was surprised when I put down my Evian bottle water n it started to roll by it self (fast enough) even though it was put on a flat street.

It is a museum showing the history of Korea, the emotions and aesthetics of Koreans. Lee joong seop died at a young age and did not leave much work. However, the well-maintained birthplace, street and cafes and crowds around them show how this artist is popularly loved by Koreans.

Is  a must visit to this market. Parking spot is very hidden. Lots of street food, souvenirs, tangerines, chocolate, fresh fish availables. Jungang Underground Shopping Center and Chilsungro Shopping Town is also next to this market. (near to entrance 4)Lots of people buying chocolates from the stall located at the intersection between entrance 3 and entrance 7. (probably the biggest stall and cheapest?)

In this market you will see what Korean people eat usually in their daily lives. Oranges are everywhere and thry are pricy. They said the oranges are very nutritious and full of vitamins. The problem is we could not tell which stalls were genuine. At night, there were two rows of street food selling korean delicatessen. Check it out!

If you want to enjoy around two hours walking without difficulties in the middle of an amazing and dense  forest I highly recommend you to visit Bijarim. Considering the time needed for these trees (nutmeg yew, family of the Taxus) to grow and the fact that normally you can only find it as bushes into other species's forest this place is a unique jewel with many of the trees aging more that 500 or indeed 800 years. Beautiful and relaxing experience that I will keep forever in my memories as a lover of trees that I am.

If you want something go, hungry go, street food go, you name they have it. Ate sushi for 3 days in a row at one of the restaurants in the market and never the same twice. Best place to try the famous Jeju pork.

If you stay in Seogwipo, this is absolutely a nice walk and visit. We payed 4,000 won for two people for entrance, which is worth the small amount of money. The area is beautiful where you can see different trees, fishes and of course the waterfall. We were there around 12 in the daytime, and it was a little bit crowded by the waterfall (since everyone wanted to take a picture and the place is small), but there is a small place where you can sit and just watch the beautiful waterfall!

If you need a good work out, this forest in Jeju is worth paying a visit. The autumn 10C air is perfect, although the leaves were only starting to blend with the sun, you can imagine the shades of red, orange and yellow if it's at its peak!  The old nutmeg trees provided good photo opportunities for those with a passion for nature.

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.

If you love nature and taking walks, you'd enjoy this place. The smell is nice and the trees are impressive, but walking around for an hour looking at hundreds of the same trees doesn't excite me. It was nice and an okay way to kill an hour, but if it's between this and doing something else, choose the ladder.
If you love black pork Korean BBQ, this is the place to be. The little street in about 50 metres long is full of black pork bbq restaurants. You cannot go wrong with any of them

If you like cats then this place is for you. There are about 20 cats roaming around the property. I am not a cat person at all but the cats did not bother me. They are friendly and stay out of the way of people. The maze was fun and somewhat challenging. I liked that they added a stamp feature (you had to find stamps on your journey) so it wasn't all about getting out. They are pretty chill here, so you could do the maze 1 million times if you wanted. If the parking lot is overflowing then I would recommend that you not go. The property isn't big enough for that many people. The positive is that there is a cave down the street you can visit as well. We didn't get to visit the cave because it was a public holiday. I would recommend that you go here, especially if you have kids. The value is not that high but most things on Jeju cost money. It is not a rip off.
If you like bonsai, tulips and great landscaping, this botanic garden is for you. I particularly loved the hundred year old bonsai trees delicately nurtured to inspire visitors of its natural beauty.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

If you can't make it to Manjanggul caves, there are caves here too. There is a lot of English signage for the trees, which is great. There is a cafe and restaurant on site. I really enjoyed the  afternoon out, lots of lovely different areas to explore.

If you are in the Seogwipo-city area and only a short time in Je-Ju this is a great find. A traditional house, a story of a great S. Korean artist, a nicely designed park and a street of small arty shops.

If you are in Jeju-do, Black Pork Street (Heuk Dwaeji) is a must visit place. As the street name given, yup.. Selling point is Black Pork. Go in to one of the many restaurants on street and try the grilled black pork meat, it is the signature dish in Jeju Island. If you try this is Seoul, it will cost you double or maybe triple the bill. Most menu are in Hangul but there will be a simple English too, the best way is to choose the set menu. Price are reasonable if you choose the restaurant that is less fancy and not those tourist welcoming type. We had the best BBQ dinner in Korea.

If you are fanatic about nature then you would probably really like this park. However if you enjoy nature but are more swept away by breath-taking scenery then in my opinion you will be really disappointed. We did the Seogwipo trail and for the effort involved the reward was just not enough. The trail took around two hours each way, and part of that was over some extremely difficult terrain. It's not that step, but walking over really large stones and boulders for over an hour can get really tiring, especially when there is no view to distract you, you are just surrounded by trees, There is nothing to see at all for the most part! At the end of the trail, the mountain lake and view of the valley is nice, but nothing that special or amazing. We were there in low season and even then it was extremely crowded, so you never have the feeling that you are really hiking a mountain. I wouldn't do it again.

If u like striking out poses with friends using the lifesize teddy bears in different costumes and characters, this is the place for u. There's also an outdoor gardens with bear exhibits, fountain and lake and a blooming grapefruit tree. Looks really good and I think it would be a nice feeling sitting around in the outdoor garden having ur lunch. That's provided it does rain. Get your tickets cheaper via taobao, the China online shopping site. They have almost 50% discount for foreigners, which we tapped on. Just need to print our confirmation and entry was a breeze. Also, this place is accessible via a bus from Jeju intercity bus terminal. Stop at jungmun resort. Nearby are alive musuem, yeomiji botanical gardens and cheonjiyeon waterfalls, good for a self planned one day trip.

If possible, I would recommend visiting this garden on a cloudy day or partly sunny. There is something peaceful about the weather and the garden that makes you want to stay forever. All the bonsai trees are beautiful and wonderfully taken care of. You can see how much great care was given to these trees. The plants, the rock artworks, and the people all create a very peaceful and very unified picture. This place is fitting for people of all ages. I would recommend everyone visiting this place.

I would say that this waterfall is higher and have better view than cheonjaeyeon waterfall althought cheonjaeyeon waterfall is close by from teddy bear museum, we take taxi in the afternoon from teddy bear museum to jeongbang waterfall and it cost around 25-30 usd, and the street is almost empty. The road down to the waterfall is much nearer and easier than cheonjaeyeon waterfall. When you take pictures, off course you would like to get closer to the waterfall, but be carefull of the rocks, they were quite slippery, we spend an hour to take pictures and sitting in the rock. The admission fee on nov 2014 is still 2,000 won per adult about $2. On winter it opens from 08.00 to 18.00

I would not call it a must see attraction, but go there if you have spare time. I really liked their collection of cacti and insectivorous plants. The glasshouse arrangement is really impressive. The tropical section had fruit-bearing mango trees which was a sight to behold (inside the glasshouse). The French garden, the Italian garden, etc are good for a stroll. Didn't find anything there specifically impressive.

I went to see the crater in middle day. Was a long bus ride to get there for a 10 min visit in all. Not what I expected. It is a very rare formed crater in the world and the explanations are on a board but kind of deceiving to look at for me. All full of lush green trees and very wide, it does not give great pics and you don't see it that well either. Not as impressive as I expected. Would tell you to prioritize other stuff if you have a tight schedule. Souvenir shop has not much to buy and there is a small restaurant for snacks or ice cream.

I went on a tour group to Jeju. The bus arrived at the Mysterious Road, all of us were waiting eagerly in anticipation of what's about to come (after hearing so much hype about it). Looking out the window, I saw a little kid on the street place a plastic bottle on the tarmac, and it looked like it was rolling up hill at first, but because of the way the bus was angled along the road, I was quick to discern that it was a mere optical illusion.As our bus reached the front of the 'queue', our driver switched off the engine, and slowly, but surely, our bus picked up speed. It was interesting as it was the first time I sat in a vehicle with it's engine switched off, THAT WAS IT. I looked out the front panel, and we were obviously going downhill, as I could not even see the sky (just trees whizzing by our bus).I'm guessing it only looks like you're going uphill from certain angles. Thankfully, we didn't spend too much time there, and off we went to our next destination!

I was thinking of skipping this attraction in favour of the natural attractions. Due to bad weather I visited this place on a whim but I enjoyed it better than expected. The building itself is quite pretty like a big greenhouse. The floral arrangement and landscaping is tasteful although not as good as Gardens by the Bay in Singapore. There are pretty sculptures dispersed through the compound. There are many different gardens to explore. We visited the indoor gardens first followed by taking the lift up to the top floor for a view of Seogwipo and lastly took the train for the outside gardens. It was too cold and windy to walk outside. There was some confusion about where to buy train tickets, the driver helped to walk to the counter and buy our tickets. Spring is probably a good time to visit since many flowers are in bloom. It would be good if they can stop the vandalism of the trees by the Koreans, many of them scratched their names on the branches.

i was spending 4 days on jeju island and i went Ecoland in the 2nd day morning. the entry fee is WON12,000 per head. parking is free. You will like here if you like tree and nature environment. the weather was nice when i visited . therefore, i took some beautiful pictures. and i also had a quick lunch here.

I was so surprised of beauty this park. I walked about 4 hours here to watch all places.in this park you can find beautiful birds, gardens, waterfall, caves, etc. to spend day here is amazing cause you feel that you in a forest with many trees and other signs of nature.

I was expecting an obvious large crater but when I saw it, it was rather underwhelming. It was filled with trees and the fact that it was a crater was very unobvious. Nonetheless, the scenery justified the short upslope walk to the crater.

I took Gwanuemsa trail up and down with Seongpanak. I find that there is nothing much to see from this trail as most of the pathways are rocky pathways with trees all around. There are 2 stations which provide toilet facilities, and one at the higher level sells called jindaraebal shelter also sells food and crampon. If you are coming in winter, do check the weather. If the pathways are filled with snow, it is better to bring along the crampon as the path will be really slippery.

I stayed at Ojo Haenyo Guesthouse area, hopped on a taxi to get to the port to Udo. The port is actually very near but I chose not to walk there. Paid less than KRW4000 for the taxi, cheap indeed.Bought a return ticket at less than KRW6000, ran towards the ferry that was about to leave for Udo, and in less than 30 minutes, we reached beautiful Udo. In case you're wondering, the ferry ride is too short to get motion-sickness :pIt rained during my short trip to this island so I didn't rent a bicycle. Instead, I got on the hop-on hop-off bus, the ticket was about KRW5000 or so. Super cheap. But the driver/tourist guide spoke only in Korean. But no worries, I did enjoy the tour.I managed to walk up to the lighthouse, had the famous peanut ice-cream overlooking a gorgeous view of the beach and a cliff, I also went to one of the beaches there. Udo is as gorgeous as Jeju. There are nice cafes with free wifis. Street food, local food, souvenirs; Udo is small but it has everything for visitors. Do wear good walking shoes, bring a ponco with you, and get on the last ferry if you can as this island is beautiful!!

I read a few reviews saying how it?s just a park with trees and birds but I love this place! The greenery is beautiful, the air is fresh with a cool breeze and the cave system is entrancing. Being from a concrete city means all this is actually quite a refreshing change of environment for me. I don?t particularly care for the animals and birds being kept in too small enclosures though. But the scenery alone is enough to give it 4*.

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I once visited this park during my short stay in Jeju City for business. It was very close to the New Jeju City area. It was a good chance to see the beautifully arranged botanic gardens made up of the trees and flowers unique to this island. Also In this park there are hills from volcanic eruption, that is called   Orum   in Jeju island dialectic. there were not very high but to get to the top I had to walk up zigzag sloped way, but it was a good experience.Although there are many tourist attractions in Jeju Island, It is worth visiting when your are near Jeju city.

I made the climb on 22.11.2013 but few days before my climb, I have been keeping my eye on the weather on the mountain. The first snowstorm hit the mountain top a few days earlier and I know that my hike will be much difficult with the snow along the path to the top of the mountain. I chose to ascend from Gwanuemsa trail and descend from Seogpanak trail and I know that I have made the right choice. Starting from Gwanuemsa trail was much tougher, with the rocky pathways in the beginning to the steep climb in the middle of the trail and snowy trail all the way up to the mountain top. Along the way, there is no food on sale but there is a shelter for people to fill up their water, at the Samgakbong Shelter. The total length of Gwanuemsa Trail is about 8.7km and Samgakbong shelter is about 6km from the starting point. To make it here will take about 2 hrs of normal walk. There is also a toilet available here but the you wouldn't want to spend more time at this toilet. The trail after Samgaokbong SHetlter has obviously been much tougher, with a lot of steep steps, or even no steps at all (all covered by thick snow) and at some point, the is a need to pull the rope along the trail to move upwards. The efforts are all worthwhile upon reaching the top of the mountain. It is good to come on a clear day because the view along Gwanuemsa trail especially upon approcahing the mountain top is spectacular.At the top of the mountain, the wind can be really strong. Be prepared with the chill and wear enough layer to prevent from getting cold. As mentioned, I descend from Seogpanak trail and this is somehow a boring trail. The total length is about 9.5km but all I can see is trees along the way. There is nothing much to see but it was quite a flat trail that make it the choice among many hikers. There are food on sale at the Samgakbong Shelter, and also a big toilet there. A good stop for hikers to build up their energy before continuing their hike. Crampon also on sale for 5000 won. Overall, it was a fresh and good place for first time traveller. If there is a chance to come back to Hallasan, I will sure try the other 2 trails on the western side of the mountain.

I love visiting botanical gardens whenever i travel.? Unfortunately this is one of the poorer ones and I feel compelled to warn others!? With an entry charge of 7000 won per person, the value is low.Let's start with the greenhouse, it was just ok, nothing exciting.? During sunny days, the greenhouse is like a toasty oven as the ventilation is poor.? There is a variety of plants but they are not well organised or well kept.? Moreover, if you live in tropical parts of Asia, you would have seen most of the fruit trees and plants in neighbourhood backyards, which makes visiting it less exciting.Besides the greenhouse, there are themed areas - e.g. Korean garden, Chinese garden, French garden etc.? I was excited to see these options but after seeing what there was at the Korean and Chinese gardens, i just gave up on the rest.? I don't have the confidence the others will be worth the time.Management of the garden needs to be improved.? When I was there, they were renovating the entrance to the greenhouse.? As a result, the smell from the paint, varnish or whatever that toxic smelling thing is, is overwhelming.? Also, there was lots of noise.? Garden management would have better managed the renovation or at least inform visitors there is renovation going on.? I tried to offer feedback to the folks at the ticket counter on my way out but they didn't seem to care.In summary, there is nothing much to see and the garden is not well taken care of (even if there is no renovation going on, I would have rated it 'Poor').? Go to this place only if you have nothing else to do.The only plus I can think of is ... parking at free!

I love this place, feel so peaceful with the wide space to walk around.  Admiring the natural landscape with pine trees, Eulalia flower and lush vegetation.  Perfect place for picnic if not for winter!  Kids can run wild or roll down the slope.  A great photography place.There are few trails to explore but we left in an hour as we have other places to visit.  A must go place in Jeju!

I love flowers and tropical exotic plants, however we were there in July 2016 we don't find too many flowers around just a few species. We did find kiwi fruit tree in there with its fruits, our first time to see the tree. It was hot and humid, so umbrella and cold bottled water are recommended.

I kindly suggest this trail!!! We started the hiking from Gwaneumsa Temple, probably the most challenging trail. The entire trail is organized and you can't choose the wrong street. It is not impossible to reach the top of the mountain but it is better to start early because after 1-2 pm they close the top of the mountain. We started at 8.30 and we reached the top in about 5 hours. Climbing down was more difficult due to the pain of knee and leg muscle but the environment and the mountain were wonderful. I have the dream to repeat the hiking again in another season, possibly easter or summer.

I hiked the Seongpanak Trail which goes all the way to the top of Halla Mountain. In order to reach the top though, you must get to the last shelter before 12:30pm. The path is covered with uneven rocks and stairs so wear good shoes. I really enjoyed the hike but was underwhelmed by the view. Most of the path is shaded and when you do finally clear the trees it was cloudy and grey. The crater lake looked more like a big puddle of mud.If you like long, challenging hikes then the Seongpanak Trail is for you. If you're only in it for the view, perhaps try going in the early spring.
I have driven pass this place coincidentally It's quite unique place, worth a visit. A few shops, restaurants, caf챕, and street food markets.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

I found pretty disappointing this 1 block Street where several pork cuisine restaurants are located, mostly for tourists, thats why the prices raises up from others in the city. Only if you go to shop nearby and want to taste Jeju pork in well decorated restaurants

I found much of Jeju island to be very commercialized and crowded with loud tour groups. This is a great place to enjoy the natural beaty of Jeju with smaller groups of people. There is a small entrance fee.  The first half mile is along a wide crushed rock road. It is lined with young   nutmeg   trees. The trees are in the yew family. They are Torreya nucifera and are native to Japan. I  visited in October when the small edible nuts ripen. The nuts are encased in a thin husk that has a wonderful aroma. You will see people collecting them under the large trees.  Eventually the road ends and then you follow a loop trail that is about 2 feet wide it is covered with a hemp rope mat that felt lovely to walk on with bare feet.  The crowds end at the beginning of the narrow trail so you can walk through this section in peace and really marvel at the enchanting colors and smells of the forest and hear the songs of the many birds.  There were signs to watch for snakes but I saw none. The yews are huge.  Make sure to investigate the tree bark it is fabric like and soft. Also many of the other plants have English name labels which is nice. The trail is flat and should take a leisurely couple of hours or less if you rush.  I noticed a lot of people sitting on benches in the first section enjoying picnic lunches.

I enjoyed this place even more than Jusangeolli, maybe because there were less people, or maybe because the view was just so serene.  It was a nice walk through some trees before getting to the viewing spot.  We went in the afternoon so the sun was just perfectly positioned.  I got some nice photos of this place, especially including the trees on top of the cliff to the right of the rock.  You can't miss seeing this place, even for just a few minutes.

I decided to go with Seongnapak trail, and was planning to go up to the summit!Rocky and stony path made me really exhausted, I managed my breath okay and left the last 1.5km as my keens!You will be accompanied by many people along the trail! It?s highly recommended to start early, I arrived by 8am, reached the shelter around 11:00am!Weather was mild as you?ll be covered by trees most of the time!

I can wholeheartedly recommend everyone visiting Spirited Garded. Even though I came in winter, it was really beautiful, actually exceeded my expectations. I enjoyed the relaxed atmosphere and learned a lot about about bonsai trees and this garden. The staff was more than kind. I really appreciate this experience and will remember it for a long time. :)Doporuuji v큄em, i v zim je to kr찼sa, atmosf챕ra kouzeln찼, pracovn챠ci neskuten mil챠. Dozv챠te se plno zaj챠mav첵ch vc챠 o bonsaj챠ch, i o dlouh챕 cest vzniku t챕to zahrady.

I can imagin Udo is a quiet and beautiful island to stroll or bike sometime, but the day we visited was full of people.  We arrived there already at noon and rented electric bicycles to start rounding the small island.  The road was full of small vehicles and bikes moving or stopping by the road, I did not feel I was in the nature but a hustle corner.  There were quite some restaurants and cafes along the route, the one we went was full of people, price of food/drink is in high end.  It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

I arrived to this temple because it was on my route between Seogwipo waterfalls. I was amazed. I thought I had seen enough temples, but this was something else. It is majestic with the palm trees and little ponds in front of it. This has been one of my favourite temples in South-Korea so far.

I and my boyfriend traveled here by public bus. We visited the place at the end of October not really December but I did a very late review. It was very easy to get to the place by public buses. The bus stop right in front of the entrance and crossing the street the take the return bus. I researched the bus number, it was wrong. So I asked the bus ticket woman for help and she was really helpful.It was a very challenging hike. Be prepared with a lot of water bottles with you and really exercises before the hike. The trail we took was Seongpanak trail, which is the easiest one. It was early of the fall season. Leaves started turning into different colors, chilling, not so cold, sunny and very enjoyable.We just finished 1500m of height and ate a noodle in a shelter. Then, we turned back (blaming non-stop walking in the previous days :D) and took a quick turn in a shortstop in Saraoseum (beautiful lake, nice view of the mountain).Overall, really enjoy it! Will try it again one day.P/S: it is a natural place so not clean bathroom. A very natural way of toiletry but I really don't like it but can't blame!!

I am really amazed and really love walking inside the forest you will feel delighted very clean and green trees, smells good and you can relax and breath well. Bijarim Forest-Is a group of about 2,800 nutmeg trees between 500 and 800 years old. They are 7-14m in height and 50-110cm in diameter. This is the largest nutmeg tree forest in the world. In the middle of the forest is an 800-year-old tree, called ?Ancestor tree of the Bija trees.

Huge, lots to see and easy to get lost in the maze of stalls. For a glimpse into local life with products ranging from clothes, fabrics, sundries, cooked/fresh food, seafood, dried goods and everything in between. Local souvenirs definitely cheaper here than duty free shops and touristy spots. Check out fresh tangerines, Jeju chocolates, hallabong jam/honey vitamins; even dried anchovies (great as Korean soup base) and ginseng roots for DIY ginseng chicken at home. Do compare prices at a few stalls and bargain with the kind ahjummas when buying several items. Souvenir hunters, moms and senior relatives will definitely love exploring the colourful atmosphere of Dongmun market. The covered market is good activity during rainy or hot days. Nearby attractions: Jungang underground shopping street, E-martNote:Street parking just outside the market can be difficult at peak hours, suggest self-drivers park around Black Pork Street or nearby hotels and walk to the market.

Hotel was right across this market so I stopped here on my first night for dinner. I was amazed by the selection of street food stalls, fresh produce and desserts. Most of the signs were in Korean but just follow the crowd and where there's a long line you'll never go wrong! I got a taste of the rice with fried black pork plus some fried octopus in batter, which were both great. Bought some boxes of cheap chocolate as well. Areas of the market selling fresh fish and vegetables are wet though so beware when walking through.

Heaven on Earth - volcanic stone sculptures abound - every tree a bonsai - cedar, pine, maple and more.  Azaleas were in full bloom and a delight in colour.  The birds, in particular the white peacock who posed displaying all his feathers fanned out.  Then onto the water garden with its lotus blooms, fish and waterfalls.  I would do anything to have a garden like this in which to spend my days.

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.
Has a little bit of eveything that Jeju offers, lots of trees, flowers, stones, caves and a tiny folk village.

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.

Hallim Park isn't worth making a special journey to go and see. The gardens and varying different areas don't have anything especially interest to see. The animals kept along side the plants are kept in cramped dirty cages and look awful. The tulip garden was pretty, as was were the bonsai trees.

Hallim Park is privately run, which would explain the cost, which is 5x the cost of entrance to Sunrise Peak, a must-do in Jeju.There are many parts to explore within the park. The most interesting sections to me was the albino peacock enclosure and the rapeseed flower garden. The cherry trees at the cherry blossom section were okay (we went during the cherry blossom festival) but why would u need to pay for that when the rest if the island (and Seoul as well) is full of cherry blossom trees.The tropical plants, wildflower and grass garden section were disappointing. There were lots of potted plants which looked unhealthy and unkempt. I really couldn't tell if the garden was supposed to be manicured or wild.Overall, I think the park is quite passable. I wouldn't visit it again, nor would I strongly recommend it to a friend.

Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection. There's an extensive range of bonsai trees at display, some of them are over 300 years old. To those unfamiliar with bonsai trees, they may just be miniature trees; but to those who know the value of these works of art, these bonsai trees are literally priceless. In fact, it's almost unbelievable how openly accessible these trees are to the guests, considering their value and need for extreme care.If you're planning on visiting, briefly study the artistry before your trip to enhance the enjoyment. This is a one-of-a-kind collection.

Hallim Park is one of the best distractions on the island. It is not just another roadside attraction. It is a botanist dream gone wild. You will see everything in this huge park. All of it captures the beauty of nature. The park seems to go on for ever and you're teated to new wonders at every bend in the path. And if that's not enough it is located right across the street from the beach.Hallim Park is great for every age group. It is very convenient to Jeju City.Take a break and take a drive out to Hallim Park, you won't be disappointed.

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Hallim is mixture of small zoo,botanical garden, lava caves and stones. We arrived     In morning after rain,park was quiet, with not many visitors, relaxing. I liked walking through volcanic caves, beautiful bonsai garden with some trees around 300year old. And completely white peacocks, I did not know before such ones even exist.

Great place to relax and take shelter form harsh weather condition.It's very peaceful and quite beautiful, particularly on the inside. The temple is spacious and also has a little garden, with a lake and several tangerine trees.We got? there by taxi but you can also take bus 600 from Jeju International Airport (Bus Stop 1).
Great place to enjoy walking and see different species of plants, trees, we enjoy palms, something special, very quiet place

Good for an afternoon stroll. Nice collection of flowers, cacti and bonsai trees. Impressive cages and not too crowded (visited in September) Enjoyed the peace and green scenery. Did not like wild birds in the garden, as I do not support animals in captivity.

From the prices I?ve seen for pork dishes in other parts of Jeju and in the rest of South Korea, I fear that some of the restaurants in this strip are somewhat overpriced (even for black pork). The restaurant we ate at required us also to order two portions of the meat (of the same type). My impression is that this is a bit of a tourist trap. This street is very close to the beachfront promenade in Jejushi and some restaurants seemed to accept guests even after 10 p.m. There is also not a huge number of restaurants lining this street. More often than not, you will have to grill / prepare your own meat over the grill at your table with minimal help from the waiters. So if you do not know how to prepare and eat samgyeopsal, it would be a good idea to read up about it a bit before eating at one of these restaurants (or any samgyeopsal restaurant for that matter).

Free admission to coastal path overlooking Saeseom Island Saeyeongyo Bridge Walk at the other end of Oedolgae Rock. Real hidden gem, much quieter than the main Oedolgae.? For 1st time hikers climbing Mount Hallasan, take note of the different hike trails AND the closing time for each trail. This is especially if you drove on your own and parked at 1 of the 5 (one of the locals told me there are 5 different car parks at different foot of the mountain)If you are climbing Mt Hallasan to reach Baengnokdam (the crater top), do not take the Eorimok trail as it does not lead there. I made the 1st mistake taking this trail and the trail ended 3 quarters way up the mountain and you only get to see the side of the mountain top. I made the 2nd mistake not watching my time and could not descend Hallasan from the trail (Eorimok) where I came as apparently it closes at 2pm, and there was a park warden stopping me from taking the trail back and kept ushering me to take the other way (towards Donnaeko trail) to descend. The descend took 4 hours and the trail was treacherously full of rocks. You could tell that it was a trail less taken as there were over-grown bushes covering parts of the trail. Your only guidance of where to go was a      thin cord string tied from tree to tree and red strips of cloth tied on the string. If you weren't too careful and lost sight of the guiding string, you may actually go off tangent of the trail. There are no lights, very few signage and are all in Korean, so if you are like me with no understanding of Korean, good luck. And that wasn't the end. Donnaeko trail actually ends up at Donnaeko cemetery. So when I got to the foot of Hallasan, it was pitch dark (6pm+ and no street lamps), by myself, and I had to walk for 1 hour through the cemetery to get to Donnaeko car park (which was 30 mins driving distance away from Eorimok car park where my car was T-T).

Bijarim Forest holds about 2,800 nutmeg trees between 500 and 800 years old and is supposedly the largest nutmeg grove in the world. A 813 years old   Ancestor tree of Bijia tree  , also dubbed the   New Millennium Nutmeg   (#0001 tree) sits in the middle of the forest. Local residents hope the spiritual power of this noble tree will bring happiness, prosperity, and health to all in the coming millennium.The trees emit phytoncide, said to strengthen one's immunity system and enhances natural healing of the human body. Japanese and Koreans advocate forest bathing, aka shinrin-yoku or 汝役 and sanlimyok ??곕┝ respectively.  Essentially this is a short, leisurely visit to absorb the forest atmosphere and was developed in Japan during the 1980s as part of preventive health care and healing.  So do walk slowly, breathe deeply, open all your senses in the revitalising woods to calm, rejuvenate and restore your body.  Truly pleasant stroll for nature lovers and family outing.Note: Despite its charm, Bijarim Forest is more popular with locals than foreign tourists due to public transportation and lack of awareness. Cover this place as part of  Manjanggul caves/Sangumburi crater tour. The woods can get mud-logged after rainfall.

Before you visit this attraction, be sure to be appropriately dressed and have the essential gear.  Hiking boots are highly recommended as the ground is uneven and mostly rock.  Sun hat and shades will also be very useful when nearing the peak as the area there is more barren without much trees.  Trekking pole will also be useful for those with knee problems.You will have to start your day early as they will disallow entry to the final stretch (at the 2nd rest point).  There are 2 rest points, both with toilets.  The 2nd rest point (higher up) sells drinks and instant bowl noodles.  Rubbish will have to be brought down and thrown when you leave the park.  I climbed in early June and there were many many many bugs and wasps at the last leg and the peak.  For those climbing during spring, please prepare some bug balm.  These are the tips;1) Start early, reach the 2nd rest stop before 12pm.  2) Have the proper gear3) If possible, have your noodles etc after you finish the peak (if you're descending via the same trail), that way, you won't have to carry your trash up the peak4) If you're driving, reach there early (before 730).  Carpark fills up pretty quick5) A mineral spring can be found along the way for cool refreshing water!

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At Hallim park, there are a few lava caves that are interesting, and very cool (temperature).  The flower gardens are very nice.  The bonsai garden has trees that date to 300 years ago.  They are constantly trimmed to keep them small.  There is a restaurant at the entrance, and a rest area with a gift shop in the center of the park.

As the title says, hiking Hallasan gives a sense of accomplishment and something to look back fondly upon. I remember reading a fellow TripAdvisor review on how she did not believe she would be able to complete the hike but she eventually did it at the expense of not being able to walk the next day.Here's my advice:- Climbing Hallasan in the winter period would have a better scenery in my opinion. Trekking during the Apr period, the barren trees across the landscape didn't look too impressive. However, looking at Hallasan pictures in winter looked amazing so that's my take on what season to climb.- Climbing gear is recommended like walking sticks for example, they would definitely be useful especially in winter or the day after heavy rain as the ground would be slip-prone.- Remember to get enough water as some have complained about the lack of water refilling stations. We had brought 3 x 2L bottles for 3 people and they were sufficient without any refill. Take note the trail with the water refills will be slightly longer than the trail without. - Best to trek early as there is a cutoff timing to reach a certain place at the trail (12.30 Korea time) - It was quite warm trekking in Apr, just prepare a jacket alongside for the peak- Buy some snacks and food for the peak and the rest stops on the way up. Also, you will see some of the Koreans pack hot water and cup noodles up to enjoy so that's an option as well.As you trek, you will see plenty of Korean elderly hiking alongside you. If they can do it, you can too. (PS, we took 9.5 hours)

A quiet valley in an evergreen forest, the place is almost free of foreign tourists and allows one to capture the most tranquil moments of nature. Where cliffs and reflective pools of crystal clear water meet, lined by stones, guarded by trees and filled with crisp air. The sunlight peeking through the trees permeates a serene and mesmerising ambience in the valley. Look out for the stone wells and Rock Shade Residence along the way. The Rock Shade Residence formed from volcanic lava were used by ancient inhabitants of Jeju Island as shelter. It is said that Andeok Valley has water flowing all seasons long.  With such charming beauty, its no wonder Chusa Kim Jeong-hee, a renowned Joseon-era scholar, used to visit here for contemplation and perhaps, inspiration. Spring and fall would be great for light trekking while the cool forest provides the ultimate summer shade. Nearby attractions: O'Sulloc Tea Museum, Camellia Hill and Jungmun Resorts.Trivia: Andeok Valley was also the filming location of historical K-drama   Slave Hunter   (Chuno in Korean)

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

Well organised tour of Korean traditional village easy to navigate takes about an hour. Stop at the gift shops in between for gifts

We were here as part of a Yeha Tour. Our guide took us around the village and pointed out some key elements of traditional KKorean living. The Village was small but well kept.
