Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.? There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This place was really unexpected. Through the Yeha Bus tour this was one of the stops and I am glad we visited this place. A lot of mini exhibits with bears dressed up according to the theme and the gift shop is great as well. For teddy bear lovers and lovers of all things cute, we recommend this place.

This place is going to be boring if obviously you do not have an interest to look at teddy bears because this is what the place is all about, various themes of teddy bears on display. It also depends on some children, they may or may not like this place. My family love this place (including my parents) so it's not only for children if one have the interest. I even bought a teddy bear wearing a hanbok as a souvenir for myself. There was also a free Elvis teddy bear mini performance which is so cute. Only consider adding this location to your itinerary if you do have the interest, don't waste your time if you don't.
This place has variety of teddy bear. Upon entering, they have a zoo theme on the 1st floor. They have many zoo animals made of stuff toys. The 2nd floor is more of a theme section.

This is NOT something to do on your own. Going with a small group is best because you will need someone to take photos of you/your friends interacting with all of the   art  . It's a silly good time with lots of themed rooms each one with loads of photos or interactive displays. Watch the floor for markers of where to stand to get the best angle for the optical illusions!

This is a Teddy Bear Museum that all inside about the Teddy Bear.  They have so many Theme of Teddy Bear.  Near the exit they also have many stuff for us to buy and bring home, such as doll, key chain, cloth, jacket, sweater, etc..  This Museum is more suitable for the children, but for adult if you are bored you can wait near the exit there are some coffe shop.

This is a straight-up collection of really adorable teddies all in different themes and characters!Some are the classic teddy bears that we grew up lovingSome are teddies dressed up as music icons, roman gods/goddesses, characters from movies, etcIf you need your fill of cute things, this place is loaded with itIt's nice if you ask meAnd it doesn't hurt that we even got free teddies after the visit! yay!

This is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall, garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These are six themed model parks jn which over 250 models are exhibited. These include glass qrt masterpieces by international famous artist from Italy, the Czech Republic, Japan and more.At least one hour explore the entire exhibitation garden. Visit at night as the place is well litted and less tourist.

They have my favourite teddy bears in different shapes and different theme. If you are a soft toy lover like me, this is definitely a place for you. A lot of photoshoot spots. They also have huge teddy bears, twice the size of you.

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. The other Teddy Bear Museum where the most expensive Teddy Bear is on display wearing a Louis Vuitton outfit costs KRW 8,000 (Php 347). This one is better because it has so many display that you will be amazed, famous scene, characters, celebrities from different industries. Very nice! This is also the museum where Princess Hour was shot, a Korean novela. I will go back!
There's a lot of themed park to choose from. But some of it can only be enjoyed during selected weather seasons (ex. winter, spring).

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)

There is a train servicing in the theme park that will drop the visitors to every station and allow them to walk around and take photo. As of the name   Eco   the theme park is closed to the mother of nature which basically full with plants and trees. Besides, highly recommend the lavender ice cream in the lavender and rose garden station.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are lots of teddy bears in different dressing inside the museum. It cost KRW10,000 per entry but my opinion is it doesn't worth this amount of money as this museum majors in displaying teddy bear collections in the display box, numerous of human size teddy bears satisfy your photo shooting desires. As compare to KRW10,000 spent in the Jeju Village Folk where cultural living of Jeju residents in the earlier century can be experienced, it's more worthy. Desire to enter this museum was due to the Korea drama series   若モ?, and I expected to have the display of the human size teddy bears in different room with different theme enable for photo session (something like Madame Tussaud's Wax museum) but it is not the way. All the theme teddy are inside the display box. You can just sight seeing it people collection.

There are a few attractions within the same area. The teddy bear museum has 3 floors,with teddy bear exhibits and also it's history. There where some with themes and also resembles idols and famous people  and some that moves. There is also an elvis show with teddy bear on level 2 theatre. The outdoor photo taking area has a few exhibits too.

There are 2 teddy bear museums in Jeju. I don't have the address of the one that I went to, but it's not the one in Jungmun, which is the older one and where you'll only see teddy bears in glass cases. The newer teddy bear museum has teddy bears that are displayed according to themes, where you can pose together  with the teddy bears, and even touch and hug them. This is definitely more interactive than the ones in glass cases.

There are 2 major teddy bear themed attractions in Jeju, One is the Teddy Bear Museum and the other is Jeju Teseum. The Teddy Bear Museum is for mohair connoisseurs, but the bears there are all boxed up in glass exhibits. That is why given the limited amount of time we had in Jeju, we chose to visit Teseum. There are a lot of photo opportunities where we and especially our kids can pose with the many cuddly large-sized teddys at Teseum. The keyword here is interaction.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The title Theme Park may confuse some people. This is not an amusement park, just some natural park with lots of greenery, ponds, windmill, etc. You get on a train that takes you around the park, stopping at several stops where you can get off and later get on the train to move on to the next stop. Honestly, the park is just okay. Not much to see or do here.  I recommend you save your time and find other, more interesting attraction in Jeju

The title summed it all up. Unlike a theme park, there is no ride here. there is only exhibition halls for you to look at. Don't expect much from it and you'll be okay. This was all a bit boring. There are too many people and it seems kind of noisy with the chatters.

The theme is good and it is very funny and interesting. Although we arrived the entrance at 18:00, we were able to complete the adventure within half an hour. Highly recommend for you especially with kids.

The Teddy Bear Museum is quite a fun attraction to visit if you like teddy bears! There's soooo many teddy bears around! With different themes, different era and even teddy bears of very popular characters! (something like the teddy bear version of Madame Tussauds)Full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/teddy-bear-museum/

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

The park is divided to theme gardens from different areas (China, Japan, Italy, ...) Huge greenhouse has tropical fruit in glass domes so yo can learn how cocoa and bananas grow. There are also glass-fibre dinosaurs and crocodiles hiding in some of the more jungle-like parts. From the viewing platform you can see all the gardens and surroundings. Place was a must-do for schools trippers, who were plenty when I visited. A relaxing stroll in beautiful surrounding.

The Ma Park was one of the best theme parks I've ever been to.  We started off with horse riding, which was led by a friendly staff along a route for about 15 minutes.  I was surprised that he spoke English quite well!  We then headed for the go karts.  The venue was very spacious and the karts were very easy to handle.  I had a lot of fun.  After that, we watched the spectacular show which was performed by around 50 elite Mongolian riders.  Before the show started, we were able to feed the horses with carrots, sold at 1000 korean won each.  I had a blast at the Ma Park and I strongly recommend families to visit.

The gardens were reasonably well tended and we liked the indoor themed zones spreading out in a cartwheel from the main atrium. Outside there are a series of larger themed gardens. Some better than others, but it is a South Korean take on these different countries garden styles. For example the fountains in the Italianate garden were quite impressive and it was good to stroll in the sunshine. We did like the many sculptures placed within the various indoor spaces and this has lifted our score from 'average' to 'very good'.

The entry fee is abit on the high side, but if you love gardens, plants, nature, and especially flowers, it’s worth every penny. My absolute favourite place to visit in Jeju. I love flowers so we spent around 4 hours here. There’s a huge variety of flowers, and the gardens/areas are very well laid-out. Besides the greenhouse, there is also an area outside where all the different-themed gardens are (Korean, Japanese, French etc), there are about 12 gardens in total I think, and all of them are really beautiful. I think this attraction is still relatively new, as I could still see gardeners setting up the flower beds and so on. But this also means that it’s not crowded yet and there are relatively few tourists compared to the other attractions. Flower-lovers, this is a must-visit!

The Eco Land Theme Park is well worth the visit. With the tram from main station to other station. Total of 5 station. Best for photo taking, scenery, and beautiful theme park. Advisable: if you really want to enjoy the theme park, Don't join the day tour. I did and regretted. Super rush and not enjoy it. Best to come with taxi/drive.

The collection of teddy bears is good and very nicely organized according to themes. I especially loved the collections of very old teddy bears and the stories behind them and their owners that really touched a soft spot in my heart. There were also very vintage Winnie the Pooh bears that were really an eye-opener, as well as bears wearing traditional korean costumes depicting scenes of ancient korean life that I liked. The outdoors section of the exhibits were however not very impressive and when my friend and I visited the museum in June, the museum was very warm indoors. We were sweating profusely as we looked at the exhibits and in fact found it a joy to go outdoors into the sun, which turned out to be cooler. This prevented me from giving the attraction a four star rating. However, the collection is really a must-see for teddy bear lovers and it will undoubtedly be a more enjoyable place to visit in other months of the year.

The building looks a bit old. There re space for parking. Inside the castle, there's hello kitty tree at the middle for photo shooting. When you walk inside, there're few theme of hello kitty for photo shooting and walk up the stair to the 2nd floor you will see a few rooms theme of hello kitty including the kitty cafe which sell drinks,Desserts and cakes. The restroom also there. The price is not high. The restaurant decorated in cute seating with hello kitty design. On the way back on ground floor you need to pass the souvenir shop. The price is not cheap for stuffs but if you are hello kitty fan it may worth.

thank you for the visit. well , first of all we are so afraid of you were not so feel good at the teddy bear museum. however our museum consist of two main theme galleries. the history and the art.  and also there are extra gallery, Elvis concert theater and out door garden. we will take an effort to present visitor more exciting display and exhibition . thank you again and have a good day ^^

Teddy Bear Safari is the world?s first exhibition theme park with various real life-sized wildlife and marine stuffed animals and teddy bears. Moreover, you will also meet our teddy bears dressed in traditional clothes of countries around the world and as gods from Greek mythology. Lastly, some of our teddy bears will be dressed up as Korean celebrities whom you may be well aware of.

Spent approximately 5 hours walking in the park. The park is sub divided into different sectors with different themes. Didn?t go to all the different sectors because some didn?t appeal to us. What I found nice and interesting were;1. The Caves2. Cultural Village3. The Bonsai & Stone Garden4. Seasonal Section - Ume FlowersWhat I didn?t like;1. Birds and reptiles in captivity2. Wild Flowers Garden - area seems to be poorly maintained. I didn?t get to see anything except grass and weedsBe prepared to walk and walk so if walking is not your thing then u better reconsider. Limited restaurants on site, so it?s best if u bring your own food and drinks.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.

Quite an interesting Teddy Bear Museum! But nearby this teddy bear museum, there are not much places of interest to go. Unless you are a teddy bear's fan or else it might not be attractive to you. There's quite a fair bit of different themes for the bears. But the gigantic bears are really cute so it is still worth going

PLAYKPOP, Must visit place in Jeju island.You can enjoy K-POP star?s concert such as GD, BIGBANG, AOA, PSY and more everyday, also can experience exciting date with G-dragon only at PLAYKPOP! PLAY KPOP is a future-oriented digital theme park where both children and adults can enjoy singing and dancing like a true star. You can also buy the STAR GOODS and jeju souvenirs at PLAYKPOP SHOP! There're many kinds of VR experience. The seat type of Jeju travel, urban pursuit and full-body walking VR,such as Mystery jungle, dark mage, haunted house.

Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Tropical garden is beautiful too.Note: Tropical garden is built one way street ? you go in and come out after long walk. You might get lost.

Overall a clean, well laid-out museum at a very reasonable price at 9,000won each for adults.- Not as many exhibits as we’ve seen at the Smithsonian in DC or Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola but still worth the visit to learn about Korea’s aviation history- Placards translated into multiple languages - Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese. - We don’t have kids but it seemed there were a large number of child friendly play and exhibit areas.- On the third floor was a go-cart type racing track and pizza cafe. It was about 30,000won a person so we didn’t try it but it looked cool.- From the 4F observatory you can see Hallasan Mt, the tea fields of O’Sulloc, and Shinwha Theme And Water Parks.We spent about an hour there in total.

Our visit to Teseum was part of a tour package, and we had a lot of fun.  Photo opportunities were plentiful, even if there were a lot of other visitors.  We enjoyed posing with the huge bears, with different theme displays.  As well, the section on classical art was quite remarkable.

one of the many trick art museums in Korea. The first bit has the usual pose-with-renaissance-paintings stuff but if you don't have that much time skip that stuff and make your way through to the end where there's a pretty cool arabian nights themed room where you pretend to run from giants climb into the sky or escape over burning bridges. the station where you pretend to skydive while strapped to a backpack on the floor is quite special. warning : wear pants when visiting this museum if you wish to avoid inadvertently flashing other tourists. the sculpture garden is nothing fantastic and   little provence   is a bunch of stuffed dogs dressed in french peasant outfits in a lackluster room.

One of the best location that i went to while i was in Jeju. Highly recommended for theme park lovers and those with kiddy heart hehe. I love Jeju so much for the uniqueness of this castle. Fancy, colourful and happy place to be!

Not to miss, though you are not a fan, you will be bought after going their collection of bears and display theme. Explore your soft side. Admission fee is reasonable, you will definitely not feel any weight lifted off your wallet.

Not so much of a theme park, there isn't any rides apart from a train. But we had fun there, many gardens, landscapes and things to see. We walked the long Eco trail. The place is well maintained and clean. Wouldn't advise to go in winter tho, as many of the flowers won't be in bloom.

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people?s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails ? Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below) ? I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that?s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of ?Jeju Island Geopark?, ?Global Geopark Networks? and ?New 7 Wonders of Nature? and a green signage ?Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m? From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes? walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term ?stepping stone? means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain ?pot-holes?. The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder ? awesome!  There?s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn?t think they were the famed ?Haenyeo? sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam) ? who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn?t like to eat raw seafood so I didn?t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don?t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

Me and my husband visited Hallim Park, the beach just outside the park is beautiful so make sure to allow some time to check it out. The park itself consists of about 7-8 different theme subsessions. It was a lot bigger than I expected. The park was very well signed and designed with lots attention to details. Of cause it is not comparable to the natural beauty of Jeju but for a man made park, it is a great choice for an outing with family for 2 hours.

Me and my hubby are teddy bear lovers. The entrance fee is a bit pricey, KRW8,000 per pax. There are lots of teddy bears display in different settings and themes and and you could take photo with them. This is indeed a great place to spend a quiet evening.

many themes in the park such as tulip garden, Canola, rapeseed, cherry blossom, more than 100 years old bonsai, folk village with traditional restaurant 竊fresh grilled mackerel竊, well decorated water pond, peacock and bird park and many more. The folk village still maintain the culture of living that one should not miss. One need half a day in completing visiting the park.

Jungmun-Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff is beautiful place where, look at huge waves crashing against volcanic rocks, one can experience the power of nature. With so much to do and so much to see, the Jeju island is certainly one of the most prominent tourist places in the world. Just about an hour's flight from Seoul, it's a paradise for nature-lovers and surfers. There are countless world class museums offering education and entertainment based on themes like Glass, Ice Sculptures, Trick Art, Folk Lore, Health and Sex, War, Art - the list is endless. Best way to explore the Island is to take taxi tours with a driver who speaks and understands little English. They ask for W150,000 for 8 hours, however, you may beat them down to W115,000 or so. For sightseeing, 5-6 days should be enough.

Jeju stone park was rated A by Korea Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in recognition that this park is excellent in term of its specialization in the theme of stone, differentiation from other facilities, and characteristics relating to mythology and the life of the people in the region.Get the map at the entrance and follow guided park course. Don't miss out the Jeju stone museum to know how the formation of Jeju Island. After a short nice walk from the entrance,the museum is just located in the basement of a building opposite the Sky Pond. Follow the map to look for Jeju traditional village with thatched roof houses. Before at the end of course, drop by the unique Gallery in the park which you may find artworks of domestic and foreign artists.It is indeed best travel Korea during Autum because even though it was sunny day, but the breeze was so cooling and the air was very refreshing. It is a museum as well as an ecological park. It is a very remarkable cultural park which sublimating nature in art ,really very fantastic.

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

Jeju Glass Castle is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall,garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These includes glass art masterpieces by international famous artists from Italy,The Czech Republic,Japan and many more. This theme park suitable for all ages. Very cold due to winter season,do put on more wear as you need to walk round the outdoor.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.

Its just teddy bears, but they have it setup really well. They have even setup themes for bears eg. Moon landing theme with Neil Armstrong bear about to take first step, etc. nice souvenir shop selling decent stuff.

It's good for what it is.  Some people have been calling this place a glass museum - it's not.  It's a theme park for glass.  I say theme park, but if you're thinking rides then you're wrong.  What they do have is lots of things made out of glass to see.  It's pretty and often colourful.  My female partner enjoyed it more than I did, and there's nothing there that would make me want to go back.  I think children might get a little bored by the place, although girls would probably enjoy it more.  As far as adults are concerned, if you think it sounds like a place you'd enjoy, then you probably would.  But if you think it sounds kinda boring then you wouldn't enjoy it.

It's a Safari Theme Teddy Bear Museum. There are all kinds of bears, including giraffe, zebras, sheeps, monkeys, pandas, etc. On the second level, there is even Egyptian theme bears decorated with crystals. Don't miss that. There are also international bears on displayed on level 2. Enjoy your visit. Don't miss out on purchasing the bears at the gift shop for souvenirs, you will be spoilt for choices. All the bears are made in Korea and worth buying for keepsake.

It?s my 3rd time to visit there. When I was there in the last time with kids, we just spent time with feeding carrots to horse.And my son had experienced horseback riding. Whenever, I visited there the time of performance didn?t allow me to enjoy it.This time I see the performance firstly. At first, I didn?t have any expectations. But all audiences were driven by their enthusiasm when the actors started to the taster performances. It?s a rather small place but filled with lots of cuteness. Safari themed, royal themed... etc. different from teddy bear museum but worth a visit at least once if you love teddy bears.

It wouldn't usually be my first choice to visit on an island filled with so many views but it was a rainy day so it seemed reasonable. Wasn't disappointed. The indoor exhibition is well arranged and themed: there was jungle, desert, and other sections. You can climb to the last floor of the tower in the middle for a nice view of the area. Can't go wrong in any way if you stop by. Didn't see the outdoor gardens since it was pouring rain but wasnt disappointed even with the indoor one alone
It may seem to be an ordinary natural tropical theme park. However, it may be seen by some of the visitors who came from different country than mine.

It is quite expensive with 12.000 won per adult, but you could easily spent 2-3 hours and it is nicely set up. Of course the glass castle has a lot of romantic photo ops for newlyweds. But also their little hiking trail is nicely decorated and I loved all the wind chimes. You could do glass blowing or get your picture in glass. They have snacks and a coffee. Overall a nice little theme park.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. It is basically a Bonsai tree-themed Garden decorated with many waterfalls and beautiful ponds full of colorful koi carps. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

is kind of pricey. there are only 2 levels of bears being exhibits and it is all behind the glass. The bears are just being display in different themes and costumes. we were impressed at the beginning but started to get bored a moment later. Overall, it is still worth a visit.

In short, I enjoyed the display of the teddy bear in this museum.  It comes with theme i.e. Snow White with 7 dwarfs, Titanic, Disney.   The museum also display famous people in Teddy i.e. Einstein, Michael Jackson.Worth visiting especially when traveling with kids.   If not mistaken, there are 2 teddy museums. I'm not really a stuffed toy type of person, but this museum was fantastic. How made, themes, history of and all shapes and sizes and clothing.

If you want to see some nature trails but can?t do long distances over natural rocky ground, then this will suit. The train ride to each destination makes it easy to travel. The walks are well groomed. Plentiful toilets. There are some theme park like features, such as boats & a pirate ship, to keep the young ones entertained along the way (at extra cost for some).

If you like small tasteless theme parks you will love this: mirror mazes, glass lilies in ponds, large mosaic teddy bear and a chance to make your own stuff too. The 9,000 won entry fee includes the fee to make something - and that price is VERY expensive for Jeju. It is also mostly outside so do not bother in bad weather. In fact, I would not bother at all.

If you are planning to visit the Hello Kitty Island, beware: there is a specific audience that his place caters to; it is not recommended for everyone. On the 3rd floor, there is an auditorium that plays a Hello Kitty-themed show. Outside is an open-air Hello Kitty-themed miniature garden maze. The view of the landscape from here is wonderful. I also liked the stamping stations spread around the place, which are reminiscent of postmarks.

If you are a teddy bear fanatic, you can give it a visit. I personally like teddy bear and was exciting to visit this place but after the first level, it was overall the same bear with different costume and theme showcase in the window and it's all in KOREAN! They charge KRW500.I was just wondering if I were to buy the bigger sized bear, so I still need to pay for the hand carry bag? I went there with my family members in a cloudy day. This place is composed with several parts of themes. Lake, play ground, short hiking with spa, and snack bars.My kids(9, 5yrs) really enjoyed the place with running, taking pictures, and eating.Even I visited in Jeju more than 10 times, this place is the most memorable place to visit. Because kids didn?t have any bother others.Additionally, there were packed with people and very noise when I waited for tour train. Then please be sure to keep you eyes on your kids. I visited there at the last of tour then I couldn't have enough time to hiking.However, I recommend you to take a walk at the picnic garden station (2nd stop).There are kids town and eco-land at Picnic garden station

I was on exchange with a couple of friends in Busan, Korea. We decided to head to Jeju for some exploration trip. The teddy bear museum is an awesome place to visit if you are a teddy bear fan! They have different themes of teddy bear at different areas! :)

I used to love watching Ripley's believe it or not when i was a kid, l love the history behind the strange things that are happening around us, and the show gave us a bit of it. So, finding that in Jeju brings back that curiosity of the kid in me. This place is perfect for those who are into weird and quirky historical stuff. Great for passing the time. It was even better than other theme parks i've been to =) Objective opinion though. ^^

I must say I am not a doll lover, nor a child, so maybe my opinion is a little bit biased. It was a disappointing visit as it took up my time and I was not enjoying myself in the museum. It was very childish and not that visit-worthy. The settings of each place were not well thought as immersions between themes are poorly structured. I believe there is not enough interesting effects to keep all audience entertained.

I loved this place!!! Maybe because I love teddy bears and collect them. But objectively, I think they did a wonderful job to dress the bears up in adorable costumes and arrange them in all sorts of different themed settings. You start at the 3rd floor and walk down to the 1st. My favourite was the 2nd floor - even though the exhibits are encased in glass, I could put my own little bears (yes, I brought my own bears with me on this trip) on the glass and take pictures with them (no flash allowed). Some of the bears have even moving parts and some are life-sized. There is a scheduled musical and dance performance by Elvis bear and friends, which my parents enjoyed. At the outdoors area, you can take photos with life-sized bears in interesting poses and themed settings and there is even a clock that chimes hourly and is accompanied by bears dancing with the chimes. There is a cafe and a souvenir shop in the ground level and you can take pictures with panda bears (not real of course) and other cute bears, and buy a souvenir bear home (but price is quite ex).

I love visiting botanical gardens whenever i travel.? Unfortunately this is one of the poorer ones and I feel compelled to warn others!? With an entry charge of 7000 won per person, the value is low.Let's start with the greenhouse, it was just ok, nothing exciting.? During sunny days, the greenhouse is like a toasty oven as the ventilation is poor.? There is a variety of plants but they are not well organised or well kept.? Moreover, if you live in tropical parts of Asia, you would have seen most of the fruit trees and plants in neighbourhood backyards, which makes visiting it less exciting.Besides the greenhouse, there are themed areas - e.g. Korean garden, Chinese garden, French garden etc.? I was excited to see these options but after seeing what there was at the Korean and Chinese gardens, i just gave up on the rest.? I don't have the confidence the others will be worth the time.Management of the garden needs to be improved.? When I was there, they were renovating the entrance to the greenhouse.? As a result, the smell from the paint, varnish or whatever that toxic smelling thing is, is overwhelming.? Also, there was lots of noise.? Garden management would have better managed the renovation or at least inform visitors there is renovation going on.? I tried to offer feedback to the folks at the ticket counter on my way out but they didn't seem to care.In summary, there is nothing much to see and the garden is not well taken care of (even if there is no renovation going on, I would have rated it 'Poor').? Go to this place only if you have nothing else to do.The only plus I can think of is ... parking at free!

I love this place. If you are teddy bear lover like me, this is   the place   you have to visit. The Museum have all kind of teddy bear with theme or famous people such as Marilyn monroe or Charlie chaplin and more. Best part of all, you can buy one or a set of teddy bear for souvenir. A highly recommended place for Teddy bear lover or stuffed animal lover!

I love dolls and looked the idea of teddy bear museum was really put my attention up. I visited teddy bear museum in Seoul 3 years ago and love to recall that exciting feeling. And yes i got it, love Jeju teddy bear museum as like as in Seoul. Indeed they have some difference in theme but love it. cute teddy bear in a lot of variety of themes, clothings, activities.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

I am not much of a teddy bear lover but I still found this place interesting. The entrance fee is a bit pricey though at KRW7,000. However, compared to the Tricky Art Museum, I think this place offers better value. I can imagine kids and teenage girls going ga-ga at this place. It lives up to its name in that there are hundreds of teddy bears in various settings and themes.There is a small park outside of the museum building with some more teddy bears but it was rather uninspiring. If you want to grab a quick bite, there is a Lotteria inside the museum.

I am not a teddy bear lover, but I found the collection very interesting. First of all, these were the collection of a Ms. Joanne Oh, a teddy bear artist. The bears date up to generations of collectibles. The design varies with time. The size of the bear are from tiny to bigger than man size. There were several hall showing different themes. Of course it will end with a souvenir shop showing many bear designs. In the international bear, there was even one of President Obama, with a letter of President Obama to Joanne Oh. The museum also has an advocacy of bear conservation. All in all, it was interesting with plenty of Photo opportunity for my wife who loved it so much. By the way, the materials used in Ms. Oh's bear were all made of ecological-friendly materials, another advocacy of this fantastic bear artist.

Honestly I never know that Kpop will be this fun after visited this place. Not only like indoor theme park, but also like a museum. You can learn about music industry in Korea from time to time. There are memorabilia for Korean musician too. The fun part is, if you are a VIP (fans of Big Bang), you have to and you must watch GDragon hologram performance. You can be GD's girl and be the part of it (I was chosen and it was really fun). After that you can take pictures with GD (using chromakey tech) and pay around 5usd to print it. Well, so much you can do here even for not so Kpop mania like me.

Here you can find a lot of beautiful flowers and tropical flora. It is very suitable for green lover. Besides, you can find some tropical fruits over here with some information. After visited four themed garden park at the ground floor, you may proceed to the top floor using the lift at the center. You can see the beautiful view at the top floor. Also, you can take a train tour outside the building. :)

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

Garden full of flower aroma when flower blossom session. Overall not very attractive. A common/general attraction with combination theme. Good for family outing. You may buy Jeju chocolate with different flavor. Its really taste nice. If you worry about the quality, free tasting available.

For a rather expensive entrance fee of KRW9,000, was somewhat disappointed with what it offered. Basically, the park is divided into 2 main areas, the inner garden and the outdoor garden. The inner garden is essentially the large glasshouse, with different sections of the glasshouse each housing a different theme, i.e. cactus garden, flower garden, aquatic garden, etc. In the centre of the glasshouse, you can take the lift / stairs to the top, where you can get a panoramic view of the entire estate. The sight was rather impressive, but the glasshouse did not seem to be maintained well. The outdoor garden is basically the land around the glasshouse. It is divided into various gardens with different themes (i.e. Korean, Japanese, etc.). In general, they were rather uninspiring and gimmicky. The French Garden was ok, but like the rest of the park, didn't seem to be maintained very well.There is a train that goes round the garden but when we tried to board it, we were told that we needed another ticket. Quite disappointing after having paid a hefty entrance fee. We decided to just walk instead.All in all, the park seems past its prime, and maintenance could have been better. I'd imagine that it was quite grand when it was first built.. especially the glasshouse.

Feel cheated even to waste time in the museum, still don?t understand the concepts.  Some of the displays are actually quite spooky and some are lack of theme. It give the feeling that the place was put up without much thought.

Fairly small place for a hefty KRW10,000 entrance fee; the most expensive Jeju attraction. Features 2 galleries of teddy bears from various countries and themes and a teddy souvenir shop.  Will appeal to ladies, children and couples keen on photo snaps with huggable teddies, especially the human-sized ones at the corner of each floor and in the gift shop. Be prepared to jostle with crowds on a busy day.  There is a 5 minute T-Elvis performance held at every 15 minute interval in the Elvis Presley theatre.  Can skip if you're not a teddy lover or been here before as exhibits hardly change.

Ecoland is a great place to hangout if you're traveling with a family and have kids in Jeju island. Lots of activities centered around kids at Ecoland. You buy a train pass for 12,000KRW and it takes you to 4 different stations with each stop has a different theme. Definitely a great to place to enjoy nature and have relaxing time with the kids. Train rides is short 5-7 mins between each station! Enjoy your vacation in Jeju!
Eco Land Theme Park - A great fun day trip is a must here, I recommend to go with friends or family.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) The museum's theme was various and unique. Maybe there was like   Guinness Book  . The exhibits was good and arouse my interest, but the price was higher than I think. There was good place to spend killing time and need to increase contents.
Book a package ticket with hello kitty island at jeju intercity bus terminal with 18,000 won. Take picture indoor and outdoor with different theme of teddy bear... not really must can see.

basically its a museum filled with teddy bears arranged to replicate some famous events and daily lives. The worst part is, there is only 2 exhibition halls for you to look at. If they were to do it like   Its a small world   theme, i think that would be more entertaining. Not really worth going, sadly.

At 10000 KRW/entry (+ discounts, if you know where to find the coupons) it can be a bit pricey for some.But I personally liked the place. It was just full of beautiful glass sculptures. Almost everything on display was glass. It required a certain amount of walking, but it was definitely worth it exploring the compound. There was even a short pathway through a mini   jungle   that had a Dinosaur theme to it. Weather that day wasn't too good and it drizzled quite a bit, making it a rather gloomy day to go about, but there were so many pretty, sparkly glass sculptures to see, so I felt that this trip was worth it. Only the area was more open-space with very little cover, so we had to stay indoors for a bit.

As mentioned this place does not get a lot of attention. Today while we were there, were surprised to see a lot of local Korean tourists. From Seogwipo bus terminal (the one near Jeju World Cup Stadium) take bus 702. There is announcement in English. Alight at Sanbangsan. This place is truly nature at it's mightiest, the wind/sea carved walls/cliffs are very different from the rest of Jeju's natural beauty. Entrance fee is 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for child. Take time to enjoy the wind, sunshine and views as you strolled. Along the way, there are old ladies selling fresh seafood and soju. There is a mini theme park next to one of the entrances. There is Viking, trampoline.. A number of stalls selling bbq squids/seafood, mandarin juice, chocolates and mini cakes. Good for the kids to take a few rides. All in all, a good half day spent in nature.

As a big Hello Kitty fan, I was excited to visit Hello Kitty Island after hearing about it. Although the museum was quite fun, it was pretty run down with many of the exhibits being kind of dirty. The cafe in particular was not on par with the Hello Kitty cafes in Seoul. At those cafes, the cakes and drinks are very fresh but at Hello Kitty Island the cake we ordered tasted (and looked!) like it had been left on the shelf for a while. Similarly the gift shop didn't stock great souvenirs. Considering the price you pay to get in, I would have expected a bit more from this place. If you're a big Hello Kitty fan, I suggest one of the themed places in Seoul.

As a bear lover, I enjoy this museum & appreciate all the hard work put into each & individual presentation & its theme. Be warn that its really for the young & young at heart. My only regret is that I missed the outdoor cafe. Didnt realised after I exited & look down thru the windows. Must have missed the signages? Overall , a good way to spend 1-2 hours

After the Jeju Love Land, w/c is a X rated (for adults) theme park. Funny, unique, it's a theme park that you will never find in any other country... This is a must visit, if u wanna hve a fun, funny Xperience!Glass castle are full of creative art works made of Glass.. Good for picture taking... Colorful, artistic, imaginative pieces of art. You'll also find here the Glass Shoes of Cinderella & their carousel.
A very nicely organized theme park with different views at different stations. If you like to take pictures, a good half day can be spent there.

A unique theme park to visit. Just love the colorful displays of glass.  This theme park has an outdoor and indoor displays of everything made in glass.  What really caught my attention was the many shoes made in glass (for Cinderella). They are just so beautiful, makes me remember the Cinderella story all over again! Indoor displays are the many works of art made in glasses, so eye-pleasing too!.  They have workshops where you can make your own piece of glass art. Kids are welcome to join the workshops too.

A pleasant theme park with train rides around 4 stations. As it's summer, can see entire fields of flowers.Lots of man made structures and buildings for educational purposes.But does not really fit in its Eco Land theme and can be too crowded in weekends

A museum showcases a huge collection of Teddy Bears with various themes and events.Kids will definitely love this place and if you are a Teddy Bear fan, then never miss it.They have maintained a beautiful garden outside the museum, while there is also a Caf챕 and a Souvenir shop.My younger daughter enjoyed every bit of it.
A lot of zone/theme - probably around 11. We like the cave, bonsai, bird park and tropical garden. The building is a little bit outdated.

3 floors of teddy bears, dressed in all forms.  Covered teddy bears from the 1900s to current, and they had bears of   famous   personalities such as Gandhi, Marilyn Monroe, The Beatles, Ab Lincoln and many more. We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The temple is extremely new as it was built only in 1990s. The outlook was grand and the temple architectural style was reminiscent of the early Korean Joseon Dynasty.  Buddhism in Jeju is unique with its own characteristics and distinctive feature. Unlike the main stream counterpart in mainland Korea Jeju's Buddhism accepts combines and adapt to the local characteristics to form an integrated form of its own. The native folks were staunch followers of Shamanistic beliefs pray to stone deities and attend to superstitious rituals but Buddhism in Jeju embodied the local belief in her Buddhist temples. Behind the Shamanistic gods idols stood the compassionate and tolerant statue of Buddha. Jeju is famous for her natural environment and Jeju's Buddhism takes a natural path towards enlightenment. In fact the repressive Joeson Dynasty suppressed Buddhism but this Buddhist temple incorporated the beauty of the Joseon temple architectural style with Buddhism worship. The compassionate hands of the Buddha practiced acceptance and non-hatred non violence in pursuit of the emancipation of the human soul. I observed that the Buddha statues in the prayer hall were magnificently golden and the grand prayer hall with a height of 28 m was reputed to be the largest in Asia. The ambience here was tranquil and serene. It was a place most suitable for meditation and prayer. I walked around the temple and felt the calmness and peacefulness in the air. From a distance I could hear the dim chanting of the Buddhist prayer. Historically this lovely island of Jeju had suffered tremendously under the repressive hands of the Mongol Empire and also during the Japanese tyrannical rule. But the island survived with the most scenic and gorgeous natural wonders of the world and may this temple bring continual peace to this natural place!.

Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on   for the most part  . Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the   tourist beach experience  , selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a   pro   if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu ? called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.
