review: Plenty to see here including traditional houses, a museum and plenty of... stones. Nothing special but a nice place to enjoy a walk.

Place for everyone who like caves, volcanos or geology. The cave is long, but the one kilometre available for tourists is enough. There are many interesting lava formations, described in English. Beside that the cave is just beautiful. The temperature inside is around 10째C, humidity close to 100%. If you are not very fond of caves, stones or walking, probably you should skip it. :-)

People still live here!     There was no admission fee.   We drove right in and walked around.     Obviously, the biggest thing is the roofs which are replaced every year.     You still have the stone walls and the entry gate.     We saw several people who still live here but didn?t interact with any of them.    The village was a convenient stop on our way back from the eastern side of the island.     I wouldn?t make a special trip to see it but it?s certainly worth 20-30 minutes if it?s on your way.

Our visit to this village was an amazing experience! We learned a lot about the history Jeju, specifically their culture and traditions. Jeju is known for its black pig pork and we were given the chance to see one at the backyard of one the old house in the village. Plus our hosts were very entertaining and discuss to us the unique heritage of Jeju. The traditional role of husband and wife, music played, beliefs, practices and their livelihood. Moreover, we were lucky because the house we visited was the location of the famous Jewel in the Palace. We were amazed with their stone structures. We took photos in almost every corner of the village. Everything there was just amazingly beautiful. The old houses, tress, the souvenirs stores being in house in the traditional homes, the government offices, the pavement, etc, everything was mesmerizing. The people are very kind, approachable and welcoming.

Our favourite activity on Jeju Island! Pretty limited view from the top due to clouds but great experience hiking up and down the mountain. We started at 7:30AM up Seongpanak trail (181 Bus until trail entrance from Jeju City 3,000 won pP) and arrived at the top of the mountain three hours later (with very short stops at the breaking points).We then went down Gwaneumsa trail which took about three and half hours (felt a bit steeper) but definitely more picturesque! At the bottom there is the 475 bus (not frequent, ca. hourly but you can kill time at the nearby temple or little supermarket). The bus gets you to Jeju National University (1,200 Won pP) and from there you can take other local busses like the 365 (also 1,200 Won pP) which get you into the city centre. Most important:- Bring lots of water (we had 2 Liters each and easily finished it before the end), some people had no water or hardly any and where really struggling! No shops on the trail!- sun screen and a hat (although ca. 2/3 of the trail was covered by trees)- take enough food because you will burn energy! (Remember to take all your trash back with you as there are no bins/cans anywhere on the mountain).- good hiking footwear because you are often skipping from stone to stone- there are cut of points on both trails ca 2km (guess) before the top which you have to pass before 13:00 in August (so don?t start your hike too late). We saw some hikers that had to run in the lunch time heat to still pass the cut off point.Hope this helps!! Enjoy!!

Our driver suggested for us to visit this place as we were fond of seeing the flame grass, of which some can be found on the roadside of Jeju.Can?t advise on the travelling mode as we booked a driver to send us there and it was by car.For entrance to the crater, you have to purchase a ticket at 6000won. The park was filled with 듭ⓒ (eok-sae) or in another name, flame grass. Our driver informed us that the grass usually grows in August and at the beginning, it?s purple in colour. Towards the October, it becomes pale golden (as it has dried up). The park is pretty big, and you can get to the top of the crater where you can look down to the middle of the crater. On the way up, you can see the remains of the volcano by the volcano rocks forming a rocky path and also the volcanic ashes amongst these rocks. Going down from the top of the crater, you will pass by many trees, leading to an empty grassland which can be good for jump shots and some random photo-taking. While making your way back to the entrance, you?ll pass by a graveyard park, of which is suspected to be the family of the owner of this place. there are stones surrounding the graves to prevent horses from coming in to eat the plants on it. It doesn?t have a creepy feel to it and there were many children playing soccer in the park itself.At the entrance, you can also purchase some snacks like hotdog and ice cream. We tried the grape and mango ice cream, which were too creamy for our liking.

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.
One may think that stones and rocks are boring, but not at Jeju Stone Park!It is fascinating to learn about how Jeju is geologically formed and see these amazing sculptures.

Once you walk up the stair, you will see the local shops which sell food snacks and fresh oranges.   You need to walk inside pass the garden then you will find a stair and walk way to see the scenic view and the stone point which it's the attraction there.For me it's too crowd with people with limit waking space. Since there were many tourists there. The view is not but not much interesting. It's good for one time visit. And it's just a corner walk to see it and back. I'm not sure it's worth to come in case you stay far from this area

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Okay so we went to the address given by Tripadvisor, and to our astonishment it was just a small garden behind a hotel. The only reason I can think why it was set to that address - is perhaps there's free parking? Dont give up if you're there! Because the actual site is only about 800m further down. There's a walking path (goes uphill from the hotel garden) along the coast, so simply walk along that and forgo the stone garden (needs an entry fee). The actual cliff site is open to public and free for viewing..Path is quite family-friendly.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

Nothing really special to me as I don't really know how to appreciate small waterfalls :p Interesting as it's the first waterfall I've seen that falls directly into the sea. Took about 10 minutes to walk down to the falls. Be sure to wear proper shoes as it's a rocky shore, all loose stones. Spent less than an hour at the place.

Not your typical stroll on a beach. This is more to walking on stones by the cliff. Please do wear comfortable shoes for walking at this location; not easy to walk on the uneven stones. Wind will be a little strong too, prepare a light windbreaker will help. There's certain times that you can't enter this attraction due to high tide (you can walk along the cliff) or strong wind. Please do check the opening time before heading there. The journey took us around 1hr to complete the cliff tour. There's a trail leading to a temple, but we did not go for it. There will be fresh seafood sold long the cliff, it cost us around 20,000 won for a plate of it. My guide told us that the price still can be negotiated.
Nice walk around to see different carvings of stones which we took lots of picture with. Not spectacular, but nice to see. There is a small entrance fee.

Myself and wifey and our 2 boys aged 12 and 15, decided to walk this mountain, and arrived just after 9.30 in the morning. This trail is supposedly the easier of what are now 3 trails that take you to the summit. Because it wasn't the weekend, there were fewer people, and this was a big bonus, as the whole way up is sectioned off with guide rope, and is either wooden stairs or stones and rock. The few times we came across people, you were held up a bit until you came across a widening where you could overtake them. I can imagine this being very irritating on a weekend, and also you lose that feeling of being out in the wilderness.On the way up we met small groups of older Koreans, who offered us cucumbers and oranges, and we greeted all we met with    hello   or    how you doing ?   in Korean. This was mostly met with a smile and a happy reply.The downside with this trail, is that you are surrounded by trees the first 8 km up, and it is not until the last kilometre that you actually begin to get an appreciation of the views. In some ways it is quite beautiful, but like I said to our two boys, the bottom of the hill is nearly like the top, because you can only see the trees- okay different formations, but no view.At the top, you have the crater sectioned off, and you can peer down into it and take pictures. Because of the distance, we rate this quite a hard going trek,and there are many loose rocks that you could easily twist your ankle on, wifey did!!We used 3 hours up, a little more down, because we had to stop for a while, so wifey could swear at me when she twisted her ankle!!

My sister and I went to Udo on a ferry ride after spending a couple of hours at Seongsan Ilchulbong. Because we did not want to go back at dawn, we limited our time to be on the island for about 2-3 hours.It is actually best recommended to spend half a day touring the island either on bus or motorbike. Since we did not have much time, we only walked to the nearby beach which was pretty deserted and that was the best part. Most of the tourist places in Jeju was crowded, but not Udo at the time we were there. The beach was beautiful with small stones and black rocks layering the sand. It was beautiful.There were plenty of cafes within walking distance but we chosed a bench facing the sea in front of a GS25 mart.I love the serenity the island offered. I just wish we had more time to go around the island.

My rating for this may be a bit harsh as I really don't know what I expected of this. It is quite literally dedicated to stones/rocks. The museum is quite a stark architectural building reminiscent of cold war Russia, flat and straight lines and all concrete. Having said that there are some really informative exhibits on the tectonic shifts and volcanoes and this general area of geology so if I had an interest I would have scored more highly.It was an experience and I was glad I did it but it's not for all.

My husband and I went to the Jeju Stone Park to see the guardian statues (Jeju stone heads) but found the park to be so much more than that.  It's a large park (and they are still enlarging it) with an emphasis on nature.  The museum and historic buildings are interesting but walking around the grounds was the high point.  Rocks in their natural shapes are placed throughout the grounds and if you are quiet and observant, the connection to nature just seeps to your being.  We found the place strangely intriguing, calming, and uplifting.

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My friends and I drove up to the visitor centre (attitude of 950 meters on the mountain) and started the hike at 5.30am on the Seongpanak Trail. It was really cold so early in the morning. The trail was clearly marked out and easy to follow. It got tiring and cold really easily so it is best if you travel as a group to motivate each other. The trail is made up of sections of large stones, forest ground and wooden blocks. Some parts are steep so hikers must practise caution especially during the descent.There are two toilet points along the trail but I heard from my friends that they were really gross. There is a checkpoint near the middle of the trail which hikers must pass by a certain time (was 1.30 pm for the month of May). At that checkpoint, there is a small shop selling essentials such as drinks and food.The ending part of the trail was the most scenic as there are few trees to block the views. However, it was very cold here and I was not dressed according. I am not sure if it was due to the season (end of spring) or the attitude.We reached the top of the mountain after hiking and resting for almost 6 hours. At the top (attitude of 1950 meters), many koreans had there mini picnics while I had to take a long break to recover from the monstrous hike. There is a crater lake at the top of the mountain but it seemed like it was drying up. Remember to take photos at the summit as it is really an achievement to complete the seemingly impossible hikers for urban dwellers like us.We took the same way down as we needed to get to the car. However, if you are not driving, you can try to take the Gwaneumsa Trail down as recommended by some people online. One must be careful on the way down, especially in sections which are steeper. Do not be shy to take breaks if you are really tired. We took nearly 4 hours to get down the mountain to the car from the top.

My friend and I loved this place. We drove in to Udo, boarding the ferry in our car (quite an experience in itself!), and only had 4 hours to explore. Jump shots at the various beaches, hiking up to the tallest part of Udo, trying Hallasan fried rice at the Pungwon restaurant, and having peanut and tangerine ice-cream at Jimmy's ice-cream were all memorable experiences. Driving around, and many a times through one-way lanes between low stone-walls that Udo is known for, was exciting as well. Udo is a must-go!

My family was recommended by our (Nam Yang Taxi) driver cum guide to this   must visit   place which was not in our initial planned itinerary. We are so glad to visit this captivating cliff by the beautiful blue sea!! It was a breezy cosy walk enjoying the marvelous scenery and shoreline natural volcanic black stone. It wasn't difficult for my parent (just walk at own comfort pace) especially for my dad whom was aided/help by our taxi driver/guide whenever required. This is our most loved sightseeing venue among others. Indeed a   must-see   attraction!!

My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people?s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails ? Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below) ? I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that?s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of ?Jeju Island Geopark?, ?Global Geopark Networks? and ?New 7 Wonders of Nature? and a green signage ?Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m? From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes? walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term ?stepping stone? means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain ?pot-holes?. The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder ? awesome!  There?s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn?t think they were the famed ?Haenyeo? sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam) ? who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn?t like to eat raw seafood so I didn?t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don?t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!

Mount Halasan is located in the southern most tip of the Korean Peninsula. The height is 1950 m, a young volcanic mountain. The scenery is lovely and unique. The climbing route is interesting and versatile. Stones, rocks, wooden planks, concrete and steps is what makes the path up to the peak Baengnokdam. It takes 4 hours one way to reach the peak and about the same time for descent. Only one canteen is available where we can get coffee, chocopie and noodle boxes. The vivid autumn colors brought joy to the heart. Thoroughly enjoyed climbing this mountain

Most of the park is outdoors, and we went when it was raining, so that wasn't that good. But the place is beautiful, with trees and stones lined up. There's also a museum about volcanoes as well as statues of historical figures. Very nice place although it is only accessible by car and very difficult to get a cab.

Massive ground. A full walk about will take 2hrs easily. Even though all the stones look similar after an hr, it's a very effective way to understand the folklores of Jeju. Cheap entrance fee of only 2K won.Some places near the museum are still under renovation when we were there.

Manjanggul is a nature creation which 1km of it is opened for visitors to walk through. However majestic it is, if you are not a keen learner of geography or stones and cave, this walk would be boring for you. If you are there in Jeju for a short trip, I would recommend you to skip this instead.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Manjanggul Cave came to me as a surprise. To walk in a lava tube is an enchanting experience. There are steep stairs and long walk so be prepared. Don't bring heavy bags. Wear jacket because its cold inside the cave. Bring good camera. As you enter the cave, you will see the limestone that looks like lava flow (see picture attached). The path is dim that completes the enchanting atmosphere. By the end of the road, you can see the lava column.
Lovely place with great seaview, but beware if you bring kids or elderly as the stone walk are not too easy.
Love this beach, we went in winter, wind very strong and cold, most of them hide inside the mini bus but few of us walk around, taking photos, see the raw seaweed near the stone
lots of nice trees, bonsais, stones & cave. This Park was made by one man alone

Lots of greenery and flowers to appreciate. Stones and sculptures were seen everywhere. A place to take it slow and just enjoy the surrounding. There were very pretty gingko trees, a sea of yellow leaves on the ground at the end of autumn..

Located on the beach, you must go down and walk on lava stones, it's a nice place, many people take photos in front of this waterfall that comes out from the massive right on the beach, this place is connected to story of a Chinese traveller speaking the elixir of eternal youth, he hoped to find it on Jeju

Located just a stone's throw from O'Sulloc Museum, this place is a must-visit! I strongly recommend making your own soap here - it is such a fun and unique experience! Do grab a bite to eat at the cafe as well as the food is not only healthy but delicious!

Legend said this stone is a woman who waited her man come back from sea. If ignore this kind of legend, this place is a good trail where you can capture a lot of good photos. Don't just look at this rock, follow the trail on the left, will guide you to a wooden bridge, there also a tiny stairs that can reach some rocks and seaside (look like ponds).

Korea can feel very touristy and materialistic. Udo is the antidote to this. A beautiful, small island... with stone fences and perfectly kept fields of rye. Cute cafes and stone beaches. You can walk all over or cycle or drive your own rickshaw. Picturesque and less changed by tourism. I wished I had spend 2-3 days here instead of Jeju.

Keep in mind, the founder, Paek Uncheol, is quoted   ?Visiting the park is intended to be a journey through the mythology of the island, entering through the ear of Seolmundae*, progressing through the body and exiting at the feet. It represents the journey of life and death.? just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.
Juju is a volcanic island. From pre-history it's peoples worked the stone. The park concentrates, in a beautiful setting, works from all periods.Free entrance for senior citizens (over 64)

Jeju stone park was rated A by Korea Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in recognition that this park is excellent in term of its specialization in the theme of stone, differentiation from other facilities, and characteristics relating to mythology and the life of the people in the region.Get the map at the entrance and follow guided park course. Don't miss out the Jeju stone museum to know how the formation of Jeju Island. After a short nice walk from the entrance,the museum is just located in the basement of a building opposite the Sky Pond. Follow the map to look for Jeju traditional village with thatched roof houses. Before at the end of course, drop by the unique Gallery in the park which you may find artworks of domestic and foreign artists.It is indeed best travel Korea during Autum because even though it was sunny day, but the breeze was so cooling and the air was very refreshing. It is a museum as well as an ecological park. It is a very remarkable cultural park which sublimating nature in art ,really very fantastic.
Jeju Stone Park is interesting. There are lots of great spots for photos and there are also lots of stone exhibits which infuses some aspects of history, culture and art.

Jeju Stone Park is a vast area with everything stone related.  With Jeju being a volcanic island, the lava stones are everywhere from the Harubang statues to the walls surrounding houses.  The park is divided into three courses which would take about an hour each at a leisurely pace.  The first course has mostly rock statues (including the Harubang statues) that most likely had some religious significance.  The second course shows how the rocks were used for more practical purposes (tombstones, tools, housing, etc) through the different eras of Korean history.  The third course specifically shows the different Jeju style housing made with mostly the volcanic rock walls.  It?s probably not the best place to be in the middle of heat in the summer but when the weather is nice, it?s a fantastic spot to spend a few hours.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju Island is indeed a unique island with so many gorgeous scenery, i had a great time travelling there in Winter, a low season with lesser tourist gives a different experience from visiting it in busy Summer. I have seen pictures about Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff (?ъ＜ⓒ\由) and was amazed by the neat shapes of hexagon stone pillars formed by volcanic lava, i totally recommend tourist to spend time walking around the nicely design olle trail in the beautiful, as well as to visit Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff during your trip in Seogwipo or Chungmun area. you don't have to plan for a long stay, a good two hours should be more than enough, as it was just a viewing spot rather than you can actually walk-in and visit. Don't worry about the transport, bus services are available (in fact it is very convenient to reach most of the travel spot around Jeju island), just drop by Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and walk about 15 minutes to the park entrance, bus drivers in Jeju are very friendly and can basic communication woudn't be a concern. there is a entrance fees of 2000won in the park.there are steps to walk down to have a clearer view, description board with picture will explain how the hexagons shapes are formed, you can take amazing pictures and enjoy the sea view too.speaking of the weather, i have quite an experience, it was sunshine at first while i was taking the bus, and soon it become heavy downpour and even snow flakes begin to attack me during my walking! i think an umbrella or raincoat is necessary for either bright sunshine or unexpected rain. i gotta say, Jeju Island's weather is unpredictable! although this is not a spot to actually feel and touch the pillars, it can be quite boring to certain people who expected more attraction, but seeing the amazing cliff, the neat pillars, it was totally worth it to witness it by your own eyes, even the finest artist surrender to this piece of art, isn't it?

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Jeju is gifted by heaven with 3 famous waterfalls. This is the most awesome one that the mother nature embraces its beauty. From far, you could see rainbows.You probably will end up like me.. leaping and hoping from rocks & stones to get close to the waterfalls. I did fell down when I pursue a step of closeness to this natural beauty. But I could not resist its charm and finally I stood firm with the beauty. Don't envy, go for it!

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

It's the first stop in our itinerary & we went to the Ssanyong cave where there are also lava tubes. It's not as big  as Manjang cave & it's better lighted. There's also a folk village in this park, a flower & bonsai garden & lots of lava stones formed into different figures. A bird sanctuary is also here.

Its really easy to reach this attraction. Parking is free however you are required to pay a minimal fee in order to view this waterfall. Walking on the stairs is easy but if you do wish to get close to the waterfall , a good pair of shoes with good grip is required as you have to walk on the slippery stone/rock. There are some women selling fresh seafood by the waterfall.

It's not worth to go, even you could feel the power of nature, but that's all...Just a small place, you can't stand on these nature stones, because they are protected, you can't touch sea because they are too high.

its my first mountain hike, its a straightforward trail but tricky with rocky stone paths at some incline parts. not recommend for those with weak knees and ankles or just go slow n wear ur ankle guards. go up seongpanak (easier as more gradual)and down gwaneumsa (alot of steps, steeper) but gwaneumsa has valley view, creek view and there?s a tiny cave opening near the base with blast out icy wind even in summer.. pretty cool. there?s a bus to and from seongpanak and take taxi from gwaneunsa or prearranged pickup as there?s hardly a bus there.its a total of 9 hrs including rest stops though i rested longer at the peak and pressed on at rest stops. do pace yourself.. calves been killing me midway down the descent. needless to say its a painful walk for the next couple of days.. i slathered all the muscle aches cream..

It's just a stadium with some architectural appeal but the shape tells a story  which is interesting. Try telling any football aficionado that it just a stadium and you will get howls of protest!From the 2002 FIFA World Cup it is designed around   the mouth of a volcano    and its roof in the shape of nets of traditional fishing boats in Jeju.So looking at it in that respect makes it more interesting.It was not open when we visited as of course there are no games here at the moment (although open during the summer months) so it was like looking into a fish bowl without the fish.Outside the stadium are many stone crafted 'dol hareubangs ' carved from porous basalt (volcanic rock).The statues' faces feature grinning expressions and bulging eyes without pupils  a long  broad nose  and slight smile and their hands rest on their bellies.These are quite common throughout Jeju and can be quite comic and a little suggestive!Have a peek here if in the area just to have at look at the stadium design and also the rock statues.Enjoy your visit!

It's a typical village, houses made with stone and mud. Modern life facilities like electricity, internet are available in the folk village.

It's a stone throw away from the Lava Tube. There are a lot of cats lying around the park. The maze is quite easy but to collect all the stamp to accomplish the mission, it takes more time. It's a place where you will stop for 30 mins max? Everyone will be queuing to take with the   dragon head  . It's a mixed review.  The ticket price is 10,000KRW per adult and since other natural attractions are around 2,000KRW, this park should be well worth it.  Highs: The caves are really cool as well as the Bansai and Stone Garden. The park is easy to walk and has shops and toilets easily available.  Transportation is also easy as it's just the 702 bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal for 1 hour. Lows: The park is dated, like late 90s with its signage and information cards.  The bird exhibit, stone exhibit and flower garden are average at best.  While the park trail is easy to walk, you do walk through gift shops for the next exhibits (so a bit too tourist-y). Overall, it makes for a decent easy afternoon, especially with kids or elderly.  The park needs some updating to be worth the ticket price, but it is close to the beach (just 5 mins walking).

It's a great honour to be able to admire Mr Sung's Spirited Garden! It's absolutely a must visit whenever you are in Jeju! The garden is a real Paradise on Earth! It's a unique place that teaches you many important things! The garden features many outstanding examples of bonsai trees, beautifully shaped stones, a waterfall, a restaurant and a souvenir shop. It's easily accessible by car or by bus, and will be a worthy place for everyone, especially the nature and art admirers. I highly advise everyone to visit this incredible place!!!

It?s a place must visit in Jeju island. Air is so fresh and the walk is tranquil. When you walk through the forest and appreciate wat the Korean say that it is a place for meditation. There is a tap near the entrance, water is so refreshing. Trees in the forest have been there for hundred of years . It?s a treat to see some trees with autumn leaves. There are some Low walls with black stone formations which apparently is the volcanic rock from Jeju itself.. Would definitely come back here again to spend more time in the forest At the end of the walk they even have the vacuum facility to blow off the red soil from your shoes

It was such a pain to get to but I loved the Stone Park. The main reason was to see the Dol hareubangs - the stone sculptures which represent Jeju. There was information about the mythology surrounding the formation of Jeju which was at times mind-boggling and contradictory. There are different routes around the park and there is an indoor exhibition which features the volcanic rocks and Jeju's origins as a volcanic island. I preferred the outdoor sections where the use of stone in Jeju was highlighted - used in things such as tombs/ shrines, walls, icons of spiritual beliefs etc. The largest sculptures are near the exit and the Dol hareubangs were awesome. They all had slightly different expressions and quirks which was cool. There are plans to expand the museum grounds and I would defo like to go back again in future. It was raining and our driver decided to start with this attraction first. Although before getting into the caves, we got a bit wet, but once inside we lost track of the rain. It was easy to tell the tourists from the locals - level of preparedness. Before I went on the hike, it amused me to see the locals fully dressed and equipped with hiking gear. As I understood it, the hike was child and elderly friendly, so I was not expecting much difficulty scaling this mountain. Halfway up, I was already regretting my choice of footwear. I had on a lightweight fleece jacket which helped to battle the cold winds at the top, so it did not feel too bad even though I was in shorts. In actual fact, it was not that difficult to climb (took me 4 hours to get to the summit) but the terrain was rough with rocks and stones making up most of the path. I guess it is my own fault that I have absolutely no instinct on where to put my foot next. Slipping often, I finally tore open my trainers on my way down after constantly stubbing my toes in the ground. My toes hurt so bad I had to stop several times (after peeling my socks off, I found two of my toes severely bruised and blackened) so the hike down took all of 4 hours. At the top, I regretted not having any headgear. The winds were so crazy it was close to impossible to take a photo without my hair whipping all over my face. Ah, even a bandana would have been enough. Overall, I would do it again, this time better equipped. Though the view was beautiful, what I remember best was climbers picnicking at the top, huddled together in groups in the bellowing winds, in their bright hiking outfits, just enjoying the time out. Next time, I will remember to bring kimbap and hot coffee!

It was a dream come true to see these beautiful hexagonal columnar formations made of lava. Also, seeing some haenyeo (women free-divers) at work near one of the lower cliffs was a nice addition. After walking along the paid promenade, we ventured down a steep paved hill to the left of the entrance (where you'll see a big conch shell sculpture and some big maps). After going down the hill, we walked along the large stones to the right, then up the large lava formation, and saw the hexagonal shapes up close and personal. What a cool little gem to find! We were the only ones there!
It is wonderful and interesting with rectangular stones and beautiful landscapes. Interestingly, you may find woman divers nearby and you may like to each fresh raw seafood there.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark.
