It is quite windy here. Lots of people visiting this beach. The beach are covered by a beautiful black stones all the way. The most memorable experience i have here is to taste the grill squid! It was so fresh and nice until i almost left by the bus just because i want to buy the squid again..haha..if i ever come to Jeju again, i'll definitely come here and looks for this nice squid.

It is my first hiking ever, I do feel some kind of relaxation after the experience. At first, I wonder how can those people climb up to reach the top, it takes more than a thousand stairs to be on the top, I was pretty scared. But when I was first stepping on the environment, I can feel the natural beauty of the nature. It enhances me to have a greater heart to finish the journey. There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before. It is a great experience to me and is memorable.The overall journey took us about 1 hour, if you are a fan of hiking, you must enjoy it as the view is priceless. **Remember to buy a bottle of water before you go, there are shops for you to buy some snacks and drinks in the beginning of the path.

It is definitely a park full of stones, but it is actually quite interesting.  There is also a museum in the park which is worth checking out.  It shows some of the history of the island and the different types of volcanic rocks that can be found on the island. If you aren't interested in parks or rocks this probably isn't a place you would enjoy, but my husband and I really enjoyed it.  Naturally shaped rock sculptures, carved rock sculptures, stacked rock sculptures, etc.

It is an attraction for people to take photos of the special ?Dragon? like stone with the endless sea. That stone is 100% organic and experience years of erosions to form today?s ?Dragon? appearance. You can spend a couple of minutes with that ?Dragon? and spend another few minutes buying and enjoying the traditional outdoor cuisines. If you are interested in buying souvenirs like key chains or the ?Dragon? like badges, there is a shop for you to go shopping. Even though the viewpoint just for people to take a photo, there would always be many tourists standing in front of the best position for taking photos, so if there are many tour groups at the moment, you really have to spend time on waiting for just a photo. So, if you don?t mind the feel of crowded or if you get plenty of time, you are recommended as it is a special attraction in Jeju. It is nearby the international airport of Jeju so you can go there at the time you arrived or before you leave Jeju.

It is a museum as well as an ecological park related to stone culture in the lives of Jeju people.  It is huge and you are required to walk a lot.  It is about 40-45 minutes drive either from Jeju Airport or Seogwipo area.  You need 1-2 hours to go around the complex and the museum.  Opening hours: 0900-1800 hrs.  Closed on first Monday of the month unless it is a holiday.  Entry fee: KRW 5,000.  It should be a MUST in your itinerary of Jeju Island.

It has always been something i try to do everytime i go for a holiday, is to go trekking in the mountains or forest. I went in late December and took a cab up to the start of yeongsil trail, and went down Eorimok trail. It was near a six hours journey, with a 20 mins lunch break. As i went during late december, the drive up the mountain area was really foggy and the visibility is only like 5 metres in front of us which is kinda scary because there were many windy roads. but as soon as we are nearing the trail, the fog seems to have been lifted due to the heights. Good info to know: Yeongsil trail have many flights of steps. Depending on what you prefer, manmade steps means relatively safe walkway but it is up most of the time.Eorimok trail has more stones steps and is more natural. But it could mean that it is more tedious, really depends on your preference.Lunch is ramen noodle at the shelter, they sell small snacks and drinks too. PS: As i went during the winter, the timing to enter certain trail is really strict because the sun sets really early like 5ish in the afternoon. So it is definitely a thing to take note of especially if you are not fast paced. Also during winter, along the trail, there will be snow left from the night before, and it IS really Slippery!! I nearly slipped many times because i was wearing a normal sneaker and not trekking shoe. And a really helpful thing to have is a walking stick! Other than that, enjoy your time with nature there!
In this place you can see the interesting formation of stones, made by the volcano. The place has a beautiful view of the sea, and also has the juices of the oranges of Jeju .. a good walk.

If you like tiking , I think you will like here! And you will see the layer of stone at the mountain. Don't forget to test very fresh seafood!! Eat like sasemi of Japanese food. And there has coffee shop as Starbuck , Dunkin donut too!

If you like cave, do not miss out.my partner pick this one as a highlight in Korea. It's very huge cave.only open 1/3 ish though, you can walk on actual lava stones all the way.* MUST bring jacket or something to warm you up and wear proper shoes. its quite cool inside and wet.

If you have limited time, I would highly recommend this garden over the Yeomiji Botanic Garden.  There is so much to see and with the very helpful signs, there was no anxiety about getting lost.  The garden is designed for 1-way traffic so once you enter into one of the many feature spaces, you can't decide to opt out but have to continue until the exit point.  We did not know just how vast the garden was and wished we had allocated more time.  The bonsai and stone garden was really outstanding.When leaving the garden, do consider taking a scenic drive along the west side of Jeju Island and head towards Jungmun.  This stretch of coast was truly out of this world beautiful.

If you are fanatic about nature then you would probably really like this park. However if you enjoy nature but are more swept away by breath-taking scenery then in my opinion you will be really disappointed. We did the Seogwipo trail and for the effort involved the reward was just not enough. The trail took around two hours each way, and part of that was over some extremely difficult terrain. It's not that step, but walking over really large stones and boulders for over an hour can get really tiring, especially when there is no view to distract you, you are just surrounded by trees, There is nothing to see at all for the most part! At the end of the trail, the mountain lake and view of the valley is nice, but nothing that special or amazing. We were there in low season and even then it was extremely crowded, so you never have the feeling that you are really hiking a mountain. I wouldn't do it again.

If staying in or visitng Seogwipo, this is a must. It's no Niagra Falls, but the quality-to-price ratio of this georgeous waterfall is difficult to overstate, as it costs only 2000 won (less than 2USD). A short walk down several staircases, passing shops along the way, will lead you to a stoney beach and the nearby waterfall. You're free to get as close as you wish, but, as many other reviewers have pointed out, the myst created by the falls makes the rocks slippery. So, wear shoes with decent treading and proceed with caution!

If it’s springtime?or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju. ? Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.? Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.? Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km? to about 250 residents.? The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.? There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.? But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.? You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.? Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?? Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.? The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.? Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.? Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:? Good points:? outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;? site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival? (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:? bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;? sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.? There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.? Getting there:? Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .? There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.? Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

I would highly recommend this place for an extremely hot or wet day.  Being covered and large enough, it was an enjoyable walk.  There was adequate lighting and enough fellow tourists not to make the cave walk too scary.  Despite the unevenness of the terrain - they are dried lava and so quite uneven, most people would be able to walk comfortably.It's certainly a nice change from limestone caves although some people may miss seeing amazing rock formations like the stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves.  In fact, I was not overly impressed with the gigantic lava mass on display at the end of the walk.  For me, the enjoyable walk was good enough.

I went to Seongsan Ilchulbong (SunRise Peak) during Mar this year 2015. The weather is cold but bearable around Jeju. However, to climb this mountain is not a great feat for my mum (age 65) but the chilling wind is the one we are defeated.We wanted to visit this peak for sunrise but somehow we are late and lost on our way there. We went to Jongbong Beach and along the coast line it is also very nice to see. We did not catch the sun rise as there are none (due to foggy weather). As we are ascending, the crowd was descending and show enthusiasm although they did not get any view of the sun rise. The climb was nice as there are even wooden/stone steps to the top. Once you reached the top, you will see the beautiful crater which happens million years ago. The view over the edge is equally stunning. Definitely a recommended place to visit when you are in Jeju-Si. The ticket cost 2000KRW each.When you descend, you may see the   Sea-Woman   whom they called Haenyeo will perform at 1.30PM and 3PM only. We did not wait for the show as there are many Sea-Woman around the whole Jeju Island.

I went at July... quite a few steps down from entrance to cave and the floor is slippery with water...  You can feel the chill at entry, I suggest you remain in motion to avoid get cold..Walking around can be a challenge for some (especially for the elderly) since the floor is very rough and uneven, this is exacerbated by poor lighting in most parts throughout the cave.. a lot people used torches from phones to get around...It?s annoying for a inquisitive person as the half of the sign and info are Korean only... The interior of the space is pretty featureless... only two noticeable Lime stone caves are a lot more pretty, but it?s worth going if you are in the area and never been in a Lava Cave

i was quite amazed to this natural wonder and i had not seen any falls which ends directly to the sea. its very close the segwipo city. You need to walk down around 100 step to reach the bottom of the falls. Careful near the bottom the stones r slippery and if its raining better be watchful for the waves. Its a delight to watch the gorge. We went to this place when it had rained a bit so the water fall was in full flow. Due to heavy wind and cyclone in china the sea was rough which added to the fun!!! one of the most memorable place i visited in jeju,highly recommend it.

I visited this place with my family, my parents are seniors. Costs 2,000 won per person. The stairs were ok for me to climb, but will be more challenging for seniors. It?s approximately 40++ floor climb (based on my watch tracking) and takes around 20++ minutes of brisk climbing to reach the top. The uneven stone flooring in certain areas can be a little tricky to climb. The views were more beautiful halfway, rather than the top. Different paths for ascending and descending so the foot traffic is smooth. The view from the peak was slightly obscured by rocks and the fence, but there?s binoculars available for use for 500 won. We visited this location close to sunset, but the view was amazing nevertheless. Surrounding the area is a lot of eateries, and there?s washroom etc nearby (important in winter :) ). Ample FOC parking spots available.

I traveled in early December and sea side wasn't a priority, and then I found this park. The monuments you are going to see at all kinds of markets of Jeju all come from this park. If you want to have some quiet time wandering in forest and looking at these cute monuments - stone park is a must do!

I quite enjoyed this place. It takes a while to walk around so don't go if you are in a hurry. If you take your time there is plenty to see, ancient tombs, traditional housing/tools, stone statues, giant stone towers, etc. The museum was also good and I learnt a bit about volcanic rock formation that I hadn't seen before.

I like to visit sites like that this because it gives you a flavor of how folks lived in the olden times before electricity and indoor piping.  They have houses made with stones and have their toilets outside  using the   pig system  .Meaning pigs eat the waste.  There are still people living in the area and i am just amazed how far technology and evolution we have gone through.  I cannot imagine living in this environment especially the cold of the winter

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.

I find it as an average, nothing special ... better to walk around outside the stone park,the surrounding is quite nice with traditional hall nice traditional look toilet (no hot water, water is icey cold) I came last month (early May)

I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

I choose the most difficult route (Gwaneumsa Trail) as the website said it offers the best view of the mountain and I stupidly assumed their difficult is not too difficult if compared to Malaysia's route (because Malaysia's one is not a proper/well maintain path).And so I was wrong :p It is all the way up up up and up, stone path (which I hate most) and wooden staircase (so descending is definitely more blessing but very challenging to your knee). I hike @ 26 April, didn't get to see much fantastic scenery as I guess I'm not at the right season as I saw some other people's review they saw great scenery. So this was more like a physical training to myself. To train the mind especially. But, the sound of the wind is like ocean waves, this was indeed very beautiful, I even record it down during descending. It took me 4hrs 10mins to reach the top, in between there are... 2 toilets I think, and if you manage to reach samgakbong shelter (1500m) not later than 12.30pm (spring/fall) you are allow to continue to hike to the top, else you'll need to return. Cross this check point there is a spring water ahead before the bridge for you to refill your water! Then what's lying ahead is the super strong wind and the sturdy steep stone/wooden staircase path ==|Long story short:1) Hike at the right season I'm sure you can see more than what I see2) choose the trail wisely. I would say as long as you have a strong will, even you are not very fit also you can do this trail, just start little bit earlier than others to give yourself more time (say 5hrs to the top). 3) Make sure you are well equip to keep yourself warm. Windbreaker and glove is a must. I had 4 layers (t shirt, thermal, windbreaker & sweater & I was still shivering at top, the wind is just too strong that we couldn't even stand still) 4) Bring water, food, chocolate and candies! 5) Good shoes is a must for less struggling during descending & less stress to your knee. Personally I don't use hiking stick so suit yourself for this. 6) count the time and familiar with your own pace if you want to reach the top. Just make sure you reach the check point then you can take your own sweet time to get to the top.Last but not least, just don't under estimate this well develop stone & wooden staircase path. Although it's only 8.7km, 1950m height, it took me 4hrs plus up and 3hrs 15mins down (with very little time rest at top coz its just too cold!)Good luck!

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I am not able to visit this park because of the bus. We went to the airport by bus in order to take the 131 bus for the park. To confirm this info from our hotel receptionist, we asked the airport tourist info counter. Correct, and we were directed to gate 1 and begun to wait for the bus. We missed the 1240 so we decided to wait for the 1340. The bus didn't come until 1400 and we went to double check with the info counter. Then we were told that 1340 is for the number 132, which is grouped together with 131. 132 doesn't head for Jeju stone park and we were told to wait for the 1530 bus. Isn't it amazing our bus waiting experience? I am sharing this as a gentle reminder for all. Plan your bus schedule properly especially for venues outside the city. Cheers

Highly expected to visit this cave from the photo on the internet, because this site listed in the UNESCO as world heritage. But there is only a cave with stone that I don't know. Reach the end of the cave only big rock that from frozen lava. Maybe for cave lover you'll like it.Tips: bring jacket because so cold inside.

Hi all!, we visited this place on 1 July, 2017. It is indeed a good place. when you are almost fatigued with seeing big big places such as Seopjikoji, Seongsan sunrise peak, you can visit this place while returning to Jeju si. the entrance is really amazing. Lots of tall and large stones will welcome you. We took lots of pictures there.  There are different carvings of stones of different types. There is a gallray of stone-made sculptures. We also noticed a nice water reservior type of thing. Really nice place.

Heaven on Earth - volcanic stone sculptures abound - every tree a bonsai - cedar, pine, maple and more.  Azaleas were in full bloom and a delight in colour.  The birds, in particular the white peacock who posed displaying all his feathers fanned out.  Then onto the water garden with its lotus blooms, fish and waterfalls.  I would do anything to have a garden like this in which to spend my days.

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.

Having just climbed Hallasan the day before, we decided to just take some pics from the ticket office entrance and treat ourselves to icecream on a hot late morning - delish. Many a shot has been taken, looking up to the falls, but did anyone ever wonder about its source? And so, on our way out, I peeked over a stone wall and sure enough, Jeongbang Falls as it drops over into the ocean. Click2. I like to think I'm the first to snap this. Ha2.
Has a little bit of eveything that Jeju offers, lots of trees, flowers, stones, caves and a tiny folk village.

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

Hallim Park has everything you would want to see. It has a big and beautiful flower garden, stone and bonsai garden, caves you can explore, a folk village, and a wonderful cactus garden.  It also has a bird garden and reptiles in cages.  You can spend at least half a day exploring everything.

Hallim is mixture of small zoo,botanical garden, lava caves and stones. We arrived     In morning after rain,park was quiet, with not many visitors, relaxing. I liked walking through volcanic caves, beautiful bonsai garden with some trees around 300year old. And completely white peacocks, I did not know before such ones even exist.

Halla Mountain or Hallasan is one sadistic hike. For the month of May 2018, Gwaneumsa Trail is the only trail open that summits Halla. Seongpanak is having maintenance done.We did Gwaneumsa Trail... with one slow hiker... we got to parking at about 7:30am and we were walking by 8:06am. It is beautiful and green, especially in Spring. There is one restroom stop about 1/4 way and another 3/4 way at Samgakbong shelter. There was no other support. Take water, take food, take toilet paper just in case.READ: There is only one potable water stop. It is after Samgakbong about 3.5 hours into the hike at the last downhill before the bridge and start of final red part of trail. There is a hose at the corner at bottom os stairs before the bridge. Fill up here both going up and down.Also wear good walking or hiking shoes. We witnessed two people's shoes rip up and one guy had to walk back 2.5 hours with no shoe. There is no rescue for small issues. There is a supply cart that goes up once or twice a day but only for serious rescue. There is AED in Samgakbong shelter too. No food for sale when we went in April 2018.The reason for the difficulty is the climb and distance... mostly on volcanic rocks... large ones... and lots of stairs of wood and of stone.We left at 8:06 and back in the parking lot at about 5:30. All day event. 9.5 hours going slow up Gwaneumsa Trail.

Great view of the rare animal cliff which is 20 meters height and surrounded by the beautiful islands. Hundreds of visitors went there to have a look of the amazing animal rock. The stone seemed independent and I like the fact that it is normal, nothing inorganic. The shape of Oedolgae formed by the daily erosion of wave and the weathering process. There is a small path in which it can walk along the edges of the island. In which I discovered that the venue was filmed by one of the most famous Korean drama - Dae Jang Geum. I was in love with the drama when I was young, I took tens of photos with the place that Jang Geum have been to.So, if you are I fan of Dae Jang Geum or you would like to see different shapes of stone, you are highly recommended to go there to have a look at the charming sea view.
Great for the caves. Do not miss them even if you've seen Manjanngul ( unless you have a real shortage of time, then choose M only for lava tubes, but the ones here are limestone meets lava.
Good for family with small children or elderly, or couples wait relaxing visits. It has lava caves, flowers, stones, old villages, excellent for us!!!

Get lost in the mazes and have fun exploring your way out. Great for everyone. This is the maze park featured by the Running Man. There are 3 mazes in this park, two with grassy walls which is for beginner and intermediate maze solver. The longest stone maze measures about 5.3km in length and it is for the advance players. If you get lost, you can get stuck there for more than an hour.

Fun for children to climb over the big stones. Our child (3) was a bit small but enjoy it nevertheless. Beautiful scenery over the cost. Entrance only W2000, nearby the small city centre. Nice visit and takes just an hour to do this. We rapidly visited before checking in to our hotel.

From Segiowipo (Jangung rotary) the park can be reached in a little over an hour on the 231 bus which will drop you at the front of the park.   Fare 1200krw. Park admission is 5000krw. I spent 2.5 hrs here doing course 1 and 2. I think you might enjoy it more if you were an artist but I liked it all the same. The stone museum, which is the first stop on course 1 tells you all about how lava rocks are formed, their different types and would be a geologists dream. After that you'll walk around the park and see the different stone sculptures, most of which are natural,  some manmade. There are also a couple of replica traditional jeju houses and local pottery too. The Obaek gallery has some driftwood on display along with 1 hall of art but it is mostly empty. I thought there would be more info on the local traditions and how they lived but the park is still a work in progress. Its not due for completion until 2020. Rug up because it seems to be colder here than other areas of the island and you will be outside most of your visit. Recommend you go on a sunny day as this area gets very heavy fog too.

Form by lava stalagmites and a long lava tube tunnels. It was cooling inside the tunnel . Stone pillars and stalactites are widely spread and the tunnels shows off the cave?s topographical features.   Stone Turtle   is especially eye-catching.

For a beginner hiker like me, this trail is acceptable, mostly stairs without much of stone paths. The view of the mountain is captivating. Hiking sticks would provide some help during the hike. I try to hike down through Donnaeko trail, it has more stone path comparing Yeongsil trail. In the end I turn back to Yeongsil trail.

Firstly, this is a tube and not a cave. Secondly, it is made of lava. So do not expect the majestic stalactites, stalagmites and other features associated with limestone caves.Although it is said to be 7 Km long, only a 1 Km length is open to the public. It is wide and not claustrophobic. Interesting features are marked and explained.It is dimly lit and you need a torch. The floor is uneven and wet.Having said that, it is a very unusual feature and worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

First, do not get lost, second prepare to spend at least 3 hours here. If you don't like nature, this is not a place for u. It's like all nature in one. There's cave inside which is to be the only cave that has limestone and lava.

First of all, this place is huge.Formed through volcanic activity which resulted in 46 'small volcanoes' in the park itself. From what i saw, they ain't 'small'!There are a few entrances and trails. I took the Eulrimok Trail. It was pretty easy as compared to other mountains i hiked. First third, about 2.4km is quite difficult. Lots of stones and steps. Then it gradually became easier. The view is definitely awesome the moment you clear the forest area.There is a reststop at about 5km. Be sure to bring your own food. There is no cafe or shop there. The locals actually even cooked their own ramyeon by bringing them and hot water too. Some used the army-styled ration. There are no trash cans. You have to bring your trash back.You can take a public bus to this trail (gotta walk in opposite the bus stop. A good almoat 2km gentle upslope).Only bus 240 brings hikers here. You might want to check.Reminder, it is super cold in winter.

Finally we met a Filipino tourist guide here in Seongeup Village. She can speak english very well but of course we used our native tounge/language so she was able to explain to us very well the history of the village and Jeju as well. It's only from her where we learned that the famous Jeju Black Pig used to eat human poop/dung (but that was circa 1940's or earlier).  We also learned from Grace (name of the Filipino guide there) that Korean women, during the early years, were the one who work for the family while the husbands only stay at home. Sad to hear that. =/ We also learned about the history of Stone Grandfather Harabong as well as the various symbolisms used in Jeju.When in Seongeup, make sure to try their Omija, an herbal drink made out of fermented berries. It can help cure acne, headache, kidney problems and good for diabetics. Kinda pricey but worth a shot. They also have other herbal medicines which you can try. As we all know, Koreans, especially their ancestors, are used to taking medicinal plants so I guess they are really credible enough when they say that this or that plant is effective for healing ailments. Google the benefits of OMIJA.By the way, this is also the place where the famous Koreanovela Dae Jangeum (Jewel in the Palace) was filmed.If you happen to visit Seongeup Village, ask for Grace as a guide. You will definitely learn a lot. And oh, we get to check out old korean houses as well. ^_^NOTE: I think there are many communities within Seongeup village but ask your guide to specifically drop you off at the community where Grace is. No entrance fee as well.

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh   ginseng of the sea   (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

Eco land has big landscape. Inside there are 4 trains station. A small train that drops people in all station, after reaching a station, people can look around and get into next train. One part is good for children, since there are kids house, kids coffee shop(miniature), fire station (miniature), bank(miniature), movie theatre(miniature) . This whole place is good for natural lovers, people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. Near this place, miniature park, Sangumburi Crater  and stone land are there. All these 3 places can be seen in one day.   So book a taxi for these 3 places.  My Taxi driver charged me 90,000 KRW for 11 AM to 6 PM.  Bus doesn't come frequently to these places. Usually if you taxi for using between 9 AM to 5 PM, you will have to pay 120,000 KRW.

Easy to travel to from either bus terminal (Jeju or Seogwipo). The hike is not daunting at all as it is primarily a flight of stairs and some inclined stones at the beginning. Entry fee is $2. No food is allowed inside so forget about having picnics. Provides a great view and the tuft is something special and best viewed in person , so do the short hike. Gets rather crowded but there are a number of places to eat at. I enjoyed it!

Do check on the sunrise timing before heading up. We took about 45-60mins to climb up, taking short breaks in between. The place can be quite dark at 430am, so do bring along a portable torchlight. The torchlight mode from Smartphones just isnt bright enough. If you enter before 7am, there is no admission fee. Or rather, the admission office starts at 7am. So, lucky for us.The stone stairs are well maintained, im amazed, especially this is a popular spot for sunrise.We went during late March, transition period to Spring and the temperature was about 12-14 degree celcius in the wee morning. Although it might be chilly in the morning, pls do not wear thick clothing or heattech, as you will start to swear & feel hot after climbing up the stairs. So just like the locals, just don something light and with a windbreaker. If you scare you still might feel chilly, have a heatpack to warm your hands. It is important to carry light.However, i didnt get to see the sunrise. ): it was way too cloudy. Oh well..
Definitely a lot of stones on this island! Discovered and are displayed and arranged beautifully. Thanks to Korean holiday week, our visit was free of charge.

Considering this is a FOC attraction, its not too bad at all.  Basically, you start at the stone pillar (which say start point).  Engage to neutral gear and lift off the pedals.  Your car will gradually roll forward, even though the gradient seems to be be positive.  This   attraction   should take no longer than 10 minutes.

Coming from Seogwipo by the bus 782 ( return by 781) we have decided to do this Trail because it begins  immediatly on the parking. It was Tuesday and the trail is really quiet (we cross less than 20  runners in allday). You need to have goods shoes because we need to walk on volcanic stones. For climbing it is ok, but with small shoes in the descente it is hard to finish. 95 % of the Times you walk in a wet Forest and it is Nice ... I Climb to the Observatory ( about 6 kms) because of you arrive after 1 pm they close the Trail for the Hallansan. Well I was not disapointed because the weather was cloudy ... So the Montain was invisible. Even if it is a difficult climbing I have spent a good day on the nature ( and was happy to have some rains to refresh). Don t forget to take water with you, the spot   potable water   .. I don t find Where I can take it. Arriving at 12, we finish a 5 pm.

Climb down stairs to reach this waterfall but the place is hard to reach cause no ground at all, have to walk on different shapes and size of stone to reach the waterfall. Only need to spend about 15 minutes here will do. Natural scene than Cheonjiyeon Falls that with man made paths.

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Beautiful scene to be seen. Very natural. 20,000 stones of different verities. Natural as traditional village houses in India. Toilet facilities are everywhere. Very clean. Dogs and cats are not allowed.Water fountain is there. very good place for peace, health and meditation.Thanks.
Beautiful place, big and many kinds of strees, flowers, stones, bird, cave...And the old town for Dechangkum film to stay here before
Beautiful   Stone Grandpa   displays in multiple setting. A nice walk around the park and also learn about the local culture and history.

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At first we didn't plan to visit the Cave as we had a tight schedule with so many other outdoor choices. Then I read something about the tube formed from volcanic lava activities so it is very unique compared to other limestone caves formed from soluble rocks.Overal the tube looked very smooth as you can imagine the hot lava flowing to make the tube. There are educational signs here and there to suggest you to look at the lava flow marks, the lava shelf marks and many others.I must say it was an eye opening hour and we learnt something new and be opened minded that it was not just another cave with so many stalagmites and stalactites that looked like different shapes in those unnatural colorful spotlights in some other countries.
Astonishing view of the sea, you can also eat seafood by the   stones  , the ajummas can speak minimum Chinese but don't ever expect anyone to help you with English. Steep steps there though.

Arriving parking lot around 4ish in the morning. It's dark but u can see other people going to same direction, just follow them. I guess we took around half an hour or less to reach the top. I didn't stop for a while because i'm so afraid I will miss the sunrise. Turns out some people arrived the top earlier than us! That day was a bit cloudy but still we can see the beautiful sunrise. It's really amazing experience! Besides I am quite impressive with their trail, well furnish with stones and woods. Quite interesting when u look down to the town, must go for Jeju trip.

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

An outdoor gallery of stone sculptures. You can find a lot of Jeju stone icon, as they call it   Grandpa Stone  .  The park is very large,  and not many visitors.  An interesting place worth visiting .

Among all the interesting place in Jeju island, i personally love Udo the most. The sky really blue, sea really blue, sand really white, stone really unique, food taste nice...you have it all. I rent a car for the trip in Jeju, therefore i bring the car to Udo by ferry. There were three of us in the car, i feel it worth the ferry ticket. As in Udo, most of the   mini car   or special bike we saw are mostly two person, so unless you rent two, you cant fit in 3 persons. So if you are driving, you have more than 2, bring your car with you. Parking is very easy to find. But please go to the port earlier as buying ticket and finding entrance to board the ferry can be very confusing..so you will need more time.

Although we went in the evening when some stalls are closed the place is quite vibrant nonetheless. If you hire a taxi for the day ask the driver to drop you off here. We kind of regretted we didn't as the taxi we hired went overtime and we were a bit tired. We took a bus at 1200 won from Jeju City (500) and it was a long and crowded trip as it had to pass through the airport first. Definitely worth a visit. Nothing much to buy other then tangerines (sold in bags of about 12 to 13) and jeju orange chocolates which you can find in Seoul. You can see the live seafood such as abalone, octopus, fishes etc. Also enjoy food such as gimbap, oden, tteoboki, fried stuff, blood sausages etc. There is also a stall selling orange jam filled cookie in the shape of the stone grandfather. Tastes good when eaten warm.

Although these lava-stone houses with the thatched roofs held on by handmade ropes are a part of Jeju's past, they are still very much occupied today.  You can see the kimchi jars and old-style gates along with satellite dishes attached out back.  This is very much a low-key place, gradual and picturesque...good photo ops and a study in contrasts.

Again, freezing of winter time and slippery step stone has discourage our tour leader to let us go any further getting inside the cave furthermore. up to the point we stand inside there, nothing special.Hard to explain accept you are cave adventurer... tourists ? it is a No No No

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

After all the hype about Manjanggul Cave, our expectations were high but were disappointed. Nothing spectacular to see unless you are interested in the stones that you will walk on in the dim, damp cave. You will come out the same way you went in.

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

Admission fee: 5000 won each.Went during Feb 14 which is winter. It was snowing where we were there and everything was covered with snow!The whole park is really huge! If you want to walk slowly and understand everything, it might take 2 hours or so. Most of the signboards are covered with icing and snow and we couldnt read it at all to understand.Of the whole time that we were there, we see no one at all until the end, we saw 1 person. A place to go if you want to relax and have a nice walk or if you are really interested in history and stones..

Absolutely stunning beach with great views of Biyangdo Island. Avoid July and August, as it's crowded. Wait for low tide, when the water ebbs quite far and you even take selfie with Stone Man that usually is submerged in the sea. Also great to watch jeju kitesurfing scene i great activity to try out.

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

A quiet valley in an evergreen forest, the place is almost free of foreign tourists and allows one to capture the most tranquil moments of nature. Where cliffs and reflective pools of crystal clear water meet, lined by stones, guarded by trees and filled with crisp air. The sunlight peeking through the trees permeates a serene and mesmerising ambience in the valley. Look out for the stone wells and Rock Shade Residence along the way. The Rock Shade Residence formed from volcanic lava were used by ancient inhabitants of Jeju Island as shelter. It is said that Andeok Valley has water flowing all seasons long.  With such charming beauty, its no wonder Chusa Kim Jeong-hee, a renowned Joseon-era scholar, used to visit here for contemplation and perhaps, inspiration. Spring and fall would be great for light trekking while the cool forest provides the ultimate summer shade. Nearby attractions: O'Sulloc Tea Museum, Camellia Hill and Jungmun Resorts.Trivia: Andeok Valley was also the filming location of historical K-drama   Slave Hunter   (Chuno in Korean)

A lovely, lovely lava tube cave - totally different from the limestone caves with regard to structures (chambers, tunnels, columns, shelves, stalagmites etc) found inside. The lighting within the tube is great - kept to the essentials for safe walking and with no glaring colourful lights that makes the structures look artificial. The temperature within the lava tube is cool and very pleasant ... could spend hours here hiding from the summer heat outside.

A little short distance adventure for about 2km round trip. Insides the lava tube, you can see different kind of volcanic stones formed by the lava last time. Be prepared with proper sports shoes as the pathway in the cave is a bit crooked. Be careful.

A good place to start your visit to Jeju, the place is very accessible to people of all ages.  There is a decent spot for photo taking though there is also a stairway down to the beach to marvel at the eroded stones as well as a view of the   Dragon Head   from the other side.  Stairs to the beach not recommended for young kids and elderly with movement issues.  There are cafes nearby like Dunkin Donuts and some hot local titbits.

You should go there. Lovely view. Great for riding a bike around the island. It takes only 1-2h only but the view is so stunning. You should not eat at restaurants at the dock. There is a lot of places to eat along the way. Food is a bit more expensive but acceptable.
You may find a lot of Korean bbq pork restaurants on this street. Some shops open till 2-3pm and some closes early for lunch. They serve almost the same menu in every shop on this street!
Wow!! This place is huge and totally worth visiting. There's a bunch of locally sourced products as well as restaurants and plenty of stuff to photograph. Take your camera.
Worth a tour if you're in the area. Fun for couples friends or families. Has a decent restaurant and lots of fun trick art poses.

Wonderful beach in Jeju island. Very clear water. Amazing colors and good vibes all around. You can spend here one day to have relax and chill out. And If you want you can walk around. There are close to the beach a lot of restaurants and caf챕s

Woke up early hoping to catch the sunrise. We stayed at a pension just 5 min walk from the entrance to Seongsan ilchulbong. It was a wonderful experience to climb in the darkness of the predawn hour. We were surprised to see so many people waiting the start the climb when we reached?? it was raining the night before so the ground was rather slippery. Thankfully the rain had stopped when we started the climb. According to a local there are 500 steps to the peak. It's  doable though it does require a good amount stamina / more time (we were pressed as we wanted to catch the sunrise). The route is easy to follow - steps all the way; there're toilets along the trail too. It was cloudy on the day we climbed so the sunrise wasn't as we'd hoped but still spectacular regardless. On the way down we took a short detour down a flight of steps to a lagoon-like region where the haenyeon dive for seafood. The view there is spectacular especially before the tide rises in the morning. There is a restaurant that sells seafood caught by the haenyeon that was very yummy  we actually took some really nice pictures there. Would return in a heartbeat just for the refreshing climb!!

What amazed us when we visited the market was the market was very organised and clean. The fish was swimming in the drainage under the bench. There were many sashimi restaurants and local food restaurant. The sellers (ahjuma and ahjeoshi) greeted us very well which made us felt very welcome. We bought the orange (halabong) fruit  juice and key chain souvenirs.

Went there as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It is a great walk and views. Avoid if raining or cloudy. The walk to the top of what is known in English as Sunrise Peak is quite strenuous and involves a lot of stairs. There are rest stops along the way. There are no lifts. It can get quite windy so jackets are required. There is a town centre area at the base with restaurants and shops.
Went here with our two sons (8M and 4Y) and it was very interesting and a bit cold.Cheap entrance fee being in Jeju.Easy to park and restaurant in front was OK.
