We went to the Pacific Land for a seafood buffet (Shangri -la seafood club) and it was okay. The restaurant was very popular with locals.This is a resort area with open air music and you can book a cruise  or sunbath on the beach.

We went here today for first time and love it?s it?s so beautiful and fun to walk around have good restaurants and coffee shop and good shop to buy thing make from jeju !! You can take bus or taxi too

We walked from our hotel located at the Arang Joeul Street to the Saeyeongyo bridge for almost 30 minutes. There were many locals visited and walking leisurely there. There many restaurants and the Seogwipo Submarine was located on the way there. You can see the beautiful ocean wave along the way to the bridge. The bridge connected to the Saesom island. The island was brighted by light and old korean song music at night. We visited the bridge twice in the evening to see the colourful light and daytime to observe the surrounding scenery. The trail to Cheonjiyeon waterfall can be found? on the way to the Saesom bridge. The entrance to the waterfall was after Chilsimnigyo bridge.

We visited this place as we were told this folk village is a well maintained place compared to others. The entrance fee is KRW11000 per person. We came here around noon. We went to the restaurant to have lunch which is just a few minutes walknas you enter the village however we were told that they are closed for a private function. We end up having junk food from the convenient store near the entrance. I wish they would have informed us much earlier or put up proper notice on the matter. Anyway we went ahead to discover the village. The paths are clearly marked and easy to navigate using the map. At each exhibit there are signage but lack of the story for each place. Some of the buildings are not so well maintained. You can't enter most of the buildings. They is a cultural show which we managed to catch which ran for about 40minutes. You need to check the timing for it. Overall the place is nice but we wish we had a tour guide who is able to explain to us in detail sp we can appreciate the village and the history of it.

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

we stayed at Black sands area and walked by Oll trail 18-19 to this beach. beach looks nice although water is cold and of course could not enjoy it fully. lots of restaurants around obviously overpriced for coming tourists.

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

We rented bycicles and ride around (It was about $15 for 2 bycicles) The stones on the beaches were special. We tried the dish of raw fish and noodles in the restaurant where my friend said to have appeared a movie/show. It's near the beach. The fish was fresh but we dont like the taste much. It's a really naturally beautiful place comparing to others in Jeju. You would want to spend half-day there to fully go around the island.

We reached in late afternoon and the place is not crowded. Very quiet and peaceful. Suitable for kids.There's a few restaurants 3 min drive away from the entrance that serves nice traditional korean food in decent price.

We only spent 4 nights in Jeju and happened to pass by this place on our way to the city center. We decided to spend half a day soaking up the sun. These 5 hours were a highlight! The town was pretty quiet and the beach wasn't too crowded. Beautiful views! There was a nice restaurant on the water to get snacks. Water was refreshing! Note: I noticed a camp ground on the far right side of the beach. Cool idea for the future. BE AWARE there are very large spiders over near that boardwalk. Yikes!

We love caverns and Manjanggul did not dissapoint. It is a good length and the world's tallest lava column at the end. They send students from Korea on field trips to learn about it so it is important to local history.There is a store and restaurant onsite  as well as a visitor center.  You can get coffee and snacks at the shop too. Well worth the buck to visit. It was 1000won or 2000won which is $1 or $2.

We have tried black pork in Seogwipo but intended to go to Black Pork Street for the Michelin starred restaurant Dombedon. However by the time we arrived they were already closing (it was close to 11PM at that time) so we went to the restaurant next door called Hwaro Hyang.We ordered 2 portions of black pork ala carte for the both of us although they have a set menu for black pork + abalone. It was not as good as the one we had in Seogwipo but still worth a visit.Will be back for Dombedon next time!

We came on a foggy and rainy day so we didn't had a great view like other did.  Nonetheless we enjoyed ourselves with the tea and cakes even though there isn't any WOW to those matcha cakes we ordered.  Beside the restaurant there isn't much to see inside other than tea tasting and tea goods.

We came at night about 8pm after having dinner at a nearby noodles restaurant. And was the last to leave the museum. It takes about an hour plus to fully explore the huge facility. While it was really cool that we didn't have to worry about our silly poses and waiting in line (quiet at this time) we also realised that there was no one to help the both of us take couple shots for some poses. However we still enjoyed ourselves very much. Perhaps it'll be better to arrive 7pm for a better experience.
We are so glad we managed to catch such a beautiful sunset here! Had a cuppa latte at the cafe. There are plenty of cafe and restaurants around. Plenty of parking lots too!

Visited this place with a group of friends. The tea plantation wasn?셳 fantastic; don?셳 expect vast rolling hills of uninterrupted shrubbery. The museum was really small and led to a shop and restaurant which was much bigger than the museum itself. The place was milling with many tourists and it was uncomfortable to browse their merchandise or eat in peace. We tried the matcha ice cream and cake and there was nothing too special about it. I don?셳 think this place is worth a visit.
Visited on a rainy day to make soap using a DIY soap kit. can map your own soap bars with different shapes and fragrances. Restaurant is very nice with interesting dishes and drinks.

Visited on a friend's recommendation and it definitely didn't disappoint.  Upon entry to the building we walked through the historical display area before getting to the shop and cafe.  There were many different types of tea for sale and all beautifully packaged.  Again thanks to the friend who asked us to help buy stuff for her we knew to get the green tea milk spread.  For the tea they had samples for you to smell before purchasing.  We got the wedding tea green tea and green tea cold sticks. Can't wait to get home to try them.  Next we had the green tea roll green tea ice cream and green tea milk shake at the cafe.  All were exquisite.  On the outdoors there are great photo opportunities near the tea plantation.  As we walked there we discovered another building called Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a health food restaurant cum shop selling body oils and moisturiser.  We had lunch there and bought some beautiful smelling body lotion.  Again all fantastic.  The whole family enjoyed O'Sulloc!
Visited during a weekend and it is full of life. A lively market that sells local produce with a handful of restaurants within the market. Worth a short visit if you are around the area.

Very nice place for a day trip. Rented a quad bike for half a day at 30000 Won. Beautiful scenery and enjoyed the slow pace at the islands. Tasted their seafood ramyeon in one of the local restaurant. Would recommend to try if you happened to pass by.
Very beautiful beach with azure sea. Lots of coffee shops and restaurants on the shoreline to grab a snack and enjoy the view.

UNESCO heritage site in Jeju. Location near the restaurant that sells live abalone and woman diver. It's crowded with holidaymakers but well worth the view. There are some cafe and restaurant at the car park. Didn't catch the sunrise as we were staying at the other side of the island.

Udo was a really fun trip! We rent a bicycle and went around the beautiful island. You able to see beautiful scenary and how local people living their lives (houses and farming) . Restaurant is everywhere and easy to get food. Thought it would be super expensive since its in an island..but its not. Ferry was pretty easy and fast (10-15mins) too. You can easily soend 2-3 hours here. Highly recommended !
Turkoise waters and great views of the beaches from multiple restaurants and coffee places all along the shoreline.May be a bit difficult to find parking though.

Took a speedboat ride of krw10k for 15mins. Fun and thrilling with a quick stop for view of seagulls and black volcano stones. Location near the restaurant that sells live abalone and woman diver.Spectacular view even when you only walk 10mins from main entrance with free telescope. Didnt managed to climb to the peak. Reached there about 2pm.
This street is near the night market in Jeju-si. A small street fill with restaurants selling black pork Korean BBQ. A great place for dinner.

This site is one of the most popular places in Jeju so be prepared for the crowds of Chinese tours.  The hiking course is all paved and has a lot of steps.  The site says it takes around 55 minutes round trip.  Of course this is just an approximation.  I found the course to be pretty easy and it only took me 15 minutes to reach the top of the crater.  At the top there is a large deck like area to sit and take a rest.  The walk down has some beautiful spots for pictures overlooking the island.  At the base there are a lot of different restaurants but they all offer the same food.  Not a lot of options

This place offers specialty items/ food of jeju. Vendors are cash only and they offer samples. There are snack stalls and a couple of restaurants inside. One restaurant even have an English translation on it.

This place is much bigger than expected and has many things to offer - from various experience programs to photo zones and even restaurants. Great for families and pretty much anyone looking for a nice stroll through flowery fields with some fun on the side.

This park is relatively new and a haven for kids. Within the park there are play areas for toddlers and young kids. There is a sandpit  a tube slide  an outdoor playground  swings  car and train rides  flying fox  indoor playground etc. The train and car rides are available at extra charges.There is a baby changing room  makes it convenient for parents with babies. Flying fox is for kids above 100cm but they have the mini version for kids below that height. Indoor playground is a rather big area which is toddler friendly. There are seats for parents to wait while the kids play their fill in the indoor playground. There is also a restaurant within the park with amazing sea views. My daughter had an amazing time as the park was not crowded when we visited. Overall its a nice park to visit if u have kids below age of 7.

This market sell all sort of things from fresh seafood to chocolate. We bought those chocolate souvenier from here. There are many shops selling similar item.One can also buy various ready to eat food (street food kind) and there are restaurants too. One thing to take note is that dustbin is rare  so you may want to bring a plastic bag to throw your litter.

This is not your traditional beach. It is quite rocky and has limited sand however really spectacular geographical features to see here. Lots of restaurants nearby and also you can visit Hallim park for a few hours. Think this beach would have been better in the height of summer (July- August).

This is more like a nice park rather than a garden. They have beautiful walks among the trees and you can have tea and cakes in a small restaurant with the terrace seats looking out the wide green field. But the staff can?셳 speak English so there must be a tour guide to take you here.

This is a refreshing place with a variety of trees. Very nice and fresh. It is packed with tourist also. There is a coffee house and a buffet dinner restaurant.

One could really understand the way of living in the old times when getting up close to the stone construction and thatched roofs and garden plots. review: There?s a few black pork restaurant in the street. The price for a person is W18000 and the portion is just right.

There were a diverse variety and choices of street food. The younger generation of entrepreneurs were experimenting with fusion and various creative combinations. The quality offered was reasonable and reflective of local tastebuds but more effort and further refinements would make them a successful household name. Generally street food was relatively cheaper choice compared to restaurants. There were also abundant fresh food to choose from.
There is no English wordings in this museum. There is a store and restaurant here. You can give it a missed if you want to know more about the tea history.
There are many restaurants along this street which serve Black Pork BBQ. We only eat here once so it is difficult to tell which one is good but all look good.
The volcano is quite scenic. The track on top a little bit steep. Great Korean seafood restaurant nearby - loved it!
The view is amazing. And the green is calming and lush. A lot of good photo spots. There are restaurants and some street food in the area.

The place is not well-maintained  to say the least. It felt like a haunted theme park experience rather than a nice museum. The place was empty from visitors  basically there were hardly any staff present. The installations are rusty  the cafe and the restaurant were closed down. All in all  it felt haunted therefore we left with some bizarre feelings. I'm sure once it was beautiful but neglect made its damage.

The place is nice but not a must. It sure shows you some korean culture there is also korean restaurant and other food spots like natural hallabong juice (orange) which I really liked. All I can say is that if you are a fan of korean culture go; if you are not I'd rather go to the beach falls.

The place is good for picture taking but can be a good climb for people who are not very active. Great view from atop while you can experience Jeju women divers if you go to the shore. Many restaurants in the area as well for those who want to taste fresh seafood like abalones shrimp crabs squid shells etc.

The person in charge of the company is really nice and caring. The date of my tour are having a typhoon and he send me notification to postpone the trip and even share with me the dos and donts during typhoon. He also recommend a nice restaurant for me to try out. The service is really nice and awesome.

The musuem is located next to the tea farm great view from the rooftopinside the musuem you can buy a range of different tea made in JEJU and evevn drink somethere is a restaurant inside where youi can eat an tea icecream or a tea cake anything which is made with tea!good for family and couple

The Lee Jung-Seob Street near the museum is where more time can be spent (than the Lee Jung-Seob Museum) with some good restaurants and cafes lining the street that is decorated with art influenced by him or replicas of his work. Visitors can also take a look at his old home located on this street.

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

The Jeju village is 5 minutes from Hyeopjae beach with plenty of restaurants and cafe nearby. It's a perfect place to start off your day or end it. It's a beautiful good size historical park with plenty of things to learn do and it's kids friendly with lot of interactive events to include a mini zoo. I would definitely put it on the itenary and start enjoying or end the day.

The folk museum is a huge cultural town-like place located at the south-east portion of Jeju Island. It is easily accessible by car. For those who are self-driving like I did fear not there is an abundant number of parking lots to park your car and it's completely free.The admission fee for an adult cost around 10000 won. Considering the size of the museum it's a rather reasonable price. The museum is divided into many different sections showcasing different cultural aspects of Korea's rich history.If you get tired from walking or can bear the scorching sun the museum provides a tram service that brings you around the museum stopping at different attractions. There are also many different restaurants and snack booths selling traditional Korean meals as well as snacks. If you have never been to Jeju before do take the opportunity to visit this place at least once! Ideal for all ages.

The famous Black Pork Street in Jeju Island is within walking distance from the Dongmun Market and the street is lined with lots of restaurant serving BBQ black pork. We tried one of the famous restaurant recommended by a Taiwanese blog and found it to be cheap and good. It's the last restaurant along the street if you're walking from Dongmun Market. Well worth a visit.

The beach was very beautiful. It has clear blue water and there were several restaurants and cafe where you can sit and enjoy the view. It was too windy when we visited though and the sand was everywhere. Spring may not be the best time to visit.

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day. Jeju Museum of War History and Peace is a must-see place if you visit Jeju. Most tourists just hang out at the beaches restaurants golf courses etc or walk on the Olle. Walking on the Olle is nice--a great pilgrimage for healing. If you really want to know about the unique history of Jeju and the Korean Peninsula however you must visit this museum. Although it's hard to get there by public transportation it's worth visiting. The museum shows how Jeju Islanders were persecuted by Japanese colonialists and then by Korean and U.S. soldiers after Korea's independence. The museum's free-guided tour takes the visitors to the harsh realities of islanders' historical suffering and the division of political ideologies between two Koreas. The highlight of this museum is its peace garden. This huge garden made me pray for peace in the Korean peninsula.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

A beautiful park there so many local tourist using this park for photo spot. The ticket price - Quite expensive. So many photo spot! Hard to find restaurant or eating place here. If you are using bus please double check the bus time. I recommend to use taxi.

you can view the teddy bears from different countries,enjoy yourself at the museum shop, caf챕, restaurant or the outdoor park where you can view the spectacular Jungmun Sea. You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

You better visit this place in the afternoon. You can try the teokpokki restaurant that shown in running man with 3,500 won. It tastes good. The chocolate souvenirs are also cheap I bought 10 boxes for 10,000 won.
Worth the climb, the view was fantastic from the peak. But a little bit crowded lots of Chinese tourists. There are nearby restaurants and starbucks too.

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

When you come to Jeju, you have to go to the lovely island of Udo. It is very touristy, but it still has much to offer and so many lovely views. The Udo icecream experience from the bluffs to the kind people, interesting black sand beaches, breath taking views, suje burger (in ho ho ho restaurant, even the ferry ride is an experience... grab some beers and enjoy the ride. We ferried over our rental (??26,000) for two pax to a grand total of ??37,000; it's ??5,500 a piece for a single passenger on the ferry roundtrip. What a fun little island! Exploring the island on a motorized bike/trike was an awesome experience. To rent the trikes an international class A drivers license is needed (US Military living in Korea can use your ID card and Korean drivers license). No license is needed for the motorized 2-wheeled bikes. This is the easiest way to travel the island making frequent stops to see the scenery or stop at one of the many cafes or restaurants. We saw tour busses, and a few regular cars, but seems like the majority of visitors chose the motorized trike to see the island. The ferry from Seongsan Port on Jeju to  Cheonjin Port on Udo runs every 30 minutes and the ride was about 15 minutes. There was an air-conditioned room on the upper deck but it was floor seating only. It is possible to see the whole island in a few hours.

Welcome to the first Teddy Bear Museum in Korea. Here you will find everything you want to know about Teddy Bears. Teddy Bears have been loved and cherished since they were first introduced over 100 years ago. There are now millions of people who collect Teddy Bears. They seek out old, unique and valuable teddy bears for their personal collections. Our Teddy Bear Museum opened especially for the European collectors. The Teddy Bear Museum is more exciting than ever with   Teddy Bear   entertainment as never seen before. Jeju Teddy Bear Museum opened on April 24, 2001. It contains two galleries, a museum gift shop, and a museum cafe. Also, on site is a museum bar/restaurant, a wonderful place to meet friends, family, and lovers. From the outside garden, there is a view of Jung-Mun Beach.

We were staying in Jungmun so it was a long drive to the peak. It was a rainy day so the steps were slippery. I made it up half way but turned back when the rain came. On the left at the base of the mountain, you could see the female divers diving at specific time. There are many restaurants at the base for you to reward yourself after the climb.

We were received by a Chinese -speaking   Villager   upon entering the village. It is well set up, which gives a glimpse of the old life style of the local Jeju islanders. However, after a brief talk about the life of the local people, the guide was more interested to get us all seated inside a hut to sell her products, such as honey, Omija tea, and lo and behold...horse bone pellets (remedy for loss of calcium)! Her sales pitch was pushy and rather unfriendly, and we were not that interested by her goods (the price was exorbitant), we could sense her attitude turned from lukewarm to really cold. There is no doubt some local people really live here, as to keep the tradition alive, also supported by the government to do so. I think is better to keep the selling of local goods to another area (like setting up a gift shop), rather than incorporating it as some kind of compulsory lecture within the guide tour. I find that most off-putting. I give this place an average rating. The surrounding restaurants which serve the famous pork dishes from black pig were good.

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

We went into a nearby shop to ask for info and were told that the restaurant at the corner - Dombedon Restaurant was good.The Dombedon Restaurant is a michelin starred restaurant. The black pork set 450g was KRW43,000 for two persons.  The bulgogi 180g was KRW18,000 for one person.  Though the price of this restaurant is higher compared to the other nearby restaurants, it's worth every cent of it.

We visited this place on a slightly gloomy day. This and the amazon green colours of the flora made it look like a mystic forest, something out of an animation. They say, walking among these nutmeg trees has healing properties, and eventhough I was sceptical at first, soon I could feel my nerves calming down. It felt like someone poured some sleeping powder on us. Oh and the smell! I've never felt such pungent yet clean fragrance in a forest before, it's truly unique. All those pretty colours and the distinctive smell of nutmeg and cinnamon trees makes this pathway a mesmerizing experience. The route takes at least 40 minutes-1 hour. There are some charming restaurants and coffee places before the entrance, and a huge parking lot. The whole are is beautiful.

We visited here in the fall during the annual Peanut Festival...yes, peanuts are grown on this island off the east coast of Jeju Island.  Autumn was a good time to visit there because it was cooler and not so crowded.  Our pension owner, Mr. Lee, picked us up at the ferry and drove us to our accommodation, right across the coast road from the famous white coral beach, the only one of its kind in Korea.  The coral beach was beautiful but much smaller than I'd expected and impossible to walk on without closed shoes.  The pension, called The Log House, is not only close to the beach, it is close to a cluster of restaurants and coffeeshops.  It is possible to do a lot of hiking and go up to the lighthouse for a 360 view and to catch the first glimpse of sunrise...which can be spectacular.  Because it was during the Peanut Festival, we could sample peanut wine and other local products, including several types of peanut icecream. We had a great room at the pension, on the corner with great views of the fishing boats and the famous Sunrise Peak crater across the channel.  The pension owner, Mr. Lee, spoke enough English to take care of all our needs.  At other pensions, little to no English is spoken by the staff/owners.  The owner also drove us to the ferry the next day.  Although bikes and ATVs are available for rent, the roads are a bit curvy and narrow for my comfort level.  If you like adventure, go for it!  Be sure to bring your international drivers license.  Enjoy!

We took bus no 100 from seogwipo city to the last bus stop. Walk up the road to the next bus stop and got on the intercity bus no 701. Got off at the beach overlooking seongsan illchubong. Plenty of spots for great pics here. Walked all the way to the entrance and up. Manageable. Highly recommend wearing good comfortable shoes. The climb up was not as bad as I thought it would be. The view from the bottom was quite intimidating at first  though. Many restaurants with reasonable prices to stop for lunch after the climb. Overall, good place to visit.

We took a local bus from Jeju City to Manjanggul Cave. It's 2,8 km walk from the bus stop to the entrance of the cave. You can hire a taxi, if you don't feel like walking. Just outside the entrance you can find a restaurant and a kiosk. The entrance fee was very cheap (2000 won). There are quite many stairs when you go down to the cave. The floor of the cave is a bit uneven, but still quite easy to walk on. The cave is quite dimly lit, moist and cold. I recommend bringing a jacket with you. All that said the cave isn't maybe a best spot to visit with small children or elderly people. For healthy adults the cave is a nice experience. There is information in English about the different formations and the history of the cave. There is only one entrance to the cave, so if you walk to the end and back, it's total of 2 km of walking. I recommend visiting Manjanggul Cave, if you're interested in Unesco heritage sties and natural beauty!

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance (I have attached the photo) and you can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We alighted and headed to the dark brown beach along Seongsan. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore where to can pick clams and walkway with dry cuttlefish along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum as we reached Jongdal Elementary school at 5.30 pm. Noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market to Jongdal Elementary school (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier. We decide to go back as it was late by bus 701 back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal from Jongdal Elementary school  as we noted that the bus will take about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.

We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.

We only managed to visit at night. The street food location is at gate 8. Some of the stalls have long long queue. The watermellon drink stall seems to be a hit... A bit pricey at KRW9000 for one watermellon drinks (2 cups equivalent).Other food is spaghetti, korean fried chicken etc. Grab the food you want and there are sitting area to eat.There are also few restaurants selling raw fish and sashimi at the same place

We loved the atmosphere and ambience here.Very local and full of fabulous caf챕s, restaurants and bars.Pretty place.For the beach itself, it is nice, but average.Whatever you do, never stay at Aqua BEAutique hotel!!

We like to hike.  Our idea of hiking is day trips and not super remote.  A 4-6 hour hike in a California Redwood state park is a good example.We took about 6 of the 20+ trails on the south and east coasts.  Every one was different and interesting in its own way.  We stayed in Jung-Mun on the south side.  Terrific little town with hole in wall places with tasty, healthy, cheap food and good bus transportation.These hikes were a little different from our standard in that they often took more than 6 hours. They also could dip in and out of populated areas. We liked that because we might trip across a restaurant run by old lady divers or an archery club doing target practice.  Most trails were not at all crowded. The worst was part of a trail where a Korean soap opera was filmed. It is hard to describe the Korean style of friendliness. They are very direct.  Example was a man at a bus stop who figured we were going to have difficulty getting to our destination. So he flagged a taxi, allegedly for himself, and invited us to hop on.  When we figured out what he was doing, we insisted on paying.  He refused. We got out, gave the driver money, he grabbed it and gave it back. We tossed the money into the window. He grabbed it again, tossed it back on the street and had the driver zip off.  There we were, picking up our money off the pavement. Anybody who has watched Koreans fight over who gets to pay the bill at a restaurant knows what I am saying. To Americans it looks like a hot argument when in fact it's best friends being best friends.  My advice is enjoy it but don't always loose the argument - sometimes you have to win and pay the bill.  This time we really tried but he was too clever for us;-)

We heard from travelers and locals that this street are famous because of their native black pork.in our 3 days stay in jeju, we have tried 3 black pork restaurants in this street. The people working in the restaurant are very accomodating, service are great! Specially the black pork itself. I must say im addicted toIt. I keep coming back when i have a chance. And the next to the street are shopping stores where you can find a lot of choices

We heard about the dragon head rock and we were brought there by our tour guide. Our guide warned us to use   a lot of imagination   when we see the rock otherwise we will not be able to see the   dragon  . Well she was right about that. Lots of tour agencies bring their groups there to see the rock and there are lots of little restaurants all the way along the walkway to entice the tourists. After a short walk from the carpark, there is a steep staircase you have to walk down to, in order to get to the spot to see the dragon head from the side. Even so, you're pretty far from the dragon head rock. And to me, it's clearly just a natural process where the rock gets eroded into a certain shape and in this case it's going there for this one rock only... which I wouldn't have if I were on a free and easy route.

We have visited this beach on our first day in Jeju island. As soon as we walked in we felt so happy to see this beautiful beach! It was beginning of September, it was hot but as soon as we went to beach we almost got frozen due to strong wind. Sand is white and when combined with clear sky water appears Caribbean blue :) it was difficult to find a place to sit as it was overcrowded. We asked a lady in a local shop to keep our belongings for us while we are swimming, she was very kind and didn't ask any money from us. We also met sunset on this beach. It was gorgeous.Tip. Take a windproof jacket with a hood of you cannot stand for wind for a long time.Renting a place on beach with umbrella costs 10,000KRW. Renting some inflatable toy (flamingo for example) is also 10,000. Life vest/goggles rent is also 10,000. And you won't see any price tags around, kind of weird.Food around. Chinese restaurant across the street serves nice jajamyun noodles for 6 or 7,000 KRW. I can recommend it. Drinks - cafe bene with gorgeous view. Average coffee. Good bagels with crab meat.

We had only a metre of visibility when we went, it was cold, rainy and foggy. My review probably doesn’t do it justice, we were just super unlucky that day. Don’t visit on a rainy day. There is however a restaurant with an exhibition on top and there is a restroom too. We didn’t even bother with the walk as it looked gloomy and we couldn’t see much.

We had lunch at this restaurant as it came highly recommended and we had heard that it was on the Michelin list of restaurants of 2011. We got there just as it opened which was a good thing as it filled out quite quickly. We later found out that reservations are highly recommended if you plan to go there for dinner. We got the mixed set for 2 and it was a lot of food for the price. The pork was very good, obviously very fresh. The side dishes were also top-notch. Service was quick and efficient and very friendly. It was a little hard to find as a number of streets around the area were being repaired when we were there but it was totally worth it.

We had dinner there the first night.  I had bulgogi before, but never presented that way.  They didn't put any plate in frot of us.  We had to ask people next to us how to cook it and to eat it.We had the ime of our life there.  Unfortunately, I don't remember the name and cannot give a specific review for that restaurant.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We finally found this street on our second attempt. Google map failed to function well in Korea, don't know why. Maps.me as suggested by other blogger was good for car travellers. It is not stable for pedestrians. Anyway, it's just opposite the jeju dongmun traditional market, cross the main road and the street is at the inner side. You may show the entrance arch to shop keepers nearby, they will indicate the direction. To me, the black pork is not anything spectacular, just common bbq as can be found elsewhere. I am not a food critic, hence I couldn't actually tell the difference. You can try any of the restaurants in this street. I guess they are the same. Enjoy!

We enjoyed our visit to Hallim Park very much. The parking was easy and ticket was very reasonable. If you like plants, then you are in luck. A lot of plants to see and I loved the lilies among other things. There are rock gardens and lava tubs (underground). Since the park is quite big (bigger than other gardens/parks on the island), you'd never feel crowded. We even had lunch at the on-site restaurant and it was quite good. As noted on the top, this is a great place to spend a few hours while visiting Jeju Island.

We enjoy shopping underground. We were able walk from one end to another. Just remember where you enter. There is a number so you will not get lost.There were beauty products, children clothing, adult clothing, bags, shoes, restaurants, etc. They are not your designer stuff but cheap items. Since winter, they sell winter wear. We bought some face masks, cleanser for less than $10. We also bought bags for $15. The lady said made in korea so we think ok. The backpack is great cos very spacous. Good for traveling. Quality is just ok. Then at one exit near to the wet market, we found a shop called bang bang. It belongs to a friend of the korean actor who starred in the famous korean drama   my love from the star   we were able to buy simple T shirts, socks. They are less than $10. Socks about $3. We actually shop here 2 times when we were staying in ocean suites hotel. It was just 10 to 15 minutes walk to this underground shopping area.There are restaurants here too. We found a good korean restaurant here. It was good food and affordable.

We drove ourselves and although a little hard to find, it was worth the effort. The area was quite well set out with information and small local restaurant and gift shop area. Entry is free to Jeju workers but about 5,000 won - the steps down are step but well made. We walked about 2 kms to the end of the tunnel - it was damp, cold and generally well lit. Wear sturdy shoes and a warm coat, take a water bottle.  Worth a look.

We drove our rented car onto the ferry which took us to Udo in 15 minutes. If the weather hadnt been so cold, we would have tried the fun looking electric scooters. We stumbled into a seafood restaurant to the left of the ferry terminal and enjoyed a sumptuous seafood kimchi hotpot. Ordering was not a problem as the service staff spoke mandarin. The place was an obvious favourite with locals. We spent 4 hours exploring various sites and even got lost. A friendly local policeman kindly pointed us the right way. We stopped by quaint coffeeshops and hugged their cute puppies. We were reluctant to leave this idyllic tiny island.

We drove our car over to Udo Island via a ferry. It was a great experience. A tip for drivers to head for the parking at the jetty as you have to fill in a form with your particulars (car number, drivers details) to purchase a ticket at the tour office. It only takes 15 mins to cross the island and thereafter we drove around. There are no maps so we went one round. It was very crowded being a Saturday so try to go on weekdays. There are a lot of interesting cafes, 4 beautiful beaches, lighthouses, lots of lovely spots for sightseeing and great photos opp. You can also take a speedboat at the black beach or visit the caves. We took the seafood pot with instant noodles for lunch in a local small restaurant. The last ferry was at 6.00pm but maybe earlier on weekdays. Overall, it was a very interesting day trip and we enjoyed ourselves.

We did the Yeongsil trail.  The first kilometer in the forest was kind of random.  But once we got above the tree line, the scenery was beautiful.The path is very well maintained with boardwalks and handrails.  But it goes up 400 meters in the first 2.5 kilometers, so it is definitely steep, with entire sections of just stairs, a little bit like climbing up the Eiffel Tower.  This is not a relaxing stroll and you need to be in decent shape to enjoy it.  When we saw it was 7.4 kilometers round trip, we thought it would take us 2 hours, but it almost took us 3, with limited rest time.The last kilometer to the junction with the other trails is all flat, with boardwalks through the highlands.  We didn't try the restaurant on top.So all in all, lots of variety, beautiful bushes, beautiful flowers, lots of birds, nice rock formations.An absolute must if you go to Jeju Island.

We did the Gwaneumsa trail up Mount Hallasan to the peak and back is over 18 miles round trip, over 3500 feet of climbing and then descending it. But it's worth it. I offer only a few points of advice. It is tougher, 800m longer, but more scenic than the Seongpanak trail. To find the Gwanmeusa trail entrance parking lot, plug in the number for the Unesco Hallasa Gwaneumsa Office: +82-64-756-9950 (you only need the last 7 digits on Jeju GPS systems if driving).1) Be prepared with good hiking and walking shoes. We saw two shoes blow out, one about 2.5 hours in. The poor guy had to walk back. There is no rescue if this happens. Also, a girl's shoe blew out on the way down about 3/4 way down, it still nearly 1.5 hours to the end depending on how slow you go. I will discuss in #3 why good shoes are so important.2) Go early, and go slow if you are not in shape or do not do activities often. Hallasan is definitely attainable by nearly anyone but it is tough, very tough because of the steep steps. Unless you are in shape and do many physical activities all the time, I recommend starting at 6AM. You MUST be at Samgakbong shelter by 12:30PM otherwise they will turn you around. It is 3/4 way up the climb. From here it is another 2 hours to the peak of the Halla.3. The volcanic stone paths and the stairs will make your legs very very tired and your feet sore. I believe they made Gwanmeusa trail challenging with rocks on purpose. These are not small rocks, they are big ones that challenge each step. Walking sticks are highly recommended. The stones seem pretty and authentic until halfway up then they are tough. Then on the way down, each step seems like a sadistic joke played by the planners. Eventually you will be relieved to make it to the bottom to your car or bus.4. Be prepared for wind. We got lucky and it was warm the day we went... in fact low warm temperatures will seem even warmer due to humidity about 1/2 the time up the mountain and back. It is a little cooler and windier at the top. Wear light, polyester clothing in layers. long sleeve tech shirt, with light jacket and light rain cover. You should be OK. Gloves and hat or scarves during cooler time. Very light during summer due to heat and humidity.After you get down on Gwanmeusa trail, there is a small restaurant with Korean snacks like pajeon and gimbap, as well as a 7/11 next door. Drink some local mokkoli or soju with with the hot snacks/food! We had a great time. Only 20 minutes out Jeju City when there is no traffic. However with rush hour traffic, or busy time it takes about 45 minutes to get back into Jeju City.

We did 3 Jeju Olle Route 1, 6 & 7 and 14-1. We did not complete all the Olle route but every one of the route was breath-taking and worth the walk. All the route were doable by public transport and car rental was not needed.Jeju Olle Route 1We did not do the entire route 1 as we wanted to visit seongsan 1st plus we started late. As we stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal, we took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. I have car sickness but it was still bearable for me. We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area. The bus journey took about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.Jeju Olle Route 6 & 7 We did not do the entire 6 & 7 trail but we visited Chilshimni Poetry Park, Hwangwooji coast, Oedolgae observatory and Oedolgae. This was a scenic trail and I highly recommend. We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10 minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline and headed to Saeseom Island. Saeseom Island was a short 20 to 30 minutes trail that brought us to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree Celsius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up a temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Park Sunshine hotel was). Then, You need to turn in to Namseong-ro road and you will see a brick wall painted dark blue with pinnochio seated on a bench (photo attached) you will passed by a ?hip?몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online - photo attached). u will then past by Poong Gyung Hotel in Jeju (not the one u can find online - photo attached) before arriving at Hwangwooji coast. I love Hwangwooji coast bcos it was like a private pool. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.  After-which we head to Oedolgae and walked till Dombenang-gil Road. We decided to head back as I needed the toilet. At the entrance to Oedolgae, there was a public toilet acorss the road. The toilet were will keep with toilet paper provided. You can watch the sunset if you have time. However, we decided to walk back to our hotel as we were tire. Jeju Olle Route 14 ? 1If you love beaches, this is a must walk route (at least it was really breathe-taking for me). We stayed at Seowipo, we took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We needed to change bus 702 (opposite the tourist infrmation counter) to Hyeojae beach. It cost 3300 won. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields (photo attached). You will see a beautiful beach 1st (Geumneung Beach) but don?t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down to Geumneung Beach later as it was part of olle route 14-1 (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up. In Summary, I always thought that you would need to rent a car around jeju. However, during my 4 days trip (even Hallasan was done using public transport ? can look at my post at tripadvisor), all our travelling was done throuh public transport. We were able to view those usual scenic places that ple usually go too! The good thing about walking was that we could stop at anytime we want to take picture or do something we did not plan for (Eg: watch how the local harvest shellfish). However, we were the kind that love to walk and could spend 7 hours walking. Therefore, we could travel in jeju with a budget using their public transport.

We decided to visit this   Green tea Museum   because it was a rainy day but could not find much of a direction - there was a mention of the tea stone experience but no further information.  We ended up going to the busy restaurant through a small 'museum' and ended up 'enjoying the $9 green tea'.  On the fields across from the museum there are kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures for photo opportunities.

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We chance upon this on our drive from Seogwipo to Hyeopjae.  The pink building is big and visible from the highway. They should have repainted it as it looks washout and faded pink. But once I step in, it?s totally new! Infact it is even newer than Sanrio Puroland which I visited in Tokyo and bigger than there! I am a true blue HK fan since 40 years ago. Once HK fan steps in, I am sure you will be transformed to a little princess at heart and you?ll be so excited again! There are a lot of Instagram worthy area to take photos. As others pointed out, it has a section that talks about the evolution of HK from 1970s till now.  There are HK rooms, dining room, bus, living room, wardrobe, dressing room etc. Even the toilets are so pretty! Level 2 offers some purikura area, a restaurant and some other HK displays.  There is a 3D dancing room too. On the 3rd floor, there is a open air rooftop HK small maze. On level 1, you go through the souvenirs shop to exit and a notice states that once u exit, u can?t go in again. So it?s best that u buy yr souvenirs when u are ready to leave. I swear I could stay there for 3 hours but as my husband is with me, it only took us about 1.5 hrs to complete our visit. Overall this place is small and not much for non Kitty fans. For us Kitty fans, it is definitely a must visit.

we can enjoy this place with family and toddler or young kids,  not recommend for gentlemen. but very educative for children. located inside the Jungmun Tourist Complex, you can get anythink you need in this tourist complex like various restaurant, hotels , 3D art museum, Belive it or not. Kpop Museum , Conventionl Centre , Waterfall Etc

We came down here because like anyone and everyone who visits Jeju, they're told to go try black pork at one of the restaurants at Black Pork street in Jeju City. So we were in town (stayed in Seogwipo) and decided to go.However me and my partner both thought that the food is over hyped and isn't as great as it's made out to be. I even go on to think that majority of the pork they serve is from regular pork... for anyone that thinks they'll be able to tell the difference is lying. Much prefer traditional Korean BBQ with beef cuts as I much prefer beef as the pork is quite fatty.Still visit for the experience but wouldn't go again if I was to go back to Jeju.

We booked one day tour, but had the best time with Andy so we decided to book one more day. We really think Andy is the best tour guide available in Jeju. Not only professional but he is very caring and very kind.He recommended the best destinations and kindly tried his best to find restaurants for us (we are vegans so it’s quite hard). It was our first time to Jeju and we felt safe traveling with him. You really want him to guide you for your Jeju trip!

We booked Mr Ko for 4 days.Though we prepared our itinerary but we end up leaving the schedule to him as he will change based on the weather condition.Looking through the photos he took for us, it?셲 all fun memories! We never had so many group photos taken as if we had a personal photographer with us.He does impromptu stops for us to take sceneries like sunset, cherry blossom view and gave us tips how we can capture those moments.He brought us to local restaurants with good value.He patiently waited for us as we time to enjoy the scenery, ended up he has to take v late lunch....He has made our jeju trip fun and memorable. We recommend his service though he speaks very little English. He provides WiFi in the jumbo taxi so we can do google translate when we had problem communicating.Thanks again Mr Ko!

We arrived here by bus from our Jeju hotel on a Friday night.  It took approximately 35-40 minutes because of the traffic and the nondirect route our bus took.  The front of the market (across the street) has a small open square area where they would have live music for the night.  We also noticed a few drunks sitting around in the area, but they seemed harmless.The market itself is quite large.  The market seemed to specialize in selling tangerines.  There were stall after stall selling local tangerines.  There is a larger variety of items offered for sale as you walk into the market some more.  We tried some food that was being sold - in this case, some pork at around 9000 won.  There is also seafood and other vegetables and meats sold.  The market seemed to extend to other areas - it's quite close to the Black Pork Street, some other more upscale shops and restaurants.  It's definitely worth a 1-2 hour walk within the market to explore.
Water was crystal clear - not too cold. Many great restaurants nearby. Floats available for rent. It was a little busy, but not too crazy.

Wasn't aware that some of the restaurants don't serve individual. Wanted to try Dombedon as it was highly recommended by friends and online raves, but was turned away in the face as they not only refuse to serve one-person (what if I can eat 2 pax portion?), they did not bother to offer other food options at all.Disappointed yet no choice, so I tried my luck at other restaurants - the one beside it was alright to serve even for one pax. Order their grilled black pork belly and it was tasteful. The side dishes were plentiful! However it was not especially fantastic with wow factor (considering it is the famous Black Pork Street area). So I guess it really depends on individual visitors. Do visit later in the day, as not all restaurants are open early.

Was here for dinner across two nights.  Managed to compare Dombedon (without knowing it's Michelin rated) and Hwaro Hyang (on our 1st night). Comparing the two restaurants, I'm wondering what's the big deal about Dombedon. For a start Dombedon seemed to be mass producing with the intent to get us through our meals asap while those at HH treated their meats with respect.  E.g. HH doesn't cook all their meats at one time while Dombedon just dumped all the meats at one time, resulting in charred meat, spoiling the experience.  I am not even sure if I was eating black pork, insignificant as it may be.  At HH, it was odd at first to see abalone being baked along with black pork, but it was a pleasure to see the shellfish curled up as it cooked.  In HH, they bothered to sprinkle salt on their pork to bring out the flavour, but Dombedon disappointedly didn't. Prices are really almost the  same anyway.  My recommendation would have been HH, though we haven't really tried the rest.(The 2nd pic is from HH and the 1st pic is from Dombedon.)

Was here during the winter, winter clothes sold at value. You can get a whole set here, from undies to mittens at a discount price.  Place is well maintained, underground so you're warm.  Not too many restaurants but the space is sprawling and windy, you can get lost. Thankfully there are maps, just remember your entry point to keep your bearings.  Toilets all around, with no bidet.  Things sold were all more or less the same as you spend a bit of time browsing.

Visiting this caves/tubes you can walk trough the geology! A huge tunnel made by lava rivers 300 thousands years ago, now accessible and well explained. A lot of lava stalactites and stalagmites and huge lava stones felt down from the ceiling. It is unbelievable how   untouched   their rest through the millenni. Nice job by the administrators of the park. It costs only 2000 won.You can also enjoy a free car parking and a small restaurant.

Visited the restaurant (Top Bupyeong Grilled Pork Bella) across the street from the Dombedon Michelin rated restaurant, since I heard that that place doesn?t serve solo travelers. This place didn?t disappoint. The black pork neck had the least amount of fat which I prefer. Many sides also for piling on as well as soup.

Visited Hamdeok Beach (⑤댁) with my boyfriend. We took a walk around the beach. It was really windy and cold. The wind was strong. The beach is very clean and beautiful. The waters are clear. We took some pictures there and we happened to see couple having wedding photoshoot (with the beautiful scenery).Many people from various age groups visited this beach. It is a nice place to take a walk and chill out. There are hotels, shops, convenience stores, cafes and restaurants nearby the beach. There is also public toilet nearby the beach (near the carpark). We drove there. It is very convenient and we can get some snacks while chilling out there.

Very talented artist and excellent works, a sad and interesting story. While the museum itself has only got a smallish collection, the park and the streets around the place is really worthwhile exploring, nice cafes and restaurants in the area too.

Very friendly and helpful to all of us, he is also very kind in recommending us the must-go attractions and even getting us discounted entrance fee around Jeju.
