One of the Olle-gil trails (trail 10-1 to be exact) goes through and around most of the island although two or three hours are enough to walk on every single path on the island.? The island is mostly covered by wheat fields with two small villages at two ends of a main road that bisects the island.? Several houses on the main road are decorated with informative murals that describe the culture and history of Gapado making it an interesting walk.? The center of the island has a view point about 20 meters above ground that’s not much different from seeing things at ground level.? Handful of Harubang statues and some rapeseed flower fields make some good photo spots.? Other than the few dozen houses, the small elementary school is the only notable building.? As it only takes a couple of hours to walk around the entire island, eating a meal is about the only other thing to do.? Few seafood restaurants serve up some raw fish but the Gapado Haemul Jjajang restaurant was the most popular spot during my trip serving up Koreanized Chinese food with plentiful seafood toppings on the jjampong (spicy broth noodles) and jjajangmyeon (black bean noodles).

One of the benefits of being an island is all the beaches. One of the drawbacks is that beaches usually draw tourists, and where there are tourists, the shallow villainy of tourist industries inevitably follows. Sehwa has not yet been targeted for development. As of this writing, the long, open expanse of Sehwa beach is still a beach in its rawest form. When the tide goes out, the volcanic rock formations nearer to the road are exposed, leaving tidal pools to explore, thriving with an over abundance of flora and fauna. The beach at low tide is enormous, and rarely crowded. There are no lifeguards. No music. No lights. Just a beautiful beach, minor waves, clean sand, and decent swimming. When the tide comes in, you can continue swimming, or you can visit some of the restaurants in the area that cater to the locals rather than skimp for the tourists. I had some shabu shabu (??\대＿?) very near Sehwa which was like a kick to the pleasure center of my brain.  Sometimes there's even a local crafts market right next to Sehwa beach, but you have to get lucky to catch it.   Basically, Sehwa is a beach that is still Jeju. It's part of a local community, part of a local ecosystem, as yet only mildly disturbed by ideas of profitability or development.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Okay judging by the other reviewers, I must have been there on a great day. The water was crystal clear and the experience was amazing. My wife and I hiked Hallasan last weekend, which was our first trip to Jeju Do. We've lived in Seoul for 5 years and finally made that trip south. We decided to take the Seongpanak Trail since it allows you to get to the top. Overall, the hike was great - beautiful scenery (although it was a hazy day for us so visibility was limited), challenging hike and it's something that will take up a whole day. We took a different trail down once we reached the top and the views were nicer on that one. I think there are only two trails that go all the way up. We're not hikers by any means so our legs were pretty tired on the way down the mountain. They estimate 8-9 hours total but we did it in 7! Be sure to pack some snacks and water as there's not much available on the hike. There's a small place at a checkpoint a couple hours into the Seongpanak trail where you can get some water, ramen and chocolate bars (along with some basic hiking gear) but don't expect much. We had only taken water with us (rookie mistake) and I was wishing for some extra snacks on the way down. There's also a store/small restaurant at the first entrance to the hike so you can stock up there. Overall, it's definitely worth doing as its one of the main attractions on Jeju.

My husband and I had an absolutely fabulous day pheasant hunting at the Daeyoo Hunting Preserve on Jeju Island in South Korea and then an excellent meal of (our) pheasant sashimi roast pheasant etc. washed down with wine at their excellent pheasant restaurant! Daeyooland also has lovely gardens a charming helpful staff and great coffee!We hunted with a guide and his trusty dog walking for miles thru the beautiful countryside... and my husband did get us a pheasant! We also got to shoot skeet (and they have ATVing as well). My husband had hunted on Jeju many years ago when he was in the US Army and stationed in Korea and I wanted to take him   home   and go hunting with him- and tourists can hunt at Daeyooland! As their website is only in Korean our concierge at the JW Marriott in Seoul (an EXCELLENT hotel which I've also reviewed) was kind enough to help make the arrangements for us. We flew to Jeju Island for the day went hunting and then walked around downtown Jeju going to museums and some of the historic markets (there are 22!) buying and eating those famous Jeju oranges! Then we flew back to Seoul in the evening having had  a GREAT day!

My hotel was almost next to exit 1 of this mall so spent quite a bit of time here shopping for Korean cosmetics but otherwise it's just a regular shopping center, nothing special. Didn't try any of the restaurants down there, as I'd prefer to spend more time in the open air. But this mall serves as a great connection point to many other areas of interest within the city including the Mok provincial government historical site and Dongmun traditional market, with clearly marked signs at each exit.

My friend and I loved this place. We drove in to Udo, boarding the ferry in our car (quite an experience in itself!), and only had 4 hours to explore. Jump shots at the various beaches, hiking up to the tallest part of Udo, trying Hallasan fried rice at the Pungwon restaurant, and having peanut and tangerine ice-cream at Jimmy's ice-cream were all memorable experiences. Driving around, and many a times through one-way lanes between low stone-walls that Udo is known for, was exciting as well. Udo is a must-go!

The food was just average, except for the stir fried rice which was spicy and delicious and the service was terrible.  My mother didn?t want the pork, rather just the noodles.  However, the server forced us to purchase the pork for her and added the noodles as a side dish, inflating the cost of our dinner.  When we asked to speak to the owner about this, we found out that she was the owner and basically yelled at us.I think because this restaurant is on the corner of Black Pork Street, they get many tourists and they don?t care about the quality of the food and service knowing tourists aren?t likely to be returning. My family walked from our hotel to the top of Ilchulbong and down. From the entrance, the mountain(?) looked formidable and it looked to be a painful hike, but it turned out to be rather a short hike. I wish I had taken more time on the way up and enjoyed the views more. On the way down, we saw a restaurant by the rocky shore.  I believe this is where mermaids do their demonstrations and sell raw oyster dishes.  I wanted to go down but my 10 & 12 yr olds won't have it.  So I missed out.         The guy who took the tickets at the entrance surprising had a good nack for taking pictures.  If he is not too busy, ask him to take your group photo. review: My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!

Must visit place if u come to Jeju Island. I rent a bicycle, cycling & round the island. It will takes around 2-3 hours. It will getting easier to stop everywhere and snap the picture. I visited Udo Island end of March and it full with the Canola Flowers!!! Don't forget to try the nut ice cream too. There have a lots of stall and restaurant selling it!!

Most people or tour guides will recommend you to go there for the seafood. However, the stall owners cannot speak other languages. The ones who do speak Chinese are too touristy. Those that sell abalone don't sell fish and vice versa. Better to go to a good restaurant for a taste of seafood stew. Fruits are ok. The good mandarin oranges are sold in boxes. I see locals buying boxes of oranges.

You can't swim because of the waves and only a small area where you can stay. The rest of the beach is for surfing. You can rent two sun beds and one parasol for 40000 Won (only cash) and other services on the beach (that we did not use). The good thing that it is a GS25-store (or 7/11 store don't quite remember) so you can buy drinks and small food. Near the beach there is a small   restaurant   but we didn't it looks so nice to eat there. There's also a restroom available and a parking lot. If you are in this area/Jungmun maybe its more preferable to stay at a resort.For families with kids; I think this beach would suit very well.

Markets have always been interesting to me. They show so much about how the locals eat, shop, trade and work. Dongmun Market is pretty laidback. The folks there are not pushy. It's hardly touristy but still attracts a fair number of tourists. You mainly get to see seafood, fruits and vegetables as you explore the many lanes at the market. Aside from the market itself, the businesses nearby are also colourful and pix-worthy.For me, the highlight of the visit is lunch at one of the several restaurants within a zone at the market. They specialise in seafood, of course, and offer sets (featuring sashimi, a grilled fish, fish stew and banchan) that are value for money.Also don't miss some snack stalls there. My favourite is operated by an old lady (probably in her 70s)  who makes hatteok, sort of a pancake filled with cinnamon sugar, on the spot. It's a sweet, hot treat.

Marado island is small island but it has amazing view. You can see the wide field, blue sea,and Jeju-representing rocks.You can borrow a bike and look around the island riding a bike. And there is also a good restaurants. They use Jeju local specialities.

many themes in the park such as tulip garden, Canola, rapeseed, cherry blossom, more than 100 years old bonsai, folk village with traditional restaurant 竊fresh grilled mackerel竊, well decorated water pond, peacock and bird park and many more. The folk village still maintain the culture of living that one should not miss. One need half a day in completing visiting the park.

Lovely place (June). Water was warm and beautiful. Walk a little bit and you will find more places and not so crowded. There aren't many restaurants for foreigners. I recommend to try the burgers at the red container (can't remember the name). If you don't enjoy fireworks, better don't do after 7pm. There are better things to see and do in Jeju but some people don't understand that!!!

Love this beach! Plenty of restaurants and convenience stores nearby. My only complaint is they wanted to charge 20,000 to use an umbrella for the day. Too expensive! In Haeundae I've never paid more than 5,000. Anyways, the water is nice..And it's less crowded than other beaches. :)

Located in the Jungmun Resort in Jeju, near some restaurants there. The palce is quite large, consisting of 12 galleries. They showed interesting exhibits collected by Ripley at reasonable price (10k won per person). Worth visiting if you want to have some indoor activity in Jeju.

Kids may enjoy posing with Cinderella's carriage & shoe collection and running around the grounds.  As I was not however, although a few glass sculptures were interesting, I did not think it was worth the time or effort (& of course the entrance fee) to go.  Agree with the comments of previous reviewers who rated   poor  .  The  fish lunch I had at the restaurant next door however, was enjoyable. On the plus side, the place is wheelchair accessible.

Just did the hike on 30 March.Trail: seongpanak up and gwaneumsa down. Goes to summit. (highly recommend to do this trail Cos going up by gweumusa is really steep though the view is nicer for gweumusa) Time taken: 4.5hrs up and 4hrs down (please go early and check the time that you need the reach the shelter and summit by.  Think should be by 1230 reach shelter and by 2 to leave summit) Weather: good.  Cold in the morning but as you hike,  you will perspire and definitely need minimum sweaters. I was only wearing teeshirt and windbreaker. In the end only tee-shirt cos it's getting warmer and you climb and when the sun is out. Need crampons?  Yes!!! It helped alot especially at the icy areas both going up and down. Not too sure where you can buy it but I managed to rent it from my hostel. Though I did see people without it,  and they did just fine.  I was wearing track shoes kind. So crampons helped alot!  How to get there: I went there from Jeju city and took bus 281 from bus terminal to seongpanak bus stop. Coming back from gwaneumsa trail: took bus 475 back to jeju  national university and change bus 360 to Jeju city.  Please check with bus driver or use kakao map/bus to help as Google Map doesn't seem to help much with he routes. Bus 475 have some timings going back. You can always find out from the visitors center at the gweumusa base. It is situated at the left side as you make your way down passing through the car park.  Shelters and food: not sure if I did miss it..  But I didn't see any food vendors, drinks stall as I hiked up and down. So I was really thirsty as the end of the trail. There's a small restaurant and a convenience store at gwaneumsa trail end. So please bring ALOT of water like at least 1.5L. Bring along food to eat up there and also plastic bag to put your trash and there are no rubbish bins around.
Just a rock but  if ur imagination is working overtime , you can see the   dragon head  . Many group of tourists see the place. Its near the seaside restaurants of which we find very expensive food.

Jungmun Daepo is the spot where the iconic columnar joint rock formations can be seen. There?s not much to do here, except take a few pictures from a distance, but it?s worth seeing if you?re in the area anyway. I can?t say much about it because there?s not much to say. except that you should allot about 15 minutes in total (including the time to get in an out).Further down the coast is Jungmun beach. I went here in March, so there wasn?t much to do when it?s 10 degrees Celsius. I imagine on a hot day it would be fun to swim here. The beach is pretty ? sand is slightly coarse but clean and lovely since it?s golden in color. The slope from the parking area/restaurants to the beach is pretty steep. I don?t know if it?s safe for people with mobility issues.One downer: I didn?t like the seafood restaurants playing loud, outdated music when we got there ? I think it would be a pain to eat here if you have to listen to that. Someone has to tell the tourism board about this.Where: Seogwipo west coast

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

Its worth it to climb up there. such a beautiful and breath taking view from the top. its a must visit place if you come to Jeju. entrance fee is just 2000krw per person. we actually drove there from our pension. many parking space. other than climbing the peak, you can also catch a Haenyo Diver Women performance at the bottom of mountain right beside it. its amazing to watch those elderly women  holding their breath for several minutes without any oxygen mask! overall its awesome! for those muslims, there's fast food restaurant Lotteria for you to grab your lunch or dinner since they have shrimp burger available. its located on your left when exit the car park area.

It's an okay, nothing to be exaggerated. However, enjoying the walk towards the fall with serene and scenic view is very relaxing. During spring, strolling under the cherry blossoms trees and get to enjoy some local live band music show with people get to move their body to the grooves! Once you got out of the fall, several merchandise shops selling local snacks and merchandise. There are also arrays of local food store nearby serving varies pick of seafood. I went to the nearest restaurant near the merchandise store with red signboard. Food potion is huge and price is reasonable. It was really fresh and tasty! I stayed in the Choi Hostel around the area, so it's quite a walk and hike on the way back, what's with full bloated tummy. BTW, I only ate 2 dishes alone :P

It's a tiny island which will only take about 1 and a half hour to explore around with an auto-bike (renting required) or spend about 2-3 hours cycling around the island. This place is surrounded with mountains, sea, greens, flowers and lovely people. Lots of tiny restaurants and decent cafes can be found in the island. Would recommend everyone to try their peanut/hallabong ice-cream! It's something very different and worth to try.

Its a really short strip of street where most BBQ restaurant are located. Most of them serve black pork . As mentioned in most reviews , the price is on the steeper side. If you like some BBQ black pork then this is the place to go. Its a tourist friendly place after all.

It's a place that is almost carbon-free. Electric cars, wind and solar panels are used for energy. It's small enough to travel around on foot or rent a bicycle. A ferry from Jeju takes about 20 minutes. Nice local restaurants to try.

It's a must do to spend some time at this museum. Located in a relatively new building right on the coast, it tells the story of these amazing women divers who work 52 weeks of the year diving for a abalone, conch and other sea products. How they managed in the winter time without wet suits astonishes me. These women also played a vital part of the resistance movement in World War II against the invading Japanese Army. Add this visit as part of your Jeju Island tour - best idea it to hire a taxi driver for a day (approx A$100). They turn out to be your tour guide, photographer and restaurant selector - fantastic value! Enjoy :)

It's a great honour to be able to admire Mr Sung's Spirited Garden! It's absolutely a must visit whenever you are in Jeju! The garden is a real Paradise on Earth! It's a unique place that teaches you many important things! The garden features many outstanding examples of bonsai trees, beautifully shaped stones, a waterfall, a restaurant and a souvenir shop. It's easily accessible by car or by bus, and will be a worthy place for everyone, especially the nature and art admirers. I highly advise everyone to visit this incredible place!!!

Price is inexpensive and there is also a small restaurant and shop. You may think of bringing a second shirt because inside the lava tube is it cold (12째C/54째F). It?s an easy drive from Jeju City. There?s a nice park and some restaurants and stores. I was there in February and it was cold, windy, and even snowing, but the beach was still beautiful with the black cliffs and the white sand. I?m sure it?d be perfect in warmer weather!

It will take about 30 to 40 minutes to hike up the mountain which involves lots of stairs. View is superb, especially during sunrise because you will be facing east. There are quite a number of shops and restaurants down there, perfect for breakfast after morning hike. Spacious carparks. p/s: I read somewhere that there will be entrance fees (KRW2000-3000). It was just perfect vacation for me & my friends. We always dream of cruises holidays amnd just had a blast on superstar gemini cruise. Hair and beauty treatment was the first thingwe went for. it was just awesome,. they made us feel us like superstars. One my friend spent all her time in the casino. Rooms were so comfy and i enjoed the food at every restaurant. busan and jeju are beautiful places and i wish to go there again!

It was a very tradional market which local vegetable, fruits and fresh seafood were sold.The seafood was very fresh and irresistible, you could find a restaurant there and ordered your favourable fresh catch fish, either cooked or sashimi, the cost was very reasonable, it was also a place to buy your souvenir.

It was a very hot day yesterday, July 31st 2018, and I got sunburn the day before so in 33 degree heat and me didn't match. I didn't go up to the top but I did go up to the first viewing platform, which i think most people would be able to manage slowly, not matter your age. It is well paved, and the views are incredible. It was a very windy day too, so there was no show by the women divers, Haenyo, but you could see where they went out and to be honest the roughness of the seas showed how tough the women must have always been. There are a few shops near the bottom and one part way up, so you can purchase drinks and trinkets if you wish. There is a Starbucks and a Dunkin' Donuts and i think a McDonald's near the car park, as well as multiple Korean restaurants. Well worth a visit, even if you can't ascend to the peak.

It was a really wonderful experience to cycle around the island, although a little tiring. You can rent a motorcycle or trike as well. It is really busy and sometimes a little crowded on the roads. There are many restaurants and a few beaches. Excellent food to be had

It was a lovely trip in Hallim Park, it has many beautiful views to take photos of.It?s so big we spent 4 hours to finish it, and after that we went to Hyeopjae beach which is 5 minutes away from there. However, I was disappointed because of there was one restaurant and it only serves Korean food.

It takes almost one and a half hour to arrive the Island from Jeju-si. But the view was stunning on the Island. There is a shuttle bus service which has 4 stops across the Island and 5000 won for each passager to have an unlimited ride. There is a famous icecream store at the first stop which sell peanut icecream which is very delicious. The beach at the third stop is so stunning with a beautiful ocean. However, the restaurant on the island are quite expensive, so better prepare your own food if you have a tight budget.

It is one of many museums in Jeju, and it's dedicated to Teddy bears. It is full of its history with all the teddy bears from all over the world. All of the ancient teddy bears is well preserved but with relatively minimal background story. Some of the information are written only in Korean, so there isn't many interactive attraction here. There is also an open garden with a few sculptures on it, a Lotteria restaurant and of course the store. The merchandise there is quite expensive and we didn't buy anything. The entrance fee when we came there is 8000 won, a little bit expensive, but quite worth it.

It is beautiful,  seeing nature transformed.  Wear comfortable shoes with traction,  closed toes. It can be slippery and the rocks can be slick. Bring a light jacket bc it is cool down there. There are about 75 to 100 steps of stairs.There is a delicious restaurant on site. They do take credit cards. There is also a mini convenience store. Restrooms are clean and well maintained.

It is an ideal place to buy souveniors and see/taste the local food.  Rather clean even we went inside the fish and vegetable market.  Along we found few food stalls and restaurants to offer seafood, we were hesitated but decided to go for fish and cuttle fish sushimi in one with rather good environment, it's food and service were up to standard, price was not high compared to those in restaurant.  Interested to see local Kimchi, fish, fruits, herds, snacks from the stores

It is a dood place to walk, think, and stare.....  Many people  come with families & friends Children have a lot of pace to play. One can  have a lunch  at the restaurant. It is a  great beautiful park   within Jeju Si.
It can be a good spot for the sunrise, if the weather is good. Lots of great local fish restaurants nearby.

If you want something go, hungry go, street food go, you name they have it. Ate sushi for 3 days in a row at one of the restaurants in the market and never the same twice. Best place to try the famous Jeju pork.
If you love black pork Korean BBQ, this is the place to be. The little street in about 50 metres long is full of black pork bbq restaurants. You cannot go wrong with any of them

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

If you can't make it to Manjanggul caves, there are caves here too. There is a lot of English signage for the trees, which is great. There is a cafe and restaurant on site. I really enjoyed the  afternoon out, lots of lovely different areas to explore.

If you are in Jeju-do, Black Pork Street (Heuk Dwaeji) is a must visit place. As the street name given, yup.. Selling point is Black Pork. Go in to one of the many restaurants on street and try the grilled black pork meat, it is the signature dish in Jeju Island. If you try this is Seoul, it will cost you double or maybe triple the bill. Most menu are in Hangul but there will be a simple English too, the best way is to choose the set menu. Price are reasonable if you choose the restaurant that is less fancy and not those tourist welcoming type. We had the best BBQ dinner in Korea.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

If it’s springtime?or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju. ? Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.? Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.? Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km? to about 250 residents.? The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.? There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.? But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.? You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.? Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?? Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.? The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.? Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.? Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:? Good points:? outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;? site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival? (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:? bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;? sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.? There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.? Getting there:? Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .? There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.? Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

I went to see the crater in middle day. Was a long bus ride to get there for a 10 min visit in all. Not what I expected. It is a very rare formed crater in the world and the explanations are on a board but kind of deceiving to look at for me. All full of lush green trees and very wide, it does not give great pics and you don't see it that well either. Not as impressive as I expected. Would tell you to prioritize other stuff if you have a tight schedule. Souvenir shop has not much to buy and there is a small restaurant for snacks or ice cream.

I wasn't expecting to have to walk up this thing, but I guess that should have been obvious to me. It was a hot and panting walk, but it was not that long. It was a sunny day, which made for great views, but not for a cool walk. I had JUST MISSED the show with the women divers, I guess it is at 1:30 and 3:00 daily. Nice panorama at the top, the view is certainly impressive.One other thing I liked a lot about this is that it is a fairly touristy area, which meant that most restaurants I passed had pictures and/or English on the menu outside and inside the restaurant, making it easier to order food,

I was very excited to visit after reading the reviews; while it was very nice, I left slightly dissapointed. Maybe we visited at the wrong time of year, but almost nothing was blooming outside. The different outdoor gardens were pretty, but I was expecting a lot more colorful displays.Inside was a bit more of what I expected (although again, not as many flowers as I thought there would be). The main area is air-conditioned, which is a HUGE relief from the heat outside (and some of the display rooms are pretty toasty, as well).? We were lucky to get a clear day, so the view from the top of the glass dome was fantastic.The garden is in a great location, with plenty of restaurants and other attractions nearby, and just a short drive from Pacificland and the beach. As a stand-alone, the garden may have been a bit of a let-down, but since we were able to spend a couple of hours here, get some lunch, and then head down to the beach for some waves, it ended up being a fun family day.

I was told the hike up will only take 30 minutes but when I looked at it I was convinced it would take longer. The hike up is quite steep, lots of stairs, however it really just took a bit more than 30 min, to my own surprise. The hike is not easy however, it requires some stamina, many people take a break or two on the way up. Definitely bring something to drink. Seongsan is quite crowded with tourists, so lots of people all over. The hike is worth it, amazing views from the top. And the hike down is much more enjoyable then the one up. At the foot of Seogsan is a large parking lot, easy to leave your rental there, plus again lots of cafes, restaurants etc. You have to pay a fee to enter.Overall worth seeing Seongsan!

I was on my way to another destination when I saw this place. I caught the 700 bus that runs around the outside of Jeju island for a cost of around $2, and wondered why so many people were getting on and off at this stop, so on my way back I got off. It ended up being my highlight of the day.It was a lovely sunny day with a few hundred people climbing up, and with ramps and steps all the way it was easy. I got to the top in about half an hour if not less. The views from the top were probably the best I experienced for my whole trip in Jeju, and that includes the view I saw from top of Mt Hallasan.At only 2000 won entry, it's a must-do when visitng Jeju, and there's lots of restaurants at the bottom.

I visited here with my family, so we drived our rental car. But if you don't have an international license, then rent a bike or motorcycle.You can rent it in a reasonable price.There are 5 bus stations here and those are nice sights.There is a beach in two sights and one of them is a popular site for jet boat.And the other one is popular for water leports.And whole Island is a heaven for riders.If you love mountian bike or road bike, then take your bike to this island.This is a perfect place for cycling.And there are many nice restaurant and dessert cafe, so enjoy yourself here.

I think it was more academic then entertaining. Despite cutting edge technology based attraction, this place has enough mixture of both interesting facts and entertainment. Restaurant was lots of fun as well. And I think it means a lot to see the corporate name. People all know   Nintendo   but not many knows a top Korean game corporate. I think it is nice.

I studied the seoqwipo bus route and decided to bring my family for a day trip to Udo Island. I stayed in Jungmun Resort vicinity. It was easy to catch bus 282 from here and made a transfer for direct bus to Udo Passenger Terminal. Upon arrival, after filling up the necessary details and proof of passports竊we went to the cruise Departure point. Luckily we chosen a weekday for this trip. The queue was short. In the cruise ship, we could find seats. A 15 min ride and we were greeted by several e-scooters and shop houses. Here, you could settle for lunch. But if it was too early for you, several sightseeing spots come with line of restaurants. We took the circular bus (white color van) which we thought was the best choice. Every stop you were  required to queue to abroad. This bus went to most attractions including black sand & Udo lighthouse. The bus route was also the route for E-scooters /car. Do be careful for safety sake. Returning from Udo Island was amazing : we could not find a bus stop that for the same bus number  supposed to bring us back to Seoqwipo! Nevertheless, luckily we had alternative plan ! we took a bus that brought us to Gimpo Airport. Got a decent dinner and then took limo bus 600 directly to our accomodation, alighting at bus stop named Jungmun Resort Entrance. This DIY by public transport comes in cheap!This trip you need a whole day.

I really love this place, sooo much. You can reach this place by bus number 710 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal directly, trip around 90 minutes & pay for bus fare by T-Money. This bus route passing some attraction in Jeju, so please stop at the attraction you wants to visit. You can rent a car too. From bus stop at Seongsan Ilchulbong, you must walking around 300 meters. What i loved about this place is, so many seafood restaurants (because it really close with ocean) & some Korean cosmetics shop too. Don't forget to bring jacket, umbrella and of course mineral water. If you have strength, you can climbs the hill (around 500 meters). But so much fog when i'm there, i can't see clearly the basin. You will met some elderly people here, at the peak. Fresh air & green vegetation will makes your eyes & breath feels relieve. You can buy some souvenirs when you get back to the foothills.

I really liked this part of the trip. We hiked up to the top, and I am a five month pregnant lady so you can do it too! The view of the city below is the most interesting view you are going to get from the top of the crater. The top of the crater itself isn't that spectacular. It was very pretty and fun! Also we happened to be there around the same time as the lady divers so we watched that and it was pretty interesting. When we were there in December they were doing shows around 1:30 and 3:30. You should definitely come here. There are also little restaurants and shops at the bottom if you are hungry!

I only went up this trail for 1.5 hours then came back as that was all I wanted to do.  I took my time and because I did that I saw deer which many people just walked by not noticing.  The trail is quite rocky.  You need good boots and cotton gear as you get quite hot. (All the Koreans dress up in this synthetic mountain looking gear and my husband who went all the way up said they were all nearly passed out on the side of the track from over heating!) Some people had these HUGE packs on their backs.  God knows what they were carrying! I had 2 bottles of water and dried octapus for sustenance and that was enough.  My husband who went all the way up used 7 bottles.  You can buy water at various places up the trail so you don't have to carry it all. There are a lot of people who do this ...or try...so it's best to start at 6am to beat the crowds.  There is also a train of sorts that you can pay for to take you most of the way up.  Not sure how much that costs.  There's a restaurant at the bottom surprisingly that's all in Korean,  no English, no pictures, which is odd for such a big tourist area. They have a beef soup, sushi rolls Kim bap and other stuff.  I'll upload a pic of the menu so you can get a translation before you go there.I'm not sure if you have to pay a fee to climb this track as we just walked up but on my return I did see a ticket box so maybe you do...

I never been to such places before so i have no reference to compare it to. I think it was worth the entrance fee, a bit hard to get there with the buses. You pay the fee for inside baths that are separated by male and females, where most of the people are naked. You pick a small locker room for your shoes and with the same key you can open a bigger locker for the fest of your belongings. You should shower before getting in the tubs and must pay to use the outdoor tubs, where both man and women can use(not naked). Try to follow the instructions in english of how to use the baths, for how long and in what order and it will be worth it. They also have massages, sleeping rooms, lounges, vibrating chairs, small restaurant ...

I love hallasan so much, this is definetly the camp, although it was winter when we got there, but really its very beautifull .... I cant imagine , hallasan when spring ... For get in here, there is bus station 15 minutes walk from the foothills, but dont know exactly the number of the bus, because we hire rental car for only 20.000 won !!! Its amazing right ?? But sadly hallasan didnt have any restaurant or proper rest area for us to enjoy the view, or it because the winter season, i dont know ...

I live quite close to this beach and really love it. On days ending on 1 and 6, there is a traditional market which is nice. Many restaurants to choose from, as well as an Olive Young, Spanish restaurant, Starbucks, etc however I prefer buying CU drinks and sitting in the sand. Sunset is AMAZING here.
I liked most the   junk   food restaurant over there :-)

I like to explore super markets in different cities and different countries. It's a good way to see what people are eating. Sometime when I have the courage, I will tried some of the local food. Dongmun Market is one of the popular traditional markets in Jeju. It is big, clean and colourful. They sell all kinds of stuff, like fruit, fresh or dry (some in gift boxes), vegetables, dry mushrooms, herbs, spices and fresh or dry sea food. There are some restaurants ready to serve you. They even sell clothing there. We walked around and took photos, but no one came to pressure us to buy stuff, I like that.Happy Travelling!

I have visited Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong) for sunrise hikes on three occasions this year. Each was very different, but all pleasant. Things to consider:- The hike is all steps, but only takes about 20 minutes for a moderately fit person.- The top is always windy. If it's already windy at the base, make sure everything you carry is tied/contained, because it can be very windy at the top.- It costs a small fee to enter when the ticket booth is open. If you get there really early, they might not be open yet!- No bathrooms after you leave the parking lot (and no secluded places), so plan accordingly!- Nothing at the base will be open before a sunrise hike, but you should be able to grab coffee/donuts after!- It's nice to carry up a picnic breakfast and sit at the top to eat and watch the other tourists.- Check the weather before you go if you really want a good view. We had a couple cloudy days that were less spectacular, but still always a refreshing hike, beautiful mountain and cool views over the ocean.We usually pair our trip with a trip out to Udo Island or to some of the other east-coast attractions like Manjangul Caves.There's a lovely motel paired with a seafood restaurant about 10 minutes walk from the entrance to the peak hike. Follow the beach sidewalk almost to the edge of town. Views from the in-room balconies over the beach. Big rooms and nice folks, even if they don't speak any English.

I have to say, when we reached the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong we were a bit underwhelmed. It's impressive if you haven't yet seen the summit of Hallasan, but if you have it really doesn't compare. The crater of Seongsan Ilchulbong is porous, so it doesn't hold water like Hallasan. And it only takes you about 20-30 mins to reach the top viewing deck. It does make for a good photo, but so do the views of Seongsan village and the coastline nearby. The view on the pathway walking towards the base of it is also impressive in itself.It's definitely worth visiting, and there are plenty of little shops/stalls selling food as well as cheap souvenirs. Nearby is Ilchulbong beach, with black sand. Haenyeo female divers are famous here, and there is a restaurant at the far end of the beach serving fresh seafood caught by the divers, but we didn't have time to eat there.

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.
I have driven pass this place coincidentally It's quite unique place, worth a visit. A few shops, restaurants, caf챕, and street food markets.

I had high hopes for this spot, but it is hard to recommend it.  What was once a pretty island is now circled by identical seafood restaurants, cafes, burger joints and other tourist shops.   Biking a loop around the island is nice enough, but the road is jammed with little electric   rickshaw   things and noisy scooters.  Honestly, this place would be a perfect case study of bad development for a tourism management class.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I got the bus here from Jungmun - a couple of hours in total but it was worth it. Really good value, lots to look at, peaceful place to walk around, beautifully done and looked after. There weren't many other people there so it felt as if I had the place to myself. I had lunch in the restaurant and that was also good. Make sure you take your camera. Hugely recommended.

I got a public bus from the Inter-city Bus Terminal at Jeju-si to this park at only Won 2000. 1 hour required.  This is the last activity of my trip and upon leaving, luckily I met an American man at the bus stop who agreed to share a taxi with me heading to the airport, otherwise I may be late.Time is rather limited for me and I took a quick and rough walk in the park after taking a 45 min lunch of seafood pot at the restaurant at the entrance.  Yummy!  Seafood is to die for in Jeju.  I like this park as it's well gardened, clean, cozy with some souvenirs shops and two restaurants inside.  And I did not meet groups of tourists which is a PLUS.  Visitors decent. Next time when I come to Jeju, I should spend plenty of time in this park.There is a famous beach opposite to the park entrance so you can have a walk there as well after leaving here.

I got 28 hour spare time before my flight to Dhaka in my last visit to Korea. When I got this break at the very last moment, I searched Jeju air ticket and hotel booking online without any delay. As I purchased it at the last moment, I had to spend USD 125 more for air ticket and hotel booking. Jeju is a rush destination in summer. It's is a fairly large island to cover within 24 hours. Thanks to TripAdvisor and reviewers for helping me to select Seongsan Ilchulbong and Hamdaeok beach from many other attractions.Tourists have time, usually visit Seongsan Ilchulbong before dawn to observe Sunrise. That why it is also known as Sunrise peak. As I did?t had that option in hand, I climbed it at afternoon. I took a taxi from my hotel at Hamdaeok beach and it costs around USD 28. Bus is always cheaper but I had only 20 hours left in my hand to catch my return flight. Sunrise peak entry ticket costs USD 2 for adults and USD1 for child. Most of the review I read earlier suggests it takes 20 minutes to climb on the peak but as an amateur I took roughly 40 to 45 minutes to climb. There are two wide and convenient stairway to climb on the peak. I selected the left side stairway and eventually it was a right decision. Because there is a small grocery in the midway selling soft drinks and water for those who didn't buy it from the base. As usual they charge double for each drinks but it was a life saver for me. When I came down from the other way I didn't find any shop like this. There are also a  midway station if you are tired want get refreshed for a while. When I reached on the peak I was almost exhausted. The view is literally breathtaking. I was sitting there more than one hour and a half as it is so charming that made for  forget everything else of life. I came down from the other stair way. The surrounding is so calm and comfortable that I stayed their until it?s dark. Tips: Try to book air ticket and hotel upfront to save cost. Rely more in internet than locals advise because there is a high chance of misleading information due to language barrier. I lost twice in the island for relying on them and lost around 3 hours of my precious time. There are halal restaurant ( Bagdad and Rajmahal) in Jeju island. 4 days are fairly enough to cover most of the attraction of Jeju. It costs total USD 400 all inclusive  for me for a quick tour , however if you are two them many cost will be shared within you. If I could catch the early morning flight from Gimpo airport at 7:30 am and save three more hours to arrive Jeju island then I could go to Udo island as well. I couldn't do that because I had to come from Suwon city. So if you stay at Seoul, you can catch 7:30 morning flight comfortably.

I found this to be the best attraction in Jeju. It really is a lot of stairs, so if you are not good in health condition, this might be very tiresome. But there are rest points a long the way, so you can take your time. There are little shops and restaurants around after you finish your hike. Beautiful views to take pictures both going up and down.

I found pretty disappointing this 1 block Street where several pork cuisine restaurants are located, mostly for tourists, thats why the prices raises up from others in the city. Only if you go to shop nearby and want to taste Jeju pork in well decorated restaurants

i feel i am lucky cos my hotel just nearby Yongduam Rock.the story behind is very attractive but won't give you a surprise when you really at there.The scale of Yongduam Rock is smaller than you think, but if you love to take picture with infinity sea or amazing sea wave, this place is a good place to go.finally, there are lot of restaurants around there, can have a good time after visit there.

I didn't know I was looking at this famous peak when we approached in a taxi (looking for a lunch spot that our kids would approve of). I was saying   Wow, look at that   as we drove towards it. Then our driver explained it was the famous peak. I can see why, even on a cloudy rainy day it was such a beautiful scene. We couldn't climb to the peak because it was closed to the public due to an impending typhoon. I was disappointed we couldnt climb but so glad that we got to see it, even from the base. Absolutely beautiful area. I want to come back to Jeju just to climb that peak and see the beauty from above.Incidentally there were plenty of restaurants and cafes and shops in the small town at the base. Even an American Embassy (i.e. Mcdonalds)

I can imagin Udo is a quiet and beautiful island to stroll or bike sometime, but the day we visited was full of people.  We arrived there already at noon and rented electric bicycles to start rounding the small island.  The road was full of small vehicles and bikes moving or stopping by the road, I did not feel I was in the nature but a hustle corner.  There were quite some restaurants and cafes along the route, the one we went was full of people, price of food/drink is in high end.  It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

I came here after a hike up Hallasan and boy the hassle of trying to find it was so worth it. The pork bbq we had (don't know the name of the restaurant) was amazing, anyone who has had Korean bbq before knows how good it is, don't miss this place.

I am not sure about the name cause it was all in Korean and nobody spoke any english or basque or language I could understand but if you can read Korean I am sure you will be able to find the place, it is just passed the underground market, there are a lot of restaurants in the area, and the place is really a must you to taste real Korean food, lot of mini restaurants every here and there all of them similar and nice, no English, Basque Italian, French Spanish... or similar language spoken so just point what you want wait and pay.

Highly recommend visiting Dongmun market! The market has plentiful, and affordable fresh meat, seafood, as well as Jeju-only snacks, beverages, restaurants and dried food. For a small fee (depending on the store, around $5 for 9 Kg), food including fresh meat and seafood can be shipped from Jeju to mainland Korea. Shipment takes about a full day. I have tried this option for fresh pork belly and abalone and both arrived the next day fresh and ready for consumption.Parking around the area is a bit difficult and waiting for an available spot does get frustrating. Parking garage fees around less than $3 for a few hours.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Hamdeok can be reached from airport by bus or taxi in 30 minutes. There are many hotels, convenient stores and restaurants in that area so We can get accommodation easily.We were staying at Ramada Hamdeok, about 1 km walking distance from the beach. Strolling at sunset time was very enjoyable. Nice weather, nice view, not too crowded. Just fine.We were hanging out until dinner time, took barbecued seafoods at outdoor table by the beach. To order the food and communicate need extra effort because we can only speak english, but the Resto staff can speak mandarin well. The food was good, drinking some soju and babunja make us warm...

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Great place to gawk at all the live seafood that Jeju has to offer. All manner of sea creatures, alive and dead, to be savoured & haggled over if you so wish to partake of feasting on them. Besides seafood, there are also veggies, Jeju souvenirs (mainly foodstuffs), a couple of seafood restaurants (which charged seating fees per person so we skipped going in) and some cooked food stalls. Great to stop by to check out the local market scene.

Great photo spot, many people use this beach for camping. Hard to find eating place or restaurant. The public transport also quite hard here! We wait so long for bus and finally we use taxi for way back hotel

Good show for young and old. No need any knowledge of Korean. Theater is located in the middle of nowhere so make sure you have your meals before going. There is a convenient shop (GS25) in the hotel nearby but limited food selection. There is also a restaurant within the hotel but only opens at 7pm (our show was 8pm) when we were there. Be punctual, the show starts on time.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

From the prices I?ve seen for pork dishes in other parts of Jeju and in the rest of South Korea, I fear that some of the restaurants in this strip are somewhat overpriced (even for black pork). The restaurant we ate at required us also to order two portions of the meat (of the same type). My impression is that this is a bit of a tourist trap. This street is very close to the beachfront promenade in Jejushi and some restaurants seemed to accept guests even after 10 p.m. There is also not a huge number of restaurants lining this street. More often than not, you will have to grill / prepare your own meat over the grill at your table with minimal help from the waiters. So if you do not know how to prepare and eat samgyeopsal, it would be a good idea to read up about it a bit before eating at one of these restaurants (or any samgyeopsal restaurant for that matter).

From Jeju City Local Bus Terminal, take bus #701, stop at Seongsan Port. It takes 90mins, 3300won.Fill up the boarding form for the ferry, before you proceed to buy the ferry ticket at the counter. Round trip charges 5500won, which takes 10mins per trip. Expect a lot of visitors during weekends or public holidays.At Udo, there are shops offer rental of bicycles, ATV, automatic scooter, etc. which can accommodate every one either youths, elders or children.You could enjoy cycling around the island the best during a windy chilling day.When I think of Udo, I will remember the kindness of restaurant owner of щ 대Ъ珥. When I was eating, I accidentally hit my dental braces with the spoon, and I was rubbing to ensure it was alright. The ajumma approached me and asked me what happened, I showed her my braces, and she was quick-witted to get scissor to cut banchan into smaller pieces, while cutting, she repeatedly saying   ottoke ottoke  .. I was really grateful to her, and I enjoyed the lunch well.

First thing we've noticed is how civilized this beach is - loads of restaurants, shops , cafes nearby. We were lucky enough to visit it in September, when holiday season is over for majority of Korean guys - so, it was not that crowded. Water was very clean and the only downside, that it was already a little bit cold. If you walk few hundred meters in a right hand direction from the main beach (towards the hill), you would see a camping ground with even smaller strip of sand - and we were absolutely alone there.

Expensive pork which is only found in jeju?Cant make out the difference between normal pork except for the price.Anyway should try once since is so famous.My family dined at Dombedon during the 1st day, compare to the another black pork restaurant in jeju (Donsadon), all of us voted for donsadon. (better taste)Anyway, the owner of Dombedon is very friendly and serve us well.both the black pork restaurant have chinese speaking staff

Every year there is a Green Barley Festival in April till Early May. So beautiful.There is a place called Gapado Seafood Jjajang & Jjampon restaurant other side of the port. This place has been on the Korean TV show for many times.They put so many different fresh hand caught seafoods and different kinds of seaweeds on the noodle. During the peak time when there is a Festival going on, a bit of waiting, however It's definitely a must try place which is the most famous restaurant in this island.

Even in peak season Sehwa Beach didn?t have nearly as many visitors as some of the more popular northeast Jeju beaches mainly because most of it is covered in volcanic rocks.  We actually weren?t even sure it was a beach at first.  We did see a handful of people in the water who had sidestepped all the volcanic rocks but most seemed happy taking photos standing on the rocks.  Cafes, restaurants, and convenience stores line the beach and all were good spots to admire the nice scenery of the beach.  For actually going in the water, the other popular beaches are more popular for that reason.

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh   ginseng of the sea   (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

Entrance ticket is 2000 won per person. The temperature inside the cave is freezing cold. Pls bring along a jacket no matter what season you are visiting. Total length of the cave is about 7.14km. They only open 1 km for public to visit. It took us about 1:20 hour thru and flow. Please visit the information office first before u going into the cave, so that u will know some information of the cave formation before u going in. Pls wear a proper shoes during your visit cos it is a lava tube with rocky road. I saw some ladies went in with their not so high, high heel. I can feel their pain. This place is about 30-45mins from Jeju City. We took a quick lunch at a restaurant at the park of manjanggul cave. Not so nice but still can eat...u can travel to seongsan ilchubong after u done with the cave. Is about 5mins drive.

Dongmun market is a must visit in Jeju. Its a market where you can get almost any local products here. In the AM, there are plenty of shops selling dry food supplies, fruits, seafood, local snacks and few small restaurants. At night, you can grab some local food here at the stalls. Prices at the stalls are quite standard, ranging from KRW1000. We tried few food here which was good.

Didn't know which restaurant to choose so just picked one which looked busy. We ordered a meal with 2 cuts of meat,   abalone  , stew, egg, and a selection of side dishes, plus a beer and makgeolli for about 60000 won which was reasonable. Staff cooked the meat for us which was helpful. A hearty and delicious meal! Must try when in Jeju!

Despite the temperature being around 17 degrees Celsius Springtime end of March, we were nearly blown away the minute we got out of our car. It was super windy & cold at the base! Had to put on extra layers, wind breakers etc. However the climb up is via long, steep stairs (my nemesis!!) so had to take off some layers halfway as I wheezed & panted my way up! View from top was just okay, wasn't as green as the photos we saw. Maybe because it was early spring. On the way down, we took a detour to the Diving Women's museum / hut / restaurant just by the rocky beach. Owing to the weather, no diving woman worth her salt, was going to do a performance in the sea. We had to contend with a couple of squirmy sea creatures in tanks, which the diving women chopped up with precision & served to us with soya sauce. The abalone, octopus & shell-fish were as fresh as you could get and tough as erasers. But we did it more for the experience than the cuisine or taste. You can pick up more tasty fare at the shops near the carpark if you're hungry.

Close to dongmun market - could ask for direction from nearby local shops. I took a look at menu of two restaurants and they are quite the same regarding price and menu options (set price for 2 is around 50k won). i must admit that although taste of black pork is more delicious, it is not exceptional if considering the price nearly double normal porks

Climbing Mt Hallasan was absolutely amazing, and I would recommend anyone going to Jeju to attempt a climb. If you?re a bit unsure, make sure to research the trails before-hand and start walking in the morning ? many trails close at 2-3pm.Bring lots of water and snacks (although in typical Korean fashion, there is a 'restaurant' at the 'top', where all the lower trails intersect. Do your research, take a car or taxi to the start of the trail (buses will drop you off much further down the mountain, and you'll have to spend time and energy walking up along a road before you can even start the trail). The views must usually be stunning, but on the day we went, it was covered in cloud/fog. Even so, I would 100% recommend it and I would definitely go again if I went back to Jeju.
Cheap and good quality food.The restaurant I went serves seafood soup and marinated raw yummy crab as side dish. Unlimited TOP up. With just 2 serving of pork about 24,000 won
