Certainly a must-visit destination in Jeju! Soak yourself in the impressive view of this UNESCO heritage site. We came on the first Monday of the month, and unfortunately the paid trail to the peak is closed. Blessing in disguise is that portion of the trail is open free to the public though it only brings us to mid-way - perfect for those who find it too challenging to climb to the top. Don?t miss the women divers show which is on the left trail, at the foot of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Showtimes are 1.30 and 3pm. It?s complimentary. And you can choose to buy and eat fresh abalone at the little restaurant. Overall a truly relaxing and uplifting experience!

caves, bonsai trees, birds, nice gardens, restaurant in traditional style, and very well maintained area, the owner really has a passion to gardening and pride for his homeland. worth to visit at anytime, in summer you can also enjoy magic sandy beaches on the other side of the park

Can't resist going there every night as it's near to my hostel. Kinda good place for dinner for solo traveller as most of the restaurant serving food for more than 2 persons. You can get local food, fusion, western, sashimi, fresh fish, pork knuckles, fresh fruits and vegetables. Price range around kw2000 to kw10,000 per dish. Now you can get hallabong orange everywhere. Sweet and seedless. Yummmm love it when it's cool. After dinner can catch the water show nearby at 8pm every night except Monday.

Can find almost everything here cosmetics (of course), vitamin, souvenir, fashion apparel, also few restaurants here. Almost can find everything here but not that fantastic. Some of the coat and sweater was expensive.This is good option to go for bad weather.

Came here to checkout the views and totally loved it. A nice small town to chill at with lots of parking if you're driving. Many restaurants, cafes and food trucks along the beach. Beautiful white sand and blue waters. Not crowded. Definitely coming back here! Didn't get enough of it.

Came here after lunch nearby , ample parking space , restaurant, cafe , beauty shops near the parking area . Need to buy tickets to enter , it was a cold & windy day . No haenyo show on that day , the view was breathtaking. Huffing & puffing all the way up the stairs .

C1 ( 2016.07.12 ) This beach was smaller than I think, but there had good view and fresh air. Many people enjoyed sea bathing, and well managed, I think. The view with beach and cliff was beautiful, and many famous restaurant and cafe was operating. Good beach in Jeju area.
C1 ( 16.07.13 ) There was good beach with many cafe and restaurant. And the lighthouse of horse shape was located. There was one of good beach in Jeju island, I think.
Breathtaking view. Very breezy at the summit. It takes a bit of exercise, but not too difficult to climb. Well surrounded by cafe, restaurants and shops. Toilets are quite clean.

Blue color of beach water. Very good.  We visited there late July. The color of beach was amazing. We enjoyed swimming. Also the sunray was very strong to enjoy sun tenning. We are food a little far from here, because restaurants near beach was expensive. Also there are good places to nearby beach ; Hyeopjae cave, botanical garden, tracking beach, etc.
best view to see sunrise but so crowed. if you want to take some photo without many pp around, you should come early then start to climb on. many nice small food talls and restaurant near by.

Because Jeju is a volcanic island, it doesn?t have too many beaches relative to its 300 km of coastline.  Hamdeok Beach is one of the closest beaches to Jeju City.  It?s also one of the most picturesque in Jeju making it quite crowded when it?s warm enough to go into the water.  Unfortunately when we went there were a lot of seaweed washed up on the sand.  Despite the crowd, the parking lot was quite large and there is a good selection of cafes and restaurants nearby making it a decent visit even if you don?t go into the water.

Be sure to wear good shoes for the somewhat uneven - but not particularly slippery - walk and a raincoat for the dripping water.    There is only 1km of the lava tube which is open to tourists, so the entire walk is 2km roundtrip.   There are a number of informational plaques along the way as well as before you even enter.    There are restrooms and a restaurant by the parking lot.

Be prepared to walk and climb and climb and climb up steps.Not diffcult but quite a way up.Good walking shoes, warm clothing and water (maybe some small snacks too) needed.There r also an different area where u can check out the Jeju women divers.Also check out the local restaurants around this attractions...They serve very good seafood food / BBQ meat.I had  some very good abalone porridge and seafood soup along some BBQ meat.

Be prepared to climb a long flight of steps to reach the top. Once you are at the top, the view is breathtaking. I love the view and the climbing is worth all the effort. There are a lot of restaurants and shops below and you can catch live performance of women divers are the bottom at certain time.

Based on a Malaysian blogger's review, we went over to one of the shops there to savour this renown dish.It was a BAD experience, the black pork sold there tough like wild boar and did not have any distinct tastes.Later on when we met some locals, they advise that locals don't eat there, only tourist who are attracted by the hype of the place.Fortunately, there are many other shops around Jeju City which served better Black Pork., In fact, we had a very good one at Halla Pork Restaurant in nearby Sehwa-ri.

At KRW2000 this was well worth the money.  Don't forget to wear a jacket or a warm Cardy though, I forgot and found it very cold.  Lots of people do this it's very popular.  We tried the restaurant there which was good enough.

At Hallim park, there are a few lava caves that are interesting, and very cool (temperature).  The flower gardens are very nice.  The bonsai garden has trees that date to 300 years ago.  They are constantly trimmed to keep them small.  There is a restaurant at the entrance, and a rest area with a gift shop in the center of the park.

As we couldn't enjoy so much autumn scenery in Seoul, Mt Hallasan in Jeju is the best spot to get revenge..haha..it is due to most of leaves are already changed their colour compared to in Seoul. The parking fee is KRW 1000 and we just enjoy the beautiful scenery from the start point of jungle trekking area as we are tired enough to climb the mountain :PThere is free wifi available and some restaurant in case that you need to fill your empty tummy.. :)

As the name implies, this street is a street of restaurants & dining. There are so many   nice   appetizing looking? restaurants as we explored the place.A very helpful   road map   at the main road entrance shows the restaurants names & types of food & exactly its location within the street.This street is nearby Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. Seogwipo main town is quite small, so most of these   attractions   are quite close by.

As the name implies, this is a street of restaurants offering black pork that is cooked in front of you. Basically, same offerings per restaurant with a lot of free side dishes (fish cake is a staple). Pork ranges fro thinly sliced to a little bit thicker. Flavorful, smoky but surprisingly, when you get out of the restaurant, the smell of cooking does not stick with you (unlike our experience back home). Way so much better than what we have in our home country as this is authenticity in the real sense of the word. We only tried 2 restaurants since we were only there for 2 nights, Dombedon and Donhyanggi. Both were ok. But I like Donhyanggi better.

As soon as arrived at the airport, went there for the dinner. Well, there are many snacks, lots of street food but made in a restaurants. Lots of fresh local fruits, really fresh fish, raw fish sashimi, etc. Compare to Seoul, all fish are much more fresh and reasonable price. I ate some crab skewer, but after 10 steps from there found new ce local pork soup restaurant. So better to have a look first then decide which Korean light snack would be good for you. I am certain all kids will love this place to have some street food here!

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

Another UNESCO World Heritage. It have a nice view from the top but you need to climb up the stairs. Perhaps is a good exercise.  :)  You may bring along the bottled water as it takes around 30 mins to the top. There have restaurants, coffee shops, food stalls, souvenir stalls at the bottom and free car park as well.

Another great beach but this time with more cafes and restaurants right outside.  There's also a supermarket right to the left of the entrance.  There's a nice boardwalk to stroll, and kayaks to rent.

amazing landscape. A nice spot to take beautiful pictures of tranquil waters with pitch black rocks and white sand. Walk right from the main entrance till the end, you will fine some nice restaurants and cheaper places to stay. From there you can climb the hill and get the whole picture of Hamdeok area.

Although there are many small vendors and shops during the day, the best part is at night when the food stalls appear. There are many (mostly Korean) options. From burgers, to tempura and ice cream burritos, you will not go hungry! On average, the food costs around 7,000 krw per meal. Smaller items like gimbap and individual tempura is cheaper. I would not recommend this market for any type of clothing shopping. The interior is mainly dried fish, nuts, juices, souvenirs, some bbq, and a couple sit down restaurants.

Allow for at least 2.5 to 3 hours to walk around. There are a number if different areas, my favourite being the bonsai trees. The park is very well kept and very tranquil. There are a couple of places that sell snacks and one restaurant on site.

after visiting the jeju folk village, this was quite smaller, still was easier to visit, shorter distance to drive, so if you stay is short in Jeju, come this village, ou will find all about the korean past culture, just missing big stores and restaurant like the main village have.

After the unpleasant beach at Udo, arriving at Hamdeok beach was a delight. With just a short trip from Jeju city this little beach village is amazing. With many restaurants and cafes along the water, one could spend a nice long day here. The water is nice and clean with showers and changing rooms available nearby.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

According to the locals, it is mostly cloudy during winter and there's no point going there for sunrise view. However we did paid a visit. As the sunrise time predicted to be at 743, we started ascending the hill at 645am. Reached the peak at 7am and there were a lot visitors waiting. However, as advised, it was very cloudy and everyone was totally disappointed . The eateries around the area closed early by 830pm, left a few local expensive local hot pot and BBQ restaurants..

Absolutely hike Oedolgae, it's a beautiful coastal walk that is part of an Olle trail. You wind all around a part of the southern coast of Jeju, and can walk as long as you please. Lots of shops and restaurants along the way. The Jeju trails are my favorite attraction on Jeju, definitely walk one! And they're free!

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A hike to the top is quite challenging especially for the elderly and family with young children as there are heaps of steps. Make sure to bring something to hydrate you as there were no drinking fountains available on your way to the top. Enjoy the views of the sea and cityscape once you're at the top. Also, there are a number of restaurants, coffee shops and food stalls at the bottom of the peak.

A great place to enjoy beautiful scenery, fresh air, the sun and the beaches. The island tour bus service is very convenient (only need to pay once) and runs on round trips whole day long, bringing you to 4 different scenic spots if you do not want to rent the bicycles, ATV or scooters. There is also a nice restaurant named Rodem Garden which offers spicy squids on hot plate and can add on with hallabong fried rice after you almost finish the squids.

A good place to go shopping and grab something to eat. You can find from cheap street food to fine dining Jeju traditional restaurant! Also, if you are a fruit lover like me, you can find all kinds of fruits in a reasonable price!
A fun beach, with lots of shallows for swimming and playing in the water.  The park is well kept, there are great coffee shops and restaurants. A very nice sandy beach which is hard to find in Jeju.

A few restaurants piled along the street selling the famous Jeju black pork bbq. Went there twice with 2 different groups. Tried to 2 eateries, menus are identical and so are their prices. The corner restaurant was a better choice (the one opposite the Michelin guided restaurant) It was more airy and the pork quality was better and tastier.

You can take photos in tea plantation visit small museum or taste not cha - great tea on spot the best is hot milk tea with tangerine and great tea yogurt ice cream but I think this ice cream was unfortunately taken out from menu now there's only green tea ice cream good as well
With all the different plants and flowers all over the park there are plenty of photo-ops opportunity.Other than that not much else.
With 20-30 Wind Power Plants on both sides of the road. It is supposed to be an enclosed private areas  but it is not fenced. Can only go with a car or rented cab.

When we arrived there it was already flooded by numbers of tourists so we had a hard time to find a seat and taste the tea sample. Maybe to avoid the bad traffic and buses of tourists you should go early in the morning before the tour buses arrived.Very futuristic design building with the tea plantation across the road perfect for photo session. Don't forget to shop O'sulloc products particularly the green tea.

Went to the museum and there was good information of the history of tea making and drinking. There is a cafe next to it where you can try tea ice cream and cakes. I enjoyed them all. Go out to the tea plantations - it is a vast area to take in the scenery and fresh air.

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.

Well if an already successful huge company invest in something new it can't go too wrong. I expected this place to be more authentic but what we got was a commercialized sugar-coated tea plantation experience. Nonetheless the place is very professional of course the quality is great and both the tea and desserts are yummy. The surroundings are beautiful the air is fresh and the scent of the plantation is amazing. It's a safe choice if you prefer a guaranteed good time over something unexpected and little bit more unique. It's a sophisticated modern place that reminds me more of a spa than a tea house. Regardless you can buy good quality tea here and some other gifts that comes in beautiful packages. All in all we had a good time!

We went here on a rainy day as we really wanted to see how the famous O'Sulloc tea was made. The museum is nothing more than a room (unfortunately not all texts are translated info english) and the majority of the space is taken up by the shop and the cafe which seems like the main focus of this location.Two things were nice getting a look of the tea plantations and having a quick tea tasting.I would recommend this only if you are a true O'Sulloc fan or if you have spare time not visiting all the other sights at Jeju island.

We visited and there were about 20 buses in the parking lot. The shop where you get the tea or ice cream was very full so we went out to the tea bushes and enjoyed our tea there. We did learn about how tea is made and seeing the actual plant was interesting to me. Wish it was less crowded.

We tried one of the best green tea latte and green tea ice cream here. Also learnt about tea planting and tea making in a short tour of the place. You can get to take some really nice photos of the tea plantation too.

We took one walk here. Vertical rise of about 200m through nature. A couple of hours of hiking & stopping to view the plants & birds. Great view of the crater from the top. Worth the trek. Carry lots of water if it hot!

We took a short walk from the nearby peace park to visit this place in October 2016. Entrance fees were nominal but visitors were few.  Looks like not a very popular tourist spot. Just as well  we could enjoy a short walk here without the crowds. Quite a nice place to walk around although there were not so many deer. You could buy some plant food to feed the deer. The main enclosure for the deer is not that big but the park itself has other longer walking paths.  If you do not wish to walk here from the peace park you can take the Jeju City tour bus but need to wait.

We took a short stroll in the tea plantation.  Somehow it did not evoke the same feelings of peaceful serenity I had expected.  Perhaps there were just too many people around hence the experience was vastly different from my previous Alishan (Taiwan) tea plantation visit.We tried the tangerine flavoured tea in the museum.  My husband loved the taste but it?셲 not for me.  Kids love the green tea ice cream.  Thumbs up.We found it hard to find a table with seats although we visited on a Monday.  It was that crowded!

We self-drive to this museum. Like everyone else we ate the green tea cake ice cream and hot green tea latte for lunch it was delicious especially for green tea lovers. It was crowded with bus loads of tourists but the cafe staff was very efficient and served quickly. Bought Jeju tangerine tea after trying the sample. We also went to the innisfree shop to buy cosmetics. And took photos of the garden that has beautiful cherry blossoms at this time. Great soothing weather and we also walked across the road to the tea plantation. Enjoyed ourselves.

We had heard about the tea plantation first on the television show Kimchi Chronicles on PBS (http://www.kimchichronicles.tv/). As an avid tea drinker I could hardly pass up the chance to check it out in person and it is amazing. We drank tea walked in the tea fields checked out the tea museum watched the roasting of tea bought tea tea soap tea lotion and tea ice cream. The museum and center are quite stunning and the drive out there interesting on some very well maintained roads. Don't miss this one if you are on Jeju Island.

We didn?셳 spend much time here which was a pity but in any case there were too many tourists. Would be a better experience when less crowded. The buildings are stylish and there is a nice view of the tea gardens. You can try the tea and they explain the tea making process. The cafe looked good with desserts like green tea cake and ice cream but we didn?셳 try as the queue was too long. Nearby was the Innisfree building where many people were making handmade soap. There was also a cafe and exhibits of the different distilled essences of flowers and plants in Jeju.

We did not spend much time at the tea plantation as it was very sunny. We were spending time in the cafe and ordered green tea ice-cream and green tea swiss roll cake. Both are delicious especially the ice-cream! Rich in flavor and not bitter at all. Swiss roll cake is fluffy enough and not overly sweet. Must try!

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.

We came by using GPS to guide us to the National Park. We entered the part called the Healing Forest. Interesting plants on healing the body. Several small huts/cabins are available for those who may like to stay in the forest for healing and relaxation. Do go into the forest for a real feel of the national park. Entrance is free.

We arrived during a typhoon so it was dumping rain and the place was crowded! Even so it was definitely worth stopping by and having some green tea treats. The line was definitely worth the wait. Due to the typhoon I was unable to see the plantation but would love to come back!

We are glad that we have our wonderful tour guide was with us thus we were able to gain better understanding n knowledge about the green tea n it's plantation.The museum itself actually showcase the different type of green tea products (including facial products) so it's a shopping paradise for some.  There are free sampling of the green tea however we like the cafe most. Though a little pricey but the green tea yogurt ice cream n also the green tea milk ice cream is yummy (it has strong green tea taste).As it was crowded when we were there the cafe seemed to be under stocked for the crowd.  A friend managed to get herself green tea macaron n said it taste superb.A good stop over for some retail therapy n tea break n photo taking.

We are big tea drinkers so we have to make a stop in this place.  The tea plantation is nothing to shout about.  The Boh Tea Plantation in Camerons Highlands in Malaysia is more impressive.  But we had to try and famous green tea ice cream and cream roll and they do not disappoint.  It was great...especially the ice cream.  Yum!
Was expecting to see more on Tea is produced but saw a big place for buying Tea Leaves and related products.  It was nice to be able to see the Tea plants outside in the field .

Was excited to see the tea museum but disappointed as it was only a 5 minute tour. We drove for about 1.5 hours to visit this museum from the other end of Jeju City.  The treats at the museum shop was a nice respite against the summer heat though. There is also the tea plantations just across the museum and Innisfree (Korean Skincare) beauty shop about 2 minutes walk away. I would recommend to go for the Stoner Tea museum tour to make this trip more worthwhile. However there are certain timings for it and we didnt manage to join.

Visited this place with a group of friends. The tea plantation wasn?셳 fantastic; don?셳 expect vast rolling hills of uninterrupted shrubbery. The museum was really small and led to a shop and restaurant which was much bigger than the museum itself. The place was milling with many tourists and it was uncomfortable to browse their merchandise or eat in peace. We tried the matcha ice cream and cake and there was nothing too special about it. I don?셳 think this place is worth a visit.

Visited on a friend's recommendation and it definitely didn't disappoint.  Upon entry to the building we walked through the historical display area before getting to the shop and cafe.  There were many different types of tea for sale and all beautifully packaged.  Again thanks to the friend who asked us to help buy stuff for her we knew to get the green tea milk spread.  For the tea they had samples for you to smell before purchasing.  We got the wedding tea green tea and green tea cold sticks. Can't wait to get home to try them.  Next we had the green tea roll green tea ice cream and green tea milk shake at the cafe.  All were exquisite.  On the outdoors there are great photo opportunities near the tea plantation.  As we walked there we discovered another building called Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a health food restaurant cum shop selling body oils and moisturiser.  We had lunch there and bought some beautiful smelling body lotion.  Again all fantastic.  The whole family enjoyed O'Sulloc!

Very well manicured plantations and garden areas. Museum is professional and store was well laid out with all their delicious teas with samples in bottles for customers to smell.Limited parking space though. Could see people parking by the sides of roads all over the vicinity.Cashier staff was very helpful combining our global tax refund receipts when we made two purchases separately.Ice cream was good. Cream roll would prefer it like a Swiss roll where cream is well spread around the roll. Current style has too much dry cake at the sides.Beautiful packaging as always.

Very interesting garden of native plants but you don't get much time to see before they herd you into a room to hard sell you into buying Ginseng. Their pitch is that they invented a new method to grow and harvest JeJu ginseng in the lab and is suppose to the best. Buy ginseng here is very expensive. I don't even think JeJu is know for ginseng.

Very crowded with tourists all enjoying the green tea rolls tea and crepe cakes.They sell many green tea products within the cafe.  Innisfree is just next door.  Quite a number of products are sold out too.Tea plantation is just outside the cafe but it is not very big.

Unique geographical nature reserve called Gotjawal is Jeju local language stands for forest(怨?Got) and thorn bushs on rock(?먯솃;jawal). The area is kept 10-15 degrees celsius throughout the year making Summer cool and Winter warm where tropical Northern hemisphere plants and frigid Southern hemisphere plants can coexist.There are four main Gotjawal terrain in Jeju Island this is the one in the South-West area. They also have a guided tour around this Gotjawal forest which you can explore the area with it's own story. The thing is they only have Korean tour so far so you might want to speak Korean or request them to open up an English tour.

Though it is not in the city area but it is easily accessible by public transport. I got there by bus and walk less than 5 mins.Not only it has a variety of tea but also has its own tea plantation and a cafe. If you are into tea you can buy the tea bags or tea leaves home as souvenirs or own consumption. I took a tea break in the cafe. Not having the tea though a lot of other customers are having either hot or cold green tea. I had a piece of green tea roll cake and a green tea ice cream. Marvellous. If you have more time have a meal there as well.

This tea museum is very interesting.  It is a very knowledgeable museum that shows the tea making process right from the planting harvesting tea leaves and processing it into dried tea leaves. It also has a cafe attached where they serve green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll cake and green tea slurpee.

This so-called museum is really a sales outlet for O'Sulloc teas.  The grounds above the tea plantation is just beautiful to walk around.  The Innis Free Jeju House on the grounds is another sales outlet for Innis Free skin care products.  They offered a hands -on activity to make your own soap.  Lunch here was great.  They pride themselves in locally sources produce. I had the rice balls and soup.  We shared the mungwork steamed buns with red beans - not much to look at but very tasty. The shaved ices are a treat not to be missed

This property is actually a garden which seems to be abandoned years ago. We knew of this attraction through the Lonely Planet guide book.Plants were over-growing and the pond murky. We spent 5 minutes browsing around and left after using the toilet.I apologise for the lack of photos as there was really nothing much worth taking pictures of or to see.

This place were providing some information about teas making and how korean history about tea production and cultures. They also provide a cafe that served tea of course and some tempting Deli. If you visit the place on winter it actually perfect to spent time to get warm up and stuff your stomach. On Summer or Spring would be great for afternoon tea or take away for your picnic basket. And once more as this place is all about teas there is cosmetic and some supplies product made from tea essence. You could also find some fun activities at the creation counter at the third building near the tea plantation. Come and have look!!

This place was crowded when we arrived and had to wait a while before we could get seats in the cafe. The museum part was small and did not provide much information. The tea plantations are also open to visitors but the grounds were muddy due to the rain hence we didn't enter them. The variety and price of products are similar to those in their seoul busan branches hence I wouldn't recommend a special visit to this place if you have been to them before.

This place so crowded. Better come early so you can try the popular green tea ice cream and any other dessert and drink. Last time I arrived around 5 pm and all the cake are sold out. Enjoy the view outside and you can take picture with the tea plantations :)

This place is nice. The museum tells you all you want to know about tea. Scent samples of tea are all over. There is a snack nook where you can try their signature desserts and beverages. I ordered the hallabong Ofredo and green tea latte cold and it was sooo good! There is a green tree plantation where you can take pictures but a warning says ?쒫eware of snakes.??So be on the safe side and that is to stay put on the edge of the plantation.:)

This place caught me by surprise. I didn?셳 really think of visiting this site but it was a wonderful surprise. Different flowers and plants bloom year round to give you all those perfect pictures and ?쏫odac??moments. Well Instagram for most of you now. This place is known as the Forest of Love and Healing. You need about 1.5 hours to see everything. Plan for 2 hours if you like to stop and enjoy a coffee/tea at the many rest stops. Don?셳 forget your camera phone tripod etc to get those awesome pictures.

This park is huge! it is divided into different areas with different themes. It has a great variety of plants and birds. There are also two underground tunnel caves which enrich the overall visiting experience. There is also an area with seasonal flowers.  Great spot for photo-taking. Highly recommended for family with children. Allocate at least two hours visiting time here.

This museum features the history of tea in Jeju as well as you can view the tea plantation from the observation deck. You also can taste the green tea ice cream and cake at the cafe besides a good place to buy green tea. This area also features innisfree shop where you can make your own soap besides a lot of innisfree products on sale.

this is not a museum. This is a place surrounded by green tea plantations. It is also a place for you to get your tea fix. They have a plenty of teas to choose from and some are packaged so Nicely as gifts. I personally go back there for my green tea facial masks and powders. Its my third time there already. But be prepared the place is on most tourist groups itinerary so it can get a tad crowded. But for me its usually pick buy and lets go. So im totally fine w it. Stop by if youre a tea fan to pick up items to bring back.

This is more of a shop and cafe than a museum. The museum part is just a few display cabinets that leads to a cafe with goods displayed for sale. The tea plantation across the street is a flat moderately sized area that pales in comparison to the vast rolling and picturesque tea plantation of cameron highlands.This attraction is not worth the time unless one is a tea-lover.

This is first time we experienced a visit to a Green Tea plantation. Walking between the rows & rows of beautifully layed out fragrant tea leaves was just great.The cafe sells nice Green Tea ice creams & cakes plus tea leaves products obviously.An Innisfree shop sells the famous Korean cosmetics plus a small cafe included.Certainly this is an attraction that should not be missed when in Jeju.

This is a very popular tourist destination there are a wide variety of teas for purchase and well as a little cafe to stop and chat over the famous green tea ice cream. Innesfree has a little shop in location where you can make your own soap. The only problem is to wash your hands afterwards you need to go to the bathrooms (outside) so I?셝 recommend taking some hand wipes unless you want soap everywhere. The property has a perfect spot to take photos with the tea plants and take a small stroll. This place can get very busy do either early morning or a little later in the afternoon are better times

This is a manmade park-like garden with a variety of plants and trees and water features. It is well worth the time it takes to walk through the grounds  just for the experience of viewing the bucolic setting. The main feature is Michon Cave which really didn't dazzle us as much as it apparently was supposed to. It's just a cave in which one walks down a slope to see some tacky lights and statues. The park  on the other hand  is scenic and pleasant. There are some concessions where they sell the usual tourist stuff.

This is a beautiful place to learn about the gardens and native korean plants.? There are many different types of gardens here and they are all well maintained and interesting.? You could stay here for a long time just learning or you could breeze through casually enjoying the scenery.? There is a tower you can go to the top of for lovely views of the area.? Bring a water bottle.

This destination was strongly recommended by our host and we loved it almost as soon as we were there. Despite the drizzle air was fresh and light. There is a variety of tea for sale and we enjoyed a good meal at the innisfree caf챕 which faces the vast tea plantation.
There's really nothing much to see for a museum but the cafe is good for a tea break and the green tea plantation is a nice backdrop for photo taking if the weather is good

There really isn't much flora and fauna (this was in March) to speak of. Even indoor plants don't seem to flourish. The only nice thing about this place is there is a big park in which you can lie down on and enjoy the sun!
There is nothing much to see at all. Bare trees and plants. And super cold in March. The only fun to do is the train ride that?s about all.

There is nothing much here at the museum but the green tea ice cream and the green tea cake roll are fabulous! The green tea cake roll sold out in a very short period of time! We reached there at around noon time and we were so lucky that we took the second last roll! I guess the cake roll is pretty popular among the locals too as we saw a lot of locals stopping by at the cafe. I saw an O'Sulloc Cafe at Myeongdong too. We went in the morning and there were still quite a few of green tea cake rolls there. I wanted to get a cake roll the night before I flew back to Singapore (in order to maintain the freshness) but the staff told us that it has been sold out! The green tea cake roll tastes really good when it's eaten fresh. People who don't like the cream in the middle might not like the cake. Other than food you can go all the way to the third floor to take some photos. Personally I feel that the scenery outside of the building is much more nicer. There's a big park right in front of the tea museum there are people who lie down and chill on the grass. There's tea plantation located opposite of the tea museum. We are allowed to wander around there for more pretty photos.

There is a cafe and merchandise shop in the tea museum which seems like it is the main attraction of the museum. So go early to beat the tour groups. If you are not a sweet tooth skip the green tea latte. Go for the soft serve ice cream. Do not miss the plantations. Plenty of photo opportunities if you venture into the green tea plantations

The roll cakes were AMAZING and i love that there is a large tea plantation nearby to see how they plant and harvest the leaves. But be warned there are a lot of people so be quick or early if you wanna visit this place

The place was drizzling when we got there and managed to squeeze in one last parking lot beside the tea museum. eent straight to the tea museum and the place was really crowded. it showcase the tools used in tea productions and Got a few tastings of various type of tea and souvenirs. Went for the famous ice cream dessert and drink - good. Next walk over to Innisfree building where they have an open area for children to  play with the playdough and display of cosmetics product as well as a cafe with seating area. Outside tourist were busy taking pictures of tea plantations and themselves !

The place is v nice and a walk in the green tea plantation is so comfy.. Cafe is small so buy take out and enjoy them in the garden as there are tables to sit ard and admire the view. Go up the top to enjoy the breeze and view..

the place is fun for walking between different kind of plants and animals. there are 3 caves and the weather inside it is cold during the summer time so you can walk there if you feel hot. there is also folk village and a water park

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

The place is busy with tourists but worth the visit. You can walk in the tea plantation & have photos taken.Do enjoy the tea time with their local different tea and cakes etc. must have is to buy the green tea milk spread to apply on biscuit or bread. Not so sweet but just a nice taste to taste bud.Buy the tea leaves rather than the instant type to enjoy real tea
the park is large with wide variety of plant species but we did not find anything special that is worth the visit. The park was clean but needs more work to make it attractive to visitors.

The O쨈Sulloc Tea Museum and tea field is a treat!  It쨈s easy to get to by the airport bus we got to it by taking the Yeha West Tour.Be prepared for crowds in the cafe.  However if you go across the road to the tea fields it쨈s easy to walk along the tea plants and be alone in a field of green tea.The museum is interesting and explains the tea picking and fermentation process.The real fun is the cafe and shopping for tea!  It쨈s a bit overwhelming but fascinating to think that so many types of tea can be produced with one leaf!O쨈Sulloc also sells a cosmetic line I haven쨈t tried any of those products so I can쨈t comment on their cosmetics versus all the other great stuff that Korea has for skin care. The cafe offers the most delicious green tea ice cream.  I쨈m dying to try the cakes but can쨈t get pass the ice cream.  There is also a brown roasted tea ice cream but I prefer the green tea one.  It isn쨈t sweet and has a distinctive green tea flavor left on your palate as you get ready for the next bite.Recommendation--I got the Cold Green Sticks which are perfect for a bottle of water.  The other teas you definitely need a strainer otherwise get the tea in teabags.Oh and O짢Sulloc has a cafe in the Nampo area in Busan if you need your green tea ice cream fix. Other cafes have green tea ice cream but OSulloc is yummy and my favorite.O쨈Sulloc seems to be branding itself as a high end tea so you just can쨈t purchase it in a grocery store nor do the hotels have it as complimentary tea a shame since it is a Korean brand. So stock up and enjoy.
The outdoor gardens lack maintenance and looks nice from a far but is very bad when up close. The plants are balding and the fountains are empty.

The Osulloc Tea Museum is located around 30 mins from Seogwipo and 35 mins from Jeju city.This pleasant venue is comprised of the Tea Museum a shop a coffee place a cosmetics shop and the tea fields.We didn't visit the museum as we are familiar with the processes. Instead we visited the coffee shop where we had a Sejak green tea an ice cream and a slice of roll cake. Everything was good!We also bought some tea cosmetics and hung around the tea plantation.
The museum has nothing much in it it is more like a cafe with overcrowding issue. The tea plantation is of decent size and good view for photo spot.

The museum doesn't offer so much there is a miniature showing about making tea leaves process starting from the plantation to end product. But I did enjoy the scenery so much a wide green tea plantation you can purchase a cup of green tea ice cream which tastes really good (you will buy the second cup as soon as you finish! enjoy the scenery and feel the wind cool breeze in Spring.

The museum can be improved with more English explanation. Go to the open air top for the best 360 view of the area and plantation. There are signs at the plantation warning of snakes but none spotted during our visit. There is a crowd at the cafe and shop but the turnover is quick as most of them followed a group tour and hence can't linger that long. You can get a seat if you are not in a rush. The stuff are expensive but it won't deter a green tea fan. Do be extra careful when crossing the roads to the opposite car parks. The cars and trucks are speed demons.

The museum becomes busier as the day goes on really busy late in the day so going early is the best plan to be stress free and see everything with little to no people there for best photo experiences.The museum is really cool and covers Korean tea history. It leads to the tea shop where you can sample some good tea cakes and teas. You can also purchase teas here as well as other tea confections.Next to the museum short 5 minute walk is the Innisfree Jeju House which I cover in another review. You can get lunch and some fresh teas to enjoy here. There is also great tea and Jeju House related products as well as fun tea soap making kits. Ones you can do there and others that you can take home.Before lunch at Innishouse but after tea and snack at the Tea Museum you should walk the plantation. Great photos in the fields next to the tea museum but across the street are two areas one with a big tree that is old an beautiful but also a tree with deep red blossom that makes for a great photo with Hallasan in the background.The Stone House was closed for renovations when we visited in April 2018.

The green tea plantation of O'sulloc was my last stop prior to my flight for Seoul. My recommendation is to try the O'Sulloc green tea ice cream. There were also other green tea based products displayed like soap and beauty products. As for me I enjoyed my green tea ice cream under the flowering Cherry Blossom tree.

The folk houses built well imitating earlier century jeju do livings. You can experience the way of living of older jeju do resident. Kinda way of knowing and understanding of Jeju resident. The living plant and animal were well maintain.
The crater is now full of trees and plants therefore looks like another mountain but I give it a rating of 5 for the fantastic views and park. Nice place to take a relaxing walk.

The best part of the tea musuem is the cafe which serve green tea latte ice cream cakes. i never get to try the green tea cheese tiramisu cake at the cafe so i headed to one of the O'sulloc in Myeongdong. It is really good. However the museum is just average. There are only cups and tea pots displayed. I think the BOH tea plantation museum in Malaysa is much better. Just my 2 cents.

Tea Plantations are not my favourite places and this is not a museum as such. But the way the Koreans have done this makes it into a relaxing afternoon experience. The cherry blossoms just came out when we visited. There were scores of Korean students on a field trip but that's OK. It's spacious enough for everyone. A short display of tea cups from around the world lines the entrance of the building. Then it's tea shopping and testing. Try the buckwheat tea! Lots of chinese speaking staff (as with everywhere else in Seoul). Here I tasted the best green tea ice cream and cake. A walk in the surrounding garden and compound is nice. There is a glass building next to the main one by Korean brand Innisfree. In it there are soap making activities a cafe and skin care shopping.

Tea plantation near the city center with a tea museum containing a few old tes pots (you will probably have wider assortment in a flea market). I will probably enjoy visiting an actual farm with fruit trees and greenhouses planted to vegetables than spending time at the tea plantation. There is no entrance fee but there is also no tour guide or someone or something to explain what there is to see.

spent 2-3 hours to walk through despite it was a hot sunny day.  The park is well designed and large and showcases a number of house and building of old Jeju.  However I would like to have more and completed information (in English).  For me a foreign visitor I have no interest in those scene for TV film making.  Again the park grows different plants which impress me.

So this is more a shop than a museum to me. But the cafe there is highly recommended!! You need to try the green tea cakes and the cookies as well! Wish i could've tried the ice cream but i was afraid i get sick. It's literally the best roll cake. The garden was nice and you can make your own shop at innisfree didnt have enough time though.. Remember to take pictures at the cup made of plants across the street..

Small tea plantation in front of cafe and Innisfree shop. Must try the latte tea and the cake. Innisfree shop is nothing extra-ordinary. Worth a short visit. You can also enjoy the tea and cake back in town at Myeondong.

Small museum which showcases lots of green tea cups from around the world. As it was raining at the time of visit I spent more time indoors and at the cafe. As this is a tourist hotspot the cafe is always full and finding a table is quite a challenge (I was lucky though). I recommend ordering the green tea ice cream and the cold drip tea which is only sold at the Jeju outlet.Will probably visit again next time to see the green tea plantations which I missed out on.This museum is a stone's throw away from Innisfree Jeju House - barely 90 seconds walk which is worth a visit as well.

Shows good selection of plants from various regions. Good organization of displays. Conveniently located near Hotel. Provided relaxed pace in touring the place. But limited information provided on plants.

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

Rows of organic tea plantations for cha lovers to scent savour and calm the senses.  A must-go on tourist itinerary so be prepared for crowds.  Long queues at the cafe for tea desserts.  Check out exquisite Samdayeon (?쇰떎??is a Korean post-fermented tea matured for a hundred days in barrels made out of cedar wood from Jeju Island) soft ice cream unique to Jeju shop only. Interesting tea blends and gifts at the tea shop. Don't miss the outdoor fields across from the museum for kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures and windmills for photo taking. A walking path connects to Innisfree Jeju House for more afternoon tea Innisfree products and craft making classes for young and old.

Read that it was man- made garden !! After the visit I felt that this was one of the best Garden ever visited. The various plants and trees were really great and we spend a good 3 hrs walking round. The cave was wonderful ... even thou only 350m is open to public. Highly recommended even for adults .

Quite frankly I am not sure how to describe the tea museum and its surrounding. I had high expectations that were disappointed. The museum is fairly small and not really that informative or wow the adjacent souvenir area and caf챕 doesn't look too appealing either. There is a small tower that offers a nice view when on top. Nearby then the Innisfree Caf챕 which was already closed when we arrived and then the tea plantation where lots of people take selfies with tea bushes in the background.And that was it. I would say good for a quick stopover but not really a destination in itself 30-60 min there more than enough.

Put your vehicle on neutral and it will seemingly be rolling uphill. Very intriguing.Unable to figure out how it happened but definitely have something to do with the way the trees were planted along the road.

People generally come here for the green tea and buying tea products. It's the best green tea I've tasted in the whole of Korea. And triumphs Malaysia's also. Their cakes dessert are just so good and you have tons of tea products to choose fromThose who like to see tea plantation can also come here to take pictures otherwise just sit back relax and enjoy green tea
Overall it more of a showroom and a cafe. If you like green tea they do have some nice green tea and swiss roll but tables are limited. Next to it is the innisfree showroom and a tea plantation.

Our tour diverted to the tea museum because we were to visit dragon head rock but the tides were too high to take out the small boat.  Anyway would've been cold on the water with the very powerful windy day.  Building is in the midst of tea fields.  You are taken through an area with China from all over the world.  Most of the China on display was either from France or Germany.  Then you enter a room where you can buy souvenirs as teas makeup made with tea and then there is a counter to buy dessert and teas or tea lattes.  They are very pricey though about $6 for a hot cup of tea.  Then after leaving that room you enter a room where you can sample tea infused makeup.  This reminded me of when we toured Fragonard perfumery in France where everyone was trying on the lotions and perfumes.  There were even large vials filled with liquids which were identified by the plant or flower beside them.  Once again similar to the perfumery labs.  Then there was a counter to order same teas dessert and even cold tea drinks that were nonalcoholic versions of cocktails but with tea in them.  These looked like they might've been good.  We finally decided we were in need of a hot drink after the sea cliffs experience.  So we bought one of those overpriced tea lattes.

O'sulloc plantation and museum was one of the most memorable places in Jeju.It's really unique and cool place.Even though museum is not that big but you can see and try a lot.They also sell some products in Green tea flavor but they are bit expensive..We tried Green Tea coctail and ice cream. Both were good and we don't regret spending money on it!~Also if you go to O'sulloc don't miss the Innisfree house.For males it might be a bit boring though..But if you are female this place is deffinetely amazing!

O'sulloc is famous for its green tea plantation. It attracts plenty of tourists who frequent the place. In one building it shows all types of green tea with tea demos. Many people comes here to buy excellent tea quality for personal use. You can also eat in its tea shop with green tea latte and green tea ice cream for taste. On another building they sell tea as a cosmetics or other uses of green tea. All in all it is very informative and zen in design. Price are very reasonable.

One of the highlight of our trip as we wanted to visit tea plantation and try the green tea products. Plantation is ok and is a good spot to take pictures. Observatory facing the plantation and museum is so so only. We tried their happy green tea green tea swiss roll and green tea ice cream. Happy green tea with a citrus taste was refreshing. Swiss roll was yummy (a must try!) and my partner loved her green tea ice cream. A great place to have our afternoon teabreak!
Nothing much in the museum but you can take photo at the green tea plantation around it and buy some freshly fried tea leaves

Nothing much here if you are not a tea people or if you are not the type who takes selfies. This is a great place for instagram pictures and selfie with the tea plantation in the background. After all the selfies there is inmisfree shop and cafe but i would reccommend to drink at O'Sullic Cafe itself as the cakes and tea are very nice. Its quite sad that they close at 6pm! Didnt get to enjoy much at the cafe but we did enjoy and took lots of selfie at the tea plantation area!

Nice view of the tea plantation facing west from the main visitors building.  Need to book tea appreciation class in advance.Green tea rolls green tea ice-cream to try.  Definitely a good weather visit only.

Nice spot for photo taking as there is a tea plantation whereby tourist pose for photos...Across the plantation sits the Tea Museum whereby you can shop for tea related products and have a drink/bite in the cafe to chill.Next to the Tea Museum is the innisfree shop whereby they conduct hands-on soap making class if one is keen.
Nice place to enjoy good afternoon tea & get involved in diy activities to make soap or card. The place is very cozy & relaxing. Do visit the tea plantation.
Nice photos around the tea plantation. Cafe is nice. Had cake roll and the green tea milk (comes in great bottle!)Enjoyed the 1.5 hours there just relaxing.

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)

My family and I reached O'Sulloc in the evening and wasted an opportunity to view the plantations.  We bought many of their products and and tried their set menu.  I love the green tea flavour ice-cream! A must try for tea lovers.

Museum is fairly small but packed with tourists. Gift shop offer wide variety of gift ideas. Cafe was too packed for us to stay around for sampling snacks and drinks.Innisfree museum and green tea plantation are nearby
Many tour buses with tourists the museum is nothing interesting at least to me. There is an innisfree outlet and an organic caf챕. The Green Tea Plantation is open to the public for photography.
Lovely place to see Korean tea plantation. Unfortunately it was raining so can't stay out long. Very crowded but it was a great place just to understand more about Korean tea culture.

Location is pretty far but it is all worth it. Too bad we came late 30 mins before closing time. We didn't know they close at 6.30pm. We rushed to get the drinks and cake but managed to get drinks and Softee instead. They stopped the cakes order eventhough I saw some cakes leftover. Maybe they had to close the cafe soon at that point of time. There is also green tea plantation opposite the building.
Large tea plantations and tea Museum cave Cafe and tea-themed food.In particular unlike other tourist establishments and also with great food and friendly staff are the best.
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: just a well maintained hill track. More like a plantation than a forest though we spotted a deer. Crowded with people going in a hurry to complete a formality. No great scenes on this trail.of course we did upto Sara Oreum only. May be the other difficult trails must be having better sceneries. If you want to go to summit better start early say by 8 am since there is no permission beyond the upper shelter after 12 noon. Not good for someone with weak knees. Avoid on rainly or cloudy days.

It's one of the best small museums on Jeju island. I went there twice and each time spent couple of hours in sheer amazement and delight. Almost each sea shell installation strikes with its beauty. The bronze things are also interesting and sometimes funny. Check the bathroom  by the way :)There is much stuff in the gift shop but quite expensive. Small cafe is cozy arranged with bronze installations and green plants. Try tea and bagels  they are tasty.

Its actually a tea plantation called a museum. Museum element not impressive but nice for a short stopover for green tea cakes and ice cream. Its skincare products with rich green tea essence is refreshing and skin feels soft and refreshed. Cleasing oil and cleasing foam is impressive a must try for sensitive skin.
It's a big park with a lot of plants from around the world with some small animals and 3 lava tunnels.Too expencive to me.

It's a beautiful park for a stroll. It has different sections with a variaton in plants. Not a lot of flowers but nice plants and trees. Also lots of shade for hot days.  It is a little out of the way though so only worth a visit when you are into parks or nearby.
It?셲 a great place to take photo. The location doesn?셳 appear on the gps so just drive to the green tea plantation and it will be next to it. Please try all the green tea dessert there too.

It was raining when we visited this museum. Many tourists frequent this place too. They have lots of tea products. They have a resto with variety of tea juices and goodies. Try to visit their tea plantation at the back.

it was a hot summer day when our tour guide took us to this park. It has a very large variety of plants and bonsai. Some of the bonsai plants are more than 100 years old!! The most interesting bit in my opinion was going into the lava tubes which are like under ground caves with unusual rock formations. Wear comfortable shoes. Its not strenuous but best to be comfortable when walking.

It tells you the history of green tea and some other info on tea plantation in Jeju. Basically you enter the small room where they display some written history of tea in Jeju. You may need to read all the information and see some displays in about 10 mins before you come to their caf챕. Outside there is a small tea leave plantation where you could take some photos. There is a small lawn for children to run around. That is all about it.

It is a park consist of many statue and also plantation made from glass. Yes. Glass. Also museum where we can learn the making process. It is quite nice as this is my first time but I don't think will revisit.
Isn't really a museum. No entry fee. Green tea sundae and swiss roll was delicious!You can take picture amongst tea plants.

Is a quaint place with some very good drinks and desserts. But the crowd is overwhelming. I would skip this place altogether if I visit Jeju next. It?셲 got nice tea plantation front of the museum but I?셶e seen better ones in Taiwan. Truth is after a torturous hike up Hallasan mountain we needed to do something easy the following day so Osulloc Tea Museum was in the itinerary. Tea culture not very well exhibited and I think this is more of a shopping excursion. The staff not friendly or helpful but rather want to be done with your query. To sum it all if you want to shop you can come but otherwise this is a place you can skip.

Innisfree is a Korean cosmetics brand known for its natural ingredients sourced directly from Jeju in Korea...think of it as a Korean Body Shop. The Innisfree House in Jeju is a combined shop and cafe located inside the Osulloc Green Tea Museum complex. You can buy products and make your own soaps as well as sit and chill with some Korean and Western fusion drinks and cafe style food. Good stop for lunch or afternoon tea and to pick up souvenirs. Recommend spending only 1 hour (combined with the green tea plantation photo op)
Innisfree cafe has lovely food. There is craft work in the cafe where you can make your own soap as a gift too. The plantation was amazing.

In this museum you get to see the rows of tea plantation outside and if you head inside you get to enjoy the awesome tasting cakes and tea. Great stop over while visiting Jeju. It also has other tea made products like soap etc.

If you don't like flowers come to this place if you love flowers then you need to come to this place. There are so many fantastic flowers colors builds plants and a lot more there can not be described with words.

If you are the fan of Korean tea you should go to this place and try yourself. They offer some tester so you can before you buy. Besides tea there are some products such as green tea milk spread cosmetic skin care etc that the main ingredient is tea are also available here. Besides the indoor museum or shop you can walk around at the tea plantation outside and take a nice camera shot.

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?곕떇留?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.
If you are a tea lover I recommend coming here to enjoy the tea and snacks available here. The view of the tea plantation is interesting too but there's little information to tell you more.

I walked along the garden path together with my best  friends during our trip to korea.each plant has their own story and some piece of advice regarding life that we can learnt from tree.The garden well kept and all the staff very friendly and can speak englishWe had a great time hereWe even get free tea.KamsahammidaⅠ

I visited Hallim Park confined in a wheelchair. Some ways are not appropiate for a wheelchair. I love gardens and seen a lot. This garden had beautiful displays although some were needing care. The park takes several hours to see. It has different plants from many parts of the word. The Bonsai collection was excellent and one of the best I seen in a botanical garden. Again this particular area was needing help with the trees. They have so many bonsais and only two workers to trim them. And the specimens available were very old.The caves are unique because I do not know any other part in the world you can see a volcanical and calcareal cave together and they have one in here. I had to use crutches to see them and I am not dissapointed of the effort.The local village moved into the park is nice and realistic (we visited a folk village the day before). The animal collection was above average. For kids they have an area to feed love birds and parakeets. Excellent fun. My youngest daughter is 25 and she was a child again in here.
I loved the indoor botanical garden. The greenery was so uplifting away from the cold winter outside. There are many species of plants and the gardens are themed from desert to jungle to fruit etc.

I live just down the road from O'Sulloc and pass it on a nearly daily basis it's always busy always!.I have visited once get past standing next to a tea plant and a big tea pot and your pretty much done there is a collection of crockery and quite a nice cafe you need to like green tea though...It takes about half an hour to see and do everything.
I have no idea why this place is so popular it's just a field full of tea plants. There is a cafe that sells tea some tea flavoured ice cream and tea flavoured cake. That's about it.

I find the osulloc tea museum a bit overrated ... I actually enjoyed the innisfree cafe next door better.  The osulloc tea cafe is crowded and very noisy (I guess is more busy because).  If weather is nice is better you buy your food and eat outdoor.Innisfree has similar tea plantation next to it so I didn't even check out the osulloc ones.  The observatory deck view is also just so so...  I would still check it out but spend more time at the innisfree cafe nearby.

I cant say this was a museum because majority of the building is dedicated to the gift shop and cafe.  They do have a small plantation across the street as well as an innisfree store next to it.  Apparently their green tea ice cream is a must try.  I thought transportation wise it was a little difficult to get to.

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

Huge crowds. Same food stuff / restaurant items as if you were visiting a cafe in Busan. Perhaps there were one or two special items but probably not worth going specially for afternoon tea / food.Outdoor tea plantations were good can take photos to mock up a scene of you on a remote tea farm.Many tours and crowded. Had to park at an alternative lot 10 minutes from the entrance

Here you can learn about Korean tea history and its tradition. I enjoyed the premium tea class which I took for the second time. Every year it is different in terms of tea flavor and desserts. After taking the tea class you can visit a caf챕 that serves various desserts and maybe the most delicious green tea ice cream in South Korea. Also you can purchase cosmetics from Innisfree Jeju House which is right next to the museum. And to get beautiful pictures you should visit tea plantations located right next to the Innisfree Jeju House.

Great selection of tea leaves in their shop and a short presentation of how O Sulloc tea came about in South Korea. There's also a cafe where you can enjoy drinks and snacks based on green tea. And across the road there is a mini tea plantation for you to explore and take great photos!

Great if u like tea quite a wide variety they sell and with a cafe that sells really good looking green tea chiffon cakes and tea snacks. Also have brunch items. There's also innisfree store there for u to make your own soaps that was quite popular with the kids and families. The tea plantation outside is great for one who hasn't seen a plantation before with its lush green bushes lined neatly over the horizon.

Great  cosy  simple with a beautiful view  countryside atmosphere and the elegance of a modern coffee place. You can see how the plants grow and you can pet animals as well. A place to drink and eat something too.
Good view. Very amazing tea recommended for people who love to drink tea. Have Great cafe to chill and relax. Varieties of place have museum cafe and tea plantation

Good to visit this place if you have extra time in Jeju Island building was surrounded with green tea plantation and a small nice walking path connecting both O'Sulloc and Innisfree. It was good to have both closed by as it was a rainy day we went in March.O'Sulloc building has a very spacious cafe serving nice desserts and many selection tea from the counter bar. Green tea cream roll is a must if you happen to be there.The souviner section has so many to choose from. Parking and admission to this place is free.
Good cafes. Nice tea tasting. Scenic and beautiful. Tea plantation is attractive. Simple and nice. Highly recommended
Get to see the tea plantation museum and buy their tea and food there. Worth going if you are a tea lover ^_^

Fun half day out !  Green tea everything from tea to face cream and our 8 year looked the GT icecream which is truly delicious. The plantation and site is is sleek spotless and well maintained but we found the prices a trifle steep. (The Euro was a bit wobbly in Aug 2010!) We got a taxi there and hitched our way back to the mainroad to pick up the bus back to Jeju Si.
Free admission.  Visited in Dec and it was extremely crowded. Tea plantation is open for public visit. Innisfree Jeju House is right next door.

For those who loves nature.. This is where you can see plants you've never seen before. The area was so huge but it did not deter us from walking and exploring. They kids also loved the exotic plants and were excited to see the carnivorous plants that were indoors.

For  tea lovers O'Sulloc Tea Museaum is a great place to visit.  There are different displays of varied teas and other beauty products derived from tea.  There is also a refreshment parlor serving anything made from tea.  Outside this museum is a big park where people may gather or just play.  Just in front of the museum is a tea plantation.

Fields of green tea leaves greeted us at our next destination - O'Sulloc Tea Museum (?ㅼ꽕濡앺떚裕ㅼ???. It was a sight to behold and similar to the tea plantations that you can find at Cameron Highlands (Malaysia) sans the slopes - rows upon rows of green leafy segregated sections. After a couple of touristy photos we headed into the museum.Apparently the 'o' in O'Sulloc has a dual meaning: to appreciate and enjoy and also stands for the the origin of Sulloc (tea). The O'Sulloc Tea Museum (?ㅼ꽕濡앺떚裕ㅼ??? first opened in September 2001 and since than visitors can enjoy unique o?셲ulloc teas and the unique views of the nearby green tea fields and the surrounding landscape. After hanging out a bit at the museum we were brought to the souvenir corner where there all sort of teas: flower tea barley tea tangerine tea etc... There was even free sampling of of their tangerine tea which was a good marketing tactic since I bought myself a packet. The tea was really fragrant (full of tangerine!). There is also a cafe nearby but I didn't get to try it.For more about my experience and photos please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/osulloc-tea-museum-and-plantation.html
Expect nothing but the best! good and healthy coffee tea and cakes.nice Garden and tea plantation to chill out.House of Innisfree..Bought lots of these products  :-)

Entrance fee cost KRW10000. We got 10% discount after show the discount voucher. No need to print just show the picture from mobile phone will do.There are more than 100 houses in this place.Among them are Mountain Village Hill Country Village Fishing Village & Shamanism Village.With the traditional houses complete with the small plantation and livestock it feel like we was teleported back to the 1890s.Everything here looks and feels so authentic.There are also various folk games which include jegi skipping rope swing etc.The village is a place various dramas and films are made.There are 13 set places built for dramas inluding Jewel in the Palace The Slave Hunters Merchant Kim Man Deok Tamna the Island etc.There are signs to show exactly where each one was filmed.

Didn?셳 wander the plantation or visit the Innisfree store - but bought green tea (of various varieties inc award winning selections) and desserts. The roll cake was good but the matcha ice cream was the best I?셶e ever had. Skip the O Fredo (ice blended cream and matcha ice cream ?쁡rink?? and just have the matcha ice cream. You won?셳 regret it.
Could sniff up the fragrance of the tea from the surrounding plantations...simple set-up that ended nicely with a scoop of green tea ice-cream and some packs of tea to take home...
