Came to look at the famous plantation and try the famous green tea deserts. Prefer the cake more than the ice cream. Bought some tea and facial foam here which was at great value and good quality. The road is very dark after sunset.

Came here for the matcha products especially the green tea and the green tea bread spread. Do try the green tea ice cream or cakes but do expect some queueing. Opposite the museum lies a field of green tea plantation good for photo opp.
Beautiful place with huge plots of green tea plantation. Lots of tourist. Popped by innisfree next door. Beautiful cafe space. Crowded with tourists. Spend an hour there. Nothing much really.

Beautiful landscape but failed to showcase the unique view in different season of Korea. There is nothing much to see in Mar as the spring has yet to set in thus what you can get is leaf-dropping trees and looking a little dry and crusty. I guess Japan has done a better job to ensure different plant is growing according to the season in their landscape which still make it look stunning during winter & autumn . But this place will definitely look beautiful when Spring set in.

Banglimwon is a large exhibition of plants. All the descriptions and signs are written in Korean maybe taking a pleisure walk was a good idea to us. We don’t think the tour guide want either being able to translate some thousands of plant names into Eng lish anyway. However this place is beautiful and worth to visit.

All the kudos to the marketing team which managed to paint this place as a touristic attraction. The surface of their parkings is bigger than the entire tea plantation. Inside you can buy any premium (overpriced) tea based products you can imagine. We went on Monday outside season and it was so crowded that I got the impression it was black Friday sales.

Actually I thought we will have a walk around tea plantations. But all I did there was to drink tea and eat cakes and buy tea products. What I enjoyed is that it is organic and there is innisfree shop there! This innifree shop is different as it allows u to make soap and your own perfume.But of cos you have to pay for it.

A very nicely designed museum with beautiful spaces and an inner garden which you could watch and have tea at its cafe. The food wasn't great but its a nice place to chill.However it can get pretty crowded with tourists pouring in occasionally. If that is the case head out to the tea plantation outside where its more spacious and great for photographs.
A nice walk to view the crater. Lovely scenes with reed plants called eoksae (flamegrass) swaying in the background. Special wonder of nature!

A nice tea museum good to learn some history about tea plantation on Jeju. But the tea sold there and the food serve is slightly over priced. The tea plantation however is nothing spectacular it?셲 only unique during spring and summer is where you get to see wild flowers blooming along the the way.
A lover of plants and trees would love to spend hours here in this park. The lava tube may be a new experience for some . . . .

A little underwhelmed but nice nonetheless. The cafe is a good place to have your fill of green tea by the pot in cake yoghurt drink and ice cream. There?셲 history of tea both western and eastern. A chance to take selfies within a tea plantation.
A good place to spend 1-2 hours. The green tea plantation area was well-maintained. Great green tea latte. I thought they should offer sampling of various merchandise.

A good place if you love tea.They have a tea plantation that you have access to and take pictures. Not bad but when we went it was pretty hot. So we opt out of that. The museum itself was alright. It has the teacups from around the world.On the ground floor itself you have the cafe as well. The cafe sells ice cream the roll and other light food. A very good place to escape the heat.Innisfree Jeju House is just next door as they are run by the same Group.
a beautiful location for a good view and some interesting plantlife. also a trail where one can go hiking.

You should be geared for a long walk inside the park. The ticket is a bit pricey (11,000 won per adult) with nothing much to see. There are plenty of palm trees and different types of pine trees as well but not really very rare or special species.They have collection of tropical plants (bananas, guava,mango , etc) which I am sure tourists from Southeast Asia will find boring. They have lots of cacti although not very extensive collection. May be we came at the wrong time because there were only few flowering plants. Overall, quite a waste of time and money ( and energy too).

When my group and I first went to this market I assumed it would be small like a on the side of the road market where they sell fruits, veggies, and jams. This market was that times ten and the market even had the kitchen sink. When we first walked through they had fresh picked flowers, potted plants, fresh spices, 15 different types of kimchi. As we walked around it wasnt just food and plants they had housewares to clothes even puppies, rabbits and chickens. then we realized that they even had a fish market. This market of cousre smelled of fish we consumers selling squid, shrimp, and tilapia. This market is such a good way to imerse oneself into a the korean culture on the island. This was one of the places on my wish list to see while my group and I were in Korea and it was much more than I expected and I am so glad I went.

When i heard that this place offers soap making - I immediately thought that i must come. It was indeed pretty fun, you can buy the material for 15k krw and it has 3 base, so it means you can share with 3 ppl. Instructions on the tablet is easy to follow and you should be done within 15-20mins. There?셲 a small tea plantation for you to take pictures.
Went with my kids and parents. We explore every part of the park. From Caves, cactus to folk villages. We enjoy the plantation at the park and flowers definitely. Must visit

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

We went there for lunch. It is next to O  Sulloc Tea Museum. There is a car park next to it, if it's is full, can park opposite next to the tea plantation. They serve Bing su (shaved ice) as well. Tried the tangerine shave ice. Average, don't waste your money. Menu limited an pricey. Can purchase Innisfree products as well. Price same as Seoul. Nice place to relax. There is soap making class, where by one cAn purchase the ingredients and make a personalize soap. There is a tea plantation next to it.

We went during the winter so most of the plants had no flowers nor leaves. The ones that did were amazing though. They have signs in Korean, Japanese, Chinese, and English. It was pretty informative. There's an aviary that's open so people can interact with some of the birds. I can imagine what it must look like in the spring. Definitely coming back to see all the flowers blooming.

We visited Hallim Park with my daughter in August. It is very nice place with diversified trees, plants, birds. Convenient infrastructure allowed us to see so many wonderful natural things during three hours. Two old cave are in the park. It is interesting to pass them especially in hot day.

We love the story around the Innisfree Jeju House. It's organic and farm to table supply chain and mission is admirable. We had the the diver's special bento and it was delicious. My wife had the blue colored tea ade and I had fresh carrot juice and all of it was great. The have beautiful cakes in the shape of Halla mountain and tiramisu with delicate flower designs. The prices are in the higher end but well worth the refined quality and experience for those who like this sort of thing. My wife loved the purity of the food and calm views of the tea plantation.They also have products for sale as well as a tea extract exhibit. They have fun hands on tea soap making as well you can purchase and do there. Or they have other ones you can purchase and take home to do. Great place to calm down, re-energize, and enjoy.

We hired a taxi for the day but this wasn't one of the place we wanted to go. The driver, Charles Cho, unilaterally decided we should stop at Sangumburi anyway. We're glad he did. We've been to Kintamani in Bali, but this crater is smaller and within a more scenic and lonely area. The surrounding mountains and farmland are serenely beautiful. One of the attractions here is a patch of tall reeds, but at this time of the year, they have not sprouted yet.The crater itself is supposedly valuable because of the unique plants and animals there, but for us casual visitors, it's a nice, green geographical feature.There are remains of tombs there, but no information on them.

We hiked this in December in the snow.  We started from the Yeongsil entrance, and just went up to the Shelter as we started pretty late.  The hike is tough for those who are out of shape but perfectly doable for regular hikers.  It took us about 2 hours up and about 1.5 hours down - the snow making it much slower than we would normally take (and more scenic, but very slippery in places).I would recommend good hiking shoes as the rocks are tough and slippery in places - I saw some people wearing what I would consider to be bedroom slippers and they were really struggling!  Those mini-crampons were also a godsend in the snow (the shop at the bottom sells them).Great views on the way up and from the top.  As we had a car, we had to go back the way we came but next time we will come when the plants are green and do a loop hike.  Can't wait.

We enjoyed our visit to Hallim Park very much. The parking was easy and ticket was very reasonable. If you like plants, then you are in luck. A lot of plants to see and I loved the lilies among other things. There are rock gardens and lava tubs (underground). Since the park is quite big (bigger than other gardens/parks on the island), you'd never feel crowded. We even had lunch at the on-site restaurant and it was quite good. As noted on the top, this is a great place to spend a few hours while visiting Jeju Island.

We decided to visit this   Green tea Museum   because it was a rainy day but could not find much of a direction - there was a mention of the tea stone experience but no further information.  We ended up going to the busy restaurant through a small 'museum' and ended up 'enjoying the $9 green tea'.  On the fields across from the museum there are kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures for photo opportunities.

We came to visit in the late afternoon, it was lovely and quiet, with a lot of plants to enjoy and two fish ponds. Very nice afternoon stroll, and a welcome escape from the city hustle and bustle. The staff were all very friendly and eager to teach us how to best view and appreciate the plants and gardens. Overall a lovely place to visit in the afternoon

Walking up the stairs is tiring but once at the top, you can see the craters which are filled with greenness of plants... View the surroundings from top is superb! Good for nature lovers yet those that do not want to hike the hill...At the seaside below the hill, you can enjoy seafood fresh fr the sea!

Walking between different kind of plants. It is nice for who love nature. Also I love folk village, cave, and Bonsai tree. It was 20,000 Won Taxi cap from Jeju Lotte Hotel, and you don't have to keep your taxi waiting for you because there are many taxi in erea.

Unique maze park where maps of the maze are provided.  If you follow the map, it will take you about 5 minutes to complete it.  But try it on your own, and you may take longer or get lost!!   Along the maze, the plant is high, so you can't see over into other areas.  There are three skywalks where you can stand and observe the entire maze and take pictures of it.  Fun for the entire family.

Udo island is a small island at east of Jeju Island. It is named after cow because of its cow alike shape. Once you reached the island, you are able to find few bike rental shop. You can rent a electrical scooter with roof or normal scooter to tour around the island. Bare in mind the speed limit is 30 km/h. Most of the rental shop offer two hours rental only. Generally, it should be sufficient if you don't linger at each place too long. Do try the peanut ice-cream as the island is famous for peanut plantation. Get your camera ready as there are many beautiful scenaries to take photos.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.? There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

This was one of the most popular things to do in jeju and we stayed close by so was a no brainer. Cost $11,000krw to get in, and had heaps of different plants and flowers from different parts of the world etc. overall not too bad, october is the off season to go so was very quiet. If you love plants you?ll love this if not properly not the place for you.

This was covered under our west course jeju tour.This is a large park with good bonsy trees ,lava caves and plants and animals and a old jeju village huts to show jeju culture.We can enjoy photography.If localite a good picnic spot.food shops available.

This place is huge, with lots of plants, flowers, caves to see. Though it may not be extra especial since it felt so artificial, it is still a cool place to visit. Stroll and take lots of pictures with friends or family. Don't join the tour because they only allow 1-1.5 hours and you'll end up just walking and not really appreciating the things that you will see.
This place is full of colorful flowers, plants, trees. Various catagories of plant life, a scenic place.Really liked it.

This place is beautiful and relaxing. It smells great too. I think best thing is to do the soap to bring home as souvenir. Besides that, taking picture with the green tea plant and trying their menu. But I'm not very fond of their drinks.

This place combines a few areas that are nice to see in one area, such as tropical plants, flowers etc. I liked the short lava tubes. There is a bonsai garden. We skipped the flower section since there were no flowers during autumn (at least the toru guid claimed, but we didn't check).

This park includes a variety of sights including two lava tubes, an aviary that includes a variety of peacocks, ostriches etc, a small traditional village, strange little rock people sculptures, and a very impressive botanical garden with outdoor sections around a pond and several green houses.   Some strange combinations in the outdoor section with large palms mixed up with various types of cacti and other random mixes of fabulous plant specimens from all over the world.  The greenhouse plants seem a bit more organized by regions or types (e.g., large cactus collection in one greenhouse; palms in another), with live animals interspersed between the plants (impressive boa and python collection, also some special turtles, and lizards such as nile monitors, iguanas, etc.).  In between plant viewing, I enjoyed a nice cool cactus juice relaxing in the herb bar.

This park has it all - Plants, bonsai, trees, birds, ostriches, stone sculptures, lava caves, folk houses. However, it is really big so you might need to have more than 3 hours to finish the entire park.

This park has a collection of 7-8 sections of different type of plants and sights, such as tropical plants, cactus collections, bonsai collection, wild flowers, cave systems, folk village, small cave system etc. You could easily spent 2 hours at this park. The park is nicely planned and appropriately signed to guide the exploration of the entire park. We really liked its cactus collection and roads lined by famous Jeju-harubang (stone human-shaped statues). We definitely recommend visiting this fabulous park.

This mystery road is just a small portion of a long road with many undulating slopes. There is sign broad showing the start of the mystery. Both sides of the road has plantation indicating the road is up slope.  Vehicles with engine killed will moves slowly from the start point with the plantation effect. At the ending point when out from the vehicle, looking at the road as if you are on the top of the small gradient.According to academic research, it is actually down slope but due to side plantation causing people to view wrongly.

This is one of the best place we visited in Jeju. Various things to see such as flowers, plants, birds, small reptiles, lava cave etc. I love the cactus garden most. Great for photo taking and a slow stroll with family members! I did not fully explore the place due to time constraint. Guess it probably need around 2-3 hrs to slowly explore the park.

This is an honest review which I?m only leaving because we weren?t allowed to leave the garden until we promised to give it a TripAdvisor review! Usually I?m much too lazy for such antics.First things first, I think it?s admirable what Bum-young Sung (the owner) has dreamt up and achieved over fifty odd years working here. I also think he has developed very sharp entrepreneurial acumen over this time - the entry fee is 12000 won and thousands of people (us included) seem to be happy to fork this out given the decent ratings Spirited Garden has achieved.Is it worth it? I?d have to say no for the following reasons:1) the garden is actually very small (you can wonder through it in 15-20 minutes).2) even though the trees are nice to look at (debatable given how some of the trees are shackled to metal frames), there are lots of signs imploring you to see the deeper meaning and philosophical undertones of the plants and stones, many of which didn?t really make a lot of sense.3) the owner will probably come to meet you at some point which seems superficially like a nice touch, but it did feel a bit mechanical - he would then get a phone call about some new guests coming into the park and suddenly have to dash off (probably to make sure they left a good TripAdvisor review)All in all, there?s a lot of great nature to see in Jeju, especially if you want to get away from the chaos and ponder the meaning of life, but why not climb up Mt Hallasan or do an Olle trail instead, and then go and spend your 12000 won on a present for yourself

This is a wonderful park-like place that includes a portion of lava tube, traditional drums that are available for people to play around on, and apparently numerous classes including pottery. The plantings are fabulous, and there are some examples of Jeju's own dialect.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.
This garden was well maintained with a wide range of flowers, plants and cactus. Relax and take a slow walk to admire the surrounding. A nice attraction not to be missed if you like garden.

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!

This botanical garden is well arranged, it enables you to travel around the world through its flora. Pleasant warm ambience, pretty flowers, trees and plants, outside garden too. Great for sunny days - you can admire the view of Hallasan volcano.

There is a train servicing in the theme park that will drop the visitors to every station and allow them to walk around and take photo. As of the name   Eco   the theme park is closed to the mother of nature which basically full with plants and trees. Besides, highly recommend the lavender ice cream in the lavender and rose garden station.

There is a reason that this place was packed.  The museum is located in a super modern building set amongst impeccably groomed grounds and a green tea plantation.  The   museum   part takes 5 minutes to get through but the caf챕 and market is buzzing with tourists enjoying an assortment of green tea treats.  I found lots more tea options at this store than any other in Korea (and there are many!)  But the bonus is the Innisfree store adjacent to the Museum on the same grounds.  Here you can make your own mask concoctions customize soap and find lots high quality unique gifts with Jeju logo on them.  I spent at least an hour here alone.  They also have a caf챕.  Definitely a must stop on Jeju!

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There is a huge greenhouse with 7 separate areas of different plants including desert, aquatic, floral, jungle, and tropical fruit. ? The tropical fruit area had platters (examples)? of many different types of the fruit of the nearby trees. ? There are a couple small shops in the greenhouse selling different items as well as food and drink.? ? There is also an elevator going up to a 5th floor observatory. ? We went on a very rainy day.? ? Couldn’t see a thing. ? The greenhouse was extremely busy, I’m sure moreso due to the bad weather.? ? ? 10,000 won to enter.

There is a cafe at level 2 and a small gift shop selling Hallabong items after walking through their tangerines greenhouse. There is also a small museum where kids could learn about tangerines but they are mostly in Korean.Outside  the korean fans dedicated a small hectre of tangerine plantation to G-Dragon. There is even a Kwon Jiyong Tree. But since we were there in late March  the weather was still pretty chilly  so the leaves are not growing yet.You could ask the reception where it is  its just nearby. However do try asking them as   G-Dragon   forest. i tried saying as   GD    but they dont really get it. Lol.

The Yeomiji Botanical Garden is easy to find and has parking places available. Entrance is not so pricy. The place is easier to enter with stroller or wheel chair. The glass house is quite big and divided into flower/aquatic/cactus/jungle and tropical fruits garden. The outdoor garden is also spacious but we did not go there. Not many people have visited the place. Consequently it was quiet and empty. The garden is very beautiful, interesting and green. It has also a lot of plants and trees but the wow effect is definitely missing.? On top of the glass house is also a view point with elevator connection. Finally I have seen much better botanical gardens.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The Spirited Garden is a great pastime to spend with friends, the garden is beautiful! There is so much plant life to see with a rich cultural and historical story behind each part of the garden! Plenty of great photo-ops here for your social media or if you are big fan of botany you will definitely enjoy it.

The soap making workshop is fun and interesting for kids and couples. Innisfree Jeju House is next to the famous O'Sulloc Green tea, you can spend at least 2 to 3 hours in these two placesfor soap making workshop, tea break and photograhping in the tea plantation.

The place is big but there are many places that are not well maintained. Tall grasses in some places and many of the plants are left to grow without some serious planning. The caves are nice though, clean and doesn't have the smell of bat urine. The bonsais are quite nice too.
the park planting many flowers and plants outside traditional housing. Very refreshing, we can teach our sister too who start to love Korean culture about traditional village.
The park is really big. Need at least 2 hrs to complete exploring. There's many things to see - from small animals, plants to caves. Great place to relax and enjoy the scenery.
The park is located close to the beach, it?s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.

The park is a great snapshot of what the island has to offer.  The gardens highlight a number of different plant species as well as shelter the lava tube which is both breathtaking and refreshing is the weather outside is toasty hot.  There are bonsai exhibits, traditional korean village exhibitions and even an aviary.  Very neat and pleasant way to spend an afternoon.

The indoor gardens are very lovely especially the flower and cactus gardens. We were there on a sunny day in May and expected it to be hot inside. But these are not just greenhouses. They are greenhouses with air conditioning and so it was pleasantly cool and we took our time to walk around and admire the plants in comfort. The gardens are very well maintained without a leaf out of place. The arrangements are very pleasing and and these two gardens are simply beautiful. Go on a sunny day when the light and shadow creates a most charming effect.As for the outdoor gardens, the Italian one is very picturesque with a magnificent water feature. This is not so much a garden but nonetheless very attractive.Definitely worth a visit.

The gardens are peaceful and pleasant to stroll around. There is a lot of emphasis on Confucian lore, which is a tad overplayed. Also overplayed is the constant homage to whatever Chinese Premier visited to dig a hole and plant a bonsai. The shop and restaurants are in beautiful buildings and of high quality. The use of local lava rock to surround the gardens makes for a sombre effect, but I guess that is the intent. This is not the sort of place the teens are going to rave about, but older folk and gardeners will very much enjoy

The garden was one of the best i have visited. Sense of peace and calm just being in here. Went on a day with good weather and the photos turned out absolutely captivating. The spirit of cultivating and nurturing bonsai plants and trees was brought across and many moments, made me ponder about life. One of the best things to do in Jeju. Definitely worth a visit

The garden is huge and beautiful. Unfortunately, it was a rainy day when we visited the garden. Different variety of plants from different part of the world are collected in a dome. A full tour throughout the dome takes around 90 minutes. There is also an observatory above the dome for people to overlook the Jungmun Tourism Complex. Though the garden is huge, I found most of the plants are not native to Korea. It is a pity that foreign tourists can not know more native plants? by visiting this garden.

The garden has probably seen better days, as some of the facilities look worn down. However, the plant life is beautiful and healthy. I enjoyed the cactus garden the best. It was a bit pricey for what it is. I’d recommend seeing the natural attractions instead.

The entry fee is abit on the high side, but if you love gardens, plants, nature, and especially flowers, it’s worth every penny. My absolute favourite place to visit in Jeju. I love flowers so we spent around 4 hours here. There’s a huge variety of flowers, and the gardens/areas are very well laid-out. Besides the greenhouse, there is also an area outside where all the different-themed gardens are (Korean, Japanese, French etc), there are about 12 gardens in total I think, and all of them are really beautiful. I think this attraction is still relatively new, as I could still see gardeners setting up the flower beds and so on. But this also means that it’s not crowded yet and there are relatively few tourists compared to the other attractions. Flower-lovers, this is a must-visit!

The Botanical gardens is set up in to different gardens and a large doom/ indoor area set up into zones. The plants on show were very nice but I have seen a lot better. This could be because of the South Korea climate. Look at the surface and it's well kept then you notice dirty water in the ponds. What I did enjoy was watching some of the workers weed some of the areas they are so methodical. As we were part of a day tour this was just one of our many stops and our time was limited. Perhaps I would have enjoyed it more if I didn't have such a tight schedule. I would rate this attraction as Good but there isn't a good rating and average would do it a disjustice. I thought the entrance fee to be very high considering the country it's in. You don't pay much more to go in Kew Gardens, London's Botanical garden that can actually take you days to get round.

The botanical garden is a place where a wide variety of plants are displayed for understanding how vast is our plant kingdom.it may also help to understand the geographical peculiarities of different countries all over the world. The best thing I have seen there was they provided each species scientific details along with the source country. It will be so exciting to see our country plant representing in a botanical garden situating in a foreign place. Furthermore botanical garden is situated in a very beautiful place with a wide variety of gardens and trees, as I said earlier all the plants and trees are named perfectly.

The area of the beach is nice but the sandy part and the open water space is soooo small... You cannot even go for a swim here. The water was dirty and full of water plants. I honestly thinking every beach in Europe is way more attractive than this. Italy, Greece, Croatia....Have they actually seen clear azure waters?! If this is jejus prettiest beach then im really sorry for koreans
Take the afternoon and walk around this beautiful park and zoo. All different kind of plants, trees, flowers, and animals, this park is way better than it seems. Don't miss it!

Such a beautiful place where I experienced peace of mind and heart. Reading how Bunjae and our lives are quite parallel really made me think twice about nature and how we should cherish it as if it was our own lives. The quote that I will keep with me forever is   Potted plants wither when their roots are not trimmed, and people age when they do not change their ways of thinking  . Thank you for providing a space for people to learn and reflect on life amongst nature. God bless.

Sangumburi crater has a circum of over 2 km deserves its title of a Natural Monument. A must visit on Jeju island you can see the variety of plant-life in the crater. It was a great place to take pictures and has amazing views. It was really nice just to wander and admire the natural beauty of this place, a highlight of our Jeju island trip if you like nature.
relaxing, lots of plants and flowers.easily needs 3 to 4 hours to explore this park.take a bus there from main bus terminal.It stop right in front of the park.

Our stay in Jeju coincide with the operational day of one of the biggest and oldest traditional market in Jeju - Grandma Market which runs on days that end with 7th of the calendar month. There are lots of other smaller scale traditional markets which are opened on different days (e.g days ending on 5th, 2nd, etc...) thru out the island but we were told that this is the biggest.There is also an area which are designated for elderly ladies aged 65 and above whereby they are not charged any fees for selling there, hence, the name of Grandma Market.Lots of things can be found in the market, from plants, to snacks to clothings to housewares. We bought some fresh ginseng, chilly flakes and also fresh gingko from the market (after tasting some that were steamed and sold as snacks), The gingko there is different from those that we get in MY (most imported from China). Their is more creamy in texture and rounded as compared to ours.Overall, quite an interesting walk for an hour or two if you're looking to buy some of foodstuff.

Our guide brought us to this place, let us alight and asked us to observe the strange phenomenon. He switched off the car engine and we saw the car still moving uphill without the engine switched on. He then demonstrated by pouring a bottle of water at one spot along the road and we could see the trail of water wriggled its way uphill without the application of any external interferences. The phenomenon was strange and unexplainable. Was it that a magnetic force beneath the earth on this road had triggered off that momentum? My guide did not explain and I could not find any explanation on any of the signboards around the vicinity. I remembered few years back when I was in Shanghai, I visited the mausoleum of the great Chinese revolutionary martyr, Song Qingling which was located at the western part of the city. Prior to her demise, she had requested that her body be buried at this cemetery site beside her late parents, the influential and rich Song family. I was astonished to learn from our tour guide and saw with my own eyes the strange phenomenon of the cypress and pine trees planted around the mausoleum was bending inwards and downwards from all angles towards the direction of the cemetery site where her body was buried. It was not just the left rows of trees, not just the right rows of trees but the trees planted at all the other corners surrounding the rectangular burial plot that were seen pointing inwards and downwards with the focus at the burial ground. The lush green trees appeared like bodyguards saluting, bending their heads and standing humbly for her directions. My guide informed us that the cemetery was a specially chosen grand and auspicious geomancy burial ground and that account for the strange phenomenon. The Chinese believed that if your body is buried on an auspiciously good Fengshui geomancy chosen ground, your future generations will benefit and prosper. I am not an expert in Fengshui and was hoping to get a scientific explanation for the weird phenomenon. Right here, at this strange mysterious road in Jeju, I was also trying to observe if the trees growing around the vicinity of the mysterious road bend towards and focused at the core center where the strange phenomenon occurred but I could not see what I saw at Song Qingling's mausoleum. Both strange phenomenon seemed to be unrelated in their nature and in terms of scientific theory of explanation that a strong magnetic force beneath the earth is in operation. The `Bermuda Triangle' is also another unexplainable phenomenon whereby it was unexplainable as to where so many ships vanished in strange occurring environment. I had watched a Chinese TV series on science whereby the film director sought to provide scientific explanations to the many strange `unexplainable' and `supernatural' phenomenon around China. I really hope that some days, the same film director could incorporate the strange phenomenon that occurred at this mysterious road, the ship vanishing Bermuda Triangle and that of the Song Qingling's burial site in his series and provide a scientific theoretical explanation for the weird occurrence. The visit to this mysterious road had triggered off my curiosity and I left the place, confused and thinking of the limits in science.

Our driver suggested for us to visit this place as we were fond of seeing the flame grass, of which some can be found on the roadside of Jeju.Can?t advise on the travelling mode as we booked a driver to send us there and it was by car.For entrance to the crater, you have to purchase a ticket at 6000won. The park was filled with 듭ⓒ (eok-sae) or in another name, flame grass. Our driver informed us that the grass usually grows in August and at the beginning, it?s purple in colour. Towards the October, it becomes pale golden (as it has dried up). The park is pretty big, and you can get to the top of the crater where you can look down to the middle of the crater. On the way up, you can see the remains of the volcano by the volcano rocks forming a rocky path and also the volcanic ashes amongst these rocks. Going down from the top of the crater, you will pass by many trees, leading to an empty grassland which can be good for jump shots and some random photo-taking. While making your way back to the entrance, you?ll pass by a graveyard park, of which is suspected to be the family of the owner of this place. there are stones surrounding the graves to prevent horses from coming in to eat the plants on it. It doesn?t have a creepy feel to it and there were many children playing soccer in the park itself.At the entrance, you can also purchase some snacks like hotdog and ice cream. We tried the grape and mango ice cream, which were too creamy for our liking.
Opposite to Hyeopjae Beach, it is an old fashioned park with almost every element in Jeju. Caves, plants, mini zoo, and even a folk village. 10000 krw entrance fee is not cheap though.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Nice place to have a relaxing walk with lots of trees and plants. If you are there try to visit the herbal cafe with the ostrich and peacocks just beside it, it was very nice having a cup of tea there.

Named as Eco-park but really artificial at all... Nothing special with ordinary decorations and plants. Fairly speaking, young children will enjoy the train ride but for adults/teenagers not worth spending time here...

My 'poetic' side has always loved gardens. Used to dream and draw secret gardens all the time. My heart and gut was somehow curious about this place, especially after reading reviews from travellers all over the world. Was made to understand that not many young people from our country like myself come to visit which intrigued the caretaker enough to see someone such as myself wandering around the garden and I was therefore approached with such warmth. Even had the pleasure of sipping tea and being in the company of the very welcoming founder owner himself Mr. Bum-Young Sung, who transformed, built and developed this garden over 40 years ago with his own bare hands when nobody but his wife believed that he could turn a wasteland into what is known and recognised now to be   The most beautiful garden in the world  . Like a poetic art carefully, passionately, calmly and beautifully crafted, Spirited Garden indeed does justice to its name. Even in winter where the trees and plants don't bloom as much, I could still feel the garden's spirit that it's almost like nature is speaking to you which gives you a sense of serenity. For a moment, Felt like I was in Edward Scissorhands's world ㅿ Learned so much about the bonsai tree, as well as the philosophical and wisdom in gardening. Thank you Spirited Garden for the beautiful inspiration.

My only concern with Hallim Park is the condition of some of the animals they have there. The 'cages' or 'presentation units' seem quite small for some of them, and some of the bigger birds didn't seem particularly happy. I don't want to give this an 'average' review because the caves are incredibly unique, the diverse array of trees and plants is also very special. But full disclosure, this place may not be for everyone.

My husband and I were staying in the Hallim area and our taxi driver mistakenly took us to Hallim Park. Especially since it was a bit chilly and an overcast day, the beautiful green houses and occasionally covered areas were a nice break from the weather. The park itself is nothing overly spectacular, but it has a little bit of everything with a nice mix of Jeju style to your typical botanical gardens type park. Plants, flowers, animals, exhibits, and fun!

My husband and I visited this park during our honeymoon and it was really beautiful. It consists of 8 botanical gardens which features different kinds of plants, a cave which you can walk through, and even an area with different kinds of birds that you can feed and interact with.We got there through the Yeha Bus Tour but you can also get there with a taxi.For those of you who are looking to experience some of the beauty of nature and interact with it, I recommend this place.
