review: My comment to my wife after touring the O'Sulloc tea museum:   It's more of a fun cafe and tea shop than a museum or   plantation   for tea enthusiasts.  It's a nice stop if you're staying closer to that side of Jeju - we traveled about 15 min. by car to reach it.  Really enjoyed the green tea cake and latte and bought some fresh tea for souvenir.  However this is not a   must see   aspect of a trip to Jeju.There is also a Innisfree cosmetics shop on the site which has a lot of products; we made a few purchases there too.  Nice little add-on for the Jeju tourist.

Mt. Hallasan is the main peak of Jeju do, a shield shaped volcano formed on the continental shelf in the Yellow Sea. It is the highest peak of South Korea (1950 meters above the base level) and the symbol of Jeju Island. The Hallasan Natural Reserve makes up of various arctic alpine plants and a forest of the Korean fir, which makes a graceful scene, and the  Baeknokdam, the Crater Lake on the top of the Mt. Hallasan, adds the scenic beauty. You can meet totally different appearance of Mt. Hallasan according to the 4 seasons.

Love this beautiful and relaxing cafe, nestled next to a tea plantation. Kids enjoyed the DIY soap and bubble bomb making workshop. Just purchase the kit at 15,000 won per set and you can spend the next 30 mins kneading and enjoying the DIY process. A fun activity for the whole family. The cakes and drinks are v nice too! An instagrammable place!

Lots of variety here from plants, pulses, clothing, fruit and veges and fish and local street food.  The prices aren't cheap as you would expect in a market but that's the same all over Korea.  A good variety is why you would go there.

Located beside O'sulloc tea museum. When I told the taxi driver he seem don't know the place but when I said O'sulloc he just get it. Outside you can see green tea plant. Inside you can buy innisfree products, make your own soap here and in the corner you can design your own postcard for free with the stamp that have been provided. For me it's closed so early on 6 pm and since I been there too late, many menu already sold out and trying the Tangerine Shave Ice which is nothing special but after all it's a nice cafe.

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.

It's more of a shopping place. The green tea ice-cream is quite blandand there's not much green tea taste.But the   saving grace   is the tea plantation . There are giant cupslots of flowers and is overall a photo taking place. We did not have enough time and did not visit the museum . There are interesting sample tea blands that you can smell with names like   Moon Walk   and   Jeju Green Tea  . Overall could be better. Might come again.

It's actually just one short stretch of the road but interesting. The road gives you an impression that its going up hill instead it's actually going down the hill. The surrounding including the plants, trees, field and fencing are giving you that up hill impression. So when you switch off the vehicle engine that you are in, the vehicle will continue to move forward. Same goes to the test where they will show you by rolling a water bottle. Try walking backward and you can feel it. You might feel a bit disappointed as there is nothing else over there

It's a stone throw away from the Lava Tube. There are a lot of cats lying around the park. The maze is quite easy but to collect all the stamp to accomplish the mission, it takes more time. However, the grass/plant at the maze seem not well taken care as you can see a lot of holes along the plant fences of the maze.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. It is basically a Bonsai tree-themed Garden decorated with many waterfalls and beautiful ponds full of colorful koi carps. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

It is just a vision trick. The road appears going up when it is really going down, so cars and buses can glide down when put in neutral. The way the trees at the side of the road is planted tricks your vision. Coming from Canada, we have seen it similar to the one in Moncton, New Brunswick.

It is a nice walk up to the top, windy.From the top we do have a nice view, wide view with many hills. Nothing special about the plants or vegetation. The entrance fee of KRW6,000 is a bit high when this is all you see.

Innisfree Jeju House can be got to by taking a bus to the O'Sulloc tea museum stop. The tea museum is a very short walk away from Innisfree Jeju House.The place is quiet and peaceful, save for the calming music they play and the chatter of tourists and other visitors, but that wasn't too bad when I was there. There's an area devoted to DIY lessons/sessions where one can try making their own soap. There's a few pretty exhibits where one can smell various scents or read a little about the Innisfree brand and its products. There's a store area, with a few products that are exclusive to Innisfree Jeju House. And there's a cafe with various light food, drink and dessert options.Outside, there are tables and benches that overlook a nice view of the tea plantation, which you can go and take pictures in. Rows upon rows of tea leaves and a few windmills. It's all very pretty and is probably the biggest selling point of the whole compound containing both Innisfree Jeju House and the nearby tea museum. It's really very pretty.I enjoyed my time there, but if Innisfree products are not for you, or if you're the thrill-seeking type, perhaps you should skip this place.

I'm sure this is a beautiful place when the flowers are in bloom but there weren't many when we went in late July.  There were still some hydrangeas and a few other flowers around but I think they could plant more varieties so that the park is pretty in different seasons.  The worst part though was the signage and map.  We got lost 3-4 times in one hour!  The map is mostly pictures without words in any language and it's hard to tell where you are.  The only way we figured it out was that there are a couple of   you are here   signs (in Korean).  They've put up some   This way please   signs but then there will be a fork in the road and there's not another   this way   sign.

If you want to come here to buy Innisfree products, the offering are far lesser than what you can find in Myeongdong. The only attraction here is the soap making experience and a small piece of tea plantation. There are no location-only products sold here. Very limited merchanise on sale. The staffs are unfriendly and always pulling a long face. Not worth visiting.

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.
If you like plants and flowers, this is the place to go. However, it's all depends on the season. Different season, you see different flowers.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

If you garden or enjoy botanics this is a fabulous place. I just visited during Tulip season and the entrance was an alleyway of color. I imagine late in May and June when more plants are blooming Hallim is an even more stunning place. It contains a huge variety of plants, wishing I could grow some of these specimens in Colorado. They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested. The grounds include a couple of lava tunnels, which don't have a lot of spectacular cave features, but I still found them worth the walk through. They also have an amazing bonsai garden and a lovely water garden.I spent almost 2 hours exploring the flora on well marked walkways and paths in this lovely park.BTW, Hallim deserves an entrance fee for all the upkeep needed, not sure why they charge 2 dollars at a number of sea cliffs etc., that should be open to the public...
If you are ona  relaxing trip and just want to see some nice scenery then this will fit the bill.  Its by no means spectacular but nonetheless very pretty, especially with the local plant growth.
If you are a family with children, it is good to visit. But if you are alone or couple, you would not be interested only with plants..

If possible, I would recommend visiting this garden on a cloudy day or partly sunny. There is something peaceful about the weather and the garden that makes you want to stay forever. All the bonsai trees are beautiful and wonderfully taken care of. You can see how much great care was given to these trees. The plants, the rock artworks, and the people all create a very peaceful and very unified picture. This place is fitting for people of all ages. I would recommend everyone visiting this place.

I would not call it a must see attraction, but go there if you have spare time. I really liked their collection of cacti and insectivorous plants. The glasshouse arrangement is really impressive. The tropical section had fruit-bearing mango trees which was a sight to behold (inside the glasshouse). The French garden, the Italian garden, etc are good for a stroll. Didn't find anything there specifically impressive.

i won't repeat what others have mentioned.personally i love this place.i went during spring in april 2017,weather was perfect.food was presented beautifully,the latte i had was delicious.the garnishing is really insta-worthy!my friends and i had breakfast at the outdoor area,overlooking the tea plantation.some of the skincare product sold was exclusive to this outlet,glad i bought a few.would surely return if i happen to visit jeju again.

I went in a hot summer day so I can't judge. It has different plants, animals, folk village and cave. If you interest in these things you might like it. I went there because I have free time to spend but I think if the weather is better it will be different

I love visiting botanical gardens whenever i travel.? Unfortunately this is one of the poorer ones and I feel compelled to warn others!? With an entry charge of 7000 won per person, the value is low.Let's start with the greenhouse, it was just ok, nothing exciting.? During sunny days, the greenhouse is like a toasty oven as the ventilation is poor.? There is a variety of plants but they are not well organised or well kept.? Moreover, if you live in tropical parts of Asia, you would have seen most of the fruit trees and plants in neighbourhood backyards, which makes visiting it less exciting.Besides the greenhouse, there are themed areas - e.g. Korean garden, Chinese garden, French garden etc.? I was excited to see these options but after seeing what there was at the Korean and Chinese gardens, i just gave up on the rest.? I don't have the confidence the others will be worth the time.Management of the garden needs to be improved.? When I was there, they were renovating the entrance to the greenhouse.? As a result, the smell from the paint, varnish or whatever that toxic smelling thing is, is overwhelming.? Also, there was lots of noise.? Garden management would have better managed the renovation or at least inform visitors there is renovation going on.? I tried to offer feedback to the folks at the ticket counter on my way out but they didn't seem to care.In summary, there is nothing much to see and the garden is not well taken care of (even if there is no renovation going on, I would have rated it 'Poor').? Go to this place only if you have nothing else to do.The only plus I can think of is ... parking at free!

I love flowers and tropical exotic plants, however we were there in July 2016 we don't find too many flowers around just a few species. We did find kiwi fruit tree in there with its fruits, our first time to see the tree. It was hot and humid, so umbrella and cold bottled water are recommended.

I found much of Jeju island to be very commercialized and crowded with loud tour groups. This is a great place to enjoy the natural beaty of Jeju with smaller groups of people. There is a small entrance fee.  The first half mile is along a wide crushed rock road. It is lined with young   nutmeg   trees. The trees are in the yew family. They are Torreya nucifera and are native to Japan. I  visited in October when the small edible nuts ripen. The nuts are encased in a thin husk that has a wonderful aroma. You will see people collecting them under the large trees.  Eventually the road ends and then you follow a loop trail that is about 2 feet wide it is covered with a hemp rope mat that felt lovely to walk on with bare feet.  The crowds end at the beginning of the narrow trail so you can walk through this section in peace and really marvel at the enchanting colors and smells of the forest and hear the songs of the many birds.  There were signs to watch for snakes but I saw none. The yews are huge.  Make sure to investigate the tree bark it is fabric like and soft. Also many of the other plants have English name labels which is nice. The trail is flat and should take a leisurely couple of hours or less if you rush.  I noticed a lot of people sitting on benches in the first section enjoying picnic lunches.

I can't make of this place. It has plants, caves, a folk village and greenhouses. Yet none of the attractions was really top rate. I would give it a miss and visit attractions with more focus on any one of the above.

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

I called it 3 in 1 experience because we get to see tea plantation, showrooms for tea & Innisfree products and cafe at the same vicinity. It's a place with good product, food & service. It's a memorable experience for me and I enjoyed it very much!

I am used of the garden by the bay in Singapore which is great, so I went there just to depend some time and expecting something just .. so so.I was actually wrong. The garden is nice, outside as inside. The round shape with all kid of plants, the elevator to go on the top and enjoy a great view, the type of gardens outside (japanese, coreen, italien, french...).Sometimes a lack of maintenance but.. definetely a nice place. Entrance is about 7usd for adults. A little train can bring you around but I didnt use it and.. not sure it is free.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012
How this park began is very interesting and I would recommend this place to visit when in Jeju. You learn a lot about different plants, animals, Jeju's history and the volcanic activity in Jeju.

Hallim Park, located western 33km away from Jeju City and west of Mt. Hallasan along the beach in Hallimeup, is one of the most popular tourist spots on Jeju Island. It faces the pleasant scenery of Biyangdo Island, Hyeopjae Beach and Geumneung Beach. The park was established on barren land in Hyeopjaeri, Hallimeup, and covered with tons of earth and began planting assorted subtropical plants in early 1971.

Hallim Park isn't worth making a special journey to go and see. The gardens and varying different areas don't have anything especially interest to see. The animals kept along side the plants are kept in cramped dirty cages and look awful. The tulip garden was pretty, as was were the bonsai trees.

Hallim Park is privately run, which would explain the cost, which is 5x the cost of entrance to Sunrise Peak, a must-do in Jeju.There are many parts to explore within the park. The most interesting sections to me was the albino peacock enclosure and the rapeseed flower garden. The cherry trees at the cherry blossom section were okay (we went during the cherry blossom festival) but why would u need to pay for that when the rest if the island (and Seoul as well) is full of cherry blossom trees.The tropical plants, wildflower and grass garden section were disappointing. There were lots of potted plants which looked unhealthy and unkempt. I really couldn't tell if the garden was supposed to be manicured or wild.Overall, I think the park is quite passable. I wouldn't visit it again, nor would I strongly recommend it to a friend.

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim Park is huge and divided into various sections. You can spend almost a day slowly strolling through the different sections for plants, animals, cactus and you can even visit underground caves. You can also visit a very small old village modelled after the olden days of Korea. It?s a place suitable for all families with kids or senior citizens. The entry ticket is on the expensive side for Jeju.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves

Hallasan National Park is a fantastic place to explore. Firstly, the vegatation between Spring and Fall is beautiful. As you hike to higher elevations the landscape and plants slowly change. Numerous rare and even some endemic species are found here. Concerning wildlife, what visitors are most likely to see are the Roe Deer. These small deer are found throughout the park, and as I hiked quitely we came upon 5-10 throughout our 6 hour trek.In 2007 Hallasan became part of the Unesco World Heritage site calle   Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes  . This honor is only bestoyed on the most unique and important natural and cultural sites on Earth. Hallasan is a geolocial wonder, and is comparable to some of the most iconic national parks in the United States. The park probably deserves 2 days as visitors will want to hike to the crater lake on Hallasan peak, but the entirity of the park holds many exceptional sites. Many trips to Jeju island are scheduled around their trek at Hallasan. Make sure to bring plenty of water, and keep an eye on weather conditions. Hikers must start early if they want to hike to the peak, late arrivals will not be permitted to make the full trek as it takes anywhere from 6-10 hours depending on your pace.
Great place to enjoy walking and see different species of plants, trees, we enjoy palms, something special, very quiet place

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The entrance fee might be a little expensive at KRW 10,000, it's money well spent.I wasn't expecting much and thought it was just another park. Hallim Park proved me wrong. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.

Finally we met a Filipino tourist guide here in Seongeup Village. She can speak english very well but of course we used our native tounge/language so she was able to explain to us very well the history of the village and Jeju as well. It's only from her where we learned that the famous Jeju Black Pig used to eat human poop/dung (but that was circa 1940's or earlier).  We also learned from Grace (name of the Filipino guide there) that Korean women, during the early years, were the one who work for the family while the husbands only stay at home. Sad to hear that. =/ We also learned about the history of Stone Grandfather Harabong as well as the various symbolisms used in Jeju.When in Seongeup, make sure to try their Omija, an herbal drink made out of fermented berries. It can help cure acne, headache, kidney problems and good for diabetics. Kinda pricey but worth a shot. They also have other herbal medicines which you can try. As we all know, Koreans, especially their ancestors, are used to taking medicinal plants so I guess they are really credible enough when they say that this or that plant is effective for healing ailments. Google the benefits of OMIJA.By the way, this is also the place where the famous Koreanovela Dae Jangeum (Jewel in the Palace) was filmed.If you happen to visit Seongeup Village, ask for Grace as a guide. You will definitely learn a lot. And oh, we get to check out old korean houses as well. ^_^NOTE: I think there are many communities within Seongeup village but ask your guide to specifically drop you off at the community where Grace is. No entrance fee as well.
Enjoyed a comfortable tour of the gardens. Has lots of plants, flowers and trees from all over the world. It is is just beautiful.

During winter time, it is surely different experience when you hike up. The view is totally different from summer. Can see icy plant. So beautiful that we wont forget. It might take about 45min to hike up if you are in good shape during winter time as it is not easy to hike up because of cold air.

Could not expect that it is so huge, need a lot of time to visit all the places. So many different plants, birds, even caves. The whole way is well organized, u just need to follow arrows to see everything step by step.There are several cultures and climates that you can see in bigger size than just normal botanical garden. Jeju culture is represented there a lot as well, so will not regret about missing local features.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. I felt good in walking road with various ecology system. All was good to me, but reptile in small transparent box was pitiful. If had time, I want to feel natural feelings in this park keeping my composure. Excellent place to enjoy reserve.

Bet ya you have never seen this before! Its real touristy but well worth the walk. From the convention centre on the east side the first road down to the sea. You can't miss the busses. Taking pictures is best in the morning because of the sun. We went at 16:00 and the sun made it impossible to take good pictures. Got a crappy camera so that could also have something to do with it. Another tip is to follow the olle trail to the east from here after about a 1,5 hour walk (through beautifull orange plantations and up and down tracks paved / dirt) you'll get to the Yakcheonsa Temple. Get from there to the 600 airportbus back to where you came from.
Beautifully laid out. Many different styles of gardens, all beautifully maintained. The class house houses a fantastic variety of plants from all around the world.
Beautiful, clean and very well maintained. It has great collection of plants, cactus etc. Beautiful cave and water garden too. Should allocate 3 hours time to enjoy this place.

Beautiful indoor gardens with several rooms leading off of main garden with specialized environments. The rooms leading from the main garden that I can recall right now are a tropical plant room with orchids, a fern room, water plant room with lilies and hyacinth, and even a cactus room. It is a large indoor garden with many colorful and unusual plants to see. It was raining the day we were there so we were happy that it was enclosed. There are beautiful Korean and Japanese style gardens, among other types of gardens too, outside. Jeju Island has many beautiful places to visit and this botanical garden was a great excursion for us.
Beautiful and blissful with great photo taking opportunites, well nurtured bonsai and plants. Great place to bring kids to see the variety of bonsai plants and neatly arranged garden.

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

After climbing the stairs for the view of the lush, plant-filled centre of the crater, you should definitely walk along part of the black sand beach that arcs around to the ?glass house.? You?ll see some amazing views of Seongsan Ilchubon there, and your pictures won?t be filled with random tourists. There are also bits of sea glass scattered along the shore, shells, and if you walk down the beach far enough, a beautiful, large ledge of lava covered in green moss you can walk on and explore. It was really easy to get to the crater by bus from Jeju-si, and it only took about 75 minutes.

A vast crater overgrown with a diversity of plants, it's especially unique in autumn when waves of silver grass unfold in front of you. Have a leisure walk up to the main viewing platform, you can embrace the incredible view of Mt. Halla. I'd say it's one of the best scenery of Jeju in autumn!

A larger version of Bontanic Gardens. Provide rental of prams for babies/ toddlers. The weather was good when I was there, hands nice and relaxing tour. They have cactus, flowers, plants, water park, caves, birds etc

2000krw entry.    Just beyond the ticket booth are pictures and descriptions of some of the highlights of the area along with bathroom facilities.    Further on, are some small shops and food stalls.      It?s a beautiful walk with lovely plants to get to the waterfall.   There are supposed to be 2 meter long, 20 kilo eels in the pool by the waterfall.   We couldn?t see any.    Waterfall was nice but nothing particularly special.
You travel to get different experiences and this was definitely one of those. Close to Jeju city and free car park. Definitely an adults only/couple only museum.
You pass the Maze Park when you head towards the Lava Cave. My mum and I went to the park after the cave on our way back up to the main road to catch the bus. It was a fun way to kill some time.

You need to do light hike up to Udo-bong Peak to reach this lighthouse park. The park contains several lighthouse miniatures around the world. Went in May pre-summer and you may need to apply sunblock and proper hat to avoid sunburn. Scenery are marvelous if you walk around the island in one day. I arrived about 830am and leaved the island about 2.30pm. Toilet is available near the horse fieldIts a must do list if you visit Jeju Island and i wish to come again to try walk in winter.

You might think a stone park is boring. But it turns out not quite right a statement. Not too many people visit it. You can enjoy 3 different routes. Very calm area with increadible examples of what the nature can present.

You could park and walk to the falls. Entrance was 2000w. Opens at 0900 not crowded. You?re able to walk right up to the edge of the falls for great photos. Some available shops for souvenirs and snacks.
You cant see the holes all it is about. If one wouldnt have known in advance or from the movie what to see(the holes) you wouldnt have found the place. The park is nice.

You cannot pass up going to this park with many trails to accommodate your experience level.  We took on of tge shorter trails but it was one of the steepest.  The views are spectacular and well worth the hike.  A must see if you are visiting the island.

Yes! I love this place for its natural scene and beautiful environment. It is really quiet and peaceful except at the base where there are plenty of tourists. Note there are several hiking trails of different distance and demands. Be sure to read to it and do note the closing time in different seasons. Some closes as early as 1330hr in winter due to early sun set. Most charged entries for vehicles into the car park. Small car (Kia Morning) which I rented from rentalcar.com was charged 1000 won (peanut) Put on right shoes and gear. There are air blower (See pic) available to dust off the mud or dirt from your shoes before u step into your car. Love that. Enjoy the beauty.
Yes! From far away it looks like a gigant clam!. No touring was available when we where there  but we parked near by and walked close and took pictures. It is huge  it is worth seeing!

Wow a brilliant fun dayloads of pic opportunity for all ages spent ages taking pics just great fun and lots to see and participate inparking easy and we got a taxi very easily afterthere's a go kart place just nextdoorplease visit if in jeju and would be a great place if raining to take the children easy spend an hour or more.
Words cannot describe this small but beautiful park. Its a great place for a quiet day out but its got tons of tourists and school excursions kids this time...

With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.
With cool weather.Like a park with natural occurrences.With a romantic atmosphere.Going with family or boyfriend is very good.Is an interesting tourist destination in Korea.
With all the different plants and flowers all over the park there are plenty of photo-ops opportunity.Other than that not much else.

While its really small against Western style theme parks we enjoyed an afternoon on the rides.  Also if you arw a US military service member or have a military ID (they don't know the difference between a dependent or soldier) you can get an amazing deal.  It was 9k won for 2 day combo pass for the theme park and the water park!!! Which is usually 39k won.  There is also a discount if ypu are staying at one of the resort hotels.  The park was clearly designed by someone who has visited and studied the Disney parks specifically Tokyo Disney Sea.  Which isnt a bad thing just needed to be mentioned.  This was our 2nd visit and have never had to wait in a line for the rides.  Also the rides are enjoyable the staff is friendly & helpful and the park is very well maintained.

What a GREAT place to spend the day. Entry was $5 and I did not expect much. We intended to spend 30 minutes here but ended up spending most of the day. Take a picnic and bottle of wine and enjoy the serenity of the park. For a full video review of this place check out my YouTube clip https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LlgzW0VCQHw
We've been here on a cloudy day which gave a nice touch.It's a pretty wal trough the park and they show as well some old korean buildings.It's more nature than the eco park next to it...

Went with my son and husband on a very hot day! Park well laid out with several drink food and shade stops on way round! We spent a few hours to see it all! Caves were a highlight - very interesting and cool!! Reptiles and birds ok - not my thing! Enjoyed water area especially cold showers we could stand under :-)) overall a good place to visit and see a range of sights! Easy to get to on main coastal bus route Enjoy

Went there with the intention to educate my kids on how lava could flow to the sea and came up with beautiful natural shapes such as those seen there. Great to have educational information nearby to explain the formation.  More should be done to explain how small stones also play a part in eroding pitfalls on the rock surfaces It was an easy walk from the carpark.  Some local snacks were sold at the entrance and tickets could be bought via a machine.
Went there Sunday mid-morning. Car park was crowded with locals after /preparing for morning walk. Take a slow stroll to soak up nature's beauty. Boardwalk wide enough for wheelchair access.
Went here with our two sons (8M and 4Y) and it was very interesting and a bit cold.Cheap entrance fee being in Jeju.Easy to park and restaurant in front was OK.

Well worth the hike even on a cloudy day. If you go to see the sunrise like we did and it's dark don't forget to read the signs! We totally missed the sign that said no eating at the top...Oops! We were going full speed on the way up to make sure we did not miss the view. Be advised....trail up and down is not the same. If you want to enjoy both make sure you give yourself enough time. Both trails are beautiful and I wish we had enjoyed the trail going up a little slower. If you are active this should be easy although expect stairs as with any Korean hike! Plenty of parking and bathrooms at the bottom.

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..

Well i get there by accident - really - i didnt plan to visit this park but good thing happened. I had so much fun back there. All labyrinths(maze) are great adventure. Just try to get lost and find way between tries without any map of maze! :P. Tickets are bit expensive but still it worth to go especially if you have kids! Well for grow ups it is also fun ( but make it harder- dont use  map)

We?re staying at the Lotte Hotel and this place is within walking distance.  First waterfall didn?t have any fall at this time due to a drought or off season maybe.  2nd fall was nice & it involved some walking down the stairs.  Overall the park is very pretty with its vibrant colors of the trees and the famous bridge you can walk across.

We were mesmerized with the glass art. Such detailed work! The route made it easier to walk and enjoy all the glass art. Admission fee is 11 000 won. There were also one part of the park that showed glass palace  but we end up walking about 10minutes and no castle was in our sight  quite disappointed. P/S: you can find cute fridge magnet of jeju at the end of the souvenir shop. There were only 1 000 won for one. Very cheap for a fridge magnet I think.

We were initially hesitant to visit the temple as we are not Buddhist.  But when we arrived we were taken in awe by the size of the place and its surrounding.  The garden and pond surrounding the temple would have one mistaken it for a park.  It was really lovely and well set up.  The temple buildings and grounds were also well laid up and pleasant to visit.  Definitely worth a visit.
we went to this lovely park with our children and we ride the horses for a 15 minutes enjoying the spectacular views. I recommend it for a visit.

We went to the beach after hallim park. It was a nice place for my little one to run around as the sand is very soft. Must be a lovely place to relax in summer. The view was beautiful. Lovely cafes along the way and we had nice pizza.
We went to Hallim Park and decided to spend a little time on the beach as it's right next door. Nice place for some fresh air and a quiet walk

We went there with a tour group as part of a package.  It's basically a long walk in the park with a bunch of photo ops.If we had kids with us I would think it was OK.  But not for a couple of retired folks.
We went on a wet and rainy afternoon. The cliff was dull and unspectacular in such weather conditions. We parked at The Seas resort carparked and strolled through their beautiful landscaped grounds.
We went on a hike at Hallasan National Park and the scenery was beautiful. The park was beautiful and well kept.

We went in Jun and there were hardly any flowers. Mainly statues. Nothing much in the cave. Just like a normal park with a small man-made waterfall. Entrance fees not cheap  too. Don't waste your time !

We went at the right season when cherry blossom just bloomed and there was a tulip festival in Hallim park. It's beautiful. There are also 2 caves in this park. This is probably the only park that is worth visiting cause it's one of the biggest.
We went as part of the Yeha Tour to the west. Bit hurried but ok.Few things are not different from any other good park but the lava cave tunnel is special here.

we visited two parks in Jeju. Hallim and Spirited Garden. ticket price was almost the same for both but Hallim was by far much better and bigger with good design and a lot of different and amazing trees and some birds too. It is really a must visit for Jeju visitors to spend around two hours enjoying the park.

We visited on 23rd October. A misfortune happened at about 5.15pm when we were about to leave  our rented car could not start due to no battery. Our baby was temporarily locked in the car so a helpful bystander helped us to opened the door using manual lock and called the car rental company. After a long wait we gotten the staffs at the park to help.the 'gatekeepers' were friendly enough to let us stayed there while awaiting help to arrive. A thin tall lady staff without spectacles came to our help and called the car rental company as we could not understand the options given in Korean. She explained to us and reassured us in English fluently. She also took extra care to follow up and waited til a tow car to help to jump start the rented car. I think by that time her shift is over as few staffs waiting for her too. We are indeed thankful for her and the staffs on that day. Cocomong Ecopark does have a good commendable staff. thank you.Park wise games and design are well thought and worth the entry ticket. The slide down on tire is fun though it looked a bit scary but it is safe. Cafe has got a nice sea view.

We visited for the night market. Nearby there is a multi storey public parking. The first stall butter fried rice with spicy pork is truly delicious and their orange juice (hallabong) freshly made is very nice though it is slightly expensive than the other stores. But it is freshly blend thus I love it and it taste good. Others stall look okay for me.

We visited at the beginning of May and it was cold. It also rained when we were on the beach. So could not enjoy the water.However beach is very nice and clean. We had coffee in the coffee shop on beach which gives you nice view of the beach.Its just opposite Hallim park so can be combined.Would nice to spend a warm and sunny day on this beach.

We visited and there were about 20 buses in the parking lot. The shop where you get the tea or ice cream was very full so we went out to the tea bushes and enjoyed our tea there. We did learn about how tea is made and seeing the actual plant was interesting to me. Wish it was less crowded.

We took many amazing pictures here against the camellia flowers. The walkways around the park were arranged nicely so we spent a few hours here easily. Overall one of the best spots we visited in Jeju this is a place you definitely have to include in your travel plans!

We took a short walk from the nearby peace park to visit this place in October 2016. Entrance fees were nominal but visitors were few.  Looks like not a very popular tourist spot. Just as well  we could enjoy a short walk here without the crowds. Quite a nice place to walk around although there were not so many deer. You could buy some plant food to feed the deer. The main enclosure for the deer is not that big but the park itself has other longer walking paths.  If you do not wish to walk here from the peace park you can take the Jeju City tour bus but need to wait.

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.
We spent over 3 hours in the park and exhibition building.Gives you a perfect view on the history and evolution of mother earth. We really enjoyed and learned a lot.

We rented a car. We reached the Tea Museum just after 12 noon. The car park was already full and we had to park by the side road. The museum is more of an exhibition of tea cups with write-ups on a brief history of tea and the origins of the Osulloc tea. Easy reading for a morning activity. There is a tea merchandise section and a cafe.We ordered the green tea ice-cream and black tea ice-cream. Both were good. The tea was very intense on both the ice cream. The green tea roll was just passable for us. Drop by if you are on the way. I think at certain times of the day there maybe some demonstration on tea but nothing was written in English so not sure of the timing.

We loved the park and spent about three hours. The cherry blossom and canola fields were the best as they were in full bloom. My little one loved the bird park and we even spotted a few peacocks roaming free in the park. The tulips were pretty but nothing extraordinary. We did not explore the caves and the hits.
We liked the place and very well keptWe spent a good three hours here and had snacks coffee and icecream (twice...) All good. easy to park too

We have fun taking photos here even some miniatures looked old and not properly maintained. It would be such nice place to introduce the world famous building and attractions to your kids (and to adult as well). I wish they add more models to the park and revamp the old ones. Nevertheless  it was fun enough for us. Make sure to go early as when there are too many people  they might disturb you while taking photos.Admission fee for adult: approx. KRW9000

We had two rounds of tea tasting - the signature green tea and another caramile version. Both are good but not great. It's more of a Cafe than museum we had a great time buying tea for our family. The sales people speaks good English and is always ready to help.Cafe is a bit crowded but the turnover is fast and it did not take long to buy our drinks and get a seat. The back garden is connected to Innisfree Cafe so don't miss that too.Parking is a pain however so remember to be aggressive. Parking is not restricted to what's marked on the ground in Jeju.
We had fun at this maze park! Seemed easy but not! My son and I had a good time trying to figure the maze out! Kids will definitely enjoy! Lovely place for good exercise too!
We had enjoyed the miniature park. it was fun . my wife love it and I like the detail models of those as a follow model maker.

We got an ATV (40000KRW for 2 hours) and rode around the island. It was really fun and you get to explore the whole island. There are small little cafes where you can just park your ATV and pop in for a coffee and a cake. The water is amazingly clear and blue.

We got a local bus to this park. When we went there it was quite windy so take a sweater.The park is very large with lots of stones to see. There is no cafe so take water or food. It is really worth the visit.
We found the park by accident while just driving around. This was one of the best places to visit in Jeju. I even purchased a miniture old man statute. Must go if you can find it.

We felt a little cheated cause the castle wasn't so much of a castle. More like a small park and it was pricey for the entrance and there wasn't much to see at all. Realised that there are plenty of museums like these to cheat tourist money in Jeju so be selective on which ones you plan to visit. This is definitely not one of them that you should go.

We engaged a Local private driver to bring us to Yongmeori Coast. He made a call to the Relevant Authority to check the weather and tide condition. Yongmeori Coast is situated beside Mt Sanbangsan.The car park was full that day and fortunately we found one lot. Our driver guided us the walking route to the coast.He was indeed a good private tour guide!We were immense into the nature and its beauty. He skilfully captured many memories into pics for us! This trip was my most memorable part in Jeju.

We didnt expect much from this park but was taken in by the amazing grand sight of the rock formations. There is also an interesting folk tale behind these formations. The scenery was beautiful and there was many small trails to explore within the park.

We decided to pop over to the maze park as we were visiting mangajul lava tubes. We were greeted by a ten to fifteen cats basking in the shade. It seems like the owner loves cats. That was a great treat for my cat loving family. The maze itself was great fun and especially if you are in a group. Not very difficult but not as easy. We could easily go around with a stroller though there are a few steps. Has a small cafeteria for icecream and coffee. Overall great fun.

We came with high hopes of being awed by beautiful camellia Flowers but left disappointed. There was really nothing much except the blooming flowers in the greenhouses. Maybe it was the timing of our visit but we felt cheated. Be prepared to walk a bit to visit the various parts of the park. I will not recommend this park.

We came to seogwipo to see the falls and have BBQ. The bridge was close to the parking lot for one of the falls and it is worth a stop to admire views although don't put your hopes up since it is just ok.

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.

We came here but it was very hot and the sun intensity was very high. Its a long walk from the parking lot but worth it when you reach.We didn't go in the water because it was quite crowded when we went. It can be a bit tricky to climb and walk on the rocks so be careful.

We came by using GPS to guide us to the National Park. We entered the part called the Healing Forest. Interesting plants on healing the body. Several small huts/cabins are available for those who may like to stay in the forest for healing and relaxation. Do go into the forest for a real feel of the national park. Entrance is free.
We are so glad we managed to catch such a beautiful sunset here! Had a cuppa latte at the cafe. There are plenty of cafe and restaurants around. Plenty of parking lots too!

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

Waterfall is easily accessible from seogwipo town and surrounded by lovely parks. Entrance fee is 2000 krw but no one was collecting fares when I was there. There is a stairway down to water fall but you can see it from the top easily. Nothing spectacular if you have seen other water falls.

Was visit here coincidentally when asking taxi driver to dragon head but was allright place was beautiful and nice scenery view surround mountain and fresh air was nothing to complain. The park suit for kiddos wiyh some museum as well.

Was expecting to see beautiful blossoms of camellia flowers but was disappointed as the blooms were over at that time. I believe if you come at the right time it will be awesome. The only blooming flowers that we saw were in the greenhouses. Park is not small so there's quite a bit of walking to visit the various parts of the park. Would recommend to check on the bloom timing before visiting the park.

Walking through this garden park is very peaceful and relaxing. There is a cool cave feature so you get to also go into caves. The captive birds are in small enclosures and the peacocks look like there tail feathers have been pulled. Also there is a white sand beach walk across the street after you are done the park. Taxi from Ramada Plaza was 26000 wan. Bus ride home was 3000 wan and took about an hour on the 702.

Walk to the top is quite easy with good views.Don't miss the signpost to the women divers near the bottom on the way down.  They do a few shows a day and you don't have to pay extra to see it.Lot's of parking and eateries in the area

Walk about 5 minutes from the parking lot to arrive at wide open grass field that showcases a cliff side view out to sea.There are tall columns of rock formation that are the site's main attraction.You can also peer down the cliff side walkways down to the waves crashing against the bottom of cliffs.Pathway consist of some stairs and portions just muddy... May be rectified as they were doing some renovation work on paving those sections.

Visited this place in Feb19 and was quite appalled by the treatment of the animals. The rabbits were allowed to roam within an enclosed area accessible to visitors. However there is no one monitoring that the rabbits are treated properly. The living conditions of the animals are filthy. The absolute horror was the black pig show. What's so entertaining about forcing terrified black pigs down a water slide?? Tasteless entertainment with no educational value. Paying the entrance fee of 13000won per person  I would expect some of it to be channeled to upkeep the living conditions of the animals. The blooms in the park were alright with spots for Instagram pictures but nothing spectacular.

Visited this park on my way back from Manjanggul Caves. There were a lot of cats there as it seems the owner is pretty fond of them. They provided me with the map but could finish in about 8 minutes without using it. Nothing thrilling about the place though and one can skip it if short of time..
Visited the park when it was raining. Still very enjoyable and there is some sort a mini bird park in there. Very interesting and relaxing walk through the park.

Visited the Park based on TA reviews. Extremely well done with extensive museums and stone displays. Allow at least 3-4 hours for the visit. Enormous work has gone into the development of the Park. Should be in the Top 5 attractions in Jeju outside the beaches.

Visited on a rainy day.  Limited parking - so had to park along the road and take a muddy path through the team garden.  Tea shop was very crowded to went to the Innisfree jeju House about 60 m away - great food and can make your own soap.

Visited at mid-day in August.  It was very hot but beautiful.  had a picnic near the carpark and took a stroll along the trail on the east end of the beach. There is a small freshwater spring on the beach at the start of the trail

Very well manicured plantations and garden areas. Museum is professional and store was well laid out with all their delicious teas with samples in bottles for customers to smell.Limited parking space though. Could see people parking by the sides of roads all over the vicinity.Cashier staff was very helpful combining our global tax refund receipts when we made two purchases separately.Ice cream was good. Cream roll would prefer it like a Swiss roll where cream is well spread around the roll. Current style has too much dry cake at the sides.Beautiful packaging as always.
Very scenic and quiet place although really hot for the summer. Take the train to get to the various sections of the park and bring a picnic mat if you are keen on having some nature time.

Very nice place and worth a visit. It will require you around 2 to 3 hours to visit the entire park. Train ride is nice too. Beautiful scenery. Love how the park or each train stop has different theme. It maybe very hot during sumer time
Very cute themepark to while away a good 1-2 hours. Good for summer when it's too hot outside. The rooms are separated into various different themes. Particularly good for silly selfies!!
Unfortunately it was raining during our stay. I believe that in a good weather we would appreciate the park more.

UNESCO heritage site in Jeju. Location near the restaurant that sells live abalone and woman diver. It's crowded with holidaymakers but well worth the view. There are some cafe and restaurant at the car park. Didn't catch the sunrise as we were staying at the other side of the island.
Unesco Heritage attraction. Ample parking space and tourist information. Worth a visit but be prepared for it. Be ready to spend a day.

Understand that the day we went weather was harsh as there?셲 typhoon warning ; the parking escort/attendant wasn?셳 helpful at all is was raining and very windy we were traveling with a 2yr old baby  ask him nicely to let us ?쁃rop off??only but he insisted that we go to the other carpark to park our cars (the carpark has open lots and a few cars are coming out) ; I don?셳 know his against foreign or what but after we parked our car Far far away carrying the baby  pram  umbrella diaper bag we saw he letting the locals go in and park . We were so piss ; and it ruin our trip in jeju as my toddler felt sick after. His now down with flu thanks to them and I still got 12 more days in Korea . Very disappointed  will not recommend any of my friends and family period
Udo Island Lighthouse Park - Really a good place for a nice evening stroll. Loved the lighthouse too.

Udo is a beautiful place that we have no regret to visit and spent 3 hours to round the island with rental electric car for KRW35000. Most shop offer KRW20000 for 2 hours and we find it will be a rush that you can?t really enjoy the scenic view of the island. Returned ferry ticket cost KRW8500/person. Rental car is currently not allowed to enter the island as a one year control started Aug 2017 so we parked it at covered parking near the port before we depart to Udo.

Two things to see here: 1) small dried up crater top that I didn't even notice after walked by. 2) a loop of man made path with silvergrass on both sides for photos. Quite crowded on my day of visit even silver grass is not uncommon in most park. Many locals come to catch the famous Korean TV series scenes for photos as the silver grass is in season.
Turkoise waters and great views of the beaches from multiple restaurants and coffee places all along the shoreline.May be a bit difficult to find parking though.

Travelled by ferry from Seongsan habour (price 5500W two way). Upon reaching the island turn right to the carpark to purchase bus tickets (price 5000W). Bought the red tickets (you can only board the red buses with the red tickets and blue bus for the blue tickets). The bus is a hop on hop off bus (can only go forward not backward); you'll have to hold on to your ticket to board the bus for the next stop. Buses come every 20-30 mins. First stop was udobong peak - we had peanut ice cream (must try!!! Albeit a little sweet. Udo is known for the peanuts). The climb up is a little slippery so I won't recommend it on a rainy day. Requires some fitness to make it to the top but it is not too difficult. Otherwise a very relaxing climb that my family and I enjoyed very much! Stopped also at the Beacon mound (second stop on red bus) which was a nice selfie spot and then headed to the beaches before catching the ferry back to the mainland (last ferry back to jeju 5.30pm). The island is quite touristy though; expect things to be a bit more expensive.

Today I hired a car and drove to Hallasan National Park. Only 1000 won to enter and park.Plenty of clean toilets. An excellent Visitor center who gave me an informative map. I did not have time to do Eorimok Trail today but will do tomorrow.I climbed the Eoseungsaengak Trail which is only 1.3km and has wooden steps all the way up so no problem with any fitness level.30 minutes up to the top. Great 360 deg.view of the surrounding mountains and a small Japanese bunker to see too. Friendly Jackdoor birds wanting a scrap of food..
This waterfall is easily accessible from Seogwipo city by taxi or bus. You can also take a walk in the Olle trail and park around the area

This was our last stop in Jeju. We arrived right after sunset and were able to walk around the island and enjoy the beautiful nature area and then walk back over the bridge while it was lit up. Good activity for young children to just get out and run. Best of all it was free! There is also a free public restroom in the parking lot.

This was one of the most interesting things I visited in the cheesy Jeju Island. It's a piece of architecture. Everything is about meditation. The buildings are angled to frame Seongsan Ilchulbong volcano and they give you different perspectives of it. I found it very cool.The entrance fee was $5 but it is worth it. You have to walk from the parking lot to this area  it's about 10 to 15 minutes. The views are nice.

This was my favorite amongst all the waterfalls I have been to as you can get pretty close to it. You can even wade in the pool if you want to as it's quite shallow. Very nice place to take photos. Took a short trek to Sojeongbang waterfall from the same parking area. For those driving you can enter the phone number 7331530 into the gps. Admission fee is 2000 won for adults. Make use of your youth ID card if you are below 24 years old! It's half the price and can save you a lot if you go to many attractions. Closes at 6pm though so plan your itinerary properly!

This spot looks like it exists purely for the 15-20 tour buses that were there when we visited as its pretty much a rock with a different shape that you can see in the picture. Save your time and your parking fee and check out the world heritage listed rocks formations around the island otherwise you will need just 1 min here to take a photo and be off again

This spectacular waterfall is worth the visit. Parking is easy and there is a small fee to walk down to the bottom of the falls. The bottom is all rocks so it could be difficult to maneuver for some. At the top is a lovely art gallery and cafe.

This show is highly recommended as it showcases the traditional beat and a fun show which can be enjoyed by the entire family. A shuttle service can be arranged at the ticket office after the show for only 1000KRW. There's a nearby park which you can visit before the show.

This place is really poor. Just plastic dinosaurs many with broken claws or tails. Our son loves dinosaurs and was pretty excited upon arrival. But for the money this attraction does not represent any value for money. Also around the grounds are many rusty rails which would cause nasty cuts if children fell on them. Some of the grassy areas would be nice to sit down in summer/spring but I would certainly never return.... especially in winter. The bronze raptors in cocomong park are far better than anything in this park.... Its in serious need of an upgrade or twenty.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.
