review: This place is pretty new I believe  it wasn't built 3 years ago when I visited. It was a very enjoyable walk around  the place is pretty huge and in some areas  construction hadn't finished yet. It's basically a really huge garden  lots of really pretty flowers and areas to take photos of. And I believe there are some animal enclosures somewhere in the middle of the park too. Our guide recommended visiting this place and the cave they had here  saying that it was all better than Hallim Park. Though I personally preferred Hallim Park. I found the cave here to be pretty creepy and really dark  best to skip over if you aren't into caves. There's nothing much to see in the cave anyway.

This place is just outside the love land . There is a huge parking lot just behind this row of shops. In front of these shops selling sausages and fruits is the road . You can borrow a bottle of water and row it down the road and miraculously it will come to a stop and row backwards! Opposite the road is a grazing field where you can see cows . Ok a visit if you are in the area.

This place is just great! I love Hallim Park especially the caves! they are so mystical!! the parks has most of the natural attractions. The park is huge and you may need to spend hours in it to enjoy everything that they offer. It was so relaxing and very nice.

This place is getting very tired. The models are worn and many broken.  Needs significant investment.  We went with friends and had 3 girls 5-6yrs and two older children.  They enjoyed themselves but probably would have as much fun together at a park.  The animals were the highlight for them.  They enjoyed feeding them.  Everything that you do inside has an extra cost except the 3D film.  Worth a look if you have young children.

This place is famous not only because of the movie but also the breath taking scenery here. You can access the place with great view here. Don't forget to walk further in to other side of the rock whereby the movie taken place. There is a small park in which you can have picnic and enjoy the scenery there.
This place is amazing. I was awed by the dark rocks and the beauty of the sea as it splash to the rocks. They also have a park where you can spend chatting and picture-taking.

This place is a hit with the tourist. Famous for Jeju local tea. If you are driving parking is free of charge and there is someone manning the traffic when it gets busy. There is a small museum showcasing the tea history but don't expect to learn much. Then you will walk into the tea shop which is quite huge followed by the cafe. We tried the green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll and jeju orange drink. Mind you the queue is very long but fast moving. I like their green tea ice cream and the swiss roll. There are few corners inside and outside of this place which is IG worthy. Nice place for the environment but it's not really museum per say. They have a branch in Seoul in case you are wondering.
This park was a five minute walk from the beach and the perfect way to pass the afternoon. It's huge! Such a great deal for the ticket price.

This park situated about 30 minutes drive from Jeju-si. Me and my husband spend about 1 hour at the park but we failed to ring the bell. We arrived late in the evening so we couldn't spend more time there since it was getting dark.

this park is right next to Jeongbang Waterfalls  and only costs 500 SKW. We spent an hour there reading up the interesting story of how Xu Fu  the elixir who was said to have stopped here while his envoy with 500 (3000) boys and girls set sail in search for immortal medicine for the Qin Emperor in 219BC. He was said to have left inscriptions on the cliff next to the waterfall marking his presence there.

This park is relatively new and a haven for kids. Within the park there are play areas for toddlers and young kids. There is a sandpit  a tube slide  an outdoor playground  swings  car and train rides  flying fox  indoor playground etc. The train and car rides are available at extra charges.There is a baby changing room  makes it convenient for parents with babies. Flying fox is for kids above 100cm but they have the mini version for kids below that height. Indoor playground is a rather big area which is toddler friendly. There are seats for parents to wait while the kids play their fill in the indoor playground. There is also a restaurant within the park with amazing sea views. My daughter had an amazing time as the park was not crowded when we visited. Overall its a nice park to visit if u have kids below age of 7.

This park is huge! it is divided into different areas with different themes. It has a great variety of plants and birds. There are also two underground tunnel caves which enrich the overall visiting experience. There is also an area with seasonal flowers.  Great spot for photo-taking. Highly recommended for family with children. Allocate at least two hours visiting time here.
This park is a whole bunch of Korean fun with a little bit of history mixed in with stuff for kids. The surrounds are peaceful and the coffee shop is a great place to finish off.
This park have what kids like: dinosaurs. They need a good painting job that I noticed but kids don't care about it. So if you have children this place is nice for them

This park has lots of models 1/25 scale of the real landmarks of the world including thw egypsian pyramids the eiffel tower the white house the forbiden gardens of china the roman ruins the mexican pyramids.....etc etc it has a Korean buffet next to it with real korean food
This park has a trail  insect specimens  pig show  petting zoo and several activities such as horse riding and tangerine picking.It is a good excursion place for everybody especially for family.

This museum is one of the most popular of the 50+ on Jeju Island and the carpark was packed with tour buses when we arrived. But if you can manage to get a slot on one of the formal tea ceremonies it really takes you out of the bustling tourist crowds and takes you to another place altogether. The time and care taken for all the preparations was amazing and could not have been more different to having a casual cuppa at home! I am not sure they do them in English - our host spoke in Korean but our little group had an interpreter to help us out. The venue used for this ceremony is also amazing. Beautiful minimal stone and wood shaped furniture in a sunlight-filled pavilion looking out onto the lawns of the museum. We also had a glimpse into the underground tea cellar area and a quick tour round the tourist shop. The collection of tea cups from different countries and eras was fascinating too in the area next to the shop.

This miniature park is more for children & the young. Needless to say  my little nephew & myself still had fun photo-taking & running around. I wish there were more miniatures to see. But still worth a visit if you haven't travelled half of the world yet

This miniature park had all the famous attractions from around the world which was great for viewing  especially when we haven't had the chance to see the real thing. However  you could see the place was a bit old and definitely needed some maintenance. So this place is definitely not for the fussy  but still worth a visit if you had time.

THis Maze Park is located between Manjanggul Cave and Gimnyeongsagul Cave. It was designed by the world famous company and jeju National University. The Park contains a maze that has 7 view incorporated in it. and here are three skywalks called ?gureum dari? and an observatory. There are four ways to get through the maze from the entrance. We had funny and enjoyable time!
This little mini-park was cute and a fun little walk-through of famous landmarks from around the world. It only took about an hour to walk through.

This is the place where Running Man shooting happened previously. Nice place to spend some time but it will be time consuming.Didn't manage to play the maze. But I'm like facade of the design of this park. And it is chilling too!

This is only a nice experience if it is not crowded. With us entered a family if four and they easily blocked 2-3 displays. The start of the tour is great. A lot of great photo opportunities. They gibe you examples and show how to pose. But suddenly this stops in the middle and you end up in a huge room with Aladdin Indiana Jones a volcano eruption? We had no clue what to do there.At the end there is a bug parking lot outside with even more displays. So if you are into instagram and pictures - this is yours. If not... well it is entertaining though. Unless there are tons of visitors.

This is not your traditional beach. It is quite rocky and has limited sand however really spectacular geographical features to see here. Lots of restaurants nearby and also you can visit Hallim park for a few hours. Think this beach would have been better in the height of summer (July- August).

This is not a place for adults like us because the tour guide could only provided us with the very basic information about the dinosaurs for the children packs traveled with us. The park also has birds and rabbits for the kids to feed and play with. We think we?셱e a bit ?쐎ut of date??for this place.

This is more like a nice park rather than a garden. They have beautiful walks among the trees and you can have tea and cakes in a small restaurant with the terrace seats looking out the wide green field. But the staff can?셳 speak English so there must be a tour guide to take you here.

review: This is located in the eastern part of Jeju Island. Taxi fare is around 30KRW one way. The place is well maintained and lots of Cats running around the park.

This is better known as Jeju Love Land Park and I thought it was hilarious! Everything that could be penis shaped is penis shaped it is full of sculptures pictures dioramas. I wouldn't call it educational or a museum but a sex themed amusement park and indeed I was amused!

This is a well maintained natural forest. You can walk here after visiting the Roe Deer Observation Centre or take the Jeju City bus.  There are many trails and a fair amount of visitors. Entrance fee is payable and a car park is available at the entrance.

This is a very spectacular waterfall plummeting down into the ocean. The boulders add to the fun of the attraction clambering over them to see the waterfall more directly .Very well organised walk from car park down to waterfall area. Some interesting stalls at the entrance. Again very cheap to visit.

This is a very lovely maze park with a beautiful garden! We absolutely enjoyed the hour we spent here. The garden is well kept and we were given little bags of cat food to feed the 40 cats scattered throughout the garden.

This is a sex park the creation of art students.I searched for this on net and thought that it is a rare park seen anywhere in the world and I SHOULD VISIT IT.I was solo without my wife or friend and so duel in mind to visit thisbut I visited this and found so many statues in different sex making positions.There were people either with their partners or friends but I was the only one solo.But I am not shy and of a higher age of 63 and sporting during travel and tour.I took lot of photoes of these statues and some were taken with theb by the hands of girls or ladies in my camera.I felt nothing wrong when they dare to visit and see and thought they will not shy taking my photo.This is a park to be visited with open non pejudised minded people.If you have free time of 2 hours in the morning you can visit it and enjoy.Of course with photo in tour camera.You would not find this anywhere in the world in a open air park form.I SUGGEST NOT TO TAKE YOUR KIDS HERE.

This is a pretty big park that has a little bit of everything from history folklore and stones.  I had to convince my friends to check it out and only won when i told them it was like 15 minutes from where we were staying.  However they both were quiet happy with the decision since it was empty and just a lovely walk through nature with some great smells.  Even the trash cans are made out od stone pits.  I thought we would only go for like 30 minutes but ended up being there for an hour and a half.  Other bonus is that for the month of may there is no entrance fee!
This is a must-go place for the tourists. The price may not be the cheapist but variety of seafood is exellent.Parking is not difficult.
This is a MUST go attraction in Jeju. You will need around 1- 1.5hrs to complete the entire trail. Parking will be 1000 won

This is a manmade park-like garden with a variety of plants and trees and water features. It is well worth the time it takes to walk through the grounds  just for the experience of viewing the bucolic setting. The main feature is Michon Cave which really didn't dazzle us as much as it apparently was supposed to. It's just a cave in which one walks down a slope to see some tacky lights and statues. The park  on the other hand  is scenic and pleasant. There are some concessions where they sell the usual tourist stuff.

This is a great place to go inside the city to get some quality exercise. The trails are in great shape and the views are magical.Going for a walk is easy and fun. Finding a parking spot is a little more challenging. This is inside the city so it is a very popular spot. Great for the whole family.

This is a fun place for the family !  To enjoy this place to the max you must not be shy about lying on the floor or doing funny expressions to pose to achieve the photo effect .  We had great fun as a family n have a good laugh as we review the photos taken.  There's also a outdoor sculpture park which we enjoyed doing funny pose with the sculpture ! We were there on a Sunday about 1030am there wasn't a crowd that allow us to have more time at each exhibit to pose without worrying on holding up others.Go n have fun !

This is a farm for Green Tea. First and foremost it is near the Glass park 5 mins drive away. So if you are planning to visit this place and have no budget constraints and have lots of time you can consider to spend 30mins at the glass park as well.The Tea farm sells tea (of course) and remember to try the green tea ice cream in the building. You can walk around the farm but be careful of the snakes. We seen one there.Nice place to visit whether alone in a group or with your family and kids.

This is a circular beach that turns into a lake on the rising tide  then dries again on the ebbing tide. m The water is not too deep (about a meter) and the half moon shaped beach is one of the largest in Jeju. The sand is particularly delicate and soft on the feet. The stone sculptures are worth a viewing too. Lots of things to do nearby  Folklore Village  Namwon Keunang and Seopjikoji. Loads of free parking close by.
This is a BIG park. There is a lots of nice scenery for photo shooting.  Do spent more time to walk around and train ride.

This is a beautiful destination. I would consider this a must do for all foreigners visiting Jeju Island. We did this stop as a part of our self drive 5 day holiday during the kids fall break. What I loved was the the design of the building and landscaping made the most of the site. It reminded me of visiting an upmarket winery. There is a fabulous view from the tower over the tea fields fabulous art displayed inside and precious tea cups to look at the amazing smell & sight of seeing tea roasting and demonstrations. The outside had sculptures. The kids loved airy ambiance of the cafe & wolfed down the Green Tea Swiss Roll. I loved my dacquoise! Plenty of parking bathroom facilities Well Done!

This beach was very beautiful and relatively clean. Water was clear and not too cold fot September. Altough it was posted reccommend  not to swim bc season ended in august the water and weather was great. Bathrooms were close by (though toilet paper was out at the one on the beach). The water was easy to swim in with children as it was very shallow and not rough. Got busier toward aftwrnoon with tourist buses and crowds though. Nice also as there were restraunts and snacks within walking distance as well as showers. 2000 won for parking but was worth it.

This beach was really clean and had many food facilities available. There was free parking. We did come in October but I could definitely see this place full of people in the summer. It is relatively close to Jeju city and has quite a bit to offer.

There really isn't much flora and fauna (this was in March) to speak of. Even indoor plants don't seem to flourish. The only nice thing about this place is there is a big park in which you can lie down on and enjoy the sun!

There is nothing much here at the museum but the green tea ice cream and the green tea cake roll are fabulous! The green tea cake roll sold out in a very short period of time! We reached there at around noon time and we were so lucky that we took the second last roll! I guess the cake roll is pretty popular among the locals too as we saw a lot of locals stopping by at the cafe. I saw an O'Sulloc Cafe at Myeongdong too. We went in the morning and there were still quite a few of green tea cake rolls there. I wanted to get a cake roll the night before I flew back to Singapore (in order to maintain the freshness) but the staff told us that it has been sold out! The green tea cake roll tastes really good when it's eaten fresh. People who don't like the cream in the middle might not like the cake. Other than food you can go all the way to the third floor to take some photos. Personally I feel that the scenery outside of the building is much more nicer. There's a big park right in front of the tea museum there are people who lie down and chill on the grass. There's tea plantation located opposite of the tea museum. We are allowed to wander around there for more pretty photos.

There is a parking lot for self park and that was handy. Luckily we found a spot as someone was leaving. Hiked up to the top for fabulous views. Came back down and had lunch at a local place just down the road since the car was parked in the lot we didn't want to try parking somewhere else. The local place was very good. Definitely have to go to this tourist destination if you go to Jeju

There are spacious parking area provided for a visitor which is very convenient to whom that driving a car here. You need to buy a ticket for entrance bit it is not that pricey. The cave requires you to have a long walk with a majestic view inside the cave. Highly recommended and a must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

There are several museum of sex & health in Jeju islands.  Jeju Loveland is one of them located a short drive from Jeju Town or Jeju Airport.  It is also a stop of Jeju Golden Bus City Tour.  There are hundreds of sexy and comic sculptures which are placed outside in a well maintained park.  There is also a soft core art galleries and adult toy stores where things are quite expensive. The entry fee: Won 12000 Timing: 0900 to 2300 hrs. Entry allowed for adults above 20 years of age.  It is something different.

There are places in Jeju that convince you that you made the right decision to go there -- they're just really beautiful. Oedolgae is one of those places. It's just a photo spot that will take about 15 minutes of your time. The rock formation is interesting and the place is just lovely in a natural way. I gave this a 4/5 because it's not difficult to get there from the entrance of the park -- no steep mountains and such to climb in order to see the view.There's not much to do here -- just check it out and move on.

There are many glass exhibits in this park with indoor and outdoor sections. There is a myriad of colours once you step inside and it is sure to lift your mood. It is recommended for families and couples as there are many chances for memorable photos. You can try out glass blowing if you have the time and willing to pay.

There are a lot of food choices in the market  especially a lot of shops selling the Jeju oranges and Jeju orange juice. You can easily get souvenirs from the market. Most of the shop keepers can speak English/Mandarin. There is a free car park just 1 min on foot from the market  another one with charge right inside the market.

The wonder of nature in Jeju!Take note that there are a few visitor centers around Hallasan National Park.  Decide the trail you want to hike before heading to the visitor center.Info extract from VisitKorea website:Hiking Course - Seongpanak Trail: Seongpanak  Dongneung Peak9.6 km / 4 hrs 30 mins each way- Eorimok Trail:Eorimok  Nambyeok Bungijeom 6.8 km / 3 hrs each way- Eoseungsaengak Trail: Eorimok  Eoseungsangak Peak1.3 km / 30 min each way- Yeongsil Trail: Yeongsil - Nambyeok Bungijeom5.8 km / 2 hrs 30 mins each way- Gwaneumsa Trail:Gwaneumsa Temple - Dongneung Peak8.7 km / 5 hrs each way

The water park is ok. It would have been way better if you didn't have to pay extra for swim vests and extra for sun beds. So practically paying entrance fee doesn't mean you go and have fun. You are forced to spend good amount of money to have a good time.

The village was rather quiet and not as lively as in the pictures shown online. We were expecting to see interesting performance with some dancing. The actual performance was below par with just 2 ladies playing stringed instruments. There were no animals around except for 1 horse. Most of the houses were bare. The Dae Chang Geum theme park touted was actually just a small hut with some boring exhibits!
The view is not bad and you can see many small fishing boat parking there. But really not particularly impressive so I think it can be skipped if run out of time
The view is magnificent! The haenyu women were modeerately fun to watch. Parking is atrocious! The walk to see the sights is rather difficult.

The trail is relatively easy and is one of the shorter trails that takes you up Hallasan. The views along the trail are amazing and very well maintained. There are plentiful rest stops along the trail with excellent views of the surroundings. There are 2 carparks here. Do wait a little or arrive early to gain access to the car park nearer to the trail. The outer carpark requires a 2 km walk. Parking is very limited and controlled vehicle entrance to the car park near to the trail. Cater around 4 to 5 hours for a return trip from the nearer car park. Definitely worth a visit.
The theme park stays true to its name. Loved the sceneries and took plenty of photos in there. The train ride is also enjoyable. Perfect for any kind of traveler.

The tea museum isn?셳 the highlight. It?셲 the cafe after. Super crowded but the staff does a great job making orders and moving people through. The garden outside is nice to walk through and the tea field makes for nice photos. Parking was free.
The sunset at Oedolgae was beautiful. It was free parking and free entrance to go in. You can go down to the sea level but we chose to be seated at the top where we can see the skyline.

The street food stalls at night were awesome in the market. However all the good one has long lines and slow moving as most of them are cooking in front of you. Not knowing which one is the best  we choose to join the crowd and stand in line with others and skipped the other with short lines. Parking is terrible even Google Maps shows many nearby parking lots. We tried two separate lots and both were full. Instead of waiting someone to pull out  I ended up parking on the side of nearby street and walked to the market.

The Sanbanggulsa Temple is located SSW of Mt. Hallasan directly at the coast. It is a very unique and colourful temple which reminds us more on the temple in Taiwan as in Korea mainland. The temple is located just below Mt. Sanbang. We had our junior with us but with older kids it is probably a nice tour on top including the temple. The view from the temple is very nice and gorgeous. Probably from top of Mt. Sanbang even better. The area is quiet and peaceful.? Except the opposite place where noisy? Korean caterwaul being played at a swing boat. The place is not reachable for stroller and wheel chair. Parking place available. Entrance fee is negligible for parking and temple access. It is definitely worth to stop and to spend some time. Religious people are probably also allowed to pray i guess. Doors are open.

The road to this temple is a single carriage way and you drive carefully.  Parking is free. Before I reached the temple I can hear the chanting and is was so soothing.  It just calm a city travellers. I didn't take any pictures inside the temple only the surrounding. It would be great to have a audio or a translator/guide to explain more of this historical and majestic temple.  The sea view from the temple is stunning. Do check out the temple second floor.

The place was drizzling when we got there and managed to squeeze in one last parking lot beside the tea museum. eent straight to the tea museum and the place was really crowded. it showcase the tools used in tea productions and Got a few tastings of various type of tea and souvenirs. Went for the famous ice cream dessert and drink - good. Next walk over to Innisfree building where they have an open area for children to  play with the playdough and display of cosmetics product as well as a cafe with seating area. Outside tourist were busy taking pictures of tea plantations and themselves !

The place is not well-maintained  to say the least. It felt like a haunted theme park experience rather than a nice museum. The place was empty from visitors  basically there were hardly any staff present. The installations are rusty  the cafe and the restaurant were closed down. All in all  it felt haunted therefore we left with some bizarre feelings. I'm sure once it was beautiful but neglect made its damage.

the place is fun for walking between different kind of plants and animals. there are 3 caves and the weather inside it is cold during the summer time so you can walk there if you feel hot. there is also folk village and a water park

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

The parking is free . Entrance fee was 2000W per Pax. You first descend about 5 minutes to a blue pond with the first waterfall . Beautiful and stunning . Then you proceed to the second waterfall about 10 walk . There was a third waterfall but it was about 40 minutes walk so we decided not to do that one . A five minute walk brought us to a bridge  which would bring you to another route . Overall expect to spend between 1-2 hours here .

The parking is 1000w. Don?t stop right after the entrance keep driving or you?ll end up walking very far. The trail is well marked no chance of getting lost. I got there about 0900 and it wasn?t busy. When I was heading back to the entrance at 1200 it was getting very crowded. The ?peak? wasn?t much of a peak. It was a flat staging area with the rock slab marking the elevation. There is a trail that leads off left of the seating area and one behind the rock slab. I followed it about 1 hour before I decided to turn back. I wasn?t sure where the path led and my car was at one end. Beautiful but easy hike. Little to no shade to wear sunscreen or hats.

The park will appeal more for kids rather than adults. The train ride provides a nice experience and there are some attractions in the park that caters for children. The tour in the park took us about 3 hours to finish.

The park was quiet when I visited. It was an easy walk with nice trees and scenery. It had a great calming effect on me. Love it. Just 5 minutes drive from the park is the Hanwha Resort Jeju which I went for a fantastic spa treatment. My afternoon was made perfect !

The park was probably pretty nice 4 or 5 years ago but now everything is falling apart and some exhibits aren't even open. My son is obsessed with going there but he is only 3 and anything dinosaur related makes him happy.
The park was poorly maintained  the water in the pond was murky and had many fallen leaves. The minatures looked so fake and some had paint chips. Give this a miss.

The park is very big so wear comfy hiking shoes!  We only saw 1 wild deer after walking the whole trail. There are however deer in captive just after the entrance. Not a bad place if you have the time and effort.
the park is large with wide variety of plant species but we did not find anything special that is worth the visit. The park was clean but needs more work to make it attractive to visitors.

The park is definitely worth a visit for people who appreciate the beauty of nature. there's so much too see that one should reserve at least half a day for that park. The caves are also very impessive. there are restrooms and benches all over the park and everything's very clean. the collection of bonsai are impressive as well as the village of traditional jeju-houses.
The park is a very big park to cover specially in a hot summer day .Has many different sections and it is easy to get lost without a map .It is a must see place
The park has 2 parts..indoor and outdoor.It just like walking around a garden that full with glass sculpture. Nice view. Worth a visit.
The park around the waterfall area was simple and not too long and tedious for a walk with your family. Waterfall was nice too for a photoshoot. Overall was great!

The only one of dolphin experiential theme park in Korea.Enjoy the nature's present at Marine Park. We are trying for people to feel what is the nature's present through communion with dolphins. We hope you to experience our programs beyond your imagination. -Programs1.Dolphin Training Experience 2.Dolphin swimming & Snorkeling3.Dolphin Diving4.Dolphin Prenatal Training Project

The museum has some interesting and sometimes humorous displays. The real attraction here is the outdoor sculpture park. A walk around it is  like no other outdoor display of art your have ever seen. Well worth the price of admission.This experience may not be for everyone. Obviously it is sexually oriented.

The museum can be improved with more English explanation. Go to the open air top for the best 360 view of the area and plantation. There are signs at the plantation warning of snakes but none spotted during our visit. There is a crowd at the cafe and shop but the turnover is quick as most of them followed a group tour and hence can't linger that long. You can get a seat if you are not in a rush. The stuff are expensive but it won't deter a green tea fan. Do be extra careful when crossing the roads to the opposite car parks. The cars and trucks are speed demons.

The museum and park are both really engaging. We learned a lot and enjoyed a family discussion on history and human nature. The park is really gorgeous and the entire experiences as moving. A highlight of our trip.
The maze park was a fun family event and we really enjoyed it. It was not overly hard so families with smaller kids can enjoy it as well.
The market is big with several lanes. There is one particular street with amazing street-food in the evenings. Parking is a bit of problem though

The Jeju village is 5 minutes from Hyeopjae beach with plenty of restaurants and cafe nearby. It's a perfect place to start off your day or end it. It's a beautiful good size historical park with plenty of things to learn do and it's kids friendly with lot of interactive events to include a mini zoo. I would definitely put it on the itenary and start enjoying or end the day.

The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

The initial part was fine. There are 3 routes within the park. Route 1 was ok. Route 2 was getting creepier as one approached further into the route. What they didn't tell you is that this is a graveyard from the ancient times and we were walking around the graves.
The house and church were korean drama set. It's easy to reach from parking lot and the scenery is beautiful. I think no need to enter the house/church  just enjoy the surroundings.
The HOLOGRAMCONCERT is the biggest attraction in our themepark.

The highest mountain in South Korea.  Several paths and some are easily accessible by public bus.  I chose the one to the summit up and down.  Clear sign and a small shop before going up the summit.  Good view.  Can get a certificate to the summit in the park office.

The hexagonal basalt columns are similar to what you see at the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but you can't actually walk on them unless you try accessing them from a park further down. There is a well laid observatory path which takes you through the best view points to view the structures. Very touristy when we were there so it was a bit of a mad house but worth visiting when in Jeju.
The green tea latte is nice ! Not too sweet for me ! Just nice !  Went over to Innisfree shop ! Taxi fare from Jeju SkyPark hotel till there  cost me around won 32000!

The folk museum is a huge cultural town-like place located at the south-east portion of Jeju Island. It is easily accessible by car. For those who are self-driving like I did fear not there is an abundant number of parking lots to park your car and it's completely free.The admission fee for an adult cost around 10000 won. Considering the size of the museum it's a rather reasonable price. The museum is divided into many different sections showcasing different cultural aspects of Korea's rich history.If you get tired from walking or can bear the scorching sun the museum provides a tram service that brings you around the museum stopping at different attractions. There are also many different restaurants and snack booths selling traditional Korean meals as well as snacks. If you have never been to Jeju before do take the opportunity to visit this place at least once! Ideal for all ages.

The drive from jeju airport area to aqua planet is around 1 hour 10 minutes passing by many small towns. The entry tickets were quite costly and I used klook to get some discounts with the tickets. Upon parking the rented car outside the vicinity of aqua planet then picked up a number from the machine next to the ticket counter. Waited for the number and redeemed my wristbands without much hassle. Kids under 3 can enter for free.There are plenty to see and we were in time to watch fish feeding a seal and dolphin show. Outside the facilities has really good view and many people were taking photos.Food in the food court was not too bad and similar like incheon airport have to be ordered and paid at the cashier counter and picked up from the individual sections when the device buzzes.Overall experience was great and worth every cent spent.

review: The crater is now full of trees and plants therefore looks like another mountain but I give it a rating of 5 for the fantastic views and park. Nice place to take a relaxing walk.

The climb is relatively easy and it's not necessary to visit there to watch the sunrise. The view in the morning is also great. There is also alot of parking space at the bottom so there no need to worry about that.

The cliffs are beautiful and wondrous. Be sure to go very early as there will be less visitors then. Once the tourist buses come and go it will be difficult to move around. You can get there by walking from Jeju International Convention Centre and going out the back door into the park and walk towards the left side of the park for about 10 minutes.
The caves are indeed worth the visit. It?s a UNESCO world heritage site with carefully preserved Lava tubes and caves. The whole Jeju island was designated as a GeoPark in 2010.

The cause of forming a wonderful Island is a Volcano and hiking to the top of it is a wonderful experience. Roads up to the height of 1100 mtrs are made cautiously and traveler friendly for pleasure with least possibility of an accident. The hiking experience is also beyond the expression in words. I can only say that visiting JEJU and Hallim park are synonyms.

The cafe is pretty good with green tea drinks of all kind and dessert! We tried the green tea ice cream which was really good. However almost EVERYONE comes here so it will take some time to find a table. Be patient and enjoy the outdoor fields. I personally thought the outdoor fields had more to see than the so called museum. They also have a variety of green tea for you to buy as souvenirs too. Really easy to find with a huge free parking lot.

The butterfly museum is interesting showcasing many species of insects but the information are all in Korean. Walk out of the building there is an outdoor park with a maze. The mirror maze is not to be missed the kids had so much fun finding their way out!

The are lots of nice background for picture - taking here. It is made area per area. Lots of youngsters also come to this place. The maze itself is nice to try. But be careful is you are with kids. They might get lost. The parking is huge.

The ?Dragon Hair? rock location is near Jeju airport and a good recommendation if you are trying to burn some time prior to departing Jeju. The location has spacious parking and allows visitors easy access to the actual rock.

Takes only 15 min if just visiting the rock and its surrounding. Parking was charged and thus we parked at the roadside only.Just go down a flight of 15-20 stairs and then follow the path and signages.

Take this opportunity to eat ?쐍on-restaurant??food. Sample things like flamb챕d cream seafood (in crab shell)  pork trotters  gimbap (Korean rice roll in seaweed)  etc. For those driving there are a couple of public car parks nearby.
Stopped by this beach after visiting Hallim Park. The sand is soft and the water is turquoise-y. But I have seen better beaches. The unique feature to me is the volcanic rock by the beaches.

spent 2-3 hours to walk through despite it was a hot sunny day.  The park is well designed and large and showcases a number of house and building of old Jeju.  However I would like to have more and completed information (in English).  For me a foreign visitor I have no interest in those scene for TV film making.  Again the park grows different plants which impress me.

Spectacular geological formations and scenery.  It really is quite unique. It's easily accessible and there's a nice small park around the top.  There's a path that can take you to the portion of the shore which is nice and not many people go to.  Jeju let's nature take center stage and they do a nice job getting you access.

Songaksan was one of the places that had actually a very small crowd of tourists so it make the hike a bit more enjoyable. At the foot of the mountain is a large parking lot with some coffee shops and restaurants from there it is a light hike up the mountain. Lots of greenery and nice views along the way. The center which I believe is a crate is closed right now I think for recovery from too many tourists. it is still a good destination to visit the hike is easy and relaxing peaceful and enjoyable.

So much to offer from beautiful botanic displays to a fabulous Bonsai area which was so peaceful and various specimens of fauna.... Plus several species of cacti. Caves to go down and lovely park area..... A lovely outing which was also very reasonably priced.

Sitting prominently on a hillside there is no missing this huge Temple and it is one of the largest in the East.There is a bit of steep walk from the carpark to the Temple complex and we rewarded ourselves with a drink from the spring well on one side of the grounds.Consisting of a main hall with a Deities sculptured side walls of Buddha a large bell a separate Pagoda Monks quarters and three or four floors upstairs that can be accessed by visitors. These floors have many donations of precious metal statues and from up here there are excellent views of the main hall.It is prudent not to use the main entry into the big hall as there are clear warnings in many languages not to so out of respect. Also shoes must be taken off before using the side entries on either side of the main doors. A group of hapless visitors ignored these signs and were promptly told off and hustled out to use the side doors.Money donations are accepted either for the upkeep of the Temple or for incense and candles.While we were there we had three or four Monks chanting and offering up to Buddha and it was very serene to hear it from upstairs while overlooking the main hall.The grounds are well maintained with a couple of restrooms around the complex a cafeteria and Temple stays are available too.Enjoy your visit!
Should be your must do list for photography activity. There is car park & toilet nearby. All Jeju coastal are unique scenery but this place has its own specialty. Good place to relax and chill.
Short walk from the carpark but need to climb down stairs and walk on rocks to go near waterfall. Not suitable for stroller or wheelchair.

Shinhwa Theme Park is unique in many ways.  First it tries to make its own characters seems as popular as Mickey Mouse and Spider Man - it doesn’t work but it’s great fun just trying to figure out who is who.  Second everything seems brand new - so it’s spotless and at the same standards as a Disneyland or Universal Studios.  Third - the rides are small but oh so knock out fun.  And there is rarely anyone there.  I don’t know if they sell a fast pass but there is no need for one because i don’t ever imagine it getting that crowded.  The food was quite delicious too - great offerings at multiple locations.  You can easily do this park in a half day and not feel like your exhausted or missing anything.  Like everything in Jeju I think they think they are expanding but who knows..  and as i remember the entry price is super affordable.  So this is really a great time for anyone with kids or who enjoys theme parks.  Don’t go in thinking it’s Disneyland though and get picky - just enjoy it for what it is...a bold effort to start something special and first class and doing very well right from the start.  It was a great day for me and my daughter and her two cousins.  Enjoy!
Seri World is a super basic theme park. To me  the only thing fun to do was ride the Go Karts  which was a good time  but expensive and pretty small. I wouldn't return.

Seobok was born in 255 B.C. In what is now present day Yongkou city of Shandong province China. That is why there is Taesan square stone donated by people's government of Shandong Province  China. There is also a Seobok monument memorial.The story of his journey to the Far East as commanded by Emperor Qinshihuang can be seen from the stone frescos. You can also get more information from the Seobok Exhibition hall. After this  you can proceed to China Park  nice garden
Scenic park with many photo opportunities. Restaurant inside the park (not the one at the entrance) served the most affordable black pork in the region.

Sarabong Park is a 143-meter hill located just east of Dongmun Rotary in Jeju. The park is best known for its spectacular sunset views which is often regarded as a perfect complement to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak's view of the sunrise.
Really the Tubes are fascinating but a little redundant. Was a long walk in the dark for a six (6) year old BUT the park is well equipped w/ Toilets and a Local Resto & Taxi Cabs!!! Enjoy.
Really enjoyed exploring this cave. Easy and convenient car parking. Great facilities. A must-see on your trip to Jeju.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

Read about it and found it really interesting and we decided to go take a look but pretty disappointed as we all tried but it was not working. One good thing was that it's not a wasted trip as it is very near to Jeju Love Land/ Park.

Pyoseon Beach is just the opposite of Jeju Folk Village.So after visited the Village  we came here.The beach is pretty large with wide white sands.It is the perfect place for families to spend some time relaxing  particularly at low tide with its lake-like pools.It has abundant parking space  public toilet (with shower) and cam-ground around the square.Near the beach  there is white lighthouse near the shore.This lighthouse is where the last scene in Kdrama Iris (2009) was film.
Pricey and most displays were in Korean. Very hokey. Recommend the Love Park outside Jeju city instead.

Pretty interesting theme park! All the sculptures displayed bluntly explain our sex life and culture. It is good to tAke photos with them and prohibited children from entering inside. Usually not crowded except special national holidays ir vacation season so whenever you could visit here freely.

Pretty big park with 2 caves that you can go through. Many school trips come here so don't be surprised to see flocks of students in the weekdays too. Nice peaceful area but there are quite a few other Jeju attractions I would see first if you're on a time limit.

Plenty of interesting glass installations in the park and museum. Really worth to see. Very nice and friendly owner. Many beautiful things and funny toys in the shop. The best way to get there is by taxi  it's about $15 from Seogwipo city center.
place is quite hugecan spend an entire afternoon there. they even have a mini theme park with a pirate ship. you may hike up the trail or visit the temples as well.

Parking was limited nearby  place was full house  quite difficult to find a table to seat for our tea time  it was a nice place though  bought some green tea spread for bread  green tea sachets and green tea chocolate to bring back home . We had the set of green tea Swiss roll which was delicious so was the green tea ice cream and green tea smoothie . Thumbs up ?몟?뤋
Park is a little small but has some fun rides. Very clean and new. Great staff. Good food (except for pizza).

Overall the park is quite old kinda poor maintenance as miniatures are surrounded with lots of grass poor paintings and not so impressive. Thought it might have alot people to visit the park but turn out seems like we are the only visitors.

Our two children loved this one. Easy to interact with and you leave with lots of funny pictures to bring home. Pizza at the restaurant was really yummy too. Nice break before you go out to the statue park in the back of the museum. Didn't seem to be well promoted - it's new and the first museum as you start on the road to the Jungmun Resort area. We took a cab from the Hyatt Regency (long uphill walk and potential rain) - less than 5000 won for the cab.

Our trip to Hallim Park was wonderful.  If you love nature you will love to explore the well maintained gardens.  I love the garden with Bonsai trees as well as the Cactus garden.  There are caves inside the park too which you can visit.

Our son LOVED it here and has been asking to go back daily since we left. It could use a few more things to do  but you can easily spend a good few hours here  especially if your children are familiar with the animation. Everything seemed very safe and well organized. We didn't pay extra money to go into the play area  but it sounded like kids were having a blast in there too. No idea why adults have to pay entrance though.... as theres nothing for adults to really do and the only reason they are entering is to go with their children. Many play parks around Korea offer free entry for adults  it's a shame here doesn't follow suit. Also  the kids play room with the balls and lego blocks is a little lacking..... our son still loved it  but it could use a few more items to build/play with etc

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Our guide brought us there and we really enjoyed walking in the park. My son was walking quietly by himself taking in the fresh air. Lovely place to find peace and tranquility and to just be in tune with yourself and nature.Lovely old nutmeg trees which give out a lovely fragrance! I could come here to walk every day!

Our first time in Shinhwa World theme park visit in December 2017. One must come with the understanding that the theme park is not yet fully developed but it has some nice rides and you can spend a few hours there . My kids had a wonderful time . Since it is new  the park is not crowded. We had lunch at the food court and it was good Korean food . We were initially disappointed when the rides were suspended due to the snow. However the rides were resumed quickly after the snow stopped. We happened to have met the theme park Manager Mr Mason Kang when we ran into communication difficulty with one of the staff attending to the ride . He was very kind to explain to us that the rides would resume soon after they dry the area . His professionalism impressed us .  Our theme park experience was a great one . My kids tried the ice skating ring within the theme park compound . Everything is new and clean . We will come again ! They are going to have a Water theme park probably year after .

Opposite the museum is the tea field which you can walk across the road to take a photo and see how they grow the tea tree. There's parking space beside the museum. Besides there's the tea cafe and souvenir shop at the arrival floor. I would recommend the green tea smoothie top with soft cream green tea latte and green tea roll cake. It's very crowd with tourists and local people. So normally the seat are full. So if you go with friend I'd recommend one to fine the seat and one to queue up to get drink and desserts. Even its long queue to buy but it doesn't keep you wait too long. The green tea spread is the signature. There're also many selection of tea with nice packages and different aromas for your selection.

Only signs we saw are those explaining whose house the thatched roofed houses were. There was nothing else much to see culturally except vacated old houses. Houses still occupied were already modern looking. Lack of signs and explanation. Would have skipped this. However the black pork outside the village in the restaurants near by the parking area was yummy.
Only did a short hike in the park but the views were amazing and I will definitely go back when I can.
One of the pit stop along the way to Yongmeori Coast via halim park route. Offer a great view. Ample prking space is available.

One of the must visit place in Jeju if you love watching sun rise. It takes about 30 minutes to climb up the steps to the viewing platform. We stayed at Sun Villa Pensions which was just above Nature Republic a stone throw away from the entrance of the park. You could see the crater from the balcony and Starbucks on the left. It was really convenient to have a place nearby as we had to wake up early  to hike up and catch the sunrise (6.45am). The only down side is that the area as well as the park have limited street lights so you'll be needing a torchlight to walk either early in the morning or at night.

One of the interesting tourist object in Jeju Island. But I don't understand why they call castle which for me it's a park with many kind of glasses art.  Anyway it's fun &  we can pretend like in wonderland.

One of the advantages of Covid is that it reduces the number of people using certain facilities and the pleasantly low number of people within the Theme Park was testament to this. Only a few of the rides were open. This led me to ponder how some rides can be more Covid friendly than others. But the conclusion I came to was that there is no Covid-difference between the rides but instead it is all just one big excuse to provide half-hearted service and blame Covid. The rides on offer were fun thought the roller coaster was a tad over before it was started. The staff seemed to be depressed. I do not know if this is because it was quiet or because they were having to work there on such a pleasant day. I think families with kids in the range 8 to 14 will like this the best. It's an enjoyable couple of hours and the models and designs in the park are fun.
One of common parks you can find in Korea but it has several memorial statues you can find including Kim Mandeok tomb and so on.

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. The reviews for this listing is a mix for the Museum of Sex and Health and for Loveland there is no actual listing on here for Loveland. We did our research first to decide which one to go to and Loveland looked like the more fun one - a lot of the pictures of outdoor sculptures on this listing are actually from Loveland not the Museum of Sex and Health). I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).

Okay if visitor is kind of tea lover. Like being here for shopping which is not that extraordinary or the must spot. Just okay for the museum zone and cafe easy and relaxing tea field or area to walk but not that wow anyway. For food and drinks good but for cake and desserts I personally feel soso. For the shop and products' variety are good. Free parking on site.
Not worth the entrance fee and time spent at the park. Unless you really have no other attraction sites to visit.
Not on the main tourist route but this is worth a visit. Offers a look into the history of Jeju and it's people as well as a beautiful park.

Not as big as the 5 day market but still provides an interesting insight into the daily food norms of the locals. It's sheltered so rainy days is not an issue though parking may be. There are a few local eateries inside but the one we went in insists we order one portion (they are big) per person. Rather than having to waste food we walked out.
Not all the shops are open when we arrived at 12pm. Do try the fried doughnut (500-1000won)!! There's a multi story carpark beside.
Not a place where you can experience nature. Next to busy road and parking place. Still pretty good compared to other beaches in Jeju.
Nice stone formation and park. It maybe very hot during summer time. But worth a visit. I went there via public bus and you can also visit ecoland just across the street
nice place for hiking but must start as early as possible. it's about 1950 metres high. no more entry to the national park after 2.30pm
Nice place but not really impressed with it. Pretty small place and take less than one hour to complete my visit.  Once is enough. There is entry fee to the park
Nice place  for young kids  is best. Not really good for adults but it was cute......will try water park next time.

Nice peaceful place to visit. Came across this place while heading to Yeogmeori coast. Can be accessed from the same parking lot to the coast. If you're driving a rented car you can key in 7942940. Recommend to drive if you are touring jeju.
nice park with a little hike.there's a lot of ahjussi and ahjumma doing a bit of workout.quite nice view from top

Nice park surrounding this unique canyon.  3 sets of waterfalls.  An interesting bridge that goes over the canyon and a path that takes you through the woods.  Takes a bit of effort but it's worth doing if you're in the area.  The falls are not that impressive but the formations and the foliage is nice.

Nice park and a great way to know about the history of the island.amazing grand sight of the rock formations.Rocks & stones everywhere. Beautiful landscape. There are nice traditional houses in the park.

Nice little amusement park at the Shinhwa Resort. We got vouchers when we checked in at Shinhwa Landing hotel that we have exchanged for all day tickets for the park for 9000 won each. It was a great deal and kids had great time. The park wasn’t busy at all so we rode some rides couple of times. Well worth it.
Nice beautiful beach with black stones contrasting white sands and blue sea. Near to Hanlim Park which is a must visit. Summer is great time to be at the beach

Never would have guessed but there's shopping  eating  a water park and movie theater at the world stadium. Jeju triathlon was headquartered here so I did that business. You can put on Hanboks (Korean clothing) and take pictures as well  that's all free.
Need only about 2 hours here.   Combination of botanical gardens and kids amusement park.  Pleasant way to take a walk through wooded areas on Jeju island
Near to Hallim Park. Small beach with brown-white sand and black rock. Better to go when low tide so you can walk a few hundred meters into the sea.

My review is a little late but it's better late than never. We've visited this place when I was four months pregnant and I was able to hike up to the summit. This place is serene. It's breathtaking to see the wonderful view when you've reach the top. The kids love the lush greens at the hilly part of this place. It's very well-maintained. There are souvenir shops located at the entrance of the park.

My friends and I were so excited about Loveland before our visit. However we were quite disappointed afterward as the park was kind of old. We expect more to see after paying so much for admission but nothing else besides statues and some aged fountains. Only visit if you really have free time to kill.

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

My 2.5 year old son loved this park so we went there twice. There are classic activities like sand and bubbles and playroom and challenging ones like big slides  tree house??My husband and I had fun too! The restaurant there has a breath taking view. If you have kids from 2-5  this is a must go park! We want to go back there again!

My 10 yo daughter and I came here on a Monday in December. There was hardly anyone in the park which meant no waits. Park is small but fun rides. We stayed about 3 hours did everything and some rides multiple times.

Meh. This museum was included in our group tour so we visited and thought it was ok. The statues are a bit silly and the overall theme of the park is sex- related so definitely not age appropriate for young kids (which we did see running around!)

Me and family went to Halla Park. I was 7month pregnant so I could not attempt the long Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trail to the summit. We picked the shortest hike Yeongsil Trail. It is about a 3.7k trail from Yeongsil Rest Area to the Witsae ?Oreum Shelter one way which took me about 2 hours of gentle walk to get to the turnaround point. The trail was well signed and marked. It was a busy day on the tail with a whole school of high school kids out for an organized hike. But the view of the trail is still very nice. The steps were all well maintained so I had no issue of going up and down by myself. I will definitely come back to attempt the longer trail to the summit in the future.

Maze park is an unique park than consists of two maze. You can play inside the maze and your friend can stand at the station to guide you. The view is nice and there is a mini museum for the maze. Try to spend more time in this park estimated 2hours.

Maybe I'm not the mini theme park type of person. It was poorly maintained and I did not enjoy it. There was a small area that showed how Korea was like in the 60s that I thought was different from the other outdoor exhibits. This is not a place I would recommend my friends to go. I think there are better places.

Max 1 and half hour. The human figures in the park shows the erotic part of the human being in different sex positions but done in an very artistic fashion. There's also shops inside selling sex toys accessories. Try not to bring underage in not sure if they restrict.
Lovely park. Went with a tour group so was a rush. Would have been better to spend more time there. The caves is a must see.

Loveland - the adult sex park.  I read about it before the trip and thought why not visit it.  Something different but we were disappointed.  The ticket was pricey @ 9000krw per person.  Inside the exhibits spread out over the park can be better sculptured and the themes in each exhibit area better managed.  Overall it was a disappointment.

Loved it! The park was extremely beautiful! Loved the bonsai and the caves the most. The only downfall was the animals. They seem a bit sad and clustered. Everything else was great. Make sure to bring bug repellent though.
Love this place! Admission is 2000won per adult and parking lots are available.  Glad that the weather was good!
Love the theme park.  It has exhibits of glass sculptures indoor and outdoor. The whole place is so colourful. You can enjoy all the glass work in this beautiful theme park.

Love Land is the place i visit and having so much fun in jeju! entrance fee w9000 per person but seriously worth it cos place is huge with indoor and outdoor. outdoor with all the sex pose statues very embarrassing while walking around the park. but i really do enjoy! its cute and some sexual knowledge >///< visit during January spend about 2 hours plus in the park. i believe can be more but due to weather is super cold we couldn't stand the windy cold we left right after round the whole park. basically is 80% outdoor and 10% indoor + 10% indoor souvenir shop.

Located on the eastern part of Jeju lies Ilchul Land  a cultural spot that showcases Jeju's ecology which consists of the Micheon Cave  Subyeon Park  Folk Village  Wild Flower Bonsai Garden  and Cactus Greenhouse etc??For fans of Running Man (?곕떇留?  this is one place to visit as the team actually filmed here before: various signboards showcasing certain place scenes (at certain corners) that occurred during the filming of Running Man; bringing you a step closer to your favorite Running Man characters! The first stop was Micheon Cave  a cave that is a designated Natural Monument and one of the representative lava tubes of Jeju. Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. The village was a replica of what would have been in the past with a millstone and buildings with commentary. There were even ?쁫ive??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html

Little walk down pathway along the cliff on the seaside.Something to see while in the area.May be difficult for elderly or those with weak walking abilities as walk to the waterfall from parking lot consist of lots of stairs and wet floors.

Just a Stone throw away from  Seongsan Ilchulbong is located the Aqua Planet. It is easy to find and has generally enough parking place available. It is quite a big building and not to over look. Entrance fee is a bit pricy. We paid for 2 adults and one child over a 100k Won if I am not mistaken. Anyway a huge Aquarium costs probably a bit more efforts as other places in Jeju. The whole aquarium is made comfortable for stroller and wheel chair. We entered 20 minutes before 3pm and did a mistake. At the entrance they told us that we have to look the show first and then go through the Aquarium. It is what we did. So after the show we had to deal with a lot of People crawling through the aquarium at the same time. Don't do this. Instead do the other way around. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. It is 40 minutes long and is divided by (20%) dolphin performance (20%) sea dog performance and some (60%) pirate story performance with humans only. Fair enough to say that over all the show was good and fascinating. Conclusion is that we visit the place again.

review: Jusangjeolli are stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju Island. Jusangjeolli Cliff was formed when the lava from Hallasan Mountain erupted into the sea of Jungmun. There is a admission fee and parking fee to enter this place. We reached there by car the other day and it was an hour journey from Seogwipo city.

Jeju stone park was not part of the regular sightseeing itineraries and do we opted for a customized private tour to visit Jeju stone park. Requires atleast 3 to 4 hours if you want to walk along the trails to cover entire area. A visit inside the museum to understand the volcanic activities and formations will help in understanding the nature of the island better. Good to go with a local guide. Interesting statues and rock formations
Jeju Starlight World Park - Seems like a awful lot of people come here with family and young children. Great fun!

Jeju National Museum is set almost in the middle of nowhere -- well it's beside an adult theme park but otherwise literally nowhere. Had a car so it wasn't tough to find but would be extremely tough using public transport.The museum and the garden that surrounds it is well sterile... for the lack of a better term. Beautiful but seems to lack any personality... it's quiet laid back and perfect for a long walk... but not much action.

Jeju love land is one of those parks that is worth going to for simply being unique. If you have a sense of humour and love all things bizarre this is worth checking out. You can grab a penis shaped dessert ice cream or beverage and there are a number of quirky and interactive sculptures to gawk at. Getting around Jeju Island isn't that easy a taxi might be your best bet. Make sure you have the address up on google maps for your driver to see.

Jeju is so famous with their dolharubang. when i hear this i was very excited to come here. But i was a lil bit dissapointed as this place have nothing much to offer.. The entrance fee is very expensive for me (7000 won) as it is just a park and you can take picture of many other type of dolharubang available and learn the history of it a lil bit. If only it have lower price i would give 4 stars instead
Jeju has the grandfather stones so was hoping to get a bit about the history but this is an artist park. It's well done but not worth a special trip. Cost is 4000 Won which is high for what you get.

Jeju has many beautiful bushland and park areas that are truely outstanding at all seasons of the year. Bijarim Forest is yet another one of these and can be different in each of the seasons. Take water if in summer and a coat if in winter!! Enjoy wandering the pathways and seating areas provided to take in the beauty.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.
Jeju April 3rd Peace Park  - really a peaceful place to visit. Walk through the small exhibitions to understand it better.
It's worth visiting. Beautiful nature. You need about two hours for this. There is also nice beach near the park.

It's the first place we went on our first day in jeju.Had fun playing with mirror and it's interesting to see insects are decorated like human.. at first we don't understand what this park do but for me it's like an insects museum

It's such a nice place to be there . It so amazing that the whole area is make of glass . There is a park that you can go around  the benches   flowers   country flag and more are made of glass. You also can see Cinderella glass shoes in different colours . It's worth to see all this thing that i dont see in my country. The most impresed me is the toilet !!!

It's quite difficult to find a parking space. Quite a few people at sunset struggling for pictures. It's not that beautiful in my opinion. There are many restaurants after walking across the suspension bridge.

It's quite a tour to walk around and see everything in this theme park. The park has some huge dinosaur statues nice views it features a bird house a maze a small museum and some food vendors. It's a museum type very laid-back amusement park with nice scenery.

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?곕떇留?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.

I have spent years reading about WW2 history so it's a sobering experience to walk the same places as the men and women who fought and died in that conflict. Altteureu Airfield was a WW2 Japanese airbase that sits in a strategic corner of Jeju Island  midway between China and Japan. In the 1930s bombing missions were launched from here to Shanghai  later it was a training base. There are 19 remaining concrete hardened shelters sized for a Zero fighter and Jeju has done a good job with preserving the site (even though most of it is active farmland)  adding a large parking lot and bathroom  and placards to explain the history and locate the structures. It's right on the Olle trail so there are many hikers passing through and it's easy to find from the shore road by car.
