Halla-san is the highest mountain in South Korea and the middle of Jeju Island.  There are two trails that go to the summit of the mountain.  There are a few other trails on Halla-san but they don't go to the top.  It is about 9KM from one side of the mountain to the top and about 10 KM on the other trail to the top.  There are water sources on the mountain so you don't need to carry much drinking water.  It took me between 2 to 2.5 hours to reach the summit and about the same time to go back to where I had parked my car.  The trail is fairly rocky and vertical.  On a clear day you can see all of Jeju Island and the sea below from the summit.  There is also a small pond in the middle of the summit of the dormant volcano that is Halla-san.

Hallam Park is one of the best botanical gardens we?ve visited. The paths are clearly posted and friendly to foreign visitors that don?t read Korean. We loved it. The restaurant at the entrance is only a good choice if you like Korean food. The barbecue spot inside might be a better choice for western visitors.

Halla Mountain is the tallest mountain in South Korea and dominates Jeju Island.  It is an old shield volcano and is snow capped.  The part of the national park that we went walking in was swathed in fog the day that we were there.  The fog gave the national park an eerie ethereal feel as you never knew what interesting things would come up ahead.  Had a great time.
Had a really good time walking around the park. The gardens are beautiful and the lava caves are cool too! Worth a visit if you're passing by.

Gwangchigi Beach is a beach near Seongsan Ilchulbong.We park our rental car on the side road.There are a few cars & tourist bus park along the road.We can see beautiful view of Seongsan Ilchulbong from this beach. The beach is long and it has black sand.The beach is unique to it own because of the green stone/rock at the shore.It produce picturesque photo because the green stone contrast with the blue sea.This beach appears on drama Warm & Cozy starred by Kang Sora and Yoo Yeonseok.

great place to visit if you are into nature. amazing long stretch of lava tube but only about 1 km is open to public. nice park before the entrance to the cave. very good information centre on how the structure is formed.
Great place to visit after the Hallim Park. The sunset was amazing. Could see the beautiful island from the distance and the sands were soft and white. Looks pretty clean.

Great place for nature lovers to soak in multi themes and explore the Hyeopjae & Ssangyong caves in one location for admission price of KRW10000. Park is wheelchair friendly and is a great place for friends and family to spend a few hours together. The park does not feel overly crowded as it is spread over 80 acres. Visitors still enjoy tranquil surroundings even though the park is crowded.
Great park with wide variety of flora and fauna and sculptures. Good to spend the day with families and friends.
gorgeous - especially in the blooming spring.  cute bridge & stream. easy access from huge parking lot
Good walk around the park and the cliffs were quite spectacular! Very interesting rocok formations that were built by lava flows.
Good view if you go on the day they don't have a heavy fog like me 555Please look for the weather forecast before you go.You have to pay 2000 KRW for a parking fee

Good to visit this place if you have extra time in Jeju Island building was surrounded with green tea plantation and a small nice walking path connecting both O'Sulloc and Innisfree. It was good to have both closed by as it was a rainy day we went in March.O'Sulloc building has a very spacious cafe serving nice desserts and many selection tea from the counter bar. Green tea cream roll is a must if you happen to be there.The souviner section has so many to choose from. Parking and admission to this place is free.

Good spot for a quick photo very close to downtown jeju . You can walk from the middle of town very easily over the bridge and then round . Walk down do the photo and from the viewing area also a car park with toilet close by .

Good scenery location for photo taking & trail walk. Area are clean and windy. They are free parking area that i just realized after finished my activity here and my rent car parked in the paying area! Paid 2000 won to old man already waiting next to my car as i went to toilet.

Good place to visit. We joined YEHA's East Course tour and this is one of the stops. A 20-25 mins walk up the slope to the tip of the peak. Nice to do this at end Nov where weather is cool. You can get a good view when you reach the top. You can visit Woman Drivers taking their dip at the base. There are many shops at the base where all buses and cars park.

Good place to see all the monuments in one time.It takes around 1 hour and half to visit all the park and the price is 9 000Krw for one adult.Some monuments needs some refresh work but the others are in a good state.
Goin on summer  like another park  but the cave lil bit creepy  and i dont know feel very cold even its on summer. No guide in cave  and creepy.
Go before 2 if you plan to hike. Trail closes and is guarded. Enjoyed the scenes. Not a lot of parking.

Glad we went here. Quite busy on a Sunday but worth it. Great views of the formations and nice parks at either side to walk through or picnic in. Very reasonable admission and we took our dog in on a lead. Lots of stunning photographs to be taken. I would say it's a must see!
Gives an idea of how volcanic eruptions must have thrown Jeju out of the sea millions of years ago. Peculiar rock formations in a green landscape towering amid whispy clouds spell this Park.
Full of people and green tea products. Good for green tea lovers. You can explore more other natural parks nearby if you don't plan to get any green tea products.

From the photo's it looked great but when we went it was black with leaves en rubbish. Not really chilling the people weren't very friendly and don't try to get something to eat at the entrance or at the parking lot. We hoped on a little paradise but it looked more like a landfill maybe it cleans up in a week or so. It doesn't have the Bali Jamaica Aruba Latin America outdoor chill vibe
For a short taste of the main national park on Jeju Eorimok is a  1 hour walk . Its easy and has a great view.

For 2000w you can walk into the park. The lookouts for the rock formations allow great photos. Similar natural rocks to those seen in Ireland. The park has some Jeju stone statues otherwise not much else to see. The parking was free.

For  tea lovers O'Sulloc Tea Museaum is a great place to visit.  There are different displays of varied teas and other beauty products derived from tea.  There is also a refreshment parlor serving anything made from tea.  Outside this museum is a big park where people may gather or just play.  Just in front of the museum is a tea plantation.

Far from city.parking is limited.cafe sells good food and cakes.thier green tea roll cake are to die for. Seats are limited too. They have innisfree boutique but price the same as those in other places.

Excellent little theme park! We are staying at a Shinhwa property so received complimentary  “big 3” tickets for the park.  Our kids (ages 14 12 9 6 3) had fun on the rides. There’s not a ton of shade and it’s a warm day. We came early (at opening) but several rides didn’t open until an hour later. Very low crowds many employees who can speak English which was very helpful!

Everything on this park looked like new and my two princesses certainly enjoyed heir time there. Therre lots of slides  playgrounds outdoors and indoors  game for litlle kids and the staff is always ready to help out. You can spend probably half day here not more Tlahn that as it is it that big either

Enter the national park through the Eorimok trail and get down through the yeongsil trail. There are different scenary when you arrive at each check point. Can't describe more by words. Experience it yourself and you will know that those endless staircase that you climbed up is just so much worth for the view up there!

Enter an oasis of watery fun  where 18 wave pools  rapids  spas and slides come together with six restaurants and a Korean-style jjimjilbang sauna to create Jeju's biggest indoor and outdoor water park. With baby nursing rooms  kids??pools  Asia's first double water slide  private cabanas  a variety of sauna rooms  hot snacks and fresh beer  there's something here for everyone in the family
Enjoyed the visitVery informativewas able to make purchase of productsGood car parking facilities

Eco Land Theme Park has different stations each station differs from the other with a theme. I Love 2nd station where the windmill is and noah's ark. it's a huge area for family and i love the train too.

During our visit to Jeju Island I fell in love with the Hareubang statues.  They are all over the Island a unique distinguishing statue you will see everywhere you look.  I had many pictures taken while standing next to one of these great statutes!  The Dolharbang Park was full of ancient statues many dating back to the 20th century.Dol means stone and Hareubang means grandfather So Dolharbang means stone grandfather.  In gift shops you can even buy small Hareubang statues keychains chocolates perfume bottles...to take home for a happy memory

Driving from Jeju city centre to Manjanggul Cave is straight forward and easy. Parking is also free for this attraction. We had to purchase a ticket prior to entering the cave through a steep and slippery rocky stair. The cave is wet and cold even in March. The grounds are contantly wet with water dripping throughout the cave. It is also not easy to walk on as the grounds are very uneven and filled with puddles of water. Walking through the cave was thrilling and filled with excitement. Round trip to and fro the cave took us about 1hr30mins. Would highly recomend to anyone visiting Jeju Island. Proper shoes are also recommended as it can be very slippery and slip and fall may happen. Kids and Older people may find this attraction tough and difficult to walk through.

did a slight detour this place  before returing to airport. the road was pretty empty except for one or 2 cars that were already. Did a u turn to face up the slope from where we got in. Followed the sign where to start and put it to Neutral and experience the pull up the slope. It was over with about 200-300m stretch and turned into the carpark beside the shop. Didn't really feel anything strange or excited about it.

Despite seeing many temples in China I have to say visiting this one may be my favourite. There are occasional Chinese tour groups coming (in this time of the year) bu they mostly take photos from the park in front or get stuck next to souvenir/food stalls which are not in or just next to temple. Beautiful peaceful relaxing music not too many tourists perfect for a short stop. Grab some food and sit next to the cave behind the temple.
Definitely you need to visit this Stone Park so you could understand how Jeju people develop. Very nice place to visit.
Climbed it now proud. Most popular place to visit in jeju. If you are climbing the mountain bring foot snow sparks so that it won't be slippery.

Car parking near the beach is a nightmare... too many cars... cars parked improperly...  but at least it was free.I really like this beach as it was very clean... although there were a lot of people the beach can easy absorb them due to its size... lots of cafe and coffee shop nearby I arrived at low tide and it wasn?t suitable for swimmers as the deepest point (next to shark nets) was only up to my thighs. So I was disappointed by that.. maybe it?s a lot better during high tide....Another negative is you have to pay to use the SHOWERS.. 3000w for adult and 2000w child.... shower gel and shampoo is available... for a price

Car park is free . Entrance fee was 12000W. The maze was great fun because of the music and also the sprinklers sprayed out a fun mist so you did not feel so hot in the maze . There was also a magical spot where they had lights hanging above and the photos turned out real nice . Best of all was the foot spa at the end . Best cold water ever . The viewing observatory was great with a lift that brings you up three stories that gave an aerial view of the area . A most enjoyable experience.

Came with the cruise ship an easy walk up the park area. There are park gymnasium equipped area and a reflexology stoned path. There's a library and a museum around the vicinity. Nice to just walk around.

Came here just to try the tea but not visit the museum. The cafe offers a good variety of nice tea. I enjoy the cakes and ice cream too. There are gifts that you can buy for friends here. Things such as green tea chocolate biscuits and facial products. It?셲 quite a walk from the carpark for my tourist bus to the museum itself.

C1 ( 2016.07.15 ) This park's theme was good and I could see world's landmark. The wide place was good to walk with famous sculpture. But the sculpure was need to mend and manage I think. Because of old and shabby sculpure my enjoyment was decreased. And the high price was not good to me with facility.

C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) This park had good theme with world architecture  and good to walk to enjoy various sculpture. But the sculpture was old and need to mend  I think. The theme was excellent  but the facility was too old and unclean. For children  there was good to see world sculpture.

Black sand beach with lots of rocks.  Didn't see much wildlife but there were tons of people there.  The water from the river is clear blue and gorgeous but cold.  There is a place where you can canoe up the river for a bit.  Side note the parking is awful.  Be prepared to park a bit away and then walk.

Been there last late autumn. Temperature around 10 in the morning. The beach was deserted with only a couple strolling on the beach. The beach is covered with beautifully covered with fine white sand interrupted only by some black rocks. Surround this beach is a park where several human size bronze artworks are erected. Nearby are several eateries and convenience stores.
beautiful park with small huts with various traditional items in.  Stone grandfathers are the best bit.  Lovely receptionist called us a taxi after our visit.

As it was raining on the day we visited we could only have tea in the cave caf챕 and look at the souvenir shop.  Despite not being able to see more of the eco park - we heard there is a zip line over the tea bushes among other things we enjoyed ourselves at the tea caf챕 and the handmade jewellery selection.  The tea was of a good quality and the cake too.  Certainly they do not look as rich as the offerings at the O'Sulloc Tea Museum (which I did not taste).The jeweller efficiently modified the earring from hook style to a poke and push stud style for my sis.  I managed to get an olive coloured leather bracelet with a sterling silver magnetic catch for my niece for a good price.  Whatever we could see of the grounds looked very promising.We will consider returning here on a fine day on our next trip to Jeju.
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: As an American when I think beach I think sand water sand castles a boardwalk and a place to grab a drink. This beach has the sand and water but that is absolutely it. Sand water then a huge hill. You have to have a car to get here. There is a parking lot a 1/4 to 1/2 mile away. At the lot there is some minor touristy things. Think about 5 minutes of time to see it all. You then walk down a steep road and are at the beach. The pros: one of the few spots on the south side with sand and not just boulders. There are bathrooms and a place to wash off. The cons: it's a beach and nothing else. Since our hotel is about 4 miles up the coast and right on the beach that is solid rock we will drive here for the kids. But this is certainly not a reason to come here.

As a rule I try not to visit places that do animal shows and keep animals in small confined places. However I came here as a part of a group and enjoyed the portion of the show with dancers and divers. One male diver in particular was very impressive for a small waterpark show. The show was all in Korean so I was unable to understand the informational portions although some parts did have subtitles. There are also animal shows with sea lions and dolphins but as mentioned previously I do not enjoy these.

review: As a resident of Jeju  I enjoy walking through this park every week. It is a great and safe place to take kids or walk dogs. There are two parts to the park: north of the road and south of the road. In the southern part  there are interesting ponds and pathways.I would not recommend this place to tourists only because there is so much else to see in Jeju Island that is far more impressive than this park. However  it is only a five minute walk from the city Center (Jungang Rotary) to the northern part so it is not far at all.

An interesting place if you have lots of time on hand to play with the maze. It's a nice place to take some photos too (:For full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/gimnyeong-maze-park/

An amusing theme park with plenty to see but not much to do (aside from take photos in compromising positions with statues). The museum does provide some interesting insight into sexuality in South Korea -- note that while full bodied male statues are plentiful the only time larger women feature is in sculptures where men are desperately trying to escape.

Ample parking space is what stood out when we parked our vehicle. Lots of restaurants across the road from beach. Family friendly. Good place to swim or just relax on the beach. Observed one strange thing that the sand on major part of the beach was covered with mesh. We were told it was to prevent it from flying off due to strong winds
Ample parking lotVery scenic mountain viewThe breeze were very strongNeed to purchase a ticket to enter

Amazing rock formations. We spent about 45 mins at the park. Its a very well-pathed park with some stairs; suitable for most people. We went in July and it was super hot. I'd recommend going either early morning or an hour or so before sunset.  The adult tickets are krw 2000 each. I think it's a fair price.

All the kudos to the marketing team which managed to paint this place as a touristic attraction. The surface of their parkings is bigger than the entire tea plantation. Inside you can buy any premium (overpriced) tea based products you can imagine. We went on Monday outside season and it was so crowded that I got the impression it was black Friday sales.
Agree with many of reviewers is pathed very well with many stairs but was worth the visit. Close to the bus stop provided great access & has large car park.

After visiting the lava tubes we got to try out the maze park.  A fun way to spend a half hour and the site of many k-dramas and korean commercials.  Romantic for a date and fun if you have kids.  We even got to ring the bell at the end!A fun excursion if you're walking to the lava tubes it's on the same road.

After few days of hiking and busy activities our family decided to have a rest and relaxing morning by visiting the tea museum.  The park is not big but quite crowd in the shopping and restaurant mainly young people.  We took few photos in the farm and spent some money in the shops and cafe then left.
Adventure seekers this cave is alive with breathtaking stone formations inside. Although a cave... its like a great park beneath with guided lights making your adventure lighter and easy.

Admission fee 12.000won per Person. Free parking. Coffee and souvenir shop inside.I would give 4 points but this museum has no information in english at all. Although they advertise the museum with ?쐀iggest sex museum in the world?? so in my opinion the translation of information in english is a must. The admission fee is way too overpriced for not understandig everything. They do translate in chinese.By the way the museum is more funny instead of ?쐓exy?? Would just go here with friends not with a date because some statues/pics etc kill every possible erotic moment. XD

According t the map the falls were 400m from my hotel - so tried to walk.  Reched the park above the falls easily but could not find a path down.  Turns out only way to access to to go 1km downstream and walk down to the car park and in the official entrance. From entrance it is a 500m walk back upstream to the falls. many people all queuing to take photos.On the way out saw a musical performance near the entrance.

A wonderful way to enjoy beautiful Udo is actually by walking the Olle Trail 1-1. There's a total of 26 trails totaling 425kms round Jeju. Website jejuolle.org. Distance is 11.2km which covers the major places on the island. Trail starts & finishes at Cheonjin-hang(port) where you arrive by ferry from Seongsan Harbour. Its a relatively easy & flat trail taking 3-4hrs. Only slight challenge is Udo Peak. There is a century old lighthouse at the peak with a Lighthouse Park with miniature lighthouses in Korea & around the world as you make you descent. Need to watch out for scooters & buses while walking.
A wonderful peaceful place to see flora and fauna and caves. Hallim Park is like a summary of Jeju Island. I loved it!

A was a very steep climb but the views were worth it. Be sure to take water and food as there is only ramen available at the top. There are also no rubbish bins so take a plastic bag. Try to arrive before 11am otherwise you may not make it to the top in time before the park closes.

A very nice nature park with lots of flora and fauna. There is lots to see and do so do set aside more time to spend at this place. Do wear a pair of comfortable walking shoes and take lots of pictures!
A very beautiful park. I think it's quite new. Lots of spots prepared to take beautiful photos. I think there 2-3 cafes and nice snacks. Lovely place.
A short walk from the parking lot. This waterfall is also connected to one of the Olle trails which you can explore from the car park area. It gets quite crowded though.

A short walk from the parking lot to the falls. Walk a little further onto the rocks to get even closer and feel the cool spray from the falls and nice breeze. Relax and watch the waves break on the rocks. Beautiful! Not to be missed!
A short walk from the parking lot to see Oedolgae rock. Keep walking along the trail to get more views of the rock from different angles.

A popular hotspot and parking can be a problem. The waterfall is nice but not very spectacular. Can stand on the rocks bottom to catch a better glimpse of the waterfall but mind the slippery rocks. Wear a sport shoes with good traction or simply walked bare footed on the rocks.
A place where you can visit to see traditional houses. The park is pretty big and takes 2 hrs to complete walking around. It?s quite informative if u are interested in folk culture.

A park full of famous world landmarks and buildings but downsized. Perhaps kids will love this place more than adults. Did a quick 45mins walk around this park and left. Skip this park for other better places in Jeju.

A nicely maintained and managed tourist sport that taps into the wonders of nature. Not just a cave attraction but a park that is family friendly for picnics. Has a couple of restaurants to eat at that are inexpensive. The cave was really good with adequate English explanations for different parts of the cave. The visitor centre gave very good information about the formation of lava caves. The park is free while the cave requires ticket purchase. But all worth it. Very well maintained cave. A must visit when in Jeju.

A nice place to go for a couple of hours if you like animals and botany but in my opinion it was too expensive at 9000 Won per person. I think a fair price would be 6000 Won per person especially as the food and drink inside the park was extremely expensive.
A nice park with nine different ereas. The only important ones in my mind ofcourse is the caves and the Bonsai garden. The other partd you can find in many places.
A must-see but be prepared for a tough climb to the top. View is fantastic! Go early if you are driving to get a parking lot (free). Beautiful flowers.
A must visit in Jeju. Nice park and a great way to know about the history of the island. I joined a tour to visit this place as it is more convenient to travel privately than the public transport.

A must see really - seems a bit underrated. Almost no people when i went. Take a gorgeous stroll through the park to see different lava stones. Get educated about the geological activity. See some traditional houses.
A lover of plants and trees would love to spend hours here in this park. The lava tube may be a new experience for some . . . .

A lot to see. So many kinds of fishes  live or cooked you name it they have it. Reasonable prices are helping you enjoy shopping more! Try street food too. You?셪l love shopping and eating in there but parking is challenging! Very crowded!

A lot of tourists about. This was a small park but it seemed quite popular. But my preference would be the village where they shot the korean series 'the legend'. Just can't remember the name of the village. Anyways I was here around 2008. Enjoyed my tour trip
A lot of people went here. The day that I went was snowing and it's hard to find the near parking lot. Tea was pretty good. Ice cream was full flavoured of Tea.
a fun place to go in jeju. there are 3 mazes at the park and the grandfather maze is the slightly challenging one. a good place to go with friends and families!

A compact park around a crater. Walk to the top and down the slope to various parts that can offer some quiet relaxation. The view is peaceful rather than spectacular but worth spending a couple of quiet hours.
A close temple that near to Jeju-Si.Nice decoration with free parking. No actual operation timing but suggest to visit before 6pm.

a cliff beside the sea fell with fresh water. Thre is a historical legend about a staff of the 1st great empire of China that he wants to be immortal. The story is also about the name of this city. sea woman inside the park.
A casual walk to various areas (with different themes) within the park was very relaxing. The park was well maintained and landscaped.  It deserved spending a few hours visiting interesting areas.

A beautiful scenic walk along the coast and the path was well taken care of. We walked to the right first and walked most of the path up until it started to inclined towards the end and then turned around and walked down the left path all the way to the parking lot. Definitely recommend walking both paths since you see different rock formations and the walk is not too difficult or long.

A beautiful park there so many local tourist using this park for photo spot. The ticket price - Quite expensive. So many photo spot! Hard to find restaurant or eating place here. If you are using bus please double check the bus time. I recommend to use taxi.

...but the place itself looks almost abbandoned. Around 10 min walk from the nearest bus stop. Artistic glasswork presented in the park. Probably it's better to visit after dawn - it will be illuminated.

You want to know about volcanoes? This is the place. The museum is interactive and informative. And not to mention it houses some of the most beautiful natural volcanic sculptures around. There are three courses to follow in order to see what the park has to offer - taking things at a leisurely pace, this can easily take 3 hours to complete. It is well worth it though - with the some of the paths in course two taking on an enchanted forest appeal. The entrance is 5000 won, and you can get to the park on the Jeju City Tour Bus. The stops are just outside the park. A good poncho will serve better during rainy weather than an umbrella here, as there are parts of the course with low lying foliage (and the wind can be a little ferocious at times too).

You should be geared for a long walk inside the park. The ticket is a bit pricey (11,000 won per adult) with nothing much to see. There are plenty of palm trees and different types of pine trees as well but not really very rare or special species.They have collection of tropical plants (bananas, guava,mango , etc) which I am sure tourists from Southeast Asia will find boring. They have lots of cacti although not very extensive collection. May be we came at the wrong time because there were only few flowering plants. Overall, quite a waste of time and money ( and energy too).

You know that line movie critics love to use when it comes to B-grade chick flicks?   Have low expectations, then you'll enjoy it.   The same can be said of Manjang Cave.The lava tube was not as spectacular as I expected it to be, but it did offer a few interesting sights here and there. Walking all the way to the end of the trail and back took about an hour, but if you walk quickly, you can complete the journey within thirty minutes.Take note that the ground is wet and rocky, so be sure to wear your walking shoes. Also, it can get quite cold, so a jacket would most certainly come in handy. For photography lovers, you may not fancy the fact that it's a bit dark in the cave, but there's nothing a few adjustments here and there can't do!Facilities include, but are not limited to, souvenir shops, toilets and lockers. Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

You have to walk a little distance from the car/coach park, but the path is flat and well paved.  The falls themselves were, however, disappointing with little water flowing.  I?m sure the falls would be more impressive after heavy rainfall.

You could easily do 4-5 hours or even a day trip at Hallim Park. The first part of the gardens is uninspired, but persevere and head to the lava caves, tulip garden (late March/early April), bonsai gardens and beyond.

You can't expect more from a park. It is good though but nothing special.During my visit, it was pouring and can't enjoy the place to much. The park was managed well but really nothing excited me when strolling around. There were some theme park there and we can using train from one place to another places. Yeah.. it was ok.

You cant come to Jeju without visiting the main volcano which made the whole island, huge park, with 4 trails (different difficulties) to reach the top (easiers ones cant reach cr찼ter) if you going to climb, even by the easiest trail, be prepared, is not that easy at all.

you can view the teddy bears from different countries,enjoy yourself at the museum shop, caf챕, restaurant or the outdoor park where you can view the spectacular Jungmun Sea. At the museum garden, you can meet the teddy bear sculptures and models. The garden decorated with various themes such as the Korean Black bear family and the magical pond. Children under are free. Lots of free parking.

You can start the trail downhill from Story Ville villas and end at Oedolgae. On that Ole trail there is a museum and a coffee shop on the way. If you drive there, there is plenty of parking and small restaurants, etc. people come here to watch the sunset.

you can skip it unless you really love glasses. the entrance fee is quite pricey for the content. we took quite fast to finish the exhibitions, there's indoors and outdoors, one with a punmpkin like carriage for Cinderella. there's also a park where glasses are scattered around purposefully. I like the quietness of the park rather than finding where are the glasses.
You can see wild grass and flower garden, caves, Jeju stones, folk village, bird garden, water garden and subtropical garden in the park.

You can reach this place with Jeju tour bus - if you're going to the Roe Deer Observatory as well, I suggest you go there first and then walk downhill to the Peace Park (less than 10 mins). If you do it the other way round, you'll have to trek uphill. The admission for the Peace Park is free and everything is in English. The museum offers a comprehensive account of a controversial point in Korean history: some exhibits are quite chilling and upsetting but I think it's important to understand the history of this island: Jeju is not all about tangerines, erotic statues and kitschy teddy bears.

You can reach Ilchulbong by bus from the Intercity bus Terminal in Jeju-Si. It takes around 1h30 to reach it. You don't really care if it is an express or intercity bus you are taking, they more or less all go at the same speed... which is quite fast. You can't really miss the stop which is quite close to the crater. Dozens of buses parked in front of the mountain kind of spoil the nice atmosphere of the place but remember you are a tourist as well...  Left to the entrance, their is a nice small temple, worth the look. The climbing to the top is all made of wooden stairs and doesn't take too long (don't remember exactly, around 30 min). We did it with kids (youngest is 6) and she could do it easily. The view from the top is nice. It is a bit disappointing not to be allowed to walk around the crater. You can just see it from a platform. Before (or after) climbing, don't forget to take a look at the beach on the left of Ilchulbong specially between 13:00 and 15:00 when the old women divers are fishing.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

Yes it is worth to go here, you need only 50 mins to complete this park. The scenes are very stunning along the coast, the cliff, the fields and the volcano landscape. The ladders to the crater is well constructed but don't expect too much about the view up there! trust me.

Wow. Just wow. We're beginners climbing up Seongpanak trail (longest trail, 9.6km). I thought I was never going to make it! But the people going down were very encouraging. Try to go early, as the carpark will be full by 9. Entrance is free, but you have to pay for the parking. Take note - you gotta reach the peak by 1.30. They'll start chasing people down by then, because you don't want to get stuck up there in the dark (trek takes approximately 4.5 hours one way) Oh, the weather was really good; it was sunny and not a cloud to be seen. It gets pretty hot up there so wear sunscreen. The lake was quite dry though.

Worth paying for. There are so many teddies in various costumes and postures. There are elvis, the paddington bear, bear at the markets. For those who loves teddy bears, you can also see the evolution of teddy bears . My personal favourite is the teddy bears as featured in Princess Hours and also few diorama of korean culture; the women's diver, korean traditional wedding. Dont forget to take the picture at the park too! My take on the souveniers, as expected is a bit pricey, but if you want to have a momento, maybe you should buy the postcards.
Wonderfull Park! If you visit Jeju Island, i recommend you to visit Yeomiji. A lot of themes. So many places to take a good pictures.

With an entrance fee of 10,000 KRW (considered high for local attractions), my high expectations was quickly grounded with its shallow presentation of regional fauna. If you're from the tropics (like me), the Subtropical Botanic Garden (common palms, bananas, Bougainvillea etc) is a major yawn fest. There was a Wild Grass and Flower section which, in the absence of signage, could be easily mistaken by anyone to be a neglected zone in the Park. We skipped 2 other zones and zoomed in on the other highlights. The Caves were fine but nothing very impressive - tiny (imagine your pinke. Halve it) stalactites and stalagmites with their equally tiny rain parade could do no more to dampen your spirits than the Park already had. Saving grace come in the form of a cutest piglet that was a pet of the owner of Macaw House (warning: there is a separate entrance fee of 1000 KRW for this attraction) though I doubt it'll stay this cute for long. If you are visiting in Apr, then the Cherry Blossoms section would be opened but  the question is why you would pay 10,000 KRW for something that would be free all over the island.

With a 2,000?? fee, this waterfall is well worth a visit! It's a short walk down from the parking lot - not hard to get to at all. You should, however, wear comfortable and supportive shoes because you need to balance on rocks in order to get close to the falls.

While we were excited to visit the longest lava cave in Asia, we were very disappointed. There is no path to walk on in the cave except for very limited areas, so this makes for a difficult walk on slipperly and very uneven surfaces with deep puddles everywhere, making it essential to watch your every step rather than enjoying the cave. The lighting in the cave is ridiculous and poorly done, with sparingly placed bright lights aimed at the path rather than on the sides of the cave, so that your eyes are hit with bright lights such that you can't see the actual cave well. The few parts they lit, they added changing colours so you can't actually see the natural colours of the cave. Walking through the 1 km available does not provide much change in the scenery, so it was more an exercise than an interesting exploration.I'd recommend that you visit the caves within Hallim Park, which are much better presented with a safe path to walk on. Although the path throught the three sections of the cave are shorter, you can see much more. Go to Halim Park and skip Manjang Cave.

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Nevertheless, we got off anyway because we saw the cashier booth.Taxi tips: later after the walk uphill, we realized we could have insisted the taxi to go a little further to the big parking area which was the main entrance. That way we would be walking downhill to see the waterfalls, and could exit at the mid hill exit near the temple, just opposite the Twosome Square. If desired, you can also continue downhill to the third waterfall.Photo tip: don't wear aqua or turquoise colors, or green or blue etc. as the the waterfall, although not big, is aqua and turquoise in colors in a sunny day. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.

Whether you're with kids, friends, or a partner, this park is tons of fun for everyone. The best part is the race factor. Start at the entrance, and separate, racing for the finish. The end line is a set of stairs that lead you to a platform where you can see the rest of the maze. You ring a bell and your fellow racers know you have won. Such a blast. It's right next to the Manjangul Caves, so definitely combine these two sites. Don't miss it!

When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world?s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html

What can be so great about a crater? First of all, it?s big. Understand that it?s 2 km circumference and 100m + deep. So it?s not just a crater, not just a park, it has its own eco system with its own unique flora and fauna. The crater itself is not accessible but they have built a park fronting it with high viewpoints overlooking the crater. The viewpoints also allow you to see the surrounding mountainous features such as the Hallasan in the distant. A well designed park which deserves a two hours of your time.

What a way to experience another side of Korea on an extinct volcano. The view at the summit was amazing. Suitable for ages, but a certain level of fitness is definitely required. The park is well maintained and well kept by the government. However, if you are looking for something more unpaved or natural this might not be the right trail as everything is already nicely laid out. (You will never get lost)
Went with my kids and parents. We explore every part of the park. From Caves, cactus to folk villages. We enjoy the plantation at the park and flowers definitely. Must visit

Went with my friend and it was really a rare experience and rare sight for us. There are a lot of sculptures in the park and all of them come in different poses. It was a good chance to take some funny photos but we found it not so appropriate to take such pictures and so we didn't take much pictures of the sculptures.We walked across the park and saw different sculptures which have different funny messages (and we had a good laugh about some of the messages). After that we went in to their indoor shop where they sell   adults toys   and some chocolates (with pictures of different poses). There are also some shops outside which sell handmade stuffs and chocolates. Overall if you are in Jeju and you are not shy take a visit here once. However the way here is not so convenient. We took a taxi from our hotel since it is near (it took about 15 mins by taxi).
Went to the cave, only walk for about 1-2 hrs as this is a short cave. see stone structure cause by volcano eruption. only go if you like nature. Can visit the maze park at the same time.

Went to hyeopjae beach just to try swimming while i was in Jeju. Rented a car and drove there, thought that parking was gonna be a challenge but managed to get one in mere minutes. Mum didnt swim, so we rented an umbrella + mat for her to wait at. Cost us 15K won. Not sure if it was cheap or expensive. They guy attending to the rental didn't speak english, thank God for a local young chap who helped us translate.Loved the vibe of the beach, everyone there was enjoying the waves. Where I'm from, our sea is not as rough. so it was really different to see everyone in their floaties waiting for waves to hit them.

Went to Hallim Park on the end of September 2015, its a good thing we came at Autumn because the weather was not hot and not too cold either. The leaves were turning orange - just like in the movies. There are several flower parks in the Hallim park, such as flowers park; cactus park; bonsai park; stone cave; bird park; and folk village - where we can stop by for lunch. This place is suitable for families travelling with old ones, since the scenery is beautiful for photo-shoots.

Went there to watch sunrise with Sunrise Peak background and foreground with water and rock.? The beach is large and we could find a spot without disturbance of others.? However, there is no official car park space.

Went there to catch sunrise, but was disappointed. Couldn't see the sun peek out over the horizon as it was cloudy.Went at about 5+ in the morning, it was freezing with the winds blowing. Its autumn. Be prepared to bring your thick windproof parkas and scarves. The walk up to the peak is about 30 minutes. For someone who doesn't exercise, I must say its quite a challenge going up. Take your time. Once up there, the view is gorgeous. Take lots of pictures.From Seogwipo-shi, we drove about 1 hour to get there. So do plan your time correctly to catch the sunrise.

Went there in early autumn, the crater is covered with silver grass field, view is breathtaking especially during sunset, drop dead gorgeous!Suggest to wear comfortable shoes as you are expected to walk on some manmade rocky pathway. Parking is free and plenty of parking lots available. Entrance ticket is 6000 won for adult, kinda pricey given the area isn't big, but if you've never been there, it's totally worth visiting especially in autumn!

Went there during peak of autumn season, how it blew my mind away. guess i mustve been so lucky to come about at the right time! The pampas grass/ silver grass leading the way up to the crater really makes a beautiful , breath-taking landscapes. With the windblows, and the clear blue sky, this place could give you that romantic vibe and really picturesque too. But I guess if I were to come during the summer, nothing will spark my interest. As for the craters ? nothing much to shout about. Its just a shape of crater, with greens covering it.

Went here on a cloudy morning and loved it. Lots of steps to get down to the falls so grandmom stayed at the top. Pretty impressive and the bottom and it?s neat to see a waterfall so close to the ocean.If you have time, don?t forget to walk along the path along the coast to the ?Castle of Shell?. You get to the boardwalk path from the other side of the parking lot and it?s not well marked. It leads to a house on a cliff and another small waterfall. This place would have been a 4 but this extra trail makes it a 5. The cost for a family of 5 was 7,000 KRW.

Went for a stroll after visiting Hanna Mountain. The cactus conservatory was impressive and we rounded up that part of Hallim Park with a thirst quenching cactus drink.  Similarly the cool walk into the lava cave, and the connecting limestone cave was particularly enjoyable, taking shelter from the melting sun. Highlight of this trip was feeding of birds inside a bird house.   We purchased their food at the vending machine.  Having them eating out of one's palm brought back fond memories of childhood.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

Well, comparing to Seogwipo Daily Olle Market, sashimi is cheaper here. The market is bigger and there are most stalls for the snacks. But majority of these stalls are not open until evening time.  It is short walking distance to the Black Pork Street.Ample parking nearby and there is also a multi storey parking which is among the most expensive parking I had in entire Jeju. 6000W.

Weather was not perfect, but the park was still well worth the visit, the walk through the caves is really fun too. Give yourself at least 2 hours there, we budgeted for one and no where near long enough

Wear sunscreen because this maze can take quite awhile to conquer!  I wouldn't advise trying to complete it during the middle of the day when there will be very little shade, because it can be quite hot while you are in the direct sunlight.There are restrooms, free parking, a small convenience store style snack shop, and a small picnic area under the trees near the parking area.  A fun stop.

We, a group of friends had visited this place last week. It was awesome! The journey to get there, parking and the walk up and back were all good. There is ample parking space and plenty of eateries that offers various types of snacks and cold drinks.The area is impeccably clean and the walking path was clear and safe. The steps may seem a little steep at certain points, but you will be well rewarded once you reach the top. The crater is a beautiful sight! Not surprising that it's the iconic image of Jeju which appears on Google. You need about an hour or so for the entire visit.

We where on the way to the Love Park, then suddenly our driver passed it by some 20 metres. He stopped the car with the 5 of us in it, we were facing up hill, he turned of the engine, took the handbrake off, put the car in neutral and I kid you not we rolled UP the hill???I am told it's obvious its an optical illusion but amazed us!! It's free by the way, it's just a normal road

We were tired in the carpark and considered sleeping but decided to go in. So glad we did, walking through the garden was a deep feeling of peace and felt refreshed. Would definitely come back. A must do in Jeju Island!

We were staying in the Seogwipo area (near the International Convention Center), so it took us about an hour by bus to get to the Stone Park. It was interesting, with some unususal lava formations, but the drizzling rain didn't help in enjoying the scenery. The   museum   is OK, but nothing spectacular. When you (if) select a sunny day!

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

We were looking for a good place to shop and buy souvenirs and we found this place in Jungang area. Lot of cheap items from clothes, bags, shoes and beauty products.Tips:- GPS: 752-8776- There is a public parking in front of Jeju Bank along Ohyeon-gil. 3-4 hours cost us 3700Krw.- Jejumok Gwana is just on the West exit (exit 11). You might want to drop by if you got time.- There are Korean food in the middle section. Cheap but taste good.

We were heading to Halim Park and chance upon this on the way. Not many people as it was winter and really cold to be at the beach but the view is just so soothing. Blue greenish ocean waters, waves splashing against the rocks, white sandy beach, etc...just picture perfect.  The wind was blowing hard on our faces. There is a stine statue there at the parking lot.Definitely want to go back again.

We were dropped by the bus at the parking lot, and had to walked through a beautiful park where seashell statues and boats placed along the path. We have to queue for about 20-30 minutes before we could really see the amazing nature-sculptured cliff.It was very beautiful, especially at sunset.

We were able to easily find a cab in the parking lot, to take us back to our hotel. The cave itself was cool, temperature wise, so bring a jacket, even in the summer.  It is amazing to walk through.  Occasionally you get wet, your socks, if you step in an unfortunate wet spot or your hands, if you touch any of the walls.

We went with my 63 year old mom, husband, and 15 and 6 year olds. It was great! It's waaaay longer, wider, taller and more interesting of a lava tube than at Volcanos national park in Hawaii! The largest accessible in the world. Bring a waterproof camera, hiking shoes or at least tennis goes, a raincoat or jacket. Won't wear white. I still can't get the ash stain out of my sons sleeve after he fell in a puddle. It's only a few dollars to get in. Do the quick museum first, if you want to know more about it. Cold, wet, dark, tired but Loved it!

We went with 3 children (aged 5,7 and 10) and two seniors, and they enjoyed the maze park. It was a smaller maze park compared to maze land, so it's not too difficult for kids. We spilt into two groups, one group managed to find out way out and rang the bell in 5 mins, while the other got lost in the maze and required rescue.  We spent about an hour or so, going through the maze thrice, and it was a fun experience.

We went up the Yeongsil side. Lots of parking cost was 1800 won. You drive about 2kms after paying.  Nice fairly easy walk. Still bits of remaining snow around. I could've done with putting my merino leggings on!  Still, forced me to walk faster!  Haha!

We went to three or four different beaches on the island and this one hands down is the best. We didn't swim as it was in September already but spent a couple of hours strolling on the boardwalk. There are plenty of eateries across the street from the beach and some were on the beach side as well. The view was fantastic and definitely worth a visit. Also, parking was quite easy as well. We stopped for coffee (of course) and sweets at the nice coffee shop right on the beach before leaving and sitting there drinking coffee and watching sunset was a real treat.

we went to this place, but we didn't went up the park/hill/rock, as it will require lots of walking, which we didn't want to do :)you will still be able to have an impressive view at the entrance, and amazed by this natural creation. you can see the people walking up to the peak, enjoy the strong wind, as it is located by the sea, do a little shopping around the entrance area, or even find a nice cafe that is facing the spot to enjoy a hot coffee!

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum only because it was right next door to the Lotte Hotel Jeju where we stayed.  At 10,000 won per adult and 8,000 won per child, it is a bit pricey.  You can be done with all the displays and the 5 minute teddy Elvis show in an hour.  If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We went to the park by a convenient bus form jejy city. If you are a scientific or a stone-lover, this is the place to go !!If this is not the case (as it was for me), I would also recomment the park as you have a few impressive stones !

We went to the one at T 724-0228, mainly after the ferry landed and we were hungry, 'tween lunch and dinner parking wS available out front.  Staff were a little underworked so we go the full service treatment, good thing not tips expected (?);  we had the less fatty pork neck.  Served with a nice crab soup and nangymun noodles as a dessert.  Can't seem to get away from grilled fatty pork in Korea, have they heard of lean tenderloin here? Marinated  Pork skin was also served,

We went to Seongsan IIchubong after our lunch.  We bought our admission ticket ??5,000 per person.  When we enter the park, we saw that the climb can be quite steep and decided to take the left trail which has very nice scenery of the cliff and sea.  If you do not intend to climb up the Peak, just take the left trail which has gentle slopes and its free admission.  You can also watch the Haonyeo performances around 3 pm from the left trail.

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We went to Hallasan NP in early November by ourselves.  It?s quite easy to take the bus to the park.  Just make sure you know which stop to get off as there are several entrances.  We decided to hike the shortest trail (1.3km).  It begins at the Hallasan National Park Visitor Centre and finishes atop Eoseungtaeng Oreum, with sweeping views of the Jeju plains and the peak of Hallasan.  The leaves are very beautiful along the trail.  With our age, being seniors, and photo stops, it took us one hour to get up to the top.  Definitely it worths the hike!

We went to Eorimok trial thinking that we can go up with normal tracking boots. To our surprise, there was snow even though it was in the middle of spring. Due to the snow, we cannot go up the mountain without crampons. We still enjoyed ourselves at the carpark area as it was beautiful.

We went to eorimok trail to enjoy the winter festival. Great outdoor fun for children. Best part its free (except for 1,000krw parking fees). My kid loves d slide!! There?s even a museum to learn how hallasan mountain was formed. In my opinion this is the best place to visit in jeju.

We went there for lunch. It is next to O  Sulloc Tea Museum. There is a car park next to it, if it's is full, can park opposite next to the tea plantation. They serve Bing su (shaved ice) as well. Tried the tangerine shave ice. Average, don't waste your money. Menu limited an pricey. Can purchase Innisfree products as well. Price same as Seoul. Nice place to relax. There is soap making class, where by one cAn purchase the ingredients and make a personalize soap. There is a tea plantation next to it.

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We went on a cloudy day and the driver drove us all the way to the entrance at Yeongsil.  Having a hot afternoon the day before, we thought it would be warmer thN the day before as we Han to walk uphill. The driver saw us in our thin layer, offered me a rain and wind breaker and a pair of gloves. I reluctantly accepted them out of courtesy but later genuinely thanked him after four hours.On a windy and cloudy October morning, the temperature actually dropped as we ascended. Two hours later it got even much colder with strong gusts, as we approached near to split of the main road to either continue uphil to the top, or to go downhill to the other parking lot. I had to use my gloves and another layer there. My husband regretted not bring his hat on a cloudy day to protect his cold ears (anyway later I found his nose sunburnt even on a cloudy day)We used our walking sticks and wore our hiking shoes, which I found very helpful. We saw some people who really had difficulty completing the loop.  I suggest tourists first decide whether you physically can complete the four hour trip (adults) to the other parking lot. If not, better discuss with your driver (if using one) to meet in the starting point, or decide where to park your car, if not taking the bus.Pack your bag reasonably and don't take any unnecessary items. Some snacks are helpful though as there are no snack bar at all. I suggest also try to bring your garbage downhill as I don't think there will be regular cleaner everyday up/downhill for hours'hike.

We went for Oedalgae and ended up taking an unplanned walk along Olle trail #7.It was drizzling when we arrived, we took some photos of the rock and explored the area. Further into the park, we followed the trail which hugged the coastline. Beautiful views all the way... We went past a cafe at some point, it would be a nice place to relax but we were short of time. We ended our hike near Storyville as the pathway was blocked by fallen trees/branches due to the recent typhoon.

We went as a family with young children (age 8-16) and they enjoyed this park. It has a few mazes to choose- all with a different configuration and theme. Just be careful to go in the maze when it's not too dark, or you just might get 'lost'! Overall, quite a fun and challenging adventure - especially for the kids!

We wanted to hike to the summit of the Hallasan mountain, and decided to use the Seongpanak trail.It's roughly 9 kms from the parking lot to the summit, and it took us around 2h50m at a constant pace with few stops. This is a very scenic hike starting in the middle of the forest, and close to the top through prairies. The hike is properly maintained with stairs and paths, but some parts have many rocks, and thus proper hiking shoes are highly recommended.The views from the summit are spectacular!

We walked the Eorimok Trail and it is a well maintained trail with signage all along the way that keeps you informed about how far you have gone, how far you have to go and categorizes the slope into three levels of difficulty (red=steep; yellow=moderate slope; green=gentle slope). It took us 2 hours to get to the tea house (Nambyrok Junction) from the parking lot at the base.  Even though we didn't go to the summit, there are beautiful views all along the trail. While this isn't a mountain climbers kind of trail, it is the tallest mountain in South Korea. My legs were sore for a week afterwards and I am in good shape. Be advised:  About 2/3s of the trail has big trees and good shade; there is no water along the trail; there are emergency phones every several hundred meters; and there is a single track 5-10m off the trail that looks like it would be used for emergency evacuation.

We visited Woljeongri Beach as a rest stop while driving just to have some ice cream.  Even though the weather wasn?t particularly good in the midst of the monsoon season, the beach still looked amazing with turquoise water.  You can go pretty far out and the water remains shallow although we didn?t go in as the water was a bit cold.  There isn?t a lot of parking available nearby but plenty of decent restaurants and cafes nearby.

We visited Udo Island in October 2016 and took the hop on hop off bus and got off at the first stop to climb up to the peak where the lighthouse was.  The climb took about an hour and though there were steps and a well travelled path, it still required some physical effort. There were hardly any trees and you would be well advised to wear a hat and sun block. Wear comfortable walking/hiking shoes and bring plenty of drinking water.  We climbed to the peak on a hot sunny day and had to stop a few times before we reached the lighthouse. The view was worth our effort.  Then we climbed down to the surrounding park, which was basically grassland with minimal trees and hardly any shelter. There were lots of other tourists.  We saw some horses grazing here and could see across to the mainland and sunrise peak as well as parts of Udo below.  This is the most enjoyable part of UDO for us and highly recommended.

We visited this site with a group of friends.Everybody had their own take on the mysterious road and all had their theories. A quick visit to the internet would provide the answer. However, this all detracts from the pure fun of the site itself. However, part of the fun is discussing the   mystery   of the road.The site is a simple narrow two-lane road. It is not huge. There is plenty of parking for visitors to stop and examine the surroundings.  There are snack stalls along the road where refreshments and some simple snacks can be bought. I noticed some posts on TA that say this is a   tourist trap  . I do not see how this would be the case as nobody is forced to buy or pay for anything.  Anything we bought was food, which, to me, does not seem to be predatory on tourists. In fact, I was hungry and thirsty and was happy to purchase some cooked local yams and cool refreshment. There are tourist traps on the island, but this is not one of them.Having said the above, the attraction is not a major development and is not meant to be a huge event to take up one's itinerary. It is a fun and simple site to visit which can be added to the list of places to visit when in Jeju.

we visited this place with little or less expectation as many friends had said it too overrated but to our surprise is pretty awesome. Maybe because there was strong wind and rain the waves were very strong. The waves were hitting almost the observation point. We bought rain coat outside the cliff entrance for 2000wons (2$) and trust me its best decision we did. We were showered with water like anything as there was rain and wind. maybe in other season you dont need to worry aobut it. the phone number listed on site took to the parking lot the resort next to cliff, had to walk a bit to reach it but got to see the resort common area with some nice garden and statues!

We visited this place on a slightly gloomy day. This and the amazon green colours of the flora made it look like a mystic forest, something out of an animation. They say, walking among these nutmeg trees has healing properties, and eventhough I was sceptical at first, soon I could feel my nerves calming down. It felt like someone poured some sleeping powder on us. Oh and the smell! I've never felt such pungent yet clean fragrance in a forest before, it's truly unique. All those pretty colours and the distinctive smell of nutmeg and cinnamon trees makes this pathway a mesmerizing experience. The route takes at least 40 minutes-1 hour. There are some charming restaurants and coffee places before the entrance, and a huge parking lot. The whole are is beautiful.

We visited this area with kids ages 3-11. Easy paved walk through a beautiful scenic shaded walkway. The falls were breathtaking. We took our shoes off and soaked our feet at the end of stairs leading into the water. Ate an easy convenience store lunch when we returned to the parking lot before heading to our next destination of the day. 1,000won for kids, 2,000won for adults. Can?t beat the price.

We visited this area on our volcanic forces lava tour through Expedia in November 2016.  It was a cool, windy day so we didn't spend even an hour here.  Maybe 45 minutes.  You have to take stairways down to the cliff area.  Then we were freezing even with our layers and coats due to the wind blowing right through us.  It reminded us of the lava cliffs along the coast of Volcanoes National Park on the Hilo-side of the Big Island.  There are even palm trees in the garden area before you start descending towards the Oceanside cliffs.

We visited the National Park as well as Mt. Hallasan during our trip to Jeju-do. It is a beautiful park with average to good hiking trails. We took the long trail (Seongpanak, 9,6km) up to the summit, which took us 2,5 hours (i will take you much longer if you hike slowly and take breaks!). The view from the Summit was just stunning! Definately worth it! I'd advise anybody hiking this trail to wear boots or other firm shoes since the trail is very steep and rock at some parts. You also have to start early in the morning (~8am) since you have to reachthe second station until 1pm to be allowed to go to the summit. Geaneumsa trail is currently closed!

We visited on a dull wet day but even then there was plenty of sparking glass to see.  Everything you can imagine made of glass.  I loved the mushrooms and pumpkins and some of the weirder sculptures.  On a sunny day it must be even better.  Great place to take kids and, except for woodland walk it is all accessible for people with walking problems.There are examples from different parts of the world and you can watch craftsmen making things - and even book an experience to try it yourself.

We visited Oedolgae with Jejueco Suite?s package tour.  Victor, our guide, told us an interesting story of a lady praying for her husband who is lost at sea.  As it was then near sunset (about 1 hour prior), the rocks were backlit and we could not take a photo of the ?praying lady and her fallen husband?. Victor told us to continue along the Jeju Olle Trail (marked by ribbons) for a seaside hike, and he will wait for us at the next carpark.  I forgot to ask him how long the walk is expected to be, so when I can?t see any carpark after 10-15min, I kept wondering if I had somehow taken a wrong path.  So for the benefit of Victor?s future guests, these are the approximate GPS coordinates:Oedolgae: 33.2390574,126.5446144Carpark: 33.2397470,126.5318070(You will pass by a cafe called 60 Beans)Along the path, there are other viewing platforms of Oedolgae Rock where it was not backlit by the sun.  However the angle was wrong, and from these other platforms, you can?t see the shape of the ?praying lady and her fallen husband?.

We visited Mount Halla National Park yesterday, Aug 25th, and it was an excellent experience and great views!It is very easy to get there by the 740 bus from Jeju Bus terminal, now here is the tricky part.. there are several entrances and trails. All of them are intense hiking. Use comfortable shoes, take lots of water and snacks.. there is nothing to buy up until the very top, which is noodle soup, water and chocolates......We took the Eorimok trail to go up to Witsae Shelter and took the Yeongsil trail to return down and my recommendation is:Take Yeongsil train, the view is by far much better than the one from Eorimok trail.In order to get there:Take 740 bus and get down on Yeongsil ticket office (@45m) and from there take a taxi to the main entrance (there is a taxi that goes up and down all the time and charges 5000). Please take the taxi, otherwise you will end up walking uphill for @2km. Once at the entrance... just follow the signs to Witse Shelter. Take lots of pictures along the way!Again ... it is uphill .. from @900m to @1750m, with lots of stairs and rock trails on both trails. Up and down in @5 hours is an ok time.Enjoy !!

We visited Jeju only for Hallasan mountain! There are two ways on top, one easier and one harder! We took the easier to get on top and the harder to get back down! Once on top you will have a beautiful view over the national park and the island! Take some good shoes with you if you want to take the harder trail! The park is easy to reach by bus

We visited Hallim Park with my daughter in August. It is very nice place with diversified trees, plants, birds. Convenient infrastructure allowed us to see so many wonderful natural things during three hours. Two old cave are in the park. It is interesting to pass them especially in hot day.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We visited Hallasan National Park in mid-November. We did the Gwanwum-sa trail up to Hallasan peak and went down the Seongpanak trail. Although Gwaneum-sa is more challenging on the way up, we totally recommend this route as Seongpanak is way more transited. The trees' autumn colours were beautiful and although at the top it was below 0 degress and misty (making it hard to see the volcano cone and lake), it was an amazing experience. Would definetely repeat!

We visited Hallasan National Park in mid December. We ascended via Gwaneumsa trail (8.7km) up to the peak and descended via the Seongpanak trail (9.6km). Gwaneumsa is shorter but more challenging on the way up, it is easier on the knees. We started at 07:30hr, which is the sunrise time. The initial hike was relatively flat, walking on uneven big rocks. There were signs throughout the trail, indicating where you are, distance and estimated time to the peak. Snow started to appear midway and we had to put on crampons on our boots. We took about 3 hours to reach the shelter and another 1 hour 45 minutes to reach the peak. Unfortunately, the weather was cloudy at the peak with low visibility. It was very windy and cold. We joined the queue to have photos taken at the iconic landmark.We started our descent at 12:45hr, arrived at the shelter at 15:15hr, had a short break before descending the remaining 4.1km. We took about 4 hours for the entire descent, exhausted by then.This is the first time my friend and I hiked in snow during winter.
