It is not for the young children. I saw many children who just wear sandals climbed the all steps to the top, and they cried and were angry because of the heat and hard work. Actually, Seongsan Ilchulbong is nice picture taking place from far, but there is nothing spectacular on the top. It is better to climb Seoungsan Ilculbong in the spring or fall, not in the summer. Otherwise, it is good enough to look at it from the parking lot and take a walk around shore areas.

Very underwhelmed. Arrived by ship & took free port shuttle into Jeju-si (capital) & dropped by the Jungang underground shopping street & Guandeokjeong. Walked past Yongyeon Bridge & past park to Dongduam rock. Pleasant walk. Then back to find Black Pork St, but didn't try it as we had heard it was nothing special. Enough to fill in a day (about 6 hours ashore.) Friends who went on a trip round the island said it wasn't terribly interesting & worth the cost. Do pick up a map from the tourist info kiosk, not far from where you arrive, then you can walk round sights described

Very talented artist and excellent works, a sad and interesting story. While the museum itself has only got a smallish collection, the park and the streets around the place is really worthwhile exploring, nice cafes and restaurants in the area too.

Very skilled young Mongolian horseriders, who perform a small Korean/Mongolian (horse)drama in an hour. Be aware of the showtimes, because I think they only have 4 shows a day. We were too late for the first show and while waiting for the next show we requested the taxidriver to bring and wait for us at Hallim park, which is only 10 minutes away. We also combined this with a short beach vsiit and local brunch at the beautifull Jeju-beach.

Very scenic place to see a pretty high waterfall flow directly into the sea!! There is an admission fee of $2000 Korean won entrance fees per Adult. Short walk from the ticket booth with steps reaching downwards to the waterfall. Interestingly if time permits, one can walk to the end of the big car park in front of the ticket office and there is an Olle trail near the sea that leads to a Castle of Shell and a smaller waterfall!

Very interesting cliff!Maybe a bit overpriced, however.Main cliff access with fee, but you could also may view a similar cliff for free from left side of the park.Better to be there as early as possible, otherwise there will be many visitors and you'll spend a time for to make nice photos or selfie.Good park at left side, for free and nice - just walk by track by coast and you'll always see the sea.
Very beautiful park with flowers and cultures, exotic animals and a continued paved walk through a number of cool dark caves.

Very beautiful beach, especially in a beautiful day. It is opposite Halim park so remember spend 10 minutes to enjoy the sea. We went there in May and the weather was great. There was a lot of dried squids there but we don't know how to buy it :D

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Unique maze park where maps of the maze are provided.  If you follow the map, it will take you about 5 minutes to complete it.  But try it on your own, and you may take longer or get lost!!   Along the maze, the plant is high, so you can't see over into other areas.  There are three skywalks where you can stand and observe the entire maze and take pictures of it.  Fun for the entire family.

Unfortunately, many attractions in Jeju are man-made and not really worth your time.  However, I wish I had spent some more time at this location as it's one of the few natural, impressive landscapes that you will see in Jeju.  Sure, there's not much to see other than the cliffs and columns, but it is good to spend some time just taking it all in.  Another idea is listening to the sounds of the waves crashing the columns.  There is only a small area for you to take pictures, so I can imagine the place can get crowded during peak season and hours.  It also gets a little cold during the off-season in the fall, so beware.There is also a small park (if that's the best way of describing it) at the entrance of the cliffs that's worth a short look as well.  There are some vendors, small stone displays, and some assorted artistic pieces.

Unfortunately we visted this the day after we climbed Hallasan, so the stairs and uneven ground were awful for my knees and sore muscles. The cave itself is pretty amazing when you think about what formed it. It didn't take long to get through, so don't plan a full day around it, but it was a must see for us. It was dark and wet throughout the whole tunnel. We enjoyed it a lot, but be prepared for the stairs and uneven ground if you have older/younger travellers with you or if you recently climbed a mountain! We had lunch at the restaurant located on the grounds. It was good but expensive (spicy pork was 占25,000 but pork cutlet was only 占10,000). Once you finish, if you love cats as much as I do, do yourself a favor and visit the Maze Park right next door.

Udo Lighthouse Park on the highest point of the island Udobong, is a nice short uphill hike (bikes are not allowed in the park area).  View of the rest of Udo and Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak) from the area is fantastic although it was very windy when I hiked up.  The lighthouse (not that impressive anyway) was off limits and there was a tacky lighthouse park with a dozen or so models of lighthouses.

Udo is like a big kids playground. You rent an electric scooter and scoot around this fun little island. We looped it in about an hour and a half, stopping for iced cream. The rental was 3 hours and so we explored the middle of the island off the beaten path. You cant really get lost and apple maps or navient works great (so does cell phone data). Some expert tips:Get the ?Harley Davidson? 2 man bike.Its rain covered, and you wont get too hot like the enclosed units. Adjust the seat forward (lever under your leg) to free up some space behind your seat for your bagOnce you get your scooter, scoot scoot! Everyone follows the same clockwise loop around the island. Open that throttle and pass those dottling tourists. Udo Awaits!Use your horn, and folks let you pass. Beep Beep!Skip the first two big pulloffs where everyone stops. Its way too crowded and you may have to pay to park! Watch for the big bus! It runs opposite motorcycle traffic and takes up most of the narrow roadway. So dont drive in the middle of the motorway. The bus driver is very safe and watches for confused motorcyclists. It was very safe.Otherwise, beep beep, scoot scoot, and enjoy the Electric Scooterland of Udo!

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.
Two floors of teddy bears for display and one floor for selling them. Outdoor park is nice to walk around. But due to hot weather, we only go out for a short while and hide indoors.

Took the Seonpanak trail, one of the 2 only trails that will lead to the summit. It is a longer route compared to the other but was supposely less challenging. Well, still a very tough hike to me. Much of the path and climbs are big rocks so good hiking shoes and walking stick will be very helpful. No water along the way though one sign mentioned there is one, which was WRONG and not updated. My son believed in that signboard and finsihed his water way before half into the hike. Big mistake!Not much to see along the way, except if you take a detour to view sara oreum. Took about 3.5hrs to reach Jindalrae office/ shelter (which is 1500m high) and after much thought, decided to turn back due to lack of drinking water.Descending is much tougher for me and took longer time. Deers and boars were spotted.Do go early so that you do not have to park too far from the park entrance as the carpark gets filled up fast and you will need to park along the roadside. Go during weekdays if possible to avoid the crowds.Take note there is time limit to reach Jindalrae so that you can continue to the summit.

Took the seongpanak trail up the mountain and must be at the last checkpoint before 1:00 pm or you'll not be allowed to the peak. from the information/parking space down to the station is about 5 km..? and from the station to the peak another 3-4 KM. approx 4-4.5 hrs (walking) from start to the peak. Trail is not very difficult, the first part is not so steep and you could run it if fit enough. but the last few Km is steep and knees gets tired climbing all that stairs. shelter at the last station do sell some drinks, chocolate bar, pie, hot coffee, ramen. Do not climb when it's raining as there's no view but you'll just get wet and cold, unless it's just the climb that's important, It's still relatively easy to go with proper weather suitable clothes.

Took quite some time to find the road. I was there few years ago and I find it very interesting, but this week when I bring my family there, I was very disappointed. We drive pass a few small stalls and want to try on the road and the nearby stall owner was very rude and tell us not to park in front of him. Thus we drive up and down slowly and try on the gravity without having the hand break on. It's a 5 minute thing, will not go again.

Too crowded.  Trail very rough - they   improved   it by adding very large rocks that make it difficult to traverse. We saw several examples of people who had hurt their ankles because of these rocks. We liked the Olle Trails very much but Halla not.  Okay view at the top. Bring layers - it can be cold and windy it the top. Very limited toilet facilities along a several hour hike - you need to hydrate but be careful not too much.The one benefit is we can tell our friends we scaled the tallest mountain in Korea - worth it just for that.  Mind you, the starting point at the park entrance is already pretty high.

To reach the waterfall from the parking area (free parking), you need to go down the stairs (not a lot of steps, but in my opinion, the steps could be quite steep). During my visit, there were a lot of school / college students, so the waterfall area were quite crowded. The view itself is actually quite spectacular, but as there were too many people that time, we decided to stay for around 15 minutes only.
To put it simply one of the best garden parks Ive ever been to. A magical place which  peacocks roam around. very professionally done, a must see while here.

To make sure hikers are able to return to base before sundown, you have to enter the trail no later than noon and must reach the final section of the approach by 12:30.  Gwaneumsa trail was about 8.7 km long taking about five hours at a leisurely pace.  Most of the hike was in a shaded area which would make it comfortable even during summer.   The first 3 kilometers were just a stroll with nicely laid out boardwalks for some stretches.  There are railings parallel to the trails in case an injured person needs to be transported from higher elevation, which made it extra reassuring for me.  Although steep, it was still a relatively easy hike and I made it through the last section without much problems.  From about 1600 m above and onwards, the trails were covered in ice and snow which slowed me down a bit as I didn?t even think about carrying crampons in late March.  As I got a late start the summit area was a little crowded with hikers having lunch or taking breaks.  Luckily, the Baekrokdam peak is a crater and there was a relatively wide area for people to sit around at the summit.  Unlike the Baekdusan Cheonji Lake, Baekrokdam is devoid of any water except a small patch of water that looks like a small puddle from the top.  While not particularly scenic, it is nice to stand at the highest point in the country.  Because of the strong winds, I didn?t stay long and started to head down the less steep Seongpanak Trail which was about 9.7 km to the parking lot.  Few kilometers from the summit was easy with boardwalk paths and steps.  There was a three kilometer stretch of snow covered trails that made the descent quite stressful though.  Once the snow covered area was cleared, it was a long but relatively flat walk rest of the way which my knees were thankful for.  The entire round trip took about nine hours total without much rest.  Having crampons would have shaved at least an hour off of that time.
Though the sight may be spectacular, the site of the cliff is actually very small, but it's nice to walk around the park.
Those columnar joints are indeed very beautiful. Not to be missed. Entrance fee is 2,000 won per adult and large parking areas.

This well set out and very informative museum recounts the history of how many of the Jeju islanders were killed and repressed during the late 1940s and early 1950s.  The visitor passes through a series of rooms, each explaining in Korean and English a different stage in the tragic events.  Apart from the actual events themselves, two things shocked me most.  Firstly, that I had never before heard of the April 3 Uprising, although some 25-30,000 people were killed by Korean government forces and their supporters.  Secondly, that even well into South Korea's democracy the events continued to be hushed up and only relatively recently has the truth begun to be told.  Just a few years ago, mass graves were discovered near jeju airport.  The museum provides such a valuable insight into the island's past that I think no visit to Jeju would be complete without coming here and learning about the events and their aftermath.  Entry is free of charge.  The peace park around the museum provides a place for contemplation after visiting the museum.

This waterfall is easily accessible in south Jeju Island with spacious parking lot at entrance.  Entrance fee is 2000 won, reasonable and worth a visit.  We arrived around 4:50pm and was just in time to watch the sun set there.  If you want to get closer to the waterfall, be prepared to get a slightly wet but it?s a great experience.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.

This was my best experience in Jeju. I went in October 2013 and we went up Yeongsil and down by Eorimok. The hike was not the most difficult, but can be quite crowded. We arrived by car around 8am and there was a queue to the carpark. Note that there are two carparks, one on the lower level (where buses drop you off) and one at the start of the trail. We waited about 45 mins to get into the first carpark, and when we saw that there was another queue to go up, we just parked at the lower carpark and started our hike from there. This is a good idea if you plan to go down by Eorimok - you won't have to climb up to get your car after taking to bus from Eorimok to Yeongsil.The hike in autumn was wonderful, the foliage was awesome and the weather was perfect. There is a rest area between both trails where you can buy cup noodles and chocolate bars. It took us around 4 hours to go up and down.

This was covered under our west course jeju tour.This is a large park with good bonsy trees ,lava caves and plants and animals and a old jeju village huts to show jeju culture.We can enjoy photography.If localite a good picnic spot.food shops available.

This was an attraction I did not plan. But was in the area and decided to do. I did enjoy the climb. They have different levels of intensity and with this views are included. You can take stairs all the way to the top or you can slowly climb. Once up there the view was amazing. If you take a different way down you can even take pictures at a mini park with swings. They also had refreshments at the entrance and a small gift shop with over priced items. Definitely a must if in the area, but not necessarily worth to go out of your way to fit this place in. As its further away from other attractions and buses here can be difficult.

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.  FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!

This was a building to commemorate those who perished when an uprising was brutally put down.  It is part of Jeju's history and should interest history buffs. As we're not history buffs, we just paid a short visit here in October 2016. The building was of fair size and the surrounding park was quite big, but not much to see. It has a serene atmosphere and a solemn place and reminds me of a cemetery.  We saw lots of local school children visiting when we were here.

This stretch of beach is very near Hallim park. We happened to drive by and stopped for photo taking.There are few restaurants, cafes around the area and a convenient store.The sea is clear and there were lots of people lazing by the beach. Was a short stopover for my family, nice scenery, no harm stopping by for quick foto shoots.

This small gallery is tucked away on the southeastern side of the island  but if you're planning on going to a folk village  it's can be easily placed into your itinerary and is a nice break from all of the tourist attractions around the island. The gallery is really just two halls of one guy  KimYoungGap's  work. The photographer  now deceased  only photographed Jeju during his career and it was interesting to see the different landscapes of the island - landscapes that most of us don't see simply because we're so busy checking off all the tourist   must-sees?? This was the only place that our driver  a Jeju native  ran into friends and it was fascinating to note that they could name practically every hill in each picture because each hill (to the natives) was so distinct.The whole visit  including the garden entrance  takes thirty minutes or so. Admissions was 4 000 KRW  but they give you a nice postcard (well  basically  they force you to buy a postcard). Still  the place is well kept  including their bathroom  and we enjoyed our visit enough to buy a photo book. Note that the parking lot is across the street and that you can't enter with beverages or big bags. You have to leave them at the front.

This Rock is believe as a Snake want to be a Dragon, so according to the local story there are God who live a the Sea.  And the Snake should have the Jade from the God and Snake steal the jade while the God is sleeping but before the snake escape the God Woke up and put an Arrow to the snake.  Half Body (Upper Part) already come out from the sea at it's become a dragon but the lower part is still below the sea and become the rock.  That's why the upper part that we can see looks like Dragon Head Rock.  This area is very near from the Parking area, here we can find Orange Seller, Snack seller, restaurant also, souvenir shop.  Nice place to see and near from Jeju Airport.. 10 Minutes from the airport.

This review will be written from the point of view of a middle aged woman of average fitness, not someone for whom a 20 km trek is a walk in the park.Mount Hallasan is the highest peak in South Korea and if you are on Jeju island it's definitely worth visiting. We took the Seongpanak trail, a scenic , easy route which reaches the summit. Plan on one day for the trek up and down. Here are some tips:1. It goes like this - You take a bus or taxi to the Seongpanak trail, and start climbing. It's a mix of  some steps and an easy trail. After a while you reach the first stop - I forget the name - where you can use  the restroom. There's a small shelter where we had our packed sandwiches. After this, the trail becomes a little steeper, and you reach the next stage - the jindeballat rest stop.( Times by which you must reach the Jindeballat stop and when you must start your descent are posted on the trail). There are restrooms here - but inspie of information to the contrary , there was no food for sale. After this the climb becomes a little tricky , and you need around 2 hours to reach the summit . The views are amazing from the summit. The Koreans hiking the mountain were not only super fit, they were the sweetest people I've met. When I became tired near the summit, so many encouraged me with words like   Fighting!     Turn around and see how far you have come.  Tips :1. Wear good hiking shoes - at points , the trail is slippery, and good shoes with ankle support are helpful.2. Carry a stick. You can get your own hiking stick or buy one from the store at the bottom.3. Carry plenty of water and snacks.4. Take a selfie at the summit and you can get a certificate at the bottom stating you have completed the climb ( costs 1000 won)5. You do need a certain degree of cardiovascular fitness to make the climb comfortably. But apart from that, the uneven  rocks and boulders are a little tough to climb, so make sure you do some core and lower body exercises too. 6. If you climb down slowly, it gets a little dark by the time you reach the base. Carry a head lamp.

This post is about logistics and what to expect from the hike. My partner and I hit Hallasan around 6:45 in the morning on a Saturday to avoid the crowds. We drove to Seongpanak parking lot (free and was filling up quickly. A tour bus with dozens of hikers was already there) which was about a 30-minute drive from Seogwipo. From there we took a $15.00 taxi ride to the Gwaneumsa parking lot. As this was not a loop trail, we wanted to take the steeper/harder route in and have gentler descent (easier on our knees) back to our car. Turns out, doing it this way we avoided what felt like hundreds of people ascending when we were heading back later in the day. The Gwaneumsa parking lot has a fee. (Sorry TA fans, I didn't get the amount since we took a cab --- I am sure it is nominal, like all fees in RoK:) People are allowed to camp at the Gwaneumsa section of the park and I saw a few people starting their day as we marched to the trailhead. We were under tree cover and walked along a dry river bed for the first couple of miles. At this time of day, we only ran into seven other hikers on this trail. After you cross the river via bridge, the hike starts to get a little steeper. About two hours in, you hit a large, modern shelter and toilets. Good time to take a break and snack. Or keep carrying-on as you will get a chance to sit, eat and gaze at another resting place. After the shelter, you will cross a much larger, newer suspension bridge. Fresh water available here. The climb will get a bit harder for next half quarter mile. Continue past the foundation of the destroyed shelter. After you ascend the 18-22 inch tall stone steps, you will reach a ridge which is the other good stop.  No shelters (in fall you should opt for the shelter), but a nice wooden platform from which to gaze at how far you've come. Crows will land in search of scraps. At this point you are very near the top, only a couple more hundred feet to go.The crater was dry when we visited (first weekend in October), but still a wondrous site. The seasoned, local hikers brought burners and ramen and were happily chowing down near the crater. Darn! That would have been nice. The  t-shirt, fleece jacket and windbreaker I was wearing barely sustained me, so the hot ramen sounded freakin' great.The hike down Seongpanak was not nearly as enjoyable since we were bombarded by the late starters heading up. At one point, the hikers coming up were in a jam ? seriously, no one could move, there were so many people. There?s a large shelter a third of the way down. As another reviewer noted, be sure to wear supportive shoes with rigid shanks as you're constantly stepping on uneven rock.  I had on trail runners, which was fine going in, but heading down, my feet were pretty battered. The boardwalk was a nice breather when we could get it.*Seongpanak gentler ascent, (and descent) but be prepared to share the trail with dozens and dozens of other people.*Free parking at Seongpanak -- fills up quickly as early as 7am on weekends.*Toilets available on trail.*Take bimbimbap for a nutritious, affordable, and portable snack. Mandoo is another good one -- good balance of carbs and fat.*Listen and look Nuthatches, Wrens, Great T*ts, and other winter birds on the Gwaneumsa trail.*The park states you must hit the summit by noon. I think this is why so many people were rushing to hit the peak at the same time.

This place is the signature sightseeing here. So every tourists would be here. It's crowd with people. There're many shops, kiosk, snack bar and food shops at the front of the sightseeing. So there are large space for parking. You need to buy ticket to get in there. Once you get ticket, you walk straight on the walk way till you see the junction. There's the highlight signage for photo shooting. And you need to choose either way to go. If you go to the right, you need to walk up to the hill and you will see the good view from there. The way to go up the mountain is fine, not too rough. But not recommend during rainy day.If you go to the left, you will see fisherman Village, sea sand sun and fresh seafood from local people. The highlight is the lady from the village dive deep into sea to get the seafood stuffs.

This place is just WOW. The views, the nature, the sea, everything. Even when it is a bit rainy or foggy, it is still a great experience. They do not let you in with any sort of snacks or food other than water, just so you know. You must try the raw seafood that the   mermaids   catch every morning. It is located at the bottom near the entrance. That is, if you like raw seafood. There is plenty of parking and there is even a Starbucks near by and other restaurants.

This place is huge!If you like nature, do visit Jeju Stone Park.  The English audio guide was excellent.  The exhibits were really interesting.  There were indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Do be selective if you have limited time.  One could easily spend up to half a day at this place.As we were a bit short on time, we browsed through the indoor museum rather quickly and still managed to pick up some interesting information.The outdoor areas were really nice and comfortable.  When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This park was the favorite place of my kids in Jeju. They could play with many kinds of birds and exploring safe caves here. My husband and I prefer watching bonsai trees and had intention of bringing some to our home if they could set them for sale. A place to have nice fun with family, just safe and green.

This park provides a pleasant, albeit uninspiring, afternoon. It's across from a pretty beach, has some nice landscaping, a sampling of lava tubes, and a some nice gardens. I wouldn't recommend driving all the way to the west side of the island just to visit Hallim, but if you're in the area, it's worth a few hours.

This park is on the mountain above the Jeju main ship port.The way up can be done with a car, then the entrance to the park is near the large white lighthouse with a great view over the coastline.you'll have their wide green areas. good for to chilling out but can be skip after the lighthouse.
This park is bigger, big to occupy few hours. The upkeep is not as good as many other parks in Korea.

This park includes a variety of sights including two lava tubes, an aviary that includes a variety of peacocks, ostriches etc, a small traditional village, strange little rock people sculptures, and a very impressive botanical garden with outdoor sections around a pond and several green houses.   Some strange combinations in the outdoor section with large palms mixed up with various types of cacti and other random mixes of fabulous plant specimens from all over the world.  The greenhouse plants seem a bit more organized by regions or types (e.g., large cactus collection in one greenhouse; palms in another), with live animals interspersed between the plants (impressive boa and python collection, also some special turtles, and lizards such as nile monitors, iguanas, etc.).  In between plant viewing, I enjoyed a nice cool cactus juice relaxing in the herb bar.

This park has many nice attractions featuring nature and props for photo moment. Personally, it will be great to visit during spring where the park is peppered with plentiful of flowers. There is very little shades and therefore kids need to have their sunblock on. My kids love trains and they had trains to bring them around between the stations. Great fun!Worth the visit but please do not expect it to be universal studio or Disneyland type of park.

This park has it all - Plants, bonsai, trees, birds, ostriches, stone sculptures, lava caves, folk houses. However, it is really big so you might need to have more than 3 hours to finish the entire park.

This park has a collection of 7-8 sections of different type of plants and sights, such as tropical plants, cactus collections, bonsai collection, wild flowers, cave systems, folk village, small cave system etc. You could easily spent 2 hours at this park. The park is nicely planned and appropriately signed to guide the exploration of the entire park. We really liked its cactus collection and roads lined by famous Jeju-harubang (stone human-shaped statues). We definitely recommend visiting this fabulous park.
This park has 9 zones, botanic garden, caves , flower garden, water garden....We spent a present day out in the park.

This park has 9 different areas to visit, including a cave region, a bonsai section and a traditional Korean village.  This will take some time to see all of this, but is well worth the visit.  It is on the west side of the island, and near some nice beaches.

This one amazing place is a must in Jeju! We were not able to go early but I think the best time is sunrise, since it is called the   Sunrise Peak   in english. There's plenty of parking, restrooms and stores for food and stuffs! Nice people around and the view is fantastic! It can be a challenge to go to the top so be sure your knees will last the climb to the peak!

This museum is interesting if you have the keen interest in geology & history of jeju volcanic past. The entire park is very well maintained and its advisable to bring an umbrella if you're those who can't really take the sunlight.For couples who would just want to take a quiet stroll, this place is strongly recommended as crowds here are lesser as compare to other tourist attraction in jeju.

This museum is intended for tourists who love to take photos. Most of the artworks housed in the museum are modified versions of original paintings so that you can integrate with the painting. Hence bringing a camera or a smartphone is a must! A companion is also a must since taking a   selfie   to achieve the desired effect might prove to be impossible.This is one of the two 3D interactive museums in Jeju Island. The other one Trick Art Museum is located farther in the eastern part of the island. We went to this place as it is nearer to the Jungmun Area where most hotels (Hyatt Regency Shilla Hotel Lotte Hotel etc.) are located.Aside from the in-house artworks there is also a park with sculptures and play sets that will be appreciated by kids. Tips: avoid flash photography to get the desired effect; bring a jacket w/ hoodie (can be used in some of the artworks); and black pants make people blend better with the background.Admission costs KRW 8000 per person. The entire area is air-conditioned and wifi access is offered for free. Other extras include lockers to deposit your bags as this may hamper your experience.This is a fun destination for couples families or small groups.

This maze park is very near to Manjunggal cave, maybe 500m away. If you have time, drop by this place for some fun activities with young children. This maze park is also have many .. really many fat furry cats. Cat lovers .. you sure love it.Children will enjoy the maze, it is not a difficult maze to go thru. In between this maze, there is 6 stations for stamping, collect all this stamps as souvenir. To complete the maze, it will take easily less than 30 minutesAdmission fee is a little bit pricey but for the children sack, the fee will exchange the children happy faces.For those who not keen to go in, there is a good resting place outside the entrance.

This maze park is fun! I was amazed by the aroma of the cypress! It was really good and it's like a natural spa to detoxify your body! It was really funny that you keep walking and seeing the same person / family for 2-3 times. Hahaha, both kids and adult enjoyed it! The Korean couple whom arrived at the centre saw us keep turning around and gave us some hint! Even just with body language and point here n there. Then we gave the same hint to another Korean old folks group. It's really an good experience and shouldn't be missed! It's just few mins away from Manjunggul Cave.Ring the Bell hard if you made it to the centre!

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking.  There are different areas to see at this park including 3 long lava caves, an area with bonsai (my favouite), an area of flowers, a water area, a stone area, old JeJu houses and my least favourite...caged birds some in dubious conditions! I took lots of photos.  Plenty of places to get snacks and drinks but chicken a la flies is not my cup of tea!  A nice place to take a picnic.  There are lots of buses there but they all follow a route...if you go left you have a reasonable amount of quiet time from the hoards of yellow hat people and all the selfie photographer's.

This is unlike most Korean beaches because most Koreans go to the beach right up the road. Lots of space to play and relax in the sand and in the water. Beautiful sunset. Emerald water. And white sand. Shallow water is great for kids. No parasols (umbrellas), and no commercial building stores  - nice! Doesn't feel like a Korea beach at all. Tip: Park on the right near the camping area. That's where you will find a nice quiet sandy spot next to natural sand dunes. Wow!

This is the local traditional market. You can buy the local products here as souvenir such as keychain (Many designs of Dol hareubang),chocolates products, tangerines chocolates, tangerines tart and etc. Most of the stall owner didn't speak English but some can speak in Chinese (Full of people). Multi level car park available here.

This is the kind of park where family with young children will enjoy at least half a day here. The maze is not that simple to fulfill from start to finish, but its a good practice of what a tram work means to the kids and how they should appreciate good team performance. Before and after the entrance of the park, there are scenic attractions where phototaking venues and selfie booth are made available. With kuds runnung around and getting more attracted to the children's playground which I think is a very well thought strategy and well kept, it is hard for parents to concentrate and take a decent picture although the scenery and amenities are so tempting to be utilised.

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!

This is super easy to do... From Jeju city go to Jeju Bus Terminal and the lady at the desk will tell you which bus to get. In this case, 740. This takes you to a ticket office and car park. From there you can get a taxi or walk 2.5km to the start of the trail. We walked and it took about half an hour (but it is all uphill). I would say there are about 3 sections to this walk:1. Through the forest - stream nearby and wildlife (I saw a deer). This is relatively flat until the end when you have to climb some stairs. 2. The hard part- walking along the ridge of the mountain going up the stairs. This is tough on the knees but there are loads of places to stop and absorb the view. 3. Along the top- relatively flat through a forest part and then open until you get to the rest stop. It is the easiest hike and does not go to the top of Hallasan, but it is beautiful and gave you stunning views of the top of Hallasan (which you would not get if you were actually on it). Make sure you bring water, snacks and hand wipes. The rest stop at the top sells only instant noodles and has no running water.

This is such a great place!Even if you don't have enough time, you can see a lot.There are few stages and different   yards   to go to.Really peacefull place if you climb few stages up.After going up you can see beautiful view of the coast as well.And the helpful thing is that they have a small shop in front of the temple (downstairs) so after climbing all mountains and the temple place you can get nice drink or ice cream. Also, they have a car parking place.

This is similar to Dongdaemun market concept in Seoul though this time around so many oranges, Jeju oranges. They are all of the same price, you got your numbers, there is no need to go further. The famous Jeju oranges looked fresher here though I think more expensive than those sold at the Dragon cliff site ? another friend had bought hers there. I am assuming that all other things go the same way here at Dongmun market, so we didn?t venture further in. Parking is a hassle if you are driving a rented car, I saw yellow lines everywhere and cars parked almost everywhere.

This is really a large park with plenty of places to visit inside. It is recommended to visit this park at spring or early summer so you can watch more blossom flowers. I visited it in October so there is only few flowers. It is still worth a visit though as you can visit the village, the stadium, the bonsai, the caves, and even a bird zoo inside.. must come.

This is our last stop of our 2nd day in Jeju Island and was worthy for the line Save the Best for last. If you are into caves and lavas then this is the right place for you. Since this is our last stop, we went there around 5PM, we were in a hurry to reach the entrance of the site. Get ready to walk on dark and cold pavements. Although it was cold we manage to take photos inside the cave (which needed editing) and was mesmerized with the unique beauty the cave has to offer. It entails walking so get ready to walk and prepare the right shoes. Plus, inside the cave is really cold, colder than the other sites so be ready with your jackets. You may also explore the park and the cafe located outside the cave. The entire place is relaxing and worth the visit. This must be part of your itinerary once you happen to visit Jeju Island.

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

This is one of the best scenic spots on Jeju Island and we intentionally chose to stay in Seongsan for that reason. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area close to the UNESCO World Heritage entrance. The climb up the tuff cone was gradual along well-marked and well-laid pathways and steps in spite of the throngs of tourists. Do stop occasionally along the route to catch your breath and to catch the surrounding views from various altitudes. On a perfect day, one can see the blue skies against the blue seas and the township of Seongsan below. As a bonus, take the side trail to the Haenyeo or Women Divers? House, to taste the fresh seafood like abalone and other shellfish, sliced and diced before your very eyes and served with kimchi and seaweed. To finish, take a peek at the Dong Am Sa Temple near the car-park. With such a majestic location, the temple is fortunately understated and does not stick out to compete with the volcano backdrop. What an incredible place to spend half a day!

This is one of the best place we visited in Jeju. Various things to see such as flowers, plants, birds, small reptiles, lava cave etc. I love the cactus garden most. Great for photo taking and a slow stroll with family members! I did not fully explore the place due to time constraint. Guess it probably need around 2-3 hrs to slowly explore the park.

This is one of my favorite oreums (volcanic hills) on Jeju!!It is not exactly close to anything so be ready to travel quite a bit.  It is also a steep hike, but each step that takes your higher gives you more and more of a view. I am telling you the negative up first but I am also telling you...it is worth it.  *On the weekends (depending on the season) you will often find coffee trucks parked at the bottom parking lot.  You cannot count on this as they come and go...but if they are there, it will be a nice treat for you.*This oreum is also host to my favorite festival in Korea.  Jeju Fire Festival.  Thousands and thousands of people come to this oreum to say goodbye to the past memories and to welcome spring.  It is a seriously amazing event.  Fire, fireworks, food, beer, shopping tents, performances.....absolutely a fantastic event.

This is one location where you do not have to worry about bad weather, actually I would recommend going here on a day with rain and wind since then you can actually experience the force of nature when the waves hit the cliffs.Easy access, parking (for a fee) and you can walk along the shore line on a board walk (sort of).

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.

This is my 4th time visiting Korea but this is my 1st time visiting Hallasan National Park. It is a great park, however do visit in the day time. Do note, Dec day time is short...do visit Hallasan National Park early.

This is just a park with some trees, caged birds, caves and bonsai. Nothing very spectacular for the krw120000 of entry fee. The signage was insufficient to the various sights so I walked around quite a bit but still didn?t find some key sights.

This is free, no entrance fee needed. But if you go by car, you need to pay the parking, about 2k Won as fas as I can remember.They have a path to walk along. You will enjoy the walk along the ocean, actually it is a quite long track, you can choose to walk from one end to another end. but during my time, we have a short time, so we just go and see the rock, took pictures, and go back. There will be a lot of people selling tangerines(oranges), their tangerines is so sweet, and it is only for 1k Won for 1 bag. and in their culture, after you eat the oranges, you can just throw it away to the ground, as it is organic, so return it back to the nature. you dont have to wait until you find the dustbins to throw it. you can throw the plastic in the dustbins but not the orange skin.

This is by far the easiest rock formation to see on the island. It?s within a stroll from the carpark and very accessible, no Long trials or multiple flights of stairs to climb. Expect bus loads of tourist though. Good views of the coast from the viewing deck.

This is an honest review which I?m only leaving because we weren?t allowed to leave the garden until we promised to give it a TripAdvisor review! Usually I?m much too lazy for such antics.First things first, I think it?s admirable what Bum-young Sung (the owner) has dreamt up and achieved over fifty odd years working here. I also think he has developed very sharp entrepreneurial acumen over this time - the entry fee is 12000 won and thousands of people (us included) seem to be happy to fork this out given the decent ratings Spirited Garden has achieved.Is it worth it? I?d have to say no for the following reasons:1) the garden is actually very small (you can wonder through it in 15-20 minutes).2) even though the trees are nice to look at (debatable given how some of the trees are shackled to metal frames), there are lots of signs imploring you to see the deeper meaning and philosophical undertones of the plants and stones, many of which didn?t really make a lot of sense.3) the owner will probably come to meet you at some point which seems superficially like a nice touch, but it did feel a bit mechanical - he would then get a phone call about some new guests coming into the park and suddenly have to dash off (probably to make sure they left a good TripAdvisor review)All in all, there?s a lot of great nature to see in Jeju, especially if you want to get away from the chaos and ponder the meaning of life, but why not climb up Mt Hallasan or do an Olle trail instead, and then go and spend your 12000 won on a present for yourself

This is Actually botany park with some few nice spots , i really don't recommend it because there is many more to see in jeju better than here and not worth to paying 10$ to seeing something u really don't understand , most of park is designed for professional botanist not for normal people .

This is a wonderful park-like place that includes a portion of lava tube, traditional drums that are available for people to play around on, and apparently numerous classes including pottery. The plantings are fabulous, and there are some examples of Jeju's own dialect.

This is a very well maintained mountain park as expected of any Unesco World Heritage site. My wife and I visited on a Monday and it was packed with people. We climbed up from Yeongsil and climbed down to Eorimok. It's impossible to lose your way. The hike is moderate and you don't have to be very fit to do it. Trainers or tennis shoes are adequate in May. You can do it at a leisurely pace or try to break a speed record. Hot noodles is available at the top (this is not the summit trail) or you can pack your own lunch and there are also a couple of water stations along the way on the Eorimok trail. The view from around the top is expansive but hardly breathtaking. Overall it's a pleasant and enjoyable hike.If you park at Yeongsil and return at Eorimok or vice versa, you can take a taxi back to your car for 20,000 wons.

This is a very nice park with some diverse points of interest. The lava tubes were interesting. Especially stunning is the walk through many, some quite old, bonsai. What was an aside visit for us became one of the highlights of our trip. I?d suggest two hours at least.

this is a very interesting park, they have at least 3 sections; a museum, 2 parks and smaller exhibits. If you like stones and interested in how they are formed and how they look like and appreciate by the people of the past and present, do visit. some stones have interesting tales like: Goddess and her 500 Sons. The whole park is pretty big, it can take up to more than 3 hours if you go through all the writings and descriptions. do go after a meal.
This is a very good park. You can see a lot of varieties of flowers, trees, and birds in this park. Also, you have a chance to see two-dimensional caves.

This is a very easy climb, you can take the bus from the city in Jeju and go all the way until the car park there the path is well marked and you just have to follow the trail it is an easy ascend to the summit then you can com back the other way (west ascend and east descend) and just follow the way back from the east, it is very easy and well marked all the way back, at the bottom yuo can take the bus back to jeju again.

This is a park for all seasons. It is beautiful any time of the year. We were there in autumn and although the colours were not significant yet, there were plenty of flowers to please any nature lover. The only set back is the cave. It can be quite wet inside and one has to be careful.

This is a nice place to have some scenic shot. The natural volcanic formation is indeed unique. The walk from the carpark to the scenic view is just a short 10 Min slow stroll. There are amble carpark but there are many tourists too. If you don?t stay at the cliff to absorb the nature then the entire place can be done in just 45mins. So if you are here, don?t rush so that you can enjoy the wind and listen the waves hitting into the cliff!

This is a nice park with a lot of different flower and tree species. It's worth a visit and also a good opportunity to have a walk. You can climb on top of the hill to have a 360 degrees view (there is also a small cemetery there, not easy to find : take the most  peripheral path). Even in autumn it is colorful !
This is a nice maze park, and is suitably quite tricky to find the middle.   When you find it you ring the bell!

This is a national park in the true sense.  There are long walking trails to see amazing sites, and you must be prepared to spend time and be in good shape for the walks.  Also, bring plenty of water for the walks.  The park has awesome views and long and winding roads.

This is a must see whether you drive, hike, or use some other means. It's scenery is stunning, the park is well kept up, the staff and other tourists are friendly, and it is some great exercise if you hike to the peak.

This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. The temperature drops quickly: it was 28C outside when we visited in late September but only 15C inside. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.
This is a huge park and we go around by trains. Not much to see other than natural scenes, but good to walk around. Access is not convenient, you need cars.

This is a heritage site regarded as one of the New 7 wonders. Many people come to this place. The parking is huge but can be tight at times. Better to come here in fair day, so that you will enjoy the view. Bring your camera and water too. There are quite number of fastfood on the area if you need to buy snacks.
This is a great park for the kids, next to a beautiful beech. Loads for the kids to do. Great place for a picnic

This is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall, garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These are six themed model parks jn which over 250 models are exhibited. These include glass qrt masterpieces by international famous artist from Italy, the Czech Republic, Japan and more.At least one hour explore the entire exhibitation garden. Visit at night as the place is well litted and less tourist.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

This is a big park where you get to sample the attractions seen in Jeju . We enjoyed visiting the folk museum, flower and bonsai garden, Jeju stone park as well as the place where they have big palm trees. Our time was limited so we didn't really stay here for long.

This is a big area in the outskirts of Jeju city, need to car to get there. There are many stone formations around the park and there is story of an old grandmother who had 500 kids and was finally cooked in the porridge and the kids ate her as they didnt know. There is a nice stone museum that explains how rock formation on Jeju is formed and all about volcanic activities and some weird looking rocks. Educational place for kids!

This Hallim Park is a big area with the palm tree, tulips, cherry blossom, etc.  They also have some cave and near to the sea.  They have Historical Story since 1971 if you see the website.  We need to have 2-3 hours i think to go arround.  When i visit here last week, we still can see the tulips.

This Eco Land is nice and Comfortable for doing Recreation.  Relaxing and Quiet Place to visit.  They also provide Train Inside the Park.   The Train come every 5-10 minutes Here we can decide which area we want to go.  There are area with Park, Lake, Holland Decoration.  There also a place that we can do Recreation with Family Complete with the children playgrond area.  They also have Garden with some Flowers, such as Lavender, Tulips, etc.  They also have Place to have some snack like coffee, churros, ice cream.  Enjoyable place to relax and need some time to enjoy all the area.  Good to Visit.

This beach was absolutely breathtaking! The sparkling fine sand, emerald clear water, and green hills all around made for a perfect beach day! Unlike what was stated in previous reviews from July 2019, we never had any problems with being able to swim freely and as far out as desired. There was also no line set out not to cross. This is the first beach I've been to with provided shading tents and umbrellas, but it was definitely nice for when we wanted a short break from the sun! We also never had to pay to use these, so I'm not sure if that is something only done during the busy season. The beach was not over crowded, especially at low tide, and it was easy to find little secluded areas if you wanted to be away from the majority of people. Locals were walking and swimming around to clean up trash, so it was honestly one of the cleanest beaches I have been to! Plenty of yummy restaurants to eat at, as well as bars for those wanting to stay out late and still have a view of the water. Be warned, there are no stores close by that sell towels, sunglasses, or other beach essentials, so make sure you are fully prepared! Definite   must see   while in JeJu!

This beach is adjecent to GeumNeung Beach - you can walk between them. Hallim Park is also next to it - all are walkable from each other. There are plenty of shops and umbrella rentals, etc. Camping is avaiable at the next door beach. Some areas are not for swimming due to strong currents. Lovely view of a nearby island. You can take the 202 bus from the 5 day market near the airport. Takes about an hour.

This attraction would be hard to describe. A huge park with magnificent exhibits of boulders and rocks. The park was so silent but the exhibits made their statements loud and clear.  An enjoyable afternoon just to immerse in the natural beauty of something as common as rocks, pebbles and such. Who would have imagined that such an outdoor exhibit could offer so much. There?s even a mothers? nursing room within the park itself.

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

This ancient historical & cultural village was meant to show its rich origin & history. Therefore, it was left intentionally in its original state ie old, rundown & unmodernised. Living in an ultra modern city, it was a very humbling experience for us to be able to witness what living conditions were like in those days.It is a very small village, so obviously there aren't much to see or photos to take. There were big portraits of the 2 lead casts of the famous Korean drama   A Jewel of the Palace,   filmed in 2003. This drama probably spark off the K-Wave phenomena worldwide. Maybe this was one of the filming sites.The resident guide gave us a walk & run up of the place. After which, we went to a small hut where she was explaining the honey & other products of this village.Sampling of honey was given. She did not hard sell nor push anyone to buy. It was the visitors' own free will if to buy.Many in our group (including us) bought the honey because they loved it & not because they were scammed or hard-sold.

These cliffs formed when Hallasan erupted and lava flowed to the sea. When the lava hit the sea, the contrast in temperatures caused the rock to form hexagonal columns, giving us this beautiful view! This is a really neat sight to see, but you don?t need to linger. It?s a great place to stop on your way to the waterfalls. Parking is cheap and plentiful.

There's parking place but there's a fee to pay around 2000 won for my rented Kia Sportage   , Entrance fee was 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for youth . We walked around the park nearby the stairs leading to view the cliff from here .
There's a lot of themed park to choose from. But some of it can only be enjoyed during selected weather seasons (ex. winter, spring).

There's a car park round the corner from the market. Came down by the lifts to the middle of the market. There's fresh sea food, vegetables, fruit and a lot of locally produced chocolates and pies. Stopped at one of the hole in the wall eateries because of the freshly shucked oysters (KRW 5,000) and sat down for seafood stew (KRW 12,000). Scrumptious lunch!

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)

There was so much to see and do, and the actual burning of the hill is spectacular. I spent half a day there and hadn?t seen everything. The thing to be aware of is the time it can take to get out of the car park afterwards, but totally worth it !

There is only 1 main maze park that separate into left and right wing. However, the maze park is not as big as expected. You will need to walk through the park and follow your   six sense   in order to reached the destination and ring the bell to prove that you have walk out from the maze. ;)

There is a train servicing in the theme park that will drop the visitors to every station and allow them to walk around and take photo. As of the name   Eco   the theme park is closed to the mother of nature which basically full with plants and trees. Besides, highly recommend the lavender ice cream in the lavender and rose garden station.

There is a start sign & stop sign. Upon reaching the start sign, switch to neutral gear, on hazard light, and keep your car engine on. It will start to move forward on a uphill slope. Very slowly. Of course, do be alert and keep your eye infront and foot hover on brake if necessary.It is a one lane traffic, so not all cars are stopping to be wow by this nature forces, you might be honked by other drivers for slowing down and doing this anti-gravity act. Well... just ignore them. They will move on by cutting your lane.There is a convenient shop next to it and car park. You can park your car there and come down to try it with a half-filled water bottle. It will perform the same too, rolling up on a up-slope.However, beware of cars. There is still on-coming traffic.

There is a stair to reach to top to this extinct volcano. It seems easy at first but you will need to be prepared to reach its top. They put places to sit through the course.Since I was there during summer time, I sweated a lot. But reaching the top pay all physical efforts!Then you can walked down in order to see (and get enjoyed by) the friendly ladies who dive! It was nice to see that they also served the seafood they've just captured! You need to see them because they are now just a few and how knows if there will be more of them in the future.Remember 1: the presentations of this ladies happen in specific times (I got their 13:30pm presentation, so I had to walk fast up and down the volcano in order to see them)Remember 2: you should pay a ticket to get inside the park.I truly recommend you to reach both the top of the volcano and see the women divers presentation.

There is a small fee to enter the area, I think around 2-3000W. Once you are inside the park, you can hang out on the paths, admiring the rolling green fields, or head up some few hundred stairs to the top of the little mountain and look at the crater. The little mountain was formed by a volcanic eruption a long time ago and around the rim of the crater there are 99 'peaks' which they call the crown. That's cool. I think that's cool.After you have taken an inappropriate amount of selfies you can head back down to a small beach area and watch traditional women divers...diving. There is also a small black stoned beach by the women divers which you can walk along and admire the beautiful black stone of the small mountain, which is Seongsan Ilchulbong.We travelled there by public transport and it wasn't difficult at all.
There is a lot of activities and nice places. Bonsai garden is incredible, and out kid loved the bird park very much!

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There are two main reasons for which I cannot rate this park a full 5/5. One being that although the park is supposed to be a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, it allows an absurd number of treacherous hikers (most of whom will be waving or dragging their useless trekking poles around, so watch your eyeballs) onto the trail each day. I do not believe that there is a limit to how many people can start the trek, which makes for a very busy and quite honestly annoying trail. Don't expect to be one with nature on this hike. Secondly, the hike itself is not a technically difficult course, but I cannot for the life of me understand why the trail is set with awkwardly placed and downright dangerous rocks. It would have been much better to leave the path completely untouched in my opinion.HOWEVER, the view from the top is well worth the rolled ankles and the gouged eye sockets to which you may subject yourself on this trek.I ascended via Seongpanak Trail (＿?깊 - 9.6km) and descended via Gwaneumsa Trail (愿???  - 8.7km) in late autumn, 2014. Having read that the hike is beautiful in every different season, I originally thought of trekking the mountain at least once per season as I'll be here for a year. I can't, however imagine - no fathom - surviving the brutal heat, humidity and mosquitoes during the summer months. There are a few different ways of reaching the summit of Hallasan and they are apparently not always open. There are also checkpoints that you need to reach before certain times during the year so make sure to get an early morning start and to do your research before attempting this hike.

There are two lava tubes/caves in this park. The tubes themselves were quite interesting but having been to other massive caves before (e.g. Mammoth cave in WA, Australia), this is tiny. Nevertheless, it is a sight to see.The entrance ticket is quite pricey but the park is huge... And i guess the ticket price is more to sustain the park. I believe some may enjoy it more than us...

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty.
