Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ? Check out of hotel for catch your flight back home.Have a safe and enjoyable holiday!Telephone Numbers of Attractions For GPS:Citrus Fruit Museum - 732 2114Geomun Oreum - 7108981Joongang Underground Mall - 723 1510Jusenggeolli Cliffs - 7381521Lotte Hotel - 731 1000Alive Museum - 805 0888Trick Art Museum - 787 8774Seongeup Folk Village - 787 1179Traditional 5 day market (Jeju-si) - 7435985Seongsan Harbour (Ferry to Udo Island) - 782 5671Seongsan Ilchubong - 783 0959Cheongyejeong Waterfall - 760 6331Cheongjiyeong Waterfall - 733 1528Jeongbang Waterfall - 733 1530Teddy Bear Museum - 738 7600Jeju Folk Village - 787 4501Jeju Sea-World - 784 2333Aqua Planet Jeju - 780 0900Manjanggul Cave - 710 7903Oedolgae - 760 3033

Sangumburi crater is a designated Natural Monument touted as the world's only flatland crater. The car park entrance showcases several large rocks from the crater such as the volcanic bomb and lava tree mold. During the eruption, molten rock flew from the volcano into the air and cooled into many exotic shapes. The area near the crater also contain several traditional Jeju graves - wide, trapezoidal stone walls surrounding the burial mounds. Visitors can walk around the extinct volcano crater rim, peer into it but cannot venture inside the crater pit covered with lush vegetation. The hills and Hallasan surrounding the crater is a picture of serenity and rustic greenery. Sangumburi is especially popular in autumn when the slopes are covered in Jeju?s famous Eulalia. Crowds and couples will be lining up for photos among the tall plume-like, silver grass swaying in the breeze. At a quiet spot, listen to the whispers of the eulalia dancing against the blue sky to add a pensive mood to the autumn romance.  Note: KRW6000 entry fee is quite expensive. Closes at 6 pm, except Nov-Feb closing at 5 pm.

Sammu Park is a destination not likely to appear on the typical package-tour’s itinerary for Jeju Island, but this downtown Sin-Jeju gem has some singularly unique features for the intrepid visitor.? First, the park was actually constructed on one of Jeju’s 368 oreums, local dialect for a small scoria (cinder) cone or parasitic/parallel volcano.? This one is Beduri oreum, surely one of the smaller ones, topping out at just 10 meters above its base with a circumference of 617 meters.? Beduri was transformed into the park in 1978 as part of an urban planning initiative. In addition to a large assortment of exercise equipment,? a children’s play area, badminton and basketball courts, and jogging/hiking trails, Beduri boasts a majestic, two-story octagonal pavilion, called Sammujeong. ? Constructed in the traditional Korean style and ringed by pine trees, the colorful wooden pavilion is almost like a giant tree-house.? It isn’t unusual to hear musicians and vocalists practicing there, taking advantage of the spot’s natural acoustics.? It’s a peaceful place to sip a beverage in any season.? Next, are you a train enthusiast or history buff?? Then you might want to visit Sammu for this feature alone:? the park is home to the last remaining steam locomotive for coal transportation in Korea.? MIKA Steam Locomotive No. 304 (registered Cultural Heritage No. 414) was manufactured in Japan in 1944, during Japanese colonial rule, and operated on Korean railroads until 1967. In 1978, President Park Chung Hee had it shipped to the park on Children’s Day, so that Jeju’s children could see a real train.? The train’s passenger car now contains a children’s library.? Finally, beginning in 2014, the park has been further renovated to be a sort of extension to the Bao Jian Street tourism and shopping district.? At the park’s south entrance, there is a giant clock surrounded by wildflowers and neon lampposts that match those on Bao Jian.? The clock has a Plexiglas dome that gives its neon face a trick-art, psychedelic look after dark.? Sammu Park is definitely worth a visit, particularly if you are staying at an area accommodation or if you will be going to Bao Jian…a chance for a little Jeju “nightlife.”

It is overwhelming with crystal clear sea water fine sandy beach, and unique volcanic rock formation within your reach.  It is free and really worth going. The intercity bus will stop right in front of the seaside.
Part of Hallim Park. Your entrance fee to the park grants access to this site. Nothing special, but already included, so check it out. Easy to go thru, even for the older less mobile people.

Parking was difficult to find in the area when we visited although the walk back to the markets was not too bad. The markets were busy with many local producers sold their wares. Tourist heaven for the local oranges, chocolates and teas with many eating places as well that served a wide range of foods from pork to sea foods, fruits, burgers, desserts, nuts and candy. Much to choose from! Smaller tourist items can also be found along with clothing of the island - not much for westerns sizes though. Fairly crowed, but an experience not to miss while on the island.

Parking is free. The place was so packed! I wanted to get their famous green tea ice cream dessert but upon seeing the queue and the crowd i decided against it. The retails are selling the same stuff you could also see them in Myeongdong O'Sulloc cafe so if you are travelling back to Seoul after your Jeju trip you could save yourself the hassle of lugging them aroung Jeju. Get them in Myeongdong instead. I learned that AFTER i arrived at Myeongdong and saw the teas that i bought earlier were there. Oh well.However there might be some   Jeju only   products available so i guess you could get them instead.So i would suggest to chill visit their museum and have desserts.

Parking is free, next to Osulloc. The ajusshi will be there to direct you in the carpark. Lovely place. I love Innisfree products and im happy to be there. However, there are only skincare products, no makeup items. There is an area for soap-making but we didnt do it. During the time we visited, noone did it too, so i cant comment how interesting it is.There is also an area which you could do ink stamping on paper. If you like ink stamping, do remember to bring some paper along. Its free.The food is organic and took quite some time to prepare. So the best is to find a table first, order your food and then do your retail shopping. We ordered 4 drinks & 2 meals, it took about 20-30 mins to be done. Yes, its that long.There are also desserts and they are made beautifully. How i wish i still have the stomach space for them. I would just come back to have tea and dessert at the place. Dont forget to look at their   Jeju only   products. There is innisfree Hallabong jam and strawberry jam. Yup, jam for bread. So look closely at the retails. The price of the retail items are comparable to those in Seoul, so need not get them unless you desperately need it. Go for their   jeju only   items instead.There is a small tea planatation outside Innisfree, where most is seen taking OOTD. Toilets are behind Innisfree.

Parking is charged. I think we were there for about 1hr? They charged my SUV for 1,000 won, which is still pretty cheap in my opinion.The place is near Jeju International Airport, so this could be your first place in your itinerary or last.So there are two staircases down to see the Dragon Head rocks. One of them is closer to the rocks, which can be hard to see the Dragon Head formation. The place can be quite windy.There are stores selling Hallabong products as well. According to my friend, the souvenirs are priced almost the same everywhere.So rocks.. yea. Im not that keen actually. But if you like nature, you might probably like this.

Parked our car at Seongsan Ferry Terminal and the ticket booth for Udo is in the building on the left. We rented ATVs from the shop just in front of the terminal. Though it was pricier as compared to what other reviewers had paid for, it was very convenient for us to return vehicles just before we board the ferryThe island is beautiful :) contrary to what some reviewers believe,  there is a path up to the lighthouse. It is by the side of a road near the area with many food storesTwo hours is enough to explore the whole island, but I would highly recommend 3 - 4 hours to leisurely and fully enjoy what the island has to offer

Overlooking the cliff from the viewing platforms, the formation is indeed unique and a beauty. Walk along the surrounding path, we get to see the different angle of the cliff and the formation.However, you can omit the park. It is just an added attraction due to the price paid for the entrance.

Overall a clean, well laid-out museum at a very reasonable price at 9,000won each for adults.- Not as many exhibits as we’ve seen at the Smithsonian in DC or Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola but still worth the visit to learn about Korea’s aviation history- Placards translated into multiple languages - Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese. - We don’t have kids but it seemed there were a large number of child friendly play and exhibit areas.- On the third floor was a go-cart type racing track and pizza cafe. It was about 30,000won a person so we didn’t try it but it looked cool.- From the 4F observatory you can see Hallasan Mt, the tea fields of O’Sulloc, and Shinwha Theme And Water Parks.We spent about an hour there in total.

Our visit was postponed for a day but it was worth the wait. There was a heavy snowstorm a couple of days prior and the roads to Hallasan National Park were closed. When access to the park was restored, a beautiful blanket of snow was awaiting.It was my first experience of snow and I loved it. I came from a tropical country (where the coldest temperature ever recorded was at 6 degrees Celsius) so experiencing snow is a surreal experience. Although we did not climb any trail to the summit, experiencing snow even just outside the Visitor Center was fun and pleasurable. The Jeju Snow Festival for 2018-2019 did not include the Visitor Center at Hallasan National Park, however, unlike the previous year so there were no attractions set up in the area.Because of this, I am going back to South Korea this coming December for another winter wonderland experience and to try out skiing.

Our tour bus driver parked the bus along the road,and stopped the engines. In a little while, the bus started moving forward. As pointed out by our tour guide, we have to take note of the inclination of the trees lining the road, which gives the impression that the road is uphill. So,that's it!As in any tour, one has to keep an open mind, curious to learn about the lives and culture of the place being visited, as well as the different places of interest.

Our stamina is not so good so it took us 5 hours round trip for Yeongsil Trail up to Witsae Oreum Shelter and back. There was no Ramen available at the shelter so if you plan to go, better bring lunch box, you will be tired and eat a lot anyway. There are plenty of hikers from old people to children so you wont get lost, even if you want. Yeongsil trail has 4 parts of itFirst part is wooden steps, you will pass some creeks and a lot of shade / trees.Second part is the most strenous part. Lots of rocks and steep climbs , so watch your step. There are some observation deck for you to take photos and rest. And more wooden steps with crazy inclination. After you pass the big rocks crossing,(third part) it will be open area with no shade and this has the best view. And the most leisure part because its flat with almost no inclination. There is water fountain where you can fill up your drink for free. Walk 10-15 minutes from the water fountain and you will reach Witsae Oreum Shelter. Tips : Use sunscreen all over your body, even if its windy and cold at the beginning of the trail, when it reach the open area with no shade, the sun ray will hit you so hard. Wear hat. My scalp got sunburnt. Even better go with long sleeve and long pants. Go very very early like 7 am because the parking lot will be full later.

Our plans to visit Hallasan were foiled by a typhoon the night before (we luckily still got to go, though), and we were all excited to do a nice hike. We came here probably 2 or 3 hours before the park closed (we did some other sightseeing instead of Hallasan, this happened to be close by), and the admission was free because the typhoon had caused some damage. Anyways, because of the typhoon and the time of day, the park wasn't very busy. It felt like we had the walking paths to ourselves most of the time (we chose one of the shorter routes because we didn't want to run out of time). It was a nice, easy, relaxing walk. It was also dead quiet except for the occasional group of ladies walking by with music playing on their phone's speaker. Oh and the crows going off every now and then, but that was kind of amusing since their call is funny to me (and different from North American crows). A good alternative if you can't go up some of the steeper stairs and stuff like in Hallasan. We got plenty of beautiful photos because the typhoon the night before gave all the woods a nice, moody atmosphere. If you like going for walks in the woods (even though these are all wooden paths), just being outdoors enjoying the fresh air, and you have enough time, this is worth a visit. If you are short on time and can only do one park or something, then make sure you try to at least go to Hallasan. I would definitely recommend this park over Hallasan though if you have any mobility issues, because the wooden paths are very easy to walk on and there doesn't seem to be a lot of uphill/stairs.

Our guide dropped us at Seonimgyo Bridge at around 8am, and said he would pick us up around 11.30am.  3.5hrs for waterfalls?  I thought he must have made a mistake...Surprise surprise... We enjoyed the morning stroll across the park near Seonimgyo Bridge (with autumn leaves still visible in end Nov).  After a million selfies, we made our way to the 1st waterfall and was awestruck!  So beautiful!  Well strictly speaking, this is not a waterfall but a lake of some sort.  But who cares about the misnomer?To reach the 2nd falls, there is a well-marked trail.  A medium-distance walk with its fair share of up and down slopes.  Not arduous and I would definitely recommend it.  The waterfall is not Niagara, but I found it pretty in its subtlety.The 3rd falls has a warning - the trail may be difficult for children and elderly.  Since I am neither, I had assumed incorrectly that I would find it manageable.  Wrong!  It was a very very long way down (which was fine), and an equally long long way up (nearly killed me).  Was it worth it?  I am afraid not... for the 3rd falls. So my recommendation would be to visit the first 2 falls, but give the 3rd a miss (unless you want a workout).

Our family hiked up with the Yeongsil trail. We parked the car, started from 1280m above sea level and did around 400m more. The trail was well managed and the hike just kept going uphill, you go through endless stairs. The view got better and there was a rest station where you can get food like cup noodles. We didn't reach the top because the path was not available when we went, definitely check out the availability of the trails before you head to any. Overall, good experience and am definitely recommending this.

Our driver suggested for us to visit this place as we were fond of seeing the flame grass, of which some can be found on the roadside of Jeju.Can?t advise on the travelling mode as we booked a driver to send us there and it was by car.For entrance to the crater, you have to purchase a ticket at 6000won. The park was filled with 듭ⓒ (eok-sae) or in another name, flame grass. Our driver informed us that the grass usually grows in August and at the beginning, it?s purple in colour. Towards the October, it becomes pale golden (as it has dried up). The park is pretty big, and you can get to the top of the crater where you can look down to the middle of the crater. On the way up, you can see the remains of the volcano by the volcano rocks forming a rocky path and also the volcanic ashes amongst these rocks. Going down from the top of the crater, you will pass by many trees, leading to an empty grassland which can be good for jump shots and some random photo-taking. While making your way back to the entrance, you?ll pass by a graveyard park, of which is suspected to be the family of the owner of this place. there are stones surrounding the graves to prevent horses from coming in to eat the plants on it. It doesn?t have a creepy feel to it and there were many children playing soccer in the park itself.At the entrance, you can also purchase some snacks like hotdog and ice cream. We tried the grape and mango ice cream, which were too creamy for our liking.
Opposite to Hyeopjae Beach, it is an old fashioned park with almost every element in Jeju. Caves, plants, mini zoo, and even a folk village. 10000 krw entrance fee is not cheap though.

Only visit uf you have too much time to spare. This park contains trees and flowers with walking paths but nothing special there. It was a nice stroll for an hour with the wind breezing but if you are pressed for time, skip this.

Only 2,000won per adult for entry and no fee for parking. It was a rainy weekend in early Sep. when we visited and wasn?t too busy for a Sunday.Amenities: There is a little restaurant, Lava Tube mini-museum/info-walkthrough and convenience store by the parking lot. There are also bathrooms by the parking lot, by the convenience store and before you enter the tubes.There are fairly steep steps entering the lava tubes but a near flat, albeit uneven walking surface through the tube. Watch your step and beware of puddle during rainy season.Dim pathway lights are set up throughout the tube and unless you have a really hard time with adjusting to the dark you should be fine.It was nice and cool inside with placards in Korean and English highlighting the features of the lava tube. We held off on pictures until the end where there is a well-lit lava flow that came from the ceiling.

One of the top places to see in Jeju.  Great view of some craggy coastline.  The other reviews are pretty good and we experienced about the same - great place, but really crowded even though it was raining!  Again...people come in waves, just wait it out.  The wind was high and seas rough so it made pretty spectacular wave crashes.  On one side there was a consistent high wind and mist/spray coming at you, so watch your cameras!  There is a 1,000 W Parking fee on top of the 2,000 entrance fee.

One of the most popular trails in Hallasan National Park.To get here, take bus 781 from Jeju City. The fare was 1 800 KRW (the driver can give change). The journey is about 40 minutes. The stops are announced in English. The stop is Seongpanak.Set out early as you have reach Jindallaebat shelter by 1 pm in summer (12 pm in winter). Otherwise you wouldn't be allowed to reach the summit.The trail is 9,6 km long (one way), about 4,5 hours without breaks. The trail is in some parts very ROCKY so good hiking shoes and walking holes are strongly recommended. Don't worry you wouldn't climb alone. A lot of Korean will be faster than you.The view on the summit is well worth and rewarding.Bring water and sun block.You can buy a certificate for 1 000 KRW.

One of the more outstanding attractions on Jeju Island. It was raining almost everyday while we were on Jeju Island, but the day we visited this cliff, the clouds lifted and we had a beautiful view of the cliff. The entrance and the rest of the park (the area surrounding this cliff) were very unassuming though, and to a certain extent, poorly maintained. Don?t waste time hanging around those areas, just head for the cliffs straight away!

One of the best UNESCO place. Worth it to come here and visit this place. We spent approximately 50minutes here included walking and taking photos. The addmission fees is ??2,000 per person still affordable for me and the rate still the same as we went here last year. The parking space were spacious with numerous parking units available for visitors. Gentle reminder, please be cautious on your steps as some of the areas are quite dark and jacket is a must to wear to enter this lava tube place.

One of the best location that i went to while i was in Jeju. Highly recommended for theme park lovers and those with kiddy heart hehe. I love Jeju so much for the uniqueness of this castle. Fancy, colourful and happy place to be!

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.

One of 3 famous waterfalls in Jeju, along with Cheonjiyeon Waterfall and Cheonjeyeon Waterfallis but apparently the only waterfall in Asia to fall directly into the ocean.  Definitely worth the short climb down to get as near the fall for nice shots and a sea splash. If lucky, you might even catch a rainbow over the fall.  Walking shoes recommended to navigate the rocky boulders.  Do come early before the tourist horde arrive.  Adventurous hiking enthusiasts can continue to the Olle trail from the carpark entrance.
One may think that stones and rocks are boring, but not at Jeju Stone Park!It is fascinating to learn about how Jeju is geologically formed and see these amazing sculptures.

on reaching the car park ., Go and grab a J - Shape ice cream before you buy the entrance ticket to this Unesco Sights . To those who is not so fit you will be able to rest on the way uphills with the friendly stools provided at different stage of the climb upwards . Wonderful Sight await you on reaching the peak and you will want to catch up on your breadth as you soak in the sights . Never to be missed !!

On April 27, 2017, We took the Yeongsil Trail up to Witse Oreum Shelter, have lunch there and took Eorimok Trail down.  It was a sunny day with cool breeze, ideal for hiking.  It was indeed a great hike, and yet when we reached Witse Oreum (at 1,700M altitude), we felt cold.  We wished there were something hot to drink, and I hoped to take a leak after the last one a few hours back.  Witse Oreum has everything I need, and, we found hot cup noodle sold in the Witse Oreum Shelter at a surprisingly low price!  It was indeed heaven-sent !  Thanks to the park management for installing such a great facility.

Okay so we went to the address given by Tripadvisor, and to our astonishment it was just a small garden behind a hotel. The only reason I can think why it was set to that address - is perhaps there's free parking? Dont give up if you're there! Because the actual site is only about 800m further down. There's a walking path (goes uphill from the hotel garden) along the coast, so simply walk along that and forgo the stone garden (needs an entry fee). The actual cliff site is open to public and free for viewing..Path is quite family-friendly.

Ok ok, to be honest...most of my rating is because of the seemingly endless cats that were here. I hadn't read any reviews of this place before going, I just thought it looked vaguely fun and was located right next yo Manjanggul Cave. Upon arriving, we noticed a couple of cats in the parking lot. I was so excited! When we got to the ticket booth, suddenly there were more cats! Directly beyond the booth is a small area with some handmade cat tower type things and some scratching posts. There were maybe around 15 cats in this area. I would estimate more than half of our time here was spent watching and petting the cats. The maze itself was fun. It was better if you ignored the map, I think. I think more people go here for kids, but if you're a cat lover, go!
Nothing much about the park that wow me. Supposed to have full bloom in of the stations, but nothing at all. quite disappointed though. Will not return after 1 visit.

Not so much of a theme park, there isn't any rides apart from a train. But we had fun there, many gardens, landscapes and things to see. We walked the long Eco trail. The place is well maintained and clean. Wouldn't advise to go in winter tho, as many of the flowers won't be in bloom.

Not only was the view after climbing to the top of Trail no. 2 breathtaking, the track up the steps and steep trail will also leave most breathless! There are markers that state you are at 2-1, 2-2 etc., the 2 in front meaning trail no. 2, but none tells you how much higher you must climb! Incidentally the top is 2-5. Its quite a struggle to reach the top but if you take it easy and take regular breaks along the way to admire the fauna & flora, take some photos and generally get your breath back, you should reach the top in about half an hour. The journey down is much easier and faster. The view on top is magnificent and definitely worth the climb! The fresh cool mountain air was great too. Highly recommend you try. PS : There were two ladies in their seventies from San Francisco who completed the climb and decent at the same time as my group. Two thumbs up to them!!There is also a museum and sculptured garden at the base of the mountain where you can sit on park benches and enjoy the air and general view of the Hallasan mountain and its surroundings.

Not many things beat the sound of a waterfall, and this one is no exception. Situated right where the river meets the ocean, it is a beautiful sight to see.There is a parking area right by the entrance to the trail. The entrance fee is ??2000 per person, and you should be careful when walking along the rocks - they tend to get quite slippery.Note: definitely not wheelchair accessible!

Not a must-visit but it's good place to explore for first-timers. The stretch of road looks like it's uphill but rolling a water bottle will make it roll uphill instead of downhill. It's interesting to watch. Since I self-drive, there is no exact gps phone number for this but you can key in Loveland and you will see signboard to mysterious road. Parking here is free and there's a nearby convenience store and one can chill at caffe bene afterwards.

No trip to Jeju Island would be complete without a trip to climb Seongsan Ilchubong (sunrise peak).  A relatively easy climb that our 4 year old was able to do herself with only a little complaining, it's mainly just lots of stairs. Round trip takes about 50min they say.  We didn't go at sunrise (we would have it we didn't have kids with us) which I imagine would be really pretty but still worth the climb up.  There is a shop selling snacks and drinks half way up if you need to, as well as many at the base car park area. There is also horse-riding for 5000krw and you can go down to the water on the other side.  Not easy to get to unless you have planned transportation or a car as not close to Jeju City, Segowipo or Jungmun.
No high expectation. I?d come after 6:30 because of free parking. Many shops and restaurants are around this attraction, but I would go Hamdeok beach instead ;)

No admission fee is required. The weather was sunny with a little breeze during my visit in end of winter season. There is a walk way to the platform that bring you to the cliff. Scenery is nice and you will be amazed how nature created such beautiful cliff. If you taking public transport, take any bus to Jeju International Convention Centre (the local call it ICC), from there walk about less than 10 minutes by the road side you will see the sign board to the cliff at a T junction. There is a park and is a good place to picnic with your friends or family.

No ! Not again another Fall ! But this one worth the peaceful walk in a nice park and by a small river. If you pass by, go there. You have to see the harbour with small fishing boats. I liked this even better.

Nice wiev, cold water. Not that big but worth going in hot summer days. Easy to reach, wide car parking. Entrance fee than stairs to reach sea level. Fun for kids, if you dare:...... get into the water!!!
Nice pictures can be taken in the park, I most liked bonsai part of the park. 2 gorgeous beaches close to the park entrance.

Nice park, relaxing. The Lava Tubes within the park were nice and cool. Try to go on a cool day. The grounds are nicely kept. The ostriches were not taken care of very well. The rest of the birds were ok. Bonsai garden was interesting. Only the hydrangeas were in season, so no flowers. Only spent a couple of hours there, then headed to the beach across the street.

Nice getaway island. We drove to the passenger terminal, park our car and take the ferry. The ferry ride there was fantastic. We fed the seagulls flying around the boat. it was a spectacular view!To travel within the island, take a bus or pay for a bike..it is a covered bike really cute. Or you can ride a bicycle.We took the bus, need to pay 6k won. There is a ticket office for shuttle bus. Buses numbered k1,k2,k3,rtc..there were 4 stops.the first stop has many actuvities, cafes, restaurants.You can spend an hour or more here. Second stop is lighthouse so we stop too.   The 3rd and 4th stops are the beaches. We did  not get off the  bus  l
nice and beautiful scenery, not very crowded easy parking and ticket were only 2000 won, around 2 dollars

Niagra falls these falls are not, but they are picturesque.  The are small, but the ticket price was also small.  It is a ten minute walk from the parking lot to see the falls, and it is a little tourist trap, but if you have the time to kill check them out, but there are probably better ways to spend your time on the Jeju.

Need more than 2 hrs here to enjoy the scenery and also street food at the entrance.  Be prepared to climb alot and travel light so you can enjoy the views. If you are driving, may need to park some place far off as the carpark can be crowded. Advisable to have a meal before hiking up and down.
Near to Hallim Park. Small beach with brown-white sand and black rock. Better to go when low tide The main beach is usually filled with many tourist, but they have umbrellas and chairs.

Named as Eco-park but really artificial at all... Nothing special with ordinary decorations and plants. Fairly speaking, young children will enjoy the train ride but for adults/teenagers not worth spending time here...

My wife and I hiked the Seongpanak Trail up Hallasan in late May 2015. The trail starts relatively easy but gets more difficult after the first shelter. Make sure you have the rights shoes as the rocks can be pretty hard on your feet. This is a long climb, and for most of the trip you will be in a forest. Keep your eyes open and you may spot some of the elusive small native deer, we saw three on our trip. I am not in great shape, so it was a tough climb for me and took us 9 hrs. round trip. The rocks are really hard on your feet on the way down. Leave early since if you don't make it to the last shelter before 1 PM they will not allow you to ascend to the summit. The last shelter sells ramen and water and a few other items, but be aware you are expected to pack all of your own trash off of the mountain. There are some stores and shops in the parking lot at the entrance to the park, we bought some kimbop for lunch and packed it up with us. This is the tallest mountain in South Korea and the summit provides wonderful views at over 1900 meters high. Climbing Hallasan was a   bucket list   item for my wife, who was born in South Korea, and a memorable experience.

My partner & I chose park our car at seongsan harbour so we could take the ATV. To our dismay, their ATV can only carry 1 driver. Therefore we rented the sheltered scooter that can sit 2. The rental of that scooter is charged at an exorbitant 15,000krw/hr. We exceed the return time by a mere 20 minutes and had to top up 10,000krw T.T Advise to all: Just drive up your car to the ferry. It's much cheaper than spending so much on a cramp scooter, especially during winter.Aside from the transport misfortune, our day afternoon in udo was well spent, but could be better. We took the 12 noon ferry and reached udo at 12:30pm. Last ferry back to seongsan was 4:30pm. We did not have time to hike up, nor enter the cave. Spent too much time cam whoring to take in every bend of the scenery. The Seobin-baeksa beach is beautiful, surrounded by crystal clear waters.Advise to all: Go in earlier, so cater time for hiking, cam whoring, and chilling by the beach. Must have lunch too, the seafood noodles has the freshest abalone and soup ever.

My only concern with Hallim Park is the condition of some of the animals they have there. The 'cages' or 'presentation units' seem quite small for some of them, and some of the bigger birds didn't seem particularly happy. I don't want to give this an 'average' review because the caves are incredibly unique, the diverse array of trees and plants is also very special. But full disclosure, this place may not be for everyone.

My husband and I were staying in the Hallim area and our taxi driver mistakenly took us to Hallim Park. Especially since it was a bit chilly and an overcast day, the beautiful green houses and occasionally covered areas were a nice break from the weather. The park itself is nothing overly spectacular, but it has a little bit of everything with a nice mix of Jeju style to your typical botanical gardens type park. Plants, flowers, animals, exhibits, and fun!

My husband and I went to the Jeju Stone Park to see the guardian statues (Jeju stone heads) but found the park to be so much more than that.  It's a large park (and they are still enlarging it) with an emphasis on nature.  The museum and historic buildings are interesting but walking around the grounds was the high point.  Rocks in their natural shapes are placed throughout the grounds and if you are quiet and observant, the connection to nature just seeps to your being.  We found the place strangely intriguing, calming, and uplifting.

My husband and I visited this park during our honeymoon and it was really beautiful. It consists of 8 botanical gardens which features different kinds of plants, a cave which you can walk through, and even an area with different kinds of birds that you can feed and interact with.We got there through the Yeha Bus Tour but you can also get there with a taxi.For those of you who are looking to experience some of the beauty of nature and interact with it, I recommend this place.

My husband and I visited Jeju last November.Mt. Halla was out of the picture on this trip ( supposed to be ) bec. I am not an adventurous person and I thought I will not have energy to climb this mountain, but after learning that it is a world natural heritage park I finally gave it a go. I was afraid at the beginning of the trail but as we climb further, higher and steeper I was in Awe! I was literally inside the mountain. Plus it  was autumn at that time and the color of the surrounding was just beautiful, it seems so peaceful all you could hear was the chirping birds, gushing winds. It was tiring but i must i was worth it so sad that we didn't reach the summit bec we started a little late. But if i could go back I will strive to reach the peak, but I was still happy though because I've seen the best Autumn inside the mountain..It is really is the Climb!

My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. The staff was so angry with us and adamant that we pay the entrance fees although we were just viewing the falls 5 steps past the ticket office. They stood right next to us and kept trying to push us back out even after we explained our situation to them. I found that absolutely ridiculous. They could clearly see for themselves that our parents were elderly and required some assistance just walking on flat road! Walking down those steps and hiking those boulders were completely out of the question.How appalling! No words can describe how utterly disgusted we felt at the attitude of the park staff.

My husband and I consider ourselves pretty fit people, we regularly run and ski seasonally but we were impressed at the older Korean folks who visited the same track we did!We visited the Eorimok Trail which was advertised as a 3 hour walk one way. This time estimate is definitely accurate especially if it's consistent walking (which we did with very little breaks) if you take a 10 min breaks every so often, it would take you longer. Definitely allocate a full day for this walk and start early in winter as day time is shorter and sun sets early. We started around 10am and made it down by 4.30pm with about an 30-45 min break at the top of the trail. Remember to bring your rubbish down with you, there are no bins at the top!This trail is definitely not pram or wheelchair friendly. If you have had any leg or hip surgery recently I would also not recommend. Even though this is an 'easier' trail the walkway access is not well paved, there are large rocks and very uneven surfaces much of the way up the trail. Near the end of the day, my husband and I witnessed at least half a dozen people needing assistance down the mountain on their 'conveyor belt pulley' which was supposed to only be used for stock to be transported up and down the mountain, but in these cases of emergency some elderly and struggling walkers were transported two at a time, down the mountain. I also witnessed an old man cramping up on his way down, but lucky he was with a walking group, so they managed to organise for him to go down safely.Like many reviews say, there are consistent reminders around noon for walkers to start making their way down the mountain for your safety.This walk was beautiful and we definitely will be back to attempt another trail of this mountain! We were lucky with the weather and there was no cloud cover when we went up, but got really windy when we descended the mountain.If you are driving to Eorimok trail by rental car and are using their rental gps, the telephone number for Eorimok trail for input into the gps is: 7139950 or 7139953, definitely go early if you can, otherwise like us we arrived around 10am and had to park at the trail driveway entrance and hiked up to the full car park :)

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

My family with two boys 10 & 12 hiked up the Yeongsil trail to Witseoreum and back down by visitor center near Eoseungsaengak trail. We made a mistake of getting dropped off at the ticketing office by Yeongsil trail and not at the entrance of the trailhead.  It added another hour to 4 hour hike. But the walk was nice nevertheless and we saw a snake and a giant snail to compensate for it.         Trails were very well maintained and clean. But be prepared for ankle twisters and knee pains. I sure wished I had my walking sticks with me. I had to drink some Hite(Korean pale beer) afterward to relieve some pain on my knees. My two boys had no problem for them being young and all.  A little one did the whole trail on sandals but I don't recommend it as there are sections of trails made up with volcanic rocks. One wrong fall and one can easily get a nasty scrape.  Oh yeah, don't forget to bring, snacks, bug repellent, bandaids, medical tapes for your toes and heels.          I enjoyed the cupnoodle at the Witsoreum.  It was only $1.50. I think coffee was $0.50 or 0.60. There are few other snacks offered at incredibly low price considering the location. They give you a plastic bag to carry all our garbage down the mountain.         One thing I really love about this place is the variety of landscapes. It felt like going to several different national parks at once.         Few things...there are no bathrooms between trailheads and Witsoreum.  Be sure to use airgun a the trailheads to blow away the ticks and other insects off your body and clothes.

review: My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people?s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails ? Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below) ? I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that?s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of ?Jeju Island Geopark?, ?Global Geopark Networks? and ?New 7 Wonders of Nature? and a green signage ?Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m? From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes? walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term ?stepping stone? means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain ?pot-holes?. The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder ? awesome!  There?s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn?t think they were the famed ?Haenyeo? sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam) ? who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn?t like to eat raw seafood so I didn?t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don?t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

My family (including 1 years old and 4 years old kid) visited this place. The experience is very good.If you plan to stay 2 nights at Seogwipo, i suggest you to arrange to go on the 1st day itself, cause the weather is very difficult to predict.Get the help of your hotel reception to 760-6321 and confirm the opening time (might close due to high tide or bad weather)Free parking space available. Have to be extra careful especially going with kids.There are 2 entrance. My daughter and I went to this place because my daughter very fond of Hello Kitty. The exhibition room quite good, but we really disappointed when we saw the park on the rooftop... My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! The maze itself was really good and it took us an embarrassingly long time to finish, :-) This is really for people of all ages! Everybody was laughing and having such a good time that the whole atmosphere was so nice. The workers were very nice, and one man who I assume is the manager had a wonderful conversation with us while we waited for the taxi they had called for us! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby. Must see in Jeju. Biggest lava tube in the world. 2 km from the bus stop, close to maze park. Do not forget tripod to take good pictures as it is rather dark in the cave. Good place to cool down after summet heat.

Mountain HallasanIt was a fanatic walk ever, friendly people all around. Unfortunate in Jeju island, English is not a common language, road signs, information boards are all in Korean, mainly people speak Korean, surprisingly, you might find people speak Japanese and mandarin. There are a few entrances from around the Moutain, make sure you do your research.I believe there are more than 4 entrances. Due to limited time, I have chosen the easiest and fastest trail (Eorimok). You could take public transport or driving. There is parking 17mins walk, and payable parking 1000won, save your time. Be prepared below- Go toilet, do the necessity before you start - Go to visitor centre get a map and find out more. ( e.g. if the convenient store is open?) - 2-3 hours walk one way, the washroom only available in the destination. Choose the hiking shoes. (Bad experience, my sport shoes are ruined) - Best to start your journey at 8 or 9 in the morning, as early as you could. If you are doing other trails, allow more than 8 hours. Eorimok entrance, it took me 5hours, I took a slow walk. - Be warned after certain time (14:30, not certain), you may not be allowed to go in. - Bring a lot of water, or bring enough cash (drinkable water is not enough to supply to public), bring your own food if you don't want to end up eating spicy instant noodle.- Store only sell, instant noodle(super spicy), and spring water. (Limited to 2 portions of instant noodle per person) price: 1000won for instant noodle, 1000won for a bottle of water- Bring extra clothe to change, bring a light weight jacket. (It is a bit chilling on top)- Bring insects repellent spray or lotion- Bring wet tissue and normal tissue- Bring a bag for rubbish, smoking and littering are not allowed.The place is well protected, please respect :)  Voila! Happy Journey!

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly.
