There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Most of the park is outdoors, and we went when it was raining, so that wasn't that good. But the place is beautiful, with trees and stones lined up. There's also a museum about volcanoes as well as statues of historical figures. Very nice place although it is only accessible by car and very difficult to get a cab.

Most of government tourist attraction charge 2.000 won, and the place are so beautiful because its natural. Halim is man made park. It's pretty. It takes around 1-2 hours inside. However the price is not value for money. A lot of other morreee beautiful park in Busan n Seoul that we can visit for free.

Might not be very tall at 1950m but it's no walk in the park. The best part though is that the path is clear and generally easy to walk especially when there are planks. Otherwise walking on volcanic rock and boulders are not so comfortable for the feet. Great views at the top and as we went in spring, flowers are in bloom.

Me and my husband visited Hallim Park, the beach just outside the park is beautiful so make sure to allow some time to check it out. The park itself consists of about 7-8 different theme subsessions. It was a lot bigger than I expected. The park was very well signed and designed with lots attention to details. Of cause it is not comparable to the natural beauty of Jeju but for a man made park, it is a great choice for an outing with family for 2 hours.

Maybe we expected too much of the beach but it we didn't enjoyed this beach too well. We hoped for a large beach where you can swim and relax and maybe some small shops/cafe쨈s around to buy some drinks/food. We spent 25 hours and it was enough since it didn't reach our expectations. We stayed at Seogwipo and took the taxi to Jungmun for around 13000 won one-way. The beach is nice/OK but its crowded (July 2018) and the beach is too small. You can't swim because of the waves and only a small area where you can stay. The rest of the beach is for surfing. You can rent two sun beds and one parasol for 40000 Won (only cash) and other services on the beach (that we did not use). The good thing that it is a GS25-store (or 7/11 store don't quite remember) so you can buy drinks and small food. Near the beach there is a small   restaurant   but we didn't it looks so nice to eat there. There's also a restroom available and a parking lot. If you want to relax on the beach I would not recommend this beach. You might skip this beach and try to find another one. If you are in this area/Jungmun maybe its more preferable to stay at a resort.For families with kids; I think this beach would suit very well.

many themes in the park such as tulip garden, Canola, rapeseed, cherry blossom, more than 100 years old bonsai, folk village with traditional restaurant 竊fresh grilled mackerel竊, well decorated water pond, peacock and bird park and many more. The folk village still maintain the culture of living that one should not miss. One need half a day in completing visiting the park.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Main target is the teddy bear in Goong drama  but just one section there..a lot of cute, handsome, pretty teddy bears are gathered in this farm..you should spend hours here as the farm is huge! easy to park your car and enjoy your fairytales day there!!

Magnificent view formed by molten lava.View is nice when high tide, crowded during noon, so try to reach there early to avoid crowd.Discount for youth (need to show passport)There is also a pampas grass field, situated at your right side once enter the booth of Jusangjeoli cliff parking lot, can walk in the field if you have no time to visit Saebyeol Oreum

Love this beautiful park in Jeju. For old folks, it provided a relaxing path to walk up to the top of the crater. And once you are on top, you get to see the mountains surrounding Jeju if the sky is clear. Amazing view. There is a minimum entrance fee to this park. There is also small shops near the entrance if you need drinks or snack. Compare to other places in Jeju, this park is less crowded. So if you want to chill and spend a couple of hours outdoor, this is an awesome place to be.

Love the place so much. The market is so big, selling variety of local produce at a very reasonable price. I enjoyed buying banchans, hallabong and fresh octopus as well as fishes. They also have night market selling variety of hot food from 6pm onwards. If you're are driving, getting a parking might be a problem. But you may opt for a multistorey parking space near door 8/5/6 of the market.

Love Hallim Park! My expectation was a quick walk around an outdoor park, but it was so much more! Easily taking an entire day if you want it to, you can meander through under ground lava tubes, fruit orchards, small animal zoos, bonsai tree forests, etc.! Highly recommended.

Lots of people, but it's expected.  Climb was not too bad but my wife did need a rest in the middle.  Provides great view on a clear day.  Take some pics of it when you are far away if you are driving.  There are places on the side of the road where you can park and take a few pictures of the entire thing.
lots of nice trees, bonsais, stones & cave. This Park was made by one man alone

Located next to Manjanggul Cave (a must-visit site), this park is great to let loose your inner child. If you have plenty of time and want to challenge yourself, go in without using the map! Remember to ring the bell when you have navigated through successfully and don't forget to collect all 6 stamps in the maze!

Located in the middle of the Jeju island, it's a very beautiful and well managed National Park. Unfortunately, we were too late for hiking to the Hallasan and back. We decided to hike to the top of a directly opposite and much lower peak. It was easier and we were almost alone on the whole trail as well as at the peak. In the end, we had a nice picknick at the tourist and information center. If you really want to hike to the Hallasan itself, arrive and start as early as possible, be prepared with enough water, some food/snacks and other important hiking utensils.

Located at the eastern end of Jeju Island. It will be about 1hr - 1.5 hrs drive if you stay at the city centre to this stunning place. Advisable to travel early in the morning if you want to avoid the tourists. I drove from Yeha Guesthouse around 7am and arrived in Seongsan Ilchulbong about 8.10am. The area was still empty with only those coming with their cars and still lots of parking lots. However if you arrived around 10am onward, rest assured the parking space will be a challenge. The entrance fee is KW2000 per adult. If you intend to hike until to the top, please wear proper shoes as the stairs can be pretty challenging and steep on the way down. The hike will take about 50 minutes if you walk slow and steady. Can be shorter if you climb faster. During the winter season, you are lucky if you can watch the sunrise. When we were there, it was cloudy and the sun is rising behind the cloud, but still the view up there is beautiful. If you don't want to climb up to the top, you can still enjoy the beautiful scenery around the area. If the time permits, you can also catch the Jeju Woman Diver (Haenyo) in action on your way down from the Seongsan Ilchulbong performing at two timing 1.30pm and 3.00pm respectively. There is a separate trail that leads down to where the action is. I wasn't able to watch it as we are rushing to go to Udo Island.There are Starbucks & Dunkin Donut for you to stop for a cup of coffee while enjoying the views and few shops that sells souvenirs. However the price may be a bit expensive as compared to Dongmun Market.Return visit : A must...for a sunrise views!

Located 25mins from Seogwipo, at the Jungmun area, this is a dramatic stretch of coast with hexagonal rock columns. They result from the rapid cooling and contraction of lava once it has met the water of the sea.There is a viewing platform right behind the Jeju ICC (convention centre), from where to admire the coast and the formations in particular.To access the platform, park the rental car at the designated park (KRW 1000) and buy the access tickets (KRW 2000). The platform is always busy and with all the selfies going on, one struggles to look at the rock formations.
Little fall, a lot of people ......It's not a great place, only a great parking, a queue to buy tickets and so much people that take pictures

Like the name of the place, the first gallery show case a few very old teddy bears (over 100 years old). Some even come with old photo of children holding the same type of teddy bear. Hundreds of teddy bears are dressed up and some with animatronic to depict their human equivalent (eg. Elvis Presley singing in a concert).A great place for teddy bear or toy fans. But beyond the teddy bears, there isn't much to see here. So, it may not be everyone's cup-a-tea.Ample free parking is available infront of the museum.Tips: Visit the Elvis concert hall one floor above the cafe. It can be easily missed.If you know when you're going to visit the museum, purchase ticket online from sites such as Klook.com or Trazy.com to save some $$.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is just beside the Manjang Cave, so I recommended a short 1hr stopover if you are heading to the cave.  Avoid the maze park on rainy days as the ground gets really muddy when it rains.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is in the east of Jeju. We stayed in the West and we took a 30,000won tax to the place. The maze isn't very big but it was quite fun. Ditch the map and have fun getting lost. You see messages and signboards at different places and dead ends. The taxi driver offered to wait for us at the Maze without any cost while waiting as there's hardly any taxi in the area. And he drove us to our next destination (charging by metre). If you are planning to self drive, it is just right next to manjanggul cave. it is worth spending the 45mins to 1 hour in the maze.

Keep in mind, the founder, Paek Uncheol, is quoted   ?Visiting the park is intended to be a journey through the mythology of the island, entering through the ear of Seolmundae*, progressing through the body and exiting at the feet. It represents the journey of life and death.? Taking a journey that ends in death, even if it is a metaphoric (mythical, mystical, mind-boggling) death, may not appeal to everyone, but it could be transformative if you're open to it. Allow for hours of contemplating stones, thousands, tens of thousands, of stones, natural, carved, authentic, replicas - millstones, mortars, volcanic bombs, boundary markers, 2000 ceramic jars, fossilized tree roots - locals thought its creator, who collected these stones for forty years, had gone mad. Three courses to follow, each taking one to two hours. *Seolmundae Halmang, the grandmother of Jeju Island.

Just did the hike on 30 March.Trail: seongpanak up and gwaneumsa down. Goes to summit. (highly recommend to do this trail Cos going up by gweumusa is really steep though the view is nicer for gweumusa) Time taken: 4.5hrs up and 4hrs down (please go early and check the time that you need the reach the shelter and summit by.  Think should be by 1230 reach shelter and by 2 to leave summit) Weather: good.  Cold in the morning but as you hike,  you will perspire and definitely need minimum sweaters. I was only wearing teeshirt and windbreaker. In the end only tee-shirt cos it's getting warmer and you climb and when the sun is out. Need crampons?  Yes!!! It helped alot especially at the icy areas both going up and down. Not too sure where you can buy it but I managed to rent it from my hostel. Though I did see people without it,  and they did just fine.  I was wearing track shoes kind. So crampons helped alot!  How to get there: I went there from Jeju city and took bus 281 from bus terminal to seongpanak bus stop. Coming back from gwaneumsa trail: took bus 475 back to jeju  national university and change bus 360 to Jeju city.  Please check with bus driver or use kakao map/bus to help as Google Map doesn't seem to help much with he routes. Bus 475 have some timings going back. You can always find out from the visitors center at the gweumusa base. It is situated at the left side as you make your way down passing through the car park.  Shelters and food: not sure if I did miss it..  But I didn't see any food vendors, drinks stall as I hiked up and down. So I was really thirsty as the end of the trail. There's a small restaurant and a convenience store at gwaneumsa trail end. So please bring ALOT of water like at least 1.5L. Bring along food to eat up there and also plastic bag to put your trash and there are no rubbish bins around.

Just an ordinary road but countless of tourist buses and vans parked along it. Explore the mystery personally to appreciate the magical side of it. We'd done all tricks - stopped the car engine and let it roll uphill, poured water on road and see the trail running upward, closed our eyes and walked both ways where we found the gravity is totally against us !! Great fun ~!

Just a rock formation that looks more like a bunny than a dragon.  Nothing much.  FOC entry but if you're driving, parking is paid when you exit the carpark.  Payment is to an attendant.  Highly touristy area and can be quite packed when the tour buses arrive.  This attraction is open 24hrs.

Jungmun Daepo is the spot where the iconic columnar joint rock formations can be seen. There?s not much to do here, except take a few pictures from a distance, but it?s worth seeing if you?re in the area anyway. I can?t say much about it because there?s not much to say. except that you should allot about 15 minutes in total (including the time to get in an out).Further down the coast is Jungmun beach. I went here in March, so there wasn?t much to do when it?s 10 degrees Celsius. I imagine on a hot day it would be fun to swim here. The beach is pretty ? sand is slightly coarse but clean and lovely since it?s golden in color. The slope from the parking area/restaurants to the beach is pretty steep. I don?t know if it?s safe for people with mobility issues.One downer: I didn?t like the seafood restaurants playing loud, outdated music when we got there ? I think it would be a pain to eat here if you have to listen to that. Someone has to tell the tourism board about this.Where: Seogwipo west coast
Juju is a volcanic island. From pre-history it's peoples worked the stone. The park concentrates, in a beautiful setting, works from all periods.Free entrance for senior citizens (over 64)

Jeolmul Natural Forest is a must-see in Jeju Island. I really love the lush greenery in the forest park. There are many trails, each with different length and level of difficulty. We only had slightly less than 2 hours in the park. Therefore we only managed to walk the Samwool-gil trail followed by climbing the Oreum Trail (many steps, may get slippery if it rain) and explore the relaxing garden/ pond area. If I come again, I will allocate at least half a day in this beautiful forest. The entrance fee in only KRW1000, and there was a small stall at the entrance whereby you can grab a coffee or buy something to eat. Do not miss it if you are in Jeju Island.

Jeju stone park was rated A by Korea Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in recognition that this park is excellent in term of its specialization in the theme of stone, differentiation from other facilities, and characteristics relating to mythology and the life of the people in the region.Get the map at the entrance and follow guided park course. Don't miss out the Jeju stone museum to know how the formation of Jeju Island. After a short nice walk from the entrance,the museum is just located in the basement of a building opposite the Sky Pond. Follow the map to look for Jeju traditional village with thatched roof houses. Before at the end of course, drop by the unique Gallery in the park which you may find artworks of domestic and foreign artists.It is indeed best travel Korea during Autum because even though it was sunny day, but the breeze was so cooling and the air was very refreshing. It is a museum as well as an ecological park. It is a very remarkable cultural park which sublimating nature in art ,really very fantastic.
Jeju Stone Park is interesting. There are lots of great spots for photos and there are also lots of stone exhibits which infuses some aspects of history, culture and art.

Jeju Stone Park is a vast area with everything stone related.  With Jeju being a volcanic island, the lava stones are everywhere from the Harubang statues to the walls surrounding houses.  The park is divided into three courses which would take about an hour each at a leisurely pace.  The first course has mostly rock statues (including the Harubang statues) that most likely had some religious significance.  The second course shows how the rocks were used for more practical purposes (tombstones, tools, housing, etc) through the different eras of Korean history.  The third course specifically shows the different Jeju style housing made with mostly the volcanic rock walls.  It?s probably not the best place to be in the middle of heat in the summer but when the weather is nice, it?s a fantastic spot to spend a few hours.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).
Jeju Kimnyoung Maze Park - What a bewitching idea, kids as well as families liked about touring here.

Jeju Island is indeed a unique island with so many gorgeous scenery, i had a great time travelling there in Winter, a low season with lesser tourist gives a different experience from visiting it in busy Summer. I have seen pictures about Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff (?ъ＜ⓒ\由) and was amazed by the neat shapes of hexagon stone pillars formed by volcanic lava, i totally recommend tourist to spend time walking around the nicely design olle trail in the beautiful, as well as to visit Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff during your trip in Seogwipo or Chungmun area. you don't have to plan for a long stay, a good two hours should be more than enough, as it was just a viewing spot rather than you can actually walk-in and visit. Don't worry about the transport, bus services are available (in fact it is very convenient to reach most of the travel spot around Jeju island), just drop by Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and walk about 15 minutes to the park entrance, bus drivers in Jeju are very friendly and can basic communication woudn't be a concern. there is a entrance fees of 2000won in the park.there are steps to walk down to have a clearer view, description board with picture will explain how the hexagons shapes are formed, you can take amazing pictures and enjoy the sea view too.speaking of the weather, i have quite an experience, it was sunshine at first while i was taking the bus, and soon it become heavy downpour and even snow flakes begin to attack me during my walking! i think an umbrella or raincoat is necessary for either bright sunshine or unexpected rain. i gotta say, Jeju Island's weather is unpredictable! although this is not a spot to actually feel and touch the pillars, it can be quite boring to certain people who expected more attraction, but seeing the amazing cliff, the neat pillars, it was totally worth it to witness it by your own eyes, even the finest artist surrender to this piece of art, isn't it?

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Jeju is know for horses and mandarins. I'd say, this is a must see for those who visit Jeju for the first time.Tickets can be bought online in Trazy.com. You should receive your e-tickets within 24hrs. Then exchange this at The Ma park's ticket booth. To get there, we took a taxi from Hyeojae Beach (costs KRW9,000). It's a must that you buy ticket in advance due to limited seats. A lot of private tour bus go here. Public transportation is very seldom in this area. If you can arrange a round trip transpo, please do so. As for us, we walked 2 KM to the main road. But again, the 1Hr show is worth seeing. =)

Jeju is famous for hiking and its Olle walking routes, chosen to hike in Hallasan National Park as part of our itinerary. My first hiking experience in oversea and it is an unforgettable experience I ever had. Fantastic !

Jeju is famous and ideal for walking, trekking and experiencing the nature. This Hallasan- the highest mountain in Jeju is a must for those who love nature and trekking. Views from high up are fantastic and the experience is well worth the few hours you spend there, but be warned as there are steep steps and sections and do taking trekking poles if you need them. We took the 'easiest' treks - Erimok up and Yongseil down, which took us a total of 7 hours of slow walk including more than 1.5 hr rest at the kiosk stop where these 2 trails meet.  The kiosks sells cup noodles (hot!) which is the best in cold weather, and it's incredibly cheap.  Do wear in layers as you'd experience vast difference in temp in the sun, shade, windy, higher altitude, etc. If you park at Erimok visitor centre, you need to take a taxi back from the foot of Yongseil (as the distance is some 17 km), but there should always be a couple there. I personally prefer Erimok which offers more shade and less steep sections.

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

Jeju Glass Castle is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall,garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These includes glass art masterpieces by international famous artists from Italy,The Czech Republic,Japan and many more. This theme park suitable for all ages. Very cold due to winter season,do put on more wear as you need to walk round the outdoor.

Jeju Glass Castle houses collection of glass arts. The glass arts are tastefully arranged in different areas of the park, most of them outdoors. The forest trail is the most interesting area. Best to be visited in good weather.

Jeju 4-3 Peace Park educates visitors thoroughly about the Jeju 4-3 Incident which was really almost a genocide when Korean government and US military killed over 30,000 Jeju residents and tortured many more.  With Korea on the brink of dividing into two, Jeju residents wrongly suspected of being Communists ended up being victims.  The government didn't even go public about the incident until the late 1990's and only officially apologized in the 2000's.  The museum describes the build up to the incident and depicts all the horrible details of what the Jeju residents went through.  Having gone through grade school in the 1980's when the incident was not public knowledge, this was a very educational experience for me.

I've visited Seongsan Ilchulbong 11 years ago and this is my 2nd visit. Why? Because this place is so beautiful. The climb is really worth it. I took about 30 minutes to reach the peak. View of the peak and below are lovely. As the path to the peak involve stairs, be careful as it can get pushy (there are just so many tourist there). Entrance fee is 2,000 won per adult. Parking area is large but you will find yourself searching for an empty lot if you come late.

I've never been in a lava tube before, but it was a lot like a cave. The formations inside are pretty interesting and the park does a good job lighting them colorfully. It was a nice walk. However, it is very touristy and if you've been to bigger caves in other parts of the world it's just cool, not extremely impressive.

I've done the hike from the trail head at Seongpanak parking lot to the summit of Halla-san 14 times.  The hike is about 9 KM to the top.  The trail is very rocky and vertical.  There are a few drinking water sources on the way to the summit.  As you get near the top, the trail becomes a series of wooden stairs.  The trail becomes seriously vertical about 7KM from the trail head.  It took me between 2 and 2.5 hours to go up and about the same amount of time to return to my car.

I've climbed Hallasan twice now, once in December and once in early March, and both times I took this route. This route is slightly longer than Gwaneumsa, but it's also a gradual incline with several easy portions. I took this route primarily because there is not a lot of public transportation available to/from the Gwaneumsa trail, plus I'm not sure I can do a steep incline the entire way up to the summit. For Seongpanak, you have about 5 km that are easy, 2.5 km that get harder, and then a pretty brutal last 2 km. Regardless, know that there are other hiking trails around the island and even around the volcano, but only the two mentioned above will lead you all the way up to the summit.Given some of the reviews I saw that are either inaccurate or not very helpful, I hope to compile a quick list to help you decide if this is something you want to do and if so, what you will need:1) It's definitely going to be an all-day kind of thing. You will be tired afterward, so you likely won't want to schedule too many other activities for the evening. Also, it's likely that you will be sore and tired the next day or two. 2) You need to start climbing no later than 8:30 AM. As several people have mentioned, you will not be allowed to access the last chunk of the way if you're not at the second shelter by 12:30 PM (this is winter time, so the schedule varies slightly from season to season... always check the Korean tourism sites).3) Even if it's sunny, there's a chance you might need crampons. In the winter months you will need them for sure, but even last weekend people were sliding down and falling repeatedly without them. I hear that it's even worse on the Gwaneumsa trail since it's a lot more shielded from the sunshine. 4) Bring food and water! The only place you can buy something is at the very beginning of the trail, and even then the options aren't fantastic. A little protein or fruit will go a long way whenever you're starting to feel tired, and it'll help you push through. Please make sure you do not leave any of your trash along the way; there are zero trashcans, so if you carry something particularly messy, you might want to pack a bag for the waste.5) Do not use the toilet in the first shelter! It's the worst smelling bathroom ever, which is rare for Korea since things are usually so clean... I suppose it's the septic system. I suggest using the toilets at the parking lot and at the last shelter (there are two). The first one is seriously a nightmare. 6) It's not an easy hike, but it's doable even for people who don't exercise strenuously. I've seen people carrying babies all the way to the top, and I've seen small children and old people make it, too. Definitely wear the right clothing, though, and especially the right shoes. If you're hiking at a time without snow, you will spend hours circumventing rocks of all sizes and ankle support will be extremely helpful for this. Anyway, thanks for reading, I hope you have a fantastic hike!

Its worth it to climb up there. such a beautiful and breath taking view from the top. its a must visit place if you come to Jeju. entrance fee is just 2000krw per person. we actually drove there from our pension. many parking space. other than climbing the peak, you can also catch a Haenyo Diver Women performance at the bottom of mountain right beside it. its amazing to watch those elderly women  holding their breath for several minutes without any oxygen mask! overall its awesome! for those muslims, there's fast food restaurant Lotteria for you to grab your lunch or dinner since they have shrimp burger available. its located on your left when exit the car park area.
It's very near Hallim Park so check it out if you are also going to Hallim Park. Nice and clean beach, and there's a small island directly opposite it.

It's the first stop in our itinerary & we went to the Ssanyong cave where there are also lava tubes. It's not as big  as Manjang cave & it's better lighted. There's also a folk village in this park, a flower & bonsai garden & lots of lava stones formed into different figures. A bird sanctuary is also here.
It's relatively easy to find this place. We need to pay 2000 won for entrance fee. If you have more time, take another walk to the parking lot, there is also beautiful scenery.

Its really easy to reach this attraction. Parking is free however you are required to pay a minimal fee in order to view this waterfall. Walking on the stairs is easy but if you do wish to get close to the waterfall , a good pair of shoes with good grip is required as you have to walk on the slippery stone/rock. There are some women selling fresh seafood by the waterfall.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.

It's good for what it is.  Some people have been calling this place a glass museum - it's not.  It's a theme park for glass.  I say theme park, but if you're thinking rides then you're wrong.  What they do have is lots of things made out of glass to see.  It's pretty and often colourful.  My female partner enjoyed it more than I did, and there's nothing there that would make me want to go back.  I think children might get a little bored by the place, although girls would probably enjoy it more.  As far as adults are concerned, if you think it sounds like a place you'd enjoy, then you probably would.  But if you think it sounds kinda boring then you wouldn't enjoy it.

Its an interesting rock formation. I think it's not as impressive as the Jusangjeolli Cliffs. It was one of those take a few photos and go type of attraction  to me. There were quite a few people wearing their swim wear and snorkels. We were prepared for that. So, we just went for a glass of iced drink at the caf챕 by the parking lot. Our server was very helpful and fun.

It's an extremely demanding 'hike' for most average people. We read about it but didnt expect it to be that difficult. We went up the Seongpanak trail, starting at 7.30am, did a short detour to see the lake and crater and eventually reaching the summit at around 1pm. We descended the gwaneumsa trail and only managed to reach the base at around 6.30pm. We aren't considered extremely fit and so the climb was considered challenging for us. Our legs hurt for the next few days. The view down was amazing, but the climb was also steeper. Many parts of the trail were rocks so that made it a little difficult to climb as well. There are many cabs waiting at the base of Gwaneumsa trail to take you back to Seongpanak where we parked our car. The cab fare was about 15000won and took about 15 minutes. Overall the hike was fulfilling albeit tiring. But the views were a good return for our efforts!

It's a stone throw away from the Lava Tube. There are a lot of cats lying around the park. The maze is quite easy but to collect all the stamp to accomplish the mission, it takes more time. However, the grass/plant at the maze seem not well taken care as you can see a lot of holes along the plant fences of the maze.
Its a nice beach, a bit small, lots of kids but nice. When we went the waves weren't very large, so didn't bother going in the water. But we walked around and there's a nice park nearby.

it's a museum dedicated to teddy bear. use teddy bear to mimic some of the famous stars, drawings, icons and characters. there is a special Teddy Elvis Presley performance to watch the teddy sings. there is also a gigantic teddy in the park, which is a hotspot for picture taking. overall it's not really impressive as it is just a display for teddy bears.

It's a mixed review.  The ticket price is 10,000KRW per adult and since other natural attractions are around 2,000KRW, this park should be well worth it.  Highs: The caves are really cool as well as the Bansai and Stone Garden. The park is easy to walk and has shops and toilets easily available.  Transportation is also easy as it's just the 702 bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal for 1 hour. Lows: The park is dated, like late 90s with its signage and information cards.  The bird exhibit, stone exhibit and flower garden are average at best.  While the park trail is easy to walk, you do walk through gift shops for the next exhibits (so a bit too tourist-y). Overall, it makes for a decent easy afternoon, especially with kids or elderly.  The park needs some updating to be worth the ticket price, but it is close to the beach (just 5 mins walking).

It's a lot of stairs and little walking to get to the top, but it's worth it with great views and a wonderful sea breeze. On one side you have views of the crater, on the other of Jeju island. There are lots of other tourists (mostly local) going up and down so be prepared for some level of crowds. There was abundant parking when we visited. There are also plenty of food stalls at the bottom along with bathrooms. On the way up, there are lots of benches, rest areas, and viewing platforms. We saw people of all ages - really old to really young doing the climb. If you're in town and you have a couple hours to spare, we'd recommend it!
Its a good family activity, especially for kids. The 4yo in our group enjoyed this maze park alot. Not overly crowded.

It's a bit of a climb to get to the top, which is mostly stairs. Once the stairs start they don't stop until the top. By this I mean there are no real breathers in between the flights of stairs and when you're on a schedule - getting to the top before sunrise, the climb can take a bit out of you. Plan for about 30 minutes or less for the healthy folk and 40 minutes or more for those of us who aren't from the parking lot.Also didn't pay entrance fees as there's no one there at sunrise.
It's a beautiful park to stroll around in the spring time (that's when I visitors Jeju) and given the good weather condition, walking around is just refreshing and calming. A must visit place

It's a beautiful island just 15mins ferry ride away from Jeju Island. Rented cars are not allowed to travel over so we parked our car at the terminal port in Seongsan. Upon arrival at the port in Udo, you will see a few shops just right infront of the port start promoting their offering on bike rentals. Standard rental is 2hrs (KRW 10,000 per pax) for a standard bicycle. So great to tour around and have the best seafood pot ever along the coastal. Peanut ice-cream is a must have, it is so good! We did not manage to visit any of the recommended sightseeing places due to short of time but we had a great time cycling around taking pictures, along with the beautiful weather. Definitely will return again.

Its a beautiful and quiet park to visit. Enjoyed the bonsai area and birds area alot with my 5 year old daughter. There are bonsais as old as 300 yrs old! Signages are clear to indicate the different areas in the park.There is a restaurant within the park itself at the folk village, serves korean food and also small food outlets selling convenient food, ice cream, drinks and beer. There is also a herb cafe in the park, selling herbal teas.A place that is away from crowds to spend an afternoon leisurely with your kids.

It?s an easy drive from Jeju City. There?s a nice park and some restaurants and stores. I was there in February and it was cold, windy, and even snowing, but the beach was still beautiful with the black cliffs and the white sand. I?m sure it?d be perfect in warmer weather!

It worth a look just to see the beautiful coastline of the Island.Most of the rocks come in various heights and sizes shaped like hexagons and if you look at certain angles, they can take on various animals etc.The black lava colour offsets against the outstanding sea and coastline.These cliffs are very similar to the Giants Causeway in Ireland with a pancake rock system but on a much smaller scale.It was crowded the day were there and we assume it is the same most days in the summer months. So a lot of people were snaking along this narrow path around the cliffs and we needed to wait our turn to see over the barriers.There are a few stallholders near the carpark (fee charged) selling fruit, souvenirs and the local home made confectionary similar to nougat.On the way out you can go to a park with some gardens and perhaps a museum type building.The hours vary seasonally however it is the standard KRW 2,000 entry fee for most monuments around the Island.Place it on your ?must see? places to visit here just for the dramatic coastline and on a rough day you may get some blow hole situations with the force of the water.Enjoy your visit!

It will take about 30 to 40 minutes to hike up the mountain which involves lots of stairs. View is superb, especially during sunrise because you will be facing east. There are quite a number of shops and restaurants down there, perfect for breakfast after morning hike. Spacious carparks. p/s: I read somewhere that there will be entrance fees (KRW2000-3000). However when we went there, the ticket booth was closed, perhaps because we went there at dawn.

It wasn't very clear from the guide books. The spot is basically a volcanic rock formation that is concave. I'm not sure that you can actually have a good view of the formation with its lush green centre from any walkable vantage point (like you get from travel books). So on nearing the spot, stop on the highway shoulder to get a distant photograph first.After you arrive, note that the car park is basically one way. Miss a turn and you have to exit the carpark and come back from the entrance. Be prepared to walk / hike as the areas open to public are quite steep. You can get a good open view of the city or the ocean. Refreshing scenery.

It was the easier but longest route to the summit of Mt. Halla. Longest day of my life but it was so worth the aches and pain and sun-burns. Couldn't have done it without the constant encouragement of my partner. Reached the peak before lunch time and saw the beautiful lake and summit. Any later, the haze will start to come in and will ruin your pictures. Bring water and snacks and lunches while hiking. there is only one point where u can get drinking water. Pack light but sensible. Be prepared to spend a whole day for this climb and the next 3 days for aching thighs. So. worth. it. There are stalls selling food, drinks and ice-creams at the park. You can refresh yourself after the climb. Best to rent a car and start early.

It was such a pain to get to but I loved the Stone Park. The main reason was to see the Dol hareubangs - the stone sculptures which represent Jeju. There was information about the mythology surrounding the formation of Jeju which was at times mind-boggling and contradictory. There are different routes around the park and there is an indoor exhibition which features the volcanic rocks and Jeju's origins as a volcanic island. I preferred the outdoor sections where the use of stone in Jeju was highlighted - used in things such as tombs/ shrines, walls, icons of spiritual beliefs etc. The largest sculptures are near the exit and the Dol hareubangs were awesome. They all had slightly different expressions and quirks which was cool. There are plans to expand the museum grounds and I would defo like to go back again in future. It was quite quiet when we were there and we only saw a few people except for a group on a guided tour at the end. Such a shame there are not more visitors but good for those who made the effort. Recommended visit in Jeju!

It was raining when we reached the place. From the parking area, you will see this beautiful crater. As we are slowly walking up the slope, the wind was too strong for us to walk further up.Decided not to go up, but must had to take a few photographs of this beautiful place with the wind, rain and waves.On Normal day, there is also diving show by the famous Sea Women - Haenyeo. Mostly are 50 and above who dive for a living.Try to plan the visit during normal weather.

It was pretty crowded when we got there at about 3pm on a weekday. From the parking area, It was a short walk down some stairs to the observation decks where you get good views of the unique (column) rock formations by the coast.However, we had difficulties getting photos of us with the rock formation because there were just too many people on the observation decks. As we exited the observation deck area, we saw a guy selling postcards of the photos he himself took of various scenic Jeju attractions and we bought some to support him.I am not sure what else there is to explore in that area because we were hurried off to the next destination on our guided tour.If you are into Geography, love cliffs by the sea and rock formations, I highly recommend this place! I loved it!
It was an okay park, easy and nice to walk around, the best part was the caves. Love exploring the caves!However, food choices are limited should one be hungry.

It was along the way to Manjanggul Cave. As we had missed the bus 990 which could take us to the Cave, we had to walk the 2.5km way. About 1.4km's walk, we came to the Gimnyeong Maze Park. It was a fun place even for adults. We did not follow the map so that it would be exciting. Indeed it was, and the more lost we were, the more exciting it got.

It was a very hot day yesterday, July 31st 2018, and I got sunburn the day before so in 33 degree heat and me didn't match. I didn't go up to the top but I did go up to the first viewing platform, which i think most people would be able to manage slowly, not matter your age. It is well paved, and the views are incredible. It was a very windy day too, so there was no show by the women divers, Haenyo, but you could see where they went out and to be honest the roughness of the seas showed how tough the women must have always been. There are a few shops near the bottom and one part way up, so you can purchase drinks and trinkets if you wish. There is a Starbucks and a Dunkin' Donuts and i think a McDonald's near the car park, as well as multiple Korean restaurants. Well worth a visit, even if you can't ascend to the peak.

It was a short drive from Seogwipo where I stayed with my son In late Dec. The trip was highly recommended by the Shilla hotel staff and I could understand why after having spent an hour on its rugged coastline. Awesome selfie spots at every turn! Another highlight was the women divers selling their harvest (sea cucumbers) on the coastline. It was a stimulating walk, with crystal clear waters lapping at our feet. We went when the tide was receding as advised by the hotel staff. So do check before venturing down. 2nd tip: go well bundled up as it can get very cold in winter. As a reward, we headed to the Hiddink cafe at the end of the trail (next to car park) for a hot cuppa. It felt like we had stepped into a Dutch village, replete with tulips and clogs. As you can probably guess, Korea is still besotted with the Dutch football coach.

It was a rainy day when we went to this beach after visiting the Hallim park, end of october. It was however a very nice experience, the sand is white and contrast nicely with the black rocks that you can see at low tide. The view on the island makes the picture even nicer.

It was a nice walk around Hallim Park especially if you like Bonsai trees, folk Village and more...We had a great walk aroundthe area and the weather was so freshly cold?. Went to the caves was also interesting. Beautiful garden. A place to come back. I like to put more pictures but I could only put 10 of them.

It was a lovely trip in Hallim Park, it has many beautiful views to take photos of.It?s so big we spent 4 hours to finish it, and after that we went to Hyeopjae beach which is 5 minutes away from there. However, I was disappointed because of there was one restaurant and it only serves Korean food.

It was a foggy day but we managed to drive to the Hallasan National Park. Once we arrived, the weather was clear and with a little sunshine. Perfect to walk the Eoseungsaengak Trail. They said it will take about one hour but that is really with no stops. We took 1.5hours. There are a lot of wooden steps up the trail and some turns. We saw mainly trees and bushes. Generally it was manageable. Do wear good walking shoes. When up the top, the weather was foggy and we could not see the surrounds which was a pity. Nonetheless, we enjoyed the clear fresh air and the workout. This trail is the shortest and the best for travelers who have no time or not as fit and mobile.

It takes 10 min tops to actually enjoy the rock.  Its unique and pretty but that's all folks!  You have to pay for parking (500 won every 30 min) and believe me, it doesn't even take that long to see all there is to see.  We had extra time before rental car needed to be returned so we stopped.  But I wouldn't have otherwise gone out of my way to see this rock formation.
It may seem to be an ordinary natural tropical theme park. However, it may be seen by some of the visitors who came from different country than mine.
It is very nearby the airport, you can stop by once you have your rental car picked up. We did a quick stop for some photos only, we did paid for the parking. There is not much to see.

It is surely a must-go attraction in Jeju. With only KWN2000 (adults) to this nice park, it is reallt worth it. Too many steps in descending and ascending way, not a wheelchair or elderly friendly place
It is really amazing to see these formations.  Small fee to park and see the formations, but still super cheap, and well worth it.m you can see it all in a half hour.

It is quite expensive with 12.000 won per adult, but you could easily spent 2-3 hours and it is nicely set up. Of course the glass castle has a lot of romantic photo ops for newlyweds. But also their little hiking trail is nicely decorated and I loved all the wind chimes. You could do glass blowing or get your picture in glass. They have snacks and a coffee. Overall a nice little theme park.
It is interesting and impressive area. If you live in west Seogwipo,it is intersting to do Olle trail cross this park, after Jungmun sandy beach.
It is easily to reach from the downtown area.  Next to the Seobok Park, at the coastal rim.  You may enjoy a nice view on the coast-front.  Good for the family for fun.

It is definitely a park full of stones, but it is actually quite interesting.  There is also a museum in the park which is worth checking out.  It shows some of the history of the island and the different types of volcanic rocks that can be found on the island. If you aren't interested in parks or rocks this probably isn't a place you would enjoy, but my husband and I really enjoyed it.  Naturally shaped rock sculptures, carved rock sculptures, stacked rock sculptures, etc.

It is a museum as well as an ecological park related to stone culture in the lives of Jeju people.  It is huge and you are required to walk a lot.  It is about 40-45 minutes drive either from Jeju Airport or Seogwipo area.  You need 1-2 hours to go around the complex and the museum.  Opening hours: 0900-1800 hrs.  Closed on first Monday of the month unless it is a holiday.  Entry fee: KRW 5,000.  It should be a MUST in your itinerary of Jeju Island.
it is a long walk up to the top of this peak, but the views are remarkable.  Bring water and be prepared to make the long climb.  Parking is difficult so go early or take a tour bus.

It is a dood place to walk, think, and stare.....  Many people  come with families & friends Children have a lot of pace to play. One can  have a lunch  at the restaurant. It is a  great beautiful park   within Jeju Si.

Is  a must visit to this market. Parking spot is very hidden. Lots of street food, souvenirs, tangerines, chocolate, fresh fish availables. Jungang Underground Shopping Center and Chilsungro Shopping Town is also next to this market. (near to entrance 4)Lots of people buying chocolates from the stall located at the intersection between entrance 3 and entrance 7. (probably the biggest stall and cheapest?)

Interesting waterfalls with a park. Lighted up at night. We came by at 8pm.  The clear and deep water of Cheonjiyeon Falls is designated as Natural Monument No. 27 and is renowned as a habitat for Mutae eels. Take a walk around the beautiful park. You can also take photos with the props such as 'Summer', hearts etc.

interesting shapes of rocks and lovely blue water.not too difficult, short walk along the trail. there are 2 different trails starting from different car park. both trails are not connected at the moment due to safety issue so make sure you visit the right one.by the look of it no.2 may not available or can be very wet @ low tide.i like the both but personally like no.1 trail little more.

Interesting if short visit. Not too well signposted, but once found, plenty of parking and a short climb downn to the beach. Depending on the season entry if 2,000 Won or free. Demonstrates well the islands volcanic cliffs.

Interesting experience  as we we pull to neutral gear, release the accerator, the car just go forward, upwards. The mysterious road is short, we made a few rounds. There is a car park where you turn in to go a few rounds if you wanted to. We tried the  same stretch to road after the end point. The car just go backward on the upward facing slope.

Initially, we were only planning on staying here for a few minutes to take some pictures because the reviews were so mediocre. We rented a car and drove to the entrance our GPS took us to (FYI if you rent a car and don't read Korean, make sure you get a GPS with it, Google maps/Apple maps/etc doesn't work in Korea, only Naver). I think it was some kind kind of back entrance, off the road, because no buses or anything were parked there. There wasn't even really a parking lot. When we walked through the village, to the other side, we saw the big parking lot and all the cheesy buildings and shops and stuff. But from the back side, it was just lots of nice little houses (some I think still had people living there) and pretty, walled-off yards. We were there in the morning and the are we were in had almost no one around, except for a few Chinese ladies who had decided to leave their tour and were having fun (we saw them rejoin with their tour later, so I didn't pull that out of thin air, lol). The main front entrance area is way more touristy and that's probably all people getting off the bus see, hence the bad reviews. If you keep walking through the whole town and take your time (if you can), it's actually pretty and peaceful. I think we spent a couple hours here.

Initially we had wanted to walk here from Seogwipo but gave up and took a taxi up the hill, the road was quite crowded with taxis and the car park filled with tour buses and cars. It is a very touristy place, there is ample reason. This is the place where Jewel of the Palace (Daejanggeum 鸚㏝룝) was filmed - one of the first Korean dramas popular all over asia. There is a cut-out of Janggeum where you can put your face and take a photo.More importantly, the scenery is lovely and dramatic. The rock column rises out of the beautiful blue sea. We left the path and tourists behind and walked around the rocks to the edge. We even came to a point where we could see Saeyeongyo Bridge in Seogwipo. We came across a blue rock thrush and a nice little coffee house before grabbing a cab on the main road. There is a bus running but we did not want to wait for it... it is about 6-8 min drive to seogwipo town

In order to reach this beautiful waterfall one has to endure walking for few minutes. We went there on April, it was the start of the spring season, yet it was windy so it was cold. For me the fall is just average, may be because I have seen more beautiful falls from the other countries. However, this is worth the walk and time. We manage to have beautiful photos near the falls and in the park.

In my journey, I went to the Hallasan National Park at Jeju. Here is a good place to walk with family, since here has a wide stretch of land at the foot of hill, you can just walk around the hill. Children can play in a nature place with good air. All the building and transport are so far away, you must feel relax and do not want to leave.If you are younger and want to see more view, I really suggest that you must walk to the peak by stairs, but you must have enough energy, because it is really tired. Take water and some food are necessary. After that, you can see a good view at the peak, just like stand on the cloud.Finally, I suggest that you will climb at evening because of the sunset is very beautiful. Also the weather is better to climb the hill.
In a few words, it is worthwhile visiting. You probably need 2-3 hours to get around the park. Check the weather before going, if its raining, simply don't go. You will be soaking in water.

I'm told that Jeju Island is called   The Hawaii of Asia  . As a Hawaii resident, I'd have to say that Jeju is very similar to Hawaii, and never more so than in Hallim Tropical Park. I felt very much like Hawaii, with lots of lush vegetation, birds, animals and humid weather! If you enjoy nature and the outdoors, you'll enjoy this park!

I'm sure this is a beautiful place when the flowers are in bloom but there weren't many when we went in late July.  There were still some hydrangeas and a few other flowers around but I think they could plant more varieties so that the park is pretty in different seasons.  The worst part though was the signage and map.  We got lost 3-4 times in one hour!  The map is mostly pictures without words in any language and it's hard to tell where you are.  The only way we figured it out was that there are a couple of   you are here   signs (in Korean).  They've put up some   This way please   signs but then there will be a fork in the road and there's not another   this way   sign.

Ilchulbong is a huge rock/volcano/crater on the North East of Jeju Island. At first it seems a little daunting when you pull into the carpark as it looks really huge and steep. Yes, there are a lot of steps, but there are plenty of places to pause or sit for a rest and once you get to the top there's a great sitting/viewing platform. The views are really spectacular in all directions and you can see all over the mountain. It's really worth a visit if ou are going to Jeju.

Iho Taewoo Beach 댄명고대? is the closest beach to Jeju-si (city) and is closed to airport too, one can look down from the plane of the two very special red and white horse-shaped lighthouses when it almost reach Jeju Airport. Beach are sandy white and swallow water that are safe to swim. It is open for public and no admission charges except if is Jeju Iho Taewoo Festival.Visitors are welcomed to camp at the camping site. Facilities like charging room and shower room with locker are available too, is chargeable.There is two entrance to Iho Taewoo Beach, one is closer to the sandy beach and camping site located in the pine forest but less parking space. The other one is close to the horse-shaped lighthouses with huge free parking space and food trucks selling food and beverage. Here you can cycling and photographing. The two white and red horse-shaped lighthouse is famous for sunset photographing, it is best to be there around 5-6pm for the best sunset moment. Iho Taewoo Festival is around Jul-Aug every year. Local and tourist will be coming to witness the happening festival and event like boat ricing, fishing competition and many more fun activities. It will be a long day event.If you are driving, key in 728-3393.If you are taking public transport, take green bus 7,17 or 60 or blue bus 36

If you've never seen hexagon rocks [I don't know what they're called], this is a pretty neat place to visit.  There are stairs and viewing platforms with smaller platforms you can stand on to get a better photo.  There's also a big park at the top where you can see the rocks from different angles and just enjoy the park.

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the   foreigner price   rule is definitely in effect at this market.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

If you're a fan of teddy bears, then you should visit this place. You can probably complete this in 1 - 2 hours time. There's a outdoor park with more pictures to capture. Didn't really change much as compared to the first visit few years ago.. You have to pay an admission fee to enter, which i can't really remember but it's not expensive.
If you want to see something colorful glass art work, you don't want to miss this spot. There are many nice glass art sculpture all around the park. Good chance to take a memorable picture in there.

If you want to see some nature trails but can?t do long distances over natural rocky ground, then this will suit. The train ride to each destination makes it easy to travel. The walks are well groomed. Plentiful toilets. There are some theme park like features, such as boats & a pirate ship, to keep the young ones entertained along the way (at extra cost for some).

If you really have a short time available at Jeju and that you want to have a glimpse of everything, Hallim Park may be your solution.  In there comprises of a tiny folk village, two lava tubes of smaller scale, water park, beautiful gardens for you to enjoy for a few hours.  One couldn't admire the courage of Mr Song who spent 40 years of his life developing Hallim Park from NOTHING.  He literally sweated & toiled through the barren rock into something magical that's been visited by dignitaries around the world.  For someone like myself who came from New Zealand, natural green is something that I have taken for granted but one would have to give Mr Sung encore for the grand vision that he did, to build a tourist attraction for Jeju when tourism wasn't a happening thing just yet.  Just like from the movie, Field of Dreams, if you build it, people will most definitely come!
If you only have one day in Jeju, come to Hallim Park because they have everything in one place! Caves, butterfly garden, flower garden, birds area, mimic folk village and so on.

If you one got time for 1 of the 3 waterfall in Seogwipo, you should choose this waterfall. View is spectacular, need to walk down the stairs to view the waterfall. and some actually walk very close to the waterfall by walk on the big rocks to get some nice photo. Plenty of parking space available, youth below 25 years get some discount for the entrance ticket (do bring along your passport). suggest to spend 1 hour there.

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.

If you like small tasteless theme parks you will love this: mirror mazes, glass lilies in ponds, large mosaic teddy bear and a chance to make your own stuff too. The 9,000 won entry fee includes the fee to make something - and that price is VERY expensive for Jeju. It is also mostly outside so do not bother in bad weather. In fact, I would not bother at all.

If you like cats then this place is for you. There are about 20 cats roaming around the property. I am not a cat person at all but the cats did not bother me. They are friendly and stay out of the way of people. The maze was fun and somewhat challenging. I liked that they added a stamp feature (you had to find stamps on your journey) so it wasn't all about getting out. They are pretty chill here, so you could do the maze 1 million times if you wanted. If the parking lot is overflowing then I would recommend that you not go. The property isn't big enough for that many people. The positive is that there is a cave down the street you can visit as well. We didn't get to visit the cave because it was a public holiday. I would recommend that you go here, especially if you have kids. The value is not that high but most things on Jeju cost money. It is not a rip off.

If you like bears, it would be fun because there are many types of bears and collections of bears from around the world and there is a outdoor park where you can take picture with human size fake bears. But it was not as big as expected and it can be finished within 2 hours.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

If you go to Jeju Island, this is a good place to go. There is a Kitty Cafe inside, it is the same as those in Seoul. Apart from the Cafe, there is also an souvenir shop, you can buy those limited edition products there. If you drive there, you may need to wait for the parking space during peak hours.

If you go in the summer, be sure to take some water with you.  It's a 10-15 minute walk to  the falls and there's not much shade on the return route or actually at the falls.  Everyone tries to get as close as they can, which is fine, but there are several places to take beautiful pictures up on the platform/courtyard in front of the falls.  There are also two smaller falls that you don't see much unless you cross the bridge about halfway between the falls and the parking lot.

If you garden or enjoy botanics this is a fabulous place. I just visited during Tulip season and the entrance was an alleyway of color. I imagine late in May and June when more plants are blooming Hallim is an even more stunning place. It contains a huge variety of plants, wishing I could grow some of these specimens in Colorado. They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested. The grounds include a couple of lava tunnels, which don't have a lot of spectacular cave features, but I still found them worth the walk through. They also have an amazing bonsai garden and a lovely water garden.I spent almost 2 hours exploring the flora on well marked walkways and paths in this lovely park.BTW, Hallim deserves an entrance fee for all the upkeep needed, not sure why they charge 2 dollars at a number of sea cliffs etc., that should be open to the public...

If you are travelling with small kids, i suggest to drive a car into the island. (They allow car to enter the island if having kids below 6 years old), really regret that we park our car at the multi storey parking, with all the high hope to rent a electric scooter (the one with 3 wheels)The electric scooter is strictly for 2 person only (they dont allow 2 adult + 1 baby too)Only those with Class A international license allow to rent the electric scooter (i am a Class B international license holder (allowed to drive car only)If you plan to travel the island by bus, it will waste lots of time on queueing and waiting for the bus. The bus driver will not explain any tourist spot in english, so you will have a hard time to decide which is the good spot to get down from the bus.Overall the island has nothing special with we are not allow to ride the electric scooter and generally the island is too crowded with tourist.

If you are into local stuff, you need to visit this market. We rented a car and it is equipped with gps, hence we drove around. There is a parking space  Earby,  just watch out for P sign. The market has plenty of fresh, live abalone freshly dugged korean ginseng, banchan, salted fish, seafood, home ware, snacks, and little eateries. It is very clean and also if you are looking at those orange chocolates or even souvenirs they have it here aa well. We manage to buy some yummy vegetable chips which cost 10000krw per pack with vegetables that you like such as chillies, apples, seaweed, and etc. Spent 1 1/2 hours here before heading back to the airport.

If you are interested in the history and culture of Jeju island, and of Korea, then I would recommend spending an hour or two at this park. If you aren't, or are expecting something more exciting, skip it. For me, who lives in Korea and is already familiar with much of Korean history, I wish I had gone elsewhere. True to previous reviews, it was beautiful, but so is most of Jeju, and there are many other places more beautiful than the park itself. Overall: if you don't care about the history behind the park, it's 2 hours of looking at rocks.

If you are in the Seogwipo-city area and only a short time in Je-Ju this is a great find. A traditional house, a story of a great S. Korean artist, a nicely designed park and a street of small arty shops.
