First of all, this place is huge.Formed through volcanic activity which resulted in 46 'small volcanoes' in the park itself. From what i saw, they ain't 'small'!There are a few entrances and trails. I took the Eulrimok Trail. It was pretty easy as compared to other mountains i hiked. First third, about 2.4km is quite difficult. Lots of stones and steps. Then it gradually became easier. The view is definitely awesome the moment you clear the forest area.There is a reststop at about 5km. Be sure to bring your own food. There is no cafe or shop there. The locals actually even cooked their own ramyeon by bringing them and hot water too. Some used the army-styled ration. There are no trash cans. You have to bring your trash back.You can take a public bus to this trail (gotta walk in opposite the bus stop. A good almoat 2km gentle upslope).Only bus 240 brings hikers here. You might want to check.Reminder, it is super cold in winter.

Figured I?d give it a walk through after getting sun burn the day before. Not crowded on a Sunday. Free parking. 10,000w entrance fee. The museum was a little hot and stuffy. The depictions of historical moments using bears was humorous at times. Most labels were in Korean with some English. Might be fun for small kids. The garden out back was nice extra touch to allow kids to run around and see more bears.

fascinating  view from bottom until top. but we went on saturday, pack with local hikers. the path is quite easy. about 18km back and forth using seongpanak trail. on the way back we tag along with the person incharge/worker of mt. hallasan, and being offered to use the little train to the way down. best of all, there is no entrence fee charge to hike the  national park.

Fall season would be dull here. We made a stop on the way to lunch. A few exhibition halls to cater for vegetation from different temperate and climate.? Otherwise, nothing spectacular in this huge park. The train ride requires a special ticket.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Everything about our favourite bear and its history. The museum has 3 floors, where you can see many different displays of teddy bears and animatronics, in a different setting. One floor is for displaying teddies from different times, another one shows teddy related artworks and finally there's a floor where you find a souvenir shop and some cafes. In the outside park you can view Jungmun sea while seeing human-sized teddy sculptures. The whole surrounding area is beautiful. Ideal for friends, couples and families as well!
Every one enjoy in eco land, a place can be visit if u like nature,can be reach by public transport, must pay entrance fee ,big park with train

Even with the crowd, it's still worth it. We took Seongpanak trail to hike up to the top in mid March and still needed snow sparks. Make sure start your hike by 9am and bring food/snack to survive for 8 hours or more. The trail is mix of rocks and boardwalks with little soft surface to walk on, so be mindful with choice of your shoes or socks.

Even though my family and I stayed in Breeze Bay Hotel which is within 3 minutes? drive to the Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak) car park, we couldn?t wake up so early to hike up to the summit to catch the sunrise. Eventually, we were at the base of the Seongsan Ilchulbong at 10am, together with hordes of tourists and locals?nd the sunny weather.Getting there and fees: GPS coordinate/code for this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument site/attraction located in the east Jeju is 7830959. As the parking lots are limited, I suggest you drive (arrive) there early (before 9am). Parking is free.  The entrance fees are 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.The attraction: A non-stop no-rest ascent for a fit person takes about 30 minutes, but with my young children and with stairs-climbing not part of our daily routine, we took about 1 hour to make complete the 182 metres climb to the summit. There are several pointers that you may want to take note:(1)
address: If you can, go on a weekday. We were there on a Wednesday mid-morning and already it was quite crowded, so I cannot imagine what the weekend would bring(2)
입력주소: Wear a pair of good-sole and comfortable walking shoes and bring enough water to hydrate yourself (you could still buy water at only one place during the ascent)(3)
X: On a sunny day, you could bring an umbrella or wear sunglasses or a cap and preferably put on sunscreen lotion(4)
Y: Take note that the ascending trail or route is different from the descending trail or route, so do take lots of photos and selfies along the way. (5)
CLSS: Hike at your comfortable pace (although I understand that may not be possible when the tour guide requires you to be back at the bus within a certain timing) and do rest at the benches and the viewpoints or points of interest (e.g. huge rocks) whenever you are out of breath (give you an excuse to take photos and selfies)(6)
PNU: There is no need to bring a jacket or sweater unless the weather becomes chilly or windy or cold (e.g. winter) or you are hiking in the wee hours of the morning to catch the sunrise. In fact, it was scorching hot when we reached the crater summit at around 11am(7)
주소구분: When you reach the summit, remember to pose with the signage says ‘Top of Seongsan Ilchulbong 180m’We started the climb after the 4 bronze round inscriptions (one of them is ‘New 7 Wonders of Nature’) on the uneven rocky or bumpy uphill sloped path. After a certain distance, this sloped ascending path became one that comprises of proper (stairway) steps. Look for the signage “Ascending Trail” and continue your ascent. Somehow the last stretch is a steep climb on continuous stairway steps and with so many people behind you, you simply cannot stop to rest. But once you reach the top, before you have time to catch your breath, your breath will be immediately taken away by the breath-taking panoramic views! You could see the flora-covered 600-meters diameter crater with 99 jagged rocky spires that resemble a crown, in addition to the Seongsan town (village), Seongsanpo-hang harbour, Cheju Haehyop (Cheju Strait), Mount Hallasan and others. It amazed me when I considered the almost symmetrical tuff cone crater was created by the explosion of an underwater volcano thousands of years ago. Due to the barriers, all visitors cannot walk into the tuff cone crater.Of course, the descent was relatively easier along wider wooden stairways with railings. When near the bottom, there are two directions to take. Going to the left, you could ride a Jeju pony (Jorangmal), which we didn’t go. Going to the right (signage “Women Diver Performance”), you would come to a black basalt rock cliff and also to a place to see the famous female divers (Haenyeo). To the right too, you would come to a lookout point for Udo Island (South Korea’s second largest island)Comparing with the only other tuff cone crater that I have climbed ? Diamond Head in Honolulu ? I find the Seongsan Ilchulbong more challenging to climb but it offers more breath-taking scenery.  So don’t miss Seongsan Ilchulbong on your Jeju itinerary! Start the ascent early to avoid the crowd.
표준구주소: If you can, go on a weekday. We were there on a Wednesday mid-morning and already it was quite crowded, so I cannot imagine what the weekend would bring(2)

review: Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.

Eorimok trail ends at Witse Oreum, at about 1700m up Hallasan. From carpark to the hut and back, including half an hour for noodles at the top is close to 4.5 hours. This includes photo times. Like everything on Jeju, this is a tourist walk, for pretty much anyone who can put one foot in front of the other up a very well marked or board-walked track. That notwithstanding, the walk is pleasant and the area itself is nice. In early Feb you will still likely have snow (we had snow from carpark to hut) and will require some small walking crampons to ensure grip. These are 5000W from the small shop at the carpark, beside the toilets and are pretty good actually. If you have some full mountaineering fangs it would almost be worth taking them for a laugh. We were the only westerners on the trail from perhaps 3-400 people and it would have only added to everyone's curiosity. Taxi from Jeju city will set you back about 20 000W and you can easily get a cab from the carpark taxi stand for your return trip. Hallasan is definitely the best, and some would say only real, attraction on Jeju and if you have half a day, then this is the track for you.

Before you visit this attraction, be sure to be appropriately dressed and have the essential gear.  Hiking boots are highly recommended as the ground is uneven and mostly rock.  Sun hat and shades will also be very useful when nearing the peak as the area there is more barren without much trees.  Trekking pole will also be useful for those with knee problems.You will have to start your day early as they will disallow entry to the final stretch (at the 2nd rest point).  There are 2 rest points, both with toilets.  The 2nd rest point (higher up) sells drinks and instant bowl noodles.  Rubbish will have to be brought down and thrown when you leave the park.  I climbed in early June and there were many many many bugs and wasps at the last leg and the peak.  For those climbing during spring, please prepare some bug balm.  These are the tips;1) Start early, reach the 2nd rest stop before 12pm.  2) Have the proper gear3) If possible, have your noodles etc after you finish the peak (if you're descending via the same trail), that way, you won't have to carry your trash up the peak4) If you're driving, reach there early (before 730).  Carpark fills up pretty quick5) A mineral spring can be found along the way for cool refreshing water!

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

As mentioned this place does not get a lot of attention. Today while we were there, were surprised to see a lot of local Korean tourists. From Seogwipo bus terminal (the one near Jeju World Cup Stadium) take bus 702. There is announcement in English. Alight at Sanbangsan. This place is truly nature at it's mightiest, the wind/sea carved walls/cliffs are very different from the rest of Jeju's natural beauty. Entrance fee is 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for child. Take time to enjoy the wind, sunshine and views as you strolled. Along the way, there are old ladies selling fresh seafood and soju. There is a mini theme park next to one of the entrances. There is Viking, trampoline.. A number of stalls selling bbq squids/seafood, mandarin juice, chocolates and mini cakes. Good for the kids to take a few rides. All in all, a good half day spent in nature.

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

As its name, here is an idea to visit for Teddy Bear lovers and who interested in. Many zone that's quite interesting such as the first Winnie the Pooh, world's all time classic paintings x Teddy Bear, characters bear like Michael Jackson or Audrey Hepburn from Breakfast at Tiffany, and Steve Jobs. Entrance fees isn't cheap but still OK. For the exhibition of Bear dolls is good but for the shop, just soso nothing attractive.Parking available. Good for friends and family.

As I didn't have access to a car and was traveling alone whilst in Jeju I caught the city bus to the national park. This was pretty simple and the bus from the main bus terminal leaves every hour between 9 and 4 (during summer) the journey coat 3100 won. The bus stops at the end of 2 trails to the west of the mountain. (Eorimok Trail, Yeongsil Trail) . Both trails meet in the same place on the mountain and both give a varied, pretty and pleasant  walk up Mt Hallasan . There are toilets and facilities at each of the trail tickets offices which are well maintained. The paths are a mix of steps and decking to help mark the trail clearly. You get great views of the different Oreum's (small volcanoes) these trails do not lead to the summit like the longer trails that start on the east. Ensure you have snacks and plenty of water

As I can clearly assure that you wont be regret if you visit this place. This is my second visit to Seongsan Ilchulbong. We went there to catch a majestic sunset.  We reached the parking area around 5 o'clock in the morning then we straight away climbed to the highest peak. For us, it took roughly 30-40 minutes to reached the top of the observatory area. It is indeed quite challenging but its worth it. Just bare in mind to wear the most comfortable shoes and jacket, plus dont forget to bring a mineral water.

As for the places we visited, we loved the Manjanggul Cave, Sunrise peak and the foot bath class at the Herbal park. The maze and folk village were ok. I probably would prefer to exchange one of those two for more time at the Woljeong beach.

As coaching parking and no admission fee needed.You could plan to visit within 30 minutes.  Don't try the seafood stall down there as not worth to do so.  Indeed, there is not much to see except popular place for group tourists guide.

Arriving parking lot around 4ish in the morning. It's dark but u can see other people going to same direction, just follow them. I guess we took around half an hour or less to reach the top. I didn't stop for a while because i'm so afraid I will miss the sunrise. Turns out some people arrived the top earlier than us! That day was a bit cloudy but still we can see the beautiful sunrise. It's really amazing experience! Besides I am quite impressive with their trail, well furnish with stones and woods. Quite interesting when u look down to the town, must go for Jeju trip.

Arrived in the morning parked easily, cost for parking at the entrance was 1800 WON and picked up a map.  Make sure you wear good shoes -- preferably with good ankle support and walking sticks.  The path is well layer out but does take some effort.  We did not get all the way to the top as it was closed due to a slide but it's nice walk.  Suggest an early start and bring water too.

Another UNESCO World Heritage. It have a nice view from the top but you need to climb up the stairs. Perhaps is a good exercise.  :)  You may bring along the bottled water as it takes around 30 mins to the top. There have restaurants, coffee shops, food stalls, souvenir stalls at the bottom and free car park as well.

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

An outdoor gallery of stone sculptures. You can find a lot of Jeju stone icon, as they call it   Grandpa Stone  .  The park is very large,  and not many visitors.  An interesting place worth visiting .

An hour is okay, but if you have the time it might be better to make this 1,5 hour. We combined this with waiting for the Mongolian horse show, which you should not miss and close to this location. You \can also enjoy the beautifull Jeju-beach on the other side of the road.This park is very well maintained. Enjoy the beautifull Bonsai trees, the waterfalls, the flowers, the cave and the statues. The cave was the least exciting to us, but the bonsai trees from over 150 years old were most impressive.

An exhibit which tells you about the life of the women divers of Jeju.  Explains to you their gear, their daily life, their history and their future as a dying trade.  Small compound without any eatery or canteen.  Parking is free.  However, food (mainly seafood) can be found at a nearby wet market to the east of the exhibition.  Driving takes only about 5 mins.
An decent park to spend 2-3hrs.Nothing great just decent.Lots of tourist thought, so don't expect a peaceful walk unless you go at odd hours.The park close at 6pm.

Among all the interesting place in Jeju island, i personally love Udo the most. The sky really blue, sea really blue, sand really white, stone really unique, food taste nice...you have it all. I rent a car for the trip in Jeju, therefore i bring the car to Udo by ferry. There were three of us in the car, i feel it worth the ferry ticket. As in Udo, most of the   mini car   or special bike we saw are mostly two person, so unless you rent two, you cant fit in 3 persons. So if you are driving, you have more than 2, bring your car with you. Parking is very easy to find. But please go to the port earlier as buying ticket and finding entrance to board the ferry can be very confusing..so you will need more time.

Although we visited this park after the flower blossom but the park was still beautiful with many tree. I really like the tunnel, it was amazing when the sunshine went through the leave and we could see the sunshine clearly.

Although we know how the illusion works, it is still crazy to watch how the bottles or cars go up hill instead of going back. You don't need much time over there though. One mysterious road (according to our touri map there are two) is located right next to the Jeju Lovepark which is interesting and funny. You can go there for 9000 Won, spend about an hour watching love sculptures. :-)

Although there is not a lot to do here, it is a short walk from the parking to see this absolutely beautiful view!  If you take a few minutes to watch the water swirling around the cliffs it will mesmerize you, so pretty!

Although it takes about an hour by bus from Seogwipo hiking up this volcanic peak was one of the highlights of our trip to Jeju.  The hike only takes about an hour round trip, if you go at 1pm or 3 pm they have a women diver's show.  Cost about 2,000 won each and there's many food vendors at the entrance of the park.

Along with Go Carts and a hot air balloon ride, the Maze Park has enough to keep everyone busy and happy! The Maze is fun to watch people navigate from the hot air balloon. A great view of World Cup Stadium too!! This was a fun day!

Allow for at least 2.5 to 3 hours to walk around. There are a number if different areas, my favourite being the bonsai trees. The park is very well kept and very tranquil. There are a couple of places that sell snacks and one restaurant on site.

After the Jeju Love Land, w/c is a X rated (for adults) theme park. Funny, unique, it's a theme park that you will never find in any other country... This is a must visit, if u wanna hve a fun, funny Xperience!Glass castle are full of creative art works made of Glass.. Good for picture taking... Colorful, artistic, imaginative pieces of art. You'll also find here the Glass Shoes of Cinderella & their carousel.

After seeing Jeongbang waterfall, this Cheonjiyeon waterfall seemed average.  Admission was the same in both waterfalls, 2,000won for adults, and 1,000won for teenagers (up to 24). To see this waterfall, you had to go thru the park, which had other monuments, trees, and flowers to admire...worth checking even in winter.

After reading the reviews i was a bit reluctant about visiting the park but i am glad i did. I only wish i had more time to see everything, like all the small trails leading to the folk villages at the far back. This is not just for people who are history buffs, this park can be enjoyed by anyone who appreciates nature and quiet, peaceful walks. It is a windy area so be prepared if visiting in cool seasons. For only ~$5 this is a nice park to spend a few hours if you want to slow it down and be in nature.

After paying for the tickets (2000 won per adult and 1000 won per child/youth), we walked about 5-10min to the waterfall. It was a therapeutic walk through the park to reach the waterfall. Recommend to stay about an hour here to take photos with the waterfall as the backdrop.

After parking the rental car at Seongsan Harbor, we hopped on the ferry (KRW 1,500) to cross over to Udo. Upon alighting from the ferry at Cheonjinhang Harbor on Udo, we headed to the Udo Tour Bus counter and got ourselves a ticket each (KRW 5,000). The whole tour is conducted in Korean. Not a single hint of English but it was enjoyable. The bus driver was also the tour guide, telling us about the significance of each stop. He'd stop for 20 minutes at each place of interest and if you do not hop back on, fret not, you may hop on the other tour buses. Keep your ticket stub.The whole tour took about 2 hours. The village roads were really interesting. If I visit Jeju again, I would want to stay overnight at Udo. The atmosphere is good, the air is fresh, people are nice.

After my Manjanggul Cave   expedition   and since the park is just along the way back, I took the chance to see what's the place could offer. I paid KW 2800 for an entrance (I have read reviews that some paid more than the cost, maybe the cost vary by seasons, not really sure). The maze can be finished roughly 10-15 mins, yet completed the maze roughly 30 mins hahaha. I just enjoyed messing around. Didn't really paid attention to the map and it's goal to ring the bell. The maze is good for family to enjoy.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

After hiking the Sunrise Peak, I was delighted by the fact that Jeongbang Waterfalls requires no rigorous hiking. We drove with our rental call and entered the phone number (7331530) into the GPS to get there. Parking is free. You just walk a short distance down a stairway and navigate through a few rocks to get closer to the waterfall. Overall, it is not difficult at all. The waterfall itself was so beautiful with the water flowing directly out to the ocean. If you've been to Yosemite, it kind of reminds me of the Vernal Falls/Mist trail without the heavy hiking up the steep steps. There were couples, seniors, and children sitting by the rocks enjoying the view. Of the three main waterfalls in the area, I would say Jeongbang is the best one.

Admission fee: 5000 won each.Went during Feb 14 which is winter. It was snowing where we were there and everything was covered with snow!The whole park is really huge! If you want to walk slowly and understand everything, it might take 2 hours or so. Most of the signboards are covered with icing and snow and we couldnt read it at all to understand.Of the whole time that we were there, we see no one at all until the end, we saw 1 person. A place to go if you want to relax and have a nice walk or if you are really interested in history and stones..

Abu Oreum was a great easy hike.? Took about 45 minutes to get to the top, hike all the way around the crater, and get back down with a 5-year-old and 7-year-old walking.? There is a trail into the crater that we didn’t take.? The climb itself from the parking lot to the top is less than 10 minutes. Has beautiful views of the countryside around it and a very pleasant walk past some cows and a small forest. It was also very easy to find and park.
About 40min drive from jeju it was a park with about 5 areas. Not bad but not amazing. Weather needs to be good or else don't bother. A few good photo's, a few short walks .... it's ok.
A waterfall at the ocean. Easily accessible. A 5-minute hike down from the parking lot. Can get crowded, have patience.
A very nicely organized theme park with different views at different stations. If you like to take pictures, a good half day can be spent there.

A unique theme park to visit. Just love the colorful displays of glass.  This theme park has an outdoor and indoor displays of everything made in glass.  What really caught my attention was the many shoes made in glass (for Cinderella). They are just so beautiful, makes me remember the Cinderella story all over again! Indoor displays are the many works of art made in glasses, so eye-pleasing too!.  They have workshops where you can make your own piece of glass art. Kids are welcome to join the workshops too.

A stunning waterfall that one can get close to it. Can be crowded especially in the afternoon. A short 5 min walk from the car park. the rocks where people usually gather to take picture of the stunning waterfall can be slippery, not recommended for elderly visitors.

A stunning view of the surrounding can be had on a clear day, but if the clouds are in then the view is not so good. A typical national park with beautiful surroundings to enjoy, trails, hikes and scenery. Not for the faint hearted and can be very tiring if fitness levels are an issue. Take plenty to drink and worth the climb once y ou get there!

A stunning architecture, indeed a church. Public access available except for church service hours. beaturiful view of the island from the location too.  There is a coffee house by the parking lot with pretty good coffee too.

A spacious and calm park! Nice place to walk around if you love nature. Best thing is it is free of charge to visit and once you come in, you are surrounded by nature. Wear comfortable shoes if you want to hike to the upper areas too!

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

A pretty large castle with grounds littered with many colourful glass decorations of animals etc. If you take a walk into the garden, you will also find colourful glass figurines of insects and animals nicely arranged in the park to create a fairy-tale like experience for the kids.

A pleasant theme park with train rides around 4 stations. As it's summer, can see entire fields of flowers.Lots of man made structures and buildings for educational purposes.But does not really fit in its Eco Land theme and can be too crowded in weekends

A pleasant park that protects the 3 holes in the ground from which sprang the demigods who founded the Kingdom of Tamna. It also houses a small museum which tells the story of the founding of Tamna, as well as buildings for the clan rituals that are held each year to mark the anniversary. Although in the city it is a fairly quiet and reflective place where you can get away from the city noise under the tall trees which provided some much needed shade during our visit.
A park with glass everywhere, you can take many colorful photos!Hard to see the blue sky in winter and this is one of the best place for photo during our trip.

A nice stop on the yeha bus tour, a lot of tourists so it easily gets overcrowded as the observation platform is small. Nice walk nearby with a small park next to the ocean. Pentagonal and heptagonal rock formations from lava cooling down. Enjoyed it and do recommend if in the area!

A nice park where you can walk up easily to see the crater. The crater is long dried up with vegetation growing and on my visit, there was a excavation truck at the bottom working! Wonder how the truck and worker get down there.Recommend to all age group.

A nice beach with fine sand and lots of facilities such as parasols for hire, cocktails and food stalls. There are showers and toilets close by too. On the downside, it's incredibly busy and parking is a nightmare. Once all the parasols and tables are out there's very little sand left! The amount of space available for swimming is small. We preferred to go to the less popular beach along the road. It's more spacious and more relaxed.

A 'must see' place when visiting the island. Lots of small shops around the entrance, a small fee (free if you work on the island), lots of stairs (a fairly tough climb) that lead to a variety of small temples and places to check out. Views are fantastic and on a clear day even better. You can get their by local bus although there is car parking but no 'wheel' access for baby strollers or wheelchairs. The golden Buddha and the drums give you an amazing feeling sitting so high above the surrounding area. Definitely worth it.
A lot of zone/theme - probably around 11. We like the cave, bonsai, bird park and tropical garden. The building is a little bit outdated.

A local has fulfilled himself a dream. He moved ground to this place and built this park with areas for Bonsai, azalees, palm trees, a natural lava tunnel, traditional houses, strangely formed lava rocks etc.The stop here is part of  a bus tour tio the Western part of the Island.

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

A larger version of Bontanic Gardens. Provide rental of prams for babies/ toddlers. The weather was good when I was there, hands nice and relaxing tour. They have cactus, flowers, plants, water park, caves, birds etc

A group of 22 of us went to South Korea from 13 - 20 April 2014.  We visited Ecoland Theme Park after our flight from Jeju Island. If you have seern Disneyland  in California, you wil;l; have some idea of what to expect from Ecoland.  However, when we were there, there was this tulip festival.  So we got to see tulips of various colours in a number of places, particularly  near the entrance. Overall, the theme park is an exciting place to visit.  I have one grouse to make.  We lined up like everyone else for the safari park ride on the bus.  Guess what? Instead of our turn to get on the bus, the ushers pushed us aside and gave some other tourists (locals I think) preference to get onto the bus.  In all my life, I have never been humiliated this way.  Come on South Korea, especially Ecoland.  You are developed country.  Civilsed society don't treat tourists to your country like that. There were not  many animals in the park.  Safari Park Indonesia beats you flat.  I like tthough the bus driver got the bears to stand to get food thrown to them.

A great place to witness how the lava which was erupted centuries ago formed the cliffs. A great place to view sunset as well. The scenery is amazing. However, that's all to it. Will prob take less than 30 mins. Entrance fee cost 2k won per person. If you are driving, do not follow the directions given by GPS. It will bring you to a hotel instead. You should instead drive to the Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and follow the signs there. The carpark is payable as well, albeit a small fee of 1-2k won, depending on the capacity of your vehicle.

A great museum well set out, very informative. Theres a short film, in English or Korean. Then a self directed tour of museum. Exhibits are well laid out with English translations. I would love to have had a translation of the interviews with the Haenyeo   women of the sea  . There is also a Haenyeo trail from the museum, taking in some of the traditional places the women divers used including the Bulteoks. You would need quite a lot of time to do both museum, park, and trail.
A fun beach, with lots of shallows for swimming and playing in the water.  The park is well kept, there are great coffee shops and restaurants. A very nice sandy beach which is hard to find in Jeju.

A difficult one if you choose to do the longest one which takes 4.5 hrs up and 4 hrs down.We went up  the  Eorimok trail which took us 2 n half hours up..its not an easy trak with steps and rocky path but the track has been laid with a lot of effort.In autumn the trees start to turn their colours .We came down the yeongsil trail which took us one hour to come down with spectac views..its an easier way to climb down than to climb up the yongsil trail.Bus 240 goes and come back at both stops with the entrance name as the stop names.But while from Eiromok entrance it's just a 10 mins walk up to the start of the trail.....its 45 mins walk to walk to the yeongsil entrance bus stop to the start of the trail.There are no tkts entrance for the hikes,but if you have rented a car then there is a parking fees.Carry some food to eat and energy bars and water n juice.

A beautiful view on top of Seongsan IIchulbong. Plenty of parking. We did this twice in the same day. The first hike (approximately 30 minutes to get to the top, started at 1pm) was extremely foggy and we couldn't see anything. We hiked back down and spent some time on the shore. Once the sun came out we hiked back to the top. There are several stops on the way with spectacular views of Jeju. You can purchase drinks and trinkets from one small shop about half way up. Use the restroom before going up as there is not one on the way. For a family of three to include a 10 year old we took one large bottle of water and a small backpack with some snacks and additional items. Bring a camera as it is absolutely beautiful. On the way we saw several different species of birds and spiders. At the top there are several benches where you can sit and enjoy the view. At the bottom there is a Mcdonalds, an ice cream shop, a souvenir shop, and other small shops. I suggest you try the orange ice drinks...they are great! Overall cost, 5,000 won for two adults and one child. We paid cash. Enjoy!

2 maze garden which worth to explore, test your capability to overcome the obstacle in finding your way out. There is 2 giant mazes within the park come with easy & challenging route to explore. RM has make this place popular
If not for the poor reptiles kept from small prisons, the park would have been

Yakcheonsa Temple is a famous Buddhist Templet located in Jeju island south of mainland Korea. The temple was built in 1981 by a Buddhist monk . It has three floors  It has a large Buddhist prayer hall. It is also famous for housing 80000 Buddhas all located on the second floor encased in glass.  It also has smaller statue of Buddha surrounded by lotus flowers under a pair of intricately carved protective dragons. The view from the top floor is veryy beaytiful facing the sea

Wow... just wow. I certainly didn't expect that. Yakchunsa isn't considered one of the must-go in Jeju so I didn't expect all that much especially given that you have to take a small road to go there. But once I arrived I was in awe. The complex is big colorful and the main pagoda-like multi-floor temple is massive and beautiful. What's even better is that the inside is at least as good as the outside view. There are three floors each with its own atmosphere and ornaments (murals candlelights wooden structures...). Take some time to go outside towards the sea to get the full perspective of the temple complex.

Wow wow wow!! This beach is absolutely stunning!! We enjoyed it while staying at the Hyatt Regency. It wasn't packed at all on the side of the hotels side but there was an area roped away that had more people. It was so beautiful and although the water was cold it was still enjoyable. Must go if in Jeju!

Wow from looking one would think the columns are man made. Indeed they are natural columns.It was late in the evening and cold like 3 degree and we did not stay long.Certainly worth another visit if we are in Jeju again.

Would have been nice to visit for sunrise but we were reliant on public transport. Still glad we did it in the morning. World heritage Site. 13km long lava tube under Jeju Island. Formed by successive eruptions. The section that can be visited is about 1km long - first descending down two levels into the lava tube where the roof has collapsed and then walking up the tube under the mountain and ending at a lava pillar where the lave cascaded down from a parallel tube running above.  There is good lighting and regular interpretive signs.  Wear good footwear as it it wet underfoot even on hot and dry days.  It is also nice a cool on a summer day.
Wonderful place to visit. Not too far from Jeju Airport.You can visit with family and friends in day time.Seaview from the top is just spactaclur.

Wonderful beach in Jeju island. Very clear water. Amazing colors and good vibes all around. You can spend here one day to have relax and chill out. And If you want you can walk around. There are close to the beach a lot of restaurants and caf챕s

With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.
Wished they opened more of the cave for public viewing though! It was very well preserved and maintained. A really long walk to and fro. My favourite attraction in jeju by a mile.
Who knew seeing tall weeds used as native house roofs would be very picturesque against the clear blue October sky? Only in Jeju and only on the way to the Sangumburi Crater!

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

While learning about the life of Jeju folk village we enjoyed the gardens farms and orchards. They are beautiful and being taken care well. It was our first time that we saw cabbage with flowers.During our visit it was almost toward the end of closing time and probably that's the reason there're not many visitors.

While in Jeju - we booked the Yeha bus tour and this is one of the places included to visit.  We really enjoyed our time here and our guide did an excellent job of recommending how to see everything in the time we had allotted.

While biking around Jeju Island my friend and I came across the world cup stadium. We took a short break and strolled around getting a good look at it. the stadium is of an interesting architectural design.

When in Jeju you can choose to go to Trick Art Museum or Alive Museum. Both are about the same you pose and take funny photos with the exhibits. The Alive Museum is divided into 5 sections Trick Art Object Art Digital Art Sculpture Art and Provence Art. If you follow the route after the first three you will get to the outdoor Sculpture Art. The last section Provence Art is basically a large room with a lot of large-sized stuff dogs in Provence village setting. The dogs are not as cute as the teddy bears at Teseum. I think Alive Museum is more suited for teenagers and youg adults visiting in groups it should be more fun for them.

When I was planning my trip to Jeju  I found this museum has got half positive and half negative comments from travelers. Well ??I decided to have a look by myself. When our car got near to the place  there was a strong smell. I was then told that there is a piggery farm nearby which stinks out the whole place. The ticket was not cheap but it included a cup of coffee plus a discount in the shop. The appearance of the building is interesting with an open courtyard. The first impression was not so bad.However when I got inside  it was quite disappointing. I think the management should consider a renovation  or at least a deep cleaning and some maintenance. I just felt I was in a dusty old weird mansion. Maybe those exhibits are precious and rare  but they are not well presented. For example  they put lots of chocolate boxes from all over the world in the same window display without proper descriptions. How can the people think that those boxes are precious when they are packed in a glass cabinet? The lighting on the second floor was horrible. The rooms were so dark adding horrific ambiance to the museum.

A short ferry trip from Jeju Island and then a bus trip around showed us the sights. We've enjoyed looking at the exhibits tasting free samples of tea and bought delicious green tea ice cream (KRW4500). Then we walked over to Innisfree to make our own soap which was so much fun - KRW15000 for one kit that makes three soaps but two people can share the kit so it's a really fun experience! You get to gift-wrap them at the end so they'd make a lovely present. You can naturally buy soap much cheaper but the experience was great and you customise and prettify the soaps as much as you like.Both O'Sulloc and Innisfree can get quite busy - as we were leaving a massive coach party arrived. It's not super-easy to find a table in the O'Sulloc cafe so beware. I saw several couples cruising around desperate to find a table while their ice cream was melting rapidly.The only negative for us was the journey: from the intercity bus terminal in Jeju-Si it took over an hour: the traffic was awful both ways! According to our travel guide it should have been 40 minutes. If you're catching the bus from the bus terminal it's number 755 from platform 10 but beware as the bus leaves before the time stated on the board/your ticket and it's a 50 minute wait for the next one (we've learnt the hard way!)
We're a tea lover and trying the best tea that Jeju Island is offering. If you happen to to visit Jeju Island try to drop by there. Just next to it you can visit Innisfree as well.

Went to this welcome center for some advice and guidance for what to do during my short stay here in Jeju and the staff there was very friendly knowledgeable and were able to give me very useful suggestions. If you don't know what to do and your hotel is close by it should definitely be worth a visit for you.

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.

Went there last week on my trip to Jeju. Its a local market where you can find shopkeepers selling almost everything. From souvenirs to sea food. And stuff is pretty cheap too. Visit once to experience the local flavour and to collect some stuff to take back

Went there in May 2015 by jeju golden city bus tour (which sucked!) and totally enjoyed our 1 hour visit! The exhibitions were amazing and the atmosphere itself is beautiful there! Adm fee is good: just 1000 won as much as I remember. Though the prices at a coffee shop were pretty expensive.

Went during the summer and its still pretty cold down there. Its a good rainy day itinerary as its entirely underground. Be warned that it can get really cold when  its raining though. Advised to wear good shoes are you wont be walking on flat ground and its quite wet and slippery. Its pretty interesting to learn  of the formation of the lava tube and a must go if its your first time in Jeju.

Went around with a friend and the place is huge. I think we managed to walk from gate 8 to gate 4 before we realized we cane there looking to eat and ended up just window shopping because there?s lots to feast your eyes on. There?s mostly food and fresh produce and seafood and food products made from Jeju oranges.

Well  that's one I definitely wouldn't recommand. There are so many things to do in Jeju and many in a 5-km radius even (Sanbangguksa  Yongmeori Beach  Songaksan...) but the Hamel Ship exhibition center is a miss. It would have actually been interesting to have place dedicated to the historical significance of Hamel and Korea through foreigners' eyes  but this was just a small collection of cheap and run-down replicas of things you could see pretty much everywhere. Maybe kids would enjoy the pirate-looking ship  but that's the only good reason to go.

We were taken to the folk village. We originally tried the Jeju Folk Village Museum but that was full of tourists. We were shown around several buildings that we were told were still lived in. Sorry but even primitive people had some form of furniture and cooking facilities. Yes some people may life on site and in other houses. But why show empty and it mean completely empty houses. Show us how you and your past folk lived. Some of the information was interesting until the sales pitch started. The selling of the honey and blackberry cordial which suppose to make you younger and fitter!!! I bought a ship load- not. They took us into a hut with chairs all in rows for a presentation on the value of the juice at $40 a litre bottle. Right next to the village are some restaurants which our guide wanted us to eat in at our expense!!! So I guess the real reason for coming here is their extra bit of money!!!!For most of us on our bus this stop was a complete waste of valuable time.

Any shock you might find in the first 10 mins or so is soon negated as this place is just straight in your face.  On the whole very well done and an extra angle on your holiday.  So why isn't their one of these in Margate ?!

We were lucky that the lady of the house was both detail and funny when explaing about the old jeju ways. A good place to visit and get to know abit of the culture.

We were in Jeju during a thypoon event and looking for indoor activities. This was one of them and to be honest we probably would have sought out a brewery regardless of the weather. The tour was in Korean which we found out on arrival. It would have been nice to have been told that when we booked by email and before we travelled out to the brewery. However after the tour the guide apologised and informed us that there needs to be 5 or more English speakers in the tour to do it in English which was fair enough. They then also gave us an unreleased Belgian Quadrupel to thank us. More importantly the beer was good and the pizza tasty.

We were glad we could catch this show in Jeju as time in Seoul were simply too precious for shopping. It's funny and you don't need to understand Korean to enjoy it. We got our taxi guide to reserve the tickets on the same day and only manage to get the VIP seats at w60k each. It would be better if you can reserve the ticket days in advance.

We went to visit this Dragon Rock and it put a bleak end to our Jeju trip. The rock is a beautiful artwork of nature but people seem to be taking too much advantages of it. We went to this place as one of the itineraries in our Jeju (East course) tour by Yeha. Here you can buy different kinds of freshly harvested teas and enjoy one of the best green tea ice cream in the world.
We went there on our way back after U-do. It offers such a gorgeous view of Jeju-do and it was a short hike - return trip of less than 1 hour. Definitely worth the hike!
We went there and enjoyed ourselves. You can get discount by using the voucher from KTO Malaysia (??800) per pax. We hang around for 1-2 hours before heading to Innisfree Jeju House.

We went here today for first time and love it?s it?s so beautiful and fun to walk around have good restaurants and coffee shop and good shop to buy thing make from jeju !! You can take bus or taxi too

We went here on a rainy day as we really wanted to see how the famous O'Sulloc tea was made. The museum is nothing more than a room (unfortunately not all texts are translated info english) and the majority of the space is taken up by the shop and the cafe which seems like the main focus of this location.Two things were nice getting a look of the tea plantations and having a quick tea tasting.I would recommend this only if you are a true O'Sulloc fan or if you have spare time not visiting all the other sights at Jeju island.

We went here as per the recommendation on Tripadvisor. We wanted to go to Udo island and then come to see the sunset on this peak.since the ferry to Udo was cancelled due to rough sea and strong winds we had to change our plan and come to peak right in the afternoon.Since it was overcast and cloudy weather we could hike easily to the top. the 360 view from top is breathtaking.hiking trails is good. You can see the black sand beach and also see the jeju fishing lady show.

We visited Yakcheonsa Temple on our Jeju Olle Trail Route 8. This temple looks delightful because of its architecture and beautiful surrounding scenery. The views from the second floor were amazing! We even had a chance to ring the bell and make wishes here! A recommended place for photographers to get vivid pictures. You can also experience a temple stay activity in this Buddhist temple.

We visited Udo in our recent visit to jeju island. We couldn't see the whole island due to rainy weather. One thing the visitor should be careful about the renting of battery bike or other types of two wheelers. The store owner will ask U something unethical rate for rent and the behaviour of them are really very very bad. They behave with us very rudely.

we visited two parks in Jeju. Hallim and Spirited Garden. ticket price was almost the same for both but Hallim was by far much better and bigger with good design and a lot of different and amazing trees and some birds too. It is really a must visit for Jeju visitors to spend around two hours enjoying the park.

We visited this museum as women diver is an unique culture in Jeju. The museum is very informative and trying to education people about the history and current stage of women diver and their significant contribution to the economy. It was an interesting place to spent an hour and we left with a whole new found respect for these brave women.

We visited the Tea Museum in a rainy windy day. The place was very crowded with tourists especially the cafe and shop. There were some history and artefacts displayed which I guess was why it's called a museum. I actually expected more from a 'museum'.The goods sold in cafe and shop were the same with other branches in Seoul maybe with a few 'only in Jeju' specials. They were quite pricey but tasted great.
We visited on a Monday morning and there are so many tourists and koreans at both the green tea cafe and shop and Innisfree Jeju House and cafe. Good green tea drink and desserts though.
We visited Oedolgae as part of our Yeha Bus tour - South Course and it is just another perfect spot to stop and see Jeju's beauty.

We visited Jeju Haenyeo museum . Story of woman divers is very inspiring . Even today woman are diving in sea to earn for their family . I salute their courage. Museum is very good . Documentary on Haenyo's was also. Must Visit if you are in Jeju Island .

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We travelled to this market in October 2016 using the Jeju City tour bus. The inside of the market was well lighted and there were lots of fruits and local goods on display. Inside there was a branch alley which sold fish and other marine products. Across the market there was an open square with a small river and we saw some tourist police on horseback. The market was not as big as we expected but OK to visit and buy some fruits.

We took VIP tickets from Jungmun Tourist centre  at 50 percent off. The show is very entertaining and involves lots of interaction with the crowd. The place is a bit far away and close to Jeju university. If you are going for 8:00pm show booking a taxi is recommended. The show is value for money for the deal we got from the tourist office. Apparently there is a rush pass which is available for discounts on shows for the same day.

We took many amazing pictures here against the camellia flowers. The walkways around the park were arranged nicely so we spent a few hours here easily. Overall one of the best spots we visited in Jeju this is a place you definitely have to include in your travel plans!

We took bus 600 from the World Cup Stadium. This bus is also the Airport Limousine. We got off at Jeju ICC and walked from there towards the sea. The geometrical volcanic rock formation simply took our breath away!  Who cut/shaped the rocks this way? A fantastic work of art created by the Master Craftsman. Another wonder of nature. The geometrical shapes were amazing! This is - must-visit site!

We took a short walk from the nearby peace park to visit this place in October 2016. Entrance fees were nominal but visitors were few.  Looks like not a very popular tourist spot. Just as well  we could enjoy a short walk here without the crowds. Quite a nice place to walk around although there were not so many deer. You could buy some plant food to feed the deer. The main enclosure for the deer is not that big but the park itself has other longer walking paths.  If you do not wish to walk here from the peace park you can take the Jeju City tour bus but need to wait.
We took a car passenger ferry to to Udo island from Jeju. This a small but beautiful island. We drove around the island and try some fresh seafood.

We took a cab and travel around Jeju. First: if you are intending to take a cab pls prepare your itinerary and let the driver know where you plan to go. 2nd: the driver will show you the mystery of the road. it seems that the bottle will roll to the steeper side of the road. bascially it is an eye illusion.

We stumbled upon this market while walking around Jeju. It was very vibrant inside with many vendors selling their products. The vendors were very friendly and tried to speak English to us. Some even gave us samples of their products. We bought some local chocolates. It was very enjoyable and a great way to spend some time.

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.

We spent like 3 hours in the museum took hundreds of funny photos! Although posing for the photos was like doing exercise quite tiring but still we had so much fun. Luckily it was not too crowded so we could take as many photos as we wanted at the same spot. There is also an outdoor space for photo-taking many creative sculptures. If you want to do something fun or if it is raining in Jeju this is the place you should visit!

We spent a half day here for a short walk. It was such a peaceful and relaxing place. You could see many coastal rocks and Udo. If you like  you could ride a horse to wander a while. You may also visit the lighthouse and the chapel nearby. This was one of must go tourist points in Jeju!

We self-drive to this museum. Like everyone else we ate the green tea cake ice cream and hot green tea latte for lunch it was delicious especially for green tea lovers. It was crowded with bus loads of tourists but the cafe staff was very efficient and served quickly. Bought Jeju tangerine tea after trying the sample. We also went to the innisfree shop to buy cosmetics. And took photos of the garden that has beautiful cherry blossoms at this time. Great soothing weather and we also walked across the road to the tea plantation. Enjoyed ourselves.

We rode most of the Olleh trail routes by bike and it was awesome.  We made a film about it (titled Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure) and met heaps of interesting people to interview.   I'd definitely recommend it as a not-to-miss part of visiting Jeju Island!   I'd like to walk some of the Olleh Trail routes next time to experience it differently and more slowly.

We rented bycicles and ride around (It was about $15 for 2 bycicles) The stones on the beaches were special. We tried the dish of raw fish and noodles in the restaurant where my friend said to have appeared a movie/show. It's near the beach. The fish was fresh but we dont like the taste much. It's a really naturally beautiful place comparing to others in Jeju. You would want to spend half-day there to fully go around the island.
We rented a car in jeju and decided to experience the mysterious road. It was amazing how your car rolls backwards when it looks like an uphill road. A must visit place if you are in jeju.

We rent a car in jeju and drove to this place.  We were pleasantly surprised and really enjoyed ourselves. If you're the sort who likes taking photos that stimulate the senses don't miss.  Quite a big museum and there are many fun and interesting spots to take photos.

We reached the cave 45 minutes before closing hour and had to walk really fast in order to reach the end of the cave to see the Lava tubes. Many friends told us it's a must visit in jeju.  But my Cousin and I were disappointed as we felt it's nothing fascinating. Better time could be spent in other attractions such as the sunrise peak and Teddy bear museum.

We only spent 4 nights in Jeju and happened to pass by this place on our way to the city center. We decided to spend half a day soaking up the sun. These 5 hours were a highlight! The town was pretty quiet and the beach wasn't too crowded. Beautiful views! There was a nice restaurant on the water to get snacks. Water was refreshing! Note: I noticed a camp ground on the far right side of the beach. Cool idea for the future. BE AWARE there are very large spiders over near that boardwalk. Yikes!

We only had a limited time in Jeju so we asked Jin to customize a tour for us to see the best of Jeju has to offer. Both Jin and June speak English fluently so it was not difficult to communicate. They are both flexible in terms of what we want to see. Excellent service!

We need to pay for the entrance fees but it is not that pricey and worth it. You need to take a few stairs to finally reached the waterfall area. The view is very sceneric and worth to take a picture on every angle of it. A must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.
We love this museum with different teddy bears and so colourful. Great for kids and adults. While in Jeju is a place to visit. Visitors are crowded so go early.
We looked up what Jeju was known for and black pork was one of the things. The food is so delicious!

We invite you to 'Figure Museum Jeju'  full of fantastic movie figures and statues! There are tons of high quality exhibits! Action figures  movie statues  life size statues  upcycling arts  game statues  etc. Everybody can enjoy and have fun here with figures from movies and games and animations.
we hired taxi for a-day trip this is the last sightseeing in jeju.totally enjoy the fun experience and fill up the puzzle.must visit once in a life time.

We had two rounds of tea tasting - the signature green tea and another caramile version. Both are good but not great. It's more of a Cafe than museum we had a great time buying tea for our family. The sales people speaks good English and is always ready to help.Cafe is a bit crowded but the turnover is fast and it did not take long to buy our drinks and get a seat. The back garden is connected to Innisfree Cafe so don't miss that too.Parking is a pain however so remember to be aggressive. Parking is not restricted to what's marked on the ground in Jeju.

We had to cancel our trip to Udo Island last minute due to heavy rain and because Jeju does not have too many indoor attractions we ended up visiting Aqua Planet. Admission is quite pricey - around USD 130 for a family of four. I am personally not a big fan of aquariums or zoos  but I was glad to learn upon arrival that this aquarium had already released its whale sharks to the ocean. The show was mostly performed by synchronized swimmers and other actors while sea lions and dolphins only played a small part. Kids got to learn some new species from tomato crabs to long-neck turtle and more. Overall it was quite a positive experience.
