입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: We had so much fun here posing in all the 3-D backgrounds. This place is huge and has so many places to take great photos. Well worth the money. Definitely a must try when on Jeju island.

We had heard about the tea plantation first on the television show Kimchi Chronicles on PBS (http://www.kimchichronicles.tv/). As an avid tea drinker I could hardly pass up the chance to check it out in person and it is amazing. We drank tea walked in the tea fields checked out the tea museum watched the roasting of tea bought tea tea soap tea lotion and tea ice cream. The museum and center are quite stunning and the drive out there interesting on some very well maintained roads. Don't miss this one if you are on Jeju Island.

We had an old Korean man who has lived there for all his life guiding us around his own house in English. He was very humorous and a very friendly guide. It was an interesting and refreshing experience of learning about the old village way of living in Jeju!

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.

We had a morning before our flight and got the bus (600)  to these cliffs. There were not too many people there on a Tuesday morning. There are explanations about the formation of these geometrically shaped columns if you're interested.We liked watching the waves hit the cliffs and have some amazing pictures.Nice activity in Southern Jeju.
We had a lovely time here checking out all the lovely glass items on display. Indeed very creative. For someone who love photo taking  this is indeed a must visit place in Jeju

We got so much help from the people to get here on the first day in Jeju. The view was really great and we felt released to enjoy the wind when walking through the trail. The horses and goats look so cozy around the trail.

We got rained out on our trip to Jeju and decided to hit the spa. It's Korean style Jimjilbang so be aware it's not like a Western spa. You can still get a massage if you want but the highlight is soaking in the various pools of many temperatures. Apparently you can sleep there for cheap too if you need a quick crash pad. Read more at by blog: Gallivantrix dot com.
We found the park by accident while just driving around. This was one of the best places to visit in Jeju. I even purchased a miniture old man statute. Must go if you can find it.

We felt a little cheated cause the castle wasn't so much of a castle. More like a small park and it was pricey for the entrance and there wasn't much to see at all. Realised that there are plenty of museums like these to cheat tourist money in Jeju so be selective on which ones you plan to visit. This is definitely not one of them that you should go.

We engaged a Local private driver to bring us to Yongmeori Coast. He made a call to the Relevant Authority to check the weather and tide condition. Yongmeori Coast is situated beside Mt Sanbangsan.The car park was full that day and fortunately we found one lot. Our driver guided us the walking route to the coast.He was indeed a good private tour guide!We were immense into the nature and its beauty. He skilfully captured many memories into pics for us! This trip was my most memorable part in Jeju.
We drove there  looking for a rest location plus how tea was made in Jeju in situ but nothing there

We drove around Jeju and decided to give this thing a go cos we didn't believe it would be possible. So we reached the road and there were signs that told you that its the starting. So all you have to do is to put your car in neutral gear and release the accelerator at the starting point and watch your friend's jaw drop. Recommended to visit together with Jeju Loveland as its just 3 minutes driave away. Admission at 8000 won per pax. pricey but its a pretty interesting visit XD

We discovered Jeju Mokgwan (the Governors historical admin center) when we drove past it then walked to it from our hotel. Of all the places we visited in Jeju City it was our favorite. Most of the signage included English translations of how Jeju-do was run in the past. The buildings are well restored pieces of art. Very relaxing.  There were also ancient games for children. The venue seemed to be set up mostly for locals for who this venue is free. Foreigners enter for a nominal fee.If you found this rating beneficial please click the helpful button.
We didn't want to waste a cloudy day so we spent it hiking.  Which was a nice little break from all the lazing around beaches we had done.  Gorgeous views of Udo and Jeju.

We didn't seek to visit Mt. Songak -- our driver just brought us there. Not knowing what to do and since he didn?셳 speak a word of English we just consulted a map near the entrance and decided that the only thing to do there really was walk up to the crater. It's a genuine natural wonder. I?셫 glad we went there because the place was just so beautiful it was worth the effort of climbing. And believe me there was some effort. Unlike other Jeju-do mountains there were rough parts in this mountain without steps or any pavement. Some bits were steep too. If you have mobility issues forget the crater; just walk around. One Korean grandpa lost his footing and scraped his hand on the rocks ??we felt bad for him.There were horses that you can ride briefly for a little bit of money. They were cute and surrounded by fields of flowers. It was like a dream to be there looking at the sky the sea the fields and the horses. Would come back if I have the chance.

We didn't bother with the museum itself. Not my thing.But the Sunday Brunch at the cafe is legendary.Smoothies come in cute glass jars with thick straws and are so full of chunks of fruit that you almost have to chew them as you drink.The brunch itself is a mix of odd elements that I wouldn't normally put together - but they work..... creamy butternut squash soup scrambled eggs mustard coated potato wedges plus a ham/cheese/vegetable panini with salad leaves and balsamic vinegar on the side. Really good food.We sat outside the weather was lovely. Great view of the tea field (part of the museum) and the road. If I come back to Jeju on a trip sometime I'll definitely return for Sunday brunch!

We didn?셳 spend much time here which was a pity but in any case there were too many tourists. Would be a better experience when less crowded. The buildings are stylish and there is a nice view of the tea gardens. You can try the tea and they explain the tea making process. The cafe looked good with desserts like green tea cake and ice cream but we didn?셳 try as the queue was too long. Nearby was the Innisfree building where many people were making handmade soap. There was also a cafe and exhibits of the different distilled essences of flowers and plants in Jeju.

We did not plan to visit the museum originally but was brought here by accident by a taxi driver who couldn't speak much English (of which there are plenty in Jeju-do). We were pleasantly surprised and really enjoyed ourselves. If you're the sort who likes taking photos that stimulate the senses don't miss.

We came here after going to the crater. We wandered around a bit and it was ok just not great- maybe it would have been better if we had purchased an audio tour. If we ever come back to Jeju I wouldn't come back here. They did have some really yummy cactus taffy we purchased though and that was fun. The best part of this place were the old games. I think this place would be better for families with small children.
We are very satisfied with the tour and will surely consider to purchase another tour from them on my next visit to Jeju.

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

We actually stayed at a hotel right on this beach.  The water is beautiful but there are signs saying no to swimming in some parts of it.  There is a cafe bene right next to it so you can grab a cup of coffee and go sit on the beach.  The only problem is that it is pretty far from anything else like all the museums and nature trails of jeju and it is kind of small which makes me think that in the summer it can get really crowded.
Way too many rules. Can't take off masks for photos  there are 3 small waterfalls that you have to pay to see. Don't waste your money. See a waterfall somewhere else in Jeju for free.

Was very crowded the day/time we were there.  There's a tiny museum which leads to shop and cafe.At the cafe we had the trio of  green tea cake/roll smoothie and ice cream which were very good.Then we headed next door to the Innisfree Jeju house.A nice way to spend a couple of hours.  There's a couple of very uncrowded O'sulloc cafes in Seoul too.

Was there at about 10ish in the morning lots of (noisy) tourist and you can hardly find a decent seat in the cafe with unruly kids running around. Difficult to take photo at the photo spot cos some particular tourists pose like nobody business and after a long time posing change friend to pose again. I gave up and went outdoors where noise will not be contained and there is more fresh air.Sadly there isn't much nor exciting to see here - yet it is a spot you have read alot before coming. Suggest to just make a brief stop to have a look.I spent more time over at the Innisfree Jeju House instead which was surprisingly very peaceful.

Was specially there to try their famous Matcha Roll and Matcha ice cream and it didn't disappoint. The cream within the Matcha roll was totally on point and delicious. The Matcha ice cream was rich and creamy. It went really well together with the matcha roll. There were too many tourist on the day we visited and was overly crowded. We were also disappointed with the innisfree shop beside the tea museum as we'd expected more product offerings. There are no cosmetics in the store. Only limited number of products. It is a 30-45mins drive from Jeju City.

Was recommended by the people at my resort to visit this place. Reason being it is very clean. I did not do too many hikes in Jeju and this was just one of the few I did. It was a small forest garden owned by a family and now looked after by the 2nd generation daughter.She gave us a brief intro in English of the forest. One that actually does not have soil and one that offers a different season from what it actually should be.Unfortunately we did not experience this difference in season while in the forest. But we just enjoyed walking around this small forest garden admiring the trees that have sprout out.A good walk if the true forest hike may be too much to bear

Was feeling really amazing when passing through this road.   The tour bus was moving even though the driver has turned of the machine. Recommended anyone coming to Jeju to try this herself/himself.* TK

Was expecting more. I think once you are in Jeju you just feel like everywhere will be magical but when you reach places that give off mediocre vibes you tend to get disappointed. So don't come here with high expectations.This place is too touristy and honestly I'd rather kayak in Bali (actually water rafting there is awesome) or in Laos. Or even in Kota Kinabalu or Thailand.

Was excited to see the tea museum but disappointed as it was only a 5 minute tour. We drove for about 1.5 hours to visit this museum from the other end of Jeju City.  The treats at the museum shop was a nice respite against the summer heat though. There is also the tea plantations just across the museum and Innisfree (Korean Skincare) beauty shop about 2 minutes walk away. I would recommend to go for the Stoner Tea museum tour to make this trip more worthwhile. However there are certain timings for it and we didnt manage to join.

Was curious about this rock formation as read the other trip advisor comment and was not disappointed at all. Its really a very interesting rock formation and its nice to just feast your eyes on this amazing view.Only 2000kW for entry fee but try to avoid peak times as I went on a Sunday the viewing bridge was packed with visitors doing their selfie shots so you are not able to see the view as clearly due to the crowds. Must visit when you Jeju island.
Walking through the lava tubes is just an amazing experience.  It is surreal and beautiful to see what millennia of lava flow has created.  One of the best places to see on Jeju Island.
Walk to the highest mountain in Jeju. Then you can find a excellent view and enjoy the strong wind. Remember bring more water and some food. And keep clean for the natural environment.

Visited this place 4 years ago. This is a iconic place in jeju Island. This place is known for its rocks formation which looks like dragon head. The ocean is also beautiful here A place for photography as a memo. Not to be missed when in jeju.

Visited this Museum in Dec 2017 with my family. Entrance ticket costs 34 000kwon for 2 adults and 2 children. The place basically is run-down  glasses broken  dirty and colour faded over the years. I didn't bother to check on the cafe inside and left the museum in 15mins. Nothing special in the gift shop as well. Total waste of my money and my time travelled to visit the so called museum. If you intend to visit this Jeju Glass Museum  don't bother!

Visited this beautiful temple while walking Olle Trail 8. Its pretty impressive with a nice location overlooking the south coast of Jeju. Easy to reach using airport limo 600. Busy place with many tourists so go early to avoid crowd to have a peaceful time to enjoy the temple. Souvenir stalls at the temple entrance.

Visited the Park based on TA reviews. Extremely well done with extensive museums and stone displays. Allow at least 3-4 hours for the visit. Enormous work has gone into the development of the Park. Should be in the Top 5 attractions in Jeju outside the beaches.
Visited the Alice museum in a rainy day in Jeju was not sure of it at first but I must say we had a pretty fun time whoever put it together has a different sense of humor

Visited Sangumburi Crater as our first stop from Jeju city centre. It was in the morning and was rather cooling and relaxing. Not much visitors at the time. Sangumburi Crater was one of my favorite attractions of Jeju (the other being Udo-bong). It was a short stroll along the way and viewing of the greenery and flowers.

Visited on a rainy day.  Limited parking - so had to park along the road and take a muddy path through the team garden.  Tea shop was very crowded to went to the Innisfree jeju House about 60 m away - great food and can make your own soap.

Visited on a friend's recommendation and it definitely didn't disappoint.  Upon entry to the building we walked through the historical display area before getting to the shop and cafe.  There were many different types of tea for sale and all beautifully packaged.  Again thanks to the friend who asked us to help buy stuff for her we knew to get the green tea milk spread.  For the tea they had samples for you to smell before purchasing.  We got the wedding tea green tea and green tea cold sticks. Can't wait to get home to try them.  Next we had the green tea roll green tea ice cream and green tea milk shake at the cafe.  All were exquisite.  On the outdoors there are great photo opportunities near the tea plantation.  As we walked there we discovered another building called Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a health food restaurant cum shop selling body oils and moisturiser.  We had lunch there and bought some beautiful smelling body lotion.  Again all fantastic.  The whole family enjoyed O'Sulloc!

Visited in the evening.  It is a local market selling Jeju specialities as well as a wet market section selling the fresh & live seafood.  Good to visit if you are into shopping for foods and want jeju local foods and street food.

Visited Hallasan during Autumn season and the weather was chilly. Best to bring an extra layer of clothing to wear esp when you?re at the top. Did the climb at 9ish in the morning and managed to reach the shelter before the cutoff time at 1230pm (if my memory didn?t fail me). Took about another 2 hours or so before we reached the peak. The trail we took was pretty gentle in the beginning but it was filled with loads of steps at the end. We were rewarded with a great view at the top so the pain of going up & down was definitely worth it. Gotta do it at least once when you?re in Jeju!
visited 3 more popular waterfalls in Jeju and this one is the best.  best visit time is summer so that you can enjoy the splash when you walk close.  Imagine it would be too chilly for winter though.

Visit this place even if you not interested or lover of sea shells at least to recognise the sheer efforts put in by Ms Myeong Yeon Sook  the director of this museum and owner of this place. This museum which has over 7 800 variety and accounting to more than millions of sea shells originating in Jeju and the world is the brain child of Ms Sook and master Metal craftsman Kwon Oh-Kyun.The beauty of these sea shells are to be seen to be believed. They have been arranged and displayed so artistically that one may easily mistake it as a painting.One may not see much of visitors around  but this really helps as we go around enjoying the magic of nature.Entrance fee is a bit high  but really worth it  considering the efforts put in to bring this huge collection of sea shells under one roof and creating the world's first seashell museum.

Viewpoint on the western end of Jeju Island.  Great place for sunset observation.  High on a cliff with good views all around.  There is a weather station here.Was here on a windy day - with field of swirling grass. To the north of the hill is a tail along the shore where it is possible to rent electric scooters.  There is also a small museum on the prehistoric settlement found in the area.
Very recommended for chocolate addict.... they sold those famous Jeju chocolate varians... you might want to try Ginseng chocolate and Cactus chocolate out of curiousity.

Very pretty and not too taxing walk to add to any outings on Jeju. Our day was a little foggy but the view was still amazing with the Spring growth just starting to show. Lots of other attractions in the near vicinity makes it a good spot to include in a day out. The short but steep hike up to the 'temple in a cave' provides some lovely views on a good day and there are several other attractions at the base of the walk including the Big Golden Buddha temples tea shops the Dutch ship and rock walks. Enjoyable.

Very Nice place to understand and enjoy Jeju in South Korea. There is old story that a women had been waited for her husband who was fisherman.  She became the rock statue(Oeidolgae) because her husband couldn't come back home while fishing sunk by windstorm.  Also another point of sightseeing is beautiful beach with rocks. There is beach of rocks in this region.   You may see pics in TripAdvisor.  Atlas Dream.
Very Nice place also very cold and we have a lot experience at this place..it is the 1st time i n my family go to the best place at jeju

Very interesting garden of native plants but you don't get much time to see before they herd you into a room to hard sell you into buying Ginseng. Their pitch is that they invented a new method to grow and harvest JeJu ginseng in the lab and is suppose to the best. Buy ginseng here is very expensive. I don't even think JeJu is know for ginseng.

Very informative on the formation of Jeju Island with the right mix of information and artifacts. You could also treat this place as an introduction to the places to visits in jeju - the natural part only. Worth about two hours of your time.
Very entertaining and funny. They perform with body language so we can understand the story easily. Recommended and must see when you visit Jeju.
Unique souvenirs from Jeju? This is the right place!

Unique geographical nature reserve called Gotjawal is Jeju local language stands for forest(怨?Got) and thorn bushs on rock(?먯솃;jawal). The area is kept 10-15 degrees celsius throughout the year making Summer cool and Winter warm where tropical Northern hemisphere plants and frigid Southern hemisphere plants can coexist.There are four main Gotjawal terrain in Jeju Island this is the one in the South-West area. They also have a guided tour around this Gotjawal forest which you can explore the area with it's own story. The thing is they only have Korean tour so far so you might want to speak Korean or request them to open up an English tour.

Unfortunately  I cannot say that this place is worth visiting. The surrounding area and sites (Sanbangsan and the temple  Yongmeori Coast) are worth the visit though  and I speculate that this is the only reason the museum has survived.The ship museum itself provides information about the Dutch sailor who landed on Jeju and was held captive and against his will for several years by Koreans (not sure why this is a source of pride as it seems to be made out). The story itself could be quite interesting  but to be honest  I would rather read about it in a well-written book than in a tacky and very cheesy museum using broken English. Children might enjoy walking through the ship replica so I suppose it could be worth visiting if you also visited the other nearby sites.I personally would never recommend this place to anyone.

review: Unforgettable Jeju Trip

UNESCO heritage site in Jeju. Location near the restaurant that sells live abalone and woman diver. It's crowded with holidaymakers but well worth the view. There are some cafe and restaurant at the car park. Didn't catch the sunrise as we were staying at the other side of the island.

Understand that the day we went weather was harsh as there?셲 typhoon warning ; the parking escort/attendant wasn?셳 helpful at all is was raining and very windy we were traveling with a 2yr old baby  ask him nicely to let us ?쁃rop off??only but he insisted that we go to the other carpark to park our cars (the carpark has open lots and a few cars are coming out) ; I don?셳 know his against foreign or what but after we parked our car Far far away carrying the baby  pram  umbrella diaper bag we saw he letting the locals go in and park . We were so piss ; and it ruin our trip in jeju as my toddler felt sick after. His now down with flu thanks to them and I still got 12 more days in Korea . Very disappointed  will not recommend any of my friends and family period

udo was one of beautiful & must visit place in jeju. we spent 1day for it for visit such  pretty landscape. we took shuttle bus for tour around the island. diff view & diff landscape. i love light house hill & whale cave. better reserve enough time for visit & enjoy the scenery

tried the forest healing program last month during my visit to jeju island. Guided by forest therapist we have completed forest healing trail. I can say it really helps me relax the body by focusing on natural noises flowing water  chirping mountain birds  fresh forest air and those Phytoncide!!! oh it just smells so nice >.< we got to try the foot bath and aromatherapy too. the therapist said they also have body bathing tub and aqua line  but since we dont have many time.. maybe next time. Good place to relax your mind and escape from hustle and bustle city. i will try another program if i have chance to visit it again.

Traversing through Manjanggul was nothing like my other spelunking experiences! This was more civilized and organized :) Manjanggul's explorable/walkable area is only 1km but it's already enough for you to appreciate how Jeju's volcanic origins formed these natural wonders for us to see.

Travelled by ferry from Seongsan habour (price 5500W two way). Upon reaching the island turn right to the carpark to purchase bus tickets (price 5000W). Bought the red tickets (you can only board the red buses with the red tickets and blue bus for the blue tickets). The bus is a hop on hop off bus (can only go forward not backward); you'll have to hold on to your ticket to board the bus for the next stop. Buses come every 20-30 mins. First stop was udobong peak - we had peanut ice cream (must try!!! Albeit a little sweet. Udo is known for the peanuts). The climb up is a little slippery so I won't recommend it on a rainy day. Requires some fitness to make it to the top but it is not too difficult. Otherwise a very relaxing climb that my family and I enjoyed very much! Stopped also at the Beacon mound (second stop on red bus) which was a nice selfie spot and then headed to the beaches before catching the ferry back to the mainland (last ferry back to jeju 5.30pm). The island is quite touristy though; expect things to be a bit more expensive.

Transportation- You can take bus 755 to the museum takes half an hour from jeju downtown. Food- nothing nearby but you can get pretty decent coffee and jeju-special tea/drinks at the 'innisfree organic green cafe' at the same compound. The museum itself is not that exciting took us 15 mins finishing off everything including the teatree garden. The innisfree cafe/store nearby is so much more fun especially for the female fellow travellers.;)

Tranditional House and village in Jeju. If you want to know about traditional life. Janggem Korean Drama has taken place the shooting here. You also could buy tea that made from bluberry and horse bone.

Totally amusing day at Alive museum at Jeju. Great place for young kids adults and even senior citizen. Was there in mid Dec with 3 different age group all enjoyed taking photo & the place is well maintain.

Today is the last day in Jeju but since the plane is evening time so we went to Jeju folk village museum.It's worth visiting there! Every one of us really enjoyed ourselves going to learn their traditional style and ways of living! Furthermore the place is very beautifully designedmaking us just want to know what that's waiting ahead of us as we go along!I'll visit this place again if ever to go to Jeju again!

To fully enjoy cultural heritage it is recommended that you spent few hours reading and inspect all the objects that represents it.Even though it was raining during the time I visited I enjoyed the Folk village because they have a very interesting culture and history dated thousands of years.In each places represents how the Koreans house hold systems livelihood and government are highly organized.I also enjoyed the art exhibit and felt honored meeting the National artist.  He even gave me one of his works on display!After roaming around you might want to experience authentic Jeju cuisine by dropping at the Traditional Market inside the Folk village at reasonable price. Oh don't forget to try the Cactus candy!It's just unfortunate that we haven't witness any Korean traditional wedding ceremony that day due to rain.This is much better Folk Village to visit as it is bigger than the other nearby.

To be honest we had already sampled the green tea cake ice cream and tea at the O'Sulloc shop and cafe in Insadong Seoul. However this tea garden featured in 'the Kimchi Chronicles' so we had to make a kind of pilgrimage to see it. The overall experience in the shop and cafe was a bit stressful because there are many tourists here at any given time of the day. It is a bit of a shame because this made it difficult to look at the teas properly and then to decide what to purchase. The prices are not cheap - even more so than  eg Fortnum and Masons but the tea is quite unique as it is grown here on the island. I guess it is worth the premium especially if you are buying the tea as a gift.Next door there is the cosmetics side to this enterprise - Innisfree. Once again the products are quite unique eg Jeju volcanic clay pore mask. I think if you are visiting Seoul or any other big city as part of your trip it would be better buying the tea and facial products there but if you are in Jeju also then it is worth popping in to see where it all happens as part of your trip.The teas cake and ice creams at the cafe are really very good but be prepared to pay a lot for it. Just tell yourself you don't do this everyday...

To be honest the place is very pretty and there is a tangerine picking farm inside (Jeju tangeries are famous in Korea) but I found the place pricey  and I have seen some animals there but I am not sure in which condition they live under. Then after I left I learned that they do pigs shows there and I don't feel really good about that.
To arrive in jeju misterious road you can go by bus or private car. If you use private car you can try how misterious that road. If you go by bus you need to walk to arrive in jeju misterious road.

This would be my favourite place in Jeju. Evey single view is so beautiful. Too bad we went with a tour and did not have much time to explore around. We did climb up to the top though. We can easily spend half a day there. Suggest to give much time and go on your own instead of tour so you will have more time to enjoy it's nature

This would be my fav market so far at Jeju. You can buy lots of local products and local delicacies to eat as well. The market was so packed with locals and tourists so you kinda need to walk slowly and try not to block the road. LOLThere are lots of exit / entrance here but rest assured that it is interconnected and you won't get lost. Most shops are selling the same products but if you really wish to buy then you need to scout for the best price!

This was the only waterfall we visited on Jeju island. It was worth the visit although somehow not terribly exciting for me. I think it would be  nicer in  the summer time when you can put your feet in the water. There is a small entrance fee.
This was the most interesting / beautiful thing we saw on Jeju - the rest of the island was pretty bland to be honest.

This was seriously one of the coolest things I've ever seen. The waves crashing against the rocks was incredible. I went on a rainy day and that didn't take away from how amazing it was. Since it was rainy it wasn't that crowded. I stayed longer than many people though. I just couldn't believe it. Stay longer if you want. Definitely try to see this in Jeju.

This was part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - that gives you an opportunity to see an old fashioned village showing homes built of thatch roofs and lava rock.  There is a couple that still lives there and explains their way of life and the way things were on Jeju.  We also got to try a tea that apparently tastes differently to people depending on what they have going on in their bodies.  I really enjoyed listening to them and learning about their culture.

This was our last stop in Jeju. We arrived right after sunset and were able to walk around the island and enjoy the beautiful nature area and then walk back over the bridge while it was lit up. Good activity for young children to just get out and run. Best of all it was free! There is also a free public restroom in the parking lot.

This was our first stop for our south jeju trip and it was beautiful . One can just admire the natural beauty on how these columns and ckiffs would have formed due to molten lava . Must see destination in jeju

This was one of the most interesting things I visited in the cheesy Jeju Island. It's a piece of architecture. Everything is about meditation. The buildings are angled to frame Seongsan Ilchulbong volcano and they give you different perspectives of it. I found it very cool.The entrance fee was $5 but it is worth it. You have to walk from the parking lot to this area  it's about 10 to 15 minutes. The views are nice.
This was one of the highlights of our trip to Jeju. We took an afternoon trip to visit and the falls themselves are beautiful as is the view over the sea.

This was one of our favourite places from the list of to do activities in Jeju. It was really exciting to see such wonders of nature . These rock formations are few million year old and have column like shape. View of the blue water from the board walk is breathtaking. A must visit spot when you are in Jeju.

This was one of my favourite parts of Jeju! Truly so beautiful!A stunning view and so much history learning about the Haenyeo (or 'Jeju mermaids') who were diving whilst we were there. We also took a ride on the jet boat which leaves from nearby. So much fun!

This was an amazing experience. The walk through the lava caves is a very enlightening experience and we had a very good time. Slightly difficult terrain to walk on but nothing too dangerous. On the whole would definitely recommend this attraction when at Jeju.

This was a tourist trap.No museum to me- just a bit of information about tea on the wall with a tea grousing machine- that?셲 it!Who calls this a museum?The rest of place was for cafe souvenir shop - some observatory deck where you could see the tea field.Honestly Amore Pacific did a great job to let people recognize that Jeju could produce tea that?셲 perfectly linked with their business. Very smart from business perspective- bravo in that sense.

This was a quite pleasant area to avoid people.  Some parts look like the backdrop of a Tim Burton movie in the winter with the leaf-less trees but it was one of the most peaceful spots in Jeju in cold weather
This tourist attraction has good view for photo. You can see the Jeju city landscape from here and the dragon head rock itself only the minor thing to see.
This temple is a jewel of jeju island. Very nicely preserved with very good painting at the roof and also the wall on the second and third floor of the main temple.
This teddy bear museum was our first stop upon arrival in Jeju Island. Its more suited for kids and I was utterly bored.
This tea museum is one of the coolest places to visit in west Jeju Island. Take your time to wefie with the giant milk tea or at the beautiful tea fields outside.
This street is near the night market in Jeju-si. A small street fill with restaurants selling black pork Korean BBQ. A great place for dinner.

This so-called museum is really a sales outlet for O'Sulloc teas.  The grounds above the tea plantation is just beautiful to walk around.  The Innis Free Jeju House on the grounds is another sales outlet for Innis Free skin care products.  They offered a hands -on activity to make your own soap.  Lunch here was great.  They pride themselves in locally sources produce. I had the rice balls and soup.  We shared the mungwork steamed buns with red beans - not much to look at but very tasty. The shaved ices are a treat not to be missed

This site is one of the most popular places in Jeju so be prepared for the crowds of Chinese tours.  The hiking course is all paved and has a lot of steps.  The site says it takes around 55 minutes round trip.  Of course this is just an approximation.  I found the course to be pretty easy and it only took me 15 minutes to reach the top of the crater.  At the top there is a large deck like area to sit and take a rest.  The walk down has some beautiful spots for pictures overlooking the island.  At the base there are a lot of different restaurants but they all offer the same food.  Not a lot of options

This sight is at the extreme south east of Jeju. There are many great views and cafes within this area. This is a short hike up a beautiful hill and after the hike there is a haenyo performance where old ladies dive without oxygen tanks to collect abalones. I regretted not spending a full day in this area to chill.
This Seongsan Ilchulbong is on the east side in Jeju. It should be the best to visit it when the sun rises. We came here in the afternoon and it was crowded with tourists.

This rock formation was spotted on the eastern side of Jeju island. I was lucky enough to see this attraction having not spotted one a long time ago.The water present in these area is crystal clear where you can see different fishes swimming in the ocean breeze.
This road is a must place to visit. It is weird and so cool. You can experience something that you never see before. I recommend you to come to here if you visit jeju.

This review is subjective because this place is number one on my list at Jeju Island. Well i love Teddy bear and i love all of them here. It's so cute with every story in there. I also bought their hanbok teddy bear doll and that was expensive but well it's worth it for me as teddy bear's fan

This really just felt like wasted time on the tour. These optical illusions can be found almost anywhere and is not a part of what I would consider makes Jeju-do a unique place to visit.Do yourself a favor and skip it.

This place was surprisingly fun! It was cooling inside and we enjoyed the view inside. Really cool place. Only went there cos' Running Man did and it turned out to be one of the more interesting places we visited in Korea. Definitely go to this place if you are in Jeju!

This place was my must visit the first time I came to Jeju and I gladly returned back. You can participate in the tea class which is just another great activity to enjoy at this place. I love that there is both the tea museum and also the Innisfree house both having something different to offer. The only downside is the insane amount of visitors at all time so be ready to wait in line if you want something!

This place offers specialty items/ food of jeju. Vendors are cash only and they offer samples. There are snack stalls and a couple of restaurants inside. One restaurant even have an English translation on it.

This place looks kind of deserted and some of the area are dirty and poorly maintained. There are also not enough signage or information around this area. One can skip it since there are many other places of interest to visit around Jeju.

This place is worth visiting given it's nice environment and a lots of things to do. Food:  I highly recommend the green tea icecream and cake at the O'Sulloc tea museum which appears to be the focus of most visitors.  But I also want to take some time to remind you that there's another little gem inside the organic cafe of Innisfree that's also within the complex--DON'T MISS OUT THE TANGERINE SHAVED ICE! It comes in a big original size that can be sufficiently shared among 3 persons or there's a mini version if you only want a taste of it.  It's not cheap but worth trying because they use Jeju Tangerine which tasted somewhat more intense and flavourful.  Drinks:  They have free tea-demo which you can try their teas.  They also sell a selection of other drinks like tea latte.  Most of them tasted and smelled spectacular.  The teabags are also wrapped individually so they make good souvenirs as well. Soap making:  If you go early do try making your own soap at the Innisfree house it's a fun experience and make good souvenirs.View and/or pictures:  The environment around and within the museum is a great place for pictures with the open tea-farm and the delicate glass buildings or the colourful interior of the Innisfree house.  There's also a viewing deck in the O'sulloc Tea Museum which you can access by taking a lift.  The view up there is pretty amazing.  Tip:  1. Go on a sunny day if you want to take great pictures in the tea-farm2. Go early if you are worried that they sell out the cakes.  The tangerine shaved ice wasn't available after 5.30pm so we went to visit again on the next day.
This place is very refreshing and calming. Great place to enjoy afternoon tea. Try their signature orange drinks. Because Jeju is very known for that.
This place is very popular in Jeju for climbing mountain and see natural beauty from the top. Highly recommended.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.

review: This place is one of the place that I wanted to visit in Jeju. I am glad that i did. I love the walk alongside  the field of tall flamegrass which bloom from Sep-Oct. The walk to the crater was nice and it was quite romantic. Though on the day of our visit it was raining  but nevertheless we enjoy and appreciate the beauty of this place. You can view the crater below and also the surrounding mountains. Will visit again when I come to Jeju next time.

This place is breathtakingly beautiful with especially kind staff. Every piece of art is a masterpiece. Nice (but expensive) giftshop and cute coffeeplace. Don't miss it if you are close by. I visited this place on the last day of a worktrip and it left a wonderful feeling about Jeju.

This place is a hit with the tourist. Famous for Jeju local tea. If you are driving parking is free of charge and there is someone manning the traffic when it gets busy. There is a small museum showcasing the tea history but don't expect to learn much. Then you will walk into the tea shop which is quite huge followed by the cafe. We tried the green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll and jeju orange drink. Mind you the queue is very long but fast moving. I like their green tea ice cream and the swiss roll. There are few corners inside and outside of this place which is IG worthy. Nice place for the environment but it's not really museum per say. They have a branch in Seoul in case you are wondering.
This place has several themed hiking trails. You can choose one of them according to your allotted time. You can walk comfortably under the shady trees. I recommend this place is a must-see in Jeju.

This place has great views  beautiful falls  and a cool folk tale about the nymphs or fairies that visit the falls. Not a particularly difficult walk  but if you have trouble with stairs  pace yourself. Only gave it 4 of 5  because the biggest and best falls are not always running. Best views require a visit after the rains. Definitely still a must do while in Jeju. Only need about 1-1.5 hours here.
This peak offers a good view of the oreums and the sea but it did get very very crowded when we arrived there at about 9am. First time to Jeju? Must visit.

This pavilion is next to Jeju Mokgwana. It is just a pavilion with its typical architecture. There wasn't anyone around. Took some photos and move on. Not worth to specially come here unless you are nearby.

This park situated about 30 minutes drive from Jeju-si. Me and my husband spend about 1 hour at the park but we failed to ring the bell. We arrived late in the evening so we couldn't spend more time there since it was getting dark.

This O'Sulloc Tea Museum locate at jeju and here we can find many things made from Green Tea.  For example we can find tea cake ice cream lotion soap and many others thing make from Green Tea.  Very Nice Place to visit or a good place to enjoy the good atmosphere.

This musuem provides quite an extensive overview of Jeju's history in relation to the 4.3 incident that occured after WWII. Gives you a lot of emotion and there is also a great outside area commeorating the ones that have been lost. Recommended to go and visit this place if you are interested in culture and history!
this must be in the itinerary if you visit Jeju!experience the beauty of mother nature seeing and learning. this lava tube is amazing!

This museum is well worth the trip and it's FREE to the public. Very informative and emotional. This museum will not disappoint. I was so impressed with the honest representation of Jeju history. This museum incorporates works of local artists to help tell the stories and are very well done and effective. The staff was very kind and helpful. You also get a great book for free when you visit. My visit here was very moving and I would recommend it to everyone. Very impressive!

This museum is one of the most popular of the 50+ on Jeju Island and the carpark was packed with tour buses when we arrived. But if you can manage to get a slot on one of the formal tea ceremonies it really takes you out of the bustling tourist crowds and takes you to another place altogether. The time and care taken for all the preparations was amazing and could not have been more different to having a casual cuppa at home! I am not sure they do them in English - our host spoke in Korean but our little group had an interpreter to help us out. The venue used for this ceremony is also amazing. Beautiful minimal stone and wood shaped furniture in a sunlight-filled pavilion looking out onto the lawns of the museum. We also had a glimpse into the underground tea cellar area and a quick tour round the tourist shop. The collection of tea cups from different countries and eras was fascinating too in the area next to the shop.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.

review: This museum is located a short distance from the city center. However a taxi ride from our centrally located hotel only cost about 6000 Korean won. On the day that we went to the museum we were able to get free admittance because they had some special promotion though I think that the admission fee is very inexpensive anyway. We enjoyed the museum very much especially the special exhibit entitled ?쏞hoe Bu`s Diary: An Unexpected Encounter with China.??This exhibition will run from July 21 to October 4 2015. There is also a fascinating diorama of a Jeju village.If you like history and historical artifacts you will enjoy this museum. It?셲 well worth a visit.

This museum is EXTREMELY well put together.  It is not often in Korea where you will find proper English translations.  This place does not disappoint. There is a wealth of knowledge to be found here for those interested in the sad history Jeju people have had to endure.  ProTip:  Make sure you take time to explore the outside part (the lands and the memorial wall). ProTip:  You do not want to rush thru this.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to really walk around and read about the history.  The museum covers almost 6 years worth of events and details!

This museum is absolutely fun. From the moment I stepped in it was simply hilarious. I have always loved historical museums but I love these interactive ones even more. I was supposed to go to the Trick museum but the concierge at my hotel recommended ALIVE museum. It was a walking distance from my hotel in Jungmun so I walked over. At the beginning of the street where this museum is I saw a big sign but no museum. I had to walk a little bit before I saw the museum. I think they have to do better with the signs on the major street so visitors will be more informed on how to get there. It also looks like some wings are in still in construction. The road leading to the building looks like it needs finishing too.That being said once you get into the museum there are lots of interesting exhibitions and pictures. Most of them were famous painting s that we could interact with while taking pictures. It was fun watching other people interact with the pictures and sculptures as they took pictures. My favorites were the ALIVE Aquarium the coiled python that was squeezing the life out of me being a mermaid being dinner and fighting the leopard for my red suitcase. They are some sculptures in the museums grounds that are very interesting and interactive too. For just about $9 USD I had a very memorable day in Jeju. This is one of my favorite attractions in Jeju Island. I highly recommend visiting the ALIVE museum while on Jeju Island.
This museum have a lot of teddy bear. You must visit this museum if u go to jeju. For me teddy bear museum is fun to visit with family like your son or your daughter.

This may not be a well known place of interest in Jeju but it was one of the highlights of our trip. Children will love the babbling brook and hopping from stone to stone. This market offer variety products from raw to ready to eat. Many stalls and shop offer local menu here. Jeju orange can be easily found here. Open till night.

This market is small compared to many others in bigger Korean cities.Anyway  Seogwipo is just a small part of Jeju Island. The temple is extremely new as it was built only in 1990s. The outlook was grand and the temple architectural style was reminiscent of the early Korean Joseon Dynasty.  Buddhism in Jeju is unique with its own characteristics and distinctive feature. Unlike the main stream counterpart in mainland Korea Jeju's Buddhism accepts combines and adapt to the local characteristics to form an integrated form of its own. The native folks were staunch followers of Shamanistic beliefs pray to stone deities and attend to superstitious rituals but Buddhism in Jeju embodied the local belief in her Buddhist temples. Behind the Shamanistic gods idols stood the compassionate and tolerant statue of Buddha. Jeju is famous for her natural environment and Jeju's Buddhism takes a natural path towards enlightenment. In fact the repressive Joeson Dynasty suppressed Buddhism but this Buddhist temple incorporated the beauty of the Joseon temple architectural style with Buddhism worship. The compassionate hands of the Buddha practiced acceptance and non-hatred non violence in pursuit of the emancipation of the human soul. I observed that the Buddha statues in the prayer hall were magnificently golden and the grand prayer hall with a height of 28 m was reputed to be the largest in Asia. The ambience here was tranquil and serene. It was a place most suitable for meditation and prayer. I walked around the temple and felt the calmness and peacefulness in the air. From a distance I could hear the dim chanting of the Buddhist prayer. Historically this lovely island of Jeju had suffered tremendously under the repressive hands of the Mongol Empire and also during the Japanese tyrannical rule. But the island survived with the most scenic and gorgeous natural wonders of the world and may this temple bring continual peace to this natural place!.

The place is good for picture taking but can be a good climb for people who are not very active. Great view from atop while you can experience Jeju women divers if you go to the shore. Many restaurants in the area as well for those who want to taste fresh seafood like abalones shrimp crabs squid shells etc.

The place is a bit run down and really short of foot traffic. We were accosted when we stepped into the museum shops. The entrance fee is relatively steep for Jeju - 12k for each adult.The exhibits are tasteful in my opinion but the rust is showing. For the entrance fee I expect to receive at least a small souvenir.
The place for food lovers. You can buy everything you dream of to bring back home from jeju in nice local prices.

The park was quiet when I visited. It was an easy walk with nice trees and scenery. It had a great calming effect on me. Love it. Just 5 minutes drive from the park is the Hanwha Resort Jeju which I went for a fantastic spa treatment. My afternoon was made perfect !

The park is definitely worth a visit for people who appreciate the beauty of nature. there's so much too see that one should reserve at least half a day for that park. The caves are also very impessive. there are restrooms and benches all over the park and everything's very clean. the collection of bonsai are impressive as well as the village of traditional jeju-houses.

The owner of the museum is an artist himself and one of the most important collectors in the world. I was totally taken away with many of the artworks and with the location itself(specially the Bike-Shop and the Cinema). One of my reasons for traveling South-Korea is discovering and enjoying modern art. This is the best collection I have seen in this country so far (out of around 30 museums and galleries). I was totally surprised to see this level of Art in Jeju and will definitely visit Arario in Space when I am back to Seoul.

The Osulloc Tea Museum is located around 30 mins from Seogwipo and 35 mins from Jeju city.This pleasant venue is comprised of the Tea Museum a shop a coffee place a cosmetics shop and the tea fields.We didn't visit the museum as we are familiar with the processes. Instead we visited the coffee shop where we had a Sejak green tea an ice cream and a slice of roll cake. Everything was good!We also bought some tea cosmetics and hung around the tea plantation.

The Osulloc Tea Museum is just not a tea museum but I would rather say a tea complex which includes a Tea Cup Gallery various Tea Culture Rooms such as exhibition hall masters of tea vessels tea life center etc. tea caf챕 and tea gardens. Tea Museum also offers a premium tea class in which brewing our own green tea and sharing with friends during the premium tea class is one of the unique experiences so far in Jeju. In the class they not only explain tea and tea brewing methods but also demonstrate the use of various tea wares and their importance in making one good cup of tea. In the end it was a good memorable day to make and drink green tea. Besides museums souvenir shops and green tea caf챕 there are few tea gardens and resting areas where people can enjoy nature relax and take pictures to keep their memory forever.
The only waterfall in Jeju that e water flows into the ocean. U can go very close to it & feel e cool Breeze. Was so amazed to c rainbow too! Worth stopping by.
The only special thing about the waterfall is that it connects to the sea. But it worths a visit in Jeju if you have time.

The only difference with other waterfalls is the water goes directly into the sea. A Hanyeo was selling her fresh catch near the Falls. A bit pricey in my opinion. Having said that it is still a must visit if it is your 1st trip to Jeju.

The only (or so I'm told) waterfall that falls into the sea in Jeju Island.  Easy walk down stairs to the bottom of the falls.  Able to walk around on the rocks and view the falls.  Really gorgeous and totally worth the visit.
The one place you have to see if you're in Jeju. No regrets going up in the midst of heavy rain. The caldera was still impressive. And the view from the top over the town is nice.

The number one attraction on Jeju and an impressive climb to the top. Lots of signs to explain the geological formations at key points en route. The attractions divides the ascenders from the descenders which helps with the climb. Wonderful view from the top. The attraction is beautifully looked after no litter and only about 짙1 to visit. If you are lucky you will also be able to see the women who dive for fish which has become infamous with the Jamie Olivier programme in the UK.Worth a visit.

The musuem is located next to the tea farm great view from the rooftopinside the musuem you can buy a range of different tea made in JEJU and evevn drink somethere is a restaurant inside where youi can eat an tea icecream or a tea cake anything which is made with tea!good for family and couple

The museum is located opposite of Jeju Korea Tourism Organisation and can be reached from Seogwipo or Airport on bus number 600. The entrance fees is 2000 won and there are 3 levels of teddy bears exhibition and the ground floor is where all sorts of teddy bears are being sold. There is a cafe within the museum and a theater showing Elvis Presley lookalike teddy bear singing Elvis's songs. It is about a 15 minutes session.
The museum is excellent. you get to understand how Jeju island is formed and the geothermal activities.The ground itself is hugh. It takes about 1-2 hours stroll.It is cold and windy in Dec.

The museum becomes busier as the day goes on really busy late in the day so going early is the best plan to be stress free and see everything with little to no people there for best photo experiences.The museum is really cool and covers Korean tea history. It leads to the tea shop where you can sample some good tea cakes and teas. You can also purchase teas here as well as other tea confections.Next to the museum short 5 minute walk is the Innisfree Jeju House which I cover in another review. You can get lunch and some fresh teas to enjoy here. There is also great tea and Jeju House related products as well as fun tea soap making kits. Ones you can do there and others that you can take home.Before lunch at Innishouse but after tea and snack at the Tea Museum you should walk the plantation. Great photos in the fields next to the tea museum but across the street are two areas one with a big tree that is old an beautiful but also a tree with deep red blossom that makes for a great photo with Hallasan in the background.The Stone House was closed for renovations when we visited in April 2018.
The mountain has a nice area of temples at the base and a UNESCO cliff along the beach so make sure you do both in one hit as the busses are infrequent from Jeju-Si. Great full day out!

The most memorable thing was rather on the ferry to Udo Island.The seagulls were hovering over those who had Calbee prawn crackers ready to feed them. They followed the ferry from Jeju all the way to Udo. That was a sight!Udo generally has good scenic views and interesting coral beach with clear blue waters.
The most impressive thing to do in Jeju. I have been in many caves before but never one that has been molded by lava. It's pretty chilly once you descend so make sure you have an extra layer or two.
The market sells mainly Jeju produce such as the famous Jeju oranges. Colourful market. Come during weekends where there is a small section selling inexpensive local food.

The last time I went to a similar place with during my childhood days. Visiting aqua planet in jeju again is a good experience. The whole place isn't all that big but there is plenty of sea marine life to see and a Enormous fish take. This place can give u a kind of relaxing atmosphere. At the end there is a performance where u can rest your weary legs. Good place to be If you have a busy trip before you came to jeju. A little break for a change. Overall I enjoy the trip here and will revisit again with my love ones if ever given the chance.

review: The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

The Jeju village is 5 minutes from Hyeopjae beach with plenty of restaurants and cafe nearby. It's a perfect place to start off your day or end it. It's a beautiful good size historical park with plenty of things to learn do and it's kids friendly with lot of interactive events to include a mini zoo. I would definitely put it on the itenary and start enjoying or end the day.

The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

The Jeju Aqua Planet really had a lot of marine creatures to showcase! There were turtles crabs varieties of fish etcWhat really solved me were the cute penguins the sea lion the sharks and the cute little spaces for photos!It's a good place if you just want to relax with your family your friends or a date :DAside from it being supposedly quiet it is very soothing to just be around such adorable sea life

review: The hidden gem in the east of the Jeju island. The best part is to come during sunrise I guess. DOn't miss its traditional ice cream.

The hexagonal basalt columns are similar to what you see at the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but you can't actually walk on them unless you try accessing them from a park further down. There is a well laid observatory path which takes you through the best view points to view the structures. Very touristy when we were there so it was a bit of a mad house but worth visiting when in Jeju.
The green tea latte is nice ! Not too sweet for me ! Just nice !  Went over to Innisfree shop ! Taxi fare from Jeju SkyPark hotel till there  cost me around won 32000!
The green tea ice cream is good and I enjoyed the hallabong O tea ice that the top not cream but ice cream. Delicious. A good place to shop for authentic tea in Jeju .

The government run museums in Jeju finally opened on a trial basis limiting a number of hourly visitors to 50 with online reservations being required (although it didn?셳 really seem like a must when we arrived).  Considering it's a large complex (which itself looks impressive) Jeju Museum of Art didn't have a whole lot in display other than a temporary exhibition consisting of mostly projected images.  Thorough explanations of the pieces were provided on pamphlets and the display although few in numbers  used the wide spaces well.

The folk village was quite large with some interesting buildings but everything looked samey after a while. I was hoping to see a variety of performances on the stage but it was only a few songs sung by a group of women - charming enough but not what we were expecting. The foodie street also didn't have alot of stalls open though we did buy some cactus taffy which tasted like treacle and raisins and lasted us most of our trip in SK. One good thing was the interactive bits such as the old games children used to play. Having been in folk villages in other countries where there were people in traditional costumes showcasing different crafts and activity the Jeju one was a little disappointing.

The folk museum is a huge cultural town-like place located at the south-east portion of Jeju Island. It is easily accessible by car. For those who are self-driving like I did fear not there is an abundant number of parking lots to park your car and it's completely free.The admission fee for an adult cost around 10000 won. Considering the size of the museum it's a rather reasonable price. The museum is divided into many different sections showcasing different cultural aspects of Korea's rich history.If you get tired from walking or can bear the scorching sun the museum provides a tram service that brings you around the museum stopping at different attractions. There are also many different restaurants and snack booths selling traditional Korean meals as well as snacks. If you have never been to Jeju before do take the opportunity to visit this place at least once! Ideal for all ages.

The folk houses built well imitating earlier century jeju do livings. You can experience the way of living of older jeju do resident. Kinda way of knowing and understanding of Jeju resident. The living plant and animal were well maintain.

The five-day markets in Jeju Island are fascinating places where locals converge for their everyday needs. Everything from hundreds of different Kimchi to farm tools to live rabbits - a visitor will find anything you need. These markets are located in various places around the island with the largest one located in Jeju city! Mostly under cover - it was a wonderful way to explore despite a rainstorm!What struck us the most was the incredible friendliness of the Korean merchants - knowing that we were not Korean - they were patient and was very open for us to try some of their foods! One vendor offered me some Kimchi and when she saw my reaction to the spicy-ness - she handed me a piece of pickled lotus root to help cool my mouth followed by a big smile!
The feeling of high place is great! Just proceed and experience the coldness (not recommend during winter). & understand a bit more about jeju history. :)
The famous orange chocolate from jeju.....You can buy in cheaper price in thereSo many kind of chocolate that you can choose to bring back to ypur country....

The famous Black Pork Street in Jeju Island is within walking distance from the Dongmun Market and the street is lined with lots of restaurant serving BBQ black pork. We tried one of the famous restaurant recommended by a Taiwanese blog and found it to be cheap and good. It's the last restaurant along the street if you're walking from Dongmun Market. Well worth a visit.

The entire place is quite nicely run by Amore Pacific who owns large green tea fields and cosmetic brands such as Innisfree. The tea museum is a small setup which links directly to the retail section. Don't expect much from the museum but the retail section is a heaven for tea fans! Adjacent to the tea museum is the local specialty shop of Innisfree. Checkout the Jeju specials such as green tea essential oil. Surrounding these 2 building are endless stretches of green tea farms.

The drive from jeju airport area to aqua planet is around 1 hour 10 minutes passing by many small towns. The entry tickets were quite costly and I used klook to get some discounts with the tickets. Upon parking the rented car outside the vicinity of aqua planet then picked up a number from the machine next to the ticket counter. Waited for the number and redeemed my wristbands without much hassle. Kids under 3 can enter for free.There are plenty to see and we were in time to watch fish feeding a seal and dolphin show. Outside the facilities has really good view and many people were taking photos.Food in the food court was not too bad and similar like incheon airport have to be ordered and paid at the cashier counter and picked up from the individual sections when the device buzzes.Overall experience was great and worth every cent spent.

review: The crater itself wasn't much to see but it was a pleasant little walk and there are very good views of Mt Halla - the best we had during our stay on Jeju.
The crater is absolutely fantastic. Great view and best among Jeju sights. Very good track for walking around.

The cliffs are beautiful and wondrous. Be sure to go very early as there will be less visitors then. Once the tourist buses come and go it will be difficult to move around. You can get there by walking from Jeju International Convention Centre and going out the back door into the park and walk towards the left side of the park for about 10 minutes.

The clear turquoise water against black sand beach is really pretty. There were no kayaks available when i was there in autumn but it was also too cold for water activities. Otherwise would have love to go for a swim. It is a nice place to just hang out with friends or pack a picnic lunch. The view is just spectacular.Highly recommended place to visit while in Jeju.

The chocolate museum was a highlight of our Jeju trip in 2020  the fresh chocolate made by the resident chocolatier is a real treat. Be aware that not only the quality  but also the price of the chocolate is on an international level  with a decent-sized box going for some 30 dollars. But for buying three boxes  we got three tickets for a chocolate making workshop  which was greatly enjoyed by the kids.We will come again  if only to get some memorable treats. The museum itself is informative  but don't expect too much.

review: The Cheonjiyeon Falls is an amazing  spot in Jeju island. It is surrounded by  rare species of subtropical flora. The walk to the fall about a km is very pleasant  and scenic.
The caves are indeed worth the visit. It?s a UNESCO world heritage site with carefully preserved Lava tubes and caves. The whole Jeju island was designated as a GeoPark in 2010.

The cave is worth a visit if in Jeju island. Although cave is 7.4km long only about 1km can be visited. Nice to visit on a cold day to feel that despite almost 100% humidity it's warmer than outside. Good enough explanations about lava formations and cave features. Lighting is sufficient to not require a flashlight.

The cave is really cold and I love it. It's really good. And daddy put me on his shoulders. I was kind of scared. If you bring your kids to Jeju it will be lots of fun. It kind of looks like a mystery to me. The lava shapes are good and look like they are made by people. But they are really made by nature. I can't believe my eyes. The end. Done.

The cause of forming a wonderful Island is a Volcano and hiking to the top of it is a wonderful experience. Roads up to the height of 1100 mtrs are made cautiously and traveler friendly for pleasure with least possibility of an accident. The hiking experience is also beyond the expression in words. I can only say that visiting JEJU and Hallim park are synonyms.

The car drives  up the road by itself! Great fun. ( visual effect)It only works one way. You need to drive in neutral towards the shops. If you arrived from Jejusi do a U turn after the shops to experience the effect. The effect is quite spectacular with a water bottle placed in the middle of the road. You will see clearly the bottle rolling up.

The brochure states that is a glass castle. This is definitely not a glass castle but a fun museum  so if you have kids and they are expecting to see a Cinderella kind of environment  well  this is not .What you find though it's the explanation on how glass in made and transformed in different shapes (entrance) to different kind of finished product. If you want  you can also have a go (helped by professionals)!It's a good  small scale museum and it's quite entertaining and educational. A mention of honor goes to the ticket guy at the entrance. On our way out we asked him to help us out to get a taxi. He was the sweetest and hard-core-customer orientated guy I saw in action in Jeju (and  I must admit they are all very good). He tried to get a taxi for us  getting the price  helping us (mind you  his English was limited  so he struggled a lot but nonetheless worked hard to explain us everything he could) and even giving us for free a cold bottle of water whilst waiting outside (for the taxi). You could see he was really trying his best and I hope someone from the Museum will read this feed-back and rewarding him.One thing I would avoid is the Coffee Shop inside the museum. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.

The brochure says that it?셲 beautiful all year round but some reviews have stated otherwise. I am delighted and overwhelmed by the beauty of this place when I visited in early December. The flowers were in full bloom. The route is easy to navigate and paths well-maintained. It?셲 the highlight of my Jeju trip.

The best of all was our retreat leader June Goh. She truly took care of us from her heart and was the kindest sweetest of souls we have ever come across. Thank you so much for making Jeju Island a memorable and wonderful experience!

The beach was rated as one of the top 10 sites to see in Jeju so we had it in our itinerary. But the beach was quite average ..Similar to what we have in Goa may be. The place was very crowded especially with a school kids and they were all outside ..None on the beach However there was a nice monkey sea lion and dolphin show at the beach . That was a must see .

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

The aquarium is good and English-friendly (so you know what you're looking at). The show at the end is aimed at kids and solely in Korean but as it's mostly visual that's not a problem. Families can definitely spend a fun few hours here. However the admission fee is excessive (40900 won for adults at time of writing) especially when most of the other main attractions in Jeju are either free entry or priced around 2000 won. I think this one ticket cost me more than all other entrance fees during my 5 day visit to the island combined. If you aren't visiting with children I suggest giving it a miss.
