Take picture with the unique statues. Listen to the local guide to understand how their ancestor's life. Do you know the 3 things Jeju women fight to keep for life: 1) Water 2) I forget you can ask if you visit but the last thing I remember: 3) MAN. :))

Such a nice place.  I wish I was visiting Jeju island during the summer time to see all the different flower.  It was pretty in the fall so I can imagine how pretty it will be in the summer.  It's a must for Jeju.

Such a beautiful place with stunning viewIt is a must visit when you come to jeju islandDon't forget to gear up with comfy shoes because you will need to hike if you want to get the best view of this placeMake sure you buy a bottled of tangerine juice because it tastes delicious

Strictly for adults this open air museum has many stone sculptures of male and female in various positions. There is also an indoor museum with miniature clay figurines a souvenir shop and a food stall within the compound. Admission fee 12.000 won. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Nexon Computer Museum.Transport tip: From the airport take bus 331 332 465 466 at airport bus stand 6 between gates 4 & 5. Alight at Jeju Museum of Art walk 400m. Bus fare is 1150 won journey about 30 mins.

Stopped here on the way to Segwipo from Jeju City. Had an incredible lunch at Innisfree House walked the gardens and then had dessert and tea at the tea museum. Highly suggest this site to anyone who enjoys serene landscapes and healthy/energizing food!

Started our trek at around 5:50am for the 6:50am sunrise and we reached the peak at around 6:20am. So many steps... for a person who hasn't been jogging often this climb was tiring! There are wet wooden bleachers at the peak for folks to sit on and await the sun to rise. Many locals head up and will exclaim when the rising red sun appears.The descend starts getting tiring again near later half of route... very peaceful and wonderful view of Jeju at the top.

Staff were so kind and taught me in detail so that I could surf well. I took lessons three times here during the trip in Jeju and couldn't calm down as my current surfing skills leveled up. It was a totally exiting memory.

Spent a few hours at the museum along with many many others! Small building with some good information but crowds crammed the shop which leads into the cafe. This caused overcrowding and did not make for the most enjoyable afternoon. Outdoors area is worth wandering through and the gardens and fields are worth looking at. The Innisfree Jeju House across the way is probably more interesting.

spent 2-3 hours to walk through despite it was a hot sunny day.  The park is well designed and large and showcases a number of house and building of old Jeju.  However I would like to have more and completed information (in English).  For me a foreign visitor I have no interest in those scene for TV film making.  Again the park grows different plants which impress me.

Spectacular geological formations and scenery.  It really is quite unique. It's easily accessible and there's a nice small park around the top.  There's a path that can take you to the portion of the shore which is nice and not many people go to.  Jeju let's nature take center stage and they do a nice job getting you access.

Specility of S. Korean is to make a simple thing also most presentable and impressive with best possible aesthetic and respectful manner.Dinosaur land on Jeju Island is one of the attracting places for a family. More details of Dinosaur are displayed with 3D models of different types of Dinosaurs. All around nature was also so well prepared that things look more natural....In short I repeat my recommendation as given in one another review.....make your visit to Jeju at least once and have your own genuine experience which you might not get so well at other places.

Soooo pretty! Absolutely stunning glass sculptures and the trail through the forest was an absolute highlight of my stay in Jeju. The glass tangelo trees must have taken FOREVER to complete and they were so well done. Loved the little farmhouse in the forest and the huge glass spider webs. So peaceful looking out at all the colours across the lake. Definitely recommend this place for something a little bit different.

Songaksan Mountain is another highly impressive place that I have visited in Jeju. It is a volcanic mountain with several craters. It is said that there are 99 small volcanic peaks besides two major craters in which the largest one is 500 m wide and 80 m deep and still covered with black volcanic soil. The walking route follows the perimeter of a volcanic mountain which allows the hikers to observe amazingly gorgeous vertical cliffs around the mountain. The walking trails at the top of these cliffs along the perimeter of the crater is just spectacular. Since the mountain lies at the edge of the southwesternmost corner of the mainland the visitors can see a wide view of the open sea at both northwest and northeast sides. The view of the Gapado and Marado islands on the northwest side and Hyeongjeseom Island and Sanbangsan Mountain on the northeast side are amazing from the observation platform.
Something not to miss on your Jeju trip but be prepared when you go as the hike will be quite a challenge.

Soesokkak is a great place to visit if you are in Jeju-do. From Seogwipo area take bus 110 and get off at Hyodon Middle School. It takes another 20 minutes of walking passing by orange farms. No entrance fees is required but if you want to try the transparent kayak or the traditional hand-pulled raft you will need to buy tickets at the counter situated on your right side before you reach the estuary. The clear green blue water is mesmerizing and definitely a great place to visit. Stop-by for a bottle of fresh orange juice to quench your thirst or a cone of ice-cream to complete the trip.

So this was my fourth time visiting Jeju and so far this is the best experience i had. Mr. Kang was not only kind but also reliable. He took us to places we have planned and gave other ideas where we should go. My friends and I had a lot of fun during the trip. Both car and van were clean and comfortable; most importantly had wifi. Oh and he speaks English too. Definitely will contact him when I visit Jeju again :)
So much history saved at Jeju Museum of War History & Peace. As they say sometime war is necessary for the peace to follow!

Small museum which showcases lots of green tea cups from around the world. As it was raining at the time of visit I spent more time indoors and at the cafe. As this is a tourist hotspot the cafe is always full and finding a table is quite a challenge (I was lucky though). I recommend ordering the green tea ice cream and the cold drip tea which is only sold at the Jeju outlet.Will probably visit again next time to see the green tea plantations which I missed out on.This museum is a stone's throw away from Innisfree Jeju House - barely 90 seconds walk which is worth a visit as well.

Small area but you can see clear waters around the rocks formed from the volcano. Do visit if you have time. I imagine it would be amazing to catch the sunset here but am unable to do so because of time constraints.Easily accessible by bus no. 462 from Jeju Bus Terminal.
small & clean water but sand just so so. since cloudy so that the color not too significant but still well enough. one of jeju beach but i don't see quite much special on it.

since it was raining heavily with winds we decided to visit this top rated museum in jeju. its similar to trick-eye museum in seoul so if you have visited that then you might not find this so exciting. There are many trick potrait where you can stand and take some nice 3d pics. Even though we didnt take much pics we were happy to see many ppl posing around. some of them are quite funny too.

simply breathtaking awesomewhite sandscrystal clear wateri was fascinated by the green algae scatterred in the sea(some are floating)i think its formed because of the jeju origin...from a volcano eruption
should walk to the peak to see the amazing view of jeju island. sunny day is the best day to go so you can get clearer view.
Should drive up early to enjoy the sunrise and if possible stay for the sunset. Breath breaking View of the Jeju island.
Should be your must do list for photography activity. There is car park & toilet nearby. All Jeju coastal are unique scenery but this place has its own specialty. Good place to relax and chill.

Shinhwa Theme Park is unique in many ways.  First it tries to make its own characters seems as popular as Mickey Mouse and Spider Man - it doesn’t work but it’s great fun just trying to figure out who is who.  Second everything seems brand new - so it’s spotless and at the same standards as a Disneyland or Universal Studios.  Third - the rides are small but oh so knock out fun.  And there is rarely anyone there.  I don’t know if they sell a fast pass but there is no need for one because i don’t ever imagine it getting that crowded.  The food was quite delicious too - great offerings at multiple locations.  You can easily do this park in a half day and not feel like your exhausted or missing anything.  Like everything in Jeju I think they think they are expanding but who knows..  and as i remember the entry price is super affordable.  So this is really a great time for anyone with kids or who enjoys theme parks.  Don’t go in thinking it’s Disneyland though and get picky - just enjoy it for what it is...a bold effort to start something special and first class and doing very well right from the start.  It was a great day for me and my daughter and her two cousins.  Enjoy!

Seriously stunning display of flowers at Camellia Hill; the biggest arboretum in Asia famous for its forest path and beautiful gardens of camellias. The arboretum is home to 6000 camellia trees of 500 different species including species that are known to produce the world?셲 largest and earliest blossoms. The place is drop-dead gorgeous and I would of spent a whole day adoring the different flowers if I wasn't rushing to maximise my day in Jeju.We were lucky to catch the early blooms of the Cherry Blossoms which was a major highlight of the trip for us. Towards the end of the trail is a small shop that should desserts coffee and souvenirs like postcards and cosmetics. I loved their postcard selection and went a little crazy on those souvenirs but no regrets. My brother enjoyed his homemade strawberry ice cream as it was packed full of flavour!
Seongsan ilchulbong is a place must visit when travel to jeju. The scenery is superb and can enjoy the women diver show as well.

Seongsan Ilchulbong also called as Sunrise Peak! It's located on the Eastern end of Jeju do Island. There is a huge crater at the top of the peak!  The place is really wonderful with magnificent view. Strong wind. Cooling. The way up are well prepared and safety. Suitable for children  so no worried.

Sarabong Park is a 143-meter hill located just east of Dongmun Rotary in Jeju. The park is best known for its spectacular sunset views which is often regarded as a perfect complement to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak's view of the sunrise.

Sanbangsan Mountain is a wonderful bell-shaped huge body of lava situated nearby the ocean. At few places it stretches into the ocean where majestic rock structures can be seen. Almost vertical cliffs with columnar joints at this mountain are impressive. This mountain is visible from almost everywhere in the southwest plains of Jeju. Also the legend associated with this mountain is very interesting. According to the legend it was plucked out from the Hallasan Mountain peak by the angry Emperor when he got hit by a misfired arrow that was shot to white deer. Interestingly it is said that the circumferences of the Sanbangsan Mountain and the crater at Hallasan are of similar size. The Jeju Olle Trail Route 10 is connected to this mountain by stairs. A Buddha temple huge Buddha statue and the caves on this mountain are very beautiful.  This mountain along with nearby Yongmeori Coast are highly recommended especially to those who love coastal cliffs and interesting rock formations.

Samyang Beach was the only beach in Jeju that took down contact info for all visitors and even had visitors put on temperature sensitive stickers.  The swimming area is quite small and most visitors were there for surfing/windsurfing lessons which most of the beach area was allocated for.  We liked the shaded areas near the water and were able to hang out without having to pay for a parasol or a cabana.  It's not a particularly picturesque beach but it's one of the few in the city.

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

Rows of organic tea plantations for cha lovers to scent savour and calm the senses.  A must-go on tourist itinerary so be prepared for crowds.  Long queues at the cafe for tea desserts.  Check out exquisite Samdayeon (?쇰떎??is a Korean post-fermented tea matured for a hundred days in barrels made out of cedar wood from Jeju Island) soft ice cream unique to Jeju shop only. Interesting tea blends and gifts at the tea shop. Don't miss the outdoor fields across from the museum for kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures and windmills for photo taking. A walking path connects to Innisfree Jeju House for more afternoon tea Innisfree products and craft making classes for young and old.

Rented a driver for 9hrs for KR150K look for an english speaking driver that can act as a tour guide as well. Have to provide for driver's meal as well.There is an Inisfree shop onsite however there are many Inisfree in Myeongdong so if you are visiting Seoul can simply skip the shop and visit other tourist spots.The green tea ice-cream is nice but for KR5000 it is abit over-priced.Nice place to visit while visiting the West Coast side in Jeju.

Reminds me of kenyas hells gate. The place is a sight to behold. Be carefull to put on comfy shoes that have great treads and grips so that you dont slip on the sometimes slippery rocks. Also find out about tides. If its high tides then definately you will be soaked by action of water on your feet. Good place though. I recommend finnishing it with a horse ride by the ajoshi at the exit for man won and a cold jeju tangerine juice.
Recommended to visit when you go Jeju Island. The view is amazingly breathtaking. We booked for a private tour for 1 day and bring us to different tourist attractions and good foods as well.
Recently visited O'sulloc tea farm while in JeJu found it to be worth the trip interesting on-site store had many tea related products better than most of the other Jeju tours

Really nice view coz the waterfall is right next to the open sea. I could feel the splash on my face when I approached its bottom.Tips: be ready to climb the stairs after viewing the waterfall. It's not too long but you may get tired after a long day of touring in Jeju.Be careful if you want to go near the waterfall coz it's all big rocks at the bottom.

Really loved this. It was a relatively easy climb that only took an hour or so at a relaxed pace. It is uphill so it can take the wind out of you but there are plenty of rest stops. The view from the top is majestic. I totally get why Jeju is a natural wonder!
Really have a great experience with Hi Jeju Taxi Tour!
Really enjoyed exploring this cave. Easy and convenient car parking. Great facilities. A must-see on your trip to Jeju.

Really cool and Interesting lava tube under the ground of Jeju island. It shows a lot of cool facts about how it happen and also how the island is formed like it is today. The attraction is both on English and Korean. The test is easy to under stand on the sign and pictures there are. Remember to bring some good walking/waterproof shoes or boots because there are water every were and the terrain is uneven because of the lava it self.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

Read about it and found it really interesting and we decided to go take a look but pretty disappointed as we all tried but it was not working. One good thing was that it's not a wasted trip as it is very near to Jeju Love Land/ Park.

Pyoseon Beach might not be the most picturesque beach in Jeju but it's vast and didn't feel that crowded even in the middle of the high season. Because of the large sand area exposed during low tides  it can be quite the hike to the water then. But the low depth of the water and the large sand area makes it a good beach for children. As with most other popular Jeju beaches  there is a good selection of restaurants nearby.

Pyoseon Beach is just the opposite of Jeju Folk Village.So after visited the Village  we came here.The beach is pretty large with wide white sands.It is the perfect place for families to spend some time relaxing  particularly at low tide with its lake-like pools.It has abundant parking space  public toilet (with shower) and cam-ground around the square.Near the beach  there is white lighthouse near the shore.This lighthouse is where the last scene in Kdrama Iris (2009) was film.

Pro: nice place as you will get free explanation of jeju. We were able to get first hand information about the traits of jeju woman and good history background of jeju.Cons: you will be exposed to v. long sales talk of made in jeju products. quite expensive and I was sitting through the talk half way i decided to leave.
Pricey and most displays were in Korean. Very hokey. Recommend the Love Park outside Jeju city instead.

Pretty big park with 2 caves that you can go through. Many school trips come here so don't be surprised to see flocks of students in the weekdays too. Nice peaceful area but there are quite a few other Jeju attractions I would see first if you're on a time limit.
Plenty of choice here. Jeju restaurants seems to like bunching cuisines together and this will meet all your black pork needs (it is delicious!)
Please help....Is there a rental boots/shoes intended for hiking near Hallasan Mountain or Jeju City? Thank you for those who can comment on this...
Place to buy famous jeju orange and the stuffs related.. Fresh seafood and vegetables are all around. A must visit place when one spend the time in Jeju

Place rather crowded. But food and drinks are the only thing that I enjoyed.And also Innisfree Jejuhouse if you are a cosmetic lovers. You can get items only available there compared to normal retail outlets.

Personally I find this place to be one of the most undervalued sights in Jeju. Mokwana represents the historic administrative center in the oldest part of Jeju City. The place is not large yet has a lot to show with stories at every corner. It takes only about half an hour from the airport and it took us about an hour to get around once inside. They have nominal admission fee (~ 1.4USD) and it was worth. The only complaint is that some of the labels for exhibits were provided only in Korean.
Part of a tour I took. I enjoyed the presentation and the chance to see and learn some of the history of Jeju.

Out of our surprise no entrance fees needed when you visit Jeju Folk museum. There was a guide that told us about their culture and was a nice experience for us and even the kids. The village was small but a nice encounter. An hour is more than enough.

Our trip in Jeju was turely a great one.  We had an excellent driver.  Mr. Kang from Jeju Day tour ( Hi Jeju Taxi tour) provided us with amazing taxi service. He also recommended good places with reasonable prices. He is very friendly and patient with us.  We were all satisfied and will surely go with Mr.Kang if we happened to visit Jeju again. Highly recommend. Thank you.

Our taxi driver recommended us to go to this folk village eventhough we requested for Jeju traditional folk village. The free tour around the village ended up with the purpose of selling you their local products.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Our first stop in the Jeju trip was the Olloc Tea Museum.Here you can take a master class about how to make tea properly and try different kinds of teas.It was a very relaxing experience and the taste of the tea was very unique.If you like tea is definitely something you have to do if you travel to Jeju.Also you can visit the Innisfree shop right next to the museum and take beautiful pictures in the green tea fields around.

Our driver Kang Dae-Hyun was super friendly and we saw a lot of things :) we could take many pictures and he showed us the best spots in Jeju :) next time we would take the tour again with him! Thank you very much!

Our driver drove us to the rest stop and from there we hiked about 30 minutes to the top. It had just rained so don't try it without solid walking shoes as it's easy to get a nasty fall. It was cloudy so we couldn't get a view of Jeju city but the feeling of being on top of the world was worth it!

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is very small (there are not many displays to see) but there is a very large shop that sells tea products and a cafe that sells drinks and desserts.  There is a very brief tea tasting demonstration w/ narrative in Korean only.  In the cafe we had the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake we've ever tasted.  Prices for drinks & dessert was expensive ($4.50USD each for a small cup of ice cream and a slice of cake; $8.00USD for a large glass of orchid flavored iced green tea).  The tea products in the shop are also expensive.  If you are a tea connoisseur then this is the place for you.  Across the street from the museum there is an open field where the leaves are grown that you can walk around.  There is a viewing tower above the museum where you can also see the tea fields.  If you are exploring the west side of Jeju island O'Sulloc makes a great rest stop. I would not deliberately drive all the way out there just to visit this museum.

Osulloc tea is known as one of the more famous and reliable brand in Jeju...most of the tea is expensive too. Thus it is not uncommon for travel agencies to include the Osulloc green tea museum into its itinerary. A walk around the museum shows you a little background of tea in particular. You can also be able to see tea cups from different countries on display. I tried the green tea ice cream and it was yummy. We were told that if we spend more than 30000 won we can get a tax refund at the airport. So we really spent more than 30000 won on tea :) I wandered alone out of the tea museum and saw Innisfree!!! They were conducting some soap making lesson when I walked in. The deco is very different from what I saw in the malls. And of course I ended up buying stuffs....some facial masks that I wasn't able to find in Singapore.
Osulloc tea house produced blended Jeju tea for many years. Quality tea but very expensive . It is better to buy tea leaves rather than tea bag packaging.

O'sulloc plantation and museum was one of the most memorable places in Jeju.It's really unique and cool place.Even though museum is not that big but you can see and try a lot.They also sell some products in Green tea flavor but they are bit expensive..We tried Green Tea coctail and ice cream. Both were good and we don't regret spending money on it!~Also if you go to O'sulloc don't miss the Innisfree house.For males it might be a bit boring though..But if you are female this place is deffinetely amazing!

Osulloc is famous for their teas. They have a green tea field right outside the museum/cafe. Recommended things to try are their green tea ice cream green tea cake and green tea latte! Great location for picture taking in the green tea field; Bring a wide angle lens! right next door is the innisfree jeju house. Estimated time spent at osculloc is 30-45 minutes tops.

O'sulloc is a green tea museum if you like green tea is a must come or visit place. Please trust me you will like it and also there is an innisfree outlet that has more limited edition products.For more information and insight visit my youtube channel (search by title) - EN CHANNEL: #3 TRAVEL BLOG DAY 2 JEJU - NATURE - GD CAFE - TEDDY BEAR - O'SULLOC
Only to pick up Jeju only products
One of the scenic places in Jeju. A must go even if you miss the sunset/sunrise. Didn't climb it but I went down to the the Hanyeo area. Tiring climb back up though. You can see Udo Island from here.
One of the places you should visit in Jeju. An interesting place for kids and adults too.   The history of teddy bears.....

One of the must visit place in Jeju if you love watching sun rise. It takes about 30 minutes to climb up the steps to the viewing platform. We stayed at Sun Villa Pensions which was just above Nature Republic a stone throw away from the entrance of the park. You could see the crater from the balcony and Starbucks on the left. It was really convenient to have a place nearby as we had to wake up early  to hike up and catch the sunrise (6.45am). The only down side is that the area as well as the park have limited street lights so you'll be needing a torchlight to walk either early in the morning or at night.
One of the must see attractions in Jeju Island. Lucky to visit during the non peak season. Nice views at the right time since we did not meet that many tourists.

One of the most memorable places during my visit to Jeju is Songaksan. Only a slight hike up and you'll get the best coastal view. The hike is so gradual that everybody can do it. The view from the top is so pretty and great for taking photos. One of the best time to go is during sunset.Will definitely recommend to everybody who visits Jeju.
One of the most amazing and picturesque natural beauty in Jeju Island. Definitely worth a visit when you go to Jeju island.
One of the many unusual museums on Jeju island. Same format and content as the american ones - but worth the trip nonetheless. Lots of great photo ops.
One of the larger temples we visited in Jeju. Beautiful well tended grounds and architecture. There is a bus stop right outside the temple which is handy!

One of the interesting tourist object in Jeju Island. But I don't understand why they call castle which for me it's a park with many kind of glasses art.  Anyway it's fun &  we can pretend like in wonderland.

One of the highlights of my visit in Jeju - there's about a 1km walk in the cave which allows you to explore the after effects of lava tubes at your own pace; very interesting and spectacular. Would advise to bring additional clothing and comfortable covered shoes as the temperature is quite cooling with moist grounds. We used flashlights from our iPhones at a few points where it gets very dark; this helps us to better see the route ahead or for looking at details of the lava tubes.  Spent about an hour at this location. A must in your itinerary!
One of the checklist in Jeju It is free and beautiful spot to take picture. You should definitely visit
one of the better swimmable beaches in Jeju. Swimming advised only during certain months though.....

One of the best waterfalls in Jeju that flows all the way to sea... Spent a wonderful time in our free and easy trip around Jeju island with a rented car! Will go to Jeju again for the third time again!

One of the best place I've been in Jeju!This place is quite isolated from the main road as I was stunning such a beautiful place exist where the river and sea water met! We can do a lot of water activities such as kayaking cycling in the water or riding a raft in a bluegreen water..Need to buy ticket in advance. If you go by evening for sure ticket will sold out. Honestly I dont want to write a review about this place as I prefer this place not to be crowded with people but well..For those going to Jeju this is a must visit place as the experience is quite rare and different from any other places.

One of my family's favorite attractions on jeju although we had to drive more than an hour from seogwipo.The enclosures were made such that you could literally be so close to the sea creatures. We were especially awed by seeing the walrus so close up. Food at aqua terrace was also decent. Animal show was better than the synchronized swimming one. Loved the place both adults and children. They did some parts better than the aquariums in Singapore Melbourne etc.

review: one of my destinations in Jeju recommended for green tea lovers. Green tea ice-cream is excellent can spend 3 hours there to deeply understand the cultivation processing and taste of green tea.  More you can find Innisfree house in the Museum.  Feel relax feel the nature there~~

One of my best spot in Jeju. We went in July end and the climate was very very hot. We were sweating like anything and in the mid way my wife said lets go back but i was like we have to go. But when we reached at the top it was so beautiful around. I forgot the stairs and all our exertion was gone. The view is so astonishing and it definitely looks like a world heritage.Tip: Do keep lot of water if visiting in summer.This peak has lot of stairs (not advisable old person or for heart patient).
one of Jeju Olle and getting beautiful landscape & sea view also cliff etc... just take 1hr for strolling is ok.
One of compulsory place to go in jeju. Beautiful. There is a wild deer too but it depends on luck to see it.
One for the books.The climb is worthit though we weren't able to watch the sunrise due to the gloomy weather. The view is relaxing - makes you think of living on this laid back place in Jeju..

One can go for a hike or just sit near the shore and enjoy the view. Along the coastline one can see a number of manmade caves which stands as a testimony to the importance of Jeju Island during WWII. These caves built by the Japanese troops served as a place for storing the weapons.Though called as a mountain it is more like a hill as it is not steep and one can enjoy the walk up the peak.

Onc e you are on the south coast you might as well stop at the highest temple of Jeju. Unfortunately all the new temples look artififial and are lacking atmosphere. Do not miss the building belkow with some 500 small Buddha statues and the the 2 Stone statues called Dolharubang.

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.

On month of June 2019 I booked 4 logs on 2 days dive plan. I went to Jeju for solo travel from Jakarta-Indonesia. Really appreciated all of GD expert Dive Masters who really assisted me to adapt on Korea water harsh condition. Even during strong currents the DMs assisted us to enjoy the dive itself it's amazing for me really excellent DMs service in the world ! If you have any plan to dive at Jeju-Korea we welcome you to the best DC in Jeju is Good Diver Jeju. Bravo GD Jeju ??????????????

On February 2019 I visit Jeju Island I go to O?셲ulloc Tea Shop This shop store provide tea product Tea  Ice cream green tea bakery mix with Green Tea all very yummy. All decorations in shop very good have outside and inside  all staff is good service.

On a 3 day trip to jeju we needed more indoor activities due to the daily snowy conditions and found Jeju National Museum. With low expectations and dampened spirits as we were expecting to visit more outdoor activities we were pleasantly happy with our choice.This museum was easily accessible from our hotel as it was only a 28 minutes bus ride (costs us 1150krw). The bus stop just outside the museum.The museum itself is quite out of the way from the city centre but so was all the other places we wanted to visit and therefore was not an issue for us.Highly recommend you taking your time to read and inspect each exhibit. It is quite amazing how history laid out the changes made due to advancement through discovery. Although for a quick browser it may only take you half an hour (it took us more than 1 hour).Entry was free and I'm not sure if this is the norm but surely worth a visit even if just as a time filler.

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. The reviews for this listing is a mix for the Museum of Sex and Health and for Loveland there is no actual listing on here for Loveland. We did our research first to decide which one to go to and Loveland looked like the more fun one - a lot of the pictures of outdoor sculptures on this listing are actually from Loveland not the Museum of Sex and Health). I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).

Offers organic green tea which I love very much.Have a lot of difference flavors to choose from.Demonstrating and tasting are available.Their green tea icecream from their cafe is a must try item not creamy and not too sweet. Some of their special blend tea leaves are only available at Jeju.Staff are super polite and helpful.

October is the most beautiful season in Jeju Island. Very blue sky so fresh air no traffic sapphire sea.....we drove morning and nightand fully enjoyed Jeju! I will miss it again and visit again soon.

review: Now I know why this place is a place to visit in Jeju. You can see the amazing natural beauty here. But you have to prepare your energy if you want to climb to the top. There are many restaurants in this place so you don't have to worry if you are starving or thirsty. You will not regret visiting this place.

Nothing much to shop as underground complex is quite small. Had Doni burger which was not bad (near exit 5). Other than that it's not really worth a visit as there are better stuff to do at jeju. Spent 6d5n in jeju and didn't finish what we set out for.
Not too much impressive but quite good with Jeju House Innis. The museum doesnt have too much information about tea.
not too bad to climb up as it looks. definately top 5 things to do in Jeju.I go there everytime I go to Jeju island.Always nice view and great feeling on the top.

Not to be missed when in Jeju...... Gorgeous greenery. Go in winter... All white with snow. The mist blowing thru the Pagoda looking tourist information cum observation deck looks very surreal and mystical.

There were even ?쁫ive??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

Jeju Museum of War History and Peace is a must-see place if you visit Jeju. Most tourists just hang out at the beaches restaurants golf courses etc or walk on the Olle. Walking on the Olle is nice--a great pilgrimage for healing. If you really want to know about the unique history of Jeju and the Korean Peninsula however you must visit this museum. Although it's hard to get there by public transportation it's worth visiting. The museum shows how Jeju Islanders were persecuted by Japanese colonialists and then by Korean and U.S. soldiers after Korea's independence. The museum's free-guided tour takes the visitors to the harsh realities of islanders' historical suffering and the division of political ideologies between two Koreas. The highlight of this museum is its peace garden. This huge garden made me pray for peace in the Korean peninsula.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.

I have spent years reading about WW2 history so it's a sobering experience to walk the same places as the men and women who fought and died in that conflict. Altteureu Airfield was a WW2 Japanese airbase that sits in a strategic corner of Jeju Island  midway between China and Japan. In the 1930s bombing missions were launched from here to Shanghai  later it was a training base. There are 19 remaining concrete hardened shelters sized for a Zero fighter and Jeju has done a good job with preserving the site (even though most of it is active farmland)  adding a large parking lot and bathroom  and placards to explain the history and locate the structures. It's right on the Olle trail so there are many hikers passing through and it's easy to find from the shore road by car.

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

I actually came here planning to pick tangerines but to my disappointment there was no sight of a tangerine picking activity in sight... until I found an English/Korean brochure at the empty information counter. The only other people whom we could ask for help are the people working at an art activity at the entrance hall. They could not speak or understand English or Mandarin very well. However  the art activity they were holding seemed very interesting if you are curious. They were designing tangerines/fruits onto these clay plates  but I was told you had to cough up some cash for. Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

I  read about this peace park in Lonely Planet and asked to go there. Our local guide had never visited there before but said he would definitely take people there now. It took us a while to find the right way to go in- lower floor. On the first floor there was a beautiful photo exhibition but the museum is the real attraction. It tells the story of post World War 2 Jeju and  especially about the massacres by different sides of politics. While the museum focuses on Jeju it provides a real insight into the sources of the 1950s Korean war and the division of the country. The USA and its military commanders certainly contributed to the problems and the terrible suffering of the Jeju people.   I highly recommend Westerners to visit this place and the labelling in English is very good.

Hallasan is the tallest mountain in South Korea. Your trip to Jeju island is not complete without climbing this mountain. There are several trails that have different difficulty.

Halla-san is the highest mountain in South Korea and the middle of Jeju Island.  There are two trails that go to the summit of the mountain.  There are a few other trails on Halla-san but they don't go to the top.  It is about 9KM from one side of the mountain to the top and about 10 KM on the other trail to the top.  There are water sources on the mountain so you don't need to carry much drinking water.  It took me between 2 to 2.5 hours to reach the summit and about the same time to go back to where I had parked my car.  The trail is fairly rocky and vertical.  On a clear day you can see all of Jeju Island and the sea below from the summit.  There is also a small pond in the middle of the summit of the dormant volcano that is Halla-san.

Hallasan is the climax of our trip to Jeju. Jeju would be non existense if not because of Hallasan. So we made it a point to spend one day out of our limited time in Jeju hiking the tallest mountain in the country.We took Eorimok trail to ascend and descend via Yongsil trail. Both are beautiful in their own way. Eorimok's view started with tall shady trees and later an open space with mountains and oerums (parasite mountains) as far as the eyes can see. Yeongsil on the other hand displayed a canvas of rocky mountain with autumn leaves colouring the picture. The steps at Yeongsil trail were endless and steep - we were glad we took the trail to descend and not ascend.I enjoy being at Hallasan. Hopefully I'll get the chance to take the other trails leading up to the peak in the future.

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.

He did such a good job in planning our itinerary that we could visit so many places of interest plus completing all our intended activities such as horse riding shooting Go karting and catching a NANTA show. Mr Kim not only drives us to destinations he was knowledgable and could enlighten us with historic information to the various places of interest. This was a big bonus to us as he served as a good tour guide and doubled up in helping us take photographs. He brought us to places for meals which are patronised by locals (not touristy places) for instance we had a yummy authentic ginseng chicken soup pork knuckles sashimi and other Korean local dishes. He is friendly and we enjoyed conversations with him along our rides. These are his info/ contact: Mr Kim Choong Kun Taxi licence plate: 2984 +82-10-63425688 Highly recommended. Good Value.

Considered one of the ten best view points of Jeju this attraction is not to be missed One can enjoy this visit if you like to soak yourself or would like to find yourself among the clouds. On a foggy day one can easily miss the existence of this mountain.If you are visiting during winter or rainy season better to plan the visit during afternoon as one can have a magnificent view from the top without much clouds around.This mountain believed to be formed by the volcanic lava houses the Sanbang-gulsa Temple and the Bomunsa Temple.It also has other attractions as Golden Bhuddha Tea Shops etc. Once on the top one can see the ridge called the Dragon Head where a memorial has been built for Hendrick Hamel the first westerner who was the first to introduce Korea to the western world after his ship got wrecked. This mountain is believed to be used as a watch tower and smoke used to be sent out during the day or fire was lit during the night if any urgent message was needed to be conveyed.Climbing the steps would be a little tough for those who are not regular walkers and for the old.

You will also find the Seonimgyo Bridge on your walk to the waterfall which is adorned by the 7 nymphs  beautifully done in metal.A definite must-do while visiting Jeju-do.

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

As part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour we were given some time to go around O'sulloc Green Tea's fields museum and cafe; as well as shop around in Innisfree's Jeju House.Queues tend to be long for both the O'sulloc Green Tea and Innisfree so it's best to prioritize one over the other if you're working with a limited amount of time. O'sulloc Green Tea displays its wide array of teas packaged in gorgeous boxes and tin cans. These are perfect as gifts for loved ones.They also house a cafe in the store where you eat and drink tea-infused items. Fortunately we were able to visit its branch in Seoul already (and bought our fare share of their tea boxes) so we focused our time in Innisfree instead.Innisfree has numerous branches in Seoul; however it's best to look out for the Jeju-exclusive items available in the Jeju house. Similar to O'sulloc Innisfree also has its own cafe which serves its own selection of drinks and food; for those not interested in its beauty products.

Whatever we could see of the grounds looked very promising.We will consider returning here on a fine day on our next trip to Jeju.

Following the instructions:1. drive car to start point, indicated by a stone pillar on the side of the road.2. engage Neutral Gear3. switch off engine4. disengage all brakes (foot and hand brakes)5. sit and relax as you feel your car roll UPHILL!Outside you you will see tour-leaders and other disbelievers coming out with all kinds of theories and proofs. They have their   spirit-levels   (as contactors carry) and cans of soft drinks to, without external force, roll uphill.All this in 5-10 mins.  Figure out HOW for yourself.

Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on   for the most part  . Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the   tourist beach experience  , selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a   pro   if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

Yongmeori is a rough and dramatic coastline shaped from lava eruptions. Walking along the spectacular rock formations is an experience that only Jeju-do can offer. Firstly, some of the water pockets with bright turquoise water are striking in their uniqueness. Secondly, the sometimes bizarre rock formation are nothing if not eye-catching. Lastly, the strange (slightly grotesque) insects that scurry along some of the rocks are strangely interesting. They never touch or climb on you, every footfall makes them scurry in all direction. Yongmeori is a bit off the   classic   tourist itinerary. Most visitors enjoy a beach or two, maybe a hike at Hallasan or the Seongsan Ilchulbong, and perhaps they fit in a waterfall and museum. Jeju has so much to offer that is often overlooked. Yongmerori Coast is one of these places.
