When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world?s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html

When me and my friend tried to look for a car rent with a driver who can guide us, we chose Hi Jeju Taxi Tour, at first because the term of payment is really easy (We can pay cash directly to the driver), and we can customize the places we love to visit.

When I thought Jeju couldn?t get any more beautiful we decided to take a trip to this graden and was proved wrong. This garden is so well put together with guides that invoke thought at every corner. Even during the fall there was so much to see, definitely visit if you get the chance!

What's there to see here? There's the rocks, the sea, and a few souvenir shops, but really, the place is, quite frankly, overrated. The rock doesn't even resemble a dragon's head!This may be one of my shortest reviews ever, but it's only because the place is not very interesting. Yes, there's a great sea view (the reason why I didn't give this attraction a   terrible   rating), but other than that, there's really no reason to visit this place.Only give this attraction a go if you really fancy posing with the rock, or if you really love the sea. My humble opinion is that Jeju definitely has more places worthy of your precious time.

What is so mysterious about this road is that vehicles can still move upslope with the engine switched off. We had the engine of the bus switched off and experienced it first hand what it felt like. The bus was first moving at a very slow speed but it started to gear up towards the end of the road. We then got off the bus to watch other vehicle move on the road. It was quite an interesting sight. Somewhere nearby, I even saw a stand giving out free Christian literature. Lots of snacks available. My first time trying the milk. At first, I thought it was some yoghurt drink or a big bottle of Yakult. Tried the one with black cap and realised that it's banana milk. I never like flavoured milk but this taste nice.More pictures available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html

What can I say...I loved Jeongbang waterfall soooo much. I went there on one of the hottest summer days in July and it was absolutely amazing. On my way down, I was complaining and whining the whole time because it was too hot. But once I got down near the waterfall, it was really windy..almost chilly!!! Cooling winds lovely views...I'll go there again before I leave Jeju!

What a fun little island! Exploring the island on a motorized bike/trike was an awesome experience. To rent the trikes an international class A drivers license is needed (US Military living in Korea can use your ID card and Korean drivers license). No license is needed for the motorized 2-wheeled bikes. This is the easiest way to travel the island making frequent stops to see the scenery or stop at one of the many cafes or restaurants. We saw tour busses, and a few regular cars, but seems like the majority of visitors chose the motorized trike to see the island. The ferry from Seongsan Port on Jeju to  Cheonjin Port on Udo runs every 30 minutes and the ride was about 15 minutes. There was an air-conditioned room on the upper deck but it was floor seating only. It is possible to see the whole island in a few hours.

we've been Udo island on the day 2 at Jeju Island after hiking to Sunrise Peak Seongsan Illchulbong. we going to the port by walking about 15 minutes from Illchulbong, and takes ferry only for 11.000W returns. the ferry takes 15 minutes to island and schedule every 10 minutes. We have only for 3 hours at the island before going back, so we chose to hiking Udo peak. takes 40 minutes - 1 hours to reach the peak, just follow the path. really recommend to going Udo island, very beautiful scenery of Seongsan Illchulbong and the cave.You also can rent a bike for around the island or motorbike if you have international license. Or shuttle bus.

Went with my friend and it was really a rare experience and rare sight for us. There are a lot of sculptures in the park and all of them come in different poses. It was a good chance to take some funny photos but we found it not so appropriate to take such pictures and so we didn't take much pictures of the sculptures.We walked across the park and saw different sculptures which have different funny messages (and we had a good laugh about some of the messages). After that we went in to their indoor shop where they sell   adults toys   and some chocolates (with pictures of different poses). There are also some shops outside which sell handmade stuffs and chocolates. Overall if you are in Jeju and you are not shy take a visit here once. However the way here is not so convenient. We took a taxi from our hotel since it is near (it took about 15 mins by taxi).

Went via a taxi tour in Early Feb 2014. Admission for each person: 2000 won.Hordes and hordes of tourists but you can still try to take some nice and pretty pictures while waiting for those tour groups passing by. Divers performance (if I am not wrong) is at 11am and 3pm. We did not went during that time so we did not manage to see it.Without going up to the peak, you can also see a nice view of the ocean and surroundings. There are also several souvenirs and food shops at the foot of the sunrise peak. It is a UNESCO site and it is a must to visit if you are in Jeju! Still awesome despite in winter.Don't forget that there are stairs and stairs up to the peak :P

Went to hyeopjae beach just to try swimming while i was in Jeju. Rented a car and drove there, thought that parking was gonna be a challenge but managed to get one in mere minutes. Mum didnt swim, so we rented an umbrella + mat for her to wait at. Cost us 15K won. Not sure if it was cheap or expensive. They guy attending to the rental didn't speak english, thank God for a local young chap who helped us translate.Loved the vibe of the beach, everyone there was enjoying the waves. Where I'm from, our sea is not as rough. so it was really different to see everyone in their floaties waiting for waves to hit them.

Went there without much training as I envisage that winter time is more pleasant to climb. We reached the base around 7.30am as we try to take the first bus. As we envisage there are snow, I have a pair of crampons bought before arriving in Jeju. Fortunately I did as the crampon sold at the shop is rather expensive. Then it was a relax 2 hours climb, I did not want to rush, but took time to appreciate the environments and snow. The crampons came in useful as you climb further up, it gets slippery. Good to have walking sticks too. At about the 1000+ meter stop, there is shop where you could buys hot noodles and drinks. I bought another set of crampons there as it is reasonable compared to the shop at the base of the mountain.After a short rest, the final climb to the top. Here there is a series of steps and staircase that leads to the top. At some point it was rather steep so have to climb up slowly, catching my breaths as the higher altitude and cold tends to slow you down. There is a timing to get down from the mountain per regulations, hence the need to get to the top early to enjoy the view and triumph. Finally reaching the top, was rewarded with a gorgeous scenery. It was kind of crowded and there was a queue of climbers taking turns to take picture with the summit monument.  After taking lots of pictures, hiking down was relatively easily, reaching the base in half the time. Took the bus back to town to enjoy a beer and fried chickens. A trip not to be missed.

Went there with my friend, we took bus from Jungmun (at the bus stop nearby tourist information center, at the right hand side). We took bus no. 781 and alighted at Teddy valley golf and resort, from there turn left (after you alighted) and walk straight for 1 min, you will see the museum at your left hand side. The entrance ticket cost 12000 won per adult. There are gift shop, Kitty History Hall, Music Education Hall, Art Gallery, Hello Kitty Caf챕, 3D Theater and more.. The Hello Kitty Cafe is very big and is beautifully designed and decorated.. There are a lot of cute hello kitty inside the museum and there are also some outside the museum. If you are a hello kitty fan, this is a must visit place when you come to Jeju.The museum closes at 6pm, so you might want to go there earlier.

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

Went there to see how the locals interact, to feel and absorb the local vibes. Nice to see how the locals live and behave. Pleasant to stroll through the stalls. Went there in the morning and saw many fresh local produce like seafood, meats, fruits, vegetables, household items, clothes, bags, shoes .......just about everything. We also saw many stalls selling street food - bungeoppang ( fish shaped bun-filled with sweet red beans) , eomuk ( fish cake ), hoppang ( steamed buns) , tteokbokki. ( stir fried rice cake) , gyeranppang ( egg bread ), dak-kkochi (korean chicken skewers ). Had a great breakfast on these streetfoods. We also saw lots and lots of hallabong too. Very juicy and sweet these Jeju?s iconic mandarin oranges. Not to be missed one must try the hallabong fruit juice and hallabong icecream. We also bought some local korean snacks , kimchi and souvenirs to bring home.

Went on a Friday afternoon at the suggestion of our hired taxi driver even though it was not in our planned itinerary as we happened to be in the area for lunch. There was no other visitor in there other then my friend and I. For 9000 won, there are many other attractions in Jeju to see. The place is small and just filled with colourful glass exhibits and decorations... we completed visiting in less than half an hour as it is a very small place.

Went during winter. The view at Seongsan Ilchulbong is amazing. The steps are very tiring, but it's definitely worth it! Very beautiful sunset from up there looking down. Next time when I go Jeju again, I'll still make a visit to enjoy the relax and beautiful scenery.

Well-known by Korean tourists to Jeju as a filming location for the very popular drama   Daejangguem  , Oedolgae is perhaps the most scenic volcanic rock formation on the island. The area is more of a viewpoint attraction, you walk the beautiful coastline only so far. Most visitors spend 30-60 minutes visiting the site, cameras are usually busy. If you're visiting Jeju during the summer, it is probably best to visit Oedolgae in the morning before it gets too busy. Jeju is full of dramatic coastline, this is one of the most picturesque locations.

Well, there has been near our place in Jeju and in our schedule. We could go by walk and bought Citrus fruit in the street, specialties of Island. The bridge leads to the road around the mountain. Can proceed to visit

Well, it is a beach. With bus 101 roughly 15 minutes away from Jeju city.As far as I remember the beach feature something like a free gym and a few toilets.I did not see much of changing facilities, showers or lockers near the beach.In my view Hamdeok Beach is less good than the beaches in Busan.During my time in Hamdeok Beach I saw three surfers who practiced their skill.

Well, comparing to Seogwipo Daily Olle Market, sashimi is cheaper here. The market is bigger and there are most stalls for the snacks. But majority of these stalls are not open until evening time.  It is short walking distance to the Black Pork Street.Ample parking nearby and there is also a multi storey parking which is among the most expensive parking I had in entire Jeju. 6000W.

Well, at the shore, practically still in the city, you can find this rock which probably originates from a lava eruptions, as everything on this island. With some imagination, I could identify a dragon's head. Nothing particular. It's like one tour guide said: everything on Jeju island is small and cute.

Welcome to the first Teddy Bear Museum in Korea. Here you will find everything you want to know about Teddy Bears. Teddy Bears have been loved and cherished since they were first introduced over 100 years ago. There are now millions of people who collect Teddy Bears. They seek out old, unique and valuable teddy bears for their personal collections. Our Teddy Bear Museum opened especially for the European collectors. The Teddy Bear Museum is more exciting than ever with   Teddy Bear   entertainment as never seen before. Jeju Teddy Bear Museum opened on April 24, 2001. It contains two galleries, a museum gift shop, and a museum cafe. Also, on site is a museum bar/restaurant, a wonderful place to meet friends, family, and lovers. From the outside garden, there is a view of Jung-Mun Beach.

We, a group of friends had visited this place last week. It was awesome! The journey to get there, parking and the walk up and back were all good. There is ample parking space and plenty of eateries that offers various types of snacks and cold drinks.The area is impeccably clean and the walking path was clear and safe. The steps may seem a little steep at certain points, but you will be well rewarded once you reach the top. The crater is a beautiful sight! Not surprising that it's the iconic image of Jeju which appears on Google. You need about an hour or so for the entire visit.

We woke up at 3am for this and didn't regret it. It was really quite awesome. We drove in the wee hours of the morning for 1.5 hrs to get there, before hiking up for about 40mins to get to the viewing deck where there are seats to see the sunrise. To best enjoy this, be well prepared and equipped for the journey. We slept early at about 9pm the previous night because we knew we had to wake up at 3am. Prepare bread for breakfast on the road because you will need the energy for the hike. Wear proper walking shoes to make it easier to climb up. Remember to check the sunrise timing the night before, set your gps early and accurately if you are driving. If you need help with Korean gps or not sure if you got the right place, always ask your hotel or hostel host to help you set it right the night before. Charge and prep your cameras, go early to get a good spot, because you are going to get some really awesome sights of the sunrise at this spot. Definitely go for this if you are in Jeju. Not to be missed for the world!

We were very happy to engage Mr. Jang as our guide in Jeju. We will definitely engage Mr. Jang again when we are back in Jeju. He is honest, genuine, reliable and he has made our visit in Jeju a very memorable one.

We were up early and looking for something that was also open early and found Halla Arboretum. Right in Jeju City and east to get to yet plenty of space, beautiful paths and forests to walk through. Great morning activity with early rising kids ans it?s free.

We were tired in the carpark and considered sleeping but decided to go in. So glad we did, walking through the garden was a deep feeling of peace and felt refreshed. Would definitely come back. A must do in Jeju Island!

We were there on a clouded day, which was perfect since you don't want to climb those stairs in a heatwave. Not alot of visitors, so we made plenty of pictures without any bombers. Definitely a must-see if you are in Jeju.

We were there at around 10 am and there were already many tourists and tourist buses. At the entrance before we climbed to the peak, I found out why it was one of the most popular tourist spots in Jeju. The view was breathtaking. At some spots, we could see Udo. Despite the flocking of tourists (majority were foreigners including us) and the time of the day we reached there, the view was so stunning nevertheless. The flight of stairs was nothing compared to the view we witnessed.

We were staying in the Lotte Hotel Jeju and it was not too far to walk to this sight from our hotel.The view is a nice one, probably not as impressive as the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but interesting nonetheless.Definitely worth a visit for the coastal scenery but doesn't occupy much time.

We were so underwhelmed when we saw the rock, we had to laugh. It was quite small so not an imposing structure like we were expecting and only very loosely resembled a dragon. We were quite flummoxed and amused as it seems to be billed as a must see destination on promotional material when there are more interesting things to see in Jeju. Go if you're near but don't make a special effort to go see it unless you want a huh? moment!

We were received by a Chinese -speaking   Villager   upon entering the village. It is well set up, which gives a glimpse of the old life style of the local Jeju islanders. However, after a brief talk about the life of the local people, the guide was more interested to get us all seated inside a hut to sell her products, such as honey, Omija tea, and lo and behold...horse bone pellets (remedy for loss of calcium)! Her sales pitch was pushy and rather unfriendly, and we were not that interested by her goods (the price was exorbitant), we could sense her attitude turned from lukewarm to really cold. There is no doubt some local people really live here, as to keep the tradition alive, also supported by the government to do so. I think is better to keep the selling of local goods to another area (like setting up a gift shop), rather than incorporating it as some kind of compulsory lecture within the guide tour. I find that most off-putting. I give this place an average rating. The surrounding restaurants which serve the famous pork dishes from black pig were good.

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!

We were looking for a good place to shop and buy souvenirs and we found this place in Jungang area. Lot of cheap items from clothes, bags, shoes and beauty products.Tips:- GPS: 752-8776- There is a public parking in front of Jeju Bank along Ohyeon-gil. 3-4 hours cost us 3700Krw.- Jejumok Gwana is just on the West exit (exit 11). You might want to drop by if you got time.- There are Korean food in the middle section. Cheap but taste good.

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We were dropped by a taxi at the beginning of the Seongpanak trail (a little way up the volcano), but you can catch the bus there if you prefer and there is a bus stop right near the entrance. The track is 9.6km (19.2km return), and took us about 6 hours return walking at a medium pace, including breaks at Sokbat shelter (4.1kms up - toilet facilities only) and at Jindallaebat shelter (7.3kms up - toilet and small kiosk). We had initially wanted to walk up the Gwaneumsa trail and then down the Seongpanak one, but were too tired to get up before 6am to achieve it in one day. Walking the Seongpanak trail up and down was a great experience in itself, even though it is apparently not as scenic as others. But, because it's one of the easier ones, it is packed with tourists, most of whom are not seasoned walkers, so be prepared for being held up a fair bit (and witnessing some pretty avoidable but hilarious injuries!).The trail is quite an easy one in comparison to other hikes we have done - no really steep bits or actual climbing - more of a gentle incline, with boardwalks in parts, dirt paths and as you get higher, rough rocky paths. The only strenuous thing about the trail is that it is long? It will take you all day, and you have to start early so you reach the Jindallaebat shelter before a certain hour (changes depending on the season, but in September it was 12:30pm) or the ranger won't let you continue - for obvious reasons, there's no lighting at night to climb back down, so he doesn't want to come and find stupidly lost tourists! You can check the times on the official Hallasan website. You don't really need proper hiking boots/other equipment for this hike (we did it in light walking shoes), but if you have weak ankles I would probably recommend wearing hiking boots with ankle support, especially for the walk back down the rocky paths. Take plenty of water and snacks - don't rely on the shelters like the Koreans do, they may sell out/be extremely busy, and you have to get to Jindallaebat by 12:30! We just bought some muesli bars, fruit, WATER and energy drinks like gatorade/powerade at a 7/11 before we left Jeju city in the morning, and were almost the only ones who had thought ahead! On the way back down, the Jindallaebat shelter will be quieter, so it's the perfect opportunity to then buy some of their hot ramen noodles or a chocolate bar. I would also recommend bringing a light rain jacket, and a waterproof backpack/cover for your backpack - it showers sporadically within the fog. I also took a plastic bag to put my camera in to keep it dry.When we began our walk, it was quite chilly at the entrance and the local walkers laughed at us wearing shorts - but by the time you get a few kilometres in, you'll be stripping off layers of clothing, so totally wear shorts if you want to - it's quite warm in the sun on the summit, so everyone will be peeling off their layers anyway! There was a thick fog hanging low over the volcano for about 2/3 of the walk, so it's a bit muggy, but the side of the mountain is lush and green, an eerily quiet forest. As you get higher, suddenly you notice you're climbing above the fog - feels like you've popped out above the clouds, on top of the world! The last part of the track is quite windy, and you can see how the wind has beaten its wooden steps, which are strewn everywhere. Be careful in the last part and beware pushy tourists! But, once you get to the summit, at Dongneung Peak (no facilities on the summit, by the way), the view is breathtakingly beautiful - like nothing I've ever seen before! The crater when we were there was overgrown with vegetation, with a small crater lake. Such a wonderful experience, and most definitely a highlight of our trip to South Korea! You must hike Hallasan during your stay at Jeju-do!

We were cruising the Far East and stopped at Jeju. The cheapest excursion was $120 per person. $240 for the two of us. Instead we walked around Jeju a little then hailed a cab. He took us all over the island doing all the same things for $100. Personal service. Stayed. As long as we wanted. Left when we were ready. One of the many ways weve seen the world much cheaper than most. 73 countries and territories so far. The village is interesting. 100 huts. Some occupied. And a black pig. A guy will tell you about a tea they sell that if it tastes salty or sweet will diagnose your ailments. We passed. Not sure how many people read my reviews. If you hit ?helpful?,  I?ll get an email and they always encourage me to write more :)

We were coming from Hamdeok Beach to the Jeongbang water falls and happened to directly pass by this place on the highway and I remembered it was one of the top places to visit in Jeju so we decided to pull over and enter.  We're very glad we did.  We spent about an hour there but you could easily spend more time.  It was awesome to see all the man made stone statues and their significance or their meaning, one of the main ones  being the mother who had 500 sons.  The museums were pretty cool as well and you could learn a ton of geography.  The setting was very picturesque with Mt. Halla in the background and the surroundings looking like you were sort of in a savanah.  We took some awesome photographs and learned a lot of information.  I think if you're able to rent a car and drive there it's a must see in Jeju.

We were a little disappointed after walking all the way down the hill at Sunrise Peak to see the women divers, only to find out that because of the holiday, they wouldn't be diving today.So as a consolation, our tour guide took us to the Haenyeo Museum.  This museum was dedicated to the Haenyeo women divers of Jeju and Japan.  It's a very nice museum with excellent displays, and you will learn a lot about the divers.I recommend seeing the video show before you start wandering around.

We went to visit many beaches during this trip. This is the only one we visited twice and would love to come again in the future to stay around this area! Nice cafe by the beach, nice trial you can climb up and many great photo spots! Don?t miss this spot when you visit Jeju!

We went to Udo island on 27th May 2016. Weather was pretty good and sunny. Udo island is a full one day trip. We took a taxi from our hotel in jeju city to intercity bus terminal. Booked our tickets to Seongsan ferry terminal bus#710. It runs on an interval of 20 minutes. We took our bus at 9.40am. It took us approximately 1hr 30min to reach the terminal. From there, we booked our return tickets for the ferry which takes you to Udo island. Return ticket is valid for the entire day and no specific return time is mentioned on it. So you can spend the day in Udo and take any ferry from Udo back to the terminal. To book ferry tickets first you will need to fill some form lying there on the tables. Then show the filled form at the ticket counter and they will give you the ticket. Ferry runs every 30 mins from the terminal. And it takes 15 mins to reach Udo by ferry. Upon arrival to Udo island, you need to walk for 2 minutes and you will see various vendors for renting bike and bicycles. For renting a bike, you need to have driving license and for foreigners international driving license. We didn't have it, so we booked a hop on hop off tour bus. There were two vendors for the bus tour - red buses and blue buses. Red bus tour vendor offered 5 destinations and blue one offered 4 both at the cost of 5,500KRW per person. We booked the red one as we wanted to cover 5 destinations. Also, red buses were available in abundance and blue buses seemed to be pretty less. Once you book the bus ticket, you need to keep the ticket safely with you for the entire trip as whenever you'll board the bus you need to show it to the driver. So DO NOT lose the ticket. Hop on the bus for your first attraction and on the way you will get to see beautiful Udo island with small and tiny roads and farming everywhere. For going to the next attraction, you can hop on any of the bus as the bus service is really good and arrives every 20 minutes at the attraction point. We loved all the attractions except for the museum which I guess was our 4th attraction on the list. You may also skip any of the attractions by not getting off the bus. We also tried peanut ice cream there which was really good and refreshing. Also, you can take a speed boat ride on one of the attractions. In our list, it was the first attraction point to the beach. They charge 10,000KRW for speed boat per person and take you to eight scenic views. We also located so many dophins in the sea which was so exciting. After all the attractions are covered, bus will drop you back to the ferry terminal and while boarding the bus driver will finally collect your ticket.All in all, a memorable and a pleasant trip for us. Just avoid going there on a rainy day. Good luck!!! :)

We went to this market 3 times and it's worth it. Basically you can finds something to eat here, various of foods offer, drinks, souvenirs and of course fruits which ia the famous one, Hallabong. For ourselves, we grab a raw salmon for dinner and hallabong juices with a few banchan for ourselves. Not to forget we bought a bundle of jeju chocholates and crunch to bring back as souvenirs and one big bag of keychain and fridge magnet. The chocholate and crunches are widely sell as for 15boxes ??10,000 and the fridge magnet with price standard ??3,000 each.

We went to this folks village on our own but not with tour, therefore when we reached there, there is only 5 of us, the staff approached us and starts telling us Jeju Folks Cultural stories, the entrance is free and the guide is free, but at the end of the guide, you'll be brought to a room where they'll start selling you the local specialties, we got some discount since we're not with tour (as usually places like this required to pay tour agent some fees), but if you don't want to buy anything, just say thank you & leave, that's all 븝

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum only because it was right next door to the Lotte Hotel Jeju where we stayed.  At 10,000 won per adult and 8,000 won per child, it is a bit pricey.  You can be done with all the displays and the 5 minute teddy Elvis show in an hour.  If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We went to the market wanted to try some fresh octopus. We bought an octopus from a stall and the nice lady told us in broken English that we can have it prepared at the nearby restaurant. So we went into that restaurant just opposite the seafood stall. None of them can't speak English, even a little bit. So went back to the seafood stall and asked the nice lady to help us. So we seated in the restaurant waiting just for our octopus to be prepared. Then they bring out the cutlery.. we were quite puzzled... why does one octopus need so many cutlery.. then they took out the big steamboat with all the seafood in it! We keep using sign language to say show we don't want the steamboat and just want our octopus prepare... after a while we gave in. and our octopus came out serve in a plate, fully chopped into tiny bits like being blended in a food processor :(we have had enough seafood steamboat over the past few days in Jeju and this is not the time we want to eat the steamboat again. oh well, all because of language barrier and luckily we still have enough cash to pay for the meal as they don't accept credit card.Besides the story, local products sell in this market are quite interesting.

We went to the Jungmun Golf Club to have a Moonlight Walking Tour as part of the preparation for the 2020 Jeju Olle Walking Festival. The tour took us only 30 minutes, and later on, we enjoyed performances by local artists under the bright moon. You can witness the mesmerizing scenery of the sunset and the sea from the golf course.

We went to the folk village and had an educational tour of how Jeju locals lived in the past and how some still choose to live in their small hut houses (with government support). Afterwards, we were offered omija tea for relaxation and for something to bring home.

We went to the cave by a convenient bus frm Jeju city. There is a 2km-wlak form bus station to the cave (I would not recommend to take the taxis that are waiting for you as a total tourist). After the 20mn-minute walk, the cave is very interesting and informations about it are quite depth.

We went to Marado Island by taking a 1 h-long ferry from Jeju Island (Daejung-Eup, Hamo ri). The ferry was nice and the could stand in either deck to enjoy the scenic view of the ocean. When you approach the island you could see the beauty of volcanic layers that forms the island and the interface of volcanic rocks and ocean was amazing. Walking is the best way to enjoy the island and you may spend nearly 3 h in the island. There are a couple of restaurants, a beautiful buddha temple, a church etc. A nice half-day trip. Highly recommended.

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many   activities   on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.

We went to Hallasan NP in early November by ourselves.  It?s quite easy to take the bus to the park.  Just make sure you know which stop to get off as there are several entrances.  We decided to hike the shortest trail (1.3km).  It begins at the Hallasan National Park Visitor Centre and finishes atop Eoseungtaeng Oreum, with sweeping views of the Jeju plains and the peak of Hallasan.  The leaves are very beautiful along the trail.  With our age, being seniors, and photo stops, it took us one hour to get up to the top.  Definitely it worths the hike!

We went to eorimok trail to enjoy the winter festival. Great outdoor fun for children. Best part its free (except for 1,000krw parking fees). My kid loves d slide!! There?s even a museum to learn how hallasan mountain was formed. In my opinion this is the best place to visit in jeju.

We went to Dongmun Market on the last day of our tour in Jeju. There are many local produce here, especially seafood and tangerines. We sampled their street food and snacks as we strolled through the rows of stalls and shops, soaking up the local atmosphere. Our taxi tour guide, Mr Lee would help us to talk to the stallkeepers, and also ensure that we did not pay any extra. We did not have enough time to thoroughly check out the market because we had to catch a flight. This is one of the places I would visit again if I return to Jeju.
We went there. picture perfect view, quiet and serene. We had a chance of  spending time there on 1 July, 2017. perhaps one of the best beach in Jeju. Please go. you will enjoy.

We went there yesterday and this my second time here! It?s so beautiful and amazing it?s so nice to relax and have fun in the same day you have to go here if you are in jeju you will have the best time , you can go for a day or you can stay overnight it?s very safe !

We went there twice on the same day as it is within walking distance to our Seaes Resort.First we went during the general time when other tourists all come the same time, which was still ok for us because we somehow could find a good spot for taking photos.Tips: don't wear black or dark grey or another other dark colors if you want to pose in the photo, unless you want to disguise as a rock formation yourself.After checking out the place we decide the best time is to return at around 6pm to tke the sunset view which was truly amazing. We visited Ireland and the Giant Causeway in Iceland before and must say the sunset here in Jeju is much more likely because of the weather, and is so much easier to visit (although the scale is smaller).More tips: When we arrived at 6pm, one would be intimidated by the tourist crowds at that time but hang on to it and stay longer if you can. The crowds probably were restricted by their guide and car, just quickly left just BEFORE SUNSET ( tours!), or some individual visitors also left right away, leaving the spot empty for a truly memorable experience.  I did my yoga there freely in the sunset until the door guard finally swept us away, about 20 min after sunset

We went there by ferry, it takes around 1 hour, small but really nice island, must visit if you are in Jeju, it is the southern area of south Korea, population is only 90 , no cars aloud on the island you can make the whole tour by foot in 1 hour and a lot of beautiful scenery to see so prepare camera

We went there by car that we brought from jeju. It's really beautiful nevertheless. 1 day is enough to tour all of it. If you want to try horseriding, there's some that offer price 5000 won per ride, while others 10k won. There's many place that offer horseriding, so if you want to save your budget without sacrifing the experience, walk some more to find cheaper ones.Try the Hallasan fried rice! It's really worth it!

We went there after a typhoon so beach was a little mixed up. It was a bit too windy for comfortable swimming, but all in all the cafes around the place and the atmosphere on the beach were good. And it was easy to get there from jeju city with buses. We visited in the beginning of October and it was still warm enough for just relaxing on the beach.

We went Seongsan Ilchulbong in the evening, even though it's known as the Sunrise Peak. The hike up was a little tiring for us as we had previously scaled up a few other peaks the same day. There are quite a few resting spots around, so rest assured you can always catch a breather before ascending the next flight of steps.Bring enough water with you as drinks sold along the way can be quite expensive!The view at the peak is surreal. The sun sets rather slowly in Jeju, so you'll have ample time to scale up and take multiple shots of the place.I will definitely visit the peak again. This time, I'll go for the sunrise. :)

We went on the first Monday of the month, and the mountaineering trail was closed, so do take note when planning. However, the first portion of the trail was still available for free, which was still amazing and less of an exercise. The view from all spots were breathtaking, making this spot a must-see when you?re in Jeju.Do catch the woman?s diver show at 1.30pm and 3pm, located down the trail. It was an interesting experience to see the elderly women dive down to retrieve the seafood in the ocean, and you can buy and eat some of their fresh catches at the shop nearby.Highly recommend for a magnificent sightseeing experience in Jeju!

We went on a tour trip to Seoul / Jeju Island. It has included with this Hello Kitty place. Frankly speaking, it has very beautiful hello kitty decorations all over. But none of us is interested as our family don?t have hello kitty fans. It?s best suitable for young little sweet girls! They?ll sure love it.

We went just one hour and a half before closing time (7:30pm). At the counter, we were told that it took about 50-minutes for round trip until the top. It was huge and made my wife hesitated to climb it at first. But by seeing the surrounding scenery, and imagining on how awesome it will be from up there, we climbed the stairs about 40 minutes (also stopped for taking pictures since the scenery was too beautiful). We could see the night view when we reached the top. It was worth it :) the best scenery I have seen in Jeju.

We went here on our way to south jeju.It was a nice place where we can see the various art forms possible with glass.A sculpture of a horse made with glass was displayed, which was really looking cool...
We went February 2015 during winter time, It freezed to death but well worth experience. Recommended and must place visit in Jeju

We wanted to visit an orange, (tangerine) farm in Jeju, where the famous Jeju oranges are grown.Through the tourists information centre, we found this farm nearest from the city centre. We had to take a bus.It is a very nice orange farm. Fee is 5,000\ per pax- with unlimited time, eat as much oranges as you want while in the orchard & get to bring back 1kg of oranges at the end of it.Great deal considering 1 small tray of oranges in the markets are selling for same price or higher.The young lady in charge was very friendly & helpful although she don't speak English ( Google Translate comes in handy everytime ).The shop was very nice too. Products made at the farm using their fresh oranges includes jams, confectionery & oranges as well. The small production factory could be seen from the shop.Free tasting of their orange jam plus few pieces biscuits included. The jam was very good, made of real oranges.

We walked up Yeongsil and down Eriomok. Would definitely recommend getting a taxi right up to the start of the trail if you want to start walking straight away. As other mentioned, it is a long, winding up hill 2.5 km walk from the bus stop. It cost us 30,000 won in a taxi from the other side of Seogwipo. The walk up was beautiful and the rest area with bathrooms at the top was  a surprise. We brought all our own food and drinks and didn?t see anywhere selling, which we enjoyed at the top. The walk down was equally lovely although the hard bit lasted longer so we were glad we did it on the way down. A short 10 minute walk from the base of Erimok are the bus stop going to Jeju City or Seogwipo. All in all it was a lovely hike and we thoroughly enjoyed it. Took us about 6 hours including numerous stops here and there and a 30 minute lunch break.

We walked up the Gwanmeusan Trail, only 20 minutes from downtown Jeju-si. It took us, going slowly with lots of rests about 9.5 hours. Good hiking shoes required. We witnessed multiple shoe failures. You have to hike back down shoeless if your shoes rip apart and they will due to the volcanic rocks used on the rrail. The rocks are cute until they aren't. They are murder on the feet, ankles, knees, and legs on the way down.We went in April 20 and it was warm... only one water stop about 3/4 way up.18+ miles round trip. Please ask questions if you have concerns. It is quite breathtaking but a strenuous hike. Many turn back early. Must make it to the Samgakbong shelter by 12:30. No support on the trail.... 2 bathrooms though about 1/4 and 3/4 way up. Must start return hike by 2PM... still took us 4 hours to down due to strenuous terrain and infinite number of stairs.

We walked to this Waterfall from our hotel (Days Hotel Jeju Seogwipo Ocean). Though it was scheduled to open at 9am, it open only at 11am as the rain the day before cause some flooding. Easy access to the Falls but needs to be careful walking on the rocks. I sprained my little toe doing this. View of the cliff and ocean is great!

We visited Udo with my brother as part of our trip on Jeju. It is easily accessible via ferry (don't forget to bring your passport to buy a ticket!). We did the recommended tour (4h, with lunch time) and it was beautiful: campaign, port, cliffs, lighthouse... We definitely recommend it. We rate it 4 stars and not 5 because of the garbages on the island, it wastes the beautiful landscapes!

We visited this tourist spot because Seongsan Sunrise Peak (=Seongsan Ilchulbong) is one of the 7 wonders.  Basically it's an archetypal tuff cone formed thousand of years.   In this area, we can also see performance of Jeju woman diver ( too bad I did not have chance to see it myself)There was stall selling sausage and korean snack on a stick (@3K-4K won) which is yummy.  Try one.  *TK

We visited this site with a group of friends.Everybody had their own take on the mysterious road and all had their theories. A quick visit to the internet would provide the answer. However, this all detracts from the pure fun of the site itself. However, part of the fun is discussing the   mystery   of the road.The site is a simple narrow two-lane road. It is not huge. There is plenty of parking for visitors to stop and examine the surroundings.  There are snack stalls along the road where refreshments and some simple snacks can be bought. I noticed some posts on TA that say this is a   tourist trap  . I do not see how this would be the case as nobody is forced to buy or pay for anything.  Anything we bought was food, which, to me, does not seem to be predatory on tourists. In fact, I was hungry and thirsty and was happy to purchase some cooked local yams and cool refreshment. There are tourist traps on the island, but this is not one of them.Having said the above, the attraction is not a major development and is not meant to be a huge event to take up one's itinerary. It is a fun and simple site to visit which can be added to the list of places to visit when in Jeju.
We visited this 1100 when we cross from jeju to seogipo and it was good to see the beautiful nature. Because of time issue, we couldn't visit on top of Mt hanla.

We visited these as part of our guided tour and were impressed by the surrounding scenery and location. It's a wonderful way to see Jeju at its best, and the rocks are quite impressive. It doesn't take as long to see as you would think, but still worth an hour or so.

We visited the National Park as well as Mt. Hallasan during our trip to Jeju-do. It is a beautiful park with average to good hiking trails. We took the long trail (Seongpanak, 9,6km) up to the summit, which took us 2,5 hours (i will take you much longer if you hike slowly and take breaks!). The view from the Summit was just stunning! Definately worth it! I'd advise anybody hiking this trail to wear boots or other firm shoes since the trail is very steep and rock at some parts. You also have to start early in the morning (~8am) since you have to reachthe second station until 1pm to be allowed to go to the summit. Geaneumsa trail is currently closed!

We visited the Jungmun Golf Club for doing the Moon Light Walking Tour. We went there to warm up for the Jeju Olle Walking Festival. The view was awesome and it was a nice experience to walk there during sunset. At the end, they prepare a concert for all the participants there.

We visited the JAM (Jeju Aerospace Museum) and it was stunning, I love anything connected with planes or space so I was in heaven, the displays are well laid out and there were so many interactive displays for kids too that it shows that there was much thought in the museum.Not only was it about aircraft, but also about Korea's history of astronomy which was so fascinating that I could have spent all afternoon in this one section, Then we went into the space exhibition and again I was stunned at how much South Korea has achieved. We always think of? USA & Russia as being at the forefront, visit the JAM to have your eyes opened.Wonderful.

We visited the cave on the way back to Udo (very easy to do both of these in one day. Very interesting and well explained. It would probably be a good idea to bring a jacket because the temperature in the cave is significantly lower than on the outside. However, it's still really cool to see and think about the implications of the event that made the cave in the overall of Jeju. Very good for kids although it can be a bit slippery inside too.

We visited Oedolgae with Jejueco Suite?s package tour.  Victor, our guide, told us an interesting story of a lady praying for her husband who is lost at sea.  As it was then near sunset (about 1 hour prior), the rocks were backlit and we could not take a photo of the ?praying lady and her fallen husband?. Victor told us to continue along the Jeju Olle Trail (marked by ribbons) for a seaside hike, and he will wait for us at the next carpark.  I forgot to ask him how long the walk is expected to be, so when I can?t see any carpark after 10-15min, I kept wondering if I had somehow taken a wrong path.  So for the benefit of Victor?s future guests, these are the approximate GPS coordinates:Oedolgae: 33.2390574,126.5446144Carpark: 33.2397470,126.5318070(You will pass by a cafe called 60 Beans)Along the path, there are other viewing platforms of Oedolgae Rock where it was not backlit by the sun.  However the angle was wrong, and from these other platforms, you can?t see the shape of the ?praying lady and her fallen husband?.

We visited Mount Halla National Park yesterday, Aug 25th, and it was an excellent experience and great views!It is very easy to get there by the 740 bus from Jeju Bus terminal, now here is the tricky part.. there are several entrances and trails. All of them are intense hiking. Use comfortable shoes, take lots of water and snacks.. there is nothing to buy up until the very top, which is noodle soup, water and chocolates......We took the Eorimok trail to go up to Witsae Shelter and took the Yeongsil trail to return down and my recommendation is:Take Yeongsil train, the view is by far much better than the one from Eorimok trail.In order to get there:Take 740 bus and get down on Yeongsil ticket office (@45m) and from there take a taxi to the main entrance (there is a taxi that goes up and down all the time and charges 5000). Please take the taxi, otherwise you will end up walking uphill for @2km. Once at the entrance... just follow the signs to Witse Shelter. Take lots of pictures along the way!Again ... it is uphill .. from @900m to @1750m, with lots of stairs and rock trails on both trails. Up and down in @5 hours is an ok time.Enjoy !!

We visited Jongbang waterfall (諛⑺) during our stay in Seogwipo. It's very conveniently located and easy to find. Entry fee is just 2000. There's very short hike (~130 steps) to get to the waterfall. It's a small-ish waterfall and don't expect it to be Niagara Falls kind of but the view is nice. Once you get down the stairs there are rocks that you can walk over to get to the bottom of the Falls, take some nice pictures and feel the water droplets. I wouldn't say it's THE things to do in Jeju island but if you happen to be staying in Seogwipo or driving by, it's worth a visit. It takes less than an hour and can be visited with kids...and if you happen to go here try some orange juice or chocolates!!

We visited Jeju only for Hallasan mountain! There are two ways on top, one easier and one harder! We took the easier to get on top and the harder to get back down! Once on top you will have a beautiful view over the national park and the island! Take some good shoes with you if you want to take the harder trail! The park is easy to reach by bus
We visited Jeju in the off season so the outside wasn't what it normally is, but the inside was absolutely beautiful.

We visited in the Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju around late Nov 2017, and it was quite empty when we visited.  The entry charges was pricey considering the only activity was to look at teddy bears in glass casings.  The glass casings made it difficult to take nice photos, as there were lots of reflections.  However, the kids enjoyed the place very much.  There is also an outdoor area (don't miss it, very nice place to take photos).  Overall, an above-average place to visit, but it is indoors so if the weather is bad, this is a place you can drop by.

We visited here in the fall during the annual Peanut Festival...yes, peanuts are grown on this island off the east coast of Jeju Island.  Autumn was a good time to visit there because it was cooler and not so crowded.  Our pension owner, Mr. Lee, picked us up at the ferry and drove us to our accommodation, right across the coast road from the famous white coral beach, the only one of its kind in Korea.  The coral beach was beautiful but much smaller than I'd expected and impossible to walk on without closed shoes.  The pension, called The Log House, is not only close to the beach, it is close to a cluster of restaurants and coffeeshops.  It is possible to do a lot of hiking and go up to the lighthouse for a 360 view and to catch the first glimpse of sunrise...which can be spectacular.  Because it was during the Peanut Festival, we could sample peanut wine and other local products, including several types of peanut icecream. We had a great room at the pension, on the corner with great views of the fishing boats and the famous Sunrise Peak crater across the channel.  The pension owner, Mr. Lee, spoke enough English to take care of all our needs.  At other pensions, little to no English is spoken by the staff/owners.  The owner also drove us to the ferry the next day.  Although bikes and ATVs are available for rent, the roads are a bit curvy and narrow for my comfort level.  If you like adventure, go for it!  Be sure to bring your international drivers license.  Enjoy!

We visited here as part of of our cruise ship day tour of the island. This is a very pretty place with amazing photo opportunities throughout. We purchased one of our favorite souvenirs from a kiosk selling genuine Jeju produced hats. We enjoyed the gardens and the walk over the bridge with the amazing views of the gorge and waterfalls. Be aware that the VERY long walk down to the   close-up   of the waterfalls is rather taxing and may not be worth the effort. Overall, a great experience!

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We visited during Dec'18 winter season and was raining the day before.  Temperature is a few degree lower when inside the cave.  Place was kept in its natural condition without much   enhancement  . Highly recommended for new visitors to Jeju....

We visited a total of 3 waterfalls (including Jeongbang Waterfall) for our recent trip to Jeju Island.  This was my favourite among the 3 waterfalls visited, as it was rather unique, flowing directly into the sea.  However, when we were there on a weekday afternoon, it was nice and quiet for only a few minutes, then a huge group of teenagers / students arrived and filled up the whole place.  It was too crowded and we had difficulty finding space to walk on the rocks and to take a good picture was nearly impossible.We would have stayed longer if it didn't get so crowded.

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We travelled on a rare rainy day in Jeju, but June, our tour guide, made our trip happy and smooth with her professional arrangement, detailed introduction of the scenic spots, fluent English, sharing on Korean culture and her personal experience on how she feels about Jeju. I am particularly impressed by the guided tour she gave us in the Manjanggul Lava Tube, her intriguing story of haenyeo and their livelihood and our hiking experience at Seongsanilchul Pong. In as short as a day we have seen most of what lies in the northern and eastern coasts of Jeju Island, felt for ourselves the beauty of the natural landscapes and understood how inhabitants of this island have lived since the last century. It was an amazing travel experience and we give credits to June for the nice private tour.

We took up this challenge in early April, just stepping into Spring. We took the bus from Jeju Express Bus Terminal, took about 40 minutes to reach the Eorimok bus stop. Before taking the bus though, we highly recommend to check with the Tourist Information Center just outside the bus terminal on the last returning bus. Thankfully we checked, the last bus in March period was 4.55pm at Eorimok. Summer periods probably have a later last bus back. This bus serves the Yeongsil trail entrance as well.There is still a ~20 mins walk along the road before reaching the entrance to the Eorimok trail. Impressive mountain views once you reach the park entrance.The Eorimok trail starts off deceptively tame for about 500m. Once you get the past the wooden bridge, the tough hike starts. For the next 2km, we experienced the toughest climb of the entire trail. Steep and large steps at times, with large, uneven rocks littering the way up. The view is mostly green at this point.Near the end of the first 2km, we started to see melting ice along the trail. Certain parts were still iced up; we had to climb on top of the ice to traverse. Due to the melt, it was quite slippery. A hiking stick or 2 is highly recommended, though we had not brought any for our trip.After 2km, the trail leveled off into a plateau, a welcome rest after a seemingly endless slog. Strong winds and rain pummeled us that day, but all the more made the challenging climb more exciting and enjoyable. The rest of the way to the Witse Oreum was of average difficulty, and the landscape was foggy and snowy/icy. We encountered many instances that we had to walk on the ice so be sure to be equipped with good shoes to reduce the chance of slipping on the ice.We finally reached the Witse Oreum after about 3 hours, and bought and slurped down the ramen and its soup, as well as a chocolate energy bar. They also carried stuff like crampons and plastic sheet raincoat (we bought it for the heat trapping characteristic rather than for shielding against rain, we foolishly did not expect snow and ice in April tbh :P).We originally wanted to go down via the Yeongsil trail which meets the Eorimok trail at the Witse Oreum, but a pair of local, seasoned hikers who turned back for Eorimok warned us that the Yeongsil trail is still mostly frozen over and is very difficult to traverse at this time. Due to the lack of proper equipment, we heeded their advice and went back down Eorimok instead.The trip down was much faster, but hurt our knees more due to the impact. Tread with care as the uneven terrain may cause slip and falls.The journey down took approximately an 1.5 hours.Overall it was really challenging but fun.Things to note:1. Take note of the last bus timing or you may have to hitch a ride back to town.2. And of course, cater buffer time to reach the bus stop, there is still a 20 min walk to it.3. Hiking gear, especially proper shoes and a hiking stick or 2 is highly recommended.4. Early April features unmelted snow in the terrain, wear proper clothing.5. The same bus goes to the Yeongsil trail, may want to try hiking that as well (on different days of course)6. The Eorimok is pretty challenging for a novice like myself, heard from locals that the Seongpanak trail on the Eastern side is more relaxing but longer.7. The Eorimok trail does not reach the summit, if you want to reach the summit, try the Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa trails instead.

we took tour to east of Jeju fm our guesthouse, Yeha. We intended to go to Seongsan Ilchulbong that why we were excited to know our time was perfect with Yeha tour. No idea that Seongsan Ilchulbong had sooo many stairs, we took a lot of stops before top. While we took rest, we turned back and saw beautiful view down the hill. Once we got on top, the view was so nice as well. It was worth it every single stair by looking the view from the top.We enjoyed our time to go down, windy and cold. We also enjoyed performance woman diver and saw directly what they collected fresh from the sea.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called   Manjanggul Cave Entrance  . However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

We took the Hallasan Yeongsil trail up to Witseoreum Shelter and back in early January (winter). The views were fantastic and the hike was just the right distance for us (1.5 hours up, 1 down). It was challenging but didn't wipe us out. Make sure you stop and have some noodles at the shelter, as dumb as it may sound I found this part to be the highlight of my Jeju experience. It would pay to do a small amount of research if you are planning to go as there are multiple trails of different lengths and difficulty. The Yeongsil trail is fairly easy apart from one steep section with ropes which were tricky in the snow (mainly going down). Most of the trail features steps when required, is well signposted and has guide ropes along the ridges. Also, make sure you head out early: we did and shared the path with only a few hikers but on our way down came across masses of people trying to go up. Most of the late arrivals didn't have snow crampons and/or not enough fitness/experience for this hike and many seemed to be turning back once it got steeper. I don't think they would had a very good time. You can buy cheap crampons at the bottom at the trail entrance and apart from warm clothes the only equipment you would need in winter (maybe hiking poles if bad knees or unsteady). In warmer months, some good boots, snacks and water would be fine.

We took the ferry to Udo Island. We went as walk ons with our tour guide. The ferry ride was short and easy. We were happy we had our guide with us because the weather was not very good that day and they were closing down the ferry service due to rough seas. We were glad she could translate this information for us.  We went over for a short visit and took the last ferry back to Jeju which was around noon. Because of the ferry schedule we did not have much time on Udo. We did go to 2 lookout spots. They were very pretty but the weather interfered. It would be a nice place on a sunny day, but there doesn't seem to be much to do on the island so plan on relaxing.

We took the ferry from jeju to udo as it was a must see... we went there off season, it might be the reason why we were not impressed by anything on the island, and disappointed for the beaches. must be tried during the tourism season otherwise you will face many closed activities

We took the Eorimok trail up and the Yeongsil trail down. It was snowy and we didn't have cramps on our shoes, better take some cramps. The last bus (740) back to Jeju-city goes about 16:30,  later you need to use a taxi.

we took some interesting shots. cool place to spend some time outdoors, it's not too big and easy to walk around. definitely worth going there!! in fact, we thought this was pretty much the most interesting thing in Jeju

We took ride on bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street to visit Teddy Bear Museum jeju which is nearby to Jungmun  tourist resort. Bus fare cost us only KRW 1150 per pax. The visit to Teddy bear museum was fantastic especially for my sister, teddy bear lover. It was amazing to see many collection of teddy bears from all over the world with different themes and events globally.  There were three sections of the teddy bear museum; starting from the history, artwork and forest of teddy bear. There was a garden outside of the museum with the construction of enormous teddy bear. We can get a glimpse of the LV and Swarvosky teddy bear. The most nostalgic teddy bear was the Princess Hour theme teddy bear. The most great thing to watch was the Elvis Presley show. However, the teddy bear sold there was expensive. It was worth to visit this place.

We took bus 701 from Jeju city... it only took 1hr 30mins when we were told it would take 2hrs which was a pleasant surprise. The walk up is (unsurprisingly) hard because of all the steep and often uneven steps. I would suggest going in the morning or late afternoon when it's not so hot because in the heat it was tough! People say it takes 20 mins which I would say is accurate but of course depends on your fitness levels. It was so worth it though, the views are incredible. They have an amphitheater like viewing platform I guess for those wanting to see sunset/sunrise. And you go down a different way so no clashing with people coming up. It can get quite busy though!

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

We took a taxi from our hotel in Jeju City, which took about an hour, to the Ferry Terminal. It was pretty easy to buy the ticket. Once we got to the island, it wasn't really clear what to do, so we followed everyone to a small building that was selling bus tour tickets. We didn't get the bus we wanted, though they both seem to just drive around the island and you can hop on and off. We found out later that we could have rented a little tricycle moped. We enjoyed ourselves. Worth the trip.

We took a relaxing stroll through a beautiful forest Bijraim Nutmeg Forest. The shade of the forest is perfect for a hot summer day. It's a beautiful small forest, but getting there was a bit time-consuming, involving a bus ride from Jeju City and some brief hitch-hiking. (We were to take a second bus, but we waited so long that decided to hitch a ride instead.) However, from Bijraim, there is a bus that takes you directly to the popular Manjanggul, so it's a good idea to visit both in the same day.

We took a local bus from Jeju City to Manjanggul Cave. It's 2,8 km walk from the bus stop to the entrance of the cave. You can hire a taxi, if you don't feel like walking. Just outside the entrance you can find a restaurant and a kiosk. The entrance fee was very cheap (2000 won). There are quite many stairs when you go down to the cave. The floor of the cave is a bit uneven, but still quite easy to walk on. The cave is quite dimly lit, moist and cold. I recommend bringing a jacket with you. All that said the cave isn't maybe a best spot to visit with small children or elderly people. For healthy adults the cave is a nice experience. There is information in English about the different formations and the history of the cave. There is only one entrance to the cave, so if you walk to the end and back, it's total of 2 km of walking. I recommend visiting Manjanggul Cave, if you're interested in Unesco heritage sties and natural beauty!

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu ? called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.

We took a cab from our hotel to this market, about 20 mins ride and we alighted at 1 of the entrance where we were greeted with stalls selling the famous Hallabong Oranges. The market is divided into different sections where there are sections selling fresh seafood, vegetables, fruits, cooked food, clothes, snacks etc. This is also the place where tourists will buy the popular souvenirs like the Mandarin Orange JeKiss brand chocolate and Hallabong Oranges related products at a cheaper price compared to the airport. A market worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

We took a cab from Jejusi Shinjeju to Yongsil trail. Cost us around 23000krw for a 30mins ride. We started hiking at 1.30pm (trail closes at 2pm) and hiked for close to 2 hours up to 1650m. Total height was around 1900++ m. Didnt reach all the way to the top. However, the view was spectacular. Defintely believe it is one of the must visit places in Jeju.

We thought we're going to be at the base only because we brought along our 3 years old son.To our surprise, our son can complete the route going up and down by himself (he refused for me to carry him). The steps were quite easy and it's really worth it.If you miss this, your visit to Jeju-do is incomplete.

We thought that since we are here in Jeju that we should visit Hello Kitty Island to buy our niece some gifts.  It turned out to be a big mistake.  First, there was this steep entry fee that you have to pay just to get into the building.  Then there was this lack of history on Hello Kitty.  Not educational for kids at all.  Finally, the stuff they sell at the gift shop were so expensive it put Japan to shame.  Not much of the products even have the trademark for specific sites.  Hello Kitty fans beware!!  You are better off going to Seoul to get gifts than here.

We stopped here on a whim to go zip lining which was pretty tame but a lovely way to view the green tea fields from above. The guides were good but very minimal English. We stopped and had some green tea ice cream at the cave cafe which is really unique. It's a true cave which gives you a break from the Jeju heat and humidity. The server here spoke English and was really nice even helping people take photos at the cave   photo spot.   We enjoyed the small tea museum too but would have appreciated translations for the exhibits. Overall a fun couple of hours.
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: We stayed in old jeju side and this fish market is located 5 minutes by walk to our hotel. A lot of souvenirs, local foods, dried fishes, seafoods and street foods. This place is a must visit and people are very hospitable

We stayed in a pension (inn) near Oedolgae for the 2nd time and it's still as beautiful as I remember it the first time 3 years ago. One of Jeju island's great   Olle   trails (#7) passes through here so you can include Oedolgae Rock in a half-day or even daylong seaside walk of up to 10 km or more. The hordes of tourists come nowadays as the province has built more facilities and cut down some trees but it's still a poetically pretty spot worth a look. Come early or late if possible and have it all to yourself.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal as we knew that we needed to take an early bus to Hallasan. We noted that we needed to reach a certain point on Hallasan by 12.30pm as they would not allow people to continue to hike up after 12.30pm due to foreseen danger. We took bus 782 at 6.00am sharp from seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and alight at Seongpanak bus stop to start our hike at Hallasan.
