We got some peanut ice cream, and some tea with honey and the special jeju fruit that i can't name (which was absolutely incredible!!!) since everything else was sold out. I would have loved to spend more time there because we only got 3 hours on Udo. In all, it was an amazing and memorable experience.

We approximate the climb to be about 2,200 steps. So about an hour  to get up and down. The view while climbing to the top is breathtaking. You get a 360 degree view of Jeju. The stairs for climbing are easy for short legs like mine. They've got railings for you to hold on to and some rest points every so often. There are speakers located in certain areas as well to tell you the history of the place in Korean and Japanese. I'm pretty sure there's an English and Chinese version too. There's a person at the top too to give you some information regarding the place. There are some shops located at the foot of the place where you can eat and shop as well. The journey to the top was better than the view of what was on top.

We agreed that visiting the Jeju Stone Park in the snow was one of the most enjoyable experiences we have had in Korea. The stones, sculptures, houses and other artefacts, as well as the lovely walks are beautiful in the snow. It also meant only a few people were visiting, so it was very peaceful and serene. The museum was excellent, very educational, and we really appreciated how the different lava types were displayed as sculptures. They are beautiful, nature?s art!

Waterfalls are very accessible in Jeju. Jeongbang is the most unique as we seldom see a waterfall that goes straight to the sea. Going by public bus is easy and the path towards the falls are already paved except for the rocky part near the falls itself. I suggest you take your time in sitting on one of the rocks and just enjoy the relaxing view. If you're patient, you can wait for 10-20 mins for tourists to leave and you can have the view all by yourself.  For photography enthusiasts, have a wide angle lens ready =D

Watching the sunrise at Seongsan Ilchulbong was definitely the highlight of my stay at Jeju. We had reserved a hotel right next to the attraction (Hotel Aroha), which was a very wise decision as all we had to do at 5 am in the morning was to get up, get ready and get going. There were hardly any people when we had started our ascent roughly 45 mins to an hour before sunrise. The hike itself is ~30 mins or less, but it can be a bit tiring because of the steep steps. We stopped a few times to catch our breaths and also interact with the locals. We had close to 10 mins before the sunrise by the time we were at the peak. The view from the sunrise is gorgeous, and even amidst so many people around you, it is still not chaotic but calm and serene. We stayed at the top for over 2 hours, taking pictures, resting, and even listening to some folk music being played by local artists. Great experience overall!The descent isn't tiring, so we took our time taking pictures and taking in the gorgeous views. At the base, we had freshly squeezed orange juice from Jeju oranges, which are again a must try!

Was wanting to catch sunset in Jeju, and it seems all will require some climbing. My family was tired, and hence chose this place instead.Not too bad for being lazy to climb. You will need to go to the far end near the hotel. The road alongside was quiet and very light traffic, so you can park there temporarily to view the sunset.

Was recommended to find dinner on this street so we decided to check it out but ended up having the best dinner in jeju. Was gonna go into a famous corner shop but the wait was too long so we went to the one beside it (2nd shop, sorry don't know the name). Ordered a mixed grill so we had black pork and abalone (famous in jeju too) with the other dishes too. Great selection of side dishes as well. But it was really expensive, maybe around 70AU$ but felt that it was worth it.

Was lucky to have been here as it was free for the entrance. Usually per entry would cost 2000 won but it was a holiday. The scenery and view is amazing up top. The view of the crater is nice but the view 180 degrees around is way better. You will see the town which you stopped at and the immense coastline around. Would highly recommend if you can catch the sunrise however it is quite a journey away from the Jeju city which means you have to time your travel right. Visiting during normal hours will still give you the breath taking view. Just a catch, you would have to hike. If you are fit enough, it should take you 15 to 20 mins up top. Can be pretty steep so take your time and rest along the way.

Want to do a bush walk with nice scenery ?  Eorimok Trail & Yeongsil Trail in Hallasan National Park in Mt Halla will be a good choice when you visit Jeju Island in South Korea. Be sure to take a bush hat, sun screen lotion and bottles of water. Along the trails, there are a couple of water refill spots for refilling water from the mountain. The cheapest way is to take a bus No. 740 from the Jeju City Outer Bus Terminal if you stay at Jeju city.  Get off at the stop for the entrance to Eorimok Trail. From there, it will be uphill passing nice vegetation & trees until you reach Yeongsil Trail. Follow this Yeongsil Trail, you may be lucky to see Mt Halla deer. Once you start walking downhill on the Yeongsil Trail, you will see beautiful mountain scene. At the exit of Yeongsil Trail, you will need to walk a couple of Km downhill along the road to reach the Yeongsil Entrance to get the bus 740 back to Jeju City Outer Bus Terminal. Bus 740 travels between Jeju City and Seogwipo-si and uses the same bus stop at Yeongsil Entrance. When you get onto the bus, be sure it is going back to Jeju City Outer Bus, not the bus going to Seogwipo-si.[ The walk on Eorimok Trail & Yeongsil Trail will easily takes 5 hours plus.   Air brushes are available at the entrance / exit of the trails ]

Walking on the beach, relaxing, and chilling.It was 20,000 Won Taxi cap from Jeju Lotte Hotel, and you don't have to keep your taxi waiting for you because there are many taxis in this erea. Pass by the delicious Pizza restruant which called   Donato's  . It is Five Min by walking. Also there is a nice park close to it.

Walking between different kind of plants. It is nice for who love nature. Also I love folk village, cave, and Bonsai tree. It was 20,000 Won Taxi cap from Jeju Lotte Hotel, and you don't have to keep your taxi waiting for you because there are many taxi in erea.

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. The area that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock is apparently the filming location of the Korean drama series, Jewel in the Palace (鸚㏝룝).For more of my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/oedolgae-rock-and-great-sea-view.html
Walk up to the peak & you'll never regret...Healing by nature. Can see beautiful view of Jeju.Though a bit tiring to walk up to peak, you'll be amazingly surprised.Will come again soon!

Visiting Manjanggul Cave is one of the main reason I visited Jeju. I and my family were not disappointed at all. We visited during late June 2015. The cave is a little bit cooler inside even in a hot summer day so remember to bring a jacket especially for kids. There was rain before our visit so the cave inside was a little bit wet but we could go inside and visit. There is a steep stair in the beginning of the tunnel/cave so one must walk very carefully. After entering the cave, there is no more stair and on flat level mainly.The whole cave is well lit so you should be able to see inside without bringing your own flashlight torches. (You can still bring it if you want to see everything in detail!)Only 1km of the cave is accessible by visitors. You go inside and walk to the end of the tunnel and then walk back the same way you go in. I suggest you riding a taxi to this place since public bus is not easily accessible to this tourist spot. There is a bathroom outside the cave only. So if you need to go to bathroom, you have to go before entering the cave.

Visiting Jeju ? Do it if you have at least4 days or more ! All the tourist attractions are in different corners of the island and they are far from each other .There are daily bus tours , running in one direction , starting at 9am coming back at 6 pm . Not every spot is so interesting , probably many of travellers have seen some similar somewhere else . The same is reg. this small beach . There are plenty of such beaches or even nicer around the world

Visited this place on 4 June but was closed for renovations. Luckily beside it, there is the O?셲ulloc Tea shop and museum. However this place is over crowded and the washroom is the most smelly I?셶e ever been in the whole of Jeju. Skip it and buy yr Innisfree elsewhere in Korea.

Visited this place 4 years ago, this place is full of different teddy bears, each with lots of different types of size and different types of theme. Although the place is quite packed, but we really enjoyed our trip there and took lots of photographs as memo, as this is a good place for photography. A place not to be missed in JeJu!!! Thumbs Up!!!

Visited Seongsan Ilchulbong on a rainy and cloudy day. It was very busy, even with the bad weather.You can walk up via the stairs to the top of the volcano. With nice weather I am sure the views are great. When the top is in the clouds as today, I suggest you visit the house of the Jeju woman. Pretty sure you will be impressed by the skills of these older ladies. A must visit when in Jeju Island and having nice weather.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

Visited just because it seems that if you visit Jeju, you should visit one of its lava cave. I searched on the internet, and i think this lava cave is the most popular amongst the touristIt's a very big cave indeed. We were amazed by the size of the tunnel and imagined how was the lava itself that made the cave. But actually, It's a long, cold, dark, pathway for nothing. Yeah, maybe you can find some weird shaped rocks caused by the lava. Then what? your journey will be finished on some kind of a deck to see a big rocks standing in front of you and highlighted by colored lights. That's all. And the only way back is the same way you came in from. So boring!

Visited Jeju Glass Castle on our second trip to the island visiting our son and daughter in law and our first grandchild. This attraction was not what I was expecting, it was very imaginative and well laid out, all displays were of glass, of course, some very talented glass blowers. Well worth a visit.

Visited DongMun on a Monday night after dinner at around 8pm and some seafood / fruit vendors are still open.  A small area adjacent to the market were doing bustling business selling street food / snack.  Having come from Seoul / Busan before JeJu,  DongMun market may be seemingly smaller but will still be a nice market to visit when in Jeju

Visited 4 times during my one year assignment in Jeju. Udo Island is very beautiful and peaceful. Rent a bike to tour around the island will definitely bring you fresh air and excitement. Stopped by at any cafe to try their peanut ice cream from udo! Really nice! I give average for their hallasan fried rice, it?s good to try but the taste is just normal. Udo has a very nice beaches around and good for photo:) recommend to go when you visit jeju.

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.

Very worthwhile museum to visit on Jeju.  Gives an in depth view into Haenyeo culture, female free divers who gather shell fish.  Since the culture of the Haenyeo is beginning to die out, the museum is an important way to keep the knowledge alive.  Movie and exhibits, with beautiful walks through the village and surrounding farm fields.
Very well performance. Very entertaining. The best attraction in Jeju for me. You wont regret it.They say that there is also a theater in Seoul, but i cant compare it

Very underwhelmed. Arrived by ship & took free port shuttle into Jeju-si (capital) & dropped by the Jungang underground shopping street & Guandeokjeong. Walked past Yongyeon Bridge & past park to Dongduam rock. Pleasant walk. Then back to find Black Pork St, but didn't try it as we had heard it was nothing special. Enough to fill in a day (about 6 hours ashore.) Friends who went on a trip round the island said it wasn't terribly interesting & worth the cost. Do pick up a map from the tourist info kiosk, not far from where you arrive, then you can walk round sights described

Very skilled young Mongolian horseriders, who perform a small Korean/Mongolian (horse)drama in an hour. Be aware of the showtimes, because I think they only have 4 shows a day. We were too late for the first show and while waiting for the next show we requested the taxidriver to bring and wait for us at Hallim park, which is only 10 minutes away. We also combined this with a short beach vsiit and local brunch at the beautifull Jeju-beach.

Very peaceful place that must be visited when you are in Jeju.  When you arrive in Udo, you can join the mini bus tour after getting off the ferry.  Of course, you can also rent the motorbike and drive around.  Be aware of the ferry time going back to the City.  It was definitely a highlight of my Jeju trip. xx
Very peaceful environment, surrounded with nature. Ideal to take a walk and appreciate nature. Not so much walking as in other sites in Jeju

Very nice island. You take a ferry from Jeju Island to Udo in 5-10 minutes you get there. I rented a quadricycle and it was fun to discover the island by this transportation mode. The ocean is clean and warm; pretty nice to bathe!The shops however don't speak English normally. If in Jeju, I totally recommend Udo as a spot to visit.

Very interesting road on the way from Jeju City to Hallasan. Haven?t quite figure out why at a certain stretch the car actually rolls upwards on a neutral gear and without brakes. Probably an optical illusion but I didn?t stay to figure out - better just take it as a mysterious road, it?s more interesting. There?s some statues of pigs nearby, symbolizing prosperity and many children. Take a picture, touch the pig?s head.

Very interesting display of modern and old teddy bears. Take the time to see the Elvis Presley gig in the theatre! A bit pricey and as most museums on Jeju is quite small, but worth it on a rainy day.

Very friendly and helpful to all of us, he is also very kind in recommending us the must-go attractions and even getting us discounted entrance fee around Jeju. He even brought us to the delicious restaurants, introduce us to all the different food around Jeju, gifted us some rice cakes. Would gladly recommend to my friends or anyone going to Jeju ?몟?뤍狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘

Very easy to go from Jeju city.. We took a bus and the time is less than 30mins for sure... Beside osulloc so good to visit both places same time.Did not try the soap making as the place is pretty small and it was pack then.. We ate at the cafe. Pretty layout, the ice is so so.. The food is nice thou.. The food is IG ready anytime, worth to make a trip there..

Very commercialized tour spot in Jeju island. I visited this place a few days ago. I have been travel Jeju island tens of times but this is first time to visit this village and realized this place for selling someting to tourist. If you come to this village, just look around and don't enter the house. There are a lot of good spots you can see in Jeju island
Very beautiful beach with clear water & nice scenery. For me, this is one of best place to visit in Jeju.
Various of restaurantes, and the owners of the pork restaurants on this street guarantee that they sell only Jeju?s black pig meat.

Using Mr.Kang service for 2 days. He is very very nice and helpful. We gave our itinerary and he will drive for us. He is very nice and even gave us a bunch of orange.. my father love it very much. This is my first time in jeju. He even took good picture for my family too. He is very nice, i recomend you for using his service. Thank you Mr.Kang and see you again :)

Use the city bus to the port, took me around 1h30mins from Jeju City. Bought the return ticket at kw8500/person. Rent a scooter near the port for kw25,000/2 hours. Beautiful ride with ocean scenery, due to time constraints, didn't manage to hike to light house. 2 hours is just nice to see udo with lunch and stop along the attractions. After udo can trek to sunrise peak and catch the women diver performance at 3pm. Just follow the olleh trail and you will be find.

Upon my arrival on the island, I bumped into Taiwanese travelers who recommended the Hallasan fried rice. The restaurant is within 15-20 walking distance to the port (where you got off the ferry).The fried rice was covered with vegetables and squid. The owner would go to each table to pour egg yolk and cheese and make the dish look like a volcano. While frying the rice, the owner would tell stories of the Jeju island and Udo island in fluent English. The fried rice then was turned into a heart shape. My family and I videotaped the process and had fun. Oh, the friend rice did taste yummy!

Unless you are under 12 years old or have a stuffed toy fetish, this is a very overpriced place. Nothing really much to see. Save your money for the caves and falls of jeju instead....real natural wonders.

Unless you are seriously prepared for an all out ascent, do not go on this trip.  It is beautiful, and we by no means tried it all, but our ascent from Seongpanak station was insane!  The paths are uneven, unsteady and unmaintained.  Handrails where they are most needed are not present, those that are present are in a terrible state of affairs.  To top it all off, the staff was 50%-50%...  some were excellent while others were downright rude and obnoxious...  and to end it all, I didn't like the looks of two of the taxi drivers who were ready to get into a knock-down, drag out fight with me when I selected a third taxi...  all I can say...  BRING IT!!!  I personally hope this attraction winds up out of business or under new management....   Was the low point of our trip to Jeju!!!

Unfortunately, many attractions in Jeju are man-made and not really worth your time.  However, I wish I had spent some more time at this location as it's one of the few natural, impressive landscapes that you will see in Jeju.  Sure, there's not much to see other than the cliffs and columns, but it is good to spend some time just taking it all in.  Another idea is listening to the sounds of the waves crashing the columns.  There is only a small area for you to take pictures, so I can imagine the place can get crowded during peak season and hours.  It also gets a little cold during the off-season in the fall, so beware.There is also a small park (if that's the best way of describing it) at the entrance of the cliffs that's worth a short look as well.  There are some vendors, small stone displays, and some assorted artistic pieces.

Unfortunately there was so much wind and rain during our stay on Jeju Island, based in Seogwipo. That day, we braved the elements and took the bus to visit the beautiful site of the volcano Seongsan-ri.The visit was worth the climb.

UNESCO World Natural Heritage. Geomun Oreum represents more than 300 oreums in Jeju Island. By experiencing the primitive form and history of oreum, u can learn the awe of nature. Anyone who wants to know the essence of Jeju Island must challenge. Even if u do not understand Korean, u will be impressed by what you see. Reservation required.

Udo, which means cow island because of its shape, has been a popular island trip from the island of Jeju.  Taking about three to four hour to circle on an electric bike, it?s a great day trip (there are plenty of lodgings for those who want to stay longer).  With only a handful of full size cars on its road, it?s a fantastic place to ride a bike around.  Also, for a small island, the amount of dining and cafe options are impressive. Just going around to sample some cafes and restaurants can easily fill up a full day on Udo.  As the island is famous for peanuts, there are lots of peanut flavored products available ranging from ice cream to makgeolli (Korean traditional wine).

Udo, is a small island located on the east side of Jeju Island. You can get there by taking a boat (around 20min) on the east side of Jeju. you can also bring your vehicle onto the boat and bring it to Udo.The island is quite big that you cannot walk around the island by feet. If you are not bringing your own vehicle, you can rent a ride near to the harbor BUT you need to have a driver's license. So prepare an international driver's license maybe (I am not sure if they accept international license though:( )There is also a bus that goes around the island and once you buy a ticket near the harbor, you can get off from the bus and get back into any bus without any extra charge.The sight around the island is beautiful. You can stop your vehicle at any time and enjoy and take photos.

Udo- we went early, were there before 9am. Spent roughly 3 hours on the key spots.1. Ferry to Udo- Our jumbo taxi driver drove us over. Needed to fill out all personal details plus showing our passports when purchasing tickets. Return trip for 5 of us plus driver plus jumbo taxi return was KRW70,000. No queues, not crowded. We went there on 2 Jun 2017 Friday. Just a 15-min ride, need to leave the car diring the trip. Have a good view of Sunrise Peak from the ferry.2. Peak- For a good view of Jeju and Udo, walk up to the peak. Be alert that the track along the coastline uphill is not an easy one for people who don't exercise a lot.  Useful to have hiking stick with you for this short track.3. Geommeollae Beach- Absolutely gorgeous scenery.  A must go place. That's where the famous peanut icecream shops are. There are two.  We tried one and it tasted well.4. Beaches- We went to two. Unforgettable colour and tranquility.  Must go as well.

Udo was the best place in my jeju visit. although the weather was very hot, but its windy too. My hat even blow off by the wind. The sea and sand were just too beautiful. its really a relaxing place when seeing the green grasses dancing all over in front of you. Besides, the zha jiang mian was really tasted good. it costed 8000won. the peanut icecream was famous too, 3000won. We sent a whole morning there. In the island, we can take bus, rent bicycle or scooter.

Udo was the best part of my Jeju visit. My sister and I rented scooters for two hours to get around the island, stopping wherever we wanted to take pictures or rehydrate (it was blazingly hot). We stopped at one of the beaches for a couple of hours, but it was just too hot to sit still on the sand. Rented scooters for the rest of the day and just zoomed around the island. True, there isn't too much to do on the island besides going to the beach or riding around the island. And the scooters/ATVs available for rent are a bit expensive (15,000won for 2 hours). But if you're looking for a relaxing day with beautiful sights, I highly recommend a visit.

Udo or ?Cow Island? lies off the UNESCO World Heritage island of Jeju and is so named because its profile resembles a sleeping or resting ox. The fun begins with a 15 minute ferry ride from Seongsan Harbour, costing ??5,500 return trip. As the boat glides over the choppy waters, you can watch on deck the antics of Korean school students on excursion feeding the seagulls in mid-flight, with lots of shrieks and screams. Upon arrival at Cheonjin Port, shuttle buses will be waiting to take you around the island for a round (hop-on hop-off) trip ticket which you pay after the first stop. It?s a pity we could not understand the Korean commentary provided by the bus driver, as he had his captive audience in stitches along the journey. We enjoyed the rustic scenes of thatched farm houses and fields, surrounded by the azure blue seas. We made stops at Geommeolle Beach (black sands and cliff backdrop) and Seobin Baeksa Beach (white grains of rhodolith). The half day excursion to Udo was a joyful and unruffled experience!

Udo Island, a small volcanic island 10 minutes by ferry from Jeju Island. A day out on this island can be a bore to those who have no affinity to the outdoors, particularly that of the sea.But if you love the care-free life of roaming from one sandy beach to another rocky one. In between with lots of coastal features to be awed by, then this is the little paradise on earth.Udo is an island which allows you to go the entire distance around the coastal roads, in under 4 hours, including stops for pictures, strolls, ice-cream, desserts and of course a whole host of meals.  There are rugged, rocky coastlines and little stretches of sandy beaches with emerald waters.Getting from point to point on the island is very easy, either on bicycles, rental motorbikes and scooters. Mainlainders can ferry in their car for their own pleasure. We rented a motor-scooter for 25, 000 Won for just over 4 hours. The rental is for 2 hours (Won 25000)

Udo Island is what I imagined Jeju to be..beautiful coast line beside grassy fields. A relaxing day trip soaking up the amazing scenery. Well worth the (little) effort if you are in the area, and consider a day trip if you aren't!The port is about a 15 minute walk from Sunrise Peak. You buy ferry tickets in a white dome building; start by going to one of the desks with pens and boarding cards. Fill out 2 boarding slips EXACTLY the same (one collected on your trip to Udo and the other collected on your way back). For example, we were a party of two, and on BOTH slips we wrote BOTH our names and details. When you have completed the slips, go to one of the ticket windows and present the slips with your PASSPORT (for international travellers), and if like me, you don't know any Korean at all, just smile and say   Udo  . The lady will ask you if you are returning the same day and issue you return tickets costing 5500 won each. She will also tell you the last ferry time coming back from the island, in our case (November) it was 5pm.Off we went! The ride is about 15 minutes and you get lovely views of Sunrise Peak on the way. When we disembarked, we were immediately greeted (sold to) by various venders renting out pedal bikes or motorised vehicles. We chose the   old fashioned   bikes and had a wonderful time. It costs 10000 each bike, for the whole day. We took 2-3 hours biking around the coast (map provided) taking breaks to admire the scenery and have lunch. If you didn't make any breaks, our vendor thought it would take 1-1.5 hours around. My partner and I are healthy late-20-somethings that don't bike often, but we felt the trip was pretty easy and relaxing as its mostly flat. There are not many cars either, and other motorised rental vehicles zipping by, are small scooters/2-3 seaters, so biking around feels very safe. There are numerous eateries and toilet facilities all around the island. We stumbled upon a cart selling home made pies (Bulgogi, Spicy Chicken, Red Bean and Apple) and they were delicious! I wish I knew the name of it, but if you happen to see it and feel like pies..these are yum!Fit in a trip to Udo if you can..Its a beautiful place to spend some time..

Udo Island is a small island located in the east side of Jeju. We visited there due the great reviews given below in TripAdvisor. It cost about 5,500 won for the ferry ride to and fro. My friend and I wanted to ride the ATV while we were there however the rental shops were strict on the rental without international driving license so in the end we took a tour bus that stops at 4 different locations and cost 5,000won per person. The bus comes at an interval of 30 minutes so once you get down in one location, you can stay at the location for 30 minutes before moving on to another place. As we went there in Spring, the canola flowers are blooming beautifully. We also went to the Black Sand Beach and also the Hyopje Beach. Quite a good worth of money if you are looking at short tours around the island.

Udo island is a small island at east of Jeju Island. It is named after cow because of its cow alike shape. Once you reached the island, you are able to find few bike rental shop. You can rent a electrical scooter with roof or normal scooter to tour around the island. Bare in mind the speed limit is 30 km/h. Most of the rental shop offer two hours rental only. Generally, it should be sufficient if you don't linger at each place too long. Do try the peanut ice-cream as the island is famous for peanut plantation. Get your camera ready as there are many beautiful scenaries to take photos.

Udo island in jeju is a must see attraction. From jeju have to take ferry to get there, you can take your car or you can go there and take either ATV or Motorbike to tour the island. We had took our rented car since we had bags and baby stuffs. There are many photo spots, beaches , light house etc., across the circumference of the island. A must go place if visited jeju.

Udo is simply beautiful. You should rent either a bike or a moped once you arrive. You can easily circle the whole island with stops in a couple hours. The enclosed beaches, volcanic rocks, crystal clear water, and very green landscape is exquisite.The road is not really crowded even during the busy summer months. I really enjoyed Udo Island, but then again what major natural location in Jeju-do disappoints? Whether you visit the lava tube caves, craters, dramatic coastline, waterfalls, nearby islands, beaches, mountains, and forests, Jeju-do is a natural paradise.

Udo is just picture perfect. We spent a few hours driving around this beautiful small island in early October. It only takes a few minutes on the ferry to go to Udo. You can hire scooters on the island but we actually brought over the scooters that we had hired in Jeju. It was approx 8000 (i think) to bring the scooter over and back. It was extremely busy when I was there but I did travel during Chuseok so I am not sure how busy it would be outside of holidays.I would definitely recommend a trip here as there are some fantastic and beautiful views. Just hire a scooter and drive around. As i mentioned earlier, if you are planning to hire a scooter on Jeju itself then do so and bring it over and it will be cheaper than renting one in Udo.

Udo is gorgeous and so relaxing. You can just rent a bike, they also have electric bikes and they are so easy and comfortable to ride. And on your own pace, go around the whole island in 2 to 3 hours, taking pictures, stopping by to enjoy beautoful scenary. I loved spending half a day, where you can enjoy natural beauty and simple life without big buildings, traffic or noise. Just a short ferry ride from the port in east jeju.

Udo is an island very close from Jeju-do. It's next to Seongsan-ilchul-bong, which is also famous. It takes about 15 minutes by boat from Seongsan port. You pay for entrance to the island with the boat fare. The usual course seems to be walking up the hill in Udo, Gummerlae, and checking out the lighthouse surrounded by lots of stones stacked on top of each other for wishes to come true. The weather was perfect when we went, very sunny :)

Udo is a very windy and beautiful island. The views from udo peak is breathtaking. There is a round trip udo tour bus for 5000won per pax which shuttle you to 5 attraction stops of the island. First stop is to the black sand beach where you can see the black sand beach and a cave (during low tide). If you want to go to the udo peak, you will need to walk a distance, climb up a hill to reach the udo peak. My first trip to udo was with my Jeju taxi guide and he drove us to udo and brought us up. My second time here was kinda cocked up because the udo tour bus driver only conveys in korean and our taxi guide this time did not accompany us to udo. Hence we did not made it to the peak. Nonetheless, we explored other stops (beaches and beaches). The sea and beaches are very beautiful. Udo is famous for their peanut and orange ice creams which I felt is a waste of money. Per cup of ice cream topped with some peanut or orange juice cost 5000won. Mcd ice cream taste nicer and bigger quantity. Oh yes, if you are willing to spend more you can rent bicycle and cycle around the island. And if you have international driving licence you can rent motorized vehicle to travel around. The roads are small and there's many tour buses shuttling people hence certain areas are abit congested.

Udo is a small island to the east of Jeju Island - about 1 hour bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Cheng Shan Port and take another 15 mins on a ferry to Udo.  Udo offers a beachside road around the island.  If you have an international driving license, you can rent a small electri car to drive around the island, if not, you can still rent a eletri bicycle or use local bus.  There are many restaurant and cafes along the beachside road.  Sometime you can see a small white sand beach between those dark volcano rocks.

Udo is a small island just off Jeju island and is a 15min ferry ride. Once you are there you can hike, hire a bike or get on a round island hop-on hop-off bus which are quite frequent.The island is a lava plateu but some beaches have golden sand or white coral sand.The island is lush and green and is apparently very fertile.As it is touristy, prices can be high but it is definitely worth a visit if it is a good day.Give yourself plenty of time.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.
Udo is a must visit place in Jeju island! go there as early as you can, so that you can spend a day trip there! Half day trip not enough time to look around.

Udo is a mini-Jeju, with traditional elements such as stone walls, farms, female divers and ocean cliffs all compressed into a much more manageable area. I rented a bicycle with a basket from an old ahjussi for 4000krw (3 hours). His stall, or rather tent, was located just at the ferry terminal. There are shops across the street that rent out bicycles, scooters and motorcycles.Cycling around Udo was a breeze. It was mainly flat terrain with some gentle slopes here and there. You will ride past white sandy beaches, rocky pools, farms, stone walls, female divers, cute puppies and cafes. Remember to grab some peanut ice cream, the island?s specialty.For more information and pictures on Udo, visit my travel blog https://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

Udo is a beautiful island but I would recommend a day trip as Jeju island has a lot more to offer. My friends and I climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong in the morning and then hopped on a boat to Udo, the port is very close and boats go regularly. If you have a car I would recommend leaving it behind as the queue for cars was extremely long. Once we got there we boarded one of the shuttle buses, while they're restricted in where they go it only costs 1,000 won for a single trip, versus renting an electric car that cost about 40,000 but only last 2 hours. The beach we went was not nice, the water was dirty and full of rubbish but the locals didn't seem to mind.Overall it's a nice island but the beaches on Jeju are a lot nicer and cleaner, a day trip is all I would recommend.

Udo feels like more of an island than Jeju itself, because it is much smaller and rural. You can hire a car, golf buggy, cycle or simply walk around this scenic little island. Very short and cheap ferry ride from Seongsan, so add this into your trip to Sunrise Peak.

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.

Turn off your engine, it will push your car uphill.The speed was fast, it is not magic, it is a real thing.You have to see it in person to believe it. If you go there after sun set, it will give you a chill.Must see place on Jeju island. I believe if you a tour, you will get a chance to experience it.

Travelled on September using the busdaytour. Its strange in this 100meter road, how it seemed to be going up, but yet though our bus' machine has been turned off, our bus seems to be going up, in about 5-10km/hour. Jeju people called this the ghost road, where they say that the ghosts are pushing us up.

Transportation: There are several buses that make stops at this destination, but just like everything in Jeju, rental car is the recommended mode of travel. Food: the lava tubes does have a restaurant colocated but I did not eat. There are also some snacks you can purchase here but you are not allowed to bring them down into the lava tubes. Attraction: The scale of the lava tube really surprised me. We descended roughly 30 feet into the lava tube after we purchased our tickets ($4 pp). The stairs were slippery, so be cautious when descending. Don?t worry if you have claustrophobia, The tube is about 25ft across and 20 feet high! There are no tour guides, so you won?t have anybody explaining the history or the geology of the tubes, but there are educational signs posted about every 100 feet. There was also a great museum on sit I recommend visiting prior to going into the lava tubes. Great place to visit, and it took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes.

Transportation to the island: rent a car to drive there, or get 4 people to share a cab (costs around 50,000 won from jeju city). There's also the bus option but I wouldn't recommend as its not the easiest to navigate around the ferry pier. Then take the ferry which leaves every one hour, costs around 5500 won. The ferry is a short ride, only ten mins away! Transportation within the island: the shuttle bus costs only 5000 won, pretty convenient, and it'll take you to the main 4 spots. There's also option of ATV and car rental, which id recommend ATV since its mostly single-lane roads on the island. Food: everyone wanna try the peanut flavored ice cream but I found it's extremely mediocre. It's not 'peanut flavored' but just normal ice cream with peanut powder sprinkled. Save your stomach for the seafood pot! Although not the cheapest I've had, but still pretty worth a try! Get the option with octopus cook on the table if you can stomach the scene (I know lots of my friends can't). A lot of light walking you can do around the island, the weather was still quite cold so we couldn't get into the water. I love that you can go hill climbing at one spot and the dip your toes into the (chilly) ocean the next.
Traditional Jeju folk village , heritage of timeless Jeju people living special roof architure . Famous Korea film drama site . Worthwhile to travel back to old times

Totally worth the climb! I consider myself to be a couch potato, so that claim was quite tough for me. It took me around 40 minutes, with short breaks in between. But once you get to the top, soak in the crisp fresh air, indulge in the magnificent view, you'll be wanting to do it all over again. Definitely recommend seongsang il chul bong if you are going to Jeju-do.

Took the visit for the sunset and it was pretty amazing. Nice volcano, ascension may not be top class but the view at the top is superb. Views of the crater from far away are nice too. A must on Jeju island.

took our family of 3 about 11hrs round trip. it can be done in 9 if you ha e the right gear and move fast. its gradual grade, so its not strenuous but the terrian is terrible. it is 85percent big rocky jagged lava chunks. if you are prone to ankle injury, this hike is not for u. you have to watch your feetthe whole time  which is fine since there is no view until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. so all in all i do not really recommend this hike unless you have lots of time in Jeju and you really wanna say you climbed Koreas highest peak.

Took bus 781 from City Hall in Jeju City about 30-40min bus ride for 1300KRW. Had some breakfast at the Seongpanak bus station (base camp), got a bottle of water and a snickers then started the hike. Read that it would take 8-9 hours roundtrip, got to the top in less than 3, a very slow and steady rising hike firstly through the forest and later up the mountain. Stunning views from about 1800m and up, saw some water also in the crater, quite crowded at the summit. Ate my chocolate bar, took a selfie and started walking down. Total time return trip to the bus station was 6 hours. Best tip is to not pause at the middle camp which you must reach before 12:00 if you want to get to the peak, but instead just walk on to the top and have some lunch or break up there, you will then skip most of the crowd, try to head back down before 13:00, as you need to leave the peak before 13:30 it does get crowded on the descent and will just increase your time spent by waiting for slow groups.The views are spectacular, do recommend, no fees.

Took a bus from Jeju bus terminal (1.5hrs) and arrived at the port. Ferry to Udo island is just 15 mins away. Arrived at Udo, we join the hop on & off bus that takes us to 4 destinations. Bus interval is every 30 mins. It is a beautiful island not to be misssed out. Spent at least half a day or more at the island.

Too bad we went in fall, I would have so wanted to go in those beautiful turquoise waters. But we sat in front of the beach and didnt realize how much time had passed by. The colours are impressive. My favorite beach in Jeju.

To see the sunrise, one has to wake up early and hike along the stairs and some stone steps and must remember to bring along a torchlight or use our smartphone's torchlight as it can be still very dark during the hike. My husband & I took 30 min to reach the peak, while waiting for the sun to rise there were many people waiting and getting ready their cameras. At the crack of dawn, one will see the sun starts to peak out and see the first rays of the sun grace the Earth. During that moment, everyone started exclaiming with delight as I believe it is not easy for some of us who do not have strong stamina when comes to hiking but it was worth seeing such glorious sight. If I have the chance to visit Jeju, I would want to visit this place again.

To be honest, I wasn't quite sure what to expect before I saw this show. I knew generally it was about performers who drew and entertained the audience somehow on stage. BUT IT WAS AMAZING! We saw   Team Chaplin,   four   hunky   young men, all dressed in decidedly stylish paint-splattered black clothing, complete with Charlie Chaplin bowlers. It could best be described as a multi-media show in which the performers draw using charcoal, paint, LED touch screens (I think!) and other art mediums and techniques to create a wide variety of images from pop culture and the classics, most of it set to contemporary music. They dance plus do a little martial arts, mime and comedy, and they use audience participation very effectively. Among the images are Michael Jackson, the Little Mermaid, Bruce Lee, Beethoven and Jeju's own icon, Dolhareubang, or   Stone Grandfather.   Even after seeing the show, I am not sure how some of the effects were achieved. I'm not going to do any   spoilers   here of the action, because the element of surprise is important for this show. But trust me, you WILL be surprised. It has many entertaining moments. If you live in Jeju or plan to visit, you should make time for the show, which is performed on the campus of beautiful Cheju Halla College...you'll be treated there to one of the best views of Halla Mountain anywhere on the island...take your camera for that, and for the photo/autograph session at the end of the show.

To be blunt, I couldn't see the dragon's head in the Dragon Head Rock, and I'm not alone. Apparently a portion of the formation fell off during a heavy storm long ago, so perhaps it was once more impressive. Currently, it has become iconic for a rather tired trend in Korean tourism. Pointing at the sky and finding clouds that look like other things is childlike. Officially naming rocks and then designating them as   important cultural artifacts   in order to manufacturer tourism is crass. In much the same way that the Korean government has become intimately involved in generating the so-called   Korean Wave   of K-pop and Korean television dramas, there is a constant rush to capitalize on landmarks, events, and experiences that will help distinguish Korea in general and Jeju specifically in the competitive marketplace of global cultural value. This push to invent cultural significance is monopolized by a predominately male class of older Korean bureaucrats who have capitalized on Confucian values in order to override younger, better ideas, fueling their own, often tedious marketing concepts despite the existence of far better and substantive materials from which to draw inspiration. Take for instance Jeju's rich history of folklore and deities. Sure, you can dawdle about with stories of a dragon stealing jade or herbs of immortality from Halla Mountain and being shot by a celestial arrow as punishment, turning it to stone; but the fact is there are literally hundreds of far better stories that have some basis in local lore rather than the distinctly artificial details surrounding the Dragon's Head Rock. If you're interested, look for books on the subject, some of which were written by expatriates in an attempt to save this rich heritage from being slowly whitewashed away by modern fabrications. A book called   Spirits: Jeju Island's Shamanic Shrines   by Joey Rositano comes immediately to mind. Or you can go to any number of local beaches and walk along paths where every 20 yards or so you can read a plaque that tells you what a large stone vaguely resembles if you squint hard and suspend your disbelief.    That said, there's nothing wrong with taking a nice stroll along the seaside in this part of town if you only have a short amount of time to spend and you need to get to the airport soon. There are some passable restaurants along the way, a couple of good caf챕s, and some great views of the ocean. However, make no mistake - this is an authorized conduit for tourists and as such you will be subject to a conveyor belt of people on the same walk, as well as an abundance of stores whose sole purpose is to extract money from you by selling tawdry bits of plastic.

TLDR:Long hike, not that easy if you're not fit. 8-9 hours, 19.6km in total.Bring at least 3L of water each. They do sell water at the checkpoint, though only in 600ml bottles.Wear shoes with good sole and ankle protectionConsider taking a small towel (or two) to wipe away sweatBring a warm jumper and possibly a clean, dry shirt. Even in summer it's cold at the topStart the hike before 8.30am if you want to reach the peak because if you don't make it past the checkpoint at around 7km in, before 12.30pm, you won't be allowed to go to the peak.Bring a plastic bag for your rubbish because there are no bins at all on the hikeFor those who want moreRemember that this hike is longer than an average work day and you will need to replace water lost through sweat. Pack around 3L of water per person. Also pack some protein and carbohydrate heavy snacks such as nuts and dried fruits to keep up your energy levels. If you sweat a lot, consider bringing an electrolyte drink sachet to use halfway (or buy a can of Pocari sweat at the checkpoint). At the checkpoint, you can buy instant noodles, 600mL water bottles and Pocari sweat. If you don't want noodles for lunch, bring lunch. But keep in mind it's cold at the top so some warm noodles can be perfect. The noodles are a bit spicy though, so if you don't like spicy food, maybe bring your own lunch. There are absolutely 0 facilities for heating or preparing food. They won't even give you hot water for any noodles you don't purchase from them. Also there are no rubbish bins on the entire hike so you'll need to bring a plastic bag to carry out your own rubbish. The toilets are pretty gross and may or may not have toilet paper so consider bringing tissues. Also the toilets generally have no sinks, so bring some hand sanitiser gel.A small towel or two to wipe away your sweat wouldn't go astray, and a warm coat/jacket and clean, dry shirt will make your time at the peak much more comfortable (addressed in a later section).We took the 781 bus from Jeju city hall at around 6.55am. We arrived at the Seongpanak stop around 7.25am.Make sure you give yourself enough time to get to the Jindallae Shelter (checkpoint around 7km into the hike) before 12.30pm. If you don't make it to the shelter before 12.30pm you will not be allowed to continue up to the peak. It's very disappointing, I'm sure, to hike for 7km, hoping to see the peak and then be told you can't go because you missed the 12.30 deadline. I can't stress this enough. At the shelter, we heard some Americans complaining that they had missed the deadline by 24 minutes (they had started the hike at 10.30am) and that there was no information available on the trail or online about this rule. They were wrong on two counts- there are at least 5 signs along the trail up to the shelter stating that you need to pass by 12.30pm (in English). Also there are a number of blogs about this hike online which also talk about the rule. Now we started at around 7.30am and made it to the shelter by 10am, but we didn't stop to rest at all before the shelter. The walk up to the shelter is 90% easy level with gentle slopes and a few short harsher sections. If you are fit enough to contemplate doing a 19.4km hike then this section should be fine for you. If you start the hike around 8.30am, you will have no issues making it to the checkpoint in time and you should make it back to the bottom by 6/6.30pm. Earlier if you don't rest too long and are relatively fit.Note: there are several places that you can stop to rest just after the shelter. If you are running close to the 12.30pm deadline, just get past the shelter and then stop to rest once you've gone past. Just make sure you don't rest too long because you've probably got another 5-6 hours before you get back to the end of the trail including the rest of the walk to the peak, and you don't want it to get dark or have to rush on the way down.The next section after the shelter is graded as 'normal' by the signs along the route. This section does have a few challenging sections but also some easier stretches as well. If you have regular short rests then it's manageable for people of minimal to moderate fitness with some huffing and puffing.The last 1-1.5km of the walk to the peak is where it starts to get difficult. By this stage you've already hiked uphill around 8km and for probably 3-3.5 hours. The way to the peak is hundreds and hundreds of stairs often with many oddly shaped rocks to navigate around whilst traversing increasingly steep steps. If you're not super fit then you will struggle on this section. At one point we were setting ourselves goals to make it up 3 sets of staircases before we would rest for 1 minute then start again. But the important point is you are so close to the top now, so just keep pushing.The top can be quite crowded. We made it by around 11.30am and hung around for about 30mins to take photos and admire the view. My next piece of advice is- bring a warm jumper because the wind is cold up there and if you're anything like me, you will be sweaty which makes the wind even colder. Another point: if you're a sweaty person, consider bringing an extra dry/warm shirt (or two) with you to change into at the top (and possibly on the way back down). If you're prone to sweat a lot, this can make a huge difference to your enjoyment at the peak because you will by dry and warm. Your photos won't look so sweaty either. Make sure you take a picture of all members of your party with the peak stone marker or the crater to prove that you reached the top.Keep in mind that the way back down can take longer than the way up because you are now passing many people on their way up and going down is very hard on your already exhausted legs and feet. It can take 4-5 hours to get back down from the peak. We started going down at 12pm and made it to the bottom by 4pm, but we stopped several times.The path is quite narrow so on your way down, you will have to stop to let people pass in the other direction many times (unless it's significantly past the 12.30pm deadline, in which case everyone will be going down). The section between the peak and the checkpoint is very hard on your feet and legs. It will feel like forever but just remember that the track gets gradually easier and gentler the closer you are to the end. Stop at the checkpoint for lunch if you haven't already had it, or you feel like some hot noodles to warm you up.Keep on all the way down, being very careful not to slip. There are many rocks and if they are slightly wet, they are very slippery. Eventually you'll make it to the bottom. Then you can take your photographic evidence of reaching the peak to the little tourist office and for 1000 won each, you'll get a certificate saying that you reached the 1950m summit of Mt Hallasan. Congratulations!Sore feet and legs and weary bodies, you can catch the 782 bus back to Jeju city for a well earned rest.

Though Dongmun turns to commercial rather for local market, its interesting to see the rich supply of seafood in Jeju. If you know Mandarin, you can communicate with the food stall owners. Quite smelly and dirty, which is expected.

This's one of the must-visit attraction in Jeju, also one of 7 new wonder of the world. It worth to climb up all stairs as you can see so beautiful scenes with mountain and the ocean, especially when you reach the peak, along with amazing trails like you often seen in Korean drama. we spent around 3hrs here, mostly for taking photo, then had lunch at Mc.Donald at the entrance of Seongsan.Admission fee is 2000w/pax. we got here by intercity bus no. 710 (East side) from jeju bus terminal and #710-1 on the way back. it took about 1hr 10 mins

This well set out and very informative museum recounts the history of how many of the Jeju islanders were killed and repressed during the late 1940s and early 1950s.  The visitor passes through a series of rooms, each explaining in Korean and English a different stage in the tragic events.  Apart from the actual events themselves, two things shocked me most.  Firstly, that I had never before heard of the April 3 Uprising, although some 25-30,000 people were killed by Korean government forces and their supporters.  Secondly, that even well into South Korea's democracy the events continued to be hushed up and only relatively recently has the truth begun to be told.  Just a few years ago, mass graves were discovered near jeju airport.  The museum provides such a valuable insight into the island's past that I think no visit to Jeju would be complete without coming here and learning about the events and their aftermath.  Entry is free of charge.  The peace park around the museum provides a place for contemplation after visiting the museum.

This waterfall was my favorite thing I saw on Jeju Island.  It is a beautiful waterfall that empties into a small pool draining directly into the ocean, and it's a lovely spot to just enjoy the sounds of the water and the tide.  Very much worth the visit.

This waterfall is easily accessible in south Jeju Island with spacious parking lot at entrance.  Entrance fee is 2000 won, reasonable and worth a visit.  We arrived around 4:50pm and was just in time to watch the sun set there.  If you want to get closer to the waterfall, be prepared to get a slightly wet but it?s a great experience.

This was the same village that Dae Jang Geum (鸚㏝룝) was filmed. It looked like a huge place in the show but in actual fact is that this place is really tiny! It should not take anyone more than 10 mins to complete. We were shown how water was collected from the rain by wrapping a rope on the tree that links into the water pots. The tourguide said that in those days, women in Jeju island work while the men stay at home. The lady touring us in the area carried the water trout to show us how Jeju women in the past used to carry water. There is one small house that according to the lady, is still inhabited. We were not allowed to enter but we can take pictures from outside the house. The house smells of the aroma of freshly cooked rice. We were told that someone is actually cooking. After touring the small compound comes the main part of the program - promoting honey. It seems like there are many version of how real honey should be. For this version, the honey doesn't melt in water. One can see the hives when it's placed in water and swirled around. We were given different honey to try: Pure honey, lingzhi and 5 flavors. For some reasons, they also sell handcream made of horse oil. It smells quite nice though. But I still have a whole box of lanolin cream at home so decided not to buy. They are not cheap either.

This was the only waterfall we visited in Jeju and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Unlike the others (according to what I read online), you can walk right up to the waterfall itself, although you'll need to brave the rocks to do it. Loved sitting here right by the edge of the water and just letting the spray wash all over me.

This was the last stop of our tour so the sun was setting by the time we got there. I recommend coming in the morning for good pictures. It was quite solemn, cold, and eerie because it was just the tour guide of the village, our tour guide, and the rest of our group in the area. The assigned tour guide had very interesting insights on the place and the rest of Jeju culture. She also sold us some products that the folks of the village made. The berry honey is definitely worth buying.

This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience. It's basically a geology lesson on the impact of lava flows. It was interesting though perhaps a little too academic for non-geologists like me. It's dark though and you have to be careful where you step as this is, after all, a cave not a paved walkway. On the whole, it was a unique experience and it gave me a different view of the beauty of Jeju.

This was the first place to visit before we headed to other place in Jeju Island.O?셎ulloc Tea Museum is also located here and we just stopped by there for lunch and check out the products at Innisfree Jeju House. The lunch was not cheap , it's organic, There were also some visitors who were learning how to make soap, I think we need to pay for that course. I just bought a box of mini masks and move on to other places.Not too bad for a short lunch time and for photos maybe. To go about Jeju Island is best with to rent a car as it's more convenient to go for one places to another unlike in Seoul or Busan where subway are available.

This was recommended by a friend and it ended up being the highlight of our trip in Jeju! We rented an ATV and just drove around the island taking in the sights. Udo Island is also where the famous women divers go to catch abalone, octopi and other seafood and it was cool just to watch them work. The shore caves were definitely a must-see for us and they did not disappoint. I would definitely go back to Udo if I'm ever in Jeju again.

This was rated as one of the top 3 to visit in Jeju so we actually stayed at the nearby Airstay Hamdeok Hotel.  It  was very nice.  The beach is clean and had pristine waters and black rocks.  The sand was fine and felt good to walk on with your bare feet.  There were some really nice picturesque views so we took a ton of photos. There was a connected path to a hill and it allowed for some decent small hikes.  We went in March so the flowers on the hill were blooming with yellow and purple colors.  There were also some white flower blossoms coming out from the trees. With the ocean or the city views in the background from the hill, it allowed for some very unique photos for your memories.  After the little hike, we played around in the water on the beach and it was nice because it was low tide and you could hang out in one of the exposed sand bars. It was very pretty and relaxing. Definitely a must see if you're in Jeju!

This was our second trip to Udo.   We were riding around Jeju Island by bicycle so decided to explore the island on foot.   The weather was very hot and exposed (Summer), so you really need a big hat.    The island is quite unique, we walked up through the middle of the island and enjoyed the barren landscape.   We came across a Buddhist temple and met the lone monk there who chatted and gave us cups of coffee and tea.  He also introduced us to his friends - a haenyeo and visiting Butoh dancer who we interviewed for our website.   We briefly visited the beaches which were nice but crowded.  The unique landscape and interesting people was the best thing about Udo.

This was our first stop during our weekend trip to Jeju. I had heard about these women before but didn't know much. First, they showed us a video (in English) all about the history. I was immediately hooked! The rest of the museum is so interesting. The pictures and artifacts tell a great story. I just wish I could have met the Haenyeo personally! Also, the women working at the museum were nice and helpful as we tried to get to our next stop.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.

This was one of the stops for the Jeju Golden Bus Tour. Since we were hungry, we got off this stop and wandered into the Dongmun market. There were lots of seafood and stalls selling Korean food; we had grilled mackerel and fish soup. With rice and lots of side dishes, the meal came to 15000 won. Though the sellers couldn't speak English, they had menus in English. Get your hallabong chocolate here too. So many other flavors to choose from as well and with so many shops competing here, you are spoilt for choice. Unfortunately, we didn't buy and regretted when we realised when other tourist places in Jeju city didn't have the the range offered in Dongmun market.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.? There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

This was one of the nicest places I had   paid   to visit in Jeju and you may ask why, when all they have is glass?I love Glass Blowing and my main reason was to make something that I can take back, unfortunately you cant collect what you make until the next day, so I had to skip this.However with a Blue Sky Day the of colors of the glass and the designs, gave me some of the best photos I have of us as a couple.

This was one of the most popular things to do in jeju and we stayed close by so was a no brainer. Cost $11,000krw to get in, and had heaps of different plants and flowers from different parts of the world etc. overall not too bad, october is the off season to go so was very quiet. If you love plants you?ll love this if not properly not the place for you.

This was one of the most exciting UNESCO sites I travelled to while in Jeju. The cave is a true demonstration of the power of nature. The walls are beautifully scarred by the movements of lava. It is definitely a place to visit for any geologist out there as well as any layperson. Not to mention, it was nice and cold down there, which is a blessing in the summer heat!

This was one of the few places in Jeju in which I wished I had more time to explore and actually take the trail up the the crater.  Moreover, the place is a UNESCO World Heritage site.The attraction is located on the eastern edge of Jeju Island.  I've heard the place is good for sunrises (why it's nicknamed Sunrise Peak).  However, that may be difficult to do if your hotel is in the Jeju City or Seogwipo areas and so far away from the attraction.  There is also a trail that heads up to the edge of the crater - which I unfortunately did not have the time to walk - but I would definitely advise anyone to take that trail if you have the time.  There is also an opportunity to go horse riding, but it looked like it was more for kids rather than adults.I did have the time to walk on the lower parts of the attraction - near the bay/harbor/cliffs area.  Notably, the area is extremely windy and cold, so be sure to bring the correct clothing especially during the off peak season.  There are some spectacular views of the cliffs and of Udo Island if the sky is clear enough on that day.  There are also some female divers that   perform   at 1:30 PM and 3 PM - although I did not get the chance to see them - if you take a trail to walk down to the bay/harbor area.This is definitely a must-see place to visit in Jeju and you'll get a lot of great photos here.

This was one of our stops in our taxi tour for that day.This is a small place showing the traditional homes of that area a long time ago.  It?s free. An English speaking guide will tour you around.  Some interesting facts, like two separate doors (one bigger for the male I think.) They will offer you a drink made of honey and some fermentation of some berries.  It?s like juice but with some tart aftertaste.  Taste good though that we spent I think $40.00 for a bottle.  In hindsight, maybe a bit too much considering it?s not an alcoholic drink (tongue in cheek).  But while drinking that juice at home, it sure brings in mind our visit to Jeju.  While there we saw a black pig with a small companion rat.  Well seems the rat was hovering near the pig pen.  Interesting place and the guide did tell some interesting stories and tidbits! (Can be done in half an hour).

This was one of my favorite parts of Jeju. We went during the sunrise which reading everywhere said was most ideal, and it was gorgeous. It?s a lot of steps to get to the top. I would suggest bringing a bottle of water.

this was one of  the most memorable places i visited in jeju. the coast was not an easy walk through, there were 2 entrances/exits for the coast. we took the one with large rocks we had to climb down through. (would recommend taking the other entrance which was behind a large ship) it was scary and there were a lot of sea roaches scurrying around. the VIEW AND WALK around the coast was worth everything though. the coast right infront of sabangsan mountain was filled with canola flowers.

This was not part of our main itinerary but we visited it as it was raining in other parts of Jeju.We saw the acrobatic performance, it was rather entertaining and sometimes hilarious though some parts were boring for us. The kids enjoyed it though. There was some reenactment of a story but it was all in Korean so we only got the gist of it.

This was my best experience in Jeju. I went in October 2013 and we went up Yeongsil and down by Eorimok. The hike was not the most difficult, but can be quite crowded. We arrived by car around 8am and there was a queue to the carpark. Note that there are two carparks, one on the lower level (where buses drop you off) and one at the start of the trail. We waited about 45 mins to get into the first carpark, and when we saw that there was another queue to go up, we just parked at the lower carpark and started our hike from there. This is a good idea if you plan to go down by Eorimok - you won't have to climb up to get your car after taking to bus from Eorimok to Yeongsil.The hike in autumn was wonderful, the foliage was awesome and the weather was perfect. There is a rest area between both trails where you can buy cup noodles and chocolate bars. It took us around 4 hours to go up and down.

This was my 3rd waterfall visit in Jeju and my favourite, probably because the waterfall goes directly to the sea. Also, we saw some haenyeo (female divers) there and they were selling fresh sashmi seafood on the rocks next to the sea. It was definitely a very unique eating experience!

This was defiantly a must do event for Jeju! We thought it would be easier than it was. Towards the top it gets very steep and with all the snow and ice it can be quite challenging, especially since we were only wearing regular footwear and no crampons or even hiking shoes!We made it and 3 days later our legs still hurt but was worth the struggle! It took us 3.5 hours each way including stops but not including the time at the very top, which was almost an hour. So 8 hours total!

This was covered under our west course jeju tour.This is a large park with good bonsy trees ,lava caves and plants and animals and a old jeju village huts to show jeju culture.We can enjoy photography.If localite a good picnic spot.food shops available.

This was a very informative and extremely moving experience, which helped me to gain a greater understanding of the Jeju people, and why, even today they see themselves as 'other', having a separate identity from the rest of the \korean people.

This was a terrific little museum. Excellent, helpful staff. Fantastic introductory film that they played in English for us, and top class exhibits. We came away with a deep admiration for the women divers of Jeju, they are tough, proud and awesome achievers :)

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.
