FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

This was a part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - and felt it was worth seeing.  It is a lava tunnel/cave, which makes it kind of unique.  Visitors are limited to how far you can explore, which is fine as you do need to watch carefully where you walk - it is a lava tube and the floor is very uneven.  It is known for   Stone Turtle   because it is shaped like Jeju island.  Be sure to have a light jacket.

This was a nice walk up to the top. There's a lot of stairs, but it's not nearly as bad as I thought it was going to be. We went in Oct on a fairly sunny day (temp was probably in low-mid 20's) and you definitely want some water and sunscreen with you. I'd recommend going when it's more cloudy, if you can. There are a couple little shops along the way to the top (the first few levels of stairs, not all the way along) where you can also purchase water, and there is some tasty Jeju orange ice cream for sale too. The views are pretty, as is the temple, and it wasn't too busy when we were there in the middle of the afternoon.

This was a nice place in Jeju to take the kids, preferably in cooler weather because we went in July, and we were dying.  Besides the weather, everything else was nice.  There's a train that will take you to different stations.  We only stopped at stations 2 and 3 because we brought our boys ages 5 and 7, and those stations had more stuff for them to enjoy.  We probably could have stopped at all stations, but it really was just so hot!  There were lots of places for photo ops, whether all cute or nature-like.  The restaurant at the main building was very limited in the food that they sell.  We ended up eating light food at station 2's cafe and also got drinks at station 3.  All the staff there were very friendly and seemed to enjoy their work.  Overall, nice place to visit.  Oh one warning though, our rental car's GPS brought us to different places even though we entered the correct phone number and even when we asked someone for help and they entered it in Korean.  Just make sure you research how to get there because it was very frustrating for us.

This was a great stop for us, and even the kids enjoyed it.  It was refreshing in the summer.  The walk was not bad at all, and the view was just beautiful.  It's nice to just pause and think about how those rocks were created.  There were a handful of people so it took some time to get a nice spot to take a photo without people in the background.  I can't imagine how much harder it is when the weather is better.  It's still a must-see when in Jeju.

This was a building to commemorate those who perished when an uprising was brutally put down.  It is part of Jeju's history and should interest history buffs. As we're not history buffs, we just paid a short visit here in October 2016. The building was of fair size and the surrounding park was quite big, but not much to see. It has a serene atmosphere and a solemn place and reminds me of a cemetery.  We saw lots of local school children visiting when we were here.

This was a beautiful climb, but let me tell you, it's a climb. Granted we seemed to go on a particularly hot day at like 1:00 pm so that didn't help.I recommend taking water with you, but if you don't feel like carrying it, there is a store about half way up that you can get water and snacks. There are also lots of souvenir stores and restaurants at the base to stock up on supplies before heading up. I also recommend sunscreen and bug spray.There was a short line to pay about $2.00 for an entry fee. You received a ticket stub with a pretty picture of the volcanic crater on it. The trail is one-way: meaning there is one trail that goes up to the peak and one that returns down. This cuts down on congestion and ensures a scenic route the entire way. There are lots of places to take pictures and rest along the way. The time it takes to complete the trail all depends on your fitness level, but it is advertised as a 50-minute round-trip experience. At the peak, there are numerous places to sit and relax. You can see a beautiful 360-degree view of Jeju and Udo. Other items of interest: Horseback riding is available here and you can see the famous female divers of Jeju.
This village have very unique culture, if you come to jeju island you must go here, and the honey in here is very good

This underground shopping street is kinda cool. It has clothes, beauty products, a large number of children's stall, and no doubt impresses the many thousands of tourists that come through Jeju City every day. However, if you have ever been to Singapore, and experienced the underground warren of the connected malls on Orchard road, this will not in any way tantalize you. At best it will make you smile at the 1970's feel of it all ;-)

This top site in Jeju island is also known as Seongsan Sunrise Peak or 掠길ε뷴낡 It earns its reputation as Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site, and once you reached the top, you will see why. Be warned, it is a reasonable difficult climb that will easily take 20min to hike up. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water during hot weather. The uphill stairway will take you to a majestic dormant crater that offers spectacular view of the sunrise, hence the name. Be prepared for massive crowd of tourists throughout your climb, and get your vantage point to capture some of the majestic scenery throughout your climb.On your way down after enjoying the panoramic view of the UNESCO World Natural Heritage surrounding, make sure you allow enough energy to take the downhill path on the left to explore the Haenyo women diver performance at certain times. We were there after 3pm, so missed out on them unfortunately.

This three tier waterfall is one of the three waterfalls in Jeju, the other two being Cheonjiveon and Jeongbang waterfalls. The forest surrounding the waterfall has been designated as a natural monument and as per Korean legend seven nymphs bath at the pond of this waterfall in the night.Located at a walkable distance from Seogwipo Harbour, the visit to this attraction calls for climbing of stairs. So avoid this place if you hate to climb steps. For others a good pair of shoes is a must.

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This small gallery is tucked away on the southeastern side of the island  but if you're planning on going to a folk village  it's can be easily placed into your itinerary and is a nice break from all of the tourist attractions around the island. The gallery is really just two halls of one guy  KimYoungGap's  work. The photographer  now deceased  only photographed Jeju during his career and it was interesting to see the different landscapes of the island - landscapes that most of us don't see simply because we're so busy checking off all the tourist   must-sees?? This was the only place that our driver  a Jeju native  ran into friends and it was fascinating to note that they could name practically every hill in each picture because each hill (to the natives) was so distinct.The whole visit  including the garden entrance  takes thirty minutes or so. Admissions was 4 000 KRW  but they give you a nice postcard (well  basically  they force you to buy a postcard). Still  the place is well kept  including their bathroom  and we enjoyed our visit enough to buy a photo book. Note that the parking lot is across the street and that you can't enter with beverages or big bags. You have to leave them at the front.

This rock is really popular location in Jeju and also  Olle trail part.We have seen it just from quite far apart, but that was worth as well.Don't miss an opportunity, because it doesn't take a lot of time.

This Rock is believe as a Snake want to be a Dragon, so according to the local story there are God who live a the Sea.  And the Snake should have the Jade from the God and Snake steal the jade while the God is sleeping but before the snake escape the God Woke up and put an Arrow to the snake.  Half Body (Upper Part) already come out from the sea at it's become a dragon but the lower part is still below the sea and become the rock.  That's why the upper part that we can see looks like Dragon Head Rock.  This area is very near from the Parking area, here we can find Orange Seller, Snack seller, restaurant also, souvenir shop.  Nice place to see and near from Jeju Airport.. 10 Minutes from the airport.

This rock has the legend of a beautiful wife praying for a loving husband who has gone missing when fishing. When you look you may find the shape of a lady praying with a man on the bottom with a big tummy. Even more impressive is the walk around the coastal nature. It is considered to be number one walking trail in Jeju, Ollegil no. 7.

This road is have trick optical, whick look like up hill but actually down hill. All the bus and car turn off their engine in the down, but the car n bus can move to the top of the road like climb without machine, but that acttualy just optical trick. Many place like this in the world, but Jeju goverment use that as a attraction, very good idea.

This review will be written from the point of view of a middle aged woman of average fitness, not someone for whom a 20 km trek is a walk in the park.Mount Hallasan is the highest peak in South Korea and if you are on Jeju island it's definitely worth visiting. We took the Seongpanak trail, a scenic , easy route which reaches the summit. Plan on one day for the trek up and down. Here are some tips:1. It goes like this - You take a bus or taxi to the Seongpanak trail, and start climbing. It's a mix of  some steps and an easy trail. After a while you reach the first stop - I forget the name - where you can use  the restroom. There's a small shelter where we had our packed sandwiches. After this, the trail becomes a little steeper, and you reach the next stage - the jindeballat rest stop.( Times by which you must reach the Jindeballat stop and when you must start your descent are posted on the trail). There are restrooms here - but inspie of information to the contrary , there was no food for sale. After this the climb becomes a little tricky , and you need around 2 hours to reach the summit . The views are amazing from the summit. The Koreans hiking the mountain were not only super fit, they were the sweetest people I've met. When I became tired near the summit, so many encouraged me with words like   Fighting!     Turn around and see how far you have come.  Tips :1. Wear good hiking shoes - at points , the trail is slippery, and good shoes with ankle support are helpful.2. Carry a stick. You can get your own hiking stick or buy one from the store at the bottom.3. Carry plenty of water and snacks.4. Take a selfie at the summit and you can get a certificate at the bottom stating you have completed the climb ( costs 1000 won)5. You do need a certain degree of cardiovascular fitness to make the climb comfortably. But apart from that, the uneven  rocks and boulders are a little tough to climb, so make sure you do some core and lower body exercises too. 6. If you climb down slowly, it gets a little dark by the time you reach the base. Carry a head lamp.

This places is one of the a must place to visit in jeju. i think its getting more popular after 1bak2il had recording here, so many tourist and their fans come here to visit. Admission 2000won, you also can try raw seafood while watching the waterfall. and you can feel the cold water sprinkle on your face.

This place will be good for nature lovers and those who are in Jeju to relax and get away from busy city life. It only takes 1hour to cover the area at a slow pace. You may get a chance to see autumn foliage here from mid to late Nov as there are quite a number of maple trees in the forest. (Note: Autumn is mild in Jeju, while northern parts of Korea are having colourful autumn foliage, we hardly see any colourful trees in Jeju till we came to Bijarim forest)

This place was very beautiful.  In winter, you can see beautiful silver grass fields. It's a different charm than summer. If you visit Jeju Island, I recommend you to go here! You should wear sneakers when visit here. Because it's high that it's hard to climb up.

This place was the first on my list of place-to-go in Jeju. We were quite rushing as we don't want to miss the Haenyeo show (I totally adore them since years ago while watching documentary!). We would love to go for hiking to the peak, but we are pretty much time-constrained. Make sure to wear comfy shoes as there are lots of stairs. Go downstairs (it's really tiring to go upstairs later) to the Haenyeo house for the show and be there early as those ahjumma (auntie) in diver suit will perform their Haenyeo song and dance before going to the sea (this is so much fun!). There is boat service provided if you'd like a tour. You may enjoy fresh raw seafood (abalones, octopus etc.) from their catch, approx. from KRW10000 for a plate. If you love horse-riding, give it a try!The area is surrounded with souvenir shops. Try Hallabong (citrus fruit), one of Jeju specialities! The sight is way too gorgeous to be missed. MUST-GO-PLACE!Haenyeo (women diver) show: 1.30 pm & 3.00 pmAdmission fee for adult: KRW2000Boat ride: KRW10000Horse-riding: approx. KRW5000++Hallabong: KRW2000 each

This place was soo dope! Take note that it was so nice to visit this place around sunrise so it was a good decision that we stay near the sunrise peak! Our airbnb owner was driving us to the sunrise peak 30 minutes before the sunrise. As a beginner, the track was good and a nice hiking for us. Definitely a must visit when you stay at Jeju Island. Note that, bring your hiking shoes and hiking outfit! If you come in the morning, you cant see the woman diver show or take a boat around, but it was nice!
This place was really pretty (though remote) close to Hyeopjae beach on Jeju's west coast. Really pretty, reasonably priced and lots to see. Would recommend to couples and families especially.

This place was one of the highlights in my jeju trip and it did not disappoint me. Seongsan area are small and stroll-able with mostly seafood restaurants. I stayed in a guesthouse that's literally right at the entrance of the peak. So took me fifteen minutes from getting up to reaching the peak. The stairs was not for the fainted heart and Or who has knee problems. If you think the stairs may concern you, come little early and really take your time there are a few platforms you can stip while climbing up.

This place was crazy crowded but it was a Sunday. Still, there was much to see. Unfortunately, the Haenyo weren't doing any demonstrations (I think the water was too rough or something). My wife and I hiked up to the 'peak' and got a nice view  both of Jeju, Udo, and also the crater. Pretty cool! The hike was a bit strenuous and it was a little warm that day, so make sure to pack enough water. There were quite a lot of people around too so mind the crowd. Either way, it's worth the visit but probably best to go mid-week if possible. There are numerous great views to appreciate both on the way up and the way down. The path down takes a slightly different route too, which is nice.

This place was breathtakingly beautiful and a light work-out, lol! Never a dull moment and an awesome experience to share with the family! We recommend this location to families and couples as a place experience while in Jeju!

This place toally blew me away with the beautiful rock erosions.  I never expected that this would be the highlight of my trip to Jeju.  I could see the clarity of the blue green water up close.  Assured that the seawater was so clean without any fishy smell, we even ventured to sample the live seashells.  What an unforgettable experience we had, dining on the rocks with the gentle waves lapping in front of us.

This place is only about 8 km from Jeju downtown.  Worth a quick visit to see for yourself the   supposedly   optical illusion where things (water, cars, etc) seem to roll uphill, instead of downhill....

This place is name the world 7 wonder of nature, and defintely live it up to the name. I love the Jeju woman's diver perfomance, they are so lively and bubbly... Climbing up the stairs is totally panting (however nearing to the top, the stairs are very steep so be more cautious) but wait till u reach the peak of it, you will find it totally worth it. You can see the blue sea from this side and the other part of Jeju on the other side. The curve in volcano is amazing too.Totally recommended but please dun go there during noon when the sun is hot...

This place is huge!If you like nature, do visit Jeju Stone Park.  The English audio guide was excellent.  The exhibits were really interesting.  There were indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Do be selective if you have limited time.  One could easily spend up to half a day at this place.As we were a bit short on time, we browsed through the indoor museum rather quickly and still managed to pick up some interesting information.The outdoor areas were really nice and comfortable.  When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This place is great for shopping with reasonable and cheaper prices compared to other places. Also, it is underground and covered, so u need not worry about the weather. U could take your meals at the big market on the  street level, get your fix of souvenirs such as jeju chocolates, crunch, tangerines and such, then head downstairs to shop. Most store ladies there could speak Mandarine and a little English so communication is not a big issue. Definitely a must come for shopping in Jeju!

This place is an epitome of beauty, beautiful rock formation, beautiful sea, beautiful waves, beautiful clouds, it is amazingly beautiful. Here you enjoy both worlds of rock formation and beautiful sea. Definitely this place is super windy and you might get wet with huge waves hitting against the rock formation. The scenery of the place couple with the beautiful sound of waves for me makes any visit to Jeju complete. Be careful in walking and exploring place, there are areas that are slippery and rough.  If you are an instagram addict this place is the best for you. You can choose to have those lovely rock formation as background or the beautiful blue sea with the huge waves and or both the lovely rock formation and waves.

This place is AMAZING. I can't describe with words how incredible it was so I will upload pictures too. I visited this place during the Jeju Olle Walking Festival and it was my favorite place. I highly recommend to visit this place. If you can, do Route 10 of the Jeju Olle Walking and you would come across this place. Also, in that place you can found ladies who are fishing and preparing dishes right away. You can try raw fish from Jeju right there. We tried and it was delicious!

This place is accessible (1.5 hours away from Jeju Bus Terminal/Airport by bus 101.  It was too cold to swim in october (and I didn't bring my trunks) but I hope to swim here another time!  Cafe Delmoondo is just next to the beach - I went there cos I needed to use the toilet (and bought an ice-cream just to be a customer), but food was so good there I ended up having lunch!  This is a nice place to hang out if you are staying in N Jeju because it was not too crowded (at least not in october), and because the view was really nice (the sea was emerald green, as the blogs say, and quite breathtaking)

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This place is a must-visit if you visit Jeju. It was a pretty long walk from one end to another end. Inside the cave, it was quite dark and you have to be extremely careful while inside as the floor might be slippery. It was a magnificient cave and if you are a nature/cave lover, you will definitely love it!

This place is a must visit when you are in Jeju. That said, expect lots of tourists. Do try to be early, before 10 am, or at odd hours like lunch time, when most tourists are somewhere else. The climb up was not too tough, my 2 boys made the climb up quite easily. The stairs up might be a little tough for older folks. Views are excellent,worth the climb. Do bring enough water and some light snacks for rest and recharge at the top. During the climb up, there are benches to sit and rest. The restaurants in surrounding area at the foot, served mainly seafood. Prices are a little high, we had an abalone porridge and grilled mackeral for 45,000 won. There is a Lotteria and a Starbucks just before the ticket office. If you are on a budget or not into seafood, do bring some sandwiches or kimbap, you will be hungry after the climb.

This place is a garden and there is cave and lot of birds, literally this place has everything. It is worth the visit, I like the cactus garden and the bird feeding area. I will definitely come back again with my family. I made a vblog during my trip, come and see if it is worth the visit.Search by title :#3 TRAVEL BLOG DAY 2 JEJU - NATURE - GD CAFE

This place is a definite must see on my list. The market is huge and includes shops that sell about everything you can imagine (clothes, kitchen appliances, souvenirs, meat, fish, ice cream, pancakes, desserts, traditional street food, oranges, oranges and more oranges). The fruit is expensive, but that's normal for Korea. The street food is cheap and absolutely delicious. It is definitely a good way to kill a couple hours and try some of Jeju's famous treats.

This place has great vibes and energy of a beautiful beach town. Many cafes offer good views. I spent about 2 hours in one of the cafes and totally enjoyed the views. There?s a very good seafood ramen and pancake restaurant nearby : Sogob-E 怨깆 ? Seafood Ramen ShopAddress: 565 Woljeong-ri, Gujwa-eup, Cheju, Jeju-do, South Korea

This place has a magnificient view of sunset and it is definitely an instaworthy place for those who love nature. We took our time to climb uphill, stopping at various points to snap photos. Although we didnt go up to the peak, the view where we were was astounding. I will go here again if I ever go to Jeju. Lovely!

This place exceeded my expectations, it is definitely a highlight of Jeju, it is perfectly organized to be a journey itself. We spent around 3 hours walking around ( it has 3 different routes well explained in the map) and simply feeling the nature was already healing. The entrance is 6.000 Korean won per person. They have drinking fountains and toilets inside. You can reach it by bus!

This park was the favorite place of my kids in Jeju. They could play with many kinds of birds and exploring safe caves here. My husband and I prefer watching bonsai trees and had intention of bringing some to our home if they could set them for sale. A place to have nice fun with family, just safe and green.

This park is on the mountain above the Jeju main ship port.The way up can be done with a car, then the entrance to the park is near the large white lighthouse with a great view over the coastline.you'll have their wide green areas. good for to chilling out but can be skip after the lighthouse.

This park has a collection of 7-8 sections of different type of plants and sights, such as tropical plants, cactus collections, bonsai collection, wild flowers, cave systems, folk village, small cave system etc. You could easily spent 2 hours at this park. The park is nicely planned and appropriately signed to guide the exploration of the entire park. We really liked its cactus collection and roads lined by famous Jeju-harubang (stone human-shaped statues). We definitely recommend visiting this fabulous park.

This one is located near  Hyeopjae  Beach,  so you can see the Biyangdo island as well. i liked it. Its pretty spacious and got necessary facilities like combini nearby, toilet and place with free water. it also got nice view and some of typical jeju sculptures of  female divers and spirits that protect the Island. Sand is white and feels nice.

This one amazing place is a must in Jeju! We were not able to go early but I think the best time is sunrise, since it is called the   Sunrise Peak   in english. There's plenty of parking, restrooms and stores for food and stuffs! Nice people around and the view is fantastic! It can be a challenge to go to the top so be sure your knees will last the climb to the peak!

This museum, which focuses on the women divers of Jeju, is well designed and well laid out. It offers a fascinating look into the lives (past and present) of these divers, who spend up to 2 minutes underwater at a time without any breathing apparatus to catch abalone and other sea life. Our guide told us that the divers' current age range is 55 to 85. Younger women have no interest incontinuing this cultural tradition, which is an incredibly difficult way to earn a living and to help support a family.Nicely curated, the museum offers an excellent film about the divers and shows various aspects of their lives, including past and current swim wear. the tools that have been used, models of fishing villages and the Jeju traditional fishing boat. I thoroughly enjoyed this close look at a rare way of life that likely won't be around much longer.

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the   Gandhi   teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the   Beatles   teddy bears, the   Chinatown   teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

This museum is interesting if you have the keen interest in geology & history of jeju volcanic past. The entire park is very well maintained and its advisable to bring an umbrella if you're those who can't really take the sunlight.For couples who would just want to take a quiet stroll, this place is strongly recommended as crowds here are lesser as compare to other tourist attraction in jeju.

This museum is intended for tourists who love to take photos. Most of the artworks housed in the museum are modified versions of original paintings so that you can integrate with the painting. Hence bringing a camera or a smartphone is a must! A companion is also a must since taking a   selfie   to achieve the desired effect might prove to be impossible.This is one of the two 3D interactive museums in Jeju Island. The other one Trick Art Museum is located farther in the eastern part of the island. We went to this place as it is nearer to the Jungmun Area where most hotels (Hyatt Regency Shilla Hotel Lotte Hotel etc.) are located.Aside from the in-house artworks there is also a park with sculptures and play sets that will be appreciated by kids. Tips: avoid flash photography to get the desired effect; bring a jacket w/ hoodie (can be used in some of the artworks); and black pants make people blend better with the background.Admission costs KRW 8000 per person. The entire area is air-conditioned and wifi access is offered for free. Other extras include lockers to deposit your bags as this may hamper your experience.This is a fun destination for couples families or small groups.

This museum is about the dwindling women divers of Jeju who dive in the sea to collect Agar and shellfish as well as octopus. They are similar to their sisters in Japan and dive without the benefit of air tanks.This tradition is sadly dying out and it is to be hoped that this neatly laid out museum will attract members to the group and also increase worldwide awareness.It is a static museum with some electronic displays but later, if you are lucky, you might see them diving off the coast of U-Do island.Worth a visit!

This museum is 90% in Korean but as they say some things are easier to understand. In the beginning the museum starts out with some interesting if broad sex-positive history. It's sex and HEALTH however so there's info about AIDS as well as misconceptions about sex and sexual health. Towards the middle of the museum it starts to go off the rails a little bit. The   Fantasy   section is a lot of chintzy garbage and mannequins in lewd/bizarre positions and tableaus. It doesn't add anything it moreso detracts from the legitimacy established in the first half. Only go if you're stuck with a rainy day. Otherwise you'd be better off enjoying Jeju's natural wonders.

This museum boasts its huge variety of old computer related exhibitions to a new one. You may enjoy the old memories of punch card, MS-DOS, APPLE I~II, to VR, motion recognition, etc. The only point you should consider is entrance fee. I was ok because I can get Jeju resident discount. But most of visitors from outside of Jeju island should try to discount chances such as Naver booking, etc.

This mountain (aka Sunrise Peak) is located to the eastern seaboard of the island and is not accessible easily if you are staying in one of the hotels in Jeju-ri (city area) in the north. You need to take public transport which can take you more than 1 hr (Blue intercity bus, flat rate 1200 W) or 50+ min by express bus (Red, flat rate 2000 W). It is advisable to put up overnight in one of the many hotels or guest houses in Seongsan itself so that you can wake up early and start your ascend to watch the sunrise.This will take about 25-40 min to climb up the well laid out steps if you do not stop along the way to take pictures. However it is advisable to stop along the numerous rest areas and take your own time to ascend. Certain parts can be quite steep so come with a good pair of canvas sneakers or hiking shoes, sunglasses, sun screen, bottles of water. The climb up is worth the effort as you will be rewarded with the fantastic views from the peak. Going down is much easier and you can stop at the foothill to watch the women divers putting up a demo at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. At the foothill is a public toilet and a McDonald and cafe apart from stalls selling souvenirs and cold drinks.

This mistery road is about half kilometer long. Stop you?re vehicle at the start of this road, put the gear in neutral, and turn off the engine. Your car slowly climbs up a pretty steep slope. At least what it looks like upward slope. It is really hard to believe that the upward slope is an optical illusion and it in reality slopes down. I have seen magnetic hill in Moncton, Canada and they have a road like this. But there is just below a mountain slope and the optical illusion is very understandable there but here there is no such thing, just a plain stretch of road. I really could not figure out how your eyes are deceiving your brain. Not a big deal,but worth experiencing it if you are in Jeju.

This market was near our hotel so we came by here a few times in the evenings (and a couple times in the day time). Mostly because we were trying to find this fried chicken restaurant that never seemed to be open and we kept going back to try to find it. Don't come here expecting a night market extravaganza like other parts of Asia. This is more strictly a   market   market, though there are lots of restaurants that have take-out. There are a few street food stalls, so you can get your fix in a couple spots. Definitely make sure you try the orange juice from one of the sellers here, Jeju has amazing oranges (and tangerines). There are some souvenir type places here, but nothing special. We bought some of the chocolates because they were dirt cheap and wanted to try them, but when we got home and ate them they were just waxy and artificial tatsing (you'll see which chocolates I mean when you get there. EVERY souvenir seller has them. Even in the airport). We bought some dried mandarins from the same vendor, and they were pretty good. We also bought a bunch of oranges to bring around with us as snacks while we were driving. If you've been to markets in Asia before, this will be nothing special. But if you're looking for something to do, it's probably worth visit - wouldn't go out of my way for it though.

This market sells many goods. I would recommend it for buying souvenirs from Jeju, like chocolate crunch and chocolate. There were also shoes and clothes for sale but not so fashionable. There are many shops selling dry and wet goods, mandarin oranges and other Jeju products. It is really large and you can spend quite a few hours there. Good for wet weather as it is covered.
This market sell a lot of Jeju specialities, eg, Hallabong, seafoods etc. Nothing really very special unless you intended to get some souvenirs from Jeju Island or you wanna to get some local food.

This market is the heaven of fresh foods in Jeju. However, it is mainly for wholesaling not retailing so much. As the market was crowded, we have some difficulties in watching out our kids. Our family enjoyed the original rice cake here but did not get anything like fresh seafood since we can?t speak Mandarin to deal with the sellers.

This market is really big, there is fish market, street food corner and the souvenir shops corners where you can buy jeju chocolates,... Anyways, I'm addicted to the street food corners here. The food marrket is at the gate 8. There are so many kind of street food with good price.

This located just opposite to the foot of Sanbangsan. We saw the supernatural volcano scenery there. If you like, you could have a few hours walk in Olle route. Lastly, be sure to try the CO2  hot springs in Sanbangsan nearby, it's very local and famous in Jeju!

This island is like a mini-Jejudo. You can see entire Seongsan Ilchubon from this island. This place is more relaxing and peaceful than Jeju-do, a bit off-touritst path compared to other places. I like the view at Udobong at its atmosphere. Which I had more time, so I can bike around the island.

This is your typically local market where you can get fresh product here.  I will NOT say this place offers the cheapest price but rather there are varieties for you to choose from.  The market has many entrance and each entrance leads to you to a particular section where they sell the same stuff ranging from clothes, fruits and to live seafood.  We picked up some Jeju tangerines and sweets here which were pretty good.  Discount?  Most shops are priced the same so its hard to get discount. Best time to come is about 2pm where there are lesser crowd.  Its also a short walk to the underground shopping mall so if you are here, do take the chance to visit the underground mall altogether.

This is worth a trip to Jeju all by itself!  Going up to the peak looks intimidating, but it was pretty easy and we saw a woman in her 70s at the top.  It's hundreds of stairs and took about 35 minutes, but they have benches and a lot of shade on the way up.  There's a path designated for ascending and another for descending, and I recommend following them as intended.  We saw some people trying to beat the crowd by going up the 'down' path, but there aren't benches to rest on and not much shade on that path; also, the ascending path is a LOT steeper and the stairs are kind of narrow (like a typical home staircase), so if you go down the 'up' path, you'll be going down very steep stairs and shuffling around people, while the designated 'descending' path is a very gradual slope and much wider.  We went on a hot & humid day, but I unquestionably would do it again.
This is within old Jeju city.  Very windy condition during visit, definitely not for raining weather.  Just 30 min will suffice.

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking.  There are different areas to see at this park including 3 long lava caves, an area with bonsai (my favouite), an area of flowers, a water area, a stone area, old JeJu houses and my least favourite...caged birds some in dubious conditions! I took lots of photos.  Plenty of places to get snacks and drinks but chicken a la flies is not my cup of tea!  A nice place to take a picnic.  There are lots of buses there but they all follow a route...if you go left you have a reasonable amount of quiet time from the hoards of yellow hat people and all the selfie photographer's.
This is to me the nicest waterfall in Jeju, having visited four in total as you can get close to it and see the waterfall right into the sea...Not grand but nice...

This is the thing you should visit when you are in jejuto go up and down it takes 1h, not too difficult but good enough to make you tired!the view is amazing at the top, bring your own water cose it can be really there is a beach on the righ side at the bottom when you go down, some grand ma are selling fish down the beach, nobody are there

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is the place you must visit if you want to understand why stones especially volcano rocks are so important to the people of Jeju. This place provides all the history about Jeju Culture as well as nice scenery for photo-shoot. The place is well-kept and huge. But, the trail is nice to walk with lovely autumn weather. Admission is only krw5000. Take bus 720 from intercity bus terminal.
This is the place you can hug, kiss and take photos with teddy bear. Jeju Teseum is Korea's first and largest teddy bear museum. If you likes Teddy bear this is the place must visit in Jeju Island.

This is the only waterfall in Asia which falls directly into the ocean. Admission fee is 2000 won. You'll need to climb over quite a number of rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. Be careful of the slippery rocks if you go after raining. In my opinion, Jeongbang Waterfall is worth to visit than any other waterfalls in Jeju.
This is the most attractive place in jeju. The view from the peak was good but not breathtaking. Anyway, it is still better than the waterfalls which are just little falls.

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.

this is the easiest waterfall among all in jeju in terms of access.we walked for about 15 minutes before reaching the waterfall.however,to reach the waters,u have to go through slippery rocks-definitely not for kids or elderly.wear comfortable walking shoes.however,the view from the upper part of the waterfall(before descending down the many stairs) was already breathtaking.there were also foodstalls selling snacks-we had the ice cream and the grilled squid.super delicious.do try it.oh and don't forget the orange juice (hallabong).the freshest i have ever tasted.good snack,superb juice to wash it down,beautiful scenery-i could not ask for more.do visit if you are in jeju.preferably early morning before the crowd.

This is the best waterfall I've seen among the famous ones in Jeju (Jeongbang, Cheonjiyeon, Cheonjeyeon). It also requires more physical effort since you have to climb and go down several stairs. There are also a number of viewing decks: for me, the one near the pavilion is the best (less people there too). Highly recommended unless you hate stairs. Best to bring shoes with good grip though since the stairs can be slippery when wet.

This is the best track if you are planning to climb mount hallasan. From Jeju you take bus number 780 to Mount hallasan. Cost of taxi is around KRW17,000. To reach on the top of the mountain, it takes 4 hours. There are a lot of facilities on the way to Mount Hallasan such as toilet and place to sleep.

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!

This is the 1st attraction we visited when we arrived at Jeju. Its near our hotel in Seogwipo.We saw a group of tough ladies, the Haenyeo, scuttling over the rocky beach. They were hunting for seafood hidden between the rocks.The waterfall was nearby, beautiful with strong steady stream of water gushing into the sea as it had been raining a lot recently.A lot of people around the area as it was an easy to reach attraction with a short walk down the stairs...

This is super easy to do... From Jeju city go to Jeju Bus Terminal and the lady at the desk will tell you which bus to get. In this case, 740. This takes you to a ticket office and car park. From there you can get a taxi or walk 2.5km to the start of the trail. We walked and it took about half an hour (but it is all uphill). I would say there are about 3 sections to this walk:1. Through the forest - stream nearby and wildlife (I saw a deer). This is relatively flat until the end when you have to climb some stairs. 2. The hard part- walking along the ridge of the mountain going up the stairs. This is tough on the knees but there are loads of places to stop and absorb the view. 3. Along the top- relatively flat through a forest part and then open until you get to the rest stop. It is the easiest hike and does not go to the top of Hallasan, but it is beautiful and gave you stunning views of the top of Hallasan (which you would not get if you were actually on it). Make sure you bring water, snacks and hand wipes. The rest stop at the top sells only instant noodles and has no running water.

This is sunrise peak at Jeju island you should to add in your travel list. Before go to Seongsan pls check the sunrise time. You will see a very fantastic view point here. Anaway, pls prepare your cloths for strong windy and cold. Along the walking platform the view is beautiful also. Do not miss it.

This is similar to Dongdaemun market concept in Seoul though this time around so many oranges, Jeju oranges. They are all of the same price, you got your numbers, there is no need to go further. The famous Jeju oranges looked fresher here though I think more expensive than those sold at the Dragon cliff site ? another friend had bought hers there. I am assuming that all other things go the same way here at Dongmun market, so we didn?t venture further in. Parking is a hassle if you are driving a rented car, I saw yellow lines everywhere and cars parked almost everywhere.

This is really amazing. It looked like I have been to the Antelope Canyon!! The nature beauty is really stunning. With the sunny weather, the whole journey took around one hour and it was a nice walk! Must go place in jeju!!

This is purely an activity you should do if you actually enjoy adventures! The guides say to get to the peak it will take 4.5 hours, 8-9.5km depending on which trail you take. We took the popular one, seongpanak because there is a direct bus route from the Jeju intercity terminal (number 781). Here's my itinerary for the day:08.45: arrived at seongpanak trail start09.45: arrived at Sokbat shelter11.10: arrived at Jindallaebat shelter12.30: arrived at peakSo in total 3.45 hours including breaks. I had around 1 hour at the top to sit, eat, take photos, luckily we chose such a clear day so everything was so visible!At 13.30, you have to head down, staff will tell you to move. We decided to take the Eorimok route (8.7km) down and made it to the bottom at 18.00. Things to note:- you have to reach Jindallaebat by 12pm or you are not allowed to the peak. - there are no trash cans, so you have to carry all rubbish. - on the seongpanak route, there is also the Saraoreum Observatory (extra 40 minute walk) which is supposed to have great views!- hiking boots or sturdy shoes are needed!I exercise everyday and managed it fine. My friend who does no exercise made it eventually and was super proud of herself!

This is probably the view that epitomises a Jeju trip - even the Jeju logo is a sun rising above the mountain.Hues of orange, pink and mauve intertwine in the distant horizon as the sea of gold gradually spreads, illuminating the lustrous greenery below.It's a 30 min climb before that, so make sure to wake early. The sunrise forecasts can be obtained on Google.This is worth booking a separate night's stay at Seongsan.

This is probably my first 1-star review on TA. Much regretted visit and the only saving grace is that this place is right next to the Osulloc Tea Museum. We were drawn to this place after very good experience at the Innifree Green Cafe at Myongdong and we expected the same (if not better) at this concept store.Product - any Innisfree shops in myeongdong or duty free can offer you a better range at much better price. As Jeju was the last leg of my trip, I was planning to make most of my innisfree purchase in this store but they don?셳 carry much range here. I don?셳 remember there was onsite tourist refund as well (like how it is in Myeongdong) - another reason not to plan your shopping here.Food - I ordered a 18000krw main dish (named herdsman?) with some cold sausages, potato mash, rice balls and orange. The presentation was really pretty but it tasted nothing special. If you are looking for good looking food and great taste at the same time, you have better chance at Myongdong innisfree Green cafe. The other two pretty drinks we ordered were not worth a mention as well. Service - We were there at 450pm and all the soap making stations were occupied. We were told by a staff the soap making would only take 15mins and the place would close at 6pm. so we decided to wait at the cafe and return when the crowd lessen. At 525pm, a staff stopped me at the cashier when I tried to purchase the soap making set. She said that they have closed the soap making station at 520pm. And then another staff came by and said the station was closed at 5pm (?!). I am not sure exactly what time the station closed as there was no sign in the store and the staff were telling different things. The store closed at 6pm sharp and the staff can?셳 wait to have all the guests out by then - this I am sure. This place is a sad contrast to the Osulloc Tea Museum next door.

This is perfect for solo and family travelers that are vacationing in Jeju. Adult admission is 5,000 KW and is well worth it. The hike takes about 30 minutes to an hour and can be  fairly steep in some areas. There are many shops, cafes, and restaurants around the area once you are done with the hike to the top. If you time it right, you will be able to see the famous Women Divers of JeJu who perform at 1:30 PM. The heritage behind it is very unique since it has been carried one for generations.

This is our last stop of our 2nd day in Jeju Island and was worthy for the line Save the Best for last. If you are into caves and lavas then this is the right place for you. Since this is our last stop, we went there around 5PM, we were in a hurry to reach the entrance of the site. Get ready to walk on dark and cold pavements. Although it was cold we manage to take photos inside the cave (which needed editing) and was mesmerized with the unique beauty the cave has to offer. It entails walking so get ready to walk and prepare the right shoes. Plus, inside the cave is really cold, colder than the other sites so be ready with your jackets. You may also explore the park and the cafe located outside the cave. The entire place is relaxing and worth the visit. This must be part of your itinerary once you happen to visit Jeju Island.

This is one road which really left my puzzled. The bus driver did turn off his enjoy but the bus still managed to roll on, to my eyes, the path was an up-sloping one. So how did the bus manage to move on its own? Does it mean the path is actually downwards sloping?This is just any other road along Jeju Island which after completion, people found out about this weird phenomenon. Well, the locals will explain to you the whole reason to this phenomenon. Don't worry, expect a crowd there with tour buses pulling over, but don't expect a fee to be paid unless you patronize the little snack shops there.

this is one of those strange Jeju adventures that's worth a quick check.  yes, just like they describe, it's a road which, when you walk down it, it feels like you're going up - and vice versus.  be careful, so you don't get hit by a car - but on your way to something else to do in Jeju, give it a go.  BTW, I  m sure kids won't get it - this is an adult thing, and I don't think I'd want my toddler walking down an active road.

This is one of the world heritage in Jeju Island. When i visit Jeju, i stayed in a hotel nearby, so i can see the sunrise from the top of seonsan Ilchulbong. To see the beautiful sunrise, i walk from my hotel at 4.30 am. You need to buy an entrance ticket to this place.You need to walk the stair path, uphill, and soon you arrive on top, you'll find so many people already setting up the camera to capture the sunrise. after enjoying the beautiful scene from top, on our way down, my eyes can't stop admiring the beauty scene of Jeju City. Everything is taking your breath away in this place.You also can ride a horse or watch the mermaid show (lady divers). If you want to buy some goods for your family from Jeju (orange, souvenirs, cake, snacks), you have to buy it in Jeju, because you can't find any of these goods in Seoul. If you want to give a second thought on it, your last chance to shop is in the Jeju International airport (price is the same everywhere in Jeju).This is a very highly recommended place to visit in Jeju Island!

This is one of the must see in Jeju. The most beautiful rocky beach in Jeju. Hamel ship (copy) is on beachside. You can check some pics on TripAdvisor. Spring season is high season.  Summer season is also high season, but check if typhoon is near. Check the typhoon, you cannot go close beach if there is typhoon. It is not normal beach, waves carved this beach for long time, hundreds of thousands of years.

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

This is one of the most beautiful beaches in Jeju island. The sea was so amazing, water so clear and having light ocean blue color. from here you could see the Biyangdo island, very close. However, it was rather cold and windy for us, so we could not swim just wandering around. we spent around 2hrs here. we got here by intercity bus no. 702 (about 1 hr) from jeju bus terminal.

This is one of the highlights of Jeju Island. If you're ever there, you MUST go on this trail, unless outdoor activities aren't your type of activity. We took the Seongpanak trail up and down via Gwaneumsa. The pathway up was well constructed with wooden planks and shades for about 3 quarters of the journey. The rest of the path was quite stony. As the Gwaneumsa trail is relatively newer, it is not as well covered with wooden planks and a bit more slippery when you hike on the rocky trails. Both trails are as spectacular and offer different sceneries. On the way down, I encountered a deer sighting!Do bring along a wind wall as the winds can get very strong as you progress towards the peak. Also, it's best to start off as early as possible (we started at 6am) to enjoy the nature scenery as much as possible.

This is one of the biggest festival celebrated in Jeju island. Free shuttle buses were provided in various pick up point within Jeju City such as Top Dong station, Jeju City Hall station and Jeju University station and more.People of Jeju and tourists like me would gather around the oreum (hill) for the stage performances, fireworks and eventually the field burning event. It is definitely worth visit if you are in Jeju.

This is one of the best scenic spots on Jeju Island and we intentionally chose to stay in Seongsan for that reason. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area close to the UNESCO World Heritage entrance. The climb up the tuff cone was gradual along well-marked and well-laid pathways and steps in spite of the throngs of tourists. Do stop occasionally along the route to catch your breath and to catch the surrounding views from various altitudes. On a perfect day, one can see the blue skies against the blue seas and the township of Seongsan below. As a bonus, take the side trail to the Haenyeo or Women Divers? House, to taste the fresh seafood like abalone and other shellfish, sliced and diced before your very eyes and served with kimchi and seaweed. To finish, take a peek at the Dong Am Sa Temple near the car-park. With such a majestic location, the temple is fortunately understated and does not stick out to compete with the volcano backdrop. What an incredible place to spend half a day!

This is one of the best place we visited in Jeju. Various things to see such as flowers, plants, birds, small reptiles, lava cave etc. I love the cactus garden most. Great for photo taking and a slow stroll with family members! I did not fully explore the place due to time constraint. Guess it probably need around 2-3 hrs to slowly explore the park.

This is one of the attraction in Jeju that nice to visit! The cave made by volcano lava. When we went there it's rain, so along the way inside the cave wet and dirty! Inside the cave quite slippery and dark. Overall I like this place! We manage to go to the deepest point and come out within 1.30 hr.

This is one of my favourite places to visit in Jeju. No matter which angle you are taking photos from, the views are gorgeous. You can hike up Seongsan as well, if you are up for it. Or you could go down nearer the shoreline to catch a glimpse of the women divers. Past that area, and you can make out Udo Island in the distance. It has gotten extremely crowded over the years though, with tons of tour groups making their way here. It still remains a must-see area in Jeju, in my opinion.

This is one of my favorite places in Jeju.? Walking up the steps to the temple you experience one enlightenment after the next.? The temple and the grounds are in immaculate condition, and clearly there is a lot of love and respect which goes into every section.? This is a wonderful hour or two to spend as you are wandering around the island - take your time, don't rush it, enjoy both the temple and its attractions, and the stunning views toward the ocean and the rest of the island.? BTW, this is not an easy stroll up the hill, but not that taxing either - if you have elders, perhaps you settle for mid-way.? if you're young - do the entire journey, you'll never know when you'll be back.

This is one of my favorite oreums (volcanic hills) on Jeju!!It is not exactly close to anything so be ready to travel quite a bit.  It is also a steep hike, but each step that takes your higher gives you more and more of a view. I am telling you the negative up first but I am also telling you...it is worth it.  *On the weekends (depending on the season) you will often find coffee trucks parked at the bottom parking lot.  You cannot count on this as they come and go...but if they are there, it will be a nice treat for you.*This oreum is also host to my favorite festival in Korea.  Jeju Fire Festival.  Thousands and thousands of people come to this oreum to say goodbye to the past memories and to welcome spring.  It is a seriously amazing event.  Fire, fireworks, food, beer, shopping tents, performances.....absolutely a fantastic event.

This is one of my favorite beaches on Jeju.  As someone who lives here, this is mainly because the beach is big enough to hold the droves of tourists who come here every summer.  During off season it is even more spectacular.  Wide stretches of sand with very few people filling it.Around the beach areas there are enough cafes, restaurants, shops to keep a person full and happy throughout the day.  ProTip: Midway down the beach (there is another set of bathrooms up the stairs.  Save yourself the trip of trying to make it to the main ones!

This is not really part of our tour in Jeju but since I researched on how to enjoy the tour with 30+ friends, I chanced upon this garden maze near Manjanggul lava tubes site (as in 500m away only).I really recommend this to friends and families who'd like to solve a mystery together and have fun doing it. The price in finishing the maze is a banner and the right to be the first to ring the bell.Please try the ice cream at the exit. You'll enjoy it after an exhilirating yet fun game (30 minutes estimated)

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. Located at Nanta Theatre about 10 kilometers away from Jeju City. Entrance fee normally 50,000 won but we managed to get only 30,000 won through our friend. Thanks to him. Really recommended.

This is my first ever hike and it was a real learning experience. Make sure to bring proper hiking shoes as the trail is VERY rocky and it can be easy to lose your footing and hurt your ankles. Walking stick is useful for the decent because it is MURDER on the knees. Coming down was much harder for me than going up. The view of Jeju at the top is amazing. But it was really crowded and I felt that the lake itself was a bit of a letdown looking like it was half drained... But overall, great hike and it's a good hike for first-timers! Bonus: I got to see a baby deer!

This is my favourite one of the three waterfalls i visited in Jeju! (April 2018)This place consist of three level waterfalls. The first level you will only see the waterfall if it has rained enough and the waterlevel is high enough to create the waterfall. The second one is the biggest of the three levels. It can be seen from two places. First is by the staircase and upclose. The second one is going over the bridge and after that (stone) stairs up on your rightside after crossing over the bridge. You can get a great view for the 2nd waterfall!The third and last level is the furtherst and the smallest one of all. If you are not fit enough or you can't walk very well, I advise to skip this one as there are a lot of stairs to go down and up afterwards.The first 2 levels are good enough to get a great view out of the place.

This is my favorite place whenever I go to Jeju. You can walk up to the peak for forty minutes where you can see the East Sea of Jeju. From there, you can leave for Cow Islet on a cruise, another destination in Jeju. This place is famous for beautiful sunrises.

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

This is just another roadside attraction that many people visiting Jeju stop by to see only because it is in the city proper. It is just a rock that could appear to look like any number of different animals.If your tour guide takes you out of your way to see this then you need a new tour guide because this rock is typical of any of the millions of rocks you run into along the seashore in Jeju.There are a lot of interesting things to see and fun places to go in Jeju but, this isn't one of them.

This is it, even though its FULL of stairs and exhausting to climb up (with lots of   take 5   in between the climb. The view is magnificent and too beautiful to behold.Consider this the best part of JEJU.

This is great place to enjoy scenry, learn about hydro-volcanic activity and Jeju island formation process if weather permite you to go there.Coz of wether change, sea level is getting higher, the days you could go getting less. So plz before you go there, call the attration site office. 064-760-6321Ejoy the this place.

This is for the female Merchant who saved people in Jeju island 17,18 Century, Joseon dynasty. Very carefully and beautifully made. However, it is limited for 3rd floor. 2nd floor is for kids' experience museum. 1st floor is for some special exposition from time to time. It is FREE, worth to visit for an hour. It is located near by Jeju coastal international port and Dongmun traditional market. Actually from this market, exit/entrance #3, it is just 500 m away. In those times, people in Jeju island could not get out of the island, however, since she saved whole population in the island, The King Jungjo wanted to give a awards but she refused. Instead, she asked him she would love to visit the peninsular once, and wanted to travel in Diamond mountain(located in North Korea now). So she could get the chance to meet the King and travel inland. Under the Patriarchal system, it must be very hard for her to work as a merchant, but became the most rich person in Jeju, then when there was big famine, she released whole rice and food for free to Jeju people. Any way, it was great fun to enjoy each section from her birth to death. All explanation are in English and in Korean both.

This is definitely a must do on Jeju Island.  Climb early in the morning to avoid the throngs of people.  If the pollution is low, you'll have a great view.  Beware, even if you climb early in the morning, it may not be peaceful.  There will be many selfie sticks! I was expecting lush green grass and canola flowers -- it became very apparent that the online images have been Photoshopped.  It is still well worth it to visit - just don't expect the view to be as stellar as what you see online.

This is arguably the longest running South Korean LIVE show ever!  Now, it is branching out to other popular tourist destinations such as Jeju Island.  You needn't understand Korean language to appreciate the show, which is leaning more towards physical action and slapstick comedy based on timing.  It revolves around cooking.  Nanta show is leaning heavily towards satisfying tour groups and the day I was there, two thirds of the theatre was filled up by tourists that came in bus loads.  Nanta is interactive too, with occasional involvement with the audience.  Children thoroughly enjoyed the show.  It was pure 90 minutes of unadulterated fun and enjoyment.  In terms of price, you can get cheaper price booked through YEHA website.  Commendable fun:)

This is an icon of Jeju, so it is hard to imagine coming to the island without seeing it, and see it you should! But try to go in the early morning or late evening, if you want to avoid the tourist crowds. We went after lunch at about 1pm on an overcast day with showers and it was still pretty crowded..it does take something away from the beauty of the place. Tickets are sold, 2000 won per person, at the base of the crater. It is mainly stairs all the way up and takes 50 minutes return trip according to the sign at the ticket counter. We found this to be accurate. There are beautiful views down to the town and coast from the top. The crater itself, my partner and I, actually found more interesting from the bottom. There are many vendors and eateries around the base for snacking/meals before or after your climb. There are also restrooms at the base and 2 others we saw on the trail.

This is an honest review which I?m only leaving because we weren?t allowed to leave the garden until we promised to give it a TripAdvisor review! Usually I?m much too lazy for such antics.First things first, I think it?s admirable what Bum-young Sung (the owner) has dreamt up and achieved over fifty odd years working here. I also think he has developed very sharp entrepreneurial acumen over this time - the entry fee is 12000 won and thousands of people (us included) seem to be happy to fork this out given the decent ratings Spirited Garden has achieved.Is it worth it? I?d have to say no for the following reasons:1) the garden is actually very small (you can wonder through it in 15-20 minutes).2) even though the trees are nice to look at (debatable given how some of the trees are shackled to metal frames), there are lots of signs imploring you to see the deeper meaning and philosophical undertones of the plants and stones, many of which didn?t really make a lot of sense.3) the owner will probably come to meet you at some point which seems superficially like a nice touch, but it did feel a bit mechanical - he would then get a phone call about some new guests coming into the park and suddenly have to dash off (probably to make sure they left a good TripAdvisor review)All in all, there?s a lot of great nature to see in Jeju, especially if you want to get away from the chaos and ponder the meaning of life, but why not climb up Mt Hallasan or do an Olle trail instead, and then go and spend your 12000 won on a present for yourself

This is an excellent museum featuring contemporary art as well as traditional art. The buildings themselves, which were designed by Tadao Ando, were amazing. It was great just walking around inside while perusing the exhibits & or going for a stroll outside. My favorite part was the sculpture garden, which featured 3 pieces. You can go on the rooftop as well to see another sculpture as well as a great view of Jeju. I was also fortunate to have an opportunity to see Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin & Infinity Mirrored Room. I don't know if it was because I went during off-season, but the museum wasn't crowded at all, so I was able to take my time. I would definitely come back here again if I had a chance

This is an easy walk from the centre of Jeju city. It'a one of the main attractions along the seafront walkway which goes all the way from the port to the airport. You often see the famous Jeju ladies, dressed in their black wetsuits, diving for pearls without breathing equipment.

This is an authentic market which embodies local life on the island. It has so much to offer... There is an entire section devoted to the economy of the elderly, selling their goods and calling sweet encouragements to passerbys. There are regional fruits and veggies, artisan crafters, cloth and clothing sellers, seafood and fresh meats, animals, and a multitude of food trucks/stalls.This is the ideal market for immersing yourself in Jeju and Korean culture. It's open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27thPictured: a pressure cooker used for puffing rice and corn, cooking beans, etc...

This is an amazing market which sells almost everything you can think of. We went with the objective to enjoy some local snacks, get some hallabong tangerine and some jeju chocolate for our friends back home. Although the season for tangerine is over, there are still many available in the market. Prices for the tangerine are quite consistent so we just bought from the first few stalls we saw. There is not many brands for the jeju chocolate so we just picked one and we were told to compare prices with different stalls. For the same brand and quantity, I was quoted 7k, 8k and 10k korean won by 3 different stalls. We ended up buying from one of the biggest stalls in a corner. That said, I do encourage you to buy from the market. I found the same chocolate at the airport and it was selling at 15k korean won. We were too tired to get any local snack in the end but if I ever go back, I will try the seafood restaurant in the market. Was told they serve the cheapest and freshest sashimi in Jeju.

This is Actually botany park with some few nice spots , i really don't recommend it because there is many more to see in jeju better than here and not worth to paying 10$ to seeing something u really don't understand , most of park is designed for professional botanist not for normal people .

This is a wonderful park-like place that includes a portion of lava tube, traditional drums that are available for people to play around on, and apparently numerous classes including pottery. The plantings are fabulous, and there are some examples of Jeju's own dialect.

This is a weak but personal reason to visit this bridge, that is to say, it featured in the first Korean Drama series I ever watched. To put it in a nutshell, the guy followed the girl all the way to Jeju-do in order to convince her he was the one for her. The bridge scene featured just after they landed on the island, so it was just nice to see it in person as part of our stay here. There's not much more to say - I guess other people would have other reasons to visit. As a bonus we spotted women divers going out in their gear so that was some cultural aspect to the visit.

This is a very long beach along the south Jeju coast near the south-western end.  You can bike (there's trial, do segway, or a long walk) or drive and stop along places to take beautiful photos. At the end of the beach is Songacsan where you can hike for an hour or so - very easy.

This is a very interesting coastline with hexagonal rock columns shooting from the water. It is very unbelievable that nature created these columns, since they actually look man-made. It is 2,000 won per person for entrance fee, and it is totally worth it. The only regret is that it is so famous, so it is packed with tourists. The endless blue ocean, dramatic coast line, and the unique stone pillars make this one of my favourite attractions in Jeju.

this is a very good island in jeju, just about 10min from the pier to there and meanwhile you can see many seagulls follow the boat, just for asking the snack in your hand~the island is a good place for a walk, or you can rent a bike, motorbike or electric car(these 2 types needa an international car license) just nearby the pier.and please remember to bring your passport to there cos you needa show your passport when you buy the boat ticket.

This is a very easy climb, you can take the bus from the city in Jeju and go all the way until the car park there the path is well marked and you just have to follow the trail it is an easy ascend to the summit then you can com back the other way (west ascend and east descend) and just follow the way back from the east, it is very easy and well marked all the way back, at the bottom yuo can take the bus back to jeju again.

This is a spot on Jeju island that celebrates its volcanic origins. The whole place is built using wood on a cliff edge with lots of steps going up and down. The viewpoints from here show the hexagonal rocks that were formed a long, long time ago.
