It is a pretty place to spend some time in - you could look out into the sea and meditate, but with the constant stream of visitors, you'd rather move on.

This is a relatively new Buddhist temple build in the 1990's.  Setting is wonderful in a set-back in an Oreum (a subsidiary volcano   mountain  ).  Gardens in front are very nice.  If you like to see Buddhist temples this is probably the biggest and nicest one on Jeju; I recommend visiting.  It's free just walk around.  Allow about 1 hour.
This is a really beautiful place to visit in Jeju! The sand is really fine, and with very refreshing breeze

This is a real village with households living inside, opposite from folk villages built in museums. In fact, the people live there are mainly the haenyeo (women divers) - there is a museum for them in the east coast of Jeju. There is no entrance fee, so the village depends on the sale of souvenirs, basically the blueberries fermented drink and the organic skin creams. A volunteer will assist you to walk around the town, which is very helpful. A site note is that it is often used as a movie set, for example for the movie entitled Dae Jang Gum.
This is a place to view sun rise (according to review), distance about 50km from Jeju-si.If the weather is raining, or cloudy, forget it, this is for the good weather visits.

This is a perfect one-day trip from Jeju, I can imagine it gets packed in season, but on this midweek October day we were pretty much the only people on the Olle trail around the island. It's mostly really easy to follow, with a mixture of red and blue ribbons tied to trees and fences, plus distinctive arrows at junctions. The trail is about 11.5km but we also climbed to the highest point and took a detour to another beach, dawdled, stopped for photos and snacks and still got round in less than 5 hours. Just time for a peanut ice-cream and a snooze on the beach before taking the ferry back. A really relaxing, varied day, like a step back in time to a simpler way of life. Highly recommended/

This is a nice place for sightseeing and exploring the Jeju waterfalls. There was a roughly 5-10 minutes walk before reaching the waterfall, which was fairly simple and pleasant too. The waterfall does not differ greatly from your other waterfalls, so if you?re looking for a unique and different sightseeing experience, I suggest giving this a miss. However, it was still quite magnificient and beautiful if you enjoy sightseeing and waterfalls. Overall, do spend about an hour here to leisurely stroll and sightsee this Jeju wonder.

This is a must-visit place in Jeju-do. Go on a clear, sunny day to enjoy a full panoramic view of east Jeju and the crater. Do try to catch the   Hanyeo   a.k.a. the female divers performance if you can! Be warned though, Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tourist hotspot and it will most certainly be crowded no matter what time you visit.

This is a must-see in Jeju city. It is a local market where they offer souvenirs, food, food, and more food. It is very different to anything I know from central Europe (not the market itself, but the offered food). Note: strong smell to spices and seafood. We bought a stone grandfather in one of the shops, which was offered for two to four (!!) times the price at touristic spots. Here, we found the cheapest price. No idea if tourists still pay a higher price, but we were fine with it (20000 KRW for a ~30cm stone grandfather).

This is a must visit place in Jeju Island. We went up by Eorimok trail and come down using the Yeongsil trail. It was a right choice! These trail doesn't lead to the crater, but the view are amazing thoughout the hiking.Definitely will be back to hike up to the crater to enjoy the breathtaking view on the mountain peak!

This is a must visit in Jeju.  Not only climbing to the peak but I think the entire area is very attractive.  There is the area where you could watch the women divers, there was the vast field where you could go for horse-riding.  It was a very enjoyable and lovely place.

This is a must place if you come visit to Jeju island. So many type of teddy bear collection inside a protected glass, enlarged version for photograph. You will fulfill your child dream and can take photo with a   human   size teddy bear!
This is a must in jeju! This is by far the largest lava tube i've ever seen! We went there just before closing, the lighting made it more majestic!
This is a must in Jeju , I went to HWARO HYANG: 27, Gwandeok-ro 15-gil, Jeju-si, Jeju-do , it is AH MAZING !!!! they have a set or 2 at 50,000 KRW, totally worth it. I will definitely go back !!

This is a must go in Jeju if you are into hiking and scenary. The paths are manageable, but I would recommend proper boots and even crampons during winter season for the snow. It gets really cold, so proper clothing is advised. Just make sure you can take them off when your body heats up during the climb. We managed the climb without crampons (as the shop at the bottom was trying to rip us off), but we took the cheap option at the 2nd check-point of Seongpanak Trail.

This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. The temperature drops quickly: it was 28C outside when we visited in late September but only 15C inside. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.

This is a long but fairly gentle trail up Mt Hallasan. It was extremely busy with people going both ways and most of the path is on wooden boardwalks and steps or basalt rocks. The later are uneven and I'd recommend hiking boots for comfort. There is a place to refill water bottles about half way up and the second of two shelters does some basic foods - noodles, but better to take everything you want with you. The toilets are grim. The crater at the top was rather disappointing with a muddy pool of water at the bottom on the day we went, but there were some splendid views across Jeju Is over all the parasitic volcanos. The lower slopes were very pretty with fall colours at the end of October. However, I've done better hiking with far fewer people in other countries.

This is a lived-in Village.  Locals are still living their lives as how they used to live centuries ago.  That being said, modernity started to encroach into the lives here with satellite dishes being placed outside their residences and that villagers explained that theft & burglary are starting to become a nuisance, most possibly caused by tourists that came to their village.  Here, you got to learn about sustainability measures that were used before and we have to ask ourselves why such tradition isn't continuing.  That being said, there are certain customs that are gone for good measures such as the black pigs that are raised there.  In the olden days, the pigs would be fed faeces by humans and then, their meat would be consumed by humans (recycling)!  Anyhow, this is only applicable if you are genuinely curious about Jeju way of life, which is VERY different from the mainland.

This is a greatt museum and more traditional compared to most of the Jeju ones which can be rather quirky. The Haenyeo museum is well resourced in English, has some lovely photos and details a really important part of Jeju's history. Definitely worth a visit

This is a great place to hike and see lots of nature from Jeju island. You can hike up to Mt. Hallasan, the peak of Jeju or just explore the nearby scenery. In any case, whether it's rainy or there's sunshine, the nature is very relaxing and beautiful. If you're lucky you might see a white deer.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.
This is a cool waterfall. With 35 degree heat the splashing from the powerful waterfall was a nice way to cool down. Of the many waterfalls in Jeju, I feel that this is the best one.

This is a big park where you get to sample the attractions seen in Jeju . We enjoyed visiting the folk museum, flower and bonsai garden, Jeju stone park as well as the place where they have big palm trees. Our time was limited so we didn't really stay here for long.

This is a big area in the outskirts of Jeju city, need to car to get there. There are many stone formations around the park and there is story of an old grandmother who had 500 kids and was finally cooked in the porridge and the kids ate her as they didnt know. There is a nice stone museum that explains how rock formation on Jeju is formed and all about volcanic activities and some weird looking rocks. Educational place for kids!

This is a beauty to behold. The site is really breathtaking! We visited the site after our lunch, it was a sunny day yet it was very cold due to the wind. The site is famous destinations, many tourists come and flock to the cliff, that is why patience is very important if you want to have  good solo and group photos. My Jeju visit was complete due to this wonderful, amazing and lovely cliff. The blue sea is just so enticing. The sound of the waves was mesmerizing and the arrangement of the stones in a unique and beautiful shapes are indeed a beauty to behold. This must be part of the bucketlist for every tourist who will come to Jeju.

This is a beautiful white sand beach. Although there were many local tourist, no one was swimming so I was not sure what was happening. The beachfront is lined with restaurants and hotels. Even the night scene was beautiful with the lighted building. I would recommend visiting this place when you are in Jeju

This is a beautiful volcanic crater well worth visiting. It doesn?t take too long to reach the top from the entrance (despite the sometimes steep stairs). The views are magnificent as you ascend, from the summit, as well as when you descend. Plus there are various volcanic rock formations that you can appreciate along the way, both ascending and descending (the two paths are different). The crater is full of trees and grass of a very unique shade of green (I?ve seen this shade of green only in the vegetation of other extinct volcanic craters such as the ones in Tanzania). There are platforms to sit on at the summit from where you can appreciate the view. After descending, make sure to visit the cove where you can meet the Haenyeo or the traditional fisher women of Jejudo. The way to the cove is clearly marked with signboards and it?s only a couple of staircases down to the beach. The Haenyeo put up a performance twice a day, which is very touristy but interesting nevertheless. You can buy all kinds of fresh seafood from them and ask them to prepare it for you to eat at the restaurant. But it?s mostly eaten raw / semi-raw with various sauces and the typical side dishes. The sea weed is particularly good, which you get as a side dish. There is unfortunately no English menu. If you don?t want to eat raw seafood, after picking your seafood portion at the entrance, take it to the counter inside the restaurant and ask that it be stir-fried (?pokkum? in Korean). Beware that even when it?s stir-fried, it?ll still be more on the raw side than the fried side. The black sand beach in the cove is also a treat. If you look closely and attentively, you?ll find all sorts of marine life among the rocks, in the pools and on the sides of the mini cliffs facing the beach.

This incredible cave flew with lava before. It is typical Jeju world heritage and must visit. The lava flew through all the tunnels and forms interesting geographic features. And another lava melted the roof of the channel and runs down to the first layer of lava. As usual, 2000 for an adult ticket.

This garden is so breathtakingly beautiful, creative, and strategic. I have never visited a garden like this before. All the hard work put into this garden reveals itself throughout the garden. Not only did I get to see the bunjaes but I also learned many valuable lessons about life. Therefore, this place is a must visit in Jeju Island!

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back. It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!

This folk village which has a collection of 600 years old thatched roof houses built using the volcanic basalt rocks and passed on from one generation to another, showcases the unique culture of Jeju Island. The stone statue of Harubang called the grandfather of Jeju and worshipped as the protector of this island can be seen in front of almost all the huts.This village is still inhabited by the locals and one can see them practicing their traditional rituals including rearing of the Black Pigs.By the way ,Jeju is famous for its Black Pork dishes.There are also sites for holding special rituals like praying God for good luck and health, place where breast feeding women pray for lack of milk etc.Our Guide cum Driver Mr Kim Nam Joon (+82-10-4616-6650) not only took us around the village but also ensured we had a good time.

This excellent beach has a lil' bit of everything.  Located not far away from Jeju City/Airport, Hamdeok provides great atmosphere filled with Restaurants, Coffee Shops, waterfronts and one of the most beautiful sunsets in Korea! We sat down in the beachfront walk, cracked open a couple of beers and enjoy the evening breeze.  It was so cool watching people prepping their dinner and drinkin' some Soju while the sound of the waves and live music was heard across the darkness of the night.  We follow the music and found this young talented musician playing guitar and singing on front of a young crowd.  That was the Cherry on top of the Cake!  Stroll & Enjoy!

This crater was a 40 mins drive from our hotel, its absolutely worth the trip. It offer one of the best view among the rest of the jeju major attraction.The climb up to the crater was relatively easy and relaxing which was suitable for all ages, entrance fees to the crater was 9000 won which was reasonable for the stunning view which the crater offered.

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. But the walk along the cliffs was really nice and I enjoyed the beautiful cliff formations.

This cave was decent but the caves in Jeju were much better. It was a nice get-away from the heat since the cave is nice and cool but when I went it was super busy so I was constantly wading through crowds while inside the cave. If you have  a chance to go, try in the off-season or go early in the day to avoid the crowds.

This bridge connects Jeju Island with the islet of Saeseom and resembles an anchored taewoo, a traditional fishing boat of Jeju coming home with a boatful of fish and its wide net streatched.? The name Saeyeongyo means creation of new connections, as it connects uninhabited Saeseom with Jeju.? Come back when it is dark and see the amazing LED light display on the guardrail of the bridge.

this beautiful mountain is located in the east side of island , from centre of jeju to mountain is around more than an hour . entrance ticket is 2 dollar and your journey will start from bottom of mountain , korean made easy stairs which really don't bother u that much . i visited mountain on evening so like sunrise which is famous , sunset can be too . this is a must so go n enjoy it .

This beach, East of Jeju city, on the North coast, is a real gem. Our favourite part is the smaller bay to the East of the main beach. You can rent a static caravan right on the beach there, with an unbeatable, uninterrupted view of the sea. Great snorkelling around the rocks to the right and you can walk up the small oreum further to the right. The main beach has a good eatery that sells Western food and Stella Artois!

This beach was absolutely breathtaking! The sparkling fine sand, emerald clear water, and green hills all around made for a perfect beach day! Unlike what was stated in previous reviews from July 2019, we never had any problems with being able to swim freely and as far out as desired. There was also no line set out not to cross. This is the first beach I've been to with provided shading tents and umbrellas, but it was definitely nice for when we wanted a short break from the sun! We also never had to pay to use these, so I'm not sure if that is something only done during the busy season. The beach was not over crowded, especially at low tide, and it was easy to find little secluded areas if you wanted to be away from the majority of people. Locals were walking and swimming around to clean up trash, so it was honestly one of the cleanest beaches I have been to! Plenty of yummy restaurants to eat at, as well as bars for those wanting to stay out late and still have a view of the water. Be warned, there are no stores close by that sell towels, sunglasses, or other beach essentials, so make sure you are fully prepared! Definite   must see   while in JeJu!

This beach is recommended by all as a   best beach on Jeju  .I'm disagree mostly absolutely.The Jungmun is perfect and ideal and best beach on Jeju for surfers only! And there are pretty overcrowded by them even in September. Waves are good there for beginners and middle surfers (at the moment I've been there).For swimming and relaxing is better to choose other beaches for example Hyeopjae Beach and few other.
This beach is one of the most beariful beaches in Jeju, with its white sand and really good restaurants and coffeeshops nearby. Really recomendable to go!

This beach is good and definitely worth visiting. Admittedly, it didn?t live up to what I had expected when I heard beach. however, I think this is due to me living near the Gold Coast & Sunshine Coast in Australia. Very good a must see of Jeju. ?

This beach is beautiful and amazing! The main beach is usually filled with many tourist, but they have umbrellas and chairs you can rent to get out of the sun every once in a while! There is a great camping site just off the beach where many families camp and it is very cheap 7,000-15,000won. The sand is so soft on the beach and in the ocean! There are many sandbars so the water isn't too deep and makes it great for relaxing in the water! There are great restaurants around, and even the best pizza restaurant place I've been to in all of Jeju! They even have Inflatable tube rides on the back of jetskis and boats. They also have smaller inflatable tubes you can rent for a small price of 5,000 won.

This beach is amazing. It is by far one of my favorites on Jeju. As soon as you arrive there is just a great atmosphere and a great vibe! The view is amazing. There are rocks to take pictures on, chairs set up for the perfect beach picture. The white sand and the blue sea water are beautiful. The water is clear and inviting! It also has great places to eat, a burger place, a taco place, and many cafes where you can get coffee, teas, ice creams, etc. It can get crowded, but should be expected for any beach in Jeju during beach season.

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

This amazing landscape is a must place to go when you visit Jeju. You have to climb up to see the creater and do not worries, just prepare you leg for a stairs (a lot of stairs hahaha). You better wear a comfortable shoes. when i came was sunny, temperature around 18C but the wind was strong, it makes my hair messy & runny nose (prepare face masker will help). The scenery along the way was refreshing & amazing, you will not disapointed.

They will be 1 million Chinese tourists there to join you on your hike up the stairs to the peak. We didn't go for the sunrise which is supposed to be beautiful. That said, the views from the peak are so-so. Hallasan offers much better views (but it's far more challenging).This place is worth stopping by if you aren't pressed for time on Jeju. I'd recommend arriving early in the morning before the hordes of Chinese tourists show up.

They are selling variety of products ranging from skin care, hair care, body care and even food and beverage. Their skin care products are popular in Korea and well known. Besides, if you have times try to buy a hand made soap pack and try to make the soap yourself. It might take time around 1 to 2 hours as there are 3 pieces of soap inside the pack. I would strongly recommend you to try this as this is only available in Jeju island not at other's innisfree branch.

These lava columns are a must to visit when staying on Jeju.  They are basalt hexagonal columns similar to The Giants Causeway in Ireland, though not as big.  We got the bus to the Conference Centre and walked through to the entrance.  They were amazing and were our favourite sight on the island, although you can't actually get down to them and walk on them.

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. The other Teddy Bear Museum where the most expensive Teddy Bear is on display wearing a Louis Vuitton outfit costs KRW 8,000 (Php 347). This one is better because it has so many display that you will be amazed, famous scene, characters, celebrities from different industries. Very nice! This is also the museum where Princess Hour was shot, a Korean novela. I will go back!

There's no variety at all, looks like... Only the exoensive overrated oranges of Jeju. don't get me wrong, they are good, but I would NEVER pay so much money for fruit! Yes, fruit is REALLY expensive in Korea, but 50k is over the top... So: Harabongs, the other oranges in sweets like tartlets and chocolates, black pork jobal, seafood, souvinirs and fruit. That's what you can buy in the market. It was nice to see and the taste some stuff, but i wouldn't visit there again

There's basically nothing here except for the black rock that is sculpted by nature to look like a dragon head.  However, the sea view is pretty. Doesn't need to spend a lot of time here.  Maybe about 10 mins max. There's also a souvenir soup nearby which sells Korean gifts. The shop is not huge but you can find stuffs that typical souvenir shops will sell. eg. keychain, pen, towels, mugs, socks (yes, for some reasons, Koreans are really fond of cute socks with cartoons)..etc.Saw the Roll Hotto snack.  In Singapore, we call this flakey flour pastry as prata. In this case, they rolled the prata with egg and ham complete with vege. Kindda cool.The ice cream they are selling at this attraction is interesting.  I chose 2 flavors: Vanilla and Strawberry. Price is KRW3,000 or RMB20. It's kind of interesting to note that RMB is accepted in Korea as a form of payment. Nonetheless, the ice cream is yummy!More photos available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html.

There's a lot to try and absorb in this open air museum. Maybe too much for your average tourist. I mean the somewhat authentic reproductions were cool for the first three or four structures. I enjoyed having a window into what life was like for peasants 100 - 300 years ago and/or the actors who currently play them in historical television dramas. However the minutia became simply overwhelming especially since there was a tendency to focus on the details as if everyone lived and breathed Korean archaeology. There was also a fairly obvious and persistent attempt to commercialize on cheesy trinkets. Some of the   traditional wares   were okay but I think you can get better quality at lower prices elsewhere. The same can be said for the food. The reenactments of wedding ceremonies and shaman rituals were entertaining and the kids could ride ponies. All in all I was glad to end my tour of this facility. It was a rather pricey way to spend an hour or two. If you were in the area or you have a passion for such things maybe give it a try. However I think there are far better ways to spend your time on Jeju. *You can catch bus 720 at the Bus Terminal for 3300 Won. The trip takes a little over an hour:http://www.rome2rio.com/s/Jeju-si/Jeju-Folk-Village-Museum*Here's a Jeju Weekly piece that might give you a better idea of what this place is all about:http://www.jejuweekly.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=4196

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)

There were many scenic views at this attraction. I enjoyed both the ascent and descent. Even with the chilly breeze, one is sure to perspire upon arrival at the peak. The view into the crater at the peak was another awesome feast for the eyes. The sea as the backdrop served as a picturesque addition to the already scenic composition. After the descent, there were opportunities to witness the infamous women free divers of Jeju. These minimalist free divers were equipped with their orange flotation devices, masks and dry suits, sustained their tradition daily in the frigid waters to harvest seafood from the shallow depths. Why pass on this opportunity?

There were a lot carter in jeju island, one of them is sangamburi.We went there by rent a car, from our hotel around 1 hour. The place is calm and nature. With mountain view, savana and trees all around.If you like nature, this place is one of your choice. One of korean movie was made there.When we entered the place, there's a garden, walked inside there's line of trees, in the middle, there's savana.Going further, you will find mountain view.

There was no sun in a June afternoon, the temperature was pleasant and the air was clear. I climbed up to the top to view the crater which is covered by lush green.  The climb was pleasant along with the gorgeous views.  The views on the way up were lovely, there were many places for great photo op. I appreciated the views from the top, views to the city and views to the sea without interruptions. It was one of the most memorable experiences I recorded in Jeju.

There lies 3 waterfall spots in Seogwipo, south of Jeju. I have went to all 3. But this Cheonjeyeon (not to be confused with Cheonjiyeon waterfall) itself has 3 waterfalls around the area. So in fact, there are 5 waterfalls in Seogwipo. The ticket is more expensive compared to the others but it is worth it as you can visit 3 falls and an arching bridge with nymphs (angels) carvings on the side. I prefer this place to Cheonjiyeon Falls.

There is only specialty on this street which is black pork. There are rows of restaurants selling the famous Jeju black pork. It is a 'Must Eat' in Jeju. There are so many restaurants to choose from so, just choose 1 and have a feast. I would say they serve similar items so doesn't matter which to choose. But as a tourist, you may want to do some homework before going down. We were told by locals to feast in Donsadong but it is not on this street. So, if you want to go to Donsadong, just hail a cab and tell the driver and he will bring you to the restaurant.

There is a secret bunker at on Jeju Island, which once housed old national communication facility and had remained unknown to the public for a long time. This large structure is covered with soil and trees, thus disguised to look like a mountain. This old national facility will be reborn as “Bunker de Lumieres”, a media art exhibition hall that will become Jeju's new landmark for culture and art.

There is a reason that this place was packed.  The museum is located in a super modern building set amongst impeccably groomed grounds and a green tea plantation.  The   museum   part takes 5 minutes to get through but the caf챕 and market is buzzing with tourists enjoying an assortment of green tea treats.  I found lots more tea options at this store than any other in Korea (and there are many!)  But the bonus is the Innisfree store adjacent to the Museum on the same grounds.  Here you can make your own mask concoctions customize soap and find lots high quality unique gifts with Jeju logo on them.  I spent at least an hour here alone.  They also have a caf챕.  Definitely a must stop on Jeju!

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There is a bus from Jeju bus terminal that takes 1hours and a half min and you have to take a Ferry that costs 5,500won.If you dont know how to plan one day travel I would like to recommend you to go Udo and  Seongsan Ilchulbong that is closer to each other If you start your day early you will probably have more time thoughTo see all island it takes 3~4hours by bus that there is Tour bus which costs 5,000wonHowever i would like to recommend you to ride a bike for some partIt is beautiful to ride around the sea and you can feel relaxed.There is 3 beaches that you can visit and those are all different atmosphereespecially there is Coral beach that are exists only 3palce on the world Please go towards the end where people are not crowdedYou will see more pretty coralUdo is famouse for peanut that if you like plz try only small amount since it is a bit expensiveI am not sure if there is famouse food for foreginer but street food is okay As my memory Udo is one of the best part in Jeju island I will recommend for my friends

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty. Yes, the beach itself is a soft sand frame for spectacular sunsets punctuated by occasionally clear blue-green waters, but it's also a growing epicenter for the worst kind of overbooked tourism. Pros: The beach itself is broad, and the area in front of the main beach lends itself to a safe experience for attended children: there is a large, open region of sand at low tide and shallow water at high tide for kids to play in.  The view is nice, and the sunsets are extravagant. There is camping nearby with good tree cover, adequate facilities for showering, stores for trinkets and swimming paraphernalia, and places to buy food and drink. There is also a small but growing night life near the beach that has a distinctly island feel, far from the thumping of your standard Korean club scene. Cons: The swimming area is unbelievably small, so not only does everyone get to experience a sardine style of   swimming   in water that rarely goes past the hips of an adult, the water is also full of sand and debris due to the high person-per-square-meter ratio. Visibility underwater is often zero, so don't expect to see fish on a busy day - which is pretty much the entire high season. There is garbage everywhere, both in the water, and in large, reeking piles near the parking lot. The noise is unbelievable (just like the parking) and the local restaurants - with only one or two exceptions - cater to the lowest common denominator for quality.  Hyeopjae is being targeted by packaged family tours, and yet there is a laughably inadequate infrastructure in place to ensure a safe, organized experience for children. The beautiful volcanic rocks along the sides of the beach and in some parts of the water are playgrounds of minor and major injury. The often unattended children that race up and down the beach are in no way warned about or protected from these hazards. The forest of beach umbrellas tightly packed on the   main beach   is both uncomfortably crowded and poorly organized for parents to keep an eye on their kids, and for kids to find their parents when they get lost. The lifeguards are simultaneously overworked and overzealous. They are simply too busy whistling at people to keep them safe from the dangers of hip-deep water (a strange and annoying tradition amongst Jeju lifeguards) to effectively keep an eye out for people - especially children - who are may be in real trouble.Bottom Line: If you've never had the chance to explore Jeju, you won?t know just how bad Hyeopjae is. Moreover, as I said in the beginning, some people actually enjoy the mass market appeal of tourist traps, and I don't begrudge them their tastes. All I'm saying is Jeju has an embarrassment of better beaches with better food and better facilities. In fact, you only have to travel up or down the road for 15 minutes in either direction to find beautiful, secluded areas where you lavish on an empty beach and swim in truly pristine waters. Q.E.D.

There are three main waterfalls in the south of Jeju and this was the first one we saw, it is the only one by the sea and is about 15 minutes walk from downtown Seogwipo. There is a nice little park before the entrance to the waterfall.We went in the afternoon and it was crowded with many people taking pictures. Would suggest going early in the morning (they open at 8am), better for pictures with the sun shining on the waterfall and less people. Bring proper footwear or shoes you don't mind getting wet as it is very rocky and you can get wet from the spray. Entrance fee is 2000 won and it is a short walk down some stairs to the waterfall.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are several trails to various peaks of Hallasan. Travelling with family and limited time, we only hiked one of the shorter trails i.e. Eorimok. The 1.3 km trail begins where the car park is. From the car park, it is only a 300 meter hike uphill and you are at the top (the lower peak). Being December, there is already snow (or frost?) at the peak. Magical... Oh, and we took a public bus from Jeju bus terminal which costs us less than KRW 2,000 per person, and the park entrance is free. You only pay for parking if you drive there

There are several things to visit and see inside the Hailim Park.  This botanical garden includes bonsai artwork and garden, a Jeju stone, a Jaeam Folk Village, an underground Hyeopjae & Sangyong Cave, and a zoo.  Well worth a visit.  Best time to visit is in the spring especially during the cherry blossom season.

There are many waterfalls in Jeju, we decided to have a look at Cheonjiyeon. There is a large parking lot, eateries and a couple of souvenir shops, 7eleven etc when you arrive. To walk to the waterfall is about 10-15 min along a small tree lined river. Many tourists and tourists groups are visiting the waterfall so it will be quite crowded. The waterfall as such is nice, but not too tall or spectacular. everybody takes a few selfies and then heads back to the parking lot pretty much. If nearby it makes to stop by and visit but it is not worth a long journey just to see this waterfall.

there are many kinds of artworks such as glass flowers,trees,music instrument,toilet,etcworld artist from japan,usa,italy, their works displayed.you can make something like glass cup if you want.it will be memorable while you are in jeju.

There are many beautiful walks along this southern side of Jeju and this is another one. As it was so hot when we visited, our driver took us to a swimming hole among the rocks, down some steep steps at the opposite end of the walk to Oedolgae itself. Our families loved this very much.

There are lots of teddy bears in different dressing inside the museum. It cost KRW10,000 per entry but my opinion is it doesn't worth this amount of money as this museum majors in displaying teddy bear collections in the display box, numerous of human size teddy bears satisfy your photo shooting desires. As compare to KRW10,000 spent in the Jeju Village Folk where cultural living of Jeju residents in the earlier century can be experienced, it's more worthy. Desire to enter this museum was due to the Korea drama series   若モ?, and I expected to have the display of the human size teddy bears in different room with different theme enable for photo session (something like Madame Tussaud's Wax museum) but it is not the way. All the theme teddy are inside the display box. You can just sight seeing it people collection.
There are a number of waterfalls in Jeju, but only one deserves your time. It's amazing to see just how close the water flows directly to the sea.

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

There are a few spots that feature the renowned Jeju women divers. However, this museum is a good place for one to be more acquainted on this tradition and the dwindling of this important part of Jeju history.

There are a few coastal scenary within this area and it's all within 10 to 20 mins drive. Even though it's not extending for miles and miles along the coast, most of the major viewpoints were wonderful. It's a must see if you are visiting Jeju island.

There are 4 main attractions and you easily spend 1.5- 2 hours there, we only go to 2 waterfalls as we afraid there won?t be enough time to go to other places.4 main attractions :Seoningmo bridgeCheonjiyeon Waterfall2nd Waterfall3rd WaterfallSome stairs here and there, don't miss it if you are in Jeju,

There are 3 teddy bear museums in Jeju Island, but this is the only one you could touch and hug, that?s why it?s called safari, while the teddy bears in the other two are kept in the glass box. Although I am not a big fans of soft toys, it?s still cute to see them.

There are 3 memorial towers, one of Kim Man Duk, civil uprising volunteers, and one of patriot at the end of Joseon dynasty. There is Kim Man Duk's grave stone, original one which moved here because of road construction in its original place. This is located in Sara-bong(hill) park. It is very low hi,, but you can enjoy beautiful sunrise on the top of hill. Even day time, I could enjoy nice view toward Jeju international port. I recommend walk around the hill first then visit Mochungsa afterwards, The Sarabong walk path is part of Olle #18. There are many locals who work out here. You can feel like a local!

There are 3 mazes in this park which you are encouraged to try all of them. There were buses of students visiting the maze land when we were there. the kids were good in the mazes and we simply followed them to get out of the mazes. There are also a 'tower' where the teachers made sure the kids don't get into accidents while playing in the mazes. Pretty amazing and fun to spend some time there. But will not return again as we have completed all 3 mazes. Unless, they expand and created a few more, then will consider visiting again the next time I go Jeju.

There are 2 teddy bear museums in Jeju. I don't have the address of the one that I went to, but it's not the one in Jungmun, which is the older one and where you'll only see teddy bears in glass cases. The newer teddy bear museum has teddy bears that are displayed according to themes, where you can pose together  with the teddy bears, and even touch and hug them. This is definitely more interactive than the ones in glass cases.

There are 2 major teddy bear themed attractions in Jeju, One is the Teddy Bear Museum and the other is Jeju Teseum. The Teddy Bear Museum is for mohair connoisseurs, but the bears there are all boxed up in glass exhibits. That is why given the limited amount of time we had in Jeju, we chose to visit Teseum. There are a lot of photo opportunities where we and especially our kids can pose with the many cuddly large-sized teddys at Teseum. The keyword here is interaction.

The world's largest nutmeg forest can be found on Jeju Island, South Korea.  A beautiful, old growth forest with a gigantic nutmeg tree as the central attraction, this forest offers quiet beauty to stroll through in a relaxed and rejuvenating atmosphere. The smell of nutmeg is distinct immediately upon entering.  Parts of the forest have beautiful red crushed stone walking paths and other parts have very well maintained wooden pathways.  To do the whole forest takes about 60 minutes at a comfortable pace.  Picture opportunities abound, and you'll likely be able to see wedding couples posing for their formal pictures amidst the beauty of the forest surroundings.  A great break from the hustle-bustle of other attractions, this forest offers the opportunity to enjoy nature in a very unique way.

The women divers of jeju are famous for their free diving culture of gathering food from the bottom of the sea such as sea cucumber, sea weed, and various shellfish. They are so dedicated to this that It is said that they will start their diving three days after giving birth. They also form unions to govern their way of life and culture. The purpose of this museum also serves to preserve their culture as less and less women are taking up this trade.

The wind blows hard in this area (as the wind turbines might hint at). But the water is beautiful, the sand is white and the rock formations around are really special. It gets crowded but not as crowded as some others on the island. I have seen better beaches for sure, but here in Jeju this one is probably as good as it gets.

The whole way from the car park to the falls itself was scenic. At the start was a pond with mandarin ducks and a bridge. There were various representative statues of Jeju. There were also souvenir shops if you want to buy some snacks or souvenirs. I liked the different types of trees grown, even though it is not autumn, the maple trees still looked very pretty. All along the way is a river, you go to the falls on one side and you can return on the other side of the river. There were plenty of explanation signs on the falls, the mottled eels and the rock face etc. The falls themselves don?t look very impressive but I still like the whole place. On the way back there is a nice flower display and large sculpture as well a stone auditorium.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The waterfall faces the ocean so you can imagine the great view there. Among the famous waterfalls in Jeju, go to this one if you only have time to visit 1. Also, wear comfortable footwear as you need to navigate pass some big unstable rocks to reach the bottom of the waterfall.

The water is amazing. There are 3 waterfall spots and a beautiful bridge to see at this attraction. Highly recommended although the walk can be a pain, especially the last waterfall.The bridge is also quite a sight to behold. This is probably the best waterfall in Jeju.

The water is a beautiful emerald color but the beach is too crowded. Too many parasols, shops, and small hotels. Go to the beach down the road if you want a more relaxing day at the beach.Tip: There are some decent beach style restaurants on the main road. There is nice a pizza cafe with covered outside seating. Also there is a Mom's Touch that servers fast food (chicken sandwiches).This beach is ranked as one of the top beaches in Jeju by Koreans. I was disappointed but I realized that the standards are different. Hey if you want simple food, people, and shade then this is the place to go.

The walking trail at Yongmeori Coast is just a few hundred meters (~700 m) long, but the layered sedimentary structures made from rocks and volcanic ashes, and dramatic shapes created by erosion from hard ocean-waves and wind make it breathtaking art of nature and truly resembles Geopark. It is known that the site is indeed designated as one of the nine Jeju sites certified by the Global Geopark Network in 2010. Personally, this is one of my best scenic places in Jeju in the view of both geology and photography lover.The part of these cliffs appeared stretched out from nearby Sanbangsan Mountain. The meaning of Yongmeori in Korean is Dragon Head. Interestingly, the rough surface of rocks and dramatic shapes formed by rocks due to erosions make it look like a dragon's head going underwater.This part of Jeju is also famous for women sea-drivers. During our visit, we have got an opportunity to try out a few fresh kinds of seafood sold by Korean grandmothers along the coastline. Another attraction near this cliff is the huge shipwreck which is actually a reproduction built as the Hamel Castaway Memorial to commemorate a Dutch sailor (Hendrick Hamel). It is said that he was drifted to the shore of Jeju by a typhoon in 1653. He then wrote a book providing the West some insights into Joseon Korea for the first time. All together this place is very impressive and must not be missed.

The walk up sunrise mountain was  windy and relatively easy. Steps all the way up with many spots for you to rest and take in the beautiful view. Don't miss out on this mountain if you are going to Jeju. Entrance fee is 2000W. They charge for everything here, waterfalls and parks all have an entrance fee.

The walk to Cheonjiyeon Falls is quite easy and beautiful. The waterfall is quire charming as well. However, compared to Cheonjeyeon Falls (which is a 3 tiered waterfall attraction in Jeju not mentioned in TripAdvisor), Cheonjiyeon is still second best.

The visit to Bijarim Forest is a relaxing visit with a closer touch to the nature, feeling calm and peace. The trees looks aged and birds chirping, soft wind blowing. There are many locals walking or jogging in the forest during my visit. I would love to revisit it again if I visit Jeju again.

The view of the so-called Dragon Head Rock will be impressive for some and disappointing for other. My friends and I definitely felt the latter. After a whole day of exploring Jeju, we decided to stop by this attraction to look at the sunset.However, we were greatly disappointed by the attraction as all 4 of us felt that the rock wasn't as impressive as the other attractions we have seen around Jeju. Not to mention the amount of tour buses at this particular attraction was ridiculous. The price of the items and food around the area was also very expensive. I would not recommend this place unless you have a lot of extra time at Jeju. I rather you spend that time on the Olle Trails which provides better view of the coast.

The view is so nice! It's a place where the sunrise and sunset look stunning. its a must visit place if you come to Jeju. I enjoyed the walk, fresh air and most of all the view. This is one of the world heritage in Jeju Island. Visited September 2014
The view is breathtaking. A must place to visit while in Jeju, i?m coming in a spring time, the weather was cool, yet so windy.

The unique thing about this waterfall is it's by the sea. Do wear proper shoes as you would have to climb down stairs and rocks if you want a closer look at the falls. Like most attractions in Jeju, it was awfully crowded. Ap, one doesn't really get a chance to sit and enjoy the falls, which is a pity.
The Udo island is one must visit place in Jeju trip, you can easy to explore the whole island by using bus purchase one ticket or rent a motorbike.

The trek and the views from the mountain were beautiful and I am glad to have spent some time there but I think I may have some had some disillusions/overly high expectations caused in part by Jeju Islands (with Mt. Halla as one of the focal attractions) recent media attention created by its addition to the 'new 7 natural wonders of the world' I found Mt. Halla to be an awesome area but not offering exceptionally greater views than  the many 'mountains' all across mainland South Korea. The trails and park area receive a constant flow of tour bus groups from China, Japan and around Korea year round so if your looking for some seclusion in a natural setting you may want to look elsewhere.  (although it is interesting to see throngs of people decked out head to toe in the latest and most expensive trekking gear unnecessarily)I am working in South Korea so for me the travel costs were rather low and thus my vacation to Jeju Island and trip up Mt. Halla was worth it but I think if I had come from anywhere that doesn't offer a direct flight to Jeju Island (China/Japan/Korea) I would have been a little disappointed.

The trail system in Jeju is quite extensive and well mapped out. Our hotel was right on Olle 7 so one day we went tracking. What started on a normal surface road became a rough surface hiking trail through bushes, up and down a rocky coastline. The trail is indicated by ribbons, from what I understand different colors for different olles. when in Jeju hiking should definitely be on the to do list.

The tour was neat until we were all trapped in a little room for a sales pitch at the end.  It felt a bit awkward for a while as the little Jeju lady gave us a bit of a stare down to purchase some tea and horse oil skin moisturizer.  If you don't speak any Korean, you do not want to go here.  You wouldn't know what is so intersting about this place other than the old, traditional looking homes with thatch roofs.

The title Theme Park may confuse some people. This is not an amusement park, just some natural park with lots of greenery, ponds, windmill, etc. You get on a train that takes you around the park, stopping at several stops where you can get off and later get on the train to move on to the next stop. Honestly, the park is just okay. Not much to see or do here.  I recommend you save your time and find other, more interesting attraction in Jeju

The title summed it all up. I love stuffed toys, but even I found the place overpriced and boring. The ones that held my interest were those actual historical bears. But that's the end it. The elvis show was terrible too. We left the place within the hour.  Take your money and time else where. Jeju has more to offer than this!

The temples and Buddhist statues were gorgeous at the two temples at the foot of Sanbang mountain. The hike up to the grotto is a short 20 minutes, but if you head up in the summer it'll be pretty hot and sweaty, but well worth it. Great cultural trip on any day in Jeju.

The Teddy Bear Museum is quite a fun attraction to visit if you like teddy bears! There's soooo many teddy bears around! With different themes, different era and even teddy bears of very popular characters! (something like the teddy bear version of Madame Tussauds)Full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/teddy-bear-museum/

The strong wind will surely blow your mind to imagination. As an avid fan of K-drama, I was fascinated by the location and the scenery that? will make a great backdrop to make a movie. It has a great view overlooking the sea and another island near to it.It was Autumn season in South Korea when I visited Jeju Island. If you are going solo, there is a public bus accessible to this place.

The story lines are the same, but the performers changed since my last visit in March 2013. However, I really enjoyed this show again! Heard that NANTA Jeju is better than the one shown in Seoul but I cannot justify that.

The stand-alone rock wasn't as impressive as say the Twelve Apostles in Melbourne, but it was nice to walk and take in the sights in the area.If you are a fan of Korean drama serial, Da Changjin (鸚㏝룝), you'll see that they filmed some scenes here (marked by some cut-out boards)On the way out, we saw a store selling black or red volcanic rocks (plus drinks and a really yummy grape ice bar). These rocks float cos of the air trapped in the holes. We bought some home as souvenirs to remember Jeju.I'll recommend taking a walk in the area. The views were great and it was most enjoyable.

The stacked cliffs of Yongmeori are beautiful! This was one of my favorite sites in Jeju. It's a very windy walk but in the summer, this provided respite from the humid heat. The rocks are uneven and bumpy, so it is a good idea to wear sturdy shoes.You have to pay a small fee but it's very much worth it. Along the walk, there are women selling raw seafood meals for 10,000 a pop. It's a very simple set-up: plastic stools and chairs, some garlic, gochujang, and soju if you wish.

The Spirited Garden was a hidden gem for us in Jeju-I stumbled upon it and found it to be very beautiful! Even in the winter, it is educational and charming and I really encourage more young people to come! RM from BTS has even visited and you can get your very own picture like him :) the owner and staff are all especially lovely too and they offer views and treats you can only get in Jeju. Here?s a pic RM posted here:

The spirited garden has a unique and impressive collection of beautiful bonsai trees, stone artwork, and tranquil ponds. Its a great place to spend a couple of hours while visiting Jeju and offers some great photo opportunities. The staff were very kind and helpful.

The soap making workshop is fun and interesting for kids and couples. Innisfree Jeju House is next to the famous O'Sulloc Green tea, you can spend at least 2 to 3 hours in these two placesfor soap making workshop, tea break and photograhping in the tea plantation.

The small village seemed to be tended by a couple who actually live in the village.  I believe the village is government subsidized as well, but perhaps the couple who lives there gets additional money from selling some products (more on that later).A lady who lives there gave us a tour of the houses at the village.  She started off with where she lives - which is traditional on the outside, but seemed to have all the modern features on the inside.  We then got a small explanation of the milling device there as well and a water collecting jar.  We were also allowed to put one of the water jars on our backs.  A little pig pen and outhouse were shown as well.Unfortunately, the final destination for the tour was a small room where our tour guide could give us a hard sell on some products - mainly some horse cream or something like that...  That sort of ruined the tour, but I could imagine that this could be the tour guide's main source of income.  And she was kind when we said no to the hard sell.The tour was informative in many ways as the tour guide provided a lot of information and stories of the hardship and struggles of the native Jeju people.

The site was the best part of an all day trip covering the eastern end of Jeju Island. Such places are always fascinating. As soon as you enter, the temperature drops to the lower double digits C.There is a one kilometer stretch you can walk. I like that it has not been jazzed up with a rainbow of colours. The floor is naturally uneven with some sectors covered in wood. The cave is 18 meters as its widest and  23 meters as its tallest. At the far end is located the world tallest lava column at 7.6 meters. When you appreciate the force of Mother Nature to cause such formations, it only adds to the visit.

The short hike is easy with stairs. I went up for sun rise and sunset. The view is magnificent. There are convenience stores CU and GS25 nearby, but GS25 is further. The CU is not opened so early for sunrise hike and its staff is rather unfriendly though. Overall, I would hike again Seongsan ilchulbong if I visit Jeju again.

The Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak has 2 main attractions. The first is obviously the climb to the peak itself. The second is the Woman Divers at the black sand beach at the bottom. We spent about 3 hours here and it was just barely enough. The climb is actually not that bad for the physically fit. The steps are steady and most are stone paved or have wooden stairs. There were quite a few elderly ladies/gents climbing too. Rest areas with benches are plentiful, so there really is no reason why you would not try for the top if you have the time. :-) Two thirds of the way up, you will see a big resting area with a marvelous view of the city below. Once you are up at the peak, you will also be able to see the city view AND into the crater. The climb back down is very safe with well made wooden staircases. Regarding the Woman Diver show at the bottom, I found the show to be a little underwhelming and a bit too touristy. However, it was still an interesting experience to see divers selling fresh seafood off the beach. If you have limited time, I would recommend that you focus on the hike/view, and just spend a couple of minutes to browse through the woman diver area. I think the Seongsan Iichulbong is a must-see in Jeju.

The Seongeup Folk Village was a walled-in village in the southeast of the island where stone homes showed the construction, culture and lifestyle of the island?s people long ago.Obviously, Jeju wants to maintain some type of historical reference to the old lifestyle.  Our tour guide made it interesting by talking about some practical aspects of the design of the huts (how it was heated, how it was built, etc), but this just wasn't my thing.  In fact, several families that help with the upkeep of the huts actually live in other huts in the community.  That said, those huts have modern adjustments like windows, electric power, etc so even they have moved beyond the   old ways  .  The village had a few shops and a restroom and outside the village was a convenience store with drinks available and another restroom. For me, the bottom line was - I would have preferred to spend the time at a natural landmark (waterfall, cave, hiking trail, etc) instead of doing this, but it was part of an all day tour.  There are simply too many other options to see in Jeju for this to make it to the top of the list, unless it is your   thing  .

The Seongeup Folk Village is huge.  The main entrance has a big car park and a side entrance where you can drive your car in.  Besides the car park, there are many restaurants, two public toilets and a few shops.From the main entrance, you can take a stroll and check out some of the conserved buildings which are open to public.  Information is available in English and you can learn about the earlier settlers and buildings of Jeju Island.  There are also some shops and restaurants inside the folk village.You can easily spend 1-2 hours inside the village and having lunch either in the restaurants inside or besides the car park.  We had delicious black pork bbq at Nammun restaurant (787 2432) located in the area besides the car park.Tip:There are other entrances to the village as well.  I was at one of these prior to finding the main entrance, and there are sales people trying to get us to into houses outside the gate and market horse oil cream and other products.  Avoid these.  While I can't verify whether the products are authentic, it definitely felt like a scam.  Seemed that some reviewers thought this is part of the folk village.

The sea in Jeju Island was very clean and a good place to enjoy the natural scenery. There were many kinds of cafes and long coastal roads. Also, the cafes had unique personalities and were good places to take pictures and the taste of coffee was good. I went there for 2 nights and 3 days, and I could see the beautiful sea when the sun was bright, and there was a dark atmosphere of the sea when the weather was cloudy. However, unlike in the past, the whole atmosphere of the sea seemed to disappear as many buildings were built. There was a wish for a return to the old sea. Nevertheless, if I visited Jeju Island again, I wanted to go to Woljeongri Beach again. Viewers of this review also recommend going to Woljeongri beach where I went.

The rocks surrounded by the island have different size and have eroded for years. But the most interesting thing is that rocks are eroded into different levels of cylinders, so it is worth to spend a couple of minutes there taking photos and have a look. Moreover, there are paths for visitors to walk around the edges of the island to have different look of the rocks. It is the margin of Jeju, so when the wave flaps the cliffs, it creates a huge noise. At first, I thought it was something like weapons exposed, my heart pumped faster than normal. After I recognize it is only the wave hits the cliffs, I can clearly experience that how the level of power that the nature can be. It was an unforgettable experience.So, if you have an iPhone which contains the program of Live Photo, try to open it before you take photos. It is because you can record the energetic movement of wave in your photo.

The rock formations are quite impressive especially if you know the history behind how it's formed. Come with no expectations and just to enjoy another set if mother nature's wonders.. Jeju is all about chilling with no expectations.. No pretense, what you see is what you get

The rock by the coastline is not really spectacular, but it is closed to the city and the hotel we stayed, we went there for watching sunset and had a good view.  I suggest you spend one evening there if you stay in Jeju city.

The road was called mysterious road as it seem to be a up slope but your vehicle can move slowly up like going down slope. The area is less crowded at around 7-9am until the tour bus came, where many people actually went down to crowd around this road. The tour bus would stop at the start of the slope and off its Engine and slowly moved up to the end and turn into the car park where the tourists would come down and see cars moving up. Some of them would pour water to show that the water went up instead of down. It is quite mind boggling. But actual fact that this road is due to the surrounding which makes you have the perception thinking it is a up slope but actually it is down.Way to get there is by Car or Bus. It is close to Jeju LoveLand and it is down the same road, so it is not too difficult to find.

The products they sell are overpriced compared to the innisfree stores in Busan, Daegu and Seoul so don't bother buying from them. There really isn't much to see apart from the fact that it is rather close to the O?셲ulloc Tea Museum.TLDR: Not worth your time, Jeju is so beautiful go somewhere else!

The previous review states that the climb was in 20 minutes but for a relatively unfit person like myself, it took me 30 to 40 minutes with numerous stops beginning from halfway till the top. Much to your agitation, we see older citizens and children alike happily and easily climbing the steps and overtook you to the top. Nevertheless, the view on the top was well worth the tough climb (according to my unfit status). Managed to take some photo shots of the surrounding and the crater itself. As it was just beginning spring, the crater floor was covered with brownish grass and vegetation, not the greenish color you would expect in summer. What I most remembered was the real cold buffeting wind of 2 Degrees Celsius blowing and you could really feel it even with winter jackets and caps worn while climbing the steps. But it was most memorable. Wife did not want to climb the steps but decided to go shopping for the famous Jeju orange chocolates in the shops at the foot of the park.

The place is small. According to the guide (a man who lives there), that is his house passed down to him by his ancestors. He speaks English and some of our Malay language (impressive). It was very compact with the history of the island, culture, food, the roles of men/ women in Jeju, architecture, etc. He was a fun man with a lively way of presenting the information. I think it was excellent. Listening to him is like reading a small introductory chapter about Jeju. There was no fee collected, I appreciate that. However, at the end of the visit, he showed us some local products which we happily bought (the tea) because the children like it.

The place is breathtaking, starting from the parking lot with all the old ladies selling the traditional stuff, the park is amazing with the clear water and swimming ducks & fish, the sakora tree is more than beautiful, then the waterfall i can?t even describe its beauty....and the ticket cost only 2000 Korean won . Inside the park there is a clean toilet and services alsoIf you go to jeju you must visit it
The place is beautiful, scenic and great for photos. The Buddha sculptures are grand. A definite place to go in Jeju. In winter time, expect snow here and it can be few inches thick.

The people here still preserve the living style from ancient time. When we mention to our driver that we wanted to visit a folk village, he asked us if we wanted to visit the   fake   or   authentic  , and here we are, chosen the original folk village.We were greeted by one of the villager there 竊sorry for not remembering his name). He brought us around for a 15 mins tour, introduction to jeju, an island with no gate, no thief and no beggar. And the introduction to jeju's   gate  , haruebang, etc.Towards the end of the trip, he was trying to sell the cactus honey and horse bones medication to us. There's no hard sell though, he just let us go after we said no.

The Peace Park is very spacious and beautifully laid out.  (Shouldn't compare but it reminded us of  a smaller version of the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, UK.)  They were still working on some landscaping while we were there.   We were lucky enough to catch the excellent art exhibition that is on at the moment and the museum display is very well laid out and informative - lots of English  so we learnt a lot about the Jeju's history around 1948.   We were there about 1.5 hours but could have stayed longer.

The park is well manicured and you can take great pictures of scenery with fences. There are swings near the top where you can enjoy the breeze while taking in the scenery of the surrounding lands and mountains.  You can also see the bottom of the   green crater   from the top.This is one of the more expensive natural attractions in Jeju (KRW6,000) but I feel it's a good place to relax and worth a visit.

The park is the mystical legend of how three gods arrived in Jeju-do and started to develop the island. The place is a great escape from the busy city of Jeju, surrounded with trees and pavilion of traditional Korean architecture. You can also sit in for a 15 minutes long animation, available both in English and Korean  describing the origins of Jeju.

The park is nice and had a good size. There are a variety of different sections and when you add it all up it gives a good mini summary of Jeju - with the caves, stone park, waterfall, historical aspects, flower garden, and bird park. If you have only 2-3 days in Jeju this should be a must on the itinerary.

The park is big and have many to see, especially for people who don't know the culture of Jeju. It would be also good for family but since it requires lots of walks I wouldn't recommend elder people who can't walk for a long time. The weather of the day we went wasn't quite good, but the drizzle and fog made that place more mysterious which is quite special because we saw different type of scenery from those pictures you can find from the Internet.

The park is a unique in the sense that it is dedicated to stones in Jeju culture. Lots of statues, pavilion with the history of volcanic activity, some traditional houses, old sculptures, big and small. Large space, a lot of walking.

The only waterfall in Jeju that drains directly into the ocean is worth stopping by for around half an hour. Ample parking space, free admission, good accessibility and the ability to get quite close to the waterfall even if it isn't that tall.

The one way trail to Mount Hallasan was a challenge... but we conquered it. It was a good work out as we climbed to the top. Good thing there were stations where we can rest, chit chat and laugh....We were inspired by the older people , even not in sneakers , who were able to achieve the same task with no complaints .... going down the trail was a breeze... a good cool down..... a must see in Jeju-do!!!
The Oedolgae Rock was just a vertical piece of rock and did not excite me too much. However, the trail after the rock is scenic and has the best sunset view in Jeju. Do not miss it!
The natural waterfall in the raw form and walking in the rocks is fun. The surprise was a fresh Jeju orange juice nearby, the seller was honest and nice.

The natural beauty of the lava tubes entertained my mother, husband, and myself for nearly two hours of appreciating God's creation. For only 2,000 kw per person, I recommend this highly as one of Jeju's most impressive tourist spots!

The Mysterious Road is an interesting to visit while in Jeju and don't need to pay. The Bus Driver show that even with the engine stopped, the bus still able to move forward. The visit won't take too much of the time, just interestingly an eye illumination.

The museum is quite interesting if you're interested in geology.  It's nice to get a decent scientific understanding of how and why the other things you'll likely be seeing on Jeju (Hallasan, Seongsan Ilchulbong, etc.) are the way they are.  If geology bores the heck out of you, then skip the museum, but don't skip the park altogether.  It's really quite a beautiful place to walk around, especially if you're in the mood for something somewhat quiet and relaxing.  Major crowds can make some of the the other sites on Jeju quite the opposite of that, so it's nice to find a place that's legitimately peaceful.

The museum is full of teddies of all sizes created from all the Korean dramas begining with the classic   Winter Sonata   till the American President Obama. On the rooftop, you can view the whole valley of Jejudo as well as the scenic Hallasan. There are some cookies for sampling and plenty of teddies for sale in the shop at the end of the tour^^~

The moment I set my eyes on this island, I knew I was in heaven. The water looked extraordinary blue and the view was nothing short of a perfect dreamy scenery. We took a day trip on the ferry from jeju. On the island, we took the hop on hop off bus. Take any bus, doesn't really matter.. They will then tell you which color buses u can hop onto at the next destination along with a list of places they will stop at. I think it costs around 2200 won. The island was crowded specially with all the bikes but still it is not to be missed. The first stop was the udo peak. A hike of around 30 mins to a lighthouse from where you can see the entire islans. The view of the sunrise peak on jeju all along the hike was incredible!
