Then the bus took us to 2 beaches..one was a black sand beach which had a little cave but tides were high that day. We missed the 2nd beach and went to the last one with white sand. This beach was quite close to the port and we walked to the port from here along the coast. It was a beautiful walk and less crowded.There are lot of shops and cafes in front of the last beach.

The market mainly consists of two parts: a fruit market (mostly for visitors) and a fish market (mostly for local, as visitors basically can?t do anything with the raw fishes). In night time, there is also food stalls near Gate 8 but the number is limited (I think there?s about 20) so the queue is often long - mostly Korean youngsters. My Korean friend told me that Jeju is unique with its rice cake (similar to Japanese mochi) and orange that even Koreans ?have to? purchase as gifts when visiting Jeju thus their prices are not cheap.

The market gets busy after lunch and into the night around 9pm. You can find all sorts of food options and souvenirs in this market...from street foods  to hand-made mochi  to yummy waffles  to restaurant food... There are many cosmetic stores around the market  where you can get cheap facial masks and reasonably priced   volcanic clay mask   jars - a must-purchase in Jeju!

The marker for Routes 13, 14 and 14-1 are located in one spot. We got confused at first that we ended up completing abour 2-3km of Trail 14 until we got to another marker that we realized we were following the wrong path. We went back to the spot and started looking for the 14-1 trail. We spent the first half of the day doing Trail 14.When we headed to Trail 14-1 which was the intial plan, it was past noon already so the sun was up and it was hot (we did the trail on a summer day). It was a cool experience because the trail will bring you to the peak where you get a great 360 degree view of Jeju! It will take you inside a forest. You might even meet some horses along the way. By the time you'll get to the midpoint, which is the Osulloc Museum, you will realize how much you miss civilization and strangers. The trail will connect you to nature. You'll even find yourself in a dense forest! There are a lot of blue/orange ribbons so you won't be lost. This trail taught me to simply trust and find the blue/orange ribbons and enjoy/embrace nature wherever the trail (or life in general) may take you. Haha. This is definitely off the beaten path but it makes your Jeju tour even more special and truly your own. I would want to do more of the Olleh Trails in the future :)

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!
The lonely tree is a amazing place for taking photos, due it's location in a vast landscape is a good place to take photos and explore the beatitude of Jeju.

The locals come here for a picnic. This place also has a few playgrounds for children. If you ever wanted to go to the observatory, it would require some hiking so wear proper clothes. Was the view worth the hike? I think other places in Jeju provide better views than the one here.

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The kids found this easier than we adults! At 3,300 for adults we found this good value.  The history behind this place was interesting.  Founded by an Aussie from WA who was the first foreigner to the area in the 80's.  He is still alive and has done much for the people of Jeju.  He obviously likes cats there's one lazing around every corner at the entrance!  It's a kids thing really but I'm glad I did it.  The guy on the door spoke quite good English and was very engaging.

The Jungang Undergroung Shopping Center was among the shopping stops that we had for our Jeju tour package. The area is sizeable. There are 12 gates conveniently marked?I had to remember Gate 5 since this is where our tour bus was scheduled to pick us up.  There were beauty products, clothes, cosmetics, more clothes, more beauty products?did I already mention clothes and cosmetics? The clothes and bags sold here are not your designer stuff but cheaper items. The cosmetics sold here are similar to what you have at every corner in Korea. If you are looking for really inexpensive items, it is better going to the Dongmun Market. If you want branded items, head to the Chilseongro Fashion Street. Both these locations are nearby, at Gates 2 and 3 respectively. The only redeeming factor that the Jungang Underground Shopping Center is that it is indoors and has climate control, which is useful for a cold winter day.

The Jeongbang Waterfall is one of the   Big Three   on Jeju. This one is particularly stunning as the water falls down over the cliffs to the beach below. You can get very close to the water (your camera will get wet) and get some stunning photos. There are good facilities at the top and the walk down isn't too strenuous.

The Jeju Uprising/Massacre (or simply 4.3), with up to 80,000 villagers killed by the military, took place just prior to the Korean War but is relevant today as South Korea re-militarizes the Island of Peace. Go to the museum, then witness the current hot protests against a naval base being constructed in the fishing/farming village of Gangjeong (between Seogwipo and Jungmun), along the Ollie Trail.

The Jeju Olle Trail is an island-wide wooden path that takes you to the hills, rivers, beaches, and into the woods of Jeju. This is the perfect break from the busy urban jungle or if you want a break from the treadmill. Once on top of a hill, you will be offered a great view of the island.I took route 8 and connected to another route. I jogged some parts of the path and walked some (as some parts of the path are composed of stairs). It may be safer to walk since some parts of the path have no railing.Bonuses:There are huts and platforms that serve as resting areas. I encountered a local doing yoga in one of the huts.The river-side path has toilets and emergency rescue equipment ( life buoy, life vest, rope). Tips: Bring a camera, some sights are worth capturing; wear running shoes; and bring a phone, your GPS can be helpful in estimating your location.The path goes through or into private properties so be mindful not to trespass.

The Jeju Mysterious Road, also known as Dokkaebi Road, lies on a hill at the foot of a mountain, and connects two major highways on Jejudo Island. It has earned its name, as objects and liquid appear to roll and flow up the hill instead of down, when, in fact, such image of gravity defiance is an optical illusion rendered by the seemingly high surroundings.

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

The Jeju Fire Festival (now renamed the Field Burning festival) takes place every year and is a huge celebration, with music, dance, enormous quantities of food from many different places. It is on The last evening that the Oreum (hill) is set fire to.Allow plenty of time to get in and park (shuttle buses from Jeju city are probably a better idea, as it can also take an hour or more to get out with your car afterwards.

The Jeju City 5-day traditional market is a place to visit if you happened to be in Jeju on the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd and 27th of the month. It is the biggest and oldest among the other 5-day markets. The place is big and the locals sell wares ranging from fishes, livestocks, clothings, hats, crockery, flowers, agricultural produce, local food stuffs, etc. The place is noisy and colorful, crowded and they add excitement to your visit. It is    When in Jeju, do as the local folks do  .

The island is beautiful but difficult to get around with out renting a motorbike. However, motorbike only fits two people and you need an international driver's permit. The wind was too strong to walk around or bike in. There were a total of 3 of us that went and it would have been worth it to drive the car over from Jeju island because it cost the same as a tourist bus for all three of us.Other than figuring out transportation, it's a beautiful island to chill at and enjoy nature.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The hike was an easy one with stairs. Less than one hour slow pace hiking up. My brother brought his baby as well in baby carrier. There are a lot of souvenir shops nearby. In my experience, the souvenir sold there is much cheaper than the one in Jeju City.

The hike up to the peak and return takes around 50 mins-1 hour. There are quite some stairs to climb so may take longer if you're travelling with elders.  The view from the top is magnificent and the trail of stairs when you look down is also amazing. On your way down, you can watch the   Sea Women Performance   where they put on their diving suits and catch clams/seafood from the sea. The show is at 1pm and 3pm and will be cancelled due to rain/poor weather. Definitely #1 attraction in Jeju. In terms of admission fee, there's a booth at the entrance so we bought tickets. But we also see quite a lot of people who went in without paying, maybe its an honour system.

The highlight of my visit to Jeju was reaching the Baengnokdam - the crater lake at the summit of Hallasan. The trail is superb with great views and different landscapes. The trail has 8.7km (one way to the summit) and one has to reach a check point that is 3km from the summit by 12pm, hence plan accordingly. During the winter I highly recommend good boots, crampons and sticks as from certain point it gets snowy and icy.It is a long and exhausting day, but completely worth it!

The highlight of my trip to Jeju was visiting Udo, which is small enough to be traversed by bike in a matter of hours. My girlfriend and I were glad to chose the pedal-bikes over the motorbikes and car tours because, with all the different little coffee shops and sites to explore, you'll want to take your time. While you may not find much in the way of   impressive historical sites   compared to other places in Korea or the rest of Asia, this is a beautiful place if you're just looking to relax, meandering the coast with friends or a loved one, and enjoying some local treats. It's also very scenic, so super easy to capture scenic photos. The people were also super-friendly in helping you get around, even despite the language barrier. I'd love to return again.

The Hallasan National Park, South Korea?s tallest mountain, is a place that is definitely worth visiting on a trip Jejudo. There are 5 trails up the Halla Mountain, but only two can lead you to the summit where the Crater Lake is. Some sections are quite steep and takes some effort and time but the view at the top is definitely worthwhile. Start the climb as early in the day as possible to avoid crowds as well as to ensure that you have plenty of time to hike up and down the mountain. The hike has to be done in one go since there are no overnight shelters available. The best descending route is the Yeongshil trail, which is the most scenic of the 5 routes. The view is just MAGNIFICENT and it is a relatively easy descent. On a clear day you could see right down to Seogwipo on your way down. You?ll also be able to see the numerous parasitic cones located around Hallasan. The terrain changes as the altitude changes and it can get chilly at the top even on a summer day. So dress in layers accordingly. Make sure to check the weather in advance and set out on a sunny day since it will be very difficult to climb in rainy or foggy weather. You will not be allowed to summit anyway under such weather conditions (or if you arrive late). There are buses which bring you to the trailheads from both Jeju city and Seogwipo. So it?s not hard to reach by public transport.

The Halla Arboretum is a sort of giant tree garden/park spread out over a mountain with innumerable trails that span the mountain side, leading to the top.  Key trees are labeled in museum fashion though the information provided is minimal.  Think of the arboretum as a park on a hillside with paths leading to a summit with views of the peak and city.  It's quietly beautiful with the cool air gently perfumed by the trees and soil.  If you are traveling on Jeju and are looking for a place to spend d1-2 hours, the Halla Arboreteum is a good call.

The grounds are HUGE! It felt like a nature forest walk, a geography and history field trip all rolled into one.I don't know if it's windy there all the time, but when we were there, it was freezing when the wind blew when we were in the shade.We had a tour guide who explained the various rock features and how/why people carved the stones for use in the past. But honestly, I was bored after awhile. This place had rocks/stones galore. Considering that there are so many other things to see/do in Jeju, I would give this place a miss.
The Glass Castle offers many interesting pieces of art for one to view, I recommend this destination to anyone visiting Jeju.

The garden was one of the best i have visited. Sense of peace and calm just being in here. Went on a day with good weather and the photos turned out absolutely captivating. The spirit of cultivating and nurturing bonsai plants and trees was brought across and many moments, made me ponder about life. One of the best things to do in Jeju. Definitely worth a visit

The first impression and experience was good. After a while, everything else looked the same. The same sea, mountains and stones, albeit in a different formation. There are beach bikes for rent, which I think will be fun but we didn't enjoy that because we had hired a taxi for the Jeju trip.
The famous black pork meat in Jeju island, great meals for the dinner. A lot of black pork restaurant at here.

The entry fee is abit on the high side, but if you love gardens, plants, nature, and especially flowers, it’s worth every penny. My absolute favourite place to visit in Jeju. I love flowers so we spent around 4 hours here. There’s a huge variety of flowers, and the gardens/areas are very well laid-out. Besides the greenhouse, there is also an area outside where all the different-themed gardens are (Korean, Japanese, French etc), there are about 12 gardens in total I think, and all of them are really beautiful. I think this attraction is still relatively new, as I could still see gardeners setting up the flower beds and so on. But this also means that it’s not crowded yet and there are relatively few tourists compared to the other attractions. Flower-lovers, this is a must-visit!

The dragon head rock is in North part of Jeju, close to the airport. It is a rock that looks like a dragon head on the coast. The Seogwipo coast line like the Jusanjeolli Cliff or the Odelgae Rock are much more interesting than this. However, if you do not have time to visit the Jungmun/Seogwipo area, this is an alternative to see the rocky coastline. The sunset here is nice, but the place is packed with tourists fighting to get photos, so it's not all that romantic. I think a beach sunset at a more remote beach on the West side would be nicer and a calmer experience.

The dragon head rock is a good place to visit, if your wanting to stay close to jeju si. It doesnt take long to look at the rock and there are many tourists but the costal road is a nice relaxing walk.

The cruise ship docked in Jeju South Koren for a few hours. We didn?t plan anything, just walked around downtown.  We saw a flight of stairs, looks like it leads to some metro station, so we went down to take a look. It is a huge underground shopping center. They sell clothing, accessories, shoes and cosmetics. This is a shopper?s haven. They also have free Wi-Fi that you can connect with family and friends. Although we don?t know their language, but the people are very friendly and helpful. I don?t mind to visit Jeju again.Happy Travelling!

The crater is one of the better natural sights on Jeju Island.  It's certainly not as picturesque or close in scale to Crater Lake in Oregon, but the area around it is quite picturesque.  The crater itself (supposedly a flatland crater) is nothing special in terms of scenery.  It just seems to be a shallow hole in the ground a two thousand feet in diameter.  However, the surrounding area has lots of grass, trees, and flowers for people to explore.  Interestingly, there also seemed to be some burial plots in the area.  I'm not sure why that was the case.Just note that there are plenty of areas to explore and some trails/walkways are fairly steep.  I can also imagine that the place would be very beautiful during a sunrise or sunset.  This was one of the few places I hoped I could have stayed a little longer to enjoy.  Note, it was quite cold, foggy, and windy when I went in November.

The cone-dome architecture is interesting, the roofs of different gardens within culminates to a peak into the center of the compound and u can take a lift up to catch a 360 panoramic glimpse of the surroundings (see pic). However, adult tix are at 9000krw per person which is not cheap for what u get within. The place has lots of potential but not that well-maintained as the place looks very weathered on the whole. There is a garden dedicated to tropical fruits but those are mostly common fruits for southeast Asians like us. There were only chrysanthemums at the entrance even though it's supposed to be in-season. Parking is easy though, and free, like most places of interests at Jeju. Overall, this place is more suitable for the elders and for people dropping by to visit Cheonjeyeon falls and Seonimgyo Bridge, which is just next door. Otherwise, my 2c worth - it'll be fine to spend your money elsewhere.

The concept of the Innisfree Jeju House is nice. Good brand extension. However, don't expect great bargains on cosmetics. As a matter of fact, the range is limited. Best to buy from Seoul or other major cities. The cafe is a nice place to rest with some interesting food choices. However, it's always crowded and thus the ambience is not too conducive for a nice tea session. Overall, it's a nice short introduction to the use of tea in Innisfree product range.

The coastline along the bottom of Jeju-do, near Seogwipo is truly beautiful. Such clear blue waters and jagged, unusually shaped rocks and little rock pools everywhere - they look as though they were made for people to swim in! Oedolgae is found along this coastline, and while it is really only mildly interesting (it is just a strange-shaped rock sticking out of the water - apparently once scared off invading Mongolians), it is worth seeking out just to walk along the paths in the park near it. The rock pools along the coast line here would be perfect to swim in, in hot weather.
The climb was relatively easy as it had well build steps all the way to the top. The view from the top of the crater, overlooking Jeju Island is what makes it all worth while.

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It?s 2000?? pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It?s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

The Cliffs are an amazing volcanic rock formation on Jeju Island. It is an easy bus ride from one of the hotels. Get off at the Convention Center and walk about 500m to the park area. You can expect the viewing areas to be very crowded, full of people taking their time with photos. Look closely for the cylindrical formations. Very cool geology.

The cliff was very beautiful and unique, and is definitely worth a visit if you?re looking for nice sightseeing views in Jeju. However, other than viewing the cliffs, there was nothing much to do, so spending an hour or less there would be sufficient. Do head down the viewing platform to the bottom of the cliffs, where you can get a magnificent view at sea level, with lesser tourists there. Overall, if you?re looking for a short sightseeing trip, these cliffs would be a good option to explore the wonders of Jeju.

The cliff is located on the southern side of Jeju Island in the township of Seogwipo. A well-laid stair-way/boardwalk has been constructed for visitors to view and appreciate the natural rock formations of hexagonal lave tubes. These make great photo shots when framed with overhanging pine trees, crashing waves, clear blue skies and setting sun. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry and hordes of tourists, especially students on excursion. What an incredible place to spend an hour or two!

The Cheonjeyeon Falls was a memorable last stop of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour. The size of the entire park the falls are situated in is generally small, but it's loaded with so many sights to see. In the entrance, you're immediately greeted with a beautiful pagoda and lush well-kept gardens. There's also a wishing fountain called the Fountain of Five Blessings that's worthy of your participation as the coins tossed inside the fountain are donated to Korea's underprivileged. Entering the site, one has to cross an intricately beautiful bridge which is elegant and regal in its own right. After that, the trek to the falls; sites begins. The entire trek is paved with concrete steps which make it more convenient and safer for visitors, especially as the trek requires ascend and decline quite a lot. Although, be prepared for a light workout as the number of steps do add up if you complete the entire trek (there are quick detours to the exit for those who don't wish to complete the entire trek or those grappling with a fear of heights).Shoutout to our amazing tour guide from Yeha Bus Tour for going the extra mile in making our entire tour enjoyable!

The cave is very nice, different from all other sights in Jeju. It?s a short walk but the ground is wet inside and can be slippery, also a bit dark in certain places. Wear a hoodie as water drops from the cave roof. Not recommended for people with mobility issues.Once inside, the sight is beautiful, it?s an amazing work of nature.

The cave is a must visit when come to Jeju. Be it winter, spring, summer, autumn... The temperate inside the cave stay the same through out the season. The rock inside the cave just so beautiful... Especially the one towards the end of the cave.

The bus driver has completely stopped the engine at the starting point of Jeju Mysterious road and once he release the break the bus moves eventhough it is an upward slope...Why? The answer we got from the tour guide is that, it is an optical illusion - that actually it is a downward slope. Well it doesnt look like that at the time and even now I couldnt believe it is a downward instead of an upward slope - believe it or not!!

The building is attached to the   jeju tourism   board (or something like that). It costs about 4 or 5 000 won to get in  then handed a coupon for a discount at the cafe or any of the products. The children enjoyed it as they got to make chocolate for 10 000 which included a take home mold. The museum isn't much to look at but just enough to make your mouth water. It is close enough to all the other activities in the area  if traveling with kids  this is a good   trade off   point to let them have some fun.

The bridge during night time was nice. I saw this on the plane from Seoul to Jeju. At first I came to see the sea next to it, but then I suddenly saw the bridge and thought it looked beautiful. It really brightens up the dark.

The best we have seen in Jeju.Though the water was a bit too cold for us to swim, it's great for wading during low tide.You can even rent clear bottom kayak to paddle around.There are lots of convenient stores, burger and coffee places and other local eateries around there.Definitely worth a visit.

The best time to go is early in the morning, to see the sun rise. I had gone a little after the sunrise and many people were already on their way down. The views are spectacular and the way up is very safe, and good for all ages. This was probably the most memorable part of Jeju Island.

the best thing to do in jeju, it wasnt that attractive for me while i search udo online, my friend made me go with her, when i got there, im so glad i did it, it was so laid back, so nice, the circle island bike was awesome, the sunset, nice people. we enjoyed it a lot and forgot the boat time. we were late for the boat back to jeju, so we have to paid for personal boat, was way so expensive.
The attraction is not very large. There is a charge of 2000 won per person, which I feel is expensive as compared to other natural wonders in Jeju. Still the views are nice and unique.

The attraction is not so exciting but still worth a visit if it is your first time in Jeju. This attraction is also pretty near Jeju's Loveland, an interesting and popular attraction that is not mentioned in TripAdvisor.

The area of the beach is nice but the sandy part and the open water space is soooo small... You cannot even go for a swim here. The water was dirty and full of water plants. I honestly thinking every beach in Europe is way more attractive than this. Italy, Greece, Croatia....Have they actually seen clear azure waters?! If this is jejus prettiest beach then im really sorry for koreans

The admission fee is 10000 won per pax, so it's probably the most expensive admission ticket you'll pay in Jeju.If you're a fan of bears, though, this is photo heaven =](And maybe shopping heaven! The prices of the bears are really exorbitant though.)

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It?s a nice experience after all and I would say it?s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

The   museum   is not too far from Jeju City so it's only a short ride in a taxi to this location.  You may want to tell the taxi driver to drive past the Jeju Mysterious Road if you are going this way as it is along the route.The museum itself attempts to shock you but you get over the shock in a few minutes and it does become a bit mundane after a while.  You do sense that the museum creators did have a good sense of humor though.  There are many many displays that feature sexual positions toys etc. but nothing that is too shocking.  The grounds are fairly immaculate too.  Many phallic symbols etc.  You know what to expect at this location.I guess it is worth the visit as there are not too many museums like this in the world but it really isn't worth an out of the way trip to this museum.

That was the first place we visited after arriving at Jeju. Really enjoyed the chill atmosphere. In September, the weather was windy and a bit cool but still loved it. We also stopped by at Delmoondo cafe.

Thanks to Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) and Jeju Olle walking Festival,  we got an opportunity to participate in the Jeju Olle Walking festival 2020 despite there was a limitation on the number of the participant due to spread of Covid-19. This year, the festival is held in a new and unique way with the slogan ?Walk Apart, Finish Together?. All participants have to register online in advance; only up to 15 participants accepted for each of 23 routes for 23 days. Also, all the participants were given Clean Kit set that includes face masks, sanitizers, and others needed for personal hygiene.Since we had just one day to participate in the walking festival, Route 10 was chosen for our team. Route 10 start from Hwasun Golden sand beach, then passes through major touristic attractions Sanbangsan Mountain, Yongmeori Coast, Songaksan Mountain, Altteureu Airfield, Victims Memorials, and finally Hamo beach which is close to the endpoint. The total distance is 15.6 km with a maximum elevation of around 60 m.The walking experience in this route was amazing. We pass various landscapes, from beaches to forest, coastal walk to mountain hiking, and finally to radish and potato farms at Altteureu Airfield site. The various volcanic and sedimentary rock structures at Sanbangsan Mountain foothills and Yongmeori Coast were amazingly gorgeous. Walking along the perimeter of volcanic mountain Songaksan was a unique experience. The cliffs of the mountain close to sea were spectacular and walking along the top of those cliffs was just amusing. This type of walking, I think, gives the opportunity to explore the hidden natural beauty of Jeju Island and its traditional cultures which we could miss if visited by other means. Thus, the Jeju Olle Trails is highly recommended for those who love hiking or walking and want to explore hidden natural beauties while enjoying local customs and local foods. I, personally, wish to complete all the Olle walking trails and get the certificate of completion from the organizer.
Thank you, Mr. Jang. If someone needs a guide in Jeju, I will recommend Mr. Jang.

Thank you ?쇱큿 for bringing us such a great traveling experience in Jeju Island! ?쇱큿 is friendly and considerate and he took good care of our family needs! thank to the Chinese tour guide, we had a very informative (and frank) introduction to the history of jeju-do. the place is also very picturesque, with all the ancient architectures. it feels like going back in time. there'll also be a sales promotion time, but the tour guide said that we do not have to buy anything if we don't want to, she just have to make an introduction of the products of jeju-do. there's no forced sale, just informative introduction of everything jeju.

Teddy bear museum located at Jungmun resort at Jeju. It's easy to reach the resort by Airport Limousine 600 from Grace hotel bus stop or others. So many teddy bear with different characters and customs. We can take a photo with big Teddy bear like Einstein, Steve Jobs, Van Gogh etc.There's a garden with many teddy bear statues. So cute!

Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju opened in 2001 and boasts for owning the largest collection of teddy bears.  What differentiates this museum from the rest is that Korea's history was told using the bears.  It was cute and a not so serious approach that would cater to the children.The museum consists of 2 Exhibition halls namely the hall of history and the hall of art.  This museum serves as the home for as many as 1,500 bears that includes the luxurious Louis Vuitton bear.

Take off the bus at Jeju International Convention Center, JICC.Since you're already here, you should go into JICC building and take a glance of it.I visited during a rainy day, I would say a rain coat is definitely better than an umbrella. The rain wasn't heavy, but the wind was strong and frequent.The wave crashing on the columnar joint, could reach few meters high. I really enjoyed viewing the waves, listening to the sea. It was picturesque!

Take a ferry from Seongsan, jump on a bicycle for the day and peddle round stopping at all the attractions. It's only 1.5hrs to cycle at a slow pace round the entire island so easily done via a day trip from Seongsan or even Jeju City if you got up early. We stayed on the island itself but truth be told there's not much added value, just do a great fun day trip / cycle - and we are very much NOT cyclists by the way!

Take a boat is convenient from Jeju to Udo (we were driving , the boat is able to carry the car) only 30 minutes boat, then arrive at Udo. We drive along the coste road, stopped by the hill, it is a 30 mins climbing, once reach the top you can have a overview of this Island  We literally turned around the island by car. Tried sea food abalone and some shellfish. It was very good experience. We star at 11.30am boat to Udo and finished at 4pm to take boat back to Jeju main land. It can be a 3-4 hours visit.

Surprisingly, despite standing tall at 1950m, Hallasan was a relatively easier climb than other mountains such as Seoraksan, Bukhansan and Dobongsan, the trio that busted my thighs and made me swear off hiking for months. Youngsil trail was indeed picturesque, with small streams, autumn foliage and sweeping visages of the sloping hills and multiple arboretums that dot the island. The trail was mainly covered with boardwalks to protect the soil from human footsteps. Some parts were difficult to maneuver due to the uneven volcanic rocks so do wear proper hiking boots (the only investment I made for hiking).Visit my travel blog for more information and pictures on Jejuhttps://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/
Sure not the most beautiful Temple (of jeju) but if you are near the place, go and take a look. I can say that the Temple near the Sangbangsan Mountain is much more beautifull.

Summary: You have to go here if you're on Jeju. But what can I add to the many reviews already here?The signs to the women's diving show are very clear. From the ticket office, just follow the signs down to the beach to the left of the peak. If the only way to make the show is to sacrifice something else on your itinerary, I wouldn't do it. But it was pretty cool if you happen to be there at the right time. You see the divers actually catch live octopus right in front of you.I recommend taking a snack up to the top and enjoying it there. There are plenty of places to sit down at the top and relax before you head back down. Also, definitely take at least one bottle of water if it's a hot day. You might even want two.If you plan to catch a taxi from this site to somewhere else, you'll have to walk just a little ways. We asked a taxi driver who was waiting on another family where we could get a taxi, and he told us where to walk. We had to wait about 10-15 minutes for one to show up that didn't already have people in it, but they always drive by eventually.

Such an awesome excursion. Doesn?t take too long and there are cool explanation signs along the way. Highly recommend and is super fun. Gets chilly so make sure you bring a sweater, it?s a nice escape from the hot humid jeju weather. Easy to park and easy to find.
Such a great waterfall in Jeju island, it's good to be able to take photo with this Mother Nature. You will not be regret to climb down and up to the waterfall. A place that must visit.

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Spirited Garden is the #1 place to visit in Jeju in my opinion. I strongly recommend paying a visit.  the garden was actually bigger than I thought, and it took about an hour to see all the places. It definitely made me relaxed and laid back! Everything was well preserved and clean. There is also a cafe with a great view of the garden. You can buy different souvenirs related to Jeju and the garden on the floor below the cafe. Feeding the fish is 1000W and you can buy it freely (you just have to put the money in the box) and it's pretty amusing.

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

Spent a lovely few hours wandering through the caves. Definately worth a visit if you are in Jeju. Lots of signs written in English giving excellent detail of the lava formations that can be seen. We travelled from Jeju City Bus Terminal on the 701. The bus journey was around 1 hour and the stop was announced in English too so easy to know when to get off. It is a long walk from the bus stop to the caves (I guess around 30 mins) but there are lots of taxis available that charge 4000 won to take you to the entrance. Easy to return home - same process, but your return ticket on the bus.Remember to wear sensible shoes and bring a jacket. The floor is very wet and pretty uneven and it is cold down there!
Spectacular. Jeju is known for it's coastline, but Jeju Stone Park in the interior is an absolute must-see.Words can not do it justice. Just see it.

Spectacular views from the bottom, the side, the peak and everywhere else. I couldn't put down my camera. After two rainy, cloudy days at Jeju, the morning of our visit to Sunrise Peak we were blessed with blue skies.The ticket booth (2000 won for adults, 1000 for youth) listed the roundtrip time as 50 minutes, but we spent 2+ hours climbing and descending the tuff cone, followed by checking out the 1:30 p.m. Haenyo woman diver performance. (There is a second performance at 3:00 p.m.)The tuff cone at the peak is something else, and the climb itself is not that bad, especially if you take it slow. The descent is arguably just as good, with cooling breezes and more picture opportunities. One Con: It can get fairly crowded. Dozens of tour buses are parked at the base, carrying mainly Chinese tourists. It get can a bit competitive at times waiting out the best picture spots, but luckily they like taking pictures by signs. Overall it's not that bad, though it was funny watching the korean couples' responses to the crowds, with the girl posing for the picture and giving the side eye while the guy patiently crouched several feet away.But hey, it's a UNESCO heritage site and definitely worth a trip!
Spacious, beautiful....wonderful. Perfect for a picnic:) Easily accessible on number 20 city bus from Jeju City. Lots of restaurants and bars in the area. A definite place to stay and enjoy.

Someone told me Udo is beautiful, so it's in my wish list when I visit Jejudo. I went there on Saturday (7.5.2016). At the harbour, there are many different type of transportation vehicles for rent to travel Udo, so, basically the narrow road at Udo is full of vehicles, no matter is two wheel, three wheel or four wheel. I did the Olle trail 1.1, travel on foot, it was frustrated and irritating when need to walk together with so many types of vehicles, noisy and crowded. But, luckily the trail does divert some part of the trekking route which is away from the vehicle road, hiking up to the light house hill and also farm house and farming area.

Solo traveling in Jeju Island is not that scary:) Koreans living nearby this tourist spot can speak English. So I am not worried about it.It was raining that day when I reach the place. Nevertheless, still can see the view at the top.The wind blowing my hair together with the greenery grasses and leaves of trees surrounding the peak.The place is accessible by public buses so I don't have difficulty in reaching this site. Though you have to walk a few distance to reach the entrance gate.There are educational boards installed for all the tourists to read and understand the history of it.It's worth visiting this place. Entrance fee is also cheap:)I visited Unesco World Heritage!

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.

So, one might think that this is a great place to see artifacts or historic pieces, but as far as we saw, everything was a replica. To include the replica lava tube entrances. Sigh. They couldn't even be bothered to completely thatch a straw hut- they had concrete roofs with thatch done at the top and edges. They do have quite the array of carefully placed rocks and replica stone statues, but seeing as how none of it was real (the whole thing was built on the site of a landfill) there are more real things to go do on Jeju. The price is cheap. Spend it looking at the columnar basalt on the beach. At least that is real.

So we went to Hallasan but didn't have much time, so we've decided to do the yeongsil train until the shelter and then go back the other way (eorekon? Haha). It was about 2hours each ways so 4 hours total. The mountain is free but to get there it's either a bus from Jeju city hall or a taxi (about 27.000 won - 25???). You have to be there before 12:00 pm otherwise it's closed. Really good activity, winter time so there was snow, pretty cool!!But wear good shoes and some coat because it's super windy there !I recommend it 100 times.

So we are sat in the car, put on neutral mode and the car actually moved! This is a really cool experience and it only takes a minute to do- I have seen mysterious roads on the travel channel before but this was my first time doing it- if you find yourself on Jeju island check it out!

So I read a review that the hike up Hallasan was not very difficult so I thought I could do it in my Asics running shoes...well, I don't recommend that you do the hike up Hallasan without proper hiking gear.  Pack lots of water and food so that you can replenish yourself on the long hike up.  We went in early October and it was warm so dressing in layers was a godsend.  The route we took was to take Seongpanak up to the summit and then take Gwaneumsa trail down.  Taking Seongpanak to the summit took approximately 4.5 hours with 1 lunch break at the 3rd resting place before the summit. The resting place had washrooms and also a snack bar.  I saw people with cup ramen etc. Be prepared for the washrooms to be stinky.  It's the nature friendly kind.  The last stretch up to the summit on the Seongpanak trail is quite steep and some parts very rocky.  But the view makes up for it all!  Instead of hiking down the same trail, we came down the Gwaneumsa trail and wow, the views were breathtaking.  There were times when I had to stop and just take in the view just a bit longer because it was so beautiful.  T he Gwaneumsa trail doesn't have as many resting places so use the washroom when you can.  It took us a total of 9.5 hours to hike up and down Hallasan and I would do it again the next time I am in Jejudo Island!!

So according to our tour guide since we've spent few days at Jeju Island, Udo Island which is to the east of Jeju with a short ferry ride is not to be missed.So we went, and he was right.Beautiful day, sunny blue sky, clouds, nice breeze, beaches, scenic sights everywhere.  We even hiked up to the lighthouse.Came back down and tried the   famous   Udo Island ice cream.  Meh, not a big deal in my book, though it quenched the thirst a little.

Small island off the Jeju coast makes for a nice day trip/excursion from the main Jeju island. We enjoyed the climb up the one and only peak for excellent views, as well as some stunning coastal caves and cliffs, lighthouse, crashing surf, and volcanic rock. At first blush it may not seem too nice but Udo kind of grows on you. I'd recommend renting a moped or bicycle and bopping around the backroads; that would be the best way to see and enjoy Udo.

Small confession: it's the only museum we've visited in Jeju so I can't compare it to others and say it was better, BUT the museum is great. It was something new and an interesting experience even for my parents who are in their early 50s. Overall, I do recommend you to go there. FYI: there aren't places there where you can refill your bottles with fresh water.

Skip this and head for Dodubong Peak, especially if you're on the Jeju Golden Bus day tour. This place is unremarkable and is honestly one of the dirtiest parts of the area; I attempted to have my photo taken and a rat scurried out from between the rocks. If you walk up the road (away from the site) about a half mile, maybe less, the photo ops are much nicer. The area near Dodubong Peak is also nicer and you can see great views of of Jeju from the summit.

Since there is not much to see in Jeju City, I liked this the most. The rock itself looks nice, so if you happen to be in Jeju City and have free time, it worth to check and enjoy the view on the rocky seaside. easy to get here from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal, just take local bus #17, and tell the driver   Yongduam   he will show the right bus stop. From there only 5 mins walk. It is just a rock, so don't expect much, but it's good trip for 20-30mins. Before going to the rock, you should definitely check the bus schedule back to the city center (bus timetable is displayed not on the bus stop, but on the shopwindow just nearby where no one would ever search), as there's 1-2 bus in every hour.

Since my hotel is located at one end of this shopping centre, I visited this place every day during my stay in Jeju. Being underground, it was great to shield the winter cold especially in the evenings.The shops essentially sell similar products - clothings, cosmetics, shoes, accessories, bags, hats, etc. There are few eateries and fast food chains too. This shopping street tends to be crowded in the evenings. There are free toilet facilities at one end, i.e. exit 1.

Since Jeju is best travelled by car, the mysterious road (it's actual name) is definitely worth checking out. Putting the car on the apparent downslope in neutral gear will make the car move backwards and vice-versa...freaked us out until we discovered the optical illusion behind it. Be careful of all the other cars trying it out as well as pedestrians attempting something similar by pouring water onto the road surface.

Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ?
