And make sure you have plenty of memory space on your camera for photos!

Needless to say that thousands of mainly local  toursts want to see the place. Extint volcano. At the waterfront you can see a show of the so called Haenyeo, more than old women that dive in their black suits for octopus, clams etc. At the visitor center you should try perfect icecream made from peanuts or tangerines. Tangerines are cultivated quite often on Jeju.

Near the Osulloc Tea Museum, the Innisfree Jeju House has a cafe and a store. The selection isn't great, and they don't give you free samples, though you could score some Jeju only products. Admittedly, there weren't at lot of these products though. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store, so you can do it on your own), it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.I like Innisfree products, so I didn't stopping by, but if you're not into that or soap making, you may want to give it a miss.

Nature attraction is the best in Jeju. To enter majanggul cave, it cost us 2,000 won per person. Beware its very cold down there (i went there on summer, but its quite cold maybe 18'C), wet, dark and slippery. Make sure to wear proper shoes (sneakers) and bring raincoat (even though it sunny day)

Nanta is like the korean Pride nonverbal performances. It's fun and defiantly great if you have kids. It's not the best nonverbal performance out there, but Jeju has regular showings and the tickets aren't the pricey.

My wife and I visited the sunrise mountain on our recent visit to Jeju Island.  Reviews had essentially undersold me on how strenuous the climb would be - it was a workout!  Took a proper 30 min of intense stair climbing to reach the top.  The views at the top were great, although the   crater   itself is just not that photogenic.  It's a big green area.  There's clearly a big appeal to seeing the sunrise but we didn't make that early morning trek.Don't miss the side paths toward the female cliff divers.  Offered some of the coolest views with the bay and the mountain.Overall, I thought it was really pretty and worth a visit but not necessarily mandatory if you're just in Jeju for relaxing.

My wife and I visited Ilchulbong at 5 pm, and unfortunately, couldn't catch the women divers in action. We made it to the top and it was quite a steep climb. We were completely winded by the time we reached the peak which has a beautiful viewing deck. The moon was up on one side while the sun was setting on the other side. It was our last day in Jeju and Korea and the beautiful sunset against the skyline of Jeju was the perfect ending we could have  asked for.

My wife and I love teddy bears, but everything here seemed outdated and boring... It simply felt like festive displays at your local shopping malls.  If you are here for photography, you will be disappointed as the exhibits were not designed with that in mind, the placement, the lightings, the space, etc... the place was crowded with tourists all trying to take photographs everywhere, and like I mentioned earlier, this place was not designed for that, so there were a lot of re-takes by everyone, so image the queue and wait at those photo points.  Jeju is a big island with a lot of awesome attractions, and you can probably only cover up to three per day. So plan your days carefully and put this attraction at the least of your priority unless you have someone in your group that loves to be around teddy bears regardless of whether the attraction has character or charm.

My wife and I hiked Hallasan last weekend, which was our first trip to Jeju Do. We've lived in Seoul for 5 years and finally made that trip south. We decided to take the Seongpanak Trail since it allows you to get to the top. Overall, the hike was great - beautiful scenery (although it was a hazy day for us so visibility was limited), challenging hike and it's something that will take up a whole day. We took a different trail down once we reached the top and the views were nicer on that one. I think there are only two trails that go all the way up. We're not hikers by any means so our legs were pretty tired on the way down the mountain. They estimate 8-9 hours total but we did it in 7! Be sure to pack some snacks and water as there's not much available on the hike. There's a small place at a checkpoint a couple hours into the Seongpanak trail where you can get some water, ramen and chocolate bars (along with some basic hiking gear) but don't expect much. We had only taken water with us (rookie mistake) and I was wishing for some extra snacks on the way down. There's also a store/small restaurant at the first entrance to the hike so you can stock up there. Overall, it's definitely worth doing as its one of the main attractions on Jeju.

My wife and I ascended Mount Hallasan in April. While it was cool in the morning, we soon had to tie our sweatshirts around our waist. We weren't sweating as much but we're winded trekking 9.6 kms. While that distance may seem daunting, the Seonpanak trail was not too difficult, even for non-trekkers like us. There are steps and wooden walkways but in parts you have to tread carefully as it gets rocky. The difficulty level steadily increases as you move upwards. But if you take little breaks and keep proceeding, your effort will be rewarded with breath taking views from the peak. Well, the Crater lake didn't match our expectations or the pictures we saw online as it had dried up. However, we were well above the cloud level and there were green and brown hills as far as the eye could see. A word of caution - there are no sources of water on the way up (although it says there's portable water at the half point) and no shops once you start the trek. So carry energy drinks and bars, at least 3-4 big bottles of water (per person) and Jeju oranges. You can get all this from the shop at the base, at the start of the trail. Go on, enjoy your trek and discover pine trees, maples trees, black Chipmunks and much more

My son live and work teaching English  in Jeju , I spent 10 days with him in his apartment and this trip to  Seogwipo and the hike will always be in my heart.  We stayed in nearby hotel and woke up 4am started walking and climbing the steps to see the sunrise on the top and its all worth it .. Indeed Jeju has teh rightful name - the island of the Gods.

My sister and I went to Udo on a ferry ride after spending a couple of hours at Seongsan Ilchulbong. Because we did not want to go back at dawn, we limited our time to be on the island for about 2-3 hours.It is actually best recommended to spend half a day touring the island either on bus or motorbike. Since we did not have much time, we only walked to the nearby beach which was pretty deserted and that was the best part. Most of the tourist places in Jeju was crowded, but not Udo at the time we were there. The beach was beautiful with small stones and black rocks layering the sand. It was beautiful.There were plenty of cafes within walking distance but we chosed a bench facing the sea in front of a GS25 mart.I love the serenity the island offered. I just wish we had more time to go around the island.

My return to Jungmun after almost seventeen years revealed that not much had changed.  This is not surprising as the main draw of the place is its steep and jagged volcanic rock formations.  The Hyatt Regency and other resort amenities were there in the 1980's when we lived on Jeju.  The concessions at beachside are still the charming   Mom and Pop   establishments serving ice cream and Korean pastries plus Yogurt beverages.

My number one favourite place in Jeju. The views are amazing and it's free! As you walk along the trail, you can get different views and there is a pool right down there where one can go for a dip or a swim. Although I didn't go for a swim there, just watching others dive and swim there is already a joy

My number 2 favourite place in Jeju after Oedolgae. The rock formation of the cliff on this volcanic island is really fascinating! Before going, do make sure it's low tide time because it will be closed during high tide as it will be too dangerous. We also saw some women (should be women sea divers) who were selling fresh sea produce to those who want to eat them fresh and raw there. From there too, we could get a clear view of Sanbang Mountain which is just nearby. There's also a ship there and you can read about the history of how the ship ended up there. Be careful as you walk along the coast as sometimes you might be shocked by the sudden strong waves that come hitting towards the coast. I saw someone who was so shocked that she nearly dropped her mobile phone into the sea. Overall, it's one of the must go places in Jeju.

My mum and i took about one hour plus to reach the top. but not to worry if you aren't that physically fit, you can always take a break at seats along the way and enjoy the nice scenery. we went around sept therefore the weather is very good though we are sweated a lot too. However once you are up at the peak, you can enjoy the full panoramic view of the sea and the eastern coastline.A place not to be missed when you go Jeju

My Korean friend brought me to this place when I visited Jeju. It was a hidden jem. I spent a couple of hours to take holographic pictures and watched the Kpop videos at the 3D theater. It was close to many tourist spots in Seogwipo city (Teddy bear museum, lotte hotel, and etc.). If you are a kpop lover, you will have unforgettable memories. It was so much fun!!!

My husband didn't want to go to this, but during the entire trip, the word 'mysterious' really peaked my curiosity so while he wasn't paying attention, I drove us to this 'mysterious road'. I didn't want to keep wondering after I left Jeju! I mean, It's got to be impressive if there are all these street signs, and they even have a food stand named after it right? Wrong!It was so anti-climatic, so short(1 minute?) and so stupid. Probably one of the dumbest attractions I have ever seen. Nothing mysterious or special about it. If you are disappointed, don't say I didn't warn ya.

My husband and I were staying in the Hallim area and our taxi driver mistakenly took us to Hallim Park. Especially since it was a bit chilly and an overcast day, the beautiful green houses and occasionally covered areas were a nice break from the weather. The park itself is nothing overly spectacular, but it has a little bit of everything with a nice mix of Jeju style to your typical botanical gardens type park. Plants, flowers, animals, exhibits, and fun!

My husband and I went to the Jeju Stone Park to see the guardian statues (Jeju stone heads) but found the park to be so much more than that.  It's a large park (and they are still enlarging it) with an emphasis on nature.  The museum and historic buildings are interesting but walking around the grounds was the high point.  Rocks in their natural shapes are placed throughout the grounds and if you are quiet and observant, the connection to nature just seeps to your being.  We found the place strangely intriguing, calming, and uplifting.

My husband and I walked here from Jeju-si (not recommended, unless you just really like to walk) so it's not far from the big hotel district. It's free to get in, but is mostly just trees and bushes, the wildflower garden was completely bare, of course, we didn't really come at the right time for that anyway. Follow the signs for   Green Shower   and you'll go up a pretty steep climb (especially for us in our flip-flops) to a nice view of the city and the ocean beyond. There's a nice lily-pad pond and a nice green   lawn   for anyone wanting a place to sit in nature. Although, the entire island of Jeju is about nature, so this wasn't a must-see for us. Just behind the Arboretum (on the left as you drive out and behind a group of concrete apartment buildings) is the ＿?由쇱?? Buddhist Temple. It has a really gorgeous campus and nice view of the city and sea, as well. If you got to the Arboretum, take the time to visit the temple, too.

My husband and I visited Jeju last November.Mt. Halla was out of the picture on this trip ( supposed to be ) bec. I am not an adventurous person and I thought I will not have energy to climb this mountain, but after learning that it is a world natural heritage park I finally gave it a go. I was afraid at the beginning of the trail but as we climb further, higher and steeper I was in Awe! I was literally inside the mountain. Plus it  was autumn at that time and the color of the surrounding was just beautiful, it seems so peaceful all you could hear was the chirping birds, gushing winds. It was tiring but i must i was worth it so sad that we didn't reach the summit bec we started a little late. But if i could go back I will strive to reach the peak, but I was still happy though because I've seen the best Autumn inside the mountain..It is really is the Climb!

My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. The staff was so angry with us and adamant that we pay the entrance fees although we were just viewing the falls 5 steps past the ticket office. They stood right next to us and kept trying to push us back out even after we explained our situation to them. I found that absolutely ridiculous. They could clearly see for themselves that our parents were elderly and required some assistance just walking on flat road! Walking down those steps and hiking those boulders were completely out of the question.How appalling! No words can describe how utterly disgusted we felt at the attitude of the park staff.

My husband and I had an absolutely fabulous day pheasant hunting at the Daeyoo Hunting Preserve on Jeju Island in South Korea and then an excellent meal of (our) pheasant sashimi roast pheasant etc. washed down with wine at their excellent pheasant restaurant! Daeyooland also has lovely gardens a charming helpful staff and great coffee!We hunted with a guide and his trusty dog walking for miles thru the beautiful countryside... and my husband did get us a pheasant! We also got to shoot skeet (and they have ATVing as well). My husband had hunted on Jeju many years ago when he was in the US Army and stationed in Korea and I wanted to take him   home   and go hunting with him- and tourists can hunt at Daeyooland! As their website is only in Korean our concierge at the JW Marriott in Seoul (an EXCELLENT hotel which I've also reviewed) was kind enough to help make the arrangements for us. We flew to Jeju Island for the day went hunting and then walked around downtown Jeju going to museums and some of the historic markets (there are 22!) buying and eating those famous Jeju oranges! Then we flew back to Seoul in the evening having had  a GREAT day!

My husband and I climb Mt Hallasan today. Though my feet are sore, i thoroughly enjoyed my hike. The trail was really well marked and in good condition (Both Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa Trail). We entered via Seongpanak Trail (9.6km gradual inclination - trail was a mix of wooden steps and rocks). It was fairly easy till Jindallaebat Shelter, and then it gets tougher but doable. We started at 8am and reached the summit at 12 pm (we?re not athletic and not super fit). We then descended via Gwaneumsa Trail (8.6km) at 1 pm and arrived at the trail head at 5.30pm. Gwaneumsa is more scenic as many blogs have mentioned so am glad we descended using this trail but Seongpanak trail is easier and is nice as well.Useful info:We took the public bus from Jeju-si city and back. Journey was about an hour one way and we found our way fairly easy with the Naver Map app. The public bus from Gwaneumsa trail entrance only runs on weekends I believe. Bring snacks, lunch and water for your climb. A windbreaker is advisable if you come from the tropics like me.Good shoes are recommended as you?ll be walking on rocks a lot of the time. Bring a raincoat too as there aren?t many shelters.Start early, you have to arrive Jindallaebat Shelter by 1230hrs (you cannot proceed after that) and you must begin your descend by 1430hrs.

My friends and I visited this museum in Jeju as our ode to one of our fave korean dram Goong. So we looked for the bears used in the drama like Alfred and the rest of the bears featured in the drama and we were quite excited seeing them in the flesh although a bit disappointed as it was not for sale.The museum features also life sized bears, bears resembling famous celebrities like michael jordan, elvis presley, the beatles,superman or bear?,old bears like old winnie the pooh, bears in hanboks, drewsed like emperors in  joseon dynasty,astronauts,a vampirebear, a Ronin bear, a Leonardo da  Vinci bear,A bear in LV get up,paddington bear,care bears,polar bears,there were bears in the outside depicting picnic, inside a telephone booth,fishing and even a bear taking a leak....one will enjoy if you are a bear lover. they also have a souvenir shop to buy of course different kinds of bears

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My friends and I didn't expect much when we headed out here. We thought it would be a short hike but we were in for a surprise. From the moment we got out of our car, the view of the ilchulbong was breathtaking. After a short 10-20? minute hike, we took a pause at the peak to take in the grand view in front of us. I believe this is the #1 attraction of Jeju island.

My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

My friend and I found this to be one of the more memorable attractions in Jeju. We were amazed by the black hexagonal columns of volcanic rock and it was wondrous to just gaze at them with the waves crashing into the columns, and also contemplate on how they were formed. This place really makes one feel relaxed and happy. Highly recommended.

My first time to Korea focusing on Jeju and Seoul. Generally I would think the overall experience to South Korea is kind of over rated. I expected more based on the comments from friends, reviews by travellers and most importantly seeing it in Korean Dramas.Udo island is an exception, it gave me the best experience in the entire 8-day trip, except the weather wasn't too good on my day trip to Udo. Rented a bike to travel almost the entire island which i think is the best mode to explore remote areas without using too much energy.  Hopping up and down to take photos by the beach, colorful cafes, yellow canola fields, uphill and downhill.Unforgettable squid volcano rice was one of its kind and one of the most satisfactory meal in the entire trip.

My first sightseeing spot upon arrival at Jeju-do. I was there last October, so the place was covered with pampas grass, with the cloud and sun giving the landscape different shades and colours, the view was simply wonderful.

My family was holiday in Jeju on 12 Dec 2011.  One of the tourists spots where we visited is the Mysterious road.  It really amazed us after we had seen in our own eyes and sitting in the car.  The driver took us to place near to our our hotel Ocean Suite Hotel.  He then switched off the engine of the car and of course, there is a spot where there is a sign show   start here  . My only suggestion would be to increase the lighting a bit so guests can really appreciate the lava markings - the atmosphere with the low light is nice but I wanted to see more of the characteristics of the lava versus a non-lava flow cave.  Some people brought a flashlight and that seems like a great idea.  The price was very reasonable and there is a restaurant and clean restrooms.

review: My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people?s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails ? Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below) ? I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that?s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of ?Jeju Island Geopark?, ?Global Geopark Networks? and ?New 7 Wonders of Nature? and a green signage ?Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m? From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes? walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term ?stepping stone? means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain ?pot-holes?. The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder ? awesome!  There?s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn?t think they were the famed ?Haenyeo? sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam) ? who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn?t like to eat raw seafood so I didn?t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don?t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

My family (2 adults & a 10 year old) recently spent 3 days doing a combination of private and small group tours of UNESCO sites in Jeju Island with June of Core Travel. It was a great balance of energetic activities (hiking craters, exploring lava tubes), museums and cultural attractions, and relaxing activities such as a sampling session at a tea farm or DIY foot massage at a herb garden.

My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. It looked like a great way to experience the culture and have a few good laughs. Also, since my cousins and I do not speak Korean, we could not understand the dialogue, which makes Nanta great for foreigners because there are not too many speaking moments. My comment to my wife after touring the O'Sulloc tea museum:   It's more of a fun cafe and tea shop than a museum or   plantation   for tea enthusiasts.  It's a nice stop if you're staying closer to that side of Jeju - we traveled about 15 min. by car to reach it.  Really enjoyed the green tea cake and latte and bought some fresh tea for souvenir.  However this is not a   must see   aspect of a trip to Jeju.There is also a Innisfree cosmetics shop on the site which has a lot of products; we made a few purchases there too.  Nice little add-on for the Jeju tourist.

My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! The maze itself was really good and it took us an embarrassingly long time to finish, :-) This is really for people of all ages! Everybody was laughing and having such a good time that the whole atmosphere was so nice. The workers were very nice, and one man who I assume is the manager had a wonderful conversation with us while we waited for the taxi they had called for us! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. They have loads of cats inside and outside that are well taken care of. This was one of our favorite parts of Jeju! You definitely should go here!

My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!

My biggest regret, if there was one for Jeju, would be to miss this attraction. The crater may not seem much to some but this site was truly amazing. The natural occurrence was a sight to behold. It may be hard for some to imagine the significance of this crater but for me, I could relate to it and blessed to witness it. A not to be missed attraction albeit out of the way. The pampas grass fields were so scenic during fall that one just cannot miss this picture taking opportunity. The were so well grown here.

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Must visit place in Jeju, it is very beautiful, view is spectacular from the top. There are stairs so it is easier to climb. Give yourself 3-4 hours to explore everything.

Must visit place if u come to Jeju Island. I rent a bicycle, cycling & round the island. It will takes around 2-3 hours. It will getting easier to stop everywhere and snap the picture. I visited Udo Island end of March and it full with the Canola Flowers!!! Don't forget to try the nut ice cream too. There have a lots of stall and restaurant selling it!!
Must see stop in Jeju. Very scenic place, not too crowded. Have a museum nearby, not worth the visit

Must see in Jeju. Biggest lava tube in the world. 2 km from the bus stop, close to maze park. Do not forget tripod to take good pictures as it is rather dark in the cave. Good place to cool down after summet heat.

Mt. Hallasan is the main peak of Jeju do, a shield shaped volcano formed on the continental shelf in the Yellow Sea. It is the highest peak of South Korea (1950 meters above the base level) and the symbol of Jeju Island. The Hallasan Natural Reserve makes up of various arctic alpine plants and a forest of the Korean fir, which makes a graceful scene, and the  Baeknokdam, the Crater Lake on the top of the Mt. Hallasan, adds the scenic beauty. You can meet totally different appearance of Mt. Hallasan according to the 4 seasons.

Mt Halla is known as Korea's jewel. It is its highest peak. And well worth the trip to Jeju. We left Seagwipo very early (around 7 am) and took bus 182 (181 also goes there) to Seongpanak because we wanted to climb up to the peak. We got to the mountain around 7:45 and started the hike. The weather was super nice when we left, and we planned it that way, because we wanted to at least get some nice views of the city, and while at the summit. This is a long day of hiking, so be prepared. Bring snacks (and a trash bag, because you have to carry everything back down), and water. There are 2 checkpoints along the way that have bathrooms. The last checkpoint sells ramen for about 1500w with hot water. This is the checkpoint you have to get to before 12:30. We made it there around 11, and up to the summit before noon On the Seongpanak trail, there is also a lake with an observatory that's worth the detour.The last part of the hike up to the summit is pretty steep and rocky, so watch your footing, especially because you might be tired from walking up. Wear adequate footwear, make sure they are sturdy and comfy!Unfortunately, we didn't get that lucky with the weather as it because overcast as we were getting up there. I guess it really depends on your luck (the next day, it was super clear! Damn you Mt Halla!!) hahaha.We took the same trail down (from the summit, there is another trail, but no buses stop there. And this is where your comfy shoes are a must. The hike up was not bad, but the hike down, was torture! Our feet kept hitting the front of our hiking shoes, so we were bruised and hurt by the time the hike was done. We were also sore for the next 2 days (and we're pretty sporty, but we rarely walk for 8 hours) Overall, it's a great hike. The trail up is covered by trees, so it is cooler than it seems, but there are still some great views, especially with the fall foliage. We'd be surprised at the range of people walking the trail, old and young love to hike up this trail, and we understand why!
