Mountain HallasanIt was a fanatic walk ever, friendly people all around. Unfortunate in Jeju island, English is not a common language, road signs, information boards are all in Korean, mainly people speak Korean, surprisingly, you might find people speak Japanese and mandarin. There are a few entrances from around the Moutain, make sure you do your research.I believe there are more than 4 entrances. Due to limited time, I have chosen the easiest and fastest trail (Eorimok). You could take public transport or driving. There is parking 17mins walk, and payable parking 1000won, save your time. Be prepared below- Go toilet, do the necessity before you start - Go to visitor centre get a map and find out more. ( e.g. if the convenient store is open?) - 2-3 hours walk one way, the washroom only available in the destination. Choose the hiking shoes. (Bad experience, my sport shoes are ruined) - Best to start your journey at 8 or 9 in the morning, as early as you could. If you are doing other trails, allow more than 8 hours. Eorimok entrance, it took me 5hours, I took a slow walk. - Be warned after certain time (14:30, not certain), you may not be allowed to go in. - Bring a lot of water, or bring enough cash (drinkable water is not enough to supply to public), bring your own food if you don't want to end up eating spicy instant noodle.- Store only sell, instant noodle(super spicy), and spring water. (Limited to 2 portions of instant noodle per person) price: 1000won for instant noodle, 1000won for a bottle of water- Bring extra clothe to change, bring a light weight jacket. (It is a bit chilling on top)- Bring insects repellent spray or lotion- Bring wet tissue and normal tissue- Bring a bag for rubbish, smoking and littering are not allowed.The place is well protected, please respect :)  Voila! Happy Journey!

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

Most of Udo island except the attractions are rural farms. We went to Udo island with a few local Koreans from jeju island. We took a 15mins ferry. I was surprised that there are no seats on the ferry, people sit on the floor instead, korean style. Interesting experience. As I went with locals, I thought they would know the way. No! They didn't and we walked 1h around the island before reaching the peak. It was beautiful. The grass was green n the sea view was nice. Though it was really windy. And thus very cold even though it was summer. Be sure to wear enough clothes.

Me and my husband visited Hallim Park, the beach just outside the park is beautiful so make sure to allow some time to check it out. The park itself consists of about 7-8 different theme subsessions. It was a lot bigger than I expected. The park was very well signed and designed with lots attention to details. Of cause it is not comparable to the natural beauty of Jeju but for a man made park, it is a great choice for an outing with family for 2 hours.

May / June may be low season in Jeju, accomodation is not expensive. But,heavy raining in the morning, it turns sunny in afternoon. If you want to trek to Hallasan Mt., avoid go in May 2016. I trek the Seongpanak trial under heavy raining, it is a bit tough no matter up or down. The view is not that scenery.

Massive ground. A full walk about will take 2hrs easily. Even though all the stones look similar after an hr, it's a very effective way to understand the folklores of Jeju. Cheap entrance fee of only 2K won.Some places near the museum are still under renovation when we were there.

Marado island is small island but it has amazing view. You can see the wide field, blue sea,and Jeju-representing rocks.You can borrow a bike and look around the island riding a bike. And there is also a good restaurants. They use Jeju local specialities.

Marado Island is remote, largely barren, and is   nearly   empty. There is a small population of island residents. There is a small oddly shaped church, a Buddhist temple, and a lighthouse. As far as buildings go, there is little of interest. The primary feature of Marado is the rugged coastline, typical of Jeju-do. Doesn't sound that appealing? Yet, I did enjoy my visit here because it is nice to see a part of Jeju that is largely unaffected by tourism, small museums, resorts, golf, or honeymooners. The ferry does not depart too frequently. Once you arrive on Marado, you really can only do one thing, walk around the entire island, which only takes 2 hours. If the weather is nice (May-August), you should be able to get some pretty pictures of the rugged coast, bright green grass, and some of the lonely buildings on the island.Some of these small island communities are such a contrast to our (foreigners) perception of Korea, that a visit in itself helps creates a more broad image of the country. A worthy experience, that I would recommend if you have plenty of time on Jeju Island.

Many things to eat and buy here! There are many shops selling tangerines (Jeju?s specialty) and local products. At the back of the market, there are also many street stalls that sell super yummy street food like fried chicken and mozzarella hot dogs. Something unique to try would be the Jeju Tangerine Garlic fried chicken from one of the stalls.

Many people go to travel in order to beautiful viewpoints(something new, special). In contrast, I prefer love to see more local traditional viewpoints. For example, Dongmun Market, this was traditional market in Jeju which could totally represent the ancient Jeju resident's market. I still remembered that because of Jeju's transportation wasn't simply because the notice language almost was Korean. Therefore, I and my friend was suffer for this situation in order to find the Dongmun Market. But no matter how we hurt for take wrong bus in long times, when we actually corrected to get off the bus to the Dongmun Market, we were very shocked, It was because that we can't find the entrance. Fortunately, we finally found that and surprised, amazed for it. Because Dongmun Market was very clear, we thought that the traditional market must dirty, but actually it was very clean. In my view, if you want to travel Jeju, I think join the tour group is the best way in order not to get lost.

Many of my friends recommended us to try Jeju black pork. However, it was definitely not a thing for me. Firstly, pricey. Secondly, nothing so special about. You can simply try any grill meat in Seoul and it tastes the same. Would recommend you to try something else in Jeju.

Manjanggul lava cave locate in the east jeju island.I was there with my husband, I think visited this location make so tired if don't like hiking or nature tour.Temparature is so cold so must prepare jacket or coat

Manjanggul is a nature creation which 1km of it is opened for visitors to walk through. However majestic it is, if you are not a keen learner of geography or stones and cave, this walk would be boring for you. If you are there in Jeju for a short trip, I would recommend you to skip this instead.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Manjamg cave is located on the north-east of Jeju, away from most of the hotels. In order to get to it, you will need to take a car, tour bus, or private taxi tour.The cave is massive and long, but not too interesting compared to real adventure caving. It is basically an uncomfortable walk in a cold and dark tunnel.Overall verdict: If you happen to go here on a tour, drive past, or have never been in a cave, go andcheck it out, otherwise don't waste your time.

Lovely place (June). Water was warm and beautiful. Walk a little bit and you will find more places and not so crowded. There aren't many restaurants for foreigners. I recommend to try the burgers at the red container (can't remember the name). If you don't enjoy fireworks, better don't do after 7pm. There are better things to see and do in Jeju but some people don't understand that!!!

Lovely botanical garden. I went there a couple of days ago with my friends during our Jeju trip.We didn’t want to get around the whole island for the short holiday, but relax. There were a number of flowers, trees, flowers, and beautiful gardens.If you are a fan of gardens or nature, you must visit there.

Loved this place for its wide variety of food stuff and lunch dinner options. Their jeju chocolates, choco crunch etc are sold in packs of 6 or 10 and one of the better deals u can get as compared to other areas in Jeju. Whether it is to take in the sights of the variety of food sold in a traditional market, get some souvenirs for the folks at home or to grab a reasonable price meal, dongmun market has it all.
Loved this island, I recommend exploring it by foot.  We interviews the monk the temple for our film   Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure   and he was super kind and served us coffee and drink.

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.

Love this beautiful park in Jeju. For old folks, it provided a relaxing path to walk up to the top of the crater. And once you are on top, you get to see the mountains surrounding Jeju if the sky is clear. Amazing view. There is a minimum entrance fee to this park. There is also small shops near the entrance if you need drinks or snack. Compare to other places in Jeju, this park is less crowded. So if you want to chill and spend a couple of hours outdoor, this is an awesome place to be.

Looking for something different when touring through Jeju? Then this is a nice alternative. Manicured gardens with stunning hydrangeas abound in this most peaceful setting. Taking about 30-40 minutes to complete, it's an enjoyable time to try and navigate through the maze without a GPS! There's a shop (there's always a shop!) compete with souvenirs, drinks and ice creams - and there's a quite spot to sit and soak up the peaceful atmosphere. Enjoy!

Located on the west side of Jeju, this gem has a very nice view, were you can see some mountains across the beach. We went there during late spring, the water was very nice while basking in the sun. There's not much people there, however when summer comes, most of them will swarm all over the place. It's better to go on spring, you can enjoy the view and just listening to the water splashing on the rocks. This is one of the best beaches in Korea.

Located on the far western shore of Jeju Island, Hyeopjae receives a fraction of the visitors compared to other well-known Korean beaches. My wife and I enjoyed a spectacular sunset here after a fun half-day spent swimming and exploring the volcanic tide pools. The beach is superb for three reasons. 1) Great location (not a city-beach), scenic view of islands and volcanic rocks strung along northern portion of the beach.2) Relatively few visitors compared to other Korean beaches3) Water and beach are clean, shallow water makes the beach great for families

Located on the beach, you must go down and walk on lava stones, it's a nice place, many people take photos in front of this waterfall that comes out from the massive right on the beach, this place is connected to story of a Chinese traveller speaking the elixir of eternal youth, he hoped to find it on Jeju

Located next to   Loveland   this museum is small modern place with beautiful outdoor features such as a reflecting pool sculptures and a small surrounding forest. There was a little bit of everything from an exhibit about a famous national artist who lived for decades on Jeju to an interesting video and poetry collaboration of Korean rappers talking about social issues. The upstairs is currently showcasing drawings and sculptures made by Korean schoolchildren in a surprisingly cheeky cheerful exhibit. Much of the museum was in English but others were only in Korean. The price of admission was only 1000 won well worth it for the experience. There were several pieces that didn't wow me and some outdoor floorboards that need repairs but all in all this is a nice little museum. Make sure to drop by the cafe on the way out for a lovely view of the reflecting pool outside as you sip your coffee!

Located in the middle of the Jeju island, it's a very beautiful and well managed National Park. Unfortunately, we were too late for hiking to the Hallasan and back. We decided to hike to the top of a directly opposite and much lower peak. It was easier and we were almost alone on the whole trail as well as at the peak. In the end, we had a nice picknick at the tourist and information center. If you really want to hike to the Hallasan itself, arrive and start as early as possible, be prepared with enough water, some food/snacks and other important hiking utensils.

Located in the Jungmun Resort in Jeju, near some restaurants there. The palce is quite large, consisting of 12 galleries. They showed interesting exhibits collected by Ripley at reasonable price (10k won per person). Worth visiting if you want to have some indoor activity in Jeju.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Located in Jungangro of downtown Jeju this underground shopping mall was the perfect spot to take in some local shopping due to the rain on the day we visited.  Most of the 280 shop locations were open but quite a few locations were in the process of or still had yet to open.  Most shops here sold shoes, clothing, and cosmetics.  We found several shops for children apparel and a few shops of general items and a couple of places to eat (which we tried - very good).  Of the shops there we didn't really find anything to our liking but the shopping experience was pleasant.  The shops varied in what they accepted for payment.  Most accepted Wans and several Credit Cards.  If any, tenants spoke very little English.

Located at the eastern end of Jeju Island. It will be about 1hr - 1.5 hrs drive if you stay at the city centre to this stunning place. Advisable to travel early in the morning if you want to avoid the tourists. I drove from Yeha Guesthouse around 7am and arrived in Seongsan Ilchulbong about 8.10am. The area was still empty with only those coming with their cars and still lots of parking lots. However if you arrived around 10am onward, rest assured the parking space will be a challenge. The entrance fee is KW2000 per adult. If you intend to hike until to the top, please wear proper shoes as the stairs can be pretty challenging and steep on the way down. The hike will take about 50 minutes if you walk slow and steady. Can be shorter if you climb faster. During the winter season, you are lucky if you can watch the sunrise. When we were there, it was cloudy and the sun is rising behind the cloud, but still the view up there is beautiful. If you don't want to climb up to the top, you can still enjoy the beautiful scenery around the area. If the time permits, you can also catch the Jeju Woman Diver (Haenyo) in action on your way down from the Seongsan Ilchulbong performing at two timing 1.30pm and 3.00pm respectively. There is a separate trail that leads down to where the action is. I wasn't able to watch it as we are rushing to go to Udo Island.There are Starbucks & Dunkin Donut for you to stop for a cup of coffee while enjoying the views and few shops that sells souvenirs. However the price may be a bit expensive as compared to Dongmun Market.Return visit : A must...for a sunrise views!

Located at the east coast of Jeju island, it is a crater of an inactive volcano lying out to the sea. A short walking trail to the top where you can get a beautiful view of the coastline. Next to the peak, you can watch the actual women divers show. Only two performance per day ( 1:30pm and 3:00pm ). Remember to bring sun glass, hat, sunscreen and water as the areas are wide open space with little cover. If you are thirsty, you can always try the famous local produce (fresh mandarin juice and mandarin ice block).

Located 25mins from Seogwipo, at the Jungmun area, this is a dramatic stretch of coast with hexagonal rock columns. They result from the rapid cooling and contraction of lava once it has met the water of the sea.There is a viewing platform right behind the Jeju ICC (convention centre), from where to admire the coast and the formations in particular.To access the platform, park the rental car at the designated park (KRW 1000) and buy the access tickets (KRW 2000). The platform is always busy and with all the selfies going on, one struggles to look at the rock formations.

Living in Hong Kong we're pretty used to tough hikes - this one is a little difficult but manageable for anyone who is reasonably fit or has some hiking experience. Whilst the incline on this hike is never that steep and the first part of the trail is easy with paved walkways, the terrain for the second half is pretty hard going with lots of rocks and boulders. We managed in trainers but hiking boots with a sturdy sole would probably be better, and some may feel more comfortable with poles. But it's ABSOLUTELY worth the effort for the view. The crater lake is quite impressive but more stunning is if you look back on Jeju from above the clouds. Took us about 6.5 hours up and down but bring plenty of snacks as there is only one point where you can buy water and some dubious looking packet noodles. Oh and there are no bins so bring a bag for your rubbish. If you are in Jeju and like hiking, you must do this as it's a great sense of achievement when you can say you've hiked S Korea's highest peak!

Likes:Beautiful light blue waters, similar to HyeopjaeLess people during the July/August period.A few empty umbrella spaces for us to squeeze in (thanks to less people)Can rent floatablesDislikes:No wavesRecommend to others?Yes, if you want to go to a beach on the west coast of Jeju

Like other hikes in Korea there are a lot of stairs. But that also means that there are plenty of places to rest which is great when you're hiking with small children. My 8 year old and 4 year old made it up and back without difficulty. They were hot but we were lucky to have had a breeze the entire time. The views were great from the top and along the way. There are two covered rest areas on the way up and plenty of benches if you get tired. The cost is the same as many other nature sites on Jeju, ??2000 per adult and ??1000 per child. There are horse rides for ??5000 at the trailhead. There is an adjacent beach and divers show but we decided not to go to and opted for food instead. Just outside the entrance there are a number of shops for ice cream, food, and fresh squeezed mandarin juice. The hike took about 60 minutes total going at a slow pace. Without kids one could do it quite a bit faster. Overall it was a great way to spend about half a day.

Lesser popular than others on Jeju like Ilchubong or Hallasan, but a pretty hike with a lovely view from the top. No sure what I expected for the silver grasses so was very impressed to see the effects of the sun on it as we took the short hike. I went late in the day so there were not as many people around which was nice. You pay a small fee to enter and the entire hike is relatively quite. The crater is nothing spectacular, however if you enjoy nature, the silver grasses are worth seeing.
Leave in the early morning from Jeju and spend the whole day on Udo, you will not regret, it extremely enjoyable.
Lava tube cave, UNESCO heritage place, is the highlight of jeju tours. Amazing georock transformation and preservation . Worth the visit.

Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site well-thronged by tourists. The uphill pathway leads to the majestic dormant crater and a path on the left of the ticket entrance brings you downwards to Haenyo women diver performance at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. Fresh catch of abalone, octopus, shells can be eaten sashimi style for about KRW50,000 per plate (pricey!).  At this spot, you're closest to the ocean for a spectacular view of the stratified cliffside and lava rock formations.  As you walk up the stairs, don't miss the platform for free binocular views of Udo Island. While the main goal of most tourists is to hike to the top of the crater,  do look back at  different vantage points for captivating views - azure sky, emerald sea, natural greens, black rocks and dotted by colourful buildings. Comfortable walking shoes recommended and beware of upskirting/fashion malfunction in the incredibly strong winds.  Jeju Weekly reported that from the 2H of 2017, hikers to Sunrise Peak will be required to book in advance via a reservation system for the route to the top of Sunrise Peak. The move comes after the Jeju Provincial Government took advice from 25 experts about how to protect the value of the island?s natural sites.

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.

Korea can feel very touristy and materialistic. Udo is the antidote to this. A beautiful, small island... with stone fences and perfectly kept fields of rye. Cute cafes and stone beaches. You can walk all over or cycle or drive your own rickshaw. Picturesque and less changed by tourism. I wished I had spend 2-3 days here instead of Jeju.

Knowns also as Sunrise Peak. We went there on afternoon as we did not know this place  can see beautiful sunrise. Must visit place when you in Jeju Island. Worthwhile hiking by stairs about 45 minutes. This wonderful craters formed from volcanic eruption l00,000 years ago. Entrance Ticket KRW2000. Twice a day can see women divers go to the sea and singing before catch their seafood such as abalone, sea urchin, etc. Overthere you can ride pony horses

Kimnyoung Maze Park is in the east of Jeju. We stayed in the West and we took a 30,000won tax to the place. The maze isn't very big but it was quite fun. Ditch the map and have fun getting lost. You see messages and signboards at different places and dead ends. The taxi driver offered to wait for us at the Maze without any cost while waiting as there's hardly any taxi in the area. And he drove us to our next destination (charging by metre). If you are planning to self drive, it is just right next to manjanggul cave. it is worth spending the 45mins to 1 hour in the maze.

Kim Mandeok Memorial.I really liked this place personally. I came to know of this woman, Kim Mandeok from this memorial museum. She was the first CEO woman in Chosun Dynasty, which was quite unusual especially as a woman. And when a famine came to Jeju, she helped people in Jeju. Because of the benevolent act, she was still remembered even now. Even a Korean drama dealt with her life. Her life is very exemplary and inspiring. You can find a fraction of Korean history here.

Keep in mind, the founder, Paek Uncheol, is quoted   ?Visiting the park is intended to be a journey through the mythology of the island, entering through the ear of Seolmundae*, progressing through the body and exiting at the feet. It represents the journey of life and death.? Taking a journey that ends in death, even if it is a metaphoric (mythical, mystical, mind-boggling) death, may not appeal to everyone, but it could be transformative if you're open to it. Allow for hours of contemplating stones, thousands, tens of thousands, of stones, natural, carved, authentic, replicas - millstones, mortars, volcanic bombs, boundary markers, 2000 ceramic jars, fossilized tree roots - locals thought its creator, who collected these stones for forty years, had gone mad. Three courses to follow, each taking one to two hours. *Seolmundae Halmang, the grandmother of Jeju Island.

just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.

just take a bus within 10min. i reached this beach. that was one of beautiful beach in jeju IMO as clear water with white sand also seaweed. it also has some windmill near around. except the beach that has a camp site. quite comfortable & relaxing place.the water was cool & the view also beautiful. it has many small crab,conch & fish. many people busy with them. ha. just no luck on i don't have a pretty sunset. anyway, worth to take time for visit here after cave & maze.

Just like everyone already mentioned, the road is indeed mysterious as the car would really move uphill on its own. However, it is only a very short stretch of the road. But I would still recommend it if you are self-driving and it's your first time in Jeju. Definitely, something you have to experience.You can also head to the museums that is nearby too after going to this road.

Just did the hike on 30 March.Trail: seongpanak up and gwaneumsa down. Goes to summit. (highly recommend to do this trail Cos going up by gweumusa is really steep though the view is nicer for gweumusa) Time taken: 4.5hrs up and 4hrs down (please go early and check the time that you need the reach the shelter and summit by.  Think should be by 1230 reach shelter and by 2 to leave summit) Weather: good.  Cold in the morning but as you hike,  you will perspire and definitely need minimum sweaters. I was only wearing teeshirt and windbreaker. In the end only tee-shirt cos it's getting warmer and you climb and when the sun is out. Need crampons?  Yes!!! It helped alot especially at the icy areas both going up and down. Not too sure where you can buy it but I managed to rent it from my hostel. Though I did see people without it,  and they did just fine.  I was wearing track shoes kind. So crampons helped alot!  How to get there: I went there from Jeju city and took bus 281 from bus terminal to seongpanak bus stop. Coming back from gwaneumsa trail: took bus 475 back to jeju  national university and change bus 360 to Jeju city.  Please check with bus driver or use kakao map/bus to help as Google Map doesn't seem to help much with he routes. Bus 475 have some timings going back. You can always find out from the visitors center at the gweumusa base. It is situated at the left side as you make your way down passing through the car park.  Shelters and food: not sure if I did miss it..  But I didn't see any food vendors, drinks stall as I hiked up and down. So I was really thirsty as the end of the trail. There's a small restaurant and a convenience store at gwaneumsa trail end. So please bring ALOT of water like at least 1.5L. Bring along food to eat up there and also plastic bag to put your trash and there are no rubbish bins around.

Just another market but in a different city. Similar in most ways.However, a distinct difference here is the huge amount of Jeju oranges (tangerines) on sale. Not just here but in other markets in Jeju too.Also it is common to see roadside trucks & makeshift stalls selling oranges - everywhere.Jeju is well known for its oranges , probably it's the season now. But they aren't exactly cheap despite the abundance of supply.We went to a nice Tangerine Orchard Farm right here in Jeju, where we paid 5,000?? admission fee per pax. And one can eat as much oranges as you want for unlimited time while at the Orchard.After which, every pax is entitled to pick/bring back 1kg free. Great experience & deal.

Jusangjeolli Cliff, designated as a natural monument of Jeju Island, is the largest columnar-jointed lava in South Korea. It was formed due to the sudden cooling of lava from the Hallasan Mountain, which erupted into the sea of Jungmun, thousands of years ago. Witnessed a picturesque view of the sea and the cliff. I recommend not wearing any hat or cap when you visit Jusangjeolli Cliff as the wind is strong there.

Jusangjeolli cliff is so worth visiting, to see such unusual yet impressive volcanic rock formations! It's really busy with other pushy tourists trying to get a photo, so I would recommend going early in the morning or later in the day. The rocks are a bit like a mini version of the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland. The water there is such a beautiful clear blue, just like the rest of the coastline around Jeju island.

Jungmun-Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff is beautiful place where, look at huge waves crashing against volcanic rocks, one can experience the power of nature. With so much to do and so much to see, the Jeju island is certainly one of the most prominent tourist places in the world. Just about an hour's flight from Seoul, it's a paradise for nature-lovers and surfers. There are countless world class museums offering education and entertainment based on themes like Glass, Ice Sculptures, Trick Art, Folk Lore, Health and Sex, War, Art - the list is endless. Best way to explore the Island is to take taxi tours with a driver who speaks and understands little English. They ask for W150,000 for 8 hours, however, you may beat them down to W115,000 or so. For sightseeing, 5-6 days should be enough.

Joined the 2016 Walking Festival to walk the olle trails & it was a fantastic experience. Yes it rained (which was unusual in October but with global warming!) & was initially disappointing as the scheduled performances were cancelled. Nonetheless it was amazing to see so many people walking together. After the Walking Festival which covered trail 1 & 2 I did trail 1-1, 5,6, 8 & 10. Each of the trails were different and beautiful. I was fortunate to get the assistance of Jim Saunders who gave me information on line & Ms Han at the Tourist Information Centre located next to Seogwipo Bus Terminal & e Mart who spoke good English.Ms Han helped me by writing in korean the bus stops & landmarks for the different trails so that I could show the bus drivers my destination  when I boarded using the T-money transport card. She even took the trouble to show me the different landmarks using satellite pictures on her computer in locating the Starting Point of each trail. The Olle Guide Book in English (which I obtained at the Olle Trail counter at the airport)was also very useful & well written.I enjoyed every trail & got to see Jeju on foot. It was also fun meeting locals walking the trails. I plan to return to walk the other olle trails.

Jeongbang Waterfall was near our guesthouse and it was the first stop of our trip to the east of Jeju. You can climb through the rocks and take a photo in the middle the small pond, in front of the waterfall. The water spray catches the light and acts as a prism to scatter the light into rainbows..pretty

Jeongbang Waterfall itself is beautiful.  A bonus to see the Haenyo (women sea divers) set up camp at the base of the waterfall selling fresh sashimi from their morning's catch.  The entrance is a bit touristy with a small market trying to see you all the typical Jeju fare (famous hallabong which mine were deceptively switched to regular tangerines, hallabong flavored everything, grandfather statues...).  But what makes the stop worth it is the   other waterfall   just a few min walk down the Olle trail at the same entrance.  That one isn't nearly as tall but way more impressive in my book.

Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest, walking through these wood is believed to enhance cardiovascular function and to prevent asthma and tuberculosis. This is the most famous forest on Jeju island and here you can taste mineral water that is thought to relieve muscle and gastrointestinal problem

Jeolmul Natural Forest is a must-see in Jeju Island. I really love the lush greenery in the forest park. There are many trails, each with different length and level of difficulty. We only had slightly less than 2 hours in the park. Therefore we only managed to walk the Samwool-gil trail followed by climbing the Oreum Trail (many steps, may get slippery if it rain) and explore the relaxing garden/ pond area. If I come again, I will allocate at least half a day in this beautiful forest. The entrance fee in only KRW1000, and there was a small stall at the entrance whereby you can grab a coffee or buy something to eat. Do not miss it if you are in Jeju Island.

Jeju's teddy bear museum is one of the most iconic destinations. I first heard about it from watching the show Goong years ago, and decided I had to visit it if I ever went to Jeju island. It was a small museum, but nonetheless i'm glad I paid a visit. The museum is a short walk from The Shilla Jeju  , which is where we stayed.

Jeju-do best attraction, the Mysterious Road (Dokkaebi Road) or Goblin road as folk story say, it was the goblins who does the trick.. sound interesting. Young and old will find this place fun and mysterious. All you have to do is just stop your car at the designation point, on the double sign(emergency light), off the engine, release the hand brake and let the car move up the hill by itself, 'Yes.. roll up the hill'.The best is, this attraction is free of charge. Along the Mysterious Road, have a few food stall, try out the grilled black pork sausage and many delicious food. For those driving, key in the number 7126988 (yup.. heading to Loveland, you will reach Mysterious Road first), most people stop by here on the way to airport.

Jeju stone park was rated A by Korea Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in recognition that this park is excellent in term of its specialization in the theme of stone, differentiation from other facilities, and characteristics relating to mythology and the life of the people in the region.Get the map at the entrance and follow guided park course. Don't miss out the Jeju stone museum to know how the formation of Jeju Island. After a short nice walk from the entrance,the museum is just located in the basement of a building opposite the Sky Pond. Follow the map to look for Jeju traditional village with thatched roof houses. Before at the end of course, drop by the unique Gallery in the park which you may find artworks of domestic and foreign artists.It is indeed best travel Korea during Autum because even though it was sunny day, but the breeze was so cooling and the air was very refreshing. It is a museum as well as an ecological park. It is a very remarkable cultural park which sublimating nature in art ,really very fantastic.
Jeju Stone Park is interesting. There are lots of great spots for photos and there are also lots of stone exhibits which infuses some aspects of history, culture and art.

Jeju Stone Park is a vast area with everything stone related.  With Jeju being a volcanic island, the lava stones are everywhere from the Harubang statues to the walls surrounding houses.  The park is divided into three courses which would take about an hour each at a leisurely pace.  The first course has mostly rock statues (including the Harubang statues) that most likely had some religious significance.  The second course shows how the rocks were used for more practical purposes (tombstones, tools, housing, etc) through the different eras of Korean history.  The third course specifically shows the different Jeju style housing made with mostly the volcanic rock walls.  It?s probably not the best place to be in the middle of heat in the summer but when the weather is nice, it?s a fantastic spot to spend a few hours.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju Olle Trail is completely round the island broken up into 21 different routes.In total we walked about 13km, about 3.5 to 4 hours time taken. Photography time included.We started our walk from Hyatt Jeju along the Jungmun Beach (we did Route 8 going eastwards) heading towards the Daepo Pego (port) and ended our walk at the Yakcheon Temple.Ensure that you look out for arrows (blue&orange) along the ground and olle trail ribbons (blue & orange as well) tying on trees along the way. Terrain is very varied, from easy tarmac lanes to quite difficult lava rocks along the bays. Suggest you wear proper walking shoes. Bring along your own water & snacks. There are a few restrooms along the way. If you are staying around Jungmun resort area (many hotels there), take airport bus limousine no 600 to go back to your hotel. Its about 1000 Korean Won per person.Overall is an interesting walk because you will see village, seaside, port & temple along the way. This is one of the very popular walk in Jeju, so its like a   must walk   walk.. We just did a short segment of the Olle Trail & apparently other segments are even more interesting.. Check out some photos for illustration.
Jeju Kimnyoung Maze Park - What a bewitching idea, kids as well as families liked about touring here.

Jeju Island is indeed a unique island with so many gorgeous scenery, i had a great time travelling there in Winter, a low season with lesser tourist gives a different experience from visiting it in busy Summer. I have seen pictures about Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff (?ъ＜ⓒ\由) and was amazed by the neat shapes of hexagon stone pillars formed by volcanic lava, i totally recommend tourist to spend time walking around the nicely design olle trail in the beautiful, as well as to visit Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff during your trip in Seogwipo or Chungmun area. you don't have to plan for a long stay, a good two hours should be more than enough, as it was just a viewing spot rather than you can actually walk-in and visit. Don't worry about the transport, bus services are available (in fact it is very convenient to reach most of the travel spot around Jeju island), just drop by Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and walk about 15 minutes to the park entrance, bus drivers in Jeju are very friendly and can basic communication woudn't be a concern. there is a entrance fees of 2000won in the park.there are steps to walk down to have a clearer view, description board with picture will explain how the hexagons shapes are formed, you can take amazing pictures and enjoy the sea view too.speaking of the weather, i have quite an experience, it was sunshine at first while i was taking the bus, and soon it become heavy downpour and even snow flakes begin to attack me during my walking! i think an umbrella or raincoat is necessary for either bright sunshine or unexpected rain. i gotta say, Jeju Island's weather is unpredictable! although this is not a spot to actually feel and touch the pillars, it can be quite boring to certain people who expected more attraction, but seeing the amazing cliff, the neat pillars, it was totally worth it to witness it by your own eyes, even the finest artist surrender to this piece of art, isn't it?

Jeju island is a really beautiful place and there is so many amazing sites but i was a bit underwhelmed by this view compared to others i saw. I'd say it was worth seeing if you are in the area but essentially its just a rock, and there are lots more, much prettier rocks, around the island!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

Jeju Island in Korea is a exceedingly wonderful place to have vacation for family and also a  place to have honey moon for lovers. After doing some traveling plans, I went to Korea with friends in April this year. It?s really a nice time to meet Jeju Island in spring, the weather is comfortable, and the flowers were growing beautifully at that time. A vast , blue as well as clear sea came into my horizon, relaxing my body and purifying my mind dramatically. Not annoyance and trouble anymore, but freedom and joy there. The blue sea does calm me down. Additionally, because of its great geographical location, we are able to taste some delicious local food, such as fresh octopus, deep-sea fish, oysters, and also famous Jeju orange chocolate.In a word, Jeju is worth going, especially for whom are fond of view of sea.

Jeju Island features a trail system that circumnavigates the island allowing the most highly motivated to hike the island, on foot.  If you want to see some great coast line and get the most out of a modest walk, look for trail #7.  It takes you along some great coastline with fantastic views of the cliffs, rocks and water.  In several areas, there are steps that take you from up high down to the surf.  If you stick to the trail, the elevation changes are modest and should be doable for anyone of moderate fitness.

Jeju Island depend 75% on tourist business nothing much in Jeju Island except for scenery viewing. A ladies brief and conducted a short tour in Folk Village.This place is very small less than 20 min you can cover the whole area. And trying to sell us very expensive Raw Honey and Omicha Health Cordial 1000gm at 40000 won each which claimed using the raw,fine,fresh,ingredient to process it.While other pharmacy and e-mart sell only approximately at 20000 won

Jeju is well known by the haenyeo, or that we usually called it as woman divers. Since it was not a good time for diving like a haenyeo and it means that it was so difficult to find one of them when i visited Jeju, i decided to visit the museum. It's not so big, but shows completely how the haenyeo's life, their lives, and their historical stories. It shows not only the diving suit they wear since long time ago until nowadays but also their house, their foods, their tools, and everything. Your journey will be started by watching a video about history of haenyeo. Then you can walk through the dioramas to learn how haenyeo live and works.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Jeju is not only beaches and shopping malls, but has also a really interesting history ! This memorial is part of this history and helps you to understand the island but also Korea better.They have english translations of most presentation boards in the memorial, so you don't need to be able to read Korean to understand this visit.The explanations and the context they gave about the uprising of April 3rd are really captivating and well presented.I highly recommend to go there !

Jeju is know for horses and mandarins. I'd say, this is a must see for those who visit Jeju for the first time.Tickets can be bought online in Trazy.com. You should receive your e-tickets within 24hrs. Then exchange this at The Ma park's ticket booth. To get there, we took a taxi from Hyeojae Beach (costs KRW9,000). It's a must that you buy ticket in advance due to limited seats. A lot of private tour bus go here. Public transportation is very seldom in this area. If you can arrange a round trip transpo, please do so. As for us, we walked 2 KM to the main road. But again, the 1Hr show is worth seeing. =)

Jeju is gifted by heaven with 3 famous waterfalls. This is the most awesome one that the mother nature embraces its beauty. From far, you could see rainbows.You probably will end up like me.. leaping and hoping from rocks & stones to get close to the waterfalls. I did fell down when I pursue a step of closeness to this natural beauty. But I could not resist its charm and finally I stood firm with the beauty. Don't envy, go for it!

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

Jeju is famous for hiking and its Olle walking routes, chosen to hike in Hallasan National Park as part of our itinerary. My first hiking experience in oversea and it is an unforgettable experience I ever had. Fantastic !

Jeju is famous and ideal for walking, trekking and experiencing the nature. This Hallasan- the highest mountain in Jeju is a must for those who love nature and trekking. Views from high up are fantastic and the experience is well worth the few hours you spend there, but be warned as there are steep steps and sections and do taking trekking poles if you need them. We took the 'easiest' treks - Erimok up and Yongseil down, which took us a total of 7 hours of slow walk including more than 1.5 hr rest at the kiosk stop where these 2 trails meet.  The kiosks sells cup noodles (hot!) which is the best in cold weather, and it's incredibly cheap.  Do wear in layers as you'd experience vast difference in temp in the sun, shade, windy, higher altitude, etc. If you park at Erimok visitor centre, you need to take a taxi back from the foot of Yongseil (as the distance is some 17 km), but there should always be a couple there. I personally prefer Erimok which offers more shade and less steep sections.

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.

Jeju has some very interesting museums, they seem to have them about everything from electricity ,to tea to, to robots! Quite quirky here and you'll see Teddy bears dressed up as Michael Jordan to famous re-enactments of history. Spent about 2 hours here just because it seemed interesting and a lot of effort has been put into the place.

Jeju has its rainy strong windy days and on a dsy like this, it was perfect for visiting the teddy bear museum.  I had to admit, my expectations were low so in turn, i quite enjoyed it!  There were sections about the history of teddy bears and even reenactment of historical scenes by the teddies!  There is also a free teddy bear Elvis performance on the other side of the museum that was quite amusing :)

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.

Jeju hanyeo, women divers are the very best symbol of Jeju.You can watch them catch sea creatures mostly any place you go in the island.However, this museum is the only and best place you can get the whole idea of who they are, what they live up for, how they do it, etc.It's a lil dificult to get there, I know. But it's worth visiting.So I highly recommend you going this place.

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

Jeju Glass Castle is the famous place at Jeju. When I first went inside, I just like walk in an unreal place. Since the entire thing is made by glass. You can see glass everywhere, such as the flowers, the trees and the artworks.One of the special things in this castle is an artwork that calls ?a moment of musical concert?, this artwork show that the moment of a band that is performing. The entire performers have different emotion and music instruments. It is very hard to do this, because each performer?s face is smaller than a coin.Here also have some funny place, such as Glass labyrinth and distorting mirror. Be careful, maybe you will lose in the labyrinth, or become a fat boy/girl in the distorting mirror.Finally, I suggest that you need to be very careful in this castle, if not you will break the glass.

Jeju Glass Castle is a must see museum. It has outdoor which can be seen with in 2 hours & indoor as well. There are a lot of glass shapes. This museum is good for people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. The entrance ticket is little bit expensive.

Jeju Glass Castle is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall,garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These includes glass art masterpieces by international famous artists from Italy,The Czech Republic,Japan and many more. This theme park suitable for all ages. Very cold due to winter season,do put on more wear as you need to walk round the outdoor.

Jeju Glass Castle houses collection of glass arts. The glass arts are tastefully arranged in different areas of the park, most of them outdoors. The forest trail is the most interesting area. Best to be visited in good weather.

Jeju 4-3 Peace Park educates visitors thoroughly about the Jeju 4-3 Incident which was really almost a genocide when Korean government and US military killed over 30,000 Jeju residents and tortured many more.  With Korea on the brink of dividing into two, Jeju residents wrongly suspected of being Communists ended up being victims.  The government didn't even go public about the incident until the late 1990's and only officially apologized in the 2000's.  The museum describes the build up to the incident and depicts all the horrible details of what the Jeju residents went through.  Having gone through grade school in the 1980's when the incident was not public knowledge, this was a very educational experience for me.

I've visited many caves but by far this is the first lava tube that I have experienced. It is interesting to know the science and geography behind this magnificent tube. However, only 1 km deep into the tube is open to tourists. You can take a public bus directly from the Jeju bus station if you opt to travel on a budget. The bus fare is less than KRW 2000 compared to very pricey tours with taxi. The bus ride is only slightly more than an hour away from Jeju City.

I've never been able to go up so close to a waterfall that flows directly into the sea. You'll need to climb over rocks to go up near to the falls. I loved being so near the waterfall and the sea at the same time!If you only have time to see 1 waterfall on Jeju island, go to this one. Cheonjiyeon & Cheonjeyeon waterfalls were quite unimpressive in my opinion.

I've been very interested in the haenyeo ever since I first visited Jeju-do. This museum has some interesting exhibitions about the life and work of the haenyeo. Admission is very cheap, a bit over 1000 won for an adult. It's recommended to watch the short documentary about the haenyeo before visiting the exhibitions, to get the most out of your visit. It plays near the lobby. There's a gift shop on site with haenyeo-related items.

Its worth it to climb up there. such a beautiful and breath taking view from the top. its a must visit place if you come to Jeju. entrance fee is just 2000krw per person. we actually drove there from our pension. many parking space. other than climbing the peak, you can also catch a Haenyo Diver Women performance at the bottom of mountain right beside it. its amazing to watch those elderly women  holding their breath for several minutes without any oxygen mask! overall its awesome! for those muslims, there's fast food restaurant Lotteria for you to grab your lunch or dinner since they have shrimp burger available. its located on your left when exit the car park area.
It's very near to Loveland. Interesting to see the car roll forward upslope. Start on the south, towards Jeju city. Length of the road is quite short, maybe 50m?

It's very near to Jeju city, within walking distance. It's nice walk strolling along the seaside to dragon head rock and even walk further from there. However this place is always full of tourist, and not easy to get a good picture of this attraction. Nevertheless the environment and surrounding is beautiful and relaxing and I was here during sunset and foggy evening, absolutely beautiful.
it's really a place that should visit in jeju.even we have to climb for 180M but when u arrived at the peak.the view is amaging, really worth to go there!!!

It's probably the best place to shop for street wear in Jeju but it's nothing compared to Seoul. It's pretty difficult using public transportation in Jeju to getting around expect using car. But this one is ok because there is bus stop in the highway, but you need to take a taxi or walking 3km from bus stop to get this place

It's not the most huge waterfall, but its certainly the closest distance you can have with that beautiful waterfalls. Brace yourself with the beauty of natural creation. Must visit whenever you go Jeju.

It's my second visit to Jeju and since I am staying in Jungmun area, we decided to visit this nearby attraction. I can't remember the name of the teddy bear museum of my previous trip but it's definitely bigger than this. You will find this attraction amazing if you are visiting a teddy bear museum for the first time, but being my second visit to such attraction, I don't find anything particularly interesting.

It's my favourite place in Jeju! It's not just an island as we thought it would be! Rmb to bring along your international license if you are planning to ride any motorised vehicles. We biked around the island which in my opinion allows you to see more attractions. (just follow the smell) try the peanut ice cream! its better than the hallabong one.

It's more of a shopping place. The green tea ice-cream is quite blandand there's not much green tea taste.But the   saving grace   is the tea plantation . There are giant cupslots of flowers and is overall a photo taking place. We did not have enough time and did not visit the museum . It's more like a zoo combined with a synthetic garden. What attracted me were the cave's and they were disappointing as well, I've been to much nicer and impressive Caves, these are just hollow space under ground. Waste of time in my opinion, there are much better and natural sights in Jeju.

It's know as Jaerae sijang.if you ask about dongmun market,korean people don't know about it.their said it jaerae sijang. From soegipwo terminal,in font of. E mart there is bus stop use bus no.100It's a small market,much sell jeju chocholate,jeju orange,n much food

It's just a stadium with some architectural appeal but the shape tells a story  which is interesting. Try telling any football aficionado that it just a stadium and you will get howls of protest!From the 2002 FIFA World Cup it is designed around   the mouth of a volcano    and its roof in the shape of nets of traditional fishing boats in Jeju.So looking at it in that respect makes it more interesting.It was not open when we visited as of course there are no games here at the moment (although open during the summer months) so it was like looking into a fish bowl without the fish.Outside the stadium are many stone crafted 'dol hareubangs ' carved from porous basalt (volcanic rock).The statues' faces feature grinning expressions and bulging eyes without pupils  a long  broad nose  and slight smile and their hands rest on their bellies.These are quite common throughout Jeju and can be quite comic and a little suggestive!Have a peek here if in the area just to have at look at the stadium design and also the rock statues.Enjoy your visit!

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

It's good place for experience the local community which they will arrange the local guide whom live tin the village to give you the informations and details about the village including the history and culture. There's the translator for the local people since they are hardly speak other language besides Korean. They will explain the way they hand the wooden stick at the gate. The meaning of the stone statue. They will have to room the tell us their history and story. They will have a village walk so everyone can see and experiences their village including photo shooting. They will show us how to make   Omecha   which it the berry layer with honey and keep in the jar for conservative before consume it. The Omecha is sticky so need to mix with water for drinking and contain a lot of vitamins. The local guide will try to up sales their local products after tour such as Omecha and horse bone. They make the bone into small pills and they said its good for those whom need calcium or need recovery from injury and also good for the growth of young kid. They also sell dried squids which already mix with sauce before dried it. It's a good experience as the village is very unique. The house is only one floor and low ceiling since Jeju is very windy. The wall also made with the lava stone from the hallasan mountain.Avoid to go during rainy day even they provide the umbrella during the walk but it's not convenience at all.

Its fish market but have a lot of store sale a souvenir and gift item like small soju and jeju orange, jeju cohocolate and sama candies and friend...and at the end of dongmun market they have delicious street food....and yummy
It's crowded but the view is amazing. If you're a first timer, I personally will recommend this than the other waterfalls in Jeju.

It's another geographical landscape that Jeju is well known for. Sungumburi Crater is one such feature. It is a caldera overgrown with grass and greeneries. It is said deers used to roam around the crater.

It's an incredible lava cave! We spent half day in this sight seeing and my daughters loved! (2 teenagers) It's very difficult to do sight seeing in Jeju without a rental car! We took almost an hour to arrive there, and the same to come back!!

It's an easy climb to the top, and there are various stops for you to take pictures. The view was spectacular and you can see Jeju island stretching out below you. You can even spot the hazy outline of Mt Halla from there.

It's actually quite interesting as the road seems like an uphill slope but vehicles will move forward (slowly) without turning on their engine. It?s some sort of an optical illusion i suppose. It just.. seems like a normal road lolIf you are around the area, you can drop by to take a look.For full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/the-mysterious-road/
It's about 1.3km from the bottom to the top. Along the way to the top, u can really enjoy the fresh air and the woods. From the top, u can see hills and jeju town.
it's a unique culture of jeju island, black lava rock wall. they do provide free guide tour, interesting explanation.

It's a traditional market where you can shop for clothes, food and make up here. There's a few souvenir shop also. The price of the make up here at jeju is very cheap compared to the price in my country. It's like 1/4 price. If you wanna buy some clothes you have to bargain it. I visited it twice coz it's easy to reach with the jeju bus. Just stop at the dongmun market stop en then go down to tge basement.

Its a short street UG mall sells things you will find in normal shops in Jeju.  The catch here is that this place is not just underground BUT its air conditioned.  Its maintained very well with clean toilets.  We spent about 40 mins leisurely but didn't buy anything in the end.  I won't say its a must-go place but if you happened to be at Dongmun market, its a short walk to this place.

It's a really really nice place except for the diver women with the fishes and dead octopus, that's gross and I'm vegan. Anyway, you can pay for a quick boat trip to see the surroundings of this place like caves and also a rock full of birds (Think of Paracas, Peru, i think it's similar). The view at the top is AMAZING, like I said, you can see all Jeju? Seogwipo? I don't know but it's BEAUTIFUL. There are also many food spots and stores plus Starbucks and Dunkin Donuts.

It's a pretty long cave but that's pretty much it. It's very cold, wet and dark down there (went during summer) so do get your windbreakers/jackets and flashlights ready. Whether you should visit entirely depends on you. If you have more more on your itinerary of Jeju, then you'd most likely want to give this place a miss.

It's a place where you will stop for 30 mins max? Everyone will be queuing to take with the   dragon head  . From time to time, you will be able to catch planes flying across the as it's near the airportYou may also find Dol Hareubang means literally ?stone grandfather? in Jeju?s dialect. They can be found anywhere in Jeju island.
