It's a place that is almost carbon-free. Electric cars, wind and solar panels are used for energy. It's small enough to travel around on foot or rent a bicycle. A ferry from Jeju takes about 20 minutes. Nice local restaurants to try.

It's a nice place and interesting concept but some of the attractions seem run down and nothing much to see.. It's good to go with kids to explore the fresh air or play area , got spare time or if u on tour good to pay a visit . If not there are many other places in Jeju with nice scenery to visit ..

It's a natural wonder.  Amazing how lava can create a tunnel as large as this. Must visit when in Jeju.  Wear a pair of walking shoes and an autumn jacket as temperature falls to around 15 inside the tube. It'll take you at least 30 minutes to walk 1km in and then another 30 minutes out.  So,  it's pretty chilly if you are without a jacket. Floor is wet therefore walk carefully & enjoy the unusual sights especially the walls & ceiling of the tube. Walk until the end as there's a lava column in there, the only one.

It's a must do to spend some time at this museum. Located in a relatively new building right on the coast, it tells the story of these amazing women divers who work 52 weeks of the year diving for a abalone, conch and other sea products. How they managed in the winter time without wet suits astonishes me. These women also played a vital part of the resistance movement in World War II against the invading Japanese Army. Add this visit as part of your Jeju Island tour - best idea it to hire a taxi driver for a day (approx A$100). They turn out to be your tour guide, photographer and restaurant selector - fantastic value! Enjoy :)

It's a mixed review.  The ticket price is 10,000KRW per adult and since other natural attractions are around 2,000KRW, this park should be well worth it.  Highs: The caves are really cool as well as the Bansai and Stone Garden. The park is easy to walk and has shops and toilets easily available.  Transportation is also easy as it's just the 702 bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal for 1 hour. Lows: The park is dated, like late 90s with its signage and information cards.  The bird exhibit, stone exhibit and flower garden are average at best.  While the park trail is easy to walk, you do walk through gift shops for the next exhibits (so a bit too tourist-y). Overall, it makes for a decent easy afternoon, especially with kids or elderly.  The park needs some updating to be worth the ticket price, but it is close to the beach (just 5 mins walking).

It's a lot of stairs and little walking to get to the top, but it's worth it with great views and a wonderful sea breeze. On one side you have views of the crater, on the other of Jeju island. There are lots of other tourists (mostly local) going up and down so be prepared for some level of crowds. There was abundant parking when we visited. There are also plenty of food stalls at the bottom along with bathrooms. On the way up, there are lots of benches, rest areas, and viewing platforms. We saw people of all ages - really old to really young doing the climb. If you're in town and you have a couple hours to spare, we'd recommend it!
It's a impressive waterfall in Jeju Island of historical significance.Should not miss this site, if it's your first trip to Jeju Island.

It's a great honour to be able to admire Mr Sung's Spirited Garden! It's absolutely a must visit whenever you are in Jeju! The garden is a real Paradise on Earth! It's a unique place that teaches you many important things! The garden features many outstanding examples of bonsai trees, beautifully shaped stones, a waterfall, a restaurant and a souvenir shop. It's easily accessible by car or by bus, and will be a worthy place for everyone, especially the nature and art admirers. I highly advise everyone to visit this incredible place!!!
It's a beautiful park to stroll around in the spring time (that's when I visitors Jeju) and given the good weather condition, walking around is just refreshing and calming. A must visit place

It's a beautiful island just 15mins ferry ride away from Jeju Island. Rented cars are not allowed to travel over so we parked our car at the terminal port in Seongsan. Upon arrival at the port in Udo, you will see a few shops just right infront of the port start promoting their offering on bike rentals. Standard rental is 2hrs (KRW 10,000 per pax) for a standard bicycle. So great to tour around and have the best seafood pot ever along the coastal. Peanut ice-cream is a must have, it is so good! We did not manage to visit any of the recommended sightseeing places due to short of time but we had a great time cycling around taking pictures, along with the beautiful weather. Definitely will return again.

It?s our 2nd time in Jeju Island so we decided to do it. We took a bus to Seongpanak and started our hike there. It took us 5 hrs to the peak. It?s not an easy hike at all. Wear comfortable shoes, hiking shoes or sneakers with very good soles. The trail is full of rocks. This will definitely hurt your feet. Don?t wear jeans. Wear something more comfortable. Also bring as much water as you can. In the map, it says there is a Water Station  but they are gone now. You have to be by the second shelter at 12:30 or else they wont allow you to go to the summit. Everybody must descend by 2pm.Going down we took the Gwaneumsa Trail which is shorter but more difficult trail. However, I would recommend this trail cause it?s more scenic. It took us another 5 hrs.
It?s most beautiful trail in Jeju even can?t make to the top top but the view just gorgeous, if you are looking for a bit challenge trail also have good view this is the one you have to go!

It?s an easy drive from Jeju City. There?s a nice park and some restaurants and stores. I was there in February and it was cold, windy, and even snowing, but the beach was still beautiful with the black cliffs and the white sand. I?m sure it?d be perfect in warmer weather!

It?s a very big place.. there are a cave, garden, mang kind of birds, trees ans flowers.. i think it is a good place to visit in jeju.. you can see many things here.. but it is difficult to find a bus to here and the bus is not ontime..

It?s a place must visit in Jeju island. Air is so fresh and the walk is tranquil. When you walk through the forest and appreciate wat the Korean say that it is a place for meditation. There is a tap near the entrance, water is so refreshing. Trees in the forest have been there for hundred of years . It?s a treat to see some trees with autumn leaves. There are some Low walls with black stone formations which apparently is the volcanic rock from Jeju itself.. Would definitely come back here again to spend more time in the forest At the end of the walk they even have the vacuum facility to blow off the red soil from your shoes
It?s a market of EVERYTHING in Jeju - fish market, food, fruits (Local oranges) and it offers not only a feast to empty stomachs but also visual show

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

It was very meaningful to spend 3 days to join the Jeju Olle walking festival in November, 2018. One route per day not only an physical exercise and challenge to myself but also a good opportunity to meet friends or make new friends there. No one push you to walk faster but we could take pictures, enjoyed nice views and landscapes on each route. Local food for lunchs were delicious. What a beautiful island, good for gathering and good for vacation. I love Jeju. It was my third time participating Jeju Olle Festival. Different experience every time.

It was ur eyes who played trick! Discovered in the 70s, there are 4 such places in the whole of Jeju island. Your tour guide will reveal to you the   secret   of the road, so I won;t be here to soil your surprise. It's fun to try to walk backward (uphill) and fell more easier than downhill.

It was the best decision to travel around the beautiful island of Jeju with Jeju Taxi Tour Samchoon Kim! He brought us to all the places in our itinerary that we intended to visit and he even checked the weather prior to that so that we would not be caught in the rain. The whole trip was very comfortable and it was not in a rush. We took our time to see and soaked in all the goodness of Jeju! Samchoon Kim is also very kind and polite, I remembered one of the day he stopped by a morning market and ran down coming back with 6 freshly made Bungeo ppang (a Korean dessert) for us. That act really warm our hearts =) Not to forget, he also always offered to snap pictures for us so we do not need a selfie stick! Thank you for being a great tour guide and driver!

It was such a pain to get to but I loved the Stone Park. The main reason was to see the Dol hareubangs - the stone sculptures which represent Jeju. There was information about the mythology surrounding the formation of Jeju which was at times mind-boggling and contradictory. There are different routes around the park and there is an indoor exhibition which features the volcanic rocks and Jeju's origins as a volcanic island. I preferred the outdoor sections where the use of stone in Jeju was highlighted - used in things such as tombs/ shrines, walls, icons of spiritual beliefs etc. The largest sculptures are near the exit and the Dol hareubangs were awesome. They all had slightly different expressions and quirks which was cool. There are plans to expand the museum grounds and I would defo like to go back again in future. It was quite quiet when we were there and we only saw a few people except for a group on a guided tour at the end. Such a shame there are not more visitors but good for those who made the effort. Recommended visit in Jeju!

It was sooo much fun to visit this place. When I visited Jeju, my Korean friend brought me to Playkpop museum. I had so much fun to watch kpop stars' videos at the 3-D theater. I spent most time to take holographic pictures. It was a hidden jem in Jeju. If you love kpop music, you will love this place!!! I definitely wanna visit again, if I go to Jeju.

It was really hot when we arrived so we did not go up the summit but explored the surrounding. You could walk to the left where you will come to several flights of steps leading down to the beach where the haenyeo or women free divers will perform their skills. If you do not fancy walking all the way down, just continue left as you will come to a cliff overseeing the Udo island. Another go to place in jeju. Understand that this island is form from volcanic eruptions much like jeju is as well. There are also lots of photo opportunities at the foot of the 180m+ mountain(?). Of course the usual F&B outlets are here as well. We also see some signage for horse riding but did not explore.
It was quite near our hotel - Jeju Ocean Palace Hotel.about 10 minutes drive away.There was raw abalone, sea cucumber and squid to eat next to the waterfall.

It was pretty crowded when we got there at about 3pm on a weekday. From the parking area, It was a short walk down some stairs to the observation decks where you get good views of the unique (column) rock formations by the coast.However, we had difficulties getting photos of us with the rock formation because there were just too many people on the observation decks. As we exited the observation deck area, we saw a guy selling postcards of the photos he himself took of various scenic Jeju attractions and we bought some to support him.I am not sure what else there is to explore in that area because we were hurried off to the next destination on our guided tour.If you are into Geography, love cliffs by the sea and rock formations, I highly recommend this place! I loved it!

It was our 2nd time visit Udo,absolutely loved it.Few tips for anyone who plan to visit Jeju:* Bring your ID with you! We went to Udo in July and we were asked to present ID at ticket office, Seongsanri Port. Saw lots tourists queuing at ticket office and pretty much everyone was holding passport!! We didn't have passport with us, but luck enough I had my driving licence in my purse. My boyfriend didn't have any ID with him, and we bought 2 ferry tickets with showing 1 ID only.  * it's an absolutely beautiful place. Tried peanut ice cream which was very refreshing. * scooter or bike? My opinion is get bike!! It costs 10000 won to get 1 bike and you can ride as long as you want, no time limit what so ever, it costs 25000 won to get a scooter, and you need to be back within 2 hours. It was kinda electric bike, so presuming the power only lasts 2 hours. If you plan spend move than 4 hours on this lovely island, bike is the option, not hard to ride around and you can stop at any cafe for a ice cream or drink and chill out at the beach for 1 hour. That's what we did :) rather than just sitting on the scooter and kept checking time consistently to make sure to get back  within 2 hours.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.

It was nice to enjoy 15-20 minutes here. Expect to compete for photo taking opportunities. 2000 won/ticket, walk down a few flights of wooden stairs, and climb over some big slippery rocks to get the best vantage point for viewing. Can feel the spray from across the pool. Accessible by bus 281 from Jeju city.

It was my first time experience in Jeju Island, but with 3 days and 2 nights , has been provided with a pleasure vacation with my family. For those who are planning to go to Jeongbang Waterfall, it is actually in Seogwipo, and you can cover two famous waterfall in this towns and most probably you can cover in a day. Thus, last time during our visit, for Jeongbang we visited early morning, and that the best time you to go, because not that many people and you can snap a photo alone instead of a lot of people.My tips:1. Go early i.e. 8.00am2. Get photo as much as you want3. Each season the waterfall will be different, if winter, you may get different panorama and landscape of the waterfall.Thank You.

It was my first hiking trip and I decided to take the Seongpanak trail (9.6km one way) so that I can reach the summit. The hike is long and steep at certain stages. Very rocky road and proper hiking shoe is strongly recommended. The hike starts from visitor center is at 750m. At 1500m, there's a Jindalrae shelter where you can take a break for hot instant noodle and refill your drinks. The hike is tough for me (someone who jog/cycle once or twice a week). Walking stick is my best friend to support me all the way. Reaching the submit at 1950m is breathtaking. You will see the beautiful Baengnokdam lake. On the way down, at 1324m we hike to see Saraoreum Lake too. The whole trail with break took me almost 10 hrs (9.15am till 7pm). It's seems to be an easy hike for the Koreans, including the elderly but to me is a lot of determination and perseverance. Will definately hike at the other trails if I have the chance to go back to Jeju. ** I saw deer **

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was just perfect vacation for me & my friends. We always dream of cruises holidays amnd just had a blast on superstar gemini cruise. Rooms were so comfy and i enjoed the food at every restaurant. busan and jeju are beautiful places and i wish to go there again!

It was felt like exercising when walking down to the see the waterfall. But just about ten steps down the stairs, the scene reveal the hidden stunning waterfall. So beautiful.  A dozen shoots were never felt enough to capture its beauty. I would recommend to spend a sufficient time just to enjoy the scenery.Please take be careful when walking in between stones near and around  the waterfalls. They are so slippery, so chose a flat surface stones as you walk? or not at all. A friend had her camera and mobile phone slipped down into water when she struggled to stand still on a stone. I was slightly more fortunate to be able to keep those gadgets of mine dry?. but not my shoes. While the water was refreshing, but I do not think you would like getting your shoes wet, particularly when you have only a pair for the whole Jeju island exploration. A wet trousers could spoil your whole day trip around the island.

It was early afternoon & very sunny, & super hot during our visit. Coupled with the long walk & return climb up from the bottom, it was terrible in the heat.Perhaps if we had come in early morning or in spring climate, would probably have enjoyed it better.The Jeju Women Divers Performance was a disappointment. With due respect to this fantastic women, the show was too commercialised.Have read much about these tenacious women & was looking forward to something better than this.However, our guide arranged for us earlier to meet up with these women not far away in another area.Most are in their 70s & had been doing this job almost their whole lives. They are so fit even at this age.Certainly respect them.There are paid boat rides as well round the area & horse riding too.
It was an easy walk, lots of street vendors, waterfall was beautiful. Perfect weather in October! We spent 2 days in jeju and just about did it all.

It was amazing!This is the worth place to go. The entrance fee is very cheap just 2000 won and the transportation arround 3300 won.Then Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak will gives unique view that you will never see in another place. It is very easy to go here, just take a bus from Jeju intercity Terminal or Seogwipo Intercity terminal then stop on Seongsan Ilchulbong  Entrance, Just walk for 10 minute from the bus stop to the ticket booth.

it was a very cold windy day we visited this place. climbed for about 30 mins to reach to the top to enjoy the scenery which is worth the climb. There are many people there but don't feel crowded at all. When you are in Jeju, make sure you visit this place, really beautiful

It was a pleasant surprise, for every day show it was very professional and very entertaining. As many people mentioned the place is on the middle of nowhere, we just took a taxi to go there from Jeju city was about 10000 KRW and after went to Nanta hotel and asked them to call us a taxi, was there in few minutes, so no problem at all.Tickets better to book online one day in advance, this case you can get 5000 KRW discount and seasonal discounts. As we wanted to go the same, we went directly there, but at the place there's no discounts or bargains, all prices are fixed, so better book on your own.
It was a nice trip. When in Jeju, try to visit here. You'll see interesting lava formations inside the cave. The entrance fee is KRW 2,000 for adults.
It was a nice place to visit , not spectacular but it is a unique place, this could be the last place to visit if you already visited other places before in Jeju.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.
It was a chilly walk up the slopes but a must-visit place on your list if u do go to Jeju island.We had many lovely photos taken there, that we brought home and i look at them a lot.

It took us more than an hour to get there. The wind was so chilly that you could feel your fingers freezing up when you take your gloves off to take photo.  But it is absolutely worth it !  The rock formation,formed layer by layer from lava erupted long long ago is so mystic & original. It's like touching rocks that are a million years ago.  Come dressed warmly in comfortable shoes  if you plan to walk along the coast as it is very very cold, wet & slippery. Nevertheless, not to be missed if you are travelling to Jeju!

It took convos with my friends who are from Korea to find out about this (I am from New York), but man was it worth it!  On a clear day this is up there with one of the prettiest sites and generally awesome vibes of anywhere I've been.  You get an incredible view, a nice short   hike   (up the stairs), AMAZING food all around, etc.  Definitely try the raw seafood caught by the diving ladies!  Explore the area.  I took a bus from Jeju City

It takes almost one and a half hour to arrive the Island from Jeju-si. But the view was stunning on the Island. There is a shuttle bus service which has 4 stops across the Island and 5000 won for each passager to have an unlimited ride. There is a famous icecream store at the first stop which sell peanut icecream which is very delicious. The beach at the third stop is so stunning with a beautiful ocean. However, the restaurant on the island are quite expensive, so better prepare your own food if you have a tight budget.

It takes about 6 hrs for hiking up and go back. The way back is rock path half of the way, so quite tough for me. But it's worth to hiking up. The scenery on the top is breathtaking and unique. I visited there on late May, which there were still some pink azalea blooming and it was very beautiful.Please beware of the weather and strong wind on the top.I'd rate it for No.1 attraction site to visit in Jeju-do.

It takes 15 min to get to Udo by ferry from Jeju, which schedule every 60 min.When you reach the island you have many shops that will offer you to rent small electric vehicles for 2 hours, it will be enough for browsing around all the beautiful circle road of the island. if you're planning to have lunch or some other activity, take 3 hours. 2 hours cost around 20,000 KRW for an electric scooter (1 person).Important Tip: 1. Take detailed pictures of the rental as they will sometimes try to blame you on some scratches they found when you return.2. Can't be miss is the   Rise Mango   100% that sell all over the Island.

It takes 1.5 hours from Jeju Intercity bus station to Seongsan IIchulbong, by bus 701. After 30 mins drive, you can see the blue sky and green sea outside of the windows. The admin fee is 200 0 KR but the great view is worth of it. You can see large grass ground and hike to the top. If there is sunshine, no doubt you can have wonderful pictures and experience even with a phone camera.

It rained almost nonstop on our trip to Jeju so we visited a lot of museums we probably would normally have not. The hologram concert is the major attraction in Play Kpop and it was good fun. The rest? Meh. The entry ticket is 15 000 won which is rather expensive since most museums on the island just cost a few thousand won. On top of that, a lot of the other attractions (like photo booths) cost extra. Kpop history was interesting enough, but most of the other stuff was quite boring.

It only takes 45 minutes to hike even with the normal speed. The top view is also amazing, The best time to come here is in the sunset time. This place is worthy even though a little far from Jeju City

It offers one of the best view in Jeju. It is free to go, no need to book, super easy to walk. I was lucky with weather this time and was able to see hallasan from here! I cannot describe how amazing it was.  It is breathtaking and good to visit anytime of days. Many people came for sunset and sunrise. It is definitely one of my favorite places in Jeju. Be prepare for strong wind and amazing view. Recommend going during fall

It must have been quite pretty here back in the days. But now this small beach is surrounded by ugly buildings, that totally do not match to Jeju Island character. Seems like no urban planning in place and land owners try to outdo one another in search of bigger and better. Shame
It is volcano. It is not active. So there are many beautiful trees and aceneries. I think it is must go place in Jeju island, South Korea. Fee: 6,000KRW.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.

It is surely a must-go attraction in Jeju. With only KWN2000 (adults) to this nice park, it is reallt worth it. Too many steps in descending and ascending way, not a wheelchair or elderly friendly place

It is quite windy here. Lots of people visiting this beach. The beach are covered by a beautiful black stones all the way. The most memorable experience i have here is to taste the grill squid! It was so fresh and nice until i almost left by the bus just because i want to buy the squid again..haha..if i ever come to Jeju again, i'll definitely come here and looks for this nice squid.

It is one of the few villages that still exist on Jeju with complete retention of the traditional houses. The villagers still live in these houses but with modernized technology. They no longer uses the open air toilets, rearing black pigs and using electricity for lights, television and wifi. This is also the village that Dae Chang Guem were filmed in the early 2000s. Interesting to walk in the village as if we have travelled the time back in the past.

It is one of the best place in the world where you can watch sunrise. Even you have to wake up early, have a tiring stair climb and difficult to get clear whether even in summer ; if you ever go to Jeju island, here is one of a place where you must go. On the way Good scenery to enjoy also. In return don't miss the chance of fisherwomen's diving coast and have great breakfast with fresh seafood in the    haenyeo jib    .

It is one of many museums in Jeju, and it's dedicated to Teddy bears. It is full of its history with all the teddy bears from all over the world. All of the ancient teddy bears is well preserved but with relatively minimal background story. Some of the information are written only in Korean, so there isn't many interactive attraction here. There is also an open garden with a few sculptures on it, a Lotteria restaurant and of course the store. The merchandise there is quite expensive and we didn't buy anything. The entrance fee when we came there is 8000 won, a little bit expensive, but quite worth it.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. It is basically a Bonsai tree-themed Garden decorated with many waterfalls and beautiful ponds full of colorful koi carps. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

It is located just beside O'Sulloc Tea Museum. To get there, just take bus no.755 from any bus stop bound for Pyonghwa-ro global education and alight at O'Sulloc Tea Museum station.They sell cosmetics, skin care products, stationaries, D.I.Y soap, etc..There are also cafe which sells bingsu, beverages and food. Tried the 珥덉퐫荑좏궎?먯씠?? (choco cookie shake), it costs 6000 won and tastes good but I think the portion is a little small (for me). Nice to visit if you are visiting O'Sulloc Tea Museum since it is just beside it. There is a big tea farm beside Innisfree Jejuhouse.. you can take some pics there, but it was raining when i visited the place so i didn't manage to take a lot of pictures.

It is just like the cheap Chinese market in my hometown, with small stalls, no room to try things on and dirty floor. We were quite surprised when we got there, as the reviews of this place are rather good. Did not buy anything there. If you want some normal shopping in Jeju, go to any Emarket instead.

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

It is fun here if you and friends like Teddy Bear.  However, it is ironic to visit Teddy here instead of visiting more about the Island's history and cultural which is unique in the world.  My ideal touring package should not include anything has nothing to do with Jeju Island.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.

It is an old village that show us the homes for the people of Jeju in the past few hundred years. We have been guided through the village by a lady, who speaks very good Chinese's Mandarin. After the tour, they try to sell their products. Some of those are quite expensive. The thing that made us a little unhappy is   I think they have been trying too hard to make us buy something   so we end-up to select the cheapest product but then it became worst when the price was 10X different from what was being offered. It was already nicely packed and we did not want to make her unhappy so we just swipe the card.Anyway, it could be a communication error but both of us are Chinese and heard the same thing. It is a nice place but just be a little careful when you purchase those items.
It is an average beach, nothing special. The water wasn?t warm.  There is a lot of sand, not just rocks as in some areas of Jeju.

You can spend a couple of minutes with that ?Dragon? and spend another few minutes buying and enjoying the traditional outdoor cuisines. If you are interested in buying souvenirs like key chains or the ?Dragon? like badges, there is a shop for you to go shopping. It is an archetypal tuff cone formed by hydrovolcanic eruptions upon a shallow seabed about five thousand years ago.  Situated on the eastern seaboard of Jeju Island and resembles a gigantic ancient castle, this tuff cone is 182 meters high, has a preserved bowl-like crater. There are two hiking trails to reach the peak , take the white path uphill and the orange path downhill. You just follow the crowd and the signages along the trail. During May and the coming summer, you do not need a jacket or pullover as it will be  hot and you will sweat a lot on the climb up. Wear covered sports shoes and  a cap / hat. The first part of the hike is the easiest and the least steep.  The rest of the path comprises steps of varying steepness. The final stretch gets very steep. Along the hiking trail, there are benches and pavilions to rest. Take a sip of water, rest your aching legs before proceeding . Toilets are available along the way. From the peak, you can see beautiful landscapes of Jeju island and do take a photo with the signage saying you are at Sunrise Peak. It took us 30 minutes to reach the top. The downhill walk was much easier, just follow the wooden stairs meandering its way down.  At the bottom, you can go for drinks at the cafetarias.

It is amazing to see nature?s wonder , a must go in Jeju. Will not take much of your time as just 1km of the cave is open to public. Must go till the end of the tunnel to see nature?s wonder. Be careful while walking as the rocks formed after lava formation is uneven.

It is a very popular tourist hotspot, but is a short trek anywhere from 30mins to 1 hour trip to the peak. Offers a very nice view of the city as well as the sea. It is called Sunrise Peak for the very reason many climb this to watch sunrise. If time allow, try to plan for either sunrise or sundown for an excellent view from a high vantage point in Jeju. Every trip to Jeju, I try to make this spot one of my visit for at most 2-3hours. But beware of the tourist shop around here, they are all overpriced.
It is a UNESCO world herritage, recommended to see if you go to Jeju. We need to hike around 30-45 minutes to the top to get the full view.

It is a truly magnificent sight to see this natural phenomenon of this Unesco Heritage Site. It's a short climb up with well maintained steps and the view from the peak is superb. We didn't make it for the sunrise as we stayed in Jeju City which is 1.5 hours away by local bus. However, the sunset is stunning. I went in December so the wind can be very chilly in the evening. Definitely worth the climb!

It is a small island. we took the boat from Jeju. In a lobby full of Korean people, speak no English or Chinese. It is a museum as well as an ecological park related to stone culture in the lives of Jeju people.  It is huge and you are required to walk a lot.  It is about 40-45 minutes drive either from Jeju Airport or Seogwipo area.  You need 1-2 hours to go around the complex and the museum.  Opening hours: 0900-1800 hrs.  Closed on first Monday of the month unless it is a holiday.  Entry fee: KRW 5,000.  It should be a MUST in your itinerary of Jeju Island.

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

It is a good place to watch the whole seaside view and the horizon of the sea where the sky meets the sea. It is a dood place to walk, think, and stare.....  Many people  come with families & friends Children have a lot of pace to play. One can  have a lunch  at the restaurant. It is a  great beautiful park   within Jeju Si.

It is a definite must-see on Jeju Island. Although there is not much else to do beside sightseeing. That said the bridge excels at what it offers, which is the breathtaking scenery and beauty. Thumbs up from Vietnam !!!

It featured the women divers as the spirit of Jeju, displaying the culture and past of the people; clothes worn then, agricultural tools, even dishes and at one time, a wall with proverbs stemming from these women. It's a two floor museum only though, but holds alot of artifact

It costs 10.000 won to enter and without kids you are going to be done within half an hour but you'll have a big smile on your face. Teddybear Ghandi, Bear Elvis and more. Very funny. Island best explored by driving, ATV or bike rental. Ferry across from mainland Jeju also carries vehicles. Many small eateries on the island. Very scenic island with lots of photo opportunity. Be wary of last ferry back or you would be stuck there overnight

Interesting volcano hike up to the crater ledge. Good views out over the coastline, even tho we had a rainy, cloudy day so didn't get the best of it! Quite steep steps and climbing at times. Exposed to wind too. We saw some of the Jeju women divers from the top just about to launch themselves into the sea. Interesting place... Love to see how they really appreciate haenyeos, as one of their mother culture... A unique and honourable profession for jeju women in the old days and even now... How women are very appreciated since born and high hopes for doing the profession as backbone of the jeju families..The museum really tells a lot about how the haenyeos lives and even their struggle in the war era... Interesting guided tour of a traditional Jeju village, showing how people in Jeju used to live. Tour was conducted in mandarin, as we were a group from Singapore. Interesting highlights include the different meanings of the poles (at the front door), the outhouse (with a pig in it) and their honeyed drink (with some kind of berry in it).  They did bring us into a small room and introduced their products for sale - products include honey, the special honeyed drink as well as horse bone powder. Interesting background as to how the peak was formed. The hike to the top gives a gorgeous view of Jeju Island, and if lucky the peak of Hallasan. Lots of visitors but the place is quite big enough not to make it crowded.
Inspiring to learn about all the very hardworking Jeju women divers, who even went to fight the Japanese!

Innisfree Jeju House is just next to O'Sulloc Tea Museum, so is great to visit both the places. Innisfree Jeju House can be got to by taking a bus to the O'Sulloc tea museum stop. The tea museum is a very short walk away from Innisfree Jeju House.The place is quiet and peaceful, save for the calming music they play and the chatter of tourists and other visitors, but that wasn't too bad when I was there. There's an area devoted to DIY lessons/sessions where one can try making their own soap. There's a few pretty exhibits where one can smell various scents or read a little about the Innisfree brand and its products. There's a store area, with a few products that are exclusive to Innisfree Jeju House. And there's a cafe with various light food, drink and dessert options.Outside, there are tables and benches that overlook a nice view of the tea plantation, which you can go and take pictures in. It's really very pretty.I enjoyed my time there, but if Innisfree products are not for you, or if you're the thrill-seeking type, perhaps you should skip this place.

Innisfree is a well-known brand with numerous outlets throughout Korea and Asia. As it originated from Jeju, this is their main outlet in Korea. It was much smaller than expected, with only a single long building housing both the shop and cafe.The shop stocked quiet a good range of their toiletries and cosmetics, with an natural soap-making activity available. You can purchase a pack from the counter, choose the scent of soap you want, and there are stations with a screen to guide you through the soap-making process step-by-step. Shop staff are on hand for assistance as well. At the end of it, you can pack the soap into an eco-bag as a gift.The organic green cafe had ample seating and a good range of food, compared to the adjacent O Sulloc tea museum. Their drinks are served in funky bottles with interesting tastes, and make a pretty picture.If in the area, the soap-making is interesting and wouldn't take too long.

It was a cloudy June day which made the setting even more mysterious. Very simple but nicely kept grounds of rolling hills and volcanic rock walls. The crater itself was one of the more bizarre and intriguing natural landscapes I've seen. If you've seen the movie   The Mummy Returns,   it's like the end of that! The surrounding grounds are lovely and you have a great view of the mountains all around you. Would be a very romantic place as well, if you're with your partner. We went to two main places, one with a speedboat ride circling the island they claimed to look like a cow laying down and another by the beach of U-do. In my opinion, there are two world heritage sites that visitors to Jeju must visit. One is Manjanggul Cave and the other one is Seongsan Illchubong. Manjanggul Cave is unique as it was formed by lava movement thousands of years ago. It provides an insight into Jeju's geographical structure. The temperature in the cave could be chilly, so bring a jacket along. Visitors to the cave usually walked for about 2 km to reach the end, where photos with a large stalactite pillar could be taken. Other features in the cave include lava formations that look like elephant feet, turtles and book shelves.

I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

Ilchulbong is a must to visit when you came to Jeju island - South Korea. There is a beautiful panoramic, not only the caldera but also sorrounding area the volcano. From here you can see grass land and the sea. If you a lover natural panoramic, take a picture in the morning is great.

Ilchulbong is a huge rock/volcano/crater on the North East of Jeju Island. At first it seems a little daunting when you pull into the carpark as it looks really huge and steep. Yes, there are a lot of steps, but there are plenty of places to pause or sit for a rest and once you get to the top there's a great sitting/viewing platform. The views are really spectacular in all directions and you can see all over the mountain. It's really worth a visit if ou are going to Jeju.

Iho Taewoo Beach 댄명고대? is the closest beach to Jeju-si (city) and is closed to airport too, one can look down from the plane of the two very special red and white horse-shaped lighthouses when it almost reach Jeju Airport. Beach are sandy white and swallow water that are safe to swim. It is open for public and no admission charges except if is Jeju Iho Taewoo Festival.Visitors are welcomed to camp at the camping site. Facilities like charging room and shower room with locker are available too, is chargeable.There is two entrance to Iho Taewoo Beach, one is closer to the sandy beach and camping site located in the pine forest but less parking space. The other one is close to the horse-shaped lighthouses with huge free parking space and food trucks selling food and beverage. Here you can cycling and photographing. The two white and red horse-shaped lighthouse is famous for sunset photographing, it is best to be there around 5-6pm for the best sunset moment. Iho Taewoo Festival is around Jul-Aug every year. Local and tourist will be coming to witness the happening festival and event like boat ricing, fishing competition and many more fun activities. It will be a long day event.If you are driving, key in 728-3393.If you are taking public transport, take green bus 7,17 or 60 or blue bus 36

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the   foreigner price   rule is definitely in effect at this market.

If you've been to Northern Ireland, I'm sure you've been to or at least heard of the Giant's Causeway. Jusangjeolli Cliffs are exactly the same. They're very nice to look at and easy to find. Of all the things we saw on Jeju, this was probably the best. That being said, they're just rocks and cliffs overlooking the ocean.
If you're looking for unique souvenirs from Jeju, this is the right place for you! Nice and cozy shop with great ambience. Love this place :))))
If you're looking for a quieter Jeju beach, this one will do it. Off the beaten path slightly and near the beautiful Yongmeori coastline. If you're in the area, check it out!

If you're into nature, love moderate hiking and stairs climbing, love to see sea and city thru the bird eye view, taking plenty of photos of nature formations and also selfies (or wefies), then wjy don't you go to Seongsan Ilchubong, Jeju Island, South Korea. Designated as Unesco World Heritage site, this mountain is one the best place that you can hike and feels the wind blows your hair or maybe yourself too. The combination of flat lands and also the hike to the peak gives you an unforgetable memories. With each steps you take to climb to the peak, you will encounter several break spots or photo viewing for you to stops and take photos. Half way thru to the peak, you can see the entire city below you and starting to see the seas too. Hike to the peak, you can the see majestic view of the Seongsan Ilchubong itself. To your front is wide sea and the flat land (heard that it's actually a death volcano, correct me if i'm wrong) and to your behind is the view of the city and their surrounding. Don't forget to take photo at the peak's signboard. The formation of the clouds and the sun may give you the awe moments to you, especially when it reflects to the sea surfaces. When you go down from the peak, try to look at your right. You may see people going down to feels the sea water. Mind you, sometimes the wind blows a bit strong.  You need to pay for entrance and you don't like to hike to the peak, the ground is enough for you. Me and my friend, went there on Nov'15. Do try to enjoy nature at their best.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

If your time in Jeju is limited, skip all those man made museums and put visiting Udo island as one of your priorities. If you have an international driving license, highly recommend to rent a scooter to tour the island, and don't forget to try the Hallasan Fried Rice.

If you?re driving around Jeju Island, this place is a must. It took me a while to figure out what was the big deal (mysterious) about this road but after I figured out the way it was described to be, it was definitely cool and somewhat mysterious. So here it goes: you drive upto the starting point of mysterious road and put the car in neutral gear. The road certainly looks like and uphill, however the car drives forward until 100m to the end of the mysterious road. Anti-gravity huh? I?m not sure of the scientific explanation for this phenomenon, but I recommend you experience this if you?re driving around Jeju Island. Takes only 15 minutes and certainly worth the time and experience!

If you want to see a waterfall without the hassle of hiking a long way, go for this one. Just a little stairways descend from the entrance and voil - you'll be greeted by this pretty view of water flowing freely to the sea of Jeju.

if you want to go to his place, you must go on the morning to see the sunrise. Seongsan is quite far from Seogwipo, so after you explore Seogwipo city, you can go to the Seongsan for stay. And then you must wake up at 5 am, and go to seongsan ilchubong by taxi. it needs 5-10minutes. Better you ask to the hotel to call the taxi. You need 20-30minutes to go to the top. The view is amazing. Very recommended. For the hotel in this area i recommended jeju lux hotel. you can read my review also.

If you want something go, hungry go, street food go, you name they have it. Ate sushi for 3 days in a row at one of the restaurants in the market and never the same twice. Best place to try the famous Jeju pork.

If you visiting to Jeju island, it is mandatory to visit this place and enjoy the special recipes of porks from Jeju. It is so yummy and tasteful. However, it is not recommended for you that in diet program, otherwise your plan will destroyed.

If you visit Jeju, this volcanic mountain should be on your shortlist! It has excellent hiking trails which are well maintained. Trails are all well documented and give explanation about the distance, altitude and rest areas along the trail. At the top you have an amazing 360 degrees panorama view on the complete island. Plan your hike carefully. Check the weather before you leave. Bring along some warm clothing and rain protective clothing. Climbing 100 meters means a temperature drop of 1 degrees Celsius. It can get cold and humid up there!
If you visit Jeju island, you should go for a trail in Hallasan mountain. I did the Eorimok-Nambyeokbungijeom trail from Eorimok visitor center. Approx. 6 hours two ways hiking - 14 km.

If you really have a short time available at Jeju and that you want to have a glimpse of everything, Hallim Park may be your solution.  In there comprises of a tiny folk village, two lava tubes of smaller scale, water park, beautiful gardens for you to enjoy for a few hours.  One couldn't admire the courage of Mr Song who spent 40 years of his life developing Hallim Park from NOTHING.  He literally sweated & toiled through the barren rock into something magical that's been visited by dignitaries around the world.  For someone like myself who came from New Zealand, natural green is something that I have taken for granted but one would have to give Mr Sung encore for the grand vision that he did, to build a tourist attraction for Jeju when tourism wasn't a happening thing just yet.  Just like from the movie, Field of Dreams, if you build it, people will most definitely come!

If you plan to go to Udo, spend at least a day here. Enjoy every part of Udo : Udo Olle Trail, Udo lighthouse, Beach. Trying the popular Halasan Fried Rice and peanut ice cream, so yummy. Really enjoy my time in Udo, fresh air, clear blue water, white sand, warm local people, beautiful scenery. This is what I picture Jeju in my mind. Everything in Udo are beautiful for me. I will regret if I didn't come here, this is my favourite part in Jeju.

If you only see one waterfall in Jeju, I would see this one. It is beautiful how it goes into the see. We visited it during a taxi tour along with Cheonjiyeon Falls. They are very close to each other so there is no need to see just one but if you are short on time I would go to Jeongbang. For 2000 won each it is a bargin. Bring shoes you don't mind getting wet and can climb over rocks in, if you want to get close to the waterfall.
If you only have one day in Jeju, come to Hallim Park because they have everything in one place! Caves, butterfly garden, flower garden, birds area, mimic folk village and so on.
If you never get the chance to come to Jeju and experience the road for yourself, at least You Tube it! This was completely crazy to see. Everything in the videos is real in case you were wondering!

If you need a good work out, this forest in Jeju is worth paying a visit. The autumn 10C air is perfect, although the leaves were only starting to blend with the sun, you can imagine the shades of red, orange and yellow if it's at its peak!  The old nutmeg trees provided good photo opportunities for those with a passion for nature.

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.

If you love the sea, sand, mountain and great scenery, you will need to make a day trip to Udo!  You can take a ferry to Udo from Seongsan Harbour.  I highly recommend that you rent a car in Jeju and drive that over to Udo as there are so much to see and do in a single day.  You can drive your car up onto the ferry to Udo.

If you love nature, then you absolutely must visit this place. According to the booklet I took, there's an outdoor and an indoor garden. The latter one has 5 different sections: a flower garden, an aquatic garden, a cactus garden, a jungle garden and a tropical fruits? garden as well as an observatory on the 5th floor.The outdoor garden contains TEN different gardens including the herb garden and a french garden. It would take about 2.5 hours to see everything it offers.TRANSPORTATION:-from Jeju: take the Airport Limusine Shuttle (approx 50 mins)-from Seogwipo: take a public bus (approx 20 mins)

If you love Alice in Wonderland you will love Maze Land.  The mazes are fun to explore and make you feel like a kid again. Also, the statue garden and rose garden are worth a look.  A really fun, unique way to spend a day on Jeju.

If you live on Jeju you have to do it at least once. I'm from the West where the mountains are huge so, when I saw Hallasan it looked like a piece of cake. How wrong I was. Mountain trails in the West take you up by switchbacks but the tail up Hallasan goes straight up  and straight down. There are no switchbacks. Only about a million steps to climb. I'm not saying that there is anything wrong with that......just be prepared. Start early and take water.When I went up I thought I was going to die. It didn't help that there was this grandpa in flip-flops who passed me on the way up and then he passed me again as I was still on my way up and he was coming down and then he passed me again going up as I was still on my way up. How embarrassing was that?????? Very embarrassing!As far as the climb went, it was great. I felt like two cent going up but once on top I felt like a million bucks. Clean air and blue sky. Views of the whole island.One good thing about going down is that it's all down hill. I do a lot of complaining about it but I've been up there five times now so  there must be something I love about it.If you do go up and you see that grandpa tell him hi from me. He passed me so many times I feel like I know him. ;)

If you like small tasteless theme parks you will love this: mirror mazes, glass lilies in ponds, large mosaic teddy bear and a chance to make your own stuff too. The 9,000 won entry fee includes the fee to make something - and that price is VERY expensive for Jeju. It is also mostly outside so do not bother in bad weather. In fact, I would not bother at all.

If you like cats then this place is for you. There are about 20 cats roaming around the property. I am not a cat person at all but the cats did not bother me. They are friendly and stay out of the way of people. The maze was fun and somewhat challenging. I liked that they added a stamp feature (you had to find stamps on your journey) so it wasn't all about getting out. They are pretty chill here, so you could do the maze 1 million times if you wanted. If the parking lot is overflowing then I would recommend that you not go. The property isn't big enough for that many people. The positive is that there is a cave down the street you can visit as well. We didn't get to visit the cave because it was a public holiday. I would recommend that you go here, especially if you have kids. The value is not that high but most things on Jeju cost money. It is not a rip off.
If you have time to visit while you are in Jeju City, Yongdu-am offers a nice walk and photo op. Yong pond is also within walking distance and had some very picturesque views.

If you have the opportunity to visit Jeju, please go to Udo Island.Even it is tiny little Island it has quite many things to explore.I learn to ride a horse, try the gu jeng ki (a green shel seafood) and met the hanyeo. The cliff view there also magnificent. I love the peanut dumplings.

If you have seen any of the large dramatic water falls around the world then you will be disappointed by this tiny cascade. Barely 60/70 ft tall and about 20/25 ft wide. A small stream tumbles directly into the ocean. The tourist brochures make this more dramatic than what it actually is. Have uploaded pictures of the falls from the top (from the platform adjacent to the ticketing office and entry barriers) and from the bridge over the stream just before it tumbles down. Would give you some idea of the size.But having said all of that, this a pleasant enough area. Pay Won 2000 for entry (entry hours 8am - 6pm/7pm, depending on summer/winter) and leisurely climb down about 60 odd feet i.e. equivalent of climbing down about 6 stories. You will arrive at a rocky area. Clambering over about 1/5th mile (300 odd mts) of large rocks to where the water falls, isn't for the aged like me! But it would be nice to get to the water's edge if you can.Not a bad idea to carry sandwiches and beer and sit on the rocks, moments of peace and quiet, isolated from bustling Segwipo all around.You wouldn't miss anything if you haven't been here. But it would be a shame to miss it if you are on Jeju.

If you have limited time, I would highly recommend this garden over the Yeomiji Botanic Garden.  There is so much to see and with the very helpful signs, there was no anxiety about getting lost.  The garden is designed for 1-way traffic so once you enter into one of the many feature spaces, you can't decide to opt out but have to continue until the exit point.  We did not know just how vast the garden was and wished we had allocated more time.  The bonsai and stone garden was really outstanding.When leaving the garden, do consider taking a scenic drive along the west side of Jeju Island and head towards Jungmun.  This stretch of coast was truly out of this world beautiful.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

If you have a lot of things you want to do in Jeju and are driving to do them, this is just kind of unnecessary. I actually had a hard time getting what I was supposed to do and once I did it I was like, meh, that was kind of a waste of time. Just keep driving to your next location.

If you go to Jeju Island, this is a good place to go. There is a Kitty Cafe inside, it is the same as those in Seoul. Apart from the Cafe, there is also an souvenir shop, you can buy those limited edition products there. If you drive there, you may need to wait for the parking space during peak hours.

If you find yourself in Jeju (May to June preferably) Halla is something that must be done. As the island is so small you can see the mountain no matter where you are. It sits there calling to you to climb it and you should. It is not one the most difficult climbs I have ever had, the end was a bit bad because there had be a storm that had damaged parts of the path. It is absolutely picturesque especially for the colour changes you see. I would suggest going up the easy path and going down the easy path for those who have trouble managing such large mountains, but no matter which you choose just go. The canteen at the halfway point was only serving instant noodles, so bring your own grub to be safe. Also have your pickup scheduled accordingly as transportation on the bottom parts of certain paths are almost non-existant.

If you enjoy nature, hiking one of the olle trails is a must-do while you're in jeju. It will not be an easy hike and not all parts of the trail are scenic but there are sufficient sights to blow you away and be left in awe of nature. This is also the best way to experience jeju's natural beauty (after all this is what its most famous for and not for teddy bears). It is also arguably the least touristy thing to do during your trip here. You can do as long or as short of the trails as you like; there are trails passing through hot tourist destinations where you'll see many tourist buses, local villages, rice fields, even resorts. You'll walk on sand, on rocks by the ocean, and if you time it correctly you'll be able to catch a gorgeous sunset along jeju's coastline. Be sure not to get stuck in a remote area after sunset as it can be difficult to get out. If you're doing a multi-day hike, there are many pensions located along the olle routes and you can just pop in for a night.Suggest to go with at least one other person in case you get lost (there are some places where the markings are not so visible/well maintained). If you rented a car, dont drive. Wear comfortable shoes and bring lots of water and snacks!

If you come to Jeju island, Hala mountain tracking is No. 1 recommendation for you if you are health and have strong two legs. My recomendation is Yong-Sil course and it will take about 5 hours round tracking. It is totally different scene when you up to the mountain and never forget this memory.

If you are women or man, either case you will be surprised and proud, to see the courage and dedication of Jeju women divers. This museum is dedicates to history of women divers and their success and spread worldwide.  Overall museum is average compared to other museum, but what it makes stand out is unique concept everything is build on. It is worth a trip to be fascinated by rare profession by women.

If you are visiting Jeju Island, this is a place that you cannot miss.It was rather crowded when we were there on weekday late morning.  According to our driver, it can get even more crowded in the afternoon.The hike can be done at your own pace, I expected the tuff cone / crater itself at the top to be more spectacular (like those tourism photos and pictures).  However, it turned out just okay.  Nevertheless, the hike up to the top was very enjoyable and views from the top was very nice.  If you like nature, this place is worth a visit.

If you are traveling to the south side of Jeju island, you must come see this cliff surrounded by emerald waters and roaring waves.Truly awesome. You will be even more surprised when you get home by the amazing photos you took. Don't focus on people shots, get the amazing rocks and waves instead! Don't worry about the apparent crowds around you, you will definitely be able to take some fantastic pictures without them.

If you are traveling alone, not planning to ride a bicycle or rent a car on the island, you can buy a local tour bus ticket. The price varies as they are several bus company. The local tour bus stops at several highlights of the island. The bus driver will introduce and talk about the island (in Korean). The scenery is excellent, a must-visit-place in Jeju. You need to spare at least 4 hours for U-do Island.
If you are out of plan and around jeju city, yongduam rock can be good alternative. There's also a beautiful bridge close to this place.

If you are only able to see one waterfall on Jeju, make sure it's this one!  The waterfall empties right into the ocean so it makes the setting pretty unique and amazing.  The trail down is pretty steep.  Wear shoes, as the base of the waterfall is a rock field and can be slippery and uneven.

If you are looking for a remote island off the coast of Jeju then this might not be for you. However, if you are after an island that is a short ferry ride away and has many activities to offer then this is it! Udo is beautiful, and attracts many tourists especially in the summer time. You can rent a bicycle for the day at about 10,000-12,000W, or rent an electronic bike/scooter thing (with an international drivers license). Caves, mountains, as well as many beaches to explore. Stay the weekend on Udo or ride the ferry back to Seongsan, you'll have a great time :).

If you are interested in the history and culture of Jeju island, and of Korea, then I would recommend spending an hour or two at this park. If you aren't, or are expecting something more exciting, skip it. For me, who lives in Korea and is already familiar with much of Korean history, I wish I had gone elsewhere. True to previous reviews, it was beautiful, but so is most of Jeju, and there are many other places more beautiful than the park itself. Overall: if you don't care about the history behind the park, it's 2 hours of looking at rocks.

If you are in Jeju-do, Black Pork Street (Heuk Dwaeji) is a must visit place. As the street name given, yup.. Selling point is Black Pork. Go in to one of the many restaurants on street and try the grilled black pork meat, it is the signature dish in Jeju Island. If you try this is Seoul, it will cost you double or maybe triple the bill. Most menu are in Hangul but there will be a simple English too, the best way is to choose the set menu. Price are reasonable if you choose the restaurant that is less fancy and not those tourist welcoming type. We had the best BBQ dinner in Korea.
If you are in jeju island of course you have to go there. A great ride, with some mysterious road,..may be some ghost... Up there get a jacket it s could be cold....

If you are going with little kids, definitely go. But otherwise it's just OK though I would say worth a visit if you are bored. Pretty much all the information is in Korean, but then again doesn't take much to identify the teddy bear version of Steve Jobs or Albert Einstein ;) The place has two floors of teddy bears, and I must say after about 25 teddies they all start looking the same. This was close to our hotel and it was raining so we paid a visit. I would advise the museum to put more info in English as Jeju is becoming more internationlised in terms of tourists.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I?m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn?t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it?s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn?t come here.If you?re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It?s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough ? if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it?s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it?s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.

if you are a nature lover like me, you should not miss this while you are in Jeju. Be ready to walk for 1 km and get prepared to experience some cold with dark which gives you an awesome feeling to enjoy the cave more.
If you are a hello kitty fans, this is a must-visit-place in jeju, accessible by public transport, is along a main road. You get to experience colouring, 3D short movie clips.

If we had known that the rock formation was disappointing, we wouldn't have taken the effort to get lost on our way there! We went there at night, and all we saw were a few spotlights shining upon a small piece of rock jutting out of the land mass - there are other wayyyy better ways to spend your limited time in Jeju. Seriously! Don't bother please.

If u like striking out poses with friends using the lifesize teddy bears in different costumes and characters, this is the place for u. There's also an outdoor gardens with bear exhibits, fountain and lake and a blooming grapefruit tree. Looks really good and I think it would be a nice feeling sitting around in the outdoor garden having ur lunch. That's provided it does rain. Get your tickets cheaper via taobao, the China online shopping site. They have almost 50% discount for foreigners, which we tapped on. Just need to print our confirmation and entry was a breeze. Also, this place is accessible via a bus from Jeju intercity bus terminal. Stop at jungmun resort. Nearby are alive musuem, yeomiji botanical gardens and cheonjiyeon waterfalls, good for a self planned one day trip.

If there is only one thing I can do during my travel in Jeju, it would be hiking at the Hallasan National Park. There were just 2 trails (Seongpanak & Gwaneumsa, where Seongpanak was easier) which can reach the top of the mountain, where you can see the Baengnokdam. You can even get a certificate (which costs only KRW1000) of climbing the Hallasan if you show the staff at the tourist centre your picture with Baengnokdam.

If it’s springtime?or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju. ? Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.? Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.? Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km? to about 250 residents.? The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.? There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.? But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.? You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.? Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?? Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.? The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.? Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.? Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:? Good points:? outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;? site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival? (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:? bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;? sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.? There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.? Getting there:? Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .? There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.? Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

If doing Hallasan is not in your plans, then go take some nice walks on Jeju's Olle Trail Routes. They are shorter mostly and they appear all over the place in Jeju. Sometimes just 20 minutes walks and some much longer. We were impressed with the conservancy of nature and the trails on Jeju.

I'd highly recommend visiting 9.81 Park on your next trip to Jeju. This place is a lot of fun. The karts are in excellent condition, the course offers some amazing sea views and the staff are very professional and helpful. Definitely worth a visit.

I’ve visited Jeju in mid-April with my friend and we’ve gotten John to bring us around in Jeju. It was a great experience, John was punctual and well-articulated(telling us fun facts/history) along the tour.
