Also, he took initiatives to show us more spots throughout the tour for “instagram worthy” photos! We will definitely get John as our tour guide if we come back to Jeju again!

I?ve visited this place with my GF. Definitely a date spot! Although some families also go with kids, from my point of view, not a family thing... but I might me wrong!It?s cold! Very cold! Wet and definitely slippery! Be prepared! But definitely amazing! 1km walk in and 1 km return walk out cane be done in quite 30 mins or so.Perfect if you go only once in your life! A must do if you are in Jeju. I guess...

I?m not a big fan of Kpop, but I do enjoy their music...and this Play Kpop Museum did impress me with their hologram concert by GDragon, photo session in holographic & can be downloaded into phone for free!!!!Definitely must go place in Jeju for Kpop fans!

i wouldnt have rate poor until i went to   Teseum  . things in teddy bear museum all mini sizes in a box well protected. they have 3 floors, and only the ground floor have some bears for picture. For me kind of bored compare to Teseum, Teseum you can touch and picture closely with those teddys. Jeju has 2 or 3 teddy bear museum, i been to 2 one is teddy bear museum & another is Tesuem. more recommended to Teseum instead of this.   links: http://english.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=701764http://www.tripadvisor.com.my/Attraction_Review-g297885-d3805571-Reviews-Teseum_Jeju-Jeju_Jeju_do.html

I would recommend that you read the book ?The Island of Sea Women? by Lisa See before visiting the museum. I felt an emotional connection to the museum, the observatory and the grounds around the area, primarily because I had some background knowledge. The museum is well laid out and interesting. Do take the time to watch the video on the main floor before going through the exhibits. If you are there around 10:00 a.m. or 1:00 p.m. you may be able to see the women divers from the observatory on the 3rd floor.  Getting there: we were on a cruise ship and took a taxi from the ship terminal in Jeju City. It took about an hour and was a very scenic drive.  Our taxi driver gave us an hour to tour the museum and grounds and then dropped us off by the main market area in downtown Jeju City. It was under $100 for four people in a taxi.

i won't repeat what others have mentioned.personally i love this place.i went during spring in april 2017,weather was perfect.food was presented beautifully,the latte i had was delicious.the garnishing is really insta-worthy!my friends and i had breakfast at the outdoor area,overlooking the tea plantation.some of the skincare product sold was exclusive to this outlet,glad i bought a few.would surely return if i happen to visit jeju again.

I went with three friends to Geomunoreum on a Sunday in February 2016. The first thing I'd recommend is ensuring that your taxi driver takes you to the right place as ours dropped us off an hour's walk away from where we were supposed to be at an abandoned building.When we finally got to the Oreum we got in for free as Jeju English teachers. I think the prices were around 5KWon per person without Jeju residency.We had to join a tour group (obviously Korean-speaking guide) for the whole walk. The stops were far too regular and spoke for too long. This is why the route options are 1 hour/2.5hours/3.5hours (I think), because the guiding makes them so long! I guess it was our fault for not being able to understand, but it did mean the walk was interrupted and the experience ruined a little by travelling in a pack. We tried to pace ourselves between groups but kept getting trapped in them. I don't think you can do this walk without a guide.That said, the views were beautiful.

I went with my boyfriend and his dad. We had our cab driver take us there at 6am from our hostel. It took us about 12hrs round trip. I'm not a experienced hiker, so it took a loooonnnngggg time because of me. View is EXCELLENT from the peak. You can see the entire Jeju-do. Hallasan is a stony mountain, so if you can, bring a pair of hiking sticks to help you, and wear hiking shoes. The rocks are pointy, and not all of them are easy to step on.

I went to this peak three times during my stay for a year on Jeju island! First time was in August when it was sweltering hot, so I never climbed it just took pictures from the bottom. The second time I went was in September when it was cooler and I climbed it and it only took the recommended time of 30 minutes. Such a beautiful view and the sign saying you reached the top is very nice. My last time climbing it was in December for the sunrise and my mom and I made it to the top just before sunrise but it was an overcast day so we only saw a tiny bit of pink under the clouds but still it was a nice view of Jeju from that height! Definitely recommend doing this while you are in Jeju :)

I went to there to have late breakfast and shopping. They mainly sell local produce of Jeju which is tangerine. It is selling almost everything with tangerine. Other than that, can go there for local food like blood sausage, dteokboki and all..Outside of the market area, there is other shopping place as well.

I went to Seongsan Ilchulbong (SunRise Peak) during Mar this year 2015. The weather is cold but bearable around Jeju. However, to climb this mountain is not a great feat for my mum (age 65) but the chilling wind is the one we are defeated.We wanted to visit this peak for sunrise but somehow we are late and lost on our way there. We went to Jongbong Beach and along the coast line it is also very nice to see. We did not catch the sun rise as there are none (due to foggy weather). As we are ascending, the crowd was descending and show enthusiasm although they did not get any view of the sun rise. The climb was nice as there are even wooden/stone steps to the top. Once you reached the top, you will see the beautiful crater which happens million years ago. The view over the edge is equally stunning. Definitely a recommended place to visit when you are in Jeju-Si. The ticket cost 2000KRW each.When you descend, you may see the   Sea-Woman   whom they called Haenyeo will perform at 1.30PM and 3PM only. We did not wait for the show as there are many Sea-Woman around the whole Jeju Island.

I went to see lighthouse in shape of horse, one is in red and the other is in white. They are well made, attractive and iconic!I too a bus heading towards West, (bus#444, it has a stop at Jeju intercity bus terminal), you would need to walk to the lighthouses or you can get off at the stop of beach.The coast line is nice, airplanes are frequently flying over the sky as it?s so close to the airport!

i went to Jeju Olle Trail number 7. it was really awesome. i was travel alone and this place really good for refreshing your mind, relaxing, just enjoy the sound of the wave and the wind. trekking without feeling exhausted. and this place are one of shooting location for Jewel On the Palace :)!!!! must visited

I went to jeju island to see some view like this and i can say this Park was beautiful one . I suggest everybody to visit jeju island in fall season because u can see colours and feel great weather . Park is actually for hiking but if u don't wanna go till top u can enjoy forest before getting top , take some snacks and drink with ureself because there is not many mart nearby just one small and limit one down of park .

I went there with my family members in a cloudy day. This place is composed with several parts of themes. Lake, play ground, short hiking with spa, and snack bars.My kids(9, 5yrs) really enjoyed the place with running, taking pictures, and eating.Even I visited in Jeju more than 10 times, this place is the most memorable place to visit. Because kids didn?t have any bother others.Additionally, there were packed with people and very noise when I waited for tour train. Then please be sure to keep you eyes on your kids. I visited there at the last of tour then I couldn't have enough time to hiking.However, I recommend you to take a walk at the picnic garden station (2nd stop).There are kids town and eco-land at Picnic garden station

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I went on a tour group to Jeju. The bus arrived at the Mysterious Road, all of us were waiting eagerly in anticipation of what's about to come (after hearing so much hype about it). Looking out the window, I saw a little kid on the street place a plastic bottle on the tarmac, and it looked like it was rolling up hill at first, but because of the way the bus was angled along the road, I was quick to discern that it was a mere optical illusion.As our bus reached the front of the 'queue', our driver switched off the engine, and slowly, but surely, our bus picked up speed. It was interesting as it was the first time I sat in a vehicle with it's engine switched off, THAT WAS IT. I looked out the front panel, and we were obviously going downhill, as I could not even see the sky (just trees whizzing by our bus).I'm guessing it only looks like you're going uphill from certain angles. Thankfully, we didn't spend too much time there, and off we went to our next destination!

I went alone in this tour, and my driver was sooo nice! He helped me take pictures, gave me awesome tips and guidance about the places we went, and he even suggested some extra stops for me because I was new to Jeju~ It was so enjoyable, and my experience was excellent because my driver went the extra mile to make sure I was comfortable and well informed~

I was very excited to visit Jeju; and this probably one of the most accessible place by Bus. There's actually public transport to this place (Yongduam Rock) from my accommodation. However, when I reached this place , i was busy looking for this legendary dragon head rock. Much to my disappointment, the rock doesn't seem to look like dragon head, you must really view it from the other side with your imagination.However, in order to reach to the other side, you need to climb all the way down the stairs, Not recommended for elderly. And if you notice carefully, you will spot alot of cockroach crawling around the rock, that totally freak me out!! Very big turn off if you spot the cockroach.the period I went was very crowded, probably around 5-6pm, This timing was quite a good timing for me, as I manage to catch a sunset. The sunset there was relatively awesome with the endless view of sea. If you can walk all the way down to those seafood stores, whereby you can enjoy fresh seafood hot pot + splendid view of sunset & sea!

I was underwhelmed by this place (and the island in general) but then I live in Thailand and am used to great beaches. There is nothing special here, I certainly saw no   white sand   and   turquoise water.   Just a very average beach and an overpowering smell of the seaweed they harvest here. I would skip this - and Jeju altogether frankly.

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I was thinking about Seongsan Ilchulbong, dreaming about it, visualizing  the moments & details of  the day, and just rushed to the legendary place sponteneously. Moved from Jeju Bus Terminal totally on my own. An hour & a half  and you are there! Enjoy:-)

i was spending 4 days on jeju island and i went Ecoland in the 2nd day morning. the entry fee is WON12,000 per head. parking is free. You will like here if you like tree and nature environment. the weather was nice when i visited . therefore, i took some beautiful pictures. and i also had a quick lunch here.

I was sold! Though it was more like a replica of a village from many, many years ago, it felt like I walked back through time to an age where everything was bathed in tranquilityI got a glimpse of houses and possible lifestyle in ancient JejuIt gave me the impression of how rough life was back then but peaceful as it appearedThough visitors may have mixed opinions about this place, to me, it works

I was really impressed by this museum, designed by the famous Japanese architet Tadao Ando. The architecture of the building and the beautiful garden make this place worth a visit, but the collection is also really interesting. I really loved the collection artefacts from the late Joseon period an the special exhibition 'Carriage to Heaven' that shows sangyeo (traditional funeral bier) and kkokdu (small statues used as decoration for the sangjyeo). The joyous artwork of Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama were a nice extra on top of all that.Not to be missed when visiting Jeju.

I was quite disapoonted when we visited the island. It's pretty and the beaches are nice. But if you've been around Jeju island for some time, there's not much here that you can't find in the main island. You can skip this if you need to cut your itinerary.

i was quite amazed to this natural wonder and i had not seen any falls which ends directly to the sea. its very close the segwipo city. You need to walk down around 100 step to reach the bottom of the falls. Careful near the bottom the stones r slippery and if its raining better be watchful for the waves. Its a delight to watch the gorge. We went to this place when it had rained a bit so the water fall was in full flow. Due to heavy wind and cyclone in china the sea was rough which added to the fun!!! one of the most memorable place i visited in jeju,highly recommend it.

I was on my way to another destination when I saw this place. I caught the 700 bus that runs around the outside of Jeju island for a cost of around $2, and wondered why so many people were getting on and off at this stop, so on my way back I got off. It ended up being my highlight of the day.It was a lovely sunny day with a few hundred people climbing up, and with ramps and steps all the way it was easy. I got to the top in about half an hour if not less. The views from the top were probably the best I experienced for my whole trip in Jeju, and that includes the view I saw from top of Mt Hallasan.At only 2000 won entry, it's a must-do when visitng Jeju, and there's lots of restaurants at the bottom.

I was on exchange with a couple of friends in Busan, Korea. We decided to head to Jeju for some exploration trip. The teddy bear museum is an awesome place to visit if you are a teddy bear fan! They have different themes of teddy bear at different areas! :)

I was looking forward to this attraction more than any other on Jeju and it didn't disappoint.  I wouldn't rate as #1 (more   touristy   than expected) but worth the stop.  If you can move past the gift stores selling trinkets, cheezy signage, animals in tiny cages and crowds, the attractions within the park are quite beautiful.  I especially liked the lava caves and the bonsai garden.  Those two areas alone were worth the stop.  If you have time, just past the park entrance is a stunning beach area.  Great for photos and possibly a toe dipped into the waters.

I was here with my family. Thinking what is so mysterious about this road? Its just a road, with nature on the sides. It?s just another ?normal? road. Sigh, a total waste of time.Until I reach the place, I was blown away! Not because of the strong wind (I was there when it was raining heavily with strong winds), but the mysterious part of this road. I was told to stay in the car, to witness the mystery of this road. The engine got turned off, hand brake was let gone, brakes were let gone too, the car automatically went up the slope by itself!It is a new experience here for me in Jeju, a totally worth of time to visit!

I was clearly the wrong age, the wrong gender, and the wrong nationality to visit this place. Despite that, I enjoyed it somewhat.  Even though I had never heard of any of these artists, aside from Psy, it was fun to see some of the exhibits.  The hologram concert was pretty well done.If I had a Korean teenage daughter who loved to take selfies with celebrities, it would have been the highlight of her trip to Jeju.

I wanted to do this at sunrise but never woke up. So I went around 11h. Lots of tourists. It's all stairs to the top but not that hard. Takes 20 min in all. Beautiful view and scenery on top. There are some souvenirs and food shops at the bottom (Dunkin Donuts, Starbucks and cie).There is also a souvenir shop at half the moutain with beautiful engraved wood done by a woman there. I bought my most beautiful souvenir to her. She engraved Jeju, the date on it and wrapped it good for me. It's a short must do thing! You will get great pics there.

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

I visited this place on October 23 2020 on my trip to Jeju Island. It was marbelous! So beautiful everywhere! Spirited Garden in Jeju is a beautiful place to relax, walk through and contemplate. It also has a healing buffet with healthy, tasty and pleasant meals for visitors. Contemplating the garden, I got inspiration and relax feeling. In the papers they say that the Spirited Garden is a symbol of Korean spirit: pioneer spirit and progressiveness, perseverance, and ceaseless endeavor.

I visited the crater approximately 1 year ago on 29 Dec 2017 during winter. It was very sunny, a good weather, and really windy as well. Really. Couldn't see the crater though as it is really foggy and misty, that was a disappointment. But the scenery was great and it is really scenic with lots of great photo spots. It also isn't really crowded, there are many people, but not crowded. I would go again if i go to Jeju again, hopefully woth a clear weather where i can see the crater like in the brochure.

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

I visited Jeju Glass Castle last winter. I went there twice while I stayed in Jeju for a week. The first time I visited, the weather was good and so my family walked around the museum with joy. We were very glad to be there. The second time, I was very thrilled to visit again, but unluckily, it was raining. Our family struggled to see the sculptures that were placed outside. I recommend that you go to Jeju Glass Castle when the weather is good.

I visited here with several work colleagues.  We had a great time and laughed so much trying to make our way through this maze.  Built by a westerner and former professor over a number of years, the time, planning and care that went into making the park are all quite easy to see and appreciate.  It is beautiful there, very green and clean, and close to Manjang Caves, another iconic Jeju attraction.  Negotiating the maze took us about 45 minutes...longer than we thought...but we laughed our way through it.  Once you make it to the center, you can climb up to a platform and ring the   finder's bell.    Great for photo ops.  They also have some traditional Korean games just outside the end of the maze...fun to play if you never have.  At the snack bars, they offer delicious Jeju-brand ice-cream.  And as a BIG added bonus for my fellow cat-lovers, LOTS AND LOTS of mascot cats, belonging to the mazepark builder.  He is now a retired gentleman, known for his affinity for cats; journalists and business persons who go to meet with him in his office are likely to find both his desk and his person draped with one or more of his uniquely colored cats...black, orange, brown, white and grey.  A GREAT activity for families (although very young children may tire unless you take them in a stroller); couples; and colleagues...good team-building exercise:  Who can lead us OUT of here?  LOL  You'll enjoy it.

I visited Dianosaur land in Jan.  with my son 4 years old. When we visited Jeju island the sky was cloudy and finally heavy snowing. However that was a great moment with dinosaurs under snowing. It seemed like we're cruising among dinosaurs at the Jurassic period. If you visit there with young boys especially we never regret you choice.With my son and wife we had gotten a wonderful time in Jeju island including Dinosaur Land.  And also I strongly recommand that  'Seopjicozy' ???肄붿? which was the shooting place of the drama   All In   and there was a lot of scenery of the sea and others around it.I think Seopjicozy is wonderful place with picnic with children.

I visited 4 different beaches in Jeju. They all had their own charms but for popularity goes to Hyeopjae Beach becaue of good size and fantastic photogenic view. If you want calmer, smaller, less crowded and less windy beach, there is Kumnyoung beach right next to Hyeopjae beach. It is good for younger children to play. Hyeopjae beach was quite windy and cold. Of course Summer time would be different story. I was looking forward to riding transparent kayak but it was not operating in Apr. There was number on banner but no one answered.

I visit the place with the tour I bought in Jeju city. The place is higher than expectation. There are several parts of the park including the real underground lava tube which is amazing. The folk village also decorated really nice. When I visit the place, it is about 5 degree c so theres not many flowers in that time. Theres also a small zoo inside as well!

I visit Jeju at December 2015 and stayed near this museum. I have no plan to visit this museum, but from the outside looks interesting. I just made a couple of photos in the front. After that I intend to buy some souvenirs, but in fact visitors should buy ticket and enter the museum first. There is no souvenir shop available outside the ticketing gate

I used to love watching Ripley's believe it or not when i was a kid, l love the history behind the strange things that are happening around us, and the show gave us a bit of it. So, finding that in Jeju brings back that curiosity of the kid in me. This place is perfect for those who are into weird and quirky historical stuff. Great for passing the time. It was even better than other theme parks i've been to =) Objective opinion though. ^^

I tried 3 different dishes of black jeju pork and could not tell any difference at all between this and any pig raised healthy. If you go to any small farmer to raises pigs the pork will taste better than ones you buy raised in factories, but this tastes no better than that. At double the price of normal pork bbq, you can skip this.

I traveled in early December and sea side wasn't a priority, and then I found this park. The monuments you are going to see at all kinds of markets of Jeju all come from this park. If you want to have some quiet time wandering in forest and looking at these cute monuments - stone park is a must do!

I took bus 281 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal at 6.24am and get off at Seongpanak stop. Start hiking at 7.30am. It took me about 4 hours to reach the top. It was hot at top. I brought 1 liter of water and some buns and it was okay for me.I walked down the Gwaneumsa Trail. It took another 4 hours. If you want to go back to Jeju Intercity bus terminal take bus 475 from Gwaneumsa to Shancheondan Altar and switch to bus 281 to the Jeju Intercity bus Terminal.Every bus fare is 1,200 won.

I took 281 busfrom Jeju Intercity Terminal at 6.24 am cost 1200 won. Get off at Seongpanak stop, approx 50 minutes. It took me about 4 hours to the top.As I did hiking on Jun, it was hot at the top. Take photo at the top as a evidence that you reached at the top so that you could get a certificate for 1000 won.I brought 1 liter of bottle water and four buns. It was okay for me.Running shoes is okay.I walked down the Gwaneumsa trail.You have to step on different size of rocks.I finished my hiking at about 4pm.If you want to go back to Jeju Intercity terminal, take 475 bus from Gwaneumsa to Sancheondan Altar 1,200 won and switch to bus 281 to Jeju Intercity Terminal.

I thoroughly enjoyed myself. It was so entertaining and fun to watch. Definitely worth going to see!! Ours was the blue team. I booked and paid direct from their website. It was very simple. Just sign up for a membership, pick the theatre, the date, time and the type of discount. Please read-up on their terms and conditions for each discount. Payment was done via credit card. I managed to get my VIP tickets for 45000KRW each and sat at D17, 18. The seats were just nice, not too far and not too close. Although maybe E would've been a better bet. Different locations have different discounts and it varies according to the different months, so just check out their website.Jeju NANTA theatre is a bit run down and the toilet wasn't very well-kept... Also, be prepared to be surrounded by bus loads of tourists from China (as with most tourist spots in Jeju.... )

I think this will be a fun experience for the family especially with small kids. I am not young anymore but it was rather interesting and fun for me as well. Not as easy as I thought and it took me 30mins to navigate through...for price of 3300won, it is a pretty economical way to spend a few light hearted hours after all the serious geographical sights in Jeju.
i think this place is over rated, other than the volcanic rocks formation, you can see planes landing to jeju airport. the view is nice though.

I think this is a must go location in Jeju. There are so many breathtaking views everywhere. Also I think the Korean drama Daejanggeum film one of its scene here, if you are fan of this drama then you have one more reason to go. You won't disappointed.

I think the word   museum   throws off this visit.  I expected to see many more interesting displays and films about tea but there is really just one room with some tea sets a few interesting facts and how Jeju tea is the best as the soil climate and underground water makes growing tea in Jeju at its optimal.  This so called museum is more of a flagship store where you can purchase tea and tea related items have a snack at the cafe/bakery that specializes in green tea ice cream and cake rolls and in a separate building building called   innis free   you can make natural soaps and enjoy Korean slushy ice in a cafe there as well and a store.  There are tea making classes but you must make a reservation to attend.  The grounds are nice and you can walk around the tea fields and go to the rooftop and get an amazing view of the surroundings.  The museum is free but for a true tea fanatic you may be disappointed as there are no samples or a big variety of tea products to choose from for purchase.
I stayed here  for a couple of hours, swam, enjoyed the sun discussed  the Jeju routs with  young travellers. We laughed a lot & practiced 3 languages. Black lava beach is happy noisy  place:-)

I stayed at Ojo Haenyo Guesthouse area, hopped on a taxi to get to the port to Udo. The port is actually very near but I chose not to walk there. Paid less than KRW4000 for the taxi, cheap indeed.Bought a return ticket at less than KRW6000, ran towards the ferry that was about to leave for Udo, and in less than 30 minutes, we reached beautiful Udo. In case you're wondering, the ferry ride is too short to get motion-sickness :pIt rained during my short trip to this island so I didn't rent a bicycle. Instead, I got on the hop-on hop-off bus, the ticket was about KRW5000 or so. Super cheap. But the driver/tourist guide spoke only in Korean. But no worries, I did enjoy the tour.I managed to walk up to the lighthouse, had the famous peanut ice-cream overlooking a gorgeous view of the beach and a cliff, I also went to one of the beaches there. Udo is as gorgeous as Jeju. There are nice cafes with free wifis. Street food, local food, souvenirs; Udo is small but it has everything for visitors. Do wear good walking shoes, bring a ponco with you, and get on the last ferry if you can as this island is beautiful!!

I stayed 4 night in Hamdeok Beach. If you are visiting Jeju for the very first time, you might want to move around because Jeju is quite big. Hamdeok is a great location to start your trip. It takes 20 mins by car, 30~40 mins by bus from Jeju International airport. It has many bus lines which offers you easy access to Airprot, Mountain Halla, Jeju city centre and even Seogwipo. I love the beach itself, but also there are lots of place to eat and chill. If you like to camp, there is a camping & caravan park at the end of beach. I loved it !!

I specifically spend half a day here during my trip at Jeju and has no regret. We rented a electric scooter with KRW30k for 2 hrs, do note that you need International Driving License to rent it. We had burger at HahaHoho cafe and the Pork burger is delicious. The landscape and view is so pretty. The road is narrow so I don't recommend you to drive rented car there. Udo island trip is definitely one of the highlight of our trip to Jeju!

I say this one should not be missed, just because there are not a lot of lava tubes that exist and are easily accessible! The whole journey from the mouth of the cave to the lava column, and back, can be done in an hour. Walking thru the varying sizes of the tube, some areas narrow and some really big with high ceilings, is a spectacular experience! The largest lava column in the world, towards the end of the permissible distance, is a little underwhelming. Still, overall a great visit. Highly recommended when in Jeju.

I saw one picture in instagram and decided to go Jeju olle train route 8. Actually, Route 8 is restricted, but you will see everyone just walk into. It is called 'Gaetkkak Columnar Jointing (媛二쇱?\由щ?)' It is better to wear comfortable shoes since you have to walk on rocks, but you better dress nice if you want to have a good picture. I saw many girls dressed up and walked on the rocks which looked extremely tiring but worth it. You might need to line up to take a photo, and I also waited to take a photo at specific spot. Now I have really cool pictures ;)

I really loved this waterfall. Just the way you can chill on the rocks and look out to the ocean or the waterfall itself. You can also get close to it also which is nice (unlike Cheonjiyeon Waterfall which in my opinion pales in comparison). It costs 2,000 KRW to get in and my advice is set aside a few hours to just chill. It's really wonderful. There is also wifi so you can video call your mates and show them how much their lives suck compared to yours. I got the 781 bus from Jeju bus terminal (3,000 KRW and 50 mins) and got off just as you get into Seogwipo (best use an offline map with gps). I wandered towards it and it's actually not that easy to find. The waterfall is on the west side but you want to get to the east side to view it. If you can't find it, there's a Buddhist arch/gate thing you can see from the main road. This marks the correct path and takes you in front of Seobok temple (Seobok temple should now be on your right and some well kept walled gardens on your left). Keep walking and you'll see the entrance. Note: as you walk on this path you'll be on a bridge at some point. If you carefully tread over the side garden you can look over the wall and see the top of the waterfall, it's not that spectacular but might as well grab a look.

I really love this place, sooo much. You can reach this place by bus number 710 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal directly, trip around 90 minutes & pay for bus fare by T-Money. This bus route passing some attraction in Jeju, so please stop at the attraction you wants to visit. You can rent a car too. From bus stop at Seongsan Ilchulbong, you must walking around 300 meters. What i loved about this place is, so many seafood restaurants (because it really close with ocean) & some Korean cosmetics shop too. Don't forget to bring jacket, umbrella and of course mineral water. If you have strength, you can climbs the hill (around 500 meters). But so much fog when i'm there, i can't see clearly the basin. You will met some elderly people here, at the peak. Fresh air & green vegetation will makes your eyes & breath feels relieve. You can buy some souvenirs when you get back to the foothills.

I really liked this cave, or lava tube as it's also called. I was hoping for more stalagmites and such but the lack thereof doesn't bring down the points due to it's massive size and length. There are also signs along the way with information about the   tube   in different languages. I really recommend giing to this place when you go to Jeju!!

I really like the view of the beach! Really crystal clear water and white sand... From the briedge you can have a really beautiful landscape view and it contains the Jeju's famous rock statues becoming a nice place to take some pictures.There is not so much things to do there, just enjoy the view and relax!

I really enjoyed wandering through Hallasan National Park. I spent 4 days here, and was quietly impressed. At times there were way too many hikers, as they often come by the bus load, but mostly you were alone with your thoughts and the environment. The trails were well marked out, and easy to follow (even for people who don't read Korean). There was plentiful assistance if you get lost, but you felt like you were alone. The other tourists were polite, interested and friendly, definietly great for conversation. Jeju would have to be one of the highlights of this particular trip to South Korea. Would definietly makee the trip again.

I really enjoyed visiting this cave. It reminded me of the beauty of God's creation. I was expecting to explore the entire cave, but unfortunately, they only allow the public to explore the first 1 kilometer. Nevertheless, it was an eye-opening experience for me.Tips:-1. Wear comfortable clothes.2. Wear a good pair of shoes.3.Bring a cap.4. Bring a torchlight. You gotta visit this place if you are in Jeju Island!

I really enjoy my visit to this site at Jeju island... Recommended for those who loves to take a short hike and enjoy sunrise... The view of the city from the top of it is also beautiful... One side you can see the sea, other side enjoy the city view... On the afternoon in the right time, you can also met the woman divers who will dive to look for abalone and other sea animals... Love this place, hope can visit again someday... v(^_^)v

I really cant say much about this. I believe that the being the largest columnar-jointed lava deserves a much better critique, but sadly not from me.In this trip, I realise something about myself which is i am just not a person who likes rocks, which is quite ironic when Jeju is known having abundance of rocks. Lol. So if you like great sea scenery & rocks, pls, do come here and be awed by nature.

I read reviews/blogs about what & where and the most economical way to explore east of Jeju in a day. One of the blogs I read mentioned about Udo on her trip (you may look for theLostWanderer's blog-Jeju in 3 days for more detailed trip in Jeju). I just love this islet. I rented a manual bicycle to get around for KW 5000 for 2hrs, yet you can rent at KW 10000 for 3hrs to the entire day. Well for my time is constrain, & travelling on a budget & also wanted to keep myself fit as a preparation for Mt Hallasan hike, gladly I did. Other than bicycle, you can rent an e-bike, ATV, and a scooter. The tranquility & scenery that the place could offer is magnificent. Shouldn't let this islet slip from your list once in Jeju.I took bus #701 after I visited Manjanggul Cave & Gimnyeong maze park (same bus stop where I alighted for the cave) & alight at Seongsan Habour. At the port, I paid KW 5500 (to & fro) for I'm going back the same day to the main Island of Jeju.

I reached out to Mr. Kang due to all the amazing reviews here and I'm glad I did! We had booked him for a single day since we unfortunately didn't have too much time at Jeju. He is super friendly and knowledgeable about the island. You could tell he really loves Jeju by his passion when talking to us even with his limited English. Although his English is limited, we never had trouble with communication. He helped with pictures and took us to an amazing lunch spot when we asked for recommendations! He took us to a seafood hotpot/stew spot and it was by the far the best I've ever had. Throughout our day, if there was a place that had a local discount he would let us know and offer to get it for us if we wanted as well. But the greatest show of service from Mr. Kang was that we had a spot that wasn't originally on our itinerary that he also didn't know about. Mr. Kang went above and beyond trying to figure it out and fit it into our day. I would HIGHLY recommend Mr. Kang to anyone and will definitely be reaching out to him whenever I visit Jeju again!

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I once visited this park during my short stay in Jeju City for business. It was very close to the New Jeju City area. It was a good chance to see the beautifully arranged botanic gardens made up of the trees and flowers unique to this island. Also In this park there are hills from volcanic eruption, that is called   Orum   in Jeju island dialectic. there were not very high but to get to the top I had to walk up zigzag sloped way, but it was a good experience.Although there are many tourist attractions in Jeju Island, It is worth visiting when your are near Jeju city.

I moved to the U.S. (from Korea) 26 years ago when I was 15. I have been coming back to visit almost every year in the past 15 years or so and visited Jeju five times thus far. I don't get to take long weeks off from work, so I always try to pack as many activities into any given trip, so I squeezed this one in on my way back from a day trip to Udo (which is my favorite place in Korea). I wanted to pay this place a visit because I came to learn of what 4.3 incident last year, and I didn't want to pass up the opportunity to learn more about it.The memorial hall was very well organized with plenty of pictures, exhibits, and videos to see. My 16-year-old kid, who almost never bothers to read through anything at museums, was taking photos and reading through the exhibits, which I found impressive.My appreciation for the island (and its residents) grew tenfold after the visit to this memorial hall.
