I mean, if you stay near the area in Jeju city, or are going to nearby attractions like the Love museum, you will have to pass by it and you can try it out. But for those staying at other places... i would say it's not really worth the drive. To put it this way, the petrol is better spent elsewhere on this beautiful island.

I mean it's not incredibly bad and not really expensive but compared to the other cool stuff you can do in Jeju it kind of sucks.The hedges are skimpy (not full and luscious as shown in the pictures) and you have lots of spiders above you.And the cats look bored.When in Jeju, you're better off sticking to the natural wonders of the island! We have to say the staff were very friendly though, and the other visitors seemed to be enjoying themselves.

I loved this seemingly unassuming place that I would have never really thought of visiting.  It was one of the most interesting and beautiful places I visited in Jejudo Island.  It is definitely a   must do  , as they say in Disney World!  We would have loved to spend more time there.  It's not just a park with a bunch of rocks so don't miss out!  It's like a natural museum/art gallery of indigenous Jejudo volcanic rocks with a splash of the island's history.  Highly recommended to spend a minimum of 3-4 hours here!!

I loved Hamdeok Beach. We live in China and visited during Golden Week, assuming the rest of China would follow us to Jeju (as is typical during ANY holiday traveling in China) and we were pleasantly surprised to find that there were little to no Chinese tourists, or really any tourists in the neighborhood. It was quiet, clean and so peaceful! I would return again in a heartbeat.
I loved all the waterfalls in Jeju, did not meet one I didn't like.  Highly recommend this one as well as each one is a bit different.

I LOVE... this museum!!! I am a teddy bear fan so this museum feels like heaven to me aside from being a K-drama fan. Before visiting Jeju, I researched on the top sites recommended to be visited, i got fascinated with the reviews about Teddy Bear museum plus knowing that some of its Teddy Bears where featured in one my favorite Korean Drama of all time PRINCESS HOURS. The teddy bears are just so cute, you can see them perform different functions and dressed of different profession and famous personalities such as Marilyn Monroe, Steve Jobs, Madonna etc. Afetr visiting the exhibit halls, we then went to the lower ground floor area where tall Teddy Bears are on display alongside Teddy Bears items that are for sale.A must visit for Teddy Bear Lovers.

I love this place, feel so peaceful with the wide space to walk around.  Admiring the natural landscape with pine trees, Eulalia flower and lush vegetation.  Perfect place for picnic if not for winter!  Kids can run wild or roll down the slope.  A great photography place.There are few trails to explore but we left in an hour as we have other places to visit.  A must go place in Jeju!

I love this place so much. Everyone can easily climb this mountain because they provide stairs which is well built, not too steep and not slippery. Although it made me tired to climb to the top but the scenery up there is very beautiful. I took so many photographs. The combination of land and sea scenery is very good.There is also many souvenir shops and food stall on the rest area with cheap souvenirs which is a good place to buy jeju souvenirs.Must visit.

I love that this beach tends to to have many waves, and is located within walking distance of places to stay and eat. The water is warm and clear,and theres a fantastic BBQ place over the little bridge to the right of the beach. I've returned to this beach both times I've come to Jeju! The sand is fantastic!

I love nature and if you do too this is a must visit if you are in jeju. A Unesco site and a new seven wonder, the view from the top is worth the climb. Depending on individual it can take up to 30 minutes to climb but take your time and enjoy the crisp air and the beautiful view of jeju. Also walk to the sea to buy life seafood caught by the locals

I love dolls and looked the idea of teddy bear museum was really put my attention up. I visited teddy bear museum in Seoul 3 years ago and love to recall that exciting feeling. And yes i got it, love Jeju teddy bear museum as like as in Seoul. Indeed they have some difference in theme but love it. cute teddy bear in a lot of variety of themes, clothings, activities.
I lost so much time trying to find that place! The GPS wouldn쨈t find it !Went there.. and didn쨈t liked... there are better place to go in Jeju... If you are not sure... go to other places, seriously

I liked this beach. We went there on a really windy day so it was... Windy. What was quite strange is you get down to shoulder level in the water then there is a hill and you end up at ankle level again. It was quite a strange experience. However it's probably a barrier to stop you going any further (?) but I didn't take note cos I am a rebel, the waves were awesome at that point. Eventually the lifeguard got tired of my antics and called me back in. He said it was because there were jellyfish out there... Unless the Korean for   you silly tourist   sounds like jellyfish?!?The black rocks (lava?) were quite awesome to hunt for crabs but there were these bugs that looked like flesh eating ones from the mummy so that freaked me out a little. You can get here from Jeju bus terminal using the 701 bus (3,000 KRW). There is a stop for it about 40 mins in. It's near Manjangul cave (6,000 KRW taxi) so worth combining it with a trip with that.

I like to explore super markets in different cities and different countries. It's a good way to see what people are eating. Sometime when I have the courage, I will tried some of the local food. Dongmun Market is one of the popular traditional markets in Jeju. It is big, clean and colourful. They sell all kinds of stuff, like fruit, fresh or dry (some in gift boxes), vegetables, dry mushrooms, herbs, spices and fresh or dry sea food. There are some restaurants ready to serve you. They even sell clothing there. We walked around and took photos, but no one came to pressure us to buy stuff, I like that.Happy Travelling!

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I learnt a lot about the brave women divers of Jeju by visiting this museum. I had hired a driver/tour guide for sightseeing in Jeju Island and got to visit some of my ?must see? attractions that were not close to my hotel. My tour guide was good so I had a great time. We visited this museum as part of our itinerary for the day, and I was glad we did. The museum charges a small entrance fee. I got to see a very interesting video about the history and lives of the women divers. There also a lot of painting, sculptures that is centered on the lives of these brave women. The museum is small but I liked it a lot. I came out more knowledgeable about the women and Jeju Island as a whole.

I know little about So Korea, and had never heard of Jeju before my cruise ship docked there so I was VERY pleasantly surprised by this lovely park. I enjoyed hiking up the steep mountain and admiring the views. Although very popular, and fairly crowded, it was never unpleasantly so. The women divers in a little cove below were kind of interesting, but it was very crowded there.  And, because I spent some of my limited time there, I didn't have enough time to make it to the top of the crater and back before my tour bus left so was sorry I'd wasted some of my time there instead of making it all the way to the top.

I initially wanted to climb this peak to watch the sunrise but due to the unpredictable weather on Jeju Island whilst we were there, we decided to visit when we thought the weather would be dry at least.As it is when we reached the peak it was a bit blustery and on our descent it began to rain heavily.But this place is totally worth making the effort to climb the steps to the peak. At various points when climbing up you are greeted with really cool views. Definitely worth a visit.

I hope you had good time in Jeju Island. Unfortunately, I think you didn't visit Kimnyoung Maze Park. Because, we have only one maze and no museum. Seems like you had visit Mazeland. Anyhow thanks to visit Jeju and hope to see you next time when you visit Jeju again! :)

I hiked up the Seongpanak trail, which was easily accessible from Jeju-si. It took only ~45 minutes to get to Seongpanak station on the 780 bus. It was crowded, but it was still a very nice hike (and luckily the weather was pretty good!). You have to reach the Jindallaebat Station by 1 pm in order to be allowed to climb to the summit. Then, you have to start your descent by 2:30 pm. Please note, the time may change depending on the season, but I?m not sure (I climbed late April). It?s a big hike, and I definitely recommend wearing good hiking boots and wearing a proper backpack. Bring lots of water. If you forget to pack food, there is some available at the Jindallaebat Station. The summit is breathtaking! I hiked back down the Seongpanak trail since the bus to get back to Jeju-si seemed more frequent than the other one. During the descent, I took a side-trip to the Sara Oreum and scenic view. It was just a good 30 minute detour, and well worth it! Once at the bottom, it was easy to catch the 780 bus back to Jeju-si.

I hiked up Hallasan via Seongpanak trail and went down the Gwaneumsa trail. The hiking was almost torturous, for a person who does only some jogging as preparation to hike Halla, but it indeed worth every step towards the peak because of the heavenly view of Jeju from there. Expect rocky trails, crazy steep staircases and trails. Bring at least 2 litres of water (you can refill your bottles at fresh water springs along Seongpanak and after the bridge in Gwaneumsa trail). There's a small shop selling hot noodles, drinking water and hot coffee at Jindallae Bat shelter. Toilets are available at Sokbat and Jindallabaet and a few more somewhere along Gwaneumsa. Start early to complete the hike early. Be sure to bring your camera. Get walking sticks too if you can, I didn't but I could still do the hike :D I went to Jeju on a solo trip and did the hike alone, but a lot of other hikers were very kind giving me words of encouragement and even waited for me along Gwaneumsa trail. A must do if you get to Jeju! No entrance fee! :D

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I highly recommend this service, and hiring Mr John Sheen in particular. Friendly, on time, courteous. I have nothing but positive things to say. Simply put: book a private driver with Jeju Taxi Tour and you'll be very happy .

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I heard from the owner of our guesthouse that this place isn?t always open because of the tides and weather, so if you have the chance to go, take it. It?s an amazing rock formation, but unlike the ones that you can see at a distance, like Oedolgae and the Jungmun Daepo, you can actually walk on it. That rocks. It took us a while ? was it an hour? ? to walk along the perimeter of this massive rock. The terrain is not smooth ? think of desert sands except that the undulating surface is made of rock instead of sand, so wear study shoes that won?t split because of the damp. It looks like a movie set -- for an alien planet. Really, I didn?t know such a place existed on earth.If I were taking someone around Jeju, I?d recommend this place and I would definitely come back so we can exclaim together.Where: Seogwipo west coast

I have spend a week on Jeju Island in September, and of my Highlights was Udo. I had time only for a day trip, and if I ever make it back to Jeju, my priority will be to spend at least one night there. Its such a lovely, small and relaxed place. From Seongsan its only 15 minutes to Udo by Ferry. There, you can take the local bus that runs along the island, you can rent small tuk-tuks / quad bikes / scooters or bicycles, you can join a tour (I think only in Korean) or you can walk (like I did, but then of course you dont get to cover the whole island).

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

I have been wanting to visit the Teddy Bear Museum for the longest time but did not get to visit the one in Seoul 2 years ago. So, when we decided to plan a 2D1N trip to Jeju, this attraction is in my itinerary list. It is not located conveniently near the city centre and about an hour's bus ride to go to the attraction. I was so excited when I saw the museum when the bus passed by and alighted with much excitement. We were greeted with a huge bear at the entrance and it was like entering a wonderland. We walked around admiring the displays, the history of teddy bears etc. We also visited the outdoor park right behind the museum which are meant for visitors only. It was a fruitful visit and did not fail my expectation though. Love all the bears on sale at the gift shop but couldn't bring them all back so only got to admire them when I was there. If you are visiting Jeju, do drop by this museum to bring back childhood memories.

I have always wanting to visit Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju because of the K-Drama - Goong.But I felt is abit over-rated as I myself is not a soft toy person.If you love soft toys or teddy bear, is a must go, otherwise, you can drop by and have a quick look.

I have always wanted to climb Hallasan so when I got the chance to visit Jeju, I included it on my itinerary. As I wasn't an expert hiker, I have opted to start my ascent at the Seongpanak trail. I wasn't disappointed. It was only a moderately steep climb for most of the trip. You will only have a more difficulty from the rest stop. The scenery wasn't as good as Gwaneumsa but if you want a more relaxing climb, I'd suggest to take this trail.

I had to high an expectation for this shop unfortunately. It isn't anything very special, and it's selection is quite small compared to the other Jeju shops I jage been to. The prices are fair though, I think it is a fine option if you are staying within Jeju city.

I had requested Tripadvisor to add this as an attractive as it was along the Jeju City Tour bus route. We decided at the last minute to get off at 'Sarabong Peak' as we wanted to see the lighthouse. However, we had a 10 or 15 minute uphill walk to reach the lighthouse during a cold December day but the view more than made up for the inconvenience. We only stayed for half an hour as we wanted to catch the bus back to town as it was already getting dark.

I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I had always wanted to go to a maze park, and finally I did in jeju :) it was a small maze but enough to make us excited to find our way out. The entrance fee is 33,000 won for adult. In front of the entrance, there were lots of cats and quite tame too.

I had a lot of fun riding the carts but also enjoying the beauty of Jeju. It's situated in such a beautiful location where you can view the ocean and take Instagram photos! The interior of the building was also cool. It was futuristic and very clean. The staff were friendly and helpful! I didn't play indoor games but there were many indoor games as well, so it seems like a place that you can have fun in any season. I will definitely recommend this place for any ages!? I will go back in a heartbeat when I visit Jeju next time!!

I guessed many have mentioned that this was a typical market and I do not think they were wrong. However, it really depends the reason for your visit. If you are here to try cheap and good raw and fresh seafood (eg: raw fish slices for 10000won only), OR to try a variety of local food (eg: Sundae aka blood sausage, traditional fishcake stick, Kimbap, fresh Jeju orange juices, different types of kimchi, korean rice cakes, croquette, Tteokbokki, hotba, Modeumjeon - where they eat during new year and jeons, OR to purchase souvenirs and snacks for your family and friends then you are at the right place! It was also cheaper to purchase dried goods like ikan bilis and kelp in the market than supermarkets.We were at Seogwipo Maeil Olleh Market before coming to this market and we found that stalls that sell Jeju's souvenirs and local snacks such as Jeju crunch chocolate were cheaper in this market. The shop owners also gave us a handful of other snacks to try after our purchase in hope that we would be back for more. In Summary, this was a good place to try many local food at a smaller amount and a place to purchase affordable snacks for gift at a cheaper price.

I got a public bus from the Inter-city Bus Terminal at Jeju-si to this park at only Won 2000. 1 hour required.  This is the last activity of my trip and upon leaving, luckily I met an American man at the bus stop who agreed to share a taxi with me heading to the airport, otherwise I may be late.Time is rather limited for me and I took a quick and rough walk in the park after taking a 45 min lunch of seafood pot at the restaurant at the entrance.  Yummy!  Seafood is to die for in Jeju.  I like this park as it's well gardened, clean, cozy with some souvenirs shops and two restaurants inside.  And I did not meet groups of tourists which is a PLUS.  Visitors decent. Next time when I come to Jeju, I should spend plenty of time in this park.There is a famous beach opposite to the park entrance so you can have a walk there as well after leaving here.

I got 28 hour spare time before my flight to Dhaka in my last visit to Korea. When I got this break at the very last moment, I searched Jeju air ticket and hotel booking online without any delay. As I purchased it at the last moment, I had to spend USD 125 more for air ticket and hotel booking. Jeju is a rush destination in summer. It's is a fairly large island to cover within 24 hours. Thanks to TripAdvisor and reviewers for helping me to select Seongsan Ilchulbong and Hamdaeok beach from many other attractions.Tourists have time, usually visit Seongsan Ilchulbong before dawn to observe Sunrise. That why it is also known as Sunrise peak. As I did?t had that option in hand, I climbed it at afternoon. I took a taxi from my hotel at Hamdaeok beach and it costs around USD 28. Bus is always cheaper but I had only 20 hours left in my hand to catch my return flight. Sunrise peak entry ticket costs USD 2 for adults and USD1 for child. Most of the review I read earlier suggests it takes 20 minutes to climb on the peak but as an amateur I took roughly 40 to 45 minutes to climb. There are two wide and convenient stairway to climb on the peak. I selected the left side stairway and eventually it was a right decision. Because there is a small grocery in the midway selling soft drinks and water for those who didn't buy it from the base. As usual they charge double for each drinks but it was a life saver for me. When I came down from the other way I didn't find any shop like this. There are also a  midway station if you are tired want get refreshed for a while. When I reached on the peak I was almost exhausted. The view is literally breathtaking. I was sitting there more than one hour and a half as it is so charming that made for  forget everything else of life. I came down from the other stair way. The surrounding is so calm and comfortable that I stayed their until it?s dark. Tips: Try to book air ticket and hotel upfront to save cost. Rely more in internet than locals advise because there is a high chance of misleading information due to language barrier. I lost twice in the island for relying on them and lost around 3 hours of my precious time. There are halal restaurant ( Bagdad and Rajmahal) in Jeju island. 4 days are fairly enough to cover most of the attraction of Jeju. It costs total USD 400 all inclusive  for me for a quick tour , however if you are two them many cost will be shared within you. If I could catch the early morning flight from Gimpo airport at 7:30 am and save three more hours to arrive Jeju island then I could go to Udo island as well. I couldn't do that because I had to come from Suwon city. So if you stay at Seoul, you can catch 7:30 morning flight comfortably.

I found this to be the best attraction in Jeju. It really is a lot of stairs, so if you are not good in health condition, this might be very tiresome. But there are rest points a long the way, so you can take your time. There are little shops and restaurants around after you finish your hike. Beautiful views to take pictures both going up and down.

I found the volcanic caves here interesting but apart from that it was just another botanic garden. We went when the rapeseed and cherry blossoms were in bloom which was very pretty and a good photo opportunity. However, the same flowers are everywhere in Jeju at that time of year and don't cost anything to take a photo.

I found pretty disappointing this 1 block Street where several pork cuisine restaurants are located, mostly for tourists, thats why the prices raises up from others in the city. Only if you go to shop nearby and want to taste Jeju pork in well decorated restaurants

I found much of Jeju island to be very commercialized and crowded with loud tour groups. This is a great place to enjoy the natural beaty of Jeju with smaller groups of people. There is a small entrance fee.  The first half mile is along a wide crushed rock road. It is lined with young   nutmeg   trees. The trees are in the yew family. They are Torreya nucifera and are native to Japan. I  visited in October when the small edible nuts ripen. The nuts are encased in a thin husk that has a wonderful aroma. You will see people collecting them under the large trees.  Eventually the road ends and then you follow a loop trail that is about 2 feet wide it is covered with a hemp rope mat that felt lovely to walk on with bare feet.  The crowds end at the beginning of the narrow trail so you can walk through this section in peace and really marvel at the enchanting colors and smells of the forest and hear the songs of the many birds.  There were signs to watch for snakes but I saw none. The yews are huge.  Make sure to investigate the tree bark it is fabric like and soft. Also many of the other plants have English name labels which is nice. The trail is flat and should take a leisurely couple of hours or less if you rush.  I noticed a lot of people sitting on benches in the first section enjoying picnic lunches.

I found it well boring to be honest. I prefer stuff like the lava caves and waterfalls - I guess I just like to be wowed. However it was a peaceful place and it was surrounded by lovely countryside. Maybe a place for a stroll with your loved one. Still if you want to get there from Jeju - you can get a bus 710-1 from the bus terminal. Note there are two 710's (assume the other one is 710-2).  It costs about 3,000 KRW (40 minute ride) and there is a designated stop about 3 or 4 stops after Gyorae Entrance (not junction which is 2 stops away). Note: Gyorae Entrance is a good stop to know about as it on the north - south road (Jeju-seogwipo) which is the 781/782 bus route.... just in case you want to go anywhere else after or get bored like me :)How helpful am I!

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.

I first heard of Saebyeol Oreum when watching Hyori's Bed & Breakfast, and I really wanted to visit this famous oreum. The hike was insanely steep, and we huffed and puffed to get to the summit (520m above sea level). The view from the top was breathtaking, and the eoksae (flamegrass) covering the entire oreum was absolutely gorgeous. We were lucky to catch the magnificent sunset, and it was a great end to our Jeju trip. Highly recommended!

I enjoyed snorkeling at the place. Inside the water is not that colorful as some famous snorkeling spot around the world, but you will see very attractive black rocks and ecosystems only seen at Jeju Island. Also there is a nice trail following the coast with great view. Though you are not going to swim, it is still good to visit.

I enjoyed my visit to Manjanggul cave, however it was not my favorite place in jeju. What i liked was that they had signs and explanations for everything in English so you could learn on how it was formed. It is a little cold down in the cave, wear a jacket and comfortable shoes.

I do feel some surprise during our visit here, but probably we expect so much. Mysterious road is a part of the road, amazing. But after i tested with two bottles of beer, it just normal. i don't understand so much. But overall it's worth visit to Mysterious Road, Jeju.

I didn't know I was looking at this famous peak when we approached in a taxi (looking for a lunch spot that our kids would approve of). I was saying   Wow, look at that   as we drove towards it. Then our driver explained it was the famous peak. I can see why, even on a cloudy rainy day it was such a beautiful scene. We couldn't climb to the peak because it was closed to the public due to an impending typhoon. I was disappointed we couldnt climb but so glad that we got to see it, even from the base. Absolutely beautiful area. I want to come back to Jeju just to climb that peak and see the beauty from above.Incidentally there were plenty of restaurants and cafes and shops in the small town at the base. Even an American Embassy (i.e. Mcdonalds)

I didn't hike the mountain because it was so tiring. But, I really enjoyed watching the natural view. Moreover, there was an outdoor displayed pictures of the species found in Jeju. I enjoyed taking many pictures there.

I crossed the Believe it or not museum many times, in New york, in Baltimore.. but never stepped in.Finally I tried the one in Jeju island and I really liked it. It is certainly similar to the others, but if you never visited one... who cares?I imagined it small but it took me 2 hours to do everything. I mean... read all, not just give a look and say : oh.. ok!It costs 10usd per person. Expensive or not depends of you.If you are curious and love to travel and discover... it is nice place.

I couldn?t resist visiting this place on our way from Jeju city to Seogwipo. It made me giddy as a child. Entry fee is now 14,000 won per adult, and either 11,000 or 13,000 for children. This place has optional guided tours and accepts credit cards. Small room of Hello Kitty history and how her image has evolved since 1976. Original design merch on display. Lots of interactive rooms for kids and 3 floors to play. As an adult I still had fun and enjoyed a Hello Kitty hot chocolate (her face is in the cream), and Hello Kitty-shaped strawberry mousse cake in the cafe. You?re paying for the experience, here, so if you or your child is not a Hello Kitty fan, don?t waste your time. The maze on the roof is shaped like Hello Kitty from an aerial view and is strictly for children?the maze walls are only about 2 feet tall. My favorite part was the art exhibit (2nd floor) and all the small, unexpectedly perfect details (heart shaped straws, Hello Kitty toilet paper!). Souvenir shop: a mechanical pencil costs 7,700 won (more than $6)?I guess this is slightly more than American Sanrio store prices. But, if you?re willing to visit this museum, you?re probably also willing to pay for a momento of your experience.

I completed every single course over a period of a year so the following comments are just my opinions. If you are staying for a short period of time in Jeju courses 6 and 7 are the most popular and will probably get the most from. Both are very scenic and you will get to see some of the major sights. If you start at one of the information sites, you can pick up a Jeju Olle guide which has maps and information of the trails, guides for the Buses, to get to and from the starting points. Also I'd recommend downloading Kakao Maps app on your phone and you can zoom in and see the actual trail that you are following when you are on it. It comes in handy especially for me when I made a wrong turn on my trips. If your doing the entire course I'd recommend buying a jeju Olle Passport. Carry it with you and get it stamped at the starting points and halfway way points of the trails. I was living near jeju city and caught most of Buses from the Jeju inter city bus centre. The 101/201 express buses will take you to/ or near a lot of the starting points but I'd recommend picking up the Olle Guide first and the info in that is invaluable.Most of the Starting points are close to the roads unless you are going to one of the 3 islands. I used booking.com most of the time to book places to stay overnight as I don't speak Korean. Jeju has a lot of places to stay and there would be abundant places to stay except for maybe a couple of the more remote locations on the trail. There are offical Olle trail Hostels throughout the trails to which are very nice. If planning for no Korean speakers just check before hand that you are not traveling on a Jeju holiday as a lot of paces close down and might be harder to find a place to stay. Of course take plenty of water and there's usually 7/11 of CV's around the place where you can get snacks to eat.The trails themselves are very beautiful , Different scenes ranging from Black volcanic rock on the coastlines, Forest trails, Beautiful beaches, Hill sides, a lot of Oreums (Jeju extinct volcanoes) small towns with a chance to see wildlife and a lot of friendly people. For myself my favourite trails were routes 11, 18-1 Chuja-Do island), 1-1 (Udo island), 7. For me the stronger trails were on the southern eastern point of the island starting from route 6 through to 15.Getting to the supporting islands it you might take note you will need your Passport to catch the ferry to Udo. You must show it when buying a ticket. There are a lot of ferries going most of the day to Udo. They have a very nice Peanut ice cream there. The smaller island Gapado at the time I went there were only 2 ferries in the day and its not the most reliable service and the ferries can be cancelled due to bad weather can be cancelled due to bad weather so check beforehand if you can. Chuja-Do island was one of my favourites. When I done it they had 2 ferries a day and you can not do the whole trail in time to catch the next ferry back so be prepared to stay over night. I have heard of instances when the weather turned bad and people had to stay a couple of nights on the island because the ferries were cancelled so just plan for that just in case. it is a beautiful Island though and one of my favourites.I would also recommend going and joining the Olle Walkers Facebook group. They take guided walks along certain courses and have great information about weather and so forth. all you need to do is contribute to the group from time to time.

I collect Teddy bears and it was only fitting that I should bring home with me the symbol of JeJu - Haenyeo woman (Mother of the Sea - diving since 200 BC and tradition is still alive.  These women are what made JeJu what it is today.  They were responsible for agriculture, diving for abalone, sea cucumber, squid etc and it was these women who stood up against the Japanese invasion during WWII.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I can't recommend Mr Jang highly enough! He is a fabulous guide who is very generous with his time and will tailor the day to suit the customer completely. If you are short on time, then this is absolutely the way to see Jeju. Mr Jang is friendly and easy-going and giving. If you're going to book a trip to see Jeju then go with Mr Jang!

I came to Udo on my 4th day in Jeju and it was the spotlight of my trip. I love the island itself and everything about it. You can rent a bicycle or a motorbike to go around the island. I didnt bring my licence so you didnt let me rent the motorbike even I told them that I am Vietnamese, I really can drive ( in Korean ) =)) It was a funny conversation, but I end up with riding the bicycle for 4 hours .. quite tired but amazing place and worth to visit.I went to Korea alone, and my days in Jeju was quite boring but Udo made my trip more memorable ^^

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

I came here by bus .. so I waited for the bus and cars to go on neutral and watch them drive up he hill hands free.Some people poured water while other rolled a water bottle.Since this attaction takes less than 15 minutes, i would suggest also going the Jeju Art Museum next door :)

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

I came here after visiting the nearby Jeju Loveland. This museum has 4 floors. First floor is the Welcome Stage, which traces the history of computers and hardwares. Second floor is Open Stage, which depicts the history and development of computer games. Third floor is Hidden Stage, which showcases how computers changed and expanded our everyday life. The Basement 1 is Special Stage, which is used for special exhibitions.Second and third floors allow visitors to play old computer and arcade games such as Space Invaders, Galaxy etc. Playing these games bring back fond memories of my younger days. Before leaving, I headed to the cafe at B1 and ordered the keyboard waffle for its novelty, not cheap at 12,000 won.Admission fees 8,000 won. Note it is closed on Monday. Worth a visit if you have half a day to spare. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Jeju Loveland.

I believe this place can be so much fun then how we experienced it. We were there quite late, hence the volunteers (as the tour guides) were in an extreme rush to go home. Totally understandable. However they were still nice enough to show us around. Interesting historical facts about the Koreans in Jeju-do and their houses. They promoted horse face cream towards the end of the tour. Apparently the appropriate time to visit this place is between 11 am - 1 pm or definitely way BEFORE 4.30 pm.

I and my family visited during late June 2015. There was a little bit of rain that day but the path to the cliff was still accessible with problem. It was a scenic walk. You can reach the main entrance from the Jeju ICC by walking about 5 to 7 minutes. There is a cheap entrance fee to pay to go inside the cliff. Even under the light rain, the view was so magnificent. We stayed there for about an hour before leaving. If the weather was better, I bet I would stay longer.I probably will visit again next time in Jeju.

I am super Hello Kitty fans and for sure go there when I was in Jeju.  Frankly, it is a place for kids rather than fans.  Not many specialty items available in the shop.  It is a good experience to have a coffee at the cafe.

I am really suprised this place has only few reviews here  it is one of the best things I got to do in Jeju  if you are afraid it's gonna be boring then let me tell you it's not  it's truely a   healing   experience  you leave phone and gadgets at the enterance and you just follow the guide and get far from everything and allow yourself to just rest  well you have to like nature to enjoy this experience for sure. Our guide was unforgettable.

I am not an early morning riser. However, since this place is one of the most recommended place to visit in Jeju, my friends and I decided to wake up super early to watch the sunrise. The stairs to get to the peak were steep, I had to stop to catch my breath a few times before reaching the peak. It was worth it though, the sunrise view was so pretty, and actually one of my best experiences in Jeju.

I am not able to visit this park because of the bus. We went to the airport by bus in order to take the 131 bus for the park. To confirm this info from our hotel receptionist, we asked the airport tourist info counter. Correct, and we were directed to gate 1 and begun to wait for the bus. We missed the 1240 so we decided to wait for the 1340. The bus didn't come until 1400 and we went to double check with the info counter. Then we were told that 1340 is for the number 132, which is grouped together with 131. 132 doesn't head for Jeju stone park and we were told to wait for the 1530 bus. Isn't it amazing our bus waiting experience? I am sharing this as a gentle reminder for all. Plan your bus schedule properly especially for venues outside the city. Cheers
i am lucky to visit udo on a sunny day. we are amazed by the unbeatable view and superb environment. spent a relaxing day in udo.if you go to jeju, you MUST go to udo!

I am interested in world heritage and Manjang Cave is included in sites of Jeju's world heritage so I went there. I had never walked inside a cave before, so it was an interesting experience. And I appreciate the carving in the walls and the shapes of rocks that were formed by volcanic activities.The temperature inside the cave is colder than the temperature outside, so it's better to bring a jacket.

I am in the middle of living in Jeju for a year and visited the Haenyeo Museum with three friends a couple of months ago. It was a really great visit and showed really well the changes in Haenyeo lifestyle as time has gone on. The top floor has a beautiful picture gallery with gorgeous views. Highly recommend. I think you need about an hour - an hour and a half here.Also the gift shop is great for cute Jeju-y things. I put some   Jeju stockings   together for my cousin's kids for Christmas all with keyrings/books/purses/other stuff bought here.

I am a resident of the Seattle metropolitan area so I have to compare it to the Chihuly Garden and Glass museum.  The Jeju Glass Castle is very different in concept as it also focuses on small to medium sized glass items.  Conversely, Chihuly Garden and Glass focuses on large scale items produced by Chihuly in small quantities.  That's not to say it was disappointing, but it wasn't that impressive in the sheer quality of the items.  However, you do get a very large variety of glass items from throughout the world so it does make it up in quantity.  Unlike the Chihuly museum, the glass castle is a very large complex.I did notice the museum seemed a little run down in a few areas - it really did seem it needs some upgrades to its infrastructure.  However, there is a maze, nicely manicured gardens, glass shoes, and a large variety of other takes on glass items.  There is also a nice trail to walk that showcases certain glass items as well.Perhaps the most interesting part of the museum is near the entrance.  You'll find a glass making room there with windows you can look through to see glass artisans at work.  It was quite interesting to see these people create glass items by sculpting it, putting it in the oven, and more.

I am a complete beginner to mountain climbing but was there thankfully with an experienced climber. We took a taxi from jeju city to Seongpanak visitor centre and the journey costs around 20,000 krw and approx 40 min. I was there on 7 December after a snowy night, and the trails were covered in snow. Poles, proper hiking shoes and crampons are absolute necessity as the snowy paths were hard to walk.  Gwaneumsa, the popular trail for descent after reaching the crater summit, was closed that day as the snowy trail was too dangerous, so it was pretty rough to get up while people are trying to get down. Especially since the trail was already made quite narrow by the snow. However, the view is great and it's like a winter wonderland all the way up. The last stretch to the crater summit was hard for a complete beginner like me. It was however considered easy for seasoned hiker like my friend. On the whole a great experience and certainly worth the trouble for the views but would recommend complete beginners like me to do some training before getting up. The rest stops are well stocked and constant announcements were made (in Korean only) to keep the hikers moving up before the gate closes at 12 pm and down before it's gets dark. Note: we were staying in Jeju city before the climb and the weather was grim with lots of rain. The weather on Hallasan was however completely different. Sunny and pleasant for climbing.  Be sure to check the weather forecast on Hallasan and not Jeju!

I always wanted to visit the Devils Postpile National Monument in California. It is a surprise to find Columnar basalt on the seashore of Jeju-do, South Korea. One can walk behind the Sailboat ladders to take a closer look at the Columnar basalt. If you have time, you can stroll along the park to enjoy the beautiful seashore.

I absolutely recommend you to take a day trip and hike up Hallasan if you are in Jeju. Even though if it takes the whole day, since it is about 20km walking, it is worth it. If you are in okay shape I'd recommend you to go up on the Seongpanak trail. It is longer but easier than Gwaneumsa trail. The hike has a lot of stairs, so don't expect climbing. Once getting up, the most thing that shocked us what the loads and loads of bugs, since we never heard about that. They don't bite but they do get on you which is annoying. That said, the view is beautiful, to the island but also to the crater. Going down I'd recommend Gwaneumsa trail since it is a lot more beautiful and more to see. It is only the first third part that is the hardest, after that it gets okay. Remember to start climbing early since you have to reach the checkpoint before a certain time depending on the year. It takes about 3 hours to get to the checkpoint so try to check what time you have to be there before. The time is there because it takes a longer time to get down than you expect. Also bring water with you. There is only one point where you can buy going up, and only one point where you can fill your water bottle on both trails!

Hyeopjae is a beautiful beach with everything you would want in a beach it's very long with thick soft sand. But, the best thing about Hyeopjae beach is the Ollhe trail that starts at the Northeast end of the beach and goes for ever. The trail runs along the shore so close to the sea that at high tide on a windy day it becomes inpassable because of the waves submerging the trail in some places. The volcanic rock along the trail forms different things. If you look at the rock closely you might see a dragon or a horse or maybe a bird. If you stay on the trail long enough you walk by G-Dragon's cafe. If you go even further you will come across a Smoke Tower that is hundreds of years old used to send a signal of a enemies ship approaching.So, while Hyeopjae Beach is 1st rate when you are done swimming take a walk through history down the Olleh trail.I'm an American that has been living in Jeju for the last 12 years and I walk this trail 3 to 4 times a week and it never gets old.

Huge, lots to see and easy to get lost in the maze of stalls. For a glimpse into local life with products ranging from clothes, fabrics, sundries, cooked/fresh food, seafood, dried goods and everything in between. Local souvenirs definitely cheaper here than duty free shops and touristy spots. Check out fresh tangerines, Jeju chocolates, hallabong jam/honey vitamins; even dried anchovies (great as Korean soup base) and ginseng roots for DIY ginseng chicken at home. Do compare prices at a few stalls and bargain with the kind ahjummas when buying several items. Souvenir hunters, moms and senior relatives will definitely love exploring the colourful atmosphere of Dongmun market. The covered market is good activity during rainy or hot days. Nearby attractions: Jungang underground shopping street, E-martNote:Street parking just outside the market can be difficult at peak hours, suggest self-drivers park around Black Pork Street or nearby hotels and walk to the market.
How this park began is very interesting and I would recommend this place to visit when in Jeju. You learn a lot about different plants, animals, Jeju's history and the volcanic activity in Jeju.

Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

Hmm... Where to start?Well, Jeju Island, being volcanic in nature, must really have places like this!Honestly saying, it wasn't something so jaw-dropping and spectacular!Just more like a place with rock formations due to the cooling of lava!The trek inside isn't hard and what I really liked was that it was chilly while we did it!It was a nice sidetrip nonetheless if you like walking and if you like all these geo stuff!If you're in Jeju, maybe you can give it a try

Hiking Hallasan is the number one experience to do on Jeju. You have to be reasonably fit but it's fairly easy to complete as a day hike and no guides are needed. The trails are well maintained and easy to follow and there are great views. If you climb in winter, it's well worth getting small instep crampons for about 10 dollars from the shop at the bottom of either the Seongpanak or Gwameumsa trails. I recommend walking up the steeper Gwaneumsa trail, and down the Seongpanak trail. I've been up four times now, different routes, and this is definitely my preferred approach. The views are much better and Seongpanak is much easier on the knees coming down.

Hiked up to the summit via the Seongpanak trail. A 35 minute ride on the 5.16 bus from the Jeju main bus terminal drops you off right at the entrance to the trail. Great hike up. Took me a little under 4 hours including a 30 minute detour which breaks off from the trail to go see the Saraureom. This trail is mostly wooden steps. Both the Saraoreum and summit crater lake were dry, but still beautiful. I do not recommend relying on the   store   at the Jinderaebal shelter. They do have hot water if you want to bring your own instant noodle mix. Bring your own food and be prepared to bag your garbage and carry it. walked down via the Gwaneumsa trail which is a bit shorter. I defenitely recommend this since the trail also has a different type of scenery, including a beautiful bridge crossing. Not sure if there is a bus back to the city from the bottom of the Gwaneumsa trail, but by the time I made it down (3 hours) I was ready to take a taxi, one of many which are available which cost me 15,000 Won (about $ 15) back to the city. Certainly worth it. Overall, a beautiful and amazing experience.One last recommendation would be NOT to attempt this hike with less than proper hiking shoes.

Hiked to the top of Hallasan yesterday morning through the Gwanmeusan Trail - started at about 7:10am and were back in our car at 2:30pm - so this start and finish time includes breaks, and you'll need them even if you are in okay or good shape. It was a bit disappointing to see the majority of water bodies in the mountain are dry at the moment - just a few ponds on the early parts of the trail, and the crater lake at the summit, which we expected would be much deeper. The trail has a combination of dirt, rocks, and steps/bridges. I wish the steps and parts of the trail didn't include so many sharp rocks - your feet WILL feel them! We did the hike in running shoes because we don't have hiking boots here. I can see the climb being a lot easier with hiking shoes. Some parts of the trail are very steep so if you have serious knee problems, I don't think this is the trail for you. Do bring lots of water and snacks - we had two liters of water for each of us and I still think my husband got dehydrated rather badly. There is really nothing to eat on the trails so bring snacks. Visibility yesterday wasn't great - pollution has been pretty high in Jeju the past couple of days - but it's still a GREAT, BEAUTIFUL view from the top. I loved all the flowers you see growing in the rocky sides of the mountain in the last third of the trail. Very happy I did it and it's a great hike, but there is not a lot to see before you get to the top. We went down the same trail, so a total of 17.4kms. It'd be interesting to see what the other trails are like, but I don't think I need to summit again.

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Having just visited the newly opened Teddy Bear Museum in Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China (by the same group), this original museum in Jeju was a little underwhelming, even for a solid teddy bear fan like me. Unlike those in Chengdu, I didn't appreciate the fact that all teddies in Jeju were enclosed in glass cases. Impossible to take a decent pic with them!There was a good collection of antique bears. Great for a collector like myself. Also there was the supposedly most expensive teddy bears in the world. The LV bear and the diamond bear.For sale of their Elvis bears I believe, there was a small theater on the second floor showing 4 mins Elvis teddy concert every quarter of the hour. Perhaps I went at a later hour (5pm), I was the only one in the theater. Appreciate that the museum is opened till 8pm in the evening, so it's great as a quick destination pre or post dinner, if you are staying or hanging around the Jungmum Resort Area. The museum was located right next to Lotte Hotel. There was a Lotteria on the ground floor but it was closed during my visit. An attractive and well stocked teddy store on the ground floor too, unlike its sad and sparse Chengdu cousin. Happy that there were some collector grade Korean handmade teddies for sale. Their house brand   so-called   limited edition replica made-in-China white Alfred bear (real limited edition would come with serial numbers) came in a nice copycat Steiff look alike gift box and a photo with a Korean prince. At only USD 35, it's great as a souvenir/gift!I like the outdoor park area. Great for kids to run around. Overall not a very big place. Whole place would take about an hour.

Having experienced caves in the USA, I was expecting a similar experience.  Not at all the the case on Jeju with the manjanggul caves.  This UNESCO site is self led, wet, slippery, dark and EXCELLENT!  Also, very cool in temperature which was very welcome in the humid conditions present on Jeju in July.

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

Has a little bit of eveything that Jeju offers, lots of trees, flowers, stones, caves and a tiny folk village.
