입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: Driving from the city to the Seongpanak trail is the most convenient way to do it, it's only 20 minutes away from the busy area of Jeju.I hiked the mountain at early morning January 01 and when i reached the Seongpanak trail the parking was crazy long that it goes as far as 1km from the side of the road. If you want to save time in walking you should be at the trail around 3am at Jan01. Anyway, the trail was relatively easy on the first 7km, it was cold around -1 to 5C that time, still manageable but the trail was slippery due to ice forming on rocks and the trail was covered with snow. So, to prevent accidents wear a mini crampons or a Yaktrak coil underneath your shoes.Don't worry hiking alone, you can do this without a guide, you probably are blind if you get lost out there. Also, the trail was properly maintained that hiking at the peak was a breeze except the last 2km of the hike. When you reached the final kilometers it starts to get steep, so take your time and avoid slippery rocks and you should be fine. Finally, the peak was amazing, you would be able to see sea of clouds if the weather permits. Overall not bad for a hike.

Don't miss this show if u are in Jeju. Only available & performing until October 2020....awesome immersive show.? @ 빛의 벙커 Bunker de Lumieres. The floors and walls become the canvas of this highly immersive digital art that come to life, as Van Gogh's art work are displayed all over and synchronised with beautiful clasical music. Definitely worth the more than an hour show.We enjoyed it tremendously!

Don't miss the authentic dohareubang (also called   useokmok     museokmok   or   beoksumeori  ) at the entrance - estimated to have been made around 1754 - now imitated widely everywhere on Jeju having become an icon of the island. A collection of small hareubang in the rooftop garden too. A pearl divers' raft and paraphernalia are also noteworthy though more English explanations of the material would be helpful.

Don't bother if you honestly hoped to gain much knowledge in green tea / tea by coming here. The   museum   per se is a small area probably 20 steps from end to end with around 30-40 exhibits I guess.Main attractions are the many tea they sold and the cafe selling green tea products. I have yet to try those tea leafs yet so I can't commend on the taste (but it was mentioned in the museum that Jeju had the most fitting environment for producing green tea) I also bought 3 slices of swiss roll a green tea roll with cheese inside a black roll with vanilla inside and another caramel roll with i think green tea inside. The roll were soft and sweet but not overtly sweet. My cousins bought their green tea ice cream but it was very milky.Still worth a visit for their products if you are in Jeju.

Dongmun Market is filled with every possible product that you can make out of tangerines.They grow tangerines on the island. There is tangerine chocolate, tangerine juice, tangerine cakes etc. There is also fish and food stalls. If you want to get your friends gifts or souvenirs from Jeju, you can buy them from here.

Dongmun market is close to Jeju airport. It is huge and so many allies for so many different stores. I had a rental car so used a public parking lot which was cheap. We had a great time exploring almost all allies, but the parking lot was a bit too tight and small. Don't forget to try out some   Omegi   rice cake which is a very authentic, famous, and delicious rice cake in Jeju.

Dongmun market is a must visit in Jeju. Its a market where you can get almost any local products here. In the AM, there are plenty of shops selling dry food supplies, fruits, seafood, local snacks and few small restaurants. At night, you can grab some local food here at the stalls. Prices at the stalls are quite standard, ranging from KRW1000. We tried few food here which was good.

Do not miss the chance to climb up to the top (180m) to see the huge crater & Jeju view! it's definitely worth it ..the staircases might seems endless but it wasn't that high actually. it tooks us less than 30mins to reach the top and there are a few stops where you can catch a breath before continue to climb up again. Even my 4 years old nephew make it on top too. Going up and going down is 2 different route. Don't forget to get yourself mineral water at the convenient store before you climb up. you will need it.If you going over to the cliffs for the seaview, check out the Haenyeo performance. The performance hours are 1:30 p.m. and 3 p.m. twice a day during summer but we are out of luck we did not see any at the 3pm slot that day. Seongsan ilchulbong is sunrise peak - famous with sunrise from the cater! The gate is open 1 hour before sunrise for those who wish to watch sunrise from the top.

Do not go to Jeju without checking out Udo. A beautiful island off the coast, you can walk the Olle trail here, or rent bikes to cover more miles! Beautiful in spring or fall. Definitely check it out!

Do not bother spending your time going here unless there is some specific item or shopping you need to do. Come on, you are on Jeju, a small slice of paradise on Earth, go see funny statues or climb a mountain.

Do it with your partner, not with your mates, not with your friends and not with a group. This is a tiny island and the ideal thing to do is to rent a bicycle and just glide around the island for a few hours. It is mostly just farms and a couple nice views, but it does make you feel like that scene in wedding crashers if you do it right. Half day is all you need, the ferries are fairly punctual but check to make sure as you would not want to get stranded. Not the number 2 thing to do in Jeju by any means, but it is pleasant.
Do catch the performance at the Ma Park on Jeju Island! From horse riding to acrobatics and showmanship, the show is a great family experience for young and old.

Disclaimer: Not a seasoned/experienced hiker. Was done on a cloudy day with a scattered drizzles.I had high expectations for the highest point in South Korea and a highly rated tourist attraction on TripAdvisor but was greatly disappointed by the experience.The reason I am giving a score of 1/5 is because there is a long hike (approximately 3-4 hours one way) with very little to see along the way, with ultimately what I would consider an   okay   view of a   crater lake   up the top. In addition, whilst walking the unpaved bits of the trail (rocks, which account for about half of the trails we walked) you will need to focus hard on walking to ensure you don't slip as it can be quite slippery. This means you don't have the luxury of looking around at the scenery/surroundings while doing the hike.It is not that the view up the top is objectively poor. It is actually decent. it is simply that the effort (3-4 hours one way) to reward (the view up top) ratio is terrible.The group of us hiked up the East trail (Seongpanak) and went down the North trail (Gwaneumsa). The hike down along the North trail provided a handful of views that were decent - better than the East trail.My experience at Mount Hallasan was preceded by Seongsan Ilchulbong the day before which to me provided a much much better experience. The hike was a lot easier and the view was much superior, offering a beautiful view of the Jeju City skyline. I personally would highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong over Mt Hallasan and would recommend against doing Mt Hallasan, unless you are someone that personally loves hiking as an activity anyway.Summary: Long 3-4 hour one-way hike (7-8 hours return) to the summit rewarded with a decent view, with a lot unpaved trail which can be slippery. Not good for people with bad knees, those expecting plenty of beautiful views, and those wanting to enjoy scenery while hiking.

Disclaimer: Everyone has their own tastes, and just because I may not like something, it doesn't mean you won't like it. And even though I might be dismissive and even sarcastic about this attraction, I am not attempting to insult anyone who thought that Jeju's   Mysterious Road   was fun. The fact is, this road would be amazing IF it wasn't swarming with tourists and IF you just happened to find it one day when you were driving around on the stunning back roads of Jeju. Jeju has Korea's best scenic driving, hands down. But this...Here's the deal. Yes, your brain will lie to you about the incline of this road and it will appear as if you are not rolling downhill, which you are. And that's a fun fact about human neurology and perception. My brain also tried to lie to me in order to convince me that the illusion was worth the large, obnoxious crowds of people that clogged the road, the busloads of hyperactive tourists on a conveyor belt from the airport, and the shops set up on either side of the road in order to overcharge them for very average products. Basically, it's a tourist trap. Sure, it has its appeal, but of all the things you could do on Jeju, why would you spend your time doing this?

Didn't think there was anything special about this as compared to other jeju attractions. Mainly a maze which could be completed in an hour, then u ring the bell at the top before making your way out. The kids would probably like that, I saw quite a number of teenagers and families with young children.

Didn't know which restaurant to choose so just picked one which looked busy. We ordered a meal with 2 cuts of meat,   abalone  , stew, egg, and a selection of side dishes, plus a beer and makgeolli for about 60000 won which was reasonable. Staff cooked the meat for us which was helpful. A hearty and delicious meal! Must try when in Jeju!
Didn't expect to see such a good view there, the rock , island, and sea makes perfect scenario. Definitely a spot to visit if visiting Jeju!

Did a soap-making session and had lunch at the Innisfree Jeju House. Building is well-lit and nice and open inside. Soap-making was a fun activity to do with our group, and I was able to make a custom souvenir to bring home. They had a selection of some products to purchase, but was small when comparing to the size of their stores. The lunch caf챕 had many options, and my super food salad was delicious. The caf챕 also offered many drinks and impressively decorated desserts. Directly outside are the tea fields that you can walk through and take pictures in.

Depending on your fitness level, conquering the mountain will take you anywhere between 20 to 50 minutes, the latter with room for many rest breaks. The climb is shorter than you think, however, and very very soon after the second pavilion you reach you will find yourself at the top and before a gorgeous volcanic crater. The views are 360 degrees spectacular and the mountain is a must visit if you come to Jeju, even if you're not there for sunrise or sundown.

Definitely worth a visit, even if you only have a few hours to spare. This attraction my husband and I completed in just over an hour, there is no audio guide but there are informative signs throughout the cave. You return to the start of the cave the same way you came in, so take your time reading the signs but if you are tight on time you can read some of it on the way back. Being a natural cave/tube the floor of the cave is pretty rocky, must wear comfortable shoes. If you are driving around Jeju, and using the rental GPS, the telephone number to type into the gps system is: 7834818
Definitely one of my favorite places in Jeju-do. Beutiful, worth visiting during the sunset. Beautiful view and the hike is quite easy, so good for families with kids as well.
Cute, fun.. there is a place for you a teddy bear museum  Jeju, a nice setting museum and you can see many different teddy bear...

Currently free due to the new status update to one of the new7wonders. Normally it would be 2,000won to visit. The walk is about 1km long and got a bit boring after a while. The lava column at the end was the most interesting thing during the walk.The bus was an easy ride from the Jeju bus station which cost 2,000won and about 50 minutes. The walk from the bus stop to the cave entrance was 2.5km and took about 45min.

Cruise stop. Jeju tour. On the way back we walked through both this and the underground mall. A million oranges and fish stores. Neat to be among the Jeju people going about their day. Try some of the food! But watch out for the guys DRIVING up and down the aisles on mopeds!I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

Couldn't believe that a car museum of such excellence would be found on Jeju Island in South Korea.the large number of cars covered all makes, types and brands and we just loved all the old advertising posters around the museum.The displays outside were also a delight and the museum was not hard to get to by public transport.? We stopped off to watch some of the races on the way back and that is also worth a visit.? They use descendants of the Mongolian ponies, and with their colourful jockeys they made a wonderful display.? The extensive grounds have lots to entertain children as well as a mini golf course in the centre of the race track.? Would definately recommend both destinations.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: Could not expect that it is so huge, need a lot of time to visit all the places. So many different plants, birds, even caves. The whole way is well organized, u just need to follow arrows to see everything step by step.There are several cultures and climates that you can see in bigger size than just normal botanical garden. Jeju culture is represented there a lot as well, so will not regret about missing local features.
Cool Place, great mountain rock formation. Ilchulbong Peak is an hour travel via InterCity Bus #701 from Jeju City Hall cost around 2,050won. There are eateries and souvenir shops nearby.

Considering that the other craters type views Seongsan Ilchulbang (Sunrise Peak) and Hallasan are a ways up, and the seaside formations such as the Yongmeori Coast a slippery path of jumping about, the Sam-Gumburi Crater is nice and leisurely. The one place that seemed wheelchair friendly.It was also less crowded compared to the Seongsan Illchulbang so we really got to enjoy the nice leisurely walk up the small hill to see this crater. If you're a faster walker, you could probably do the whole thing in less than an hour (needless to say, we lazy walkers, took a little more than an hour). If you wanted to just roam about, you could spend a lot more time as well (there are different paths, one that's all stairs, one that is like a ramp, etc.). Anyways, this was probably the only geological tourist attraction that was wheelchair friendly and even seemed to have a few out in the front for rental. The ramp would be a bit steep but at least do-able. A lot of the other sites had either a lot of stairs/walking or way too many people for the elderly or others with bad knees to maneuver well.  Perhaps that's why we saw a number of couples with strollers.That said, this place had one of the most pricy admissions costs that we encountered. It is privately owned or something. So, instead of the usual 1,000-2,000KRW per person, we paid 6,000KRW per person. We were told that the place is nicer during the reed season, but we enjoyed the crater all the same. We'd recommended it to anyone looking to do a Jeju geotourist site without all the hard work.

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. The rocks are just unique, I only saw it in the movie! And it's kind of amazing that you see it in real! I visited here in end April with strong wind and warm sun. If you have time, you can even just stroll along the walkway or sit a bit to have a casual chat with your friends.  Please do expect a lot of tourist and students visits and long queue for toilet. But this is kind of normal for all the unique sight seeing point at Jeju Island. I would recommend this place if you happens to be in this area, and I will skip the waterfalls :)

Come with my little girl, stayed at the hotel besides the beach.It is very hot in jeju in july, 35 degree in the afternoon.  We went to the beach at noon, water is clear and cool and the sand is smooth.Rental of umbrella and shelter at 25000w and 100000w respectively.  It is recommended to bring your own shelter.

Come in the morning to avoid large crowds. The island is so peaceful - different from the Jeju mainland. A return ticket costs 8500W. You can see a lot of pension homes here. I rented a regular bike (10000W) and cycled around the island. The path was relatively easy with only very minimal inclination. It took me about 4-5 hours to cover the whole island, together with stops for photographs and visit to the lighthouse. I did not stop for any food though. By the time I left, which was about 2 pm, a large number of people started arriving. Also, parking at the Seongsanhang Port was 8000W, but I got a 50% discount (not so sure why).

Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

Closed. Our daughter chose this as her number one thing to do while vacationing at Jeju Island. The sign on the door said it had closed down in November 2019. Recommend instead visiting the nearby and very cool Figure Museum or the shooting range or maze. Lots to do here so no worries, you?re going to have a blast visiting Jeju!
Close to the Jeju Loveland Park and worth the stop. Mind boggling how a car moves up a hill, merely a trick of the eye.

Climbing up the iconic Seongsan Ilchulbong, by all means, is not an easy climbHowever, with the refreshing Jeju breeze, the beautiful landscape, and with a little thirst for excitement, it gets you going!The peak! though as you may predict how it would look like to be in the middle of the crater, the wind was so cool and refreshing and the view of Jeju, while going to the sides, makes the climb all worth it!Just too bad there wont be climbs at night to see glittering Jeju but seeing that it's no easy trek, I think it's understandableI am so thankful for the chance to see the sunrise and Jeju from the top!It was a breathtaking experience to see and not to mention, good exercise too!If you head over to Jeju, never miss this iconic place!To me, this is the overall representation of what Jeju has to offer!A promise of fun, beautiful and laidback adventure :)Another side of a Korean holiday experience

Climbing Mt. Halla was a highlight of our trip to South Korea! We climbed up the Eorimok trail and then down the Yeongsil trail. I would recommend going this way because Yeongsil was a lot of stairs - I'd rather do that on the way down than up. Going up probably took us a little over two hours and wasn't too strenuous (though we are in good shape). The trails are very well kept and there are signs all along (in English) showing how far you've gone and how far you have left, and how easy/difficult the next stretch is. The view from the top (even though it wasn't even the top) was unbelievably beautiful! To get there, we hailed a cab from Jeju city. We just told him we wanted to start at Eorimok trail. I would recommend a cab because if you take the bus, you have a pretty large hill to walk up before you even get to the mountain because of where it drops you off. I think the cab cost about 15,000 won. The way home, we were waiting for a bus and then saw a cab so we hailed him. This guy charged us 30,000 won, I think because Jeju city was out of his way. Make sure to bring plenty of water - at least two bottles per person - and snacks.

Climbing Mt Hallasan was absolutely amazing, and I would recommend anyone going to Jeju to attempt a climb. If you?re a bit unsure, make sure to research the trails before-hand and start walking in the morning ? many trails close at 2-3pm.Bring lots of water and snacks (although in typical Korean fashion, there is a 'restaurant' at the 'top', where all the lower trails intersect. Do your research, take a car or taxi to the start of the trail (buses will drop you off much further down the mountain, and you'll have to spend time and energy walking up along a road before you can even start the trail). The views must usually be stunning, but on the day we went, it was covered in cloud/fog. Even so, I would 100% recommend it and I would definitely go again if I went back to Jeju.

Climbing Hallasan Mt. Is one of my bucket list and It's in jeju island thats why i love jeju. The climb is so worth it and really something you can achieve even choosing the most difficult trail. You get close to the nature as you walk through the vast rich forest with different species of trees, Hear the birds singing harmonizing with the crickets chirping, Colorful flowers & sighted a roe deer along the way. The sweats you get from those steep rocky path is nothing when you reach the summit, it was so awesome! witnessing the wonders of nature & learnt some historical events happened many years ago. It is well preserved and well managed. Definitely will come back again to try another trail to see more what hallasan Has to offer. RockNroll!P.S. Going there must wear proper hiking attire that suits the weather condition.You can still try to hike even though you're not that hiking type of person as the trail has pretty nice part. Just be pro and you're good to reach the summit! Have fun!

Climb was ok, first smooth hill roads, then mainly steps to the top. View wemhile climbing was nice. We did not manage to catch the sunrise due to cloudy skies. However, the view of jeju from pre dawn to dawn while climbing up was worth it. U literally see the city lights up before ur eyes.
Cliffs formed by flowing lava and water and wind form dramatic coastline of Jeju island, great place for photos, in sunny days nice walks, don't miss it

Clearly, going in early spring is not the best idea; water's still too cold for swimming but it was perfect to go walking barefoot in the fantastically clear water. It was pleasant to walk into random warm currents while chasing after fish in the shallow water. Our driver said it was the best beach on Jeju but he said that about Hallim Park too so I would not take his word for it.
Clear skies, great sun, not overly hot. Only bad thing is the parking but other then that spend about 2-3 hours here sipping jeju famous harubong tea is definately a luxury!
Clean, plenty of foliage, great views, this is my fave photo spot and overall chill spot in Jeju. You'll find it less crowded than other beaches and a lot less polluted. Best during spring or fall.

Chilshimni Poetry Park is part of Jeju Olle Route 6 that was easy to located as it was along the main road, Namseongjung-ro road where Park sunshine hotel or Poong Gyung Hotel were. It was a free general park with playground where the locals hang out and it can be finish in 30 minutes for less. However, the highlight of the park was the ability to have a clear view Cheonjiyeon waterfalls from a height for free! We spent some time chilling at the table and benches to appreciate the falls. There was also a stairway down to Saeyeongyo bridge. As the park was part of Jeju Olle Route 6, we went out to the main road, Namseongjung-ro road, and followed the orange/blue ribbons to Oedolgae. I have rated this park a 4 stars for the beautiful view of the Cheonjiyeon waterfalls.

Cheonjiyeon, Cheonjeyeon and Jeongbang Falls are all located around Seogwipo, the southern city of Jeju. The first two has very similar names so don't be confused. This one is located nearer to city while CheonjEyeon is located nearer to the Ripley's and Alive Museum to the west. Cheonjiyeon is less majestic than CheonjEyeon. You can actually see 3 falls within Cheonjeyeon. Confused? In other words, visit Cheonjeyeon instead of Cheonjiyeon if you have limited time!

Cheonjiyeon Falls is a peaceful stop for those that want some refreshing time. Unofrtunatelly swimming is not allowed here. Good for a quick visit before visiting the Saeyeongyo Bridge. The nature also is astonishing, a glimpse of tropical nature in Jeju.

Certainly a must-visit destination in Jeju! Soak yourself in the impressive view of this UNESCO heritage site. We came on the first Monday of the month, and unfortunately the paid trail to the peak is closed. Blessing in disguise is that portion of the trail is open free to the public though it only brings us to mid-way - perfect for those who find it too challenging to climb to the top. Don?t miss the women divers show which is on the left trail, at the foot of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Showtimes are 1.30 and 3pm. It?s complimentary. And you can choose to buy and eat fresh abalone at the little restaurant. Overall a truly relaxing and uplifting experience!

Came here in the evening to get dinner as well as to see what Dongmun Market was about.  With ample parking closed to the area, we entered via the night food market side.  The snacks sold here were very un-korean that largely appeals to the young family and the young.The market itself as expected were not all open, yet many stalls were. From Jeju Tangerines to chocolates and other local produce, it is still worth taking a look in the evening if u want to avoid the morning crowd.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This columnar joint was located in South Jeju, and had beautiful sight. This place was good to enjoy view made by wave and sight and sound made by wave and cliff. I didn't expect this area, but there was excellent, And had walking road was good with exotic atmosphere. Very beatutiful place to me.

C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) This museum was meaningful museum of Jeju's anti-Japanese. This museum's outside had monument, square and sculpture about anti-Japanese. The museum was not bigger than I think, but there was operating about 10 years, and had meaningful exhibits. That's good to visit bright attraction in Jeju, but I think this meaningful attraction was good to visit sometimes.

C1 ( 2016.07.12 ) This beach was smaller than I think, but there had good view and fresh air. Many people enjoyed sea bathing, and well managed, I think. The view with beach and cliff was beautiful, and many famous restaurant and cafe was operating. Good beach in Jeju area.
C1 ( 16.07.13 ) There was good beach with many cafe and restaurant. And the lighthouse of horse shape was located. There was one of good beach in Jeju island, I think.

By the time we reached Seongsan mountain, it's already 3.30 pm! On reaching there, and by the look at the mountain, it seems as if there's nothing to enjoy but after my daughter stated that it's world wide attraction, I reluctantly followed them up the 274 meter high mountain with unbelievable thought!But after going uphill, I have another thought!On looking down as I rested after some stairs, the beautiful scenery blaff me! Then as we climbed up stairs after stairs, we took lots of pictures. By the time we reached the top which is the most and satisfying view of sceneries surrounding all sides! I took only a few mountain top scenery because my camera's battery was flat! I sat on top of the mountain and look down at the serenity scene of parts of Jeju Island with the blending on sun setting! Just imagine the feel and satisfaction I gain and feel!But it's time to go down so as we're going down, we enjoyed ourselves by watching the sun going down slowly!

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Brought by our taxi driver/guide to this place since it was were the Korean drama Jewel in the Palace was filmed supposedly. The lady owner gave us a tour of her property with the pigpen where we saw the famous Jeju black pig, the old kitchen and the living/bedroom quarters which was all good but at the end she brought us to a room where we sampled the nice tea and the sales talk began. It was uncomfortable since we specifically told our driver that we don't want to go to any shopping place. Another thing I didn't know that we were supposed to give a donation for the tour and I'm not sure if the 5 dollars I gave for 2 people was enough.

Breathtaking!  Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of Jeju's Crown & Jewel destinations.  This beautiful natural wonder provides awesome 360 degrees views, fresh air and an escape for all the current issues impacting the World.  The hike up there is a lil' bit strenuous, but the result waiting for us at the top is pretty rewarding. If you visit Jeju this trip is a most...enjoy!

Breathtaking view of Jeju at the Peak of Seongsang iichulbong. Is cooling while walking up the Peak during winter. But no regret and is worth to go up the Peak and see the huge crater. Is not difficult to walk up, there is properly staircase and path. Young children and elderly also can walk up. There are CCTV at some of the pitstop.

Book the jeju tour under Rakso travel from the Phillipines. Visited mt halla on dec.31,2015. We were lucky as snow during the week was scant but during our visit, snow is falling and everything transformed to a magical sight.This is the first time my children saw snow falling. However, i noticed that the falling snow are not flakes but more like 'dippin dots' unlike the one i experienced in switzerland.Nevertheless, the moment and the view were enchanting!. Highly recommended!!.
Book a package ticket with hello kitty island at jeju intercity bus terminal with 18,000 won. Take picture indoor and outdoor with different theme of teddy bear... not really must can see.

Best for sunrise. There are well-built boardwalks up to the peak of the extinct volcano. Overran by nature but the shape of the crater is still visible. The view of Jeju from the peak of the mountain is amazing, never fails to disappoint.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Before traveling to Jeju I was unaware that there was a horse show.  Our guide asked us if we wanted to see a horse show and we said ?sure?.  We had no idea what to expect.  It appears that this show caters towards Korean tourists and the show is only in Korean.  However, there was a pamphlet available in English.  I didn?t see any other foreigners in the audience.  The show takes place in a large arena and lasted about an hour.  The seats are covered in case of rain.  The show is supposed to take place during the Mongol invasions of Korea during the 1200s.  They had mock battles, displayed archery skills, performed equestrian vaulting, and a variety of other skills.  I thought that the show was entertaining, well performed, and the Mongolian riders were very talented.  My 3 year old, was a bit scared by the battles.  The horses appeared to be well cared for and healthy.  At the beginning and end of the show you can purchase a carrot to feed to the horses.  I believe that the cost of the show was 18,000 won, but our guide was able to get us a discount.  Overall, I thought that it was fun and would go back.

Been to a lot of caves in my life but these are so interesting as they have been shaped by the lava flow. There are information boards throughout the caves telling you how certain things in the cave were formed from the lava - definitely a must see if you are going to Jeju!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater, Seongeup Folk Village, Oedolgae Rock, and finally Jeongbang Falls. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

Because Jeju is a volcanic island, it doesn?t have too many beaches relative to its 300 km of coastline.  Hamdeok Beach is one of the closest beaches to Jeju City.  It?s also one of the most picturesque in Jeju making it quite crowded when it?s warm enough to go into the water.  Unfortunately when we went there were a lot of seaweed washed up on the sand.  Despite the crowd, the parking lot was quite large and there is a good selection of cafes and restaurants nearby making it a decent visit even if you don?t go into the water.

Beautiful, serene and breathtaking views. A mid-level challenge to hike up and carrying extra water was mandatory in the heat. It is the highest peak in South Korea and the geographical centre of Jeju. A most worthwhile wander.
Beautiful, peaceful, such an amazing experience. First time on jeju and it is def a place you must go and see. Mr. Sung is adorable and kind hearted
Beautiful, haunting, natural. An absolute must if you're based in Jeju city (can be accessed via the city tour bus) and is amazing value for money (just 1,500 won). A definite must.

Beautiful waterfall. I went to all 3 waterfalls in Jeju, and this is the most amazing and my favourite. It's also along the Jeju Olle Trail 6. A short walk from the waterfall, there is a mini waterfall called Sojeonbang waterfall, which also falls into the ocean.

Beautiful thatched-roofed houses, monuments and stories about Jeju that will make you appreciate the island more. Ask your tour guide or whoever works there what is the story about the gates with 3 log sticks. Found the history behind that very intriguing.

Beautiful small island - green hills, lava rocks and small beaches. It's about one hour and a half by bus from Jeju-city to Seongsan ferry terminal (final stop) and 10 minutes by ferry.  We rented ATV to get around the island. The weather changed quickly and suddenly we found ourselves in the middle of the storm. We had a lot of fun riding ATVs through the heavy rain and felt like we are true rangers.  It was too cold to go swimming and by such a weather we couldn't explore the shore caves. So we skip it for the next time.

Beautiful scenery at the top with breathtaking surrounding views of Jeju. Well maintained stairs, although uneven at first because they use the volcanic rocks, Many resting places as you go up. There is a lady at the top who explains the origins of the peak in English, which was a pleasant surprise. Large carpark area, fast food stores and souvenir shops.

beautiful place & good for take 1day visit if you have time in jeju. we take off bus stop prior to entrance and take many picture at the outside of Seongsan Ilchulbong. it has a beautiful beach & flower and horses etc... after that, went inside the hill. we went to the end of cliff that has a show for haenyeo starting time was 1330 & 1530. that has a dance & sing a song before go inside the sea. first time to close view their hard duty as actually jeju still getting many haenyeo woman as i viewed that carrying the orange ball inside the sea. some near coastal and some in the middle of ocean. seem take a long time duty such a hard duty.after that we went to hill of Seongsan. good view but the summit just a half & not easy to identify. but overall view & trail was enjoyable. must see
Beautiful park, great wonderful helpful staff, totally enjoyed it. Must go when in Jeju Island! Recommend for everyone!!

Beautiful location. Relatively easy to get to (just one change from Jeju City Bus Terminal). The park is beautiful and I'd really recommend taking your time and enjoying the scenery as much as possible. The park contains different areas (bonsai, water gardens, caves, animals, cactus) and it's so hard to believe that it's man-made. Loved the diversity here.

Beautiful landscape where we can see ocean from the hill. Transport from Jeju city to here could use taxi, tour or bus. I use bus from Jeju Intercity terminal. Using bus no 701 and went back with bus no. 710-1.

Beautiful indoor gardens with several rooms leading off of main garden with specialized environments. The rooms leading from the main garden that I can recall right now are a tropical plant room with orchids, a fern room, water plant room with lilies and hyacinth, and even a cactus room. It is a large indoor garden with many colorful and unusual plants to see. It was raining the day we were there so we were happy that it was enclosed. There are beautiful Korean and Japanese style gardens, among other types of gardens too, outside. Jeju Island has many beautiful places to visit and this botanical garden was a great excursion for us.
Beautiful beach in jeju, street parking available and is free. nice scenery and good for kids. toilets available to washing off the sands after playing at the beach.

Be sure to visit even if you come to Jeju by only 3-4 days. Climbing is better to start early in the morning. At the beginning, some steep, climb to 1/3 after it enjoyed, leisurely walk along the gentle slope, wooded, narrow mountain road is very cool. Slightly sweating, big mouth breathing, anxious to put lung wash. I think is better shoes for climbing than sneakers because the rocks often.

Be prepared to walk and climb and climb and climb up steps.Not diffcult but quite a way up.Good walking shoes, warm clothing and water (maybe some small snacks too) needed.There r also an different area where u can check out the Jeju women divers.Also check out the local restaurants around this attractions...They serve very good seafood food / BBQ meat.I had  some very good abalone porridge and seafood soup along some BBQ meat.

Basically a market place that sells the usual basic seafood and fruits. Practically all the fruit stalls sell the same things; mango, Jeju mandarin orange, peaches, etc. Do try the peaches if they are in season. They are huge, soft and fragrant.A lot of stalls are selling the same Jeju chocolate, mandarin or Hallabong tea & jam, etc.There are several stores that sell street food like oden, teokbokki, sundae, etc. In fact there is one particular stall that seems to be very famous due to the Korean variety show 'Running Man'. There is a long queue by 5pm; with people waiting to get a table to try all their Korean snack food. The teokbokki, sundae and fried fritters are really good.Do try the Jeju orange ice cream on a stick if you come across them. They are really nice and fragrant; especially on a warm day.

Based on a Malaysian blogger's review, we went over to one of the shops there to savour this renown dish.It was a BAD experience, the black pork sold there tough like wild boar and did not have any distinct tastes.Later on when we met some locals, they advise that locals don't eat there, only tourist who are attracted by the hype of the place.Fortunately, there are many other shops around Jeju City which served better Black Pork., In fact, we had a very good one at Halla Pork Restaurant in nearby Sehwa-ri.

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

Awesome view.I went to hike from Eorimok.i went there by taxi because the bus from Jeju city to Eorimok only operate on weekend Saturday and Sunday.Due to the winter season and I do not wear specific hiking gear, i only hike halfway.Want to hike Hallasan again next time.

Attended the 1st day of the 2014 Jeju Olle Walking Festival, infectious mood with music and performances at various parts of the scenic seaside trek during the full day walk. We climbed up the Dodu-bong, a short hill with a panaromic view of the route, planes taking off from the airport runway and the sea. While it was quite sunny, late afternoon the sea breezes can get quite chilly. However at the end of the trek there were performances and hot local food, so overall it was a satisfying Day 1 of the trek.

At eye level, the short stretch looked like an upward sloping road, but it was actually a 3 degrees downhill slant. A bit out of the way, would not recommend making a trip there unless you're from Jeju-si enroute to Hallasan National Park. Many of the 'mysterious bottle rolling uphill' videos have been posted on youtube in case you want to see the mystery! The real attraction here was the huge iconic black pig family statue. It was detailed and incredible. LOL

At east spot of Jeju. Takes about 1.5 hour bus ride from the intercity bus terminal. Free entrance. Although the peak is only 180 metres, it's still challenging to climb because of the steepness. Very beautiful view along the way. The ocean and the mountain are all visible. Highly recommend.
as you said , our museum is the most fun place stop over during the visit Jejudo.
as you mentioned , teddy bear museum is the one  highly recommend place in Jejudo. have a nice day ^^ thank you

As you are planning to visit jeju and there are not alot of activities there, i recommend you to visit this market. You will see lots of differnt and new things to see, also you can enjoy the food there, so dont miss it

As with everything on Jeju, this is built for tourists. The cave itself is interesting but understand there is nothing but this one section of one cave that you can access. This is not in the least bit adventurous - the cave is lit well all along its length. It's the kindergarten of caves but if you haven't been in a lava tube before then it may be for you. Beware that if you take the bus to the caves, you still have 2.5 km on foot to the cave entrance, though you can flag a cab down if one happens past.  Overall ok, but don't expect to be blown away.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. When we reached Chilshimni Poetry Park (is just beside Park Sunshine hotel), we were lucky to catch a view of  the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top. There was also a resting shelter with table and benches if you want to enjoy the view of the waterfall while having snacks or lunch. Afterwhich, we left the park to the main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was) and headed to Namseong-ro road which was indicated by the blue/orange ribbons for Oedolgae. Along the way, you will pass by몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online) before reaching Hwangwooji coast first (it is a very beautiful coast with a private emerald green pool. Then there was a trail to Oedolgae where was a cliff top that you can view the Saeyeongyo bridge. Oedolgae trail is  free 1 to 2 hours trail and it is not a difficult trail, it is pretty gentle with lots of benches for rest breaks as needed. It has pretty nice coast view. There were fruits and snack sold along the trail where you just need to place 1000won at the basket where you take the fruits/snacks from (there is not one attending to the store). It is based on trust. There were rest rooms outside the trails if needed with food stalls near the free public toilet with toilet paper provided. We need all the trail by foot and there is really no need for a car.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed Jeju Olle Route 6 from Chilshimni Poetry Park (to see the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top) to Oedolgae and happened to see this Hwangwooji coast (probably part of olle route 6) which was my favourite spot of the day. You will walk along Namseong-ro road and passed by 외돌개나라 Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online). I love the place bcos it was like a private pool and it is free. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.? After-which we head to Oedolgae.You can walk there and you do not need a car. Probably a 15 minutes walk from the main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Poong Gyung Hotel or Park sunshine hotel jeju is) and walk in to Namseong-ro road where? 외돌개나라 Hostel is.

As we couldn't enjoy so much autumn scenery in Seoul, Mt Hallasan in Jeju is the best spot to get revenge..haha..it is due to most of leaves are already changed their colour compared to in Seoul. The parking fee is KRW 1000 and we just enjoy the beautiful scenery from the start point of jungle trekking area as we are tired enough to climb the mountain :PThere is free wifi available and some restaurant in case that you need to fill your empty tummy.. :)

As we booked for a tour package in Jeju ofcourse Mt. Hallasan will be on the list. Experiences the thin layer of snow on the park which is perfect for strolling, walk a couple of meters and go back. And yeah visit the museum to see some photo gallery. Its worth to see.

As there are not much railings inside the cave to guide the tourists while walking and steps are uneven, make sure to wear comfortable walking shoes. It is beautiful and a must visit when in Jeju. I joined a tour for this visit as it is quite far from where I stayed. Tourist spots in Jeju are not close to each other and I didnt quite see a lot of public transport the in the area.
As the only show in Jeju (while in Seoul have 3 theatre) so always full. Interesting, Fun & a Must see Show.

As the Haenyeo is unique to Jeju, this museum is dedicated to them and their story. I found it very informative, interesting and of great value to understand the traditions of the island and the long association of these incredible women. Quality displays in Korean and English explain the history and feats of these remarkable women with several outside areas to explore as well. Certainly worth a visit.

As per previous reviewers, we are greeted by a China lady who bring us around the village explaining the history of this village. I admit her stories and sayings are interesting and we learnt more about the old jeju village. After we say no to her products, she left us free to explore the small village. Not a place I will go back but i remembered the stories.

As part of the tour, we had a short stop at dragon head rock, where you can see the head of a dragon naturally carved on a big rock. There is also a small mermaid sculptured on a rock for photo opportunity. This is more of a photo stop. Jeju as an island attraction have plenty of rock formation, volcanic rocks, and shoreline with plenty of rock. Again like all part of Jeju, the place has good breeze and quite comfortable.

As our tour guide said nest stop is the beach... i was wondering how can any beach rival Philippine beaches? But as we get nearer i saw it,,, a hill with a small island... really shaped like an oriental dragon serpent just starting to submerge into the water. It was a sight to behold! so we went down the trail and enter the coastline path... it was so beautiful! the coastline is carved by ancient volcanic eruptions and was smoothened by the waves. it was a 30min walk around the coast line and as we were walking the view just gets better and better. when we turned a corner around 14 minutes in the walk. The best view suddenly came out. no amount of words can describe the rock formations we saw. we felt small beside it. Along the way were many old ladies selling seashells and sea urchins and sea cucumbers for us to taste as sashimi (raw fish) to be downed together with soju(rice wine).These ladies were the famous jeju island deepsea divers. They dive without oxygen tanks. After the walk we were all tongue tied at the beauty of the past 30 minutes. Yongmeori means dragon head coast. and it really took a dragon size breath away from me. Entrance only 6000won (6us$)

As mentioned this place does not get a lot of attention. Today while we were there, were surprised to see a lot of local Korean tourists. From Seogwipo bus terminal (the one near Jeju World Cup Stadium) take bus 702. There is announcement in English. Alight at Sanbangsan. This place is truly nature at it's mightiest, the wind/sea carved walls/cliffs are very different from the rest of Jeju's natural beauty. Entrance fee is 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for child. Take time to enjoy the wind, sunshine and views as you strolled. Along the way, there are old ladies selling fresh seafood and soju. There is a mini theme park next to one of the entrances. There is Viking, trampoline.. A number of stalls selling bbq squids/seafood, mandarin juice, chocolates and mini cakes. Good for the kids to take a few rides. All in all, a good half day spent in nature.

As mentioned in the title, out of the few waterfalls that Jeju have, i think Jeongbang waterfalls is the best one. It?s just a short descent and you can go close to the waterfalls depending how brave you are. You get a good view of the sea as well.

As I rented a car to explore Jeju (highly recommended), we came here a couple of times to enjoy the experience putting the gear at N position and realizing how the car went up the hill.We also tried on the road with a can of beer that also was rolling hill up apparently. It is maybe an optical illusion but when you are there it looks clearly and without any doubt that cars and things go up the road. The kids were amazed and really enjoyed as we also did.Try to avoid the afternoons, as most of the guided tours are here at that time with many buses horning in hurry to repeat the experience several times and many pedestrians around. In the morning the day after it was almost empty !

As I didn't have access to a car and was traveling alone whilst in Jeju I caught the city bus to the national park. This was pretty simple and the bus from the main bus terminal leaves every hour between 9 and 4 (during summer) the journey coat 3100 won. The bus stops at the end of 2 trails to the west of the mountain. (Eorimok Trail, Yeongsil Trail) . Both trails meet in the same place on the mountain and both give a varied, pretty and pleasant  walk up Mt Hallasan . There are toilets and facilities at each of the trail tickets offices which are well maintained. The paths are a mix of steps and decking to help mark the trail clearly. You get great views of the different Oreum's (small volcanoes) these trails do not lead to the summit like the longer trails that start on the east. Ensure you have snacks and plenty of water

As a scuba diver I was very eager to go to this museum and get to know more about the   Jeju Mermaids  . The museums has lots of interesting information about how they live, the risks of their profession, the   team system   they use (I loved this part). If you like the underwater world, I highly recommend a visit to this neat museum.

As a part of our school's field trip program, we went to the one of the known attraction in Jeju-do which is the Jeju mysterious road. While inside of the bus, our tour guide asked the driver to turn the engine off. Our tour guide pointed out that even though the engine is turned off, the bus still continues to move   way up  . But in reality, our bus moved downwards. It was like an optical illusion. For me, this attraction is not that amazing, just a normal road. On a positive note, if you have a lot of time to spend in the island, give it a try and experience the illusion.

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.

Arriving parking lot around 4ish in the morning. It's dark but u can see other people going to same direction, just follow them. I guess we took around half an hour or less to reach the top. I didn't stop for a while because i'm so afraid I will miss the sunrise. Turns out some people arrived the top earlier than us! That day was a bit cloudy but still we can see the beautiful sunrise. It's really amazing experience! Besides I am quite impressive with their trail, well furnish with stones and woods. Quite interesting when u look down to the town, must go for Jeju trip.

Armed with a Jeju Travel Guide map for cruise tourists, on 9 October we walked in the short distance from the Mariner of the Seas to Dongmun Market and the adjoining Jungang underground shopping street.Wandering through both of these sites provides the contrasting opportunity to encounter local culture with its unique produce, sights and smells  as well as standard internationally branded shopping in a bazaar environment.As a short term tourist visitors we 'soaked up' what we saw and, of course, the market with its variety from fruit, vegetables, meat, seafood and food stalls came out on top.It was a rewarding morning off the boat, very easy to undertake.

Apparently, this is what happens when magma cools - it contracts and splits into pentagonal or hexagonal columns. Come here and see for yourself. It only costs 2,000 Won per head unless you are a member of the Korean armed forces (Sergeant or below) in which case you only pay 1,000 Won !We had picture postcard perfect weather during our visit so the photographs ought to look good. This place is along one of Jeju's Olle walking trails, so why not combine a visit here with a good walk ? Why not indeed ?

Another UNESCO site in Jeju, hence there are always a lot of people there. But the climb is actually not that difficult, as the way is nicely paved with stairs, and there are quite a few resting places along the way. Took us around 1 hour to climb up to the peak and down again, but other than climbing up to the peak you can also go down to the seaside to see the diver's performance! Unfortunately, when we were there the sea was rough, so there was no performance.

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

An outdoor gallery of stone sculptures. You can find a lot of Jeju stone icon, as they call it   Grandpa Stone  .  The park is very large,  and not many visitors.  An interesting place worth visiting .

An hour is okay, but if you have the time it might be better to make this 1,5 hour. We combined this with waiting for the Mongolian horse show, which you should not miss and close to this location. You \can also enjoy the beautifull Jeju-beach on the other side of the road.This park is very well maintained. Enjoy the beautifull Bonsai trees, the waterfalls, the flowers, the cave and the statues. The cave was the least exciting to us, but the bonsai trees from over 150 years old were most impressive.

An exhibit which tells you about the life of the women divers of Jeju.  Explains to you their gear, their daily life, their history and their future as a dying trade.  Small compound without any eatery or canteen.  Parking is free.  However, food (mainly seafood) can be found at a nearby wet market to the east of the exhibition.  Driving takes only about 5 mins.

An amazing scenic spot with stunning view. Try to hike along the trail for panoramic view of jeju island and the ocean. If you have limited time, it is not necessary to hike up the peak since the best scenery is blocked by the fences. The descending path has much better scenery that the ascending one! p.s. Try out the hanrabong ice-cream! One of the best way to recharge after hiking

An amazing cave; one of nature's wonder!  Must wear a good pair of walking shoes, and be prepared to walk some distance. Enjoy the strange and mysterious dark tunnels. Dimly lit, but well kept with small platforms and bridges, this UNESCO heritage site is one selling point selling for Jeju! Worth paying a visit.

An absolutely beautiful island that will take you at least half to a full day to properly explore. Rent a bike or a moped and go around the island, stopping for maybe a burger and the location's signature peanut ice cream. With idyllic beaches and spectacular views it is an unforgettable must-visit destination during Jeju.
An absolute must while in Jeju. The walk up is stimulating rather than stressful and the morning views are wonderful. 5,000 won well spent.
An absolute must see in Jeju. An amazing experience. If you have even the slightest interest in geology, this place is a wonder. If you don?t, it may instill an interest.
a-must-see place in jeju-do.easy hike, must try egg puff w/honey. yummy~great view on top of seongsan.

Among the beaches in Korea, this is the one that most resembles Hawaii/Australia/Thailand.  White sands and turquoise waters, with striking black lava rock.  The water is warmer than on the mainland, and it's never been as crowded as Haeundae (in Busan) when I've gone. It's easy to go, even alone, and spend a relaxed afternoon swimming and sunbathing without feeling as though you're ruffling anyone's feathers.  This beach is always the first place on my checklist when I go to Jeju!

Among all the interesting place in Jeju island, i personally love Udo the most. The sky really blue, sea really blue, sand really white, stone really unique, food taste nice...you have it all. I rent a car for the trip in Jeju, therefore i bring the car to Udo by ferry. There were three of us in the car, i feel it worth the ferry ticket. As in Udo, most of the   mini car   or special bike we saw are mostly two person, so unless you rent two, you cant fit in 3 persons. So if you are driving, you have more than 2, bring your car with you. Parking is very easy to find. But please go to the port earlier as buying ticket and finding entrance to board the ferry can be very confusing..so you will need more time.

amazing, fun to visit, u can find anykind of teddy bear, diving teddy, chef teddy, bride and groom teddy. there are many kind of thematic also here, underwater, zoo, kitchen, mini and giant teddy. unfortunately, Tesuem (teddy bear museum) have minim space for us to move and take photo. most off all..one of must-visit when u're in jeju.
Amazing view, one of the nicest place & must visit attraction to discover beauty of jeju.Highly recommended.
Amazing view , the unique of natural for the cliff rock. Must not miss during visited Jeju island. Highly recommended visited during sunny day.

Amazing performance and one of the world's best shows. Can you imagine four guys who dance K-pop style and draw like professional artists in various media to produce an awesome work of art? A lot of talent, training and hard work goes into this kind of production. This is one attraction worth going back to in Jeju.
Amazing beach, arguably the best one in whole Jeju Island. Transparent kayaks are amazing never neen to one before. Is 20,000 KRW for 30 mins. A lot of coffee places around the beach too.

Am not much of an active person who trek but managed to finish the hike.  Pretty easy to find alternative transport instead of cab.   I took a cab to Jeju bus terminal and ask for the bus to seongpanak hallasan.  There are announcements and signboard to alert one for each stop and hence I manage to align at the seongpanak stop with no difficulty.  The trek was okay for the first leg (pre-rest stop) and got more challenging at the final leg.  Not knowing much, realised that most of the hikers have their hiking stick while I was on my own - then again I survive the hike abit limping for the long long hike :). In all, I enjoy the hike with not regrets

Always wanted to see a lava cave and I finally did. It was quite chilly in there so do bring a jacket. And the ceiling is always dripping, so bring an umbrella or raincoat as well. The whole lava tube is about 2.5km long. Pleasant walk on slightly uneven ground. Took bus 701 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Manjanggul Cave. Remember to always press the bus bell for the stop you want to get off! We had a crazy bus driver that just kept on driving until we told him to stop (he didn't even stop to pick up the couple who were waving at the bus stop, bizarre!). Anyway the bus only stop out on the main road, there is still a 2.5km walk to the cave entrance. You can flag down a taxi and it cost 2800 won to the entrance.
Always a joyful climb up the steps to the top and capture a view of the ocean. Awesome view, great exercise! Must do in Jeju

Although we went in the evening when some stalls are closed the place is quite vibrant nonetheless. If you hire a taxi for the day ask the driver to drop you off here. We kind of regretted we didn't as the taxi we hired went overtime and we were a bit tired. We took a bus at 1200 won from Jeju City (500) and it was a long and crowded trip as it had to pass through the airport first. Definitely worth a visit. Nothing much to buy other then tangerines (sold in bags of about 12 to 13) and jeju orange chocolates which you can find in Seoul. You can see the live seafood such as abalone, octopus, fishes etc. Also enjoy food such as gimbap, oden, tteoboki, fried stuff, blood sausages etc. There is also a stall selling orange jam filled cookie in the shape of the stone grandfather. Tastes good when eaten warm.

Although we know how the illusion works, it is still crazy to watch how the bottles or cars go up hill instead of going back. You don't need much time over there though. One mysterious road (according to our touri map there are two) is located right next to the Jeju Lovepark which is interesting and funny. You can go there for 9000 Won, spend about an hour watching love sculptures. :-)

Although this place was packed with tourists, it was my favorite site in jejudo. The rock formations are like Giant's causeway in Ireland with the hexagonal rock formations at different levels. Since we visited right after the hurricane, the waves would cover the lower level of rocks but it was amazing when the water subsided and the rocks were revealed in those amazing shapes!

Although these lava-stone houses with the thatched roofs held on by handmade ropes are a part of Jeju's past, they are still very much occupied today.  You can see the kimchi jars and old-style gates along with satellite dishes attached out back.  This is very much a low-key place, gradual and picturesque...good photo ops and a study in contrasts.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

Although it takes about an hour by bus from Seogwipo hiking up this volcanic peak was one of the highlights of our trip to Jeju.  The hike only takes about an hour round trip, if you go at 1pm or 3 pm they have a women diver's show.  Cost about 2,000 won each and there's many food vendors at the entrance of the park.

Although a very steep hike, this long flight of stairs does include many view points and amazing views at the summit. It was a little cloudy the day we climbed the summit and so did take away from the view a little but nevertheless was still great. I did the climb around  March but it was still very windy, make sure if you go during this time you take something to cover you face/ears if possible as the strong winds make your face go numb with the cold. Would highly recommend to anyone who visits Jeju Island.

Also known as Sunrise Peak, this crater formation can be ascended and descended in about 50 minutes total. Path is uneven and includes lots of stairs, some steep. The viewing platform up top is all stairs, but many places to rest. Very windy. Accessible by bus 201 from the downtown Jeju/Jeju-si bus terminal.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

All these places are being preserved by the government to protect the rich history of Korea and Jeju. The place still has people staying there especially the old and young.The whole   village   is bonding as a big family which anyone has their main job to do. The guide will explain some of the daily things in the past with many preserved items. They will introduce the medicines they use such as honey, horse bone power and 5 taste tea; you also can purchase it.It is good experience.

All the museums were great in jeju island if you're in and out within a hour or so.? But i think i stayed in this automobile museum for at least 3 hours.? My hobby and passion is cars back home jn the States so for any car lover,? this is the place.? From the model T,? old school Bentley and rolls royce to The original 300sl class Mercedes,? you see it all.? A must for car lovers...
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
