review: after visiting the jeju folk village, this was quite smaller, still was easier to visit, shorter distance to drive, so if you stay is short in Jeju, come this village, ou will find all about the korean past culture, just missing big stores and restaurant like the main village have.

After the unpleasant beach at Udo, arriving at Hamdeok beach was a delight. With just a short trip from Jeju city this little beach village is amazing. With many restaurants and cafes along the water, one could spend a nice long day here. The water is nice and clean with showers and changing rooms available nearby.

After the Jeju Love Land, w/c is a X rated (for adults) theme park. Funny, unique, it's a theme park that you will never find in any other country... This is a must visit, if u wanna hve a fun, funny Xperience!Glass castle are full of creative art works made of Glass.. Good for picture taking... Colorful, artistic, imaginative pieces of art. You'll also find here the Glass Shoes of Cinderella & their carousel.

After parking the rental car at Seongsan Harbor, we hopped on the ferry (KRW 1,500) to cross over to Udo. Upon alighting from the ferry at Cheonjinhang Harbor on Udo, we headed to the Udo Tour Bus counter and got ourselves a ticket each (KRW 5,000). The whole tour is conducted in Korean. Not a single hint of English but it was enjoyable. The bus driver was also the tour guide, telling us about the significance of each stop. He'd stop for 20 minutes at each place of interest and if you do not hop back on, fret not, you may hop on the other tour buses. Keep your ticket stub.The whole tour took about 2 hours. The village roads were really interesting. If I visit Jeju again, I would want to stay overnight at Udo. The atmosphere is good, the air is fresh, people are nice.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

After climbing the stairs for the view of the lush, plant-filled centre of the crater, you should definitely walk along part of the black sand beach that arcs around to the ?glass house.? You?ll see some amazing views of Seongsan Ilchubon there, and your pictures won?t be filled with random tourists. There are also bits of sea glass scattered along the shore, shells, and if you walk down the beach far enough, a beautiful, large ledge of lava covered in green moss you can walk on and explore. It was really easy to get to the crater by bus from Jeju-si, and it only took about 75 minutes.

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

After a 1.5-hour drive in the wee hours of a beautiful night, we finally got to the ticket office at 5:50am.... we didn't expect to see this crowd (well, we thought we alone were the crazy ones).... we embarked on the trek saying... not bad!!! After 5 minutes, if was like... pooff!!!! After  another 10 minutes, we were exhausted.. after yet another 5 minutes, it was a killer.... anyways, we made it to the peak at 6:18am and imagine our shock... there was a sea of people up there all set with their cameras...At precisely 6:28, it was there... flaming orange and rising at a speed unmatched (in sunrise). Spectacular!!! Fabulous!!!! Breath-taking!!! Start of a new day... a new way... new hopes... everything positive. It was so worth that strenuous climb.. If you are in Jeju, you gotta do this! Yes, the steps are high and tough, but so doable. We saw some people in ballerina shoes, with their fancy skirts and stockings.. keep the dressing for the yatch tours.. for this one, be ready for a mini hike.

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

Actually originally didn't think to visit this place. But coincidence have the chance, me and my travel partners was shock to see with our own eyes for the water and bottle both run to the upfront road which its was suppose to be opposite way....Make youself drop by to see this amazing effect while you around in Jeju. This place is just very nearby the Sex Museum which we didn't go but passby~

Actually like the other ones, I felt quite surprise at the my first visits since last year 2011. The guide showed me that I were in the bottom of the slope, she pointed to the tree lines along  the side of the road and truly, it has made me believe what she said. Some one said it caused by a natural magnetic power (as above), other one assumed by the trick of the sun's lighting a man nearly lying face down to the road parallel to look forward to the starting point... others wisely poured the water to see the flows .... Of course, our guide has explained the cause but I really do not want to tell you, let's explore by yourself.Definitely, this places is quite appropriated for your family with kids. Aside the road, there are the Korean traditional food shops who sells fried fish ball, rice cake... but they are almost fried into the oil ...This places are really attracted a lot of people from Asia like Chinese, Vietnamese, Indian... I think you might found the similar road like the Jeju Mysterious Road of your own country but the Korean was wise to promote it via the drama film series currently expanding over the Asia.Totally, Jeju is an beautiful island and you should visit one time. With me, I could said   you could make the money by the very simple things

According to legend, Samseung Hyeol is where three demigods emerged from the ground to become the founding fathers of Tamna. This is the basis of the legend, and it is well-known to most Jeju residents. The Tamna kingdom ended in 1404 when it was absorbed by the newly founded Joseon Dynasty. While this rather small shrine is undobutably not THAT ancient, it is a unique site. There is a small museum which shows a video that tells the full legend of Tamna's founding.One plus of this site is the original Dol hareubangs (Grandfather statues) located at the entrance. These statues are unique to Jeju island, with a similar variation in Korea's southern coast. There are only 48 remaining Dol hareubangs left on Jeju-do. These   grandfather   statues were made between 1763-65.

Absolutely stunning location. Great place to sit on the beach and relax while the waterfall sprays you! If you're travelling from Jeju City, make sure you ask for directions before you try and find this waterfall (there are no buses that take you directly there so you have to walk for 15 minutes). - Guess that isn't the waterfall's fault though!

Absolutely stunning beach with great views of Biyangdo Island. Avoid July and August, as it's crowded. Wait for low tide, when the water ebbs quite far and you even take selfie with Stone Man that usually is submerged in the sea. Also great to watch jeju kitesurfing scene i great activity to try out.

Absolutely hike Oedolgae, it's a beautiful coastal walk that is part of an Olle trail. You wind all around a part of the southern coast of Jeju, and can walk as long as you please. Lots of shops and restaurants along the way. The Jeju trails are my favorite attraction on Jeju, definitely walk one! And they're free!
absolutely beautiful cliffs, great views of lava cliffs. a must see for anyone traveling to Jeju Island!only quirk is the small shops selling touristy things.

About half-way between U-do and Jeju City, it's not too difficult to drive to. I would allocate not more than 1 1/2 hours to visit this attraction. The volcanic tunnels are very interesting to see. It rained for several days before our visit, so water was dripping from the cave so it's a good idea to bring a hat. Also wear good shoes. There is plenty of signage that explains the rock formations  English.If you found this review beneficial, please click   helpful.   Thanks.
About 40min drive from jeju it was a park with about 5 areas. Not bad but not amazing. Weather needs to be good or else don't bother. A few good photo's, a few short walks .... it's ok.
About 40 min taxi from the airport. The cave is a must see if you visit Jeju. Walk inside the cave, beutiful lighting. Amazing.

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.

A workout by renting bikes at port to ride around the whole island.  You get to see very different types of sand and beaches, you?ll better realize why they call it mini-jeju island.  The island?s famous peanuts have thin skin and not bitter as your typical peanut skins.  If you have elderly with you, there are golf carts for rent too!

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A visit to Sanbanggulsa Temple was part of one of my favourite day trips in Jeju. It is about an hour west of Seogwipo-si by bus and across the street (albeit a bit of a hike) from Yongmeori Coast which I very highly recommend. Getting to the temple requires a short and easy climb up some stairs where there is a huge golden Buddha, an army of miniature mint-green budhhas, and a gorgeous panoramic view of the ocean and village below. A little further up is another fascinating statue of Buddha in a cave. Overall, this is a nice place to visit and a great opportunity for photography.

A very small traditional village attraction with free guide who can speak Mandarin. Very limited traditional houses to look at. No big deal. The attraction is apparently made famous by a TV series that filmed there. Nothing much to see but the guide took great efforts in explaining about each mini-attraction in the village. We ended up in a hut being given explanations on the local products they were selling (e.g. local honeys, herbal health drinks, horse bone powder, horse creams). We were not forced to buy but given that the tour was free, we were obliged to buy stuff that we could easily find for lower prices as the markets, especially Dongmun Traditional Markets in Jeju City.

A very pretty place with some hiking and climbing but it gets pretty cold with the cold wind blowing as you climb higher.. so, be prepared even if you think March won't be too cold! This place is definitely worth visiting (:For full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/seongsan-ilchulbong-sunrise-peak/

A very lovely place to have some fun with your friends and family, also a very nice place to take lots of pictures. But beware, do not buy your ticket online such as jejupass as they were not recognise in this place. We have to meet the director of the maze to solve this, and thank god she was such a warm person, she let us in for free even though she did not know about jejupass. Highly recommended place in jeju!

a very friendly owner who is a famous personality on Jeju, the area has nice nature surroundings with nice cats:) close to Mangjang cave, don't confuse the location, there are several other mazes on Jeju as well:)
A very entertaining place if you run out of place to visit in Jeju. You can listen to KPOP music from the 90s, sing, dance, DJ, watch a concert......

A vast crater overgrown with a diversity of plants, it's especially unique in autumn when waves of silver grass unfold in front of you. Have a leisure walk up to the main viewing platform, you can embrace the incredible view of Mt. Halla. I'd say it's one of the best scenery of Jeju in autumn!

A trip to Jeju's and S. Korea's highest mountain is a refreshing experience. It is still nice and cool in the morning up here but no snow in late May. Oh well, may plan a winter trip back here for a more thrilling and chilling experience!
A trip made more memorable by great food, great scenery, and a great guide. Highly recommended to anyone who wishes to visit Jeju!??

A traditional market which sells a lot of Jeju Oranges, jeju chocolates, seafoods (e.g. Fish, abalone, etc), pork, orange juices and many more.. the price of the chocolates is the same as any other stores outside. The price of the other products are also reasonable.You can visit this market and have a feel of their largest traditional market in Jeju. I went there with my friend before 8pm but some of the stores had started cleaning and preparing to close the shop. The market is open till 9pm (if I am not wrong).

A traditional market situated in Jeju City that gives you a real and authentic taste of the local lifestyle in Jeju. It sells a wide range of local produce and goods. Buy all your local souvenirs such as hallabong orange, jeju chocolates and snacks here! The shopkeepers will toss in freebies (they call it   service  ) as well! It is near the black pork street which is also worth the visit.
a smmall island about 3.5 km off jeju. same as jeju, it's also a volcano lava island. can take hop-on-hop-off bus to go round the island with very reasonable price

A scenic spot to visit in Jeju. Recommended for travellers who like nature and sightseeing. However, It requires u to climb stairs in order to reach the peak. It might be tough for elderly. Scenery is definitely good with nice view and breezing air.

A really beautiful and picturesque waterfall! I was in awe when I first saw the waterfall and couldn't stop taking pictures of it from all angles. After passing the entrance, you can just follow the steps down and you can already catch an amazing view of the waterfall. Many people, including my family and I, took one step further and went down the rocks so that we could really catch the waterfall right in front of us. It was truly a spectacular view and the waterfall seemed so majestic. Definitely recommend to visit at least once when visiting Jeju!

A quiet valley in an evergreen forest, the place is almost free of foreign tourists and allows one to capture the most tranquil moments of nature. Where cliffs and reflective pools of crystal clear water meet, lined by stones, guarded by trees and filled with crisp air. The sunlight peeking through the trees permeates a serene and mesmerising ambience in the valley. Look out for the stone wells and Rock Shade Residence along the way. The Rock Shade Residence formed from volcanic lava were used by ancient inhabitants of Jeju Island as shelter. It is said that Andeok Valley has water flowing all seasons long.  With such charming beauty, its no wonder Chusa Kim Jeong-hee, a renowned Joseon-era scholar, used to visit here for contemplation and perhaps, inspiration. Spring and fall would be great for light trekking while the cool forest provides the ultimate summer shade. Nearby attractions: O'Sulloc Tea Museum, Camellia Hill and Jungmun Resorts.Trivia: Andeok Valley was also the filming location of historical K-drama   Slave Hunter   (Chuno in Korean)

A quick 20 min ferry ride from Jeju.  We went there on a rainy day, however so did not get the whole experience of Udo.  It looked to be a beautiful and very serene island.  Seafood is good here.  Homemade peanut ice cream was also very good here.A great option for a day trip.

A place to walk, relax, and connect with nature! The Spirited Garden is regarded as one of the world's most beautiful gardens. The entire garden was designed by one man, Mr. Sung, which is quite interesting. The Spirited Garden includes 7 smaller gardens. The Secret Garden, one of the seven small gardens, is a world-class location for business meetings and diverse performance. It has received several awards, including Korea Unique Venue, Green MICE Venue, Jeju Unique Venue, etc. This garden is an unmissable place for those who love nature!

A place not to miss if visit Jeju. Hello Kitty Island is not very big, to complete the whole place plus take photos it takes around 2hrs.The entrance fees was quite reasonable. Can take a short break at their cafe, their cakes are delicious. The public bus stop is very near the museum,just less than 3 mins walk. This place is also near to Alive Museum.
A place for you to amaze how is The jeju island is so beatiuful. and if you one of the korean movie lover, do you know the place is used for one of the famous movie ?
A nice break from the heat, it's nice and cool down there!You can walk 1km, I think we spent about an hour down there total.Really slippery, be careful!One of the coolest things I did in Jeju.

A must-see place when you visit Jeju. It may a bit tiring to climb until the top, but the view is breathtaking. The hiking track also made it easy to climb because they've built a stairs until the peak. Try to visit early in the morning, because around 9 am, the crowd starts to gather, so it may be a little difficult to take a picture without some people intrude in the background. In addition, if the weather forecast is great, try to see the sunrise from the peak. Too bad it's cloudy when we visited, so we didnt try to see the sunrise.

A must-see in Jeju island. During this time of the year, there are pink Azalea blossoms that decorate the mountains. Though the Eojimok trail is the most easiest one, it still took us more than 3 hours. The view along the Yeongsil Trail is particularly memorable. Hiking in Hallasan is a refreshing experience for travelers who would like to explore the essence of Jeju island.

A must visit place when you are visiting Jeju island! The president of this Spirited Garden spent his whole life to establish this place, and you will be surprised after the visit. I enjoyed, learned a lot from his philosophy in this garden. Truly amazing.

A must see when on Jeju Island. The trail to the top is well maintained and well build. Gets a bit steep at some points. If you're going doing the summer, as i did brings som water. It gets very hot and humid.

A must see when in jeju. Jeonbang Waterfall is the only waterfall that falls directly into the ocean. It?s a beautiful sight to see. However, if you are handicapped it is not accessible, as there are stairs. Make sure to wear gym/grip shoes as there are lots of rocks/ slopping hazard. There are also (henyo) female scuba divers that harvest abalone and various seafood that are available to eat nearby. Definitely check it out!
A must see if you are at Jungmun Resort Complex.  The teddy bears are very cute, would have loved to buy more at the gift store...too bad they didn't have tshirts with TBM and Jeju as a souvenir...

A must go place when visiting Jeju-do. Although it was slightly drizzling on that day, there was still quite alot of local and tourists taking the hike. The climb was a smooth one with well laid pathway. Good exercise and a closer touch with nature.View was awesome and air was fresh, really heavenly and relaxing.
A must go place if you are at jeju. Amazing view not only at sunrise, but also for sunset. 4 stars are given instead of 5 because it was too clouded. Otherwise it is prefect.

A must do in Jeju. We hired a taxi driver to take us and it was 2000won a person to enter. We wanted to go for sunrise but there was an extra fee to hire them that early. (If you want to rent a car, make sure you have an international license - it's about 1.5hr from Jeju city) The hike really isn't too bad. It is an incline, and yes there are lots of stairs, but it is do-able. There were plenty of elderly hiking up and lots of places to stop. Beautiful view from up top. Entrance also allows you to go down to the beach and see the women divers and eat fresh catch.

a must climb to catch the view from the top. we were prized with a scenic view of jeju around seongsan after a less than 20 minutes climb. there were alot of eateries and cafes, souvenir stores surrounding seongsan.

A lot of stairs to take, so wear the correct shoes. It would take up to 20 minutes to go up. There are spots to take a rest. View from the top is cool, natural. You would take around 20 minutes on top. Going down is from a different set of stairs. Too many tourists around you :-) something must visit in Jeju.

A group of us, 22 in number, visited South Korea from 13- 20 April, 2014.  One of the highlights of our visit was to Jeju Glass Castle. We went to the Glass Castle on 15 Apri;, 2014.  Glass is a common item we use daily.  But there in the Glass castle, they have made beauty out of something ordinary to something beautiful, works of art actually.  However, many tourists were not aware that there is a trail going round the Castle where you can see more sculptures placed along the trail.  A prominent signpost placed at the entrance to the trail will be helpful.  i am glad my friends and I didn't miss this trail.  To make sure it is not slippery during rainny season, the managements have placed gunny sacks along the trail.  This helps greatly for many of us.So if you are in Jeju, don't miss Jejeu Glass Castle.

A group of 22 of us went to South Korea from 13 - 20 April 2014.  We visited Ecoland Theme Park after our flight from Jeju Island. If you have seern Disneyland  in California, you wil;l; have some idea of what to expect from Ecoland.  However, when we were there, there was this tulip festival.  So we got to see tulips of various colours in a number of places, particularly  near the entrance. Overall, the theme park is an exciting place to visit.  I have one grouse to make. Instead of our turn to get on the bus, the ushers pushed us aside and gave some other tourists (locals I think) preference to get onto the bus.  In all my life, I have never been humiliated this way.  Come on South Korea, especially Ecoland.  You are developed country.  Civilsed society don't treat tourists to your country like that. There were not  many animals in the park.  Safari Park Indonesia beats you flat.  I like tthough the bus driver got the bears to stand to get food thrown to them.
A great variety of exotic trees & flowers, marvellous birds, unusual sculptures,charming waterfalls, traditional symbols of  Jeju Island.  Beautiful inspiring day.
a great understanding on how the women divers work, salute them...but men at Jeju really don't need to work?

A great place to witness how the lava which was erupted centuries ago formed the cliffs. A great place to view sunset as well. The scenery is amazing. However, that's all to it. Will prob take less than 30 mins. Entrance fee cost 2k won per person. If you are driving, do not follow the directions given by GPS. It will bring you to a hotel instead. You should instead drive to the Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and follow the signs there. The carpark is payable as well, albeit a small fee of 1-2k won, depending on the capacity of your vehicle.

A great museum in Jeju with all its collection of computers and video games. Pay around 8 USD and we can enjoy this museum along with playable exhibitions.Not only we can go back in time with old videogames and computers, we can even try to play the latest videogames (Xbox, Playstation etc) and just forget the time while you are inside!Basement is worth to visit if you really want to spend your day playing games.. quite a varsity of collection.Don't forget to try ordering the keyboard waffle... ^^

A good place to start your visit to Jeju, the place is very accessible to people of all ages.  There is a decent spot for photo taking though there is also a stairway down to the beach to marvel at the eroded stones as well as a view of the   Dragon Head   from the other side.  Stairs to the beach not recommended for young kids and elderly with movement issues.  There are cafes nearby like Dunkin Donuts and some hot local titbits.

A good place to go shopping and grab something to eat. You can find from cheap street food to fine dining Jeju traditional restaurant! Also, if you are a fruit lover like me, you can find all kinds of fruits in a reasonable price!
A fun beach, with lots of shallows for swimming and playing in the water.  The park is well kept, there are great coffee shops and restaurants. A very nice sandy beach which is hard to find in Jeju.

A few restaurants piled along the street selling the famous Jeju black pork bbq. Went there twice with 2 different groups. Tried to 2 eateries, menus are identical and so are their prices. The corner restaurant was a better choice (the one opposite the Michelin guided restaurant) It was more airy and the pork quality was better and tastier.

A fantastic view of jeju and sea.... it takes about 40 to 45mins to climb up slowly... remember wear a pair of comfortable shoes to climb all the stairssss   and bring a bottle of water as you can have rest a point to view some scenary and rest your feet and thirst  before continue to climb to the top . You can get a very nice view at the top of the peak.. it quite cold windy as we went in October early morning around 7am seoul time, so do bring a jacket /wind breaker as well.

A fantastic show a must see in Jeju. Lots of laughs and you don't need to understand Korean. We brought our tickets at the show, which was full by the time of opening. They were very talneted actors. The show has been done in numerous countries around the world

A country is evaluated by its culture and only in a province of Jeju in South Korea that we visited many many museum. They are about arts, life and musics. This museum is to introduce the life of the divers in Haenyeo. Very interesting to see the divers reanimated in small scenes very real. The tour guide here could speak English, not very fluently but that?s the best English speaking tour guide in Jeju we?ve met.
A counterpart of Giant?s Causeway. It?s part or along the Olle trail of Jeju. The viewing place is not that big, but if you are visiting Jeju, it is worth visiting.

A bit difficult to find, but a gorgeous location.   The waterfall flows into a small pool and then flows into the sea.  It was pretty crowded when we went, but still worth going.  The rocks are SLIPPERY.  Be careful when moving around on them as we saw a few people fall.  There are a few shops selling snacks and Jeju treats at the top and a proper coffee shop as well.
A beautiful wild landscape worth visiting! If you are lucky, you may also see the women divers that Jeju island is very famous for :)

A beautiful view on top of Seongsan IIchulbong. Plenty of parking. We did this twice in the same day. The first hike (approximately 30 minutes to get to the top, started at 1pm) was extremely foggy and we couldn't see anything. We hiked back down and spent some time on the shore. Once the sun came out we hiked back to the top. There are several stops on the way with spectacular views of Jeju. You can purchase drinks and trinkets from one small shop about half way up. Use the restroom before going up as there is not one on the way. For a family of three to include a 10 year old we took one large bottle of water and a small backpack with some snacks and additional items. Bring a camera as it is absolutely beautiful. On the way we saw several different species of birds and spiders. At the top there are several benches where you can sit and enjoy the view. At the bottom there is a Mcdonalds, an ice cream shop, a souvenir shop, and other small shops. I suggest you try the orange ice drinks...they are great! Overall cost, 5,000 won for two adults and one child. We paid cash. Enjoy!

A beautiful garden to wander through. The museum played us an English 3D film introducing us to the legend of the three demigods who founded Jeju culture. Then we got to see the place where they sprang from the earth, infused with the spirit of the volcano.
A   walkable   mountain for elderly. Enjoyed the very good view at the top on the mountain. I'll be there if I go Jeju again. For sure

8000 KRW for entry, it makes Yeomiji one of the most expensive attractions on Jeju Island. The Italian Garden was a laughing stock and several of its gardens are in a terrible state.The only redeeming attraction of this place is its glass dome which has tropical gardens etc. However, if you are on a short trip in Jeju, you should give this place a miss and go see some real nature outside.

30 mins drive out from Jeju City.  My Wife and Daughter accompanied me on the first 2.5km of the 11.1km yellow route, then they took a short cut back (around 1.2km) to relax at the Korean style picnic tables and visit the carp pond.  I took another 1.5 hrs or so to complete the yellow route, which by the way is circular, not an up and back as reported sometimes previously. I came across plenty of deer, as well as some beautiful birds and flowers.  The first 5km or so has hessian Mats to walk on, which is very peasant, but then it gets a bit muddy and rocky, with a few steep sections.....walking boots or trail shoes are definitely best, although possible in Trainers.  Really enjoyed the hike.

20km return, 8 to 10 hours hiking (be there really early in the morning - around 7-8am), some steep parts, beautiful views and pics, bring water and food (they sell only water and noodles up there) highly recommended for hike lovers. Best thing to do in Jeju!

2 days in Jeju, this was probably the highlight of our trip. We didn't for the sunrise/sunset, but came in the middle of the day.  The place was packed with tourist, but it didn't take away from the beauty of the place.  The is a fairly long climb of a series of stairs to get to the top.  But totally worth it.  On our way down, we were able to catch the women divers head out, which was a nice treat.

1 KM of it is open to tourists. 2000 won entrance fee.Inside is cool and damp, so something warm is highly recommended. Ground is uneven and wet so comfortable walking shoes should be worn. Beautiful lava column located at the very end of the tunnel that's open to tourists.Tip: If you didn't drive, just splurge for a taxi. It looked like we had to take three different buses from Jeju City, which was too tedious. The cab from Jeju City was only about 26K won. Finding a cab for the way back was very difficult though.

*Firstly, don't go here. Instead, go to the 5 Day Market (誘쇱ㅼ쇱 Minsok O-il Jang) in Jeju-si. It is open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27th.*As for Dongmun, the best part is the 몃 (Hoddeok). Along one of the side alleys are these beautiful grandmas (癒몃 Halmeoni) who sell fried rice pastries filled with cinnamon, brown sugar, and nuts (Hoddeok). This is some of the best I've had in Korea. SO delicious. There are three of these stalls in this alley. The best, and oldest one, is furthest inside the market.The bad: vendors are rude and over priced. Their goods are not the highest quality and they know that the tourists don't know how to find better quality.
#3 TRAVEL BLOG DAY 1 JEJU-DO

- Jeju is also known for it's high quality green tea. And here O'Sulloc Tea Museum you can taste many green tea-flavored foods.- Though this place has a   Museum   on its name it's more like tea shop & garden observatory.- Good place for spending time and chat.- Various kinds of  flavored-tea-products are so attractive. you can smell them before you buyTIP:   Innisfree house  (cosmetics shop) is just 1-min away by it's walk.

We went to the beach after hallim park. It was a nice place for my little one to run around as the sand is very soft. Must be a lovely place to relax in summer. The view was beautiful. Lovely cafes along the way and we had nice pizza.
We went to Hallim Park and decided to spend a little time on the beach as it's right next door. Nice place for some fresh air and a quiet walk

We went at the right season when cherry blossom just bloomed and there was a tulip festival in Hallim park. It's beautiful. There are also 2 caves in this park. This is probably the only park that is worth visiting cause it's one of the biggest.

We visited at the beginning of May and it was cold. It also rained when we were on the beach. So could not enjoy the water.However beach is very nice and clean. We had coffee in the coffee shop on beach which gives you nice view of the beach.Its just opposite Hallim park so can be combined.Would nice to spend a warm and sunny day on this beach.

This place is pretty new I believe  it wasn't built 3 years ago when I visited. It was a very enjoyable walk around  the place is pretty huge and in some areas  construction hadn't finished yet. It's basically a really huge garden  lots of really pretty flowers and areas to take photos of. And I believe there are some animal enclosures somewhere in the middle of the park too. Our guide recommended visiting this place and the cave they had here  saying that it was all better than Hallim Park. Though I personally preferred Hallim Park. I found the cave here to be pretty creepy and really dark  best to skip over if you aren't into caves. There's nothing much to see in the cave anyway.

This place is just great! I love Hallim Park especially the caves! they are so mystical!! the parks has most of the natural attractions. The park is huge and you may need to spend hours in it to enjoy everything that they offer. It was so relaxing and very nice.

This is not your traditional beach. It is quite rocky and has limited sand however really spectacular geographical features to see here. Lots of restaurants nearby and also you can visit Hallim park for a few hours. Think this beach would have been better in the height of summer (July- August).

The cause of forming a wonderful Island is a Volcano and hiking to the top of it is a wonderful experience. Roads up to the height of 1100 mtrs are made cautiously and traveler friendly for pleasure with least possibility of an accident. The hiking experience is also beyond the expression in words. I can only say that visiting JEJU and Hallim park are synonyms.
Stopped by this beach after visiting Hallim Park. The sand is soft and the water is turquoise-y. But I have seen better beaches. The unique feature to me is the volcanic rock by the beaches.

Our trip to Hallim Park was wonderful.  If you love nature you will love to explore the well maintained gardens.  I love the garden with Bonsai trees as well as the Cactus garden.  There are caves inside the park too which you can visit.
Near to Hallim Park. Small beach with brown-white sand and black rock. Better to go when low tide so you can walk a few hundred meters into the sea.

I visited Hallim Park confined in a wheelchair. Some ways are not appropiate for a wheelchair. I love gardens and seen a lot. This garden had beautiful displays although some were needing care. The park takes several hours to see. It has different plants from many parts of the word. The Bonsai collection was excellent and one of the best I seen in a botanical garden. Again this particular area was needing help with the trees. They have so many bonsais and only two workers to trim them. And the specimens available were very old.The caves are unique because I do not know any other part in the world you can see a volcanical and calcareal cave together and they have one in here. I had to use crutches to see them and I am not dissapointed of the effort.The local village moved into the park is nice and realistic (we visited a folk village the day before). The animal collection was above average. For kids they have an area to feed love birds and parakeets. Excellent fun. My youngest daughter is 25 and she was a child again in here.

I had a lovely day at Hallim Park. There's a lot to see and do and I spent quite a few hours there. I would recommend this for couple/families/friends wanting a lovely day out in Jeju. It's also right next to the beach!!

Hyeopjae beach is opposite with hallim park. You guys should to visit if you have plans to visit hallim park. This beach unable to swim because there are a lot of stones but you can chill out with nice view. Reach the beach by bus 702 from Jeju intercity  bus station to Hyeojae beach.
Great place to visit after the Hallim Park. The sunset was amazing. Could see the beautiful island from the distance and the sands were soft and white. Looks pretty clean.
A wonderful peaceful place to see flora and fauna and caves. Hallim Park is like a summary of Jeju Island. I loved it!

You could easily do 4-5 hours or even a day trip at Hallim Park. The first part of the gardens is uninspired, but persevere and head to the lava caves, tulip garden (late March/early April), bonsai gardens and beyond.

While we were excited to visit the longest lava cave in Asia, we were very disappointed. There is no path to walk on in the cave except for very limited areas, so this makes for a difficult walk on slipperly and very uneven surfaces with deep puddles everywhere, making it essential to watch your every step rather than enjoying the cave. The lighting in the cave is ridiculous and poorly done, with sparingly placed bright lights aimed at the path rather than on the sides of the cave, so that your eyes are hit with bright lights such that you can't see the actual cave well. The few parts they lit, they added changing colours so you can't actually see the natural colours of the cave. Walking through the 1 km available does not provide much change in the scenery, so it was more an exercise than an interesting exploration.I'd recommend that you visit the caves within Hallim Park, which are much better presented with a safe path to walk on. Although the path throught the three sections of the cave are shorter, you can see much more. Go to Halim Park and skip Manjang Cave.

Went to Hallim Park on the end of September 2015, its a good thing we came at Autumn because the weather was not hot and not too cold either. The leaves were turning orange - just like in the movies. There are several flower parks in the Hallim park, such as flowers park; cactus park; bonsai park; stone cave; bird park; and folk village - where we can stop by for lunch. This place is suitable for families travelling with old ones, since the scenery is beautiful for photo-shoots.

Went for a stroll after visiting Hanna Mountain. The cactus conservatory was impressive and we rounded up that part of Hallim Park with a thirst quenching cactus drink.  Similarly the cool walk into the lava cave, and the connecting limestone cave was particularly enjoyable, taking shelter from the melting sun. Highlight of this trip was feeding of birds inside a bird house.   We purchased their food at the vending machine.  Having them eating out of one's palm brought back fond memories of childhood.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

We visited Hallim Park with my daughter in August. It is very nice place with diversified trees, plants, birds. Convenient infrastructure allowed us to see so many wonderful natural things during three hours. Two old cave are in the park. It is interesting to pass them especially in hot day.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We spent the afternoon at Hallim Park and thoroughly enjoyed the statues, the bonsai garden, the rock sculptures, the caves and the traditional village.  The grasses section appeared to be very dry and in need of some immediate cleaning up.  We were shocked and saddened by what we saw in the bird section.  The ostriches were clearly in distress as they had lost many feathers and were showing signs of balding.  They were enclosed in an area devoid of greenery and appeared to be desperately seeking out food by nipping the air.  The enclosure did not allow for these beautiful birds to run and get the necessary exercise.  Yes, there were food dishes in various locations however they didn't seem to meet the needs of the ostriches.  The peacocks were also showing signs of stress as their plumage was rather thin.  They were enclosed in an area where the floor was of interlocking brick.  This is as far from a natural setting as possible. Our visit ended on a sour note and it is our hope that the dire situation of these birds will be addressed by those in charge.  We highly advise anyone who visits this park to make his/her concerns known as it is the only way to rectify this sad situation.

We spent around 2-3 hours in Hallim Park, and didn't regret it. The flowers and the botanical garden were beautiful, the cave and the water area were also very interesting. Very good opportunities to take photos. As we went in April, we got to enjoy the countless cherry blossoms! My personal highlight was the 300-year old bonsai in the bonsai area. If you're in the area, this is definitely worth a visit. There are several restrooms inside the park, as well as spots where you can buy food at a reasonable price.

We originally got the bus here to go to hallim park. we noticed this beautiful beach and decided to check it out. anyway we ended up staying here all day. Was so nice to be on such soft, yellow sand with clear waters. There was quite a few families with young children which was nice to see all the children playing. Unfortunately there was a digger truck digging the sand while we were there for a few hours and a man kept blowing his whistle at everyone walking near the truck. if it wasnt for this it would have been excellent. Theres shops and restaurants close by and toilet blocks that provide flowing water to wash off but this is cut off around 5 or 6 pm. Sunset here was amazing.

We enjoyed our visit to Hallim Park very much. The parking was easy and ticket was very reasonable. If you like plants, then you are in luck. A lot of plants to see and I loved the lilies among other things. There are rock gardens and lava tubs (underground). Since the park is quite big (bigger than other gardens/parks on the island), you'd never feel crowded. We even had lunch at the on-site restaurant and it was quite good. As noted on the top, this is a great place to spend a few hours while visiting Jeju Island.

We drove by after a visit to Hallim Park and couldn't resist this beautiful place.Totally unprepared for the beach, we went for a short walk around the area. The water was cool & clear. There were many tide pools for the kids to explore and catch crabs, little fishes & shrimp. The weather was perfect.The kids wished that they could stay there all day but we had to leave for another place.We would go back there again when we visit Jeju the next time.

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We came here for the sunset view, because that was the recommendation for this place. But we were disappointed.We reached Jeju via plane around 1pm and went to Hallim park (5min walk to Hyeopjae beach) after check in. After a walk around Hallim park we walk to Hyeopjae Beach for sunset watching. The weather is just nice, no rain, not too hot. The sand beach was covered with plastic material (?), I guess so tourist can walk on it. There was few garbage lying around the beach and it was a bit crowded with people, both local and tourists. The sunset view is not that nice.Again, to be fair, we come from the tropic. The Bornean sunset is probably the best sunset. So for people from the tropics, you can skip this place if you want to. But if you have nothing to do in Jeju, I guess you can come here to relax, after a walk at Hallim Park.To go here: Take bus #710 bound for Hyeopjae beach (or Hallim Park if you want to go there first. It's just 5min walk to Hyeopjae beach).

We arrived in late autumn nearing winter so there were not many flowers on display. We still managed to see chrysanthemum in various colours!! We also managed to spot the peacocks and ostriches. There's a small enclosure for kids (and adults) to see the various birds they have there. We also visited the 2 caves within Hallim Park. There's also a big bonsai area in the park.The park is huge, so allocate about 2 hours to visit everything!

Very skilled young Mongolian horseriders, who perform a small Korean/Mongolian (horse)drama in an hour. Be aware of the showtimes, because I think they only have 4 shows a day. We were too late for the first show and while waiting for the next show we requested the taxidriver to bring and wait for us at Hallim park, which is only 10 minutes away. We also combined this with a short beach vsiit and local brunch at the beautifull Jeju-beach.

This stretch of beach is very near Hallim park. We happened to drive by and stopped for photo taking.There are few restaurants, cafes around the area and a convenient store.The sea is clear and there were lots of people lazing by the beach. Was a short stopover for my family, nice scenery, no harm stopping by for quick foto shoots.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

This Hallim Park is a big area with the palm tree, tulips, cherry blossom, etc.  They also have some cave and near to the sea.  They have Historical Story since 1971 if you see the website.  We need to have 2-3 hours i think to go arround.  When i visit here last week, we still can see the tulips.

This beach is adjecent to GeumNeung Beach - you can walk between them. Hallim Park is also next to it - all are walkable from each other. There are plenty of shops and umbrella rentals, etc. Camping is avaiable at the next door beach. Some areas are not for swimming due to strong currents. Lovely view of a nearby island. You can take the 202 bus from the 5 day market near the airport. Takes about an hour.
There are pretty parts to the garden, but it's definitely not worth the 9,000 won entrance. It's very stereotyped. Hallim Park is far better for a half-day trip and a similar price.

The actual Hyeopjae beach, at the north end of town can get very crowded, but is close to the cafes on the main street. Personally we prefer the Geunmung beach end which is to the south, just past the Hallim park entrance.Both beaches are stunning with turquoise water and great views out to the island. The beaches shelve very gently which makes them great for kids. Geunmung particularly is awesome for the kids as it has little bays and rock pools too.
Quite windy, nearby Hallim Park and HyeopJae beach. Camping available. Showers with cold water for 2000 won. Foot washing station. Small convenience store.
Part of Hallim Park. Your entrance fee to the park grants access to this site. Nothing special, but already included, so check it out. Easy to go thru, even for the older less mobile people.
Near to Hallim Park. Small beach with brown-white sand and black rock. Better to go when low tide The main beach is usually filled with many tourist, but they have umbrellas and chairs.

My only concern with Hallim Park is the condition of some of the animals they have there. The 'cages' or 'presentation units' seem quite small for some of them, and some of the bigger birds didn't seem particularly happy. I don't want to give this an 'average' review because the caves are incredibly unique, the diverse array of trees and plants is also very special. But full disclosure, this place may not be for everyone.

My husband and I were staying in the Hallim area and our taxi driver mistakenly took us to Hallim Park. Especially since it was a bit chilly and an overcast day, the beautiful green houses and occasionally covered areas were a nice break from the weather. The park itself is nothing overly spectacular, but it has a little bit of everything with a nice mix of Jeju style to your typical botanical gardens type park. Plants, flowers, animals, exhibits, and fun!

Me and my husband visited Hallim Park, the beach just outside the park is beautiful so make sure to allow some time to check it out. The park itself consists of about 7-8 different theme subsessions. It was a lot bigger than I expected. The park was very well signed and designed with lots attention to details. Of cause it is not comparable to the natural beauty of Jeju but for a man made park, it is a great choice for an outing with family for 2 hours.

Love Hallim Park! My expectation was a quick walk around an outdoor park, but it was so much more! Easily taking an entire day if you want it to, you can meander through under ground lava tubes, fruit orchards, small animal zoos, bonsai tree forests, etc.! Highly recommended.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe
It's very near Hallim Park so check it out if you are also going to Hallim Park. Nice and clean beach, and there's a small island directly opposite it.

It was a rainy day when we went to this beach after visiting the Hallim park, end of october. It was however a very nice experience, the sand is white and contrast nicely with the black rocks that you can see at low tide. The view on the island makes the picture even nicer.

It was a nice walk around Hallim Park especially if you like Bonsai trees, folk Village and more...We had a great walk aroundthe area and the weather was so freshly cold?. Went to the caves was also interesting. Beautiful garden. A place to come back. I like to put more pictures but I could only put 10 of them.

It was a lovely trip in Hallim Park, it has many beautiful views to take photos of.It?s so big we spent 4 hours to finish it, and after that we went to Hyeopjae beach which is 5 minutes away from there. However, I was disappointed because of there was one restaurant and it only serves Korean food.

If you really have a short time available at Jeju and that you want to have a glimpse of everything, Hallim Park may be your solution.  In there comprises of a tiny folk village, two lava tubes of smaller scale, water park, beautiful gardens for you to enjoy for a few hours.  One couldn't admire the courage of Mr Song who spent 40 years of his life developing Hallim Park from NOTHING.  He literally sweated & toiled through the barren rock into something magical that's been visited by dignitaries around the world.  For someone like myself who came from New Zealand, natural green is something that I have taken for granted but one would have to give Mr Sung encore for the grand vision that he did, to build a tourist attraction for Jeju when tourism wasn't a happening thing just yet.  Just like from the movie, Field of Dreams, if you build it, people will most definitely come!
If you only have one day in Jeju, come to Hallim Park because they have everything in one place! Caves, butterfly garden, flower garden, birds area, mimic folk village and so on.

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

I was not sure what to expect when we went to Hallim Park, but we really enjoyed it. It's a really nice walk, with flowers, statues waterfalls, caves and animals. It's nice to get away from the city noises if you have been on the mainland for a while. It's not a place you can spend an entire day, and for us was a bit of a trek to get there so make sure you plan your day to only be there a couple of hours.

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

Hamdeok beach is just so beautiful. It offers you black rocks, white sand, and breathtaking views. It was our first destination for the day after we landed in Jeju. I found the beach quite peaceful and calm. It is very near to Hallim park. Just took us about 2 mins to reach the park by a car. I wish we could spend some more time at the beach but we had to rush to our next destination. Good place to stop by and click some nice pics. Good luck!!! :)

Hallim Park, located western 33km away from Jeju City and west of Mt. Hallasan along the beach in Hallimeup, is one of the most popular tourist spots on Jeju Island. It faces the pleasant scenery of Biyangdo Island, Hyeopjae Beach and Geumneung Beach. The park was established on barren land in Hyeopjaeri, Hallimeup, and covered with tons of earth and began planting assorted subtropical plants in early 1971.

Hallim Park was definitely one of my favourite spots in Jeju.There were so many different areas to visit within the park and so much to do and see. Of course, I went in May and the weather was superb. Bright and sunny with clear blue skies.I liked that there was a bit of everything to see and do here. Do take note that it can get quite chilly in the underground lava tubes, so bring a jacket when you go in. Don't say you weren't warned! Pleasantly surprised to see peacocks, some were even let loose and just strolling around us like it was the most normal thing on earth.

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.
Hallim Park look older , inside not much fun , and tickets expensive too , inside some area was not clean !

Hallim Park isn't worth making a special journey to go and see. The gardens and varying different areas don't have anything especially interest to see. The animals kept along side the plants are kept in cramped dirty cages and look awful. The tulip garden was pretty, as was were the bonsai trees.

Hallim Park is so big, we didn't even get to see everything. Spend at least 3 hours here (I think). That should be enough time. I loved the caves, the bonsai garden, the cactus garden, the cherry blossoms, and the tulips festival! Lovely park to visit.

Hallim Park is really a variety of interesting elements of Jeju Island rolled into one. The cave located within Hallim park is one of the main attractions. Other attractions include a multitude of gardens, some animal exhibits, and even a small recreated folk village.If you have more than 3-4 days on Jeju island, I would highly recommend Hallim Park. It can be combined with the excellent Hyopjae Beach located close by. Great day for families. If you are staying less than 3 days, it would probably be best to focus on the main natural attractions Jeju Island is so famous for.I enjoyed exploring the park, taking some pictures with my wife, and then relaxing at the beach.

Hallim park is quite big park and there are many things inside. Tickets 10,000won. Sightseeing times around 1 and half hours. On April has tulips festival in park. There's different flowers in each months. From bus terminal take bus no 702 (1 and half hours) for reach there. Hallim park fits with everyone.

Hallim Park is quite a beautiful park. There are so many things to see, and the flora is really quite spectacular; however, the living conditions of the animals in the park killed the whole experience for us. The turtles are in aquariums that are much too small, and the aquariums don't contain any kind of natural vegetation for the turtles. In fact, only a few turtles had only a single rock in their containers. If that wasn't depressing enough, the living conditions of the peacocks were, quite simply, inhumane. Although some lucky peacocks got to roam around in an area that was relatively open, most of the peacocks were living in small enclosures and sharing those enclosures with up to 13 other peacocks. There was hardly enough room for them to move around, and the birds seemed to be living in quite stressful conditions.  Then, there were the ostriches. All of the ostriches we saw had a terrible looking skin condition, and most of them were going bald. Compared to the flora in the park, it just seemed like the park put no effort into properly caring for the animals at all. If Hallim Park would put a little more effort into making sure their animals are properly cared for and provide better living conditions for the animals, I would recommend going to this place. However, with the current living conditions of the animals, I absolutely cannot recommend anyone go to this place.

Hallim Park is privately run, which would explain the cost, which is 5x the cost of entrance to Sunrise Peak, a must-do in Jeju.There are many parts to explore within the park. The most interesting sections to me was the albino peacock enclosure and the rapeseed flower garden. The cherry trees at the cherry blossom section were okay (we went during the cherry blossom festival) but why would u need to pay for that when the rest if the island (and Seoul as well) is full of cherry blossom trees.The tropical plants, wildflower and grass garden section were disappointing. There were lots of potted plants which looked unhealthy and unkempt. I really couldn't tell if the garden was supposed to be manicured or wild.Overall, I think the park is quite passable. I wouldn't visit it again, nor would I strongly recommend it to a friend.
Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection.An hour is okay

Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection. There's an extensive range of bonsai trees at display, some of them are over 300 years old. To those unfamiliar with bonsai trees, they may just be miniature trees; but to those who know the value of these works of art, these bonsai trees are literally priceless. In fact, it's almost unbelievable how openly accessible these trees are to the guests, considering their value and need for extreme care.If you're planning on visiting, briefly study the artistry before your trip to enhance the enjoyment. This is a one-of-a-kind collection.

Hallim Park is one of the best distractions on the island. It is not just another roadside attraction. It is a botanist dream gone wild. You will see everything in this huge park. All of it captures the beauty of nature. The park seems to go on for ever and you're teated to new wonders at every bend in the path. And if that's not enough it is located right across the street from the beach.Hallim Park is great for every age group. It is very convenient to Jeju City.Take a break and take a drive out to Hallim Park, you won't be disappointed.

Hallim Park is located at the West part of Jeju island, approximately 20 minutes drive from Jeju City. The park is pretty large as it has a wide range of gardens (cactus, bird park, flowers) and it also has a couple of lava caverns. The park does not have spectacular sites but it is a great and cozy place to spend time especially for families. Do wear comfortable shoes.

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim Park is huge and divided into various sections. You can spend almost a day slowly strolling through the different sections for plants, animals, cactus and you can even visit underground caves. You can also visit a very small old village modelled after the olden days of Korea. It?s a place suitable for all families with kids or senior citizens. The entry ticket is on the expensive side for Jeju.

Hallim Park is a jack of all trades but a master of none. It is rather unusual to find a mini bird park, caves and gardens altogether in the same place (but not all of them were stunning). Some of the vegetation were not well maintained. That said, if you enjoy viewing cherry blossoms and tulips, this is your chance. When we went last week, the cherry blossoms and tulips were in full bloom and they were absolutely a wonderful sight. We were hoping to see cherry blossoms in Jeju and didn't know we will catch them right here at Hallim Park. You can miss everything else, but don't miss these seasonal flowers.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves
Hallim park has it all. It has nice gardens, lava caves, birds, bonsai garden etc. It is easy to reach by public transport and is a pleasure to visit.We really enjoyed this park.

Hallim Park has everything you would want to see. It has a big and beautiful flower garden, stone and bonsai garden, caves you can explore, a folk village, and a wonderful cactus garden.  It also has a bird garden and reptiles in cages.  You can spend at least half a day exploring everything.

Hallim Park has a mixed big of attractions --- from folk village, lava cave to bonsai and tropical gardens.  It is worth spending a couple of hours exploring.......many nice spots for taking pictures around the park........beware though, each of the attraction is not very spectacular or unique, but the park just gives a sense of the essentials in Jeju in one place

Hallim Park features an extremely interesting cave complex quite unique as it has been dug by lava, a traditional Korean village, beautiful waterfalls, a bonsai garden and a section with creative sculptures. The price is very affordable and you can also visit the beautiful beach opposite the park while you're there. Worth a visit if you have spare time on your hands as it is quite far from the main attractions.

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The entrance fee might be a little expensive at KRW 10,000, it's money well spent.I wasn't expecting much and thought it was just another park. Hallim Park proved me wrong. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.
