Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

Hiking up Mt Hallasan was such an incredible adventure - you really can't experience the island for what it is without giving it a go. The vegetation on the volcano changes as you get higher, ranging from lush dark-green forests and pines, to beautifully unusual flowers and scrub as you get closer to the summit. There are several trails up the mountain, but only two reach the summit - Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa. Seongpanak is the easiest, but is a long trail (19.2km return), whereas Gwaneumsa is one of the most scenic. The views from the summit really are breathtaking, and quite unusual if you have never hiked up a volcano before. Hiking up Hallasan was a great way to experience South Korea's natural beauty.

Hiked to the top of Hallasan yesterday morning through the Gwanmeusan Trail - started at about 7:10am and were back in our car at 2:30pm - so this start and finish time includes breaks, and you'll need them even if you are in okay or good shape. It was a bit disappointing to see the majority of water bodies in the mountain are dry at the moment - just a few ponds on the early parts of the trail, and the crater lake at the summit, which we expected would be much deeper. The trail has a combination of dirt, rocks, and steps/bridges. I wish the steps and parts of the trail didn't include so many sharp rocks - your feet WILL feel them! We did the hike in running shoes because we don't have hiking boots here. I can see the climb being a lot easier with hiking shoes. Some parts of the trail are very steep so if you have serious knee problems, I don't think this is the trail for you. Do bring lots of water and snacks - we had two liters of water for each of us and I still think my husband got dehydrated rather badly. There is really nothing to eat on the trails so bring snacks. Visibility yesterday wasn't great - pollution has been pretty high in Jeju the past couple of days - but it's still a GREAT, BEAUTIFUL view from the top. I loved all the flowers you see growing in the rocky sides of the mountain in the last third of the trail. Very happy I did it and it's a great hike, but there is not a lot to see before you get to the top. We went down the same trail, so a total of 17.4kms. It'd be interesting to see what the other trails are like, but I don't think I need to summit again.

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!

For a rather expensive entrance fee of KRW9,000, was somewhat disappointed with what it offered. Basically, the park is divided into 2 main areas, the inner garden and the outdoor garden. The inner garden is essentially the large glasshouse, with different sections of the glasshouse each housing a different theme, i.e. cactus garden, flower garden, aquatic garden, etc. In the centre of the glasshouse, you can take the lift / stairs to the top, where you can get a panoramic view of the entire estate. The sight was rather impressive, but the glasshouse did not seem to be maintained well. The outdoor garden is basically the land around the glasshouse. It is divided into various gardens with different themes (i.e. Korean, Japanese, etc.). In general, they were rather uninspiring and gimmicky. The French Garden was ok, but like the rest of the park, didn't seem to be maintained very well.There is a train that goes round the garden but when we tried to board it, we were told that we needed another ticket. Quite disappointing after having paid a hefty entrance fee. We decided to just walk instead.All in all, the park seems past its prime, and maintenance could have been better. I'd imagine that it was quite grand when it was first built.. especially the glasshouse.

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.
Fare was expensive but nothing to see inside almost flower and tree ,some place was not very clean ..

But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. Eventhough going there during late autumn may not be able to see nice flowers blooming, can still see a very peaceful scenery especially sunset within the crater. Very beautiful sunset.

Didn't have any high expectation when visiting this spot after the waterfalls. Compare to Jeongbang waterfall, this place is much more worth for a visit as it surrounded with cherry flowers. It will definitely a nice view when full blossom of cherry flowers. By the time we visit Ecoland, it's already 4pm so  time limited as it closes at 5 pm!We took a long train that stop at every 4 places of visiting.In the first stop, we went through attraction on beautiful scenery and artistic work and went to another second stops to wait for the train. big enough & diff topic in park. you could see the flower, bird, cave etc,,,,not too crowded when i visited, good place for spending time
Beautiful place, big and many kinds of strees, flowers, stones, bird, cave...And the old town for Dechangkum film to stay here before

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At Hallim park, there are a few lava caves that are interesting, and very cool (temperature).  The flower gardens are very nice.  The bonsai garden has trees that date to 300 years ago.  They are constantly trimmed to keep them small.  There is a restaurant at the entrance, and a rest area with a gift shop in the center of the park.

Apart from the waterfall there are many beautiful shots you can take including the trees which have beautiful flowers, a bridge overlooking a stream, a river crossing with many ?square steps? (don?t know how to nest describe it), etc. Apparently this opens till night as well and I heard the night scenes are beautiful as well. Worth a stop.

An hour is okay, but if you have the time it might be better to make this 1,5 hour. We combined this with waiting for the Mongolian horse show, which you should not miss and close to this location. You \can also enjoy the beautifull Jeju-beach on the other side of the road.This park is very well maintained. Enjoy the beautifull Bonsai trees, the waterfalls, the flowers, the cave and the statues. The cave was the least exciting to us, but the bonsai trees from over 150 years old were most impressive.

Although we visited this park after the flower blossom but the park was still beautiful with many tree. I really like the tunnel, it was amazing when the sunshine went through the leave and we could see the sunshine clearly.

To see this waterfall, you had to go thru the park, which had other monuments, trees, and flowers to admire...worth checking even in winter.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

A pleasant theme park with train rides around 4 stations. As it's summer, can see entire fields of flowers.Lots of man made structures and buildings for educational purposes.But does not really fit in its Eco Land theme and can be too crowded in weekends

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

A larger version of Bontanic Gardens. Provide rental of prams for babies/ toddlers. The weather was good when I was there, hands nice and relaxing tour. They have cactus, flowers, plants, water park, caves, birds etc
A great variety of exotic trees & flowers, marvellous birds, unusual sculptures,charming waterfalls, traditional symbols of  Jeju Island.  Beautiful inspiring day.

30 mins drive out from Jeju City.  My Wife and Daughter accompanied me on the first 2.5km of the 11.1km yellow route, then they took a short cut back (around 1.2km) to relax at the Korean style picnic tables and visit the carp pond.  I took another 1.5 hrs or so to complete the yellow route, which by the way is circular, not an up and back as reported sometimes previously. I came across plenty of deer, as well as some beautiful birds and flowers.  The first 5km or so has hessian Mats to walk on, which is very peasant, but then it gets a bit muddy and rocky, with a few steep sections.....walking boots or trail shoes are definitely best, although possible in Trainers.  Really enjoyed the hike.
You pass the Maze Park when you head towards the Lava Cave. My mum and I went to the park after the cave on our way back up to the main road to catch the bus. It was a fun way to kill some time.

You need to pay to climb up and stop at the observatory area allow you to capture a nice view of the open sea. There's only a temple at the top of the track and when i went there it was closed. Not worth to climb up until the cave/temple.
you have to walk 2km into the cave and it is cold! Nice feeling and nice view too~ bring your own umbrella as I went when raining.
You have to be prepared as we were not warned that the cave could be very cold.  The one kilometer lava tube is fascinating that one can learn all about lava terminologies.
Worth the walk to see the cave and also get photos of the ocean from the top. ? Be prepared for a few stairs to get to the top.
Wished they opened more of the cave for public viewing though! It was very well preserved and maintained. A really long walk to and fro. My favourite attraction in jeju by a mile.
While it rained most of the weekend.  There was still traffic to and from the caves and the sights we great

When the temperature reaches 40 degrees Celsius outside you must visit this cave for a good cool down. The cave formation and geo qualities are one of the finest to find. If you are into nature and its spectacular formations definitely go.

What a quirky little place to visit! Just wish I had got my international drivers license before we left Australia though because then I would have been able to drive one of the fun little 3-wheel vehicles to get around the island. A short ferry trip from Jeju Island and then a bus trip around showed us the sights. A must-do is to get off the bus at the first stop and explore the 2 caves down on the beach - stunning and quite a spiritual experience. Absolutely loved our visit to this little island!

Went with my son and husband on a very hot day! Park well laid out with several drink food and shade stops on way round! We spent a few hours to see it all! Caves were a highlight - very interesting and cool!! Reptiles and birds ok - not my thing! Enjoyed water area especially cold showers we could stand under :-)) overall a good place to visit and see a range of sights! Easy to get to on main coastal bus route Enjoy

Went there after the manjang cave. It is very near. About less than 5 mins drive away. Admission: 2000 wonOur taxi driver went in with us and walked us through the maze amazingly fast! Actually there is a some hints along the way and arrows to point you to the correct direction if you can find it :DA fun way to spend your time if you are coming here in groups :)
Well maintained. It is basically a km long walk into a cave (which is created by lava). Some structures inside from the lava. But otherwise nothing interesting. It is cold in there so be prepared.
Well I'm a geology lover so of course Manjanggul cave was a priority to visit. Located in a nice place of course underground but it was so interesting.

We were taken to Manjanggul lava Cave as part of a day tour. I've never been in one before and this was pretty neat. Comfy shoes are a must. The feeling under your feet is a slippery one and one of many uneven ridges. The cave is dimly lit which does give it atmosphere but does pose problems if you are unsteady on your feet. The 1km tube takes about 25 mins to walk to the middle of where the volcano erupted. You can't go any further in. We thoroughly enjoy this fab experience and would highly recommend it. It is not suitable for people in wheelchairs or strollers. There are lots of information boards through out the lava tube giving you lots of nformation. The coloured lighting adds to highlight the different textures and forms of the rocks.

We went to explore this lava cave made by erupted volcano and it was spectacular. It has the consistent temperature throughout the whole year with 11-21 degree celsius with awesome looking columns. Never forget this cave.!

we went on a rainy day & late (about 5pm) which they close at 7pm. many area closed due to our late entry but at least we got a 20% discount for the tickets. tulips are beautiful. the caves inside are nice too (good to get some shade from the rain). but pity I didn't manage to visit the cherry blossom garden because it was near to 7pm already which the cherry blossom garden is supposed to be the last stop.

We went in Jun and there were hardly any flowers. Mainly statues. Nothing much in the cave. Just like a normal park with a small man-made waterfall. Entrance fees not cheap  too. Don't waste your time !
We went during the spring festival where we had free entry to the caves.It was really amazing and with lots of details so a guide is not needed and you can enjoy at your own pace.

We went at the right season when cherry blossom just bloomed and there was a tulip festival in Hallim park. It's beautiful. There are also 2 caves in this park. This is probably the only park that is worth visiting cause it's one of the biggest.
We went as part of the Yeha Tour to the west. Bit hurried but ok.Few things are not different from any other good park but the lava cave tunnel is special here.

We was surprised to see cave cafe because we asked our driver to go to O Sulloc Tea Museum but he took us to this place. We paid 5000 krw for cafe beverages and we choose green tea ice cream which the most milky and light tea ice cream ever. Love the cold and dampness in the cave but the museum was dissaponting coz no english translations how you expect us to read hangul

review: We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.

We travelled here by bus and got completely soaking wet walking the 20 minutes from the main road to the cave. Unfortunately it wasn't worth the soaking! It was pretty boring and after 30 minutes walk up and down we were out in the ran again.I would only recommended visiting if you have a thing for geology or if you have a car and happen to be passing by.

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.
We stumble upon this beach enroute to the caves. We didnt regret it a bit. The view is stunning and one of the most beautiful beach we have ever seen.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.

We reached the cave 45 minutes before closing hour and had to walk really fast in order to reach the end of the cave to see the Lava tubes. Many friends told us it's a must visit in jeju.  But my Cousin and I were disappointed as we felt it's nothing fascinating. Better time could be spent in other attractions such as the sunrise peak and Teddy bear museum.
We loved walking throughout the cave and having the experience of walking on something that was once lava.  It is cheap and impressive.  Check out the worlds largest lava stack.

We loved the park and spent about three hours. The cherry blossom and canola fields were the best as they were in full bloom. My little one loved the bird park and we even spotted a few peacocks roaming free in the park. The tulips were pretty but nothing extraordinary. We did not explore the caves and the hits.

We love caverns and Manjanggul did not dissapoint. It is a good length and the world's tallest lava column at the end. They send students from Korea on field trips to learn about it so it is important to local history.There is a store and restaurant onsite  as well as a visitor center.  You can get coffee and snacks at the shop too. Well worth the buck to visit. It was 1000won or 2000won which is $1 or $2.
We highly enjoyed visiting the Songaksan and its temples especially the one within a cave after climbing some stairs up!

We finally got a good clear day.Yesterday at Sunrise Mountain we had been in the clouds.  Some nice views down the coast. Not a terrible tough or long hike to get to the end of the trail with a small temple cave. Number of mostly coffee shops at the bottom and bathroom facilities.
We enjoyed walking until the end point.It is recommended during summer since inside the cave is cool ..
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

We caught the ferry over to the island (remember your passport or other form of photo ID) and hired a two person battery operated bike which was great fun.   Hired for 2 hours which was ok but if you want to spend longer at each stop then I would recommend at least 3 hours.   We went all around the island.  We stopped the longest at a small village where you can go down some steps to the beach and go and investigate a large cave.   There was an outdoor cafe on the beach serving fish -  very busy.  Can't remember the name of the village but it was towards the end of our circuit.  Definately a good weather day activity.

Walking through this garden park is very peaceful and relaxing. There is a cool cave feature so you get to also go into caves. The captive birds are in small enclosures and the peacocks look like there tail feathers have been pulled. Also there is a white sand beach walk across the street after you are done the park. Taxi from Ramada Plaza was 26000 wan. Bus ride home was 3000 wan and took about an hour on the 702.

Visited the cave cafe only. Due to rain we unable to cover the entire place. Limited choice of drinks: Organic Green Tea Latte Coffee Latte & Americano - Krw6000-8000/cup. Serve only rice cakes with filling (black sesame green beans & red bean) Krw6000/packet. Nicely decorated with luminous lights and some cartoons character.

review: Visited many caves in different countries. this one was formed from flowing volcanic lava instead of the usual subterranean water hundreds of thousand of years ago.
Visited mainly to see the lava caves. Walked past the bird enclosure on the way out and was shocked to see the crowded small bare enclosures they are kept in.

Visited during Dec. The place is nice and cool. Do put on some thick coat or rain coat before there as there will be water dripping on your head. There is bat in the cave. Do not bring a stroller as the road inside the cave is very uneven. Do bring touch light along during your visit as the light inside the cave is not so bright.

Very pretty and not too taxing walk to add to any outings on Jeju. Our day was a little foggy but the view was still amazing with the Spring growth just starting to show. Lots of other attractions in the near vicinity makes it a good spot to include in a day out. The short but steep hike up to the 'temple in a cave' provides some lovely views on a good day and there are several other attractions at the base of the walk including the Big Golden Buddha temples tea shops the Dutch ship and rock walks. Enjoyable.
Very interesting! I learned a lot. The experience made for some great photos. It was also very cool inside the cave which was a pleasant break from the heat.
Very interesting Mother Nature Creation.It is cold in the cave so bring extra clothing along.Be careful of the uneven ground.Experience the creation yourself.. =D
Very impressive bonsai tree collection. Interesting underground caves with both lava and lime. Not crowded.

Very educational and interesting. How the cave was formed and the type of formation. It was nice and cool there. Be careful not to slip as the rocks can be wet and slippery. Some stairs with no wheelchair access.
very cool. a cave that was chilling yet interesting always cool to have a look into the past as it is.

Very big cave formed by the volcanic larva. You feel that we have walking in the cave where long back very hot volcanic larva has travelled. But dont be under the impression that it will be hot in there. It is very cold inside and be prepared with the winter clothing and a trekking shoes. It was a long walk and a nice experiences. A must visit cave.
Uneven staircase down. Uneven flooring in cave. This cave is pretty natural and includes unusual formations. It's worth seeing but take a flashlight as the lighting is very poor.
UNESCO siteVery cooling area; great for visit during summer I took a stroll from the main road ( aroun 2.5km) into the lava tube cave.
unbelievable.  The cave is too fantastic - never before visited such deep unusual and historic cave before - real eye-opener.  Geological wise must visit

udo was one of beautiful & must visit place in jeju. we spent 1day for it for visit such  pretty landscape. we took shuttle bus for tour around the island. diff view & diff landscape. i love light house hill & whale cave. better reserve enough time for visit & enjoy the scenery

Tulips are great. But cherry blossom are ending. The tropical garden is very impressive. If only the other parts of the garden were better maintained. I would have rated this place 5 stars. The caves was very interesting. From hot garden to cold caves. The follow by waterfall. It?s very nice transition. One must spend about 3-4 hours to fully explore this garden and use the guide to walk through the garden. I really enjoyed walking this garden with many different theme. Keep up the good work and hopefully with your increased price you can do better maintenance.

Truly a unique lava cave that is open to public. Should not miss the opportunity. Very well managed with descriptive dual language (English and Korean) on all the unique naturally formed features along the long and winding 1.2 km long tube/cave. The 13 deg C temperature inside was a pleasant reprieve from the outside summer temp of 38 deg. Can be a little wet and the floor is not so flat and as such reasonably appropriate footwear is recommended.
This was worth seeing and an unusual geological feature. Not the best caves in Korea (for me this is Gosu cave in Danyang) but pretty impressive all the same.
This was my first visit to a lava tube or cave.  It was a great little walk through a dark and amazing cave.

This was an amazing experience. The walk through the lava caves is a very enlightening experience and we had a very good time. Slightly difficult terrain to walk on but nothing too dangerous. On the whole would definitely recommend this attraction when at Jeju.
This UNESCO cave is well worth it. It's a long walk through the black lava cave but fascinating. Leave plenty of time if you are a slow walker because of uneven surfaces.

This place is pretty new I believe  it wasn't built 3 years ago when I visited. It was a very enjoyable walk around  the place is pretty huge and in some areas  construction hadn't finished yet. It's basically a really huge garden  lots of really pretty flowers and areas to take photos of. And I believe there are some animal enclosures somewhere in the middle of the park too. Our guide recommended visiting this place and the cave they had here  saying that it was all better than Hallim Park. Though I personally preferred Hallim Park. I found the cave here to be pretty creepy and really dark  best to skip over if you aren't into caves. There's nothing much to see in the cave anyway.

This place is just great! I love Hallim Park especially the caves! they are so mystical!! the parks has most of the natural attractions. The park is huge and you may need to spend hours in it to enjoy everything that they offer. It was so relaxing and very nice.
This place is a gorgeous volcanic cave which has been presented beautifully. It is not too long in length and not a difficult walk.

This park is huge! it is divided into different areas with different themes. It has a great variety of plants and birds. There are also two underground tunnel caves which enrich the overall visiting experience. There is also an area with seasonal flowers.  Great spot for photo-taking. Highly recommended for family with children. Allocate at least two hours visiting time here.

This mountain is definitely worth a visit. I recommend a nice espresso and carrot juice at the bottom at Lazy Place Cafe - cool place with great views. It takes a little effort to get up to the cave with the water falling from the ceiling but well worth it especially if you?셱e a spiritual person. The other temples are serene. It is an UNESCO site of outstanding natural beauty with an historical layer at the coast below. A Dutchman was shipwrecked here in the C17th and wrote the first description of the Kingdom of Korea published in the West. I had a wonderful time with my girlfriend. Close place to stay is Mirabil.

THis Maze Park is located between Manjanggul Cave and Gimnyeongsagul Cave. It was designed by the world famous company and jeju National University. The Park contains a maze that has 7 view incorporated in it. and here are three skywalks called ?gureum dari? and an observatory. There are four ways to get through the maze from the entrance. We had funny and enjoyable time!

This maze is right next to the lava caves and it offers kids to burn up those excess energy by going through this maze and reaching to its end to ring the bell. There is also a small garden of flowers for the family photographers to indulge in

This lava tube is different from a cave. it is as big as the new york subway in headroom and width. runs for 7 over km but tourist are allowed to see over 1 km in a safe environment. The ground is most and uneven in some locations so wear comfortable hiking shoes. Entrance is very reasonable for this UNESCO world heritage site!
This is the must place to visit in Jeju island.Beautiful cave with very cold inside.The floor of this cave are total wet so when you walk please be careful
This is one of the UNESCO Heritage site.The entire cave is around 1km and the temperature of the cave is around 10-15째짤
This is not a cave that was slowly worn away.  It is a tube that was created in a speck of time.  The unique conditions needed to make a lava tube of this size and length is pretty impressive.

This is a natural cave and you have to walk down a stair at the entrance. It is dark inside the cave and be aware of your step as the stone on the floor are not plain. Better bring a jacket with you as the temperature inside is around 10-degree celsius only.

This is a manmade park-like garden with a variety of plants and trees and water features. It is well worth the time it takes to walk through the grounds  just for the experience of viewing the bucolic setting. The main feature is Michon Cave which really didn't dazzle us as much as it apparently was supposed to. It's just a cave in which one walks down a slope to see some tacky lights and statues. The park  on the other hand  is scenic and pleasant. There are some concessions where they sell the usual tourist stuff.

This is a great volcanic cave with very interesting information cards dotted around to teach the novice geologist more about how it was formed and the story of the cave. Its a bit out the way but you can get the 101 circle route to nearby then one of the 7xx buses up to it

This is a bit of a must see in Jeju. Its a walk underground in a lava tube obviously created by a volcano. The tunnel has some nice features but the payoff is at the end as there is a big lava colomn. Also if it's a hot day it's really refreshing as it is quite cold down there. A jacket or vest is recommended. The way is lit by lights but all in all a flashlight comes in handy but the one on your smartphone will do. The floor is very uneven so people who aren't that nimble might have problems. Finally there are bats in the cave who probably won't bother you but make the place a tad creepy as you sometimes see their shadow. Getting there with public transportation is hard drive or get a taxi. However the grey ones are cheaper than the black ones.

This cave is well preserved. There are a lot of information provided in term of how this cave is form and how some of the formation is created. It is a good educational trip for those who is interested.
This cave is just ok. It's a long walk in the dark for a nice photo of a buddhist altar at the end of it. It was cold when I went so I didn't enjoy it all that much

They had light installations outside the cave which would have been cool at night but we were there during the day. We couldn?셳 find the restaurant and the cafe wasn?셳 that great as they only had a handful of average coffee drinks and some rice cakes. The zip lining seems to be the main attraction which we weren?셳 interested in.

입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: These caves are quite common all around the island  and this one is a well maintained and easily accessible example. Be aware though that if its been raining the day before you are likely to be dripped upon  but it's tolerable. Also  depending on the time of year  you will probably want to wrap up warm as it can be quite fesh inside.
There really isn't much to it. You walk down a long flight of stairs into a large cool dark cave which is lit enough to see.

There are spacious parking area provided for a visitor which is very convenient to whom that driving a car here. You need to buy a ticket for entrance bit it is not that pricey. The cave requires you to have a long walk with a majestic view inside the cave. Highly recommended and a must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.
the walk through these gardens is amazing.  From 300 year on Bonsai trees to the very cool acres of caves below.  very relaxing and plenty to see and learn about.

The temperature in the cave is at least 5 to 10C lower so please bring a jacket and wear proper shoes when going in. The entrance fee is cheap at 2K each for an adult.There are many locals visiting during the weekends so it's recommended you visit during weekdays if possible.The cave is dark and wet so we spent more time watching the floor as opposed to the cave.

the place is fun for walking between different kind of plants and animals. there are 3 caves and the weather inside it is cold during the summer time so you can walk there if you feel hot. there is also folk village and a water park

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

The park is definitely worth a visit for people who appreciate the beauty of nature. there's so much too see that one should reserve at least half a day for that park. The caves are also very impessive. there are restrooms and benches all over the park and everything's very clean. the collection of bonsai are impressive as well as the village of traditional jeju-houses.
The mountain and associated temples and caves are peaceful in the middle of a busy island. The weather is different that lower areas. Hot rainy humid etc. I would take time to visit!
The most impressive thing to do in Jeju. I have been in many caves before but never one that has been molded by lava. It's pretty chilly once you descend so make sure you have an extra layer or two.

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water
The Manjanggul Cave was a nice outing for my family and I. Very dark and wet and long but was interesting to read the facts along the way. Would definitely visit again.

The Manjanggul Cave is splendid and provides an excellent Geology lessons on how the caves are formed over thousands of years. A must for cave lovers and nature lovers. The walk is relatively easy for elderly and young kids as well.

The Manjanggul Cave does not look like a cave. More like a tunnel. A tunnel or tube formed by hot lava a few thousand years ago. The entrance fee was 3000 KRW. Toilets and drinkable water provided free of charge.I was staying at a hotel in Hamdeok beach and went by taxi to this place. A number of tour buses seem to make a stop there. I did not see any public bus that traveled to this place.In walking distance is a maze. Myself I loved the underground walk. Good walking shoes are an advantage.You can walk for 1 kilometer from one end to the other end and back. If you are looking for Stalagmites - you won't find them there. This is a lava cave. If you are looking for a narrow path - you won't find them there. The cave is big enough to host a philamonic orchestra.
The caves are indeed worth the visit. It?s a UNESCO world heritage site with carefully preserved Lava tubes and caves. The whole Jeju island was designated as a GeoPark in 2010.
The caves are a nice break from the blistering heat. Smart to bring a jacket if you get cold easily. Difficult to take pictures cause of dim lighting.
the cave was so dark. it's hard to walk since the surface is rough.they should put more lights so that visitors can walk easily and see the beautiful structure of the cave better.

The cave is worth a visit if in Jeju island. Although cave is 7.4km long only about 1km can be visited. Nice to visit on a cold day to feel that despite almost 100% humidity it's warmer than outside. Good enough explanations about lava formations and cave features. Lighting is sufficient to not require a flashlight.
The cave is very impressive.  The walking is quite rough. Watch your step!  Worth a visit- but it is a cold wet cave....
The cave is very cool and seems to go on forever.  There are informative photos with descriptions along the way so you know what it is you are looking at.

The cave is very chilling and quite dark. The path inside the cave is quite well lit up but it is still not very easy to walk as the path is uneven and at time quite slippery due to the water being collected. But it is still a good experience to walk inside volcano carved cave to understand how nature is formed. And the power of the nature. So best to wear some comfortable and non slip type of walking shoes.
The cave is really huge and long. You have to be outfit ready when you go here. The floor is also somewhat slippery that's why wear good shoes. The cave is filled with facts about how it is formed.

The cave is really cold and I love it. It's really good. And daddy put me on his shoulders. I was kind of scared. If you bring your kids to Jeju it will be lots of fun. It kind of looks like a mystery to me. The lava shapes are good and look like they are made by people. But they are really made by nature. I can't believe my eyes. The end. Done.

The cave is cold and wet. It's not easy to walk on undulating floor filled with watery potholes. Certain section you have to bend your body as the ceiling is too low. The cave looks the same from the opening to the end.

Surreal and spooky!! A must see place! Amazing place to see geological transformations and an interesting experience to enjoy. The caves were dimly lit and was quite slippery so be careful when visiting.

Suitable for anyone who can walk without aid as there were steep stairs leading in/out of cave. Floors were uneven as can be expected. We entered just after the rain so the place was literally dripping from the ceiling. One way in and out from the same entrance. Midpoint (the deepest part of the cave) was a formation that was supposedly the highlight. Lighting was sufficient to find your way around but not for taking pictures unless you are equipt with an SLR and a tripod. My 10yr old couldn't wait to get out as he was rather bored. No thanks to his father(me) who was busy taking pictures with long exposure :-)

So much to offer from beautiful botanic displays to a fabulous Bonsai area which was so peaceful and various specimens of fauna.... Plus several species of cacti. Caves to go down and lovely park area..... A lovely outing which was also very reasonably priced.

So many stairs but a great place to visit.  There are places were the rocks get a little rough so recommend wearing good shoes.  It was raining outside and the inside of the 1 kilometer cave was chilly and wet.

So dont get this place confused with maze land.  This one is near the lava cave.  Here it has one maze only.  It would have been fun and peaceful but then 3 buses of middle school children arrived and all hell broke out.  Very hars to walk around it when a bunch of kids are running past you.  But the maze owners also have a bunch of cats that were super friendly.

Sanbangsan Mountain is a wonderful bell-shaped huge body of lava situated nearby the ocean. At few places it stretches into the ocean where majestic rock structures can be seen. Almost vertical cliffs with columnar joints at this mountain are impressive. This mountain is visible from almost everywhere in the southwest plains of Jeju. Also the legend associated with this mountain is very interesting. According to the legend it was plucked out from the Hallasan Mountain peak by the angry Emperor when he got hit by a misfired arrow that was shot to white deer. Interestingly it is said that the circumferences of the Sanbangsan Mountain and the crater at Hallasan are of similar size. The Jeju Olle Trail Route 10 is connected to this mountain by stairs. A Buddha temple huge Buddha statue and the caves on this mountain are very beautiful.  This mountain along with nearby Yongmeori Coast are highly recommended especially to those who love coastal cliffs and interesting rock formations.

Rented a scooter for 4 hours and went around the entire island. Renting is easy- just go to one of the places right next to the ferry docks. You have to go to the cliffs and the black sand beach below them. Cross the beach to the rocks where they have the boat then go inside the cave. Walk all the way to the left and go out the small opening- this place have practically no other tourists. Then if it's low tide- climb to the right to the small opening into another cave but this is a lot cooler!

Really nice walk up some steps to a cave on the mountain with a Buddha inside for people to make offerings. There is a temple below with beautiful statues and stunning views of the sea. Worth the short hike up the stairs.
Really enjoyed exploring this cave. Easy and convenient car parking. Great facilities. A must-see on your trip to Jeju.

Read that it was man- made garden !! After the visit I felt that this was one of the best Garden ever visited. The various plants and trees were really great and we spend a good 3 hrs walking round. The cave was wonderful ... even thou only 350m is open to public. Highly recommended even for adults .

reach here after Manjanggul cave as sunny & good weather. it has some cats near around all of them were sleepy or lazily style. before went inside the maze. it has a small garden with some flowers. and the maze actually not to difficult or complex but good for take rest when you finished the game. it has shelter & you could buy a cold drink at there. ok to try if you got time.

Pretty big park with 2 caves that you can go through. Many school trips come here so don't be surprised to see flocks of students in the weekdays too. Nice peaceful area but there are quite a few other Jeju attractions I would see first if you're on a time limit.
Prepare umbrella or raincoat as water drips in the cave. It's amazing to see the rock formation and lava tubes. It's dark and the path is rocky and slippery so becareful.

Place where you can consider one of the exercise from steps and all the way to the end to view the nature of Lava.You can learn about the Manjanggul Cave as there's information along the way. Cool weather as we went during the winter. Not sure if you go during any other season.Must come as you might not get it from your own country.

Our trip to Hallim Park was wonderful.  If you love nature you will love to explore the well maintained gardens.  I love the garden with Bonsai trees as well as the Cactus garden.  There are caves inside the park too which you can visit.
Our first stop on was this place. the driver took a couple of photos and then we entered into the cave. we were thrilled. we took 40 minute to cover the entire tube.

One of the highlights of my visit in Jeju - there's about a 1km walk in the cave which allows you to explore the after effects of lava tubes at your own pace; very interesting and spectacular. Would advise to bring additional clothing and comfortable covered shoes as the temperature is quite cooling with moist grounds. We used flashlights from our iPhones at a few points where it gets very dark; this helps us to better see the route ahead or for looking at details of the lava tubes.  Spent about an hour at this location. A must in your itinerary!

One can take a slow walk inside the cave and enjoy the art form by mother nature. It maybe one in a life time to walk on cool off lava where the surface is not smooth but rather come in difference shapes.

One can go for a hike or just sit near the shore and enjoy the view. Along the coastline one can see a number of manmade caves which stands as a testimony to the importance of Jeju Island during WWII. These caves built by the Japanese troops served as a place for storing the weapons.Though called as a mountain it is more like a hill as it is not steep and one can enjoy the walk up the peak.
Nothing much in this cave except it was very cold for me.. would suggest to go in with shoes. And iz a 1000m walk from the start till the end
Not bad but more suitable for young kids. We went there only cos it is next to the Manjanggul Cave which was close on the day we went.

Not a bad way to fill in a couple of hours. The cave floor is very uneven as you are walking on solidified lava be sure to wear comfy shoes. Also can be quite damp so if you don't want to have water dripping on you maybe take an umbrella. Lots of information provided throughout the walk in several languages to keep you engaged also
No trip to jeju should be without a visit to this amazing cave. Comfortable walk inside the cave as long as one has suitable shoes.  Take the time to enjoy this cave. Last entry should be at 5:10 pm.
Nice walk through with lots of photo chances. All the descriptions were in korean but still was nice. The cave was nice and i liked it was self guided. The cactus display is worth visiting.

Nice walk inside the huge lava cave since it's cool and you won't really feel the 1-km walk inside but wait until you realize that you have to walk another kilometer back! hehe... It was nice seeing the different lava rock formations but be careful since most of the floor is wet and ragged so you have to pay attention to where you are stepping.

nice place to visit to see how nature works!!!....u can see how jeju was made thousands years ago.....beautiful cave!!!...but you must be fit to walk about 2km and walking in a slippery floor is not really easy in the dark....beautiful!!!!
nice hike up the mountain and great views. check out the WW II history close by - man made caves and bunkers byu the Japanese  to store planes
Nice attraction that suitable for all. Must walk all the way in order to see the main tube. Nice temperature inside the cave. Wear a cover walking shoe!
Nearby the lava cave so we stopped by. The size of maze is smaller than expected but good enough for young kids. There's plenty of cats outside the maze entrance which my girl loves.

Nature is amazing and the lava tubes at manjang is worth seeing. The walk is about 1km in and same way out. Wear good shoes. Walk is not as tiring as climbing up other steep sites in jeju. Educational Signs in English are available. A bit chilly in autumn in the caves.

My rating is based on my love of caves.  This one is quite long. Part of the cave you walk right on the cave ground itself/ there are also some walkways.  Explanations are also in English. It is cold inside so bring a sweater. Down the street is a Maze ( which I didn?t see)
My kid love everything about volcano and nature. He love science so we bring him here for him to see how the cave look like and he enjoy it.
My family visited Ilchul Land in a humid  scorching hot summer days. Michun Cave is the place you should visit and feel refreshed in summer.
My 10-year old and I had a great fun at the maze.  The maze layout is challenging.  The garden  is beautiful and well-maintained.  It is worth going and it is near to the Manjang cave anyway.

Must visit a place. The experience of walking inside the cave where once the lava used to flow was chilling and amazing. The cave temperature was around 13 degree Celsius. The water drops were dripping from the cave top surface. There were information boards about the cave surfaces and other features as you walk inside the cave.

Me and my friends really enjoyed our time around the Sanbanggulsa temple and really enjoyed the serenity and tranquillity it provided. The location within the mountain itself is breath taking and it really does give this temple a unique look compared to other temples. The stream that runs down into the cave is incredible and this place allows you to connect with your spiritual side.

Maybe it?s just me but I found I didn?t find it very interesting. There was an entrance fee of 2000 krw per person. We descended around two flights of stairs before reaching the cave. The cave is similar to a looong tunnel and it was very cold. There were some interesting formations on the wall but it gets monotonous after several meters.

Manjanggul is one of the 10 longest lava caves in the world and deserves a visit. It is exhilarating to see the different formations due to the lava flow. As almost everything in Korea there are plenty info and it is very well taken care of.

Manjanggul Cave was a thoroughly interesting experience. The structure itself is awe inspiring and feels like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Be prepared for water droplets plopping on your head! It was a bit chilly when we visited as well.
manjanggul cave is one of the UNESCO World Heritage and it is one of the finest lava tunnel. it is quite cold inside the tunnel so make sure to wear a jacket!

Manjang Cave is made of lava formation or lava tube as it is called. We walked about 1-2 km stretch of it only as not the whole tube was opened for tourist visitation.It is cold and dark. it is one of the longest lava tube in the world but it just is not my cup of tea. No  remorse on going into it but just was not awe blown away with it either. Go if you are a nature lover. skip if you are looking for awesome scenery to capture picture moments
Lovely park. Went with a tour group so was a rush. Would have been better to spend more time there. The caves is a must see.

Loved it! The park was extremely beautiful! Loved the bonsai and the caves the most. The only downfall was the animals. They seem a bit sad and clustered. Everything else was great. Make sure to bring bug repellent though.
Longest lava cave over the world. It's quite dark and rocky so remember to wear comfortable shoes. It's also quite cold down there so my suggestion is to bring your coat.
Long lava tube and if you are into stones and caves you will find it interesting. Inside was cold and some water drops coming from ceiling. Once you reach the end that it just take a picture then go.
Long dark cooling walk. Only a small section of the cave was opened. Amazing sight. The entire walk will take more than 1 hour

Long cave path that has been carved out by lava flows.  Its just basically a walk thru the cave and back.  Paths are not paved and can be treacherous at times.  Wear good walking shoes.  Bring a tripod if you want to take some nice pics inside the cave.  Fairly dark in spaces.  The walk should take about 1.5 hours.

Located on the eastern part of Jeju lies Ilchul Land  a cultural spot that showcases Jeju's ecology which consists of the Micheon Cave  Subyeon Park  Folk Village  Wild Flower Bonsai Garden  and Cactus Greenhouse etc??For fans of Running Man (?곕떇留?  this is one place to visit as the team actually filmed here before: various signboards showcasing certain place scenes (at certain corners) that occurred during the filming of Running Man; bringing you a step closer to your favorite Running Man characters! The first stop was Micheon Cave  a cave that is a designated Natural Monument and one of the representative lava tubes of Jeju. Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. The village was a replica of what would have been in the past with a millstone and buildings with commentary. There were even ?쁫ive??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html

Less crowded than many other attractions somehow. A beautiful temple and big! Small cave behind temple worth checking out. Don't forget to drink of the water legend has it you will live a longer life!
Large tea plantations and tea Museum cave Cafe and tea-themed food.In particular unlike other tourist establishments and also with great food and friendly staff are the best.

review: KRW 2k for adults. Worth the 2km to and fro walk and all information panels in the cave have english. Not suitable for very old and very young. A lot of un even steps and walkways and high steps sometimes. Dark. Wear good tracking shoes.

Just below the Sanbangsan cave  by the Yongmeori coast here is a replica of Hamel ship from the 1600. A dutch sailor who sank on the coast on its way to Japan. I guess he liked the coast  he stays in Korea for 13 years before returning to write his memoire.Very basic site attraction with activities on the side for kids and food stalls  there is not much. It is just an addition to the other visit around I guess.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 안덕면 사계남로216번길 24-30 용머리 해안

review: Jeju  has volcanic beauty throughout its precinct. This one is underground and was discovered by a teacher loafing with some students.  A 1 km underground walk best done with a flashlight and your head covered  as the cave is moist. Unmissable in Jeju.
It's well maintained and well organized. The Micheon cave is one of a kind with colorful nooks worthy of a snapshot.
It's very cooling in the cave. Recommend to wear good pair of shoes as it can be very slippery inside.

It's supposed to be one of the seven winders of nature but not exactly my kind of travel destination. It's amazing for the sheer length of the cave (7km) although you are only allowed to go to the first km. We only managed to go 300 m since there wss not much to see except for molten rocks along the cave. There was not much to sustain interest in going further inside the cave so we decided to just go back. At least it was cool inside although the path was wet but nit muddy. Wear comfortable and non slippery shoes if you wish to see the cave.
It's a very long cave. It's dark and wet inside the cave. Very interesting. It explain how the lava were being formed. Good education.
It's a nice place for sight-seeing on how a cave is naturally made from melted larva. It's span up to 1.5km in length.
It's a Lava cave about 1 km. The walkway was very hard to walk because it's a lava rock. And it's wet because of the rain. It's OK. I didn't feel woww. If you have a free time you can go there.
It's a great place to know about cave. Not recommended for weak heart. tons of stairs. (even before reaching the cave)
It?s the longest cave I have ever visited . Very cool inside and you will need a jacket. Round trip is about 2km. It?s really long but one can only visit a small part of it.

It?s like a walk in the dark. Watch your steps as the floor is uneven and could be slippery. Nothing much to see unless you are into geography. there are definitely nicer places in Jeju to visit than this cave.
It?s a small park with an uninteresting lava cave trip unless you are interested in geology.Went in with free entry on their 70th anniversary.

It was quite a strenuous climb up to the shrine in the cave at the top. Although it was a very hot afternoon. The views on the way up are beautiful and you can see for miles. Lots of great photos. Places to eat and souvenirs at the bottom near the car park.

It was my first time walking through a lava cave which was an enjoyable experience. I appreciated the natural formation of the tubes and to think that lava once flowed through was exciting. Others might think it's just a cave and the first few meters is the same throughout which is fair enough but I loved it.

It was hot at the cave entrance at 32 degrees.  There is notice at entrance on temperature drop to 10 degrees as we continued the walk.  It is a 1 hour to and fro walk along the dark and slippery caveт囹. Good for those who like trekking.

It was an interesting experience walking through the immense cave network. It's mind-boggling that this is only a very small part of a much larger system formed through volcanic activity. Do go to the visitors center to find out more information before venturing in.

It was almost 1.5 hrs drive from our hotel but was worth it. It's the only 1 of the 8 caves (I think 8) that is open to public . Amazed by how mother nature ends up creating such beautiful sites . You can keep walking for almost a km in the cave where lava used to flow when volcano erupted . It has some signs describing the various locations. Tip: wear shoes and take a jacket if travelling with kids as it gets really cold inside

It was a unique experience. Were totally in awe. Temperature inside the cave is much lower than outside. Jacket is a must. Most important is wearing comfortable footwear. Sports shoes would be right. There is lighting inside but you could carry a good torch light as well for better visibility.

it was a hot summer day when our tour guide took us to this park. It has a very large variety of plants and bonsai. Some of the bonsai plants are more than 100 years old!! The most interesting bit in my opinion was going into the lava tubes which are like under ground caves with unusual rock formations. Wear comfortable shoes. Its not strenuous but best to be comfortable when walking.

It was a 2km walk (1km each way) and it is not easy to walk in low light and on uneven ground. Suggest to make bring your own led light especially if with old folks. It was interesting to see how this cave was formed by lava.
It really is a must go this place. Even though it can be a bit crowded. Down in the cave you get a sense og what a force a lava stream is. Pack an extra shirt - it gets very cold down below.

It is worth a visit when you are in Jeju Island.We enjoy the two kilometres walking vv. please make sure that you have a comfortable shoes no  as the surface is really from the lava. This cave is one of three unesco heritage sites in Jeju Island.Nice and cool inside the cave and interesting marks of lava. We enjoyed it very much.

It is soooo dark in the cave. You couldn?t see the formations or well anything except the puddles of water. I have been to other caves before and they had dramatic lighting that shows off the details. We walked about half way and turned back as it was the same thing the whole way through. It does get a little chilly down there. It was our least favorite thing we did on Jeju.
It is really an amazing and stunning cave. Only first 1km is opened to public and it takes about 40mins for the whole journey. Very worth to visit it.
It is interesting to see the longest cave although it is a bit boring if you do it alone! I liked it and I learned something!
It is attraction. You can see a lot of caves everywhere but not such long and big. It has safety signs inside.

It is actually quite nice the cave was very well developed; it has proper lighting and the pathway had been established. The statues were a bit unclear though but it were quite attractive. The folk village was good. The bird park was also nice with ostrich and peacock. I did not go to the rest of the attractions as 1 hour visit was not enough to cover all
It is a well preserved lava cave. Very interesting to see. It is very dark inside. Not stroller friendly. Has no baby changing station.

It is a nice place to visit. We have stayed there for the whole afternoon. Driving around the green tea field with a car having bibibah for lunch nice visit to the Cave Cafe and enjoying an exciting journey on the Zipline! I will try to visit there again in the spring time so as to collect the tea leaves.
