Unfortunately, beyond the concept of actually walking through lava tubes, the entire experience was rather disappointing.  It was dark, wet and cold. The ground was uneven and hence quite slippery with many puddles.  After the first few hundred metres, my older daughter lost interest but we insisted on walking further.  However, it was pretty much more of the same so we did not finish the entire course of 7.4 km (since it would actually be 14.8 if you consider you also have to walk back)!  So unless you are in the area and really into geography, I would give this a miss.

Visited just because it seems that if you visit Jeju, you should visit one of its lava cave. I searched on the internet, and i think this lava cave is the most popular amongst the touristIt's a very big cave indeed. We were amazed by the size of the tunnel and imagined how was the lava itself that made the cave. But actually, It's a long, cold, dark, pathway for nothing. Yeah, maybe you can find some weird shaped rocks caused by the lava. Then what? your journey will be finished on some kind of a deck to see a big rocks standing in front of you and highlighted by colored lights. That's all. And the only way back is the same way you came in from. So boring!

Visit the lava tube only if you are easily awed by geological creations. 4 of us went, and not all were impressed as they thought it was just another cave. We read the description boards, and tried to spot the highlights to better our experience in the tube. As we went during winter, our coats were suffice for the low temperature within the tube. Wear sturdy footwear as the floor is uneven and wet.
Viewing of lavas in the cave was interesting.  But having been to other caves in other countries, like the Postjna Cave ins Slovenia, this place is rather boring.
very unique cave. the cave's lenght around 1,4 km. You will feel the sensation of cold air while down the cave. Don't forget to wear comfy shoes and jacket.

Very nice, for some reason some people gas different view. This is volcanic cave, cave size is very big, you don't neet to bend. Just enjoy. A little dark. In my opinion, if you mix this cave with other tousist spot it is really good place.

Very interesting cave, which has been created by the vulcano. 1km long tunnel available for tourists inside of old not active  vulcano. Not difficult to reach and walk. Little dark, but lamps inside are giving sufficient light. Very good level of safety. Info how long to walk, communication system with support team,  stairs, bridges, walking paths. Information boards describing what you can see in cave. Even young children like 3-6y can easily enjoy this trip.

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the   ground   is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

Very cool trip and 2km walk underground in the lava tube. Largest in the world. It is dark, cool and damp. The walking surface is cooled lava, so I'd recommend appropriate footwear. The lighting is respectful for the nature of the cave and energy efficient. Plenty of photo opportunities, for the low entrance price I was very pleased!!I wouldn't recommend any strollers or children who are learning to walk unless you plan to carry them the entire cave visit.
Very beautiful park with flowers and cultures, exotic animals and a continued paved walk through a number of cool dark caves.

Unlike other caves, this cave was a natural lava tube...worth experiencing, if you've never been to one.  However, there are a lot of steps to get down to the cave level, and the walk itself is not smooth...basically dried lava beds from thousands of years ago, uneven, yet well preserved.  There was sufficient lighting, but not bright enough for great pictures, so make sure your camera is capable of this.  Cave was cool and dark in most areas, and you may experience drips from stalactites above!

Unless you are under 12 years old or have a stuffed toy fetish, this is a very overpriced place. Nothing really much to see. Save your money for the caves and falls of jeju instead....real natural wonders.
Unique geological features.  Definitely worths a visit. We were quite impressed.  Yet wet floor, can be getting cold inside the cave.  Need sturdy shoes and warm clothings.

Unfortunately we visted this the day after we climbed Hallasan, so the stairs and uneven ground were awful for my knees and sore muscles. The cave itself is pretty amazing when you think about what formed it. It didn't take long to get through, so don't plan a full day around it, but it was a must see for us. It was dark and wet throughout the whole tunnel. We enjoyed it a lot, but be prepared for the stairs and uneven ground if you have older/younger travellers with you or if you recently climbed a mountain! We had lunch at the restaurant located on the grounds. It was good but expensive (spicy pork was 占25,000 but pork cutlet was only 占10,000). Once you finish, if you love cats as much as I do, do yourself a favor and visit the Maze Park right next door.

Udo was easy to get to and a great place to camp with full amenities. There are 2 main beaches; one on the West side and one on the North East side. Both are beautiful but the one that has sand made of seashells (West Side) is a little hard on your bare feet  and it was much busier there. The other has soft fine sand that makes for a great camping spot. There are no taxis on the island. In hindsight, we would have taken the other ferry to the port that was a bit closer to Hagosudong Beach (the NE side), but there is this drop on and off Bus Tour System that costs 5000won/person. You can get on from the ferry, drop off and set up your camp at the beach, then hop back on. It runs frequently but only stops at 4 main sightseeing spots (beach 1, beach 2, caves and ___ ) . We were able to use the bus for the two days we were there for on the same fare, but there are times/stops that are crazy busy. We watched at least 6 packed buses go by before we decided to stay the night. Honorable food mention: Pirate Caf챕. Really interesting place and staff. Great BiBamBap and you get to sign a plaque and hang it from their wall when you?re done eating.Friendly people, campfire and camping friendly, personal beer cooler (at the convenience stores directly behind the beach), and lots of cats.

Udo is simply beautiful. You should rent either a bike or a moped once you arrive. You can easily circle the whole island with stops in a couple hours. The enclosed beaches, volcanic rocks, crystal clear water, and very green landscape is exquisite.The road is not really crowded even during the busy summer months. I really enjoyed Udo Island, but then again what major natural location in Jeju-do disappoints? Whether you visit the lava tube caves, craters, dramatic coastline, waterfalls, nearby islands, beaches, mountains, and forests, Jeju-do is a natural paradise.

Udo is a very windy and beautiful island. The views from udo peak is breathtaking. There is a round trip udo tour bus for 5000won per pax which shuttle you to 5 attraction stops of the island. First stop is to the black sand beach where you can see the black sand beach and a cave (during low tide). If you want to go to the udo peak, you will need to walk a distance, climb up a hill to reach the udo peak. My first trip to udo was with my Jeju taxi guide and he drove us to udo and brought us up. My second time here was kinda cocked up because the udo tour bus driver only conveys in korean and our taxi guide this time did not accompany us to udo. Hence we did not made it to the peak. Nonetheless, we explored other stops (beaches and beaches). The sea and beaches are very beautiful. Udo is famous for their peanut and orange ice creams which I felt is a waste of money. Per cup of ice cream topped with some peanut or orange juice cost 5000won. Mcd ice cream taste nicer and bigger quantity. Oh yes, if you are willing to spend more you can rent bicycle and cycle around the island. And if you have international driving licence you can rent motorized vehicle to travel around. The roads are small and there's many tour buses shuttling people hence certain areas are abit congested.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

Too fascinating when seeing all the traits of massive lava flow in the cave, which is actually part of the lava tube. Must bring along a powerful torch if you want to enjoy from the ceiling to the ground. Relying just on the phone torch or the lights inside will hinder your enjoyment and appreciation of this natural masterpiece as you will be only focusing on your steps. Do walk the entire 1 km so you can see the big massive lava lumps which stretches from the ground to the ceiling. Water drippings and water patches are common, wear a cap and windbreaker will help. In fact the temperature inside is a few degrees lower than the outside
To n fro distance of 1km apart. The underground lava cave is natural and unspoilt, unlike some with artificially colorful lightings to spruce up the area. Overall a great place to explore

To be honest, it?s quite dark and your attention will be used on minding your steps rather than looking up. Rocky slippery trails and it?s 2km in total, in and out the same way. Worth a visit once as its not often you get to trek in a lava cave. Would recommend warmer clothes and proper footwear.

This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience. It's basically a geology lesson on the impact of lava flows. It was interesting though perhaps a little too academic for non-geologists like me. It's dark though and you have to be careful where you step as this is, after all, a cave not a paved walkway. On the whole, it was a unique experience and it gave me a different view of the beauty of Jeju.

This was recommended by a friend and it ended up being the highlight of our trip in Jeju! We rented an ATV and just drove around the island taking in the sights. Udo Island is also where the famous women divers go to catch abalone, octopi and other seafood and it was cool just to watch them work. The shore caves were definitely a must-see for us and they did not disappoint. I would definitely go back to Udo if I'm ever in Jeju again.

This was probably my favorite attraction - it wasn't a place where you go and just take pictures but also get to learn something. Throughout the cave, there are display boards highlightng the different lava formations. Plus, it's pretty awesome to be walking in a cave formed by lava flow. I felt like Indiana Jones! If you walk all the way to the end of the cave, you will see a pretty magnificent lava formation.Wear proper shoes as the cave floor is wet and being a jacket as it gets fairly cool underground.

This was our first visit to a lava tube, and we enjoyed it very much. The lava tube cave is maintained in natural state. Hence the floor is uneven and you need to watch your step. It is also very wet and little cold in side. Apart from that the walk is very enlightening. We learned many new things about lava tubes.The lava column at the end of the cave is a must see and is the highlight of the whole walk.Must visit.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.

This was one of those places on earth that fascinates me... It was a rare opportunity to see and walk through a lava cave!  There is no place like this where I'm from, so I thought it was delightful! The day I went, it was hotter than Hades outside. Once we were inside, the air temperature immediately dropped. The farther down you went, the cooler the air. My hands were actually freezing cold.  Although its not necessary, I recommend you bring a light jacket and explore!

This was one of the most expensive tourist attraction that we did, at 6,000 kw per person. There was a lot of hype related to this attraction and I was not impressed with the crater. There should be no charge for this site as it is a concave valley in the earth. If you like hotdogs, then get a hotdog.

This was one of the most exciting UNESCO sites I travelled to while in Jeju. The cave is a true demonstration of the power of nature. The walls are beautifully scarred by the movements of lava. It is definitely a place to visit for any geologist out there as well as any layperson. Not to mention, it was nice and cold down there, which is a blessing in the summer heat!

This was fun. it only took about an hour to go all the way through. there is a 2,000W charge. its chilly inside so if you bring the kids, pack their jackets. Its solid lava so it is not as colorful or full of stalagtytes as other natural caves but being in a lava tube is a unique experience and this one is really big. enjoy!

This was covered under our west course jeju tour.This is a large park with good bonsy trees ,lava caves and plants and animals and a old jeju village huts to show jeju culture.We can enjoy photography.If localite a good picnic spot.food shops available.

This was an interesting place that was well preserved. Wear a good pair of walking shoes as the place is quite dark with very uneven floors so watch your step. The air in the cave is kept at a constant temperature of about 19-20 degrees all year round, not a problem as we went in winter. Very good if you have not seen anything similar to this before.

This was a very interesting Lava Tube cave.  There were signs in English as well as various other languages describing what you were looking at.  The signs were informative.  The cave is cool, so I recommend a zippered sweatshirt or windbreaker.  Also, the floor of the cave is uneven, so you definitely want to have good walking shoes.  I was just fine wearing old jogging shoes.  We went as part of a guided tour - I would have liked to spend just a little more time there, but that's how it goes on bus tours...  There may be more beautiful caves, but overall, it was the nicest cave I've been in - very nice Lava Tube - you will enjoy it.

This was a part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - and felt it was worth seeing.  It is a lava tunnel/cave, which makes it kind of unique.  Visitors are limited to how far you can explore, which is fine as you do need to watch carefully where you walk - it is a lava tube and the floor is very uneven.  It is known for   Stone Turtle   because it is shaped like Jeju island.  Be sure to have a light jacket.

This tunnel cave is amazing! You can just imagine how this lava came to be and now you are standing in the middle of it all! It is quite a long walk, uneven ground, damp, dark and wet. Don't let that discourage you! Wear proper shoes and bring a flashlight, if you like. The cave is dimly lit though.At the end of the cave you will see beautiful, coloured lava. Experience of a lifetime!

This place is interesting only in concept - because it's one of the longest lava tunnels in the world.  But in reality, you climb down a hole and then walk for about a kilometer in what looks like a dirt tunnel made for a subway train with virtually northing to look at.  Then you arrive at a lava column which is far from impressive.  There are numerous amazing caves in the world such as the ones in Ha Long bay.  We are very unimpressed.

This place is huge, with lots of plants, flowers, caves to see. Though it may not be extra especial since it felt so artificial, it is still a cool place to visit. Stroll and take lots of pictures with friends or family. Don't join the tour because they only allow 1-1.5 hours and you'll end up just walking and not really appreciating the things that you will see.

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.

This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This place is a must-visit if you visit Jeju. It was a pretty long walk from one end to another end. Inside the cave, it was quite dark and you have to be extremely careful while inside as the floor might be slippery. It was a magnificient cave and if you are a nature/cave lover, you will definitely love it!

This place is a garden and there is cave and lot of birds, literally this place has everything. It is worth the visit, I like the cactus garden and the bird feeding area. I will definitely come back again with my family. I made a vblog during my trip, come and see if it is worth the visit.Search by title :#3 TRAVEL BLOG DAY 2 JEJU - NATURE - GD CAFE

This park was the favorite place of my kids in Jeju. They could play with many kinds of birds and exploring safe caves here. My husband and I prefer watching bonsai trees and had intention of bringing some to our home if they could set them for sale. A place to have nice fun with family, just safe and green.

This park has it all - Plants, bonsai, trees, birds, ostriches, stone sculptures, lava caves, folk houses. However, it is really big so you might need to have more than 3 hours to finish the entire park.

This park has a collection of 7-8 sections of different type of plants and sights, such as tropical plants, cactus collections, bonsai collection, wild flowers, cave systems, folk village, small cave system etc. You could easily spent 2 hours at this park. The park is nicely planned and appropriately signed to guide the exploration of the entire park. We really liked its cactus collection and roads lined by famous Jeju-harubang (stone human-shaped statues). We definitely recommend visiting this fabulous park.
This park has 9 zones, botanic garden, caves , flower garden, water garden....We spent a present day out in the park.

This park has 9 different areas to visit, including a cave region, a bonsai section and a traditional Korean village.  This will take some time to see all of this, but is well worth the visit.  It is on the west side of the island, and near some nice beaches.

This maze park is very near to Manjunggal cave, maybe 500m away. If you have time, drop by this place for some fun activities with young children. This maze park is also have many .. really many fat furry cats. Cat lovers .. you sure love it.Children will enjoy the maze, it is not a difficult maze to go thru. In between this maze, there is 6 stations for stamping, collect all this stamps as souvenir. To complete the maze, it will take easily less than 30 minutesAdmission fee is a little bit pricey but for the children sack, the fee will exchange the children happy faces.For those who not keen to go in, there is a good resting place outside the entrance.

This maze park is fun! I was amazed by the aroma of the cypress! It was really good and it's like a natural spa to detoxify your body! It was really funny that you keep walking and seeing the same person / family for 2-3 times. Hahaha, both kids and adult enjoyed it! The Korean couple whom arrived at the centre saw us keep turning around and gave us some hint! Even just with body language and point here n there. Then we gave the same hint to another Korean old folks group. It's really an good experience and shouldn't be missed! It's just few mins away from Manjunggul Cave.Ring the Bell hard if you made it to the centre!
This location is nearby Manjanggul cave so if you have time specially have a kids, suggest you can visit, inside have some of Kids facilities and one more thing, there have a lot of FAT FAT Cat.

This Lave cave is long, dark, cold and wet and the ground uneven due to the Lava deposits.  My partner did it as he is physically fit.  I needed help because of the uneven ground and the dark and wet ground.  If you are fit then it is a good experience.

This lava cave is interesting if you are into nature and ok to walk in the dark on uneven rocks for 2km. I like the experience but my elderly parents didn't really appreciate the dark long walk, especially with the steep stairs. So unless your elderly members are physically fit, it will be much better if they skipped this.

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking.  There are different areas to see at this park including 3 long lava caves, an area with bonsai (my favouite), an area of flowers, a water area, a stone area, old JeJu houses and my least favourite...caged birds some in dubious conditions! I took lots of photos.  Plenty of places to get snacks and drinks but chicken a la flies is not my cup of tea!  A nice place to take a picnic.  There are lots of buses there but they all follow a route...if you go left you have a reasonable amount of quiet time from the hoards of yellow hat people and all the selfie photographer's.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is the longest lava tube/cave in the word, so they claim, with a longitude of four kilometers. About one kilometer is accesible to the public. Interesting to see. Some explanations. Very dim light. The lava column at the end is impressive.

This is the first UNESCO world heritage that we visited in Korea. Walking distance about 1km, so be prepared to wear the comfort shoe. Some area a bit dark so be careful. Overall nice experience to visit this nature cave.

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.

This is really a large park with plenty of places to visit inside. It is recommended to visit this park at spring or early summer so you can watch more blossom flowers. I visited it in October so there is only few flowers. It is still worth a visit though as you can visit the village, the stadium, the bonsai, the caves, and even a bird zoo inside.. must come.

This is quite an interesting place to visit. Do remember it's a long lava tube cave.Take note:1) Stairs to the cave can be steep.2) The floor of the cave is in its natural form. It's wet, slippery, jagged and uneven. There are large puddles everywhere so watch where you step.3) When we went, there isn't really any special colorful lighting in it. It was quite dim. We used our cellphone as our flashlight in some of the darker and very uneven floor areas.4) It's cold so wear some warm clothing. There may be water dripping from the ceiling as well. Overall we enjoyed the lava cave.

This is quite a long, dark cave with uneven rough ground surface so it's a bit dangerous. One must be careful with every step. However, inside is a treasure of lava tubes & our guide told us that each one represents a volcanic activity. At the far end is a unique rock formation or a stalactite shaped like a mother & child. Really amazing!

This is our last stop of our 2nd day in Jeju Island and was worthy for the line Save the Best for last. If you are into caves and lavas then this is the right place for you. Since this is our last stop, we went there around 5PM, we were in a hurry to reach the entrance of the site. Get ready to walk on dark and cold pavements. Although it was cold we manage to take photos inside the cave (which needed editing) and was mesmerized with the unique beauty the cave has to offer. It entails walking so get ready to walk and prepare the right shoes. Plus, inside the cave is really cold, colder than the other sites so be ready with your jackets. You may also explore the park and the cafe located outside the cave. The entire place is relaxing and worth the visit. This must be part of your itinerary once you happen to visit Jeju Island.

This is one of the best place we visited in Jeju. Various things to see such as flowers, plants, birds, small reptiles, lava cave etc. I love the cactus garden most. Great for photo taking and a slow stroll with family members! I did not fully explore the place due to time constraint. Guess it probably need around 2-3 hrs to slowly explore the park.

This is one of the attraction in Jeju that nice to visit! The cave made by volcano lava. When we went there it's rain, so along the way inside the cave wet and dirty! Inside the cave quite slippery and dark. Overall I like this place! We manage to go to the deepest point and come out within 1.30 hr.

This is not a cave, this is a lava tube so do not expect what you see in caves.  The tube is huge in size.  From the entrance you are able to walk 1km.  At the end you can see the remains of where lava had gone up and out of the tube.  It is not very impressive.  The tube itself is a large tunnel like structure.  There is not much to see and the lighting is a bit insipid.  The good thing is that the entrance fee is only like $2 so you don't need to worry about wasting money.  I am glad I visited but I would have been happy to have just walked down into the tube about 5 minutes, turned around and left.  Walking to the end of the open area is unnecessary and a bit of wasting time.  Spend about 10 minutes and its enough.

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is like a must-see attraction according to the reviews and the crowds there.... so despite there is nothing much to see when you reach the summit.... just some balding green on a small concave patch of land  .. it is probably still worth the 20 odd minutes climb up , for health sake.. .   Some cardio exercise is always good after all the black pig meals ! If you arrive at the right time at the foot of the hill, you may be lucky to  catch some women divers performing there..

This is just a park with some trees, caged birds, caves and bonsai. Nothing very spectacular for the krw120000 of entry fee. The signage was insufficient to the various sights so I walked around quite a bit but still didn?t find some key sights.

This is enormous highly worthwhile visiting. While I've visited caves around the world this is the first time I've seen lava tubes. They are huge you could drive a semi trailer through most of them. Defiantly worth seeing just for this aspect.It's quite wet on the floor of the cave, while you won't get wet, there are puddles of water. The ground is extremely uneven in places so good footwear is essential.There is heaps of signage in English on how they were formed.Highly worthwhile.

This is all about geology.... How lava tubes are formed during volcanic eruptions and the rock formations produced. It's something different from what most resort islands offer. A journey to the center of the earth.... cut short to about 1 km. Yes 1 km. So, if you aren't into walking for 1 km in and 1 km out, this is not the place for you. Especially so since the temperature drops significantly as you descend down the steps. It was the month of May, with outside temperatures ranging from 25-28 degrees Celsius, but as you walk into the cave, the chill can get to you. The ground is uneven and wet, with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Be prepared for all this.
This is a very good park. You can see a lot of varieties of flowers, trees, and birds in this park. Also, you have a chance to see two-dimensional caves.

This is a UNESCO World Heritage listed site. It is indeed one of the largest lava cave/tube I have ever seen. It is awesome, dark, wet and huge. Its floor uneven, wet and slippery. Artificial lighting is minimal and don't attempt to take photos as it is too high to be lit by ordinary flash lights. You need to watch where you are going. The result of a fall can be serious. Minor twist ankle is common. The experience is well worth the trip. Do not forget to take extra clothes and be prepared to have a thorough shampoo and shower that night as it drips everywhere.

This is a UNESCO site and I find it quite awesome, how Mother Nature made these underground caves. Do note that you'll have to climb steep stairs up and down to the caves, so I wouldn't recommend the elderly folks to go in. Do bring along a jacket as it can get chilly down in the caves. Also bring along a torch and have good anti-slip walking shoes as it can be a little wet and slippery.

This is a relatively easy to walk cave with interesting volcanic formations. You walk all the way, about a 20 minute walk ( 1 -way ) to the end to see a lava formation and walk back. It's quite cold in the cave, even with the blazing sun outside, so do bring a light jacket. Also, it may get slippery inside, so wear good grip shoes.

This is a really interesting place to visit, although, be warned, if you're taking the city bus, the actual caves are about a 20 minute walk from the stop. Be prepared to pay for a taxi (who will hassle you to hire him for a full day tour) or walk.

This is a really cool place to visit, one of the best activities in the Island.  Inside the cave it can be a bit cool so do not forget to bring a jacket or a sweater. We went inside the lava tunnel all the way to the end, at least to the section where you are allowed to walk. It will take you about 45 minutes walking, then we came back running, it was fun and a good exercise but you have to be careful as the floor is uneven.  Some of the views are quite spectacular.  The whole experience will give you a sense of peace and adventure.

This is a park for all seasons. It is beautiful any time of the year. We were there in autumn and although the colours were not significant yet, there were plenty of flowers to please any nature lover. The only set back is the cave. It can be quite wet inside and one has to be careful.

this is a must-see. A temple in the cave made by ancient volcano corruption. It is on the top on the hill. Great views on the sea, pieceful atmosphere. You can drink water from thespring, it is a water from the mountain and it is clean.

This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. The temperature drops quickly: it was 28C outside when we visited in late September but only 15C inside. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).

This is a good location you should spend time to visit, nice and you can see some different kind of cave, some of the cave have spotlight follow so amazing. friendly reminder, please wear a shoes instead of slipper or sandals because the floor very wet.

This is a cave formed by molten lava melting the rock layers away over a very very long time. So expect a huge dimly-lit tunnel with uneven walking surface. The small museum does a good job of explaining the geological aspect of the cave. The 2 km round trip into the cave is not difficult but wear a pair good walking shoes and if you need, bring a small torch. This cave is located on the eastern part of the island so best to visit nearby attractions like the Ichulbong, Phoenix Island etc.Another tip: if you hated Geography in school, give this place a miss. LOL!

This incredible cave flew with lava before. It is typical Jeju world heritage and must visit. The lava flew through all the tunnels and forms interesting geographic features. And another lava melted the roof of the channel and runs down to the first layer of lava. As usual, 2000 for an adult ticket.

This Hallim Park is a big area with the palm tree, tulips, cherry blossom, etc.  They also have some cave and near to the sea.  They have Historical Story since 1971 if you see the website.  We need to have 2-3 hours i think to go arround.  When i visit here last week, we still can see the tulips.

This could be an amazing place to visit provided you have good weather and great friends. Scootering around the tiny island can be fun if you stop off at the beaches, swim along the way and explore the caves and tunnels by the black sand beach. Definitely keep an eye out for the giant burger restaurant and the peanut Makgeolli stand (留嫄몃━, it's alcoholic rice wine!), both are delicious! Don't over-hype it or expect too much, just go to have fun and you'll be happy you went.

This cave was decent but the caves in Jeju were much better. It was a nice get-away from the heat since the cave is nice and cool but when I went it was super busy so I was constantly wading through crowds while inside the cave. If you have  a chance to go, try in the off-season or go early in the day to avoid the crowds.

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

This cave is actually a volcanic Lava tube, not limestone cave. So don't expect to see amazing things like what you see in Guilin and Yunan.Same as reviewer ggkoh, I visited there after a day of persistent rain. The cave is wet, filled with small pool of water here and there. The floor bed is rocky and uneven. So be equipped with a jacket comes with hood (or raincoat) and a good pair of track shoes.
This cave is a lava cave, quite interesting if you are a geology lover. So no need to go if you are not. Do ware good shoes as the path is rocky inside the cave

This attraction was quite an adventure and somewhat scary at the same time. Throughout the long walk to the end of the cave, it was very dark, wet, slippery and bumpy. Make sure that you wear sturdy shoes(no sandals, flip flops), carry a light/flashlight, and something to cover yourself/head (jacket w/ hood, hat). The entire trek (roundtrip) took about let's say 45 min. to an hour- depending on your pace. Also, it's difficult to take a good picture due to the lack of light and darkness - FYI

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

This ?Unesco? lava grot is quite nice. You can walk a kilometer underground in a dark cave with lots of information panels in English and Korean/Hangul. The Floor is uneven and the temperature is ten degrees Celsius. We did not expect something special, but overal it was a nice experience with a rewarding pilar at the end of the walk.

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)

There is nothing much to see except of the cave. But if you spend time to read and understand the formation of the cave. Its quite educational for me.You will be more enjoyed if you slows down your steps and admiring the unique walls in the cave. Instead just walk, walk and walk until the end and took picture of the end of the cave then went back.

There is not much to say about this: It's just plain boring; an unimpressive, badly lit cave. It isn't pretty either. Only recommended if you have a thing for geology: The history of a variety of rock formations is nicely explained.
There is no harm to walk and hike to see the view of coastline and ocean.? The temple is not grand or manificent.? It is hard to hike to the budda in the cave, but you can try.

There are two lava tubes/caves in this park. The tubes themselves were quite interesting but having been to other massive caves before (e.g. Mammoth cave in WA, Australia), this is tiny. Nevertheless, it is a sight to see.The entrance ticket is quite pricey but the park is huge... And i guess the ticket price is more to sustain the park. I believe some may enjoy it more than us...

There are statues of the Future Buddha, Maitreya; Bodhisattva of Compassion,? an outdoor huge Golden statue of Buddha, hundreds of miniature green Buddhas.? If you climb up the 471 steps, you will reach a cave with a statue of the Bodhisattva of Compassion. The tears that she constantly cries for all the pain of this   ocean of suffering   world collects in pools up the stairs below the altar.? Visitors drink it and make prayers before it. If you drink 3 sips of the water, you will enjoy longevity in good health. Great temple to visit.

There are several things to visit and see inside the Hailim Park.  This botanical garden includes bonsai artwork and garden, a Jeju stone, a Jaeam Folk Village, an underground Hyeopjae & Sangyong Cave, and a zoo.  Well worth a visit.  Best time to visit is in the spring especially during the cherry blossom season.
There are lots of things to see here, we spend 2 hours here. Beautiful trees, caves, stones, small waterfall. It is all about nature and traditional korea living.
There are a cave, plum garden, rock garden, birds, and everything!

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the   Manjanggul Lava Tube   enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

The walk in the cave is about 1km, which is pretty long. Please be careful as the cave is long, dark and slippery. In fact I think I spent more time looking on the ground than at the actual cave walls. But safety always comes first, and you can always stop at certain junctures to take a good look at the walls/ceilings.Nonetheless, the lava shelves and cave features were a wonderful sight to behold, especially for someone who appreciates geography/geology like me :) I have went to this attraction twice, and both times I have found the visit worthwhile.
The UNESCO Lava Tube. Beautiful in the tube. Can get to see the trail of lava movement,  the moulden formation. It is common to visit caves, but a lava tube, is rare.
The texture of the cave and the formation were very interesting and unique. The walk into the cave was a bit tedious due to the uneven ground. Otherwise, had a great outing.

The temperature inside the cave is between 13 and 16 degrees celsius despite outside summer weather. Hence it is good if you can bring along a sweater or jacket. Also bring something to protect your head from the cold cave droplets. Overall, it is a wonderful experience to explore this amazing cave. Look for the iconic turtle rock as well as the large column rock at the end of your 1km trail.

The temperature drops dramatically after you descend 15 stairs into the cave entrance.  There was a cloud that had formed at the entrance due to the humidity which was really cool to see.  Walked about a km to the end where there is a lava column - a frozen in time dripping of lava from above.  Fascinating walk, lots of people (some in heels which I wouldn't recommend).  Really beautiful way to spend an hour or so.  Especially when it is super hot and humid outdoors!

The stairs down into the cave system are steep and plentiful, so if you have trouble with stairs then you should skip it.  Also, if you don't like walking on uneven ground then you should skip it, because most of the cave floor is natural stone, so it's rough and uneven in many places.  There's also small standing pools of water in places, so watch where you step.  You don't have to walk the whole cave length, since it's very long indeed, so you can just do what we do and walk part of the way and then back again.  But you do need appropriate footwear, and no, high heels are NOT appropriate footwear.And remember, this is a natural cave system, not a fun park, so don't go expecting anything beyond what it is.

The site was the best part of an all day trip covering the eastern end of Jeju Island. Such places are always fascinating. As soon as you enter, the temperature drops to the lower double digits C.There is a one kilometer stretch you can walk. I like that it has not been jazzed up with a rainbow of colours. The floor is naturally uneven with some sectors covered in wood. The cave is 18 meters as its widest and  23 meters as its tallest. At the far end is located the world tallest lava column at 7.6 meters. When you appreciate the force of Mother Nature to cause such formations, it only adds to the visit.

The silvery field of   grass   or   weed   is amazing if you come at the right season. Definitely a great photo taking opportunity. You can also catch the Halla mountain in the backdrop. Romantic and almost magical if not for the crowd. The place is getting more popular as words spread.The crater itself is not much to see but could be interesting if the leaves turn red or yellow. Visited here while on the way to the Manjanggul Cave

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The Seongeup Folk Village was a walled-in village in the southeast of the island where stone homes showed the construction, culture and lifestyle of the island?s people long ago.Obviously, Jeju wants to maintain some type of historical reference to the old lifestyle.  Our tour guide made it interesting by talking about some practical aspects of the design of the huts (how it was heated, how it was built, etc), but this just wasn't my thing.  In fact, several families that help with the upkeep of the huts actually live in other huts in the community.  That said, those huts have modern adjustments like windows, electric power, etc so even they have moved beyond the   old ways  .  The village had a few shops and a restroom and outside the village was a convenience store with drinks available and another restroom. For me, the bottom line was - I would have preferred to spend the time at a natural landmark (waterfall, cave, hiking trail, etc) instead of doing this, but it was part of an all day tour.  There are simply too many other options to see in Jeju for this to make it to the top of the list, unless it is your   thing  .

The prospect of walking through a cavern formed by lava was extremely exciting for my wife and me. So although we were staying in Seogwipo and wanted to see Udo Island and Ilchulbong on the same day, we decided to visit Manjangul. It was a 3.5-hour long journey by bus and another 15-minute walk from the bus stop. It was a hot and humid day, but as we entered the cavern, it was cool. Droplets of water trickled down on us and the deeper we went, the cooler it got. The cavern is lit up just adequately to help you find your way around and read the signages about the different formations inside the cavern. Watch your step and mind your head. The floor is wet and slippery and there are low rocky ceilings in places. So have a safe and enjoyable experience. It's cool, in every way.
The place is very unique as it used to be a lava tube. Very cooling in the cave, only 13oC. Would suggest to bring gloves if you are afraid of the cold. Unique and must visit.

The place is big but there are many places that are not well maintained. Tall grasses in some places and many of the plants are left to grow without some serious planning. The caves are nice though, clean and doesn't have the smell of bat urine. The bonsais are quite nice too.
The park was full of nice gardens and i was really impressed by the caves. Was only 10,000 won entry and i think it was worth the visit
The park is really big. Need at least 2 hrs to complete exploring. There's many things to see - from small animals, plants to caves. Great place to relax and enjoy the scenery.

The park is quite large. Access to the cave is via two flight of stairs downwards into the earth. The temperature inside is colder than the outdoors, with the pathway often wet with water dripping from above the cave. Lighting is limited, and one has to use flash to take pictures, though a little tweaking of the camera could bring pretty good results without using the flash. There are written explanations regarding the lava layers. Because of time constraints, we were not able to finish exploring the cave to its end.

The park is nice and had a good size. There are a variety of different sections and when you add it all up it gives a good mini summary of Jeju - with the caves, stone park, waterfall, historical aspects, flower garden, and bird park. If you have only 2-3 days in Jeju this should be a must on the itinerary.
The park is located close to the beach, it?s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.
The park has different areas including water garden, bird garden, bonsai garden, cave and folk village... Overall, the garden is very nice, huge but the entrance ticket is a bit bit bit pricey.
The park has birds area , flowers area, caverns with lots of other attractions probably you need 4 hour to see it all.We like the caverns more than anything else
The only things good at here is the cave. Others than that you can see all the stuff in other places. Maybe the bonsai tree abit special but, not to my interest.

The moment I set my eyes on this island, I knew I was in heaven. The water looked extraordinary blue and the view was nothing short of a perfect dreamy scenery. We took a day trip on the ferry from jeju. On the island, we took the hop on hop off bus. Take any bus, doesn't really matter.. They will then tell you which color buses u can hop onto at the next destination along with a list of places they will stop at. I think it costs around 2200 won. The island was crowded specially with all the bikes but still it is not to be missed. The first stop was the udo peak. A hike of around 30 mins to a lighthouse from where you can see the entire islans. The view of the sunrise peak on jeju all along the hike was incredible! Then the bus took us to 2 beaches..one was a black sand beach which had a little cave but tides were high that day. We missed the 2nd beach and went to the last one with white sand. This beach was quite close to the port and we walked to the port from here along the coast. It was a beautiful walk and less crowded.There are lot of shops and cafes in front of the last beach.

The maze is closely located to Manjanggul cave.The entrance fee is KRW3,300. The entrance is fill of cute cats.The maze is constructed by high and neatly-trimmed bush walls.It is not too large.There is an observation decks/bridge. From here you can clearly see path.As we're running out of time, we use the map to solve the maze.It took us 8 min to ring the victory bell.

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The Manjang Cave was one of the   must-dos   in my itinerary. I can only say it was somewhat a disappointment. It was not quite as spectacular as I have thought it would be. I was with my mum and dad both 60. My mum did not take the walk well and headed back halfway. My dad stayed behind to do some photo-taking, Here's the bottomline:- If you have never ever been in a lava cave before - go for it!- If you are traveling with young children / older folks / people with bad knees and weak ankles - give this a miss. The initial flight of stairs can be quite a walk. The floor of the cave can be wet and uneven- If you have been to lava caves before and if you do not have a mental benchmark - go for it if you have time- If you have seen the most wondrous lava caves and already formed expectations - skip it... more than likely this might underperform

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!

The lava tube is really interesting to see.  Definitely unique looking, especially if you were expecting a limestone cave or something similar.  Bring shoes as the rock can be sharp and the lighting is not too great.  Make sure you bring a coat or sweater as it gets a bit chilly inside the cave!

The lava tube is different from other lime stone or erupted caves I seen before, this one is very big and the its formation and feature is fantastic.  Try to avoid the high crowd and prepare jacket, poncho and hiking shoes.  We took good camera and tripok to take picture.

The lava cave which need you to walk about one km in and walk back the same distance. You can walk with/ without a torchlight as there are lights in the cave as well, wear jacket as it's quite cooling in the cave. Better wear sport shoes since walkway is wet and slippery and uneven too. Overall its a nice attraction to visit :)

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The lava cave is like a small adventure if you are keen at exploring. Bring a torchlight or make sure you have one installed in your handphone as the cave floor is uneven and slippery. Wear good shoes and a warm jacket with hoodie or wear a cap as water occasionally drips from the top. There is a short trek up a flight of stairs to reach the cave entrance. Lockers available near toilets. Set aside one and a half hours to finish the cave and return as it is slippery at certain sections. Wear good shoes and walk slowly and carefully. I was apalled at how some kids manage to walk pretty fast without their parents holding on to them. In summary, I do not find this cave spectecular, not much for photography too. Just a straight tunnel like structure. We were tired out by the time we went to the cave as we climbed seongsan ilchubong in the morning. Not recommended to combine the cave with other trekking activities in a day. Imo, I find the cave interesting but not a must visit.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The hike to the end of the cave was not short, so be prepared to walk a few kms if you plan to visit this place. The cave itself was wet and cool, which is good if outside was hot. You get to see different formations and immerse yourself deep underground at the same time. So, the time was well spent here. Afterward, you can stop by the restaurant near the entrance and have some cheap Korean food.  The admission to the cave was very reasonable as it is a government owned attraction.

The grounds are amazing and beautiful. Different times of year you can see beautiful blooms like azaleas, hydrangeas, bougainvillea, etc. It?s definitely worth some time to see the natural beauty of the flora. The animal enclosures are very disappointing, because as a true natural park, you would expect better conditions for the animals. The caves are a good break from the sun and heat. They are a wet cave, so prepare to get drops on your head. They have a tour route that allows you to see everything. Recommend taking 2-3 hours to see everything.

The experience was exactly like what I read from reviews and so I'll just focus on key things.-If for youngsters,  no issues.-For people not used to visiting caves-*wear shoes that don't slip*bring a torch if darkness is a concern *wear a light jacket- there are unexpected water drops, huge temperature difference with outside -Using mobile phones, not easy to take good photos. What you see is better than what is captured by phones. Online photos look so much better than what we saw.-Flowers outside the cave are lovely. Good photo taking spots.

The entrance fee was 2000W . You descend down about three to four flights of stairs to this Long tunnel cave. Temperature drops to about 15 degrees . No toilets in the cave so go to the bathroom before you descend . The floor of the cave was wet , slippery and uneven not suitable for young children and elderly. Most of the time you are looking down to avoid stepping into puddles and holes. A torchlight or handphone light is a must unless you have amazing night vision . Also the ceiling drips water constantly so can get quite wet so bring a hat. The walk to the end takes about 45 min to an hour . We gave up after about 35 minutes though some of our friends made it to the end to see the giant structure . If you do not want to do such a Long walk , do 10 minutes . The cave looked the same all the way through.

The entrance fee is 2,000 won for adult. And if you are below 24 years old, you might get 1,000 won cheaper:) The length of the cave is 1km (one-way). The ground was uneven, so make sure sure you wear suitable shoes. The landscape was nice but not much extraordinary shapes to see. Make sure you walk until the end of the path to see the main attraction for this cave, the lava column, which is the largest in the world. It would be nice of there are more lights (colourful lights might be good) to emphasize the unique structure of the cave.

The caves are amazing, well maintained and secured, very clean.  I am just wondering why other tourist doesn't want to go inside. If you visit hallim, don't ever miss passing the caves before going to other attractions of the park.  The second thing that attracted me most are the wide bonsai collection and the stones. They are really beautiful, picture perfect.

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

The Cave was very different to other caves I have been to. It was like a Subway train tunnel. You can way approx 1 km of the reported 7km+ lava tube tunnel. Did have much of the usual Stalagmite and stalactite and crystal formations. The Lava tracks /grooves where interesting to me. But I was not a   Wow   experience.

The cave takes about an hour, nice walk. Wear sensible shoes as the floor is not even and take a small jacket as it gets colder the further in you go. It was an interesting walk and we got to see bats at the end.

The cave is very nice, different from all other sights in Jeju. It?s a short walk but the ground is wet inside and can be slippery, also a bit dark in certain places. Wear a hoodie as water drops from the cave roof. Not recommended for people with mobility issues.Once inside, the sight is beautiful, it?s an amazing work of nature.

The cave is very dimly lit. The floor was very uneven (we are not blaming.. it's the natural formation of the lava) and slippery. I could only look down to make sure that I am walking safely and properly. I had no time to stop and look up and admire the caves. The cave is also very dimly lit, which makes the walk more challenging. We decided to turn back after 20 mins.

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

The cave is really nice, and amazing as it was created by the lava tunnel, thus the floor is the original ground where the lava froze. The journey is 1km one way, butnthe cave is lit, so you dont need torchlight or guide inside. There's interactive exhibitions too inside about the structure of the cave that was created by lava, unlike any other limestone cave.

The cave is nice if you are natural lovers, weather becomes cold inside the cave around 13 degree celcius. It should takes around 1 or 2 hours to explore the cave. For people travelling by bus, i recommends to use kaokao map and naver at the same time to find bus route and english name of bus station to get off
The cave is more with basalt stones, which makes it dull compare to limestone caves.
The cave is dark and cold especially nearing winter. If you are into cave exploration, then be sure to bring along a flashlight to brighten up. Be careful walking in the cave.
