The cave is a mysterious wonder that Mother Earth presented to us. This cave is a long lava tube in which once lava flowed many years ago. You could guessed the history and patterns of how lava had flowed from the lines, colors and patterns on the wall of the cave. If only the whole 4km could have been opened to public instead of just the 1km. I believe that they are more wonders along the rest of the tube. I would spend the whole day here if I could.

The cave is a must visit when come to Jeju. Be it winter, spring, summer, autumn... The temperate inside the cave stay the same through out the season. The rock inside the cave just so beautiful... Especially the one towards the end of the cave.

the cave is 1 km long you walk mostly in dark.not too.kuch to seeat the end there is a pillar but if you have been to.caves in the world before, it's not as fascinating as you see on the pictures not a real must

The cave has a number of formations throughout and there are information boards explaining what they re, and the English is good. The cave was a cool 13 degrees when I went down but outside was 34 so it was a welcome temperature.The steps down are a little deep so if you have vertigo or need help walking, it could be a little tough. It is wet under foot, I walked in flipflops and it was ok, but if you are a bit unsure of your footing, wear trainers. The cave is lit well  but some lights shine up into your eyes, which I found incredibly annoying, as it ruined my night vision. There are some areas with wooden bridges over the areas very difficult to walk on, so you aren't constantly in need of watching your footing.Worth a visit, as it it is not something you will see in many other places. I have been twice now, and it seems much more tourist friendly now.

The cave floor is uneven combined with inadequate lighting makes the winter walk very uncomfortable and after some distance, we gave up. Our youngsters were bored as the couldn't see the cave's beautiful features. Rather disappointed.

The cave and formation is very unique. Must go and it's not expensive. Only 2000 won per adultAs for transportation, we took bus 701 and waiting for bus 990. Note that bus 990 is not very frequent and be prepared to walk 2.5km. It's quite a pleasant walk though. So take note.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.
Summer is very hot and visiting the cave is a relief from the hot weather .Very nice place and well maintained , slippery floor .English translation of the plates were very helpful .

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

Stay in touch with nature and culture with this big park. Take time to appreciate the caves and read about the stories. I especially like the bonsai park. During spring, make sure to check out the rape seed canola flower beds and the cherry blossom trees on bloom.

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

Spent approximately 5 hours walking in the park. The park is sub divided into different sectors with different themes. Didn?t go to all the different sectors because some didn?t appeal to us. What I found nice and interesting were;1. The Caves2. Cultural Village3. The Bonsai & Stone Garden4. Seasonal Section - Ume FlowersWhat I didn?t like;1. Birds and reptiles in captivity2. Wild Flowers Garden - area seems to be poorly maintained. I didn?t get to see anything except grass and weedsBe prepared to walk and walk so if walking is not your thing then u better reconsider. Limited restaurants on site, so it?s best if u bring your own food and drinks.

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

Spent a lovely few hours wandering through the caves. Definately worth a visit if you are in Jeju. Lots of signs written in English giving excellent detail of the lava formations that can be seen. We travelled from Jeju City Bus Terminal on the 701. The bus journey was around 1 hour and the stop was announced in English too so easy to know when to get off. It is a long walk from the bus stop to the caves (I guess around 30 mins) but there are lots of taxis available that charge 4000 won to take you to the entrance. Easy to return home - same process, but your return ticket on the bus.Remember to wear sensible shoes and bring a jacket. The floor is very wet and pretty uneven and it is cold down there!

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.
so many beautiful flowers, with mini bird park. also caves where you can learn about geography. there is an entrance fee but cheap. so just enjoy the beauty!

Small island off the Jeju coast makes for a nice day trip/excursion from the main Jeju island. We enjoyed the climb up the one and only peak for excellent views, as well as some stunning coastal caves and cliffs, lighthouse, crashing surf, and volcanic rock. At first blush it may not seem too nice but Udo kind of grows on you. I'd recommend renting a moped or bicycle and bopping around the backroads; that would be the best way to see and enjoy Udo.

Since the cave is managed by government, the ricket price is cheap. Just 2.000 won.It takes around 30 minutes in and 30 minutes out  of the cave. Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ? Check out of hotel for catch your flight back home.Have a safe and enjoyable holiday!Telephone Numbers of Attractions For GPS:Citrus Fruit Museum - 732 2114Geomun Oreum - 7108981Joongang Underground Mall - 723 1510Jusenggeolli Cliffs - 7381521Lotte Hotel - 731 1000Alive Museum - 805 0888Trick Art Museum - 787 8774Seongeup Folk Village - 787 1179Traditional 5 day market (Jeju-si) - 7435985Seongsan Harbour (Ferry to Udo Island) - 782 5671Seongsan Ilchubong - 783 0959Cheongyejeong Waterfall - 760 6331Cheongjiyeong Waterfall - 733 1528Jeongbang Waterfall - 733 1530Teddy Bear Museum - 738 7600Jeju Folk Village - 787 4501Jeju Sea-World - 784 2333Aqua Planet Jeju - 780 0900Manjanggul Cave - 710 7903Oedolgae - 760 3033

Sanbangsan (?곕갑?? isn't a really big mountain but it has an interesting and distinguishable shape. It is about an hour west of Seogwipo by bus which stops conveniently right in front of the mountain.There is a nice temple at the base of the mountain called Sanbanggulsa (?곕갑援댁궗) with a huge golden Buddha a wonderful view of the town below and the ocean and an army of miniature mint-coloured Buddhas (I think). All make for great photos. Further up the mountain (you can climb up a long flight of stairs) is a small temple in a cave with an even better view of the town below. Worth visiting if you have made it this far. There is also an interesting story about a monk who hid in the cave during a violent time (can't exactly remember details). Down below south of the street in front of the mountain is a really really nice coastal walk with impressive cliffs that have been ocean and wind-swept into wonderful formations. This place is called   Yongmeori Coast   and also makes for great picture. (Worth knowing that the coast closes during heavy rain for safety reasons.)(Also of interest in the area to some is Hamel's Ship (a replica/museum of an old Dutch ship that landed on Jeju ages ago and the story of the Dutchman that was held captive in the island) and horseback riding (though it's only in a circle). Could be good for kids though these two are the least attractive for me personally.)

Samchoon (Mr Kim Si-Nam), was our guide for a 2 day taxi tour in jeju! Samchoon was super friendly, considerate and warm hearted! Samchoon really felt more like family to us!Samchoon texted me 2 days before to confirm the time and location of pickup and asked about my itinerary and gave suggestions on the order of location we should visit first. Samchoon made sure we get the best experience we could have in jeju!Samchoon was very well prepared. In his taxi, he had prepared water, phone cable for charging, wet & dry tissues, umbrellas, raincoats and even torchlights for caves.First thing he told me was that we didn't have to worry about time and that we can take as much time at any location. He wouldn't rush or give us a time limit. So that we could enjoy every place to the fullest. Samchoon even said that he will not charge us extra even if we exceed 8 hours, he said that he would want us to enjoy and not feel rushed. Samchoo said he was a photographer in the past and actively helped to take beautiful pictures throughout the 2 day trip. He knew exactly where the spots to stand so that the pictures came out amazing!Samchoon was very accomdating to our changes in the itinerary he gave suggestions on alternatives. Samchoon knew that we like to take photos to so on the last day he brought us to see the sunset so that we could take nice pictures! True enough the sunset and view was breath taking! Samchoon is really familiar with all the places and routes and the rides between locations was really smooth and comfortable! Samchoon even has a 40 year accident free award!To Samchoon, A very big thank you for making our jeju trip so fun and enjoyable! Thanks for taking such good care of us! We will miss you and the beautiful Jeju island! Will definitely go back to look for him when in jeju!

Really interesting lava tube which is definitely worth the visit if you are in Jeju. Spent about an hour plus walking through the cave back and forth. Temperature was pretty cold down there so make sure you are well insulated and wearing good footwear for slightly uneven terrain. Beautiful lava formation with stalactites and other rock features. A must visit for geog geeks and nature lovers! youths get discount off entrance fee, just flash your identification card or passport.

Really great to see and well maintained. Wonderful visit. Went on a rainy day and it was still a pleasant experience. The bus to the cave is very slow and infrequent so you either have to walk or take an expensive taxi which is inconvenient, but otherwise very good

Really enjoyed the place, great place to visit. As mentioned, more for casual visitors, not cave-experts. Can drip quiet a bit in places, so a rain jacket or hat can be helpful. Good shoes definitely a plus, though it is not a difficult walk and lit well enough. About 1km in, same way back out. Didn't feel too cold, pleasant.

Really enjoyable walk through the dark and luminous cave created by the eruption of Halla. It will take a decent time and is right next to a maze filled with cats!Unfortunately there isn't convenient bus transport as you have to walk about 30 minutes from the bus stop but if you're relatively fit, it will be no problem (aside from your friends nagging you how long till you get there).
Really dark in there, gives a good feel of being in a cave.  If you want decent pictures in there. Must take tripod and use long exposure.
Really amazing cave. Just 1,000 KRW the admission price. So cheap! It's pretty cool down there, a lot colder than outside.

Read the introductions and you will find the visit to this cave that much more interesting. It is not that dark so you don?t really need a torchlight. Take bus 201 from Jeju city bus terminal. It is worth making that 1hour trip. If you don?t wish to walk 25min or so from the bus stop, change to another bus that will bring you to the doorstep
Reach there at 1710. Just nice they close the entry at 1710. I'm  disappointed with their generosity, as a tourist, i wish they just let me visit the cave.

Raincoats were sold in the small shop near the cave, and there are cabs waiting for travellers too. The cave is very cool as you can see how lava shaped the cave with different patterns. But it is important to watch where you step as it is easy to trip and fall in the cave where lighting is dim.

Quite long caves, but we do enjoy walking through it until the end of the caves. It was cold inside, feels like we are walking inside a room with air-conditioner. Lols. My friend do enjoy reading all those facts and information on the formations, and I find it quites helpful for those who are interested in geology thing. Maybe.It is quite large caves too. For those who are on tight budgets like us, you can take a bus and walk 2km to the caves. Not tiring at all as the view is very nice.

Quite a small cave.  Different coz it's a lava tube.  Go if u have time.  Needs about 1-2 hours.  Bus stops outside at main road which is half an hour's walk to the entrance.  Try to get a taxi to take u to the entrance.  Otherwise, skip this.
Pro: Great caves, delicious hallabong icies, beautiful water liliesCons: Quite expensive, a little bit dated, the peacocks look sickly

Pretty interesting experience. You can spend as long as you like there and it's only 2,000 KRW entry.  It's lovely and cool for a hot day too. We took the bus from the Jeju bus terminal. The 701 bus has a dedicated stop about 40-50 mins in called Manjangul and our driver shouted it out so all good. It costs about 3,000 KRW for the bus one way. Once you get off the bus you have 2.5k walk slightly uphill. I recommend a taxi which are frequent up and down the road - that will cost about 3,000 KRW. The maze is on the same road should you wish but I would recommend visiting Gimnyeong beach (6,000 KRW by taxi from cave and on the way back to Jeju-si, walk into town and get the bus 702 back after). So there you have it. Have a great time.
Pleasantly surprized that there are varied natural creations to view. Caves, Bonsai, fruits...Delighted with the free calender.

Place is very interesting but gets a little boring sometimes especially if you don't see anything special anymore. If you are alone while exploring, the cave might bore you. But formations, especially the lava lines on the wall are very interesting. I just don't think if finishing the 1km lava tube is worth it. Place is very developed already compared to other caves in other places, especially in the Philippines. By the way, it's very cold inside so wear a jacket or gloves.

Place for everyone who like caves, volcanos or geology. The cave is long, but the one kilometre available for tourists is enough. There are many interesting lava formations, described in English. Beside that the cave is just beautiful. The temperature inside is around 10째C, humidity close to 100%. If you are not very fond of caves, stones or walking, probably you should skip it. :-)

Our first lava tube cave experience ; feel like we are in a Indiana Jones movie exploring the dark and wet cave don?t know what?s ahead of you. Abit slippery and rocky , would recommend a pair of non slip shoes as I saw a few people fell .
Opposite to Hyeopjae Beach, it is an old fashioned park with almost every element in Jeju. Caves, plants, mini zoo, and even a folk village. 10000 krw entrance fee is not cheap though.

Only 1km of the 7.5km lava tube is open to the public, but I highly recommend coming! Expect to spend about an hour admiring the beauty of this natural volcanic formation!While we were there, it had rained the night before and was still drizzling slightly, so the ground was damp. Good to wear proper shoes with good grip (we were thankful for our boots) as the ground is a rather uneven terrain and can be slippery when wet. It's also rather dimly lit, with some lighting inside to guide your path and highlight specific features found in the cave.Even though there is only one entry/ exit point, there is much to see (if you're into geology/ geography/ nature lover, otherwise it'll just look like the same dark cavernous backdrop) as you loop back to the exit point.

One of UNESCO site, worth visiting. It is a good experience walking through a dark, deep and huge cave.  Very important to wear a proper walking shoes if you are exploring the caves as it is not easy to navigate the 1KM long rough path of lava stones.  Bring a jacket as the temperature is cold inside (14 degree celsius), and a torch light if you can to help you as some rock surfaces were slippery with puddles of water around throughout the journey. It is rather tiring to navigate in the dark as you will be focusing on the ground instead of enjoying the surrounding lava structures.

One of the real highlights for my visit to Jeju Island. It's absolutely fascinating and I've been to a few different caves before. It's different because it's a lava tube cave and there are a few different information boards in there to explain the different features which helped to understand how it was formed. It's very well and cold in there so bring a wet jacket and comfortable walking shoes (waterproof/ resistant if possible) with good traction. There is a small descent but other than that it's rather flat in there so most people should be able to do it, just watch out for the wet surface. If you go to Jeju, you must visit this cave.

One of the finest lava tunnels in the world and listed as Unesco World Heritage. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to the tourists. Temperature inside the cave is low (around 11 to 21'c) so bring a cardigan or jacket if you afraid of cold. Do wear a covered shoe (best is sport shoes) as the surface of the cave is wet and water are ponding in some area and your shoes is definitely going to get wet. Also, the floor / surface is rough and uneven, not easy to walk fast especially for elderly who have weak knees or children below 2. Along the route there are board with explanation about different kinds of lava rocks in the cave (in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean). It's interesting. At the end of the route is the Lava Column behind a platform where everyone will take a picture before going back. Oh..this is not the end, you still need to walk another 1km to go back to where you begin (that's where you exit too). So total journey is actually 2km.

One of Jeju's three UNESCO world heritage sites, only a 1km section is open to tourists. It took about 40 minutes to walk to the huge lava column and back to the entrance. The tube is interesting and quite impressive as it is very large. There are also many interesting formations and explanations to look at along the way.It is cold inside about 11-15 degrees, so do bring a jacket. Wear good walking shoes as the floor is wet and very rocky. I saw people walking with wedges and shivering in their t-shirts, can't be nice. There are dim lights all along the cave. For people who are afraid of dark, wet caves, go look at the replica fountain of the lava column in the park.
Once you enter the cave and start to walk inside the cave, you will get a good amount of knowledge about the cave and how it is form. Very educational and quite a good 1 hour walk inside the cave.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

Ok ok, to be honest...most of my rating is because of the seemingly endless cats that were here. I hadn't read any reviews of this place before going, I just thought it looked vaguely fun and was located right next yo Manjanggul Cave. Upon arriving, we noticed a couple of cats in the parking lot. I was so excited! When we got to the ticket booth, suddenly there were more cats! Directly beyond the booth is a small area with some handmade cat tower type things and some scratching posts. There were maybe around 15 cats in this area. I would estimate more than half of our time here was spent watching and petting the cats. The maze itself was fun. It was better if you ignored the map, I think. I think more people go here for kids, but if you're a cat lover, go!

Obviously, caves don't tend to be the most exciting things in the world, but Manjangul is a part of UNESCO's world heritage list (the Jeju Volcanic Island & Tubes) for a reason - it is pretty impressive.  Manjgangul is a 7km long volcanic tube, though you can only walk a small portion of it.  It is dimly lighted, with a few descriptive signs along the way (in Korean, English, Chine and Japanese, of course).  It's an interesting sight, a pleasant enough walk, and admission is just W2,500.

Not suitable for old folks, because is full with rocks.. Better prepare a torch light or you handphone torch light. Inside very dark. The lights not that bright enough. Prevent any injury. Walking distance to the end about 1km, one way. Winter season, very fresh air inside the cave.

Not cheap entrance fee however there are lots of things to see.Even if you don't have much time, do not miss out their caves especially in hot days as it's so nice and cool inside. :)tiny little things to see everywhere and exotic animals as well.

Nice place to visit. U walk into the tunnel until its very derp end almost 1km in..... Then finally at the end of the tunnel u will get to see the light and the only stalagmite in the entire cave.... Lights in the caves are sufficient but not bright enough. The thing is, we thought the wet floors would be slippery but surprisingly thruout our entire walk into and out of the cave, there was absolutely no spot thatvwas slippery, thanks to the natural grooves on the ground which may have been created by the lava flow hundreds of years ago. Nice to explore, but obviously not for those who are claustrophobic.

Nice place to visit. Long walk, 1000 meters in 1000 meters back. Long ways down feels like even longer climbing back out. Dress warm the water that drips on you is cold. But the sites in the cave can really get your imagination going when you start thinking about this is where lava flowed. Have lunch at the restaurant typical Korean food that is very good and not over priced.

Nevertheless, people always recommend us to visit this cave when we're in Jeju. what we found is around 2km long cave with cold temperature all the way. if you quite a fan for geology and similar, this cave is exactly for you.the 'main' attraction is located at the very end of the cave. nothing more , nothing less...come if you have free time.. but not suitable for older people due to steep stair and slippery.

Never been to lava cave before..it's fascinating..the colour led lighting makes the cave more beautifull..to reach the end of a cave you had to walk for about 1km..maybe because it's rain outside,the temperature inside the cave is more colder..you should wear a long shirt and a long pants..

Nature attraction is the best in Jeju. To enter majanggul cave, it cost us 2,000 won per person. Beware its very cold down there (i went there on summer, but its quite cold maybe 18'C), wet, dark and slippery. Make sure to wear proper shoes (sneakers) and bring raincoat (even though it sunny day)

My partner & I chose park our car at seongsan harbour so we could take the ATV. To our dismay, their ATV can only carry 1 driver. Therefore we rented the sheltered scooter that can sit 2. The rental of that scooter is charged at an exorbitant 15,000krw/hr. We exceed the return time by a mere 20 minutes and had to top up 10,000krw T.T Advise to all: Just drive up your car to the ferry. It's much cheaper than spending so much on a cramp scooter, especially during winter.Aside from the transport misfortune, our day afternoon in udo was well spent, but could be better. We took the 12 noon ferry and reached udo at 12:30pm. Last ferry back to seongsan was 4:30pm. We did not have time to hike up, nor enter the cave. Spent too much time cam whoring to take in every bend of the scenery. The Seobin-baeksa beach is beautiful, surrounded by crystal clear waters.Advise to all: Go in earlier, so cater time for hiking, cam whoring, and chilling by the beach. Must have lunch too, the seafood noodles has the freshest abalone and soup ever.

My only concern with Hallim Park is the condition of some of the animals they have there. The 'cages' or 'presentation units' seem quite small for some of them, and some of the bigger birds didn't seem particularly happy. I don't want to give this an 'average' review because the caves are incredibly unique, the diverse array of trees and plants is also very special. But full disclosure, this place may not be for everyone.

My husband, 17 month old son, and I visited the caves and had a nice time. It was different from caves I'd seen before because of the lava that formed this one. The walk is 1 km of uneven pathways in dim lighting, but there didn't seem to be a problem for any of the elderly or very young we saw. My husband carried our son on his back in a carrier. Be prepared for the cool air though. We regret not packing light jackets, so we rushed actually rushed through to avoid our son getting sick. We would have loved to examine the structures more. Nice experience overall!

My husband and I visited this park during our honeymoon and it was really beautiful. It consists of 8 botanical gardens which features different kinds of plants, a cave which you can walk through, and even an area with different kinds of birds that you can feed and interact with.We got there through the Yeha Bus Tour but you can also get there with a taxi.For those of you who are looking to experience some of the beauty of nature and interact with it, I recommend this place.

My family visited Manjanggul Cave in late July 2017. It was sizzling, humid day, and Majanggul was the best solution for my tired family. It was cool and refreshing inside. It was quite big and long to explore. we had great fun. One of complaint was that it was quite crowded, but no wonder that everyone wanted to be inside the cave during the hot summer days.

My family explored this location during a family trip to Jeju Island.  My toddler twins are three years old and, with help, were able to navigate the entire length of the cave and back to the entrance.  The lava caves are fascinating and it's a good workout.  It is very damp, cool, and dripping inside - make sure to bring a windbreaker with a hood.  You can do it without (we had just sweaters) but it would have been better to be wearing that.  Plus, there are extensive puddles so waterproof shoes are a good option!  My only suggestion would be to increase the lighting a bit so guests can really appreciate the lava markings - the atmosphere with the low light is nice but I wanted to see more of the characteristics of the lava versus a non-lava flow cave.  Some people brought a flashlight and that seems like a great idea.  The price was very reasonable and there is a restaurant and clean restrooms.

My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

Must see in Jeju. Biggest lava tube in the world. 2 km from the bus stop, close to maze park. Do not forget tripod to take good pictures as it is rather dark in the cave. Good place to cool down after summet heat.

Mind your step! The cave is long, dark and slippery. This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience.The price is reasonable. A number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing.

Manjanggul lava cave locate in the east jeju island.I was there with my husband, I think visited this location make so tired if don't like hiking or nature tour.Temparature is so cold so must prepare jacket or coat

Manjanggul is a nature creation which 1km of it is opened for visitors to walk through. However majestic it is, if you are not a keen learner of geography or stones and cave, this walk would be boring for you. If you are there in Jeju for a short trip, I would recommend you to skip this instead.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul cave is world historic place of volcanic lava formation! The cave path is very unsmooth with bumpy small rock patches and wet so we had to walk steps by steps very slowly to the end! All along to the main attraction, there are small lamps and lamppost to guide us along.Took us one and a half hours to reach the main attraction of lava formation.We spent a few minutes taking some picture there and proceeded back out of the cave.I think I won't be going there again because I'm not interested in geography.

Manjanggul Cave is unique as it is essentially a lava tunnel instead of the usual stalactites and stalagmites found in typical cave. Only 1km of the tunnel is open to visitors. Lighting is a bit dim. The ground may be wet and slippery, hence wear comfortable shoes.The highlight should be at the end of tunnel with its unique 70cm lava stalagmites . Entrance fee 3,000 won. Toilet facilities available just before the cave ticketing office.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.
Manjanggul cave is a nice place that worth to visit, history how the cave made by. The length of cave is around 1 kilometre.

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Manjanggul Cave came to me as a surprise. To walk in a lava tube is an enchanting experience. There are steep stairs and long walk so be prepared. Don't bring heavy bags. Wear jacket because its cold inside the cave. Bring good camera. As you enter the cave, you will see the limestone that looks like lava flow (see picture attached). The path is dim that completes the enchanting atmosphere. By the end of the road, you can see the lava column.

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world. It is one of the UNESCO heritage. There's a good 1km walk from the entrance of the cave til you get to the end of the tunnel to sight the beautiful stalactites.  The tunnel is of course much longer than that however access is only allowed up to the 1km mark. The path is dark, chilly,  rocky and slippery. Please wear good shoes and bring a jumper and mini torchlight if you wish.

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and it is a designated as a natural monument.Not an easy walk as lots of even walkway,  slippery and dark. Take a slow walk to enjoy the surrounding and was cooling as you walk. You will be able to see the trace of the lava that flow through the cave. I saw some who rush all their way in and out.With young children do note of their safety, for older people who having legs problem do not try. Partly, you need to walk down the stairs which is not easy and when you finished you need to walk up again.We really enjoyed the nature of this cave.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Manjang cave is impressive! One of our party has arthritic feet, but even she managed to navigate the uneven surfaces by taking great care. The entry/exit includes steep stairs and be aware the handrail is slippery. There are two sections with ropelike lava walkways (one worse than the other) - these are by far the most difficult and uneven terrain to walk. The lava tube itself is pretty much on plane... no significant inclines or decents. Be aware that at the end you retrace your steps to the entrance.

Manjang cave in overall was really nice expierence, but we got a bit cold.When outside is more than 30 degrees, and you go downstairs, it's a bit...cool.And wet as well.But I won't whine about it, because the expierence you get there is more important!We were walking really slowly taking pictures of everything (if you don't have a good camera, pictures won't bet any good ://)They have diferent color lights and it makes cave more visitor-friendly.Only thing is that there is really crowded...Even though we went there on a weekday.So be prepared to see a lot of people there as well.

Manjamg cave is located on the north-east of Jeju, away from most of the hotels. In order to get to it, you will need to take a car, tour bus, or private taxi tour.The cave is massive and long, but not too interesting compared to real adventure caving. It is basically an uncomfortable walk in a cold and dark tunnel.Overall verdict: If you happen to go here on a tour, drive past, or have never been in a cave, go andcheck it out, otherwise don't waste your time.

Make sure to bring a jacket with you to the cave if you get cold, there is about a 10C temperature difference from outside to inside. So if you visit in Summer, it's a great break from the heat and humidity. It's about a kilometer walk, so give yourself plenty of time. Overall,a. Great attraction for all those visiting the island!!
Loved my first visit to a lava tube cave. Dark, lots of texture, educational information provided. Lots of fun and nice even on a rainy day!
lots of nice trees, bonsais, stones & cave. This Park was made by one man alone

Located next to Manjanggul Cave (a must-visit site), this park is great to let loose your inner child. If you have plenty of time and want to challenge yourself, go in without using the map! Remember to ring the bell when you have navigated through successfully and don't forget to collect all 6 stamps in the maze!

Located in the north eastern part of the island.  Took us an hour from hotel.  The cave temperature is 5-10C lower than outside, so suggest to bring a jacket and don't wear your Jimmy Choos.  Is wet and slippery with uneven grounds.  (Not suggest for elderly)The open part in 2017 is the 2nd section.  which is about 1km from start to end. First you walk down a steep stairs 3 floors down and you start walking. When you reach the large platform at the end and see the huge lava rocks, take photo and then you walk back .Spent about 2 hours there.
little bit disappointed, I wish I can see spectacular stalagmites and special lighting. but the cave very ordinary.

Lava tubes are different all over - so these have their own special yet similar features. The overall experience was well worth it and I certainly recommend the visit. The trail is reasonable well developed with stairs down into the tubes. Though basically light, I thought the selected illuminations added to the features and overall feel of the caves. It is not overly spectacular in showing off the various formations and features, but it still gives a good view of the tube walls. Be careful of the path as it does have rough spots and puddles. Moist, cool and over 2 kms of walking, I enjoyed the visit, although not the most impressive caves I have visited.
Lava tube cave, UNESCO heritage place, is the highlight of jeju tours. Amazing georock transformation and preservation . Worth the visit.
Lava cave. Big, huge cave. cold inside. can see the lines and cracks that lava form. The spotlight makes the rocks wall look beautiful

Kimnyoung Maze Park is just beside the Manjang Cave, so I recommended a short 1hr stopover if you are heading to the cave.  Avoid the maze park on rainy days as the ground gets really muddy when it rains.

Kimnyoung Maze Park is in the east of Jeju. We stayed in the West and we took a 30,000won tax to the place. The maze isn't very big but it was quite fun. Ditch the map and have fun getting lost. You see messages and signboards at different places and dead ends. The taxi driver offered to wait for us at the Maze without any cost while waiting as there's hardly any taxi in the area. And he drove us to our next destination (charging by metre). If you are planning to self drive, it is just right next to manjanggul cave. it is worth spending the 45mins to 1 hour in the maze.

just take a bus within 10min. i reached this beach. that was one of beautiful beach in jeju IMO as clear water with white sand also seaweed. it also has some windmill near around. except the beach that has a camp site. quite comfortable & relaxing place.the water was cool & the view also beautiful. it has many small crab,conch & fish. many people busy with them. ha. just no luck on i don't have a pretty sunset. anyway, worth to take time for visit here after cave & maze.
Just next to Manjanggul caves. Good place to go after your kids get bored of seeing lava formations. Tickets are around $3 SGD per person, not very expensive and some adventure for the kids too.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).
Just another cave. Gua tempurung in Ipoh, Malaysia is much more interesting and adventurous than this. This is just a route cave which you have to go out using same route
Just another cave. Cold and damp, dark and wet. However, it is one of the Unesco heritage site. Hence you should pay a visit. Just walk in 1km and another 1km out.

Jeju island is a really beautiful place and there is so many amazing sites but i was a bit underwhelmed by this view compared to others i saw. I'd say it was worth seeing if you are in the area but essentially its just a rock, and there are lots more, much prettier rocks, around the island!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

I've visited many caves but by far this is the first lava tube that I have experienced. It is interesting to know the science and geography behind this magnificent tube. However, only 1 km deep into the tube is open to tourists. You can take a public bus directly from the Jeju bus station if you opt to travel on a budget. The bus fare is less than KRW 2000 compared to very pricey tours with taxi. The bus ride is only slightly more than an hour away from Jeju City.

I've never been in a lava tube before, but it was a lot like a cave. The formations inside are pretty interesting and the park does a good job lighting them colorfully. It was a nice walk. However, it is very touristy and if you've been to bigger caves in other parts of the world it's just cool, not extremely impressive.

It's the first stop in our itinerary & we went to the Ssanyong cave where there are also lava tubes. It's not as big  as Manjang cave & it's better lighted. There's also a folk village in this park, a flower & bonsai garden & lots of lava stones formed into different figures. A bird sanctuary is also here.

It's quite exciting to walk down the huge lava tube and imagine the flow of lava melting its way to the ocean. You see the striped walls indicating different levels of the flow, each stripe has a bit different color. Glossy lava sinters, black, dark red and orange. Fantastic landscape of big and small stalactites and stalagmites. It's a shame, only a small part of the lava tube is opened for public. And the trail is arranged pretty dull. Nothing (except the natural beauty of the cave) would take your breath away and make you come again.There are many tunnels that branches from the main tube and go further and further after the end of the main trail. With a proper lighting and clever management it could be a fantastic place that would attract plenty of tourists and make them come again and again to explore this place.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.

its my first mountain hike, its a straightforward trail but tricky with rocky stone paths at some incline parts. not recommend for those with weak knees and ankles or just go slow n wear ur ankle guards. go up seongpanak (easier as more gradual)and down gwaneumsa (alot of steps, steeper) but gwaneumsa has valley view, creek view and there?s a tiny cave opening near the base with blast out icy wind even in summer.. pretty cool. there?s a bus to and from seongpanak and take taxi from gwaneunsa or prearranged pickup as there?s hardly a bus there.its a total of 9 hrs including rest stops though i rested longer at the peak and pressed on at rest stops. do pace yourself.. calves been killing me midway down the descent. needless to say its a painful walk for the next couple of days.. i slathered all the muscle aches cream..

It's my favourite place in Jeju! It's not just an island as we thought it would be! Rmb to bring along your international license if you are planning to ride any motorised vehicles. We biked around the island which in my opinion allows you to see more attractions. Do time checks regularly as the ferry leaves at around 5pm, note that the timings given on the booklet is not accurate. Had the best Jakk Pong (seafood noodles) on this island near the cave! (just follow the smell) try the peanut ice cream! its better than the hallabong one.

It's more like a zoo combined with a synthetic garden. What attracted me were the cave's and they were disappointing as well, I've been to much nicer and impressive Caves, these are just hollow space under ground. Waste of time in my opinion, there are much better and natural sights in Jeju.

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.
