Its definitely a worthwhile trip to make and just walking through the Lava Tube is quite an experience.  It is not everyday one has the opportunity to walk through and see the various formations, the caves formed, columns, the different textures formed, etc.One needs to be relatively fit to do the walk with comfortable shoes as the location tends to be wet. Elderly should have a walking stick which will help and carry a torchlight.  Its a few degrees lower underground.

it's definitely a unique place to visit but you should wear proper shoes as the 2km walk to and from the entrance has lots of rocky areas...the cave was dark,cold and wet but worth the visit if it's part of your tour.

It's an incredible lava cave! We spent half day in this sight seeing and my daughters loved! (2 teenagers) It's very difficult to do sight seeing in Jeju without a rental car! We took almost an hour to arrive there, and the same to come back!!

It's a really really nice place except for the diver women with the fishes and dead octopus, that's gross and I'm vegan. Anyway, you can pay for a quick boat trip to see the surroundings of this place like caves and also a rock full of birds (Think of Paracas, Peru, i think it's similar). The view at the top is AMAZING, like I said, you can see all Jeju? Seogwipo? I don't know but it's BEAUTIFUL. There are also many food spots and stores plus Starbucks and Dunkin Donuts.

It's a pretty long cave but that's pretty much it. It's very cold, wet and dark down there (went during summer) so do get your windbreakers/jackets and flashlights ready. Whether you should visit entirely depends on you. If you have more more on your itinerary of Jeju, then you'd most likely want to give this place a miss.

It's a nice stop in general but also when you visit the nearby Manjanggul Cave Lava Tube. The whole maze property is very well maintained and nicely done, a great place for a picknick. The maze itself isn't that difficult and with the map really easy. Some fun for the young as well as the older ones. I also found out how useful a drone can be - to exit a maze easily :)

It's a mixed review.  The ticket price is 10,000KRW per adult and since other natural attractions are around 2,000KRW, this park should be well worth it.  Highs: The caves are really cool as well as the Bansai and Stone Garden. The park is easy to walk and has shops and toilets easily available.  Transportation is also easy as it's just the 702 bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal for 1 hour. Lows: The park is dated, like late 90s with its signage and information cards.  The bird exhibit, stone exhibit and flower garden are average at best.  While the park trail is easy to walk, you do walk through gift shops for the next exhibits (so a bit too tourist-y). Overall, it makes for a decent easy afternoon, especially with kids or elderly.  The park needs some updating to be worth the ticket price, but it is close to the beach (just 5 mins walking).
It's a lava cave, national herritage. Nothing special in there, it was dark and only rocks along the way. You need to be careful because the floor was wet and slippery.

It's a hedge maze straight out of the movies, except with nothing popping up to scare you. It is only the hedge.  It takes about 20 minutes to find your way out and costs 3,300 for an adult. It's 500m down the road from Manjanggul cave, so if you're going to the cave you could stop by, but not worth the trip otherwise.
It's a cave, so it's dark and humid.  I learnt something new about lava cave though.  Worth the stop if you're around and have time.

It's a 1 km walk from the entrance to the inner of the cave. Remember you need to walk 1km back, the place you enter is also the exit. Before you embark on your walk, there is a long flight of stairs to go down to the cave. If you have elderly people traveling with you, they may want to skip this place as the area is wet and slippery. There are lights to guide your path in the cave too but it is dim lit. Else, I would recommend this place for a great cooling walk, some geology insights for tourists too.
It's 1km walk.You can learn about geographical things about caves as you walk by.It is colder than outside, you should bring clothes with you.
It?s very cold in the cave. So dress warm for this location. Try wearing waterproof shoes, lots of puddles.
It?s like a Learning journey, pretty cold 8 degree) and dark in the cave.Just need to follow the pavement and keep walking to the end of the cave.

It?s about an hour?s drive from the airport. Entrance is KRW11,000 for one adult.  The tulips and cherry blossoms were in full bloom. So lovely!  A surprise was the caves. It?s so cool!  Really worth the visit.

It?s a very big place.. there are a cave, garden, mang kind of birds, trees ans flowers.. i think it is a good place to visit in jeju.. you can see many things here.. but it is difficult to find a bus to here and the bus is not ontime..

It?s a cave, but a long one. With a story to tell. Interesting rock features related to how it was formed with good signage in Korean, English & Chinese. Areas marked out & lit appropriately for safety. Well thought out balance between safety & keeping the natural features.

It wasn't very clear from the guide books. The spot is basically a volcanic rock formation that is concave. I'm not sure that you can actually have a good view of the formation with its lush green centre from any walkable vantage point (like you get from travel books). So on nearing the spot, stop on the highway shoulder to get a distant photograph first.After you arrive, note that the car park is basically one way. Miss a turn and you have to exit the carpark and come back from the entrance. Be prepared to walk / hike as the areas open to public are quite steep. You can get a good open view of the city or the ocean. Refreshing scenery.

It was, by far, the longest cave I've ever explored. It was freaking cold, so I do recommend to bring a jacket. It was also really slippery at some areas since water was dripping from the ceiling, so wearing closed comfortable walking shoes would really help. By the time we reached the end, there was this impressive looking lava tube. Take note that the attraction only accepts admission up until around 3pm since it takes time to wander about the 1km cave. Time spent depends on how fast you walk or how long you stop and stare at the magnificent natural wonders made inside. There was even this natural-made rock formation of Jeju-do! Awesome.

It was very cooling in the cave, you can feel the temperature difference at the entrance of the cave. It was dark and slippery, be careful! It was really amazing to see the insides of this cave, definitely eye-opening experience~

It was very cool inside the cave and it took more than 30 minutes to walk from the entrance to the end of the cave. Explanatory boards were posted along the way to tell how the tube, the columns were formed.

It was raining and our driver decided to start with this attraction first. Although before getting into the caves, we got a bit wet, but once inside we lost track of the rain. This is a lava cave and quite different from the usual limestone caves. The only problem is that we have to backtrack all the way out. When we came out, the rain has stopped and the sun was out. Just Nice.

It was not the best weather day on Jeju Island, so opted to go to the cave. I was looking forward to it based on other cave visits in different countries but it did not turn out that way. The exterior garden was more interesting. It great from a historical UNESCO standpoint but it does not standout as a tourist list must see attraction when there's so many choices. The plus side, you're next to 2 other tourist attraction, forest and maze. But for the cave itself, it's large for multiple people to walk through at a time, mostly straight path and you get to the end of a platform and that it. Not too much variation of rock formations, colors, not a photographic, boring, not worth on a must do list.

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

it was just a super long cave that is really cold, perfect when you are visiting during the hot summers. Wear comfortable shoes because you will be avoiding water puddles, trekking on uneven rocky floors. Its just a super long walk in and out.

It was indeed a unique experience entering a lava tube. We do enjoyed the view of spectacular work of Mother Nature. However, do be prepared for a sudden plunge in temperature. The temperature outside doesn?t not reflect the exact temperature inside. We weren?t prepared for a sudden drop from 25C to 12C when we walk further into the cave. Also, do come with shoes with good grip as the flooring is filled with pot holes and it?s always wet. Do highly recommend a visit to this really unique cave.

It was cool to see the lava patterns, but I don't think one needs to go beyond 70 meters.  It is dark and the ground is not level in the cave, so my caution to you is to watch your step.  A lady from my tour group had sprained her ankle while we were in there.  It is easy to just look up and sideways, but if you don't want your trip marred with pain and discomfort, watch your step.  It is very interesting, informative, and very cool to see how this little island was formed.

It was around a 20 minute walk into the cave and another 20 minutes going out... Path was dark and wet, so you must be careful walking inside the cave... It was a good experience with a little workout.
It was an okay park, easy and nice to walk around, the best part was the caves. Love exploring the caves!However, food choices are limited should one be hungry.

It was an interesting experience to walk through the 1km long tunnel if you enjoy understanding and seeing the various structures and rock formations formed from the lava flow. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip, tunnel is rather slippery and rocky.  On a side note, I think I enjoyed walking through the Manjanggul Caves better than the DMZ Third Tunnel. :)

It was an interesting 1 km walk into the cave. It had some level of lighting in there. There were information boards along the way regarding certain volcanic & rock formations. It an unusual cave. Yes,a recommended visit.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

It was along the way to Manjanggul Cave. As we had missed the bus 990 which could take us to the Cave, we had to walk the 2.5km way. About 1.4km's walk, we came to the Gimnyeong Maze Park. It was a fun place even for adults. We did not follow the map so that it would be exciting. Indeed it was, and the more lost we were, the more exciting it got.

It was a rainy morning that my friend and I visited this cave. We were greeted with a flight of stairs entering the cave. The temperature in the cave was so much lower, approximately 10 degrees celsius. It was dark and slippery too. The further we walked in, the colder it gets. The pathways are actual lava that hardened over the years therefore, it was not a smooth walk. A lot of locals enjoyed their walk, some strolling while youngsters brisk walk, talking and laughing along the way, making the whole cave not too scary. It was a nice morning walk looking through the structure left behind by the once active volcano forming rocks, mini wells naturally. The work of nature. Beautiful!

It was a nice walk around Hallim Park especially if you like Bonsai trees, folk Village and more...We had a great walk aroundthe area and the weather was so freshly cold?. Went to the caves was also interesting. Beautiful garden. A place to come back. I like to put more pictures but I could only put 10 of them.
It was a nice trip. When in Jeju, try to visit here. You'll see interesting lava formations inside the cave. The entrance fee is KRW 2,000 for adults.
It was a nice mix of gardens, animals, nature (caves).  Good for families.  Not great in anything but a good variety to keep everyone interested.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

It was a hot day so felt great to get away from the  heat and descend into the cave. It felt about 10 degrees colder so be prepared with a light jacket. As with all caves, this has rocky wet floors that are very treacherous for those without proper track shoes. Very interesting signboards with geographical  information about the formation of lava caves too.

It was a 1km walk in and 1km out again. The lights were pretty dim unless there are signboards. The path inside is quite rocky with puddles of water here and there. Spent most of time watching out for puddles of water and where to walk instead of enjoying the lava cave. The cave was colder than outside, so might have to prepare a thin jacket.

It took me a long time to get there. All those folks with cars would have no problems. But I am on a budget, and I am bussing it all the way. I came here from the Seongsan Ilchulbong crater thing, and I took the 701 bus to the stop that said it was for the cave. Then I walked 2.5km to the cave. The cave was gloriously cold inside, as I was a hot sweaty mess by then (Korean people staring at the fat, sweaty American haah!). I took my time through the cave, it was nice and worth the trip for me, even though it took me almost 2 hours to get back after I was finished. I think you could take a cab for a reasonable price... but I am cheap.

It is the longest lava tube in the world. It is nature in its untouched, pristine form. If you walked inside the cave, the place is cooling and dark. Spotlights are only at some places where they are installed to highlight the lava formations. The ground is also wet and  be aware of puddles of water. Along the way, stop at the attractions , read the information given and you will understand what you are looking  at. There is a Stone Turtle in the shape of Jeju island and  at tge end of the walk  you will come face to face with the lava column, the best spot in the cave.
It is the first lava cave I visit, easy to walk in and the temperature is not too cold or too humid.

It is such a beautiful place to go! The scenery inside the cave is breathtaking and it is unbelievable for such a view. It is a bit cold and dark tho, but it has light installed along the pathway. A very nice place!

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)

It is said to be one of the longest lave tube caves in the world. This one is over 7km and about 1 km is open for public. I saw quite a few natural caves with stalagmites and stalactites, but this one was different. It is made by lava river flowing underground.

It is really long cave. Pls wear sensible shoes and high heels are NO NO there.I think it is nice for the first 15 min but after 15min it all looks the same. So unless you really knows you rocks well, or else it will be just a walking trip

It is not the most beautiful cave. The size was impressive. There is also a lava column which is the largest known in the world, but when I saw it, I did not have the feeling that it was so large that this would be the largest of the world, but the lava column itself was wonderful.

It is not only a botanical garden. They also have local animals on display, their cave system is quite big with three caves and their bonsai garden is beautiful. You could easily spend here a whole day. 12.000 won per adult sounded pricey at the beginning but these huge gardens and animals need a lot of maintenance and are in good conditions. We enjoyed our visit.

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.
It is good for students to learn about Lava structures, properties. May be a bit boring for common folks. But can be visited once to see a lava caves.

It is definately a fun and interesting place for geography nerd. For us, the normal tourist, it is still quite interesting walk. Along the walk, there are board explaining different phenomena and lava structure that happen in the cave many years ago. At the end of the walk, you able to see how the lava flow into the cave. Then you have to walk back to entrance to exit.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.

It is amazing to see nature?s wonder , a must go in Jeju. Will not take much of your time as just 1km of the cave is open to public. Must go till the end of the tunnel to see nature?s wonder. Be careful while walking as the rocks formed after lava formation is uneven.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

It is a lava tunnel. It's interesting to see but not a must-see. There were some stairs to descent into the tunnel at the entry and it gets pretty dark inside. Your eyes will need to adjust, and there isn't any place to grip along the wall. Please wear comfortable shoes and some layers since it gets wet and chilly inside. Walking paths are uneven on some areas, and most are not well-lit. The tunnel is purposely not well-lit to preserve the natural habitat of its resident animals. A round trip from the entrance will take about 30-40 mins if you're strolling through the tunnel. We visited this cave as part of Yeha East course tour. If you have interest in geological formation, stalagmite, and nature, you may find it interesting.

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.

It felt pretty surreal to walk through the caves, and I mean it in a good way! Definitely worth the visit.Just one advice - grab a cardigan when you go: even in hot summer days it is pretty cold in the cave! and also a torch can be useful so you can see better the shapes of the lava walls.
Interesting! There are quite a few things to visit like Botanic Garden, Bonsai Garden, Folk Village, Lava Cave, Bird Garden, Water Garden etc. Recommended!

Interesting cave, for someone who has stayed in a city for the whole of her life. We went in winter and what is interesting is that the cave is considered warm for winter. Be prepared for the long walk to and back and the path would be too rocky for strollers or wheelchairs

In this cave, you're allowed to walk about one kilometer in the lava tube where you'll find a lot of variation in the formation and environment. It's a lot of space in one of the tubes (the other one was closed off during our visit). In the tube, there has been several different lava levels and different factors, creating unique patterns on the walls, floor and ceiling. It's recommended to bring something warm down the cave, since it's a bit chilly.Along the way, there is several signs about detail information (both in Korean and English) about the different shapes and things in the cave.

In the summer heat, Manjanggul is the perfect place to escape the heat. It's quite cold inside, and water drips from the ceiling. I changed into jeans and a light sweater before going in, which was perfect. The texture of the cave is fascinating! There are good informational English placards that explain how the cave formed. The floor of the cave is quite bumpy, so take care not to trip.It's a popular destination but getting there and leaving can be time-consuming unless you are with a tour. I took a bus from the Bijarim Forest to get to the cave, which dropped us off right at the cave. The bus leaving right from Manjanggul only leaves once an hour, so I recommend checking the bus departure times before you go into the cave and plan your stay accordingly. Otherwise, there are taxis but the drivers are rudely persistent, charge a non-negotiable flat price, and refuse to go by the meter. They kept pestering us the entire hour we waited for the bus, even after we rejected many times and had begun ignoring them.

In my opinion, there are two world heritage sites that visitors to Jeju must visit. One is Manjanggul Cave and the other one is Seongsan Illchubong. Manjanggul Cave is unique as it was formed by lava movement thousands of years ago. It provides an insight into Jeju's geographical structure. The temperature in the cave could be chilly, so bring a jacket along. Visitors to the cave usually walked for about 2 km to reach the end, where photos with a large stalactite pillar could be taken. Other features in the cave include lava formations that look like elephant feet, turtles and book shelves.

In fact it's just a large cave which is a Creation of mother earth, if you expect more human artificial you won't find it here. If you are a nature person you should totally come. It's huge and long though i think they should consider to bring more light in the cave.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

I'm from Hawaii, but this cave was very impressive, not to mention a welcome reprieve from the heat and humidity!Walking on wet lava rock is not for the faint-of-heart, so wear a good pair of tennis shoes that can provide some traction, because it is slippery!

I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

If you've been in a real cave, you'll only be downgrading if you go to this lava tube. It is a plane tube with lots of lights. There is no cool dark places, and the only formation at the end is meh. I prefer a normal cave with formations and a tour in which everyone turns of the lights ^^.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

If you're in the area I'd pop in but don't make a special trip - It's nice seeing all the old huts and how they used to live but once you've seen one set of huts they are all pretty similar. i think they have some events on sometimes as there is a stage, but when we were there, there was just four girls playing drums and no one was watching them. Oh and they randomly have some ostriches - didn't figure out why but they were pretty cool!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Oedolgae Rock, and finally Jeongbang Falls. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.

If you were to Seongsan Ilchulbong and to Manjang cave next, you can grab the taxi if there is no bus.. The fare is quite reasonable.Wouldnt expect that the cave would be that cold but it is as cold as Seoul during Spring time.. The lighting is very good. Though it is  a long walk to the end, it id worth it.. The deeper, the colder it is..
If you only have one day in Jeju, come to Hallim Park because they have everything in one place! Caves, butterfly garden, flower garden, birds area, mimic folk village and so on.

If you love trees and plants, caves, etc then you will enjoy Hallim Park. Great signage. Also the traditional village with thatched roofs was a treat. Had Mung bean pancake and fried pork for a tasty lunch. Great way to learn about Jeju and also a host of trees and plants from around the world. The volcanic caves were very interesting. Mr Song, the park's creator, had a great idea. Reasonable price as well. Highly recommend it.

If you love nature and have never seen any volcanic formation before, it would be worth the visit. Personally,  i enjoyed walking inside the cave and having a look at the volcanic formation.  It's like you can almost imagine how the lava flowed inside the tunnel a few thousand years ago :) i was in awe of how powerful mother nature can be. It was quite cold inside. Wear layers and proper shoes.  Can be quite slippery as well.

If you like caves, then you have to visit Manjunggul Cave. It is simply fascinating! It is an extremely cheap entry fee and an easy kilometer walk inside the lava tube. Though the weather outside was rainy and wet, we thought the cave would be drippy and wet as well. It was quite dry. The interior is spacious and equipped with fairly good lighting along the guided route. For kids learning about volcanoes and the structures of the earth, this is a great field trip.

If you like cave, do not miss out.my partner pick this one as a highlight in Korea. It's very huge cave.only open 1/3 ish though, you can walk on actual lava stones all the way.* MUST bring jacket or something to warm you up and wear proper shoes. its quite cool inside and wet.

If you like cats then this place is for you. There are about 20 cats roaming around the property. I am not a cat person at all but the cats did not bother me. They are friendly and stay out of the way of people. The maze was fun and somewhat challenging. I liked that they added a stamp feature (you had to find stamps on your journey) so it wasn't all about getting out. They are pretty chill here, so you could do the maze 1 million times if you wanted. If the parking lot is overflowing then I would recommend that you not go. The property isn't big enough for that many people. The positive is that there is a cave down the street you can visit as well. We didn't get to visit the cave because it was a public holiday. I would recommend that you go here, especially if you have kids. The value is not that high but most things on Jeju cost money. It is not a rip off.
If you have not experience going into a lava tube, you have to try Manjanggul Cave. A nice 30 mins walk inside the tube, and you will find a beautiful Manjang-gul at the end of the tube.

If you have limited time in Jeju and like nature, visiting Hallim Park should be very high up on your list (if not your number one). Its beautiful and very varied. Palm trees, beautiful gardens, plants, flowers, birds, reptiles, 2 caves, a   traditional village   (where you can get a tasty traditional lunch) - its full of highlights and in 2-3 hours you can see so many different things. This is one of the most beautiful parks I have ever visited and I think everybody can find something they like there. If the weather is good, you can also combine the visit to Hallim Park with some time on a nice sandy beach just infront of the park.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

If you garden or enjoy botanics this is a fabulous place. I just visited during Tulip season and the entrance was an alleyway of color. I imagine late in May and June when more plants are blooming Hallim is an even more stunning place. It contains a huge variety of plants, wishing I could grow some of these specimens in Colorado. They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested. The grounds include a couple of lava tunnels, which don't have a lot of spectacular cave features, but I still found them worth the walk through. They also have an amazing bonsai garden and a lovely water garden.I spent almost 2 hours exploring the flora on well marked walkways and paths in this lovely park.BTW, Hallim deserves an entrance fee for all the upkeep needed, not sure why they charge 2 dollars at a number of sea cliffs etc., that should be open to the public...

If you can't make it to Manjanggul caves, there are caves here too. There is a lot of English signage for the trees, which is great. There is a cafe and restaurant on site. I really enjoyed the  afternoon out, lots of lovely different areas to explore.

If you are there and have no place to visit, perhaps you may want to waste and hour or 2 to walk into the cave. There is no special attraction inside the cave that will give you a WOW factor. By end of the trail, you would just like saying...err...thats it? Its cold in winter and the floor are wet with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Its dark too.

If you are looking for a remote island off the coast of Jeju then this might not be for you. However, if you are after an island that is a short ferry ride away and has many activities to offer then this is it! Udo is beautiful, and attracts many tourists especially in the summer time. You can rent a bicycle for the day at about 10,000-12,000W, or rent an electronic bike/scooter thing (with an international drivers license). Caves, mountains, as well as many beaches to explore. Stay the weekend on Udo or ride the ferry back to Seongsan, you'll have a great time :).

If you are interested in caves at all, this one is unique.  Easily accessible, this horizontal lava tube demonstrates the vocanic processes happening over 100,000 years ago.  Cool, wet and accessible with helpful descriptions in multiple languages and little anthropromorphizing of geological shapes.  A quick visit taught us a lot....and our 7 and 10 year old kids enjoyed the walk.  Modest fee.

If you are expecting stalagmites and stalactites, this is not a place. If there were, we probably missed them. It?s a dark underground cave and very interesting to see the lava flows. You can see imprints of such flows on the actual ground you?re walking on. It?s a bit nippy, so if you are prone to being cold, may want to take a light sweater. There is no bathroom in the tunnel (which my son figured out trying to get out halfway in the tunnel/cave. He had to run back the way we came to find one.) It?s interesting. I just wished that there were more lights in the tunnels so one can appreciate it more. Uneven ground due to the lava flows, as expected. 2000W/$1.75 to get in, half for kids.If you've never been into one of these types of caves, you should.  If you have, maybe worth skipping.

If you are expecting something out of the ordinary, this case just isn't for you. No, there isn't any sign of life (bats) in it. It's just a natural cave formed, with tracks at it's natural state. Dark ambience, only with some help provided through man-made lights. But don't worry, the road before you is still visible.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I?m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn?t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it?s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn?t come here.If you?re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It?s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough ? if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it?s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it?s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.

if you are a nature lover like me, you should not miss this while you are in Jeju. Be ready to walk for 1 km and get prepared to experience some cold with dark which gives you an awesome feeling to enjoy the cave more.
If u have  visited any cave in China, anyone of them is much better than this one. Since the one in korea only open a tiny portion to tourists

I would highly recommend this place for an extremely hot or wet day.  Being covered and large enough, it was an enjoyable walk.  There was adequate lighting and enough fellow tourists not to make the cave walk too scary.  Despite the unevenness of the terrain - they are dried lava and so quite uneven, most people would be able to walk comfortably.It's certainly a nice change from limestone caves although some people may miss seeing amazing rock formations like the stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves.  In fact, I was not overly impressed with the gigantic lava mass on display at the end of the walk.  For me, the enjoyable walk was good enough.

I would echo an earlier review that said that you should not bother with this if you have done any caving or similar - this is aimed at casual visitors not experts. It is a gentle wander in a cool cave that is appropriately lit, reasonably level and there is enough English signage to explain what you need to know. It is the fact that this was a lava tunnel that is not interesting and the signs do explain how the lava flowed, melted and cut down and through from other tunnels. 1) Wear sensible shoes.2) If it has been raining it can drip a lot inside though on our visit I did not think so.3) Some might feel it is cold - I did not
I went to Manjang Cave. It  was really good place to see. It was very cold when we got in side and we can see you cave of Volcano, while you are walking the water drop down and very lively..

I went there during the peak of summer, it was scorching hot outside, but once you step down about 10steps into the cave, the temperature dropped instantly about 10degree celcius. It was dark inside, the floor is uneven, it's basically the original form of the cave. There's water dropping from the ceiling, but that's just the natural way it is inside the cave. Despite all that though it is a safe place to walk to, and it's really quite amazing inside the cave. You can see the signs of the lava once flowing through inside. Quite a fun experience for me =)

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I went their with my wife. I didn't find the place as interesting and exciting as other people claimed. My recommendation, unless you are a geologist this place has nothing substantial to offer. Take a warm cloth and comfortable shoes when you visit this place. The temperature in the cave is low(you feel cool even in summer) and the floor is wet and a little bit slippery.A person can have knowledge about lava tubes but personally I felt unsatisfied. The cave is very dark for anyone to figure out things inside. Information boards inside give information about the site. If a visitor has enough time to visit, you can drop by this place. But, if your schedule is tight you can skip this place.

I went in a hot summer day so I can't judge. It has different plants, animals, folk village and cave. If you interest in these things you might like it. I went there because I have free time to spend but I think if the weather is better it will be different

I went at July... quite a few steps down from entrance to cave and the floor is slippery with water...  You can feel the chill at entry, I suggest you remain in motion to avoid get cold..Walking around can be a challenge for some (especially for the elderly) since the floor is very rough and uneven, this is exacerbated by poor lighting in most parts throughout the cave.. a lot people used torches from phones to get around...It?s annoying for a inquisitive person as the half of the sign and info are Korean only... The interior of the space is pretty featureless... only two noticeable Lime stone caves are a lot more pretty, but it?s worth going if you are in the area and never been in a Lava Cave

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I was so surprised of beauty this park. I walked about 4 hours here to watch all places.in this park you can find beautiful birds, gardens, waterfall, caves, etc. to spend day here is amazing cause you feel that you in a forest with many trees and other signs of nature.

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was on my wear the Toms until they literally fall off my feet, and this definitely got them about there. If you do anything before going to this cave, make sure you have the right waterproof, grippy-ish shoes for the job. But really, this was cool, literally.  I managed to be hot and sweaty almost everywhere we went while on the island, but in the cave he temp drops to a comfortable 50something degrees. Just glorious! Is it worth the walk? I'm not sure. It was nice enough, and definitely cool to say I have been inside a cave at least once. So I guess I would put this on the itinerary if you are visiting the island for he first time. Would I go again? Likely not, I think once was enough!

I was not sure what to expect when we went to Hallim Park, but we really enjoyed it. It's a really nice walk, with flowers, statues waterfalls, caves and animals. It's nice to get away from the city noises if you have been on the mainland for a while. It's not a place you can spend an entire day, and for us was a bit of a trek to get there so make sure you plan your day to only be there a couple of hours.

I was looking forward to this attraction more than any other on Jeju and it didn't disappoint.  I wouldn't rate as #1 (more   touristy   than expected) but worth the stop.  If you can move past the gift stores selling trinkets, cheezy signage, animals in tiny cages and crowds, the attractions within the park are quite beautiful.  I especially liked the lava caves and the bonsai garden.  Those two areas alone were worth the stop.  If you have time, just past the park entrance is a stunning beach area.  Great for photos and possibly a toe dipped into the waters.

I was hoping to see how magnificient the lava is in one of the widest lava tube before going into the Manjang Cave. It is quite disappointing to realise that the cave is not entirely illuminated. The lighting is minimal in the cave which made walking and lava observation really difficult. I was going with my mum of around 60 years old, it is really difficult for her to see clearly in the tunnel. And the fact that you have to walk for  ~1 km into the tunnel and then the same way back is not entiring pleasing. When I was walking down the tunnel, I always thought   there will be better illumination/rocks in the next turn  . However, it was quite disappointing that this happens only at the end of the tunnel where you saw an illuminated lava pillar. I would recommend you to go to other caves if you want to see the lava clearly.

I was excited to see the Manjanggul Lava Tubes up close and personal, but I was rather disappointed after my visit..The Caves were poorly lit and without using a flashlight, one can barely see the markings on the rocks. The ground is very uneven and understandably so. However, for older people, children and people prone to ankle injuries, the lighting does not allow one to see where one is walking and injury can can easily occur.

I was excited to go see the Manjanggul caves, and had an image in my mind that unfortunately didn't fit what I saw. The whole experience is pretty cool, the floor is uneven, dodging water droplets becomes a game, the lava flow marks are beautiful, but lack of light, lack of stalactite formations, and a lot of areas that are fenced off let me down slightly. However, cheap entrance, and the atmosphere is actually quite lovely. If you get the chance to go, try and do it.

I was a bit disappointed because it was raining the day I visited the cave, the grandeur of it all totally depends on how beautiful it is outside.  Depends on how the sun hits it, you may get amazing colors in the cave.

I visited here with several work colleagues.  We had a great time and laughed so much trying to make our way through this maze.  Built by a westerner and former professor over a number of years, the time, planning and care that went into making the park are all quite easy to see and appreciate.  It is beautiful there, very green and clean, and close to Manjang Caves, another iconic Jeju attraction.  Negotiating the maze took us about 45 minutes...longer than we thought...but we laughed our way through it.  Once you make it to the center, you can climb up to a platform and ring the   finder's bell.    Great for photo ops.  They also have some traditional Korean games just outside the end of the maze...fun to play if you never have.  At the snack bars, they offer delicious Jeju-brand ice-cream.  And as a BIG added bonus for my fellow cat-lovers, LOTS AND LOTS of mascot cats, belonging to the mazepark builder.  He is now a retired gentleman, known for his affinity for cats; journalists and business persons who go to meet with him in his office are likely to find both his desk and his person draped with one or more of his uniquely colored cats...black, orange, brown, white and grey.  A GREAT activity for families (although very young children may tire unless you take them in a stroller); couples; and colleagues...good team-building exercise:  Who can lead us OUT of here?  LOL  You'll enjoy it.

I took public transport to get to the caves. There will be a city bus that stops at the bus stop: Manjanggul caves and from there you can either walk in (at least half an hour walk) or take a cab for 4,000 won. I would advise on taking the cab as it is rather cheap. The inside of the cave is rather wet and cold so you could bring a sweater if you're gonna stay in there for long. The pathway is rather rocky (as it is after all a lava tube cave) so good walking shoes would be great! There is only one entrance and one exit so be prepared for a long walk if you intend to check the cave out till the very end!

I think it really depends on what kind of traveler u are. Some people might find it boring, some people might find it cool. I love it. I've never been in a cave nor a lava tunnel so for me it was a new and exciting experience. The cave is huge, wet and super duper cold, colder than outside in fact and lit up enough to see where you're walking. It's nice to see and feel how hardened lava looks and feels like. Walking into Manjanggul's huge cave feels like a scene from Prometheus.. Awesome!

I say this one should not be missed, just because there are not a lot of lava tubes that exist and are easily accessible! The whole journey from the mouth of the cave to the lava column, and back, can be done in an hour. Walking thru the varying sizes of the tube, some areas narrow and some really big with high ceilings, is a spectacular experience! The largest lava column in the world, towards the end of the permissible distance, is a little underwhelming. Still, overall a great visit. Highly recommended when in Jeju.
I recommend you this place if you have a rent-a-car. It?sa very long cave, and registered as a UNESCO heritage.

I really liked this cave, or lava tube as it's also called. I was hoping for more stalagmites and such but the lack thereof doesn't bring down the points due to it's massive size and length. There are also signs along the way with information about the   tube   in different languages. I really recommend giing to this place when you go to Jeju!!

I really enjoyed visiting this cave. It reminded me of the beauty of God's creation. I was expecting to explore the entire cave, but unfortunately, they only allow the public to explore the first 1 kilometer. Nevertheless, it was an eye-opening experience for me.Tips:-1. Wear comfortable clothes.2. Wear a good pair of shoes.3.Bring a cap.4. Bring a torchlight. You gotta visit this place if you are in Jeju Island!

I really enjoyed my visit here. I've never visit a volcanic cave before but its an very cool place (literally!). The temperature in the cave is much cooler than outside, although be careful, because they keep it quite dark so it can be difficult to walk on without good shoes.

I read reviews/blogs about what & where and the most economical way to explore east of Jeju in a day. One of the blogs I read mentioned about Udo on her trip (you may look for theLostWanderer's blog-Jeju in 3 days for more detailed trip in Jeju). I just love this islet. I rented a manual bicycle to get around for KW 5000 for 2hrs, yet you can rent at KW 10000 for 3hrs to the entire day. Well for my time is constrain, & travelling on a budget & also wanted to keep myself fit as a preparation for Mt Hallasan hike, gladly I did. Other than bicycle, you can rent an e-bike, ATV, and a scooter. The tranquility & scenery that the place could offer is magnificent. Shouldn't let this islet slip from your list once in Jeju.I took bus #701 after I visited Manjanggul Cave & Gimnyeong maze park (same bus stop where I alighted for the cave) & alight at Seongsan Habour. At the port, I paid KW 5500 (to & fro) for I'm going back the same day to the main Island of Jeju.

I read a few reviews saying how it?s just a park with trees and birds but I love this place! The greenery is beautiful, the air is fresh with a cool breeze and the cave system is entrancing. Being from a concrete city means all this is actually quite a refreshing change of environment for me. I don?t particularly care for the animals and birds being kept in too small enclosures though. But the scenery alone is enough to give it 4*.

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I love this cave as it was calmy, a little bit wet but make you comfortable after a long walk from the bus stop. I had to walk 3km or more (I think) coz my legs felt so sore, but I love the walk inside the cave. If you take a public bus, don't finish up too late as you might miss the last bus.

I love nature but somehow Manjang Cave failed to impress me. I expected to see more so i was kinda dissapointed. Unless you're studying about lava formations, otherwise there was really nothing much to see. Wearing good sport shoes is recommended since some of the path is quite bumpy.

I liked this beach. We went there on a really windy day so it was... Windy. What was quite strange is you get down to shoulder level in the water then there is a hill and you end up at ankle level again. It was quite a strange experience. However it's probably a barrier to stop you going any further (?) but I didn't take note cos I am a rebel, the waves were awesome at that point. Eventually the lifeguard got tired of my antics and called me back in. He said it was because there were jellyfish out there... Unless the Korean for   you silly tourist   sounds like jellyfish?!?The black rocks (lava?) were quite awesome to hunt for crabs but there were these bugs that looked like flesh eating ones from the mummy so that freaked me out a little. You can get here from Jeju bus terminal using the 701 bus (3,000 KRW). There is a stop for it about 40 mins in. It's near Manjangul cave (6,000 KRW taxi) so worth combining it with a trip with that.

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I haven't been anywhere else in the world where there has been the option to walk a couple of kms through a volcanic cave. The experience is quite surreal. From 30+ degrees on the outside you soon plummet down to perhaps 10-15 degrees, damp and dark. The rock formations are stunning and they've done a good job to keep it natural without too much human interference.Bring sensible shoes.

I have visited Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong) for sunrise hikes on three occasions this year. Each was very different, but all pleasant. Things to consider:- The hike is all steps, but only takes about 20 minutes for a moderately fit person.- The top is always windy. If it's already windy at the base, make sure everything you carry is tied/contained, because it can be very windy at the top.- It costs a small fee to enter when the ticket booth is open. If you get there really early, they might not be open yet!- No bathrooms after you leave the parking lot (and no secluded places), so plan accordingly!- Nothing at the base will be open before a sunrise hike, but you should be able to grab coffee/donuts after!- It's nice to carry up a picnic breakfast and sit at the top to eat and watch the other tourists.- Check the weather before you go if you really want a good view. We had a couple cloudy days that were less spectacular, but still always a refreshing hike, beautiful mountain and cool views over the ocean.We usually pair our trip with a trip out to Udo Island or to some of the other east-coast attractions like Manjangul Caves.There's a lovely motel paired with a seafood restaurant about 10 minutes walk from the entrance to the peak hike. Follow the beach sidewalk almost to the edge of town. Views from the in-room balconies over the beach. Big rooms and nice folks, even if they don't speak any English.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

I had read the reviews here before my boyfriend and I went, but I am glad I didn't let the negative ones sway me. This place is really awesome. Just imagining the lava flow through as we were walking was mind blowing! And it's really NOT that dark down there. I mean it is a cave so don't expect the sun to be shining but I don't know what people were expecting! It's a really great experience and we loved seeing all the different ways lava forms after hardening. I highly suggest this! It was a bit wet down there so wear a hood or hat and some sneakers.

I had read some reviews that it was damp and dark and not worth a visit. So, I went with little expectation. When I stepped into the cave, I was amazed! It was definitely a place for people who love nature! As I walked through the tunnel, I tried to imagine the hot volcanic larva flowing through larva tube, leaving these marks and traces. I would highly recommend the place to people who really love the wonders of nature. Yes, the place was damp, with water dripping from the ceiling and very uneven floors and puddles of water everywhere.I still find it worth the 2.5km walk from the bus stop at the main road. To get there, we took bus 701 and got off at the Manjanggul Cave Bus Stop. Bus 990 could take us right to the entrance but the bus was so irregular. We had just missed one. Therefore we decided to walk in. It was an okay walk.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I guess if you've been inside a really spectacular cave before this won't be much to you but for someone who doesn't go into caves that often, like me, this is a cool experience. the cave is nice and cool so it is refreshing on a hot day. It's also good to visit during a rainy day as it is underground. It's dimly lit and has a spooky ambiance. part of the walls look like they're melting chocolate. I would recommend it as it is one of the highlights of the island.

I found the volcanic caves here interesting but apart from that it was just another botanic garden. We went when the rapeseed and cherry blossoms were in bloom which was very pretty and a good photo opportunity. However, the same flowers are everywhere in Jeju at that time of year and don't cost anything to take a photo.

I found it well boring to be honest. I prefer stuff like the lava caves and waterfalls - I guess I just like to be wowed. However it was a peaceful place and it was surrounded by lovely countryside. Maybe a place for a stroll with your loved one. Still if you want to get there from Jeju - you can get a bus 710-1 from the bus terminal. Note there are two 710's (assume the other one is 710-2).  It costs about 3,000 KRW (40 minute ride) and there is a designated stop about 3 or 4 stops after Gyorae Entrance (not junction which is 2 stops away). Note: Gyorae Entrance is a good stop to know about as it on the north - south road (Jeju-seogwipo) which is the 781/782 bus route.... just in case you want to go anywhere else after or get bored like me :)How helpful am I!

I find walking in this lava cave is interesting as it is so cool inside and surprisingly there is no bad smell as it is rather wet. The cave produces it's on air conditioning as the temperature inside is around 15-17 Celsius. Some areas are well lighted and some are not, proper walking shoes are needed as there are many uneven areas along the path provided. Good experience for the ones who loves outdoor!

I find this cave beautiful as it is made by nature. It is just 1km long, it is good for a short trip. The place is cold, that's why Koreans go here in the summer. If you get bored easily, this place is not for you as the cave doesn't have a variety of rock formations.Furthermore, if you do not like to walk in rocky paths, you may not appreciate this. This place is dimly lit to preserve the cave, so you have to be careful. Overall, a good place to visit if you appreciate nature.

I expected a longer walk for this, given that this is what Mother Nature had blessed us with, but this cave is only opened for the first 1km to the public. Still, it was an amazing sight (with the turtle-like rock formation and the various lava formations). Wear comfortably with a cap or hoodie as the cave will be chilly and the water will drip from above! Also, bring flash lights as it can get quite dark!

I enjoyed my visit to Manjanggul cave, however it was not my favorite place in jeju. What i liked was that they had signs and explanations for everything in English so you could learn on how it was formed. It is a little cold down in the cave, wear a jacket and comfortable shoes.

I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

I can't make of this place. It has plants, caves, a folk village and greenhouses. Yet none of the attractions was really top rate. I would give it a miss and visit attractions with more focus on any one of the above.

I can imagin Udo is a quiet and beautiful island to stroll or bike sometime, but the day we visited was full of people.  We arrived there already at noon and rented electric bicycles to start rounding the small island.  The road was full of small vehicles and bikes moving or stopping by the road, I did not feel I was in the nature but a hustle corner.  There were quite some restaurants and cafes along the route, the one we went was full of people, price of food/drink is in high end.  It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I?d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There?s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

I arrived that place on a sunny afternoon.When I entered the cave, I immediately felt very chilling and refreshing!I was really amazed, beautiful formation from the lava, 'elephant toes' 'cupola' etc.The floor is wet and uneven, so be careful.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

I am interested in world heritage and Manjang Cave is included in sites of Jeju's world heritage so I went there. I had never walked inside a cave before, so it was an interesting experience. And I appreciate the carving in the walls and the shapes of rocks that were formed by volcanic activities.The temperature inside the cave is colder than the temperature outside, so it's better to bring a jacket.

Holy cow, you should see the bonzai park in this amazing place. also the caves were amazing. one life saving advice though: bring your bug repellant othervise you'll return home with very nasty fly bites.

Highly expected to visit this cave from the photo on the internet, because this site listed in the UNESCO as world heritage. But there is only a cave with stone that I don't know. Reach the end of the cave only big rock that from frozen lava. Maybe for cave lover you'll like it.Tips: bring jacket because so cold inside.

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.

Heard there are several entrance, but only one is open to public. The cave has been fitted with a pathway that takes away the hard work of walking on rocky surface for you. It is still quite deep though and will be challenging for anyone with lower fitness level. The tube is lit along the way and it is quite cold. If you've visited a natural cave before, this cave might be less interesting.

Having visited other caves in Vietnam and Australia, I was expecting a more developed tourist spot. The visit is essentially a 2km walk under low-light and chilly conditions. Most of the place is wet and somewhat slippery. I will not recommend it unless you have spare time in Jeju

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.

Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed.
