You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Having never been to a lava cave before,  this was definitely a new and cool(literally,  because it is a few degrees colder than the outside temperature in the cave) experience for us. There's quite a bit of walking involved-about 1 km in almost darkness. There are a number of different formations such as stalactites, etc marked along the way, until you finally reach the lava column. If you don't have a car, getting here is quite difficult since the bus stop is almost 2 km away-the walk was very beautiful though, along one of the oreums.

Having experienced caves in the USA, I was expecting a similar experience.  Not at all the the case on Jeju with the manjanggul caves.  This UNESCO site is self led, wet, slippery, dark and EXCELLENT!  Also, very cool in temperature which was very welcome in the humid conditions present on Jeju in July.
Has a little bit of eveything that Jeju offers, lots of trees, flowers, stones, caves and a tiny folk village.

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.

Hallim Park is so big, we didn't even get to see everything. Spend at least 3 hours here (I think). That should be enough time. I loved the caves, the bonsai garden, the cactus garden, the cherry blossoms, and the tulips festival! Lovely park to visit.

Hallim Park is really a variety of interesting elements of Jeju Island rolled into one. The cave located within Hallim park is one of the main attractions. Other attractions include a multitude of gardens, some animal exhibits, and even a small recreated folk village.If you have more than 3-4 days on Jeju island, I would highly recommend Hallim Park. It can be combined with the excellent Hyopjae Beach located close by. Great day for families. If you are staying less than 3 days, it would probably be best to focus on the main natural attractions Jeju Island is so famous for.I enjoyed exploring the park, taking some pictures with my wife, and then relaxing at the beach.

Hallim Park is located at the West part of Jeju island, approximately 20 minutes drive from Jeju City. The park is pretty large as it has a wide range of gardens (cactus, bird park, flowers) and it also has a couple of lava caverns. The park does not have spectacular sites but it is a great and cozy place to spend time especially for families. Do wear comfortable shoes.

Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Hallim Park is huge and divided into various sections. You can spend almost a day slowly strolling through the different sections for plants, animals, cactus and you can even visit underground caves. You can also visit a very small old village modelled after the olden days of Korea. It?s a place suitable for all families with kids or senior citizens. The entry ticket is on the expensive side for Jeju.

Hallim Park is a jack of all trades but a master of none. It is rather unusual to find a mini bird park, caves and gardens altogether in the same place (but not all of them were stunning). Some of the vegetation were not well maintained. That said, if you enjoy viewing cherry blossoms and tulips, this is your chance. When we went last week, the cherry blossoms and tulips were in full bloom and they were absolutely a wonderful sight. We were hoping to see cherry blossoms in Jeju and didn't know we will catch them right here at Hallim Park. You can miss everything else, but don't miss these seasonal flowers.

Hallim park is a good place for a day of relaxation and enjoyable experiences.The entrance fee is KRW10,000. You will be provided the map of the park.The park divided into 9 different themes. We didn't have chance to explore all of it.There is a beautiful cascading waterfall. If you are pressed for time, it is better to visit this place first.Hallim Park also have traditional-styled houses as folk village in Jeju.Within the park,there is also a plant nursery. Different species of flowers are found here.Throughout the park, there are numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather.Other than that, it have Bird Garden, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves
Hallim park has it all. It has nice gardens, lava caves, birds, bonsai garden etc. It is easy to reach by public transport and is a pleasure to visit.We really enjoyed this park.

Hallim Park has everything you would want to see. It has a big and beautiful flower garden, stone and bonsai garden, caves you can explore, a folk village, and a wonderful cactus garden.  It also has a bird garden and reptiles in cages.  You can spend at least half a day exploring everything.

Hallim Park has a mixed big of attractions --- from folk village, lava cave to bonsai and tropical gardens.  It is worth spending a couple of hours exploring.......many nice spots for taking pictures around the park........beware though, each of the attraction is not very spectacular or unique, but the park just gives a sense of the essentials in Jeju in one place

Hallim Park features an extremely interesting cave complex quite unique as it has been dug by lava, a traditional Korean village, beautiful waterfalls, a bonsai garden and a section with creative sculptures. The price is very affordable and you can also visit the beautiful beach opposite the park while you're there. Worth a visit if you have spare time on your hands as it is quite far from the main attractions.

Hallim is mixture of small zoo,botanical garden, lava caves and stones. We arrived     In morning after rain,park was quiet, with not many visitors, relaxing. I liked walking through volcanic caves, beautiful bonsai garden with some trees around 300year old. And completely white peacocks, I did not know before such ones even exist.
Hallim is a beautiful place where you could see a little bit of everything (cave, flowers, village etc). Each sector is small, but it does deserve a visit while in Jeju.

Had a mixture of nice gardens, some birds and lava caves. When I entered and started walking, it did not sem like much, but then impressed me as I went on. So enjoyed it quite a bit, was a good pleasant walk. Worthwhile if you go to Jeju.

Great visit for the curious or those interested in nature and/or rocks. Nimble feet required. Numerous formations and lava sights to see and learn about.We took a taxi from Jeju city, around 22,000 won one-way. Very inexpensive entry fee though!The lava tube is more than 7 km long and 1 km is open to the public. There is modest lighting throughout though the footing is uneven at times. But hey, you're in a cave. We saw some Korean tourists carrying their infants to and fro inside! It took us more than an hour total to explore the whole thing.It gets really cool (temperature-wise) down there, so those sensitive to cold should bring an extra layer.
Great for the caves. Do not miss them even if you've seen Manjanngul ( unless you have a real shortage of time, then choose M only for lava tubes, but the ones here are limestone meets lava.

Great experience being in the caves, reading the explanation on the formation of the stalactites, lava lines and reason for the uneven heights at certain lengths of the cave. There are summarised English translation on the explanation boards which makes it easier to understand what we are looking at. Trail wise, the ground is made up of flat rocks with some shallow water holes. Wearing comfortable cover shoes would help. We saw some families with young children, about 6 years and above and they could run about on their own, so I would think this would be OK for families who want to bring their kids alone. Overall a good experience and good change from seeing the land attractions. At 2000KRW for an adult ticket, it is definitely reasonable and worth your every cent.
Good, worth experiencing if you haven't been to a lava tube cave before, but do watch your step. Uneven ground with deep cracks at some places

Good to go if you have not been to a cave before. Be prepared to walk though. Into the cave and out takes about 50mins including taking photos and reading the signboards. If u r taking bus 701, stop at manjanggul stn n take a cab.it is only 1.7km so shld cost u 2800won. But taxi driver will ask for 4000won.

Good spot to wander about. Make sure its your first place to visit. Afterwards you go to diving museum, miniparks and other closeby places. 40 to 50 minutes is enough for your journey in the cave. 5he weather inside the cave is lovely and chilling if you're going there in summer.
Good for family with small children or elderly, or couples wait relaxing visits. It has lava caves, flowers, stones, old villages, excellent for us!!!
Good experience to go into a lava cave. But floor in the cave is wet,slippery and uneven. Not meant for family with very young children and old people. Ok

Good experience if you have not been to one.You need to have the passion in Nature and interest in Volcanology to appreciate the beauty, otherwise it is just a boring cave.There was this big group of young students walking and singing. When they reached the end at the lava column, they took some pictures and headed back. I guess they are too young to understand mother nature.

From Jeju city it?s quite easy to reach by car. I had rented a car so no problems with public transportation or finding cabs.Going to the caves with a cab won?t be the problem. Unless you have instructed your driver to stay, you will get a problem to find a taxi.The cave can be a bit wet and slippery, so don?t go there thinking you are going to the beach. Dress accordingly is the advice.I found it quite interesting and definitely a must see when you are staying in Jeju.

Form by lava stalagmites and a long lava tube tunnels. It was cooling inside the tunnel . Stone pillars and stalactites are widely spread and the tunnels shows off the cave?s topographical features.   Stone Turtle   is especially eye-catching.

For visitors arriving by bus: Take Bus 201 from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal and get off at the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. At the same stop, wait for Bus 711-2 to reach the actual Manjanggul Cave site entrance (transfer at KWR 0 cost if using T-money or CashBee card).Note: It's a 2.5km distance from the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. Being a UNESCO Heritage site, we had expected a much better set up for the cave site. Overall lighting could be improved; brighter lighting for better visibility of the rugged paths and water puddles along the 1km lava tube (reduce risks of slipping or tripping as a fall could be quite fatal).The temperature underground can get chilly so be sure to wear warm jackets/coate and proper shoes with good traction (saw some visitors in flip-flops and sneakers, and they ended up almost slipping).

For those visiting this cave expecting amazing cave formations you may be disappointed. On Jeju island all caves are more accurately defined as lava tubes. These vestiges from Jeju's volcanic origins are strange, dark, and geological wonders.Tips for visitors, expect Manjang Cave to be cold, dark, and rough surfaces to walk on. NO sandals or high heels! Hiking boots are a far better option. If you come into the lava tube expecting glittering cave formations you may not have a great time. However, if you want to explore a truly rare geological wonder, take this journey into the darkness to enjoy a unique experience.

For such a long bus ride and such great reviews, I was hoping for much more. We stayed on the Southwestern side of the island and took the nearly two hour bus trip to see this amazing cave that was rated near the top on TripAdvisor. However, we were sorely disappointed. If you've never been to a cave before, you should go. It's a unique type of cave, which is why I gave it a 3-point rating, but there is nothing that draws the attention. In most caves, there is at least one aspect that management (or whoever it is) chooses to make important, such as a really long stalactite that has a cool creation fact...but this cave had none of that. I think they only had around 3 or 4 sets of very cool lighting, illuminating barely anything. In a cave, lighting techniques are your best friends. The entire trek was actually incredibly dark, making viewing anything difficult. (I know that sounds funny if you've never been to a cave before, but those that have know that certain lighting highlights unique aspects but if there is minimal lighting, even walking is annoyingly difficult.) Finally, at the end of the cold, long trek through floors that you have to pay more attention to than the walls, we came to a column of something that almost reached the ceiling and could have been the highlight of the cave trip. The management simply didn't choose to beef this thing up. The lighting on the end piece was regular. There was no sign explaining what is was or how it came to be. It was simply the end of the road. And guess where the exit is? You have to walk back the exact way you came. So, we were bored twice. In short, I gave a 3 out of kindness for its unique type. The cave has potential. I simply wish whoever is in charge would utilize what they have to the fullest.

for me there is nothing special about this cave. the only thing we can do is just walking straight through the cave almost 1km (cmiww). and after we arrive to the end of the tunnel , we just see a small stage and some pic as i remembered. if you traveling with child , pls be carefull when you step the floor. because its really slipper..
Floor of cave dark, wet and uneven. Bring torch and must be able to walk on wet slippery uneven ground to enjoy this national heritage site.

Firstly, this is a tube and not a cave. Secondly, it is made of lava. So do not expect the majestic stalactites, stalagmites and other features associated with limestone caves.Although it is said to be 7 Km long, only a 1 Km length is open to the public. It is wide and not claustrophobic. Interesting features are marked and explained.It is dimly lit and you need a torch. The floor is uneven and wet.Having said that, it is a very unusual feature and worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

First, do not get lost, second prepare to spend at least 3 hours here. If you don't like nature, this is not a place for u. It's like all nature in one. There's cave inside which is to be the only cave that has limestone and lava.

First time to see a lava tube. It was not the most impressive thing to see but it was such an eye opener for me! Learned a lot about this amazing geological formation. Information boards explain well the interesting features in the cave. The entrance fee (KRW 2000) is an absolute bargain. A must see in Jeju! Despite the summer heat, it was very cold inside! Bring a layer!

First time in a cave, so I really enjoyed the experience and learning about the history of the formation of the cave and Jeju island itself. Its a UNESCO site also, which gives the site a more special reason to visit. Be careful as the surface can be slippery, but in general the walk can take about over an hour.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.

Entrance ticket is 2000 won per person. The temperature inside the cave is freezing cold. Pls bring along a jacket no matter what season you are visiting. Total length of the cave is about 7.14km. They only open 1 km for public to visit. It took us about 1:20 hour thru and flow. Please visit the information office first before u going into the cave, so that u will know some information of the cave formation before u going in. Pls wear a proper shoes during your visit cos it is a lava tube with rocky road. I saw some ladies went in with their not so high, high heel. I can feel their pain. This place is about 30-45mins from Jeju City. We took a quick lunch at a restaurant at the park of manjanggul cave. Not so nice but still can eat...u can travel to seongsan ilchubong after u done with the cave. Is about 5mins drive.
Entrance fee costed me 4 000 krw. Reachable by bus. The view inside of the cave is very intriguing and fascinating. For me, it is worth it to visit.
Drove to this national park as planned, the park are well organised with the different type of flowers and cactus, caves tunnels, animals and birds. My family spend almost 3 hours in this huge park.

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)

Despite the heat, its very cooling inside the cave. Took a walk and I find that it was smaller than what I expected. Path is quite rocky and its good to wear proper shoes instead of sandals or slippers. It can be quite slippery too. Its good to visit but if you are tight on your schedule I think you can give it a miss :)

Definitely worth a visit, even if you only have a few hours to spare. This attraction my husband and I completed in just over an hour, there is no audio guide but there are informative signs throughout the cave. You return to the start of the cave the same way you came in, so take your time reading the signs but if you are tight on time you can read some of it on the way back. Being a natural cave/tube the floor of the cave is pretty rocky, must wear comfortable shoes. If you are driving around Jeju, and using the rental GPS, the telephone number to type into the gps system is: 7834818

Definitely a special cave. As it is a lava tube, the floor is also made of solid lava, aka uneven flooring. Bring good hiking boots as it takes at least 40 minutes to reach the end. Advice to use a tripod for good photos.

Dark cave, chilly, dripping water and uneven steps were all I felt for one hour journey in and u-turn out of the cave. Not much to see really unless you are acompanied by an expert or archelogist who can make rock and mud come alive and tell stories. I have been to few caves over the world and find this least interesting and dull.

Currently free due to the new status update to one of the new7wonders. Normally it would be 2,000won to visit. The walk is about 1km long and got a bit boring after a while. The lava column at the end was the most interesting thing during the walk.The bus was an easy ride from the Jeju bus station which cost 2,000won and about 50 minutes. The walk from the bus stop to the cave entrance was 2.5km and took about 45min.

Could not expect that it is so huge, need a lot of time to visit all the places. So many different plants, birds, even caves. The whole way is well organized, u just need to follow arrows to see everything step by step.There are several cultures and climates that you can see in bigger size than just normal botanical garden. Jeju culture is represented there a lot as well, so will not regret about missing local features.
cool cave in a beautiful park setting, we were there when it rained, so was pleasant inside actually

Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

Chose to visit this attraction because it is UNESCO world heritage site. I and my kids went into the cave, make our way to the lava column, took some photos, then u-turn to make our way out. Nothing to see unless you are a geological fan. It is OK, just another   for the experience   trip.

caves, bonsai trees, birds, nice gardens, restaurant in traditional style, and very well maintained area, the owner really has a passion to gardening and pride for his homeland. worth to visit at anytime, in summer you can also enjoy magic sandy beaches on the other side of the park
Cave is big and long, take around 1 hour to come and back. Nothing much to see and it's dark so it's hard to take photo. Average compare to other caves

careful of when walking in the cave, very uneven and wet grounds. The cave is very far from the city, the public bus does not go direct and takes 45min with many stops in between. When arriving at the destination, its about 2.4km walk to the entrance of the cave. If you are lucky to get a taxi when u alight from the bus, they will charge u 4000won to drive u to the cave entrance to purchase your ticket to the cave

Can only walk about 1km of the cave as the other area is restricted, back and forth will take about 45mins. Inside of the cave is pretty cooling and nice to see such a natural occurring sight but I would say nothing much as the lighting inside is also pretty dark.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This temple's shape was unique and located in cave. The way to this tempe was about 15 minutes in uphill stairs and had good view. Though it was hard to temple, but after climbing there was good, and could drink mineral water. Sometimes there was no climbing because of bad weather. There was another temple at the entrance of way to this temple, that temple was good and beautiful sculpture. Good place to enjoy temple and view.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. I felt good in walking road with various ecology system. All was good to me, but reptile in small transparent box was pitiful. If had time, I want to feel natural feelings in this park keeping my composure. Excellent place to enjoy reserve.

Bring your jackets, better to be water proof! Cave temperature is around 10 plus degree or lower. Also ground is uneven so wear good shoes and walk slowly. But overall fascinating to see how geography works

Blue color of beach water. Very good.  We visited there late July. The color of beach was amazing. We enjoyed swimming. Also the sunray was very strong to enjoy sun tenning. We are food a little far from here, because restaurants near beach was expensive. Also there are good places to nearby beach ; Hyeopjae cave, botanical garden, tracking beach, etc.

Bijarim Forest holds about 2,800 nutmeg trees between 500 and 800 years old and is supposedly the largest nutmeg grove in the world. A 813 years old   Ancestor tree of Bijia tree  , also dubbed the   New Millennium Nutmeg   (#0001 tree) sits in the middle of the forest. Local residents hope the spiritual power of this noble tree will bring happiness, prosperity, and health to all in the coming millennium.The trees emit phytoncide, said to strengthen one's immunity system and enhances natural healing of the human body. Japanese and Koreans advocate forest bathing, aka shinrin-yoku or 汝役 and sanlimyok ??곕┝ respectively.  Essentially this is a short, leisurely visit to absorb the forest atmosphere and was developed in Japan during the 1980s as part of preventive health care and healing.  So do walk slowly, breathe deeply, open all your senses in the revitalising woods to calm, rejuvenate and restore your body.  Truly pleasant stroll for nature lovers and family outing.Note: Despite its charm, Bijarim Forest is more popular with locals than foreign tourists due to public transportation and lack of awareness. Cover this place as part of  Manjanggul caves/Sangumburi crater tour. The woods can get mud-logged after rainfall.
big enough & diff topic in park. you could see the flower, bird, cave etc,,,,not too crowded when i visited, good place for spending time

Besides the short walk up to the Buddhist cave, there is a lovely temple and huge golden Buddha just up from the carpark. It does cost money to get in but being able to get up close to the Buddha was excellent. And there are nice views of the coast too.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Been to a lot of caves in my life but these are so interesting as they have been shaped by the lava flow. There are information boards throughout the caves telling you how certain things in the cave were formed from the lava - definitely a must see if you are going to Jeju!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater, Seongeup Folk Village, Oedolgae Rock, and finally Jeongbang Falls. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.
Beautiful, clean and very well maintained. It has great collection of plants, cactus etc. Beautiful cave and water garden too. Should allocate 3 hours time to enjoy this place.

Beautiful small island - green hills, lava rocks and small beaches. It's about one hour and a half by bus from Jeju-city to Seongsan ferry terminal (final stop) and 10 minutes by ferry.  We rented ATV to get around the island. The weather changed quickly and suddenly we found ourselves in the middle of the storm. We had a lot of fun riding ATVs through the heavy rain and felt like we are true rangers.  It was too cold to go swimming and by such a weather we couldn't explore the shore caves. So we skip it for the next time.
Beautiful place, big and many kinds of strees, flowers, stones, bird, cave...And the old town for Dechangkum film to stay here before

Beautiful location. Relatively easy to get to (just one change from Jeju City Bus Terminal). The park is beautiful and I'd really recommend taking your time and enjoying the scenery as much as possible. The park contains different areas (bonsai, water gardens, caves, animals, cactus) and it's so hard to believe that it's man-made. Loved the diversity here.

Beautiful authentic cave that gives you an idea about the magma power. I visited with my dad, but teenagers, couples with small children and elders. There are stairs and very variable ground so it is not recommendable for those who have trouble walking.

Be prepared to climb back up after going down the steps. Will need proper shoes as the floor is uneven, and does have small puddles of water  here and there.It was a nice walk in the cave, and getting a better understanding of nature involving volcanic lava flow.

Be amazed how it was formed. Well maintained facility. A good place to visit for kids who are interested to know about rock formation and caves. It's a 7km in length, however you can only go up to the 1st kilometer.

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

Awesome cave! The ticket price was 2,000KRW.  The transportation is a bit tricky as the bus stop isn't that close to the caves (additional 2.5 km walk).  You can take a taxi from the bus stop (4,000 KRW one way).

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At Hallim park, there are a few lava caves that are interesting, and very cool (temperature).  The flower gardens are very nice.  The bonsai garden has trees that date to 300 years ago.  They are constantly trimmed to keep them small.  There is a restaurant at the entrance, and a rest area with a gift shop in the center of the park.

At first we didn't plan to visit the Cave as we had a tight schedule with so many other outdoor choices. Then I read something about the tube formed from volcanic lava activities so it is very unique compared to other limestone caves formed from soluble rocks.Overal the tube looked very smooth as you can imagine the hot lava flowing to make the tube. There are educational signs here and there to suggest you to look at the lava flow marks, the lava shelf marks and many others.I must say it was an eye opening hour and we learnt something new and be opened minded that it was not just another cave with so many stalagmites and stalactites that looked like different shapes in those unnatural colorful spotlights in some other countries.

As with everything on Jeju, this is built for tourists. The cave itself is interesting but understand there is nothing but this one section of one cave that you can access. This is not in the least bit adventurous - the cave is lit well all along its length. It's the kindergarten of caves but if you haven't been in a lava tube before then it may be for you. Beware that if you take the bus to the caves, you still have 2.5 km on foot to the cave entrance, though you can flag a cab down if one happens past.  Overall ok, but don't expect to be blown away.

As there are not much railings inside the cave to guide the tourists while walking and steps are uneven, make sure to wear comfortable walking shoes. It is beautiful and a must visit when in Jeju. I joined a tour for this visit as it is quite far from where I stayed. Tourist spots in Jeju are not close to each other and I didnt quite see a lot of public transport the in the area.

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

As for the places we visited, we loved the Manjanggul Cave, Sunrise peak and the foot bath class at the Herbal park. The maze and folk village were ok. I probably would prefer to exchange one of those two for more time at the Woljeong beach.

As all caves are, the interior is dark. But there is lighting along the way that is sufficient to show the wall and ground.The ground is not even, but one just need to be careful and pay attention when walking. A touch will help (I carried one). Wear sports shoes for easy and safe walking.We walk for about 30 minutes to reach the end, with stops to read the explanation posted along the way.

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Arrived around 4pm and bought 4 tickets...2,000?? for adults and 1,000?? for children. That's about $5-6 USD. It was 90 degrees outside but cool and refreshing inside. At the start it was 50F and got colder as we got deeper. If you get cold easily, you should bring a light jacket. I would wear shoes because it's a bit wet and rocky but I saw many people walk through with sandals and slippers. It's about a 25 minutes one way. It is pretty well lit for a  tunnel/cave. There's no climbing or steep terrain except for the way down but there are handrails. You will enjoy the experience. It's informative as well.
Approximately 2km walk all the way in then back out. Cooling inside the cave. If I were to go again, I would bring a torch so I can take better pictures and videos inside.

Apart from walking 2.5km in the extreme summer heat from the bus stop outside (pls find alternative routes), the cave was unique and pretty interesting to see. Love the temperature inside to cool us down and be away from the heat too.

Anyone who can appreciate nature, especially geology, will love this. There are only about 5 countries in the world where you can go walk in a lava tube and South Korea is one of them.It's inexpensive to enter (2000won for those over 24, discounts for younger ages) and it is worth it.There are lights installed, but bring lights if you can. The ground is not paved and it's easy to trip. The cave also drips water, so there are puddles around. It was suuuuuper cold inside the cave in March-so cold that when we came outside to the 40 degree weather it felt like summer!!
An interesting walk underground in a 1 km long cave. Some people would find fascinating, others might get abit claustrophobic.Very cheap, about 90 pence per person. Beautiful grounds on the outside.

An hour is okay, but if you have the time it might be better to make this 1,5 hour. We combined this with waiting for the Mongolian horse show, which you should not miss and close to this location. You \can also enjoy the beautifull Jeju-beach on the other side of the road.This park is very well maintained. Enjoy the beautifull Bonsai trees, the waterfalls, the flowers, the cave and the statues. The cave was the least exciting to us, but the bonsai trees from over 150 years old were most impressive.

An amazing cave; one of nature's wonder!  Must wear a good pair of walking shoes, and be prepared to walk some distance. Enjoy the strange and mysterious dark tunnels. Dimly lit, but well kept with small platforms and bridges, this UNESCO heritage site is one selling point selling for Jeju! Worth paying a visit.

Amazing lava tube, much bigger than other ones I've seen. The 1km each way feels like a very long distance!I went in the middle of a storm - the cave had waterfalls and streams flowing... quite surreal underground. A raincoat and torch are a must.

Amazing cave carved by molten lava moving underground with many interesting features, however, you need to be prepaired for dim lighting, uneven floor with many tripping hazards as well as uneven steps/stairs.  Not suitable for young children or older folks who have trouble with sight or walking.

Amazed by the view inside the cave. Overall distance travel back and forth takes 1 hour to complete, approximately 2km. Advised to wear comfortable shoes (rocky slippery floor) and jacket as it can be very cold inside the cave. Bring an umbrella if you need it as there?s water droplets from the top of cave.

Always wanted to see a lava cave and I finally did. It was quite chilly in there so do bring a jacket. And the ceiling is always dripping, so bring an umbrella or raincoat as well. The whole lava tube is about 2.5km long. Pleasant walk on slightly uneven ground. Took bus 701 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Manjanggul Cave. Remember to always press the bus bell for the stop you want to get off! We had a crazy bus driver that just kept on driving until we told him to stop (he didn't even stop to pick up the couple who were waving at the bus stop, bizarre!). Anyway the bus only stop out on the main road, there is still a 2.5km walk to the cave entrance. You can flag down a taxi and it cost 2800 won to the entrance.

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.

although it just open 1/3 of area for tourist but there was quite big & long cave actually. slipping & uneven floor sometimes. light setting not bad compared with other country. it was cold esp for you need to take walk over 1hour if you don't do fast pace to finish it. actually, it has 1km. the rock & lava also impressive. good to take time for it.and i reached here at 11am, maybe the sunlight with cool air. i saw some spot light before went inside the cave. that was beautiful.

Although I am not a Geography buff, I found Manjang Cave an interesting place to visit.  Only 1km was open to public.  Walking in was 1km and walking back to the entrance was another 1km, so total was 2km.The ground was very slippery and wet and lighting was not bright in the cave.  Good shoes and waterproof jacket will be advisable for visiting the cave.  The feeling of walking in a lava cave was a pretty awesome feeling to me.  The explanation of how certain formations came about were good and clear.If you have not seen lava cave before, I think it is worth a visit.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

Again, freezing of winter time and slippery step stone has discourage our tour leader to let us go any further getting inside the cave furthermore. up to the point we stand inside there, nothing special.Hard to explain accept you are cave adventurer... tourists ? it is a No No No

after taking a few geology classes as an adult, it was exciting to see the lava tubes. Would recommend taking a glow stick or a small flash light if prone to having a hard time seeing in the dark. Plus, the glow sticks added some fun to the darkness.  Slightly cold like most caves, bring a sweatshirt is a good idea. This offered something to do when it is raining and could  be a great break from the sun if traveling in the summer time.

After my Manjanggul Cave   expedition   and since the park is just along the way back, I took the chance to see what's the place could offer. I paid KW 2800 for an entrance (I have read reviews that some paid more than the cost, maybe the cost vary by seasons, not really sure). The maze can be finished roughly 10-15 mins, yet completed the maze roughly 30 mins hahaha. I just enjoyed messing around. Didn't really paid attention to the map and it's goal to ring the bell. The maze is good for family to enjoy.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.  We ended up there around dusk, and it was sort of a break from the winter wind.  We were lucky because during the week between Christmas and New Years, the Cave admission was free of charge.  Nothing is very difficult about managing the cave. If you can walk and handle a few stairs at the entrance you can handle this attraction.  Although it was dark outside and underground, the cave was lighted for foot traffic and more than manageable.  Lighting and some signs help highlight the different formations in the cave (i.e. stalagmites, lava lines, and rock formations).  The 'stone turtle' formation is supposed to be shaped like the island itself. I didn't see it, but some have a better imagination than I do.In any case, this attraction is one of the natural monuments of not only Jeju, but Korea and  one of the longest of its kind.  If you're into geology and cultural interest, you cannot miss the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site and volcano museum that is Manjang. Geoparks, Geosightseeing, hiking recovery day

After being in the cave, this is a good way to warm your body under the sun (well, at least during this season).So, it took 10 minutes to work out the right direction with the map, then we tried without the map and again it was ten minutes, then we left our 5 years old daughter to find the way out...still 10 minutes.I cannot define it challenging but fun for sure and super-rewarding to see your kid beaming with light every time she play the bell!Definitely worth combining cave and maze!

After all the hype about Manjanggul Cave, our expectations were high but were disappointed. Nothing spectacular to see unless you are interested in the stones that you will walk on in the dim, damp cave. You will come out the same way you went in.

About half-way between U-do and Jeju City, it's not too difficult to drive to. I would allocate not more than 1 1/2 hours to visit this attraction. The volcanic tunnels are very interesting to see. It rained for several days before our visit, so water was dripping from the cave so it's a good idea to bring a hat. Also wear good shoes. There is plenty of signage that explains the rock formations  English.If you found this review beneficial, please click   helpful.   Thanks.
About 40 min taxi from the airport. The cave is a must see if you visit Jeju. Walk inside the cave, beutiful lighting. Amazing.

About 1km of this underground cave is open to tourists, bring good shoes and be wary as the ground is uneven and very wet with puddles everywhere. You will be dripped on. A light jacket is also recommended as the temperature drops sharply once you go underground. Inside there is not much to see as you will be walking through a dimly lit cave toward your destination, a colorfully lit rock formation. An interesting place to visit nonetheless and a recommended experience for Jeju. Can be done in about an hour.

About 1 kilometer of the lava tube  is open to walk through. You descend a long staircase into the cave. You will be walking on the old lave flow, so the floor is uneven & pitted, and full of puddles. There is dim lighting, so you really need to bring your own flashlight to see where you are stepping. The wall are fairly smooth & rounded, you will only be seeing a few small formations. If you are a nature geek (like me) you will enjoy this. If you want  lots of stalactites & large formations, this is not for you.

A visit to Sanbanggulsa Temple was part of one of my favourite day trips in Jeju. It is about an hour west of Seogwipo-si by bus and across the street (albeit a bit of a hike) from Yongmeori Coast which I very highly recommend. Getting to the temple requires a short and easy climb up some stairs where there is a huge golden Buddha, an army of miniature mint-green budhhas, and a gorgeous panoramic view of the ocean and village below. A little further up is another fascinating statue of Buddha in a cave. Overall, this is a nice place to visit and a great opportunity for photography.

A very wide (23m), high (18m) and long cave (7+ km) one can walk along by yourself (about 1km is open to the public). The temperature inside is perfect, when there is a heatwave outside (which was the case in August 2016). It is doable with a small kid, however you can't bring a stroller as the surface is too uneven in the cave. Also bring solid shoes, it is slippery. Some visiters had flipflops or even some kind of high heals - truly not recommended.
A very long cave made from lava tube. Cold and dark, no bat dung smell though  as claimed. Kids having good time despite being city boys. Good new experience for us

a very friendly owner who is a famous personality on Jeju, the area has nice nature surroundings with nice cats:) close to Mangjang cave, don't confuse the location, there are several other mazes on Jeju as well:)

A unique must-do in my books to go where lava has gone before.   It is also a cave, so it dark, a little chilly with the occasional water drop.  The cave is left largely in its raw form (which was great) but it also meant an uneven and potholed path which requires a great deal of care walking it.

A pretty long walk over some decent grounds and some stairs to get through the entire cave. Its a little chilly down there so bring some easy to shed clothing. Really a vast and large cave, not something you get to see very often elsewhere and for the small entry fee... you cant beat it.
A place worth visiting. Found a new love for cave trekking. Beautiful lava cave, can see the tracks of nature.
A place to discover the force of the nature, slighly cold inside the cave

A lovely, lovely lava tube cave - totally different from the limestone caves with regard to structures (chambers, tunnels, columns, shelves, stalagmites etc) found inside. The lighting within the tube is great - kept to the essentials for safe walking and with no glaring colourful lights that makes the structures look artificial. The temperature within the lava tube is cool and very pleasant ... could spend hours here hiding from the summer heat outside.
A lot of zone/theme - probably around 11. We like the cave, bonsai, bird park and tropical garden. The building is a little bit outdated.

A little short distance adventure for about 2km round trip. Insides the lava tube, you can see different kind of volcanic stones formed by the lava last time. Be prepared with proper sports shoes as the pathway in the cave is a bit crooked. Be careful.

A lava tube showing the flow of lava and various natural formation such as the lava shelves or columns. Inside the cave is chilly (around 11c when outside is around 25c), dark, wet and slippery. Bring your jacket and sturdy shoe for this visit. Heels is a definite no no. Forget about your camera (too dark for photo taking) and just enjoy the brisk walk. To and fro takes you around 45mins-1hr.

A larger version of Bontanic Gardens. Provide rental of prams for babies/ toddlers. The weather was good when I was there, hands nice and relaxing tour. They have cactus, flowers, plants, water park, caves, birds etc

A cave system that can get in easily just by walking down the step.according to the tour guide, this special cave is cold during summer and warm during winter. By the time i go is summer, it is real chill inside the cave
1st visit in the cave tube. Really fascinated cold, dark, wet cave. The ground is uneven so walk with caution. It's good to walk in a group for safety.
