Here is much more the beauty of the man made. The Bonsai garden made in an Arboretum which otherwise would've been an entirely sandy/rocky area. A good place to stroll completely away from the coastline. But given that Jeju's primary attractions are natural, spend time here only after seeing the real natural stunners.

Heaven on Earth - volcanic stone sculptures abound - every tree a bonsai - cedar, pine, maple and more.  Azaleas were in full bloom and a delight in colour.  The birds, in particular the white peacock who posed displaying all his feathers fanned out.  Then onto the water garden with its lotus blooms, fish and waterfalls.  I would do anything to have a garden like this in which to spend my days.

Hallim Park isn't worth making a special journey to go and see. The gardens and varying different areas don't have anything especially interest to see. The animals kept along side the plants are kept in cramped dirty cages and look awful. The tulip garden was pretty, as was were the bonsai trees.

Hallim Park is so big, we didn't even get to see everything. Spend at least 3 hours here (I think). That should be enough time. I loved the caves, the bonsai garden, the cactus garden, the cherry blossoms, and the tulips festival! Lovely park to visit.
Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection.An hour is okay

Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection. There's an extensive range of bonsai trees at display, some of them are over 300 years old. To those unfamiliar with bonsai trees, they may just be miniature trees; but to those who know the value of these works of art, these bonsai trees are literally priceless. In fact, it's almost unbelievable how openly accessible these trees are to the guests, considering their value and need for extreme care.If you're planning on visiting, briefly study the artistry before your trip to enhance the enjoyment. This is a one-of-a-kind collection.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.
Hallim park has it all. It has nice gardens, lava caves, birds, bonsai garden etc. It is easy to reach by public transport and is a pleasure to visit.We really enjoyed this park.

Hallim Park has everything you would want to see. It has a big and beautiful flower garden, stone and bonsai garden, caves you can explore, a folk village, and a wonderful cactus garden.  It also has a bird garden and reptiles in cages.  You can spend at least half a day exploring everything.

Hallim Park has a mixed big of attractions --- from folk village, lava cave to bonsai and tropical gardens.  It is worth spending a couple of hours exploring.......many nice spots for taking pictures around the park........beware though, each of the attraction is not very spectacular or unique, but the park just gives a sense of the essentials in Jeju in one place

Hallim Park features an extremely interesting cave complex quite unique as it has been dug by lava, a traditional Korean village, beautiful waterfalls, a bonsai garden and a section with creative sculptures. The price is very affordable and you can also visit the beautiful beach opposite the park while you're there. Worth a visit if you have spare time on your hands as it is quite far from the main attractions.

Hallim is mixture of small zoo,botanical garden, lava caves and stones. We arrived     In morning after rain,park was quiet, with not many visitors, relaxing. I liked walking through volcanic caves, beautiful bonsai garden with some trees around 300year old. And completely white peacocks, I did not know before such ones even exist.

Great experience walking around and reading the story,  The owner had a lot of faith that he could change this area into something wonderful.  Glad we made the time to stop and check out the Bonsai's!

Good for an afternoon stroll. Nice collection of flowers, cacti and bonsai trees. Impressive cages and not too crowded (visited in September) Enjoyed the peace and green scenery. Did not like wild birds in the garden, as I do not support animals in captivity.

Flowers, nature, lava tube, animals...  You can find all these in Hallim Park. The entrance fee might be a little expensive at KRW 10,000, it's money well spent.I wasn't expecting much and thought it was just another park. Hallim Park proved me wrong. The more I explored, the more impressed I was with the exhibits. Plants from around the globe, all climates. We spent a good 4 hours exploring the Park. The lava tubes were impressive, the model thatched house and bonsai garden.A very relaxing place for a long stroll. I would recommend a visit.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.
Enjoyed wandering through flowers, and bonsai trees. Interesting look at the folk village and some gorgeous peacocks. Takes a couple hours tops but a nice place to visit
Don't rush through this place, it's definitely worth several hours. The mega-sized bonsais were a particular highlight for us.

caves, bonsai trees, birds, nice gardens, restaurant in traditional style, and very well maintained area, the owner really has a passion to gardening and pride for his homeland. worth to visit at anytime, in summer you can also enjoy magic sandy beaches on the other side of the park

Beautiful location. Relatively easy to get to (just one change from Jeju City Bus Terminal). The park is beautiful and I'd really recommend taking your time and enjoying the scenery as much as possible. The park contains different areas (bonsai, water gardens, caves, animals, cactus) and it's so hard to believe that it's man-made. Loved the diversity here.
Beautiful and blissful with great photo taking opportunites, well nurtured bonsai and plants. Great place to bring kids to see the variety of bonsai plants and neatly arranged garden.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At Hallim park, there are a few lava caves that are interesting, and very cool (temperature).  The flower gardens are very nice.  The bonsai garden has trees that date to 300 years ago.  They are constantly trimmed to keep them small.  There is a restaurant at the entrance, and a rest area with a gift shop in the center of the park.

An hour is okay, but if you have the time it might be better to make this 1,5 hour. We combined this with waiting for the Mongolian horse show, which you should not miss and close to this location. You \can also enjoy the beautifull Jeju-beach on the other side of the road.This park is very well maintained. Enjoy the beautifull Bonsai trees, the waterfalls, the flowers, the cave and the statues. The cave was the least exciting to us, but the bonsai trees from over 150 years old were most impressive.

Although the weather was uncomfortably hot and humid, we decided to check out the Spirited Garden based on its raving reviews.  The garden is a pleasant peaceful spot to relax for about an hour.  Although it?s not as picturesque as some of the famous Japanese gardens, the bonsai tree collection is quite impressive.  The display on how to observe the trees was especially interesting.  Few demerits here for the excessive amounts of signs with visitor comments saying how great their visits were at this place.  The ?history hall? was just photos of famous visitors with quotes about how great the garden was.  One almost felt an obligation to enjoy the visit because these photos and comments were plastered all over the place.

Allow for at least 2.5 to 3 hours to walk around. There are a number if different areas, my favourite being the bonsai trees. The park is very well kept and very tranquil. There are a couple of places that sell snacks and one restaurant on site.

A nice botanic garden with interesting elements. I particularly like the bonsai garden with lots of areas to sit and admire the specimens. Since we only had a very limited time, we were not able to see the other areas.
A lot of zone/theme - probably around 11. We like the cave, bonsai, bird park and tropical garden. The building is a little bit outdated.

A local has fulfilled himself a dream. He moved ground to this place and built this park with areas for Bonsai, azalees, palm trees, a natural lava tunnel, traditional houses, strangely formed lava rocks etc.The stop here is part of  a bus tour tio the Western part of the Island.

A little disappointed with this park as I was expecting lots of blooming flowers. Unfortunately I came at the wrong season of the year (autumn) so very little flowers. However it's a lovely park with lots of attraction to go to. For those who like flora and fauna it's a must go.It's quite a long walk but don't worry about getting lost. It's a one way street with ample signage to guide you along. Not to forget, for those with small kids there's a stroller rental service at the entrance. In the park there's a folk village, a lava tube, bonsai garden, water lily pond, bird park and many others. So there's something for everyone.

What is offered at the Glass Museum does not justify its 9 000 won entrance fee.There is a garden with glass flowers  glass birds  and other ornaments. The displays are dull and although they probably took a lot of time and effort to make  the whole place seems like something that would have been more interesting 15 years ago.

What a beautiful place! This bridge looks like it is hanging in the air. A short loop around the island offer a lot of bird sightseeing. You can also see female divers at work right next to the bridge.

Went with my son and husband on a very hot day! Park well laid out with several drink food and shade stops on way round! We spent a few hours to see it all! Caves were a highlight - very interesting and cool!! Reptiles and birds ok - not my thing! Enjoyed water area especially cold showers we could stand under :-)) overall a good place to visit and see a range of sights! Easy to get to on main coastal bus route Enjoy
Well set out with a large variety of natural features although we felt a bit sorry for some of the reptiles and birds in confined cages. The highlight is possibly the two lava tubes.

We were there late at 5:30 on a cloudy day my son insisted to explore the area and shooting birds.  He took rount 1 and came back in about 45 mins.  He said to me he heard lots of bird but only captured the photo of one Woodpecker.

we visited two parks in Jeju. Hallim and Spirited Garden. ticket price was almost the same for both but Hallim was by far much better and bigger with good design and a lot of different and amazing trees and some birds too. It is really a must visit for Jeju visitors to spend around two hours enjoying the park.

We took one walk here. Vertical rise of about 200m through nature. A couple of hours of hiking & stopping to view the plants & birds. Great view of the crater from the top. Worth the trek. Carry lots of water if it hot!

We made a wrong turn and found this place by chance.? Amazing view. The bridge connects you to bird Birds Island. It's 1.2km walking path. Best to visit before the Sunset and you will be blown away with the views around this area. A good place to stroll and relax.

We loved the park and spent about three hours. The cherry blossom and canola fields were the best as they were in full bloom. My little one loved the bird park and we even spotted a few peacocks roaming free in the park. The tulips were pretty but nothing extraordinary. We did not explore the caves and the hits.

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

Walking through this garden park is very peaceful and relaxing. There is a cool cave feature so you get to also go into caves. The captive birds are in small enclosures and the peacocks look like there tail feathers have been pulled. Also there is a white sand beach walk across the street after you are done the park. Taxi from Ramada Plaza was 26000 wan. Bus ride home was 3000 wan and took about an hour on the 702.
Visited the park when it was raining. Still very enjoyable and there is some sort a mini bird park in there. Very interesting and relaxing walk through the park.
Visited mainly to see the lava caves. Walked past the bird enclosure on the way out and was shocked to see the crowded small bare enclosures they are kept in.

tried the forest healing program last month during my visit to jeju island. Guided by forest therapist we have completed forest healing trail. I can say it really helps me relax the body by focusing on natural noises flowing water  chirping mountain birds  fresh forest air and those Phytoncide!!! oh it just smells so nice >.< we got to try the foot bath and aromatherapy too. the therapist said they also have body bathing tub and aqua line  but since we dont have many time.. maybe next time. Good place to relax your mind and escape from hustle and bustle city. i will try another program if i have chance to visit it again.

Today I hired a car and drove to Hallasan National Park. Only 1000 won to enter and park.Plenty of clean toilets. An excellent Visitor center who gave me an informative map. I did not have time to do Eorimok Trail today but will do tomorrow.I climbed the Eoseungsaengak Trail which is only 1.3km and has wooden steps all the way up so no problem with any fitness level.30 minutes up to the top. Great 360 deg.view of the surrounding mountains and a small Japanese bunker to see too. Friendly Jackdoor birds wanting a scrap of food..

This park is huge! it is divided into different areas with different themes. It has a great variety of plants and birds. There are also two underground tunnel caves which enrich the overall visiting experience. There is also an area with seasonal flowers.  Great spot for photo-taking. Highly recommended for family with children. Allocate at least two hours visiting time here.

This is not a place for adults like us because the tour guide could only provided us with the very basic information about the dinosaurs for the children packs traveled with us. The park also has birds and rabbits for the kids to feed and play with. We think we?셱e a bit ?쐎ut of date??for this place.

This is a beautiful spot to sit and enjoy nature at its best. We saw some amazing little birds and the waterfall is stunning. There was a lot of water going down the falls when we visited in April this year. This is a must do! Be ready to go up and down a lot of stairs. :)

This bridge connects Seogwipo Port to Birds Island and its design is inspired from the Jeju traditional log boat- Tewu.The best time to view this bridge is in the night. One can walk around the bridge and enjoy the scenery during the day and early evening.

Our 4yo liked it well enough. We spent about 2hrs and spent more money at the gift shop than on admission (24000 won) and if it were nicer out we probably would have spent longer. Botanical garden a small garden maze Fossil museum animal feeding station bird attraction and the really TALL dinosaurs scattered throughout made for an enjoyable afternoon outing before nap time.
NIce? walk across the bridge facing the sea on one side and port on the other .Bridge connects Seogwipo Port to Birds Island and its design is inspired from the Jeju traditional log boat- Tewu

nice view everywhere. took the ferry and saw people feeding the birds. took the bus tour but seems more fun taking the ATV which many young people are taking. we took the speed boat at udo peak area and was quite fun & exciting. can spend at least half a day in udo.

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)
My daughter enjoyed the live dolphin monkey seal and bird show. Not much else to see though because this is a just an aquarium.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: Lot of trees. Fresh air. Nice walk. Most of the trees are old and have description in Korean . It has oldest nutmeg tree. Can hear lot of different birds. Love nature then must see.

Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.

It's quite a tour to walk around and see everything in this theme park. The park has some huge dinosaur statues nice views it features a bird house a maze a small museum and some food vendors. It's a museum type very laid-back amusement park with nice scenery.

It is actually quite nice the cave was very well developed; it has proper lighting and the pathway had been established. The statues were a bit unclear though but it were quite attractive. The folk village was good. The bird park was also nice with ostrich and peacock. I did not go to the rest of the attractions as 1 hour visit was not enough to cover all

I was expecting a rough n tough hike into the Falls but i was so wrong. Everything is nicely paved. Despite the fact that it is touristy it still does not take away the beauty of the place. The ducks and birds really add the beauty.

I visited Hallim Park confined in a wheelchair. Some ways are not appropiate for a wheelchair. I love gardens and seen a lot. This garden had beautiful displays although some were needing care. The park takes several hours to see. It has different plants from many parts of the word. The Bonsai collection was excellent and one of the best I seen in a botanical garden. Again this particular area was needing help with the trees. They have so many bonsais and only two workers to trim them. And the specimens available were very old.The caves are unique because I do not know any other part in the world you can see a volcanical and calcareal cave together and they have one in here. I had to use crutches to see them and I am not dissapointed of the effort.The local village moved into the park is nice and realistic (we visited a folk village the day before). The animal collection was above average. For kids they have an area to feed love birds and parakeets. Excellent fun. My youngest daughter is 25 and she was a child again in here.

I enjoyed walking through the park. It's was pretty. I didn't really like birds being caged though. Bonzai trees were fun and pretty cool. It's near one of the nicest beaches I ever been too.  It's an easy place to walk around with family.

Husband and mate returned there 3 days in a row!!... You get skeet shooting but also real pheasant hunting.... they got 6 birds and invited the wives down to join them for lunch of shabu shabu with the pheasants they caught!!!  Nom Nom Nom
You can see wild grass and flower garden, caves, Jeju stones, folk village, bird garden, water garden and subtropical garden in the park.
You can see there so well cared garden. There is also many different snakes, birds, turtles etc. The caves and botanic garden makes me happy too. Take time and relax. Eeva A
You can have a relaxed stroll over the bridge and on the route around the Bird Island.? Nothing spectacular, but see the coastine and three island out of the city.

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.? This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.

Went to Hallim Park on the end of September 2015, its a good thing we came at Autumn because the weather was not hot and not too cold either. The leaves were turning orange - just like in the movies. There are several flower parks in the Hallim park, such as flowers park; cactus park; bonsai park; stone cave; bird park; and folk village - where we can stop by for lunch. This place is suitable for families travelling with old ones, since the scenery is beautiful for photo-shoots.

Went for a stroll after visiting Hanna Mountain. The cactus conservatory was impressive and we rounded up that part of Hallim Park with a thirst quenching cactus drink.  Similarly the cool walk into the lava cave, and the connecting limestone cave was particularly enjoyable, taking shelter from the melting sun. Highlight of this trip was feeding of birds inside a bird house.   We purchased their food at the vending machine.  Having them eating out of one's palm brought back fond memories of childhood.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and   rare   factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

We went during the winter so most of the plants had no flowers nor leaves. The ones that did were amazing though. They have signs in Korean, Japanese, Chinese, and English. It was pretty informative. There's an aviary that's open so people can interact with some of the birds. I can imagine what it must look like in the spring. Definitely coming back to see all the flowers blooming.

We visited on a sunny day, a nice change from the rain from the day before.At the entrance, you have the choice to walk around the short & free pathway by the sea or you could pay an entrance fee to hike up to the top of Seongsan for a birds eye view. We opted for the hike up.I wasn't very fit so it took me a couple of stops before I got up eventually..but the view was worth it. If you go earlier, you could catch the performance by the Haenyeo down by the shore at the bottom of Seongsan. Sadly, we did not manage to catch the performance.

We visited Hallim Park with my daughter in August. It is very nice place with diversified trees, plants, birds. Convenient infrastructure allowed us to see so many wonderful natural things during three hours. Two old cave are in the park. It is interesting to pass them especially in hot day.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

We stopped at Jungmun tourist complex to visit teddy bear museum by taking bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street in Seogwipo.  It was 6 minutes walk to Cheonjeyeon waterfall. Do not confuse this waterfall with Cheonjiyeon waterfall. The admission fee was KRW2,000 per pax. You can kill two birds with one stone. You get to see two attractions the famous Seonimgyo bridge with seven nymphs carves (fairy bridge) and the three-tiered waterfall. We did not go for the third waterfall as the trail was quite steep. We only went to the pond of fairy and the second waterfall.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal as we knew that we needed to take an early bus to Hallasan. We noted that we needed to reach a certain point on Hallasan by 12.30pm as they would not allow people to continue to hike up after 12.30pm due to foreseen danger. We took bus 782 at 6.00am sharp from seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and alight at Seongpanak bus stop to start our hike at Hallasan. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The ride took about 30 minutes. The cost of the ride was less than 2000won and the bus driver could provide change if needed. We alighted at Seongpanak bus stop on the side with a hiking track. That track was not the track up to Hallasan. We needed to cross to the opposite side and pass the souvenir and rest stop place to the correct Hallasan track (free entrance). In the beginning the track was gentle and doable. We managed to spot birds and deer grazing around. However, the rest of the track up was pretty boring as there was nothing much to see. After 1-2km, the hike started to be more steep (as in more elevated with steps) as there were many rocky steps to hike up. There were two rest stops before the summit that provided fairly clean and well-maintained toilet with toilet paper. However, there would not be any tap to wash hands. Therefore, remember to buy wet wipes to clean your hands. At the second rest stop, raman, drinks and crampons were sold. Get all the supplies you need before hiking up as there is no shops at the summit. It will be good to bring tomatoes or fruit for the hike as those provide fluid as well as sugar (instead of salty food item with msg ? this will make you feel sick). Anyway, you are not suppose to cook at the summit. Remember to bring trash bag to clear your trash too. From the second rest stop onwards, the steep rocky steps continued with harsher windy condition as you progress to the top. Therefore, remember to bring windbreaker and windproof pants as the wind was rather strong 1 to 2km before reaching the summit. We hike on 24 April with a summit temperature of 6 to 12 degree Celsius. We were blessed as there were no rain snow during the hike. The 1 to 2km up the summit consist of wooden steps that I found difficulty tracking up due to the wind and my lack of motivation (as I kept on looking at the summit and felt that it was so far away). Therefore, it would be better to just look at the steps in front of you and conquer those instead. When we finally reach the summit, we had a view of Baengnokdam crater and the surroundings. I was feeling nausea partly due to the fatigue as I did not exercise for 2 month prior to this hike. However, we managed to hike up to the summit in 3.5 hours. The wind continued to be harsh on us. Therefore we stayed for 15 minutes and decide to just hike down. Take pics even if you feel unwell. You will feel better as you ascend down. We hike down from the other hard track, the Gwaneumsa Trail although I was super tired. I did not regret that choice as it was much more scenic in comparison with the Seongpanak track. I thought that descending would not be a toll on me but I was wrong. As the track consist of many rocky steps, it was hard on my knees and I had to work on my balance too. The ajumma (they were over 50 years old) were able to hike way faster than me (in my early thirties). There was one rest stop only and we stop for the toilet. It was again clean with toilet paper provided. Generally, it was a descending hike with minimal ascending (with only a few flights of stairs up). We took 4.30 hours to hike down and I was totally shacked. The rest area at the bottom was also much more beautiful as compared to the Seongpanak rest stop. We wanted to take a bus back but we were told that there were no buses on Monday. There were buses back to Jeju city on other day from Gwaneumsa. (we noted that one of the bus come around 4pm towards Jeju city). We took a cab back to Jeju Dongmun Traditional Market for 20, 000 won. From the traditional market, we took a taxi for 3200 won to the bus terminal (bought bus ticket from the counter) to take bus 781 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (the journey was more than 1.5 hours).Personally, I find the hike difficult and I would suggest some stamina training to enjoy the hike better. I would suggest to hike when there is good weather as I find the hike difficult even in good weather (due to the rocky steps). Having said these, I would still recommend the hike as I love the challenge.

We stayed at Clouds Pool and Spa Hotel which is 1km away so we could reach there at 5am to do the climb. It is fairly an easy climb aided by a lot of stairs. We had breakfast at Paris Baguette which is opposite the mountain. They open at 5am. We had peaceful breakfast as we were the only couple there. The top of the peak offers beautiful panorama view of the green grass crater, sea view skyline and the other side is the Jeju city bird?s eye view.  Air is fresh and very windy on the peak (I thought I could fly away). There were only 3 persons on the peak when we arrived. We could stay there for about half an hour to enjoy the scenery and the peace. The female divers abalone catching activities happen at 1.30pm or 3.30pm below the mountain. It?s another steep way down from carpark infront of Seongsan Mountain. From my hotel room, I could see people walking up to the mountains all day and evening. It?s definitely a must visit when you come to Jeju!

We started at 8.30 at Yeongsil and exited at 1 pm from Eorimok . Lovely walking and climbing experience. Fresh air, lot of greenery, lot of birds. Just us and nature and fellow hikers. It was fun. Very exhausting but refreshing.One must have good pair of shoes. It has lot of rocky patches.Carry water and some snacks. Sunhat is must. The trail is well guided with sign boards and emergency numbers. It becomes windy on top so a jacket is useful.Must visit place.

We spent the afternoon at Hallim Park and thoroughly enjoyed the statues, the bonsai garden, the rock sculptures, the caves and the traditional village.  The grasses section appeared to be very dry and in need of some immediate cleaning up.  We were shocked and saddened by what we saw in the bird section.  The ostriches were clearly in distress as they had lost many feathers and were showing signs of balding.  They were enclosed in an area devoid of greenery and appeared to be desperately seeking out food by nipping the air.  The enclosure did not allow for these beautiful birds to run and get the necessary exercise.  Yes, there were food dishes in various locations however they didn't seem to meet the needs of the ostriches.  The peacocks were also showing signs of stress as their plumage was rather thin.  They were enclosed in an area where the floor was of interlocking brick.  This is as far from a natural setting as possible. Our visit ended on a sour note and it is our hope that the dire situation of these birds will be addressed by those in charge.  We highly advise anyone who visits this park to make his/her concerns known as it is the only way to rectify this sad situation.

We spent a morning in the park. The 9 different themes covers all the specialty of Jeju, include traditional-styled houses as folk village, numerous sculptures, among others the famous Stone Grandfather. Bird Garden with peacock and ostricts, Hyeopjae & Ssangyong Caves. If we were here earlier, could have skip the other caves which basically the same.

We should have just come here on Day 1 instead of on our last day in Jeju.It has the caves, stone statue, flower, cactus, bonsai, reptiles, birds,  etc all within the park. Even though it was winter, we still enjoy the visit. There were no beautiful flowers but we could still see cactus, birds, reptile, tropicals ferns, etc. If you enjoy botanic garden , stress free walk, you will love this place. It is huge place so we find ourselves rushing to try to see everything. I m sure there are more beautiful gardens and caves in other countries but in jeju, i consider this good. This park is near to 2 beautiful sandy beaches so you can spend a day innthis area. There are restaurants, cafes, etc near the beach but cos winter most were closed.If you are driving just drive along the coast to see the beaches. Our first trip is a touch and go but our hext trip, we will focus on one  or two main areas. We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.
We saw birds, ostrich, peacocks and various bonsai trees. You need at least 2 to 3 hrs to enjoy the place. There is also a cave with paved walkways.

We loved walking through Halla Park. The paths are organized and cultured so beautifully. Every turn brings new surprises. There are bonsai trees galore, rock formations, fountains, and green spaces the lure you in. The caves are small, but fascinating. The birds here are delightful, from parakeets to peacocks and ostriches. We would definitely come back and have a picnic here in the springtime.

We hiked up the mountain with our kids age 6 & 8. This is the shortest trail in Hallasan National Park (Infor: 1.3 km / 30 min each way/ only 1 trail, you won't get lost). The trail is rather easy to hike and shady all the way to the peak. The path is either with wooden staircase or laid with rubber mat on slippery path. Along the way, you can hear birds chirping. The 360 scenery view at the peak is breathtaking.

We have no idea that such place exist until we drove along the Hallasan range from North to the southern part of the island. Spotted the beauty along the road, we saw a parking space opposite the 1100 Altitude Wetland, decided to stop and take a look. There is a 1-km boardwalk which we stroll along the peaceful woods and admire the trees, stones, frozen stream, mountain range. As it is winter, we could not spot any birds, or wildlife.However, we are pleased with a little surprise that we have added a new destination of the day to our itinerary.

We entered this park with great expectations - the gardens themselves are great, the bonsai area stands out as superb, and the Lava Caves offer some welcome respite from the heat.Everything in the garden was destroyed by the horrific and unacceptable conditions of the birds and other animals.  There was a smallish section with parrots, a few other birds, a monkey in a tiny cage and a few other small furry creatures.  It was filthy, some of the animals had no water, the temperature must have been 35 degrees.  There was one small animal that was clearly suffering greatly (in one of the cages with no water). I emptied the contents of my water bottle into it's water bowl, and reported its condition to a member of staff - who did nothing.We went on to see peacocks and ostriches, yes in slightly larger enclosures, but with no shade, no vegetation, and 13 peacocks in a tiny cage.  The birds were in obvious distress with obsessive grooming and clear skin infections.I've travelled all over the world, and been to many places like this and never, from the poorest, to the richest countries, have I seen animals kept in these conditions. I rarely, if ever, write reviews, but I am so angry at the conditions here, that it's important to be aware.The gardens are immaculate, the conditions of the animals are disgraceful, and should be an embarresment to whoever runs this organisation.Do not visit!

We did the Yeongsil trail.  The first kilometer in the forest was kind of random.  But once we got above the tree line, the scenery was beautiful.The path is very well maintained with boardwalks and handrails.  But it goes up 400 meters in the first 2.5 kilometers, so it is definitely steep, with entire sections of just stairs, a little bit like climbing up the Eiffel Tower.  This is not a relaxing stroll and you need to be in decent shape to enjoy it.  When we saw it was 7.4 kilometers round trip, we thought it would take us 2 hours, but it almost took us 3, with limited rest time.The last kilometer to the junction with the other trails is all flat, with boardwalks through the highlands.  We didn't try the restaurant on top.So all in all, lots of variety, beautiful bushes, beautiful flowers, lots of birds, nice rock formations.An absolute must if you go to Jeju Island.

We did 3 Jeju Olle Route 1, 6 & 7 and 14-1. We did not complete all the Olle route but every one of the route was breath-taking and worth the walk. All the route were doable by public transport and car rental was not needed.Jeju Olle Route 1We did not do the entire route 1 as we wanted to visit seongsan 1st plus we started late. As we stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal, we took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. I have car sickness but it was still bearable for me. We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area. The bus journey took about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.Jeju Olle Route 6 & 7 We did not do the entire 6 & 7 trail but we visited Chilshimni Poetry Park, Hwangwooji coast, Oedolgae observatory and Oedolgae. This was a scenic trail and I highly recommend. We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10 minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline and headed to Saeseom Island. Saeseom Island was a short 20 to 30 minutes trail that brought us to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree Celsius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up a temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Park Sunshine hotel was). Then, You need to turn in to Namseong-ro road and you will see a brick wall painted dark blue with pinnochio seated on a bench (photo attached) you will passed by a ?hip?몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online - photo attached). u will then past by Poong Gyung Hotel in Jeju (not the one u can find online - photo attached) before arriving at Hwangwooji coast. I love Hwangwooji coast bcos it was like a private pool. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.  After-which we head to Oedolgae and walked till Dombenang-gil Road. We decided to head back as I needed the toilet. At the entrance to Oedolgae, there was a public toilet acorss the road. The toilet were will keep with toilet paper provided. You can watch the sunset if you have time. However, we decided to walk back to our hotel as we were tire. Jeju Olle Route 14 ? 1If you love beaches, this is a must walk route (at least it was really breathe-taking for me). We stayed at Seowipo, we took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We needed to change bus 702 (opposite the tourist infrmation counter) to Hyeojae beach. It cost 3300 won. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields (photo attached). You will see a beautiful beach 1st (Geumneung Beach) but don?t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down to Geumneung Beach later as it was part of olle route 14-1 (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up. In Summary, I always thought that you would need to rent a car around jeju. However, during my 4 days trip (even Hallasan was done using public transport ? can look at my post at tripadvisor), all our travelling was done throuh public transport. We were able to view those usual scenic places that ple usually go too! The good thing about walking was that we could stop at anytime we want to take picture or do something we did not plan for (Eg: watch how the local harvest shellfish). However, we were the kind that love to walk and could spend 7 hours walking. Therefore, we could travel in jeju with a budget using their public transport.

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We arrived in late autumn nearing winter so there were not many flowers on display. We still managed to see chrysanthemum in various colours!! We also managed to spot the peacocks and ostriches. There's a small enclosure for kids (and adults) to see the various birds they have there. We also visited the 2 caves within Hallim Park. There's also a big bonsai area in the park.The park is huge, so allocate about 2 hours to visit everything!

This post is about logistics and what to expect from the hike. My partner and I hit Hallasan around 6:45 in the morning on a Saturday to avoid the crowds. We drove to Seongpanak parking lot (free and was filling up quickly. A tour bus with dozens of hikers was already there) which was about a 30-minute drive from Seogwipo. From there we took a $15.00 taxi ride to the Gwaneumsa parking lot. As this was not a loop trail, we wanted to take the steeper/harder route in and have gentler descent (easier on our knees) back to our car. Turns out, doing it this way we avoided what felt like hundreds of people ascending when we were heading back later in the day. The Gwaneumsa parking lot has a fee. (Sorry TA fans, I didn't get the amount since we took a cab --- I am sure it is nominal, like all fees in RoK:) People are allowed to camp at the Gwaneumsa section of the park and I saw a few people starting their day as we marched to the trailhead. We were under tree cover and walked along a dry river bed for the first couple of miles. At this time of day, we only ran into seven other hikers on this trail. After you cross the river via bridge, the hike starts to get a little steeper. About two hours in, you hit a large, modern shelter and toilets. Good time to take a break and snack. Or keep carrying-on as you will get a chance to sit, eat and gaze at another resting place. After the shelter, you will cross a much larger, newer suspension bridge. Fresh water available here. The climb will get a bit harder for next half quarter mile. Continue past the foundation of the destroyed shelter. After you ascend the 18-22 inch tall stone steps, you will reach a ridge which is the other good stop.  No shelters (in fall you should opt for the shelter), but a nice wooden platform from which to gaze at how far you've come. Crows will land in search of scraps. At this point you are very near the top, only a couple more hundred feet to go.The crater was dry when we visited (first weekend in October), but still a wondrous site. The seasoned, local hikers brought burners and ramen and were happily chowing down near the crater. Darn! That would have been nice. The  t-shirt, fleece jacket and windbreaker I was wearing barely sustained me, so the hot ramen sounded freakin' great.The hike down Seongpanak was not nearly as enjoyable since we were bombarded by the late starters heading up. At one point, the hikers coming up were in a jam ? seriously, no one could move, there were so many people. There?s a large shelter a third of the way down. As another reviewer noted, be sure to wear supportive shoes with rigid shanks as you're constantly stepping on uneven rock.  I had on trail runners, which was fine going in, but heading down, my feet were pretty battered. The boardwalk was a nice breather when we could get it.*Seongpanak gentler ascent, (and descent) but be prepared to share the trail with dozens and dozens of other people.*Free parking at Seongpanak -- fills up quickly as early as 7am on weekends.*Toilets available on trail.*Take bimbimbap for a nutritious, affordable, and portable snack. Mandoo is another good one -- good balance of carbs and fat.*Listen and look Nuthatches, Wrens, Great T*ts, and other winter birds on the Gwaneumsa trail.*The park states you must hit the summit by noon. I think this is why so many people were rushing to hit the peak at the same time.

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking. This is one of the new world wonders and indeed it's a beautiful mountain with flights of stairs to climb. It's a good exercise as the weather was nice and breezy. The bird eye view was great but the peak, to me, was a bit disappointing.

This is one of the best place we visited in Jeju. Various things to see such as flowers, plants, birds, small reptiles, lava cave etc. I love the cactus garden most. Great for photo taking and a slow stroll with family members! I did not fully explore the place due to time constraint. Guess it probably need around 2-3 hrs to slowly explore the park.

This is just a park with some trees, caged birds, caves and bonsai. Nothing very spectacular for the krw120000 of entry fee. The signage was insufficient to the various sights so I walked around quite a bit but still didn?t find some key sights.
This is a very good park. You can see a lot of varieties of flowers, trees, and birds in this park. Also, you have a chance to see two-dimensional caves.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

This happened to be our favorite place even though we got up early to see the sunrise but the clouds blocked the sun. It was still beautiful and the surrounding area is gorgeous. This bridge in Seogwipo harbour goes across to a small island which takes about 20 minutes to walk around.? It is a nice place to go at sunset, there are nice views and many birds in the trees.? Also nearby are the Cheoniyeon waterfalls, and a few shops and cafes.

The park is located close to the beach, it?s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.
The park has different areas including water garden, bird garden, bonsai garden, cave and folk village... Overall, the garden is very nice, huge but the entrance ticket is a bit bit bit pricey.

So much fun!  I've been twice and would like to go back very soon.  In the spring, tulips everywhere!  So many different things to do and see here.  I fed the birds this time around and what joy.Note that some animals were not in the best shape (summer heat maybe).
so many beautiful flowers, with mini bird park. also caves where you can learn about geography. there is an entrance fee but cheap. so just enjoy the beauty!

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

I found much of Jeju island to be very commercialized and crowded with loud tour groups. This is a great place to enjoy the natural beaty of Jeju with smaller groups of people. Eventually the road ends and then you follow a loop trail that is about 2 feet wide it is covered with a hemp rope mat that felt lovely to walk on with bare feet. There were signs to watch for snakes but I saw none. The yews are huge.  Make sure to investigate the tree bark it is fabric like and soft. Hallim Park is quite a beautiful park. There are so many things to see, and the flora is really quite spectacular; however, the living conditions of the animals in the park killed the whole experience for us. The turtles are in aquariums that are much too small, and the aquariums don't contain any kind of natural vegetation for the turtles. In fact, only a few turtles had only a single rock in their containers. If that wasn't depressing enough, the living conditions of the peacocks were, quite simply, inhumane. Although some lucky peacocks got to roam around in an area that was relatively open, most of the peacocks were living in small enclosures and sharing those enclosures with up to 13 other peacocks. There was hardly enough room for them to move around, and the birds seemed to be living in quite stressful conditions.  Then, there were the ostriches. All of the ostriches we saw had a terrible looking skin condition, and most of them were going bald. Compared to the flora in the park, it just seemed like the park put no effort into properly caring for the animals at all. If Hallim Park would put a little more effort into making sure their animals are properly cared for and provide better living conditions for the animals, I would recommend going to this place. However, with the current living conditions of the animals, I absolutely cannot recommend anyone go to this place.

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

A great variety of exotic trees & flowers, marvellous birds, unusual sculptures,charming waterfalls, traditional symbols of  Jeju Island.  Beautiful inspiring day.

A beautiful view on top of Seongsan IIchulbong. Plenty of parking. We did this twice in the same day. The first hike (approximately 30 minutes to get to the top, started at 1pm) was extremely foggy and we couldn't see anything. We hiked back down and spent some time on the shore. Once the sun came out we hiked back to the top. There are several stops on the way with spectacular views of Jeju. You can purchase drinks and trinkets from one small shop about half way up. Use the restroom before going up as there is not one on the way. For a family of three to include a 10 year old we took one large bottle of water and a small backpack with some snacks and additional items. Bring a camera as it is absolutely beautiful. On the way we saw several different species of birds and spiders. At the top there are several benches where you can sit and enjoy the view. At the bottom there is a Mcdonalds, an ice cream shop, a souvenir shop, and other small shops. I suggest you try the orange ice drinks...they are great! Overall cost, 5,000 won for two adults and one child. We paid cash. Enjoy!

30 mins drive out from Jeju City.  My Wife and Daughter accompanied me on the first 2.5km of the 11.1km yellow route, then they took a short cut back (around 1.2km) to relax at the Korean style picnic tables and visit the carp pond.  I took another 1.5 hrs or so to complete the yellow route, which by the way is circular, not an up and back as reported sometimes previously. I came across plenty of deer, as well as some beautiful birds and flowers.  The first 5km or so has hessian Mats to walk on, which is very peasant, but then it gets a bit muddy and rocky, with a few steep sections.....walking boots or trail shoes are definitely best, although possible in Trainers.  Really enjoyed the hike.
What a cool find we only knew about because of a brochure from our hotel. So many different animals to see and we even got to touch and feed some of them!

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We took our 27 month old daughter here mostly because she was about to fall asleep on our bike ride and we didn't want to mess up her nap schedule. When you first walk in  they have a walk through of the animals of Africa. Our daughter had a ball naming the animals and learning new ones. We loved the learning experience she got while she stared bright eyed at all the big (and small) animals. She even loved the art and seeing all the different designs (although we admittedly had to go a bit faster than normal through the rest of the museum). For this being an unplanned stop  we were thrilled we did. What a nice addition to our vacation.

Was there during winter  thus not much water can be seen under the bridge. Can see far away on the bridge  and the view was nice. Other than that  nothing much at the attraction. There was one fountain of various animals heads  and supposedly you are to face any one of them to throw in a coin and make a wish according to what you wanted.

Visited this place in Feb19 and was quite appalled by the treatment of the animals. The rabbits were allowed to roam within an enclosed area accessible to visitors. However there is no one monitoring that the rabbits are treated properly. The living conditions of the animals are filthy. The absolute horror was the black pig show. What's so entertaining about forcing terrified black pigs down a water slide?? Tasteless entertainment with no educational value. Paying the entrance fee of 13000won per person  I would expect some of it to be channeled to upkeep the living conditions of the animals. The blooms in the park were alright with spots for Instagram pictures but nothing spectacular.

Trip with friends to see underwater animals; sharks star fishes and other tortoise and outside aquarium full happiness with mini korean mart coffee and drinks and if you all like Korean food & beverages terrace

Our guide recommended visiting this place and the cave they had here  saying that it was all better than Hallim Park. Though I personally preferred Hallim Park. I found the cave here to be pretty creepy and really dark  best to skip over if you aren't into caves. There's nothing much to see in the cave anyway.

They enjoyed themselves but probably would have as much fun together at a park.  The animals were the highlight for them.  They enjoyed feeding them.  Everything that you do inside has an extra cost except the 3D film.  Worth a look if you have young children.

The actual performance was below par with just 2 ladies playing stringed instruments. There were no animals around except for 1 horse. Most of the houses were bare. The Dae Chang Geum theme park touted was actually just a small hut with some boring exhibits!

The place is good for children. Can occupy them almost half a day! There are plenty of Dino for photo moment. There is also a place to feed little cute animals and appreciate the flora in a green house. Can also drop by to catch the 3D movie. Worth a visit but please don?셳 expect a Disneyland or a universal studio.

the place is fun for walking between different kind of plants and animals. there are 3 caves and the weather inside it is cold during the summer time so you can walk there if you feel hot. there is also folk village and a water park
The place is a bit in middle of nowhere but was still good for our 3 year old who enjoyed herself watching the fake dinosaurs and the 3D show along with feeding the live animals.

The performance itself is worth the price of admission. Make sure you arrive before one of the three showtimes during the day. They provide drums and you can jam along with the performers. I find this satisfying when you have so many museums in area feigning novelty. So again  If you can get your toddlers away from the stuffed animals  then there is a rewarding human element waiting on the bottom floor.

The folk houses built well imitating earlier century jeju do livings. You can experience the way of living of older jeju do resident. Kinda way of knowing and understanding of Jeju resident. The living plant and animal were well maintain.

The aquarium is spacious.  You can see a lot of sea animals no matter how hot cold or rainy the outdoor is.  Taking a leaflet at the entrance is a must because the show time is up-dated.  It is so funny to see the penguins line up to eat food and jump up the stairs.  The otters are also interesting when you see them playing through the tunnels and on the swinging bed.  The 'stars' of the aquarium can be seen at the theatre which is attractive and interesting. My family stayed there for more than three hours.  The soft toys sold there are in good quality and my daughter bought a penguin as a souvenir.  There are food shops for people to enjoy but we didn't try any.
